# Coopmat default flip: the rung and the K24 selector ship ON (2026-11-07)

Lane `lane/coopmat-default-flip`, from main
333f35407f38e9b99d40a412e86dcf41569bbad6. The Q4_K
coopmat routing switch (`WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT`)
and the K24 v2 selector inside it
(`WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT_V2`) flip their shipped
defaults from OFF to ON, together, in the shape of
the three earlier flips (MMV ceiling b342cdf,
staged flash 82017ad, K21F head d9825eb): named
`DEFAULT_` / `_FALLBACK` constants, unset resolves
to the shipped default, a present but unrecognized
value resolves to the closed fallback (never to
the default) and is logged by name at
construction. VM gates only on this lane; no
server GPU jobs. The card evidence this flip
stands on was measured by the wave20 session,
cited below; this lane changed the two resolvers,
the bridge implication the rung needs, their
docs, and their tests. The kernels, the routing
order, and the fallback chain are untouched.

Authority: David's standing order of 2026-11-07,
"anything that makes sense engine go faster
should be set to on", applied to the wave20
verdict.

## The evidence

1. **The build and its rule**
   (bench/coopmat-v2-2026-11-07.md). K24 is the
   register-resident rebuild of the v1 coopmat
   kernel (K23): fragments and folds live in
   registers instead of staging through workgroup
   memory, the defect the v1 autopsy convicted
   (v1 measured 4.0x SLOWER than K13 on the card
   and its switch stayed off). Its element mapping
   at wave64 could not be transcribed from llama
   (which forces wave32 on AMD), so it was derived
   from Mesa's lowering source and cross-validated
   against the wave32 case; the note's decision
   rule, written in advance: K24 earns a
   default-flip proposal only on a material
   kernel-line win over K13 with speculative
   identity intact, and the numeric gates run
   first because they are the mapping proof.
2. **The verdict** (bench/wave20-session-2026-11-07.md,
   leg 2, staged from main 515ce23, all arms
   interleaved, every run failure-bundled):
   - Numeric gates EXECUTED on the card:
     tests/k24_coopmat.rs 3 passed, 0 failed, no
     skips. K24 against the host reference at
     relative error at most 1.158e-6; against K13
     at most 2.9e-7. The wave64 mapping is PROVEN.
   - Kernel line at the 1,022-token prefill shape,
     2,912 dispatches per arm: k24_q4k_coopmat
     1,737.2 / 1,751.9 ms (112 GB/s) against
     k13_q4k_mmq 4,021.0 / 4,046.5 ms (48 GB/s),
     about 2.3x faster. Prefill walls 4,052 /
     4,085 ms against 6,307 / 6,401 ms, about 36
     percent lower. The K23 v1 arm in the same
     session: 16,900.4 / 16,963.0 ms, reproducing
     its standing verdict (correct, ~4x slower);
     K23 stays a fallback, never the default.
   - Identity + golden with COOPMAT=1 +
     COOPMAT_V2=1 (+ BRIDGE=1): IDENTITY PASS and
     GOLDEN PASS, the spec stream byte-identical
     to the golden stream, spec accounting
     (rounds=38, proposed=37, accepted=25)
     identical to the shipped-default control.
     The diag manifest carried
     "coopmat":"true", "coopmat_v2":"true".
   - Autopsy: K24 LDS 33,792 B (exactly the five
     staging arrays), VGPR 132 (not the 256 cap),
     zero spills, zero scratch.

   The decision rule is MET, on every clause.

## Why both switches together

The rung and its selector are one feature.
Defaulting only the rung would ship the coopmat
path serving K23, the kernel measured ~4x slower
than K13: a regression wearing the flip's name.
Defaulting only the selector would change nothing
at all: the selector is consulted only inside an
armed rung. So `DEFAULT_COOPMAT` and
`DEFAULT_COOPMAT_V2` move in the same commit, and
each env keeps its own independent rollback.

## The bridge question

The coopmat pipelines exist only on a device the
coopmat bridge opened (VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix
enabled through wgpu-hal interop), and the bridge
had its own exact-"1" switch,
`WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT_BRIDGE`, read in
`GpuContext::open` before either routing resolver
exists. Every wave20 arm set BRIDGE=1 explicitly.
With the routing defaults on and the bridge left
exactly as it was, an unset run would open the
stock device, find no coopmat pipeline, refuse by
name at plan build, and serve K13: the flip would
be a log line, not a route. The smallest coherent
change, made in `coopmat_bridge.rs`:

- `coopmat_bridge_requested()` now reads: a
  PRESENT bridge value decides on its own, exactly
  as before (`1` opens the bridge; anything else
  refuses it, logged by name however the decision
  lands), so `WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT_BRIDGE=0` stays
  a deliberate stock-device run even with the
  routing default on, and a malformed bridge value
  can never be widened by the routing default.
- With the bridge variable UNSET, the request
  defers to the routing switch's unset position
  (`compute::resolve_coopmat(None)`, which is
  `DEFAULT_COOPMAT`): routing default on means the
  device opens through the bridge so the rung can
  engage; `WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT=0` means nothing
  asks for a bridged device and the stock open
  serves byte-for-byte as before the flip.

Nothing about the bridge itself changed: the
probes (extension exposed, feature bit, the
required s8 x s8 to s32 16x16x16 subgroup property
row) still gate every bridged open, every refusal
is still named on the diag channel with the stock
device serving instead, and the defaults-confirmation
session already proved the bridge numerically
transparent (bench/defaults-confirmation-2026-11-07.md,
leg 3: a bridge-only run's stream byte-identical
to the stock run's). Consequences of the new
default, stated plainly: every default run now
pays the bridge's device-open probes (read-only
driver queries at startup) and, on a card without
coopmat, logs the bridge refusal once and serves
the stock ladder exactly. On the target card the
probes pass and the rung engages.

## The semantic matrix (final, both envs)

| env value | rung (`WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT`) | selector (`WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT_V2`) |
|---|---|---|
| unset | ON (the shipped default) | SELECTED: K24 serves the rung |
| `1` (trimmed) | ON | SELECTED |
| `0` (trimmed) | OFF (explicit off; the rollback) | DESELECTED: K23 serves the rung (explicit off; the rollback) |
| anything else | OFF, fail-closed | DESELECTED, fail-closed |

A malformed value resolves to the closed fallback
(`COOPMAT_FALLBACK` / `COOPMAT_V2_FALLBACK`, both
`false`), NOT to the shipped default, and the
refusal is logged by name at construction:
`mmq coopmat env WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT=<value> is
not a recognized value ("1" or unset enables, "0"
disables); failing closed, the coopmat rung is
OFF`, and the selector's twin line. The
construction log lines now read
`mmq coopmat config: enabled=<bool> (env
WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT, "1" or unset enables, "0"
disables); k23_coopmat=<bool>` and
`mmq coopmat v2 config: selected=<bool> (env
WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT_V2, "1" or unset selects
K24, "0" selects K23; consulted only when the
coopmat switch is on); k24_coopmat=<bool>`.
Resolution still happens once at backend
construction; the `coopmat` / `coopmat_v2`
accessors and the resolved pair in both sessions'
diag manifests are unchanged in shape and now
report the flipped defaults.

Rollbacks, each one variable, no rebuild:
`WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT=0` closes the rung (the
pre-flip ladder exactly); `WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT_V2=0`
keeps the rung and restores K23 as its form;
`WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT_BRIDGE=0` forces the stock
device (the rung then refuses by name and the
standard ladder serves).

## What did not change

- The kernels (K23, K24, their shaders and
  artifacts), the routing order in
  `session::mmq_product_q4k` (coopmat rung first,
  K24 inside it, then wide, K22, K23-repack, K13),
  and the fallback chain: a K24 prepare refusal
  falls through to K23 by name, a K23 refusal to
  the standard ladder, and a missing pipeline
  refuses by name at plan build.
- The K23_MMQ repack switch (a different K23,
  measured 2.15x slower in its own verdict) stays
  exactly as it was: default off, untouched by
  this flip.
- Split-K, f16 KV, and every other default: this
  lane flips the coopmat pair only.

## Pins

- `compute::tests::coopmat_switch_resolution`
  re-pinned to the flipped matrix (unset on,
  `1` on, `0` off, malformed off), comments citing
  the wave20 kernel-line and wall numbers; the
  unset arm pins `DEFAULT_COOPMAT` and the
  malformed arms pin `COOPMAT_FALLBACK`.
- `compute::tests::coopmat_v2_selector_resolution`
  re-pinned the same way (unset selected, `0`
  deselects), citing the wave20 numeric-gate
  bounds (1.158e-6 against the reference, 2.9e-7
  against K13) and the 2.3x line; pins
  `DEFAULT_COOPMAT_V2` and `COOPMAT_V2_FALLBACK`.
- New `compute::tests::coopmat_value_recognition`
  and `compute::tests::coopmat_v2_value_recognition`,

===== FILE: bench/coopmat-feasibility-2026-11-06.md =====
# Coopmat prefill feasibility: is WMMA reachable from this stack? (2026-11-06)

Lane: lane/coopmat-prefill-spike, based on main a064b5d.
Local VM work only: crate sources read in the local cargo
registry, repo sources read in this worktree, two web checks.
No server GPU time used.

**Verdict in one line:** cooperative matrix is NOT
reachable through anything wgpu exposes: the locked wgpu
27 stack has no coopmat feature, no WGSL syntax, and no
Naga support for it, at any layer. It IS reachable through
one unsafe bridge this codebase could build: create the
Vulkan device ourselves with VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix
enabled, hand it to wgpu through its hal `device_from_raw`
API, and feed hand-compiled SPIR-V through wgpu's
passthrough shader path. The driver side is not the
obstacle: RADV has exposed the extension on RDNA3 since
Mesa 23.3 and llama.cpp runs coopmat matmuls on this card
class in production. **No prototype is built in this
lane**, for one concrete reason stated in full below: the
coopmat SPIR-V blob, the one artifact that makes it a
prototype, cannot be produced or validated by any tool
present on this VM or in the lockfile, so the lane ships
this evidence file, the costed build plan, and the exact
server protocol to judge the build when it is ordered.

## The three layers of the answer

| Layer | Coopmat? | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hardware + driver (gfx1100, RADV, Mesa 26.0.8) | YES | Extension exposed for GFX11+ under ACO since Mesa 23.3; llama.cpp coopmat pipelines run on RDNA3 today |
| Vulkan bindings in the lock (ash 0.38) | YES | Complete KHR_cooperative_matrix bindings, already a transitive dependency |
| wgpu 27 (safe API, WGSL, Naga, hal device creation) | NO | Zero support at every layer; see below |

## Evidence 1: the wgpu stack has no coopmat anywhere

Versions are the repo's own lockfile (Cargo.lock: ash
line 31, naga line 569, wgpu line 1016, wgpu-hal line
1119): wgpu 27.0.1, wgpu-core 27.0.3, wgpu-hal 27.0.4,
wgpu-types 27.0.1, naga 27.0.3, ash 0.38.0+1.3.281.

Method: case-insensitive grep for `cooperative` over the
`src` trees of the extracted registry sources of wgpu,
wgpu-types, wgpu-core, wgpu-hal, and naga. Result: **0
hits in all five crates.** Only ash has hits (149),
because ash generates bindings for every Vulkan
extension regardless of who uses them.

Corroboration from the feature surface itself:
wgpu-types 27.0.1 `src/features.rs` defines the complete
native `Features` set; the shader-relevant entries are
`SHADER_F16` (bit 9 in the WebGPU set), `SUBGROUP`
(1 << 38, features.rs:1070), `SUBGROUP_VERTEX`,
`SUBGROUP_BARRIER`, and
`EXPERIMENTAL_PASSTHROUGH_SHADERS` (1 << 52,
features.rs:1233). There is no cooperative-matrix
feature, and no feature bit is left ambiguous: the list
was read in full. Naga 27.0.3 has subgroup support
(`src/back/spv/subgroup.rs`) but no cooperative matrix
type in its IR, no WGSL syntax for one, and its SPIR-V
frontend cannot ingest the coopmat opcodes (the
`spirv` header crate it shares does define them:
`TypeCooperativeMatrixKHR = 4456`,
`CooperativeMatrixLoadKHR = 4457`,
`CooperativeMatrixMulAddKHR = 4459`, capability
`CooperativeMatrixKHR = 6022`, in
spirv-0.3.0/autogen_spirv.rs:2232 and :3366-3369; the
opcodes exist as constants, with no consumer).

Consequence for this codebase: every shipped kernel
(K1-K22) is WGSL compiled by Naga, and the crate's
shader_compile test gate validates each one on the VM
before any card time is spent. A coopmat kernel cannot
enter through that door at all.

## Evidence 2: the passthrough door exists but does not open by itself

wgpu 27 does ship an experimental shader passthrough:

- `Device::create_shader_module_passthrough`
  (wgpu-27.0.1/src/api/device.rs:189), unsafe, "passes
  data to the backend as-is".
- wgpu-core gates it on the device feature:
  `require_features(EXPERIMENTAL_PASSTHROUGH_SHADERS)`
  (wgpu-core-27.0.3/src/device/resource.rs:2144), then
  wraps the caller's words as `hal::ShaderInput::SpirV`
  for the Vulkan backend.
- wgpu-hal's Vulkan backend feeds those words verbatim
  to VkShaderModule creation:
  `ShaderInput::SpirV(data) =>
  ShaderModule::Raw(self.create_shader_module_impl(data, ...))`
  (wgpu-hal-27.0.4/src/vulkan/device.rs:1963-1965).
- The Vulkan adapter advertises the feature
  unconditionally (wgpu-hal-27.0.4/src/vulkan/
  adapter.rs:567, in the base feature set).

But a passthrough SPIR-V module that declares
`OpCapability CooperativeMatrixKHR` requires, per the
VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix specification, the extension
enabled on the VkDevice and the
`VkPhysicalDeviceCooperativeMatrixFeaturesKHR.
cooperativeMatrix` feature turned on; pipeline creation
against a device without them violates the spec's
valid-usage rules and is undefined behaviour territory,
not a portability bet. And wgpu-hal's own device
creation can never enable it: the device extension list
is computed from the requested wgpu features by
`PhysicalDeviceCapabilities::get_required_extensions`
(wgpu-hal-27.0.4/src/vulkan/adapter.rs:985), consumed by
`required_device_extensions` (adapter.rs:1878), and the
crate contains no reference to the extension at all
(the zero-hit grep above covers this file). There is no
public wgpu knob, flag, or env var that adds a device
extension. **Path A, passthrough on the wgpu-created
device, is therefore not a shortcut; it is a spec
violation. Nobody should ship it.**

## Evidence 3: the bridge wgpu does offer

wgpu-hal's Vulkan adapter exposes the raw-device
integration route, and the safe wgpu crate wraps it:

- `PhysicalDevice::device_from_raw(raw_device:
  ash::Device, ...)` (wgpu-hal-27.0.4/src/vulkan/
  adapter.rs:1932) builds a hal device around a
  VkDevice the caller created. Its companion
  `physical_device_features` doc comment states the
  intended use: "it's fine to add more extensions to
  the list" (adapter.rs:1906).
- `Adapter::create_device_from_hal`
  (wgpu-27.0.1/src/api/adapter.rs:76) turns that hal
  device into a normal (wgpu::Device, wgpu::Queue);
  `Instance::from_hal` (instance.rs:328) and
  `Instance::create_adapter_from_hal` (instance.rs:385)
  cover the instance and adapter ends.

So the caller can create the ash instance and device
with `VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix` in
ppEnabledExtensionNames and
`vk::PhysicalDeviceCooperativeMatrixFeaturesKHR`
(ash-0.38.0: src/vk/definitions.rs:54385) chained into
device creation with cooperative_matrix = true, hand
the device to wgpu, and from then on use the ordinary
wgpu API, including passthrough shader modules whose
coopmat pipelines the driver will now accept. ash's
bindings for the extension are complete, including
`get_physical_device_cooperative_matrix_properties`
(ash-0.38.0: src/extensions/khr/
cooperative_matrix.rs:1-17), which is how the supported
shapes get probed at runtime. ash 0.38 and wgpu-hal 27
are already in this repo's lockfile as wgpu's
dependencies; making them direct dependencies of
wgpu-compute adds no new packages to the lock.

## Evidence 4: the driver and the reference implementation

- RADV merged VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix for RDNA3
  (GFX11) and newer on top of the WMMA instructions in
  Mesa 23.3 (Phoronix, "RADV Vulkan Driver Merges
  Cooperative Matrix Support Using RDNA3 WMMA"). Mesa's
  own extension table conditions it on
  `gfx_level >= GFX11 && !pdev->use_llvm` and the
  feature on the ACO compiler path. The server's
  gfx1100 under Mesa 26.0.8 with ACO satisfies both,
  three Mesa majors past the introduction.
- llama.cpp's Vulkan backend, the same tree whose
  baselines this project measures against (prefill
  998.43 tok/s on this card), selects cooperative
  matrix variants of mul_mm whenever
  `device->coopmat_support` is true, with GLSL shaders
  (`mul_mm_cm1.comp`, gated on
  `VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix` +
  `GGML_VULKAN_COOPMAT_GLSLC_SUPPORT`) that dequantize
  into shared memory and run fp16 coopmat GEMMs. In
  2026 it added an int8 coopmat1 MMQ shader covering
  q4_k and q6_k on RDNA3/RDNA4 (ggml-org/llama.cpp
  PR #27952, shipped in release b11160). The mechanism
  this note evaluates is therefore not speculative: it
  is the incumbent's production prefill path on this
  hardware family.

What remains genuinely unknown until a probe runs on
the server: the exact cooperative matrix property rows
RADV reports for gfx1100 (the RDNA3 WMMA shape is
16x16x16, f16 inputs, f32 accumulate; the int8 rows
llama's MMQ relies on, and the per-scope support, must
be read from
`vkGetPhysicalDeviceCooperativeMatrixPropertiesKHR`,
not assumed), and whether the wave32 subgroup pinning
llama applies to its coopmat pipelines (RDNA WMMA is
wave32-native; at wave64 each op issues as two halves)
can be expressed through wgpu pipeline creation or must
ride in the SPIR-V execution modes. Both are step 0 of
the server protocol below, deliberately before any
shader work.

## Why this lane ships evidence, not a prototype

The buildable path needs one artifact this lane cannot
produce: a compiled coopmat SPIR-V module. The facts:

- No GLSL/SPIR-V toolchain exists on this VM:
  `glslangValidator`, `glslc`, `spirv-as`, `spirv-dis`
  are all absent from PATH, and `apt-get install
  --dry-run glslang-tools` answers "Unable to locate
  package". The lockfile contains no shaderc, glslang,
  or spirv-tools crate; adding shaderc-sys means a
  vendored C++ build (ninja is also absent) and a
  workspace-level dependency change, the opposite of a
  minimal spike.
- Hand-assembling SPIR-V words in Rust is possible in
  principle (the header constants above), but the
  result would be unverifiable here by construction:
  Naga cannot parse it (Evidence 1), no validator is
  installed, and this VM enumerates no Vulkan ICD at
  all (`/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d` does not exist), so
  not even wgpu's passthrough acceptance could be
  smoke-tested. Every prior kernel in this project
  (K19-K22 included) was Naga-validated on the VM
  before it consumed serialized card time; a coopmat
  blob would arrive at the card with zero validation
  of its most failure-prone component, and its first
  card session would be spent on load errors instead
  of measurement.
- The device bridge code itself (300-500 lines of
  unsafe, see costing) type-checks but likewise
  executes nothing on this VM: with no adapter, every
  run is the skip path. Writing it blind, unexecuted,
  alongside an uncompilable shader, produces an
  artifact whose honest label is "draft", and this
  project's rule is that claims separate what was
  executed from what was merely accepted.

The settlement the lane was asked for does not depend
on the prototype: reachability is a property of the
APIs and the driver, and both are now pinned to file
and line. The build is a follow-on lane with a known
shape, costed next.

## The build, costed (Path B, the only viable one)

If ordered, in order:

1. **Probe first** (server, minutes): the step-0
   protocol below. If RADV's property rows lack an
   f16 16x16x16 row usable from compute, the project
   stops here for the cost of one probe run.
2. **Device bridge** in crates/wgpu-compute/src/
   device.rs: replace the `adapter.request_device`
   call (device.rs:89) with hal instance init,
   physical-device selection identical to today's,
   ash device creation adding VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix
   plus its feature struct (and every extension/feature
   wgpu-hal requires for the requested feature set,
   obtained from `required_device_extensions` /
   `physical_device_features` so the two never drift),
   then `device_from_raw` +
   `create_device_from_hal`, requesting
   EXPERIMENTAL_PASSTHROUGH_SHADERS. Estimate 300-500
   lines, all unsafe, behind the existing GpuContext
   constructor so no call site changes. New direct
   deps: ash = "0.38", wgpu-hal = "27" (both already in
   the lock). RISK, stated plainly: the bridge becomes
   load-bearing for every kernel, not one; a bridge
   defect breaks the whole backend, and wgpu minor
   upgrades can move the hal integration surface.
   Mitigation: the bridge is used only when an env
   flag asks for it, with the shipped request_device
   path as the default and fallback, until the coopmat
   verdict is in.
3. **The shader**: a GLSL compute shader modeled on
   llama.cpp's mul_mm_cm1 shape (dequantize Q4_K to
   f16 tiles in LDS, coopmat load/mul-add/store,
   16x16x16), specialized for the prefill band (batch
   64, hidden 6656, the K13 shapes), compiled to SPIR-V
   by glslangValidator. The toolchain decision is part
   of the cost: either a build.rs step invoking
   glslangValidator (present on the server inside the
   llama.cpp build tree; a new host dependency for any
   other machine) or a committed .spv with its .comp
   source beside it and the compile command recorded.
   Estimate 400-700 lines of GLSL. Permanent gate hole,
   disclosed: Naga cannot validate this module, so the
   crate's shader_compile test can never cover it; its
   correctness rests on the on-card numeric test alone,
   like the driver itself.
4. **Routing**: a prefill-only arm beside the MMQ
   ladder in the prepare path, env-gated
   (WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT=1), default off, falling back
   to K13/K14 on any refusal, with diag stamps from
   birth. Q6_K follows only if Q4_K pays; the tiny
   256-wide Q6_K KV shapes stay on the fusion fix
   (attack 5), not on coopmat.
5. **Tests**: numeric correctness against the K13 MMQ
   output on identical inputs under the crate's
   existing tolerance rules, resident identity +
   golden with the flag on, prefill A/B through the
   prefill_profile harness, env-unset no-leak check.
   Same shape as the K22 protocol, plus the probe.

Total estimate: 900-1,400 lines across the bridge, the
shader, routing, and tests, one new host toolchain
dependency, one permanent validation-gate hole, and a
second prefill code path to keep correct forever. The
ceiling it buys is the profile note's own arithmetic
(bench/prefill-profile-2026-11-05.md:281-290): the
same 650 GB/s streaming bound as the plain MMQ rework,
about 347 tok/s wall on the 1,022-token profile,
because the binding constraint becomes the dequant
feed, not the multiply. Coopmat does not raise the
ceiling; it changes which wall you hit first, and it
is the only remaining path whose instruction stream
bypasses the VGPR-256 occupancy wall entirely (the
matrix units hold the accumulators, not the register
file). That, and not a higher ceiling, is the honest
case for building it after K22's verdict.

## Rejected paths

- **Path A, passthrough on the stock device.**
  Invalid, not merely risky: the extension is never
  enabled (Evidence 2). Any "it worked on my run"
  result would be a driver accepting a spec violation.
- **Path C, a native Vulkan side channel** (a second
  ash instance/device beside wgpu, behind the Backend
  trait). wgpu's public API offers no external-memory
  import or export for its buffers; `create_buffer_
  from_hal` (wgpu-27.0.1/src/api/device.rs:371) wraps
  only buffers belonging to the same hal device. A
  side device therefore cannot read the resident
  weights or write results the session can consume:
  it would need its own 16.76 GB copy of the model,
  a host round-trip for every chunk's activations and
  outputs, and its own synchronization domain, forking
  the Compute seam end to end. Strictly worse than
  Path B on every axis; dead unless Path B's probe
  fails in a way that leaves raw Vulkan viable, which
  it would not (same driver).
- **Path D, wait for upstream wgpu/Naga support.**
  Nothing in the locked stack points at it: no feature
  bit, no IR type, no frontend support, and WGSL
  itself has no cooperative matrix types. Not a plan.

## Ranked next-best prefill levers (updated)

From bench/prefill-profile-2026-11-05.md's ranked
list, re-stated at today's state (GPU total 6,659 ms,
MMQ pair 5,542 ms of it, on the 1,022-token profile):

1. **MMQ rework for occupancy** (attack 1). Ceiling:
   at the GEMV-proven 650 GB/s the pair's 5,542 ms
   becomes 371 ms, wall about 2,945 ms, about
   347 tok/s; at 300 GB/s, about 274 tok/s. Status:
   the register-organization variant (K22) is spent,
   ACO re-inflated it to the 256 cap; what remains
   inside this attack is llama's staging repack with
   permuted B order (K22's named follow-up) and
   schedule variants not yet tried. Still the only
   lever with a multiple in it that stays inside the
   WGSL/Naga gate.
2. **Coopmat MMQ** (attack 3, this note). Same
   347 tok/s ceiling, higher risk, second code path;
   ranked above the rest now only because attack 1's
   cheapest variant is spent and coopmat is the one
   path that exits the register file entirely.
3. **Host serialization removal** (attack 2). DONE
   and confirmed since the profile: the shipped
   prefill wall is 6,330 ms (161.5 tok/s) against the
   profile's 8,116 ms. Its ceiling is spent; listed
   so the ranking stays honest.
4. **Flash attention rework** (attack 4). Halving
   flash saves 507 ms at 1,022 tokens (about
   166 GPU-bound tok/s) and grows quadratically; at
   the 131k context target this becomes the first
   lever. Sequencing, not size, keeps it here.
5. **Fuse the tiny Q6_K KV-side dispatches**
   (attack 5): 416 dispatches, 186 ms at 3.2 GB/s,
   2.8% of GPU time. Small, safe, independent; the
   natural filler lane while a big one runs.
6. **Raise chunk rows 64 -> 128+** (attack 6): low
   single digits until a kernel streams properly;
   valuable only after 1 or 2 lands.

## Server protocol to judge the build (for the follow-on lane)

Run under the phase lock, card cleared, staging
verified, in this order; stop at the first failure
and report it by name:

0. **Probe.** A minimal ash probe (or vulkaninfo
   --json) on the server: confirm
   VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix in the device extension
   list for the gfx1100 device and dump every
   CooperativeMatrixPropertiesKHR row (M, N, K,
   A/B/C/accumulator types, scope). Confirm an f16
   16x16x16 f32-accumulate row exists for compute.
   Also confirm glslangValidator's location in the
   llama.cpp build tree. No shader work before this
   passes.
1. **Compile + inspect.** glslangValidator -V
   --target-env vulkan1.3 on the .comp source;
   spirv-dis the result and confirm
   OpTypeCooperativeMatrixKHR and
   OpCooperativeMatrixMulAddKHR are present and the
   CooperativeMatrixKHR capability is declared.
2. **Bridge smoke.** The bridged device initializes
   through GpuContext with the flag on; the full
   resident suite passes on it with coopmat routing
   still off (the bridge must be a no-op for every
   existing kernel before it carries a new one).
3. **Correctness.** The coopmat Q4_K product at batch
   64, hidden 6656 against the K13 MMQ reference on
   identical inputs, under the crate's tolerance
   rules; then resident identity + golden with
   routing on.
4. **Prefill A/B.** prefill_profile harness, flag on
   vs off, against K13's recorded 4,199.9 ms /
   46.4 GB/s for the Q4_K MMQ line and the current
   shipped wall of 6,330 ms.
5. **No-leak.** Flag unset: dispatch-for-dispatch
   identical to today's shipped path.

Decision rule, written before the run: coopmat
routing earns a default only if step 0 shows the
shapes, step 3 is clean, and step 4 beats the K13
line materially (not within noise) at equal
correctness. Anything less and it stays an env-gated
experiment, like K18/K19/K22 before it.

## Caveats and claims ledger

- Executed in this lane: the greps and source reads
  above (all local, reproducible from the registry
  paths cited), the lockfile read, the PATH/apt
  probes. Nothing was compiled, and nothing ran on a
  GPU; this VM has no Vulkan device to run on.
- Read, not executed: every wgpu/wgpu-hal/wgpu-core/
  ash behavior claim rests on the cited source lines
  of the exact locked versions.
- Web-sourced: the RADV support facts (Phoronix on
  the Mesa 23.3 merge; Mesa's extension condition)
  and llama.cpp's coopmat usage (ggml-org/llama.cpp
  PR #27952 and the b11160 release notes). Both are
  corroborated by the server's own recorded baseline:
  llama.cpp Vulkan prefill at 998.43 tok/s on this
  card is not achievable through the scalar path
  alone, and its coopmat pipelines are the documented
  difference.
- The one fact this lane could not settle locally is
  RADV's exact property rows on gfx1100; it is step 0
  of the protocol, priced at minutes, and gates
  everything after it.

===== FILE: bench/coopmat-v2-2026-11-07.md =====
# Coopmat v2 (K24): autopsy of v1, the register-resident rebuild, and the card protocol owed

Date: 2026-11-07. Lane: lane/coopmat-v2, from main
0ecdc8ff5efc3da0d00b5806c8f2796b65096132. VM work only;
no server GPU jobs were run for this lane. The card
verdict is owed under the protocol at the end.

State of the art this builds on: the coopmat bridge
works and is numerically transparent
(bench/coopmat-build-2026-11-06.md,
bench/defaults-confirmation-2026-11-07.md). The v1
kernel (K23, stamp k23_q4k_coopmat) is correct
everywhere and 4.0x slower than K13 at the kernel
line: 16,951.3 ms / 11.5 GB/s against K13's
4,250.1 ms / 45.9 GB/s over 2,912 dispatches at the
1,022-token prefill shape; wall 19,851 ms against
7,164 ms. The routing flag WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT
stays off. This note is the v2 build record: the
autopsy first, then what v2 changed, then the exact
card protocol that judges it.

## The autopsy: v1 against llama's mul_mmq_cm1

Sources read in full for this diff: our
crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/coopmat/k23_q4k_coopmat.comp;
llama.cpp's ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/vulkan-shaders/
mul_mmq_cm1.comp and mul_mmq_cm1_funcs.glsl (VM
mirror, sha256-identical to the server tree of the
a7af149 lineage); ggml-vulkan.cpp's cm1 enablement
and warptile construction; Mesa's
src/amd/vulkan/nir/radv_nir_lower_cooperative_matrix.c
(the RADV lowering that defines the fragment layouts
on the target driver).

### Structural diff, axis by axis

**Cooperative-matrix tile shape and tiles per
subgroup.** Same 16x16x16 s8 x s8 to s32 tiles (the
only shape the card's property rows offer). Per
subgroup the warp tile differs in size, not shape:
llama's large class runs BM 128 x BN 128 with
WM 32 x WN 32 warp tiles at wave32 (16 subgroups of
32 in a 512-thread workgroup, cms_per_row =
cms_per_col = 2, CM_ELEMS 8, 32 f32 sums per thread).
v1 runs 128 x 64 with WM 64 x WN 32 at wave64 (4
subgroups of 64 in a 256-thread workgroup,
cms_per_row 4, cms_per_col 2, 32 f32 sums per
thread under its slice mapping). The batch side is
capped at 64 by this backend's MMQ band contract
(K13's MMQ_MAX_BATCH), so the 128-wide batch tile is
not available to either of our kernels; that is a
contract difference, not a craft difference.

**Subgroup width (the axis v1's build note did not
name).** llama runs cm1 on AMD at wave32:
ggml-vulkan.cpp computes cm1_use_wave32 (vendor AMD,
subgroup size control present, range covering 32)
and builds the pipeline requiring a 32-wide
subgroup, with WARP set to 32, so USE_MAGIC_BIAS is
false on this stack. Our stack cannot do that: the
passthrough path hands wgpu a shader module and
wgpu creates the pipeline; there is no
required-subgroup-size control through it, so our
kernels run at the device subgroup size the bridge
probes, 64, and K23's constructor requires exactly
that. Every wave-dependent choice in v2 is made for
wave64 on purpose, below.

**Weight staging.** Identical in structure: llama's
split layout transcribed in v1 (raw nibble codes at
QPITCH 36 with the +4 bank skew, (d*scale,
-(dmin*min)) vec2 pairs in a separate array). One
real difference: llama splits staging into a
PREFETCH_BLOCK (global loads into registers) and a
STORE_BLOCK_TO_LDS, prefetching the next chunk
while the current one computes. v1 loads global to
LDS directly per chunk, behind barriers. The B-side
x4 de-interleave repack in mul_mmq_funcs.glsl
belongs to llama's scalar MMQ path and its packed
input layout; our K12 output is already flat, and
v1's activation staging already mirrors the cm1
layout, so there is no repack gap on the coopmat
path.

**Activation staging and quantize path.** Identical:
K12's Q8_1 words staged flat, (d, d*sum) split into
two float arrays, the sum pre-scaled by d under the
same convention ggml's MMQ quantizer uses.

**The product loop (where the kernels actually
differ).** Per 32-element sub-block:
- Fragment loads: v1 loads fragments inside the
  (r, c, h) nest, 32 coopMatLoads: the A fragment
  reloaded once per column tile (x2), the B
  fragment once per row tile (x4). llama preloads
  register arrays once per sub-block (its Q4_K
  branch comment: "Preload all A/B fragments up
  front (ILP)"), 12 loads, reused across all tiles.
- The fold: v1 stores every finished 16x16 int tile
  to a shared fold tile (coopMatStore), subgroup
  barrier, scalar fold by the half of the subgroup
  whose columns fall in the tile, subgroup barrier:
  per staged chunk (4 sub-blocks x 8 tiles) that is
  32 coopMatStores and 64 subgroup barriers, with
  the matrix units serialized behind scalar LDS
  folds. llama folds in-register: it reads acc[e]
  directly and applies cm1_accumulate per element,
  with the element's row given by cm_elem_row and
  its column fixed per thread. Zero coopMatStores,
  zero barriers in the compute phase.
- Scale reads: v1 re-reads the weight scale pair
  per folded element out of the fold loop; llama
  reads scale_a/ma once per (r, e) and scale_b/bs
  once per (c) into registers. A consequence of the
  fold form, not a separate cause.

**Occupancy limiters.** v1 stages 37,888 B of LDS,
which caps it at 1 workgroup per CU on RDNA3's
64 KB LDS, and its grid at the wide prefill shapes
is 52 workgroups (out 6656 / 128) against K13
m64's 104, on a 96-CU card: 44 CUs idle and no
second workgroup anywhere to hide latency. No ACO
shaderstats for v1 were ever captured (the build
note records VGPR/spill data only for the WGSL
kernels); from the source's resource shape, v1's
per-thread state is small (32 f32 sums, few
indices), so LDS, not VGPR, is its occupancy cap.
llama's cm1 large class runs 512-thread workgroups
over a 128 x 128 tile: at out 6656 and batch 128
that is 52 x 8 = 416 workgroups. Our batch cap
makes that grid unreachable regardless of kernel
craft.

### Ranked causes

1. **The LDS fold in the inner loop.** 32
   coopMatStores plus 64 subgroup barriers per
   128-element chunk, each tile's product waiting on
   a scalar fold performed by half a subgroup while
   the other half idles. This is the only per-tile
   synchronous LDS round-trip in either kernel, it
   sits on the critical path of every sub-block, and
   it was the v1 build note's own first-named
   suspect ("the element-extraction epilogue in
   llama's cm_elem_row form"). Evidence: v1 source;
   llama's fold is register-only.
2. **Fragment reload multiplication.** 32
   coopMatLoads per sub-block against llama's 12,
   each an LDS cooperative load issued between
   muladds instead of once up front. The A-side
   reload factor is 2 (per column tile), the B-side
   4 (per row tile). Evidence: v1's loop nest
   against llama's cache_a/cache_b preload.
3. **Occupancy and grid (context, not the design
   target).** 37,888 B LDS pins 1 workgroup per CU
   and the grid is half of K13's at the wide shapes,
   so nothing hides the latency of causes 1 and 2.
   Deleting the fold tile returns only 4,096 B
   (33,792 B still exceeds the 32 KB that a second
   workgroup per CU would need), so this cause is
   recorded, not chased: v2 removes the latency
   itself instead of trying to hide it.

## What v2 changes (one design story)

K24 (stamp k24_q4k_coopmat; module
crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/k24_q4k_coopmat.rs;
shader crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/coopmat/
k24_q4k_coopmat.comp): the product loop stops
round-tripping through LDS; fragments and folds
live in registers.

- **Fragment preload.** Per sub-block, cache_a[4*2]
  and cache_b[2*2] register arrays loaded once with
  v1's exact coopMatLoad expressions, then reused
  for every (r, c) tile: 12 loads per sub-block.
- **In-register fold.** Per (r, c): the accumulator
  is built from the cached fragments and folded
  element by element with llama's cm1_accumulate
  identity in its plain (non-magic-bias) shape,
  sums[tile_idx * CM_ELEMS + e] in llama's indexing.
  buf_tile, every coopMatStore, and every
  subgroupBarrier are deleted; the workgroup
  barriers around staging are the only barriers
  left. The final store is llama's per-element
  guarded form.
- **The element mapping, and its evidence.** The
  fold reads acc[e] as tile element (row, col) with
  col = inv % 16 and row = (inv / 16) + 4e,
  CM_ELEMS = 4. This is Mesa's GFX11 wave64
  accumulator layout, read out of
  radv_nir_lower_cooperative_matrix: its load, store,
  and element-coordinate lowerings compute
  base_row = inv / 16 (radv_get_base_row),
  row_iter = e * wave_size / 16 = 4e at wave64,
  inner_idx = inv & 15, and the accumulator length
  16*16/64 = 4. The same formulas at wave32 give
  row (inv/16) + 2e and 8 elements, which is exactly
  llama's cm_elem_row, cross-validating the method
  against an independent implementation. llama's
  formula transcribed blindly would have been wrong
  here precisely because llama runs wave32 and this
  stack runs wave64 (see the autopsy). The mapping
  is a GFX11 layout; GFX11.5/12 take a different
  branch of the Mesa lowering and are out of scope,
  as they are for K23. The card numeric gate below
  is the proof on the target card: a wrong mapping
  scrambles rows and columns and fails by a wide
  margin, not by noise.

### Deliberately not changed

- Staging layout, loaders, QPITCH 36, the (d*scale,
  -(dmin*min)) and (d, d*sum) split arrays: byte for
  byte v1's transcription of llama's.
- Tile geometry: 128 x 64 workgroup tile, four
  subgroups of 64 owning 64 x 32, BK 32 in BK_STEP 4
  chunks, 256 threads. Same grid math (52 x 1 at
  out 6656, batch 64).
- The accumulate identity and its term order (the
  fma form is llama's expression shape; reassociation
  noise stays inside the MMQ check_close band the
  K13 parity gate uses).
- Magic bias: not adopted. llama's AMD
  configuration does not use it (WARP 32 makes
  USE_MAGIC_BIAS false), and at wave64 the plain
  path's float(acc[e]) conversion is exact for this
  kernel's dots (bounded by 32 * 15 * 127 = 60,960,
  far inside f32's exact-integer range).
- Staging prefetch split (llama's PREFETCH_BLOCK):
  a staging-side change and a different design
  story. Recorded here as the next step if the card
  convicts staging after the product loop is fixed.
- The buffer contract, the shape contract, and the
  call shape: K24's prepare/run are K23's, so plans
  swap forms without moving a byte.

### Routing

Behind the existing pair of switches, both
fail-closed exact-"1", resolved at backend
construction in compute.rs: WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT
(the routing switch, unchanged) arms the coopmat
rung; WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT_V2 (new) selects K24
over K23 inside that rung. Selector on but pipeline
absent, or K24 prepare refusing: the refusal is
logged by name and the v1 form serves, then the
standard ladder, exactly the rung's existing
fallback discipline. Both resolved values are named
in both sessions' diag manifests (coopmat,
coopmat_v2 pairs beside k21f_head). At shipped
defaults (both unset) nothing changes: the coopmat
rung is out of the ladder and K13 serves.

### Build and VM gates

- The shader was compiled on this VM with glslang
  16.6.0 (official Khronos release binary). Before
  trusting it, the same binary recompiled v1's
  checked-in shader to a byte-identical artifact
  against the server-produced original, so the
  toolchain is proven equivalent on this exact
  shader family. spirv-val (SPIRV-Tools 2025.1)
  passes on the v2 artifact (22,392 B).
- The disassembly (checked in beside the artifact)
  shows the structural claim at the binary level:
  OpTypeCooperativeMatrixKHR, OpCooperativeMatrixLoadKHR,
  and OpCooperativeMatrixMulAddKHR present;
  OpCooperativeMatrixStoreKHR absent (0 occurrences).
  Its workgroup variables are exactly the five
  staging arrays (uint[4608], vec2[512], uint[2304],
  float[256], float[256] = 33,792 B), matching the
  Rust constructor's STAGING_BYTES, which a unit
  test re-derives.
- rebuild-k24.sh sits beside rebuild.sh and asserts
  the same inventory (store absent) after a rebuild.
- Unit tests (VM): shape contract and grid math
  (K23's pins), the staging-bytes derivation, the
  artifact instruction walk (coopmat ops present,
  store count exactly 0), shader-text pins for the
  v2 structure (preload array declarations and
  sizes, the wave64 cm_elem_row formula, CM_ELEMS,
  QPITCH and the staging array declarations, the
  sums indexing, and the absence of buf_tile,
  coopMatStore(, and subgroupBarrier(), and the
  selector resolution test in compute.rs. The
  on-card numeric fixtures (tests/k24_coopmat.rs:
  host reference, K13 parity, and K23 A/B parity at
  width 6656, batches 64 and 62; the full square;
  the batch-band refusals) skip by name on this
  adapterless VM, as v1's do; they execute in the
  card protocol below.
- Gate tallies (this lane tree, after the final
  edit): cargo test -p wgpu-compute green across all
  targets (lib suite ok, 0 failed; the six new tests
  are compute::tests::coopmat_v2_selector_resolution
  and the five kernels::k24_q4k_coopmat::tests);
  integration targets k23_coopmat 3 passed and
  k24_coopmat 3 passed, both on the adapterless-VM
  skip path by design; clippy -p wgpu-compute
  --all-targets -D warnings clean (one dead-code nit
  on the first pass, the shader-source const moved
  into the test module, re-run clean); fmt --check
  clean; cargo test -p dflash 24 passed; cargo test
  -p itak-spec 49 passed; cargo check --workspace
  clean.

## The card protocol owed

Run on ubuntu-server (RX 7900 XTX, RADV Mesa
26.0.8), staging synced to the merged commit and
the staged hash verified, tenants cleared under
the standing card rule and restored after, every
run wrapped in bench/failure-bundle.sh. Decision
rule, stated up front: K24 earns a default-flip
proposal only on a material kernel-line win over
K13 with speculative identity intact; otherwise
the selector stays off and K24 joins K23 as a
measured reference.

1. **Numeric gates first** (they are also the
   element-mapping proof): WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT_BRIDGE=1
   cargo test -p wgpu-compute --test k24_coopmat on
   the bridged device. All three tests must EXECUTE
   (not skip): reference and K13 and K23 parity at
   6656 x batches 64/62, the 6656 full square, the
   band refusals. Any failure here stops the
   session: the mapping claim is wrong on the real
   driver and the note gets a correction record,
   not a tuning pass.
2. **Kernel-line A/B, interleaved**: prefill_profile
   at the 1,022-token prefill shape, arms K13
   (shipped), K23 (COOPMAT=1), K24 (COOPMAT=1,
   COOPMAT_V2=1), interleaved arm order, diag timing
   on: the k24_q4k_coopmat line against
   k23_q4k_coopmat's 16,951.3 ms and k13_q4k_mmq's
   4,250.1 ms over 2,912 dispatches, plus diag-off
   walls per arm. Report GB/s per arm.
3. **Session identity + golden** with COOPMAT=1 and
   COOPMAT_V2=1: the five golden prompts, identity
   against the shipped-default control, and the
   diag manifest must carry coopmat=true and
   coopmat_v2=true with k24_q4k_coopmat stamps in
   the capture.
4. **ACO autopsy of v2's compiled form** (the pass
   v1 never got): VGPR count, spills, scratch, and
   LDS for the K24 pipeline via pipeline executable
   properties or RADV shader stats, beside K23's
   for comparison, recorded in the verdict note.

Open items this lane does not close: the staging
prefetch split (named above); any Q5_K/Q6_K coopmat
form (K24 is Q4_K only, like K23); GFX11.5/12
element mappings; wave32 through the passthrough
(would need bridge work to request a subgroup size,
a separate lane's decision).

## Supersession (2026-11-07): the decision rule was met; both defaults flipped on

The card protocol above ran in full as leg 2 of
the wave20 consolidated session
(bench/wave20-session-2026-11-07.md, staged from
main 515ce23). Every leg of it discharged:

1. **Numeric gates**: tests/k24_coopmat.rs executed
   on the card, 3 passed, 0 failed, no skips. K24
   against the host reference at relative error at
   most 1.158e-6 (batch 62; batch 64 read 7.956e-7);
   against K13 at most 2.9e-7 relative. The wave64
   accumulator element mapping this note derived
   from Mesa source is PROVEN on the target card; a
   wrong mapping would have scrambled rows and
   columns and failed by a wide margin.
2. **Kernel-line A/B, interleaved** at the
   1,022-token prefill shape, 2,912 dispatches per
   arm: the k24_q4k_coopmat line ran 1,737.2 /
   1,751.9 ms (112 GB/s) against k13_q4k_mmq's
   4,021.0 / 4,046.5 ms (48 GB/s), about 2.3x
   faster; prefill walls 4,052 / 4,085 ms against
   6,307 / 6,401 ms, about 36 percent lower. The
   K23 v1 arm reproduced its standing verdict
   (16,900 / 16,963 ms): correct, about 4x slower
   than K13, never a default.
3. **Identity + golden** with COOPMAT=1 and
   COOPMAT_V2=1 (plus BRIDGE=1): IDENTITY PASS and
   GOLDEN PASS, the spec stream byte-identical to
   the golden stream, spec accounting (rounds=38,
   proposed=37, accepted=25) identical to the
   shipped-default control; the diag manifest
   carried "coopmat":"true", "coopmat_v2":"true".
4. **Autopsy**: K24 LDS 33,792 B (exactly the five
   staging arrays), VGPR 132 (not the 256 cap: the
   register-resident fold confirmed at the binary
   level), zero spills, zero scratch.

The decision rule stated at the top of the card
protocol (material kernel-line win over K13 with
speculative identity intact) IS MET. Under David's
standing order of 2026-11-07 (anything that makes
sense engine go faster should be set to on), the
flip lane `lane/coopmat-default-flip` moved BOTH
defaults together, recorded in
bench/coopmat-default-flip-2026-11-07.md: an unset
WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT now arms the rung and an
unset WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT_V2 now selects K24
inside it; either env at `0` is a one-variable
rollback of its own part (the rung closed, or K23
serving the rung), and a malformed value fails
closed to off, logged by name. The bridge the rung
needs follows the routing default when its own
switch is unset (a present bridge value still
decides on its own). The routing order and the
fallback chain are unchanged: a K24 refusal still
falls through to K23 by name, a K23 refusal to
K13, and a device without a coopmat pipeline
serves the standard ladder exactly, with the
refusal on record. This section supersedes the
Routing section's "at shipped defaults nothing
changes" and the protocol's "the selector stays
off" branch; the rest of this note stands as the
build record.

# Defaults confirmation session (2026-11-07)

One consolidated card session on ubuntu-server against main
7940bcf70, the first tree where all three shipped defaults are
live at once: the MMV band gate open to cap 16
(WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS default 16), K21F finish-carrying
head routing behind that gate, and staged flash on
(WGPU_COMPUTE_FLASH_STAGED default on). Four legs: K21F
exposure and identity, flash default exposure, coopmat bridge
smoke, and shipped-default speculative rates.

Headline, stated plainly first: **leg 1 FAILS.** With every
env var at its shipped default, the speculative stream is NOT
token-identical to plain greedy. The divergence is
deterministic, reproduces in every default-configuration run
in this session (eight of them, both depths), and is
attributable to the K21F head route by the isolation arms
below. The configuration is faster than the baseline
session's cap-16 arms at both depths, and that speed and the
divergence are the same phenomenon, so the rate gains in
leg 4 cannot be credited until the K21F numerics are fixed
and identity passes again. Legs 2 and 3 pass on their own
criteria. The control arm (the whole MMV gate closed by
WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=1) passes identity and golden, so
a one-variable rollback exists, at the price of every MMV
route, not just the head's.

===== FILE: bench/dflash-gpu-2026-11-03.md =====
# DFlash on GPU: the draft's resident forward (2026-11-03)

Lane `lane/dflash-gpu` (on `lane/spec-gpu` tip d10987e). This note
is the design record and the server proof script for removing the
blocker `bench/spec-gpu-port-2026-11-03.md` named: the DFlash
draft had no GPU path, a draft block cost roughly 31-35 s on CPU
against GPU verify rounds in tens of milliseconds, and T-9.6's
speed bar (88.6 tok/s effective) could not pass until the draft
ran on GPU. The draft now has a resident GPU forward behind the
same Speculator seam. Nothing in this note claims a server
verdict: the local gates are green (below), and every
adapter-bound proof below still has to run on the server.

## What was built

- `crates/dflash`: one new error variant,
  `DflashError::StepFailed { step, detail }`, the draft-vocabulary
  mirror of `GlimmerError::StepFailed`, so backend refusals reach
  the speculative loop as `SpecError::DraftRefused` and never as
  raw backend errors.
- `crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/k15_dflash.rs` (K15): the two
  primitives no existing kernel provides.
  - NEOX rotate: K5's rotate is the interleaved (GPT-J) pairing;
    the draft's arch rotates half-split (NEOX,
    `torch_math::rope`). Positions come from a device array,
    because inject rows carry caller-supplied positions while
    block rows carry a contiguous span. Inverse frequencies are
    host-computed in f64, stored f32, the K5 convention.
  - Draft attention: K6 is causal, ring-addressed, and
    Glimmer-shaped. The draft's attention is (on the real file)
    non-causal, reads a sparse position-addressed committed set
    plus the block's own K/V in one visible set, and masks by
    sliding window over absolute positions. One workgroup per
    (query row, query head), the GQA group folded in, online
    softmax with f32 accumulation throughout (the CPU two-pass
    softmax's math, reassociated).
- `crates/wgpu-compute/src/dflash_session.rs`:
  `DflashRawWeights` mirrors `dflash::Weights::load` over raw
  `TensorView`s (same variant gates, same shape checks, same
  `fc`-width derivation, same error names), and `DflashSession`
  mirrors `DflashModel`'s two passes in the resident pattern:
  weights uploaded once through the resident session's own
  `upload_proj`/`upload_norm`, one command chain per pass, plans
  cached per row count, logits readback appended to the chain's
  encoder. Composition: K1/K2/K3 GEMV projections at every batch
  (no activation quantization anywhere in the draft path, so
  parity is by construction rather than by tolerance luck), K4
  norms and residual closes (per-head norms fold heads into
  rows; the optional post norms use K4's weighted-residual
  form, the CPU composition's exact math), K7 SwiGLU, K8
  embedding gather, K15 for rotate and attention.
  - Resident KV is a flat position-addressed space (slot =
    absolute position), NOT a ring: the CPU cache is a
    position-keyed map whose reads filter by mask, and the flat
    layout is that map's exact device shape. The sliding window
    stays a read-side mask, as in the CPU implementation.
    Injection lands rows with encoder copies, coalesced over
    contiguous position runs, segmented at 64 rows per segment
    inside one submission per segment.
  - Validation order and diag event names match the CPU model
    (`inject.begin`, `forward_block.end`, and friends, on the
    draft's `Diag` seam). KV capacity is session config
    (`DflashSessionConfig::kv_capacity`, default 8192 positions,
    about 320 MB at the real geometry), never a compiled
    constant; an injection reaching past it refuses by name.
- `crates/itak-spec`: `DflashSpeculator` gains a backend enum.
  All loop bookkeeping (capture staging and its refusals,
  commit consumption, proposal row slicing, the greedy/sampled
  arms) is shared code above the arm; the arm only answers
  inject, forward_block, and committed_len. The GPU arm holds a
  `DflashSession<'static>` (the runner leaks the backend, the
  discipline it already uses for the target's resident
  session). Selection is config with a default:
  `SpecConfig.draft_backend: DraftBackend` (library default
  Cpu). `spec.model()` became `spec.config()`, which both arms
  answer; `SpecSession` needed no other change.
- The runner (`spec_generate_gpu`) takes `--draft=gpu|cpu`
  (its own default is gpu; unknown values refuse by name) and
  `--kv-capacity=<positions>`. Both residents share one leaked
  backend in phase B. Draft weights load per arm inside phase
  B, so a GPU run never pays the CPU dequantization.

## Local gates (this VM, no adapter)

Executed for real here:

- `cargo test --workspace`: 447 passed, 0 failed.
- The raw-load refusal battery (missing tensor, variant gate,
  wrong shape, fc width not a multiple of the target layer
  count) executes on CPU and passes; the K15 geometry guards
  and the session's bookkeeping helpers (contiguous runs,
  reported width, config default) execute and pass; the
  itak-spec suite (37 tests, including the speculator staging
  contract and the DraftBackend default/parse test) passes
  unchanged on the shared bookkeeping.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`: clean.
  `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.

Compiled and skipped here (the workspace's standard printed
skip, "no suitable adapter (enumerated: [])"), to execute on
the server:

- `wgpu-compute/tests/dflash_session.rs`: session parity
  (fuse, inject, block logits vs the CPU model over contiguous
  and sparse commits), construction refusals, K15 rotate vs
  `torch_math::rope`.
- `wgpu-compute/tests/shader_compile.rs`: the K15 pipeline
  build test.
- `itak-spec` speculator test `gpu_arm_shares_the_speculator_bookkeeping`.

## Server proof (ubuntu-server, GPU free, merged tree)

```bash
export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH
cd <merged tree>

# 1. Fixture parity, executed for real on the XTX. The parity
#    fixture feeds the CPU model the dequantization of the very
#    bytes the session uploads, so a failure here is device
#    arithmetic, not fixture drift. Bar: per-row argmax
#    agreement and max-abs logit drift under 0.5, the resident
#    tests' cross-backend bar.
cargo test -p wgpu-compute --test dflash_session
cargo test -p wgpu-compute --test shader_compile
cargo test -p itak-spec

# 2. The spec-gpu lane's owed resident pin, still outstanding
#    from its note:

# 3. Real-file parity between the draft arms, at the loop
#    level: one plain stream, then each arm in spec mode
#    against it. Both must print IDENTITY: PASS. This is the
#    check that the GPU draft and the CPU draft drive the same
#    committed stream on the real files.
cargo build --release -p itak-spec --example spec_generate_gpu
T=/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf
D=/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/dflash-Muse-Glimmer-30B-Q4_K_M.gguf

./target/release/examples/spec_generate_gpu $T $D 64 6 "The capital of France is" spec /tmp/plain_stream.txt --draft=cpu

# 4. The T-9.6 verdict run with the GPU draft (identity first,
#    then the speed bar; exit code follows correctness only):
./target/release/examples/spec_generate_gpu $T $D 64 6 --draft=gpu
```

## Honest expectations

- The draft side stops being the wall. Per block, the GPU
  draft streams about 2.5 GB of weights (about 1.5 GB of layer
  projections, 0.12 GB of `fc`, and about 0.92 GB of the
  borrowed Q5_K head, which is the single largest stream in
  the pass); at the K1/K2/K3 rates this workspace measured
  (about 815 GB/s), that is roughly 3 ms per block, plus about
  0.2 ms per commit for injection. Against 31-35 s, the draft
  rounds become noise next to the target's verify forwards.
- Whether T-9.6 flips to a full PASS is NOT this lane's to
  promise. The remaining terms are the verify side's cost per
  round and the real acceptance rate at depth 6 (the llama.cpp
  sweep measured 0.541 on its harness; this stack's acceptance
  on the proof prompt is whatever step 4 prints). The
  arithmetic says the bar is reachable; the run decides.
- Memory: phase B now holds the target resident (about
  17 GB) plus the draft resident (about 2.5 GB of weights,
  320 MB of KV at the default capacity, small scratch) on one
  24 GB card. It fits, with a few GB of headroom; if a future
  run shares the card, `--kv-capacity` is the knob.
- First-failure triage if step 1 fails on the server: the
  rotate test isolates NEOX; the fuse comparison isolates the
  fc + norm prefix; the block comparison then implicates the
  per-layer chain or the K15 attention (the newest math). All
  three signals are separate tests for exactly this reason.

## Named gaps and deliberate differences

- Borrowed-table resolution (missing table, wrong shape)
  happens at session construction, not at first forward as on
  the CPU pass, because the session uploads the tables once.
  Same error names, same order (embedding before head).
- Only the quantized projection families (Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K)
  map onto the GEMV kernels; an F32 projection or head refuses
  at session build with `StepFailed`, the same refusal the
  resident target path gives. The real draft and target files
  are entirely in-family. The embedding gather additionally
  accepts F32/F16/BF16/Q8_0 through K8.
- The K15 attention refuses `value_length` above 1024 by name
  at prepare time (per-lane accumulator stride cap). The real
  file's value length is 128.
- RoPE angles are computed in f32 on device (host f64
  inverse frequencies, the K5 convention) where the CPU
  reference uses f64 angles. Inside the cross-backend bar at
  proof-scale positions; at very long contexts the drift
  grows, and a future precision pass would start here.
- Long generations: commits grow monotonically, so a run
  whose committed length passes the KV capacity refuses at
  that commit by name. The 64-token proof never nears the
  default 8192; production-length runs set `--kv-capacity`
  (full 131072-position residency at the real geometry costs
  about 5.2 GB, a deployment choice, not a code change).

===== FILE: bench/diag-capture-2026-11-06.md =====
# Diag capture level (2026-11-06)

Lane: `lane/diag-capture`, from main `2f8b3ae`. Status: built and
VM-verified (full wgpu-compute suite green, clippy clean). No card
runs in this lane; the card legs are checklist items at the end.

## What capture adds

`WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing` answers "how long did each dispatch
take". It cannot answer "what did the run compute": a run can be
timed perfectly and still be wrong, and two runs can only be
compared by eyeballing outputs. `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=capture` is the
third mode of the same diag system (timestamps.rs). It implies
timing everywhere: the device requests the timestamp features,
the recorder is built under the same feature gate, sessions drain
and report exactly as timing runs do, and the timing tally and
summary CSV are byte-identical. Any value other than `timing` or
`capture` still fails closed to off, and the off path is
unchanged (the existing off-path pins pass; their guards now skip
when the mode is anything but off, so they stay correct under a
capture environment too).

On top of timing, capture adds three things:

1. **A run manifest**, begun when a resident session is built,
   printed on the diag channel (`[wgpu-compute-diag] manifest:
   {...}`) and written at finish to the sidecar
   `<WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG_OUT>.manifest.json`. It states: the diag
   mode; the build version (`CARGO_PKG_VERSION`) and the git
   revision when the build exported `ITAK_GIT_HASH`
   (`"unknown"` otherwise, never guessed); the adapter name,
   backend, device type, and the driver and driver-info strings
   the adapter itself reports; every resolved `WGPU_COMPUTE_*`
   configuration value the run actually runs with (small-batch
   cap, MMV ceiling, the full MMV band table in its described
   form, chunked-GEMV cap, the K22 switch, the wide-MMQ floor:
   resolved values, not raw env text); the model file (path,
   size, content fingerprint, method) when the driver noted it
   (`ResidentSession::note_model_file`) or registered it once
   per process (`register_model_file`); and the session shape
   (kind, layers, hidden, vocab, context length, sliding window,
   key/value lengths, KV ring capacity, chunk rows cap).

2. **Data fingerprints** of what each completed forward
   computed, recorded into the session's accumulator and written
   at finish to `<WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG_OUT>.capture.csv`, one line
   per record on the diag channel as they happen
   (`[wgpu-compute-diag] capture #<seq> ...`). Kinds:
   - `forward`: a plain forward's (or capturing forward's)
     finished logits: fingerprint plus the greedy argmax token.
   - `block`: a block forward's finished logits, all rows (the
     speculative verify forward's shape); no single argmax.
   - `argmax`: a device-argmax forward's winner; the
     fingerprint covers the (id, logit) pair, the only output
     that forward reads back.
   - `round`: one speculative round: the draft's proposed ids
     (fingerprinted) plus the accepted count, recorded through
     `ResidentSession::note_spec_round` (wiring step below).
   The hash runs over the vector the forward already read back.
   Capture adds no GPU work and no readback.

3. **A mechanical diff**: `examples/diag_diff.rs` takes two
   `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG_OUT` prefixes, compares the manifests
   field by field, then the capture records position by
   position, and names the first record whose kind, value
   count, fingerprint, argmax, or accepted count differs (or
   that one run lacks). Exit 0 identical, 1 any difference, 2
   usage/IO errors. Verified end to end on fixtures: a one-nibble
   fingerprint change at seq 1 and a driver-string drift were
   each named exactly.

Capture records are session-lifetime, like the timing groups:
they are never windowed or dropped mid-run (a long run's record
list grows by one small record per forward), and the finish
writes the whole list. The accumulator API is mode-gated: every
capture entry point is a no-op (returning `None` where it
returns a record) below capture mode, so timing and off runs
pay one mode check per forward and nothing else.

## Exact formats

**Fingerprint** (`Fnv1a64` in timestamps.rs): word-wise FNV-1a
64 over the byte stream `count_u64le || payload`, where the
payload is each `f32`'s `to_bits` little-endian bytes (or each
`u32`'s little-endian bytes). The stream folds eight bytes at a
time (XOR the little-endian word into the state, multiply by
the FNV prime `0x100000001b3`, offset basis
`0xcbf29ce484222325`); a final partial word folds byte by byte.
The result depends only on the byte sequence, never on feed
chunking (pinned by a unit test). Rendered as 16 lowercase hex
digits. Golden values, computed independently of the
implementation and pinned in the test suite:

- `fingerprint_f32(&[])` = `af63bd4c8601b7df`
- `fingerprint_f32(&[1.0])` = `d9c063aea94e0421`
- `fingerprint_u32(&[201818])` = `c3bd5d17f5820309`

**Model file fingerprint**: method string
`fnv1a64w(size_u64le || whole_file_if_size<=2MiB_else_first_1MiB || last_1MiB)`,
recorded in the manifest next to the value. At most 2 MiB is
read however large the file is; a byte in the unsampled middle
of a large file cannot move the fingerprint, and a unit test
pins exactly that so the method is never mistaken for a
whole-file hash.

**Capture CSV**: header `seq,kind,values,hash,argmax,accepted`,
one row per record in run order, empty fields for data a kind
does not carry.

**Manifest JSON**: one compact document, fixed field order:
`format` (`wgpu-compute-diag-manifest`), `format_version` (1),
`diag_mode`, `build {version, git}`, `adapter {name, backend,
device_type, driver, driver_info}`, `resolved_config` (object of
name to resolved value), `model` (object `{path, size_bytes,
fingerprint, fingerprint_method}` or `null`), `session` (object
of name to value).

## Overhead (measured on this VM, release build)

The fingerprint cost was measured before and after one
optimization, and the first form was rejected on its numbers:

- Byte-wise FNV-1a (first version): 9.56 ms per forward at
  Glimmer's vocab (202,048 f32 values), 138 ms per 16-row
  block. Too slow: the block form alone would have taxed every
  speculative round.
- Word-wise (shipped): **1.60 ms** per single-row forward
  (505 MB/s of f32 data on this VM's CPU), **29.2 ms** per
  16-row block fingerprint, negligible for an argmax record
  (16 bytes hashed). The measurement test is in the suite
  and ignored by default: `cargo test --release
  -p wgpu-compute --lib capture_hash_cost_measurement
  -- --ignored --nocapture`.

Against the card's current timings (decode step about 52 ms at
19.26 tok/s), a 1.6 ms host hash per decode forward is about
3 percent, paid after the readback on the host. A speculative
round's verify block (17 rows, about 31 ms of hashing at the
VM's rate) is the heaviest leg and is material relative to a
round's GPU time; capture is a diagnostic mode, never on for
verdict runs, and the server CPU will differ from this VM's.
The end-to-end capture tax on the card (tok/s with capture on
versus timing only) is **unmeasured**; it is a checklist item
below, not a claim. The model fingerprint reads at most 2 MiB
once per noted file. The manifest is one line at session start
and two small file writes at finish.

## Integration steps left for other lanes (named, not done here)

This lane's scope was timestamps.rs, the accumulator, and the
resident session's hooks. Two wirings remain, both one-call
sized:

1. **DflashSession mirror hooks** (dflash lane): its
   accumulator already comes from `DiagAccumulator::from_env()`
   (dflash_session.rs:1006), so under `DIAG=capture` it is
   capture-mode today and its timing side already works; what
   it lacks is (a) a `begin_manifest` call in its constructor
   with its own session pairs (kind `dflash`, draft depth,
   block size, target shape), (b) one
   `acc.record_forward(KIND_BLOCK, &logits)` at the
   `forward_block` exit (dflash_session.rs:1698), and (c)
   `note_model_file` / `note_spec_round` / capture-record
   passthroughs mirroring ResidentSession's.
2. **Spec round wiring** (spec lane): call
   `ResidentSession::note_spec_round(&draft_ids, accepted)` on
   the target session once per completed round, at the point
   inside the round where the draft's proposed ids and the
   accepted count are both in hand. `RoundOutcome` carries only
   the proposed count, not the ids, so the call cannot be made
   from the outcome after the fact.

## Additions to the next card session's checklist

- Run `glimmer_generate` and one speculative phase B under
  `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=capture` with `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG_OUT` set;
  confirm each run leaves `<out>.manifest.json` and
  `<out>.capture.csv` beside the timing CSV, and the manifest
  states the real adapter driver string and the resolved band
  table of that run.
- Diff two same-build, same-config capture runs with
  `diag_diff`: expected result is zero divergence, exit 0. Any
  divergence is a real nondeterminism find, not a tool artifact.
- Diff one cross-config pair (different MMV band routing):
  expected divergence localized to verify forwards once the
  routing change first bites, with all earlier records agreeing.
- Measure the capture tax: decode tok/s and one spec phase
  under capture versus timing-only in the same session, and
  record both numbers in that session's note (this lane's VM
  numbers are host-only and do not substitute).
- Pipeline statistics queries (open evaluation from the
  2026-11-04 visibility research): from the adapter at runtime,
  state whether `wgpu::Features::PIPELINE_STATISTICS_QUERY` is
  offered on gfx1100 under RADV in the same session, and if it

- RGP trace (same open evaluation; the trace lane owns the

  was captured in the same session as the timing/capture runs,
  and if so the trace file's name beside the session's other
  artifacts, so a kernel-level question can be answered from
  the same run that produced the fingerprints.

## Completion: the two wirings above are closed (lane/diag-capture-wiring)

Both items from "Integration steps left for other lanes" are
now wired, in one code commit on top of this note's main.

**1. DflashSession mirror hooks**
(`crates/wgpu-compute/src/dflash_session.rs`):

- The constructor now builds its accumulator as a local and
  calls `begin_manifest` with `DflashSession::capture_manifest`,
  built exactly the resident way (build identity, adapter and
  driver identity, the backend's resolved configuration in
  resolved form). The session section comes from the pure
  `capture_session_pairs` helper: `kind=dflash`, `depth`,
  `block_size`, then the target shape (`hidden`, `vocab`,
  `context_length`, `target_hidden`, `conditioning_width`,
  `kv_capacity`). One naming fact the original item left
  open: a draft session has no speculative depth (that is
  `SpecConfig.depth` in itak-spec, and this session never
  sees it), so the `depth` pair states the draft model's
  layer count, `block_count`.
- The block record sits at the one real exit: both public
  forwards funnel through `run_block`, whose single `Ok`
  return now calls `capture_block(&logits)`
  (`record_forward(KIND_BLOCK, ...)`) just before it. Two
  corrections to the item's description, from the shipped
  code: the cited line (dflash_session.rs:1698) predates the
  capped-forward merge, there is no standalone
  `forward_block` exit to hook; and for
  `forward_block_capped` the fingerprint covers the
  returned prefix rows, the only data that forward reads
  back, which is the capture level's own
  no-extra-readback rule.
- Passthroughs mirroring ResidentSession's, all four:
  `note_model_file`, `note_spec_round`,
  `diag_capture_records`, `diag_manifest_json`.

**2. Spec round wiring** (`crates/itak-spec`): `SpecSession`
is generic over its target driver, so the call could not
name ResidentSession directly. `TargetDriver` gained a
record-only seam, `note_spec_round(&proposed, accepted)`,
defaulting to a no-op (the CPU driver records nothing);
`ResidentTarget` overrides it to forward to
`ResidentSession::note_spec_round`. `speculative_round`
calls it exactly once per completed round, after the
commit and the `spec.round.accept` event, at the point
where `proposal.tokens` and `accepted` are both in hand;
a round that fails anywhere above is never recorded, and
the call feeds nothing back into sampling, acceptance, or
control flow. `RoundOutcome` is unchanged.

**Test evidence** (VM, this lane): wgpu-compute 234 passed
/ 0 failed, itak-spec 49 / 0, dflash 24 / 0; clippy

===== FILE: bench/diag-drain-2026-11-05.md =====
# Diag drain fix: real runs emit the per-kernel timing report

Date: 2026-11-05. Branch: `lane/diag-drain` (from main
`3b2afbcc3d59d9e583acc1fe78e1067f371c328a`). Crate:
`wgpu-compute`.

## The defect

The per-kernel GPU timestamp instrumentation (David's order,
2026-11-04: debugging all the way through everything) could
only produce output inside one test. `DiagRecorder::drain` —
the only call that resolves the timestamp query window and
emits records — had exactly one caller in the tree: the smoke
collector in `crates/wgpu-compute/tests/resident_session.rs`.
That test was also the only reader of `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG_OUT`.

Proof, from the cleared-card baseline lane on the server
(2026-11-05): two full generation runs of 28,480 dispatches
each, with `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing` and
`WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG_OUT` set, emitted **zero**
`[wgpu-compute-diag]` records and no file. The wave-7
acceptance had proven the machinery only where the collector
drains it; no session, example, or engine path ever drained.

## The fix

The sessions own the drain now.

- **`DiagAccumulator`** (new, `crates/wgpu-compute/src/timestamps.rs`):
  the session-side running summary. It drains the recorder,
  folds the resolved records into per-kernel aggregates (the
  same sums `summarize()` computes, kept incrementally, so
  memory is one row per kernel however long the run), and at
  finish prints the one-line tally through the diag channel
  and writes the summary table to the `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG_OUT`
  file when one was named at construction. Its rendered table
  is byte-identical to `render_summary` over the raw record
  set; a unit test pins that equivalence across multiple
  folds. Diagnostics never fail the run they observe: a failed
  drain or write is counted and reported on the channel, and
  generation proceeds.
- **`ResidentSession`**: carries an accumulator exactly when
  its backend's context carries a recorder. `forward_chunk`
  calls `drain_diag()` after the chunk's submission has been
  submitted and read back, so every chunk of every public
  forward (`forward`, `forward_argmax`, `forward_capturing`,
  `forward_block_capturing`) is drained by the same single
  call site. `finish_diag_report()` (one last drain, then the
  tally and file) is public for deterministic callers and is
  also called from `Drop`, so every timing run leaves its
  report behind. Accessors `diag_dispatch_count()`,
  `diag_kernel_names()`, and `diag_summary_csv()` expose the
  folded state mid-run.
- **`DflashSession`**: the same treatment, for the spec
  loop's draft side — drain after every submitted chunk of
  `inject` and `fuse`, after `forward_block`, same accessors,
  same finish-at-drop. The two sessions share one recorder
  per backend, so each one's drains also flush the other's
  pending stamps; the records' kernel names keep the families
  distinguishable in one report.

## Why this cadence cannot lose stamps on long runs

The recorder's window holds 2048 dispatches
(`MAX_DISPATCHES`); overflow is the only stamp-loss path.
One chunk is one submission whose dispatch count does not
grow with its row count (every dispatch spans all rows): the
full model's chunk measured 445 dispatches (28,480 over 64
chunks in the baseline run), the fixture's 69–93. Draining
after every chunk therefore keeps pending stamps at one
chunk's worth — under a quarter of the window — for runs of
any length. A single chunk larger than the whole window
would still drop, counted by the recorder and surfaced in
the finish tally; no current plan shape comes close.

Two recorder-design facts the fix relies on, verified in
`timestamps.rs`:

- Overflow never corrupts: when the window fills, `begin`
  returns `None` and that dispatch runs unstamped, counted in
  `dropped`. Stamps already in the window stay valid because
  `drain` converts ticks by each pending stamp's stored slot,
  not by order.
- `dropped` is cumulative for the recorder's lifetime and is
  never reset by a drain. Per-session finish lines therefore
  report the per-backend total; on a shared backend (target +
  draft sessions) both report the same counter.

One boundary kept deliberately: the `Compute` trait path
(one-shot forwards through `GlimmerModel` on the GPU backend)
still does not drain. Its runs are test-driven, one forward
per process in practice, and a caller there can drain through
the context's recorder directly. The resident sessions are
the production generation paths, and they are covered.

## The off path

Unchanged, by construction. With `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG` unset
or not `timing`, `GpuContext` creates no recorder, so the
sessions create no accumulator, `drain_diag()` is one
`None` branch after each chunk, no query resources exist, no
drain cost is paid, and the encode path is byte-identical.
The existing pins stay green (`off_mode_context_carries_no_recorder`),
and a new session-level test
(`resident_session_diag_off_by_default`) asserts no report,
no records, and a no-op finish through the session API.

## Tests

- `timestamps.rs` unit tests (adapter-free, run everywhere):
  `accumulator_folds_and_renders_like_the_collector` (fold
  math + byte-identical render across folds) and
  `accumulator_writes_its_report_once` (file lands once, an
  empty run writes nothing, the finish is idempotent — the
  drain-trigger's sink logic, pinned without a device).
- `resident_session_diag_drains_itself` (new, executing):
  timing mode + adapter; a plain session's records are
  already folded when a forward returns — no collector, no
  manual drain, no finish call. This is the exact shape of
  run that emitted zero records before the fix.
- `resident_session_diag_smoke_report` (the collector,
  re-pointed): same env gates and assertions, now read from
  the session's own report, including the file the session
  wrote at finish.
- `resident_session_diag_off_by_default` (new): the off
  path through the session API.

Gate results (this VM, final tree): `cargo test -p
wgpu-compute` all suites green, 0 failed — lib 90 passed
(including the 2 new accumulator unit tests),
`resident_session` 6 passed (the 3 diag tests skip cleanly
here: this VM has no GPU adapter and the timing tests also
require the timing env, the crate's standing skip design),
`diag_timestamps` 1 passed (the off-path pin). `cargo test
-p itak-spec`: 47 passed. `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
`cargo clippy -p wgpu-compute --all-targets -- -D warnings`:
clean. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`: clean. The
executing legs of the new tests first run on the server, per
the confirmation protocol below.

## Server confirmation protocol

On the cleared card (or any card window), from the staged
tree:

1. One plain generation run with timing on:
   `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG_OUT=/tmp/diag-plain.csv`
   on the loader's `glimmer_generate` example (it drives a
   `ResidentSession`). Expect: `[wgpu-compute-diag]` dispatch
   lines on stderr during the run, a
   `[wgpu-compute-diag] session report:` tally at exit, and a
   populated `/tmp/diag-plain.csv` whose `TOTAL` row counts
   the run's dispatches.
2. One spec phase A leg with timing on (the spec example's
   plain/target leg): same expectations; the CSV's kernel
   rows are the per-kernel table for that leg.

Note: spec phase B (draft + verify sessions together) still
needs a host-RAM window on ubuntu-server — the phase B
harness peak is ~35 GB and the box offered ~33 GB on
2026-11-05 — which is unrelated to this fix. When it runs,
both sessions drain into the shared recorder and each
finishes its own report; expect two tally lines (draft and
target) and the later finisher's file content at the shared
`WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG_OUT` path.

Protocol above, run from main
`c439e3af45e30275601129568e3e9cb3a89590cb`, staged at

1. Plain generation, `glimmer_generate` with

   `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG_OUT` set: 28,480 per-dispatch
   `[wgpu-compute-diag]` lines on stderr during the

   `[wgpu-compute-diag] session report: 28480

The defect this fix closed — two full 28,480-dispatch
real runs with timing on emitting zero records and no
