===== FILE: bench/diag-env-wiring-2026-11-07.md =====
# Diag env wiring: the Category H HIGH (2026-11-07)

Lane `lane/diag-env-wiring`, from main
012396ad8ce7bf4273f58b4c1183617dbb984ba3. Code and tests in the
first commit on this lane; this note and the RUNBOOK table are
the second commit. All runs executed on this VM against this
lane's tree; no server jobs.

Source of the work: the cold critic panel of 2026-11-07
(`CRITIC-ENGINE-MERGE.md`, Category H; evidence executed by the
operability seat). The build law says every module ships
debugging from birth: a structured diagnostic channel, a way to
turn it on, and a test proving it fires. Linting was clean
everywhere; the debugging half was decoration for six crates:

- attention, cpu-compute, wgpu-compute, torch-math and itak-kv
  exposed only a programmatic `set_debug` / `set_debug_enabled`
  with no env var and no caller anywhere in the workspace, so in
  the shipped engine binary those channels were permanently off.
- tokenizer's seam was the `debug-log` cargo feature; no
  dependent enabled it, so the shipped tokenizer compiled its
  diag macro to nothing.
- Debug self-tests existed only in gguf, itak-loader and
  itak-engine: 10 of 13 seams had none.

## The fix, per crate

Env twins in the gguf shape. gguf's `debug_enabled()` checks the
explicit flag first, then the env var on every call (present with
any value other than `0` or empty enables). Each flag-based crate
now does exactly that, so any binary linking the crate (the
engine included) can enable its seam with no code change and no
rebuild. No engine startup wiring was needed: per-call
consultation is the mechanism, the same one gguf and itak-loader
already ship.

| Crate | Env var | Setter (unchanged) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| attention | `ATTENTION_DEBUG` | `set_debug_enabled` |
| cpu-compute | `CPU_COMPUTE_DEBUG` | `set_debug` |
| wgpu-compute | `WGPU_COMPUTE_DEBUG` | `set_debug` |
| torch-math | `TORCH_MATH_DEBUG` | `set_debug` |
| itak-kv | `ITAK_KV_DEBUG` | `set_debug_enabled` |
| tokenizer | `TOKENIZER_DEBUG` | `set_debug` (new) |

Names are the crate name uppercased plus `_DEBUG`, which is
exactly the convention the two already-wired crates follow
(`GGUF_DEBUG`, `ITAK_LOADER_DEBUG`). wgpu-compute's var is
deliberately distinct from `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG`, the per-dispatch
timestamp system in `timestamps.rs`; the diag.rs header says so,
and that system is untouched.

Emission shape: each macro crate's lines now flow through one
`emit_debug` path (the macro still checks `debug_enabled()` first
and evaluates no format arguments while off). In test builds
`emit_debug` also captures the exact formatted line into a
test-only buffer, the gguf channel's pattern, which is what makes
the capture tests below possible. No call site changed in any
crate.

tokenizer: converted to the runtime flag. The `debug-log`
feature is removed from its manifest (nothing enabled it; the
workspace builds clean without it), `dbglog!` now checks
`diag::debug_enabled()` at runtime, and its `diag` module became
`pub` like every sibling crate's (it was the only private one,
which is part of why the seam was unreachable). One test drives a
real production refusal (an unsupported tokenizer family) and
asserts the refusal line lands on the channel.

Trait seams (arch-llama, dflash, itak-spec, muse-glimmer) needed
no wiring change: a caller passes the sink, and the engine
already wires muse-glimmer's. What they lacked was the self-test;
each gains a capturing-sink test in the itak-engine shape.

## Before / after evidence

Failing before, executed: before the fix, each flag crate's new
`env_twin_enables_debug` test was added alone and run against the
unmodified seam. All five FAILED at the "must enable" assertion
(attention diag.rs:52, cpu-compute diag.rs:49, wgpu-compute
diag.rs:49, itak-kv diag.rs:52, torch-math lib.rs:210): the env
var was simply never read. The seat's grep evidence stands as the
before-proof for tokenizer (feature off in every dependent) and
for the missing self-tests.

Passing after, 17 new tests, all green:

- `env_twin_enables_debug` (attention, cpu-compute, wgpu-compute,
  itak-kv, torch-math `diag_tests`, tokenizer): var `1` enables,
  `0` and empty do not, removal restores off.
- `seam_fires_when_on_and_is_silent_when_off` (same six crates):
  a probe line through the crate's own macro is captured with its
  prefix while on, and produces nothing while off.
- `a_real_refusal_emits_through_the_seam` (tokenizer): the
  unsupported-family refusal path emits `refusing unsupported
  tokenizer model` while debug is on.
- `seam_delivers_events_to_a_sink` (arch-llama, dflash,
  itak-spec, muse-glimmer): a capturing sink receives the event
  verbatim; NullDiag drops silently; StderrDiag writes without
  panicking.

Diag tests within a crate hold a per-crate lock: the flag and the
env var are process-global, so parallel flips could otherwise
satisfy each other's assertions. Capture assertions search for
per-test unique probe strings, per the gguf buffer discipline.

## Gates, as observed on the lane tree

- `cargo test --workspace`: 781 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored
  (68 suites). The 17 tests above are this lane's addition.
  Lib suites for the touched crates: arch-llama 7, attention 30,
  cpu-compute 11, dflash 25, itak-kv 23, itak-spec 70,
  muse-glimmer 16, tokenizer 21, torch-math 46, wgpu-compute 199.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean (the fmt pass over the new
  test code is folded into the code commit).
- `cargo check --workspace`: clean.
- Platform (shared tree stayed whole): `go build ./...`,
  `go vet ./...` clean; `go test ./...` 115 tests, all packages ok.

Every default is still OFF and the off path is unchanged: with no
env set, `debug_enabled()` returns the flag exactly as before and
the macros evaluate nothing. Existing tests passed unmodified;
the only test changes are the additions above.

## RUNBOOK outcome

Included in this commit: a Diagnostics switches table at the end
of RUNBOOK's "Run locally" section (kept inside the file's
declared structure rather than as a new section) listing each
switch, its owner module, its default, and its effect, including
the pre-existing `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG`, `ITAK_KV_PREFIX_*`, and
`TORCH_LOG_LEVEL` switches the operability seat found
undocumented. That closes the Category H RUNBOOK MEDIUM.

## Deliberately left

- The Category H platform MEDIUM (slog coverage in the Go
  platform's auth, cache, chattemplate, engine and scheduler
  modules, and the platform README sentence) is out of this
  lane's scope and remains open.
- Supervised reach: a torchd-supervised engine child receives an
  allowlisted environment (PATH plus `ITAK_ENGINE_*` only,
  `platform/internal/supervisor/supervisor.go` `childEnv`), so
  the `*_DEBUG` switches reach a hand-run engine today but are
  filtered out before a supervised child. The RUNBOOK table
  states this plainly. Extending the allowlist (or adding an
  `ITAK_ENGINE_*` startup resolution in the engine) is follow-up
  work in the platform, not silently folded into this lane.
- The `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG` timestamps system and the examples'
  programmatic `set_debug` calls are unchanged; the env twin
  makes the second unnecessary for shipped binaries, which was
  the panel's point.

===== FILE: bench/draft-mmv-routing-2026-11-06.md =====
# Draft MMV routing: the DFlash session walks the band ladder, 2026-11-06

Lane `lane/draft-mmv-routing`, based on main `d3adec4`.
Question (from bench/spec-round-economics-2026-11-06.md,
F1/F2/F4): the speculative round's draft block forward
costs ~40.6 ms of GPU per round at 54-66 GB/s because
the draft session's projections never routed through
the MMV band policy; the single fattest dispatch is the
draft's Q5_K head, 17.21 ms streaming 924.6 MB at
53.7 GB/s. This lane routes the draft's projections
through the resident ladder. Nothing here changes a
shipped default.

## What was built

`crates/wgpu-compute/src/dflash_session.rs`:

- `prepare_proj` now walks the same ladder the
  resident session walks below its matrix threshold:
  the register-streaming MMV products first (K19 for
  Q4_K, K20 for Q6_K, K21 for Q5_K), the K18
  small-batch products behind them, the chunked GEMV
  form behind those, and the plain K1/K2/K3 GEMV last.
  A rung whose prepare refuses falls through to the
  next rung with the refusal logged by name, the
  resident ladder's own discipline. The matrix forms
  are the one resident rung the draft does not take:
  its row counts are block and segment counts, and
  the MMQ forms' activation quantization is a prefill
  tool (the dflash module docs carry the updated
  composition paragraph).
- The resolution is one pure function,
  `proj_candidates`, over the resolved policy values
  (the backend's `MmvBands` table, the
  `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS` ceiling, the small-batch
  ceiling, the chunked ceiling). Its expressions are
  the resident predicates' own (`MmvBands::routes`
  with `mmv_shape_of` classification, the batch bounds
  of `session::small_batch_applies` /
  `session::chunked_gemv_applies`, and
  `session::GEMM_MIN_ROWS` itself, now crate-visible)
  and `prepare_proj` walks exactly the list it
  returns. The ceiling-admits-but-cell-excludes case
  logs the same fall-through line the resident ladder
  logs, so an A/B sees the exclusions it is made of.
- The draft head is a plain Q5_K projection with no
  fused finish, so it routes through the Q5_K band
  cell to the existing K21 kernel directly; the
  finish variant the target's head needs is a
  separate lane's work and is not touched here.
- The K18 rung needs the K12 quantize staging: the
  draft `Scratch` gains a `q8_qs`/`q8_ds` pair sized
  at the largest plan rows and the widest projection
  input, the resident scratch's own sizing rule. The
  pair is allocated unconditionally (about 3 MB at
  the Glimmer draft's geometry) and read only when
  the small-batch ceiling opens the rung.
- Gating: the global gate is the same
  `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS`; the per-cell env
  overrides (`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_*_ROWS`) apply to the
  draft unchanged, because the draft resolves through
  the backend's one table. No new env flags.
- The capped readback (`forward_block_capped`,
  6d260e2) is untouched: routing changes plan
  construction only; the same plan encode and
  readback code serve capped and uncapped forwards.

Supporting, behavior-neutral changes:
`compute.rs` gains a `mmv_bands()` accessor (and the
test-only `default_mmv_bands` is crate-visible so the
draft tests pin against the shipped table itself);
`session.rs` makes `GEMM_MIN_ROWS` and `pow2_chunks`
crate-visible. The resident path's code is otherwise
byte-identical.

Disclosure: the draft module docs used to claim
cross-backend parity "by construction" from staying
on the GEMV family. That claim is retired in the
module docs: routed draft projections now carry the
same tolerance-class guarantee the resident routing
carries, and the card's identity/golden gates are
the arbiter, same as for the resident session.

## Which dispatches change route

At shipped defaults, none: every ceiling is 1, the
candidate list is empty at every batch, and the GEMV
form serves exactly as before (pinned by
`draft_ladder_ships_closed_at_default_ceilings`).

With `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=16` (the setting the
consolidated session already runs), at the block's
constant 16 rows:

| dispatch | per round | before | after | why |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| Q5_K head | 1 | k3 GEMV, 17.21 ms | **k21 MMV** | Q5_K cells admit 16 in every shape class; the head is FFN class (6656 in, 202048 out) and its cell is 3-16 |
| Q4_K layer projections | 25 | k1 GEMV, 14.00 ms | k1 GEMV (unchanged) | shipped Q4_K cells end at 12; the sweep never measured MMV at 16 (MMQ served both arms) |
| Q6_K layer projections | 10 | k2 GEMV, 8.77 ms | k2 GEMV (unchanged) | shipped Q6_K cells end at 12, same reason |
| inject fc + K/V | per segment | GEMV | GEMV at the usual 64-row segments; MMV/K18/chunked resolve per policy at tail segments of 2..15 rows | segment counts are the batch; 64 is outside every rung |

The Q4_K/Q6_K stay is policy, not a kernel limit:
K19/K20 accept batch 16, and an operator can widen
the cells by env (`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_Q4K_ATTN_ROWS`
and friends) if a future sweep measures those cells.
This lane does not widen them on inference.

## Expected recovery, stated honestly

The head is the only block dispatch whose route
changes, so the recovery is the head's alone.

- The sweep's Q5_K FFN ratio at 16 rows is 0.494
  (bench/mmv-band-routing-2026-11-06.md), which puts
  the head at ~8.5 ms, saving ~8.7 ms.
- K21's absolute streaming on the sweep's shapes is
  64-112 GB/s, not the 648-869 GB/s single-row GEMV
  streams at. The head's output is 10x wider than the
  sweep's FFN shape, which amortizes fixed costs
  better; on rate grounds the head lands at ~5-9 ms,
  saving ~8-12 ms of the 17.21.
- The often-quoted bound (the head at plain decode's
  868.6 GB/s = 1.06 ms, saving ~16 ms) is a ceiling
  K21 has never measured at on any shape. Do not
  plan on it.

At the saving's range: draft GPU 40.6 ms falls to
~29-33 ms; the depth-1 round (86.1 ms wall, verify
unchanged) falls to ~74-78 ms, worth roughly
21-22 tok/s against the current 19.26 best arm. The
depth-6 draft wall falls by the same absolute amount
(the draft is depth-independent, F3).

===== FILE: bench/f16-kv-2026-11-07.md =====
# f16 KV cache for the resident session (2026-11-07)

Status: BUILT on lane/f16-kv, default OFF. The card gate below is
owed; the default does not move until it passes.

## Why

The resident session stored its per-layer K and V buffers as f32.
At full Glimmer context that is the single largest resident
allocation after the weights, and every decode step re-reads the
whole stored KV through the attention kernels. Storing K and V
as f16 halves the bytes and halves the KV read traffic in the
flash kernels, and it matches llama.cpp's default KV type
(`-ctk f16 -ctv f16` is its out-of-box cache type). The
llama-parity specs (bench/llama-parity-specs-2026-11-06.md)
sequenced this as its own gated step; this note is that step's
build record.

## Memory math (computed from the config, pinned in tests)

Rows at full context = 13 global layers x 131,072 + 39 sliding
layers x 2,048 = 1,703,936 + 79,872 = 1,783,808 rows. One row
holds K (2 KV heads x 128) + V (2 x 128) = 512 elements.

- f32: 1,783,808 x 512 x 4 B = **3,653,238,784 bytes** (~3.40 GiB)
- f16: 1,783,808 x 512 x 2 B = **1,826,619,392 bytes** (~1.70 GiB)

`full_context_kv_bytes` (k6_attention.rs) computes both from a
`GlimmerConfig`; `tests/kv_f16.rs` pins the two figures against
the real Glimmer shape. Discrepancy against the lane tasking,
stated plainly: the tasking quoted 1,826,619,392 as the f32
total. That figure is one side (K or V) in f32, equivalently
K+V in f16. The K+V f32 total is twice it. The halving claim is
exact under either reading, and the engine's number is the
config-derived one above.

## Design

Storage format: packed f16. Two values share one u32 word in
`array<u32>` storage buffers; the even element sits in the low
half, the odd element in the high half (WGSL
`pack2x16float`/`unpack2x16float` component order). No shader
extension and no `f16` WGSL type is needed: conversion goes
through the core pack/unpack builtins, so the shaders validate
under stock Naga and run anywhere the f32 forms run.

Format plumbing:

- `KvStorage { F32, F16 }` (k6_attention.rs) rides on
  `DeviceKv` (fixed at construction) and on every `LayerKv` it
  allocates. `DeviceKv::new` keeps its signature and means F32,
  so the trait path's `GpuKvState` is f32 by construction and
  untouched. `DeviceKv::new_with_storage` is the explicit form
  the resident session uses.
- `ensure_layer` allocates `capacity x kv_width x elem_bytes`;
  the geometric-growth copy is a raw byte copy and is
  layout-preserving under either format, so growth needed no
  format-specific code. Packed storage requires an even KV row
  width (two elements per word); an odd width under F16 is
  refused by name at allocation. Every served shape is even
  (head dim is even by the K9 bound; KV width multiplies it).
- Selection: `WGPU_COMPUTE_KV_F16` resolved once at backend
  construction with the codebase's fail-closed pattern: only
  the exact value `1` (trimmed) enables; unset, `0`, and
  anything else are off, and an unrecognized value is logged by
  name at construction. The resolution logs at construction
  (`kv storage config: ...`), the session logs its resolved
  format at construction, and the resident capture manifest
  records `kv_f16` beside `k21f_head`. Default OFF in this
  lane: unlike the flash and K21F flips, unset does not enable;
  the flip is a later decision gated on the card evidence
  below.

Conversion points (exactly the two the data flow has):

- **Write, once per token, in K9.** `PREP_F16_SHADER` is the
  fused preparation with the KV bindings packed. Norms,
  rotation, slot law, params, grid, and the Q output are the
  f32 form's, operation for operation. Of the three KV write
  sites, the rotation path already computes each adjacent pair
  in one lane, so that lane packs its pair directly. The
  non-rotated K path and the V path produce one element per
  lane, so the head row is staged through the workgroup `vals`
  array (the same array the rotation path uses) and the even
  lanes pack the pairs; head dim is even and at most 128, so a
  pair never straddles a head row. `PrepArgs::kv_f16` carries
  the layer's own storage flag into prepare, which selects the
  pipeline (and the diag stamp `k9_attn_prep_f16`) and takes
  the bind group layout from that pipeline, so a packed buffer
  can only bind to the packed shader.
- **Read, every step, in the flash kernels.** `FLASH_F16_SHADER`
  and `FLASH_STAGED_F16_SHADER` bind K/V as `array<u32>` and
  convert on read through shared load helpers (`kv_load_keys`
  / `kv_load_values`, spliced into both shaders from a single
  text constant so the copies cannot drift; two functions
  reading the globals directly, because Naga's validator
  rejects a pointer-to-storage function parameter's access
  mode, a defect the lane's Naga gate caught before any
  driver saw the shader). The staged twin
  unpacks each element exactly once, at the staging loads,
  into the same f32 workgroup tile the f32 form stages into:
  its workgroup-memory set is byte-identical
  (`FLASH_STAGED_LDS_BYTES` unchanged) and everything after
  staging is the f32 operation sequence. The shipped twin
  unpacks per load in its dot and reduce loops (one unpack per
  element per use, the price of not staging). `prepare_flash`
  and `prepare_flash_staged` select the twin from the layer's
  own `storage`, with distinct diag stamps
  (`k6_attn_flash_f16`, `k6_attn_flash_staged_f16`), so card
  evidence shows the f16 forms firing by name.
- **The two-pass form refuses f16 by name.** Scores/reduce
  have no f16 twin, by design: they serve the trait path,
  whose state is f32 by construction, so an f16 layer there
  can only be a wiring mistake. `prepare_scores` and
  `prepare_reduce` return a named refusal instead of binding
  a packed buffer to an f32 shader and reading garbage.

Flag off means the pre-lane engine, exactly: `DeviceKv` format
F32, the original pipelines at every prepare, byte-identical
buffers and dispatch shapes. The new pipelines are built at
construction (so a shader defect fails there, not on first
use) and never prepared against.

Scope: the resident session only. The DFlash session does NOT
share these structures: it owns per-layer `kv_k`/`kv_v` f32
buffers sized by its own `kv_capacity` config
(dflash_session.rs), read by the K17 draft kernels. Converting
it is separate work (its own write/read sites in K17), and it
is out of this lane. K5's append likewise has no f16 form: it
writes the trait path's KV, f32 by construction.

## Precision analysis (from the math)

f16 (IEEE half) carries an 11-bit significand (10 stored bits
plus the implicit leading 1): about 3.3 decimal digits.
Round-to-nearest-even conversion of a normal value errs by at
most half an ulp, a relative error of at most 2^-11 =
4.88e-4. Subnormal results (magnitudes under 2^-14) sit on a
fixed 2^-24 grid, absolute error at most 2^-25 = 3.0e-8.
Overflow needs |x| >= 65,504; post-norm K/V rows in this
engine sit near unit scale (RMSNorm output times a learned
weight), so overflow is not a live case, and values that small
that they go subnormal contribute negligibly to a dot product
either way. The host fixture measures the realized error over
a sweep, on the build VM, through the crate's own conversion
pair (`f32_to_f16_bits` / gguf's `f16_to_f32`, the host mirror
of the shaders' pack/unpack): all 63,488 representable finite
f16 values round-trip exactly, and over 200,423 arbitrary
inputs the max relative error measured 4.8804295e-4, just
under the 2^-11 bound (4.8828125e-4), with the max subnormal
absolute error at exactly 2^-25. One conversion caveat,
stated for the card run: the mirror assumes the driver's
`pack2x16float` rounds to nearest even, as WGSL specifies and
RADV implements; a driver that truncated instead would show
up in the fixture's session delta and in the identity gate,
which is part of why the gate is empirical.

How that noise reaches the logits:

1. **Scores.** A K element error of relative size up to
   4.88e-4 perturbs each attention score by at most
   sum over the head dim of |q_d| x |delta_k_d|. For
   unit-scale q and k at head dim 128 that bound is loose
   (errors are independent roundings, not aligned): the
   random-walk size is about 4.88e-4 x sqrt(128) x typical
   |q||k| product, order 1e-3 to 1e-2 on the unscaled dot,
   and the 1/sqrt(128) score scale shrinks it further.
   Softmax weights move by roughly the score perturbation
   itself (relative), so per-key weights shift by well under
   a percent in the typical case.
2. **Values.** V errors enter the attention output linearly
   through the softmax-weighted sum: relative size again
   bounded by 4.88e-4 per element, damped by the weighted
   average (no single key's error dominates unless its weight
   is near 1, in which case the output error is that value's
   own rounding, still 4.88e-4 relative).
3. **Compounding.** The perturbed attention output feeds the
   rest of the layer stack, 52 layers deep on the real model,
   each adding its own fresh KV rounding. Nothing amplifies
   systematically (norms re-normalize each block), but errors
   accumulate like a random walk rather than canceling on
   schedule; the honest expectation for finished-logit deltas
   on the real model is the 1e-2 scale, occasionally larger at
   long context where more keys vote.

Why greedy identity MIGHT hold, and why it might not: greedy
decoding only cares about the top-1 margin. The one margin
this project has measured at a failure point is instructive:
in the K21F episode the position-23 top-2 margin in finished
logits was +0.38, and a one-sided dequant corruption with a
max vocab delta of 2.04 flipped it. f16 KV noise is two-sided,
unbiased rounding with an expected finished-logit effect
around 1e-2, roughly forty times under that margin, so
identity holding on the golden prompt is the expectation, not
a hope. But margins are a distribution, not a constant: some
position in a long generation will eventually present a
near-tie (margin under the noise), and there the f16 stream
can pick the other token and diverge for good. That is the
same standing risk llama.cpp accepts with its default f16 KV,
and it is why the gate is identity+golden on the real file
rather than an argument: the question is empirical, and a
fixture cannot answer it for the real model.

The fixture in this lane (tests/kv_f16.rs, device leg) runs
the cross-fixture model in both storage modes under a shared
greedy script: top-1 agreement at every step is asserted, the
measured max logit delta is printed (on the build VM the leg
skips, no adapter enumerated, so no delta exists yet; gate
item 4 below is where the number comes from), and the
assertion ceiling is the crate's cross-backend bar of 0.5,
disclosed here as a breakage tripwire rather than a measured
bar: the card session replaces it with the measured value.
The round-trip leg's bound, by contrast, is a theorem (half
an ulp), and it is asserted tightly.

## The card gate (owed, later session)

Run on the 7900 XTX against the real Glimmer file, flag on,
with the failure-bundle wrapper:

1. **Identity + golden**, flag on: speculative identity and
   the golden 8 tokens, depths 1 and 6, at literally
   `WGPU_COMPUTE_KV_F16=1`, with the diag stamps checked for
   `k9_attn_prep_f16`, `k6_attn_flash_f16`, and
   `k6_attn_flash_staged_f16` firing (and the manifest
   carrying `kv_f16=true`). Pass = identity and golden hold;
   a divergence is reported with its stream index and the
   top-2 margin at the split, wave17-style.
2. **Long-context prefill A/B, interleaved**: the 8,202-token

   phantom-cost lesson: no wall claim from

   modest win at long context (attention reads halve) inside

3. **Decode rate A/B, interleaved**: plain decode tok/s both

4. **Fixture delta on card**: run `cargo test -p wgpu-compute
   --test kv_f16` on the server and record the printed
   f16-vs-f32 fixture delta and round-trip maxima in the flip
   note that follows this gate.

Only after 1 passes does the default-flip question open, and

===== FILE: bench/failure-bundle.sh =====
#!/bin/bash
# Failure bundle wrapper: run a bench or harness command
# and, if it fails, preserve EVERYTHING about the run in a
# bundle under bench/failures/ so the wrong data survives
# to build fixes on. Passing runs leave one line in
# bench/failures/INDEX.md and their bulky logs are deleted.
#
# Why this exists: David's standing want is every form of
# debugging data we can squeeze out, and the WRONG data kept
# in full. Until now wrong outputs were preserved only by
# hand (one example: the degenerate top-5 output a lane
# refused to commit and kept on the server as
# ~/overnight-golden/out/glimmer.top5.degenerate.jsonl).
# This wrapper makes the preservation automatic and
# uniform. The convention, the bundle format, and the list
# of historical wrong-data artifacts live in
# bench/failure-bundles-2026-11-06.md.
#
# A run FAILS when the command exits nonzero OR when its
# combined stdout+stderr matches any FAILURE_MARKERS entry
# (a clean exit with wrong data is still wrong data; the
# degenerate top-5 run exited 0). Either way a full bundle
# is assembled. The wrapper exits with the wrapped
# command's exit code in all cases, so a marker-only
# failure still exits 0: callers detect it through the
# bundle and the INDEX, not the exit code.
#
# Usage:
#   bench/failure-bundle.sh <slug> [outdir] -- <command...>
#
#   slug     short name for the run; sanitized to
#            [A-Za-z0-9._-] and used in the bundle
#            directory name.
#   outdir   optional directory the command writes its
#            output files into; on failure its contents
#            are copied into the bundle under outputs/.
#   command  the bench/harness command. It runs from the
#            repo root (this script cd's there, like the
#            other bench scripts) and must be a foreground
#            run; its stdout and stderr are tee'd to the
#            caller's terminal and to the bundle logs.
#
# Environment knobs:
#   FB_MODEL  model file path for the manifest's
#             path/size/sha256 block. Default: the first
#             command argument that is an existing *.gguf
#             file. Hashing is streamed (sha256sum) and
#             cached by path+size+mtime in the vault's
#             model-hash-index.tsv, so a 16 GB model is
#             hashed once, not once per run.
#   FB_VAULT  vault directory. Default: bench/failures
#             under the repo root.
#
# shellcheck: NOT RUN. shellcheck is not installed on the
# build VM (checked 2026-11-06: `command -v shellcheck`
# is empty), so this script carries the repo bench style
# (set -u, everything quoted) without a shellcheck pass.
# Run `shellcheck bench/failure-bundle.sh` on any host
# that has it before relying on a clean bill.

set -u

# Failure markers: fixed strings, case-sensitive, matched
# as substrings against the combined stdout+stderr of the
# wrapped command. This list decides what counts as wrong
# data; extend it in review, never silently.
FAILURE_MARKERS=("FAIL" "FAILED" "mismatch" "DIVERGES" "REFUSED" "degenerate")

usage() {
    echo "usage: bench/failure-bundle.sh <slug> [outdir] -- <command...>" >&2
    exit 64
}

[ $# -ge 1 ] || usage
slug_raw=$1
shift
slug=$(printf '%s' "$slug_raw" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '-')

outdir=""
if [ $# -ge 1 ] && [ "$1" != "--" ]; then
    outdir=$1
    shift
fi
[ $# -ge 1 ] && [ "$1" = "--" ] || usage
shift
[ $# -ge 1 ] || usage

caller_pwd=$PWD
# Resolve caller-relative paths before the cd to repo root.
if [ -n "$outdir" ]; then
    case "$outdir" in
        /*) ;;
        *) outdir="$caller_pwd/$outdir" ;;
    esac
fi
fb_model=${FB_MODEL:-}
if [ -n "$fb_model" ]; then
    case "$fb_model" in
        /*) ;;
        *) fb_model="$caller_pwd/$fb_model" ;;
    esac
fi

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 64
repo_root=$PWD
vault=${FB_VAULT:-"$repo_root/bench/failures"}
case "$vault" in
    /*) ;;
    *) vault="$caller_pwd/$vault" ;;
esac
mkdir -p "$vault"

# --- start-of-run state ---------------------------------------------
utc_start=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
local_start=$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z)
epoch_start=$(date +%s)
host_name=$(hostname)
uname_line=$(uname -a)
git_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
git_branch=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
git_status=$(git status --porcelain=v1 2>/dev/null || echo "unavailable")
if [ -z "$git_status" ]; then
    git_dirty="clean"
else
    git_dirty="dirty"
fi

ram_bytes() {
    # MemAvailable from /proc/meminfo, in bytes; empty if unreadable.
    awk '/^MemAvailable:/ {print $2 * 1024}' /proc/meminfo 2>/dev/null
}
vram_used_bytes() {
    # First amdgpu-style sysfs counter that exists; empty otherwise
    # (this VM has no GPU at all, and that is recorded, not hidden).
    local f
    for f in /sys/class/drm/card*/device/mem_info_vram_used; do
        if [ -r "$f" ]; then
            cat "$f"
            return 0
        fi
    done
    return 0
}
human() {
    # Bytes to human size when numfmt exists; raw bytes otherwise.
    if [ -n "$1" ] && command -v numfmt >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        numfmt --to=iec "$1"
    else
        printf '%s' "$1"
    fi
}
ram_start=$(ram_bytes)
vram_start=$(vram_used_bytes)

# The resolved engine environment: every WGPU_COMPUTE_* and
# ITAK_* variable currently set (set-but-empty included).
env_lines=$(env | grep -E '^(WGPU_COMPUTE_|ITAK_)' | sort || true)
if [ -z "$env_lines" ]; then
    env_lines="(none set)"
fi

# Quote the command once, for the manifest, REPRO, and index.
cmd_quoted=""
for arg in "$@"; do
    printf -v q '%q' "$arg"
    cmd_quoted="$cmd_quoted $q"
done
cmd_quoted=${cmd_quoted# }

# --- run the command, tee'd ------------------------------------------
stage=$(mktemp -d)
fifo_dir="$stage/fifos"
mkdir -p "$fifo_dir"
mkfifo "$fifo_dir/out" "$fifo_dir/err"
tee "$stage/stdout.log" < "$fifo_dir/out" &
tee_out_pid=$!
tee "$stage/stderr.log" >&2 < "$fifo_dir/err" &
tee_err_pid=$!
"$@" > "$fifo_dir/out" 2> "$fifo_dir/err"
cmd_rc=$?
# The tees end when the command closes the fifos; wait reaps
# them, so both logs are complete and flushed before we read.
wait "$tee_out_pid" "$tee_err_pid" 2>/dev/null

# --- end-of-run state -------------------------------------------------
utc_end=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
local_end=$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z)
epoch_end=$(date +%s)
duration=$((epoch_end - epoch_start))
ram_end=$(ram_bytes)
vram_end=$(vram_used_bytes)

cat "$stage/stdout.log" "$stage/stderr.log" > "$stage/combined.log"
matched_markers=""
for marker in "${FAILURE_MARKERS[@]}"; do
    count=$(grep -c -F -- "$marker" "$stage/combined.log" || true)
    if [ "$count" -gt 0 ]; then
        matched_markers="$matched_markers $marker($count)"
    fi
done
matched_markers=${matched_markers# }

verdict="PASS"
fail_reasons=""
if [ "$cmd_rc" -ne 0 ]; then
    verdict="FAIL"
    fail_reasons="exit code $cmd_rc"
fi
if [ -n "$matched_markers" ]; then
    verdict="FAIL"
    if [ -n "$fail_reasons" ]; then
        fail_reasons="$fail_reasons; failure markers matched: $matched_markers"
    else
        fail_reasons="failure markers matched: $matched_markers"
    fi
fi

# --- model file block (path/size/sha256, hash cached) -----------------
model_path=""
if [ -n "$fb_model" ] && [ -f "$fb_model" ]; then
    model_path=$fb_model
else
    for arg in "$@"; do
        case "$arg" in
            *.gguf)
                if [ -f "$arg" ]; then
                    model_path=$arg
                elif [ -f "$caller_pwd/$arg" ]; then
                    model_path="$caller_pwd/$arg"
                fi
                if [ -n "$model_path" ]; then
                    case "$model_path" in
                        /*) ;;
                        *) model_path="$repo_root/$model_path" ;;
                    esac
                    break
                fi
                ;;
        esac
    done
fi
model_size=""
model_mtime=""
model_sha=""
model_cache="none"
if [ -n "$model_path" ]; then
    model_size=$(stat -c %s "$model_path")
    model_mtime=$(stat -c %Y "$model_path")
    cache_file="$vault/model-hash-index.tsv"
    if [ -f "$cache_file" ]; then
        model_sha=$(awk -F '\t' -v p="$model_path" -v s="$model_size" -v m="$model_mtime" \
            '$1 == p && $2 == s && $3 == m {print $4}' "$cache_file")
    fi
    if [ -n "$model_sha" ]; then
        model_cache="hit"
    else
        model_sha=$(sha256sum "$model_path" | awk '{print $1}')
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$model_path" "$model_size" "$model_mtime" "$model_sha" >> "$cache_file"
        model_cache="computed and cached"
    fi
fi

# --- index line (written for passes and failures alike) ---------------
index_file="$vault/INDEX.md"
if [ ! -f "$index_file" ]; then
    {
        echo "# Failure vault index"
        echo ""
        echo "One line per wrapped run (bench/failure-bundle.sh). FAIL rows"
        echo "point at a full bundle directory in this folder; PASS rows are"
        echo "the whole record, because a pass deletes its bulky logs by"
        echo "design. The convention is bench/failure-bundles-2026-11-06.md."
        echo ""
        echo "| UTC | slug | verdict | bundle | command |"
        echo "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |"
    } > "$index_file"
fi
index_cmd=$(printf '%s' "$cmd_quoted" | tr '|' '/')

if [ "$verdict" = "PASS" ]; then
    echo "| $utc_start | $slug | PASS | - | $index_cmd |" >> "$index_file"
    rm -rf "$stage"
    echo "[failure-bundle] PASS: $slug (index line only, logs deleted)" >&2
    exit "$cmd_rc"
fi

# --- assemble the failure bundle --------------------------------------
bundle_name="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)-$slug"
bundle="$vault/$bundle_name"
n=2
while [ -e "$bundle" ]; do
    bundle="$vault/$bundle_name-$n"
    n=$((n + 1))
done
mkdir -p "$bundle"
mv "$stage/stdout.log" "$bundle/stdout.log"
mv "$stage/stderr.log" "$bundle/stderr.log"
printf '%s\n' "$env_lines" > "$bundle/env.txt"

outputs_note="not given"
outputs_count=0
if [ -n "$outdir" ]; then
    if [ -d "$outdir" ]; then
        mkdir -p "$bundle/outputs"
        cp -a "$outdir/." "$bundle/outputs/"
        outputs_count=$(find "$bundle/outputs" -type f | wc -l)
        outputs_note="captured from $outdir ($outputs_count files)"
    else
        outputs_note="given as $outdir but not a directory after the run; nothing captured"
    fi
fi

{
    echo "slug: $slug"
    echo "verdict: FAIL ($fail_reasons)"
    echo "command: $cmd_quoted"
    echo "exit_code: $cmd_rc"
    echo "markers_matched: ${matched_markers:-none}"
    echo "utc_start: $utc_start"
    echo "utc_end: $utc_end"
    echo "local_start: $local_start"
    echo "local_end: $local_end"
    echo "duration_seconds: $duration"
    echo "host: $host_name"
    echo "uname: $uname_line"
    echo "repo_git_sha: $git_sha"
    echo "repo_branch: $git_branch"
    echo "repo_dirty: $git_dirty"
    echo "model_path: ${model_path:-none detected}"
    echo "model_size_bytes: ${model_size:-}"
    echo "model_mtime_epoch: ${model_mtime:-}"
    echo "model_sha256: ${model_sha:-}"
    echo "model_hash_cache: $model_cache"
    echo "ram_available_start_bytes: ${ram_start:-unavailable}"
    echo "ram_available_start_human: $(human "$ram_start")"
    echo "ram_available_end_bytes: ${ram_end:-unavailable}"
    echo "ram_available_end_human: $(human "$ram_end")"
    echo "vram_used_start_bytes: ${vram_start:-unavailable}"
    echo "vram_used_start_human: $(human "$vram_start")"
    echo "vram_used_end_bytes: ${vram_end:-unavailable}"
    echo "vram_used_end_human: $(human "$vram_end")"
    echo "outputs_dir: $outputs_note"
    echo ""
    echo "engine environment (also in env.txt):"
    printf '%s\n' "$env_lines"
    echo ""
    echo "git status --porcelain at start of run:"
    if [ "$git_dirty" = "clean" ]; then
        echo "(clean)"
    else
        printf '%s\n' "$git_status"
    fi
} > "$bundle/manifest.txt"

{
    echo "# Repro: $slug"
    echo ""
    echo "## Command"
    echo ""
    echo '```sh'
    echo "$cmd_quoted"
    echo '```'
    echo ""
    echo "Run from the repo root (the wrapper's working directory),"
    echo "with the environment in this bundle's env.txt."
    echo ""
    echo "## Pass condition that failed"
    echo ""
    echo "Expected: exit code 0 and none of the failure markers"
    echo "(${FAILURE_MARKERS[*]}) in the combined stdout+stderr."
    echo ""
    echo "Observed: $fail_reasons."
    echo ""
    echo "## State at the run"
    echo ""
    echo "- git: $git_sha (branch $git_branch, working tree $git_dirty)"
    echo "- model: ${model_path:-none detected} sha256 ${model_sha:-n/a}"
    echo "- full output: stdout.log and stderr.log in this bundle"
    if [ -n "$outdir" ]; then
        echo "- command outputs: outputs/ in this bundle ($outputs_note)"
    fi
} > "$bundle/REPRO.md"

echo "| $utc_start | $slug | FAIL | $bundle_name | $index_cmd |" >> "$index_file"
rm -rf "$stage"
echo "[failure-bundle] FAIL: $slug -> bench/failures/$bundle_name ($fail_reasons)" >&2
exit "$cmd_rc"

===== END FILE: bench/failure-bundle.sh =====

===== FILE: bench/failure-bundles-2026-11-06.md =====
# Failure bundles: the wrong-data vault (2026-11-06)

## Why

David's standing want: every form of debugging data we can
squeeze out, and the WRONG data kept in full, because wrong
outputs are what fixes are built on. Until now, failures
were preserved only by hand. The standing example: the
first top-5 probability run came back degenerate (every
record's top-5 list held 1 entry, every top-1 probability
exactly 1.0), the pickup lane refused to commit it, and the
file survived only because someone kept it on the server
by hand as glimmer.top5.degenerate.jsonl. A failure that
exists only in a log someone happened to save is a failure
we will eventually lose.

`bench/failure-bundle.sh` makes the preservation
automatic and uniform: one wrapper around any bench or
harness command, and a failed run assembles its own
evidence bundle before anyone has to remember to save it.

## The convention

Every future verdict protocol wraps its runs in
bench/failure-bundle.sh:

```sh
bench/failure-bundle.sh <slug> [outdir] -- <command...>
```

- A run FAILS when the command exits nonzero OR when its
  combined output matches a failure marker. Both shapes
  produce a full bundle.
- A failure without a bundle is an incomplete report.
  When a verdict note says FAIL, the bundle directory
  name goes in the note next to the claim, the same way
  raw logs are cited today.
- The wrapper never changes the run: output is tee'd to
  the caller's terminal live, and the wrapper exits with
  the wrapped command's exit code in all cases. A
  marker-only failure therefore still exits 0; it is
  detected through the bundle and the INDEX, not the
  exit code. Protocols that need a hard stop on wrong
  data check for the bundle.

## Bundle format

Bundles live in the vault, `bench/failures/` (override
with FB_VAULT), one directory per failed run, named
`<UTC timestamp>-<slug>`:

| file | contents |
| --- | --- |
| manifest.txt | slug, verdict with fail reasons, the exact command (shell-quoted, re-runnable), exit code, matched markers with counts, UTC and local start/end, duration, host and uname, repo git SHA, branch, dirty state with the full porcelain listing, the model block (below), the engine environment, free RAM (MemAvailable) at start and end, VRAM used at start and end (amdgpu sysfs; "unavailable" is recorded, never hidden, on hosts without the counters) |
| stdout.log | the command's full stdout, as printed |
| stderr.log | the command's full stderr, as printed |
| env.txt | every resolved WGPU_COMPUTE_* and ITAK_* variable, sorted |
| outputs/ | copy of the caller-named output directory's contents, when one was given |
| REPRO.md | the exact command line and the pass condition it failed: expected (exit 0 and no markers) against observed (exit code, matched markers), plus the state summary |

The model block records path, size, mtime, and sha256.
The hash is streamed (sha256sum) once and cached by
path+size+mtime in the vault's `model-hash-index.tsv`,
so a 16 GB GGUF is not re-hashed on every run. The model
is taken from FB_MODEL when set, else from the first
command argument that is an existing *.gguf file.

Failure markers are fixed strings, case-sensitive,
matched as substrings against the combined output. The
list is the FAILURE_MARKERS variable at the top of the
script, and it decides what counts as wrong data:

```
FAIL  FAILED  mismatch  DIVERGES  REFUSED  degenerate
```

Extend it in review, never silently.

Passing runs keep no bundle and no logs: exactly one line
in `bench/failures/INDEX.md` (UTC, slug, PASS, command),
so the vault holds every failure in full and every pass
as an index line. FAIL runs also get an INDEX line,
pointing at their bundle.

## Demo evidence (this VM, 2026-11-06)

Three trivial runs through the wrapper, no GPU involved:

1. `demo-fail`: prints "top5 mismatch at row 3", exits 3.
   Bundle 20261106T224349Z-demo-fail assembled (reasons:
   exit code 3; marker mismatch x1); wrapper exit 3. The
   run carried WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=16, and that line
   is what env.txt and the manifest recorded.
2. `demo-marker`: prints a "degenerate" line, exits 0.
   Bundle 20261106T224352Z-demo-marker assembled (reason:
   marker degenerate x1); wrapper exit 0, the wrapped
   code, per the exit-code rule above. This is the
   top-5 shape: clean exit, wrong data, still vaulted.
3. `demo-pass`: clean output, exits 0. No bundle; one
   PASS line in INDEX.md; wrapper exit 0.

The committed demo bundles are skeletons: their stdout
and stderr logs were stripped before commit, with each
removed log's size and sha256 recorded in the bundle's
LOGS-STRIPPED.txt. Real failure bundles always keep
their logs; the strip is a commit-size rule for the
demo only, and it is labeled in the bundle itself.

shellcheck could not be run on this lane: it is not
installed on the build VM (`command -v shellcheck` is
empty). The script says so in its header and follows the
repo bench style (set -u, everything quoted); run
shellcheck on it from any host that has it.

## Retro-bundle candidates

Historical wrong data that predates the wrapper. None of
it is lost yet, but none of it is in the vault either.
At the next server session, wrap or hand-assemble each
of these into a bundle so they sit under the same
convention:

1. **The degenerate top-5 output (2026-11-05).** Every
   top-5 list held exactly 1 entry and every top-1
   probability was exactly 1.0: the generator requested
   post_sampling_probs at temperature 0, collapsing each
   distribution to a one-hot. Refused at verification,
   never committed. Lives on the server at
   ~/overnight-golden/out/glimmer.top5.degenerate.jsonl;
   the full story is in bench/overnight-golden-2026-11-05.md.
2. **The wide-MMQ session hang (2026-11-04/05).** The
   K15/K16 wide MMQ ladder ran about 3.5x slower per
   tensor than K13/K14 and then hung a real resident
   session: RADV reported the context lost with a hard
   recovery, and no prefill line was ever produced, at
   both bench lengths. Recorded in
   bench/mmq-wide-tile-2026-11-03.md; the compiled-form
   conviction (1,041 to 1,213 spilled VGPRs, 78 to 86 KB
   scratch) is in bench/shader-autopsy-2026-11-04.md,
   with raw dumps under /tmp/shader-autopsy/ on the
   server (ephemeral; may already be gone). The hang's
   own session logs were never bundled. That gap is
   exactly what this wrapper closes.
3. **The K18 loss runs (2026-11-04).** Correct output,
   losing speed, kept deliberately as the negative
   result: depth 6, 8.13 tok/s against the 9.19 control
   (verify 178.0 ms against 149.8); depth 1, 8.90
   against 14.22 (verify 125.1 ms against 55.3). Verdict
   and numbers in bench/small-batch-2026-11-04.md; the
   raw run logs sit in the 2026-11-04 wave staging trees
   (~/gpu-wave*) on the server, exact directory to be
   confirmed when the retro-bundle is assembled.
4. **The phase B OOM kills (2026-11-05).** Six phase B
   attempts across two windows, every one killed by the
   host OOM killer during verify-session construction,
   exit 137, at 34.6 to 34.7 GB anon-rss per kill. The
   accounting that explained them is in
   bench/phase-b-footprint-2026-11-05.md and the verdict
   record in bench/mmv-verdict-2026-11-05.md; the run
   logs are preserved on the server under
   ~/gpu-wave10/logs, ~/gpu-wave10/logs2,
   ~/gpu-wave10/logs3, and the ~/gpu-wave8 outputs.

Each retro-bundle gets a manifest and REPRO written from
its bench note, with the note cited as the source, so a
hand-assembled bundle never pretends to be a wrapped
run.

# Failure vault index

One line per wrapped run (bench/failure-bundle.sh). FAIL rows
point at a full bundle directory in this folder; PASS rows are
the whole record, because a pass deletes its bulky logs by
design. The convention is bench/failure-bundles-2026-11-06.md.

What a committed bundle contains: the two bundles below are the
synthetic demos from the tooling proof, not production failures.
By the wrapper's design (bench/failure-bundle.sh), a bundle's
env.txt holds only the resolved WGPU_COMPUTE_* and ITAK_* engine
tuning variables, never the process environment, and its
manifest.txt holds repro facts (host name, kernel string, repo
SHA and branch, timestamps, model path and hash). No bundle
carries credentials; the capture pattern cannot match a key or
token variable. The demo bundles' logs were stripped before
commit under the size rule recorded in their LOGS-STRIPPED.txt.

| UTC | slug | verdict | bundle | command |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-11-06T22:43:48Z | demo-fail | FAIL | 20261106T224349Z-demo-fail | bash -c echo\ \"synthetic\ wrong\ data:\ top5\ mismatch\ at\ row\ 3\"\;\ echo\ \"harness\ noise\ on\ stderr\"\ \>\&2\;\ exit\ 3 |
| 2026-11-06T22:43:52Z | demo-marker | FAIL | 20261106T224352Z-demo-marker | bash -c echo\ \"run\ completed\;\ output\ is\ degenerate:\ every\ top-1\ probability\ is\ exactly\ 1.0\"\;\ exit\ 0 |

===== FILE: bench/flash-chunk-2026-11-04.md =====
# Flash attention for chunk plans (2026-11-04)

Lane: lane/flash-attn, based on merged main 864dffd.
Implements candidate C1 of the prefill chain profile
(~/workspace/lanes/profile/PROFILE-prefill-chain-2026-11-03.md):
the resident session's chunk-plan attention now runs the
fused flash form instead of the staged two-pass
scores + reduce.

Nothing in this note was measured on a GPU. This VM enumerates
no wgpu adapter, so every GPU test below compiles and skips
here by the crate's established adapter-absence policy. All
performance figures are EXPECTATIONS derived in the profile
note, labeled as such; the server commands at the end are
what turns them into measurements.

## Design

The surprise of the lane: the flash kernel needed no change.
K6's FLASH_SHADER was already shape-generic, and the profile
note's sketch (an env toggle at plan build) was only ever an
A/B vehicle. The kernel takes one workgroup per (query row,
Q head) at any row count, computes the causal position per
row (`start_pos + row`), applies the sliding mask in the
form `kp + window <= p` (no underflow), slots keys modulo
the ring capacity exactly as the scores kernel does, and
carries online-softmax state across 256-key tiles in
ascending order, which is the two-pass operation sequence
per output element. The sliding window at chunk shapes and
the chunked ring (window + cap - 1) therefore carry over
unchanged; the tiling cannot fail to express the mask,
because it never expressed anything else.

What changed is the session wiring:

- `ChunkPlan::build` prepares K6 flash for every layer at
  every row count. The `rows == 1` selection is gone;
  `LayerPlan` holds one `flash: K6FlashCall` (no longer
  optional, no scores/reduce calls beside it).
- The scores scratch is deleted from plan scratch. No
  session buffer grows with the stored position count
  anymore, so plan currency is KV-buffer currency alone:
  the scores-capacity growth rebuilds in `forward_chunk`
  are gone with the buffer they served.
- The scores budget is deleted (`SCORES_BUDGET_ELEMS` and
  the shrink inside `chunk_rows`). Under the two-pass form,
  chunk rows decayed as context grew (32 rows at 16,384
  stored, 4 rows at the full 131,072 context), multiplying
  per-chunk submits, syncs, and host records. Chunks now
  hold their cap at any context length.
- Chunk sizing is config-driven, per house law. The cap
  resolves once at session construction from
  `WGPU_COMPUTE_CHUNK_ROWS` (default 64, the value every
  recorded bench ran at), validated against the structural
  ceiling `MAX_CHUNK_ROWS` (64: the largest chunk the ring
  algebra is built around); unparsable or out-of-range
  values fall back to the default, and the resolution is
  logged through the diag channel at construction. The
  windowed ring capacity (window + cap - 1) and the
  `rewind_to` bound derive from the resolved cap, so a
  lowered cap shrinks the ring and tightens the rewind
  bound together, keeping the aliasing algebra sound.
  The pure sizing law (`resolve_chunk_rows`,
  `chunk_rows_for`, `ring_capacity`) is unit tested on the
  host: 4 tests, run for real on this VM.
- Dispatch accounting: the per-layer base drops from 17
  to 16 unconditionally (the flash form is one K6 dispatch
  where the two-pass form was two, on chunk plans; decode
  plans already counted it). Decode behavior is otherwise
  untouched: a one-row plan prepares the same flash call
  with the same geometry as before, so the decode path is
  bit-identical by construction.
- The two-pass form is NOT deleted: the trait path
  (`compute.rs`, one row per step) still runs the K6
  one-shot scores + reduce, and the K6 module docs now say
  which form serves which driver.

Refusals stay named: kernel refusals still surface under
the `attention` step through the existing `we(...)` wrap,
the head-dim bound (128) still refuses in
`ResidentSession::new` and in `K6Pipeline::check_geom`, and
the rewind refusal now names the session's resolved cap.

## Expected deltas (from the profile note, DERIVED there)

Per 64-row chunk on the real model (731 dispatches derived
by the profile from the plan builder's own accounting):

- Dispatches: 52 fewer per chunk, one per layer
  (731 to 679 derived). On the resident fixture the session
  stats pin moves from 57 to 51 dispatches per chunk,
  asserted in `resident_session_matches_trait_and_cpu`.
- Scores traffic: the scores buffer round trip is gone:
  8.39 MB written and 8.39 MB read per layer at 1,024
  stored, about 873 MB per chunk, plus the scores scratch
  allocation itself (up to 64 MiB under the old budget).
- Softmax work: the reduce's per-lane exp stream (about
  268M exp evaluations per layer at 1,024 stored, one per
  (row, head, key, lane)) collapses to one exp per
  (row, head, key), about 2.1M per layer.
- Chunk shape at depth: rows stay 64 at the full 131,072
  context instead of decaying to 4, so per-chunk fixed
  costs (submit, blocking sync, head, host record) are
  paid up to 16x less often per token at deep context.

What this does NOT promise: the profile showed the chain
is bound by instruction mix and serialization, not DRAM
bytes, and the per-stage split of the roughly 3.03 ms/token
chain was never measured. Flash at chunk shapes is proven
only at decode geometry (within noise of two-pass at 69
stored); the win is an S-scaling claim. The recorded
baselines to beat are the MMQ build's: marginal 161 tok/s,
gross 135.8 tok/s at 1,024 tokens. The profile's kill
criteria stand: a session marginal gain under 10% at
S=1024, or any exactness gate moving, kills the switch.

## Parity bar and tests

- `k6_flash_matches_two_pass` (tests/fused_kernels.rs)
  extended with four chunk geometries at the file's
  established bar (max abs diff under 1e-6 against the
  two-pass form over the same resident KV): a 64-row global
  chunk over 1,024 stored (four tiles, per-row causality);
  a 64-row sliding chunk at window 512, ring 575, slots
  wrapping, both masks biting; the full-context sliding
  geometry (window 2048, ring 2111, nine tiles, deep
  absolute positions); a 16-row partial chunk crossing one
  tile boundary.
- `resident_session_matches_trait_and_cpu` now exercises
  flash inside chunk plans against BOTH references at the
  cross-backend bar (argmax agreement at every step,
  max-abs logit diff under 0.5): the CPU model and the
  trait path (which still runs two-pass K6 per step), over
  a 4-row chunk, five decode steps, and a 70-token two-chunk
  prompt through a window-4 ring.
- Host unit tests for the sizing law (above).

## Server proof (ubuntu-server, GPU free, one heavy job)

Stage this branch's tree, verify the staged hash equals the
branch tip, then:

```sh
export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
# 1. Kernel-level parity must EXECUTE (not skip):
cargo test -p wgpu-compute --test fused_kernels k6_flash_matches_two_pass -- --nocapture
# 2. Session parity against CPU + trait, dispatch pin 51/chunk:
cargo test -p wgpu-compute --test resident_session -- --nocapture
# 3. The spec path's resident block pin and shader compile gate:
cargo test -p wgpu-compute --test resident_block -- --nocapture
cargo test -p wgpu-compute --test shader_compile
cargo test -p wgpu-compute -p itak-spec
```

Then the prefill bench on the real file, same discipline as
the earlier notes (medians of 3, same window, this branch
against merged main as the two-pass control):

```sh
cargo build --release -p itak-loader --example glimmer_generate
GEN=./target/release/examples/glimmer_generate
MODEL=/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf
# The repeated-sentence prompts from bench/mmq-wide-bench.sh
# (about 254 and about 1,024 tokens), greedy, resident path:
$GEN "$MODEL" "<254-token prompt>" 32 --gpu
$GEN "$MODEL" "<1024-token prompt>" 32 --gpu
# A 4,096-token prompt exercises the removed chunk decay:
$GEN "$MODEL" "<4096-token prompt>" 32 --gpu
```

Read `phase=prefill ms=` from each run and compute gross
and marginal rates between the two standard lengths.
Acceptance, all in the same window:

1. Gross and marginal at 1,024 tokens improve over the
   two-pass control build; the recorded MMQ-era baseline
   (marginal 161 tok/s, gross 135.8) is the floor the
   control should reproduce, and flash must beat the
   control, not just the record.
2. Exactness gates from the profile's M5: first-token
   probability 0.403462, the 8/8 Stage 1 ids, and generated
   continuations token-identical to the two-pass control at
   254 and 1,024 tokens.
3. SessionStats dispatches per 64-row chunk drop by 52
   against the control (the derived 731 to 679), and the
   per-chunk lines show 64 rows held at the 4,096-token
   prompt's depth.

===== FILE: bench/flash-default-flip-2026-11-07.md =====
# Staged flash default flip: off to on (2026-11-07)

Lane: lane/flash-default-flip, based on main
910b800ea6d716aed18a708bb0cb47312cd5a206. Code commit
03fc780. VM gates only on this lane; no server GPU
jobs. The card evidence this flip stands on was
measured by two earlier sessions, cited below; this
lane changed one resolver, its docs, and its tests.

## What changed

`WGPU_COMPUTE_FLASH_STAGED` (crates/wgpu-compute/src/
compute.rs) shipped with an opt-in resolver: only the
exact value `1` enabled K6's staged flash form, and an
unset variable meant off. The resolver now ships the
staged form as the default for multi-row attention
calls. Rollback is one env var:
`WGPU_COMPUTE_FLASH_STAGED=0` restores the shipped
flash form exactly, no rebuild, no other setting.

### The semantic matrix (final)

| env value | resolved | notes |
|---|---|---|
| unset | ON | the new shipped default |
| `1` (trimmed) | ON | unchanged: a value that meant on before the flip means on after |
| `0` (trimmed) | OFF | the explicit off; the rollback |
| anything else | OFF | fail-closed; the refusal is logged by name at construction (`flash staged env ... is not a recognized value ... failing closed, the staged form is OFF`), following the MMV band fallback pattern |

The single-row exclusion is not part of the switch
and did not move: session.rs still routes staged only
when the switch is on AND the staged pipeline exists
on the device AND the call carries more than one row.
Single-row calls (decode) run the shipped flash form
in every switch position, as before.

## The evidence chain

1. **The kernel and its rule**
   (bench/flash-rework-2026-11-06.md). The staged form
   stages K/V blocks of 32 keys in workgroup memory,
   8 query rows per workgroup, same bindings, params,
   output layout, and per-element float sequence as
   the shipped flash. Its decision rule, written in
   advance, required for a default flip: autopsy clean
   (LDS 21,632 B, VGPR at most 128, zero spills);
   every correctness leg green including identity and
   golden with the switch on; the staged flash total
   at 1,022 tokens at most 760 ms (25 percent under
   the recorded 1,013.1 ms) WITH the prefill wall
   improved against the same-session control; the
   staged total ahead at 8k tokens or more; no-leak
   clean and decode unmoved.

2. **The split verdict**
   (bench/baseline-session-2026-11-06.md, leg (i)).
   Autopsy PASS (VGPR 60, zero spills, zero scratch).
   Correctness PASS (exactness test, resident suite,
   spec identity and golden at depths 1 and 6, all
   with the switch on). Kernel row at 1,022 tokens:
   605.9 ms against the control's 972.9, a 37.7
   percent improvement, clearing the 760 ms bar.
   Long context: flash row 47,360.9 to 22,820.3 ms
   (51.8 percent) and phase wall 93,509 to 66,704 ms
   (28.7 percent) at 8,202 tokens. But the 1,022 wall
   clause FAILED on that session's single pair of
   runs: 6,383 ms off against 6,558 ms on, read as
   roughly 540 ms of non-kernel time appearing with
   the switch on. The flip was correctly refused on
   that evidence.

3. **The phantom**
   (bench/flash-host-cost-2026-11-06.md). A dedicated
   lane hunted the 540 ms segment by segment under
   interleaved, cache-controlled, repeated
   measurement (arms interleaved off/on/on/off at
   1,022, fresh shader caches priced separately,
   every run failure-bundled). Findings: the
   wall-minus-GPU gap segment reads 201.5 to 226.9 ms
   in BOTH forms with no form-locked offset; the wall
   delta matches the GPU kernel delta to within
   scatter at every shape; session stats are
   identical between forms at every shape (same
   submissions, readbacks, dispatch counts), so no
   extra submit, sync, or readback exists to pay;
   pipeline compilation lands in backend_open before
   the measured window and is form-neutral; slice 0
   shows no deferred compile. The staged form wins
   the wall at every shape measured: 1,022 tokens
   about 6,150 ms on against 6,490 ms off (timing-off
   pair 6,025 against 6,342), 2,052 tokens 13,500
   against 15,227, 4,102 tokens 29,885 against
   36,945, 8,202 tokens 66,546 against 93,402 (the
   long-context win reproducing the baseline
   session's step 3 almost to the digit). The 540 ms
   was an artifact of the first verdict's evidence
   shape: one non-interleaved pair of wall samples,
   from a session whose own note records a host under
   parallel CPU collection with wide scatter; a
   +175 ms single-sample wall delta and a 367 ms
   kernel saving were combined into a host penalty
   that does not exist in the code.

With step 2's wall clause discharged by interleaved
evidence, every clause of the rework note's decision
rule holds, and the default flips. David approved
proceeding on that basis.

## Tests

- `flash_staged_switch_resolution` (compute.rs unit
  tests): re-pinned to the new matrix (unset on, `1`
  and trimmed `1` on, `0` and trimmed `0` off,
  `true`/empty/`11`/`on` off), with the justification
  cited in the test body
  (bench/flash-host-cost-2026-11-06.md, interleaved
  arms).
- `flash_staged_value_recognition` (new): pins the
  recognized set the construction log consults
  (unset, `1`, `0`, trimmed forms) against the
  unrecognized set that fails closed with a named
  refusal.
- The fused-kernel device tests that exercise the
  staged form directly
  (`k6_flash_staged_matches_shipped_at_glimmer_shapes`)
  do not consult the switch and are unchanged; the
  single-row routing exclusion is unmodified code.

## Gates (this lane, VM)

- `cargo test -p wgpu-compute`: 254 passed, 0 failed,
  1 ignored (the ignored one is the pre-existing diag
  hash-cost probe), across 27 test binaries; lib 146.
  Device tests skip on the VM, which enumerates no
  adapter, as throughout this crate.
- `cargo test -p dflash`: 24 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p itak-spec`: 49 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p wgpu-compute --all-targets -- -D
  warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`: clean.

## What a card run still owes

Nothing for the flip itself: correctness with the
staged form engaged was proven on the card by both
earlier sessions (exactness, resident suite,
identity and golden at depths 1 and 6, prefill argmax
identical between forms at every shape, bit-for-bit
on id and logit). The first post-merge session that
runs with the variable unset should see the
construction line read `flash staged config:
enabled=true`, and multi-row forwards should stamp
`k6_attn_flash_staged` where the shipped form used
to stamp `k6_attn_flash`; that is the exposure check
that the new default is what production runs get.

===== FILE: bench/flash-host-cost-2026-11-06.md =====
# Flash host cost hunt: the 540 ms does not exist (2026-11-06)

Lane: lane/flash-host-cost, based on main
2c1f8c7ef3c5c634d504e687d8c4ae4075f580a4. Evidence under
review: bench/baseline-session-2026-11-06.md leg (i),
where the staged flash kernel won its kernel row by
37.7 percent at 1,022 tokens (972.9 to 605.9 ms) yet the
prefill phase wall moved the wrong way (6,383 off vs
6,558 on), implying roughly 540 ms of non-kernel time
that appears with WGPU_COMPUTE_FLASH_STAGED=1 at the
short shape. This lane's job was to find that time,
segment by segment, and either fix it or ship a
measurement-justified length gate.

**Verdict up front: there is no host cost to fix and
no length gate to ship.** Under interleaved,
cache-controlled, repeated measurement on the server
card, the staged form is faster on the wall at every
shape measured, including 1,022 tokens, and the wall
delta matches the GPU kernel delta to within noise at
every shape. The wall-minus-GPU gap segment is the
same for both forms. The 540 ms was an artifact of
the baseline session's evidence shape: one
non-interleaved pair of runs, from which a +175 ms
single-sample wall delta and a 367 ms kernel saving
were combined into a phantom host penalty. Every
structural candidate this lane was asked to eliminate
(extra submits, extra readbacks, per-call prepare
cost, pipeline compilation inside the measured window,
drain behavior) is eliminated below by measurement,
not by argument. No code changes on this lane; the
switch, its semantics, and the shipped default are
untouched. The staged form's own decision rule from
bench/flash-rework-2026-11-06.md (kernel row bar plus
same-session wall improvement at 1,022) now PASSES on
interleaved evidence; whether the default flips is
the parent's call, as it was before.

## Method

Server session staged from this lane's head into
~/gpu-wave15 (394 files, sha256 manifest verified,
0 mismatches). All card runs inside
`flock -w 14400 /tmp/itak-phase.lock`, Cortex tenants
stopped before and restored after every card block,
VRAM guard read before each block (clear card
33,271,808 B used, the driver-residue value), every
run wrapped in bench/failure-bundle.sh (all 15
wrapped runs PASS in the staging tree's
bench/failures/INDEX.md, slugs fh-*; raw logs on the
server in ~/gpu-wave15/logs15/, per-kernel summaries
committed with this note under
bench/results/flash-host-cost-20261107/).

Harness: prefill_profile, fox prompt ("The quick
brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. " x102 = 1,022
tokens; x205 = 2,052; x410 = 4,102; x820 = 8,202),
slices of 64 rows. Arms at 1,022 were interleaved
off, on, on, off with diag timing on, plus a
timing-off pair (the wall-of-record surface), plus a
cold-cache pair in which each form got its own fresh
MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR so first-in-process pipeline
compilation is priced and located. Mid and long
shapes ran as off/on pairs on the warm shared cache.

## Segmentation at 1,022 tokens (diag timing on)

Kernel rows reproduce the baseline session almost
exactly: shipped flash 966.4 to 974.0 ms across the
three off arms; staged flash 605.0 to 606.6 ms across
the three on arms (baseline read 972.9 / 605.9).

| arm | cache | prefill wall | GPU total | gap (wall - GPU) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| off-cold | fresh | 6,454 | 6,252.5 | 201.5 |
| on-cold | fresh | 6,175 | 5,950.5 | 224.5 |
| off-w1 | fresh | 6,500 | 6,297.4 | 202.6 |
| on-w1 | warm | 6,137 | 5,910.1 | 226.9 |
| on-w2 | warm | 6,125 | 5,911.9 | 213.1 |
| off-w2 | warm | 6,539 | 6,316.2 | 222.8 |

The gap segment (host encode, submits, per-slice
drains and readbacks: everything in the wall that is
not a timed kernel) reads 201.5 to 226.9 ms in BOTH
forms, with no arm-locked offset; the largest
cross-form difference between any two arms is inside
the within-form scatter (off arms alone span 201.5
to 222.8). The wall delta (on faster by 279, 363,
and 414 ms in the three pairings) matches the GPU
total delta (302, 387, 404 ms) to within that same
scatter. The kernel saving passes through to the
wall 1:1. There is no segment left for 540 ms to
hide in.

Timing-off pair (wall of record): off 6,342 ms, on
6,025 ms. The staged form wins the 1,022 wall clause
on the shipped surface too, by 317 ms.

Per-segment elimination of the named candidates:

- Submissions and readbacks: session_stats are
  IDENTICAL in every arm pair at every shape
  (1,022: forwards 16, chunks 16, submissions 16,
  aux_submissions 3, readbacks 16, dispatches 10,448;
  same identity at 2,052, 4,102, and 8,202). The
  staged form submits nothing extra, syncs nothing
  extra, reads back nothing extra.
- Per-call prepare cost: the two prepares share one
  body (prepare_flash_form in k6_attention.rs) and
  differ only in pipeline, diag name, and grid; the
  per-slice times show it. Slice 0 reads 395 to 426
  ms in all twelve 1,022 arms regardless of form;
  steady-state slice means are 382 to 385 ms (on)
  against 403 to 408 ms (off), the kernel saving
  visible slice by slice, with no first-slice or
  first-forward spike in any on arm.
- Pipeline compilation placement: a fresh shader
  cache costs about 1,080 ms, and it lands in
  phase=backend_open (1,495 and 1,484 ms cold vs 406
  to 415 ms warm), BEFORE the prefill window, for
  both forms equally (cold off 1,495 = cold on
  1,495). The staged shader adds no measurable
  compile delta there, and slice 0 of the cold on
  arm (414 ms) shows no deferred compile arriving
  inside the window either. Compilation is real host
  cost, but it is construction cost, it is
  form-neutral, and it never enters the phase wall.
- Session construction: phase=session_build ranges
  9,505 to 12,326 ms across all arms with the forms
  fully interleaved in that range (weight upload
  noise); no form offset.
- Drain behavior: the harness drains the diag
  recorder after every slice in both forms; drained
  patterns and the gap segment above already include
  it, identically.

## Mid and long shapes (diag timing on)

| shape | form | wall | GPU total | gap | flash row |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2,052 | off | 15,227 | 14,833.1 | 393.9 | 4,184.0 |
| 2,052 | on | 13,500 | 13,121.2 | 378.8 | 2,462.9 |
| 4,102 | off | 36,945 | 36,217.7 | 727.3 | 14,825.2 |
| 4,102 | on | 29,885 | 29,162.0 | 723.0 | 7,944.7 |
| 8,202 | off | 93,402 | 91,956.3 | 1,445.7 | 47,300.1 |
| 8,202 | on | 66,546 | 65,182.6 | 1,363.4 | 22,816.0 |

The long-context win does not regress; it
reproduces the baseline session's step 3 almost to
the digit (their wall 93,509 to 66,704, a 28.7
percent improvement; here 93,402 to 66,546, 28.8
percent; flash row 47,360.9 to 22,820.3 there,
47,300.1 to 22,816.0 here). The wall delta tracks
the kernel delta at every shape (2,052: 1,727 wall
vs 1,712 GPU; 4,102: 7,060 vs 7,056; 8,202: 26,856
vs 26,774), and the gap segment stays form-neutral
at every length. A length gate at any threshold up
to 8,202 would delete measured wall wins of 317 ms
(1,022, timing-off), 1,727 ms (2,052), and 7,060 ms
(4,102) to defend against a cost that does not
measure. That is why this lane ships neither a fix
nor a gate: both branches of its orders were
conditioned on a mechanism the measurements refute.

## Correctness re-proof (this lane, on the card)

- fused_kernels flash tests, bundle fh-flash-
  exactness PASS: k6_flash_matches_two_pass and
  k6_flash_staged_matches_shipped_at_glimmer_shapes
  both ok, executed on the 7900 XTX (3.84 s of real
  device time, not a skip).
- resident_session suite with
  WGPU_COMPUTE_FLASH_STAGED=1, bundle
  fh-resident-staged-on PASS: 7 passed, 0 failed,
  executed on the card.
- wgpu-compute lib flash tests with the switch on,
  bundle fh-k6-flash-tests PASS: 16 passed.
- Output agreement across every prefill arm: the
  harness's prefill_argmax is identical between
  forms at every shape, id and logit bit-for-bit
  (1,022: id 7235, logit 12.233533 in all six arms;
  2,052: 7235, 11.904436; 4,102: 29, 10.458983;
  8,202: 7235, 8.854626).
- Identity and golden with the switch on were
  proven in the baseline session on this same code
  (leg (i) step 1: spec IDENTITY and GOLDEN pass at
  depths 1 and 6); nothing in the flash path changed
  since.

## What this does and does not settle

Settled: the 1,022 wall clause of the staged form's
decision rule passes on interleaved evidence; the
540 ms non-kernel penalty is not a property of the
code, the switch, or the shape. Not settled, and not
claimed: why the baseline session's single
on-sample read 6,558 ms. Its own note records a host
under parallel CPU collection with wide scatter on
other surfaces that day, and single samples carry
that scatter whole; this lane's six interleaved
1,022 arms bound the form effect at every segment
instead. If a future session ever reproduces a real
wall regression for the staged form, the
segmentation table above is the checklist to rerun:
gap segment first, then stats identity, then slice 0
against the cold-cache backend_open price.

## Session hygiene

Tenants (cortex-cortex-chat-1, cortex-cortex-embed-1,
cortex-embed.service) were stopped before each card
block and restored after each; final state verified:
both containers Up (healthy), service active, VRAM
settled at 8,932,147,200 B (about 8.9 GB, the normal
tenant footprint) against the 33,271,808 B
clear-card guard during measurement. Production
llama-server on localhost:8080 was never touched.
No code commits on this lane: the fix branch and the
gate branch of the orders both required a mechanism,
and the measurements found none.
