===== FILE: bench/flash-rework-2026-11-06.md =====
# Flash attention rework: K/V staged in workgroup memory, 2026-11-06

Status: BUILT and VM-gated. The staged flash form exists in
`crates/wgpu-compute`, env-gated off, with its correctness
tests written and its card protocol below. No card run has
happened yet; every number in this note that is not from
the 2026-11-05 profile is a prediction or a bound, and is
labelled as one.

## Why

The prefill profile (bench/prefill-profile-2026-11-05.md)
puts the shipped flash kernel at 1,013.1 ms of 6,659 ms
GPU time at 1,022 tokens (15.2 percent; 832 dispatches,
sliding layers 764.0 ms, global layers 249.2 ms), growing
from 3.2 ms in chunk 0 to 125.7 ms in chunk 15, the last
four chunks carrying 44 percent of it. The parity
extraction (bench/llama-parity-specs-2026-11-06.md, gap 5)
names the structural cause: the shipped kernel stages
only a 256-wide score tile in workgroup memory; its score
phase reads every key row from global memory once per
query row, and its reduce phase re-reads every value row
from global memory, per lane, inside the tile loop. The
profile's attack 4 prices halving flash at 507 ms at this
context and calls it plausibly the number one lever at
4k tokens.

## The spec taken from llama.cpp

All citations verified against the server tree
(/home/server/llama.cpp), which the parity note verified
identical to the VM mirror for the ggml-vulkan sources.

- Blocked form: `Bc = 32` KV positions per block,
  staged in shared memory; query rows blocked by `Br`
  (vulkan-shaders/flash_attn_base.glsl:4-21: WorkGroupSize
  128 default, Br 1, Bc 32, HSK/HSV specialized per head
  dim, D_split 16, row_split 1, SubGroupSize 32, and the
  SHMEM_STAGING flag as a first-class spec constant).
- AMD scalar tuning (ggml-vulkan.cpp:1200-1245,
  `get_fa_tuning_params_scalar`): on AMD non-GCN at head
  dim 128, row_split is 1 (hsk 128 meets the
  row_split_max_hsk of 128 for n_rows > 8) and block_cols
  is 32 ((hsk|hsv) = 128 has no factor 8). block_rows at
  row_split 1 is 8 for n_rows > 8 when n_kv >= 1024, and
  the workgroup size resolves to subgroup_size * 4 = 256
  at the device subgroup size of 64.
- Path choice (ggml-vulkan.cpp:1334-1375,
  `get_fa_tuning_params`): a single query row always
  takes the scalar path ("scalar is faster than coopmat
  when N==1"). This lane's routing mirrors that rule
  against our own forms: one-row calls keep the shipped
  kernel even with the switch on.

One nuance, recorded so it cannot be misread later:
llama's AMD scalar tuning sets SHMEM_STAGING to 0 (the
flag is enabled only for NVIDIA in the scalar tuner), and
its scalar path reads K from global memory with vec4
loads. The staged layout is the form its matrix paths
(coopmat1/coopmat2) run and the form the base spec
constants describe. This lane builds the staged form as
its charter orders, against OUR shipped kernel as the
baseline; the card A/B below is the judge, and no claim
of AMD-scalar parity is made for it.

## The design (FLASH_STAGED_SHADER in k6_attention.rs)

Same bindings (q, keys, values, out, params at 0..4),
same FlashParams struct, same output layout as the
shipped flash kernel, so the one resident call site swaps
forms without moving a byte. KV stays f32 end to end
(the f16 KV change is a separate gated step, per gap 5's
own scoping), and nothing here touches the coopmat path
(the bridge lane's).

- Grid: one workgroup of 256 threads per (block of
  Br = 8 query rows, Q head). At the prefill chunk shape
  (64 rows, 32 heads) that is 256 workgroups against the
  shipped form's 2,048.
- Thread map: `tid / 32` is the query row inside the
  block, `tid % 32` the lane. Score phase: lane j scores
  key j of the block (full head-dim dot from the staged
  tiles). Reduce phase: lane l owns channels l, l+32,
  l+64, l+96 of its row.
- Phases per 32-key block: stage K (coalesced global
  loads, slot-mapped exactly as the shipped kernels slot:
  ring modulus is the ring capacity, never the window),
  barrier, score into the score tile, barrier, stage V
  into the same tile, barrier, online-softmax reduce
  reading V from the tile, barrier. Four barriers per
  block. The query block is staged once before the walk.
- Bank behaviour: the K/V tile's row stride is padded by
  one float (head_dim + 1). The stride is odd for every
  even head dim, hence coprime with the 32 workgroup
  banks, so the score phase's reads across keys and the
  reduce phase's reads across channels are conflict-free
  at the head dims this engine serves (128, 64). The
  query tile is read broadcast (a warp shares its row).
- Math contract: the per-element float operation
  sequence is the shipped flash kernel's, exactly. Same
  ascending-channel dots over the same values, same
  scale multiply, same -1.0e30 mask sentinel and -1.0e29
  skip test, same per-key online-softmax rescale in
  ascending key order, state carried across blocks. Only
  the storage operands pass through differs. Outputs
  therefore agree with the shipped form to the bit in
  exact arithmetic, and to driver float-contraction
  noise in practice; the device tests hold them to the
  same 1e-6 the shipped form is held to against the
  two-pass form.
- Bounds: rows past the call's row count stage as zeros,
  compute, and never write out, so every barrier is in
  uniform control flow. Head dim is capped at 128 by the
  shared `check_geom` (the query tile is sized at that
  bound). Staging reads only slots the shipped form
  reads: every key in the stored range is visible to at
  least the block row at its own position.

## LDS arithmetic (per workgroup)

| Array | Shape | Floats | Bytes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| kv_tile | 32 keys x 129 stride (128 + 1 pad) | 4,128 | 16,512 |
| q_tile | 8 rows x 128 (head-dim bound) | 1,024 | 4,096 |
| s_tile | 8 rows x 32 keys | 256 | 1,024 |
| **Total** | | **5,408** | **21,632** |

`FLASH_STAGED_LDS_BYTES` = 21,632 in the code, pinned
against the shader's declared arrays by a unit test. The
pipeline builds only when the device grants at least
that much workgroup storage (the K13 for_device terms):
the backend requests the adapter's own limits, RADV
grants 64 KiB (65,536 B), so on the server card the set
fits with the CU residency bound at 3 workgroups per CU
by LDS (3 x 21,632 = 64,896 <= 65,536). Under wgpu's
default limits (16,384 B) the pipeline is absent and the
absence is logged by name at construction; the shipped
form's own tile is 1,024 B, so LDS never binds for it.

## The switch and the routing

- `WGPU_COMPUTE_FLASH_STAGED` (crate::compute): the
  exact value `1` (trimmed) enables; unset or any other
  value is off, fail-closed, resolved once at backend
  construction, in the K22 switch's pattern. The backend
  construction log prints both the switch and whether
  the staged pipeline exists, so a run that cannot
  engage names it instead of timing the shipped form
  under the staged name.
- Routing (session.rs, the one prepare_flash call site):
  staged form iff switch on AND rows > 1 AND the staged
  pipeline exists on this device. Otherwise the shipped
  call, unchanged. With the switch unset the dispatch
  stream is the shipped stream exactly.
- Diag: the staged form stamps `k6_attn_flash_staged`
  from birth (the shipped form stamps `k6_attn_flash`),
  so a timing run attributes every dispatch to its form.

## VM gates (executed 2026-11-06, this lane)

- `cargo test -p wgpu-compute`: 201 passed, 0 failed
  across 23 test binaries (the lib binary carries 110).
  The new unit tests were verified by name on this tree:
  the resolver semantics
  (`flash_staged_switch_resolution`), the LDS pin
  (`staged_lds_arithmetic_matches_the_shader`), and full
  Naga parse + validation of the staged shader
  (`staged_shader_validates_under_naga`). The generated
  WGSL was also dumped and read end to end by the author.
- The device correctness tests
  (`k6_flash_staged_matches_shipped_at_glimmer_shapes`
  in tests/fused_kernels.rs) skip on the VM, which
  enumerates no adapter, exactly like every device test
  in this crate; they are step 1 of the card protocol.
  Their shapes are the real model's: head dim 128, 32 Q
  heads over 2 KV heads, the 2,048 window with ring
  2,111 at deep positions, block edges at stored 31/32/33
  and rows 9, a 64-row global chunk over 1,024 stored,
  and decode rows.
- `cargo clippy -p wgpu-compute --all-targets -- -D
  warnings`: clean. `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
  `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`: clean.

## Lose-conditions (named in advance)

1. **Occupancy.** 21,632 B of LDS per workgroup caps
   residency at 3 workgroups per CU (768 threads, 37.5
   percent of the 2,048-thread ceiling), where the
   shipped form is thread-bound at 8. If the score
   phase's serial 128-deep dots cannot hide
   workgroup-memory latency at that occupancy, the
   staged form loses despite strictly fewer global
   reads. This is the primary risk and the A/B exists
   to measure it.
2. **Small stored counts.** Four barriers per block
   plus staging loads are pure overhead when the stored
   set fits in one or two blocks (early chunks, short
   prompts). Flash is 3.2 ms in chunk 0; there is
   nothing to win there and a little to lose.
3. **The verify band.** Multi-row forwards of 2..7 rows
   run one row block with 6..1 of 8 rows idle in the
   score and reduce phases (staging is shared, so the
   waste is compute, not traffic), and launch only
   32 workgroups (one block x 32 heads), far under the
   card's 96 CUs. Spec verify may prefer the shipped
   form; the identity+golden leg runs it, the timing
   there is read from the same runs' diag tables.
4. **f32 traffic is unchanged in size.** Staging moves
   the same f32 bytes llama moves at f16. The win on
   the table is coalescing, shared reuse across 8
   rows, and no per-row global re-read of V, not halved
   traffic. If the shipped form's V reads were already
   landing in L2 at these shapes, the measured win will
   be smaller than the traffic arithmetic suggests.
5. **Shared-memory throughput.** The score phase
   issues 256 threads x head_dim shared loads per
   block. Conflicts are designed out, but raw shared
   bandwidth may bind before the saved global bandwidth
   pays.

## Card protocol (parent runs this, serialized)

Stage from the post-merge main, manifest-verified,
under `flock -w 14400 /tmp/itak-phase.lock`, VRAM guard
(33,271,808 B) before every measured arm. The Cortex
backends are stopped for the session and restored
after, per the standing card rule.

- **Step 0, autopsy.** Compile the staged shader under
  RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats (bench/shader-autopsy.sh
  pattern): LDS must read 21,632 B, VGPR at or under
  128, zero spills, zero scratch. A spill-heavy or
  LDS-mismatched compile stops the protocol here; the
  numbers are the finding.
- **Step 1, correctness.**
  `cargo test -p wgpu-compute --release --test
  fused_kernels k6_flash_staged` on the card: every
  case must run (no skip line for the staged pipeline)
  and pass at 1e-6 against the shipped flash and, where
  sized, the two-pass form. Then the resident suite
  with the switch on: `WGPU_COMPUTE_FLASH_STAGED=1
  cargo test -p wgpu-compute --release --test
  resident_session`. Then identity + golden through
  the spec harness with the switch on (both mode,
  depths 1 and 6): IDENTITY + GOLDEN PASS.
- **Step 2, prefill A/B at 1,022 tokens.**
  `prefill_profile` on the real GGUF, diag timing on,
  two arms in one session: switch unset (control) and
  `WGPU_COMPUTE_FLASH_STAGED=1`. Compare the
  `k6_attn_flash` total against the
  `k6_attn_flash_staged` total and the walls. Recorded
  marks: flash 1,013.1 ms of 6,659 ms GPU time; the
  current shipped wall is 6,330 ms (2026-11-06 host-gap
  confirmation). The same-session control arm is the
  operative baseline; the recorded marks are context.
- **Step 3, long-context leg.** Same harness, same two
  arms, prompt built by repetition to at least 8,192
  tokens (the harness prints `prompt_tokens=`; the leg
  is valid only if that line reads >= 8192). No recorded
  baseline exists at this length; the comparison is
  same-session, flash total against flash total and
  wall against wall. This is the leg the design exists
  for: flash's share grows quadratically, so a staging
  win must show here if it is real.
- **Step 4, no-leak.** Switch unset, diag timing on,
  one plain run: the diag table shows `k6_attn_flash`
  rows and zero `k6_attn_flash_staged` rows, and the
  construction log reads `enabled=false`. With the
  switch ON, a plain glimmer_generate decode run must
  still land in the recorded 35.5-35.7 tok/s band
  (single-row calls never route staged by construction;
  this measurement is the proof of that construction).

## Decision rule (written in advance)

The default does not move in this lane. A proposal to
flip `WGPU_COMPUTE_FLASH_STAGED`'s default (or to make
the staged form unconditional for multi-row calls) is
earned only if ALL of these hold:

1. Step 0: LDS reads 21,632 B, VGPR <= 128, zero
   spills.
2. Step 1: every correctness leg passes, including
   identity + golden with the switch on.
3. Step 2: the staged flash total at 1,022 tokens
   beats the recorded 1,013.1 ms by at least 25
   percent (<= 760 ms), with the wall improved
   against the same-session control.
4. Step 3: the staged flash total at >= 8k tokens
   beats the same-session control's flash total.
5. Step 4: no-leak clean, and decode with the switch
   on stays in the recorded band.

If step 2 fails but step 3 passes decisively, the
honest follow-up is a stored-count gate (staged only
above a context threshold), proposed with its own
numbers, not taken here. If both fail, the flag stays
off, the numbers are the finding, and gap 5's remaining
half is the f16 KV step, which this lane deliberately
did not touch.

===== FILE: bench/gate-skip-visibility-2026-11-07.md =====
# Gate skip visibility: the Category J HIGH, and the spec-runner depth default (2026-11-07)

Lane `lane/gate-skip-visibility`, from main
34358e33f6b0fe8f0ef5977675ed10e04228501a. The wrapper, the
runner defaults, and the sweep wording are the first commit on
this lane; this note is the second. All runs executed on this
VM against this lane's tree; no server jobs. The VM enumerates
no Vulkan adapters at all (the wrapper's probe readout, below),
so every GPU test here takes its skip path by design; the card
is the only place the adapter-present branch runs for real, and
that branch is exercised here by the wrapper's documented
override instead.

Source of the work: the cold critic panel of 2026-11-07
(`CRITIC-ENGINE-MERGE.md`, Category J [HIGH] and the defaults
table's row 22 [NIT]).

## Item 1: the green gate hid the skips

The finding: roughly 120 of 758 Rust tests pass vacuously on
any adapterless machine, and the standard gate hides it. A
`--nocapture` run printed 119 "skipping" lines while every
suite reported ok, because the default gate discards a passing
test's stderr. There is no CI in the tree to run them on the
card (TODO T-1.7 would create one and is still open; this lane
does not build CI).

### The panel's observation, reproduced at this lane's base

Failing-before evidence, run on the untouched tree at base
34358e3 before any edit:

- The documented gate, `cargo test --workspace`, reports
  **781 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored** across 68 suites, and its
  captured output contains **zero** lines with "skipping". The
  green result shows no trace that anything skipped.
- The same suite under `--nocapture` prints **134 lines
  containing "skipping"**: 126 adapter-skip lines and 8 other
  lines (itemized below). The proof surface for every shipped
  GPU behavior was invisible in the gate that claims it.

### The skip-idiom survey

Every skip is announced by the tests themselves on stderr;
there are exactly two adapter-absence idioms and a small set
of configuration/capability prints. Surveyed file by file:

Adapter-absence idioms (the vacuity signal):

- **A. `skipping <name>: no suitable adapter (enumerated:
  [...])`** — printed when `WgpuCompute::new()` refuses with
  `NoSuitableAdapter`, by the per-file `backend_or_skip()`
  helpers in 24 wgpu-compute integration files (chunked_gemv,
  dflash_session, fused_kernels, k10_k11_gemm, k12_k14_mmq,
  k15_k16_mmq_wide, k18_small_batch, k19_mmv, k1_synthetic,
  k20_mmv, k21_finish, k21_mmv, k21f_head_routing, k22_mmq,
  k23_coopmat, k23_mmq, k24_coopmat, k2_k3_synthetic,
  k4_k8_kernels, k8_argmax, prefix_kv_session, proj_bench,
  resident_block, splitk_mmq), by inline variants in
  cross_backend, kv_f16, resident_session, and
  diag_timestamps, by unit tests inside wgpu-compute
  (src/compute.rs, the k21 finish registration test) and
  itak-spec (src/speculator.rs, the gpu arm test), and by
  itak-spec's ngram_gpu_runner integration test.
- **B. `skipping <name>: wgpu enumerates no adapters
  here`** — the shader-compile wording: shader_compile.rs
  (14 print sites) and one site in k4_k8_kernels.rs.

Named exceptions (printed skips that are NOT adapter absence;
they fire by configuration or by device capability, so zero
is not their expectation on any machine):

- k21f_head_routing's env-arm routing pins (3 lines at
  shipped defaults): each arm prints when the
  WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD / WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS position
  it needs is not the process position.
- Diag capture arms needing an opt-in environment:
  dflash_session's diag timing and diag capture tests
  (DIAG_OUT / WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG unset), resident_session's
  diag smoke (WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG_OUT unset) and diag
  self-drain (WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG not `timing`), and the
  "this process runs with diag on" off-mode checks.
- Device-capability gates, reachable only when an adapter IS
  present: the k23/k24 "stock device (no coopmat bridge)" and
  "device fails the kernel's gates" prints, "timing requested
  but the device granted ..." arms, and staged-flash /
  parity-leg device refusals. None of these can fire on an
  adapterless machine, because the adapter print fires first.

### Measured counts at base 34358e3 (adapterless VM)

From the `--nocapture` evidence run (781 passed, 0 failed,
1 ignored):

| Class | Lines |
| :--- | ---: |
| Adapter idiom A ("no suitable adapter") | 111 |
| Adapter idiom B ("wgpu enumerates no adapters here") | 15 |
| **Adapter skips, total** | **126** |
| Env-arm exceptions (k21f pins 3, diag arms 4) | 7 |
| Interleaving artifact (one merged line) | 1 |
| **All lines containing "skipping"** | **134** |

Counting rules, as the wrapper implements them: a line counts
as an adapter skip when it contains "skipping" and either
idiom's marker; any other line containing "skipping" counts
as an other skip. Raw marker counts in the same log are 112
lines containing "no suitable adapter" and 15 containing
"wgpu enumerates no adapters here"; the one-line difference
against the table is output interleaving: under `--nocapture`
parallel tests share stderr, and fragments merge. One merged
line in this log reads `skipping test
resident_block_logits_and_captures_match_cpu ... ok` (a skip
fragment fused with a libtest result line), and one adapter
line is fused with its test's `test ... ` prefix. Counts are
therefore exact to within a line or two, run to run: the
wrapper's own run below counted 127 adapter / 7 other against
this survey's 126 / 8, with raw idiom totals identical (112 +
15) in both logs. The gated rule (any adapter skip fails on
an adapter machine) and the beside-the-pass-count reporting
are both robust at that tolerance.

### The wrapper: bench/gate.sh

Per the panel's fix: a gate wrapper that counts skip lines
and fails when they exceed the adapterless expectation on a
machine with an adapter; the adapterless-expected skips
listed as T-1.7's explicit exception set; until CI exists,
gate reports state the skip count beside the pass count.

`bench/gate.sh` runs the first of the RUNBOOK's plain gate
commands — and only that one; clippy, fmt, cargo deny, and
the Go platform suite stay the plain commands beside it —
with two changes of lens:

1. It runs `cargo test --workspace -- --nocapture`, tee'd to
   the terminal and a log, and sums the per-suite
   `test result:` lines into passed / failed / ignored.
2. It counts adapter skips and other skips by the idioms
   above and prints one summary line with the skip counts
   beside the pass count, in both branches.

Adapter detection mirrors the tests' own skip signal. The
tests skip when `WgpuCompute::new()` refuses under
`DetectPolicy::default()` (crates/wgpu-compute/src/
detect.rs): enumerate Vulkan adapters through a wgpu
instance, and qualify only a discrete one (an integrated or
other adapter qualifies only under an explicit non-default
policy; a CPU-type adapter such as llvmpipe never qualifies,
per BACKEND.md Section 6). The wrapper probes with the
crate's own readout example, `adapter_features`, which
enumerates through the same wgpu Vulkan path and prints each
adapter's facts; the machine counts as adapter-present when
any printed adapter line carries `device_type=DiscreteGpu`,
exactly the default policy's qualifying class. A probe that
fails to run fails the gate: the wrapper will not guess its
premise.

Verdicts:

- Tests failed (cargo exit nonzero or any failed count):
  FAIL, either branch.
- Adapter present: any adapter skip FAILS the gate, with the
  first 10 offending lines printed; other skips are reported
  in the summary, not gated (the card sessions own the
  device-capability verdicts).
- Adapterless: PASS, with the summary naming the skips as
  adapterless-expected. If the adapter count drifts from
  EXPECTED_ADAPTER_SKIPS (126, the base measurement above),
  the wrapper prints a drift note naming the enumerated
  expectation and still passes; the script's header carries
  the full enumeration (suites and idioms composing the set)
  as T-1.7's exception list in starting form, and the note
  asks for it to be updated when drift is reviewed.

`GATE_ASSUME_ADAPTER=1|0` overrides the probe so the gate
logic can be exercised on either class of machine; a forced
decision is always named in the wrapper's output. House
style follows bench/failure-bundle.sh (set -u, quoted
expansions, exit 64 for usage). shellcheck is not installed
on this VM (verified 2026-11-07: `command -v shellcheck` is
empty), so like failure-bundle.sh the script carries that
fact in its header instead of a clean bill; `bash -n` runs
clean.

### Demonstration 1: adapterless (the probe path), this VM

The probe's full readout on this machine is one line —
`adapter_features: no Vulkan adapters enumerated` — so the
decision is ABSENT on enumeration alone, before the policy
question even arises. The wrapper's own lines, verbatim:

```text
gate: adapter decision: ABSENT, no qualifying discrete Vulkan adapter (adapter_features probe (/tmp/gate-probe.crkz2Q))
gate: running: cargo test --workspace -- --nocapture (full output: /tmp/gate-test.nC02WY)
gate: note: adapter skip count 127 differs from the enumerated expectation (126 at base 34358e3); when the drift is reviewed, update the enumeration in bench/gate.sh so T-1.7 inherits a current exception list
gate: passed 781, failed 0, ignored 1; skipped 127 adapter (adapterless-expected: no qualifying adapter on this machine), 7 other (named exceptions, not gated)
gate: full output: /tmp/gate-test.nC02WY
gate: PASS
```

Exit code 0. The 127/7 against the survey's 126/8 is the
interleaving tolerance described above (raw idiom totals
112 + 15 identical in both logs); the drift note firing on a
one-line interleave difference is the conservative direction
— it asks for a review, it does not hide one.

### Demonstration 2: forced adapter-present (GATE_ASSUME_ADAPTER=1)

The same tree, the same machine, the decision forced. The
wrapper's lines, verbatim (summary and verdict from stdout,
offender list from stderr, trimmed to the first lines):

```text
gate: adapter decision: PRESENT (GATE_ASSUME_ADAPTER=1 (forced; probe not run))
gate: running: cargo test --workspace -- --nocapture (full output: /tmp/gate-test.aYqwXG)
gate: passed 781, failed 0, ignored 1; skipped 127 adapter (adapter present: expectation 0), 7 other (named exceptions, not gated)
gate: adapter skips observed (first 10):
skipping gpu arm speculator test: no suitable adapter (enumerated: [])
skipping n-gram GPU runner construction test: no suitable adapter (enumerated: [])
skipping k21 finish registration test: no suitable adapter (enumerated: [])
skipping GPU test: no suitable adapter (enumerated: [])
... (6 more of the first 10, same idiom)
gate: FAIL: 127 adapter skips on a machine with a qualifying adapter
```

Exit code 1. The failure mode is real: a tree whose GPU
tests all skipped can no longer report a clean gate on a
machine that could have run them. The 7 other skips (the
named env-arm exceptions) are reported and do not gate.

## Item 2: the spec runners' depth default (defaults row 22)

The panel's NIT: both spec runners defaulted their depth
argument to 6, contradicting the library's measured default
of 1; anyone benchmarking from runner defaults measured the
slower operating point. The library's own record is
unambiguous: SpecConfig's depth default is 1, the winner of
this stack's T-9.7 sweep (bench/spec-sweep-gpu-fixed-2026-
11-04.md: depth 1, acceptance 0.615, 16.86 tok/s, picked by
SPEC 9.4's smallest-depth-within-2% rule); depth 6 is the
llama.cpp operating point.

Changes, additive only (no flag renames; explicit depth
arguments parse and behave exactly as before):

- `crates/itak-spec/examples/spec_generate.rs` and
  `spec_generate_gpu.rs`: the depth argument's absent and
  unparsable fallbacks now use a named `DEFAULT_DEPTH: usize
  = 1` in each file, documented as the T-9.7 winner and
  SpecConfig's default. The GPU runner's bar comment keeps
  its depth-6 reference deliberately: the 88.6 tok/s bar IS
  the recorded llama-server operating point at depth 6, a
  fact about the bar's provenance, not about this runner's
  default.
- `crates/itak-spec/src/sweep.rs`: the candidate-set doc no
  longer calls 6 "the standing default that sweep picked".
  It now states the set is the 2026-10-30 llama.cpp sweep's
  menu kept for cell-for-cell comparability, that this
  stack's own sweep (T-9.7) picked depth 1, which is
  SpecConfig's standing default, and that the 6 in the set
  is the measured llama.cpp operating point. The set itself
  is unchanged: [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16].

Pins: the depth default lives in the two examples' `main()`
functions and is not reachable from a library test (examples
are not importable), so it is pinned by the named constant
and its doc, and by the gates below (both examples build
under clippy --all-targets and cargo check). What IS
reachable is pinned in sweep.rs's
`default_config_is_valid_and_covers_the_operating_point`,

contains 1 ("the standing default is swept"), and keeps the

operating point is swept"). The neighboring rendering test's

6 is the correctly rendered winner of that fixture. It is
deliberately untouched, and named here so a future reader
does not mistake it for a third stale default. SpecConfig's
own default (depth 1) was already pinned before this lane
and is unchanged.

===== FILE: bench/gate.sh =====
#!/bin/bash
# Gate wrapper with skip visibility: run the workspace test
# suite (the first of the RUNBOOK's plain gate commands) with
# per-test output captured, count what passed, what failed,
# and what SKIPPED, and fail the gate when tests skip on a
# machine that could have run them.
#
# Why this exists: the cold critic panel's Category J finding
# (bench/critic report 2026-11-07, merged verdict DO NOT SHIP
# on other grounds). Roughly one Rust test in six in this
# workspace needs a GPU adapter and, on a machine without
# one, prints a "skipping" line and passes vacuously. The
# plain gate (`cargo test --workspace`) captures a passing
# test's stderr and discards it, so the green result shows
# no trace that anything skipped: at the panel freeze the
# suite reported 758 passed while 119 skip lines sat hidden,
# covering effectively every kernel-parity, resident-session,
# prefix-KV, DFlash, coopmat, and F16-KV test. The standing
# lesson is the K21F mask error earlier in this project's
# history: a one-character shader defect shipped through
# green gates and was caught only on the card, because the
# tests that would have caught it were silently not running
# on the machines that ran the gates. Until CI exists (TODO
# T-1.7, still open; this wrapper is NOT that CI), a gate
# report must state the skip count beside the pass count,
# and on a machine WITH an adapter any adapter skip is a
# failure, not a footnote.
#
# What counts as a skip: the tests announce their own skips
# on stderr (visible only under --nocapture, which is how
# this wrapper runs the suite). Two adapter-absence idioms
# exist in the tree, surveyed file by file 2026-11-07:
#
#   A. "skipping <name>: no suitable adapter (enumerated:
#      [...])" — printed by the per-file backend_or_skip()
#      helpers and their inline variants when
#      WgpuCompute::new() refuses with NoSuitableAdapter.
#   B. "skipping <name>: wgpu enumerates no adapters here"
#      — the shader-compile suites' wording for the same
#      absence.
#
# A line counts as an ADAPTER SKIP when it contains
# "skipping" and either idiom's marker ("no suitable
# adapter" or "wgpu enumerates no adapters here"). Any
# other line containing "skipping" counts as an OTHER SKIP:
# the named exceptions below. Under --nocapture, parallel
# tests' output interleaves and a line can be garbled or
# merged (one such merged line was observed in the base
# measurement), so counts are exact to within a line or
# two; the adapter-machine rule (any adapter skip fails)
# and the printed beside-the-pass-count numbers are both
# robust at that tolerance.
#
# The adapterless-expected set (T-1.7's exception list,
# starting form). On a machine with no qualifying adapter,
# the adapter skips below are EXPECTED; they compose from:
#
#   - wgpu-compute integration suites, via backend_or_skip()
#     helpers: chunked_gemv, dflash_session, fused_kernels,
#     k10_k11_gemm, k12_k14_mmq, k15_k16_mmq_wide,
#     k18_small_batch, k19_mmv, k1_synthetic, k20_mmv,
#     k21_finish, k21_mmv, k21f_head_routing, k22_mmq,
#     k23_coopmat, k23_mmq, k24_coopmat, k2_k3_synthetic,
#     k4_k8_kernels, k8_argmax, prefix_kv_session,
#     proj_bench, resident_block, splitk_mmq.
#   - wgpu-compute integration suites with inline variants
#     of the same print: cross_backend, kv_f16,
#     resident_session (including its diag smoke, self-drain,
#     and off-check adapter arms), diag_timestamps.
#   - idiom B: shader_compile (14 print sites) and
#     k4_k8_kernels' shader-compile test.
#   - unit tests inside the crates: wgpu-compute's k21
#     finish registration test (src/compute.rs), itak-spec's
#     gpu arm speculator test (src/speculator.rs).
#   - itak-spec's ngram_gpu_runner integration test.
#
# Measured at base 34358e3 (2026-11-07) on the adapterless
# build VM: 126 adapter-skip lines beside 781 passed,
# 0 failed, 1 ignored (full survey and evidence:
# bench/gate-skip-visibility-2026-11-07.md). When the count
# drifts from EXPECTED_ADAPTER_SKIPS below on an adapterless
# machine, the wrapper still passes but prints the drift;
# update the enumeration in this header and the constant
# when the drift is reviewed, so T-1.7 inherits a current
# list instead of a stale one.
#
# Named exceptions (OTHER SKIPS: printed and counted, never
# gated). These fire by configuration or by device
# capability, not by adapter absence, so zero is not their
# expectation on any machine:
#
#   - env-arm routing pins in k21f_head_routing: each arm
#     prints a skip when the WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD /
#     WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS position it needs is not
#     the process position (3 lines at shipped defaults).
#   - diag capture arms that need an opt-in environment:
#     dflash_session's diag timing and capture tests
#     (DIAG_OUT / WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG unset), resident_session's
#     diag smoke (WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG_OUT unset) and diag
#     self-drain (WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG not `timing`), and the
#     "this process runs with diag on" off-mode checks.
#   - device-capability gates, reachable only when an
#     adapter IS present: the k23/k24 "stock device (no
#     coopmat bridge)" and "device fails the kernel's
#     gates" prints, "timing requested but the device
#     granted ..." arms, and staged-flash / parity-leg
#     device refusals. On an adapter machine these are
#     reported in the other-skip count for a human to read;
#     the card sessions own their verdicts.
#
# Adapter detection: the wrapper must decide "could this
# machine have run them" with the SAME signal the tests
# use to skip. The tests skip when WgpuCompute::new()
# refuses: detect() (crates/wgpu-compute/src/detect.rs)
# enumerates Vulkan adapters through a wgpu instance and
# ranks them under DetectPolicy::default() — a discrete
# Vulkan adapter qualifies, an integrated or other adapter
# qualifies only under an explicit non-default policy, and
# a CPU-type adapter (llvmpipe) NEVER qualifies (BACKEND.md
# Section 6: a software adapter counts as no adapter). The
# wrapper probes with the crate's own readout example,
# adapter_features, which enumerates through the same wgpu
# Vulkan path and prints each adapter's facts; the machine
# counts as adapter-present when any printed adapter line
# carries device_type=DiscreteGpu, exactly the default
# policy's qualifying class. GATE_ASSUME_ADAPTER overrides
# the probe (see below) so the gate logic itself can be
# exercised on either class of machine.
#
# Usage:
#   bench/gate.sh
#
# Runs from the repo root (the script cd's there, like the
# other bench scripts). The suite's full combined output is
# tee'd to the terminal and to a log whose path is printed;
# the summary line names that log. The remaining RUNBOOK
# gates (clippy, fmt, cargo deny, the Go platform suite) are
# unchanged plain commands beside this wrapper; the wrapper
# wraps only the Rust test suite, which is where the skips
# live.
#
# Environment knobs:
#   GATE_ASSUME_ADAPTER  1: decide as if a qualifying
#                        adapter were present (the probe is
#                        not run). 0: decide as if none
#                        were. Unset: probe. Exists to test
#                        the gate logic; a forced decision
#                        is always named in the summary.
#
# Exit codes: 0 = gate passes; 1 = gate fails (tests
# failed, or adapter skips on an adapter machine, or the
# probe itself failed); 64 = usage error.
#
# shellcheck: NOT RUN. shellcheck is not installed on the
# build VM (checked 2026-11-07: `command -v shellcheck` is
# empty), so this script carries the repo bench style
# (set -u, everything quoted) without a shellcheck pass;
# `bash -n` was run clean. Run `shellcheck bench/gate.sh`
# on any host that has it before relying on a clean bill.

set -u

# Adapter-skip lines expected on an adapterless machine,
# measured at base 34358e3 (see the header enumeration).
EXPECTED_ADAPTER_SKIPS=126

usage() {
    echo "usage: bench/gate.sh" >&2
    exit 64
}

[ $# -eq 0 ] || usage

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 64

adapter_present=""
adapter_source=""
case "${GATE_ASSUME_ADAPTER:-}" in
    1)
        adapter_present=1
        adapter_source="GATE_ASSUME_ADAPTER=1 (forced; probe not run)"
        ;;
    0)
        adapter_present=0
        adapter_source="GATE_ASSUME_ADAPTER=0 (forced; probe not run)"
        ;;
    "")
        probe_log=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gate-probe.XXXXXX")
        if ! cargo run --quiet -p wgpu-compute --example adapter_features > "$probe_log" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "gate: FAIL: the adapter probe (cargo run -p wgpu-compute --example adapter_features) did not run; the gate cannot establish whether this machine could have run the GPU tests" >&2
            echo "gate: probe output: $probe_log" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        if grep -q 'device_type=DiscreteGpu' "$probe_log"; then
            adapter_present=1
        else
            adapter_present=0
        fi
        adapter_source="adapter_features probe ($probe_log)"
        ;;
    *)
        echo "gate: GATE_ASSUME_ADAPTER must be 0 or 1 when set (got: ${GATE_ASSUME_ADAPTER})" >&2
        usage
        ;;
esac

if [ "$adapter_present" -eq 1 ]; then
    echo "gate: adapter decision: PRESENT ($adapter_source)"
else
    echo "gate: adapter decision: ABSENT, no qualifying discrete Vulkan adapter ($adapter_source)"
fi

log=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gate-test.XXXXXX")
echo "gate: running: cargo test --workspace -- --nocapture (full output: $log)"
cargo test --workspace -- --nocapture 2>&1 | tee "$log"
test_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

counts=$(grep -E '^test result:' "$log" | awk '{for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) {if ($i == "passed;") p += $(i - 1); if ($i == "failed;") f += $(i - 1); if ($i == "ignored;") g += $(i - 1)}} END {print p + 0, f + 0, g + 0}')
passed=${counts%% *}
rest=${counts#* }
failed=${rest%% *}
ignored=${rest##* }

adapter_skips=$(grep 'skipping' "$log" | grep -c 'no suitable adapter\|wgpu enumerates no adapters here' || true)
total_skips=$(grep -c 'skipping' "$log" || true)
other_skips=$((total_skips - adapter_skips))

verdict="PASS"
fail_reason=""
if [ "$test_rc" -ne 0 ] || [ "$failed" -ne 0 ]; then
    verdict="FAIL"
    fail_reason="cargo test exited $test_rc with $failed failed"
fi

if [ "$adapter_present" -eq 1 ]; then
    summary="gate: passed $passed, failed $failed, ignored $ignored; skipped $adapter_skips adapter (adapter present: expectation 0), $other_skips other (named exceptions, not gated)"
    if [ "$adapter_skips" -ne 0 ]; then
        verdict="FAIL"
        if [ -n "$fail_reason" ]; then
            fail_reason="$fail_reason; "
        fi
        fail_reason="${fail_reason}$adapter_skips adapter skips on a machine with a qualifying adapter"
        echo "gate: adapter skips observed (first 10):" >&2
        grep 'skipping' "$log" | grep 'no suitable adapter\|wgpu enumerates no adapters here' | head -10 >&2
    fi
else
    summary="gate: passed $passed, failed $failed, ignored $ignored; skipped $adapter_skips adapter (adapterless-expected: no qualifying adapter on this machine), $other_skips other (named exceptions, not gated)"
    if [ "$adapter_skips" -ne "$EXPECTED_ADAPTER_SKIPS" ]; then
        echo "gate: note: adapter skip count $adapter_skips differs from the enumerated expectation ($EXPECTED_ADAPTER_SKIPS at base 34358e3); when the drift is reviewed, update the enumeration in bench/gate.sh so T-1.7 inherits a current exception list"
    fi
fi

echo "$summary"
echo "gate: full output: $log"
if [ "$verdict" = "FAIL" ]; then
    echo "gate: FAIL: $fail_reason" >&2
    exit 1
fi
echo "gate: PASS"
exit 0

===== END FILE: bench/gate.sh =====

===== FILE: bench/gated-swiglu-routing-2026-11-06.md =====
# Gated and SwiGLU routing: the last two unrouted projections join the ladder (2026-11-06)

The spec-round cost map
(`bench/spec-round-economics-2026-11-06.md`, finding F1)
left one verify cost unrouted: at depth 6, 52.5 ms of
GPU per round is the gated output projection and the
SwiGLU-fused down projection running their fused GEMV
forms (the unrouted `k1_q4k_gemv` row at 26.60 ms and
the unrouted `k2_q6k_gemv` row at 25.88 ms of that
note's verify table). They were unrouted for a
structural reason, not an oversight: `prepare_gated_proj`
and `prepare_swiglu_proj` in
`crates/wgpu-compute/src/session.rs` never pass through
`prepare_proj`, so the band-routed MMV ladder
(`bench/mmv-band-routing-2026-11-06.md`), the K18
small-batch rung, and the chunked GEMV rung never see
them. This lane closes that gap. The DFlash session's
own prepares are a different lane's territory and are
untouched.

## The routing change, per function

Both functions keep their existing matrix-range forms
exactly (batch at or past `GEMM_MIN_ROWS` = 16: the
fused MMQ forms, the fused GEMM forms behind them).
Below that range, each gains a routed branch in front
of its fused GEMV fallback:

- `prepare_gated_proj` (Q4_K only, as before; its
  signature now takes the weights as `&ProjWeights` and
  destructures, because the routed branch needs the
  enum form for `prepare_proj`): when the caller
  supplies a materialization buffer and
  `routed_product` returns a product, the result is
  `ProjCall::ActProj { act, proj }`: K7's strided gate
  (`prepare_gate_strided`) materializes
  `attn * sigmoid(gate)` into the session's existing
  `scratch.attn_gated` rows, and `proj` is a plain
  `prepare_proj` over those rows.
- `prepare_swiglu_proj` (Q4_K and Q6_K arms; the Q5_K
  refusal is unchanged): the same shape, with K7's
  strided SwiGLU (`prepare_swiglu_strided`)
  materializing `silu(gate) * up` from the pair buffer
  into the existing `scratch.ffn_act` rows, then a
  plain `prepare_proj` for the down product.

`routed_product` is the shared gate, and it is
deliberately narrow. It returns a product only when
**all** of these hold: batch in `2..GEMM_MIN_ROWS`;
`routed_rung_admits` says a rung below the matrix
forms serves this (family, shape, batch), meaning the
band-routed MMV cell admits it (`mmv_applies`), or the
K18 band admits it and the device built that family's
K18 pipeline, or the chunked band admits it
(`chunked_gemv_applies`); and `prepare_proj` itself
succeeds. Any failure (out of range, no rung, a ladder
refusal, logged by name) returns `None` and the fused
form serves the projection, exactly as it did before
this lane. Batch 1 is never routed: every rung starts
at 2 rows, and there the fused form is the ladder's
own answer (the plain GEMV product) with the
activation folded in, in one dispatch instead of two.

The gating is the existing config only:
`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS` plus the band cells (and,
behind the same composition, the K18 and chunked
ceilings). No new env names. At shipped defaults every
rung is closed, `routed_rung_admits` is false at every
batch, and the plans are byte-identical to the
pre-routing code: same dispatches, same kernels, same
order. The two call sites that already materialized
into `attn_gated` / `ffn_act` for the trait composition
prove the scratch buffers' sizing; the routed branches
reuse those same buffers, which no other dispatch in a
fused layer's plan reads.

One accounting note: a routed projection records
`1 + proj.dispatches()` dispatches (the K7 plus the
product's own count). The layer dispatch accounting
(`layer_dispatch_count`) already adds each
projection's extras over one back into the layer
total, and the fusion shape still subtracts the K7
the fusion removed, so a routed layer's count is
exact by construction: fused count, plus the product
rung's extras (a chunked product at batch 7 records
its three window dispatches, and so on).

## The K7 strided form

Routing needs the activation as data, and the fused
forms read it through a geometry K7's flat kernels
cannot express: the gate rides inside the QKV batch
buffer at a row stride and an offset (`K1ActGeom`:
`a_stride_elems`, `b_stride_elems`, `b_off_elems`),
and the FFN pair rides one buffer at twice the width
with the up half offset by the width. K7 therefore
gains two entry points in its existing shader module,
`gate_strided_main` and `swiglu_strided_main`:
`out[r][c] = a[r * a_stride + c] * sigmoid(b[r *
b_stride + b_off + c])` and the silu twin, writing
packed rows. The params struct grows the four stride
fields for every entry; the flat prepares fill them
with the flat-consistent values (width = strides = n,
offset 0), under which the strided map reduces to the
flat map exactly (pinned by a host test). The strided
prepares stamp the existing diag name
`k7_swiglu_gate`, with the geometry in the stamp's
shape field.

## The math-equivalence argument

The decomposition is not a new approximation; it is
the composition the codebase already trusts, reassembled:

1. **The activation values are identical.** The fused
   kernels were built to reproduce K7's math: K1's
   module docs state the gated form applies "K7's
   exact sigmoid over the same gate values" and the
   SwiGLU form is "K7's exact silu" in its quotient
   form. The routed path runs K7 itself (the strided
   entry applies the same branch-stable sigmoid and
   the same `x / (1 + exp(-x))` quotient, term for
   term; the strided index map is pinned against the
   `K1ActGeom` contract by host tests). So the product
   behind the routed form consumes exactly the f32
   activation rows the fused form computes internally.
2. **The elementwise math after the product does not
   exist.** Neither site applies anything after its
   product: the gate and the SwiGLU activation are the
   product's *input* transform, and both are fully
   carried by step 1. There is no finish to keep
   identical because neither fused form has one (the
   finish-carrying site in this model is the head,
   which is not one of these two functions).
3. **The product is the ladder's product.** What
   changes is only which kernel multiplies: the same
   choice `prepare_proj` already makes for every plain
   projection of the same family and shape, under the
   same correctness discipline the sweep verified
   (`agree=1` in all 99 cells of both arms,
   bench/mmv-band-routing-2026-11-06.md). The MMV and
   chunked and GEMV rungs consume the f32 rows
   directly; the K18 rung quantizes them with the
   plain K12 quantize, the same Q8_1 step the plain
   projections already answer for under the crate's
   quantization tolerance. A routed site's output is
   therefore exactly a trait-composition output (K7
   activation, plain product): the resident forward
   already produces bit-comparable results through
   that composition on every non-fusing layer and
   family today.
4. **Batch at or past 16 is untouched**, so the
   fused MMQ/GEMM activation quantize (K12's gated /
   SwiGLU forms) and its numerics are exactly as
   shipped.

What is NOT claimed: bit-identity with the fused
GEMV form in general. The fused GEMV and the MMV /
chunked / K18 products sum in different orders (and
K18 quantizes), so a routed site's output differs
from the fused form's by the same reassociation /
quantization deltas the ladder already introduces
for plain projections. Identity and golden on the
card are the arbiters, as they were for every
routing change before this one; the server protocol
below runs them in both arms.

## Which band cells these shapes land in

Shape classification is `mmv_shape_of`, unchanged:
out <= in/8 is kv, out >= 2*in is ffn, else attn.

| site | weights | in | out | class | cell | verify rows (2..=7) admitted |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gated O | Q4_K | 4,096 | 6,656 | attn | Q4_K attn `6-12` | **6, 7 only** |
| FFN down | Q6_K | 19,968 | 6,656 | attn | Q6_K attn `2-12` | **2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 (all)** |

The down projection's family is Q6_K in the real
file (bench/dflash-e3-2026-10-30.md records
`ffn_down` Q6_K [19968, 6656]; the loader uploads
per-tensor, so a Q4_K down tensor would take the
Q4_K arm and its cell `6-12` instead: rows 6, 7 only.
The code routes by the family it is handed, per
layer.)

The caps, stated plainly:

- **The gated projection's cell excludes most of the
  verify band.** Rows 2-5 (depths 1-4) stay on the
  fused GEMV form even with the MMV ceiling wide
  open; only rows 6 and 7 (depths 5 and 6) route.
  This is the measured table's answer, not an
  oversight: Q4_K attention-class cells at rows 2-4
  were measured losses (ratios 1.33 / 1.20 / 1.14 at
  the swept geometry), and routing them would rebuild
  the cliff inside the verify.
- **Both geometries are unmeasured in-widths.** The
  sweep measured in = 6,656 shapes only. The gated
  projection (in 4,096) and the down projection
  (in 19,968) inherit the attn cell by
  classification, the same disclosure standard as
  the band-routing note's treatment of the Q, O, and
  down geometries there. If a future sweep measures
  these widths and disagrees, the cells are env
  config and this table is the thing to correct.
- The K18 and chunked rungs, if the session ever
  enables them, admit by their own ceilings
  (2..=ceiling), not by these cells; at their shipped
  defaults they admit nothing.

## Honest expected recovery against the 52.5 ms

At depth 6 (7 rows, the economics note's measured
round), both sites route: the gated site at the
Q4_K attn cell's row-7 proxy ratio 0.889 and the
down site at the Q6_K attn row-7 proxy ratio 0.762
(both measured at in = 6,656; see the in-width
disclosure above). Applied to that note's per-site
rows:

- gated: 26.60 ms x (1 - 0.889) ≈ **3.0 ms** saved
- down: 25.88 ms x (1 - 0.762) ≈ **6.2 ms** saved
- gross ≈ **9.2 ms of the 52.5 ms (about 17%)**,
  before the materialization cost: two extra K7
  dispatches per layer (104 per verify forward),
  each moving at most 7 x 19,968 f32 of activation
  traffic; the economics note's own chain-kernel rows
  put elementwise dispatches in the ~6 µs class, so
  the honest charge is ≈ 0.5-1 ms, for a **net
  expectation of roughly 8-9 ms per depth-6 round**
  (verify GPU 102.0 ms toward ~93 ms; the 166.0 ms
  round toward ~157 ms). This is an estimate from
  proxy ratios, not a measurement; the A/B below is
  the verdict.

At depth 1 (2 rows) the gated site does not route
(cell starts at 6) and the down site does (Q6_K
attn row-2 proxy ratio 0.690). The economics note

## Correction (2026-11-07): the small-rows dispatch prediction

Appended by the hygiene-bundle lane, 2026-11-07. The
sections above are the lane's record as written and are
not edited; this section corrects one prediction in the
server protocol, on the baseline session's measurement
(bench/baseline-session-2026-11-06.md, leg (f)).

**What was predicted.** Depth 1: only the down site
routes, so +52 dispatches per verify forward, 52
`swiglu_strided` records, zero `gate_strided`. Depth 6:
both sites route on all 52 layers, +104 per verify
forward (52 gate + 52 swiglu).

**What was measured.** Depth 6, rows-7 verify forwards:
exactly 52 gate_strided + 52 swiglu_strided per
forward, +104 total. That half of the prediction was
exact. Depth 1 (rows 2 every round): gate_strided
exactly 0, but swiglu_strided counts **26.0 per
forward** against the predicted 52, and the net
dispatch delta is +26 (472 vs 446), not +52. The same
half-count appears in the depth-6 rows-3 and rows-5
forwards (26.0 swiglu_strided each), and the
decomposition's one plain-phase firing, a prefill
chunk at rows 6, added the full +104.

**The corrected rule, from the session code.** The
decomposition fires per layer, and the layer's own
down-tensor family decides admission:
`prepare_swiglu_proj` (crates/wgpu-compute/src/
session.rs) matches on the down weights' family; its
Q4_K arm consults the routed ladder for
`MmvFamily::Q4K` and its Q6_K arm for
`MmvFamily::Q6K`. The down shape (in 19,968, out
6,656) classifies as attn under `mmv_shape_of`, so
the Q6_K arm admits batches 2..=12 and the Q4_K arm
admits batches 6..=12, per the shipped band table.
This note's own cell-table caveat stated the rule
correctly ("a Q4_K down tensor would take the Q4_K
arm and its cell 6-12 instead: rows 6, 7 only. The
code routes by the family it is handed, per layer.");
the protocol prediction then applied the Q6_K row to
all 52 layers anyway.

**Why the prediction went wrong.** The cell table's
census line took the down family from
bench/dflash-e3-2026-10-30.md, which is the DFlash
draft file's census (5 layers, `ffn_down` Q6_K on
every one). The target file's down tensors are mixed:
**26 layers carry Q6_K down and 26 carry Q4_K
down.** The split is pinned arithmetically by the
defaults-confirmation session's prefill summaries
(bench/results/defaults-confirmation-20261107/
leg2-default.csv and leg2-off.csv; identical counts
in both arms): 16 chunk forwards at 64 rows carry
2,912 `k13_q4k_mmq` dispatches, 182 per chunk, which
is the 3-per-layer Q4_K base (attention batch, gated
output, FFN gate+up pair: 156) plus exactly 26 Q4_K
down products; and 832 `k14_q6k_mmq`, 52 per chunk,
which is 26 Q6_K down products plus the 26 Q6_K V
products of the partial-batch layers (the same half
of the file whose V is Q6_K; see the plan builder's
comment in session.rs).

**Corrected per-forward arithmetic** (verify forwards,
batch = depth + 1, one K7 materialization added per
firing layer, the product staying one dispatch):

| batch | gate_strided | swiglu_strided | net delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2..=5 | 0 | 26 (Q6_K-down layers only) | +26 |
| 6..=7 | 52 | 52 | +104 |

So: depth 1 adds +26 per verify forward, not +52;
depth-6 full rounds (batch 7) add +104, as predicted;
depth-6 tail rounds (batch 3 and 5) add +26. The
rows-6 prefill chunk's +104 is the same rule at
batch 6, not a separate case. No timing claim in
this note changes: the depth-6 recovery estimate was
computed at rows 7, where the prediction was exact,
and no millisecond figure was promised at depth 1.
Correctness was never in question: identity, golden,
acceptance, and streams passed in both arms of the
baseline session's A/B.

===== FILE: bench/gguf-mmap-2026-11-05.md =====
# GGUF file image is memory-mapped, 2026-11-05

PLAN T-2.1, landed on `lane/gguf-mmap`. `GgufFile::open` no longer
reads the whole GGUF into anonymous RAM. This is reduction #2 of
the phase B footprint audit (bench/phase-b-footprint-2026-11-05.md):
the audit's rows 1 and 3, the target and draft file images held via
`std::fs::read`, were 17.11 GiB of the 32.70 GiB kill-window
residency that got the speculative harness OOM-killed nine times.

## The change

- `crates/gguf/src/file.rs`: the `GgufFile.bytes: Vec<u8>` field is
  now a private `ImageBacking` enum, `Owned(Vec<u8>)` or
  `Mapped(memmap2::Mmap)`, with one `as_slice()` accessor. `open`
  and `from_bytes` split into constructors over a shared private
  `parse(backing)`; the parse itself (header walk, metadata,
  tensor directory, bounds checks) is byte-for-byte the code that
  ran before, reading through the slice either backing serves.
- `open` maps the file read-only. One special case: a zero-length
  file cannot be mapped (memmap2 refuses it), so `open` parses an
  empty owned image instead, which produces exactly the named
  failure the in-memory path has always produced for an empty file
  (`Truncated` reading the magic) rather than an Io mapping error.
- `crates/gguf/src/lib.rs`: `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` becomes
  `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`. The map call is the crate's only unsafe,
  isolated in `file::map_file` under an item-level
  `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` with the full safety contract written on
  it: the file must not be truncated or rewritten while a
  `GgufFile` opened from it is alive (reads past a truncated end
  fault with SIGBUS instead of failing named; that is inherent to
  mmap and is the same assumption llama.cpp's reader makes). Model
  files are immutable during a run and replaced by rename between
  runs; `deny` still makes any second unsafe block in the crate a
  lint error.
- Dependency: `memmap2 = "0.9"` (resolved 0.9.12), added to the
  gguf crate only. It was not in this workspace's lockfile before;
  it is the standard mapping crate, it was already present in this
  machine's cargo registry cache, and there is no std API for file
  mapping. The lockfile gained exactly one package (memmap2); its
  platform dependencies (libc, windows-sys) were already in the
  lock via other workspace crates. The gguf crate previously had
  zero dependencies; the parser, metadata, and dequantizers remain
  std-only.

## API compatibility

- The public API did not change: `open`, `from_bytes`, `file_len`,
  `tensor_bytes`, `load_f32`, `metadata`, and the rest keep their
  signatures and semantics. All 70 `GgufFile::open` / `from_bytes`
  call sites across the workspace compiled and passed unchanged;
  no consumer was edited.
- Alignment is not part of the contract and never was: consumers
  receive `&[u8]` and read it byte-wise (a workspace-wide search
  finds no bytemuck, `align_to`, or typed cast over tensor bytes;
  a `Vec<u8>` only ever guaranteed alignment 1 anyway). GGUF
  tensor data offsets keep the file's own alignment (32 by
  default) from the mapping base, as they did from the Vec.
- No consumer needed a new owned copy because of this change. The
  one pre-existing copy, the loader adapter's per-tensor
  `Arc::from` (audit row 2, 15.59 GiB), is untouched: it is
  reduction #3's seam (zero-copy tensor views), a separate task.
  With only this fix, that copy becomes the whole remaining anon
  footprint, which is the point: either reduction alone suffices.

## Failure behavior (pinned by crates/gguf/tests/open.rs)

Five new tests run the same fixture through both paths and compare
observables, including the Display text of errors:

- missing file: `Io` with `ErrorKind::NotFound`, as `fs::read`
  produced before.
- empty file: `Truncated { context: "magic" }`, Display-identical
  to `from_bytes` (this pins the zero-length fallback above).
- bad magic: `BadMagic`, Display-identical to `from_bytes`.
- truncated file at two cut points (mid-directory and mid-data):
  the error text is identical between `open` and `from_bytes` at
  both cuts.
- full parity: version, file_len, data_start, alignment, metadata,
  tensor names and order, per-tensor raw bytes, and `load_f32`
  values all equal; a missing tensor still names `MissingTensor`.

Not tested: a file shrinking after it is mapped. That cannot be
tested without racing the mapping (the read faults at the OS
level, it does not return an error), so it is covered by the
written contract on `open` and `map_file` instead, per the task's
terms.

## RSS evidence (this VM)

`crates/gguf/examples/mmap_rss.rs` writes a synthetic GGUF with one
F32 tensor of the given size, then reports /proc/self/status at
each phase. A hard in-test RSS assertion would be flaky (parallel
tests share a process), so the evidence is this example plus the
recorded runs, per the task's allowance. Commands:

```
cargo run -p gguf --release --example mmap_rss -- 512  <dir>
cargo run -p gguf --release --example mmap_rss -- 1024 <dir>
```

(`<dir>` must be a volume that can hold the file; this VM's /tmp
is a 512 MB tmpfs, so the runs used the workspace volume.)

512 MiB tensor:

| phase | VmRSS | RssAnon | RssFile |
|---|---|---|---|
| start | 2.2 MiB | 0.1 MiB | 2.0 MiB |
| mapped open | 2.3 MiB | 0.1 MiB | 2.1 MiB |
| mapped touch 3 pages | 2.3 MiB | 0.1 MiB | 2.2 MiB |
| mapped touch every page | 487.7 MiB | 0.1 MiB | 487.6 MiB |
| mapped dropped | 2.2 MiB | 0.1 MiB | 2.1 MiB |
| owned read + from_bytes | 514.2 MiB | 512.1 MiB | 2.1 MiB |

1024 MiB tensor: same shape. Mapped anon stays 0.1 MiB at every
phase; the every-page touch reaches VmRSS 1014.0 MiB, all of it
RssFile (1013.8 MiB); the owned path reads RssAnon 1024.1 MiB.

Reading: opening and fully reading a mapped 1 GiB model costs
0.1 MiB of anonymous RSS at both sizes, flat; the owned path costs
exactly the file size in anonymous RSS. Mapped pages count in
VmRSS as file RSS: present while touched, evictable under
pressure, and absent from the anon-rss figure the OOM killer
acts on (the kills were recorded in anon-rss).

## Expected phase B peak after this fix

Audit arithmetic, unchanged rows: row 2 (the extracted `Weights`
copy, 15.59 GiB) plus the bounded residue (about 0.4 GiB) is all
that remains in the anonymous tally at the kill window: about
16 GiB, against the observed 32-38 GB-free nights that killed the
old code at 35.5 GB. Phase B should now complete at a normal RAM
moment on the loaded server, without waiting for a 40 GB window.

# GPU proof + DFlash depth sweep, 2026-10-30 (TODO T-9.5/T-9.7 window)

## GPU proof: correctness

Prompt "The capital of France is", tokenizer ids printed by the
runner before any weight work:

```text
prompt_ids=[200000, 954, 7963, 323, 11698, 373]
coverage: expected=731 found=731 missing=0
generated_ids=[13796, 26, 1573, 373, 290, 2167, 26899, 1212]
generated_text=" Paris. It is the most populous"
```

All 8 generated ids match the verified reference
[13796, 26, 1573, 373, 290, 2167, 26899, 1212] exactly. First-token
probability on the GPU: 0.403462 (CPU-verified stack: 0.4035;
llama.cpp reference: 0.3962). The 64-token continuation on the same
prompt is coherent text (" Paris. It is the most populous city in
France and the most populous city proper in the European Union. The
Paris Region had a population of 12,405,426 in January 2023, ..."),
so the GPU forward is not merely argmax-lucky on one prompt shape.

## GPU proof: performance (first composed forward, honestly read)

| Phase | Measured |
| --- | --- |
| File open + parse | 4.9 s |
| Host weight load (itak-loader) | 4.6 s |
| Backend open (device + pipelines) | 0.02 s |
| First forward = prefill of 6 tokens, incl. one-time upload of the full 15.6 GiB weight set to the card | 3.15 s (8-token run), 3.27 s (64-token run) |
| Wall clock, process start to first token | ~12.7 s |
| Decode, 64-token run, steps 3..64 (n=62) | mean 505.8 ms/token, median 495 ms, min 475, max 621 → **1.98 tok/s** |
| Peak VRAM during the 64-token run | 17,332,375,552 bytes (16.1 GiB) over the 0.11 GB idle baseline: the full weight set resident plus KV and scratch |
| Peak host RSS | 33,093,324 KB (~31.6 GiB); the host keeps its own copy of the weights |

Against the llama.cpp Vulkan baselines on this card (998.43 tok/s
prefill, 44.31 tok/s decode solo), the composed GPU forward is at
1.98 tok/s decode, roughly 22x slower, and its 6-token prefill is
dominated by the one-time residency upload, so no prefill rate is
quoted against the 998 anchor.

The gap is composition, not kernels, and the mechanism is visible in
the crate contracts. The K1/K2/K3 GEMV kernels bench at 816.5 /
831.9 / 813.2 GB/s in isolation (BACKEND.md), at or above llama.cpp's
708 GB/s effective stream. But the `Compute` trait as wired returns
host `Vec<f32>` values: every projection's output round-trips to the
host, and the attention step reads the rotated K back once per layer
per token so the host mirror holds what the GPU computed. A decode
token is ~700 blocking submissions and readbacks; the measured
475-621 ms band is that latency, flat with position, which is why the
rate does not degrade as the context grows. The fix direction is
already named in the tree: device-resident activations end to end
(the K4 crate carries a fused `norm_residual` entry point kept "for
the future device-resident forward"), with host readback only for the
final logits. Until that lands, the GPU backend is a correctness
oracle at serving-incompatible speed, exactly what this proof was
scoped to establish.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| plain | 41.64 | 1.00x | n/a | n/a |
| 1 | 61.36 | 1.47x | 1057/1232 = 0.858 | 0.85 |
| 2 | 83.05 | 1.99x | 1391/1795 = 0.775 | 1.52 |

Per-prompt medians worth noting: MATH peaks at depth 6 (107.5) a

**Operating point: depth 6.** SPEC 9.4's rule (smallest depth within
2% of the best median): the best median is depth 6 at 107.39, the 2%
band floor is 105.24, and depth 4 at 103.01 sits 4.1% under the best,
outside the band, so 6 is the pick on this harness. It is a soft win:
depth 4 is within noise of 6 on two of three prompts and remains the
recorded production profile; the honest statement is that the curve
is flat between 4 and 6 and falls off a cliff at 8.

**Depths 8 and up are dead weight on this stack.** Accepted tokens
per request saturate from depth 6 onward (1,749 → 1,755 → 1,781 →
1,866 across depths 6/8/12/16) while proposed tokens grow linearly,
so each round verifies 8-16 positions to bank ~3.2-4.3 tokens, and
wall time at depth 8 drops below the plain non-speculative rate.
The draft's useful horizon on these prompts is about 3 accepted
tokens per round; the pasted article's depth-16 claim (75 to 110+
tok/s, REFERENCES.md) is not reproduced: depth 16 measured 49.97
median, and even the best depth (6) only just reaches the article's
band at 107.39.

**Anchor finding (a finding, not a rounding error, per RUNBOOK).**
The harness did not reproduce the recorded anchors within a few
percent: plain measured 41.64 against the recorded 44.31 (-6.0%),
and depth 4 measured 103.01 against the recorded 88.6 (+16.3%), so
the recorded 2.00x ratio becomes 2.47x here. The recorded numbers
came from different harness shapes (llama-bench tg128 after a
512-token prefill for the 44.31; the 2026-10-28 model-suite run for
the 88.6), while this sweep reads llama-server /completion eval
rates on short raw prompts with fixed 256-token generations. The
sweep is internally consistent (one binary, one prompt set, one
discipline for every cell), so the operating point stands; but the
recorded anchors are harness-relative, and any future comparison of
our stack against "44.31 / 88.6" must either re-run this harness or
re-baseline. A DECISIONS.md entry records this in the same pass, per
SPEC 9.4. Acceptance is reported as cell totals because llama-server
timings expose no per-position breakdown; per-position acceptance
(SPEC 9.3) remains measurable only on our own stack's diag events.

## Final server state (window close)

- Production Glimmer llama-server (pid 683675): stopped at window
  open and **left down on David's instruction**. Port 8080 answers
  nothing. Restart truth is the verbatim command line in the
  production-stop section above.
- Temporary sweep server on 18923: terminated by the sweep driver
  after the last cell; port confirmed down.
- VRAM: back to the 111,964,160-byte idle baseline. No stray
  llama-server processes; the two Qwen3-Embedding servers on 8091
  were never touched.
- Nothing else on the host was started, stopped, or reconfigured.

  crates/itak-loader/examples/glimmer_generate.rs, the wgpu-compute
