# GPU resident forward: the device-resident session, measured (2026-10-30)

Follow-up to bench/gpu-proof-2026-10-30.md. That proof matched the
reference 8/8 tokens on the GPU trait path but decoded at 1.98 tok/s
against llama.cpp's 44.31: the kernels bench at llama.cpp bandwidth
in isolation (813 to 832 GB/s), so the composition (host Vec<f32>
per step, rotated K read back per layer per token, roughly a
thousand blocking submissions per token) was the cost. This note
records the fix and its measurements.

## Window

2026-10-30, roughly 07:25 to 08:05 ET, on ubuntu-server's RX 7900
XTX (card2). Production Glimmer stayed DOWN the whole window on
David's instruction (it stays down until this work is done). The
only other tenants were the two Qwen3-Embedding llama-servers
(pids 1315625, 1466491), never touched. VRAM baseline before the
runs: 111,964,160 bytes. Tree: local workspace copied to
~/resident-run on the server, release profile.

## What was built

`ResidentSession` in crates/wgpu-compute/src/session.rs, beside
the trait path (which stays as the executable reference):

- Weights upload once at session build (K1/K2/K3 weight handles,
  norm vectors dequantized to f32 buffers, embedding table in its
  file dtype). Session build for the real file: 3.1 to 7.0 s
  depending on page-cache warmth.
- The session owns the activation scratch (two ping-pong stream
  buffers), per-layer KV in `DeviceKv` (the storage half factored
  out of the trait path's `GpuKvState`), and the logits buffer.
- A forward chunk is ONE submission: embedding gather (K8
  multi-row variant, token ids read from a device buffer), the
  weightless embedding norm, then per layer the exact
  `GlimmerModel::forward_rows` step order (K4 norms with the
  fused post-norm-plus-residual entry closing each half-layer,
  K1/K2/K3 projections, K5 RoPE and append on sliding layers
  only, K6 attention, K7 gate and SwiGLU), the last-row copy,
  final norm, head, K8 finishing (scale then softcap), and the
  logits copy into the readback staging, all in the same
  command buffer. The dispatches compose into ONE compute pass
  per segment (chain, then head), not one pass per dispatch:
  the per-pass composition measured about 46 ms/token, the
  single-pass composition about 34 (see below). Argmax stays
  on the host: the session returns the finished logits, one
  readback per chunk, and nothing else crosses the bus.
- Submissions per token after the change: **1** (plus a KV
  growth copy submission on the rare chunks where a global
  layer's buffer doubles; 1 such aux submission across the
  whole 64-token run). Dispatches per token: 1,071, now inside
  the single submission. Readbacks per token: 1 (808 KB of
  logits).

## A correctness find: the chunked sliding-window ring

The first cross-path run at a 70-token prompt produced NaN
logits in BOTH GPU paths (the trait path included: it had only
ever been driven at 9 rows or fewer). Root cause: appending a
whole chunk before attending it evicts, from a window-sized
ring, keys that earlier queries in the same chunk still attend
to; a fully-masked query row then reduces to 0/0 in K6. The
fix is structural and lives in the shared K6 layer:

- The windowed ring capacity is now `window + MAX_CHUNK_ROWS - 1`
  for the resident session (the trait state keeps ring == window;
  its step-at-a-time driving never spans a chunk). With the
  headroom, every position any query in a chunk can see survives
  the chunk's appends.
- K6's single `window` parameter conflated the mask distance
  with the slot modulus. The shaders now take both: `window`
  masks (distance), `ring` slots (modulus). The trait path
  passes ring == window, so its behavior is unchanged (the
  cross-backend test still passes on the server).

## Proof: synthetic cross-path (server, release)

tests/resident_session.rs runs one synthetic model (the
cross-backend fixture: hidden 512, FFN 1024, vocab 1024, six
layers in a sliding/global mix, window 4, Q4_K weights, Q5_K
head) through the CPU reference, the GPU trait path, and the
resident session, comparing every token:

- Prompt of 4 plus 5 greedy steps (9 positions through a
  window of 4): top-1 agreement at every step across all three
  drivers; max-abs logit diffs at most 1.1e-6 (bar: 0.5).
  Session counters after this phase: 6 forwards, 6 chunks, 6
  submissions, 6 readbacks, 762 dispatches, 1 aux submission.
- A 70-token prompt (past the 64-row chunk cap, so prefill
  splits 64 + 6) plus one decode step: agreement again,
  diffs at most 1.1e-6. The session's reset() is exercised
  between phases.

## Proof: the real file (server, release)

Stage 1 prompt "The capital of France is"
(ids [200000, 954, 7963, 323, 11698, 373]), `--gpu`:

```text
generated_ids=[13796, 26, 1573, 373, 290, 2167, 26899, 1212]
generated_text=" Paris. It is the most populous"
```

Exact against the verified reference, 8/8. First-token
probability 0.403462, matching the trait-path GPU proof's
0.403462. The 64-token continuation stays coherent (city /
France / population text, same as the reference family's).

## Performance (server, release, medians of 3 discipline)

| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Decode steady state, steps 8..64, median per-token | 34 ms = **29.4 tok/s** (two runs, medians identical; mean 33.0 to 33.2 ms) |
| Decode, tight-loop probe (argmax only between forwards) | 31.8 ms median = 31.4 tok/s |
| Prefill, 98-token SUMMARY golden prompt, first use (plan builds included) | 2,202 ms = 44.5 tok/s |
| Prefill, same prompt, warm plans (probe, reps 2 and 3) | 1,415 to 1,428 ms = **69 tok/s** |
| Prefill, 6-token Stage 1 prompt | 1,038 to 1,060 ms (rows=6 plan build included) |
| Peak VRAM during the 64-token decode | 17,533,157,376 bytes (17.53 GB) |
| Submissions per decode token | 1 (1,071 dispatches inside it) |

Time to first token, from the 64-token run's phase lines:
file open and parse 8,451 ms (cold page cache; 4,841 warm),
host weight load 4,629 ms, backend open 34 ms, session build
(weight upload) 3,087 ms, first forward 1,060 ms. First token
at about 17.3 s from process start cold, about 12.6 s warm;
in a persistent server the load terms are paid once at boot,
not per request.

## Where decode lands, honestly

- Trait path (previous composition): 1.98 tok/s. Resident:
  29.4 tok/s, a 14.8x improvement from composition alone.
- llama.cpp solo baseline: 44.31 tok/s. **Not beaten.** The
  byte-math ceiling at the isolated kernels' 818 GB/s and
  14.89 GiB streamed per token is about 51 to 53 tok/s
  (a 19.5 ms floor); the resident forward's median is 34 ms.
- What the remaining ~14.5 ms is made of, by measurement and
  arithmetic: (1) in-chain dispatch cost: 1,071 dispatches at
  an effective ~12 microseconds each of launch and barrier
  time inside one pass (the per-pass era priced the same
  chain's overhead at ~26 microseconds per dispatch: 46 ms
  total vs 34 after pass merging, with identical math);
  (2) host-side chain recording and the ~160 uniform rewrites
  per token, serialized before the submit (~2 ms); (3) the
  logits readback synchronization (~1 ms). The GEMVs
  themselves stream the same bytes the isolated benches
  measured; nothing in the run suggests they slowed down.
- Closing the rest is kernel-count work, not composition:
  llama.cpp runs this model in roughly 150 dispatches per
  token (fused norm-plus-projection epilogues, one attention
  kernel). The follow-on that buys the most: fuse the four
  per-layer K4 norm dispatches and the RoPE/append into their
  neighboring GEMVs, and give K6 a single fused
  scores-plus-reduce for decode rows. Prefill is bounded by a
  different property: the GEMV kernels only partially amortize
  weight reads across batch rows (69 tok/s warm at 98 tokens),
  so a GEMM-class (MMQ-style) prefill kernel is the prefill
  follow-on.
- Note the trait path's own latent limit found above: a
  single multi-row trait forward over windowed layers was
  only ever correct within the first window-span of positions
  (it NaN'd at 70 rows). The ring split does not change the
  trait layout (ring == window there), so trait multi-row
  forwards over windowed layers remain a decode-shaped tool;
  the resident session is the prefill path.

## Gates

- cargo test -p wgpu-compute: green locally (GPU tests skip
  with a printed reason; this VM has no suitable adapter) and
  the resident_session and cross_backend tests pass on the
  server's GPU in release.
- cargo clippy -p wgpu-compute --all-targets: clean.
- Workspace, `cargo test --workspace --exclude dflash --lib
  --tests`: 1,062 passed, 5 failed. The 5 failures are all in
  the sibling itak-engine lane (generate tests in
  crates/itak-engine/src/engine.rs and src/protocol.rs, e.g.
  run_generate_end_to_end_over_real_socket,
  generate_returns_prompt_echo_prefill_ids); they appear only
  under the workspace invocation's feature unification and
  the same package run solo passes 17/17. The dflash crate
  (also a sibling lane, uncommitted at this snapshot) does
  not compile its own tests yet and is excluded for that
  reason. Every crate this task touched or depends on
  (wgpu-compute, muse-glimmer, cpu-compute, attention, gguf,
  tokenizer, itak-loader) is green in its own run.

## Fusion pass (2026-10-30, later): 1,071 -> 445 dispatches per token

The kernel-count work named above, done in measured stages.
Every stage gated the same way: wgpu-compute suites green
locally and on the server GPU, clippy clean, and the
real-file Stage 1 + 64-token run exact (first-token prob
0.403462, generated ids matching the known-good stream
through all 64 tokens). Decode numbers are the bench
method's clean-run means over steps 8..64, 3 runs each;
medians run 1 ms coarser. Baseline for the pass: 1,071
dispatches/token at ~33.0 ms mean (~29-30 tok/s).

| stage | what fused | dispatches/token | ms/token (mean) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| A | K9 attention prep: Q/K norms + RoPE + KV append, one dispatch (was K4 x2 + K5 x3 per layer) | 889 | ~32.7 |
| C+D+E | Batched QKV(+gate) GEMV (upload_multi concat), gate sigmoid fused into the output projection's activation (K1 gated form), FFN gate+up pair with SwiGLU fused into the down projection (K1/K2 act forms) | 655 | ~28.4 |
| F | Flash attention for decode rows (scores + online softmax + V reduce in one kernel; chunk plans keep two-pass) | 603 | ~28.7 (within noise at 69-token context; the win grows with stored length) |
| G | K4 norm chains: post-attention norm + FFN norm in one dispatch, and the boundary chain (post-FFN norm + next layer's attention norm), the intermediate row register-resident | 500 | ~25.5 |
| batch3 | Partial QKV batch for the 26 layers whose V is Q6_K: Q, K, gate concatenated (gate is the third segment), V separate; K9 takes a separate V stride | 448 | ~25.1 |
| F6b | Head finishing (scale / tanh softcap) fused into the Q5_K head kernel's final store; bitwise identical on the server GPU | 447 | ~25.2 (within noise) |
| F6a+F6c | Embedding gather + weightless norm in one dispatch (bitwise identical); final norm folded into the last layer's close (the close emits the head input, the last-row copy disappears) | 445 | ~25.2 |

Final decode: **445 dispatches/token at ~25.2 ms/token,
about 39.7 tok/s**, against llama.cpp's 44.31 tok/s
(22.57 ms). The gap did not close; what remains is not
dispatch count in the fusion sense. Per-layer decode is
now 8 sequential kernels (Q4_K-V layers) or 9 (Q6_K-V
layers): batch, prep, flash, gated output, norm chain,
FFN pair, fused down, boundary chain. Every one consumes
the previous one's full output, so no two can merge
without cross-workgroup synchronization the platform does
not offer. The honest decomposition at 445:

- Weight + KV streaming floor: ~19.5 ms (14.89 GiB/token at
  the kernels' measured ~818 GB/s).
- The remaining ~5.7 ms rides on the ~445 kernel
  boundaries (the pass measured a consistent ~12-15 us of
  pipeline drain per dependent GEMV-class boundary, ~2 us
  for tiny kernels), plus ~1 ms readback sync and the
  host's per-token record/sample work inside the step time.

Named next levers, in order: (1) multi-row decode batching
(amortizes boundaries and weight streams across tokens;
out of scope for this pass, and it is the lever that
remains if the target must be beaten), (2) an in-chain
per-kernel timestamp profile to split the ~5.7 ms between
boundary drain and in-chain stream slowdown precisely,
(3) host-side overlap: an on-GPU argmax head so the
per-token readback shrinks from 808 KB of logits to one
index, letting recording of the next chunk start earlier.
Prefill spot-check after the pass: warm 64-row chunks run
at ~78 tok/s or better (258-token prompt, marginal rate),
at or above the 69 tok/s baseline; chunk plans keep the
two-pass attention by design.

## GEMM prefill path and on-device argmax (2026-10-30, later still)

**Prefill: K10/K11 tiled GEMM.** Past 16 rows, chunk plans
no longer replay the GEMV chain per prompt row. K10 (Q4_K)
and K11 (Q6_K) stage each super-block column's dequantized
tile in workgroup memory once and apply it to all 64 chunk
rows from per-thread 4x4 register sub-tiles, carrying K1's
gated and SwiGLU activation forms with the same K1ActGeom
addressing, so the plan's fused projections (gated output,
SwiGLU-fused down) dispatch through the GEMM unchanged.
Weights bind the K1/K2 uploads' one resident buffer per
tensor. Single-row decode keeps the fused GEMV chain,
untouched by construction; a device granting under 16 KiB
of workgroup storage builds no GEMM pipelines and the
session keeps its GEMV chunk plans (the fallback is read
from the backend, never substituted silently).

Per-tensor bench (examples/k10_bench, batch 64, real file,
two healthy windows; ms per pass over the tensor):

| tensor | GEMV replay | t64x256 | t64x128 | t32x128 (shipped) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Q6_K ffn_down 19968x6656 (109 MB) | 6.4-6.8 | 5.15 | 3.18 | 2.99 |
| Q4_K ffn_gate 6656x19968 (74.7 MB) | 4.4-4.5 | 3.50 | 2.04 | 1.95 |

Session prefill (glimmer_generate --gpu, repeated-sentence
prompts, two runs each; totals include first-chunk plan
builds):

| prompt | t64x256 | t32x128 (shipped) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 254 tokens | 5,062 / 4,957 ms (50 tok/s) | 3,495 / 3,534 ms (72 tok/s) |
| 1,024 tokens | 17,744 / 17,647 ms (58 tok/s) | 11,773 / 11,810 ms (87 tok/s) |

Marginal rate between the two lengths: 60 tok/s at
t64x256, **93 tok/s at the shipped t32x128**, against the
pre-GEMM warm marginal of ~78 tok/s and llama.cpp's 998.
The GEMM closes only a slice of the gap, and the reason is
measured: per-tensor effective stream is ~36 GB/s against
the ~818 GB/s the GEMV achieves at batch 1, so the kernel
is bound inside the workgroup at ~5.7 TFLOPS effective
(FP32 peak ~61), not at DRAM. Each staged f32 element is
re-read from workgroup memory at roughly one FMA per LDS
byte, staging barriers land every 128 staged columns, and
256-deep tiles measure worse than 128-deep at both widths
(more barrier-serial staging per workgroup, less
occupancy): the narrow tile wins on shape, not capacity.
Decomposition of the 10.75 ms/token marginal: ~72% the
GEMM projections at the rates above, ~28% the
non-projection chunk chain (two-pass K6 attention over the
chunk's queries and the stored context, prep, norms,
gather, dispatch boundaries).

Named next lever, with its evidence: an MMQ in
llama.cpp's actual sense. Quantize each activation block
to int8 on the fly and run the inner product on DP4A
integer dot instructions against the weights' integer
payloads, folding per-block scales back at the store.
That is the design that reaches 998 tok/s on this card;
the f32-tile GEMM here is the correctness-first stepping
stone, and its staging discipline, act forms, and session
wiring carry over. Secondary: a 4x8 per-thread sub-tile
halves staged-tile LDS reads per FMA (the register budget
allows it on RDNA3) for an estimated 1.5-2x on the
projection share. The 28% non-projection share wants its
own timestamp profile before anyone optimizes it.

Gate honesty: the first server run of the GEMM tests
caught a real bug, in the one-shot helpers rather than the
kernels: K10Pipeline::run and K11Pipeline::run encoded
their dispatch into a command encoder they never
submitted, so their readbacks mapped initial zeros (the
act-form paths and the session, which submit, were correct
throughout; no session proof ever touched the broken
helpers). Isolated by driving prepare with manual buffers
on the device, fixed with the missing submit, and the
test's tolerance re-based to the result set's magnitude
scale: the fixture's random f16 headers put outputs at
~1e3, where summation order alone is worth ~1e-2 absolute.

**Argmax tail.** K8 gains a two-stage reduction (128
workgroups of (value, index) partials, one finish
workgroup) under the host sampler's exact greedy rule:
maximum value, lowest index on an exact tie, a total
order, so the staged result equals a sequential scan on
any finite input. ResidentSession::forward_argmax runs
the identical chunk chain with the reduction appended to
the head segment; the per-chunk readback is 8 bytes
(winning index, winning logit) instead of the logits
vector's 808 KB at the real vocabulary, and SessionStats
counts argmax readbacks separately. Real-file proof:
--gpu-argmax's 64-token generated stream is byte-identical
to the logits-mode stream, the prefill winner's logit
matches to all printed digits (17.343929, prob 0.403462),
and the run's stats show 64 argmax readbacks and 0 logits
readbacks. forward is unchanged for sampling and top-k
callers. Synthetic gates: tests/k8_argmax.rs (bit-exact
winning logit against the host scan, engineered ties, tail
and all-negative cases, empty-input refusal) and the
resident argmax-tail test (two-chunk prompt plus a 12-step
greedy generation against forward plus the host pick).

## MMQ prefill path (2026-10-30, later still): the integer-dot kernels

The GEMM section above named the next lever: true MMQ,
llama.cpp's design. It is built. K12 quantizes activation
rows on the fly into Q8_1 form (per 32 elements: packed
int8 words plus the (d, s) pair ggml's MMQ layout wants,
with the two 16-element half sums Q6_K's fold needs added;
scales stay f32 in this device-only format). The
activation transforms live in the quantizer, in the same
K1ActGeom addressing the GEMM act forms use, so the gated
output and SwiGLU-fused down projections run through the
new path unchanged in shape: one quantize dispatch
(ACT_NONE / ACT_GATED / ACT_SWIGLU) feeds one product
dispatch. K13 (Q4_K) and K14 (Q6_K) run the products as
DP4A integer dots (`dot4I8Packed`, the WGSL spelling of
the instruction ggml-vulkan reaches through
`dotPacked4x8EXT`) against the weights' staged integer
payloads, folding per-sub-block scales in f32 at the
store, in super-block order, term for term with
`vec_dot_q4_K_q8_1` / `vec_dot_q6_K_q8_1`. The session
prefers MMQ past the same 16-row threshold, keeps the
f32 GEMM as the fallback for devices and shapes MMQ
refuses by name, and leaves single-row decode on the
fused GEMV chain untouched.

**Is the integer path real?** A probe kernel
(examples/dp4a_probe.rs) runs three register loops at
identical geometry: `dot4I8Packed` measures 9.79 TOPS of
int8 MACs, the unpack-into-vec4<i32> emulation 2.84 TOPS,
an FP32 FMA chain 6.57 TFLOPS. The unpack path scalarizes
on this backend (3.4x slower), so the fallback the task
allowed for would have capped the design near GEMM
rates; the packed intrinsic reaches the hardware dot.
(The probe's per-step LCG update dilutes all three
numbers alike; they are comparative, not peaks.)

**Per-tensor, batch 64, real file** (mmq_bench, same
discipline as k10_bench; product time, quantize is
0.02-0.06 ms and composes to within noise of the product
alone):

| tensor | GEMV replay | GEMM t32x128 | MMQ m32 | MMQ m64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| blk.0 ffn_down (Q6_K, 109 MB) | 6.73 ms | 3.02-3.09 ms | 4.02 ms | 2.52-2.55 ms |
| blk.0 ffn_gate (Q4_K, 74.8 MB) | 4.57 ms | 2.05-2.09 ms | 1.88 ms | 1.49-1.51 ms |

**The bank-conflict find.** The first MMQ build measured
at or below the GEMM (Q4_K m64 2.26 ms, Q6_K m32
3.42 ms). The cause was not the dots: the staged
activation tile's 64-word row stride puts all sixteen
batch lanes of a wavefront on the same LDS bank for
every activation load (their addresses differ by whole
rows), a 16-way conflict on the kernel's most frequent
load. Skewing the tile to a 65-word row stride, one word
of padding per row, moved Q4_K m32 2.41 -> 1.88 ms and
m64 2.26 -> 1.49 ms, and Q6_K m64 3.63 -> 2.52 ms.
Q6_K m32 regressed 3.42 -> 4.02 ms under the same change
(recorded, not explained away; its fold does twice the
f32 work per dot and its resident set is one 128-thread
workgroup per CU). The wide tile wins both families, so
m64 is the shipped shape and m32 remains for devices
whose workgroup-storage grant fits it but not m64. An
earlier experiment, unrolling the sub-block loop at
generation time so staged offsets are literals, changed
nothing measurable; the compiler had already
strength-reduced the addresses. Recorded as a negative
result so nobody re-pays for it.

**Session prefill, real file, same prompts both
builds** (the pre-MMQ resident build is the A/B control):

| prompt | GEMM build | MMQ build |
|---|---|---|
| 254 tokens | 3,130 ms | 2,760 / 2,941 ms |
| 1,024 tokens | 11,446 ms | 7,541 / 7,558 ms |
| marginal rate | 92.6 tok/s | 161 tok/s |

Gross at 1,024 tokens: 89.5 -> 135.8 tok/s. The MMQ
path is 1.74x the GEMM on the marginal rate.

**Correctness.** Synthetic gates (tests/k12_k14_mmq.rs):
the products match a host reference running the same
quantized math (exact integer dots, same fold) at ~2e-7
relative across batches 1-64, both tile shapes, and the
plain/gated/SwiGLU forms; against the exact f32 product
the activation-quantization band measures 0.36% (Q4_K)
and 0.42% (Q6_K) of the result scale, which is the Q8_1
design's error, gated separately from kernel correctness.
The quantizer itself matches its host reference
bit-exactly on the test data (scales within 1 ulp: RADV's
division is not correctly rounded, measured). Real file:
the Stage 1 first-token probability prints 0.403462 (all
digits), the 8/8 stream is exact, the 254- and
1,024-token continuations are token-identical to the
GEMM build's, and the 64-token argmax-mode stream is
byte-identical to logits mode on this build.

**Where it lands against 998, honestly.** The marginal
rate is 161 tok/s, 1.74x the GEMM and still 6x short of
llama.cpp's Vulkan number. What binds, with the
measurements: the Q4_K product runs at 5.7 T int8
MACs/s and the Q6_K product at 3.4 T, against the
probe's diluted 9.8 TOPS and a much higher architectural
ceiling. Three named causes. (1) Occupancy: the m64
tiles stage 41-45 KB of workgroup memory, so one
workgroup is resident per CU; the tile is one
super-block deep with a barrier per super-block (78
barriers across an ffn_down workgroup), so latency
hiding rests on in-thread ILP alone. (2) Fold issue:
the per-sub-block f32 fold competes for the same VALU
issue as the dots, and Q6_K folds twice per 32 elements
(two 16-element halves), which is most of why its
product trails Q4_K's despite identical dot counts.
(3) The session ceiling: the non-projection chunk chain
was 28% of the marginal at GEMM time and this pass did
not touch it; infinitely fast projections would still
bound the marginal near 330 tok/s under the current
chain. Closing the rest of the gap is the wide-tile
(128x128-class) double-buffered MMQ plus a profile of
that chain, a kernel project of its own, not a tuning
knob on this tile. The 4x8 f32 GEMM sub-tile noted as
the secondary option in the GEMM section was not built:
the MMQ proved possible on this backend, which was its
condition.

===== END FILE: bench/gpu-resident-2026-10-30.md =====

===== FILE: bench/gpu-trace-2026-11-06.md =====
# GPU trace tooling: SQTT, hang dumps, host telemetry, canary (2026-11-06)

Lane: lane/gpu-trace-tooling, based on main 2f8b3ae.
Tooling and documentation only: one new bench script
(`bench/gpu-trace.sh`) and this note. No engine code
touched, no server GPU jobs run in this lane (card time
is serialized by the parent and several verdict lanes
are queued ahead of the first traced run).

**Verdict in one line:** the four visibility forms the
2026-11-04 streaming-rate research identified but nobody
wired into a repeatable tool — SQTT thread traces, hang
forensics dumps, a host telemetry timeline, and a
bandwidth canary — now run as one command around any
bench binary and file themselves as one run directory;
the wrapper and its telemetry sampler are demonstrated
end to end on the build VM (which has no GPU, so the
trace-side artifacts degrade honestly there and the
server run below is the first real capture).

## What already existed, and what was missing

- Per-dispatch GPU timing (the diag system,
  `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing` + `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG_OUT`):
  says how long each kernel ran. It cannot say where the
  card's waves stalled while they ran.
- The shader autopsy (`bench/shader-autopsy.sh`):
  captures the compiled form (RADV_DEBUG
  shaderstats/asm) of every kernel family, but only
  inside dedicated autopsy sessions, never attached to
  an ordinary measured run.
- Host readings (VRAM from amdgpu sysfs counters,
  process RSS from /proc) were taken by hand during
  verdict sessions and survive only in those notes'
  prose: the cleared-card guard numbers, the phase-B
  footprint audit's 34.6 GB anon-RSS kill signature.
  Nothing sampled them during a run.
- Missing entirely until now: SQTT captures (never
  taken on this stack), a hang-forensics readiness
  position (the one production symptom on record, the
  wide-MMQ session hang of 2026-11-04, was diagnosed
  after the fact from compiled form alone), and a
  same-session bandwidth canary to set kernel stream
  rates against.

## The tool

`bench/gpu-trace.sh LABEL [--] COMMAND [ARGS...]` runs
COMMAND with the visibility env applied to the child
only (via env(1)) and creates
`bench/traces/<UTC stamp>-<label>/`:

| artifact | what it answers |
| --- | --- |
| stdout.log, stderr.log | what the run said, streamed live and filed |
| `*.rgp` + rgp-sources.txt | where the card's waves actually stalled (below) |
| shaderstats.txt, asm/ | the compiled form of whatever this run actually compiled |
| telemetry.csv | was the host or the card the wall (below) |
| canary.txt | the honest ceiling for the day (below) |
| manifest.txt | command, env applied, git SHA, Mesa version if readable, exit code, inventory |

plus one appended line per run in `bench/traces/INDEX.md`.
The wrapper preserves the command's exit code exactly
and never times the command out.

### SQTT: where the waves stalled

Env: `MESA_VK_TRACE=rgp` with `MESA_VK_TRACE_PER_SUBMIT=1`.
These are the current correct switches (Mesa envvars
documentation, verified live by the 2026-11-04 research):
RADV's built-in capture writes .rgp files that open in
AMD's Radeon GPU Profiler, which shows wavefront
occupancy over time, per-instruction timing, pipeline
and barrier stalls, cache behaviour, and (Mesa 26-era
RADV) LDS bank-conflict counters on GFX11. That is the
view that separates the streaming-rate hypotheses the
diag timings cannot: not enough waves in flight vs
long memory latency vs LDS-path stalls vs barrier
lock-stepping. `MESA_VK_TRACE_PER_SUBMIT` is Mesa's
documented knob for compute-only workloads, which is
what every bench binary here is. The old
`RADV_THREAD_TRACE` controls were removed from Mesa;
a correction on exactly this point was delivered with
the 2026-11-04 research report, and this script does
not use them.

Mesa's dump directory is not settable through a
documented env var, so after the child exits the
wrapper sweeps the working directory, /tmp, and $HOME
for .rgp files newer than the run's start marker and
moves them into the run dir, recording each file's
origin in rgp-sources.txt. The sweep is the reason
traced runs belong inside the phase lock like every
other card session: the lock is what makes "newer than
the marker" mean "ours".

The child also gets a private `MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR`
inside the run dir (a caller-set value is kept and
recorded). Without it, a warm shared cache compiles
nothing and RADV prints no stats or disassembly at
all — the same cold-cache discipline the autopsy uses.

### Hang forensics: the wedge kit

`GPU_TRACE_HANG=1` adds `hang` to the child's
RADV_DEBUG. RADV_DEBUG=hang makes RADV dump its state
(and umr register/wave/ring dumps, unless disabled)
when a queue hangs, which is the evidence a wedged
card can still give. The standing example is the
wide-MMQ (K15/K16) session hang of 2026-11-04: the
session wedged once, and the cause (1,041-1,213
spilled VGPRs, 78-86 KB scratch in the compiled wide
forms) was convicted a day later from the autopsy,
because no hang capture existed at the moment of the
wedge. That diagnosis should never again depend on
reconstructing the moment afterwards.

The wrapper is built for this case: it never times
the child out, and telemetry keeps sampling while the
card is wedged, so the timeline leading into the hang
survives. The operator kills the child; the wrapper
files everything and preserves the kill as the exit
code.

**Standing rule, from this note forward: any future
card hang gets exactly one hang-forensics rerun —
the same command under `GPU_TRACE_HANG=1
bench/gpu-trace.sh <label>-hang -- <command>` —
before anyone reboots the host, resets the card, or
changes the code under test.** One rerun, because the
first hang's own artifacts (telemetry up to the wedge,
the hung session's logs) plus one instrumented
reproduction are the evidence set; repeated wedging
of the card for curiosity is not.

### Telemetry: host or card

An embedded python3 sampler (no new dependencies;
python3 is already the bench scripts' extractor)
samples for the wrapped process's lifetime at about
10 Hz (`GPU_TRACE_INTERVAL`, default 0.1 s):

- `vram_used_bytes`: the big card's
  `mem_info_vram_used` (device chosen by the bench
  runners' existing rule, VRAM total over 20 GB) —
  the same counter the cleared-card guards read.
- `proc_rss_kib`: the wrapped process's VmRSS from
  /proc/<pid>/status. The process only; children it
  forks are not summed (declared in the CSV header).
  This is the column that would have drawn the phase-B
  footprint curve (a ~35 GB anon-RSS climb into the
  OOM killer) as it happened instead of after.
- `load1`: /proc/loadavg field 1.
- `gpu_edge_temp_millic`, `gpu_power_microw`: the
  amdgpu hwmon's temp1_input and power1_average —
  the throttling evidence: a run that slows while
  temperature or power sits at the cap is a different
  finding from a run that slows cold.

Absent sources degrade honestly: the column stays
empty and the CSV header names the source ABSENT.
Lining the timeline up against the diag output is by
run window: manifest.txt records start/end epochs,
the telemetry rows carry epoch seconds, and the diag
CSV's per-kernel totals (plus the per-dispatch
`[wgpu-compute-diag]` lines the wrapper files in
stderr.log) describe the same window.

### Canary: the ceiling for the day

After the child exits — never concurrently, so the
canary cannot steal bandwidth from the measured run —
the wrapper runs vkpeak, or clpeak if vkpeak is
absent, into canary.txt (180 s timeout). That is the
same-session practical ceiling to set kernel stream
rates against, replacing the habit of comparing a
run against numbers from other days: the recorded
references are the card's 960 GB/s spec, GEMV's
649.5 GB/s measured in the 2026-11-05 prefill
profile, and the MMQ pair's 43.5 GB/s in the same
profile. If neither tool is on PATH, canary.txt
records the absence and names those references
instead of inventing a reading.

## VM demonstration (this lane, 2026-11-06)

This VM has no GPU and no RADV (no /sys/class/drm
devices, no amdgpu hwmon, no vulkaninfo), so the
trace-side artifacts cannot be produced here; what
was demonstrated is the wrapper machinery and the
sampler against dummy processes. Demo run directories
were removed after capture; the wrapper recreates
everything per run.

1. `bench/gpu-trace.sh vm-demo -- sleep 3` — exit 0
   preserved. telemetry.csv: 27 rows over the 3 s
   lifetime at ~10 Hz; RSS live (1,752 KiB, sleep);
   load live (2.20); VRAM/temp/power columns empty
   with header lines `# vram source: ABSENT (no
   amdgpu mem_info counters on this host)` and the
   hwmon equivalents. manifest.txt complete (command,
   child env, git SHA 2f8b3ae, Mesa "not readable on
   this host", inventory). rgp collected: 0; stats
   blocks: 0; asm/NO_ASM_FOUND.txt written; canary:
   ABSENT (neither vkpeak nor clpeak on PATH here).
2. RSS tracking: a python3 dummy that allocates and
   touches 200 MB, then sleeps 2 s. Peak
   proc_rss_kib in its telemetry.csv: 205,760 — the
   sampler follows the target process's growth.
3. Exit-code preservation:
   `bench/gpu-trace.sh vm-exit -- sh -c 'echo demo-out;
   echo demo-err >&2; exit 7'` returned exactly 7,
   with demo-out in stdout.log and demo-err in
   stderr.log.
4. Hang knob: `GPU_TRACE_HANG=1 bench/gpu-trace.sh
   vm-hang -- true` recorded
   `RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats,asm,cs,hang` in the
   manifest's child_env line.
5. INDEX.md gained exactly one line per demo run,
   in the documented format.

## Not verified locally (server run settles these)

- Whether Mesa 26.0.8's RADV writes per-submit .rgp
  files for headless compute at all, how many, and
  exactly where (CWD vs /tmp). The sweep covers both;
  a clean server run that collects zero .rgp files is
  itself the finding, and the follow-up would be the
  trigger knobs (MESA_VK_TRACE_TRIGGER /
  MESA_VK_TRACE_FRAME), not silent re-runs.
- The exact stderr spellings of the stats and
  disassembly headers on the server's Mesa. The
  extractors key on the autopsy's proven patterns
  plus a loose 'disassembly' key; stderr.log is filed
  raw either way, so a spelling miss loses nothing
  but the extraction, and the note for that run
  should record it.
- vkpeak/clpeak presence on ubuntu-server. The
  wrapper checks at run time; canary.txt is the
  record either way.
- shellcheck was not run: it is not installed on
  this VM (checked 2026-11-06). The script header
  carries the same note; run shellcheck on the
  server before the first traced session.

## First server run (to schedule)

One 1,022-token prefill_profile run under the wrapper,
from the staged tree (manifest-verified, as every
proof run), inside the phase lock, card cleared, the
Cortex tenants stopped before and restored after per
the restart sheet (~/card-clear-2026-11-05.md). This
is the natural first capture: prefill is the measured
problem (MMQ pair at 43.5 GB/s against GEMV's
649.5 GB/s in the same profile), and the RGP is the
tool the research prescribed for exactly those
kernels before any further redesign.

```sh
ssh -F /home/hatch/.ssh/ts/config ts-server
cd ~/gpu-wave<N>   # staged tree for the current main
flock -w 14400 /tmp/itak-phase.lock bash -c '
  set -u
  systemctl --user stop cortex-embed.service
  docker stop cortex-cortex-chat-1 cortex-cortex-embed-1
  # VRAM guard (prefill-profile-run.sh rule): the big
  # card must read at or under 500 MB used; cleared
  # state reads about 33 MB. Abort if not.
  used=$(cat /sys/class/drm/card2/device/mem_info_vram_used)
  echo "vram used before: $used"
  [ "$used" -le 500000000 ] || { echo "CARD NOT CLEAR"; exit 1; }
  export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
  export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_=0
  cargo build --release -p itak-loader --example prefill_profile
  sentence="The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. "
  prompt_long=""
  for i in $(seq 1 102); do prompt_long="$prompt_long$sentence"; done
  WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing \
  WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG_OUT="$PWD/gpu-trace-first-diag.csv" \
    bench/gpu-trace.sh prefill-1022 -- \
    target/release/examples/prefill_profile \
      /mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf \
      "$prompt_long"
  echo "wrapper exit (prefill_profile exit): $?"
  docker start cortex-cortex-chat-1 cortex-cortex-embed-1
  systemctl --user start cortex-embed.service
'
```

(The card2 sysfs path is the one the 2026-11-05
sessions read on this host; if the enumeration moved,
read `mem_info_vram_used` from whichever card device
reports the 25.75 GB total.)

Acceptance for the run, checked in the run directory
under bench/traces/: wrapper exit 0; at least one .rgp
collected (or the zero-.rgp finding above recorded in
that session's note); shaderstats.txt block count
above zero; telemetry.csv rows spanning the run at
~10 Hz with VRAM, RSS, temperature, and power all
live; canary.txt holding a vkpeak (or clpeak) reading
or the recorded absence; the diag CSV populated
beside it. Open the .rgp in Radeon GPU Profiler and
read the MMQ kernels' occupancy, instruction timing,
and LDS bank conflicts before the K23/flash/coopmat
lanes draw conclusions the profile alone cannot
support.

## Going forward

- Kernel verdict sessions (K23, flash rework, the

  this wrapper, so their notes can cite waves and
  stalls, not just durations.
- Any hang: the standing rule above, one
  GPU_TRACE_HANG=1 rerun before any reboot or reset.

===== FILE: bench/gpu-trace.sh =====
#!/bin/bash
# GPU trace wrapper: run one command with every form of GPU
# and host visibility this stack can produce switched on,
# and file the artifacts as one run directory.
#
# Why: the diag system gives per-kernel GPU durations but
# not where the card's waves actually stalled; the shader
# autopsy (bench/shader-autopsy.sh) captures compiled form
# only inside dedicated autopsy sessions; and the host
# readings that decided past verdicts (VRAM from amdgpu
# sysfs, process RSS from /proc) were taken by hand and
# lived in chat logs, not next to the runs they describe.
# The 2026-11-04 streaming-rate research named the four
# remaining forms: SQTT thread traces, hang dumps, a host
# telemetry timeline, and a bandwidth canary. This wrapper
# packages those four around any command.
#
# What the wrapped command gets (env applied to the child
# only, via env(1); the caller's shell is untouched):
#   MESA_VK_TRACE=rgp            SQTT capture for Radeon
#                                GPU Profiler, via RADV's
#                                built-in capture. The old
#                                RADV_THREAD_TRACE switches
#                                were removed from Mesa; do
#                                not use them.
#   MESA_VK_TRACE_PER_SUBMIT=1   per-submit capture, the
#                                documented knob for
#                                compute-only workloads.
#   RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats,asm,cs
#                                compiled-form dumps on the
#                                child's stderr (the same
#                                flags as the autopsy), plus
#                                `hang` when GPU_TRACE_HANG=1
#                                is set, plus any caller
#                                RADV_DEBUG appended.
#   MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR        private to the run dir, so
#                                shaders compile cold and the
#                                stats/asm dumps actually
#                                happen (a warm shared cache
#                                compiles nothing and prints
#                                nothing). A caller-set value
#                                is kept and recorded.
#
# Artifacts, in bench/traces/<UTC stamp>-<label>/:
#   stdout.log, stderr.log  the child's output, streamed
#                           live through tee and filed.
#   *.rgp                   the SQTT capture (or the
#                           per-submit set Mesa produced),
#                           collected after the run from the
#                           working directory, /tmp, and
#                           $HOME: Mesa's dump directory is
#                           not settable through a
#                           documented env var, so the
#                           wrapper sweeps. The sweep is
#                           why traced runs belong inside
#                           the phase lock like every other
#                           card session.
#   rgp-sources.txt         where each .rgp was found.
#   shaderstats.txt         stats blocks extracted from
#                           stderr.log (the autopsy
#                           extractor's shape).
#   asm/                    one numbered file per
#                           disassembly block (RADV dump
#                           headers carry no shader name),
#                           or asm/NO_ASM_FOUND.txt when no
#                           block matched the key.
#   telemetry.csv           host timeline at ~10 Hz for
#                           the child's lifetime: VRAM
#                           used, child RSS, CPU load,
#                           GPU edge temperature and power
#                           (amdgpu sysfs). Absent sources
#                           degrade to empty columns and
#                           are declared in the header.
#   canary.txt              vkpeak (or clpeak) output,
#                           read AFTER the child exits so
#                           the canary can never steal
#                           bandwidth from the measured
#                           run; or the recorded absence
#                           of both tools.
#   manifest.txt            command, env applied, git
#                           SHA, Mesa version if readable,
#                           exit code, artifact inventory.
# And one line per run appended to bench/traces/INDEX.md.
#
# Exit status: the wrapped command's, preserved exactly.
# The wrapper never times the child out. If the card
# wedges, telemetry keeps sampling until the operator
# kills the child; the wrapper then files everything.
# That is the hang-forensics case: see
# bench/gpu-trace-2026-11-06.md for the standing rule
# (one rerun under GPU_TRACE_HANG=1 before any reboot
# or reset).
#
# Usage:
#   bench/gpu-trace.sh LABEL [--] COMMAND [ARGS...]
# Knobs: GPU_TRACE_HANG=1     add RADV_DEBUG=hang
#        GPU_TRACE_INTERVAL  telemetry period in seconds
#                            (default 0.1, about 10 Hz)
#        GPU_TRACE_DIR       artifact root (default
#                            bench/traces under the repo)
#        EXPECTED_SHA        manifest SHA when the tree
#                            has no .git (archive stage;
#                            same convention as the
#                            autopsy script)
#
# shellcheck: NOT RUN for this script. shellcheck is not
# installed on the build VM (checked 2026-11-06:
# `command -v shellcheck` prints nothing) and this lane
# installs nothing. The script follows the quoting
# discipline of bench/shader-autopsy.sh and was exercised
# end to end on the VM, including the exit-code and
# telemetry demos recorded in bench/gpu-trace-2026-11-06.md.
# Run `shellcheck bench/gpu-trace.sh` on the server before
# the first traced verdict session and fix what it says.
set -u
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT" || exit 2

usage() {
  echo "usage: bench/gpu-trace.sh LABEL [--] COMMAND [ARGS...]" >&2
  echo "  runs COMMAND with SQTT capture, RADV shader dumps," >&2
  echo "  host telemetry, and a bandwidth canary; artifacts in" >&2
  echo "  bench/traces/<UTC stamp>-<label>/; exit code is the" >&2
  echo "  command's. Knobs: GPU_TRACE_HANG=1, GPU_TRACE_INTERVAL," >&2
  echo "  GPU_TRACE_DIR, EXPECTED_SHA. See bench/gpu-trace-2026-11-06.md." >&2
}

if [ "${1:-}" = "-h" ] || [ "${1:-}" = "--help" ]; then
  usage
  exit 0
fi
[ $# -ge 2 ] || { usage; exit 2; }
LABEL_RAW="$1"; shift
if [ "${1:-}" = "--" ]; then shift; fi
[ $# -ge 1 ] || { usage; exit 2; }

LABEL="$(printf '%s' "$LABEL_RAW" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '-' | cut -c1-48)"
[ -n "$LABEL" ] || LABEL="run"
TRACES_DIR="${GPU_TRACE_DIR:-$ROOT/bench/traces}"
INTERVAL="${GPU_TRACE_INTERVAL:-0.1}"
STAMP="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
RUN_NAME="$STAMP-$LABEL"
RUNDIR="$TRACES_DIR/$RUN_NAME"
n=2
while [ -e "$RUNDIR" ]; do
  RUN_NAME="$STAMP-$LABEL-$n"
  RUNDIR="$TRACES_DIR/$RUN_NAME"
  n=$((n + 1))
done
mkdir -p "$RUNDIR/asm" || { echo "FAIL: cannot create $RUNDIR" >&2; exit 2; }

CMD_STR="$(printf '%q ' "$@")"
SHA="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "${EXPECTED_SHA:-unknown}")"

mesa_version() {
  local v
  v="$(vulkaninfo --summary 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'driverInfo' | head -1 | sed -E 's/^[^=]*=[[:space:]]*//')"
  if [ -n "$v" ]; then echo "$v (vulkaninfo driverInfo)"; return; fi
  v="$(dpkg-query -W -f='${Version}' mesa-vulkan-drivers 2>/dev/null)"
  if [ -n "$v" ]; then echo "$v (dpkg mesa-vulkan-drivers)"; return; fi
  echo "not readable on this host (no vulkaninfo, no dpkg mesa-vulkan-drivers)"
}

# Effective child environment (recorded in the manifest).
EFFECTIVE_RADV_DEBUG="shaderstats,asm,cs"
if [ "${GPU_TRACE_HANG:-}" = "1" ]; then
  EFFECTIVE_RADV_DEBUG="$EFFECTIVE_RADV_DEBUG,hang"
fi
CALLER_RADV_DEBUG="${RADV_DEBUG:-}"
if [ -n "$CALLER_RADV_DEBUG" ]; then
  EFFECTIVE_RADV_DEBUG="$EFFECTIVE_RADV_DEBUG,$CALLER_RADV_DEBUG"
fi
if [ -n "${MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR:-}" ]; then
  EFFECTIVE_CACHE="$MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR"
  CACHE_SOURCE="caller"
else
  EFFECTIVE_CACHE="$RUNDIR/shader-cache"
  CACHE_SOURCE="private (run dir)"
fi

MANIFEST="$RUNDIR/manifest.txt"
{
  echo "run: $RUN_NAME"
  echo "label: $LABEL"
  echo "start_utc: $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
  echo "start_epoch: $(date +%s)"
  echo "host: $(hostname)"
  echo "kernel: $(uname -srm)"
  echo "repo_root: $ROOT"
  echo "git_sha: $SHA"
  echo "command: $CMD_STR"
  echo "child_env: MESA_VK_TRACE=rgp MESA_VK_TRACE_PER_SUBMIT=1 RADV_DEBUG=$EFFECTIVE_RADV_DEBUG MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR=$EFFECTIVE_CACHE"
  echo "shader_cache_source: $CACHE_SOURCE"
  echo "caller_radv_debug: ${CALLER_RADV_DEBUG:-(unset)}"
  echo "hang_mode: ${GPU_TRACE_HANG:-0}"
  echo "telemetry_interval_s: $INTERVAL"
  echo "mesa_version: $(mesa_version)"
} > "$MANIFEST"

echo "[gpu-trace] run dir: $RUNDIR"
echo "[gpu-trace] command: $CMD_STR"
touch "$RUNDIR/.start-marker"
START_EPOCH="$(date +%s)"

# --- the wrapped command -----------------------------------
# Streams live through tee to the terminal and to the logs;
# backgrounded only so the telemetry sampler can be aimed
# at its PID. `wait` below returns the child's own status.
env MESA_VK_TRACE=rgp MESA_VK_TRACE_PER_SUBMIT=1 \
    RADV_DEBUG="$EFFECTIVE_RADV_DEBUG" \
    MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR="$EFFECTIVE_CACHE" \
    "$@" > >(tee "$RUNDIR/stdout.log") 2> >(tee "$RUNDIR/stderr.log" >&2) &
CHILD_PID=$!
echo "[gpu-trace] child pid: $CHILD_PID"

# --- telemetry sampler (embedded python3) -------------------
python3 - "$RUNDIR/telemetry.csv" "$CHILD_PID" "$RUNDIR/.stop" "$INTERVAL" <<'PYEOF' 2>"$RUNDIR/sampler.err" &
import glob, os, sys, time

out_path, pid, stop_path = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3]
interval = float(sys.argv[4])

def read_first(path):
    try:
        with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as f:
            return f.read().strip()
    except OSError:
        return None

def find_vram():
    # The big card, by the same rule the bench runners use:
    # the amdgpu device whose VRAM total exceeds 20 GB.
    for dev in sorted(glob.glob("/sys/class/drm/card[0-9]*/device")):
        total = read_first(os.path.join(dev, "mem_info_vram_total"))
        used = os.path.join(dev, "mem_info_vram_used")
        if total is None or not os.path.exists(used):
            continue
        try:
            if int(total) > 20000000000:
                return used
        except ValueError:
            continue
    return None

def find_hwmon():
    for h in sorted(glob.glob("/sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*")):
        if read_first(os.path.join(h, "name")) == "amdgpu":
            t = os.path.join(h, "temp1_input")
            p = os.path.join(h, "power1_average")
            return (t if os.path.exists(t) else None,
                    p if os.path.exists(p) else None)
    return None, None

vram_path = find_vram()
temp_path, power_path = find_hwmon()

def rss_kib():
    txt = read_first("/proc/%d/status" % pid)
    if txt is None:
        return ""
    for line in txt.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("VmRSS:"):
            parts = line.split()
            if len(parts) >= 2:
                return parts[1]
    return ""

def load1():
    txt = read_first("/proc/loadavg")
    return txt.split()[0] if txt else ""

def val_or_empty(path):
    if not path:
        return ""
    v = read_first(path)
    return v if v is not None else ""

f = open(out_path, "w", buffering=1)
f.write("# gpu-trace telemetry: host context for the wrapped run.\n")
f.write("# vram source: %s\n" % (vram_path or
        "ABSENT (no amdgpu mem_info counters on this host)"))
f.write("# temp source: %s\n" % (temp_path or
        "ABSENT (no amdgpu hwmon on this host)"))
f.write("# power source: %s\n" % (power_path or
        "ABSENT (no amdgpu hwmon on this host)"))
f.write("# rss source: /proc/%d/status VmRSS (wrapped process only;"
        " children it forks are not summed)\n" % pid)
f.write("# load source: /proc/loadavg field 1\n")
f.write("utc_iso,epoch_s,vram_used_bytes,proc_rss_kib,load1,"
        "gpu_edge_temp_millic,gpu_power_microw\n")

max_samples = int(21600 / max(interval, 0.01))  # about 6 h, anti-orphan
count = 0
while count < max_samples:
    if os.path.exists(stop_path):
        break
    if not os.path.exists("/proc/%d" % pid):
        break
    now = time.time()
    f.write("%s,%.3f,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s\n" % (
        time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime(now)),
        now,
        val_or_empty(vram_path),
        rss_kib(),
        load1(),
        val_or_empty(temp_path),
        val_or_empty(power_path)))
    count += 1
    delay = interval - (time.time() - now)
    end = time.time() + max(delay, 0.0)
    while time.time() < end:
        if os.path.exists(stop_path):
            break
        time.sleep(min(0.02, max(end - time.time(), 0.0)))
f.close()
PYEOF
SAMPLER_PID=$!

wait "$CHILD_PID"
CHILD_RC=$?
END_EPOCH="$(date +%s)"
echo "[gpu-trace] child exit: $CHILD_RC"

# Stop the sampler, then drain the tee processes.
touch "$RUNDIR/.stop"
for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
  kill -0 "$SAMPLER_PID" 2>/dev/null || break
  sleep 0.1
done
kill "$SAMPLER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$SAMPLER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
wait 2>/dev/null || true
if [ -s "$RUNDIR/sampler.err" ]; then
  echo "[gpu-trace] sampler wrote errors; kept as sampler.err"
else
  rm -f "$RUNDIR/sampler.err"
fi

# --- collect the SQTT captures ------------------------------
: > "$RUNDIR/rgp-sources.txt"
for base in "$ROOT" /tmp "$HOME"; do
  [ -d "$base" ] || continue
  find "$base" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.rgp' \
       -newer "$RUNDIR/.start-marker" 2>/dev/null
done | sort -u | while IFS= read -r f; do
  case "$f" in
    "$RUNDIR"/*) continue ;;
  esac
  dest="$RUNDIR/$(basename "$f")"
  if mv "$f" "$dest" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "$f -> $dest" >> "$RUNDIR/rgp-sources.txt"
  fi
done
RGP_COUNT="$(find "$RUNDIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.rgp' | wc -l)"
echo "[gpu-trace] rgp files collected: $RGP_COUNT"

# --- extract shader stats and disassembly from stderr -------
python3 - "$RUNDIR" <<'PYEOF'
import re, sys, pathlib
rundir = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
stderr = rundir / "stderr.log"
text = stderr.read_text(errors="replace") if stderr.exists() else ""
lines = text.splitlines()

# Shader stats blocks: the autopsy script's extractor shape.
pat = re.compile(r"(vgpr|sgpr|spilled|scratch|lds|code size)", re.I)
blocks, cur = [], None
for ln in lines:
    if re.search(r"shader statistics|shader stats", ln, re.I):
        if cur: blocks.append(cur)
        cur = [ln]
    elif cur is not None:
        if ln.strip() == "":
            blocks.append(cur); cur = None
        elif pat.search(ln):
            cur.append(ln)
if cur: blocks.append(cur)
stats_path = rundir / "shaderstats.txt"
if blocks:
    stats_path.write_text(
        "# shader stats blocks extracted from stderr.log by\n"
        "# bench/gpu-trace.sh. RADV dump headers carry no shader\n"
        "# name; order is stderr order; stderr.log is the ground\n"
        "# truth.\n\n" +
        "\n\n".join("\n".join(b) for b in blocks) + "\n")
else:
    stats_path.write_text(
        "# no shader stats blocks found in stderr.log\n"
        "# (causes: no Vulkan device on this host, the wrapped\n"
        "#  command compiled no shaders, or the dumps landed\n"
        "#  somewhere else; stderr.log is the ground truth)\n")

# Disassembly blocks: keyed on short header lines naming a
# disassembly; a stats header or the next disassembly header
# closes a block. RADV spells these headers itself, so the
# key is deliberately loose and NO_ASM_FOUND says so.
asmdir = rundir / "asm"
asmdir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
asm_blocks, cur = [], None
for ln in lines:
    if re.search(r"disassembly", ln, re.I) and len(ln) < 200:
        if cur: asm_blocks.append(cur)
        cur = [ln]
    elif re.search(r"shader statistics|shader stats", ln, re.I):
        if cur: asm_blocks.append(cur)
        cur = None
    elif cur is not None:
        cur.append(ln)
if cur: asm_blocks.append(cur)
if asm_blocks:
    for i, b in enumerate(asm_blocks[:1000], 1):
        (asmdir / ("shader-%04d.asm" % i)).write_text("\n".join(b) + "\n")
else:
    (asmdir / "NO_ASM_FOUND.txt").write_text(
        "No disassembly blocks matched in stderr.log (keyed on\n"
        "short lines containing 'disassembly'). If RADV spelled\n"
        "its headers differently on this Mesa, the dumps are\n"
        "still in stderr.log; fix the key in bench/gpu-trace.sh\n"
        "and record it in the bench note for the run.\n")
(rundir / ".extract-counts").write_text("%d %d\n" % (len(blocks), len(asm_blocks)))
print("stats_blocks=%d asm_blocks=%d" % (len(blocks), len(asm_blocks)))
PYEOF
STATS_BLOCKS=0
ASM_BLOCKS=0
if [ -f "$RUNDIR/.extract-counts" ]; then
  read -r STATS_BLOCKS ASM_BLOCKS < "$RUNDIR/.extract-counts"
fi
echo "[gpu-trace] stats blocks: $STATS_BLOCKS; asm blocks: $ASM_BLOCKS"

# --- bandwidth canary (after the run, never concurrent) -----
run_canary_tool() {
  if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    timeout 180 "$@" 2>&1
  else
    "$@" 2>&1
  fi
}
CANARY_TOOL="absent"
{
  echo "canary for run: $RUN_NAME"
  echo "timing: read after the wrapped command exited, never concurrent"
  if command -v vkpeak >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    CANARY_TOOL="vkpeak"
    echo "tool: vkpeak at $(command -v vkpeak)"
    run_canary_tool vkpeak
    echo "vkpeak exit: $?"
  elif command -v clpeak >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    CANARY_TOOL="clpeak"
    echo "tool: clpeak at $(command -v clpeak)"
    run_canary_tool clpeak
    echo "clpeak exit: $?"
  else
    echo "ABSENT: neither vkpeak nor clpeak is on PATH on $(hostname)"
    echo "at $(date -Is). No canary reading this run. Kernel stream"
    echo "rates from this run compare against the recorded references"
    echo "instead: card spec 960 GB/s; GEMV measured 649.5 GB/s and"
    echo "the MMQ pair 43.5 GB/s in the 2026-11-05 prefill profile."
  fi
} > "$RUNDIR/canary.txt" 2>&1
echo "[gpu-trace] canary: $CANARY_TOOL (see canary.txt)"

# --- finalize manifest and index ----------------------------
TELEM_ROWS="$(grep -cE '^[0-9]{4}-' "$RUNDIR/telemetry.csv" 2>/dev/null || true)"
# The scratch files have served their purpose by here (the
# sweep used the marker, the sampler used the stop file,
# the counts are read); remove them before the inventory
# so the inventory lists only real artifacts.
rm -f "$RUNDIR/.start-marker" "$RUNDIR/.stop" "$RUNDIR/.extract-counts"
{
  echo "end_utc: $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
  echo "end_epoch: $END_EPOCH"
  echo "child_pid: $CHILD_PID"
  echo "child_exit: $CHILD_RC"
  echo "child_wall_s: $((END_EPOCH - START_EPOCH))"
  echo "rgp_files_collected: $RGP_COUNT"
  echo "shaderstats_blocks: $STATS_BLOCKS"
  echo "asm_blocks: $ASM_BLOCKS"
  echo "telemetry_rows: ${TELEM_ROWS:-0}"
  echo "canary_tool: $CANARY_TOOL"
  echo "--- inventory (bytes path; manifest.txt itself excluded) ---"
  (cd "$RUNDIR" && find . -type f ! -name 'manifest.txt' -printf '%s %p\n' | sort -k2)
} >> "$MANIFEST"

INDEX="$TRACES_DIR/INDEX.md"
if [ ! -f "$INDEX" ]; then
  {
    echo "# GPU trace runs"
    echo
    echo "One line per bench/gpu-trace.sh run. Artifacts live in the"
    echo "run directory named on each line. See bench/gpu-trace-2026-11-06.md."
    echo
  } > "$INDEX"
fi
INDEX_CMD="$(printf '%s' "$CMD_STR" | tr '`' "'")"
echo "- \`$RUN_NAME\` — exit $CHILD_RC — \`$INDEX_CMD\` — rgp: $RGP_COUNT; stats blocks: $STATS_BLOCKS; asm blocks: $ASM_BLOCKS; telemetry rows: ${TELEM_ROWS:-0}; canary: $CANARY_TOOL" >> "$INDEX"

echo "[gpu-trace] done: $RUNDIR (child exit $CHILD_RC preserved)"
exit "$CHILD_RC"

===== FILE: bench/k21-finish-2026-11-06.md =====
# K21F: the finish-carrying K21 variant for the Q5_K head (2026-11-06)

Lane `lane/k21-finish`, from main a064b5d7. New
kernel module
`crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/k21_q5k_mmv_finish.rs`
(pipeline `K21FinishPipeline`, call `K21FinishCall`,
diag stamp `k21_q5k_mmv_finish`), registered on the
backend as `WgpuCompute::k21_finish` and built
unconditionally at backend construction like its
siblings. NO session code routes to it in this
lane: the routing change is a separate lane, and
this note carries the protocol that earns it.
GPU-less VM gates only here; the card verdict is
sequenced below.

## Why this exists: the zero in the verdict

The 2026-11-06 server verdict on K21
(bench/mmv-q5k-2026-11-05.md) is the whole reason:
K21 is correct (card-executed against the CPU
reference and K3 at batches 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 16, both
reduction shapes), compiled clean (zero spills,
zero scratch, LDS 1,024 B, VGPR 96 plateau), and
faster than the K3 GEMV at nearly every in-band
Q5_K row of the sweep harness. It also fired zero
times in 46,739 per-dispatch diag lines of the
flagged real resident runs, because on the
Muse-Glimmer-30B Q4_K_M file the Q5_K tensors in
the resident forward are the head, and the head
sites prepare K3 with a fused finish
(`prepare_with_finish`: logit scale, and the tanh
softcap when the file carries one) that plain K21
does not carry. The note named the follow-up in
its own text: "The head-sized prize needs a
finish-carrying K21 variant." This is that
variant, built to the evidence.

The prize is sized in bench/dflash-gpu-2026-11-03.md:
the borrowed Q5_K head is the single largest
stream in the DFlash pass (the head tensor is
about 0.86 GiB, read once per block row batch).
The site that can feed it is the BLOCK head: the
session prepares it at the chunk's full batch
(`rows`), which on the speculative paths is the
DFlash block width, inside this kernel's 2..=16
band. The standard head runs at batch 1, below the
band floor, and stays K3 by construction; nothing
in this variant pretends otherwise.

## The design

One structural variable against plain K21: the
finish at the store. One against K3: the workgroup
organization. The arithmetic is shared with both.

- The product generator mirrors K21's `mmv_shader`
  line for line (the crate's per-kernel generator
  idiom): same shape (`K21Shape`, K21's
  `shipped_shape`, imported, not re-typed), same
  per-batch generation literals and fully unrolled
  accumulators, same dequant and dot text (verified
  byte-identical against K21's generator literals
  for the dequant block, the dot block, and the
  reduction scaffolding during the build), same
  reduction orders in both shapes, same band
  (2..=16) with the same refusal text, same
  one-workgroup-array invariant (the reduction
  partials only). The half-conversion WGSL is
  K21's own constant bound by reference
  (`pub(crate)` widening in k21_q5k_mmv.rs, the
  only edit to that module), so the two generators
  cannot drift on it.
- The finish is K3's, whole: the `finish_apply`
  WGSL is K3's function text character for
  character (mode 1: `v * scale`; mode 2:
  `cap * tanh(scale * v / cap)`, K8's expressions
  in K8's order), the mode constants are K3's
  `FINISH_SCALE` / `FINISH_SOFTCAP` imported from
  k3_q5k_gemv (never redefined), and mode, scale,
  and cap travel as uniform words in the params
  tail exactly as K3's do (scale and cap as f32 bit
  patterns; word order pinned by a unit test,
  because a transposed tail compiles clean and
  only a wrong answer would show it). The finish
  is uniform state, not a generation literal, so
  the variant count stays K21's 15 per shape.
- The prepare surface is K3's signature verbatim:
  `prepare_with_finish(ctx, weights, input,
  output, batch, mode, scale, cap)`, so the head
  site can swap product engines without changing
  what it asks for. Validation is K3's, with K3's
  refusal words: a non-finishing or unknown mode
  refuses ("finish mode {mode} is not a finishing
  mode"), a softcap with a non-positive cap
  refuses ("softcap {cap} is not positive"). The
  band and buffer checks are K21's, with K21's
  words. Validation is factored into a free
  function and the params packing into another, so
  both are unit-tested on a GPU-less machine.
- Dispatch count is 1, the same as K3's fused head
  dispatch and K21's own: routing the block head
  here changes the product engine, not the plan's
  dispatch accounting, and no K8 finish dispatch
  appears or disappears (the Q5_K head never paid
  one; its `finish` slot in the plan is `None`
  today and stays `None`).
- Diag instrumentation from birth (David's rule):
  prepare stamps `k21_q5k_mmv_finish` through
  `ctx.diag_stamp` with rows, cols, quant `Q5_K`,
  weight bytes, and a `batch=<n> finish=<mode>
  grid=<x>x<y>` shape string (K3's stamp
  convention for the finish field, under this
  kernel's own name so the timing table separates
  it from both plain K21 and K3).
- Env gating: none of its own, consistent with
  the family. When routing lands, it rides the
  shared `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS` threshold
  like K19, K20, and K21; the shipped default
  stays governed by the K19 verdict (off).

## The math-equivalence argument

Claim: for any input the head site can present,
this kernel's output equals the shipped head
composition's output (K3 product + K3's fused
finish) inside the family's reassociation bound,
shrunk by the finish. Three steps.

1. Same product math. The dequant and dot text is
   K3's verbatim in both K21 and this variant
   (K21 is a proven port of the same mul_mat_vec
   family), and the reduction sums the same
   per-thread partials in the same orders per
   shape. The raw sums therefore differ only by
   f32 reassociation, the bound the family is
   already gated on: card-measured for K21 against
   both the CPU reference and K3 at 2.0e-3 to
   2.9e-3 absolute on fixture set scales of 1.8e4
   to 3.3e4 (bench/mmv-q5k-2026-11-05.md, step 1).
   This variant changes nothing under the sum.
2. Same finish, same position. The finishing map
   is a pure elementwise function of the fully
   reduced sum. K3 applies it at the reduction's
   final store, the only store of each element;
   this kernel applies the identical function at
   the identical position in both reduction
   shapes. There is no intermediate buffer, no
   second pass, and no other writer of the output
   elements in either kernel, so no ordering or
   rounding difference can enter between the sum
   and the map.
3. The map contracts differences. Both modes are
   Lipschitz with constant `scale`: mode 1
   multiplies by `scale` exactly; mode 2's
   derivative is `scale * sech^2(scale * v / cap)`,
   at most `scale`. So |finish(a) - finish(b)| is
   at most `scale * |a - b|`, and at Glimmer's
   logit scale (0.19611613) the finished outputs
   agree to about a fifth of the raw bound. The
   one evaluation that is not shared arithmetic,
   `tanh`, is the driver's WGSL `tanh` in both
   kernels on the same device, so even it is the
   same evaluation in the production comparison;
   the test bound still carries a 2e-5 absolute
   slack for it against the host-composed
   reference, where the host's f32 `tanh` is a
   different implementation.

The unavoidable difference, stated plainly: none
in the finish itself. The only difference from
the shipped head is the one K21 already carries
against K3, f32 reassociation in the product,
bounded in step 1 and shrunk in step 3. If a
future driver compiled this shader's accumulators
into spills, that would be a performance
difference, not a math one; step 0 of the
protocol below checks the compiled form before
any timing is read.

Inherited parity, not a new decision: like K3,
the prepare does not validate `scale` (any f32
passes to the uniform) and a NaN softcap cap is
not caught by the `cap <= 0.0` check (NaN compares
false). Both behaviors are the shipped head's;
this variant matches them rather than quietly
diverging, and any change belongs to a lane that
changes both kernels together.

## The routing change this hands to the next lane

Specified here so the integration is mechanical;
NOT done in this lane (session.rs is untouched).

1. A `ProjCall::MmvQ5KFinish(K21FinishCall)`
   variant: encode_into delegates to the call;
   `kernel_name()` returns `k21_q5k_mmv_finish`;
   `dispatches()` is 1; `quantized()` is false
   (the form consumes f32 rows, like the other MMV
   arms).
2. A `try_mmv_q5k_finish(backend, weights, input,
   output, batch, mode, scale, cap)` beside
   `try_mmv_q5k`, gated on `mmv_applies(backend,
   batch)`, preparing through
   `backend.k21_finish().prepare_with_finish(...)`,
   logging any refusal by name and returning None
   (the ladder continues to K3, whose call the
   head site builds today).
3. At the BLOCK head site only (the Q5_K branch
   that today calls
   `backend.k3().prepare_with_finish(...)` at
   `rows`): try the finish form first when the
   band applies, fall back to the existing K3 call
   on None. The standard head site (batch 1) is
   not touched: the band refuses it by
   construction, and decode stays K3's.
4. Dispatch accounting does not move: both forms
   are one dispatch with the finish fused, and the
   site's `finish` slot stays `None` on both
   paths.
5. `K21FinishPipeline::precompile` at the block
   batches the session will run, at plan time, as
   the family does for K21.

## Server verdict protocol (the next lane)

Preconditions: the card cleared per David's
standing order (he clears Cortex tenants for test
sessions; production Glimmer stays down); the
phase lock `flock /tmp/itak-phase.lock` held; one
heavy job at a time; the staging tree synced to
the merged commit and its hash verified before
any run; `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS` unset for
every control.

0. Shader autopsy of the compiled finish variants,
   before any timing: extend the
   bench/shader-autopsy.sh pattern to the
   K21Finish pipelines at batches 2, 7, and 16 and
   record VGPR, SGPR, spills, scratch, and LDS per
   variant, against plain K21's recorded form
   (zero spills, zero scratch, LDS 1,024 B, VGPR
   84 at batch 2 rising to the 96 plateau). The
   claims to check: the finish (a multiply, and a
   tanh in softcap mode, at the store only) adds
   no spills and no scratch, and LDS stays the
   partials size. A spill the finish introduces
   would be a finding against the fusion, priced
   before any speed number is believed.
1. Correctness gates execute (no skips) on the
   card:
   `cargo test -p wgpu-compute --test k21_finish -- --nocapture`
   (batches 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 16 against the CPU
   composition and against K3's fused finish, both
   reduction shapes, both finish modes at
   Glimmer's real scale and softcap; the 768 x 101
   deep geometry; the head's own 6,656 width; the
   named refusals) and the compile leg:
   `cargo test -p wgpu-compute --test shader_compile k21_finish`
   (all 15 batch variants, both shapes). Record
   the max abs diffs the file prints: the argument
   above predicts them at or below about a fifth
   of K21's recorded raw diffs (2.0e-3 to 2.9e-3)
   at the same fixtures, i.e. roughly 6e-4 or
   under; a larger finished diff contradicts the
   Lipschitz step and stops the protocol until it
   is explained.
2. Exposure check FIRST, before any speed reading,
   in a real resident run (this requires the
   routing change above to be in the staged tree):
   with `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=16` and
   `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing`, run itak-spec's
   `spec_generate_gpu` against the real target and
   draft files at depth 6 and depth 1, greedy,
   Stage 1 prompt. Read the per-dispatch diag lines
   in the run log (NOT the `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG_OUT`
   CSV: the 2026-11-06 verdict recorded that
   successive session reports overwrite it, and the
   surviving file can be the wrong session's).
   Require: `k21_q5k_mmv_finish` lines present,
   stamped `finish=2` (Glimmer's softcap position),
   at the block batches the run executes; the
   head's `k3_q5k_gemv` lines reduced to the
   standard head's batch-1 calls only. Zero
   `k21_q5k_mmv_finish` lines means the routing did
   not land or the band did not open; stop there
   and say so, as the K21 verdict did.
3. Identity + golden with the finish form routed:
   the same runs as step 2 must print IDENTITY and
   GOLDEN PASS in the on position before any speed
   number is read. Control: the same runs with the
   variable unset (the head entirely on K3, as
   shipped; identity and golden must pass there
   too, and the diag table must show zero
   `k21_q5k_mmv_finish` lines, proving the off
   position is the shipped composition exactly).
4. Head-heavy timing comparison: the DFlash pass
   is the head-heavy surface (the head is its
   largest single stream). From the step 2/3 runs'
   diag tables, compare the head's per-dispatch
   totals: `k21_q5k_mmv_finish` against the
   control's block-head `k3_q5k_gemv` rows (same
   batches, same tensor), and report end-to-end
   effective tok/s and acceptance at depths 6 and
   1 for both arms, against the recorded baselines
   (depth 6 control 9.09 to 9.21 tok/s, depth 1
   control 14.22 to 16.98 tok/s, from the K19/K21
   verdict sessions). Acceptance must be identical
   per depth across arms (the finish form changes
   no math beyond the bound in step 1 of the
   argument); an acceptance change is a correctness
   finding, not a speed result. Plain decode is
   batch 1 and cannot route here; its rate must
   read unchanged (35.45 tok/s class) in both arms
   as the no-leak check, as in the family's earlier
   protocols.

Decision rule: the routing stays behind the
shared MMV threshold, whose default is governed
by the K19 verdict and does not move on this
variant's evidence alone. This variant's own gate
is narrower: it earns its routing when steps 0
and 1 are clean AND step 2 shows it firing at the
block head in the real forward AND step 3 passes
identity and golden in the on position AND step 4
shows the head's diag time no worse than K3's at
the same batches. Anything less, the block head
keeps preparing K3 and the table is recorded here
as the finding.

## The routing (lane/k21f-routing, 2026-11-06)

Landed as specified above, in commit d0ebbd9 on
`lane/k21f-routing` (from lane/k21-finish
b4f6549). What routes where:

- The BLOCK head site only (`ChunkPlan::build`'s
  Q5_K branch, prepared at the chunk's full batch
  `rows`): `try_mmv_q5k_finish` (beside
  `try_mmv_q5k` in session.rs) runs first, gated
  on `mmv_applies` (the shared
  `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS` threshold; shipped
  default 1 = closed). On `Some`, the plan's
  block head is `ProjCall::MmvQ5KFinish`
  (encode delegates to the call, diag name
  `k21_q5k_mmv_finish`, dispatches 1,
  `quantized()` false). On `None` the site
  prepares the K3 fused call it built before this
  lane, unchanged.
- The fallback rule: every refusal path returns
  `None` and falls back: gate closed (batch under
  2 or past the resolved threshold), the kernel
  band's own refusal at prepare (batch past 16,
  geometry), and the finish validation's refusal
  (non-finishing mode, non-positive softcap cap),
  the prepare refusal logged by name on the diag
  channel ("mmv q5k finish refused at the product
  prepare: ...; the k3 fused form serves it").
  The fallback K3 call is asked for exactly what
  the finish form was asked for (same mode
  derivation from `cfg.logit_softcap`, same
  `cfg.logit_scale` and `cfg.logit_softcap`
  expressions), so the site's finish request is
  identical on both paths; only the product
  engine changes. Nothing in the routing touches
  the finish's order or drops an element: the
  mode, scale, and cap travel as the prepare's
  arguments verbatim on both paths, and the
  finish itself is K3's function at the same
  store position inside K21F (the build lane's
  argument above; nothing in this lane re-opens
  it).
- The standard head site is untouched: it
  prepares K3 at batch 1, and batch 1 never
  passes the gate at any threshold (pinned), so
  decode stays K3's by construction. The draft
  session is untouched (its head is a plain
  projection and already routes through the
  plain ladder). Dispatch accounting does not
  move: the routed form is one dispatch with the
  finish fused, and the site's `finish` slot
  stays `None` on both paths.
- The registration's `#[allow(dead_code)]`
  markers on the backend field and accessor are
  lifted, as the build lane instructed: the
  accessor has its first reader. The band
  arithmetic is factored into the pure
  `mmv_band_admits(max_rows, batch)` helper
  (`mmv_applies` delegates to it) so the gate is
  unit-pinnable without a device.

Two readings of the spec, recorded honestly:

- Step 5 of the hand-off (a
  `K21FinishPipeline::precompile` at plan time
  "as the family does for K21") has no separate
  call, here or anywhere in the session: no
  session code calls `precompile` for any MMV
  family member in this tree. The family's
  actual mechanism is that `prepare` compiles
  the batch variant on first use, and every
  prepare in `ChunkPlan::build` happens at plan
  build, before any forward runs, so the block
  batches' finish variants compile at plan time
  by the same construction K21's do. Adding a
  redundant precompile call would only duplicate
  the cache lookup; none was added.
- The kernel module's doc header still reads
  "no session code prepares this pipeline yet":
  kernel files were out of this lane's scope, so
  the line is stale as of this commit and is
  flagged here for whichever lane next touches
  that module.

Tests added with the routing: two unit pins in
session.rs (`mmv_band_never_admits_batch_one_
so_the_batch_one_head_stays_k3`,
`mmv_band_admits_the_block_batch_only_when_the_
gate_is_open`) and `tests/k21f_head_routing.rs`,
two env-gated arms in the diag-smoke discipline
over the resident cross-backend fixture (whose
head is Q5_K with Glimmer's finish values):
the closed arm asserts the block head stamps
`k3_q5k_gemv` and never `k21_q5k_mmv_finish`;
the open arm (`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=16`)
asserts the finish stamp at the block batch, a
batch-1 forward's head still stamping K3, and
both arms hold the block logits to the CPU
model's block forward at the cross-backend bar
(per-row argmax, max-abs under 0.5), which is
the end-to-end pin that the finish parameters
reach the K21F call unchanged. On this GPU-less
VM both arms self-skip with their reasons
printed (adapter absent; gate env unset), as
the family's device pins do.

Gate results on this VM: `cargo test
-p wgpu-compute` 206 passed, 0 failed (lib 109,
including the two new pins;
`--test k21f_head_routing` 2 passed via skips);
`cargo test -p dflash` 24 passed; `cargo test
-p itak-spec` 47 passed; clippy `--all-targets
-D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt --check` clean;
workspace check clean.

Card protocol status: steps 0 through 4 above
are ALL still owed to a card session. The new
integration arms are a fixture-scale rehearsal
of step 2's exposure half and step 3's
agreement half, not a substitute for them: the
exposure that counts is `k21_q5k_mmv_finish`
stamped `finish=2` in a real `spec_generate_gpu`
run against the real target and draft files
(step 2), preceded by the step 0 autopsy and
the step 1 real-geometry correctness gates, and
followed by identity + golden on the real file
(step 3) and the head-heavy timing comparison
against the recorded baselines (step 4). The
decision rule above is unchanged by this lane:
the routing rides the shared threshold, whose
default does not move on this variant's
evidence alone.
