===== FILE: bench/k21f-default-flip-2026-11-07.md =====
# K21F head switch default flip: the route earns its default back (2026-11-07)

Lane `lane/k21f-default-flip`, from main 7531139.
The K21F finish-carrying head route's own switch
(`WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD`) flips its shipped
default from OFF to ON. The switch, the combined
gate, and the kernel are unchanged; only the
unset position moved, in the same shape as the
MMV ceiling flip (unset resolves to the shipped
default; a present but unrecognized value
resolves to the closed fallback, never to the
default).

## The evidence chain

1. **The guard and its criterion.**
   bench/k21f-default-guard-2026-11-07.md: after
   the defaults-confirmation session proved
   speculative identity FAILS on the real file
   with the head route live (deterministic
   divergence at stream index 23, depths 1 and
   6), the route got its own fail-closed switch,
   default OFF, with a written reopen criterion:
   on the card, on the real files, with the
   switch explicitly on, identity PASSES at
   depths 1 and 6 and GOLDEN PASSES in the same
   runs that show the exposure stamps.
   Fixture-scale agreement explicitly does not
   count.
2. **The root cause and the fix.**
   bench/k21f-mask-fix-2026-11-07.md: the
   divergence was a truncated dequant mask in
   the K21F shader (the qc line masked with
   `0x0f0f0f` instead of `0x0f0f0f0f`), zeroing
   the fourth byte so 16 of 256 elements per
   Q5_K super-block lost their entire low
   nibble. One-token fix; all four dequant
   lines pinned verbatim in both K21 modules'
   shader-text tests, with a negative pin
   against the truncated literal; a typo-class
   sweep found no other truncated mask in the
   workspace. The wave17 diagnosis
   (bench/k21f-divergence-diagnosis-2026-11-07.md)
   measured the failure at the real geometry
   (margin +0.382801 at the split; worst logit
   deviation 2.04) and its attribution is
   reconciled there.
3. **The retest.** bench/k21f-retest-2026-11-07.md
   (wave18, staged from the fixed tree): REOPEN
   CRITERION MET. With `WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD=1`:
   identity and golden PASS at depths 1 and 6,
   with finish stamps in the same runs; the
   in-situ divergence at index 23 is gone
   (worst deviation 1.8e-5, was 2.04); K21F's
   finished output is bit-identical to K3's at
   the real head geometry; the finish and
   routing test files execute green on the
   card. The shipped default of that session
   (switch off) also passed identity and golden
   with zero finish stamps, so the guard held
   while it was the default.

Per the guard note's terms, the route has
earned its default back. This lane is that
flip, and nothing else.

## The change

- `compute::resolve_k21f_head` now resolves in
  the MMV ceiling flip's shape, over two named
  constants: `DEFAULT_K21F_HEAD` (`true`, the
  shipped default) and `K21F_HEAD_FALLBACK`
  (`false`, the closed fallback). New semantic
  matrix:

  | value | resolves |
  |---|---|
  | unset | ON (the shipped default) |
  | `1` (trimmed) | ON |
  | `0` (trimmed) | OFF (the explicit off; the one-variable rollback) |
  | any other text | OFF, fail-closed, logged by name at construction |

  A present-but-malformed value does NOT
  silently open: it resolves to the fallback,
  and `log_k21f_head_fallback` names it in the
  construction log, on the flash-staged
  fallback pattern. The construction log line
  now reads: `k21f head config: enabled=<bool>
  (env WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD, "1" or unset
  enables, "0" disables)`. Resolution still
  happens once at backend construction; the
  `k21f_head` accessor and the `k21f_head`
  resolved-config pair in both sessions'
  diag-capture manifests are unchanged in
  shape and now report the flipped default.
- The combined gate is untouched:
  `session::k21f_head_admits` still requires
  the switch AND the shared band, batch 1
  still never routes, and the fallback on any
  refusal is still the exact K3 fused call.
  No other MMV route changes; the K21F kernel
  is untouched (its header's routing paragraph
  is updated as docs only).
- Doc updates where the old default was
  stated: the env, resolver, field, and
  accessor docs and the construction comment
  in compute.rs; the gate doc, the
  `try_mmv_q5k_finish` doc, and the block-head
  site comment in session.rs; the K21F
  paragraph in kernels/mod.rs; the routing
  paragraph in the K21F kernel module header.
  bench/k21f-default-guard-2026-11-07.md gains
  an appended supersession section (its
  history stands); bench/k21-finish-2026-11-06.md
  gains one supersession line in its guard
  section.

## Pins

- `compute::k21f_head_switch_resolution`
  re-pinned to the full new matrix (unset on,
  `1` on, `0` off, malformed off), with the
  retest cited as the justification; the two
  named constants are pinned transitively
  through the resolver arms.
- `compute::k21f_head_value_recognition` (new):
  the recognized positions are exactly unset,
  `1`, `0`.
- `session::k21f_head_gate_requires_both_halves`
  reframed: the off half is now the explicit
  `0` (or fail-closed) position and admits
  nothing at ceiling 16 or `u32::MAX`; the on
  half is the shipped default position and
  admits exactly what the band admits.
- `tests/k21f_head_routing.rs` is now four
  arms: switch-off (exercised explicitly with
  `WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD=0`; unrecognized
  values land here too, the fail-closed pin),
  default construction (both envs unset; the
  block head must stamp the finish form: the
  flip's central pin), band-closed, and
  both-gates-open (explicit `1`). The
  closed-gate arm now selects on the ceiling
  being explicitly set to a closing value:
  before the flip it could proceed at an unset
  ceiling, which was only sound while unset
  resolved both gates closed; unset now
  resolves both open, so the arm names
  `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=1` as its
  condition. Arm selection verified with
  `--nocapture` in five env positions on this
  VM (unset: default-construction arm proceeds;
  `=0`: switch-off arm proceeds; `=1` with
  ceiling 16: open arm proceeds; `=1` with
  ceiling 1: closed-gate arm proceeds; `=true`:
  switch-off arm proceeds). All four arms
  self-skip on this GPU-less VM; their on-card
  execution rides the next card session, the
  same position the guard lane's arms were in
  before wave18 executed them.

## Rates now in force

The shipped default (route live) now carries
the wave18 session's honest, identity-passing
rates, measured with the switch on under diag
timing on the real file: **22.07 tok/s at
depth 1, 16.80 tok/s at depth 6** (medians of
3). The defaults-confirmation session's
23.16 / 21.65 figures stay struck from the
record as speed claims: they were produced by
the corrupted head, whose depth-6 acceptance
was inflated by the corruption itself
(bench/k21f-retest-2026-11-07.md).

## Rollback

```
WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD=0
```

One variable restores the guarded composition
(block head on the K3 fused call) exactly,
with every plain MMV route keeping its cap-16
opening: the position the guard shipped is now
the rollback instead of the default.

## Gates on this VM

- `cargo test -p wgpu-compute`: 267 passed,

===== FILE: bench/k21f-default-guard-2026-11-07.md =====
# K21F default guard (2026-11-07)

Lane `lane/k21f-default-guard`, from main 7940bcf.
This note records a safety correction, not a kernel
fix: the K21F finish-carrying head route gets its
own fail-closed routing switch, default OFF. The
kernel (`k21_q5k_mmv_finish`) is untouched, and no
other MMV route changes.

## The card failure that forces this

The defaults-confirmation session
(bench/defaults-confirmation-2026-11-07.md, staged
from main 7940bcf70, real Glimmer Q4_K_M file plus
the DFlash drafter, card cleared, phase lock held)
ran its leg 1 against the exact configuration
shipped on main: MMV ceiling open to 16, staged
flash on, K21F head routing live behind the shared
MMV gate.

- Exposure PASSED: `k21_q5k_mmv_finish` fired 36
  times at depth 1, every one at the block batch
  with `finish=2`; the batch-1 head stayed on K3.
  The route was provably live.
- IDENTITY FAILED: plain and speculative streams
  agree through index 22 and diverge at index 23
  (plain 589, spec 1573). Deterministic: eight
  default-configuration runs in that session, at
  depths 1 and 6, all diverged at the same index.
- GOLDEN PASSED in every arm (the first 8 tokens
  precede the divergence).
- Control arm (the whole MMV gate closed,
  `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=1`): identity and
  golden PASS, zero finish stamps. A rollback
  existed, at the price of every MMV route.
- Isolation: defaults plus `FLASH_STAGED=0` failed
  identically (staged flash is not a contributor);
  the baseline session's matrix supplies the other
  cells (MMV cap 16 without K21F passed; flash on
  without K21F passed). Between the baseline tree
  and 7940bcf70 the only spec-path delta that can
  move a verify argmax is the K21F chain. The
  session's reading: the K21F call as a unit
  (product core plus carried finish) produces head
  logits that flip a borderline verify argmax at a
  near-tie. The delta is below the fixture pins'
  cross-backend bar (max-abs 0.5): both fixture
  arms passed while the real file failed, so only
  a real-file near-tie exposes it.
- The leg-4 rates measured in that configuration
  (23.16 tok/s depth 1, 21.65 depth 6 medians) are
  NOT credited: the speed and the divergence are
  the same phenomenon until identity passes again.

Whether the delta sits in the product core or the
finish application is the fix lane's question.
This lane's question is narrower: a route proven
to break identity on the real file must not be
live by default while that fix is outstanding.

## Why the default closes

The route's only gate was the shared MMV ceiling
(`mmv_band_admits` over `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS`).
That ceiling is the plain products' gate (K19,
K20, K21), and its default opened to 16 on the
2026-11-06 baseline evidence, evidence gathered
for the plain products' shapes. The head route
opened with it as a side effect: nothing in the
flip's decision rule spoke for the head, whose
own verdict protocol (bench/k21-finish-2026-11-06.md)
had never run on the card. A shared gate lets one
route's proof silently arm another route. The
codebase's standing pattern for an unproven route
is a dedicated fail-closed switch (K22, K23,
coopmat: exact `1` enables, everything else off);
the head route now follows it.

## The change

- New env `WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD`
  (`compute::K21F_HEAD_ENV`), resolved once at
  backend construction by `resolve_k21f_head` on
  the exact-`1` fail-closed pattern, stored as
  `WgpuCompute::k21f_head`, and logged by name at
  construction: `k21f head config: enabled=<bool>
  (env WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD, only "1" enables)`.
  Semantic matrix:

  | value | resolves |
  |---|---|
  | unset | OFF (the shipped default) |
  | `1` (trimmed) | ON |
  | `0`, `true`, `11`, empty, any other text | OFF, fail-closed |

- `session::try_mmv_q5k_finish` now requires BOTH
  gates through the pure helper
  `k21f_head_admits(head_switch, max_rows, batch)`:
  the head switch on AND the shared band admitting
  the batch (the same `mmv_band_admits` arithmetic
  as before). Batch 1 remains K3 (the band floor
  refuses it at every switch position). The
  fallback on any refusal is the exact K3 fused
  call the site built before the route existed,
  asked for the identical finish; the finish math
  order is untouched.
- The resolved switch is recorded in both
  sessions' diag-capture manifests as the
  `k21f_head` resolved-config pair, beside
  `k22_mmq`, so a capture diff shows the route's
  position by name.
- Doc corrections where the old rule was stated:
  the `try_mmv_q5k_finish` and block-head site
  comments and the `mmv_band_admits` doc in
  session.rs; the construction comment, accessor
  docs, and env doc in compute.rs; the K21F
  paragraph in kernels/mod.rs; the routing
  paragraph in the K21F kernel module's header
  (docs only; the kernel's code and tests are
  untouched). bench/k21-finish-2026-11-06.md gains
  a supersession section pointing here; its
  earlier sections stand as the historical record
  of the design and the routing as landed.

## Pins

- `compute::k21f_head_switch_resolution`: the
  resolver matrix above, plus the env-name pin.
- `session::k21f_head_gate_requires_both_halves`:
  switch off admits nothing at ceiling 16 or even
  `u32::MAX` (the default-construction position:
  no K21F is prepared with the shared ceiling at
  its shipped 16); switch on admits exactly what
  the band admits and nothing when the ceiling is
  closed.
- The two pre-existing band pins stay, reframed as
  the gate's band half; the batch-1 pin now also
  asserts the combined gate refuses batch 1 with
  the switch on.
- `tests/k21f_head_routing.rs` is now three arms:
  switch-off (default construction; malformed
  switch values land in this arm by construction,
  which is the fail-closed pin), band-closed, and
  both-gates-open. The open arm requires
  `WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD=1` in addition to the
  ceiling at 16. All arms keep the CPU-agreement
  half at the cross-backend bar. On this GPU-less
  VM all three arms self-skip; arm selection was
  verified with `--nocapture` in three env
  positions (unset: switch-off arm proceeds;
  `=1` with ceiling 16: only the open arm proceeds;
  `=true`: switch-off arm proceeds and the open arm
  skips naming the head switch).

## Re-enable recipe (for the fix lane)

```
WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD=1
WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=16   # or unset: 16 is the shipped default
```

Both gates open, the route behaves exactly as it
did in the defaults-confirmation session, finish
stamps and all, so the fix lane reproduces the
failure and proves its fix in the same position
that failed.

## Rollback, and the reopen criterion

This guard IS the rollback from the broken
default: with it merged, shipped defaults serve
the block head on K3 while every plain MMV route
keeps its cap-16 opening. (On a tree without the
guard, the only rollback remains
`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=1`, which closes all
MMV routes.) To close just the head route by hand
on a guarded tree: leave `WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD`
unset or set it to anything but `1`.

The switch's default may move to on, or the guard
may come out, only when ALL of the following hold
on the card, on the real files, with the switch
explicitly on:

1. Speculative identity PASSES at depth 1 and at
   depth 6 (the two depths that diverged), in the
   same runs that show the exposure stamps.
2. GOLDEN PASSES in the same runs.
3. The exposure check shows `k21_q5k_mmv_finish`
   firing at the block batches (the pass must be
   the route's, not the control's).

Fixture-scale agreement does not count toward the
criterion: it passed while the real file failed.

## Gates on this VM

- `cargo test -p wgpu-compute`: 265 passed,
  0 failed, 28 test binaries (base 262; +1 resolver
  pin, +1 combined-gate pin, +1 integration arm).
- `cargo test -p dflash`: 24 passed.
- `cargo test -p itak-spec`: 49 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p wgpu-compute --all-targets
  -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean (one fmt pass over
  the new construction log line).
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`: clean.

Still owed to a card session (the fix lane's):
the three integration arms executing on the card,
and the reopen criterion above. Nothing in this
lane ran on the server.

## SUPERSESSION: the default flipped back to on (lane/k21f-default-flip, 2026-11-07)

The reopen criterion written above has been MET
and this guard's default is superseded. The chain:

1. The root cause was found by the read-only math
   audit and fixed in lane/k21f-mask-fix: a
   truncated dequant mask in the K21F shader
   (`0x0f0f0f` for `0x0f0f0f0f` on the qc line),
   dropping one nibble in sixteen elements per
   super-block. Record:
   bench/k21f-mask-fix-2026-11-07.md. The wave17
   diagnosis (bench/k21f-divergence-diagnosis-2026-11-07.md)
   measured the failure at the real geometry and
   carries the parent reconciliation of its
   attribution.
2. The wave18 card retest
   (bench/k21f-retest-2026-11-07.md) ran this
   note's reopen protocol against the fixed tree
   with the switch explicitly on: IDENTITY and
   GOLDEN PASS at depth 1 and depth 6 in the same
   runs that show the exposure stamps (criterion
   items 1-3 above), the kernel gates executing
   green on the card, and K21F's finished output
   bit-identical to K3's at the real head
   geometry. Verdict recorded there: REOPEN
   CRITERION MET.
3. Lane `lane/k21f-default-flip` therefore moved
   the switch's default: unset now resolves ON,
   in the MMV ceiling flip's shape. New semantic
   matrix (the matrix above is superseded):

   | value | resolves |
   |---|---|
   | unset | ON (the shipped default) |
   | `1` (trimmed) | ON |
   | `0` (trimmed) | OFF (the explicit off; the one-variable rollback) |
   | any other text | OFF, fail-closed, logged by name at construction |

   The switch itself, the combined gate
   (`k21f_head_admits`: switch AND shared band),
   the batch-1 floor, and the K3 fused fallback
   are unchanged; only the unset position moved.
   The flip is recorded in
   bench/k21f-default-flip-2026-11-07.md.

Everything above this section stands as the
historical record of why the guard existed and
what it demanded. The re-enable recipe section is
moot (the route is live at the shipped default);
the rollback now is `WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD=0`.

divergence at stream index 23 (plain 589, spec 1573;
prompt "The capital of France is", spec_generate_gpu
both mode, 64 tokens) with numbers. Raw logs:
~/gpu-wave17/logs17/ on the server. Bundles:
~/gpu-wave17/bench/failures/ (20261107T060222Z-leg1-
spec-default-d1, 20261107T060302Z-leg1-spec-default-d6,
20261107T060348Z-leg1-spec-control-d1, plus the failed
first shape-probe build 20261107T060946Z, fixed and
rerun). Tenants stopped before card work (VRAM
33,271,808 B) and restored after (8,932,147,200 B);
production llama-server never touched; no reboot.

## Read the reconciliation section before citing attribution

This note's measurements stand. Its original attribution
(the finish, not the product core) does NOT survive the
parent reconciliation at the end of this file: the
kernel probe never measured K21F's own raw product, and
the static math audit proved a product-core defect in
K21F's shader text. The numbers below are the pre-fix
baseline the wave18 retest compares against.

## Reproduction (this staging, this session)

- Default, depth 1: rounds=37 proposed=36 accepted=26,
  IDENTITY FAIL, GOLDEN PASS. Streams agree through
  index 22; index 23 plain 589, spec 1573.
- Default, depth 6: rounds=26 proposed=147 accepted=37,
  IDENTITY FAIL, GOLDEN PASS.
- Control (WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=1), depth 1:
  rounds=38, IDENTITY PASS, GOLDEN PASS.

Identical to the defaults-confirmation session on its
own staging, as expected.

## Method 1: diag capture cannot yield top-2

WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=capture runs at depth 1 (default and
control) and depth 6 (default). What survives to disk
in spec_generate_gpu is one `block` record per round:
the target session's verify block forwards,
fingerprinted over every row's finished logits
(values=404096 = 2 x 202,048 at depth 1; 1,414,336 =
7 x 202,048 at depth 6; 37 records at depth 1, 26 at
depth 6, matching the round counts). diag_diff on the
depth-1 pair: manifests differ only in
resolved_config.mmv_max_rows (16 vs 1, the intended
single variable); the first capture divergence is at
seq 0, field hash: the very first verify block's logits
already differ between the arms, consistent with a head
deviation present on every call whose early argmaxes
simply had margins too large to flip. But a block
record carries only the FNV-1a hash: no argmax, no
logits, and the argmax record kind folds its logit into
the hash rather than storing it. Capture can prove the
verify forwards differ from the first round; it cannot
produce a top-2, a margin, or a per-element delta.

## Method 2: in-situ head comparison at the divergence

A throwaway probe (k21f_insitu_probe.rs, server staging
~/gpu-wave17/crates/itak-spec/examples/, never
committed) replays the plain greedy stream through a
ResidentSession with batch-1 forwards, saves the
batch-1 distribution that emits index 23, then rewinds
and runs the two block geometries that could have
produced that distribution inside a round through
forward_block_capturing: geometry A [g22, 1573] (index
23 as a round's first row) and geometry B [g21, g22]
(index 23 as the bonus row). Three arms: shipped
defaults, gate closed, and a head-only isolation
(ceiling 16 with all nine band cells set to "1", so
every projection falls back to GEMV while the head
still routes to K21F; the finish stamp fired).

Under K3 (batch-1 reference, both probe processes agree
to 6e-6): top-1 is 589 at 15.359117, top-2 is 1573 at
14.976315. **The top-2 margin at the divergence is
+0.382801.**

- Control arm: both block rows are BIT-IDENTICAL to the
  batch-1 distribution (max-abs delta 0.000000 across
  all 202,048 logits, both geometries). The all-GEMV
  block forward is exactly the batch-1 math;
  block-vs-single drift is zero in this stack.
- Default arm: both block rows flip. 1573 at 15.268591
  over 589 at 15.186872, margin -0.081719. **Delta at
  589: -0.172245. Delta at 1573: +0.292275.** Combined
  swing 0.464520 against a margin of 0.382801, which is
  the flip. Max-abs delta across the vocab: **2.040238
  at id 157652**; RMS delta 4.397e-1.
- Head-only arm: the same row to ~3e-6 (1573 at
  15.268585, 589 at 15.186869; delta[589] -0.172242,
  delta[1573] +0.292279; max-abs 2.040238 at the same id
  157652). Band-routed projection drift inside the block
  forward contributes at most ~1e-5 to the head row.
  The K21F head call alone, on identical inputs,
  produces the entire in-situ delta.

## Method 3: product vs finish split on the real weights

A second throwaway probe (k21f_kernel_probe.rs, server
staging ~/gpu-wave17/crates/wgpu-compute/examples/)
loads the real head tensor (output.weight, Q5_K,
6656 -> 202,048) and runs, on identical synthetic
inputs at batches 2 and 7 (the two verify widths),
three input distributions (uniform, unit-RMS Gaussian,
Gaussian with outlier dimensions): K3 plain product,
K21 plain product, K3 fused finish, K21F fused finish
(softcap mode, scale 0.19611613, cap 20.0), and an f64
host reference. 27 rows measured. In every row:

- max|prodK21 - prodK3| = 0.000000.
- max|prodK21 - f64 ref| and max|prodK3 - f64 ref| are
  both at most 1.0e-5.
- K3 finish fidelity, max|finK3 - finish64(prodK3)|:
  1.07e-6 to 1.91e-6.
- K21F finish fidelity, max|finK21F - finish64(prodK21)|:
  0.31 to 1.87, and equal to max|finK21F - finK3| row
  for row (batch 2 gauss row 1: 1.741 against 1.741250;
  batch 7 gauss row 5: 1.868 against 1.868393).

Discriminators (two further probes, same staging):

- Shape and mode (k21f_shape_probe, batch 2 gauss): the
  fidelity error is the same in the workgroup-tree and
  subgroup reduction shapes (agreeing to 1e-6) and in
  FINISH_SCALE (row 1: 1.745408) as in FINISH_SOFTCAP
  (1.741250).
- Ratio (k21f_ratio_probe, scale mode): the implied
  ratio got/(scale*prod21) over elements with
  |want| > 0.5 spans min -1.78 to max +4.02; at the five
  largest elements of a row it wanders 0.897 to 1.216.
  The worst elements have near-zero true values (prod
  0.178 becomes -1.710; prod -1.185 becomes +0.936).

The lane read these results as: the deviation is
manufactured after the product, additive and
element-varying, on the order of one super-block
segment's partial sum. See the reconciliation for why
that reading is consistent with, and superseded by, the
product-core defect the audit proved.

## Why the existing gates missed it (lane's reading)

tests/k21_finish.rs gates K21F against the CPU
composition and against K3 at inn=512 and inn=768 with
synthetic Q5_K headers, tolerance about 1e-3.
tests/k21f_head_routing.rs holds block logits to the
cross-backend bar (max-abs under 0.5) at fixture scale;
the in-situ max delta at real geometry is 2.04. (The
audit's reading differs on why the finish tests missed
it: they never executed on a GPU at all before this
wave. Both readings agree on the missing pin: a
real-geometry, on-card gate. The mask-fix lane added
VM-runnable shader-text pins for the proven defect; the
real-geometry gate remains the retest's job.)

## Parent reconciliation (added at filing, 2026-11-07)

Two investigations ran in parallel and appeared to
disagree. They do not.

1. The static math audit (read-only, against the same
   tree) found the defect by reading K21F's own shader
   text: in crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/
   k21_q5k_mmv_finish.rs the qc dequant line masked its
   word with 0x0f0f0f (24-bit) instead of 0x0f0f0f0f,
   zeroing the fourth byte, so 16 of 256 elements per
   Q5_K super-block lose their entire low nibble. Both
   sibling kernels (plain K21, K3) carry the correct
   mask. That is a product-core defect, proven in
   source, and it is fixed on main (6ee2d68).
2. The kernel probe above never ran K21F's raw product:
   K21F exposes only the fused call, so its "finish
   fidelity" compared K21F's finished output against
   the finish of PLAIN K21's product. A product error
   inside K21F therefore presents, in that comparison,
   exactly as a finish error. The probe's other
   findings fit the mask defect one for one: the
   corruption is additive and segment-sized (dropped
   nibble terms over one sub-block segment), appears
   identically in the linear scale mode (it is upstream
   of the finish map), in both reduction shapes (it is
   upstream of the reduction too), with a non-constant
   ratio (an additive error is not a scale error), and
   hits hardest where the true value is near zero
   (dropped terms dominate small sums).
3. The lane's inference that the defect "engages only
   at 26 super-blocks per row" is not established and
   is not needed: the mask defect fires at every
   geometry, and the fixture gates that might have
   caught it at 512/768 wide never executed on a GPU
   before this wave (they skip on adapterless
   machines). What the real-geometry runs add is the
   size of the effect at the geometry that matters:
   margin +0.382801 at the split, deltas -0.172245 /
   +0.292275 at the two ids, max-abs 2.040238.
4. Arbitration: the wave18 retest reruns this note's
   kernel and in-situ probes against the fixed tree.
   If fidelity returns to the 1e-6 class and the
   in-situ delta collapses, the single-defect account
   is confirmed end to end. If a residual remains, this
   note's numbers bound it and the hunt reopens with
   them.

===== FILE: bench/k21f-mask-fix-2026-11-07.md =====
# K21F qc mask fix (2026-11-07)

Lane `lane/k21f-mask-fix`, based on main f57c087. The one-token
kernel fix, the test-gap closure, and the typo-class sweep. The
card retest is a separate lane after merge; nothing here ran on
the server.

## The bug

`crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/k21_q5k_mmv_finish.rs`, in the
generated shader header (the per-row body literal): the qc
dequant line masked its weight word with a 24-bit literal,

```wgsl
let qc = vec4<f32>(unpack4xU8(w1 & 0x0f0f0fu)) + 16.0 * bits_c;
```

where every sibling line, and the same line in
`k21_q5k_mmv.rs` and `k3_q5k_gemv.rs`, carries the 32-bit
`0x0f0f0f0fu`. One `0f` byte dropped out of the literal when
the finish variant was written as a copy of K21's text.

## Blast radius

The mask zeroes the fourth byte of `w1` before the nibble
unpack, so that byte's low nibble is always read as zero.
Per Q5_K super-block (256 elements), 16 elements lose their
entire low nibble: the qc elements at sub-blocks 4 and 6,
position `l0+3` in each affected quad. Each affected weight
dequantizes low by `nibble * d * scale` (nibble 0..15): the
error is deterministic and one-sided (always an
underestimate, never noise in both directions), which is why
it survived casual inspection of outputs while corrupting
them. Only the finish-carrying copy was wrong: plain K21
(the non-finish MMV product) always had the correct mask, so
the defect lived exactly on the resident block head route
and nowhere else. On the real file it first flipped a token
at stream position 23 of the defaults-confirmation identity
run (bench/defaults-confirmation-2026-11-07.md); the
read-only math audit against main 7940bcf then isolated it
to this line, with everything else in K21F (finish form and
position, accumulation order, partial combination,
plumbing) audited clean against K3.

## Why the VM gates could not catch it

Three gaps stacked:

1. The execution tests that would have caught it
   (tests/k21_finish.rs, the resident suites) are
   device-gated and self-skip on this GPU-less VM; the card
   protocol for the routing was still owed when it shipped.
2. The in-module shader-text test pinned only the qa line's
   mask of the four dequant lines (qa/qb/qc/qd), in both
   K21F and its K21 sibling. Three of four lines were
   unguarded text.
3. The routing test's fixture (tests/k21f_head_routing.rs)
   masked its Q5_K scale bytes with `& 0x07` and used
   d = 0.005, shrinking a dropped-nibble error far under
   its 0.5 max-abs bar.

## The fix and its companions

- The mask: `0x0f0f0fu` -> `0x0f0f0f0fu` on the qc line.
  Nothing else in the kernel changes.
- Both shader-text tests now pin ALL FOUR dequant lines
  verbatim (qa/qb/qc/qd) and carry a negative pin: the
  truncated literal `0x0f0f0fu` must never appear in the
  generated text. These are pure text tests; they run on
  the GPU-less VM.
- The routing fixture's Q5_K scale bytes are full-range
  random bytes (the k21_finish fixture's discipline),
  widening only the head tensor; the Q4_K fixture tensors
  keep their calibrated construction, and the argmax +
  max-abs assertions are unchanged. The finish (logit
  scale 0.196, tanh softcap) still compresses the logits
  the 0.5 bar reads, so honest reassociation drift does
  not widen toward the bar; the widened fixture's
  GPU-vs-CPU agreement itself is exercised by the card
  retest below, since the routing test is device-gated
  and skips here. The text pins above are the gate that
  runs everywhere.

## Demonstration: the pins bite

With the buggy mask temporarily restored in the finish
kernel, the extended test FAILS:


===== FILE: bench/k22-mmq-2026-11-05.md =====
# K22 Q4_K MMQ occupancy prototype (2026-11-05)

Lane: lane/k22-mmq, from main 060546b. Status: built and
gated on the VM; NOT measured on the card. The server
verdict protocol is at the bottom. The kernel ships
behind `WGPU_COMPUTE_K22_MMQ=1`, default OFF; at shipped
defaults the session ladder is byte-identical to the
ladder every prior proof ran on.

## The problem, from the measurements

Prefill profile (bench/prefill-profile-2026-11-05.md,
cleared RX 7900 XTX, real Glimmer Q4_K_M, 1,022 tokens):

| kernel | count | total_ms | share | GB/s | % FP32 peak |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| k13_q4k_mmq | 2,912 | 4,199.9 | 63.1% | 46.4 | 17.2% |
| k14_q6k_mmq | 832 | 1,342.0 | 20.2% | 34.6 | 8.8% |
| k3_q5k_gemv (lm_head) | 16 | 22.8 | 0.3% | 649.5 | 3.1% |

Shader autopsy (bench/shader-autopsy-2026-11-04.md):
K13 compiles to VGPR 256, the architectural per-wave
maximum, zero spills, LDS 41,984 B reported. Occupancy
per CU is at the floor, which costs latency hiding; the
GEMV control case in the same run proves the memory
system can stream at ~650 GB/s. Verdict in the profile's
own words: neither stream-bound nor compute-bound;
occupancy/instruction bound. The fix must live inside
the kernel: fewer live values per thread.

## What K22 is

K13's exact math and contracts, llama.cpp `mul_mmq`'s
register organization:

- Same staged values, same K12 Q8_1 input layout, same
  bindings, same params, same `[batch][out]` output, so
  the session swaps forms without moving a byte. The
  prepare contract is K13's (batch 1..=64, same named
  refusals).
- Tile coverage unchanged: 64 output rows x 64 batch
  rows per workgroup, same dispatch grid as K13 m64.
- 128 threads instead of 256. Warp tiling mirrors
  llama: four warps, each on a 16-output-row x 64-batch
  warp tile. Per thread: 4 output rows x 8 batch rows =
  32 f32 accumulators.
- Per 32-element sub-block, the thread loads its four
  rows' operands into a named register cache (8 packed
  words + the `(d*scale, dmin*min)` pair per row), then
  walks its eight batch columns one at a time: load the
  column's 8 words + `(d, s)` pair, run four scalar i32
  dots (8 DP4A each), fold each into its accumulator
  immediately. No `isum` array, no fold phase.
- One staging change: the weight tile's row stride is
  padded 64 -> 65 words, the skew K13 already applies
  to its activation tile. K22's mapping puts four
  distinct output rows on one wavefront load instruction
  (K13's puts two); at a 64-word stride those addresses
  share one LDS bank. Staging total 41,472 B (K13 m64:
  41,216 B; the +256 B is exactly the padding).

## Register arithmetic

Source-level live values at the inner peak. K13's row is
read off its generated shader text; its compiled result
is the autopsy's measured 256.

K13 (per generated sub-block scope, unrolled x8 with no
barrier between sub-blocks):

| live set | values |
|---|---|
| f32 accumulators `acc[16]` | 16 |
| i32 `isum[16]`, live across all 8 word steps | 16 |
| operand lets per word step (4 weight + 4 activation words) | 8 |
| fold pairs `c[4]` + `dm[4]` (vec2) | 16 |
| row/col indices, staging and address state | ~15-25 |
| named peak | ~75-85 |

The gap between ~80 named and 256 compiled is the
scheduler's freedom: the eight unrolled sub-blocks are
independent until their folds, so latency hiding rewards
keeping several sub-blocks' operand windows (and their
staging address chains) in flight at once. The autopsy
cannot attribute the 256 more precisely from outside;
what it proves is that the compiled form, not the
algorithm, is the cost.

K22 (per generated sub-block scope):

| live set | values |
|---|---|
| f32 accumulators `acc[32]` | 32 |
| register cache: 4 rows x (8 words + vec2 pair) | 40 |
| column operand: 8 words + vec2 pair | 10 |
| scalar dot accumulators in flight (one per row) | 4 |
| row/col index lets, live across the K loop | 12 |
| loop/address state | ~6 |
| named peak | ~104 |

Expected compiled band: 96-128 VGPR. Even if the
scheduler hoists one full sub-block of cache loads
(+40), it lands near 140, still off the cap. At 128
VGPR, resident waves per SIMD double versus the
256-VGPR floor. This is a prediction with its arithmetic
shown; step 0 of the verdict protocol measures it, and
the prototype's claim stands or falls there.

LDS traffic per DP4A also improves on paper: K13 reads
64 operand words per thread per sub-block for 128 dots
(0.50 reads/dot); K22 reads 96 for 256 dots (0.375),
because the A-side cache is reused across 8 columns
instead of 4. The DP4A count is identical (2,048 per
thread per super-block at K22's 32 outputs; 262,144 per
workgroup per super-block either way).

## Deliberately not copied from llama's mul_mmq

- **Its Q4_K staging repack.** llama interleaves two
  16-element halves into each staged word
  (`vals0 | vals1 << 4`) and permutes the activation
  order to match, extracting nibbles by shifts inside
  the dot. That halves the register cache's words per
  row entry (4 vs K22's 8; llama's whole cache_a is 48
  values to K22's 40 for half the rows). Not copied
  because it changes the staged byte layout and the
  B-side element order: a second design variable and a
  new correctness surface, in a prototype whose single
  variable is register organization. It is the named
  follow-up if K22's organization wins but its cache
  still costs too much.
- **The coopmat (WMMA) form.** The profile note ranks
  it below the plain rework: same 650 GB/s streaming
  ceiling, more risk, a second code path.
- **Load width 4 in `mm_load_vec_a`** (the mul_mm f32
  path's staging width). K22 stages from DRAM exactly
  as K13 does (the staging loops are K13's, with the
  one stride change); the A-operand width that matters
  for the register question is the LDS-to-register
  cache load, which is word-granular in both K13 and
  K22.

## Routing

`mmq_product_q4k` in session.rs: wide (K15) first past
its threshold, then K22 when `backend.k22_mmq()` is on
and its pipeline exists, then K13. A K22 prepare refusal
is logged by name and K13 serves the projection, the
ladder's standing rule. The switch is resolved at
backend construction from `WGPU_COMPUTE_K22_MMQ`; only
the exact value `1` enables it (fail-closed, unit-tested).
The pipeline itself is built at construction regardless,
so a shader defect fails there, not on first routed use.

  93 passed, including K22's own: staging bytes
  (41,472, exactly 256 over K13 m64), shader structure
  (@workgroup_size(128), both 4,160-word staging
  arrays, `array<f32, 32>` accumulators, 2,048
  dot4I8Packed calls, no `isum` text), and full Naga
  parse + validation of the one generated shader. The
  `k22_mmq` integration tests (3) and the
  `shader_compile` K22 leg pass with the GPU legs
  skipping cleanly, as designed on a machin

## Server verdict protocol

Preconditions: card cleared per David's order, phase
lock held, staging synced to the lane commit and
hash-verified, the prefill profile harness
(`prefill_profile`, from lane/prefill-profile) available
for step 3.

0. **Shader autopsy first.** Compile K22 in isolation
   (the shader_compile leg) under
   `RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats,asm,cs` with a private
   `MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR`. Read VGPR, spilled VGPR,
   scratch, LDS. The prototype's premise is the VGPR
   line: if it reads 256 (or spills), the organization
   failed in compiled form and steps 1-3 are moot;
   stop and report.
1. **Correctness on the card.** `cargo test -p
   wgpu-compute --test k22_mmq` must actually execute
   (not skip): reference and K13 parity at batches 16,
   32, 64 and the 62-row tail, plus the band refusals.
   Also `resident_session` with `WGPU_COMPUTE_K22_MMQ=1`:
   identity + golden on the real file before any speed
   number is read (the dispatch-count pins will move by
   design under the env; the token checks are the gate).
2. **Kernel-level A/B.** The `mmv_sweep`-style per-tensor
   bench is small-batch; for the MMQ band use the
   profile harness: same 1,022-token prompt, diag timing
   on, K22 env on vs off. Compare the `k22_q4k_mmq` row
   against K13's recorded 4,199.9 ms / 46.4 GB/s and the
   total GPU time against 6,659 ms. Report the achieved
   GB/s and % of FP32 peak beside K13's.
3. **Prefill A/B, session level.** `glimmer_generate
   --gpu` wall on the same prompt, env on vs off, three
   runs each, timing-off walls compared (the profile's
   off wall was 8,116-8,169 ms).
4. **No-leak check.** With the env unset, plain decode
   and the spec verdict harness must reproduce their
   recorded numbers (decode 35.45 tok/s class); K22 is
   unreachable with the switch off, so any movement is a
   routing leak, not a kernel result.

Decision rule: the switch's default stays OFF unless
step 0 shows VGPR off the 256 cap with zero spills AND
step 1 passes in full AND step 2 shows the Q4_K MMQ
line materially faster (a wash inside run-to-run noise
is not a win; the profile's two runs agreed to 0.5%).
Any default flip is a separate change with this note's
numbers attached, and the Q6_K sibling (K14, same
disease at 20.2% of GPU time) gets its own prototype
before the pair is called fixed.

## What could still make K22 lose to K13 on the card

Honest list, in the order I would bet on them:

1. **ACO ignores the source organization anyway.** The
   scheduler may hoist and interleave K22's sub-blocks
   just as it does K13's and land at or near 256 VGPR.
   The braced scopes bound live ranges in the source,
   but nothing in WGSL forces an allocation. Step 0
   exists precisely to answer this cheaply.
2. **The 256-thread workgroup was hiding something.**
   K22 halves the threads per tile; if K13's rate was
   partly thread-parallelism over the staging loops
   (256 threads stage the same bytes in half the
   passes), K22's staging phase per super-block round
   runs longer, and at 52 layers x 26 columns that adds
   up inside the same barrier structure.
3. **LDS read pattern.** K22's cache loads are
   broadcast-friendly by construction, but its B-side
   reads stride across the skewed activation tile in
   (wsic, cc) order; a bank pattern I got wrong costs
   ds_load throughput on every one of the 96 reads per
   sub-block. The 4-way weight-side conflict the skew
   fixes could also reappear through the vec2 pair
   arrays (8-byte elements pair lanes differently).
4. **The fold is more frequent per accumulator.**
   K22 folds 32 times per sub-block per thread (once
   per (row, column)) where K13 folds 16; the fold's
   f32 ops per output are the same, but K22's are
   interleaved with the dots, lengthening the dependency
   chain each accumulator waits on if the scheduler
   cannot find independent work inside one thread.
   Occupancy is supposed to cover exactly this; if it
   does not, the chain shows.
5. **Instruction count.** Same DP4A count, but K22
   issues more LDS load instructions per super-block
   per thread (768 word loads vs K13's 512) and more
   address arithmetic for the cache indexing. At 17%
   of FP32 peak the kernel is not dot-throughput-bound,
   but it could be issue-bound in a way the profile
   cannot distinguish from occupancy.

## Server verdict, 2026-11-06: step 0 FAILS the premise; steps 1-3 moot per protocol

From main `c439e3af45e30275601129568e3e9cb3a89590cb`,
staged at `~/gpu-wave11` (manifest-verified), cleared
card (guard 33,271,808 bytes), phase lock held. RADV
dump in `~/gpu-wave11/logs11/k22-autopsy-dump.err` on
the server.

**Step 0, autopsy.** The `shader_compile k22` leg
compiled K22's one generated shader (the geometry is
fixed, so there is exactly one variant) twice under
`RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats,asm,cs` with a private
`MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR` (identical driver pipeline
hash both times; the leg itself passed):

| VGPR | spilled VGPR | scratch | LDS | code size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **256** | 0 | 0 B | 41,984 B | 51,732 B |

VGPR reads **256, the architectural cap, the same
number as K13**. Zero spills and zero scratch, and
the LDS is the designed staging class, but the
prototype's single design variable was register
organization, and in compiled form the organization
did not survive: ACO hoisted and interleaved the
braced column scopes and re-inflated the live range
to the cap. This is lose-condition 1 in this note's
own list ("ACO ignores the source organization
anyway"), the one it ranked most likely.

**Protocol consequence.** Step 0's written rule: if
VGPR reads 256 (or spills), the organization failed
in compiled form and steps 1-3 are moot; stop and
report. Accordingly the k22_mmq numeric tests, the
resident identity + golden run under
`WGPU_COMPUTE_K22_MMQ=1`, the prefill A/B, and the
no-leak check were NOT run in this session; there is
no K22 speed number and none is claimed. The kernel
remains in the tree behind its exact-value env switch
(off by default, unreachable when unset), which is
where a compiled-form failure belongs: the source
organization is a faithful port of llama.cpp's
mul_mmq shape, but the register outcome that shape
depends on is a compiler behavior RADV's ACO does
not reproduce from WGSL source structure.

**Decision against the note's rule.** The default
stays OFF: the rule's first condition (step 0 shows
VGPR off the 256 cap with zero spills) fails on the
VGPR half. The MMQ occupancy problem (K13/K22 both at
the cap, 43.5 GB/s combined in the prefill profile)
is therefore not a source-organization problem this
codebase can restructure its way out of; the
remaining named lever for the prefill band is the
profile note's attack 3 (coopmat MMQ, a different
instruction path entirely), still ranked below the
plain rework and still unbuilt.

===== END FILE: bench/k22-mmq-2026-11-05.md =====

===== FILE: bench/k23-mmq-repack-2026-11-06.md =====
# K23: the Q4_K MMQ staging repack - design, layout arithmetic, and the card verdict protocol

Lane `lane/k23-mmq-repack`, built 2026-11-06. State: code
complete and VM-gated (counts below); the card verdict
protocol is written and NOT yet run (the parent serializes
card time). The routing switch defaults OFF; nothing in the
shipped ladder changes with the switch unset.

## The problem, from the measurements

The prefill profile (`bench/prefill-profile-2026-11-05.md`)
put the Q4_K MMQ kernel (K13) at 4,199.9 ms of a 6,659 ms
GPU total for the 1,022-token prefill - 63.1% of GPU time
streaming at 46.4 GB/s against a card that streams a GEMV
at 649.5 GB/s in the same run. K13 compiles to the VGPR
256 cap. K22 attacked the register organization and hit
the same cap in compiled form (autopsy in
`bench/k22-mmq-2026-11-05.md`: VGPR 256, zero spills, LDS
41,984 B - ACO re-inflated the organization, steps 1-3
never ran). The parity extraction
(`bench/llama-parity-specs-2026-11-06.md`, gap 2) then
named the one structural difference left: the staging.
K13 stages a whole 256-element super-block column per
barrier round, scale pairs interleaved beside the data
they scale, one 65-word skew on the activation rows.
llama's MMQ stages in 128-element rounds, qs arrays
pitched with a skew, scale pairs split into their own
arrays. K23 copies that staging onto K13's organization
and changes nothing else, so whatever the card says is
attributable to the staging alone.

## What K23 is

A new env-gated Q4_K MMQ kernel
(`crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/k23_q4k_mmq.rs`) with
K13's tile coverage (64 output rows x 64 batch rows),
K13's thread organization (256 threads, sixteen
output-row groups by sixteen batch-row groups, a 4x4
sub-tile per thread, the `isum` array, scalar
`dot4I8Packed`, immediate per-sub-block folds in K13's
exact order and expression), K13's bindings, params,
prepare contract (batch 1..=64), and `[batch][out]`
output layout. A plan can swap K13, K22, and K23 without
moving a byte. The single design variable is the
staging, transcribed from llama's mul_mmq_cm1 (see the
layout arithmetic).

## Layout arithmetic, with llama citations

llama sources are the vulkan-shaders tree at llama.cpp
a7af149, verified sha256-identical between the server
tree and the VM mirror by the parity note.

**The round quantum.** `BK = 32` (mul_mmq_cm1.comp:89),
`BK_STEP = 4` (mul_mmq_cm1.comp:93, the non-`MUL_MAT_ID`
form): one staging round covers BK x BK_STEP = 128 K
elements. A Q4_K super-block column is 256 elements, so
a column is two rounds: stage, barrier, four sub-blocks
of dots, barrier, twice per column (K13: one round of
eight sub-blocks, two barriers per column; K23: four
barriers per column).

**The pitch.** `QPITCH = BK_STEP * (BK / 4) + 4 = 36`
(mul_mmq_cm1.comp:97). Each staged row segment holds 32
words of one round's qs data plus a 4-word skew.

**The split arrays** (mul_mmq_cm1.comp:99-110), with
llama's BM = BN replaced by this tile's 64:

| array | llama declaration | K23 declaration | bytes |
|---|---|---|---|
| w_qs | `buf_a_qs[BM * QPITCH]` (:99) | `array<u32, 2304>` (64 x 36) | 9,216 |
| x_qs | `buf_b_qs[BN * QPITCH]` (:106) | `array<u32, 2304>` (64 x 36) | 9,216 |
| w_dm | `buf_a_dm[BM * BK_STEP]` (:101) | `array<vec2<f32>, 256>` (4 x 64) | 2,048 |
| x_d | `buf_b_d[BN * BK_STEP]` (:107) | `array<f32, 256>` (4 x 64) | 1,024 |
| x_s | `buf_b_s[BN * BK_STEP]` (:110) | `array<f32, 256>` (4 x 64) | 1,024 |

Staged set total: **22,528 B**, against K13's 41,216 B
designed (41,984 B compiled class) and K22's 41,472 B at
the same tile. The set halves because a round stages
half the K span; the pitch adds 4 words per row per qs
array (512 B across both).

**A-side staged addresses.** llama's Q4_K
`block_a_to_shmem` (mul_mmq_cm1_funcs.glsl, the
`DATA_A_Q4_K` branch at :246, the function at :274)
writes `buf_a_qs[buf_ib * QPITCH + ks * (BK / 4) +
loadr * 2 + {0,1}]`, loadr in 0..4 walking the four
word-pairs of a sub-block's 8-word group; the staged
word is the raw Q4_K word masked `& 0x0F0F0F0F` for an
even sub-block or `(raw >> 4) & 0x0F0F0F0F` for an odd
one (the `block_a_load` nibble select on `ib % 2`).
K23's store is `w_qs[n * 36 + ks * 8 + loadr * 2 +
{0,1}]`, the same index arithmetic. The scale pair is
deposited by the loadr == 0 task at
`buf_a_dm[ks * BM + buf_ib]` in llama; K23 writes
`w_dm[ks * 64 + n]`. The VALUE keeps K13's convention
`(d * scale, dmin * min)`: cm1 stages
`(d * scale, -(dmin * min))` and subtracts in its fold,
K13's fold text carries the negation
(`acc += c.x * (dm.x * isum) - c.y * dm.y`), and K23's
fold text is K13's byte for byte, so the pair's sign
convention stays with the fold it feeds.

**B-side staged addresses.** llama's `block_b_load`
(mul_mmq_cm1_funcs.glsl, just above :529) loads
`data_b[ib_outer].qs[ib_inner * 2 + loadr]`, one ivec4
of a `block_q8_1_x4` group, loadr in 0..2 covering the
block's two 4-word halves; `block_b_to_shmem` (:529)
scatters its components to
`buf_ib * QPITCH + ks * (BK / 4) + loadr * 4 + 0..3` and,
on loadr == 0, writes `buf_b_d[ks * BN + buf_ib]` and
`buf_b_s[ks * BN + buf_ib]`. K23's store is
`x_qs[m * 36 + ks * 8 + loadr * 4 + c]` with
`x_d[ks * 64 + m]` / `x_s[ks * 64 + m]` on loadr == 0 -
the same arithmetic over K12's flat streams (see the
honesty paragraph).

**Consumption addresses.** Per sub-block ks of a round,
a thread reads `x_qs[m * 36 + ks * 8 + w]` and
`w_qs[n * 36 + ks * 8 + w]` for its 4x4 sub-tile,
`c = w_dm[ks * 64 + n]`, and
`dm = vec2(x_d[ks * 64 + m], x_s[ks * 64 + m])`.

**What the de-interleave means on our buffers.** The
gap note's phrase "de-interleaves the x4-packed Q8_1 B
layout into consumption order" describes llama's DRAM
format: `block_q8_1_x4` (types.glsl:267) groups four
Q8_1 blocks, their four (d, s) pairs collected in a
header array ahead of the qs words, each block's 8
words contiguous at `qs[8 * ib_inner ..]` (producer:
quantize_q8_1.comp:87 and :116). The scalar
`block_b_to_shmem` (mul_mmq_funcs.glsl:651) pulls each
block's pair out of that header into its own staged
slot. Our K12 output is two flat streams - qs words in
plain (row, block, word) order, one scale vec4 per
block - so there is no group header to undo: within a
block, the permutation is the identity by construction,
and K13's own B-side staging (a flat coalesced copy) and
K23's scatter write the same qs values; they differ in
the staged ADDRESSES (pitched, split scales) and in
which scale array a pair lands in. The transcription's
structural content is the addresses, the split, the
pitch, and the round size - not a data permutation.
Anyone reading a K23 win or loss should read it as a
verdict on those, not on de-interleaving work our
buffers never needed.

## Computed bank analysis (analysis, not measurement)

llama's +4 skew is tuned for cm1's coopmat fragment
loads. What it does under K13's scalar consumption
mapping (4-row lane groups; addresses below are word
addresses, 32 LDS banks) is computable, and it is not
uniformly good:

- **Activation qs loads** (16 distinct addresses per
  instruction, row step 4 rows): K13's 65-word pitch
  gives step 260 = 4 mod 32, eight banks, a 2-way
  conflict. K23's full-column row pitch is 72 words
  (two 36-word round segments): step 288 = 0 mod 32,
  two banks, an **8-way conflict - worse**.
- **Weight qs loads** (2 distinct addresses): K13's
  unstaged-pitch 64 gives step 256 = 0 mod 32, same
  bank, 2-way. K23's step 144 = 16 mod 32, different
  banks, **conflict-free - better**. (K22's 65-word
  weight skew also lands conflict-free here.)
- **Weight pair loads** (2 distinct addresses): K13's
  `w_sm[n * 8 + sub]` gives step 32 = 0 mod 32, 2-way.
  K23's `w_dm[ks * 64 + n]` gives addresses 4 apart,
  different banks, **conflict-free - better**.
- **Activation pair loads** (16 distinct addresses):
  K13's `x_ds[m * 8 + sub]` gives step 32 = 0 mod 32 -
  all sixteen addresses in ONE bank, a **16-way
  conflict** on every dm load. K23's
  `x_d[ks * 64 + m]` gives step 4, four banks, a 4-way
  conflict - **better**, and the single largest
  computed improvement in the layout.

Net: the scale loads improve sharply, the weight qs
loads improve, and the activation qs loads - half the
dot loop's word loads - regress from 2-way to 8-way.
The sign of the total is genuinely not computable from
here; that is what the card protocol is for.

## Deliberately not copied

- **K22's register organization.** One design variable
  per experiment; K23 keeps K13's organization.
- **The scalar mul_mmq A-side interleave repack**
  (mul_mmq_funcs.glsl:530, the Q4_K branch):
  `vals0 | vals1 << 4` packing with per-dot shift
  extraction. It serves the scalar path's register-file
  consumption; the cm1 A side stages nibbles already
  separated, so the interleave has no consumer in this
  layout. Named here so a later lane can take it
  deliberately; gap 2's remaining piece after K23.
- **Coopmat and per-device tile specialization**: the
  coopmat feasibility note owns that question.

## Routing

`mmq_product_q4k` gains one rung: wide K15 (batch at
the wide threshold), then K22 under
`WGPU_COMPUTE_K22_MMQ=1`, then **K23 under
`WGPU_COMPUTE_K23_MMQ=1`**, then K13. The resolver is
the K22 pattern exactly (exact value `1` after trim;
everything else off; unit-tested both ways). The
backend builds the pipeline at construction regardless
of the switch and prints `mmq k23 config: enabled=...`
through the diag log channel, so a shader defect fails
at startup, not on first routed use. Diag stamp from
birth: `k23_q4k_mmq` (DispatchMeta at prepare, K22's
shape). ProjCall gains `MmqK23Q4K` with encode,
dispatch-count, and `kernel_name() = "k23_q4k_mmq"`
arms; it is classified quantized (it carries the K12
quantize), like every MMQ form. With the switch unset
the ladder is the shipped ladder exactly.

## Server verdict protocol

Preconditions: card cleared per David's standing GPU
order (tenants stopped, restored after), phase lock
held, staging synced to the lane commit and
hash-verified, `prefill_profile` available. Run on the
RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100, RADV Mesa 26.0.8) - the same card
and driver class as every recorded comparison number.

0. **Shader autopsy first.** Compile K23 in isolation
   (the `shader_compile` k23 leg) under
   `RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats,asm,cs` with a private
   `MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR`. Read VGPR, spilled VGPR,
   scratch, LDS. The numbers that matter: VGPR against
   K13's/K22's 256 cap, spills and scratch against
   their zero, LDS against K13's 41,984 B compiled
   class (K23's designed set is 22,528 B; the compiled
   line should land on it). If VGPR reads 256 AND the
   compiled LDS is not materially below K13's class,
   the staging changed nothing the compiler prices;
   record both lines and still run step 1 (correctness
   is owed regardless), but steps 2-3 become
   confirmation, not a flip case.
1. **Correctness on the card.** `cargo test -p
   wgpu-compute --test k23_mmq` must actually execute
   (not skip): reference and K13 parity at batches 16,
   32, 64 and the 62-row tail, plus the band refusals.
   Also `resident_session` with
   `WGPU_COMPUTE_K23_MMQ=1`: identity + golden on the
   real file before any speed number is read, and the
   diag CSV for the run must show `k23_q4k_mmq` stamps
   on the Q4_K projections (the exposure check: K23
   unrouted would be a silent no-op A/B). The K12
   quantize dispatch counts stay identical to the
   control run; only the product kernel name changes.
2. **Kernel-level A/B.** Through `prefill_profile`:
   the same 1,022-token prompt, diag timing on, K23 env
   on vs off, same session conditions. Compare the
   `k23_q4k_mmq` row against K13's recorded 4,199.9 ms /
   46.4 GB/s and the total GPU time against the
   profile's 6,659 ms. Report achieved GB/s beside
   K13's line.
3. **Prefill A/B, session level.** `glimmer_generate
   --gpu` wall on the same prompt, env on vs off, three
   runs each, timing-off walls compared against the
   current recorded 6,330 ms (post host-gap fix). The
   profile's two historical runs agreed to 0.5%; a
   difference inside that band is a wash.
4. **No-leak check.** With the env unset, plain decode
   and the spec verdict harness must reproduce their
   recorded numbers, and a diag run must show zero
   `k23_q4k_mmq` stamps. K23 is unreachable with the
   switch off, so any movement is a routing leak, not a
   kernel result.

**Decision rule, written in advance.** The default
stays OFF unless one of two cases holds, with step 1
green in both: (a) step 0 shows an autopsy improvement
- VGPR off the 256 cap with zero spills and zero
scratch, or the compiled LDS materially below K13's
41,984 B class with no spills/scratch regression
(noting the occupancy caveat in lose-condition 5: LDS
alone does not raise occupancy while VGPR pins the
register file, so an LDS-only improvement supports a
flip only together with a step 2 or 3 win); or (b)
step 2 or step 3 shows a material prefill win - the
Q4_K MMQ line or the wall faster by more than the
0.5% run-agreement band, with correctness green.
Otherwise the flag stays off and the numbers are the
finding, recorded in this note like K22's verdict was.
Any default flip is a separate change with this note's
numbers attached.

## What could still make K23 lose to K13 on the card

Honest list, in the order I would bet on them:

1. **ACO still caps the registers at 256.** K23 keeps
   K13's organization, and K13 compiles to the cap;
   K22 proved the allocator does not take source-level
   hints from this codebase. A smaller staged set does
   not by itself give the allocator fewer live values:
   the `isum` array, the 64 staged-word lets per
   sub-block, and the accumulators are unchanged. Step
   0 exists to answer this cheaply.
2. **The activation-qs bank regression is real and the
   scale-load wins are not.** The computed analysis
   above: xv loads go from a 2-way to an 8-way
   conflict, and they are half the dot loop's LDS word
   loads; the dm improvement (16-way to 4-way) touches
   one load per (row, sub-block) against eight word
   steps of qs loads. If LDS throughput is the binding
   constraint, K23 is slower than K13 by construction.
3. **The repack costs staging instructions.** Each raw
   weight word is read twice - once per nibble half,
   in cm1's per-sub-block load shape - where K13 reads
   it once and extracts both halves in one task. The
   pitched scatter and the split d/s deposits add
   address arithmetic per staged word, and barriers
   double (four per column against K13's two), adding
   serialization points where the whole workgroup
   waits on the slowest staging task.
4. **The split layout fits WGSL's storage model
   worse than it fits GLSL's.** cm1's arrays are plain
   shared arrays; in WGSL the fold assembles dm from
   two separate scalar loads (x_d, x_s) where K13
   loads one vec2, and five workgroup arrays (against
   K13's four) mean more base-address registers held
   across the inner loop. Small, but it pushes against
   lose-condition 1.
5. **The LDS halving cannot pay alone.** At VGPR 256,
   a 256-thread workgroup occupies 256 x 256 x 4 B =
   256 KB of register file - the whole CU file - so
   occupancy is one workgroup per CU no matter how
   small LDS gets. The smaller set only converts to
   occupancy if VGPR also falls; read step 0's pair of
   lines together, never the LDS line alone.
6. **The B staging's global-load pattern is less
   coalesced.** Tasks stride by activation row (32
   useful bytes per task span) where K13's flat copy
   reads contiguously; worst case about 4x cacheline
   waste on activation staging reads. Bounded small
   (the activation tile is 16 KB per column pass), but
   it is a real cost the flat copy does not pay.
7. **Half the lookahead per round.** A round holds
   four sub-blocks of independent dot work against
   K13's eight; inside a round the scheduler has half
   as much independent work per thread to hide LDS
   latency with, at the same per-thread register
   budget. If latency hiding was part of K13's rate,
   the round structure taxes it.

===== END FILE: bench/k23-mmq-repack-2026-11-06.md =====

===== FILE: bench/kv-snapshot-decode-safety-2026-11-07.md =====
# KV snapshot decode safety: the Category A crafted-file pair, plus the store preamble message (2026-11-07)

Lane `lane/kv-snapshot-decode-safety`, from main
85beb8ab6ae8accf8aaf7cee916e08b9f455d919. Code and tests in
3e146c0cf88638fb4dee1aa3c79b1957da13b7ab; this note is the
second commit. VM gates only on this lane; no server jobs.

Source of the work: the cold critic panel of 2026-11-07
(`CRITIC-ENGINE-MERGE.md`, Category A; probes executed by the
security seat and the failure seat). The snapshot format's own
docs claim decoding is "strict and total" and the crate's
contract (lib.rs) is "named errors instead of panics on
anything read from disk". Three crafted inputs broke that
contract in the decode and store-open paths. Each fix below
got a regression test written first, proven failing on the
unfixed tree, then proven passing after, in both build
profiles where the defect was profile-dependent.

## Finding 1 [HIGH]: decode pre-allocates from a file-controlled layer count

`KvSnapshot::from_bytes` read `layer_count` (a raw u32) from
the buffer and immediately sized two `Vec::with_capacity`
calls with it, before the checksum, geometry, or any other
trust check could refuse the file.

Crafted input (security seat probe, re-run as the regression
test): a 32-byte snapshot header, magic `ITKV`, version 1,
fingerprint length 0, token_count 0, heads 1, dim 1,
layer_count = u32::MAX.

Before: the decode demanded a 68,719,476,720-byte allocation
and the process died with SIGABRT ("memory allocation of
68719476720 bytes failed", signal 6). An allocation abort is
not a catchable error, and the store decodes entries during
lookup, so one planted file in a store root killed the
serving process.

Fix: bound the count before it sizes anything. Every layer
header costs 28 bytes on the wire (new constant
`LAYER_HEADER_LEN`: tag 1 + reserved 3 + window 8 +
first_position 8 + row_count 8), so a count larger than
`reader.remaining() / LAYER_HEADER_LEN` is impossible and is
refused by name with `KvError::InconsistentSnapshot`. This is
the same "declared length larger than the rest of the file
is impossible" argument the GGUF parser already uses for
metadata arrays (crates/gguf/src/file.rs). After the bound,
the two capacities are proportional to the actual buffer
size.

Regression test: `decode_refuses_a_layer_count_that_cannot_fit_the_buffer`
(snapshot.rs tests). Before: test binary aborted (SIGABRT).
After: named refusal, test passes in debug and release.

## Finding 2 [HIGH]: validate() multiplies file-controlled sizes unchecked

`KvSnapshot::validate()` compared stored lengths against
`expected_rows * row` with unchecked arithmetic, and
`KvGeometry::row_floats()` multiplied heads by dim unchecked.

Crafted input (failure seat probe, re-run as the regression
test): a hand-built snapshot with a valid FNV-1a checksum,
fingerprint "x", token_count = 2^32, num_kv_heads = 65536,
head_dim = 65536 (so the row width is 2^32), one global layer
with row_count 0 and zero payload rows.

Before: release builds ACCEPTED the snapshot
(`Ok(KvSnapshot { token_count: 4294967296, ... })`) because
2^32 * 2^32 wraps to 0, exactly the stored length; debug
builds PANICKED at snapshot.rs:188, "attempt to multiply
with overflow". The two profiles disagreed about what is a
valid snapshot, and any consumer trusting a validated
`token_count` acted on a forged count.

Fix: checked products everywhere the width meets stored
data.

- New `KvGeometry::row_floats_checked()`: `checked_mul` on
  heads x dim, refusing with `KvError::InconsistentSnapshot`
  on overflow. The decoder and the validator both take the
  row width from here. The plain `row_floats()` stays for
  geometry built from a live cache, whose fields the cache
  itself already bounded; every external caller of it in the
  workspace is a test fixture over hand-built sane geometry.
- `validate()` computes `expected_rows.checked_mul(row)` and
  refuses by name on overflow instead of comparing against a
  wrapped product.

One correction to the probe's framing, found while writing
the regression test: two u32 wire fields cannot overflow a
64-bit usize product ((2^32-1)^2 < 2^64), so the row-width
half of this hole is reachable through the wire only as the
expected-rows product above. It IS reachable through
`validate()` on an in-memory snapshot, whose geometry fields
are public usizes: a second regression test builds one with
heads = dim = 2^32 directly. On the unfixed tree that test
panicked in debug at the `row_floats()` multiply
(snapshot.rs:66) and returned Ok(()) in release; after the
fix both profiles refuse by name.

Regression tests: `decode_refuses_geometry_whose_row_products_overflow`
(the wire probe) and `validate_refuses_geometry_whose_row_width_overflows`
(the in-memory geometry). Both fail before (panic in debug,
acceptance in release) and pass after, in both profiles.

## Finding 3 [MEDIUM]: the store preamble's own refusal message multiplies unchecked

`parse_preamble` (store.rs) checked `tokens_bytes` against
`(token_count as u64).saturating_mul(4)` but then formatted
its refusal message with the raw `token_count * 4`.
token_count comes straight from file bytes at offset 40.
`rescan` runs `parse_preamble` over every `.kv` file in the
store root at open.

Crafted input (failure seat, re-run as the regression test):
a planted 72-byte file (exactly one preamble) with the entry
magic, version 1, token_count = u64::MAX, tokens_bytes = 0.

Before: debug builds panicked at store.rs:596, "attempt to
multiply with overflow", during store open; release builds
wrapped and printed a wrong number in a message nobody could
act on.

Fix: bind the saturating product once
(`expected_tokens_bytes`) and use it in both the comparison
and the message, so the check and its refusal can never
disagree and neither can overflow.

Regression test: `open_refuses_a_planted_garbage_entry_by_name`
(store.rs tests): plants the file, opens the store, asserts
the open succeeds with the entry refused by name in the diag
log and left unindexed (zero entries). Before: debug panic
at open. After: passes in debug and release.

## Sibling arithmetic audit (snapshot.rs, whole file)

Every other multiplication in snapshot.rs that can touch a
file-controlled value, examined one by one:

- `from_bytes` payload sizing (`row_count * row`): already
  `checked_mul`, refuses by name. Unchanged.
- `Reader::f32s` (`count * 4`): already `checked_mul`.
  Unchanged.
- `LayerSnapshot::rows`: already `checked_div`. Unchanged.
- `KvGeometry::bytes_per_token` and `stored_bytes_for`:
  unchecked u64 products and a u64 sum over geometry fields.
  These are sizing estimates (the store's byte accounting and
  capture's diag line), and a foreign geometry could wrap or
  panic them even though no decode path trusts them for
  correctness. Made saturating throughout
  (`saturating_mul`, `saturating_add`), the same tool
  `parse_preamble` already used: identical values for every
  real geometry (the Glimmer sizing pins in
  `glimmer_sizing_math` still pass exactly), saturation
  instead of a wrap or panic for a foreign one. This is the
  only behavior-adjacent change beyond the three findings,
  and it cannot alter any value a real cache geometry
  produces.
- `capture()`'s `Vec::with_capacity(visible * row)`: both
  factors come from a live `KvCache` built by the attention
  crate, not from file bytes. Not file-controlled; unchanged.
- `Reader::take`'s `at + n`: an addition over a cursor bounded
  by the buffer length plus one u32-derived length; cannot
  overflow on a 64-bit target. Unchanged.
- store.rs neighbours of finding 3: the failure seat already
  checked `verify_candidate`'s capacity and the `tokens_end`
  computation and found them gated by the candidate filter
  (`token_count <= query.len()`); this lane changed only the
  named message line there, per the panel's own fix text.

No other unchecked multiplication on a file-controlled value
remains in snapshot.rs.

## Gates (lane tree, as observed)

- `cargo test -p itak-kv`: 25 passed, 0 failed (21 base + 4
  new), debug AND `--release` (finding 2 is profile-dependent;
  the regressions pass in both).
- `cargo test -p wgpu-compute`: 318 passed, 1 ignored,
  0 failed (the prefix-KV session suite consumes this crate).
- `cargo test -p attention`: 26 passed. `-p dflash`: 24
  passed. `-p itak-spec`: 70 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p itak-kv --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.
  `cargo clippy -p wgpu-compute --all-targets -D warnings`:
  clean.
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean. `cargo check --workspace`:
  clean.

Not covered by this lane, by design: the remaining Category
A items (the f16/prefix composition guard in
wgpu-compute/session.rs, the midway-failed install, the
unbounded candidate read, temp-file collisions, the 100%-hit
recapture) are separate lanes. This lane closes only the
decode-safety pair and the store preamble message.
