# llama.cpp parity specs: what llama's Vulkan backend actually runs, field by field against ours, 2026-11-06

David's question: can we open the llama.cpp repo, take the specs
out, and be on par with them? Answer: yes for the specs. This note
is the extraction, with receipts. Every llama value below was read
from the real sources and is cited to file and line; every one of
our values was read from this repo's code the same way. Fields are
marked MATCH, DIFFERENT, or ABSENT, with the measured consequence
where our bench record has one.

## Sources and verification

- llama.cpp: the server tree at `/home/server/llama.cpp`, git
  commit `a7af149a2a7768d4b1f6f02c6ce26a17fba11376` (2026-10-28),
  the tree that built `build-vulkan2`, the binary behind every
  recorded llama baseline in this repo (Vulkan prefill 998.43,
  decode 44.31 tok/s).
- The reading was done in the VM mirror at
  `~/workspace/meta-cookbook/build-site/repos/ggerganov__llama.cpp/`.
  Its git HEAD differs (74a4fb00), so the mirror was verified
  against the server tree before anything was cited from it:
  all 187 files under `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/vulkan-shaders/` and
  `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp` are sha256-identical
  between the two trees. Citations below name the path inside
  `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/`; line numbers are that verified content.
- Ours: this repo at main a064b5d, `crates/wgpu-compute/src/`.

## License note

llama.cpp is MIT licensed (LICENSE, "Copyright (c) 2023-2026 The
ggml authors"). Specs, algorithms, constants, tile shapes, and
buffer layouts are facts about how the program works; reimplementing
them in our own WGSL is clean-room work and needs no permission.
Copying llama's GLSL source text into this repo would require
keeping their copyright and license notice with the copied material,
and mostly would not translate anyway: GLSL specialization constants,
`layout(local_size_x_id)`, and subgroup intrinsics have no direct
WGSL equivalents, which is why every kernel here is a re-expression,
not a port. This note extracts facts, not code.

## The host selection logic (llama's routing, for our routing lane)

This is the cross-check table for the band-routing work: the exact
thresholds llama itself uses to pick a kernel per product.

| Decision | llama's rule | Citation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| vec vs matrix path | `mul_mat_vec` when the batch (dst rows of src1, `ne[1]`) is 1, or `<= mul_mat_vec_max_cols` with the batch dims of src1 equal to 1; anything larger goes to `ggml_vk_mul_mat_q_f16` (the mul_mm family) | ggml-vulkan.cpp:7402 |
| The vec column cap | `mul_mat_vec_max_cols = 8` | ggml-vulkan-types.h:362 |
| Single-row transposed trick | One output row with batch > 8 and no fused ops is run through mul_mat_vec swapped (B^T*A) | ggml-vulkan.cpp:7394 |
| Vec workgroup size on AMD | `DMMV_WG_SIZE_SUBGROUP` (one subgroup) is the default; the LARGE (4-subgroup) variant is chosen only for NVIDIA post-Turing and Intel. The heuristic never fires for AMD | ggml-vulkan.cpp:5628-5648 |
| Rows per vec workgroup (NUM_ROWS) | Defaults rm_stdq 1, rm_kq 2; AMD GCN raises to 2 and 4; RDNA3 keeps rm_kq 2 for K-quants in the f32/f16-activation path | ggml-vulkan.cpp:2866-2874 |
| MMVQ rows on RDNA3/4 | In the Q8_1 integer vec path, NUM_ROWS is forced to 4 when NUM_COLS >= 5 ("above four columns, static 4 rows bench faster") | ggml-vulkan.cpp:2880-2885 |
| MMVQ (quantize activations for the vec path) | Used when integer dot product exists and: batch n > 1 always (subject to vendor rules); on AMD, single-column use needs k >= 2048; Q6_K weights are excluded on every vendor except Intel | ggml-vulkan.cpp:6656-6700, gate at 6783 |
| Matrix tile size class | Selector over (m, n): m <= 32 or n <= 32 gives small; m <= 64 or n <= 64 gives medium; otherwise large. On AMD the large class exists only when coopmat is present and the driver is not AMD proprietary | ggml-vulkan.cpp:2852-2859, 4807 |
| Matrix path activation choice | Activations are quantized to Q8_1 (MMQ path) when integer dot product OR coopmat integer support exists and precision allows; with coopmat present and quantized weights, f16 activations are preferred otherwise | ggml-vulkan.cpp:6431-6445 |
| Split-K | When k >= 2048 and the tile grid fills at most half the shader cores, split K by up to 8x (aligned to 256) and reduce with `mul_mat_split_k_reduce.comp` | ggml-vulkan.cpp:5916-5955 |
| Coopmat enablement | Build must have glslc coopmat support; device must enumerate VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix and `GGML_VK_DISABLE_COOPMAT` must be unset; the device feature `cooperativeMatrix` must be on. f16 shapes are then scanned: first subgroup-scope f16 x f16 shape sets coopmat_m/n/k; a 16x16x16 shape with f32 accumulate sets the f32acc flag, f16 accumulate likewise. An s8 x s8 to s32 subgroup shape sets coopmat_int_support and the integer dims. Coopmat2 is VK_NV_cooperative_matrix2, NVIDIA only | ggml-vulkan.cpp:4087-4101, 4556-4557, 4701-4748 |
| Coopmat integer MMQ on RDNA3/4 | `use_cm1_int = coopmat_int_support && (RDNA3 || RDNA4)`; the cm1 MMQ pipelines are created under exactly that condition. On this card, llama's Q4_K/Q5_K/Q6_K x Q8_1 prefill products are the cm1 (coopmat) shaders, not the scalar mul_mmq | ggml-vulkan.cpp:1877, 2481-2494 |

Ours, for contrast (session.rs, compute.rs): the matrix switch is
one constant, `GEMM_MIN_ROWS = 16` (session.rs:215); below it the
shipped default is one whole-batch GEMV dispatch per projection,
with the MMV band (2..=16), K18 band, and chunked band all behind
env flags that default off (compute.rs:107-215). llama's vec band
ends at 8 and its matrix path starts at 9; ours starts at 16 and
the 2..15 band ships as repeated per-row weight streaming.

## Family 1: mul_mat_vec (decode and small batch) vs GEMV K1/K2/K3

llama shader: `vulkan-shaders/mul_mat_vec.comp` +
`mul_mat_vec_base.glsl`. Ours: `kernels/k1_q4k_gemv.rs`,
`k2_q6k_gemv.rs`, `k3_q5k_gemv.rs` (the "llama shapes" family).

| Field | llama | Ours | Mark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Workgroup | One subgroup (BLOCK_SIZE = subgroup size, spec constant 0); dispatch x covers rows in NUM_ROWS chunks, y is the batch | 128 threads (4 subgroups of 32) | DIFFERENT |
| Rows per workgroup (NUM_ROWS, spec constant 1) | 2 for K-quants on RDNA3 (rm_kq), 1 for plain quants (rm_stdq), 4 in the MMVQ path at NUM_COLS >= 5 | 2 (shipped_shape, k1_q4k_gemv.rs:271-279) | MATCH |
| Batch per thread (NUM_COLS, spec constant 2) | 1..8 pipelines, one per column count; accumulators `temp[NUM_COLS][NUM_ROWS]` live in registers | The GEMV kernels take the batch as a runtime loop over rows in one dispatch; the register-resident batch form is the separate K19/K20/K21 family (Family 2) | DIFFERENT |
| Weight handling | Dequantized in registers per thread (`dequantize4`), never staged; K_PER_ITER 8 elements per thread per iteration for quantized A, vec4 B loads at a stride of QUANT_K/2 (mul_mat_vec.comp:12-16, 34-46) | Same: register dequant, no weight staging, vec4 traffic (LEGACY shape) and buffer_load-style wide loads in the llama shapes | MATCH |
| Reduction | subgroupAdd within the subgroup, then either nothing (one subgroup per workgroup) or a shared partials array `tmpsh[NUM_COLS][NUM_ROWS][BLOCK_SIZE]` (mul_mat_vec_base.glsl:145) | Segmented subgroup butterfly inside each 16-thread segment plus shared partials across the 128-thread workgroup | DIFFERENT |
| Activation precision | f32 or f16 B pipelines per type; f16 halves activation traffic | f32 shipped; f16 shapes exist but are bench-only (measured slower, error above the crate tolerance; k1_q4k_gemv.rs shipped_shape docs) | DIFFERENT (measured, ours is a deliberate refusal) |
| Fusion | Bias add and scale fused into the reduce step via push-constant fusion flags (mul_mat_vec_base.glsl:124-141) | K1 carries gated and SwiGLU activation forms; the head finish lives in K3's finish form | MATCH in kind |
| Measured standing | llama.cpp Vulkan decode 44.31 tok/s on this card (whole-engine figure) | Our GEMV streams at up to 816.5 GB/s in isolation (115% of llama's measured 708 GB/s for the same kernel class); our whole-engine plain decode is 35.5-35.7 tok/s | Kernel MATCH or better; engine gap is elsewhere (chain and launch structure, not this kernel) |

## Family 2: the small-batch band, mul_mat_vec at NUM_COLS 2..8 and MMVQ vs K19/K20/K21 (+ K18, chunked)

llama runs batches 2..8 through the same mul_mat_vec shader with
NUM_COLS set to the batch; past 8 the matrix path takes over.
There is no third band and no per-family threshold split. When
integer dot product is available, the band's activations are
Q8_1 (MMVQ) and the dots are integer DP4A with the Q8_1 sum
correction; Q6_K weights are excluded from MMVQ off Intel
(ggml-vulkan.cpp:6656-6700).

| Field | llama | Ours | Mark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Band range | 2..8 in mul_mat_vec; 9 and up in mul_mm | MMV kernels accept 2..16 (k19_q4k_mmv.rs:120,127), shipped off; shipped default band behavior is GEMV per-row streaming | DIFFERENT |
| Accumulator residence | Registers, proven shape (our autopsy of the equivalent form: K19 compiles to VGPR 72-96, zero spills) | K19/K20/K21 copied this form exactly; autopsy matches (VGPR 60-96, zero spills, LDS 1,024 B) | MATCH |
| Activation form in band | Q8_1 integer (MMVQ) when the gate passes; f32/f16 otherwise | f32 activations, f32 dots, no quantize dispatch in front (the GEMV's exact math) | DIFFERENT, sign unmeasured: llama moves 1 byte per activation element in band, ours moves 4; our f32 form still won its cap-16 A/B by 13% (bench/mmv-verdict-2026-11-05.md) |
| Rows per workgroup in band | NUM_ROWS 2 (f32 path), 4 (MMVQ path, NUM_COLS >= 5) on RDNA3 | 2 (k19 shipped_shape, k19_q4k_mmv.rs:221-228) | MATCH for the f32 form; the MMVQ 4-row variant is ABSENT |
| Per-family thresholds | None inside the band; the Q6_K MMVQ exclusion is the only per-type rule | None shipped (one global env cap); the routing lane's per-family win map is the in-flight fix | DIFFERENT (ours is the known cliff: caps 4/8/12 lose, 16 wins) |
| Fallback when the band form refuses | None needed; one shader family covers 1..8 | Ladder: MMV, K18, chunked, GEMV (session.rs prepare_proj docs) | DIFFERENT in structure, no measured cost |

## Family 3: mul_mm / mul_mmq (prefill) vs K13/K14, wide K15/K16, K22, GEMM K10/K11

llama shaders: `mul_mm.comp` (f16/f32 activations, dequant to
shared), `mul_mmq.comp` (Q8_1 activations, integer dots),
`mul_mmq_cm1.comp` (coopmat integer, the RDNA3 path). Ours:
`k13_q4k_mmq.rs`, `k14_q6k_mmq.rs`, `k15_q4k_mmq_wide.rs`,
`k16_q6k_mmq_wide.rs`, `k22_q4k_mmq.rs`, with the f32 GEMMs
`k10_q4k_gemm.rs` / `k11_q6k_gemm.rs` as the fallback rung.

| Field | llama | Ours | Mark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tile classes | Three (small, medium, large), picked per product by the (m, n) selector above | One shipped tile per kernel (K13/K14 m64; K22 64x64); the session chunk cap is 64 rows (session.rs:144,158), so the batch side never exceeds llama's medium class | DIFFERENT |
| Medium tile (the class a 64-row chunk runs) | BM 64, BN 64, BK 32, BLOCK_SIZE 128, WN 32, WMITER 2, TM 4, TN 2, TK 1, WM and WARP = mm_warp_8 = min(device subgroup size, 64) (ggml-vulkan.cpp:1678-1684, 1798-1803; warptile field order per mul_mmq.comp:74-85) | K13 m64: 256 threads, tile 64 out rows x the whole 64-row batch, each thread a 4x4 sub-tile (k13_q4k_mmq.rs:69-87) | DIFFERENT in organization: llama splits the batch across BN 64 within a 128-thread workgroup of 4 warps with a 32-wide warp tile; ours gives one 256-thread workgroup the full batch with 4x4 thread tiles |
| Large tile (n > 64, AMD with coopmat) | BM 128, BN 128, BK 32, BLOCK_SIZE 256, WN 64, WMITER 2 (1 for K-quants in the integer path, with TM 4, TN 2), WM and WARP = mm_warp_8 / mm_warp_16 as above (ggml-vulkan.cpp:1846-1850) | ABSENT (no tile above 64 rows of batch, no 128-row weight tile) | ABSENT |
| K step | BK 32, BK_STEP 4: 128 K elements staged per pass in mul_mmq and mul_mm (BK 16 for non-quant mul_mm) (mul_mmq.comp:87-97, mul_mm.comp:173-177) | K13 stages one super-block column (256 elements) per pass | DIFFERENT |
| Staging layout, weights | mul_mmq stages per-super-block structs: packed qs words and the (d, dmin) pair side by side per block (mul_mmq_shmem_types.glsl); mul_mmq_cm1 splits them into separate arrays: `buf_a_qs[BM * QPITCH]` with QPITCH = BK_STEP*(BK/4)+4 (the +4 is a bank-conflict skew), plus `buf_a_dm` vec2 pairs (mul_mmq_cm1.comp:103-122) | K13 stages weight words (tile_n x 64 words), activation words with a 65-word row stride (the same skew idea), and scale pairs, interleaved per super-block column (k13_q4k_mmq.rs:120-122); m64 staging 41,216 B (autopsy: LDS 41,984 B compiled) | MATCH in kind (skew present), DIFFERENT in split: cm1 separates qs from scales into their own arrays; K13/K22 do not |
| Staging repack, activations | The B side is REPACKED during staging: B arrives as `block_q8_1_x4_packed128` (four Q8_1 blocks interleaved in one 128-byte struct) and `block_b_to_shmem` de-interleaves it (ib_outer = ib/4, ib_inner = ib%4, qs scattered to `qs[iqs*4 + 0..3]`) so the dot loop reads unit-stride (mul_mmq_funcs.glsl, block_b_to_shmem) | K13 stages activation words in source order with the row skew only; no de-interleave repack. K22's note names this exact omission: the repack was deliberately not copied | ABSENT (named gap, see ranked list) |
| A-side load width into staging | LOAD_VEC_A per type at shader generation: 4 for Q4_K and Q5_K in mul_mm, 2 for Q6_K (mul_mm.comp:43-48 defaults, per-type defines; Q6_K branch in mul_mm_funcs.glsl uses 2 values per index). mul_mmq uses LOAD_VEC_A = 4*QUANT_R_MMQ, LOAD_VEC_B 16 (mul_mmq.comp:105-106) | K14 stages Q6_K from the 212-byte padded block layout (k14_q6k_mmq.rs:42); the width-2 fact is llama's own staging wart in the f16 path, recorded in bench/mmv-q6k-2026-11-05.md; it does not apply to the cm1 path llama actually runs on RDNA3 | Informational: no action (see gap list tail) |
| Register organization | mul_mmq: register cache `cache_a[WMITER * TM]` per thread plus one `cache_b`, dots through DP4A on staged data. K13's compiled form: VGPR 256 (the cap), zero spills (our autopsy) | K13/K14: VGPR 256, zero spills, same saturation. K22 copied mul_mmq's 128-thread organization and braced column scopes and still compiled to VGPR 256 (verdict, bench/k22-mmq-2026-11-05.md) | MATCH on the scalar path, including the failure mode: register organization alone does not move ACO off the cap in either codebase's scalar form |
| Split-K | Present, rule above, with a reduce shader | ABSENT in K13/K14/K22 (one workgroup owns its tile's whole K) | ABSENT |
| Wide variant | None: llama has no wider-than-large tile; width comes from the tile classes and split-K | K15/K16 wide MMQ exists and is convicted: 1,041-1,213 spilled VGPRs, 78-86 KB scratch (bench/shader-autopsy-2026-11-04.md); shipped off by the row threshold | DIFFERENT (ours is a dead end llama never built) |
| Measured standing | llama.cpp Vulkan prefill 998.43 tok/s (whole engine, 1,024-token class prompts) | Our MMQ pair: 83.2% of prefill GPU time at 43.5 GB/s combined (k13 4,199.9 ms at 46.4 GB/s, k14 1,342.0 ms at 34.6 GB/s); our prefill wall 161.5 tok/s after the host-gap fix (bench/prefill-profile-2026-11-05.md, bench/prefill-host-gap-2026-11-05.md) | The gap is this family plus Family 4 |

## Family 4: the coopmat path vs our stack

On RDNA3 with RADV, llama's device probe finds VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix
with subgroup-scope 16x16x16 shapes (f16 in, f32 or f16 accumulate;
s8 in, s32 accumulate). That flips three things on, per the
enablement chain in the host table: the large mul_mm tile class
(AMD rule, ggml-vulkan.cpp:4807), the cm1 integer MMQ shaders for
Q8_1 products (ggml-vulkan.cpp:2481-2494, tile spec in
mul_mmq_cm1.comp:89-100: BLOCK_SIZE 256, BM 128, BN 128, WM 64,
WN 32, TM/TN/TK = the 16x16x16 fragment, WARP 32; those are the
shader-declared defaults, and the host warptile overrides
BLOCK_SIZE and WM per size class, ggml-vulkan.cpp:1807-1813), and the
coopmat1 flash path for multi-row attention (Family 5).

| Field | llama | Ours | Mark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cooperative matrix anywhere | Yes: mul_mm, mul_mmq_cm1, flash_attn_cm1 | No occurrence in any crate (grep over crates/: the only hits are the English word in comments and K22's doc mention) | ABSENT |
| Why absent | n/a | Our backend is wgpu/WGSL; WGSL has no cooperative-matrix type and Naga exposes none, so the path needs either a wgpu extension that does not exist in the pinned wgpu or a non-WGSL side channel | Structural, stated plainly: this is the one spec in this note that cannot be taken by re-expression inside the current shader language |
| Prefill consequence | llama's prefill products on this card run on WMMA tensor pipes at 16x16x16 per subgroup | Our prefill products run scalar DP4A at 43.5 GB/s combined (Family 3) | The single largest measured gap (see ranked list) |

## Family 5: flash_attn vs K6 flash

llama shaders: `flash_attn.comp` + `flash_attn_base.glsl`, plus
`flash_attn_cm1.comp` / `flash_attn_cm2.comp` and the two-phase
decode pair. Ours: `k6_attention.rs` FLASH_SHADER (the resident
form), with the scores+reduce pair as the trait-path form.

Spec constants (flash_attn_base.glsl:4-21): WorkGroupSize 128,
Br 1 (query rows per workgroup), Bc 32 (KV block), HSK/HSV
specialized per head dim, D_split 16, row_split 1, SubGroupSize
32, SHMEM_STAGING and LIMIT_OCCUPANCY_SHMEM flags.

Path choice (ggml-vulkan.cpp:1334-1375): coopmat2 if present,
else coopmat1 when `coopmat1_fa_support` (coopmat plus full
subgroup support) and the 16x16x16 shape and shared-memory checks
pass, else scalar. One query row always takes the scalar path
("scalar is faster than coopmat when N==1"). Scalar tuning on
AMD non-GCN (ggml-vulkan.cpp:1200-1245): subgroup size is the
device size for n_rows >= 4; row_split rises to 4 when
hsk > 128 (for n_rows > 8); block_rows 8 at row_split 1 for
n_rows > 8; block_cols 32 when (hsk|hsv) has no factor 8, else
64. Coopmat1 tuning: 16-row by 16-col fragments, block_cols =
16 * num_subgroups (ggml-vulkan.cpp:1275-1304).

| Field | llama | Ours | Mark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Workgroup shape | 128 threads default (spec constant), one workgroup per (Br query rows, head) | 256 threads, one workgroup per (1 query row, Q head) (k6_attention.rs:232-262) | MATCH in structure (Br 1 class), DIFFERENT in size |
| KV blocking | Bc 32 keys per block, K and V staged in shared memory (SHMEM_STAGING) for the matrix paths | 256 keys per tile, but only the SCORES are staged (a 256-f32 workgroup array); K and V are re-read from global memory per lane in the reduce loop (k6_attention.rs:264-325) | DIFFERENT: no K/V staging at all |
| Softmax | Online, inside the flash kernel, same as ours in kind | Online, inside the flash kernel | MATCH |
| KV precision | K/V read at cache precision (f16 cache standard; quantized cache types dequantized in-shader via flash_attn_dequant.glsl) | KV buffers are f32 end to end | DIFFERENT: llama moves half the KV bytes per key |
| Decode form | n_rows 1 takes the scalar path, plus dedicated two-phase decode shaders with split-K over the KV length (flash_attn_decode_phase_1/2.comp) | Same fused flash kernel at every shape; no KV split | DIFFERENT: no decode split-K |
| Long-context behavior | Blocked matrix form: cost grows linearly per block with shared-memory reuse | Each query lane re-reads V rows from global memory inside the tile loop; measured flash time grows quadratically across the prompt chunks (125.7 ms in the last chunk of the 1,022-token profile) and totals 1,013.1 ms, 15.2% of prefill GPU time | DIFFERENT with measured cost |

## Family 6: quantize_q8_1 vs K12

llama: `quantize_q8_1.comp`. Ours: `k12_q8_quant.rs`. Both exist
for one reason: feed the MMQ integer dots, once per projection
input, shared across the layer's projections in our session
(quantize-once, HShare) and per product input in llama.

| Field | llama | Ours | Mark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Block | 32 elements per Q8_1 block, scale d = amax/127, plus the block SUM stored beside d as f16 pair `ds = (d, sum * d)` for the DP4A correction (quantize_q8_1.comp:78-107) | 32 elements per block (Q8_BLOCK_ELEMS, k12_q8_quant.rs:64), d and sum carried in the ds stream the MMQ kernels consume | MATCH |
| Workgroup | GROUP_SIZE = subgroup size (spec constant 0, host-set, ggml-vulkan.cpp:3242); 8 threads per block, one vec4 per thread, subgroup clustered max/add reductions | 256 threads per workgroup, one workgroup covers 256 elements (eight blocks, QUANT_CHUNK_ELEMS, k12_q8_quant.rs:69) | DIFFERENT in shape, same math contract |
| Output packing | The shipped pipeline is the x4 variant: four blocks packed into `block_q8_1_x4` structs (ggml-vulkan.cpp:6328), the layout Family 3's staging repack later de-interleaves | Packed qs words and ds pairs in two flat streams (qs_words / ds_vec4s layout, k12_q8_quant.rs) | DIFFERENT: llama's x4 interleave exists to feed its staging repack; ours feeds K13's direct staging |
| Rounding | `round()` in shader (ties to even via GLSL round) | Documented divergence: our reference rounds ties away from zero, the shader builtin may differ on exact ties; bounded at one quant step, inside the MMQ parity band (k12_q8_quant.rs module docs) | MATCH within a disclosed tie rule |
| Measured standing | Part of the MMQ path cost | k12 is 0.5% of prefill GPU time (32.9 ms of 6,659 ms) | Not a gap |

## Family 7: get_rows, rms_norm, rope, softmax vs K8 gather, K4, K5, K9

| Field | llama | Ours | Mark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Embedding gather | `get_rows.comp`: 512 threads, one element per thread, grid-stride over rows and batches; a separate `get_rows_quant.comp` dequantizes during the gather for quantized embedding tables | K8's gather reads token ids from a device buffer (session.rs:22); the embedding table in the resident session is uploaded dequantized, so the gather is a plain copy | MATCH for our (dequantized) table; the quantized-gather variant is ABSENT and would matter only if the table stayed quantized on device |
| RMS norm | `rms_norm.comp`: one workgroup per row, BLOCK_SIZE a spec constant (default 512) with host variants 128, 256, 512, 1024 chosen so ncols <= 2*BLOCK_SIZE (ggml-vulkan.cpp:3264-3269); a partials two-pass variant for wide rows; FUSION variants run norm+rope, norm+add, and norm+set_rows as one shader, the norm output passing to rope through shared memory (rms_norm.comp:15-40) | K4: one workgroup per row, fixed 256 threads, lanes striding the row (k4_rmsnorm.rs:48); norm, residual add, and the chain forms are separate small kernels; the attention-side fusion llama does at this seam exists in ours one level up: K9 fuses the Q/K norms, RoPE, and KV append into one dispatch per layer (k9_attn_prep.rs module docs) | MATCH in geometry class; fusion placement DIFFERENT (theirs inside the norm shader, ours at the attention prep seam) |
| RoPE | `rope_norm.comp` over `rope_head.glsl`: local size (1, 256), each thread rotates one pair (i0 = 2*global y); also fused into rms_norm (above) and a neox variant | K5: 256-thread workgroups over pairs, plus the KV append in the same module (k5_rope_kv.rs:45) | MATCH |
| Softmax (standalone) | `soft_max.comp`: one workgroup per row, BLOCK_SIZE = subgroup size spec constant, plus a 512-wide variant and a three-pass large-row form (ggml-vulkan.cpp:3503-3505) | No standalone softmax kernel in the resident path; softmax lives inside K6 (online, in the flash and reduce forms) | ABSENT as a standalone, unused by the Glimmer path; not a gap for this engine |

## Ranked gap list

Ordered by expected payoff against our measured numbers. Each
gap names its owner: a lane in flight, or the follow-up that
should be created.

1. **Coopmat integer MMQ (cm1) is ABSENT from our stack; it is
   the path llama actually runs for prefill on this card.**
   Spec: VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix, subgroup scope, 16x16x16
   s8 x s8 to s32 fragments set coopmat_int dims
   (ggml-vulkan.cpp:4740-4748); on RDNA3/4 with that support,
   Q4_K/Q5_K/Q6_K x Q8_1 products are created as cm1 pipelines
   (ggml-vulkan.cpp:1877, 2481-2494) with BM 128, BN 128,
   BK 32 tiles and the 16x16x16 fragment as TM/TN/TK
   (mul_mmq_cm1.comp:89-100). Payoff: our MMQ pair is 83.2% of
   prefill GPU time at 43.5 GB/s; the profile note prices the
   streaming-bound ceiling of any MMQ rework at about 347 tok/s
   wall against today's 161.5, and coopmat is the only variant
   that changes the math pipe, not just the schedule. Blocker
   is structural (WGSL has no coopmat), so the owner is the
   coopmat lane in flight, whose feasibility verdict decides
   whether this is a build or a permanent documented gap.
2. **The MMQ staging repack and split staging layout are ABSENT
   in K13/K14 and were deliberately not copied by K22.**
   Spec: B de-interleave in `block_b_to_shmem`
   (mul_mmq_funcs.glsl) out of the x4-packed Q8_1 layout, and
   cm1's split arrays (qs in `buf_a_qs` at QPITCH with the +4
   skew, scales in `buf_a_dm`) (mul_mmq_cm1.comp:103-122).
   Payoff: this is the remaining untested structural difference
   between K13 and llama's scalar MMQ after K22 proved register
   organization alone compiles to the same 256 VGPR cap. Owner:
   a K23 follow-up lane (K13-form kernel with the repack and
   split staging, nothing else changed), gated by autopsy first
   (spills and VGPR) before any timing run.
3. **Band routing thresholds DIFFER: llama ends the vec band at
   8 and starts the matrix path at 9, with RDNA3-specific
   NUM_ROWS tuning inside the band (4 rows at NUM_COLS >= 5 in
   the integer path); ours ships a single matrix threshold at
   16 and per-row GEMV streaming below it.**
   Spec: ggml-vulkan-types.h:362, ggml-vulkan.cpp:7402,
   2880-2885. Payoff: our dose sweep shows the cost of the
   wrong band shape directly (caps 4/8/12 below control, 16
   above; bench/mmv-verdict-2026-11-05.md), and decode-side
   verify batches live exactly in this band. Owner: the
   band-routing lane in flight; llama's 8-cap and the RDNA3
   4-row rule are the cross-check values its win map must
   reconcile with our per-family sweep data (our K20/K21 win
   rows llama's MMVQ gate would exclude for Q6_K, so the map
   is a cross-check, not a copy).
4. **Split-K is ABSENT in our MMQ.**
   Spec: k >= 2048 and tile grid at most half the shader cores
   gives up to 8 splits, 256-aligned, with
   `mul_mat_split_k_reduce.comp` (ggml-vulkan.cpp:5916-5955).
   Payoff: our profile's worst per-byte dispatches are the
   small ones split-K exists for: the 256-wide Q6_K KV-side
   projections run 416 dispatches at 3.2 GB/s for 186 ms
   (2.8% of prefill GPU time), and at batch 64 with M 256 the
   tile grid is 4 workgroups on a 96-CU card. Owner: the K23
   MMQ follow-up (same lane as gap 2, second step), or the
   dispatch-fusion follow-up the profile note already names;
   split-K and fusion attack the same 186 ms from opposite
   sides and only one should be built first, decided by the
   K23 autopsy results.
5. **Flash attention: no K/V shared-memory staging, f32 KV,
   and no coopmat1 path in K6.**
   Spec: Bc 32 blocks with staged K/V (flash_attn_base.glsl:
   4-21), path selection and AMD scalar tuning
   (ggml-vulkan.cpp:1200-1245, 1334-1375), f16 cache
   precision. Payoff: flash is 1,013.1 ms, 15.2% of prefill
   GPU time at 1,022 tokens and grows quadratically in chunk
   position; the profile note prices halving it at 507 ms now
   and calls it the likely #1 lever at 4k context. Owner: the
   flash rework follow-up (profile attack 4); the f32 to f16
   KV change is a resident-KV format change and must be its
   own gated step, not folded into a kernel rewrite.
6. **MMVQ (Q8_1 activations in the vec band) is ABSENT; our
   band kernels run f32 activations.**
   Spec: ggml-vulkan.cpp:6656-6700 and 6783 (batch > 1 always
   quantizes on AMD when k >= 2048; Q6_K excluded off Intel).
   Payoff: unmeasured on our side, and the sign is genuinely
   open: llama accepts a quantize dispatch and integer dots
   to cut activation traffic 4x in the band, while our f32
   K19 already beat its control by 13% at cap 16. Owner: a
   small prototype inside the band-routing lane's follow-up,
   judged by the same sweep harness; do not build before the
   routing map lands, because the two changes confound.
7. **RMS norm + RoPE fusion placement DIFFERS (theirs inside
   the norm shader, ours at K9 attention prep), and the
   standalone norm chain has no partials path for wide rows.**
   Spec: rms_norm.comp:15-40 fusion variants, block sizes
   128-1024 host-chosen (ggml-vulkan.cpp:3264-3271). Payoff:
   the whole norm chain is 0.7% of prefill GPU time
   (43.5 ms); at decode it is a handful of small dispatches
   per token against a 28 ms token budget. No lane; record
   only, revisit if decode chain overhead becomes the named
   blocker in the spec-round cost map.
8. **llama-side wart, no action: Q6_K gets staging load
   width 2 in mul_mm while Q4_K/Q5_K get 4**
   (mul_mm.comp:43-48, mul_mm_funcs.glsl Q6_K branch). It
   applies to the f16-activation staging path, not to
   mul_mat_vec and not to the cm1 path RDNA3 runs. Recorded
   so nobody imports it as a spec to match; our K14/K20
   already document the same finding
   (bench/mmv-q6k-2026-11-05.md).

## What this settles

The specs are all takeable, and most of them are already taken:
the GEMV family matches llama's shape and beats its measured
streaming rate; the MMV band matches in form; the chain kernels
match in geometry. The parity gap concentrates in exactly two
places: the prefill product (coopmat cm1, the staging repack,
split-K, tile classes above 64) and the band thresholds. Both
already have lanes or named follow-ups above; nothing in this
note requires a new research question, only builds.

===== END FILE: bench/llama-parity-specs-2026-11-06.md =====

===== FILE: bench/mmq-wide-bench.sh =====
#!/bin/bash
# Wide-tile MMQ prefill proof: session-level A/B of the
# resident prefill ladder, old MMQ vs wide MMQ, on the real
# Glimmer file.
#
# The A/B switch is the backend's own config, not a rebuild:
# WGPU_COMPUTE_MMQ_WIDE_MIN_ROWS names the chunk row count
# at which the session starts preferring the wide-tile
# double-buffered products (K15/K16) over the standard ones
# (K13/K14). Setting it to 65 (past the 64-row chunk cap)
# takes the wide form out of the ladder entirely: that is
# the "old" position. The default (32) is the "wide"
# position. Decode is untouched in both positions (the
# wide form only exists on the matrix path).
#
# Method, matching bench/gpu-resident-2026-10-30.md's
# session prefill record: repeated-sentence prompts at two
# lengths (about 254 and about 1,024 tokens; the exact
# counts come from the runner's own prompt_tokens= line),
# gross tok/s at the long length, and the marginal rate
# between the two lengths, which strips the fixed cost.
# Each (config, length) runs twice and the faster prefill
# time stands (clock-state noise only ever slows a run).
# The per-tensor half of the proof is the mmq_bench table
# at batch 64, run once at the end (its `mmq wide w<N>`
# rows against the `mmq m<N>` rows).
#
# Run on ubuntu-server with the GPU free:
#   bench/mmq-wide-bench.sh [MODEL]
# MODEL defaults to the same path mmq_bench uses. Logs and
# the summary land in /tmp/bench-results/.
set -u
OUT=/tmp/bench-results
mkdir -p "$OUT"
MODEL="${1:-/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf}"
[ -f "$MODEL" ] || { echo "SKIP: model not found: $MODEL" | tee -a "$OUT/summary.txt"; exit 0; }

export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT" || exit 2
echo "=== mmq wide bench $(date -Is) ===" | tee -a "$OUT/summary.txt"
echo "model: $MODEL" | tee -a "$OUT/summary.txt"

cargo build --release -p itak-loader --example glimmer_generate 2>&1 | tail -2
cargo build --release -p wgpu-compute --example mmq_bench 2>&1 | tail -2
GEN="$ROOT/target/release/examples/glimmer_generate"
MMQB="$ROOT/target/release/examples/mmq_bench"
[ -x "$GEN" ] || { echo "FAIL: glimmer_generate did not build" | tee -a "$OUT/summary.txt"; exit 1; }

# Repeated-sentence prompts (the gpu-resident note's
# method). "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog."
# tokenizes to about ten tokens; the runner reports the
# true counts and the math below uses those, not these
# targets.
sentence="The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. "
prompt_short=""
for _ in $(seq 1 25); do prompt_short="$prompt_short$sentence"; done
prompt_long=""
for _ in $(seq 1 102); do prompt_long="$prompt_long$sentence"; done

# run_prefill CONFIG MIN_ROWS PROMPT LOG
# Prints "<ms> <tokens>" of the faster of two runs.
run_prefill() {
  local cfg="$1" min_rows="$2" prompt="$3" log="$4"
  local best_ms="" best_tok="" rep ms tok
  for rep in 1 2; do
    WGPU_COMPUTE_MMQ_WIDE_MIN_ROWS="$min_rows" \
      "$GEN" "$MODEL" "$prompt" 4 --gpu >> "$log" 2>&1
    read -r ms tok <<< "$(grep -E '^phase=prefill ' "$log" | tail -1 \
      | sed -E 's/.*ms=([0-9]+) prompt_tokens=([0-9]+).*/\1 \2/')"
    [ -n "${ms:-}" ] || { echo "FAIL $cfg rep $rep: no prefill line in $log" | tee -a "$OUT/summary.txt"; return 1; }
    if [ -z "$best_ms" ] || [ "$ms" -lt "$best_ms" ]; then best_ms="$ms"; best_tok="$tok"; fi
  done
  echo "$best_ms $best_tok"
}

declare -A MS TOK
for cfg in old wide; do
  if [ "$cfg" = old ]; then min_rows=65; else min_rows=32; fi
  for len in short long; do
    if [ "$len" = short ]; then prompt="$prompt_short"; else prompt="$prompt_long"; fi
    log="$OUT/mmq_wide_${cfg}_${len}.log"
    : > "$log"
    read -r MS[$cfg,$len] TOK[$cfg,$len] <<< "$(run_prefill "$cfg" "$min_rows" "$prompt" "$log")" || exit 1
    echo "$cfg $len: ${TOK[$cfg,$len]} tokens in ${MS[$cfg,$len]} ms (log $log)" | tee -a "$OUT/summary.txt"
  done
done

for cfg in old wide; do
  awk -v cfg="$cfg" \
      -v ms_s="${MS[$cfg,short]}" -v tok_s="${TOK[$cfg,short]}" \
      -v ms_l="${MS[$cfg,long]}" -v tok_l="${TOK[$cfg,long]}" '
    BEGIN {
      gross = tok_l / ms_l * 1000
      marg = (tok_l - tok_s) / ((ms_l - ms_s) / 1000)
      printf "%s: gross at %d tokens %.1f tok/s; marginal (%d -> %d tokens) %.1f tok/s\n", \
        cfg, tok_l, gross, tok_s, tok_l, marg
    }' | tee -a "$OUT/summary.txt"
done

echo "--- per-tensor table (mmq_bench, batch 64) ---" | tee -a "$OUT/summary.txt"
"$MMQB" --model "$MODEL" --batch 64 > "$OUT/mmq_wide_pertensor.log" 2>&1
grep -E "^adapter|mmq |gemm |gemv " "$OUT/mmq_wide_pertensor.log" | tee -a "$OUT/summary.txt" || true
echo "MMQ_WIDE_DONE" | tee -a "$OUT/summary.txt"

===== END FILE: bench/mmq-wide-bench.sh =====

===== FILE: bench/mmq-wide-tile-2026-11-03.md =====
# Wide-tile double-buffered MMQ for prefill, 2026-11-03 (draft)

Status: code landed on the build lane; parity and compile gates run on
the build VM (results below); the server rate proof is scripted and
waiting on a free GPU window. Nothing in this note claims a server
rate until `bench/mmq-wide-bench.sh` has run there.

## The problem this attacks

From `bench/gpu-resident-2026-10-30.md`'s session record on the
RX 7900 XTX: the MMQ build prefills at a marginal 161 tok/s (gross
135.8 tok/s at 1,024 tokens) against llama.cpp Vulkan's 998 tok/s on
the same card. That note names the causes, in order: (1) occupancy:
the m64 MMQ tiles stage 41-45 KB of workgroup memory, so one
workgroup is resident per CU, one super-block deep, with a barrier
per super-block (78 barriers across one ffn_down workgroup), so
latency hiding rests on in-thread ILP alone; (2) the Q6_K fold does
twice the f32 work per dot; (3) the non-projection chunk chain was
28% of marginal time at GEMM-era measurement, which bounds the
session marginal near 330 tok/s even with infinitely fast
projections, until that chain is profiled and attacked separately.
This lane attacks cause (1) only. The note's own named next step
was "the wide-tile (128x128-class) double-buffered MMQ plus a
profile of that chain"; the chain profile remains open work.

## What shipped

Two new kernels behind the existing selection seam:

- `crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/k15_q4k_mmq_wide.rs`: K15, the
  Q4_K wide-tile double-buffered MMQ.
- `crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/k16_q6k_mmq_wide.rs`: K16, the
  Q6_K sibling.

Both consume exactly what K13/K14 consume (the weights' existing
device layouts, K12's quantized activation buffers) and write the
same output layout, so the session swaps product forms without
moving a byte. The math is K13/K14 term for term: exact i32
DP4A dots, the per-sub-block scale fold in f32, no downcast before
the accumulation completes. Decode (1-row) paths are untouched:
the wide form exists only on the matrix path past
`GEMM_MIN_ROWS`, same as the standard MMQ.

Selection ladder (session.rs, via `mmq_product_q4k` /
`mmq_product_q6k`, shared by the plain, gated, and SwiGLU forms):

1. Wide product (K15/K16) when the chunk batch is at or past the
   backend's wide row threshold.
2. Standard product (K13/K14) behind it.
3. GEMM form (K10/K11), then the GEMV forms, as before.

Every refusal in the ladder is logged by name through the crate's
diag seam; the choice is made at plan-build time, never inside a
dispatch.

The wide row threshold is config, not a compiled constant:
`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMQ_WIDE_MIN_ROWS`, default 32, resolved at backend
construction in compute.rs and logged. Setting it to 65 (past the
64-row chunk cap) removes the wide form from the ladder entirely:
that is the A/B control position the bench script uses, so old vs
new is one process flag, not a rebuild.

## Tile geometry, and why

Tile: `tile_n` output rows x the full 64-row batch, computed by
`tile_n * 2` threads. Each thread owns a 4-output-row x 8-batch-row
sub-tile (32 accumulators). Against K13/K14's 4x4 sub-tiles:

- The batch axis doubling (4 to 8 rows per thread) is what makes
  the wide tile affordable: every staged weight word feeds 8
  activation rows instead of 4, so the weight tile for 128 output
  rows costs the staging of K13's 64, per step.
- Workgroup sizes are 128-256 threads (vs K13's 128/256 at
  m32/m64), so the wider tile does not shrink the thread count
  that hides latency inside the workgroup.

K direction: staging runs in half-super-block steps of 4
sub-blocks (128 elements). A step is the unit the ping-pong
pipeline moves. The half split is not arbitrary: it is Q4_K's own
group boundary (sub-blocks 2h and 2h+1 share a group's raw words)
and Q6_K's own half boundary (sub-blocks 0-3 are h=0, 4-7 are
h=1), so neither family's staging straddles a step.

Double buffering: two parity buffer sets, generated as separate
named arrays (w_qs0/w_qs1, x_qs0/x_qs1, and the scale planes).
The step loop is unrolled by parity (steps processed in pairs) so
every workgroup-memory offset in the inner product is a
compile-time constant: K13's record is explicit that its first
runtime-indexed build ran at the f32 GEMM's rate, and the wide
kernel keeps that addressing discipline. The pipeline form is:
prologue stages step 0, one barrier; then per pair, stage step
s+1 into parity 1 (its global loads issue first), compute step s
from parity 0, one barrier, stage step s+2 into parity 0,
compute step s+1, one barrier. One barrier per step, against
K13's two barriers per super-block (four per two steps), and the
next step's loads are in flight across the current step's
compute. Parity buffers are only overwritten after a barrier
separates the overwrite from the buffer's last reads.

Why not a full-super-block (or deeper) double buffer: it does
not fit. Workgroup storage for Q4_K totals 320*N + 20,992 bytes
at tile width N (per parity buffer: weight words 128 B/row,
weight scale pairs 32 B/row, the skewed activation tile 8,448 B,
the activation scale pairs 2,048 B), so a full-K-depth scheme
at any useful width, or a 128-wide tile with whole-super-block
steps (640 B/row/parity), exceeds the 64 KiB grant outright. The half-step pipeline at w128 stages 61,952
bytes total for K15. For K16 the same geometry costs 5,120 bytes
more across the two parities (its activation record is a vec4,
carrying the two precomputed half sums the Q6_K fold needs, where
Q4_K's is a vec2), so w128 would stage 66,048 bytes: 512 bytes
over the grant. K16 therefore ships w112 (60,928 bytes) on a
64 KiB device. The candidate ladder [128, 112, 96, 64] is shared;
each family ships the widest candidate its own staging fits, and
refuses by name below the narrowest. The recorded staging table:

| shape | K15 (Q4_K) bytes | K16 (Q6_K) bytes |
|-------|------------------|------------------|
| w128  | 61,952           | 66,048 (over)    |
| w112  | 56,832           | 60,928           |
| w96   | 51,712           | 55,808           |
| w64   | 41,472           | 45,568           |

The activation tile keeps K13/K14's bank-conflict fix: row
stride 33 words (32 + 1 skew) per step.

## Parity results (build VM)

Run 2026-11-03 on the build VM, `cargo test -p wgpu-compute`
(debug profile): all 13 test targets pass, 98 tests total,
including the 48 lib unit tests. Of those, the wide kernels'
own in-module tests pass: the staging table above (asserted
byte for byte at all four candidate widths, both families),
the shipped-shape selection against storage grants (16,384 B
grants nothing; 41,472 B grants K15 w64; 45,568 B grants K16
w64; 65,536 B grants K15 w128 and K16 w112), the candidate-set
refusal, and the shader-structure tests (workgroup size,
DP4A presence, both parity buffer sets present, exactly
three `workgroupBarrier()` sites in the generated source).
The backend's wide-threshold config resolution is unit-tested
(default, explicit values, the 65 control position, garbage
input falling back to the default). `cargo fmt --check` and
`cargo clippy -p wgpu-compute --all-targets` are both clean.

What did NOT run here, stated plainly: this VM enumerates no
wgpu adapters at all. The six GPU parity tests in
`crates/wgpu-compute/tests/k15_k16_mmq_wide.rs` (batch sweep
1-64 at every buildable wide shape for both families, the
deep-width and short-width pipeline geometries, the gated
and SwiGLU activation forms, the prepare refusals) therefore
skip under the default selection policy, exactly as the
K13/K14 gates do on this machine, and the shader-compile leg
in `tests/shader_compile.rs` reports the same absence: the
generated WGSL has not yet been through a driver's validator
anywhere. Both gaps close on the server before any rate is
trusted: the parity file runs there under
`cargo test -p wgpu-compute --test k15_k16_mmq_wide` (the
server adapter is policy-eligible), and both bench vehicles
construct the K15/K16 pipelines before timing anything, so a
WGSL defect fails the run loudly at construction instead of
producing a number.

## What the server run must prove

First the correctness gate that could not run on the build VM:
`cargo test -p wgpu-compute --test k15_k16_mmq_wide` on the
server must pass all six parity tests with the measured diffs
and quantization bands printed (the K13/K14 record's bands were
0.36% for Q4_K and 0.42% for Q6_K; the wide kernels run the
same math, so bands in that neighborhood are the expectation,
and anything visibly wider is a defect, not a tuning fact).

Then run `bench/mmq-wide-bench.sh` on ubuntu-server with the
GPU free. It builds both bench vehicles, then runs the
resident session (`glimmer_generate --gpu`) on the real
Glimmer file at two repeated-sentence prompt lengths (about
254 and about 1,024 tokens) in both ladder positions, and
finishes with the per-tensor `mmq_bench` table at batch 64.
The run proves the lane if, in the same window:

1. Per-tensor: the `mmq wide w128` (Q4_K) and `mmq wide w112`
   (Q6_K) rows beat the best standard-MMQ rows (`mmq m64`) on the
   largest tensors of each family, product-only and with the
   quantize composed in.
2. Session: gross prefill tok/s at the long prompt and the
   marginal rate between the two lengths both improve over the
   old-ladder position in the same run. The comparison that
   matters is old vs wide in one window, not either number
   against the 2026-10-30 record (different window, different
   clocks).
3. Canary discipline from the earlier notes still holds: the
   batch-1 GEMV stream rates in the per-tensor table stay in
   their healthy band (~816 GB/s Q4_K, ~832 GB/s Q6_K), so a
   slow window cannot masquerade as a kernel verdict.
4. The generated tokens are unchanged: same prompt, greedy
   session, the wide ladder must produce the old ladder's token
   stream (the parity tests gate the math; this gates the
   wiring).

Expectation management, stated before the run: even a perfect
projection kernel cannot lift the session marginal past roughly
330 tok/s while the non-projection chunk chain keeps its
measured share (cause 3 above). A wide-MMQ win that lands the
marginal in the 200-330 band is the design working as intended;
closing the rest of the gap to llama.cpp's 998 is the chain
profile and whatever it indicts, which is the next lane, not
this one.

## Open edges

- The default wide threshold (32 rows) is a reasoned starting
  value, not a measured one. The bench script's per-tensor table
  is at batch 64; if the server window allows, a batch-32
  mmq_bench run (`--batch 32`) checks the threshold's edge
  directly, and the default moves if the table says so.
- Occupancy after this change: w128/w112 stage 57-62 KB, still
  one workgroup resident per CU. The win, if it comes, comes
  from barrier count, load/compute overlap, and per-thread ILP
  depth (32 dots per sub-block step against 16), not from
  residency. If the server table shows the wide rows at parity
  with m64, the next lever is a narrower activation record
  (staging the Q6_K half sums only, not the vec4) to buy a
  second resident workgroup, and that trade belongs in a
  follow-up note with this run's numbers attached.

## Server A/B verdict (2026-11-04, RX 7900 XTX, main 864dffd)

The wide kernels are numerically correct (parity gate green on the
adapter, quantization bands 0.0036 Q4_K and 0.0042 Q6_K at batch 64)
and they FAIL their purpose:

- Per tensor they are about 3.5x SLOWER than the standard MMQ:
  Q6_K m64 product 2.567 ms against wide w112 9.003 ms; Q4_K m64
  1.556 ms against wide w128 5.350 ms.
- In the real session the wide ladder HANGS: RADV reports the
  context lost with a hard recovery, and no prefill line is ever
  produced, at both bench lengths. The card recovered on its own.
- The old ladder in the same window: gross 123.1 tok/s at 1,022
  tokens, marginal 139.6 tok/s (252 to 1,022).

Verdict: the standard MMQ (K13/K14) stays the shipping position.
DEFAULT_WIDE_MIN_ROWS is now 65 in compute.rs, which takes the
wide form out of the ladder by default; it remains in the tree,
opt-in by env, for whoever wants to chase the occupancy question
with these numbers attached.

===== END FILE: bench/mmq-wide-tile-2026-11-03.md =====

===== FILE: bench/mmv-band-routing-2026-11-06.md =====
# MMV band routing: the mid-band cliff removed by routing (2026-11-06)

The 2026-11-06 K19 verdict continuation
(`bench/mmv-verdict-2026-11-05.md`, steps 2-4) proved
the register-streaming family correct everywhere and
fast at the top of its band, and convicted it in the
middle: at depth 1, session dose caps 4, 8, and 12 all
landed BELOW the shipped control (14.71 / 15.23 /
15.20 effective tok/s against control 16.98, verify
medians about 50 ms against 45), while cap 16 landed
above it (19.26, verify about 38.5 ms). The verdict's
decision rule therefore kept the default at 1 (off):
the no-cliff condition was not met. The verdict named
the remedy itself: "Any future flip needs a band floor
informed by the per-batch table (for example, routing
only the top of the band)".

This lane is that remedy, in its general form. The
single global ceiling (`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS`)
no longer decides routing alone. Under it sits a
routing table keyed by (quant family, shape class):
each family's register-streaming product (K19 for
Q4_K, K20 for Q6_K, K21 for Q5_K) serves a projection
only at batch rows where the 2026-11-06 sweep
measured it beating the GEMV form it displaces.
Every other cell falls through to the ladder exactly
as before (MMV, then K18, then chunked, then GEMV;
the ladder's order and every kernel are unchanged).
This note is the table's audit trail: the measured
cells, the rule that turned them into ranges, and
the config surface that carries them.

## Method

Data: the committed verdict sweep,
`bench/results/mmv-sweep-20261106-212335/`
(control.csv, mmv.csv; the K18 and chunked arms are
not inputs to this table). Every cell agreed with
GEMV under the harness's correctness guard
(`agree=1` in all 99 cells of both arms), so every
number below is a timing verdict on a correct
kernel, never a correctness trade.

A cell is (family, shape, rows): the control arm's
GEMV median against the MMV arm's median at the same
cell, both from the same run, 25 reps, diag
timestamp timing. Verdicts:

- WIN: MMV median < 0.98 x control median.
- TIE: within +/-2% (0.98-1.02). A tie is not a
  measured win: the cell falls through. GEMV is the
  incumbent; routing needs evidence, not parity.
- LOSS: MMV median > 1.02 x control median.

Measured rows are {2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 12, 16}.
Measured cells are authoritative, including where
they break a run (Q4_K FFN row 3 is a measured LOSS
between wins at rows 2 and 4; the table routes
around it, see below). Rows the sweep did not
measure (10, 11, 13, 14, 15) are admitted only
where two measured WINs bracket them inside the
MMV-routed range: rows 10-11 inherit wherever rows
9 and 12 both win, and rows 13-15 inherit only for
Q5_K attention and FFN, where rows 12 and 16 both
win. For Q4_K and Q6_K there is no MMV measurement
at row 16 at all (both arms serve the MMQ forms
there; the matrix rung runs before the MMV rung in
`prepare_proj`), so their cells end at 12, the last
measured win, and rows 13-15 fall through.

control. "Routed" is the shipped table's answer for
the cell under a fully open ceiling.

## The derived routing table

Reading the WIN cells as inclusive batch ranges
(with the bracketing rule for unmeasured rows)
gives the shipped defaults. This is the whole
policy; it lives in `default_mmv_band` in
`crates/wgpu-compute/src/compute.rs`, and the unit
test `mmv_default_bands_match_the_measured_win_map`
pins it batch by batch against this section.

| family | shape | routed batches | env override |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q4_K (K19) | attn | 6-12 | `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_Q4K_ATTN_ROWS` |
| Q4_K (K19) | ffn | 2, 4-12 | `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_Q4K_FFN_ROWS` |
| Q4_K (K19) | kv | 2-3 | `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_Q4K_KV_ROWS` |
| Q5_K (K21) | attn | 2-16 | `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_Q5K_ATTN_ROWS` |
| Q5_K (K21) | ffn | 3-16 | `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_Q5K_FFN_ROWS` |
| Q5_K (K21) | kv | 16 | `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_Q5K_KV_ROWS` |
| Q6_K (K20) | attn | 2-12 | `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_Q6K_ATTN_ROWS` |
| Q6_K (K20) | ffn | 2-12 | `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_Q6K_FFN_ROWS` |
| Q6_K (K20) | kv | 12 | `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_Q6K_KV_ROWS` |

Cell syntax, for the defaults and the overrides
alike: comma-separated inclusive ranges, each a
single row ("16") or a span ("6-12"), whitespace
ignored. Parsed ranges are intersected with the
kernels' own band (2..=16). Any malformed item
(empty, non-numeric, a reversed span) makes the
whole value unparsable, and the cell falls back to
its shipped value: the fail-closed direction every
resolver in compute.rs takes, with the fallback
logged at construction by name
(`log_mmv_band_fallbacks`). Setting a cell to "1"
closes it (a valid cell that routes nothing).
The global ceiling composes on top, unchanged:
a batch routes only when it is inside its cell
AND at or under `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS`, so
the dose caps of the A/B clip the table from above
(cap 4 admits only the routed cells at rows 2-4,
and so on). The construction log prints the
resolved table on the diag channel (`mmv config:
...; bands q4k[attn 6-12 ffn 2,4-12 kv 2-3]
q5k[attn 2-16 ffn 3-16 kv 16] q6k[attn 2-12 ffn
2-12 kv 12]`), and a batch the ceiling admits but
a cell excludes is logged by name at plan build
(`mmv q4k attn excludes batch 2 ...; the ladder
continues`) wherever a binary enables the crate's
debug flag (`diag::set_debug`), the same seam the
kernel refusals already use.

Two cells deserve a named sentence each. Q5_K
attention row 4 is the thinnest win in the table
(ratio 0.979 against the 0.98 line); it also sits
between wins at rows 3 and 5, so the bracketing
rule would admit its row even as an unmeasured
one. Q5_K KV row 7 is the worst cell in the table
(ratio 3.229); under the old flat routing every
cap that reached row 7 paid it on any Q5_K
KV-shaped projection the ladder saw.

## Shape classification, and what it does not know

The sweep measured three shapes, all at input
width 6656: attn (out 6656), ffn (out 19968), kv
(out 256). A session sees more geometries than
that, so `mmv_shape_of` (compute.rs) classifies by
relative geometry: out <= in/8 is KV, out >= 2*in
is FFN, everything else is attention. The measured
cells sit far from both boundaries (256 is 1/26 of
6656; 19968 is 3x), so every real Glimmer
projection classifies unambiguously:

| projection | in | out | class | measured? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| attention K, V | 6656 | 256 | kv | yes, the kv cells |
| attention Q | 6656 | 4096 | attn | class only |
| attention O | 4096 | 6656 | attn | class only |
| FFN gate, up | 6656 | 19968 | ffn | yes, the ffn cells |
| FFN down | 19968 | 6656 | attn | class only |
| lm_head (Q5_K) | 6656 | 202048 | ffn | does not route here |

The disclosures, plainly: input-width variation is
unmeasured everywhere (the sweep fixed in=6656),
and the Q, O, and down geometries inherit the
attention cells by classification, not by
measurement. If a future sweep measures those
geometries and disagrees, the cells are env
config and this note's table is the thing to
correct. The lm_head never reaches `prepare_proj`
(it is served by the fused-finish path), so no
Q5_K cell binds it today; the Q5_K cells bind in
the sweep harness (`ProjBench` prepares through
`prepare_proj` itself) and on any plain Q5_K
projection, which is exactly the exposure finding
of `bench/mmv-q5k-2026-11-05.md` restated.

## The session working points under routing

At the two depths the verdict A/B ran, the verify
batch is the whole story (depth 1: batch 2;
depth 6: batch 7):

- Batch 2 routes: Q4_K ffn (0.722), Q4_K kv
  (0.859), Q5_K attn (0.756), Q6_K attn (0.690),
  Q6_K ffn (0.757). It no longer routes Q4_K attn
  (1.331, the depth-1 cliff's largest single
  cell), Q5_K ffn (1.297), Q5_K kv (1.117), or
  Q6_K kv (1.213).
- Batch 7 routes: Q4_K attn (0.889), Q4_K ffn
  (0.629), Q5_K attn (0.599), Q5_K ffn (0.515),
  Q6_K attn (0.762), Q6_K ffn (0.449). It no
  longer routes any family's kv cell (Q4_K 1.039,
  Q5_K 3.229, Q6_K 1.021).

Under the caps the dose sweep convicted, routing
admits only measured wins: cap 4 admits Q4_K ffn
{2,4}, Q4_K kv {2,3}, Q5_K attn {2,3,4}, Q5_K ffn
{3,4}, Q6_K attn/ffn {2,3,4}; cap 8 adds the
winning cells at rows 5-8; cap 12 adds rows 9 and
12 and Q6_K kv {12}; cap 16 adds the Q5_K run to
16. No cap can rebuild the cliff out of these
cells; that is the claim the server A/B below is
sequenced to test.

## What did not change

The ladder order (MMV, K18, chunked, GEMV), every
kernel, the kernels' own band (2..=16, refused at
prepare), and the fall-through contract: a cell
exclusion returns `None` from the same `try_mmv_*`
composition step a prepare refusal uses, and the
next rung serves the projection. The shipped
ceiling default stays 1 (off). The verdict's rule
moved defaults on session evidence, and this lane
has none: it makes the routed configuration
cliff-free per the micro-bench table, and whether
that earns a default flip is the A/B's question,
not this note's.

## VM gates (this lane)

- `cargo test -p wgpu-compute`: 212 passed, 0
  failed across the crate's binaries, including
  the six new policy tests (parse forms, malformed
  rejection, fallback resolution, shape
  classification, the win-map pin, ceiling
  composition). GPU legs skip on this VM by
  design, as everywhere in this crate.
- `cargo clippy -p wgpu-compute --all-targets -- -D warnings`:
  clean.
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

## Server A/B protocol (the cliff proof)

Run on the cleared card (VRAM guard reads
33,271,808 bytes before every arm), under the
phase lock, staged from the main this lane merges
into, manifest-verified like the verdict runs.
Build once:

```
cargo build --release -p itak-spec --example spec_generate_gpu -p wgpu-compute --example mmv_sweep
```

Session arms: `spec_generate_gpu`, both mode,
default Stage 1 prompt, 64 tokens, GPU draft, at
depths 1 and 6, for each of: control (env unset)
and routed at `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS` =
4, 8, 12, 16, with NO `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_*_ROWS`
set (the shipped cells are the configuration
under test):

```
[WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=<cap>] ./target/release/examples/spec_generate_gpu \
  /mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  /mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/dflash-Muse-Glimmer-30B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  64 <depth>
```

Pass criteria, per depth:

- IDENTITY PASS and GOLDEN PASS in every arm.
- Acceptance and resident dispatch counts
  identical across arms (the verdict's purity
  condition: differences are timing only).
- Every routed cap's effective tok/s >= the
  same-session control's. Caps 4, 8, 12 are the
  cliff test: the flat routing put them at
  14.71 / 15.23 / 15.20 against a 16.98 control;
  routed, they must not land below control.
- Routed cap 16 >= the flat-routing cap 16 on
  record (19.26 at depth 1, 10.27 at depth 6),
  within session noise: routing removed only
  losing cells from that configuration.
- Verify medians (`spec.verify.end`) at or under
  control at every cap.

Sweep confirmation, same session: re-run
`bench/mmv-sweep.sh`. In the mmv arm's CSV
(`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=16`), the `kernel`
column must show k19/k20/k21 exactly in this
note's routed cells and the GEMV kernels exactly
in the unrouted ones, cell for cell against the
table above; routed-cell medians should reproduce
the 2026-11-06 MMV arm within noise, and
unrouted-cell medians the control arm's. Any cell
that disagrees with its table entry is a finding
against this note, and the cell's env override is
the interim fix while the table is corrected.

===== END FILE: bench/mmv-band-routing-2026-11-06.md =====

===== FILE: bench/mmv-bench-harness-2026-11-05.md =====
# Small-batch sweep harness (2026-11-05)

One harness that measures every small-batch kernel
variant head to head through the session's own
routing, so the MMV verdict (and every later
autotune pass) reads from one table instead of four
ad hoc benches.

## What landed

- `crates/wgpu-compute/examples/mmv_sweep.rs`: the
  harness binary.
- `ProjBench` / `ProjBenchCall` in
  `crates/wgpu-compute/src/session.rs` (exported from
  the crate root): a projection uploaded from raw
  parts that prepares through `prepare_proj` itself,
  the session's routing ladder, and reports which
  kernel form the ladder chose (`kernel_name()`),
  whether that form quantizes its activation
  (`quantized()`), and its dispatch count. The
  harness measures the variant a forward would
  dispatch under the same environment, by
  construction: there is no second routing
  implementation to drift.
- `crates/wgpu-compute/tests/proj_bench.rs`: the
  handle's contract (routes to the GEMV form at
  shipped defaults and matches it exactly; an
  uncovered dtype is refused by name).
- `bench/mmv-sweep.sh`: the arm runner (below).

## The cell matrix

Per run: quant family {Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K} x shape x
rows {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 12, 16} = 99 cells.
Shapes are synthetic tensors at the real Glimmer
geometry, input width 6656 (the model's hidden)
throughout:

| shape | out | what it stands for |
|---|---|---|
| attn | 6656 | the attention-sized projections |
| ffn | 19968 | FFN up |
| kv | 256 | the K and V projections |

The KV width is the model's real one:
`GlimmerConfig::k_width()`, KV heads times key
length, 2 x 128 = 256
(crates/muse-glimmer/src/config.rs, whose real-file
test pins `k_width() == 256`; session.rs sizes its
K/V projection buffers from it). An earlier sketch
of this harness carried 2048 for this row; that is
the sliding window size, not a projection width,
and no tensor in the model has it.

Synthetic weights use the kernel tests' fixture
discipline (rotating f16 scale headers over LCG
payloads, tests/k18_small_batch.rs), one tensor per
(quant, shape), reused across all row counts. Peak
device memory is about 0.8 GB (both the routed
handle and the direct GEMV control hold a copy).

## Measurement method

- Warmup dispatches (3 by default) are excluded;
  every cell then gets 25 timed repetitions by
  default (the verdict floor is 20; a run below it
  prints that it is a smoke, not a verdict run).
  The CSV reports median and min per cell.
- GPU time comes from the diag timestamps system:
  one `DiagStamp` around the whole projection
  composition per repetition, so a composed form
  (K12 quantize plus its product) is timed as the
  session pays for it, whole. Available when the
  context carries a recorder
  (`WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing` and a device granting
  `TIMESTAMP_QUERY` plus
  `TIMESTAMP_QUERY_INSIDE_PASSES`); the sweep script
  exports the env. Otherwise each repetition is
  bracketed on the wall clock around submit plus
  poll, which includes submit overhead. The run
  prints `timing_method: diag_timestamps|wall_clock`
  on stdout, and the script keeps it in the arm log.
  A cell whose stamp records do not line up with its
  repetition count (dropped or missing records) is
  re-timed on the wall clock, with the substitution
  printed on stderr and in the log.
- `gbps_median` is the tensor's resident bytes over
  the median time: the stream rate of one dispatch
  of the composition. For the GEMV form at R rows
  the hardware re-reads the tensor per row inside
  the dispatch, so effective DRAM traffic is R times
  the CSV's `weight_bytes`; the matrix and
  small-batch forms stream it once. (The same
  convention as bench/small-batch-2026-11-04.md.)

## Correctness guard

Before any timing, each cell's routed output is
compared against the GEMV form's output for the
same inputs, the GEMV prepared directly from the
kernel pipelines (K1/K2/K3) over the same bytes.
Agreement mirrors the crate's kernel tests
(tests/k18_small_batch.rs): a form that quantizes
its activation (the MMQ and small-batch forms)
answers to the 5% quantization band
(`check_quant_band`), an f32 form to the tight
reassociation bound `2e-3 + 5e-5 * scale`
(`check_close`). A cell that disagrees is written
with `agree=0` and named on stderr; it is timed
anyway, because a fast wrong kernel is a finding,
but it can never pass as agreement.

## CSV shape

One row per cell:

```
variant_env,kernel,quant,rows,out_cols,median_ms,min_ms,weight_bytes,gbps_median,agree
```

`variant_env` is the arm label plus the routing env
actually present in the process
(`WGPU_COMPUTE_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS`,
`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS`,
`WGPU_COMPUTE_WIDE_MIN_ROWS`,
`WGPU_COMPUTE_CHUNK_ROWS`,
`WGPU_COMPUTE_CHUNK_MAX_ROWS`), or `env:none`.
`kernel` is the form the ladder chose, under its
diag-system name; at 16 rows the control arm itself
routes to the matrix forms (that is the shipped
`GEMM_MIN_ROWS` behavior), and the column says so.

## Running the verdict

On the server, card clear, under the phase lock:

```
flock -w 14400 /tmp/itak-phase.lock bench/mmv-sweep.sh
```

That builds the harness once and runs four arms,
writing `bench/results/mmv-sweep-<timestamp>/`
with `control.csv`, `k18.csv`, `mmv.csv`,
`chunked.csv`, and a `.log` per arm (adapter name,
timing method, per-cell lines, disagreement
warnings). Read the arms side by side per
(quant, shape, rows): `median_ms` is the verdict,
`kernel` proves which form each arm actually ran,
and any `agree=0` cell disqualifies its row.

Partial sweeps forward extra harness args to every
arm, for example `bench/mmv-sweep.sh --rows 2,7`
for the two verify working points. A single arm by
hand is just the binary under that arm's env:

```
WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=16 \
  target/release/examples/mmv_sweep --label mmv --out mmv.csv
```

One naming caveat, stated once: the chunked arm's
env in the script is `WGPU_COMPUTE_CHUNK_MAX_ROWS`.
If the chunked-GEMV prototype lands under a
different variable, edit the script's one `CHUNK_ENV`
line; until it lands at all, the chunked arm's CSV
shows the control kernels it really ran, and its
`variant_env` stamp shows an env nothing consumed.

===== FILE: bench/mmv-default-flip-2026-11-06.md =====
# MMV global gate: shipped default flipped from 1 (off) to 16 (2026-11-06)

Lane: lane/mmv-default-flip, based on main 2c1f8c7.
Decision: David, 2026-11-06, on the baseline session's
card verdict. This note records the evidence, the exact
semantic change, and the re-pinned tests. No server GPU
jobs ran for this change; the card evidence is the
baseline session's, cited below, and the merge carries
the standard obligation to re-run the resident and spec
suites on the card against the new default.

## The evidence

bench/baseline-session-2026-11-06.md leg (d) ran the
band routing A/B on the cleared card (spec_generate_gpu,
64 tokens, both mode, diag timing; control = MMV unset,
caps 4/8/12/16, depths 1 and 6, no per-cell overrides):

- Effective tok/s at cap 16: depth 1, 21.73 against the
  17.39 control; depth 6, 16.33 against 10.14. Cap 16
  also beat the recorded flat-routing numbers (19.26 at
  depth 1, 10.27 at depth 6).
- Every routed cap at or above the same-session control
  at both depths. The flat-routing cliff does not recur
  under the band table: caps 4/8/12 at depth 1, which
  flat routing put at 14.71/15.23/15.20 against a 16.98
  control, all beat this session's control.
- Verify medians at or under control at every cap
  (depth 1: 41 ms routed vs 51 control; depth 6: 82/82/83
  at caps 8/12/16 vs 153 control).
- IDENTITY and GOLDEN PASS in all 10 arms; round counts
  and acceptance identical across arms at each depth;
  the spec stream byte-identical in every arm.
- Sweep re-run: 0 disagreeing cells in all four arms,
  and the mmv arm's kernel column matches the shipped
  band table in 99 of 99 cells.

Leg (e) of the same session priced the draft side at
the same ceiling: exposure exactly one k21_q5k_mmv per
round at cap 16, draft medians down 10 ms at both
depths (42 to 32, 44 to 34), attribution arm returning
draft time to exactly the unset value when the Q5_K
FFN cell is closed.

## The exact semantic change

One resolver, one constant: in
crates/wgpu-compute/src/compute.rs,
`DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS` moves from 1 to 16, so
`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS` unset now resolves to the
kernels' full band instead of closing the gate.

Everything else is deliberately untouched:

- Any set value wins exactly as before. In particular
  `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=1` still closes the gate,
  and intermediate values still clip the band from
  above.
- A present but unparsable value keeps its pre-flip
  fail-closed behavior. It resolved to the default when
  the default was 1; it now resolves to the new
  constant `MMV_MAX_ROWS_FALLBACK` (1), never to the
  shipped default, so a typo in the environment cannot
  widen routing. This split (unset opens, malformed
  closes) is pinned by test, below.
- The band table (`MmvBands` shipped cells) is
  unchanged, as are the per-cell env overrides
  (`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_*_ROWS`), which still narrow or
  close individual cells on top of the ceiling.
- The K18 small-batch ceiling and the chunked-GEMV
  ceiling keep their shipped defaults of 1 (off).
  Only the MMV ceiling moves.
- The construction log already printed the resolved
  ceiling and the default from the constant, so it
  agrees with the new default without a wording
  change; the docs around it were updated to match.

## The re-pinned tests, and why each is still a real pin

- `mmv_max_rows_resolution` (compute.rs). Was: unset
  resolves to a default of 1; malformed falls back to
  the default. Now: unset resolves to 16 (asserted
  against the constant and the literal); a set "1"
  still wins (the explicit close); malformed resolves
  to `MMV_MAX_ROWS_FALLBACK` (asserted 1). Still a real
  pin: it fails if the default moves again, if the
  explicit close stops winning, or if the malformed
  case ever falls back to the open default.
- `mmv_routes_ceiling_composition` (compute.rs). Was:
  the shipped ceiling (1) routes nothing across the
  full family x shape x batch grid. Now: the same full
  grid is asserted against the explicit close
  (ceiling 1), and a second block pins the shipped
  default itself: at `DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS` routing
  equals the band table (Q4_K attn 6 routes, 2 does
  not; the Q4_K FFN row-3 hole holds; Q4_K KV 2 routes,
  12 does not; Q5_K KV 16 routes; Q6_K KV 12 routes;
  Q6_K attn 16 does not). The cap-clipping and
  kernel-band assertions below it are unchanged. Still
  a real pin: it fails if the default moves, if the
  close leaks, or if ceiling composition stops being
  table-then-clip.
- `draft_ladder_ships_closed_at_default_ceilings`
  (dflash_session.rs), rewritten and renamed
  `draft_ladder_ships_open_at_default_ceilings`. The
  old test passed literal ceilings (1, 1, 1) and so
  pinned the close, not the default, despite its name.
  The new test reads the ceilings from the constants
  (`DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS`, `DEFAULT_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS`,
  `DEFAULT_CHUNKED_GEMV_MAX_ROWS`, asserted (16, 1, 1))
  and pins the shipped resolution: the draft head at
  the block batch routes to K21 (ProjForm::Mmv)
  through the Q5_K FFN cell; measured in-band admissions
  route (Q4_K attn 7, Q6_K KV 12, Q5_K KV 16); the
  table's exclusions stay exclusions (Q4_K/Q6_K admit
  nothing at batch 16, the Q4_K FFN row-3 hole, Q5_K KV
  at 12, batches 1 and 64 everywhere); and the original
  full-grid assertion survives verbatim against
  (1, 1, 1), so the explicit close still restores the
  pre-flip ladder exactly. Still a real pin: it fails
  if any shipped ceiling moves, if the head stops
  routing at the default, or if the close leaks.
- `proj_bench_routes_to_gemv_at_shipped_defaults_and_matches_it`
  (tests/proj_bench.rs, device-gated). Its fixture was
  a KV-class shape (512 in, 4 out) at batch 2, inside
  the Q4_K KV cell (rows 2-3): at the new default that
  cell routes to K19, so the test's subject (the
  ProjBench handle naming the GEMV form, and routed
  output bit-identical to a direct GEMV) no longer
  holds at that shape. The fixture moved to an
  attention-class shape (512 in, 512 out), whose Q4_K
  cell starts at row 6, so batch 2 is outside every
  open cell and the GEMV form serves at shipped
  defaults for a stated reason. Still a real pin: it
  fails if the Q4_K attention cell ever widens to
  row 2, if the handle misnames the served form, or
  if the routed GEMV's stream diverges from the
  direct one.

One harness correction rides along, in
bench/mmv-sweep.sh: the control arm used to unset
`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS`, which meant "the shipped
default" when the default was off. Unset now means
the open default, so the control arm pins
`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=1` explicitly to keep
measuring the pre-flip ladder, and the k18 and chunked
arms pin it closed as well, so each arm measures only
its own rung. Without this, every future sweep's
control, k18, and chunked arms would silently include
MMV routing and read as wrong data.

Docs updated to agree with the new default:
compute.rs (env, default, and accessor docs; the
construction comment), session.rs (mmv_applies,
prepare_proj, the ActProj variant, routed_rung_admits),
dflash_session.rs (proj_candidates), kernels/mod.rs
and the K19/K20/K21 module docs. The band table's
`describe()` output carries no default and needed no
change; the diag manifest prints the resolved ceiling
from the backend, so it agrees by construction.

## Gates on this lane (VM, no adapter)

- cargo test -p wgpu-compute: 238 passed, 0 failed,
  1 ignored (the pre-existing hash-cost probe),
  25 binaries. Device legs skip on the VM by design.
- cargo test -p dflash: 24 passed, 0 failed.
- cargo test -p itak-spec: 49 passed, 0 failed.
- cargo clippy -p wgpu-compute -p dflash -p itak-spec
  --all-targets -- -D warnings: clean.
- cargo fmt --check: clean.
- cargo check --workspace: clean.

## Rollback

Set `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=1`. That restores the
pre-flip ladder exactly, no rebuild needed.
