===== FILE: bench/mmv-prototype-2026-11-05.md =====
# K19 MMV prototype: the register-streaming small-batch product (2026-11-05)

Lane `lane/mmv-prototype`, from main e537764f. New
kernel K19 (`crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/
k19_q4k_mmv.rs`), routed in `prepare_proj` behind
`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS` (default 1 = OFF). No
server GPU work in this lane; the card verdict is
sequenced below for a separate lane.

## Why a third attempt, and what it changes

Two one-stream attempts are measured and convicted:

- Wide MMQ (K15/K16): numerically correct, about
  3.5x slower per tensor than standard MMQ, one real
  session hang. The shader autopsy
  (bench/shader-autopsy-2026-11-04.md) shows why in
  compiled form: 1,041 to 1,213 spilled VGPRs and
  78,080 to 86,528 bytes of scratch on the wide
  shaders.
- K18 (bench/small-batch-2026-11-04.md): correct,
  streams the weights once as designed, but at
  about 70 to 130 GB/s against GEMV's up to
  676 GB/s on the same tensors; a loss in the spec
  verdict at both depths (9.19 to 8.13 at depth 6,
  14.22 to 8.90 at depth 1).

What the two slow kernels share and the fast one
lacks is weight staging through workgroup memory:
both stage weight tiles in LDS (K18: 15,424 to
25,664 bytes per workgroup; the wide MMQ's compiled
LDS runs to 62,464 bytes), and the autopsy cleared
GEMV's compiled form and the compiler with it
(GEMV: VGPR 48 to 72, zero spills, zero scratch,
LDS only 1 to 4 KB of reduction partials). The
streaming-rate research (run folders
`~/workspace/research_notes/what-is-everything-
that-can-be-done-to-a-20261104-1632/` and
`~/workspace/research_notes/gpu-streaming-rate-
exhaustive-20261104-2133/report.md`) reached the
same verdict from the literature side: llama.cpp's
fast small-batch Vulkan path dequantizes weights in
registers and never stages them.

K19 is that shape, built in this crate: the Q4_K
small-batch product (batch 2..=16) as a widened
GEMV, not as a shrunken MMQ.

## What it borrows from mul_mat_vec, with sources

The design was read from the actual sources, not
reconstructed: `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/vulkan-shaders/
mul_mat_vec.comp` (264 lines) and
`mul_mat_vec_base.glsl` (242 lines) in the server's
llama.cpp tree at `/home/server/llama.cpp`; the same
files, at the same line counts, sit in this VM's
meta-cookbook mirror at `~/workspace/meta-cookbook/
build-site/repos/ggerganov__llama.cpp/`. Term for
term:

- Register accumulators per (column, row):
  `temp[NUM_COLS][NUM_ROWS]` in the source is
  `acc[rows * batch]` here, one f32 accumulator per
  (output row, batch row) pair, every index a
  compile-time constant (see the WGSL note below).
- The batch is a column count inside the workgroup
  (NUM_COLS), specialized per batch count from 2 to
  16. The dose-response that justifies the cap is
  llama.cpp issue #25356, as recorded in the
  research lane digest
  (`~/workspace/research_notes/what-is-everything-
  that-can-be-done-to-a-20261104-1632/lane-C-kernel-
  techniques.md`, line 5): the stock NUM_COLS cap of
  8 cliffs at batch 9 (Mistral-Small-24B 125.0 t/s
  at batch 8 down to 19.7 at batch 9); a cap of 16
  gives 131.5 at batch 9 and 158.5 at batch 16,
  beating the matmul path even at batch 32. PR
  #27652 proposes raising the cap under
  `GGML_VK_MMV_MAX_COLS`.
- Rows per workgroup (NUM_ROWS) is 2, the value
  ggml-vulkan picks for K-quants on RDNA3 and the
  tile K1 already ships.
- Per super-block, weights are dequantized in
  registers and dotted against the activation quads
  (`dequantize4` + `get_dm` in the source). Here the
  dequant and dot text is K1's llama-family WGSL
  verbatim: the sixteen-thread group assignment,
  the packed scale extraction, and the dot math are
  character-for-character K1's, because K1 is itself
  a proven port of `mul_mat_vec_q4_k.comp` and this
  prototype's question is workgroup organization,
  not dequant arithmetic.
- The reduction keeps the source's one shared-memory
  exception: llama's hybrid mode writes per-group
  partials to `tmpsh`; K19's only workgroup array is
  its reduction partials (at most 256 f32 in the
  subgroup form, 128 in the tree form). No weight
  byte and no activation tile is staged anywhere.
- The input is the f32 activation rows themselves,
  as in the source: no K12 quantize dispatch rides
  in front, and the output layout is the GEMV's
  `[batch][out_rows]`, so a plan can swap K19 for K1
  without moving a byte. Its dispatch count in a
  plan is 1, the GEMV's own count.

## How it differs from K18 and the wide MMQ

| | K18 | Wide MMQ (K15/K16) | K19 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weights in workgroup memory | Yes, staged tiles (15,424 to 25,664 B) | Yes, double-buffered staged tiles (LDS to 62,464 B compiled) | No. Reduction partials only (at most 1 KB) |
| Activations | Q8_1 quantized on device (extra K12 dispatch), DP4A integer dots | Same MMQ math | f32 rows directly, f32 dots: the GEMV's exact math, no extra dispatch |
| Batch in the shader | Runtime loop bound over staged tiles | Runtime, in tile geometry | Generation literal, accumulators fully unrolled |
| Tile | 32/64 output rows x batch | 128-class output tile | 2 output rows x the whole batch (llama's NUM_ROWS / NUM_COLS split) |
| Correctness bar | Parity band vs GEMV (quantization noise) | Parity band vs GEMV | The CPU f32 reference at the reassociation bound, plus direct K1 agreement |

## The env flag and the ladder

`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS`, resolved at backend
construction like its two predecessors
(`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMQ_WIDE_MIN_ROWS`,
`WGPU_COMPUTE_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS`), default 1 =
OFF: `prepare_proj` never consults K19, and shipped
behavior is byte-identical (the off position is
covered by the crate's existing dispatch-count pins,
which do not move). With the band open, K19 is tried
in the Q4_K branch after the matrix ladder and
before K18: when both thresholds are enabled, the
register-streaming form takes precedence, because it
is the band's structural challenger and the A/B
should not be confounded. Every refusal inside the
band is logged by name and the ladder continues to
K18, then K1; nothing substitutes inside a dispatch.

Diag instrumentation is in from birth (David's
rule): K19 prepare stamps `k19_q4k_mmv` through
`ctx.diag_stamp` like every other kernel, with rows,
cols, quant `Q4_K`, weight bytes, and a
`batch=<n> grid=<x>x<y>` shape string, so the
timestamp system can time it the moment the server
lane turns `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing` on.

## Where WGSL could not follow the GLSL design

Named precisely, because the verdict must be read
against them:

1. No specialization constants. llama selects
   NUM_COLS / NUM_ROWS / BLOCK_SIZE through GLSL
   `constant_id`; WGSL through wgpu in this crate
   has no equivalent in use, so the batch is baked
   into the generated shader as literals (the
   crate's own idiom: K13 and K18 also generate).
   Cost: 15 compiled variants, one per batch count.
   Mitigations in the build: a per-batch pipeline
   cache, the band-floor variant compiled at
   construction as the family's smoke check, and
   `K19Pipeline::precompile` so a session warms the
   counts it will run at plan time.
2. Register residence is a compiler outcome, not a
   WGSL guarantee. A runtime-indexed local array in
   WGSL is free to spill to function memory, which
   would quietly rebuild the staging this kernel
   exists to avoid. The generator therefore unrolls
   the (row, batch) loops at generation time so
   every accumulator index is a compile-time
   constant: the strongest position WGSL offers,
   and the same trick K13/K18's generators use for
   their inner products. Whether ACO actually keeps
   `acc` plus the dequantized quads in VGPRs at
   batch 16 (32 accumulators, 16 quad values, scales
   and headers per thread) can only be proven by
   the server shader autopsy in step 0 of the
   protocol below. If a spill cliff exists, the
   dose-response sweep (step 4) finds where.
3. Activation quads are re-read per output row.
   llama loads the B vector's quads once per
   super-block into registers (`bv0`/`bv1`) and
   shares them across all NUM_ROWS rows. K19
   re-reads them from the input buffer per row, the
   trade K1's port already made: the activations
   are the small side (16 rows x width, hundreds of
   KB against the weight stream's GBs) and ride the
   cache, while the weights, the stream that
   matters, are loaded and dequantized exactly once
   per workgroup. Deliberate: the prototype differs
   from K1 in exactly one structural variable, the
   workgroup organization.
4. The subgroup reduction needs the SUBGROUP
   device feature, with K1's workgroup-tree
   fallback where it is not granted. The server
   card grants it (K1's shipped shape uses it), so
   the verdict runs the subgroup form; the tree
   form is gated in this lane's tests wherever a
   device builds it.

What this VM could and could not prove, named

## Server verdict protocol (the next lane)

Preconditions: the card cleared per David's

===== FILE: bench/mmv-q5k-2026-11-05.md =====
# K21 MMV prototype: the Q5_K register-streaming small-batch product (2026-11-05)

Lane `lane/mmv-q5k`, from main 88cb83a2. New kernel
K21 (`crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/k21_q5k_mmv.rs`),
the Q5_K arm of the register-streaming small-batch
family (K19 carries Q4_K on `lane/mmv-prototype`,
K20 carries Q6_K), routed in `prepare_proj` behind
`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS` (default 1 = OFF). No
server GPU work in this lane; the card verdict is
sequenced below for a separate lane.

Merge note for the parent: this lane branches from a
main where the MMV family does not exist yet, so it
carries the family's shared plumbing in its Q5_K
form: the `MMV_MAX_ROWS_ENV` / `DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS`
/ `resolve_mmv_max_rows` resolution in compute.rs,
the backend's `mmv_max_rows` field and accessor, and
the session's `mmv_applies` helper. The K19/K20 lanes
carry the same names from their own branches; the
parent reconciles the three copies into one at
merge (they are written to be textually identical in
name and semantics). K21's own additions are the
`k21` pipeline field, the `MmvQ5K` plan variant, and
`try_mmv_q5k`.

## Why a third attempt, and what it changes

Two one-stream attempts are measured and convicted:

- Wide MMQ (K15/K16): numerically correct, about
  3.5x slower per tensor than standard MMQ, one real
  session hang. The shader autopsy
  (bench/shader-autopsy-2026-11-04.md) shows why in
  compiled form: 1,041 to 1,213 spilled VGPRs and
  78,080 to 86,528 bytes of scratch on the wide
  shaders.
- K18 (bench/small-batch-2026-11-04.md): correct,
  streams the weights once as designed, but at
  about 70 to 130 GB/s against GEMV's up to
  676 GB/s on the same tensors; a loss in the spec
  verdict at both depths (9.19 to 8.13 at depth 6,
  14.22 to 8.90 at depth 1). Its Q5_K form shares
  the design exactly: the same staged tiles, the
  same extra K12 quantize dispatch.

What the two slow kernels share and the fast one
lacks is weight staging through workgroup memory:
both stage weight tiles in LDS (K18: 15,424 to
25,664 bytes per workgroup; the wide MMQ's compiled
LDS runs to 62,464 bytes), and the autopsy cleared
GEMV's compiled form and the compiler with it
(GEMV: VGPR 48 to 72, zero spills, zero scratch,
LDS only 1 to 4 KB of reduction partials). The
streaming-rate research (run folders
`~/workspace/research_notes/what-is-everything-
that-can-be-done-to-a-20261104-1632/` and
`~/workspace/research_notes/gpu-streaming-rate-
exhaustive-20261104-2133/report.md`) reached the
same verdict from the literature side: llama.cpp's
fast small-batch Vulkan path dequantizes weights in
registers and never stages them.

K21 is that shape, built in this crate: the Q5_K
small-batch product (batch 2..=16) as a widened
GEMV, not as a shrunken MMQ.

## What it borrows from mul_mat_vec, with sources

The design was read from the actual sources, not
reconstructed: `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/vulkan-shaders/
mul_mat_vec.comp`, `mul_mat_vec_q5_k.comp`, and
`mul_mat_vec_base.glsl` in this VM's llama.cpp
mirror at `~/workspace/meta-cookbook/build-site/
repos/ggerganov__llama.cpp/` (the same files, at the
same content, as the server's tree at
`/home/server/llama.cpp`). Term for term:

- Register accumulators per (column, row):
  `temp[NUM_COLS][NUM_ROWS]` in the source is
  `acc[rows * batch]` here, one f32 accumulator per
  (output row, batch row) pair, every index a
  compile-time constant (see the WGSL note below).
- The batch is a column count inside the workgroup
  (NUM_COLS), specialized per batch count from 2 to
  16. The dose-response that justifies the cap is
  llama.cpp issue #25356, as recorded in the
  research lane digest
  (`~/workspace/research_notes/what-is-everything-
  that-can-be-done-to-a-20261104-1632/lane-C-kernel-
  techniques.md`, line 5): the stock NUM_COLS cap of
  8 cliffs at batch 9 (Mistral-Small-24B 125.0 t/s
  at batch 8 down to 19.7 at batch 9); a cap of 16
  gives 131.5 at batch 9 and 158.5 at batch 16,
  beating the matmul path even at batch 32. PR
  #27652 proposes raising the cap under
  `GGML_VK_MMV_MAX_COLS`.
- Rows per workgroup (NUM_ROWS) is 2, the value
  ggml-vulkan picks for K-quants on RDNA3 and the
  tile K3 already ships.
- Per super-block, weights are dequantized in
  registers and dotted against the activation quads.
  In `mul_mat_vec_q5_k.comp`'s `calc_superblock`,
  the thread's four quant quads are built by folding
  the qh plane's fifth bits into the ql nibbles
  (packed-word masks `0x01010101` / `0x02020202` /
  `0x10101010` / `0x20202020` over the packed qh
  word) and the dot accumulates as
  `d * (sc . qx) - dmin * (mins . sum(x))`. Here the
  dequant and dot text is K3's llama-family WGSL
  verbatim: the sixteen-thread group assignment,
  the packed scale extraction (the same
  `(m16 << 16) | s16` construction with the
  `0x3f3f3f3f` / `0xc0c0c0c0` masks), the qh fold in
  f32-after-unpack form (`nibble + 16.0 * bits`,
  value-identical to llama's packed add), and the
  dot math are character-for-character K3's, because
  K3 is itself a proven port of the same shader
  family and this prototype's question is workgroup
  organization, not dequant arithmetic.
- The reduction keeps the source's one shared-memory
  exception: llama's hybrid mode writes per-group
  partials to `tmpsh`; K21's only workgroup array is
  its reduction partials (at most 256 f32 in the
  subgroup form, 128 in the tree form). No weight
  byte and no activation tile is staged anywhere.
- The input is the f32 activation rows themselves,
  as in the source: no K12 quantize dispatch rides
  in front, and the output layout is the GEMV's
  `[batch][out_rows]`, so a plan can swap K21 for K3
  without moving a byte. Its dispatch count in a
  plan is 1, the GEMV's own count.

## How it differs from K18's Q5_K form and the wide MMQ

| | K18 Q5_K | Wide MMQ (K15/K16) | K21 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weights in workgroup memory | Yes, staged tiles (15,424 to 25,664 B) | Yes, double-buffered staged tiles (LDS to 62,464 B compiled) | No. Reduction partials only (at most 1 KB) |
| Activations | Q8_1 quantized on device (extra K12 dispatch), DP4A integer dots | Same MMQ math | f32 rows directly, f32 dots: the GEMV's exact math, no extra dispatch |
| Batch in the shader | Runtime loop bound over staged tiles | Runtime, in tile geometry | Generation literal, accumulators fully unrolled |
| Tile | 32/64 output rows x batch | 128-class output tile | 2 output rows x the whole batch (llama's NUM_ROWS / NUM_COLS split) |
| Correctness bar | Parity band vs GEMV (quantization noise) | Parity band vs GEMV | The CPU f32 reference at the reassociation bound, plus direct K3 agreement |

## The env flag and the ladder

`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS`, resolved at backend
construction like its two predecessors
(`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMQ_WIDE_MIN_ROWS`,
`WGPU_COMPUTE_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS`), default 1 =
OFF: `prepare_proj` never consults K21, and shipped
behavior is byte-identical (the off position is
covered by the crate's existing dispatch-count pins,
which do not move). With the band open, K21 is tried
in the Q5_K branch before K18: when both thresholds
are enabled, the register-streaming form takes
precedence, because it is the band's structural
challenger and the A/B should not be confounded.
Every refusal inside the band is logged by name and
the ladder continues to K18, then K3; nothing
substitutes inside a dispatch.

Diag instrumentation is in from birth (David's
rule): K21 prepare stamps `k21_q5k_mmv` through
`ctx.diag_stamp` like every other kernel, with rows,
cols, quant `Q5_K`, weight bytes, and a
`batch=<n> grid=<x>x<y>` shape string, so the
timestamp system can time it the moment the server
lane turns `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing` on. (The
timestamps system has no central registry table to
append to: registration IS the stamp, per kernel, as
K19's `k19_q4k_mmv` stamp shows.)

## What K21 does not cover: the Q5_K head

K21 carries no fused finish, the same contract K18
keeps: K3's logit scale and softcap modes stay
K3's. The resident session's two Q5_K head sites
(the standard head and the block head) prepare K3
with a finish directly and are NOT routed to K21 by
this lane. That matters for reading the verdict: on
the current Q4_K_M target file, the Q5_K tensor in
the resident forward is the head (the borrowed
Q5_K head is the single largest stream in the
DFlash pass, bench/dflash-gpu-2026-11-03.md), so a
flagged spec run may route few or no projections
through K21 at all. The diag timestamp table is the
instrument that says whether `k21_q5k_mmv` fired;
if it did not, the spec A/B below measures nothing
for this variant and the verdict rests on steps 0
and 1 plus a routed-projection micro-bench. The
head-sized prize needs a finish-carrying K21
variant, which is the named follow-up if the kernel
gates and the autopsy earn it.

## Where WGSL could not follow the GLSL design

Named precisely, because the verdict must be read
against them:

1. No specialization constants. llama selects
   NUM_COLS / NUM_ROWS / BLOCK_SIZE through GLSL
   `constant_id`; WGSL through wgpu in this crate
   has no equivalent in use, so the batch is baked
   into the generated shader as literals (the
   crate's own idiom: K13 and K18 also generate).
   Cost: 15 compiled variants, one per batch count.
   Mitigations in the build: a per-batch pipeline
   cache, the band-floor variant compiled at
   construction as the family's smoke check, and
   `K21Pipeline::precompile` so a session warms the
   counts it will run at plan time.
2. Register residence is a compiler outcome, not a
   WGSL guarantee. A runtime-indexed local array in
   WGSL is free to spill to function memory, which
   would quietly rebuild the staging this kernel
   exists to avoid. The generator therefore unrolls
   the (row, batch) loops at generation time so
   every accumulator index is a compile-time
   constant: the strongest position WGSL offers,
   and the same trick K13/K18's generators use for
   their inner products. Whether ACO actually keeps
   `acc` plus the dequantized quads in VGPRs at
   batch 16 (32 accumulators, 16 quad values, the
   four qh bit quads, scales and headers per thread;
   Q5_K carries more live register values than
   Q4_K's form) can only be proven by the server
   shader autopsy in step 0 of the protocol below.
   If a spill cliff exists, the dose-response sweep
   (step 4) finds where.
3. Activation quads are re-read per output row.
   llama loads the B vector's quads once per
   super-block into registers (`bv0`/`bv1`, and the
   by-pairs in the Q5_K form) and shares them across
   all NUM_ROWS rows. K21 re-reads them from the
   input buffer per row, the trade K3's port already
   made: the activations are the small side (16 rows
   x width, hundreds of KB against the weight
   stream's GBs) and ride the cache, while the
   weights, the stream that matters, are loaded and
   dequantized exactly once per workgroup.
   Deliberate: the prototype differs from K3 in
   exactly one structural variable, the workgroup
   organization.
4. The subgroup reduction needs the SUBGROUP
   device feature, with K3's workgroup-tree
   fallback where it is not granted. The server
   card grants it (K3's shipped shape uses it), so
   the verdict runs the subgroup form; the tree
   form is gated in this lane's tests wherever a
   device builds it.

## Server verdict, 2026-11-06: compiled form clean, executed, but never fires in the real forward

From main `c439e3af45e30275601129568e3e9cb3a89590cb`,
staged at `~/gpu-wave11` (manifest-verified), cleared
card (guard 33,271,808 bytes before every run), phase
lock held. Logs and RADV dumps in `~/gpu-wave11/logs11/`
on the server.

**Step 0, autopsy** (`shader_compile k21_q5k_mmv`
under `RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats,asm,cs`, private shader
cache; 33 compiled shaders, the same attribution
pattern as K19/K20). Every K21 variant: **zero spilled
VGPRs, zero scratch bytes, LDS 1,024 B**. VGPR: batch
2 = 84 (the four extra qh bit quads per thread cost
registers against K19's 72 and K20's 60 at batch 2),
rising to the same 96 plateau by mid-band, batch 16 =
96 in both shapes (code 3,680 B at batch 2; 18,424 /
17,140 B at batch 16). The risk this step existed to
retire (Q5_K's extra live values spilling at high
batch) does not occur: register residence holds for
K21 at batch 16 included.

**Step 1, executed correctness.** `cargo test
--release -p wgpu-compute --test k21_mmv` on the card:
3 passed, 0 failed, executed on the real adapter
(batches 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 16 against the CPU f32
reference and against K3/GEMV in both reduction
shapes, plus the deep geometry and band-edge
refusals). Max abs diffs 2.0e-3 to 2.9e-3 on fixture
set scales of 1.8e4 to 3.3e4 (worst relative about
1.2e-7). The `shader_compile k21_q5k_mmv` leg passed
in the same session.

**Step 2, exposure check: K21 never fired.** The
flagged spec run (`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=16`,
`WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing`, depth 6, real target and
draft; IDENTITY and GOLDEN PASS) produced 46,739
per-dispatch diag lines across its three sessions.
The MMV family accounts for 4,290 of them (k19 at
verify batches 3-7, k20 on the KV projections at the
same batches). **`k21_q5k_mmv` accounts for zero.**
One measurement trap, recorded so nobody repeats it:
the run's `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG_OUT` CSV was overwritten
by three successive session reports (phase A target,
phase B target, phase B draft, in that finish order),
and the surviving file is the DRAFT session's report;
the exposure answer comes from the per-dispatch lines
in the run log, not from the CSV.

The zero is exactly the outcome this note's head
section predicted: on the Q4_K_M file the Q5_K
tensors in the resident forward are the head, and the
head routes through the fused-finish path
(`prepare_with_finish`, scale and softcap), which K21
deliberately does not carry. Per this note's step 2
rule, the verdict therefore rests on steps 0 and 1
plus the routed-projection micro-bench: in the sweep
harness run of the same session (which routes through
`prepare_proj` itself), k21 served all 30 Q5_K cells
and beat the K3 GEMV control at nearly every in-band
row (attention shape: rows 2 0.1219 vs 0.1613 ms;
rows 9 0.2515 vs 0.4310; rows 12 0.3629 vs 0.5195;
rows 16 0.4757 vs 0.6457), with 0 disagreeing cells.
K21 is a fast, correct kernel with no production
caller on this model file. The follow-up that would
give it one (a finish-carrying K21 variant for the
head sites) is unchanged and still gated on exactly
this evidence; the shared MMV flag decision is
governed by the K19 verdict (default stays off).

===== FILE: bench/mmv-q6k-2026-11-05.md =====
# K20 MMV prototype: the Q6_K register-streaming small-batch product (2026-11-05)

Lane `lane/mmv-q6k`, from main
88cb83a22c009db26d03ee841200e3d752b02f33. New
kernel K20 (`crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/
k20_q6k_mmv.rs`), routed in `prepare_proj` behind
`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS` (default 1 = OFF). No
server GPU work in this lane; the card verdict is
sequenced below for a separate lane. K20 is the
Q6_K arm of the register-streaming prototype whose
Q4_K arm is K19 (lane/mmv-prototype,
bench/mmv-prototype-2026-11-05.md); the two share
the design, the band, and the routing threshold,
and differ only in the dequant text.

## Why a third attempt, and what it changes

Two one-stream attempts are measured and convicted:

- Wide MMQ (K15/K16): numerically correct, about
  3.5x slower per tensor than standard MMQ, one real
  session hang. The shader autopsy
  (bench/shader-autopsy-2026-11-04.md) shows why in
  compiled form: 1,041 to 1,213 spilled VGPRs and
  78,080 to 86,528 bytes of scratch on the wide
  shaders.
- K18 (bench/small-batch-2026-11-04.md): correct,
  streams the weights once as designed, but at
  about 70 to 130 GB/s against GEMV's up to
  676 GB/s on the same tensors; a loss in the spec
  verdict at both depths (9.19 to 8.13 at depth 6,
  14.22 to 8.90 at depth 1).

What the two slow kernels share and the fast one
lacks is weight staging through workgroup memory:
both stage weight tiles in LDS (K18: 15,424 to
25,664 bytes per workgroup; the wide MMQ's compiled
LDS runs to 62,464 bytes), and the autopsy cleared
GEMV's compiled form and the compiler with it
(GEMV: VGPR 48 to 72, zero spills, zero scratch,
LDS only 1 to 4 KB of reduction partials). The
streaming-rate research (run folders
`~/workspace/research_notes/what-is-everything-
that-can-be-done-to-a-20261104-1632/` and
`~/workspace/research_notes/gpu-streaming-rate-
exhaustive-20261104-2133/report.md`) reached the
same verdict from the literature side: llama.cpp's
fast small-batch Vulkan path dequantizes weights in
registers and never stages them.

K20 is that shape, built in this crate: the Q6_K
small-batch product (batch 2..=16) as a widened
GEMV, not as a shrunken MMQ.

## What it borrows from mul_mat_vec, with sources

The design was read from the actual sources, not
reconstructed: `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/vulkan-shaders/
mul_mat_vec_q6_k.comp` and `mul_mat_vec_base.glsl`
in the server's llama.cpp tree at
`/home/server/llama.cpp`; the same files sit in
this VM's mirror at `~/workspace/meta-cookbook/
build-site/repos/ggerganov__llama.cpp/`. Term for
term:

- Register accumulators per (column, row):
  `temp[NUM_COLS][NUM_ROWS]` in the source is
  `acc[rows * batch]` here, one f32 accumulator per
  (output row, batch row) pair, every index a
  compile-time constant (see the WGSL note below).
- The batch is a column count inside the workgroup
  (NUM_COLS), specialized per batch count from 2 to
  16. The dose-response that justifies the cap is
  llama.cpp issue #25356, as recorded in the
  research lane digest
  (`~/workspace/research_notes/what-is-everything-
  that-can-be-done-to-a-20261104-1632/lane-C-kernel-
  techniques.md`, line 5): the stock NUM_COLS cap of
  8 cliffs at batch 9 (Mistral-Small-24B 125.0 t/s
  at batch 8 down to 19.7 at batch 9); a cap of 16
  gives 131.5 at batch 9 and 158.5 at batch 16,
  beating the matmul path even at batch 32. PR
  #27652 proposes raising the cap under
  `GGML_VK_MMV_MAX_COLS`.
- Rows per workgroup (NUM_ROWS) is 2, the value
  ggml-vulkan picks for K-quants on RDNA3 (its Q6_K
  mmv pipelines are created with the same `rm_kq`
  row count as Q4_K's) and the tile the MMV family
  ships. K2's GEMV ships 1 row of 256 threads for
  its own runtime-row form (its bench picked it by
  1.6%, 831.9 against 818.6 GB/s median); the family
  holds one geometry across both arms so the A/B
  differs in the dequant text and the quant family,
  not the tile. The geometry sweep is the autotune
  follow-up the research names, not this prototype.
- Per super-block, weights are dequantized in
  registers and dotted against the activation
  quads. Here the dequant and dot text is K2's
  llama-family WGSL verbatim: the sixteen-thread
  group assignment (`ql0_off = 16*half + v_in`,
  `qh_off = 32 + 8*half + v_in`, `s_off = 8*half +
  v_in/4`), the 6-bit reconstruction masks
  (0x03030303, 0x0c0c0c0c, 0x30303030, 0xc0c0c0c0),
  and the scale fold are character-for-character
  K2's, because K2 is itself a proven port of
  `mul_mat_vec_q6_k.comp` and this prototype's
  question is workgroup organization, not dequant
  arithmetic.
- The reduction keeps the source's one
  shared-memory exception: llama's hybrid mode
  writes per-group partials to `tmpsh`; K20's only
  workgroup array is its reduction partials (at
  most 256 f32 in the subgroup form, 128 in the
  tree form). No weight byte and no activation tile
  is staged anywhere.
- The input is the f32 activation rows themselves,
  as in the source: no K12 quantize dispatch rides
  in front, and the output layout is the GEMV's
  `[batch][out_rows]`, so a plan can swap K20 for
  K2 without moving a byte. Its dispatch count in a
  plan is 1, the GEMV's own count.
- The weights are K2's device layout, consumed
  through `K2Weights`: the 210-byte file block
  repacked to a 212-byte device stride at upload,
  so one upload rule serves the whole Q6_K family
  and the diag stamp accounts device bytes
  (`byte_len * 212 / 210`, K2's stamp rule).

One Q6_K asymmetry the research flagged, checked
against the source and recorded so nobody chases
it in the wrong kernel: in the matrix path
(`mul_mm.comp`, `mm_load_vec_a`), Q4_K and Q5_K
get load width 4 while Q6_K is unlisted and falls
to the default 2. That is the prompt-processing
path's staging width, not `mul_mat_vec`'s: the mmv
Q6_K shader loads single words per thread (packed16
pairs assembled into u32), exactly as K2 and K20
do. If a Q6_K matrix-path gap is ever measured,
width 2 is the first place to look; it says
nothing about this kernel.

## How it differs from K18 and the wide MMQ

| | K18 | Wide MMQ (K16) | K20 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weights in workgroup memory | Yes, staged tiles (15,424 to 25,664 B) | Yes, double-buffered staged tiles (LDS to 62,464 B compiled) | No. Reduction partials only (at most 1 KB) |
| Activations | Q8_1 quantized on device (extra K12 dispatch), DP4A integer dots | Same MMQ math | f32 rows directly, f32 dots: the GEMV's exact math, no extra dispatch |
| Batch in the shader | Runtime loop bound over staged tiles | Runtime, in tile geometry | Generation literal, accumulators fully unrolled |
| Tile | 32/64 output rows x batch | 128-class output tile | 2 output rows x the whole batch (llama's NUM_ROWS / NUM_COLS split) |
| Correctness bar | Parity band vs GEMV (quantization noise) | Parity band vs GEMV | The CPU f32 reference at the reassociation bound, plus direct K2 agreement |

## The env flag, the ladder, and the merge note

`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS`, resolved at backend
construction like its two predecessors
(`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMQ_WIDE_MIN_ROWS`,
`WGPU_COMPUTE_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS`), default 1 =
OFF: `prepare_proj` never consults K20, and shipped
behavior is byte-identical (the off position is
covered by the crate's existing dispatch-count
pins, which do not move). With the band open, K20
is tried in the Q6_K branch after the matrix
ladder and before K18: when both thresholds are
enabled, the register-streaming form takes
precedence, because it is the band's structural
challenger and the A/B should not be confounded.
Every refusal inside the band is logged by name
and the ladder continues to K18, then K2; nothing
substitutes inside a dispatch.

Diag instrumentation is in from birth (David's
rule): K20 prepare stamps `k20_q6k_mmv` through
`ctx.diag_stamp` like every other kernel, with
rows, cols, quant `Q6_K`, device weight bytes, and
a `batch=<n> grid=<x>x<y>` shape string, so the
timestamp system can time it the moment the server
lane turns `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing` on. The name
is also registered in the timestamps system's own
test suite (an append-only test in
`crates/wgpu-compute/src/timestamps.rs`:
`k20_q6k_mmv_records_group_under_their_kernel_name`
pins that records under the name aggregate and
render).

Merge reconciliation (for the parent): this lane
branches from main 88cb83a, where the MMV family
does not exist yet, and the Q4_K lane
(lane/mmv-prototype) builds the same shared pieces
from the same base. At merge, keep ONE copy of
each shared piece and both arms' specifics:

- compute.rs: `MMV_MAX_ROWS_ENV`,
  `DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS`, `resolve_mmv_max_rows`,
  the `mmv_max_rows` field and accessor, and the
  `mmv_max_rows_resolution` test are defined
  identically in both lanes (same names, same
  semantics; the doc wording differs only in which
  arm it names first). The per-arm pieces are the
  `k19` / `k20` fields, construction blocks, and
  `k19()` / `k20()` accessors.
- session.rs: `mmv_applies` is shared (defined in

  of `prepare_proj`, each ahead of its K18 rung)

- lib.rs: K19's lane re-exports its `MmvShape` and
  band constants at the crate root; this lane

## Where WGSL could not follow the GLSL design

Named precisely, because the verdict must be read
against them:

1. No specialization constants. llama selects
   NUM_COLS / NUM_ROWS / BLOCK_SIZE through GLSL
   `constant_id`; WGSL through wgpu in this crate
   has no equivalent in use, so the batch is baked
   into the generated shader as literals (the
   crate's own idiom: K13 and K18 also generate).
   Cost: 15 compiled variants, one per batch count.
   Mitigations in the build: a per-batch pipeline
   cache, the band-floor variant compiled at
   construction as the family's smoke check, and
   `K20Pipeline::precompile` so a session warms the
   counts it will run at plan time.
2. Register residence is a compiler outcome, not a
   WGSL guarantee. A runtime-indexed local array in
   WGSL is free to spill to function memory, which
   would quietly rebuild the staging this kernel
   exists to avoid. The generator therefore unrolls
   the (row, batch) loops at generation time so
   every accumulator index is a compile-time
   constant: the strongest position WGSL offers,
   and the same trick K13/K18's generators use for
   their inner products. Whether ACO actually keeps
   `acc` plus the dequantized quads in VGPRs at
   batch 16 (32 accumulators, 16 quad values, the
   scale words and headers per thread) can only be
   proven by the server shader autopsy in step 0 of
   the protocol below. If a spill cliff exists, the
   dose-response sweep (step 4) finds where.
3. Activation quads are re-read per output row.
   llama loads the B vector's quads once per
   super-block into registers and shares them
   across all NUM_ROWS rows. K20 re-reads them from
   the input buffer per row, the trade K2's port
   already made: the activations are the small side
   (16 rows x width, hundreds of KB against the
   weight stream's GBs) and ride the cache, while
   the weights, the stream that matters, are loaded
   and dequantized exactly once per workgroup.
   Deliberate: the prototype differs from K2 in
   exactly one structural variable, the workgroup
   organization.
4. The scale bytes take the register path, not
   llama's scale cache. `mul_mat_vec_q6_k.comp`
   passes its sixteen int8 scales through a small
   shared array (`sccache`, double-buffered,
   2 x (BLOCK_SIZE/16) x 16 values) because its
   packed-struct access pattern makes each thread
   read scales another thread loaded. This crate's
   word-addressed layout has no such constraint:
   each thread loads the block's four scale words
   straight from the weight stream, as K2 does, and
   extracts its bytes in registers (`scale_at`).
   The deviation runs AGAINST shared memory, in the
   direction of the design law; it is named so the
   autopsy can confirm the shader carries no scale
   staging either (its one workgroup array is the
   reduction partials, asserted in the module's
   shader-text test).
5. The subgroup reduction needs the SUBGROUP
   device feature, with K2's workgroup-tree
   fallback where it is not granted. The server
   card grants it (K2's shipped shape uses it), so
   the verdict runs the subgroup form; the tree
   form is gated in this lane's tests wherever a
   device builds it.

## Server verdict protocol (the next lane)

Preconditions: the card cleared per David's
2026-11-05 order (the Qwen3-Embedding pair on port
8091 and the Qwen3-4B on 8092 gone; the spec phase
needs about 25.3 GB of the 25.75 GB card); the
phase lock `flock /tmp/itak-phase.lock` held; one
heavy job at a time; the staging tree synced to
the merged commit (this lane merged with the K19
lane, since the threshold and ladder are shared)
and its hash verified before any run; production
Glimmer stays down.

0. Shader autopsy of the compiled variants, before
   any timing: extend the bench/shader-autopsy.sh
   pattern to the K20 pipelines at batches 2, 7,
   and 16 and record VGPR, SGPR, spills, scratch,
   and LDS per variant. The claims to check: zero
   or near-zero spills, LDS at the partials size
   only (1 KB subgroup form). A spill cliff at high
   batch is a result, not a surprise: it sets the
   ceiling the sweep in step 4 then maps.
1. Correctness gates execute (no skips) on the
   card:
   `cargo test -p wgpu-compute --test k20_mmv -- --nocapture`
   (batches 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 16 against the CPU f32
   reference and against K2, both reduction shapes,
   plus the 768 x 101 deep geometry) and the compile
   leg:
   `cargo test -p wgpu-compute --test shader_compile k20_mmv`
   (all 15 batch variants, both shapes).
2. Identity + golden first:
   `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=16` in the
   environment, run itak-spec's `spec_generate_gpu`
   against the real target and draft files at depth
   6 and depth 1, greedy, Stage 1 prompt. IDENTITY
   and GOLDEN must PASS in the on position before
   any speed number is read. Control: the same runs
   with the variable unset. The construction log
   must show `mmv config: max_rows=16` in the on
   position and `max_rows=1` in the control.
   Attribution: run with `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing`
   and read the summary table: the `k20_q6k_mmv`
   rows are the proof K20 actually dispatched (and
   how many times, at what GB/s) during the verdict
   runs, since the on position opens both MMV arms
   at once and the end-to-end rate alone cannot
   separate them.
3. Spec A/B against the recorded baselines (K18
   note): depth 6 control 9.19 tok/s, depth 1
   control 14.22 tok/s (same-day verdict controls
   9.21 / 14.60 in the spec suite). Report effective
   tok/s and acceptance per arm, plus verify ms:
   verify is the term the MMV family exists to
   shrink, and its Q6_K share is read from the diag
   table of step 2.
4. Dose-response sweep: depths 1 and 6 at
   `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS` in {4, 8, 12, 16}.
   Two warnings from the research ride on this
   step: llama's dose-response says the win grows
   through 16, but the strix-llama fork found
   non-monotonic per-batch behavior on RADV (their
   split-column batches 3, 5, 6 ran several times
   slower than 1, 2, 4; exhaustive report, line
   136). The sweep exists to catch exactly that on
   this card and driver (Mesa 26.0.8).
5. Plain decode A/B: plain decode is batch 1,
   below the band, so K20 cannot touch it; the
   honest check is that the off and on positions
   produce the recorded plain-decode rate (35.45
   tok/s) unchanged, proving the routing did not
   leak. No MMV prefill claim is made: chunk rows
   at 16 and up belong to the matrix ladder.

Decision rule: `DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS` moves only
if identity and golden pass in the on position AND
depth 6 beats its control AND depth 1 beats its
control, with the dose-response sweep showing no
cliff inside the band the default would open.
Anything less, the default stays 1 and the sweep
table is recorded here as the finding: a register-
streaming kernel that still loses on RADV would
close the small-batch line of attack and push
T-9.6's speed half toward chunked GEMV, the
research plan's next entry.

===== FILE: bench/mmv-sweep.sh =====
#!/bin/bash
# Small-batch sweep: build the harness once, then run
# the variant matrix (control, K18, MMV, chunked)
# through the session's own routing ladder and write
# one timestamped CSV per arm under bench/results/.
#
# Each arm is the same binary (examples/mmv_sweep.rs)
# under a different environment; the harness sets no
# routing env itself and stamps the active env into
# every CSV row. The kernel column of each CSV shows
# which kernel form actually served each cell, so an
# arm whose env name does not match a landed kernel
# reads as the control kernels it really ran, never
# as a silent pass.
#
# The chunked arm's env name is the one line to check
# when the chunked-GEMV prototype lands: it shipped as
# WGPU_COMPUTE_CHUNKED_GEMV_MAX_ROWS (corrected at merge;
# the harness lane had guessed WGPU_COMPUTE_CHUNK_MAX_ROWS
# before the arm landed). Change CHUNK_ENV below and
# nothing else if it ever moves again.
#
# Usage: bench/mmv-sweep.sh [extra mmv_sweep args...]
# Extra args forward to every arm (for example
# --rows 1,2,7 for a partial sweep). Verdict runs take
# no extra args: the defaults are the discipline
# (25 timed repetitions per cell, 3 warmup).
set -u
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

CHUNK_ENV=WGPU_COMPUTE_CHUNKED_GEMV_MAX_ROWS
EXTRA=("$@")

export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
cargo build --release -p wgpu-compute --example mmv_sweep || exit 1
BIN=target/release/examples/mmv_sweep

TS=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
OUTDIR="bench/results/mmv-sweep-$TS"
mkdir -p "$OUTDIR"
echo "results: $OUTDIR"

# Diag timestamps are the timing method when the
# device grants them; the harness falls back to wall
# clock per repetition and prints which it used (the
# arm logs record it).
export WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing

run_arm() {
    label=$1; shift
    echo "arm: $label"
    env "$@" "$BIN" --label "$label" --out "$OUTDIR/$label.csv" "${EXTRA[@]}" \
        > "$OUTDIR/$label.log" 2>&1
    tail -2 "$OUTDIR/$label.log"
}

# Since the 2026-11-06 default flip the UNSET MMV
# ceiling resolves to 16 (the shipped default), so the
# control arm pins the gate closed explicitly to keep
# measuring the pre-flip ladder, and the k18 and
# chunked arms pin it closed too, so each of those
# arms measures only its own rung. The mmv arm sets
# the ceiling it measures; it equals the shipped
# default, and is set anyway so the arm's CSV records
# the value it ran under.
run_arm control \
    -u WGPU_COMPUTE_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS \
    WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=1 \
    -u WGPU_COMPUTE_WIDE_MIN_ROWS \
    -u "$CHUNK_ENV"
run_arm k18 \
    WGPU_COMPUTE_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS=16 \
    WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=1
run_arm mmv \
    WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=16
run_arm chunked \
    "$CHUNK_ENV=16" \
    WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=1

echo "done: $OUTDIR"
ls -la "$OUTDIR"

===== END FILE: bench/mmv-sweep.sh =====

Verdict protocol from `bench/mmv-prototype-2026-11-05.md`, run on
the cleared RX 7900 XTX (ubuntu-server, gfx1100, Mesa 26.0.8 RADV).

**Staged tree: main `dff3494639ac7e6ea652e9f7743cc57bae079e38`**
(the merge of lane/mmv-prototype `40c11c3`), exported with
`git archive`, staged at `~/gpu-wave10` on the server. Full
manifest diff against the local tree at that SHA: 335 files,
identical. Sentinels: `crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/k19_q4k_mmv.rs`
sha256 `f47bb3c7dd1e976ee97ff4648433baaebdf1a50364ffe971def4531362a3b273`,
`crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/mod.rs`
`fad8c52e05ef2200e0cb47d9cfcd88ebbbc2264e0c7fc47cfebb4d06c3b6afa6`,
this verdict's protocol source `bench/mmv-prototype-2026-11-05.md`
`dbd9b0cc864dc54ef56c1fc9d16192d32e548e8485b580d427d8bca691bef6c0`.

**Card state and the taint record.** Before the first
measurement, and at every per-arm guard through the measurement
runs, `/sys/class/drm/card2/device/mem_info_vram_used` read
33,271,808 bytes: driver residue only, no tenant resident.
The 16:47-16:52 EST tenant blip the Cortex chat reported had

At 22:03 UTC a later Cortex deploy restarted
`cortex-cortex-chat-1` and `cortex-cortex-embed-1`

Tenants are left as found; nothing was stopped or started by
this lane beyond its own harness processes.

## Step 0: shader autopsy (RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats,asm,cs)

All 15 batch variants of both shapes were compiled under the
dump (33 compute shaders total; the two non-K19 blocks are
small device-internal shaders). Series attribution is proven,
not assumed: the subgroup batch 2 variant appears twice with
the identical driver pipeline hash (2617757115), once from the
`K19Pipeline::new` construction smoke compile and once from
`with_shape`; the subgroup series carries DPP shuffle counts of
exactly 4 per accumulator slice, the tree series carries
s_barrier counts growing 4 per batch step.

Subgroup reduction form (the form the verdict runs use; the
server adapter grants SUBGROUP):

| batch | VGPR | spilled VGPR | scratch | LDS | code size |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 72 | 0 | 0 B | 1,024 B | 3,292 B |
| 7 | 96 | 0 | 0 B | 1,024 B | 7,984 B |
| 16 | 96 | 0 | 0 B | 1,024 B | 16,660 B |

Every batch 2..16 in this form: VGPR 72 up to a 96 plateau,
**zero spilled VGPRs, zero scratch bytes**, LDS 1,024 B
(RADV's reported allocation; the declared partials array is at
most 256 f32 = 1 KB, at batch 16; no weight byte is ever
staged). Workgroup-tree fallback form, for the record: batch 2
VGPR 72 / code 3,828 B, batch 7 VGPR 84 / 8,712 B, batch 16
VGPR 96 / 17,720 B, likewise zero spills and zero scratch at
every batch.

**Register residence held, at batch 16 included.** The failure
mode the prototype note named as its first risk, the one that
convicted the wide MMQ (1,041-1,213 spilled VGPRs and
78,080-86,528 B of scratch in the 2026-11-04 autopsy), does
not exist in K19's compiled form. SGPR reads 108 in every
variant, the ACO allocation constant already recorded in the
earlier autopsy, not a signal.

## Step 5: plain decode, no leak: PASS

Cleared card, split-mode plain arms, 64 tokens, prompt

| arm | decode rate | stream |
|---|---|---|
| MMV unset (shipped default) | 35.45 tok/s | (reference stream) |
| `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=1` | 35.41 tok/s | byte-identical to unset |

Both streams begin with the golden first 8 tokens
[13796, 26, 1573, 373, 290, 2167, 26899, 1212]. The unset
rate lands exactly on the recorded plain-decode reference of
35.45 tok/s. `max_rows=1` is indistinguishable from off, as
designed (the band starts at row 2).

## Decision

**The default for `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS` stays 1
(off).** The prototype note's rule moves the default only if
identity and golden pass in the ON position AND depth 6
beats its control AND depth 1 beats its control AND the
sweep shows no in-band cliff. The first condition could not
be evaluated on this box today (host-RAM OOM in the harness's
phase B, then the tenants' return), so the rule cannot be
satisfied and the default does not move. The reason is
evidentiary, not a K19 failure: every gate that could run
passed, including the compiled-form question the prototype
most needed answered (step 0: register residence holds at
batch 16, zero spills) and the executed numeric gates
(step 1), and step 5 is clean.

Unblockers, in order: (1) re-run steps 2-4 when the card is
in the cleared state again AND phase B can get its roughly
35 GB host peak, either from a lower-RAM moment on the box or
by first proving the `--kv-capacity=2048` probe lets phase B
fit; (2) the fresh cleared-card spec controls are owed by the
same wall (the baseline lane hit it too) and should be taken
in the same session as the retry, so the A/B stays
same-session.

### Step 3: spec A/B, fresh same-session cleared-card controls

Effective tok/s (generate phase; all-in in parentheses).
Acceptance was identical per depth in every arm (depth 6:
32 rounds, 180 proposed, 31 accepted, rate 0.1722;
depth 1: 38 rounds, 37 proposed, 25 accepted, rate
0.6757), and resident dispatch counts were identical per
depth across arms (14,717 at depth 6; 17,393 at depth 1),
so every difference below is pure timing on identical
trajectories.

| arm | depth 6 | depth 1 |
|---|---|---|
| control (env unset) | 9.09 (9.06) | 16.98 (16.67) |
| `MMV_MAX_ROWS=16` | **10.27 (10.24)** | **19.26 (18.96)** |

Verify time per round (median of the first 12 rounds,
`spec.verify.end` diag lines): depth 6, on about 124 ms
vs control about 159 ms; depth 1, on about 38.5 ms vs
control 45 ms. Verify is the term K19 exists to shrink,
and at the top of its band it shrinks: depth 6 effective
+13.0 percent, depth 1 effective +13.4 percent over the
same-session controls.

For the record, today's cleared-card controls against
the 2026-11-04/05 pressured-card controls: depth 6 9.09
vs 9.19-9.21 (same class), depth 1 16.98 vs 14.22-14.60
(the cleared card lifts the depth 1 control). Phase A

the recorded cleared-card band.

### Step 4: dose-response sweep at depth 1

| `MMV_MAX_ROWS` | effective tok/s | verify median |
|---|---|---|
| unset (control) | 16.98 | 45 ms |
| 4 | 14.71 | about 50 ms |
| 8 | 15.23 | about 51 ms |
| 12 | 15.20 | about 50 ms |
| 16 | 19.26 | about 38.5 ms |

The dose response is **non-monotonic**: caps 4, 8, and
12 all land BELOW the unset control, with verify
medians above the control's, while cap 16 lands above
the control on both measures. This is the in-band cliff
pattern the research warned about (the strix-llama fork's
split-column finding) and the pattern this sweep exists
to catch. Per-batch attribution (which batch sizes in
the band carry the loss, and which carry the cap-16
gain) is read from the sweep-harness table and the diag
exposure run in the same 2026-11-06 session, recorded
in `bench/mmv-bench-harness-2026-11-05.md` and
`bench/mmv-q6k-2026-11-05.md`.

### Decision against the prototype note's rule

The rule moves `DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS` only if identity
and golden pass in the on position AND depth 6 beats
its control AND depth 1 beats its control AND the
dose-response sweep shows no cliff inside the band the
default would open.

- Identity + golden in the on position: PASS (step 2).
- Depth 6 beats its control: YES (10.27 vs 9.09).
- Depth 1 beats its control: YES at cap 16 (19.26 vs
  16.98).
- No cliff inside the band: **NOT SHOWN.** Caps 4, 8,
  and 12 sit below the control at depth 1; the middle
  of the band loses on this card and driver (Mesa
  26.0.8) even though the top of the band wins.

**The default stays 1 (off)**, per the rule as written:
the no-cliff condition is not met, and the rule's own
fallback applies (the default stays and the sweep table
is the finding). The finding, precisely: K19's
register-streaming form is correct everywhere it ran
(identity + golden at both depths, all caps) and fast
at batch 16, but a mid-band range of batches runs
slower through it than through GEMV on RADV, enough to
drag caps 4-12 below the shipped control at depth 1.
Any future flip needs a band floor informed by the
per-batch table (for example, routing only the top of
the band), which is a new prototype decision, not a
default change this verdict authorizes. T-9.6's speed
half remains open: even the winning arm (19.26 tok/s at
depth 1) is far under the 88.6 tok/s bar, because
verify is no longer the whole cost once it shrinks;
the draft and the round overhead dominate what is left.

# Model Suite — every model on the drive, one engine, one test set (2026-10-28)

Engine: llama.cpp master a7af149, **Vulkan** build, RX 7900 XTX (24 GB), one model at a
time with the GPU exclusive, full offload (`-ngl 999`), fixed 16K test context, temperature 0.
Speed: `llama-bench` pp512 / tg128. Time to first token: llama-server, streamed, warm run,
fixed ~600-token passage with a one-sentence summary request. Quality: 3 coding + 3 reasoning
prompts with a known answer key, 1024-token budget, each model's own chat template at default
settings (including default reasoning behavior). Raw per-model JSON + full answer text:
`/mnt/models/bench-2026-10-28/results/` on ubuntu-server; harness: `bench.py` alongside it.

## Results

| Model | File (GB) | Prompt t/s | Gen t/s | TTFT | Load | Score | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite (Q4_K_M) | 10.36 | 5427 | 267.0 | 0.008 s | 4 s | 4/6 | Fastest raw speeds here; failed the bat-and-ball trap ($0.10) and botched 240/10 as 12 min |
| gpt-oss-20b (MXFP4) | 12.11 | 5159 | 228.2 | 0.027 s | 4 s | **6/6** | Perfect score at MoE speed; smallest VRAM footprint |
| Nemotron-Cascade-2-30B-A3B (IQ4_XS) | 18.17 | 4338 | 198.3 | 0.056 s | 4 s | **6/6** | Verbose (500-800 tok/answer) but always lands |
| North-Mini-Code-1.0 (UD-Q4_K_M) | 19.20 | 3411 | 187.7 | 0.067 s | 6 s | **6/6** | Code specialist matches its billing |
| Devstral-Small-2-24B (Q4_K_M) | 14.33 | 1153 | 42.9 | 0.036 s | 4 s | **6/6** | Concise, zero reasoning overhead, dense-model speeds |
| Qwen3.8-27B (UD-Q4_K_M) | 16.46 | 1015 | 41.7 | 0.159 s | 4 s | **6/6** | Disciplined reasoning (fast, short); see MTP below |
| Muse-Glimmer-30B (Q4_K_M) | 16.76 | 999 | 44.4 | 0.165 s | 4 s | **6/6** | Heavy default thinking (1.5-2.1K chars/answer, 9-22 s each); see DFlash below |
| Qwen3.6-27B (Q4_K_M) | 16.82 | 987 | 40.5 | 0.170 s | 4 s | 2/6 | Runaway thinking: 4 of 6 answers never emerged inside the 1024-token budget (all budget burned in reasoning, empty content) |
| Gemma-4-31B-it (Q4_K_M) | 18.32 | 869 | 38.5 | 0.477 s | 6 s | **6/6** | All correct, slowest TTFT; one answer consumed the full 1024 tokens |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-32B (Q4_K_M) | 19.85 | 811 | 38.4 | 0.035 s | 6 s | 4/6 | Coding perfect; reasoning sloppy: bat-and-ball $0.10, tank 20 min (same 240/10 slip) |
| DiffusionGemma-26B-A4B (Q4_K_M) | 16.81 | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | blocked | `unknown model architecture: 'diffusion-gemma'` in llama.cpp a7af149; file byte-verified good, waits on upstream |

Quality key: C1 write dedupe function + state its output on a sample; C2 find and fix an
off-by-one slice bug; C3 predict a sorted-reverse index print; R1 bat-and-ball ($0.05);
R2 syllogism (yes); R3 fill/drain tank (24 min). Every 6/6 model's C1 function was correct
and stated `[1, 2, 3, 5]`.

## Speculative decoding (measured, same C1 code prompt)

| Model | Drafter | Base gen | With drafting | Gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8-27B | MTP head (Q4_0) | 41.7 t/s | **102.9 t/s** | 2.47x |
| Muse-Glimmer-30B | DFlash (Q4_K_M) | 44.4 t/s | **88.6 t/s** | 2.00x |

The pasted article's DFlash claim (75-110+ t/s) lands inside its range on this hardware:
88.6 t/s measured. The Glimmer server on ubuntu-server was restarted WITH the DFlash
drafter enabled after this suite.

## Caveats

- Quality set is 6 prompts: a smoke gate, not a benchmark like LiveCodeBench. Treat score
  differences of one prompt as noise; the structural findings (Qwen3.6's runaway thinking,
  the two 240/10 arithmetic slips) are the signal.
- Default template settings were used deliberately: reasoning models were NOT throttled
  (no reasoning_strength injection). That is why Qwen3.6 starved and Glimmer is slow per
  answer; both behave differently with reasoning controls set.
- VRAM delta readings from sysfs under-read on this driver and are not reported per model;
  generation speeds confirm full offload (a CPU-bound 30B dense model does not reach 40 t/s).
- HIP cross-check exists for Glimmer only (October + this session): HIP wins prefill ~17%,
  loses generation ~7% vs Vulkan. Suite ran on Vulkan, the serving pick.

===== FILE: bench/mojo-d3-gemv-ladder-2026-11-07.md =====
# Mojo/MAX engine — Wave D lane D3: GEMV tuning beyond K1 (2026-11-07)

Lane: `lane/mojo-d3-gemv`, cut from `mojo-max-engine` head
`2c1802c`. Job, in priority order: tune the Q6_K GEMV
(ffn_down + attn_v), tune the Q5_K GEMV (output.weight,
202,048 rows per token), F32/F16 if time remained. Method =
Lane A2's ladder discipline: correctness gate FIRST on every
iteration against the shape's Wave A bar; interleaved timing
against the Wave A port measured fresh in the same window on
the same fixtures; rejected iterations recorded with their
numbers. K1 was NOT revisited (see the K1 verdict).

All server numbers below are direct foreground reads of the
window logs (`~/d3-stage/logs/window{,2,3}.log` on
ubuntu-server). Staging was git archives with STAGED_COMMIT
files and sha256-verified kernel sources in every window;
the phase lock was held throughout each window; only
`cortex-embed.service` was stopped and restored (verified
active after every window); `cortex-cortex-1` and
`cortex-cortex-surrealdb-1` were never stopped; port 8080
was clear in every window; VRAM bookends were identical in
all three windows: 2,584,600,576 B before clear, 33,271,808 B
drained, 2,584,600,576 B after restore.

## Fixtures and bars (stated before starting, from the Wave A note)

Fixtures are built by `bench/mojo-d3/extract_fixtures.py`
from the real model file
(`/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf`),
with independent Float64 numpy references (the extractor's
dequant was cross-checked exactly against a literal
transliteration of `crates/gguf/src/dequant.rs` on random
blocks before any GPU run). The rel metric is
`bench/mojo/compare.py`'s: max_abs_err / max(1, max|ref|).

- Q6_K corr: blk.0.ffn_down rows 0..63 x 19968, k2_check's
  LCG seed-42 input. Bar (k2_check class): rel <= 1e-4,
  cosine >= 0.999999. Wave A port recorded rel 9.710e-08.
  Timing fixture: the full tensor, 6656 rows, 109,025,280 B.
- Q5_K corr: output.weight rows 0..63 x 6656. Bar (k3
  class): rel < 1e-4, cosine > 0.999999. Wave A port
  recorded rel 9.425e-08. Timing fixture: rows 0..16383,
  74,973,184 B.
- F32/F16 corr: the first 64 real F32 [6656] rows in file
  order (norm weights), F16 = the F16 encoding of the same
  rows. Bar (k3 class): rel < 1e-4, cosine > 0.999999. Wave A
  recorded F32 rel 8.426e-07, F16 rel 1.033e-06. Timing
  fixtures are SYNTHETIC 6656x6656 (seeded; no real F32
  tensor of timing size exists - the real F32 rows are
  [6656] vectors): F32 177,209,344 B, F16 88,604,672 B.
  Wave A recorded no GB/s for any of these ports, so each
  window measured the port arm fresh, interleaved.

Fixture validation: in window 1 the freshly measured port
arms reproduced Wave A's recorded figures almost exactly
(Q6_K port rel 9.686e-08 vs recorded 9.710e-08; Q5_K port
9.695e-08 vs 9.425e-08; F32 port 8.414e-07 vs 8.426e-07;
F16 port 1.033e-06 vs 1.033e-06), so the ladders stand on
the same ground Wave A did. Timed-run outputs were also
compared against the full-fixture references for both arms
in every window; all passed their bars.

## Q6_K ladder (blk.0.ffn_down; wgpu K2 shipped r1sg = 831.9 GB/s reference)

Port (window 1, interleaved): 103.11 / 95.23 / 98.16 GB/s,
median **98.16**. Gate rel 9.686e-08.

Iteration 1 — KEPT. The wgpu K2 r1sg structure translated
onto the RAW 210-byte block layout (no repack: device
weights and the CPU twin are untouched): 256 threads as 16
groups of 16, one group per super-block, thread owning the
four streams' quads at byte column 4*(t%8) of half t//8.
The layout fight is real and is the shape's whole
difference from K1: 210 is not a multiple of 4, so odd
blocks start two bytes into a word and no aligned u32 load
can serve them. Words are rebuilt from aligned u16 pairs
(every word offset the kernel builds is even), the f16
super-scale is read as a single u16 (never overreading the
block tail), the 6-bit quant words use ggml's own masks
(ql low/high nibbles, qh bytes as 2-bit planes at shifts 0
and 4), signed sub-block scales are read as single bytes,
and the reduction is K1's segmented shuffle_xor butterfly
plus a shared finish.
Window 1: 410.93 / 397.64 / 412.68, median **410.93 GB/s**
(4.19x the port, +319%; 49.4% of wgpu K2). Gate rel
5.960e-08, cosine 1.000000000000; full timing fixture rel
6.879e-08. Window 2 re-measure of the same binary: median
410.26. Final-tree gate (window 3): rel 5.960e-08; spot
timing 401.12 / 403.26.

Iteration 2 — REJECTED (no win). `load_word` as a single
u16x2 vector load + bitcast (half the load instructions of
iteration 1's two scalar loads + shift/or). Gate identical
(rel 5.960e-08, as expected for a pure load-route change).
Window 2, interleaved against iteration 1: 416.71 / 409.02
/ 406.27, median **409.02** vs iteration 1's 410.26 in the
same window - reps split, no win. Dropped; iteration 1's
form is what ships.

## Q5_K ladder (output.weight; wgpu K3 shipped r2sg = 813.2 GB/s reference)

Port (window 1): 35.23 / 35.40 / 35.52 GB/s, median
**35.40**. Gate rel 9.695e-08. (The port recomputes every
element's scale/min from the header bytes per element; at
44 words per row-block it is the slowest of the four ports
by an order of magnitude.)

Iteration 1 (rows=2) — superseded by iteration 2. The
wgpu K3 r2sg structure, K1's own tuned shape: 2 rows per
128-thread workgroup as 8 groups of 16, header loaded as
one vec4, packed scales factored once per super-block (not
per element), the fifth-bit assembly done per block (one
qh word per thread; per sub-block the (qh >> s) &
0x01010101 plane unpacked to the bits the four quant quads
need), activation quads loaded once per super-block and
shared by both rows, dots in the d*sc*dot(q,x) -
dmin*m*sum(x) form, segmented butterfly + shared finish.
176-byte blocks are word-aligned, so every load is a
direct u32 load exactly as in K1.
Window 1: 337.38 / 332.55 / 337.70, median **337.38 GB/s**
(9.53x the port). Gate rel 2.216e-07, cosine
1.000000000000; full timing fixture rel 2.650e-07.

Iteration 2 (rows=4) — KEPT (promoted). Same per-row math,
tile widened to 4 rows per workgroup: activation quads
loaded once per super-block serve four rows; per-row block
contribution factored as `q5k_block_dot`. Tried as a bench
experiment (`bench/mojo-d3/exp_q5k_r4.mojo`) because the
wider tile had NOT won on K1's ladder (A2 iteration 5) -
on this shape it did: window 2, interleaved against
rows=2, it won every rep: 366.42 / 361.92 / 358.16,
median **361.92 GB/s** vs rows=2's 341.30 in the same
window (+6.0%; 10.22x the port overall; 44.5% of wgpu K3).
Gate rel identical to rows=2 (2.216e-07; the tile changes
only which rows share a workgroup), full timing fixture
rel 2.650e-07. Final-tree gate (window 3): rel 2.216e-07;
spot timing 360.58 / 361.31. gpu_layer follows through the
imported ROWS_PER_WG constant (grid rows//4; odd
row counts refused by name in `gpu_layer_check_proj`);
output.weight's 202,048 rows are a multiple of 4.

## F32 / F16 ladder

Port (window 1): F32 432.13 / 450.54 / 419.92, median
**432.13 GB/s**, gate rel 8.414e-07. F16 180.22 / 180.15,
median **180.19 GB/s**, gate rel 1.033e-06. (The F16 port
decodes every element through the exact scalar f16 route;
the F32 port is a clean streaming kernel and was already
the fastest port of the four shapes.)

F32 tuned iteration — REJECTED. The K1 segment shape (2
rows per 128-thread workgroup, 8 groups of 16 striding the
row in 256-element segments, vec4 loads only, activation
shared by both rows, hybrid reduction): 415.42 / 419.42 /
403.86, median **415.42 GB/s** - slower than the port in
every rep (0.96x). The vec4 segment shape buys nothing
when the port's bottleneck is not instruction count. The
port kernel is restored verbatim (own F32_THREADS=256
constant; gpu_layer F32 launch back to grid=rows; the
2-row-tile refusal now applies to F16 only). Window 2/3
confirmation gates on the restored kernel reproduce the
port's figure exactly (rel 8.414e-07), and the final tree
carries the port.

F16 tuned iteration — KEPT. The same segment shape over
the raw half bytes, each quad arriving as two u32 words
decoded through the K1 bit-trick route (`f16_quad_from_words`,
proven exhaustively against the exact decode on the VM):
717.68 / 718.20, median **717.94 GB/s** (3.98x the port,
+298%). Gate rel 7.944e-07, cosine 1.000000000000; final-tree
gate identical. No real Glimmer slot routes F32/F16 through
the GEMV (norms and the embedding take other paths -
checked in DESIGN.md's slot map and in gpu_layer), so the
2-row F16 tile cannot refuse a real tensor; the standalone
mains carry the named refusal for odd shapes.

## K1 verdict

NOT revisited. The bar stands where Wave A left it (rel

and David's question about moving the bar is still open -
it does not move in this wave. This lane's time went to
priorities 1-3, all of which landed; no K1 iteration was
attempted, so there is nothing to prove twice.

## Integration notes

- gpu_layer launch geometry changed: Q5_K grid is rows//4
  (the Wave A port launched one workgroup per row; this
  lane's iteration 1 made it rows//2), F16 grid is rows//2,
  F32 unchanged, Q6_K unchanged (256 threads). `gpu_layer_check_proj`
  refuses Q5_K rows not divisible by 4 and F16 rows not
  divisible by 2, by name. Re-run the Wave C GPU golden on
  the integrated tree (window 3 ran it on the lane tree and
  it passed).
- Standing gap, unchanged from K1: the tuned Mojo GEMVs sit
  at 44-49% of the wgpu kernels' recorded throughput
  (Q6_K 410.93 of 831.9; Q5_K 361.92 of 813.2), the same
  Mojo-codegen ceiling class A2 recorded for K1 (624.1 of
  838.4, 74% - K1's layout is friendlier). Q6_K's raw-layout
  u16-pair word rebuild is the visible extra cost the wgpu
  kernel does not pay (it reads a repacked layout); closing
  that gap means a repack decision, which is a weights-
  residency call for a later wave, not a kernel-local one.
