===== FILE: bench/mojo-engine-gap-audit-2026-11-08.md =====
# Mojo engine: runner-vs-wall decode gap audit (2026-11-08)

Question (David's zero-trust sheet, 2026-11-08): Wave E
recorded two decode speeds for the same engine on the same
model: a WALL measure of step+logits = 32,491 us (30.78
tok/s) and the runner's own approx of 49,130 us per step
(20.35 tok/s). The 16,639 us difference per token (34% of
the runner step) was unexplained. Was the wall figure
missing a trailing device sync the runner pays (a), was
the runner burning the gap in host-side work (b), or a
split (c)? Neither figure counted as the true baseline
until this audit answered.

Answer: NEITHER (a) NOR (b). The gap is a measurement
artifact inside the runner's approx construction itself,
proven same-binary below (section 3). The wall figure was
never missing its sync (section 2). Per-step host work
inside the decode loop is real but small and already
inside both measures (section 4). Verdict class: the
sheet's (b) named the right side of the comparison (the
runner's number, not the wall's, is the wrong one) but
the wrong mechanism: no per-step host work accounts for
the gap; a one-time cost inside the runner's timed
window does.

## 1. Method and staging

Tree: mojo-max-engine at e08546b0b63888c6e60fb1aff94f605
0657071b3 (engine 1.07), staged by git archive into
~/gpu-gap-audit on ubuntu-server, STAGED_COMMIT stamp in
place, sha256 of gpu_model.mojo, generate.mojo,
gpu_layer.mojo, config.mojo verified identical between
the integration worktree and the server staging before
anything ran. Measurement builds lived ONLY in staging
(tests/server_proof_gap_audit.mojo,
tests/server_proof_gap_runner.mojo) and are not in the
repo. One card window under the phase lock; two runs of
every binary; every number below is a direct foreground
read of the window's log files.

Arms:
- STOCK: the production runner binary
  (src/runner/generate_main.mojo), two runs.
- A1: the stock runner construction inside the audit
  binary: generate() over a fresh GpuGlimmerModel, then
  prefill timed on a second fresh model (forward_rows),
  approx = (generate_ms - prefill_ms)/15, exactly the
  shipped formula.
- A2: the same stock generate() call, but the prefill
  subtracted is prefill() timed on a fresh model of the
  SAME process BEFORE generate() runs (same value
  class: 210/215 ms vs A1's 209/212), generate() itself
  on a third fresh model. A1 and A2 ran back to back in
  the same binary, same window.
- B: the Wave E wall method (E2's phase_wall shape):
  prompt stepped per-row, 3 warmup + 10 measured
  free-running steps, step and logits timed apart.
- C: direct instrumented decode on one model: batched
  prefill() timed (203/202 ms), two generate-mirror warm
  steps, then 10 measured steps of model.step timed
  directly (the step ends in a host-blocking download,
  so its span is the device-complete cost), model.logits
  timed, and the host argmax timed SEPARATELY from the
  logits call.
- GAPRUNNER: the production runner with ONE added step:
  PREFILL_MS_TRUE (a fresh model's forward_rows timed in
  the same process BEFORE generate()) and the approx
  formula re-applied with it. Two runs.

## 2. The wall figure was never missing its sync

model.step() cannot return early: every layer ends in
download_f32 of the hidden row (a host-blocking copy)
and the append inside the layer synchronizes the queue;
the step's wall span therefore includes all device work
by construction. Arm C timed the step directly, inside
a real decode loop: median 30,737 / 30,835 us. Arm B
(the wall method, same window) read step 31,191 /
31,493 us and logits 1,450 / 1,471 us, step+logits
32,641 / 32,965 us = 30.64 / 30.33 tok/s against Wave
E's 32,491 us / 30.78. Arm C's full loop cost per token
(step + logits + the separately timed host argmax):
32,368 / 32,523 us = 30.89 / 30.75 tok/s. Three
independent constructions agree within noise. The wall
figure stands.

## 3. Where the 16,639 us actually is: inside the
##    runner's generate window, not in any step

Same binary, same window, back to back:

| arm | generate_ms | prefill_ms | per step |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 run 1 | 957 | 209 | 49.87 ms (20.05 tok/s) |
| A2 run 1 | 706 | 210 | 33.07 ms (30.25 tok/s) |
| A1 run 2 | 967 | 212 | 50.33 ms (19.87 tok/s) |
| A2 run 2 | 705 | 215 | 32.67 ms (30.62 tok/s) |

The ONLY difference between A1 and A2 is whether a full
model build + prefill ran earlier in the same process.
A1's generate() is the FIRST model use in its process;
A2's generate() runs after two. The generate window
itself differs by 251 / 262 ms (16.7 / 17.5 ms per
nominal step), reproducing the Wave E gap (16,639 us)
almost exactly, with zero change to any decode step.

Corroboration from the runner runs: the stock approx in
this window read 45.13 ms/step and 81.33 ms/step in two
consecutive runs of the SAME binary (generate 891 ms and
1,435 ms; the second run's extra ~544 ms is the same
one-time class landing inside the window a second time,
cause not isolated). The GAPRUNNER's two generate
windows read 716 / 710 ms (per-step totals consistent
with arm C), while its stock PREFILL_MS (measured after
generate, on the process's second model) read 215 / 214
and its PREFILL_MS_TRUE (measured before generate, on
the process's FIRST model) read 463 / 446: the first
model use in a process carries a one-time cost of
roughly +230-250 ms wherever it lands, and the approx
formula books it against decode whenever it lands inside
the generate window, which is exactly where it landed
in Wave E's final window (49.13 ms/step) and in both
audit A1 runs (49.87 / 50.33, bracketing Wave E's
figure).

Mechanism, stated at the level the evidence supports:
a one-time first-use cost of ~200-260 ms attaches to a
process's first full model run (first GEMM-class
launches and first allocations at production shapes).
Wave E's lane note had already spotted its signature (a
one-time ~200 ms stall on the first logits after GEMM
prefill) without attributing the runner gap to it; the
teacher-forced totals show the same shape (450 ms
against ~245 ms accounted). Identifying the precise
first-touch item (kernel module load vs allocator arena
growth vs first-touch page cost) was not needed to
attribute the gap and is NOT claimed here.

## 4. The per-step host work that IS real (inside both
##    measures, not the gap)

- Host argmax: greedy_argmax over the 202,048-wide
  logits row, timed on a live row: median 207 / 261 us
  per call. It is INSIDE the runner's generate window
  and inside arm C's loop figure, and OUTSIDE the wall
  method's step+logits figure (E2 timed
  step-then-logits; its loop also computed an argmax
  per iteration, untimed): the wall figure overstates
  the true loop rate by this ~0.2 ms, ~0.7%: 30.78
  becomes ~30.6 honest. (An inline re-scan of the same
  row printed 0 us at ms-floor precision; the
  sampler's own figure is the one quoted. The scan
  itself is ~0.2 ms of the ~1.4-1.5 ms logits span:
  the rest is the head chain, norm + Q5_K GEMV +
  final_logit + the 808 KB logits download, measured
  by E2 at 1,414-1,574 us.)
- Per-token log flushing: ZERO in the measured runs.
  The diag seam was off; log_debug still builds its
  message string and consults the env var per call
  (~55 calls per step across layers, step, and
  sampler), which is inside every figure above and
  bounded by them: arm C's directly timed step agrees
  with arm B, so the whole class is inside the noise
  band between 30,737 and 31,493 us, well under 1 ms.
- Host allocations per step (~27 buffers/layer) and
  the per-layer host boundary: real, already charged
  to BOTH measures (the wall step contains them; E2's
  profile priced them), and they are the Wave F1-A
  targets. They explain why the true rate is ~30.6
  and not higher; they do not explain any part of
  the 16,639 us.

Attribution of the 16,639 us, in one line: ~16,600 us
one-time first-use cost amortized over 15 steps by the
approx formula (section 3); ~200 us of it is the real
per-step host argmax the wall figure omits (section 4)
- the two overlap in sign only; the measured gap is
the first item.

## 5. Golden guard

Every runner run (stock x2, GAPRUNNER x2) printed the
exact golden 16 tokens with GOLDEN_FIRST8_MATCH 1 and
TEXT_STRICT_OK 1: [13796, 26, 1573, 373, 290, 2167,
26899, 1212, ...], identical to the Wave B/C/D/E
record.

The audit proof's own arms fed the tokenizer-exact
prompt ids as literal data ([200000, 13796, 26, 1573,
373, 290]) and produced the sequence [7963, 323, 11698,
341, 290, 2167, 26899, 1212] from all three arms: that
is the golden stream CONTINUED from position 6 (the
prompt fed as data was the golden stream's own first
ids, so greedy decode continues it: 7963 = " of",
323 = " the", 11698 = " city"...). The arms are
token-identical to each other and decode the same
continuation the runner's own stream shows from its
position 8 onward in shifted form (290, 2167, 26899,
1212 recur). Timings were therefore taken on the
production path with the production token stream, and
the guard's purpose - prove no arm measured a
different path - is met by the runner runs' exact
match plus the arms' mutual identity. Recorded
plainly because the audit arms' literal first-8 does
not equal the golden first-8: the input construction
differed (stream-as-prompt), not the engine path.

## 6. Hardware witness (Trap 1)

Background sampler over /sys/class/drm/card2 +
hwmon6 at ~100 ms cadence for the whole window:
3,276 samples. Peak VRAM used 23,412,744,192 B
(21.8 GiB, above the 15.5 GiB bar) while Glimmer was
loaded. gpu_busy_percent took 82 distinct values,
0-100, not flat. Power swung from 3 W idle to a 400 W
peak reading. Verdict:
GPU execution VERIFIED, not UNVERIFIED_GPU_EXECUTION.

## 7. The honest baseline

DECODE BASELINE OF RECORD: ~30.6 tok/s steady state
(short context, greedy, this tree): the wall method's
32.5-33.0 ms step+logits, plus the ~0.21 ms host
argmax per token the wall figure omits. The runner
approx (20.35 tok/s in Wave E; 19.87-22.16 in this
window's stock-class runs, swinging to 12.30 when the
one-time cost lands twice) is NOT a decode measure and
should not be quoted as one: it divides a window
containing a one-time ~200-260 ms first-use cost by
the step count. Wave F measures against ~30.6.

## 8. Closeout and owed follow-ups

Server closeout, direct reads at window end and again
after: cortex-embed.service stopped for the window
(VRAM drained to 33,271,808 B at entry) and restored
active, /health {"status":"ok"}; containers
cortex-cortex-1 and cortex-cortex-surrealdb-1 up
throughout, never touched; ports 8080 and 18767
clear at entry and closeout; production Glimmer never
started; no reboot. Staging ~/gpu-gap-audit left in
place with its logs (window.log, witness.log, the six
run logs, three build logs).

Proposals (NOT in this commit; the note is the only
change):
1. Runner approx fix: warm the chain before timing
   (one throwaway generate or a pre-timed first model
   use in-process), or time decode steps directly in
   the runner the way arm C does. Until then, quote
   the wall-class figure for decode.
2. First-use cost hunt: ~200-260 ms on a process's
   first model run is worth one profile pass of its
   own; it taxes every short benchmark and every cold
   serve start.
3. The host argmax (~0.21 ms/token) and the logits
   download are the honest small change after F1-A's
   structural items; a device-side argmax would
   retire both.

===== END FILE: bench/mojo-engine-gap-audit-2026-11-08.md =====

===== FILE: bench/mojo-engine-wave-a-2026-11-07.md =====
# Mojo engine Wave A: loader, tuned K1, GEMV family, ops, tokenizer

Date: 2026-11-07. Branch `mojo-max-engine`. Engine version
1.1 -> 1.2. Built on David's order: "launch all the sub agents
you can and let's get this built fast." Five lanes ran in
parallel in their own worktrees on disjoint file sets; the
coordinator integrated them one at a time in dependency order
(A1, A3, A4, A2, A5), ran the full Mojo suite after each
integration, pushed the branch after each, and closed with an
independent verification pass over the integrated tree.
Remote main never moved off b416987.

Suite at wave end (VM, `tests/run_tests.sh`): 78 tests across
16 TestSuite files plus the 3-test seam-on diag rerun, config
probes, and the engine hello: PASS, 0 failed, 0 skipped. An
independent rerun from a scratch copy reproduced 81/81 test
executions passing.

## Lane A1: GGUF loader (src/gguf/loader.mojo)

Staged file read, not mmap (Mojo 1.2's stdlib has no mmap
binding; MAX host buffers would force a device context on a
pure host loader). Header/metadata/directory parse through a
buffered sequential reader; tensor bytes served by seek +
chunked read. Same observable semantics as the Rust mmap
loader. Version 3 only, alignment from `general.alignment`
else 32 with power-of-two validation, mainline ggml type
table, supported set F32/F16/Q8_0/Q2_K/Q3_K/Q4_K/Q5_K/Q6_K/
BF16, parse-time element-count and tensor-range validation,
all 13 metadata value types. Named refusals: gguf_bad_magic,
gguf_unsupported_version, gguf_truncated,
gguf_unknown_dtype, gguf_unsupported_tensor_type,
gguf_tensor_not_found, plus nine more (missing metadata,
type mismatch, invalid utf8, length overflow, bad element
count, out of bounds, invalid format, io error).

Proofs: VM synthetic round-trip suite 14/14 in both seam
modes (17 metadata keys covering every value type incl. 4
array kinds; F32, F32-2D, Q4_K tensors; 11 crafted bad files
each asserting their named refusal). Server proof against
the real Glimmer file (sha256 4cc57c0f...f60e): exactly 731
tensors, 32 metadata KV, version 3, alignment 32, data_start
13,116,544 (matches an independent Python parse). Spot
values exact: general.architecture muse-glimmer, block_count
52, embedding_length 6656, head_count 32, head_count_kv 2,
context_length 131072, tokenizer.ggml.tokens length 202048.
Fixture tensor blk.0.ffn_gate.weight (6656x19968, Q4_K,
74,760,192 bytes): FNV-1a64 over loader-served bytes
0x88b58419387d763c, identical to an independent Python FNV
over the raw file range; sha256 of the loader-served dump
6f877bd6...7142 also identical to an independent extraction.

## Lane A2: tuned K1 (src/kernels/k1_gemv.mojo)

The shipped wgpu r2sg shape expressed in Mojo/MAX idioms:
128 threads/workgroup as 8 groups of 16, 2 rows per
workgroup, one 16-thread group per Q4_K super-block, packed
scale extraction from header words loaded as one vec4,
activation quads loaded once per super-block and shared by
both rows, per-sub-block dots in d*sc*dot(q,x) - dmin*m*sum(x)
form, vector nibble unpack, bit-trick f16 decode, segmented
shuffle_xor butterfly plus a shared-memory finish.

The ladder (RX 7900 XTX, cleared card, fixture
blk.0.ffn_gate.weight, 74,760,192 B/iter, 200 iters + 20
warmup, correctness gate first every window; gate: rel no
worse than 1.267e-07, cosine 1.000000000 class):

- Straight port baseline: 39.8 GB/s recorded median
  (in-window arm 40.3).
- Iter 1, r2sg restructure: 633.5 median. 15.7x baseline.
- Iter 2, workgroup sweep: WG64 617.9, WG256 605.4, both
  worse and rel drifted up; WG128 kept.
- Iter 3, header vec4 load: 637.6 median (vs 626.2 same
  window). Kept.
- Iter 4, helper/SIMD-accumulator refactor: 580.2 (-9%),
  reverted; rows=4 in that form 610.5.
- Iter 5, rows=4 scalar-unrolled: 624.5 vs 631.2 same window.
  No win.
- Iter 6, super-block loop unroll-by-2: 647.5 median but rel
  rose to 1.490e-07, over the gate. REJECTED; the gate was
  not traded for speed.

Final committed kernel, fresh staged window: correctness rel
1.267e-07, cosine 1.000000000 (vs the wgpu output rel
1.788e-07), exactly the shipped wgpu kernel's recorded
figures. Timing 620.5 / 626.2 / 624.1, median 624.1 GB/s =
74.4% of the recorded wgpu median 838.4 GB/s.

VERDICT, plainly: BELOW the within-10% line (754.6 GB/s) by
~130 GB/s. A 15.7x speed-up over the straight port, not
parity. Remaining-gap analysis (the lane's, recorded as
analysis): the binding constraint measured is the
correctness gate itself; every accumulation reorder that
bought speed moved rel to 1.34-1.49e-07 (all would pass a
1.267e-6 bar; whether the bar should move is a decision for
David, not a lane). Beyond that: Mojo/MAX codegen issues
scalar u32 qs loads per lane where the WGSL path gets better
scheduling, reduce_add on SIMD4 lowers to scalar chains vs
WGSL dot(), all 16 lanes redundantly load/decode the header,
and shuffle_xor's RDNA lowering cost is unmeasured. Future
levers: ISA/occupancy inspection, MAX block-reduction
primitives, finer launch-config sweep.

## Lane A3: dequant + GEMV family (src/kernels/)

Census (crates/muse-glimmer weights.rs/config.rs, verified
live on the server file; full-file census: Q4_K 365, F32 313,
Q6_K 52, Q5_K 1, F16 0): Q6_K = blk.*.ffn_down [19968x6656]
and blk.*.attn_v [6656x1024]; Q5_K = output.weight only
[6656x202048]; F32 = all norms; F16 = no weight tensors in
this model (built as the loader-served storage variant).

Files: dequant.mojo (shared: exact f16->f32, Q6_K and Q5_K
per-element dequant mirroring crates/gguf/src/dequant.rs term
for term), q6k_gemv.mojo, q5k_gemv.mojo, f32_gemv.mojo (F32
and F16-storage kernels). Each: GPU kernel + CPU twin, diag
wired, named refusals. Straight ports per the wave charter;
tuning them is later work.

VM proofs (synthetic fixtures, named as such, in-test
independent Float64 references; bars cosine >= 0.999999999,
rel <= 1e-5): Q6_K cosine 1.0 rel 0.0; Q5_K cosine 1.0 rel
0.0; F32 pass; F16 cosine 0.9999999999999934 rel 2.94e-07.
One real bug found and fixed en route (Q6_K stream nibble
selection).

GPU proofs: Q6_K by the lane on the real blk.0.ffn_down rows
0..63 (k2_check LCG seed 42, independent Float64 numpy
reference): cosine 1.000000000, rel 9.710e-08, at the
recorded k2_check bars. Q5_K, F32, F16 by the independent
verification pass on the integrated tree, same window
discipline, rows 0..63 x 6656, k3-class bars (rel < 1e-4,
cosine > 0.999999):

- q5k_gemv: cosine 0.999999999999996, rel 9.425e-08. PASS.
- f32_gemv (f32): cosine 0.999999999999790, rel 8.426e-07.
  PASS. Fixture: the first 64 real F32 [6656] tensors in file
  order (the file's only F32 tensors are norm vectors).
- f32_gemv (f16): cosine 0.999999999999710, rel 1.033e-06.
  PASS. Fixture: the F16 encoding of those same real rows;
  the file carries zero native F16 tensors, so this proves
  the kernel against real model values in F16 storage, not
  against a native F16 tensor. Stated plainly.

## Lane A4: elementwise ops (src/ops/)

Files: rms_norm.mojo (weighted + plain forms; Glimmer's
embedding norm is a distinct step in the Rust code),
rope.mojo, swiglu.mojo, residual.mojo, softmax.mojo,
final_logit.mojo (its own module: scale first, then
cap * tanh(z/cap), exactly muse-glimmer model.rs
softcap_scale), embedding.mojo (F32 row gather; quantized
dtypes refuse by name, dequant belongs to the kernels
family). Each: CPU twin + GPU kernel, diag wired, named
refusals.

Values with Rust citations: RMS epsilon 1e-5
(crates/muse-glimmer/src/config.rs census + config test);
formula from crates/torch-math/src/norm.rs (Float64
mean-of-squares). RoPE base 500,000 (same census); pairing is
the interleaved NORM (adjacent) pairing from
crates/torch-math/src/rope_interleaved.rs (the half-split
NEOX in rope.rs is qwen2's); head dim 128. RoPE supports
NoPE global layers by the caller simply not calling it; no
skip flag exists. Final logit scale 0.1961161345243454,
softcap 20.0, scale-then-softcap order per model.rs.

CPU proofs (synthetic fixtures, independent in-test Float64
references; 16/16 pass): rms_norm max_rel 5.66e-08 (plain
4.04e-08); against Rust's recorded known_vector [1,2,3,4]
max_abs 1.75e-05 inside Rust's own 1e-4 bar (no recorded RMS
fixture file exists; the Rust unit-test vectors are the
closest recorded fixture and were used). RoPE max err
5.94e-08. SwiGLU max_rel 1.05e-07. Residual exact 0.0.
Softmax max err 1.39e-08 (incl. a 1000-magnitude stability
row). Final logit max err 1.04e-06; the Rust recorded case
[0,20,-20,1000] at scale 0.5/cap 20 matched within 5.1e-08
(this case distinguishes scale-first from cap-first).
Embedding exact 0.0; Q8_0 refuses by name.

GPU proof by the lane (server card): rms_norm row max_abs
1.19e-07, softmax 2x128 max_abs 3.73e-09, GPU_PROOF PASS.

## Lane A5: tokenizer (src/tokenizer/)

Mirror of crates/tokenizer semantics. The file declares
tokenizer.ggml.model "gpt2", pre "llama4"; 202,048 tokens,
439,802 merges, bos 200000, eos 200001, pad 200018, no
unknown token id. Both families implemented: byte-level BPE
(GPT-2 byte alphabet, GPT-4o pre-tokenizer pattern as
llama.cpp assigns to pre "llama4", merges lowest rank first,
specials matched literally longest-first, no BOS/EOS added)
and SentencePiece BPE (space escape, score-ordered merges).
Named refusals across the module family (missing vocab
metadata, invalid token id, invalid merge, empty vocab,
duplicates, length mismatches, unsupported model,
unencodable symbol, malformed byte token, invalid UTF-8).

# Mojo engine Wave B: KV cache, attention, model forward, generation loop

Date: 2026-11-07, closed 2026-11-08. Branch
`mojo-max-engine`. Engine version 1.3 as of the wave's
closing commit: the golden verdict is in and it PASSED (see
THE GOLDEN VERDICT below for rung 2 counted, rung 3 8/8, and
the end-to-end run). Remote main never moved off b416987.

Suite at this writing (VM, `tests/run_tests.sh` via pixi):
107 tests green (Wave A 78 + B1 9 + B2 7 + B4 9 + B3 4),
plus the 3-test seam-on diag rerun, config probes, and the
engine hello: PASS, 0 failed, 0 skipped, reproduced after
every integration.

## Lane B1: KV cache (src/kv/cache.mojo, 595 lines; tests 9/9)

Mirror of crates/attention/src/cache.rs semantics: LayerKind
(global | windowed), the Glimmer pattern (52 layers, global
at index % 4 == 3, windowed 2048 elsewhere), flat f32 rows
[num_kv_heads][head_dim], windowed ring slot = position %
window with slot_position tracking, appends refused by name
out of order / out of range / wrong shape, reads by absolute
position refused by name when evicted or unwritten. Proofs:
global round-trip exact; small-window wraparound exact at
every boundary; the REAL window 2048 shape at positions
2047/2048/2049 exact; a global sibling unaffected by a
windowed wrap; 11 named refusals asserted. Size accounting
CORRECTED the wave brief's reading: the recorded full-context
figure 3,653,238,784 B is the WINDOW-CAPPED sum (13 x 131072
+ 39 x 2048 positions), and the all-global upper bound is
13,958,643,712 B; the accounting exposes both and the tests
assert both. No checkpoint/rewind (later wave), stated in the
module header.

## Lane B2: attention (src/attention/attention.mojo, 528 lines; CPU tests 7/7, GPU proof PASS)

RoPE findings from the Rust CPU path, now the engine's law:
rotation happens at WRITE time in CpuCompute::attention
(cpu.rs rope_row); Q and K rows rotate at the position's
absolute position with the SWA base (500,000); the cache
holds ROTATED K; globals never rotate; the attention math
core takes pre-rotated rows (scale 1/sqrt(head_dim), GQA
kv_head = h // 16, causal + window masking over absolute
positions). The lane shipped both seams against flat K/V
stores: attention_cpu (raw K, rotates at read) and
attention_cpu_rotated_cache (rotated K, rotates only Q
internally), proven equivalent. CPU proofs against in-test
Float64 references: tiny GQA max_err 1.18e-07, causal
3.32e-07, window boundary 4.80e-08, global NoPE 8.87e-08,
sliding RoPE 1.02e-07, prefill loop worst 6.93e-08, 5 named
refusals. GPU proof on the card (64 positions, head_dim 128,
RoPE on): cosine 0.9999999999999861, rel 5.13e-07, VRAM
bookends measured exactly (drained 33,271,808 B, restored
8,932,147,200 B), tenants healthy after. Flash status,
stated plainly: the GPU kernel is flash-STYLE decoding (one
block per Q head, single streaming pass, online softmax, no
materialized score row); shared-memory K/V tile staging and
split-KV parallelism are OWED (occupancy work), recorded in
the module header.

## Lane B4: generation loop + greedy sampler (src/generate/, tests 9/9 in both seam modes)

The brief's function-parameter seam does not compile in Mojo
1.2 (thin calling-convention mismatch, probed both
spellings); the seam as built is a ForwardModel trait
(step/logits) with generate() generic over it. Sampler:
first-max (lowest index) tie-break exactly as
crates/itak-engine/src/sampler.rs; empty logits refuse by
name instead of the Rust stochastic path's silent 0. EOS is
EXCLUDED from the returned ids, uncounted, and never fed
back (crates/itak-engine/src/engine.rs generate_inner; the
speculative session's inclusive truncation is its own rule
and was not followed). Mock proofs assert the exact generated
ids AND the exact (token, position) call sequence across the
prefill/decode boundary, EOS stop, max-tokens stop, and the
named refusals.

## Lane B3: model forward (src/model/model.mojo, 690 lines; rung 1 tests 4/4)

Built by the coordinator directly (the subagent spawn
facility failed twice with a reservation error during this
wave; the lane worktree lane/mojo-b3-model carries the work
and it integrated through the same merge + suite + push
gate). ModelConfig from the file's own metadata (all
muse-glimmer.* keys; the sliding_window_pattern bool array
wins, cross-checked against the derived pattern on a
52-layer file, refusal by name on disagreement). Weights
handle resolves all 731 expected tensors by name and refuses
by name on any miss; weight BYTES ARE CACHED at load (the
loader's per-call staged reads would re-read ~17 GB from
disk per token; the serving wave can revisit). Projections
dispatch by dtype to the Wave A GEMV CPU twins (Q4_K, Q6_K,
Q5_K, F32, F16). The embedding handles its actual storage
dtype by per-row dequant for Q4_K/Q6_K/Q5_K, direct gather
for F32/F16 (the Wave A census says this file's F32 tensors
are the norms, so the quantized path is the live one; the
server proof prints the measured type ids). Step order is
model.rs forward_rows statement for statement, including the
weightless embedding norm, per-head Q/K norms, sigmoid
attn_gate, and both post norms at POST_NORM_EPS 1e-8.
Captures (embed, named-layer in/out) are built in for
divergence isolation.

# Mojo engine Wave C: the forward on the GPU

Date: 2026-11-07, closed 2026-11-08 (the final window ran
2026-11-08 03:26 UTC, 22:26 EST). Branch `mojo-max-engine`.
Engine version 1.4 as of the wave's closing commit: the
golden verdict on the GPU path is in and it PASSED (see THE
GOLDEN VERDICT below). Remote main never moved off b416987.

The seam contract the lanes coded against is
`mojo-engine/WAVE_C_INTERFACES.md` (committed first, at
da91f34). The port shape, as shipped: weights and the KV
cache resident on device, per-position step semantics
identical to the CPU model, activations as host rows at the
layer boundary (each op uploads its input row, launches
against resident weights/KV, downloads its output row).

## Memory budget: planned vs observed

Planned (contract, before the first run): weights at most
16,756,683,904 B (the whole file as the bound), device KV
3,653,238,784 B at context 131,072, scratch envelope
536,870,912 B; planning total 20,946,793,600 B against a cap
of 24,696,061,952 B (card total 25,769,803,776 B minus a
1 GiB reserve; `MOJO_ENGINE_GPU_BUDGET_BYTES` overrides).

Observed (Lane C1's server proof, staged 5147c2e): exact
resident weights 16,743,567,360 B (the 13,116,544 B under
the planning bound is file header/metadata), device KV
3,653,238,784 B exactly as planned, reserved total at full
build 20,933,677,056 B (exact weights + KV + scratch
envelope), under the cap with about 3.76 GB to spare. The
budget is enforced by the runtime ledger BEFORE allocation
(`gpu_budget_exceeded` refused first). One ledger behavior
to know: the ledger is per-`GpuRuntime`; it does not sum
across runtimes in one process (see the runner phasing fix
under Integration - that is why the phasing matters).

## Lane C1: device plumbing (src/gpu/, config addition)

`GpuRuntime` (DeviceContext ownership, budget ledger,
upload/download helpers, refusals `gpu_no_device` /
`gpu_budget_exceeded` / `gpu_copy_shape`), `DeviceWeights`
(every slot resident: quantized/F16 as uint8 buffers over
raw bytes, F32 as float32 buffers; named accessors for
embedding/output/final-norm; per-layer access by (layer,
suffix_index)), `DeviceKvCache` (B1 layout byte for byte;
append via one-row staging + scatter kernel; B1 refusal
names under a `gpu_kv_` prefix). Config gained
`MOJO_ENGINE_GPU_BUDGET_BYTES` with the same parse/refuse
discipline as the other values.

Server proof (cleared-card window, log read in the
foreground from ~/gpu-wave-c1/run.log): PROOF GPU_PLUMBING
PASS, 35 PROOF EXACT lines. blk.0.ffn_gate.weight
downloaded from device hashes FNV-1a64
0x88b58419387d763c, equal to the host's, 0 byte mismatches;
an F32 slot (blk.0.attn_norm.weight) downloads value-exact.
Device KV sequences element-exact against B1's CPU cache
fed identical rows (synthetic window-4 + global; the real
2048 window with reads at 0, 1, 777, 2046, 2047; a global
sibling). DeviceWeights built in 7,021 ms.

DEVIATION, kept and recorded: B1's CPU cache accepts
windowed appends past the window and evicts (ring); the
device cache refuses the first wrap append with
`gpu_kv_window_wrapped`, exactly the contract's stated Wave
C limit (the attention kernel consumes visible rows in slot
order from offset 0). The proof demonstrates both behaviors
on identical rows. A device-side visible-order gather is
owed work; contexts past the window stay on the CPU path.

VM findings from the lane: `mojo build` AOT fails with
target 'unknown' for any file that launches GPU kernels on
the GPU-less VM (pre-existing; reproduced on Wave A's
untouched gpu_proof_ops.mojo). Those mains compile on the
card host. Lane C3 later found the VM-side compile route:
`mojo build --target-accelerator gfx1100`.

## Lane C2: GPU layer assembly

`src/model/gpu_layer.mojo` (777 lines): `gpu_layer_step`
statement-for-statement the CPU `layer_step` (norms via
rms_norm_kernel with resident norm buffers; projections by
slot dtype; per-head Q/K norms grid=heads width=head_dim;
sliding layers rotate K before the KV append and Q before
the attention launch, base 500,000 - the kernel contract is
PRE-ROTATED Q/K; attention_kernel on the DeviceKv buffers;
a new `attn_gate_kernel` for attn*sigmoid(gate); swiglu;
post norms at 1e-8; residual adds are HOST adds on the
downloaded boundary rows, stated in the header) and
`gpu_logits` (final norm + Q5_K head over 202,048 rows +
final_logit_kernel, scale/softcap from the CPU model's
config). `src/ops/gpu_embedding.mojo`: device dequant of
one embedding row for the table's actual dtype.

Attempt ladder: (1) first build against guessed contract
surface with per-call norm uploads - dropped mid-lane when
real C1 landed with resident accessors; (2) adapted to real
C1 (`DeviceWeights.build`/`DeviceKvCache.build`, mut rt,
slot views) - kept; (3) server proof against real C1 on a
merge tree with the lane's VM stand-in package deleted from
staging - PASS on every leg, first card attempt.

Server proof numbers (bars: cosine >= 0.999999, max rel
<= 1e-4, argmax exact; log ~/gpu-wave-c2/proof.log):
embedding tokens 13796 and 200000 max abs 0.0 (exact).
Layer 0 (sliding, position 0): cosine 0.9999999999985569,
max rel 2.33e-06, GPU sum 65.22703143954277 vs the counted
65.22733633872122; GPU 16 ms vs CPU 4,002 ms. Layer 3
(global, position 0): cosine 0.9999999999983837, max rel
8.41e-07, GPU sum 157.77902115881443 vs counted
157.77914571017027; GPU 15 ms vs CPU 4,110 ms. The counted
full rows were never published (sum + first8 only), so the
proof verified its in-process CPU row against the counted
record, then the GPU row against that CPU row over the full

Unproven legs, plainly (from the lane): GEMV dispatch

## Integration record

Order: C4 (merge 3f92928, pushed), C1 (merge 39ebf1c +

Reconciliation fixes in 7ba701f (coordinator): C3's six

files (add/add conflicts resolved to the integrated side);
builder spellings `GpuRuntime.create` /

Runner phasing fix in 521cb5e (coordinator, caught by

Wave B runner construction holds the generate model and
the fresh prefill-measurement model alive simultaneously.
On CPU that is host RAM; on device it is two resident

# Mojo engine Wave D: the speed wave (wave record)

Date: 2026-11-08. Branch `mojo-max-engine`, engine version
1.5. Base for the wave: Wave C head 2c1802c (engine 1.4,
GPU golden PASS). All four lanes cut from 2c1802c, proved
on their own trees, and integrated onto this branch; D3
and D4 were integrated by the wave coordinator, D2 arrived
as a pre-reconciled port onto the D3+D4 tree
(lane/mojo-d2d4-reconciled), and D1 was merged last by the
landing agent after the coordinator went inactive. The
per-lane records are bench/mojo-engine-wave-d1-gemm-
2026-11-07.md (D1), bench/mojo-engine-wave-d-d2-2026-11-07
.md (D2), bench/mojo-d3-gemv-ladder-2026-11-07.md (D3),
and bench/mojo-engine-wave-d-lane-d4-2026-11-07.md (D4);
this note is the wave-level summary and the integration
record. Remote main verified at b416987 before and after,
never moved.

## Lane outcomes

### D3, GEMV tuning beyond K1 (integrated first)

- Q6_K tuned to the wgpu K2 r1sg shape: 410.9 GB/s, 4.19x
  its Wave A straight port.
- Q5_K tuned to the K3 r2sg shape with a rows=4 tile
  promoted into the engine kernel: 361.9 GB/s, 10.2x port.
- F16 tuned to the segmented vec4 shape: 717.9 GB/s,
  3.98x port.
- F32: the tuned iteration was REJECTED on window-1
  numbers and the port kernel kept (recorded in the lane
  note, not rounded up).
- K1 untouched, inside its existing bar (624.1 GB/s,
  rel 1.267e-07); the bar question stays David's open call.
- Lane-level engine measures on the D3 tree: decode
  9.09 tok/s (Wave C: 6.62), 6-token prefill 563 ms
  (Wave C: 684 ms).

### D4, activation residency + device KV wrap

- Device-buffer chained layer step (gpu_layer_step_
  resident): residual stream, norms, projections,
  attention, and MLP stay on device; hostchain kept as
  the A/B baseline. Warm medians on the C2 harness
  shapes: 1.91x (layer 0) and 1.60x (layer 3) against
  the hostchain.
- Device KV window wrap: B1 ring semantics on device
  with a visible-order gather kernel; the Wave C refusal
  (gpu_kv_window_wrapped) is retired from DeviceKvCache.
  Wrap proof: 83 element-exact lines, the real 2,048
  window replayed past wrap, and synthetic generation
  0..2063 running on device.

### D2, attention occupancy (via the reconciled port)

- attention_tiled_kernel: shared-memory K/V tile staging
  (tile 32 kept), one block per (Q head, split), barriers
  per tile instead of per position; split-KV partials
  merged by attention_merge_kernel with exact logsumexp
  rescaling - no approximation, CPU twins mirror the
  float path tile by tile.
- Card trials (two windows, interleaved old-vs-new):
  stored 1,025 at the chooser's splits 3: 842.3 -> 315.1
  us (2.67x); stored 4,096 splits 8: 3,138.4 -> 486.9 us
  (6.45x); stored 4,096 NoPE splits 4: 3.64x. Correctness
  inside the Wave B bars on every fixture (cosine >=
  0.999999999, rel <= 1e-5; observed rel 4.36e-07 ..
  9.07e-06).
- Short-regime cost stated plainly: at stored <= 512 the
  single-split new path runs 0.91-0.95x of the old kernel
  per launch and the prefill sweep 0.81-0.83x; the merge
  launch is the mechanism, and per full step it is under
  half a millisecond against a ~109-151 ms step.
- Baseline finding: the retained Wave B kernel drifts
  just past its own 1e-5 rel bar at stored 4,096 NoPE
  (rel 1.09e-05, deterministic across both windows), a
  fixture size Wave B never ran. The production path no
  longer uses it; it stays as the A/B baseline, relabeled
  BASELINE in the proof output and not gated.
- Config: MOJO_ENGINE_ATTN_TILE_POSITIONS 32,
  MOJO_ENGINE_ATTN_MAX_SPLITS 8, MOJO_ENGINE_ATTN_SPLIT_
  SPAN_POSITIONS 512, named refusals; knobs thread
  EngineConfig -> runner -> GpuGlimmerModel -> the
  resident layer launch.

### D1, GEMM prefill path (integrated last)

- New src/kernels/gemm.mojo: one GEMM launch per

## What remains owed after Wave D

- Batched prefill still crosses activations per op as
  host rows and runs KV appends + causal attention per
  position: residency INSIDE prefill is the next lever
  (D1's own analysis; the kernel-level win is 2.0-2.1x,
  the end-to-end win 1.83x, the gap is this shape).
- The batch layer step on the tiled split-KV attention
  (see the integration seam above). This is now the
  measured prefill bottleneck: on the integrated tree
  the per-row resident path prefills 1,022 tokens in
  48.4 s against the batched path's 76.6 s, so wiring
  residency + tiled attention INTO the batch step (or
  routing long prefills through the resident step loop
  until then) is the first speed item of the next wave.
- Launch-geometry drift is a named hazard after this
  landing: three of the wave's integration defects were
  the same shape (a caller keeping a kernel's old
  grid/block geometry after another lane changed the
  kernel). Any future kernel promotion must grep every
  enqueue site for that kernel in the same commit.
- Decode's remaining gap to the reference points (Rust
  engine ~34.5 tok/s, llama Vulkan 44.59 tok/s on this
  card).
- A splits==1 direct-output variant of the tiled kernel
  would remove the merge launch in the short regime
  (D2's note; not built - not the bottleneck at recorded
  step times).
- Budget-ledger unreserve (owed since Wave C) and the
  Wave C harness verdict-line extraction shape fix.
- K1's correctness bar (rel 1.267e-07) still binds its
  tuning: faster reorders land at 1.34-1.49e-07. Whether
  the bar moves is David's call, recorded again here,

# Mojo engine Wave D, Lane D4: activation residency + device KV window wrap

Date: 2026-11-07 (server windows ran 2026-11-08 04:06-04:14
UTC, 23:06-23:14 EST). Branch `lane/mojo-d4-residency`, cut
from `mojo-max-engine` head
2c1802c4d9a764899f56178e673e183d70301749 (remote branch head
verified equal before the cut; remote `main` verified at
b416987a736b0a63c9f7815ec4b4fbc84e4dd2dd and never touched).
Lane commits are listed at the bottom; the coordinator
integrates and pushes.

## (a) Activation residency - DONE, full chain

`gpu_layer_step` now runs `gpu_layer_step_resident`
(src/model/gpu_layer.mojo): the layer's input row uploads
once, and the residual stream, norm outputs, Q/K/V rows,
the gated attention output, and the MLP intermediates stay
as device buffers passed op to op. The KV append is
device-to-device (`DeviceKvCache.append_device`), the
residual adds are device adds (`residual_add_kernel`, the
same plain f32 per-element add the host add did), and the
output row downloads once. `gpu_logits` chains the same way
(one upload, one download). The Wave C step survives as
`gpu_layer_step_hostchain`, the A/B baseline.

Remaining host crossings, stated exactly: (1) the layer
boundary itself - one hidden-row upload + one download per
layer, the contract's boundary shape, crossed 52 times per
model step by the model-level chain (embedding and logits
in gpu_model still hand host rows between layers; a
cross-layer resident chain is a different change); (2) no
other activation crosses inside a layer. Past a KV wrap,
attention's K/V source is a device-to-device visible-order
gather, not a host crossing.

Correctness (server proof, C2 harness shape, fresh KV per
step, rung-2 input construction): the resident row is
numerically IDENTICAL to the hostchain row at every printed
figure, both layers, every round - layer 0 cosine
0.9999999999985569, max rel 2.33e-06, sum 65.22703143954277
vs counted 65.22733633872122; layer 3 cosine
0.9999999999983837, max rel 8.41e-07, sum 157.77902115881443
vs counted 157.77914571017027. The in-process CPU rows match
the counted sums exactly (sum_rel 0.0). Bars were cosine
>= 0.999999, max rel <= 1e-4: RESIDENCY PROOF PASS.

Timings (interleaved rounds, warmup excluded, medians of 4;
window 2 at microsecond resolution, logs
~/gpu-wave-d4b/residency_us.log read in the foreground):
- Layer 0 (sliding): hostchain median 3,578 us, resident
  median 1,871 us - 1.91x.
- Layer 3 (global): hostchain median 2,964 us, resident
  median 1,847 us - 1.60x.
Per-round pairs (us, host/resident): layer 0: 4257/2919,
3519/1831, 3578/1800, 2931/1871; layer 3: 4074/2856,
2964/1762, 2792/1785, 2782/1847. Context for the Wave C
record: Wave C's single cold steps printed 16 ms / 15 ms;
this proof's warmup round printed hostchain 8,828 / 8,193 us
and resident 3,641 / 3,170 us. The warm per-layer saving is

End-to-end regression on the resident path (same window):

## (b) Device KV window wrap - DONE, refusal retired

`DeviceKvCache` appends now wrap the ring with B1's exact
semantics (slot = position % window, slot_position tracks
the holder, stored/first_visible unchanged in meaning);
`kv_append_refusal` no longer returns
`gpu_kv_window_wrapped` for any append. Readers get
`DeviceKvCache.gather_visible`: the raw buffer when its slot
order already is the visible order (global layers, and
windowed layers whose first visible position lands on slot
0 - including first_visible exactly 2048), otherwise
`kv_visible_gather_kernel` materializes the visible rows in
absolute-position order into a scratch buffer (at most
window x row floats, inside the scratch envelope) that
attention_kernel consumes unchanged. The resident attention
(`attention_device_resident`) reads through it; the legacy
hostchain step still refuses past the window by the old
name, stated in its header - the name survives ONLY there.

Proofs (tests/server_proof_gpu_kv_wrap.mojo, WRAP PROOF
PASS; 83 WRAP EXACT lines, 0 mismatches):
- Synthetic window-4 replay, positions 0..11 (three wraps),
  device vs B1 CPU cache: after EVERY append, stored_len and
  first_visible agree and every visible row compares

# Mojo engine Wave D, Lane D1: GEMM prefill path

Date: 2026-11-07 (windows ran 2026-11-08 UTC by the server
clock). Branch `lane/mojo-d1-gemm`, cut from mojo-max-engine
2c1802c (verified equal to the remote branch head before the
cut; remote main verified at b416987 and never moved). Work
was NOT pushed; the coordinator integrates. Engine stays 1.4
(version bumps are the coordinator's wave-close act).

## What was built

Prefill no longer runs the GEMV family once per prompt row
for its projections. New module src/kernels/gemm.mojo: one
GEMM launch per projection for the whole prompt batch
against the same resident weight buffer, dequant in-kernel
exactly as the GEMVs do (Q4_K via k1_gemv's own unpack/scale
helpers and accumulation form; Q6_K/Q5_K via
kernels/dequant's per-element helpers; F32 plain). Layouts:
X flat [batch][cols], Y flat [batch][rows]. Shapes built:
Q4_K, Q6_K, Q5_K, F32 - the GPU layer's projection dispatch
census. F16 (zero Glimmer weight tensors) refuses by name in
the batch path; single rows keep the GEMV path.

Wiring: src/model/gpu_layer_batch.mojo (gpu_layer_step_batch,
statement-for-statement gpu_layer_step over flat batches;
projections via GEMM, norms/RoPE/gate/SwiGLU batched by their
existing launches, KV appends and causal attention per
position with stored = start+i+1), GpuGlimmerModel.prefill /
prefill_batch in gpu_model.mojo, and ONE defaulted method on
the ForwardModel trait (generate/generate.mojo): the default
prefill is the Wave B/C step loop verbatim, so the CPU
adapter and the test mock are byte-identical without defining
anything; the GPU model overrides it. generate() now calls
model.prefill for the prompt phase. step() and logits() -
the decode path - are untouched. Runner threads the two new
config knobs (src/config.mojo:
MOJO_ENGINE_PREFILL_GEMM_MIN_BATCH default 2,
MOJO_ENGINE_GEMM_TILED_MIN_BATCH default 8, named refusals;
setting the first above any prompt length disables the GEMM
path, which is the A/B control used below).

## Trial ladder (correctness gate first, every iteration)

(1) MAX's own kernel library matmul: NO FIT. In MAX 26.7 the
only quantized matmul surface is the Python graph op
max.graph.ops.qmatmul (encodings Q4_K and Q6_K only - no
Q5_K; inspected live in the VM pixi env). It lives in the
MAX graph/pipeline world: it takes TensorValues in MAX's
repacked quantized layout, it QUANTIZES the lhs activations
to the rhs encoding before the product (not this engine's
f32-activation semantics and not the K1 accumulation form),
and it is not callable from Mojo kernel code - no Mojo-side
matmul module resolves in this toolchain (probed:
max.kernels.matmul, max.nn, kernels.matmul, max.kernels all
fail). Adopting it means rebuilding the forward inside MAX
graphs: a different engine, not a prefill path for this one.

(2) Straightforward batched GEMM (the GEMV workgroup body
with batch offsets, one launch per projection): CORRECT
everywhere (below) and kept as the below-tile-threshold
structure. Timing at batch 64, real shapes, interleaved
medians of per-pass ms (server proof, window 2): Q4_K
ffn_gate 19968x6656: 6.34 ms vs the per-row GEMV arm's 6.73
(1.06x). Q6_K ffn_down 6656x19968: 131.58 ms vs GEMV 86.45
(0.66x - SLOWER than per-row GEMV; recorded as measured: the
weight stream is still re-read per batch row and the caches
do not save it).

(3) Register batch-tiled GEMM (one workgroup owns one output
row - K1: the row pair - for a tile of 4 batch rows; each
weight element / Q4_K header+quads loaded and dequantized
once per workgroup and applied to all 4 rows): CORRECT
everywhere and the measured winner. Same timing pass: Q4_K
3.34 ms (2.02x vs GEMV arm, 1.90x vs (2)); Q6_K 41.16 ms
(2.10x vs GEMV, 3.20x vs (2)). Effective GB/s on the
weights-read-once basis: Q4_K 22.4, Q6_K 2.65 (the GEMV arms'
raw streamed figures: 710.8 GB/s Q4_K - K1 at its Wave A
class - and 80.7 GB/s Q6_K, the untuned straight port).
Production dispatch as proven: (3) at batch >= 8, (2) below
it. A future tuning note, recorded not actioned: (3) also
won at every smaller batch it was correctness-proven on, so
lowering the tiled threshold is a candidate change for a
later window, not something this lane changed after its
proof window.

## Correctness: per shape, per row count

Fixtures SYNTHETIC (LCG bytes, tamed f16 super-scales, the
Wave A pattern), rows 64, cols 1024 (fixture A) plus Q4_K at
cols 6656 (fixture B, the real accumulation length); batches
1, 6, 64, 256; both structures; metrics are k1_check's
(rel = max_abs_err / max(1, max|ref|), Float64 cosine).
tests/server_proof_gemm.mojo, window 2 log
~/gpu-wave-d1/out2/gemm.log read in the foreground:
80 GEMM_CHECK lines, 0 FAIL.

Gate K (the decisive one: GEMM output vs the GEMV KERNEL's
own output on the same fixture): rel 0.0 and cosine 1.0 for
every shape, structure, and batch in fixtures A and B -
the GEMM kernels are BIT-IDENTICAL to the GEMV kernels per
output row. The GEMM path is exactly as accurate as the
shipped GEMV path, no more, no less.

Gate T (vs the GEMM CPU twins, which are the GEMV CPU twins
per row; k3-class bar rel <= 1e-4, cosine >= 0.999999):
PASS everywhere. The ONLY nonzero gate-T distances in the
whole log are Q4_K fixture B (cols 6656): batch 64 rel
1.4420996624982054e-07 and batch 256 rel
1.2287723982866891e-06, both structures. Every other shape,
fixture, and batch - Q4_K fixture A, Q6_K, Q5_K, F32 - is
rel 0.0 against its CPU twin. See the rejected iteration
below for why fixture B is the interesting case.

VM side: tests/test_gemm_cpu.mojo proves the CPU twins
bit-identical to per-row GEMV twin calls at batches 1/3/6
plus grid arithmetic and named refusals; tests/
test_gpu_prefill_vm.mojo covers the batch layer's shape
validators (including the F16 batch refusal) and row
slice/place. Full tests/run_tests.sh at d7d9bef: PASS,
135 cases across 25 TestSuite files plus the seam-on diag
rerun, config probes, engine hello (0 failed, 0 skipped).

## REJECTED ITERATION, recorded with numbers

Window 1 (staged d7d9bef, log ~/gpu-wave-d1/out/gemm.log)
gated every shape vs the CPU twin at K1's absolute recorded
bar (rel <= 1.267e-07) on the synthetic fixtures and FAILED
on exactly four checks, all Q4_K fixture B (cols 6656):
batch 64 s2 and s3 rel 1.4420996624982054e-07, batch 256
s2 and s3 rel 1.2287723982866891e-06 (cosine 1.0 and
0.9999999999999992). Fixture A (cols 1024) passed at rel
0.0 at every batch, as did Q6_K, Q5_K, and F32; the proof
stopped at GEMM_CORRECTNESS FAIL and no timing section
ran. Verdict after window 2's gate K: the bar, not the
kernels, was wrong for this fixture - K1's 1.267e-07 was
recorded on the REAL fixture tensor whose output scale
(the rel denominator) dwarfs the tamed synthetic fixture's,
and gate K proves the GEMM outputs are bit-identical to
the GEMV kernel's on identical inputs, so the fixture-B
distance is the GEMV family's own kernel-vs-CPU-twin
distance at cols 6656, not a GEMM defect. The proof was
revised to the two-gate form above (commit af77035; the
only diff from d7d9bef is that test file) and window 2
passed all 80 checks with the identical fixture-B figures
under gate T. Whether K1's absolute bar should also be
re-stated for synthetic fixtures generally is David's
call, the same question Wave A left open; this lane did
not move any kernel's bar.

# Mojo engine Wave E: batch-step residency, decode launch
overhead, hygiene debts (wave record)

Date: 2026-11-08. Branch `mojo-max-engine`, engine version
1.6. Base for the wave: Wave D head fa7221e (engine 1.5,
golden PASS, plus the repo-record fix pass). Three lanes
cut from fa7221e, proved on their own trees, integrated
by the coordinator one at a time in the order E3, E1, E2;
the golden gate ran on the final integrated tree
(2f1c091). The per-lane records are
bench/mojo-engine-wave-e1-batch-2026-11-08.md (E1),
bench/mojo-engine-wave-e2-decode-2026-11-08.md (E2), and
bench/mojo-engine-wave-e3-hygiene-2026-11-08.md (E3);
this note is the wave-level summary and the integration
record. Remote main verified at b416987 before and
after, never moved.

## Lane outcomes

### E1, residency + tiled attention in the batch step

The headline fix. Wave D closed with the 1,022-token
prefill INVERTED: the GEMM batch arm (76,579 ms) lost to
the per-row arm (48,415 ms) because the batch step still
crossed activations per op as host rows and ran the
Wave B attention kernel per position, while the per-row
path had gained D4 residency and D2 tiled attention.

- gpu_layer_batch.mojo rewritten: gpu_layer_step_batch_cfg
  keeps activations resident on device across the layer
  (one upload, one download, residual adds on device,
  KV appends device-to-device through a scatter kernel
  driven by the cache's own slot logic), and attention
  is a new batched twin of D2's pair
  (attention_batch_tiled_kernel +
  attention_batch_merge_kernel): one tiled + one merge
  launch per layer for the whole batch, exact logsumexp
  merge, each element's splits partition its own causal
  stored count so causality matches the per-position
  steps exactly. Window-wrap refusals kept by name; a
  CPU twin (attention_batch_causal_cpu) carries the VM
  proofs.
- Per-layer proofs on the lane tree AND re-run on the
  integrated tree in the final window, batch vs per-row
  resident, bar cosine >= 0.999999999 / rel <= 1e-5:
  layer 0 @6 rel 2.49e-07, layer 0 @64 rel 4.76e-07,
  layer 3 @6 rel 1.65e-07, layer 3 @64 rel 3.42e-07,
  stored counts agreeing on both arms. PASS all four,
  digit-identical between the lane tree and the final
  tree.
- Routing, measured on the real model (interleaved
  fresh-model arms): batch loses at 6 tokens (286 vs
  218 ms on the lane tree) and wins at every measured
  length from 16 up (16: 1.53x lane / 1.38x final;
  32: 1.60x / 1.45x; 64: 1.46x / 1.34x; 128: 1.26x /
  1.15x; 256: 1.30x / 1.19x; 512: 1.37x / 1.26x;
  1,022: 1.39x / 1.29x). RULE: per-row below 16 tokens,
  batch at/above 16, as the config knob
  MOJO_ENGINE_PREFILL_BATCH_MIN_TOKENS (field
  prefill_batch_min_tokens, default 16), composed with
  PREFILL_GEMM_MIN_BATCH so the Wave D A/B control
  still forces the per-row arm alone.
- 1,022-token arms on the integrated tree (final
  window): batch 34,852 ms (29.3 tok/s) vs per-row
  45,042 ms (22.7 tok/s), speedup 1.29x, argmax exact.
  Against Wave D: batch arm 76,579 -> 34,852 ms
  (2.20x), per-row arm 48,415 -> 45,042 ms. The
  inversion is gone on the integrated tree, not only
  on the lane tree (lane arms were 34,786 / 48,475).
- Flagged discrepancy (recorded, not hidden): the
  production batch step's Q5_K tiled GEMM launch uses
  block_dim Q6_THREADS (256) while the 44ab4cf-corrected
  GEMM proof uses Q5_THREADS (128). E1's dispatch
  mirrors the production site; Glimmer's per-layer
  slots never exercise the Q5 tiled branch, and every
  measured arm passed bit-exactness and argmax. One of
  the two sites is wrong; settling it needs a Q5 tiled
  run at both block dims (owed, below).

### E2, decode: profile first, then launch overhead

- Profile (window 1, real model, enqueue+sync medians):
  baseline walls step 33,815 us, logits 1,414 us,
  step+logits 35,230 us = 28.38 tok/s steady state
  (step-loop method, context 4096). Isolated ops sum
  to about 1,258 us/layer against a 683.5 us whole-
  layer wall: host launch/alloc time overlaps GPU
  work, and the queue drains only at the KV append's
  sync and the layer-end download. Launch census
  about 76 enqueues/layer (about 3,900/step), 21 of
  them zero-fill launches. The profile pointed at
  launch overhead, not GEMV math.
- Pre-fix (the Wave D defect class, fourth instance):
  the resident _buf dispatch launched the promoted
  F16 GEMV at grid rows (kernel computes 2 rows per
  workgroup: writes up to 2x rows out of bounds) and
  the F32 GEMV at block 128 (kernel reduction spans
  256: half the columns summed). Both latent on
  Glimmer (no layer slot routes F16/F32 through that
  dispatch). Found by grepping every f16/f32 GEMV
  enqueue site; fixed to the hostchain geometry.
- Iteration 1, KEPT: resident-chain outputs take raw
  buffers (_alloc_f32) instead of create_zero_f32;
  every consumer kernel writes every element (audit
  in the docstring). Step 33,815 -> 31,327 us
  (-7.4%).
- Iteration 2, KEPT: splits==1 direct-output tiled
  attention (attention_tiled_direct_kernel): the
  tiled kernel's loop with the final write in the
  same launch, no partial buffers, no merge launch.
  CPU twin proven EXACT (0.0) against the split path
  at splits==1 and <= 1e-5 vs Float64; device proof
  PASS at stored 16/128/512 (rel <= 1.37e-07). Step
  31,327 -> 31,035 us (-0.9%).
- Final lane numbers: step+logits 32,491 us = 30.78
  tok/s steady state (same WALL method; -8.2% step
  alone). The runner approx on the lane tree read
  52.87 ms/step (18.92 tok/s) against Wave D's 51.7
  (19.35); the approx carries a measured one-time
  ~200 ms stall on the first logits after GEMM
  prefill, amortized over 15 steps, so at this delta
  it sits inside window noise; the WALL series is the
  sensitive measure and it moved -7.8%. On the final
  integrated tree the runner approx read 49.13 ms/step
  = 20.35 tok/s (see the golden section).
- Rejected/not attempted, recorded in the lane note:
  rope position-buffer sharing (bounded below
  iteration 2's win); GEMV retuning (K1's bar is
  David's open call, untouched; no gate moved).

### E3, the owed hygiene items

- Budget-ledger unreserve (Wave C debt): GpuRuntime
  was reserve-only; two server proofs reset ledger
  fields directly, naming the missing API. Now: pure
  budget_release (over-release refuses by name, the
  ledger cannot go negative), unreserve_weights /
  unreserve_kv, release_reservation on DeviceWeights
  and DeviceKvCache (exact build totals, double
  release refuses by name), and
  GpuGlimmerModel.release_reservations() as the
  destroy path. Proof: reserve-to-cap, refusal,
  release, identical re-reserve, in the plumbing
  suite (+2 tests). The release path executed on the
  card in the final window via the layer proof.
- Harness verdict-line extraction (Wave C debt):
  wave_c_timing.sh extracted the proof's HEADER line
  as the teacher-forced verdict and could not fail on
  a verdict-less log (reproduced on synthetic logs
  pre-fix). It now accepts only the anchored
  TEACHER_FORCED_GPU <n>/<m> line; 7/8 fails as
  NOT_FULL_PASS; a missing verdict fails loudly,
  exit 1. Self-test tests/wave_c_timing_extract_test.sh
  passes 4/4 and is wired into run_tests.sh.
  wave_d_timing.sh never had the bug.

  the batch path at very long contexts (the route

  not yet separately proven).

===== FILE: bench/mojo-engine-wave-e1-batch-2026-11-08.md =====
# Mojo engine Wave E, Lane E1: residency + tiled attention in the batch step

Date: 2026-11-08. Branch `lane/mojo-e1-batch`, cut from
fa7221e (engine 1.5). Lane commits are listed at the
bottom; the coordinator integrates and pushes.

## The problem (Wave D record)

On the Wave D integrated tree, the 1,022-token prefill
arms INVERTED: the GEMM batch arm took 76,579 ms against
the per-row arm's 48,415 ms, even though the GEMM kernels
beat the GEMV kernels 2.0-2.1x at batch 64 with
bit-identical outputs. The batch step lost end to end
because (a) it launched the Wave B attention kernel per
position instead of D2's tiled split-KV attention, and
(b) it round-tripped activations through host rows per
op instead of keeping them resident like D4's chain.

## What was built

1. `src/model/gpu_layer_batch.mojo` rewritten around
   `gpu_layer_step_batch_cfg` (the Wave D
   `gpu_layer_step_batch` signature is kept as a wrapper
   with the config-default attention knobs):
   - Residency: the input batch uploads once; the
     residual stream, norm outputs, Q/K/V, the gated
     attention output and the MLP intermediates stay in
     device buffers op to op; the residual adds are
     device adds (`residual_add_kernel`); the output
     batch downloads once. GEMM launches take resident
     buffers with the Wave D launch geometry unchanged,
     site for site.
   - KV appends are device to device: a new
     `kv_batch_scatter_kernel` (the offset twin of
     device_kv's `kv_scatter_kernel`, which carries no
     source offset) scatters each batch row from the
     resident K/V batch buffers into its cache slot,
     validated and committed through the cache's own
     `_append_slot` / `_append_commit` - the same calls
     `append_device` makes for one row.
   - Attention: `attention_batch_tiled_kernel` +
     `attention_batch_merge_kernel`, a batched twin of
     D2's tiled split-KV pair living in this file: same
     shared-memory tile staging, same online-softmax
     partials, same exact logsumexp merge. One block per
     (batch element, Q head, split); each element's
     splits partition its OWN causal stored count
     (start + i + 1), so element i sees exactly the rows
     the per-position steps would have seen, even though
     the whole batch is appended before the layer's
     attention launch (the Wave D append order). Split
     count comes from `attn_split_count` at the LAST
     element's stored count; earlier elements' ranges
     shrink by the same chooser arithmetic and trailing
     empty splits merge as no-ops. K/V are read through
     `DeviceKvCache.gather_visible`, like the resident
     step. ONE tiled launch + ONE merge launch per layer
     for the whole batch, against the Wave D batch step's
     `batch` Wave B launches (each with a host sync).
   - Guards kept: a windowed batch that would reach its
     window refuses `gpu_kv_window_wrapped`; attention
     refuses by the same name when the visible rows do
     not start at position 0. The attention knobs are
     validated BEFORE any KV append, so a bad knob
     refuses without mutating the cache.
   - CPU twin for the causal arithmetic:
     `attention_batch_causal_cpu` (per element, D2's
     `attention_split_cpu` over the causal prefix),
     VM-proven in tests/test_wave_e_batch_vm.mojo.
2. Routing knob (config.mojo): 
   `MOJO_ENGINE_PREFILL_BATCH_MIN_TOKENS`, field
   `EngineConfig.prefill_batch_min_tokens`, parser
   `parse_prefill_batch_min_tokens` on the shared
   `_parse_positive` (refusal strings byte-identical in
   shape to the other knobs). The rule lives in the pure
   helper `config.prefill_uses_batch`: the batched route
   serves a prompt only when its length reaches BOTH
   the GEMM minimum batch (so the Wave D A/B control -
   raising the GEMM minimum above any prompt - still
   forces the per-row arm alone) and the new routing
   minimum. Threaded config -> runner
   (generate_main's GPU phases) -> GpuGlimmerModel ->
   prefill(). The model field and constructor parameter
   were APPENDED at the end of the parameter list, and
   every positional construction site was re-grepped
   (see the hazard check below). Default: 16 tokens,
   from the crossover measurement below (batch loses at
   6, wins at 16 and at every larger measured length).
3. Proofs (new files):
   - tests/test_wave_e_batch_vm.mojo (VM): routing rule,
     knob parser/default, causal stored counts, and the
     batch attention CPU twin against per-element split
     twins (exact) and the single-position math core
     (Wave B bar class). NOT wired into run_tests.sh
     (lane rule); listed for the coordinator below.
   - tests/server_proof_wave_e_batch_layer.mojo (card):
     per-layer batch vs per-row resident at rows 6 and
     64, layers 0 and 3, bar cosine >= 0.999999999,
     rel <= 1e-5 (the D2 class).
   - tests/server_proof_wave_e_prefill_route.mojo
     (card): interleaved batch-vs-per-row arms at
     6/16/32/64/128/256/512/1022 tokens, fresh model per
     arm, cross-arm last-hidden at the Wave C/D class
     (cosine >= 0.999999, rel <= 1e-4, argmax exact);
     prints the crossover and the 1,022 arms.
   - tests/wave_e_timing.sh: the window harness
     (staging stamp, builds, the four runs, verdict
     extraction from the on-disk logs in the foreground).

## Trial record

- T1 (VM test, first run): test_wave_e_batch_vm ran 4/5;
  the failure was a bug in MY test case, not the engine:
  the "short stores" refusal case handed the twin a
  store of exactly the required length (a valid shape),
  so no refusal fired. Case corrected to a genuinely
  short store; 5/5 after.
- T2 (proof parse): server_proof_wave_e_batch_layer
  named a variable `ref`, which this Mojo version
  reserves; `mojo format` refused to parse the file.
  Renamed to ref_flat; the file then formatted and
  compiled clean. No other file used the name.
- T3 (evidence hazard, the Wave B/D failure class): the
  first full-suite run's backgrounded delivery text
  reported a compile failure in
  tests/test_gpu_prefill_vm.mojo that does not exist in
  the on-disk log. Foreground rerun of that file passed
  3/3, and the suite log read in the foreground shows
  156/156 PASS (see Results). Every number in this note
  was read in the foreground from an on-disk log, local
  or server, never from a delivery text.
- T4 (no rejected kernel iteration): the batched tiled
  attention + resident batch chain compiled for
  gfx1100 on the first build and passed its per-layer
  gate on the first card run at both batch sizes and
  both layers; there is no rejected device iteration
  to record. The design choices that were settled
  BEFORE building, from the Wave D record: splits are
  chosen at the last element's stored count (per-element
  split counts would need per-element launches and lose
  the one-launch shape); the Q5_K tiled GEMM block dim
  mirrors the production batch site (hazard section).

## Hazard check (Wave D's three geometry/positional burns)

- No kernel signature or geometry in kernels/, attention/
  or gpu_layer.mojo was changed by this lane. The new
  GEMM launch sites in gpu_layer_batch.mojo copy the
  Wave D batch sites' grids and block dims exactly
  (gemm_plain_grid / gemm_tiled_grid / gemm_k1_grid /
  gemm_k1_tiled_grid; K1_THREADS / Q6_THREADS /
  F_THREADS), and the rms_norm / rope / gate / SwiGLU /
  residual launches copy the resident step's geometry.
- One observed discrepancy, recorded not changed: the
  Q5_K TILED GEMM launch in the Wave D batch step uses
  block_dim=Q6_THREADS (256), while the Wave D landing
  fix (44ab4cf) corrected the GEMM PROOF's Q5 tiled site
  to Q5_THREADS (128). The new resident GEMM dispatch
  mirrors the production batch site (Q6_THREADS), not
  the proof, so this lane introduces no unproven
  geometry; no Glimmer per-layer projection slot is
  Q5_K (the census's one Q5_K tensor is the head, which
  the batch step never dispatches), so the branch is
  not exercised by the model. Flagged for the
  coordinator: one of the two sites is wrong and a
  future lane should settle it with a Q5 tiled
  correctness run at both block dims.
- GpuGlimmerModel.__init__ gained ONE parameter,
  appended LAST (prefill_batch_min_tokens). Every
  construction site was grepped after the change:
  gpu_model.open (passes it through as the last
  positional), gpu_model.open_attn (defaults), and both
  generate_main.mojo constructions (the runner threads
  config.prefill_batch_min_tokens as the last argument
  through _gpu_generate_phase / _gpu_prefill_phase /
  _run_gpu). EngineConfig.__init__ likewise gained the
  field last; its load() return passes it last.

# Mojo engine Wave E, Lane E2: decode speed (2026-11-08)

Lane: `lane/mojo-e2-decode`, cut from `fa7221e` (engine
1.5, Wave D integrated tree). Job: profile one decode step
on the real model, attack the largest measured item with
the Wave A/D ladder discipline, close what measurement
honestly supports of the gap to the reference points
(Rust engine plain decode ~34.5 tok/s, llama Vulkan
44.59 tok/s on the same card; Wave D integrated decode
19.35 tok/s by the runner approx, 51.7 ms/step).

All server numbers below are direct foreground reads of
the window log files. Staging was git archives with
STAGED_COMMIT stamps and sha256-verified sources in every
window; the phase lock (`flock -w 14400
/tmp/itak-phase.lock`) was held for every card window.
Server state at window entry, as observed: port 8080
clear (the Glimmer llama-server stayed DOWN per David's
standing order), the cortex-embed payload answering
`{"status":"ok"}` on 8091 with cortex-embed.service
INACTIVE (the Wave D closeout state; the payload's
~1.9 GB footprint left ample room, so nothing was
stopped for these windows and there was nothing to
restore), containers cortex-cortex-1 and
cortex-cortex-surrealdb-1 Up throughout, never touched.

## 1. The profile (window 1, tree fc9f4ae = fa7221e +
##    geometry fix + gated instrumentation + this proof)

Harness: `tests/server_proof_decode_profile.mojo` (new
this lane). Phase WALL times the production
GpuGlimmerModel path with no instrumentation (prompt
stepped at positions 0..5, 3 warmup decode steps, 10
measured free-running steps, context 4096). Phase OPS
times every resident-chain launch shape on layer 0's
real slots, enqueue + synchronize per rep (the D2/D3
pattern), medians over 30-50 reps after warmup. The
in-path cross-check is the MOJO_ENGINE_DEBUG-gated
PROFILE_LAYER / PROFILE_LOGITS wall lines added to
gpu_layer_step_cfg / gpu_logits this lane (off by
default, zero behavior change when off).

### Clean walls (baseline tree)

- Step (52 layers): median 33,815 us. Logits: median
  1,414 us. Step + logits: 35,230 us = 28.38 tok/s
  steady-state engine rate at short context.
- Teacher-forced proof, same window: 8/8, step_ms 33
  (integer print) per step, total_ms 450.
- Runner, same window: GOLDEN_FIRST8_MATCH 1,
  TEXT_STRICT_OK 1, tokens identical to the Wave B/C/D
  record, PREFILL_MS 423, DECODE_STEP_MS_APPROX 55.27
  (18.09 tok/s). Wave D's final tree read 51.7 / 19.35
  in its window. The approx is (generate_ms -
  prefill_ms) / 15; the generate phase carries a
  one-time ~200 ms stall on the first logits after the
  GEMM prefill (visible in the teacher total too:
  450 ms against 7 x 33 ms of steps + 8 x ~1.4 ms of
  logits ~= 245 ms accounted), which the approx
  amortizes over 15 steps. The steady-state per-token
  cost is the WALL figure above; both measures are
  reported for every arm below, the runner approx for
  comparability with the Wave D record.
- PROFILE_LAYER (debug run, same teacher binary):
  steady layers 582-690 us, median ~630 us; sliding
  layers ~615-660 us, global layers ~582-638 us (the
  sliding delta is the rope pair + windowed append
  shape). PROFILE_LOGITS steady 1,358-1,459 us.

### Per-op table (isolated enqueue+sync medians, us)

| op (layer 0 shapes) | us | notes |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| GEMV attn_q Q4_K 4096x6656 | 64.4 | incl zero+alloc |
| GEMV attn_k Q4_K 256x6656 | 33.5 | incl zero+alloc |
| GEMV attn_v Q6_K 256x6656 | 32.9 | incl zero+alloc |
| GEMV attn_gate Q4_K 4096x6656 | 67.5 | incl zero+alloc |
| GEMV attn_output Q4_K 6656x4096 | 59.3 | incl zero+alloc |
| GEMV ffn_gate Q4_K 19968x6656 | 193.9 | incl zero+alloc; see anomaly |
| GEMV ffn_up Q4_K 19968x6656 | 114.2 | incl zero+alloc |
| GEMV ffn_down Q6_K 6656x19968 | 215.0 | incl zero+alloc |
| GEMV head Q5_K 202048x6656 | 1,379.7 | LAUNCH ONLY (925 MB, ~670 GB/s) |
| gpu_logits whole | 1,574.5 | norm+head+final_logit+download |
| rms_norm hidden 6656 | 33.3 | incl zero+alloc |
| rms_norm Q heads (32x128) | 23.8 | incl zero+alloc |
| rms_norm KV heads (2x128) | 23.8 | incl zero+alloc |
| rope Q (32 vec) | 37.6 | incl zero + pos host alloc + copy |
| rope K (2 vec) | 37.5 | incl zero + pos host alloc + copy |
| KV append pair (append_device) | 22.5 | incl its internal synchronize |
| attention resident, stored 16, splits 1 | 38.7 | tiled + merge + 3 partial allocs |
| attention resident, stored 128, splits 1 | 117.3 | same shape, longer scan |
| attn_gate elem 4096 | 22.3 | incl zero+alloc |
| swiglu 19968 | 22.5 | incl zero+alloc |
| residual_add 6656 | 25.2 | incl zero+alloc |
| final_logit 202048 | 27.5 | incl zero+alloc |
| create_zero_f32 (4096/6656/19968/202048) | 20.5 / 20.8 / 21.1 / 23.2 | alloc + zero launch + sync |
| raw enqueue_create_buffer (same sizes) | 16.5 / 16.7 / 16.6 / 19.3 | alloc + sync |
| upload_f32 6656 + sync | 38.0 | per-layer boundary, in |
| download_f32 6656 (incl sync) | 27.4 | per-layer boundary, out |
| bare synchronize, empty queue | 0.35 | sync itself is cheap |
| WHOLE resident layer step, layer 0 | 683.5 | production entry, all-in |
| WHOLE resident layer step, layer 3 | 657.8 | production entry, all-in |

Anomaly, recorded not smoothed: ffn_gate (193.9) and
ffn_up (114.2) are the same dtype and shape; gate was
timed first among the large GEMVs in the proof's order
and shows the lower effective bandwidth. The
reconstruction below leans on the whole-layer
cross-check, not on either figure alone.

### Reconstruction and where the profile pointed

Sum of the isolated per-op medians for one sliding
layer is ~1,258 us, against 683.5 us for the whole
layer measured through the production entry: the
isolated figures overstate every small op, because in
the real chain the host enqueues ahead while the GPU
works - allocator and launch host time overlaps GPU
execution. The queue drains at exactly two points per
layer: append_device's internal synchronize (mid
layer) and the layer-end download. Launch census of
one sliding layer in the baseline tree: 24 compute
kernels (6 norms, 8 GEMVs, 2 rope, 2 KV scatters,
tiled + merge attention, gate, swiglu, 2 residuals)
+ 21 zero-fill kernels + ~27 buffer allocations
(outputs, partials, rope position buffers) + 4 copies
(upload, 2 rope positions, download) ~= 76 enqueues;
per decode step ~= 3,900 enqueues plus the head
chain. GEMV weight streaming is the largest GPU-time
class (the eight layer GEMVs sum to ~781 us isolated;
the head GEMV alone is 1.38 ms launch-only), but the
largest REDUCIBLE item the profile exposes inside
this lane's files is the launch/allocation overhead
riding on every op:

1. 21 zero-fill launches per layer (1,092 per step)
   in front of kernels that write every output
   element - pure overhead, removable inside
   gpu_layer.mojo alone. -> Iteration 1.
2. The merge launch + 3 partial allocations in the
   splits == 1 regime (stored <= 512: all of early
   decode and, at span 512, everything up to 512
   stored), the D2 note's named candidate (a).
   Attention at stored 16 measured 38.7 us through
   the production pair. -> Iteration 2.
3. Structural items OUTSIDE this lane's file
   ownership, recorded for the coordinator: (a) the
   per-layer host boundary - upload + download +
   synchronize x 52 per step - is baked into the
   gpu_layer_step_cfg List-in/List-out signature and
   gpu_model's step loop; a step-level resident chain
   (hidden row stays on device across all 52 layers)
   removes 104 crossings per step; (b)
   DeviceKvCache.append_device's mid-layer
   synchronize caps host lookahead at half a layer -
   a no-sync append variant in device_kv.mojo would
   let the host enqueue the whole step ahead of the
   GPU; (c) buffer allocation itself (~16-19 us
   isolated per enqueue_create_buffer with sync;
   the chain allocates ~27 buffers per layer) - a
   scratch-pool chain needs a stateful design above
   this lane; (d) gpu_model's embedding norm uploads
   a fresh ones row every step.

## 2. Pre-attack fix (commit d9f2fa0): resident F16/F32

f16_gemv_kernel / f32_gemv_kernel site in src+tests
grepped - gpu_layer's _device twins and the kernels'
own standalone mains already correct,
server_proof_gemm corrected at Wave D landing

not these kernels. No behavior change on the Glimmer
path; no gate moved.

# Mojo engine Wave E, Lane E3: hygiene (budget ledger, harness verdict, GLIMMER fold)

Date: 2026-11-08. Lane branch `lane/mojo-e3-hygiene`, based on
fa7221e, engine version 1.5 (unchanged: no item here is a
release feature). Worktree: `~/workspace/lanes/mojo-e3-hygiene`.
One commit per item, not pushed (the coordinator integrates):

- Item 1 (budget-ledger unreserve): 9baa030
- Item 2 (harness verdict-line extraction): aecb9f7
- Item 3 (GLIMMER_* defaults into EngineConfig): da170d8
- This record: a separate docs commit after item 3.

Baseline on the fa7221e tree (coordinator-verified, and
reproduced on this lane before any edit): full VM suite
