## Item 1: budget-ledger unreserve (owed since Wave C)

Before-state, verified on this tree. `GpuRuntime` in
`src/gpu/context.mojo` had `reserve_weights` / `reserve_kv`
(check-then-apply against the cap) and NO release path of
any kind; the Wave C note lists "A budget-ledger
release/unreserve call" under Still owed. The debt was
visible in two proofs, which reset the ledger field
directly because a destroyed cache's reservation otherwise
kept counting against the cap:

- `tests/server_proof_gpu_layer.mojo`: `rt.kv_bytes = 0`,
  with a comment naming the missing unreserve API.
- `tests/server_proof_gpu_residency.mojo`: `rt.kv_bytes = 0`
  twice per round.

What changed:

- `src/gpu/context.mojo`: pure helper
  `budget_release(current, amount, what)` (returns
  current - amount; refuses `gpu_budget_exceeded` by name on
  a negative amount or on releasing more than the bucket
  holds, so the ledger can never go negative), plus
  `GpuRuntime.unreserve_weights` / `unreserve_kv` delegating
  to it one line each, with diag lines in the existing
  `gpu` phase style ("unreserve weights -N total_weights=M").
- `src/gpu/weights.mojo`: `DeviceWeights.release_reservation(rt)`
  returns the exact total `build()` reserved; a
  `reservation_released` flag makes a double release refuse
  by name even if another build reserved in between.
- `src/gpu/device_kv.mojo`: same shape,
  `DeviceKvCache.release_reservation(rt)`.
- `src/model/gpu_model.mojo`:
  `GpuGlimmerModel.release_reservations()` - the
  model/context destroy path: releases KV, then weights,
  on the model's own runtime.
- Both server proofs now call `release_reservation` instead
  of resetting ledger fields; no direct ledger-field writes
  remain outside `context.mojo` itself.

Proof (before/after). The runtime methods need a
DeviceContext, which this device-less VM cannot construct,
so the VM proof drives the ledger state as plain ints
through the SAME pure functions the methods delegate to
(`check_gpu_budget` is the reserve methods' check;
`budget_release` is the unreserve methods' whole
arithmetic) - a clearly argued unit proof, with the
delegation one line each in the source. New tests in
`tests/test_gpu_plumbing.mojo` (an existing, already-wired
suite file):

- `test_budget_release_reserve_cycle`: at cap 1000 /
  scratch 100, reserve weights 800 + KV 50 (total 950);
  a second KV reserve of 100 REFUSES `gpu_budget_exceeded`
  (the before behavior: destroyed structure still counted);
  release both; totals return to the scratch envelope alone;
  the identical reservations then SUCCEED (950 again); a
  partial release frees exactly its amount.
- `test_budget_release_refusal_names`: over-release,
  release from an empty bucket, and a negative amount each
  refuse `gpu_budget_exceeded`; exact and zero releases are
  legal.

Plumbing suite: 9/9 (was 7). The four GPU consumers compile
on the VM with `mojo build --target-accelerator gfx1100`
(the Wave C route): server_proof_gpu_layer,
server_proof_gpu_residency, server_proof_gpu_generate, and
the runner - all exit 0. Untested leg, plainly: the release
path has not EXECUTED on the card (no server window was
expected for this lane, and none was taken); the next
cleared-card window that runs the layer or residency proof
exercises it for real, since both proofs now call it.

Suite after the commit: 158 passed, 0 failed (156 + 2 new).

## Item 2: harness verdict-line extraction (owed since Wave C)

Before-state, reproduced on this tree before editing, with
synthetic logs in /tmp (a teacher log carrying the proof's
header lines, per-step idx lines, and the verdict line;
valid GPU runner logs; a matching staged stamp):

- Good log: the harness exited 0 but reported
  `TEACHER_FORCED_VERDICT_LINE=GPU_GENERATE_PROOF context_len 4096`
  - the header line, exactly the Wave C wart.
- Verdict-less log (verdict line removed): the harness STILL
  exited 0 and reported the same header line. The extraction
  could not fail; that is the real bug behind the wart.

Root cause (as recorded in Wave C): `teacher_verdict_line`
tried a generic `GPU_(GENERATE|PROOF)` shape before the
count shapes, and the header matches that shape.

What changed (`mojo-engine/tests/wave_c_timing.sh`):

- Extraction accepts only the proof's verdict shapes, in
  order: (1) an anchored `^TEACHER_FORCED_GPU <n>/<m>` line
  (the real verdict, e.g. `TEACHER_FORCED_GPU 8/8
  total_ms=...`; anchored so idx= lines and headers can
  never match), (2) a TEACHER line carrying `pass=<n>/<m>`.
  The generic proof shape and the any-line-with-8/8 shape
  are deleted.
- The full-pass gate now also checks the verdict's bare
  `<n>/<m>` count (it previously checked only `pass=`, so a
  7/8 verdict line would have sailed through): a partial
  verdict fails `TEACHER_FORCED_NOT_FULL_PASS`.
- A verdict-less log fails loudly:
  `TEACHER_FORCED_VERDICT_LINE_MISSING`, exit 1.
- Header comment updated with the fix and the lineage note:
  `wave_d_timing.sh` was checked - it greps the exact
  `TEACHER_FORCED_GPU 8/8` string and never had this bug, so
  no change there. For Wave E the coordinator should use
  this fixed wave_c harness (it is the rich-summary one);
  if a `wave_e_timing.sh` is wanted, it should be a copy of
  THIS fixed file, not of the pre-fix shapes.

Proof: new `mojo-engine/tests/wave_c_timing_extract_test.sh`
builds synthetic logs in a temp dir and runs the harness's
`--extract-only` mode over four cases - GOOD (header +
verdict extracts the verdict verbatim), MISSING (fails by
name, nonzero exit), PARTIAL 7/8 (fails
TEACHER_FORCED_NOT_FULL_PASS), PASS_EQ (the `pass=8/8` shape
still extracts). Result: PASS, 4/4 cases. This test file is
NOT wired into `run_tests.sh` (the coordinator wires it if
wanted; `run_tests.sh` itself was not edited).

Suite after the commit: 158 passed, 0 failed, plus the
extract test 4/4 above.

## Item 3: GLIMMER_* defaults into EngineConfig (Wave A open item)

Before-state, verified on this tree by grep over
`mojo-engine/src/` and `tests/` - Wave B/C/D had NOT
partially folded any of it. Exactly 7 constants in 4 ops
files:

| Constant | File | Value | Readers on this tree |
|---|---|---|---|
| GLIMMER_RMS_EPS | src/ops/rms_norm.mojo | Float32 1.0e-5 | tests/test_ops_rms_norm.mojo only |
| GLIMMER_ROPE_BASE | src/ops/rope.mojo | Float32 500000.0 | tests/test_ops_rope.mojo only |
| GLIMMER_HEAD_DIM | src/ops/rope.mojo | 128 | none |
| GLIMMER_LOGIT_SCALE | src/ops/final_logit.mojo | Float32 0.1961161345243454 | tests/test_ops_softmax_logit.mojo only |
| GLIMMER_LOGIT_SOFTCAP | src/ops/final_logit.mojo | Float32 20.0 | tests/test_ops_softmax_logit.mojo only |
| GLIMMER_HIDDEN | src/ops/embedding.mojo | 6656 | none |
| GLIMMER_VOCAB | src/ops/embedding.mojo | 202048 | none |

Key fact about the before-state: the ops never read their
own constants in the math - eps/base/scale/cap/hidden are
function parameters - and production code reads none of the
seven. For a loaded model, the values in effect come from
the GGUF file through `ModelConfig`
(`src/model/model.mojo`: rms_eps, rope_base / rope_base_swa,
logit_scale, logit_softcap, hidden, head_dim, vocab). The
GLIMMER_* constants served only callers/tests naming the
recorded model without a file in hand.

What changed:

- `src/config.mojo`: the defaults live ONLY here now, in a
  clearly delimited "BEGIN/END Wave E Lane E3 block" grouping
  (defaults block, parsers block, struct fields, init params,
  load() section, each marked) so the merge with lane E1's
  config addition stays mechanical:
  `DEFAULT_RMS_EPS`, `DEFAULT_ROPE_BASE`,
  `DEFAULT_LOGIT_SCALE`, `DEFAULT_LOGIT_SOFTCAP`,
  `DEFAULT_HEAD_DIM`, `DEFAULT_HIDDEN`, `DEFAULT_VOCAB`
  (values byte-for-byte the old constants);
  EngineConfig fields `rms_eps`, `rope_base`, `logit_scale`,
  `logit_softcap`, `head_dim`, `hidden`, `vocab`;
  env overrides `MOJO_ENGINE_RMS_EPS`, `MOJO_ENGINE_ROPE_BASE`,
  `MOJO_ENGINE_LOGIT_SCALE`, `MOJO_ENGINE_LOGIT_SOFTCAP`,
  `MOJO_ENGINE_HEAD_DIM`, `MOJO_ENGINE_HIDDEN`,
  `MOJO_ENGINE_VOCAB`, following the existing pattern
  (getenv in load() only, parsers split out and testable).
  Named refusals are `mojo_engine_config` naming the env
  var, in the existing style; float validation mirrors the
  ops' own rules (eps > 0, rope base > 1, softcap >= 0 with
  0 = no cap, logit scale any finite value; NaN and the
  infinities PARSE as floats in Mojo, so `_parse_float`
  refuses them explicitly).
- The 7 constants are deleted from `src/ops/`
  (rms_norm, rope, final_logit, embedding); each module's
  header now points at the config home. `grep GLIMMER_` over
  the Mojo sources finds only historical comments.
- The three consuming tests now import the defaults from
  `config` (`DEFAULT_RMS_EPS`, `DEFAULT_ROPE_BASE`,
  `DEFAULT_LOGIT_SCALE` / `DEFAULT_LOGIT_SOFTCAP`).
- `tests/config_probe.mojo` prints the seven new fields, so
  the process-level probe shows them.

Deliberately NOT done, per the item's own stop rule (this
item is structure, not tuning): loaded-model execution was
NOT rewired to EngineConfig. The GGUF file stays the source
for a loaded model's values, exactly as before, so no
numeric behavior anywhere changes; the precedence is stated
in the config block header. Nothing was left half-folded:
all 7 constants moved.

Proof:

- `tests/test_config.mojo`: +3 tests -
  `test_glimmer_op_defaults_are_the_recorded_ones` (the
  defaults and a clean-env load() against the recorded
  literals), `test_parse_glimmer_op_knobs_accept` (incl.
  `1e-5` scientific form and softcap 0), and
  `test_parse_glimmer_op_knobs_refuse_by_name` (15 bad-value
  cases, each asserting the refusal names both
  `mojo_engine_config` and its env var). Config suite 11/11

# Mojo engine Wave F1-A: residency, no-sync KV append,
# scratch pooling, RoPE sharing (integration + card window)

Date: 2026-11-09. Branch `mojo-max-engine`, engine version
1.07. The F1-A lane (lane/mojo-f1a, four commits over base
e08546b0b) was integrated onto the branch head 202eca870
(engine 1.07 + test bench + gap audit note + no-nightly
note) one feature per push, full suite after each landing,
then measured in one combined card window against the
pre-F1-A tree (202eca870) staged side by side. Remote main
verified at b416987a736b0a63c9f7815ec4b4fbc84e4dd2dd
before and after, never moved.

## The four items (Wave E owed list)

1. Step-level activation residency: the decode step's
   hidden row stays on device from the embedding to the
   logits download (before: upload + download + sync at
   every one of the 52 layer boundaries, plus a separate
   upload into the head). step() is now the resident step
   plus the one hidden-row download; generate_device runs
   the resident seam end to end.
2. No-sync KV append: DeviceKvCache.append_device no
   longer ends in rt.ctx.synchronize(); the sync capped
   host lookahead at half a layer.
3. Scratch-arena pooling: a GpuScratch pool on the
   runtime interns device buffers by (dtype, length);
   the resident chain draws its scratch from the pool
   instead of allocating per call.
4. Shared RoPE position buffers: the step's RoPE position
   buffers are built once on the runtime and shared
   across layers (a fixed 2,048-position table; positions
   at or beyond it refuse by name, gpu_rope_position_cap).

| 2: item 2 (no-sync KV append) | 633430c | 0038a310459127d2a1e820aa7401f2f3960616c1 | 200 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped |

  to parse when f takes list arguments by value; the

===== FILE: bench/mojo-kernel-test-2026-11-07.md =====
# Mojo kernel test: K1 Q4_K GEMV ported to Mojo and raced (2026-11-07)

## Verdict, against the pre-set rule

**NOT READY for a second kernel on this card today.** The pre-set
rule (written before the race, not moved): Mojo is ready only if
its correctness sits inside the shipped K1's tolerance (cosine
1.000000000 to the harness's printed precision, max rel err no
worse than 10x the shipped record's 1.267e-7, i.e. 1.267e-6)
AND its interleaved median speed is within 10 percent of the
wgpu arm's interleaved median in the same window, or beats it.

- Correctness leg: **PASS, with margin.** Mojo vs the CPU
  reference: cosine 1.000000000, rel 8.941e-08 (tighter than the
  shipped kernel's own 1.267e-7). Mojo vs wgpu directly: cosine
  1.000000000, rel 1.788e-07. Identical across all three reps.
- Speed leg: **FAIL, by a wide margin.** Interleaved medians:
  wgpu 838.4 GB/s, Mojo 39.8 GB/s. The within-10-percent bar was
  754.6 GB/s; Mojo reached 4.7 percent of the wgpu median. The
  wgpu arm was 21.1x faster.

Feasibility itself passed cleanly: a Mojo toolchain with MAX GPU
support exists today, it lists this card as a supported target,
and a checked Mojo GPU kernel ran on the RX 7900 XTX with an
exact result. What failed is not aim; it is speed of a first,
straightforward port against a hand-tuned kernel.

## Step 1: feasibility (the cheap gate)

Toolchain state found: no `mojo`, `max`, `pixi`, or `modular`
binary on this VM or on ubuntu-server. Prior research on file
(~/workspace/research_notes/mojo-critic-2026-10-28/REPORT.md):
Mojo 1.2.0 (2026-10-22), deps via pixi, channels
`https://conda.modular.com/max` plus conda-forge.

Modular's current hardware compatibility page lists RDNA3
`gfx1100` (Radeon RX 7900) as a supported arch target for Mojo
GPU programming, via the AMD HIP path (`libamdhip64.so`, AMD
driver 6.3.3 or later). The server carries
`/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libamdhip64.so.7` system-wide.

Install, self-contained on the server under `~/mojo-probe/`
(nothing in the repo tree): pixi 0.84.1 with
`PIXI_HOME=~/mojo-probe/pixi` (the pixi installer appended its
PATH line to the server's `~/.bashrc`, its standard behavior),
project `~/mojo-probe/probe` resolving **Mojo 1.2.0 (2016d0cd)**
and **MAX 26.7** from the Modular channel; environment size
1.4 GB.

Probe: a throwaway Mojo vector add over 1,000,003 elements
(odd size, bounds-checked on the host afterward) under the
phase lock, tenants up (a probe is not a measurement; 24 GB
card, probe footprint is megabytes). Result:

```
PROBE: DeviceContext created
PROBE_RESULT mismatches = 0 of 1000003
```

Outcome (a): it runs on the card and the result checks out.
Footnote: the probe process printed `Warning: Resource leak
detected by SharedSignalPool, 77 Signals leaked.` on exit, a
runtime housekeeping warning with no effect on the result.

## Step 2: the port

`bench/mojo/k1_gemv.mojo` (this lane): a standalone Mojo program
running the same Q4_K GEMV math as the shipped K1 (the r2sg
shape's math, ported from the repo's own sources, not from
memory: `gguf::dequant::dequant_q4_k` and `scale_min_k4` for the
super-block dequant, the same 144-byte super-block layout, low
nibbles first then high). Workgroup shape is the port's own
choice: one 256-thread block per output row, each thread summing
26 strided columns, shared-memory tree reduction. Exact f16 to
f32 conversion (normals and subnormals both exact).

Fixture, from the repo's own harness so the comparison uses the
SAME data and the SAME bars: `k1_check`'s tensor
`blk.0.ffn_gate.weight` ([6656 x 19968], 74,760,192 bytes), its
seed-42 LCG input, and its CPU reference path (gguf dequantizer
plus torch-math matvec). A new bench example,
`crates/wgpu-compute/examples/k1_fixture_dump.rs`, writes the
raw Q4_K bytes, the input, the CPU reference output, and the
wgpu output into a fixture directory, printing k1_check's own
comparison line as provenance. No library code was touched and
no shipped crate depends on Mojo.

Debug law, from birth: `MOJO_KERNEL_DEBUG` (any value other
than 0/empty) enables named `[k1_gemv_mojo][phase]` log lines;
bad usage, bad shapes, and fixture size mismatches produce
named `REFUSAL k1_gemv_mojo: ...` lines and exit code 2.
Tooling: `mojo format` run on the final source (it reformatted;
the formatted file was rebuilt and re-proven against the
fixture), final `mojo build` warning-free. `compare.py`
(this lane) scores outputs with k1_check's exact definitions.
The runner is `bench/mojo/run_k1_race.sh` (arm selection via
`K1_BENCH=wgpu|mojo|both`).

## Step 3: the race

One cleared-card session on ubuntu-server, phase lock held,
tenants stopped (cortex-embed.service, cortex-cortex-chat-1,
cortex-cortex-embed-1) and restored after. VRAM: 1,680,437,248
bytes in use at lock acquisition (as observed), **33,271,808
after the clear (the exact drained figure)**, **8,932,147,200
after restore (the exact standing figure)**, embed service
active and both containers healthy at closeout. Production
Glimmer never started, port 8080 untouched, no reboot.

Correctness first, as observed:

| comparison | max rel err | cosine |
|---|---|---|
| wgpu vs CPU ref (fixture dump) | 1.267e-07 | 1.000000000 |
| wgpu vs CPU ref (k1_check anchor) | 1.267e-07 | 1.000000000 |
| Mojo vs CPU ref | 8.941e-08 | 1.000000000 |
| Mojo vs wgpu (direct) | 1.788e-07 | 1.000000000 |

The wgpu arm reproduces the shipped 2026-10-30 record
(1.267e-7, cosine 1.000000000) exactly on this fixture.

Speed, interleaved in one window, 200 iterations plus 20
warmup per rep, each iteration streaming the same 74,760,192
bytes (one resident tensor both arms; the wgpu arm is
`k1_bench --budget-mib 72`, whose greedy pack under that budget
is exactly one 74,760,192-byte tensor):

| rep | wgpu GB/s | Mojo GB/s |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 864.0 | 39.78 |
| 2 | 838.4 | 40.14 |
| 3 | 831.3 | 39.77 |
| median | **838.4** | **39.8** |

Compile and startup costs, stated separately and excluded from
both timed loops (both loops run after warmup with data already
resident): Mojo clean-rebuild wall 1.10 s (`pixi run mojo
build`, compiled binary about 0.16 MB); the Rust bench examples
built once in 38.83 s for all three. Per-process startup
(DeviceContext creation, fixture upload) sits in the untimed
correctness section of each Mojo run, as does pipeline setup on
the wgpu side.

## Why the gap, and what a follow-up costs

Labeled analysis, not measurement: the port recomputes the f16
decode and the scale unpack for every element, loads weights
one byte at a time, and reduces through shared memory; the
shipped r2sg kernel's speed comes from packed scale extraction,
shared activation quads, subgroup butterfly reduction, and
2-rows-per-workgroup streaming. Nothing in this run shows MAX
cannot express those shapes; it shows a first port does not get
them for free. Closing a 21x gap is a tuning project, not a
tweak: mirror the r2sg structure inside the Mojo kernel
(vectorized loads, hoisted per-group dequant, subgroup
reduction), re-prove correctness, re-race. Realistic cost is
days of kernel work for K1 alone, with no guarantee the gap
closes inside the 10 percent bar; the cheap decision point is
one tuned attempt on K1 before any talk of a second kernel.

## Files and state

- Lane bench code: `bench/mojo/k1_gemv.mojo`,
  `bench/mojo/run_k1_race.sh`, `bench/mojo/compare.py`,
  `crates/wgpu-compute/examples/k1_fixture_dump.rs`
  (rustfmt clean, `cargo check` clean on the VM, release build
  clean on the server; the formatted example re-ran the fixture
  dump and reproduced the PASS line exactly).
- Server scratch, kept out of the repo: toolchain and probe
  project in `~/mojo-probe/`, staging tree and fixture in
  `~/gpu-mojo-test/` (session log `~/mojo-probe/race-session.log`).
- Nothing merged, nothing pushed, no engine flag, no default
  changed.

===== FILE: bench/mojo/compare.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compare K1 fixture outputs with the harness's own metrics.

Bench tooling for the Mojo kernel test (see
bench/mojo-kernel-test-2026-11-07.md). Definitions match
crates/wgpu-compute/examples/k1_check.rs exactly:

  rel    = max_abs_err / max(1.0, scale), scale = max |reference|
  cosine = dot(a, b) / (|a| * |b|), accumulated in float64

Usage:
  compare.py FIXTURE_DIR [MOJO_OUT ...]

With no MOJO_OUT arguments, compares gpu_f32.bin and
mojo_out_f32.bin in FIXTURE_DIR against ref_f32.bin, plus the
direct mojo-vs-gpu pair. Extra arguments are treated as
additional candidate files compared against ref_f32.bin and
gpu_f32.bin.
"""

import math
import struct
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def load_f32(path: Path) -> list[float]:
    data = path.read_bytes()
    if len(data) % 4 != 0:
        raise SystemExit(f"{path}: {len(data)} bytes is not a whole f32 count")
    return list(struct.unpack(f"<{len(data) // 4}f", data))


def compare(name_a: str, a: list[float], name_b: str, b: list[float]) -> None:
    if len(a) != len(b):
        raise SystemExit(f"{name_a} has {len(a)} values, {name_b} has {len(b)}")
    max_abs = 0.0
    scale = 0.0
    dot = 0.0
    norm_a = 0.0
    norm_b = 0.0
    for x, y in zip(a, b):
        max_abs = max(max_abs, abs(x - y))
        scale = max(scale, abs(y))
        dot += x * y
        norm_a += x * x
        norm_b += y * y
    cosine = dot / (math.sqrt(norm_a) * math.sqrt(norm_b))
    rel = max_abs / max(1.0, scale)
    print(
        f"{name_a} vs {name_b}: outputs {len(a)}: "
        f"max_abs_err {max_abs:.6f} at output scale {scale:.3f} "
        f"(rel {rel:.3e}), cosine {cosine:.9f}"
    )


def main() -> int:
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print(__doc__)
        return 2
    fixture = Path(sys.argv[1])
    ref = load_f32(fixture / "ref_f32.bin")
    gpu = load_f32(fixture / "gpu_f32.bin")
    compare("gpu", gpu, "ref", ref)
    candidates = sys.argv[2:] or [str(fixture / "mojo_out_f32.bin")]
    for cand in candidates:
        values = load_f32(Path(cand))
        label = Path(cand).name.removesuffix(".bin")
        compare(label, values, "ref", ref)
        compare(label, values, "gpu", gpu)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

===== END FILE: bench/mojo/compare.py =====

===== FILE: bench/mojo/k1_gemv.mojo =====
# K1 Q4_K GEMV port in Mojo (bench code for the Mojo kernel test;
# see bench/mojo-kernel-test-2026-11-07.md). NOT part of the
# shipped engine: a standalone bench program that runs the same
# Q4_K GEMV math as crates/wgpu-compute's K1 kernel (the r2sg
# shape's math: ggml Q4_K super-block dequant plus a dot product
# per output row) on the fixture k1_fixture_dump writes.
#
# Debug law: structured log lines behind MOJO_KERNEL_DEBUG (any
# value other than "0"/empty enables), every line named
# [k1_gemv_mojo][phase]; every bad input shape gets a named
# REFUSAL line and exit code 2.
#
# Usage:
#   k1_gemv <fixture_dir> [--rows N] [--cols N] [--iters N]
#           [--warmup N] [--out PATH]
# Defaults: rows 19968, cols 6656 (the fixture tensor's shape),
# iters 0 (correctness only), warmup 3, out <fixture_dir>/mojo_out_f32.bin.
# With --iters N > 0 the process additionally runs a timed loop
# of N launches after warmup and prints a MOJO_TIMING line whose
# GB/s counts the same streamed weight bytes the wgpu k1_bench
# counts (rows * row_bytes * iters / elapsed).

from std.os import getenv
from std.time import perf_counter_ns
from std.sys import argv, exit
from max.gpu import thread_idx, block_idx, block_dim, barrier
from max.gpu.host import DeviceContext
from max.gpu.memory import AddressSpace
from std.memory import stack_allocation

comptime THREADS = 256
comptime SB_ELEMS = 256
comptime SB_BYTES = 144


def log_debug(phase: String, msg: String):
    var flag = getenv("MOJO_KERNEL_DEBUG")
    if flag != "" and flag != "0":
        print("[k1_gemv_mojo][", phase, "] ", msg, sep="")


def refuse(what: String, detail: String) -> None:
    print("REFUSAL k1_gemv_mojo: ", what, ": ", detail, sep="")
    exit(2)


def f16_to_f32(bits: UInt16) -> Float32:
    # Exact f16 -> f32: normals via (1 + frac/1024) * 2^(exp-15)
    # (both factors exact in f32, power-of-two scaling exact);
    # subnormals via frac * 2^-24 (exact); zero signed.
    var sign: Float32 = -1.0 if (bits >> 15) & 1 == 1 else 1.0
    var exp = Int((bits >> 10) & 0x1F)
    var frac = Int(bits & 0x3FF)
    if exp == 0:
        return sign * Float32(frac) * 5.9604644775390625e-08
    if exp == 31:
        # Weights never carry inf/NaN; refuse silently wrong math
        # by returning a NaN the comparison will catch.
        return Float32(0.0) / Float32(0.0)
    var v = Float32(1.0) + Float32(frac) / Float32(1024.0)
    var e = exp - 15
    var scale = Float32(1.0)
    if e >= 0:
        for _ in range(e):
            scale *= Float32(2.0)
    else:
        for _ in range(-e):
            scale /= Float32(2.0)
    return sign * v * scale


def scale_min_k4(
    j: Int, w: Pointer[UInt8, MutAnyOrigin], sb_off: Int
) -> Tuple[Float32, Float32]:
    # Mirrors gguf::dequant::scale_min_k4 over the 12 scale bytes
    # at sb_off + 4: returns (scale, min) as plain counts.
    if j < 4:
        var sc = Int(w[unsafe_offset=sb_off + 4 + j]) & 63
        var m = Int(w[unsafe_offset=sb_off + 8 + j]) & 63
        return (Float32(sc), Float32(m))
    else:
        var hi = Int(w[unsafe_offset=sb_off + 4 + (j + 4)])
        var sc = (hi & 0xF) | (
            (Int(w[unsafe_offset=sb_off + 4 + (j - 4)]) >> 6) << 4
        )
        var m = (hi >> 4) | ((Int(w[unsafe_offset=sb_off + 4 + j]) >> 6) << 4)
        return (Float32(sc), Float32(m))


def k1_gemv_kernel(
    w: Pointer[UInt8, MutAnyOrigin],
    x: Pointer[Float32, MutAnyOrigin],
    y: Pointer[Float32, MutAnyOrigin],
    cols: Int32,
):
    var row = Int(block_idx.x)
    var tid = Int(thread_idx.x)
    var row_bytes = (Int(cols) // SB_ELEMS) * SB_BYTES
    var base = row * row_bytes
    var shared = stack_allocation[
        THREADS, Float32, address_space=AddressSpace.SHARED
    ]()
    var acc = Float32(0.0)
    var steps = Int(cols) // THREADS
    for k in range(steps):
        var col = tid + k * THREADS
        var sb = col >> 8
        var within = col & 255
        var sb_off = base + sb * SB_BYTES
        var d_bits = UInt16(w[unsafe_offset=sb_off]) | (
            UInt16(w[unsafe_offset=sb_off + 1]) << 8
        )
        var dm_bits = UInt16(w[unsafe_offset=sb_off + 2]) | (
            UInt16(w[unsafe_offset=sb_off + 3]) << 8
        )
        var d = f16_to_f32(d_bits)
        var dmin = f16_to_f32(dm_bits)
        var g = within >> 6
        var p = within & 63
        var sc: Float32
        var m: Float32
        var q: Float32
        if p < 32:
            var sm = scale_min_k4(2 * g, w, sb_off)
            sc = sm[0]
            m = sm[1]
            q = Float32(Int(w[unsafe_offset=sb_off + 16 + g * 32 + p]) & 0xF)
        else:
            var sm = scale_min_k4(2 * g + 1, w, sb_off)
            sc = sm[0]
            m = sm[1]
            q = Float32(
                Int(w[unsafe_offset=sb_off + 16 + g * 32 + (p - 32)]) >> 4
            )
        var val = d * sc * q - dmin * m
        acc += val * x[unsafe_offset=col]
    shared[unsafe_offset=tid] = acc
    barrier()
    var stride = THREADS // 2
    while stride > 0:
        if tid < stride:
            shared[unsafe_offset=tid] = (
                shared[unsafe_offset=tid] + shared[unsafe_offset=tid + stride]
            )
        barrier()
        stride //= 2
    if tid == 0:
        y[unsafe_offset=row] = shared[unsafe_offset=0]


def read_file_exact(path: String, expected: Int) raises -> List[UInt8]:
    with open(path, "r") as f:
        var data = f.read_bytes(expected + 1)
        if len(data) != expected:
            print(
                "REFUSAL k1_gemv_mojo: fixture size mismatch: ",
                path,
                " has ",
                len(data),
                " readable bytes, expected ",
                expected,
                sep="",
            )
            exit(2)
        return data^


def arg_value(args: List[String], flag: String, default: String) -> String:
    for i in range(len(args) - 1):
        if args[i] == flag:
            return args[i + 1]
    return default


def main() raises:
    var args = List[String]()
    for a in argv():
        args.append(String(a))
    if len(args) < 2:
        refuse(
            "usage",
            (
                "k1_gemv <fixture_dir> [--rows N] [--cols N] [--iters N]"
                " [--warmup N] [--out PATH]"
            ),
        )
    var fixture_dir = args[1]
    var rows = Int(arg_value(args, "--rows", "19968"))
    var cols = Int(arg_value(args, "--cols", "6656"))
    var iters = Int(arg_value(args, "--iters", "0"))
    var warmup = Int(arg_value(args, "--warmup", "3"))
    var out_path = arg_value(args, "--out", fixture_dir + "/mojo_out_f32.bin")
    if cols % SB_ELEMS != 0:
        refuse(
            "bad shape",
            "cols must be a multiple of 256 (Q4_K super-block), got "
            + String(cols),
        )
    if cols % THREADS != 0:
        refuse(
            "bad shape",
            "cols must be a multiple of the 256-thread block, got "
            + String(cols),
        )
    var row_bytes = (cols // SB_ELEMS) * SB_BYTES
    var weights_bytes = rows * row_bytes
    log_debug("load", "fixture dir " + fixture_dir)
    var w_host = read_file_exact(
        fixture_dir + "/weights_q4k.bin", weights_bytes
    )
    var x_host = read_file_exact(fixture_dir + "/input_f32.bin", cols * 4)
    log_debug(
        "load",
        "weights "
        + String(weights_bytes)
        + " bytes, input "
        + String(cols)
        + " f32",
    )

    var ctx = DeviceContext()
    log_debug("device", "DeviceContext created")
    var w_dev = ctx.enqueue_create_buffer[DType.uint8](weights_bytes)
    var x_dev = ctx.enqueue_create_buffer[DType.float32](cols)
    var o_dev = ctx.enqueue_create_buffer[DType.float32](rows)
    var w_src = ctx.enqueue_create_host_buffer[DType.uint8](weights_bytes)
    var x_src = ctx.enqueue_create_host_buffer[DType.float32](cols)
    for i in range(weights_bytes):
        w_src[i] = w_host[i]
    for i in range(cols):
        var p = x_host.unsafe_ptr().unsafe_bitcast[Float32]()
        x_src[i] = p[unsafe_offset=i]
    ctx.enqueue_copy(src_buf=w_src, dst_buf=w_dev)
    ctx.enqueue_copy(src_buf=x_src, dst_buf=x_dev)
    log_debug("device", "fixture uploaded")

    ctx.enqueue_function[k1_gemv_kernel](
        w_dev, x_dev, o_dev, Int32(cols), grid_dim=rows, block_dim=THREADS
    )
    ctx.synchronize()
    log_debug("run", "correctness launch done")

    var o_host = ctx.enqueue_create_host_buffer[DType.float32](rows)
    ctx.enqueue_copy(src_buf=o_dev, dst_buf=o_host)
    ctx.synchronize()
    var out_bytes = List[UInt8](capacity=rows * 4)
    out_bytes.resize(rows * 4, UInt8(0))
    var op = out_bytes.unsafe_ptr().unsafe_bitcast[Float32]()
    for i in range(rows):
        op[unsafe_offset=i] = o_host[i]
    with open(out_path, "w") as f:
        f.write_bytes(out_bytes)
    print("MOJO_OUT wrote", out_path, rows, "f32")

    if iters > 0:
        for _ in range(warmup):
            ctx.enqueue_function[k1_gemv_kernel](
                w_dev,
                x_dev,
                o_dev,
                Int32(cols),
                grid_dim=rows,
                block_dim=THREADS,
            )
        ctx.synchronize()
        var t0 = perf_counter_ns()
        for _ in range(iters):
            ctx.enqueue_function[k1_gemv_kernel](
                w_dev,
                x_dev,
                o_dev,
                Int32(cols),
                grid_dim=rows,
                block_dim=THREADS,
            )
        ctx.synchronize()
        var elapsed = Float64(perf_counter_ns() - t0) / 1.0e9
        var streamed = Float64(weights_bytes) * Float64(iters)
        var gbs = streamed / elapsed / 1.0e9
        print(
            "MOJO_TIMING iters",
            iters,
            "(+" + String(warmup) + " warmup):",
            Int(streamed),
            "bytes in",
            elapsed,
            "s =",
            gbs,
            "GB/s",
        )
        log_debug("timing", "loop done")

===== END FILE: bench/mojo/k1_gemv.mojo =====

===== FILE: bench/mojo/run_k1_race.sh =====
#!/bin/bash
# Interleaved K1 race driver (bench tooling for the Mojo kernel
# test; see bench/mojo-kernel-test-2026-11-07.md). Runs on the
# server: holds the phase lock, clears the card tenants, proves
# VRAM drained, then alternates the wgpu and Mojo arms.
#   K1_BENCH=wgpu|mojo|both   arm selection (default both)
#   REPS=N ITERS=N WARMUP=N   shape of the race (defaults 3/200/20)
set -u
ARM="${K1_BENCH:-both}"
REPS="${REPS:-3}"
ITERS="${ITERS:-200}"
WARMUP="${WARMUP:-20}"
STAGE="$HOME/gpu-mojo-test"
FIX="$STAGE/fixture"
BIN="$STAGE/target/release/examples"
export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$HOME/mojo-probe/pixi/bin:$PATH"
export PIXI_HOME="$HOME/mojo-probe/pixi"
export PIXI_NO_TELEMETRY=1

exec 9>/tmp/itak-phase.lock
echo "race: waiting for phase lock"
flock -w 14400 9
echo "race: phase lock held"

vram_used() { cat /sys/class/drm/card*/device/mem_info_vram_used 2>/dev/null | head -1; }

echo "race: VRAM before clear: $(vram_used)"
echo "race: stopping tenants (cortex-embed.service, cortex-cortex-chat-1, cortex-cortex-embed-1)"
systemctl --user stop cortex-embed.service
docker stop cortex-cortex-chat-1 cortex-cortex-embed-1 > /dev/null
sleep 5
echo "race: VRAM after clear: $(vram_used)"

restore() {
  echo "race: restoring tenants"
  docker start cortex-cortex-chat-1 cortex-cortex-embed-1 > /dev/null
  systemctl --user start cortex-embed.service
  sleep 10
  echo "race: VRAM after restore: $(vram_used)"
  systemctl --user is-active cortex-embed.service
  docker ps --format '{{.Names}} {{.Status}}' | grep -E 'cortex-cortex-(chat|embed)-1'
}
trap restore EXIT

echo "=== fixture dump (wgpu correctness vs CPU reference) ==="
"$BIN/k1_fixture_dump" --out "$FIX"
echo "=== k1_check anchor (official harness) ==="
"$BIN/k1_check"

echo "=== mojo correctness run ==="
( cd ~/mojo-probe/probe && MOJO_KERNEL_DEBUG=1 ./k1_gemv "$FIX" --iters 0 )

echo "=== mojo compile timing (clean rebuild) ==="
( cd ~/mojo-probe/probe && rm -f k1_gemv && /usr/bin/time -f "mojo build wall: %e s" pixi run mojo build k1_gemv.mojo -o k1_gemv 2>&1 | tail -2 )

echo "=== interleaved race: REPS=$REPS ITERS=$ITERS WARMUP=$WARMUP ARM=$ARM ==="
for rep in $(seq 1 "$REPS"); do
  if [ "$ARM" = "both" ] || [ "$ARM" = "wgpu" ]; then
    echo "--- rep $rep wgpu ---"
    "$BIN/k1_bench" --budget-mib 72 --iters "$ITERS" --warmup "$WARMUP" | grep -E "resident set|iters|verdict" 
  fi
  if [ "$ARM" = "both" ] || [ "$ARM" = "mojo" ]; then
    echo "--- rep $rep mojo ---"
    ( cd ~/mojo-probe/probe && ./k1_gemv "$FIX" --iters "$ITERS" --warmup "$WARMUP" --out "$FIX/mojo_out_rep$rep.bin" | grep -E "MOJO_TIMING|MOJO_OUT|REFUSAL" )
  fi
done
echo "race: done"

===== END FILE: bench/mojo/run_k1_race.sh =====

===== FILE: bench/ngram-gpu-runner-2026-11-07.md =====
# N-gram GPU runner wiring, 2026-11-07

Lane `lane/ngram-gpu-runner`, based on main `0ecdc8ff` with
the n-gram lane cherry-picked on top (originals `4e86e5ad`
code and `76aa1265` note on `lane/ngram-spec`; landed here as
`78fa7d7` and `ebc5b98`). Question: can the GPU runner
`spec_generate_gpu` run the n-gram arm the CPU runner already
runs, so the resident stack gets a real-file n-gram
measurement? Answer: yes, it is a flag, exactly as the n-gram
note predicted; this lane wires it and pins the construction
path. No card run here (VM only); the protocol below is what
the card session now executes.

## What was wired

One file changed in the runner, `crates/itak-spec/examples/
spec_generate_gpu.rs`:

- New flag `--drafter=<dflash|ngram>`, spelled and parsed
  exactly as the CPU runner's: `SpecMode::parse` (the shared
  parser the n-gram lane added as `DraftBackend::parse`'s
  twin; no second parser exists), admitted values exactly
  `dflash` and `ngram`, default `dflash`. The GPU runner's
  pre-existing `--draft=<gpu|cpu>` (the DFlash device path)
  is a different flag and is untouched; `--drafter=...` does
  not match its prefix scan and vice versa.
- Refusal before any model load: `--drafter` with an unknown
  value, or with a value that parses but is not a runner
  draft source (`off`, `medusa`), prints `FAIL: --drafter
  must be dflash or ngram, got ...` and exits 2, before the
  target or draft file is touched. Proven on the built binary
  on this VM: `--drafter=bogus` and `--drafter=off` both exit
  2 with that line and no load attempt.
- N-gram mode never opens the draft file. Following the CPU
  runner's precedent exactly: the positional draft path is
  still required by the usage line (pass any placeholder),
  its contents are ignored, and the run says so out loud:
  `drafter: ngram prompt-lookup (draft file <path> not
  loaded; --draft and --kv-capacity configure the dflash arm
  only)`. Proven on this VM: with a nonexistent placeholder
  in the draft slot and a nonexistent target, the n-gram arm
  prints that line and fails at the TARGET open; the dflash
  arm in the same setup fails at the DRAFT open. No stricter
  rule was invented for the draft-path argument.
- `--draft` and `--kv-capacity` in n-gram mode: still parsed
  and validated by name (an unknown `--draft` value refuses
  as before), and not used; the line above states that they
  configure the dflash arm only, so nothing is silently
  ignored.
- Phase B construction: in n-gram mode the runner builds
  `NgramProposer::new(NgramConfig::default(), vocab)` and
  the session through `SpecSession::new_ngram` over
  `ResidentTarget::new(resident_session)` — the same
  resident session, backend, and leak discipline as the
  DFlash arm — with `SpecConfig { mode: Ngram, depth,
  eos_tokens, .. }`. No `DflashSpeculator`, no draft session,
  no draft weights in that arm. The prefill line distinguishes
  the arm the CPU runner's way: `spec prefill (resident,
  plain + proposer commit)` versus the DFlash arm's unchanged
  `spec prefill (resident, capturing)`.
- Everything downstream is the shared code: the same
  `generate`, the same `spec stats: rounds= proposed=
  accepted= acceptance_rate= ... tokens_per_round=` line,
  the same resident counters, the same effective / all-in
  rate lines, and the same IDENTITY, GOLDEN, SPEED, and
  T-9.6 verdict block, so a card run in n-gram mode is
  directly comparable to the DFlash arms line for line. The
  exit code still follows correctness only (identity and
  golden); the SPEED line prints either way against the same
  88.6 tok/s default bar.

## Tests

The GPU runner had no argument tests of its own, so per the
lane terms the parse-level coverage went beside
`SpecMode::parse`'s round-trip test instead of into a new
harness: `config::tests::runner_drafter_vocabulary_accepts_
only_dflash_and_ngram` pins the parse half of the runners'
guard (admits `dflash` / `ngram`; refuses `off`, `medusa`,
`gpu`, `cpu`, the empty string, and case variants).

The construction path is pinned by a new integration test,
`crates/itak-spec/tests/ngram_gpu_runner.rs`: it builds the
wgpu-compute resident suite's synthetic model (hidden 512,
vocab 1024, six layers), constructs a `ResidentSession`,
attaches a default-config proposer, and builds the session
through `new_ngram` over `ResidentTarget`, then runs
`begin` and an 8-token generation and asserts the stream and
the round accounting (`accepted <= proposed`, rounds >= 1).
No draft file, speculator, or draft config exists anywhere
in the test. It follows the suite's adapterless skip pattern
(`WgpuCompute::new` returning `NoSuitableAdapter` prints the
reason and returns); on this VM it took that path, verified
with `--nocapture`: `skipping n-gram GPU runner construction
test: no suitable adapter (enumerated: [])`. Its live-backend
assertions therefore remain card-owed, like every GPU test
authored on this VM.

## Gates (this lane)

- `cargo test -p itak-spec`: 69 lib tests passed (68 from the
  cherry-picked lane plus the new parse test), 1 integration
  test passed (adapterless skip path), 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p dflash`: 24 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p wgpu-compute`: 277 passed, 1 ignored,
  0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p itak-spec --all-targets -- -D warnings`:
  clean (one `if_same_then_else` in the new test's fixture
  builder was caught by this gate and fixed by merging the
  K/V and gate/up branches, the resident fixture's own form).
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- `cargo check --workspace`: clean.
- `cargo check -p itak-spec --example spec_generate_gpu`:
  clean; the refusal and not-loaded behavior was additionally
  exercised on the built debug binary (see above).

## The card protocol now runnable

Server, card free, release build, every run wrapped in
`bench/failure-bundle.sh` per the standing convention (the
SPEED line will trip its FAIL marker on the n-gram prose
arms; that is the target line, not a leg verdict — IDENTITY
and GOLDEN inside the log are the leg verdicts, as in the
baseline session's bundles). Paths: target
`/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf`,
DFlash draft
`/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/dflash-Muse-Glimmer-30B-Q4_K_M.gguf`.

Build: `cargo build --release -p itak-spec --example
spec_generate_gpu --example spec_generate` (plus
`spec_generate` for the CPU arm).

1. N-gram GPU arms, default prompt, `both` mode, 64 tokens,
   at depths 1 and 6:
   `spec_generate_gpu <target> unused.gguf 64 <depth> "The
   capital of France is" both <stream-file> --drafter=ngram`
   Record: IDENTITY, GOLDEN, the spec stats line (rounds /
   proposed / accepted / acceptance_rate / tokens_per_round),
   spec rates (effective and all-in), spec resident counters,
   and phase walls. Compare arm to arm against the standing
   DFlash GPU numbers at the same depths (wave18 retest,
   diag timing: depth 1 effective 22.07 tok/s, depth 6
   effective 16.80 tok/s, both identity-passing).
2. N-gram GPU arm on a repetitive prompt (a repeated
   instruction block as the prompt text, same token count
   and depths): this is the arm the fixture record says the
   proposer exists for; acceptance and effective rate against
   arm 1's prose numbers is the contrast that matters.
   IDENTITY still must pass (the plain phase A stream is
   generated in the same run); GOLDEN prints only for the
   default prompt.
3. DFlash control arms at the same depths if the session
   wants same-day, same-card comparisons rather than the
   wave18 record: `--draft=gpu` (the runner default) with
   the real draft path and no `--drafter` flag.
4. CPU-driver real-file acceptance (the n-gram note's owed
   item 1, independent of the card):
   `spec_generate <target> <any-placeholder> 64 <depth> "The
   capital of France is" both <stream-file> --drafter=ngram`
   at depths 6 and 1. Minutes-to-hours class; it measures
   acceptance on the real tokenizer's stream, which neither
   fixture could.

## Honest expectation

From the n-gram lane's fixture record
(`bench/ngram-spec-2026-11-07.md`): on a recorded repetitive
stream the proposer accepted everything proposed (rate
1.0000, 4.23 stream tokens per round at depth 6); on prose
it proposed almost nothing and accepted nothing (1.008
tokens/round, the bonus-token floor — plain speed, never
worse). The fixture target sessions read lower (repetitive
0.45 at depth 1 falling to 0.17 at depth 6 by rate, with the
accepted COUNT nearly flat in depth; prose 0.29 at depth 1,
0.07 at depth 6) because a random-weight model's stream is
not text. Expect the real file to land between those records
and to split by content: chat boilerplate, code, lists, and
quoted or templated passages should accept heavily; novel
prose should sit near the floor, where the n-gram arm's win
over DFlash is only the draft forward it never pays (about
40.6 ms per round in the round-economics record) minus its
own wider verify. Whether that trade nets out on the real
chat/code mix is exactly the open measurement arms 1 and 2
take; nothing in this lane's fixtures settles it.

Files: `crates/itak-spec/examples/spec_generate_gpu.rs`
(`--drafter` wiring), `crates/itak-spec/src/config.rs`
(parse-guard test), `crates/itak-spec/tests/ngram_gpu_
runner.rs` (new; resident construction test and fixture).

===== END FILE: bench/ngram-gpu-runner-2026-11-07.md =====

===== FILE: bench/ngram-spec-2026-11-07.md =====
# N-gram self-speculation for itak-spec, 2026-11-07

Lane `lane/ngram-spec`, based on main `0ecdc8ff`. Question: can
the speculative loop draft from the sequence itself, with no
draft model and no training, and what does acceptance look like
where that can be measured on this VM?

## Why

`bench/spec-round-economics-2026-11-06.md` measured the DFlash
draft block forward at about 40.6 ms per round, about 47% of a
depth-1 round, and the drafter is a separate model that must be
loaded, conditioned, and kept in sync. Prompt-lookup (n-gram)
drafting proposes tokens from the sequence itself: find the most
recent prior occurrence of the last N tokens and propose the
tokens that followed it. It costs microseconds on CPU, needs no
training and no second model. The loop's verifier
(`SpecSession::speculative_round` over the target driver)
already guarantees token-identical output for ANY proposer, so
the only question is the acceptance rate.

## Design

New module `crates/itak-spec/src/ngram.rs`:

- `NgramProposer` implements the crate's `Speculator` trait and
  carries an inherent `propose_block(pending, n, arm, rng)` with
  `DflashSpeculator::propose_block`'s exact shape, so the session
  dispatches to either source through one form.
- State is one `Vec<u32>`: the committed token history, appended
  by `commit` under the trait's contract (after a commit, the
  proposer's state equals having processed exactly the committed
  sequence). At propose time the searched sequence is
  `history + [pending]`, indexed virtually; a long history is
  never copied per proposal.
- Lookup: for match length L from the configured maximum down
  to the configured minimum, take the sequence's L-token suffix
  and scan occurrence starts from most recent backwards; the
  first hit returns its continuation, capped by the ask and by
  what actually follows the occurrence. Ranking: longest match
  wins; among occurrences of that match, most recent wins
  (recency is the standard prompt-lookup choice and makes the
  scan a first-hit search). No hit at any length returns an
  empty proposal, and the round degrades to a plain step's
  worth of progress, never a wrong token.
- Sampled arm: distributions are one-hot rows at the proposed
  tokens. That is exact, not an approximation: drawing from a
  one-hot yields its token with probability 1, and
  `sampler::correct_sampled` divides the target row by the
  one-hot and rejects into the normalized residual `(p - q)+`,
  so the emitted distribution is the target's. The greedy arm
  carries no distributions, like the DFlash greedy arm.
- Pure CPU: no GPU or model types. The only geometry the
  proposer knows is the target's vocabulary width, which the
  one-hot rows are built at (the same reason `DflashConfig`
  carries `vocab_size`); session creation validates it against
  the target and refuses mismatches by name.

All limits are `NgramConfig` fields with defaults (build law;
nothing compiled in):

| field | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `max_match_len` | 8 | longest suffix tried first |
| `min_match_len` | 2 | shortest suffix allowed to propose |
| `max_proposals` | 16 | per-proposal cap; the proposer's `max_depth` |
| `search_window_tokens` | 65,536 | how far back an occurrence start may sit (0 = whole history) |
| `max_history_tokens` | 1,048,576 | retained committed history, oldest dropped first (0 = unbounded) |

## The seam change

The trait was not the problem; the session was. `SpecSession`
held `Option<DflashSpeculator>` concretely and called
DFlash-only inherent methods, so a second proposer could not be
attached at all. Smallest change that admits one, all inside
`session.rs`:

- A private `DraftSource` enum (`Dflash(DflashSpeculator)` /
  `Ngram(NgramProposer)`) with four delegating methods
  (`max_depth`, `propose_block`, `note_captures`, `commit`). The
  round loop is otherwise untouched.
- `SpecSession::new` keeps its exact signature and behavior; it
  wraps its draft in the enum and delegates to a shared
  `new_inner`. New constructor `SpecSession::new_ngram(driver,
  Option<NgramProposer>, config, diag)` is the n-gram door.
  Validation: n-gram mode requires the proposer (else
  `DraftNotLoaded`), checks vocabulary agreement
  (`DraftTargetMismatch`), depth in `1..=max_proposals`
  (`DepthOutOfRange`, block size reported as max + 1), and
  `depth + 1 <= max_round_tokens` (`RoundBoundTooSmall`). A
  proposer under mode `dflash` refuses with a named
  `SessionState` mismatch. Capture layers stay empty on the
  n-gram arm: there is nothing to condition.
- One refusal changed in a corner: `SpecSession::new` with mode
  `ngram` and NO draft attached previously returned
  `ModeUnavailable` (mode checked before draft presence); it
  now returns `DraftNotLoaded`, which is the accurate refusal.
  With a DFlash draft attached it still returns
  `ModeUnavailable`, and the existing test
  (`creation_refusals_are_named`) passes unchanged.
- `begin()` gains an n-gram arm: plain `forward(prompt)` (no
  capturing forward exists for this source), then
  `proposer.commit(prompt)`, seeding the lookup history with
  exactly the prompt. DFlash's begin path is byte-identical.

Selection follows the crate's config-first style:
`SpecConfig.mode = SpecMode::Ngram` plus the matching
constructor. `SpecMode::parse` was added as `DraftBackend::parse`'s
twin, and the CPU runner `spec_generate` gained a
`--drafter=<dflash|ngram>` named flag in the GPU runner's
`--draft` style: with `ngram` it never opens the draft file and
runs phase B through `new_ngram`, so the same IDENTITY and
GOLDEN verdicts measure this arm on the real file. The GPU
runner is not wired: the proposer is driver-agnostic and
`new_ngram` works over `ResidentTarget` unchanged, so that
wiring is a flag, not a design question (follow-up below).

## Measured fixture acceptance

Three harnesses, three different claims. All greedy numbers are
under a hard identity assertion (stream equals plain greedy).

**1. Fixture target sessions** (synthetic Glimmer target,
vocab 128, random weights; `ngram::tests::fixture_acceptance_measurement`,
96 generated tokens per row):

| fixture | depth | rounds | proposed | accepted | rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| repetitive prompt | 1 | 85 | 22 | 10 | 0.4545 |
| repetitive prompt | 4 | 82 | 68 | 13 | 0.1912 |
| repetitive prompt | 6 | 81 | 84 | 14 | 0.1667 |
| prose prompt | 1 | 91 | 14 | 4 | 0.2857 |
| prose prompt | 4 | 91 | 46 | 4 | 0.0870 |
| prose prompt | 6 | 91 | 60 | 4 | 0.0667 |

Reading: accepted count is nearly flat in depth (10/13/14
repetitive, 4/4/4 prose) while proposals grow, so on this
stream extra depth mostly buys rejected tokens. Caveat, stated
plainly: the fixture target's greedy stream is a random-weight
model's stream, not text. These numbers prove the mechanism
end-to-end in the loop (and identity), not real-text
acceptance.

**2. Recorded-stream lockstep** (`examples/ngram_acceptance.rs`:
the session's greedy accounting replayed at the proposer level
over word-tokenized text; prompt 24 tokens):

| stream | depth | proposed | accepted | rate | stream tokens/round |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| repetitive template (354 tokens) | 6 | 252 | 252 | 1.0000 | 4.231 |
| prose (143 tokens) | 6 | 6 | 0 | 0.0000 | 1.008 |
| repetitive template | 1 | 147 | 147 | 1.0000 | 1.803 |
| prose | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0.0000 | 1.008 |

Word-level tokenization overstates repetition versus the real
model's subword stream (function words repeat as whole tokens),
so read the rates as directional; the gap is the finding. On
repetitive text the proposer is essentially free throughput
(4.23 tokens per verify round at depth 6); on prose it
proposes almost nothing and the session runs at plain speed
(1.008 tokens/round is the bonus-token floor), never worse.

**3. Stub driver** (`driver::tests::stub_driver_carries_ngram_with_greedy_identity`):
the deterministic successor stream is eventually periodic, so
once an orbit pair repeats, 2-gram continuations are exact.
The test asserts identity over 300 tokens with proposed > 0
and accepted > 0 through the full session/driver seam.

## Honest limits

- Acceptance collapses on non-repetitive text. That is the
  nature of the method, not a defect to tune away: on novel
  prose the proposer is silent and the win is zero (never
  negative; the verifier sees to that). This complements
  DFlash, it does not replace it: DFlash proposes from a
  learned model and accepts on text the lookup has never seen;
  n-gram is free exactly where text repeats itself (code,
  logs, templated and structured output, lists, repeated
  instructions, quoted passages).
- Depth economics differ from DFlash: proposals cost
  microseconds, so depth costs only verify width, but the
  fixture rows show acceptance saturating early. Depth stays
  configuration; the real file decides its operating point.
- The lookup is a naive backward scan, linear in the searched
  window per length tried. At session-scale histories that is
  microseconds; a hash index over suffixes is future work if a
  profile ever names the scan.
- The sampled arm materializes one-hot rows at full vocabulary
  width (at the real vocab and depth 16, about 13 MB per round
  of zeros with depth ones). It is the trait contract's shape
  and the DFlash shim pays the same on its cold path; the
  greedy arm carries no distributions.

## Owed: the real-file measurement

Not run by this lane (VM-only, and the CPU runner is
minutes-to-hours class on the real file):

1. CPU target driver: `spec_generate <glimmer.gguf> <any> 64 6
   "The capital of France is" both plain_stream.txt
   --drafter=ngram` for IDENTITY + GOLDEN plus acceptance from
   the printed spec stats, and the same at depth 1; then a
   repetitive prompt (a repeated instruction block) where the
   proposer should shine.
2. GPU resident driver: wire `--drafter=ngram` into
   `spec_generate_gpu` (a flag over `new_ngram`, no design
   work) and measure acceptance AND round wall at depths 1 and
   6 against the DFlash arms' 22.07 / 16.80 tok/s. The
   interesting question is whether free proposals at prose
   acceptance rates beat a 40.6 ms draft forward at DFlash
   rates, and on repetitive output it should not be close.

# Overnight baseline agreement run: our CPU stack vs llama.cpp on the real Glimmer file (2026-11-05)

TODO T-9.3 / T-9.4 baseline: a fresh, fully recorded agreement
run between our stack and llama.cpp on the real Glimmer file at
temperature 0, token agreement and probability agreement on a
fixed prompt set, including the open residue from the T-9.3
record (our first-token top-1 probability 0.4035 vs llama.cpp
0.3962 on the golden prompt, first measured 2026-10-29 in
crates/itak-loader/INTEGRATION-RUN-B.md and repeated on the GPU
at 0.403462 in bench/gpu-proof-2026-10-30.md).

## Verdict

**Full token agreement, and the probability residue reproduces
at exactly its recorded size without growing.** All five
prompts: prompt token ids identical between the engines, and
all 16 greedy tokens identical, 80 of 80 positions, no first
divergence anywhere. The golden prompt's first-token top-1
probability is again ours 0.4035 vs llama.cpp 0.3962 (delta
+0.0072), digit for digit the October values. Across the set
the first-token delta is prompt-dependent in sign (+0.0072,
+0.0049, -0.0016, +0.0002, -0.0005), and per-position top-1
deltas over all 80 shared positions stay within +/-0.0291
with mixed signs and no growth with position. That is the
signature of f32 accumulation-order noise between two correct
implementations, not a structural logit-path difference. No
engine code was changed by this task; this is measurement only.

## Setup

- Branch `lane/overnight-baseline` from main
  bda7ff55ea57f4a764afddf9ba2e050c59b86916. The branch adds
  bench harness files only; every engine crate is byte-identical
  to main. Harness as staged and run: commit
  1605ffcfd1a10c65712be36eadbfa41b065d0d1f. (A compare-phase
  fix, aa7c926, landed after the run; see Incidents. It touches
  no engine code and none of the recorded raw outputs.)
- Server: ubuntu-server, kernel 7.0.0-42-generic, 123 GB RAM
  (69 used / 54 available at start). Staging tree
  `~/overnight-baseline`, rsynced from the worktree; staged file
  hashes verified before the run (MANIFEST.txt, 192 files, 0
  mismatches). Run executed under the phase lock
  (`flock -w 14400 /tmp/itak-phase.lock`), after the sibling
  overnight lanes ahead of it in the lock queue finished.
- Model: `/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf`
  (16,756,683,904 bytes), coverage 731/731 in our loader.
- Reference: llama.cpp `version: 0.7.0-dev (build 137, commit
  a7af149)`, `~/llama.cpp/build-vulkan2/bin/llama-server`,
  CPU only (`-ngl 0`), `-c 512`, `-t 8`, loopback port 18923,
  started for this run and killed at the end of its phase.
  Production Glimmer stayed down throughout; ports 8080,
  8091, 8092 were never touched.
- Ours: `target/release/examples/glimmer_generate` (the

- Protocol, both sides: temperature 0, 16 generated tokens.

## The residue, stated plainly (T-9.3)

- On the golden prompt it **reproduces exactly**: 0.4035 vs
  0.3962, the same four-decimal values recorded on 2026-10-29
  (CPU) and 2026-10-30 (GPU, 0.403462 at six decimals). It has
  not grown and not shrunk in a week of engine changes; the
  value is a stable property of the two implementations'
  arithmetic on this prompt.
- It is **prompt-dependent**: first-token deltas across the
  set are +0.0072, +0.0049, -0.0016, +0.0002, -0.0005. The sign
  flips; there is no constant offset a correction could
  subtract.
- It does **not accumulate**: over 16 positions the deltas
  wander within +/-0.0291 with no trend, and greedy token
  agreement is perfect everywhere, including the two prompts
  whose distributions stay near-saturated for long stretches.
- Reading: this is the expected distance between our f32
  reference math (f64 softmax over finished logits) and
  llama.cpp's kernel accumulation order. T-9.3's proof bar
  (logit comparison against the reference on a fixed prompt
  matches within tolerance at temperature 0) is met on the
  golden prompt inside the historically recorded 0.015 band
  for the first 8 positions; the honest wider statement is
  +/-0.03 per-position top-1 probability noise across this
  set, with exact token agreement.

## Incidents and recoveries

- First launch (staged bfcd09f) failed before any measurement:
  the non-interactive server shell has no cargo on PATH
  ("cargo: command not found"). Fixed in the runner (1605ffc)
  by exporting ~/.cargo/bin; re-staged, hashes re-verified,
  relaunched. No data was produced by the failed attempt.
- The run then waited in the phase-lock queue behind the
  sibling overnight-golden and overnight-logitscale lanes, per
  protocol; environment stamp 2026-11-05T04:40:57Z is when this
  lane's script took the lock.
- The staged driver's compare phase crashed at the very end
  with KeyError 'prob': this llama.cpp build's /completion
  returns logprob-shaped probabilities, which the llama phase
  tolerated (it reads only ids) but the compare code did not.
  All per-prompt raw JSONs and engine logs were already saved,
  so nothing was lost. The fix (shape-tolerant prob reading)
  and a standalone recompute tool landed as aa7c926, and
  compare.json was recomputed from the saved outputs with the
  recorded results above. The engine runs themselves were not
  repeated and did not need to be.
- Total our-side wall time for the five prompts: 13,943 s
  (about 3.9 h). The CPU reference path remains minutes-class
  per token by design; this run measures agreement, not speed.

## Final server state

- The throwaway llama-server was terminated at the end of its
  phase; port 18923 confirmed down afterwards, and no
  Glimmer llama-server process remains.
- Production Glimmer was never started. The Qwen3-Embedding

NEW generator golden/gen_first_token_probs.py (same throwaway

all 15 prompts of set 1.0. First attempt failed with
KeyError 'probs': this llama.cpp build reports per-step
alternatives under the key "top_probs", each entry
{"id", "token", "bytes", "prob"} (tools/server/server-task.cpp,
completion_token_output::to_json in the server's own source tree;
confirmed by a live probe whose step keys were
[bytes, id, prob, token, top_probs]). The generator was fixed to
that shape, restaged with hash verification, and rerun.
STATUS (updated 2026-11-05): the first landed run was DEGENERATE
and was refused at verification. It requested
post_sampling_probs=true at temperature 0, so the greedy sampling
chain collapsed every distribution to a one-hot: each record's
top5 held exactly 1 entry and every top-1 probability was exactly
1.0 (that output is preserved on the server as
~/overnight-golden/out/glimmer.top5.degenerate.jsonl). Model
sha256, build a7af149, record count (15), and the top-1 tokens
were all correct; only the probability semantics were wrong.
Fix: the generator now requests PRE-sampling (logit)
probabilities, post_sampling_probs=false. Field name and
semantics were confirmed in the server's own source before the
change (tools/server/server-task.cpp,
completion_token_output::to_json and probs_vector_to_json;
tools/server/server-context.cpp, populate_token_probs and the
need_pre_sample_logits gate): with the flag false this build
answers "top_logprobs", log-probabilities taken from the raw
logit distribution via get_token_probabilities, and the generator
converts them back with exp() so the fixture keeps plain
probabilities and its original schema. A hard validation guard
(validate_records in the generator) now runs before any write:
unless every record holds exactly N_PROBS top entries and the
top-1 probabilities are not all exactly 1.0, the run raises and
writes no fixture, so this failure mode can never file silently
again. The fixed generator is commit 7dcf01c on this lane
(sha256 f6bdbd0b8aa8...), restaged with hash verification, and
rerun under the phase lock; the waiter queued at 08:46Z acquired
the lock in the final minute of its 4 h window and the fixture
landed at 2026-11-05T12:46Z. LANDED FIXTURE:
golden/fixtures/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.top5.jsonl
(sha256 0e36c10d8178...), metadata verified: model sha256
4cc57c0f51040a22..., build 0.7.0-dev (137, a7af149), flags
post_sampling_probs=false, 15 records, exactly 5 entries per
top5, every sampled token equal to its record's top-1, top-5
probability sums all below 1. factual_capital top-1 is id 13796
(" Paris") at 0.396216, against 0.3962 from the baseline
agreement run (diff 1.6e-05, inside the n_probs reporting-path
tolerance); runner-ups are " a" 0.096076, " the" 0.051315,
" one" 0.046183, " known" 0.032286. Everything else in this note
is final.

===== FILE: bench/overnight-logit-scale-2026-11-05.md =====
# Overnight experiment: forcing Glimmer's logit scale to 1.0

Run 2026-11-05 (server, CPU forward only). Experiment, not a fix:
shipped defaults are unchanged. Branch `lane/overnight-logitscale`,
hook commit `5dbaaadab8922fd1752f59f9d71440c46bf94a2b` on top of main
`bda7ff55ea57f4a764afddf9ba2e050c59b86916`.

## Question

TODO T-9.3's residue: on the golden prompt our first-token top-1
probability is 0.4035 against llama.cpp's 0.3962 (gap 0.0073), with
identical tokens. The finish in `crates/muse-glimmer` applies
`logit_scale` (file value 0.19611613) FIRST, then softcap
`20.0 * tanh(z / 20.0)`. This experiment forces the scale to 1.0
(5.0990 times the file value), order and cap unchanged, and measures
exactly what moves: could a scale mishandling produce a
probability-only residue of that size, and does forcing 1.0 move our
number toward or away from llama.cpp's 0.3962?

## Method

- Hook: example-only env override `ITAK_EXPERIMENT_LOGIT_SCALE` in
  `crates/itak-loader/examples/glimmer_generate.rs`. When set to a
  positive finite number it replaces `cfg.logit_scale` after
  `load_config`; unset, the file value is used untouched. No library
  code reads it. Unit tests cover unset / set / invalid values.
  Gates: `cargo test -p itak-loader` green, clippy clean, fmt clean.
- Harness: the same example's CPU path (`cpu-compute`), release
  build, real GGUF
  `/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf`,
  staged at `~/overnight-logitscale` on the server (example sha256
  verified against the worktree:
  `f59903d01b0007ecc2d460a36de6c8a654bfbc40b2fa1bfd0d6be1aa878321ca`).
  Runs executed under the shared phase lock; raw logs are in
  `bench/overnight-logit-scale-logs/` and on the server in
  `~/overnight-logitscale/results/`.
- Arms per prompt: baseline (env unset, file scale 0.19611613) and
  forced (`ITAK_EXPERIMENT_LOGIT_SCALE=1.0`), softcap 20.0 in both.
  Recorded per prompt: first-token top-5 (id, token, finished logit,
  probability), a stats line (finished range; pre-softcap range
  recovered by inverting the softcap; implied raw lm_head range;
  count of logits saturated to the cap; count of the top 100
  finished logits beyond `0.9 * cap` = 18.0), and 16 greedy tokens.
- Prompts: golden `factual_capital` "The capital of France is"
  (ids [200000, 954, 7963, 323, 11698, 373]), "The capital of Japan
  is" (6 ids), "The chemical symbol for water is"
  (ids [200000, 954, 12332, 9985, 393, 3427, 373]).
- Note on the recovery math: the pre-softcap range is computed as
  `cap * atanh(finished / cap)` over entries that did not saturate.
  For near-cap entries this inversion is ill-conditioned; the forced
  arm's recovered maximum carries visible error (see golden: forced
  recovery says 135.0004 against the baseline arm's raw maximum
  134.7835 for the identical body output). Minima agree to 1e-3.
  Treat recovered near-cap maxima as approximate.

## Results: golden prompt "The capital of France is"

First-token top-5. llama.cpp reference (INTEGRATION-RUN-B):

  thousand tokens share the head mass almost equally.

  step 4 (id 373): baseline top-1 prob 0.856342, forced 0.003043;
  step 2 (id 26): 0.481786 against 0.002340.

## Analysis: the residue question, answered explicitly

1. **Could a scale error produce a probability-only residue with
   identical tokens? Yes, in principle, and by construction.** Both
   finish steps (multiply by a positive scale, then
   `cap * tanh(z / cap)`) are strictly increasing functions of each
   logit. Any error confined to the finish (wrong scale, wrong cap,
   swapped order, different precision) remaps every probability and
   can never change an argmax or a ranking, at any position, ever.
   The T-9.3 residue's shape (identical tokens, top-1 prob off by
   0.0073) is exactly the fingerprint of a finishing-stage
   difference. It is not the fingerprint of a body-numerics error,
   which would eventually flip some argmax somewhere. This run
   demonstrates the extreme case empirically: a 5.0990x scale error
   left all 16 greedy tokens and every top-5 ranking untouched on
   the golden prompt while moving the top-1 probability by 0.4025.

2. **Does forcing 1.0 move our number toward llama.cpp's 0.3962?
   No. It moves away, catastrophically, and overshoots.** Forced
   top-1 is 0.000968 against llama.cpp's 0.3962: the forced move is
   -0.4025, about 55 times the 0.0073 residue, in the downward
   direction. So the residue is NOT "the scale is effectively 1.0"
   or any error of that size. Whatever separates us from llama.cpp
   at the finish is percent-level at most.

3. **Why the effect reverses sign: the softcap.** In the unsaturated
   regime a larger scale sharpens softmax (top-1 prob rises). But
   Glimmer's raw logits are huge (range about [-80, +135] on the
   golden prompt): at scale 1.0 the leaders land at tanh arguments
   of 5 to 6.7, where tanh is flat, so the cap crushes their
   differences to under 0.0025 of logit and the head mass smears
   across roughly a thousand near-tied tokens. p1(scale) is
   therefore non-monotone: it rises in the mild regime and collapses
   in the saturated regime. A 0.0073 residue in the upward direction
   (ours is HIGHER than llama.cpp's) is consistent with a slightly
   LARGER effective scale in the mild regime (for example a
   precision difference in how the scale multiply is evaluated),
   but the 5.1x endpoint cannot be linearly extrapolated to size
   it; a dedicated small-perturbation sweep (for example scale
   factors 0.95x to 1.05x of the file value) is the instrument for
   that, and this experiment deliberately did not change the ship
   default to find out.

4. **What the scale is actually doing at the file value.** At
   0.19611613 the scale pulls the raw range [-80, +135] down to
   [-15.8, +26.4] before the cap, so the softcap operates mostly in
   its gentle region (only the top few logits pass tanh argument
   1.0) and the distribution keeps a decisive head (top-1 0.40).
   The scale is the thing that makes the softcap a soft cap instead
   of a wall: at 1.0 the cap becomes a wall and the model's
   preferences among its top thousand tokens are effectively
   erased.

## Run record

- Baseline golden: prefill 1,497,849 ms (6 tokens), 16 tokens in
  2,211 s, rc=0. Forced golden: prefill 1,464,484 ms, 2,186 s, rc=0.
- Baseline japan: prefill 1,468,680 ms, 2,191 s, rc=0. Forced japan
  (n=1): prefill 1,447,180 ms, 1,470 s, rc=0.
- Baseline water: prefill 1,656,259 ms (7 tokens), 2,384 s, rc=0.
  Baseline 16 greedy tokens: [465, 30, 59, 26, 2473, 2406, 290,
  220, 30, 310, 465, 30, 59, 3641, 1044, 45]. Forced water (n=1):
  prefill 1,651,736 ms, rc=0.
- Top-up runs (forced japan n=16, forced water n=16) were queued
  after the core matrix in the same session to confirm greedy
  identity empirically on the remaining two prompts; their logs
  land in `~/overnight-logitscale/results/` on the server. The core
  verdict does not depend on them: greedy identity is proven
  mathematically for any monotone finish and was confirmed in full
  on the golden prompt.
- Server session: build 36 s (warm staging cache), runs serialized
  under `/tmp/itak-phase.lock` behind the other overnight lanes;
  the queue wait (about 8 h across three queued sessions) is
  recorded here because it dominated the lane's wall clock.
- Production Glimmer was never started; ports 8080, 8091, 8092 were
  never touched.

===== FILE: bench/overnight-q2k-q3k-dequant-2026-11-05.md =====
# Q2_K / Q3_K dequantizers: port and cross-check against ggml (2026-11-05)

Branch `lane/overnight-q2q3` (from main `bda7ff5`). Verdict up front:
**both dequantizers are bit-exact against ggml's reference
implementation on every vector tried: 223,744 values, 0 diffs.**

## What landed

- `crates/gguf/src/dequant.rs`: `dequant_q2_k` and `dequant_q3_k`
  (plus `unpack_scales_q3_k`), ported operation-for-operation from
  ggml, wired into `dequantize`. Unit tests pin the Q3_K scale
  unpacking against a hand-computed vector, the Q2_K plane/chunk/
  sub-block walk, the Q3_K mask sign rule (set bit: value stands;
  clear bit: subtract 4), the second chunk's mask bits 4..8, and the
  scale extremes. Mutation-checked: flipping the Q3_K mask rule fails
  3 tests, swapping the Q2_K min nibble fails 1 test.
- `crates/gguf/src/ggml.rs`: `GgmlType::Q2K` (id 10) and
  `GgmlType::Q3K` (id 11), `from_id`, block size 256, block bytes
  84 / 110. The audit-era pin asserting id 11 must stay unsupported
  was replaced deliberately (comment in the test) with pins asserting
  support; Q8_1 (id 9) remains the pinned unsupported type.
- Supported-set text updated everywhere it is user-visible:
  `error.rs` (the `UnsupportedTensorType` message), `lib.rs`,
  `file.rs` (`load_f32` docs), `ggml.rs` header, and the `probe`
  example gained `q2_k` / `q3_k` arms.
- `crates/gguf/tests/synthetic.rs`: the unsupported-types fixture
  swapped Q3_K for Q4_0 (id 2, still unsupported) with a comment
  recording why, and a new `q2_k_and_q3_k_tensors_load` integration
  test loads both types end to end through `GgufFile`.
- Cross-check tooling committed under `bench/q2q3-xcheck/`
  (`harness.c`, `gen_vectors.py`, `diff.py`, `extract_real.py`,
  `run-server.sh`, `compare.sh`) so the whole check re-runs.

Scope note: this is loader support. The compute crates
(`cpu-compute`, `wgpu-compute`) keep their own `Dtype` sets and still
refuse Q2_K/Q3_K tensors for math; nothing there changed.

## Sources read (primary: the server's llama.cpp tree)

From `/home/server/llama.cpp/ggml/`:

- `src/ggml-quants.c`: `dequantize_row_q2_K`, `dequantize_row_q3_K`
  (the ports), `quantize_row_q2_K_ref`, `quantize_row_q3_K_ref`
  (round-trip vector generation).
- `src/ggml-common.h`: `block_q2_K` (scales[16], qs[64], d, dmin;
  static_assert 2*2 + 256/16 + 256/4 = **84 bytes**) and
  `block_q3_K` (hmask[32], qs[64], scales[12], d; static_assert
  2 + 256/4 + 256/8 + 12 = **110 bytes**). QK_K = 256.
- `src/ggml.c`: type traits for both types (blck_size QK_K,
  type_size sizeof(block)).

Geometry was confirmed three ways: the static_assert arithmetic,
the harness printing ggml's own `sizeof` (84 / 110, QK_K 256), and
`GgmlType::byte_len` tests (84 per 256, 220 per 512, non-multiples
rejected).

Note the block field order differs from Q4_K..Q6_K: in Q2_K the
scales and quants come FIRST and d/dmin last; in Q3_K the order is
hmask, quants, scales, d. The ports follow the structs, not the
Q4_K habit.

## Cross-check method

Harness (`bench/q2q3-xcheck/harness.c`) calls ggml's own
`dequantize_row_q2_K` / `dequantize_row_q3_K` on caller-supplied
blocks and `quantize_row_*_ref` on f32 rows. The Rust side is the
crate's `probe` example (shortest round-trip text, parses back to
the exact f32). `diff.py` compares bit patterns, not tolerances.

Vector sets (generator seeded, deterministic):

- **synth** (134 blocks/type): all-zero block; all-0xFF payload with
  max finite scales; d = 0 and dmin = 0 variants; nibble-ladder
  scales with patterned quants; alternating mask patterns for Q3_K
  including the unit-test scale bytes; 128 seeded random blocks.
  All f16 scale fields are finite (exponent != 0x1F) by design:
  NaN payload handling belongs to the f16 conversion table, not to
  these dequantizers.
- **dsweep** (248 blocks/type): the scale `d` walks every finite
  f16 exponent (0..30), four mantissa patterns, both signs.
- **quant** (7 blocks/type): blocks produced by ggml's own
  `quantize_row_*_ref` from uniform, approx-normal, zero, constant,
  sine, wide-range (+-100), and tiny-with-one-spike f32 rows, then
  dequantized by both sides.
- **real** (48 blocks/type): real model bytes, see below.

### Where the harness ran, stated plainly

The server protocol queues all server work behind
`/tmp/itak-phase.lock`; six overnight lanes were ahead and the
baseline lane held the lock for hours, so the queued server run
(`~/overnight-q2q3/run-server.sh`, linking the tree's built
`libggml-base.so`) had not fired when this note was filed. It is
still queued and will drop its outputs and `SHA256SUMS` in
`~/overnight-q2q3` as an independent re-confirmation.

The results below come from the identical harness built locally
against the checkout at
`~/workspace/meta-cookbook/build-site/repos/ggerganov__llama.cpp/`,
after verifying that checkout's ggml is byte-identical to the
server tree's for everything this check touches (sha256 of the
extracted texts, first 16 hex digits):

| text | sha256 prefix (both trees) |
|---|---|
| `dequantize_row_q2_K` | 5dbd7936514edc14 |
| `dequantize_row_q3_K` | f1ee74eb91b6cdfa |
| `quantize_row_q2_K_ref` | cfcac20bce126975 |
| `quantize_row_q3_K_ref` | 264e4eda1b92b700 |
| `block_q2_K`/`block_q3_K` structs | 54ed0c8a6ef0023e |
| Q2_K/Q3_K type traits | 81be9313f95e7943 |

The port itself was written from the server tree's source, read
directly over SSH before any local file was touched.

## Real bytes: yes, for both types

`/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf`
(Unsloth dynamic quant of Glimmer itself) mixes types: of its 731
tensors, 206 are Q3_K and 42 are Q2_K (313 F32, 112 Q4_K, 38 Q5_K,
20 Q6_K). Extracted 16 blocks each from:

- Q3_K: `blk.0.attn_gate.weight`, `blk.0.attn_q.weight`,
  `blk.0.ffn_down.weight`
- Q2_K: `blk.10.attn_q.weight`, `blk.12.attn_gate.weight`,
  `blk.12.attn_q.weight`

Tensor offsets came from a local parse of the file's directory
(prefix fetched read-only over SSH, blocks cut with `dd`). The
parse was proven globally, not spot-checked: with each type's
block geometry, all 731 tensors tile the data section back to back
with zero mismatches (first data offset 13,113,888; last tensor
ends at 13,360,983,072). Extracted blocks' `d` fields are all
small finite values of weight-scale magnitude, as real blocks
should be. No other file under `/mnt/models` was needed; the
brief's fallback (quantize-ref blocks) also ran, as the `quant`
set above.

## Gates

- `cargo test -p gguf`: pass (19 lib + 20 integration + 1 doc).
- `cargo clippy -p gguf --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --check -p gguf`: clean.
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`: pass (the new enum
  variants break no exhaustive match; other crates only construct
  `GgmlType`).

## Verdict

Q2_K: **exact**. Q3_K: **exact**. Support is real, not faked:
the loader now dequantizes both types with ggml-identical output
on synthetic edge cases, a full finite-f16 scale sweep,
ggml-quantized blocks, and real Glimmer UD-Q3_K_XL bytes.
