# Prefix-KV store foundation (2026-11-07)

Lane `lane/prefix-kv-store` on main `0ecdc8f`. VM-only work; all
proof is fixture-level. Two commits: the crate, then this note.

## Premise correction, on evidence

The task brief said itak-kv already has versioned save/load of KV
state. It does not: at the base commit there is no `itak-kv` crate
and no KV save/load anywhere in the tree. What exists is the
`attention` crate's in-memory `KvCache`, plus the repo's own plan
naming itak-kv as the future home of exactly this contract:
`docs/specs/SPEC-itak-spec.md` ("itak-kv ... the separate save/load
contract"), `crates/muse-glimmer/src/cache.rs` ("That storage is
the KV crate's job (TODO T-2.4, `itak-kv` in the workspace plan)"),
and TODO item T-2.4. So this lane creates `crates/itak-kv` per the
plan instead of building on a crate that was not there. It depends
only on `attention`.

## What was built

### Snapshot format v1 (`crates/itak-kv/src/snapshot.rs`)

`KvSnapshot`: the KV state of exactly one sequence prefix, in the
versioned layout the format documents in its module header (magic
`ITKV`, format version, model fingerprint string, token count,
geometry, per-layer headers and rows, trailing FNV-1a 64 checksum
over all preceding bytes). Only visible rows are stored: global
layers store every row; windowed layers store the last `window`
rows, tagged with the absolute position of the first stored row.

- `KvSnapshot::capture(&KvCache, fingerprint)` refuses a cache
  whose layers disagree on position (`IncoherentCache`) instead of
  snapshotting a torn state.
- `KvSnapshot::from_bytes` is strict and total: bad magic, unknown
  version, truncation, checksum mismatch, trailing bytes, and
  header/row disagreement each refuse by name. A snapshot is
  handed out only whole.
- `restore()` rebuilds a fresh `KvCache` and returns it only on
  full success; nothing is ever partially applied.
  `restore_checked(geometry, fingerprint)` adds the caller's
  required geometry and model fingerprint as named refusals.
- Known cost, stated plainly: restoring a windowed layer replays
  zero rows for evicted positions ahead of the first stored row,
  because the host cache's append API is strictly in-order and
  position-checked. The zeros land only in slots the stored rows
  overwrite or in slots already outside the window, so restored
  views are exact (proven bitwise by the fixture below). For a
  4k-token Glimmer prefix that is 2,048 evicted positions per
  windowed layer, roughly 160 MB of host-side zero traffic,
  negligible. For a full-context snapshot it is 129,024 positions
  per windowed layer, seconds-scale; a bulk-restore constructor in
  `attention` is the named follow-up if full-context restores ever
  become a hot path.

### PrefixStore (`crates/itak-kv/src/store.rs`)

One file per entry under a configurable root. Entry layout: a
fixed 72-byte preamble (magic `ITKVPENT`, version, created and
last-used unix stamps, prefix hash, token count, payload length),
then the full token-id list, then the snapshot bytes.

- `put(tokens, snapshot, now)`: refuses an empty prefix, a
  token-count mismatch, and an entry that alone exceeds the byte
  cap, each by name. Writes are atomic: temp file in the same
  directory, sync, rename. Re-putting the same token list replaces
  its entry.
- `lookup(query, expected_geometry, expected_fingerprint, now)`:
  longest-prefix match over the index, longest first. A verified
  hit restamps last-used with an 8-byte in-place write (entries
  can be gigabytes; the file is never rewritten on a hit).
- Eviction: after every put, while the store is over its cap, the
  least recently used entry other than the one just written is
  deleted. Stamps are the preamble's last-used field, not file
  mtimes, so they survive copies and clock-safe ordering is the
  caller's clock (tests drive a fake clock).
- Configuration (`crates/itak-kv/src/config.rs`), all following
  the codebase's env conventions: `ITAK_KV_PREFIX_STORE` is the
  master switch in the fail-closed shape of `WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD`
  (trimmed exact `"1"` enables, everything else is off);
  `ITAK_KV_PREFIX_DIR` overrides the root (default
  `$HOME/.cache/itak/prefix-kv`); `ITAK_KV_PREFIX_MAX_BYTES` is the
  byte cap with `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES` = 8 GiB, where a malformed or
  zero value falls back to the default logged by name, because a
  cap is a bound, not a gate.
- The index is built by scanning the root at `open` (with a public
  `rescan()`); files another process writes afterwards are seen
  on the next open or rescan. That matches the session model: a
  serving process opens the store once at startup.

## Keying and trust model

Key: FNV-1a 64 over the token ids as little-endian u32 words, the
same hash family as the diag capture fingerprints. FNV is not
cryptographic, and the design never asks it to be: the hash is an
index, never a proof. A lookup candidate becomes a hit only after
all of these pass, in order:

1. The stored token ids hash back to the entry's key
   (`PrefixHashMismatch` refusal otherwise). This is the
   hash-collision guard: a forged or corrupted entry whose token
   copy was swapped cannot reproduce its key.
2. The stored ids equal the query's prefix token for token. A
   genuine hash collision (different ids, same hash) lands here
   and is simply not a match; the search continues to shorter
   prefixes. Filenames carry a second independent FNV hash as a
   discriminator, and if two different token lists ever collide
   on both, a counter suffix keeps both entries.
3. The payload decodes whole (its own checksum and consistency
   checks) and its token count agrees with the preamble.
4. When the caller requires them, the snapshot's geometry and
   model fingerprint match (`GeometryMismatch`,
   `FingerprintMismatch`).

Any refusal is named in the diag log and falls through to the
next-longest candidate: a corrupt long entry never blocks a
shorter honest one. The store directory itself is trusted-local,
the same trust level as the model files; a keyed hash is a
possible future hardening, not a correctness need, because
verification is token-exact.

## The session seam: specified, not wired

State of the seam in this lane: the store, the format, the
KV-state-level restore, and the fail-closed enable switch are
built and tested. The `ResidentSession` wiring is NOT built; the
task's own fallback applies, for three concrete reasons found in
the tree:

- The resident session holds no host-side KV copy and has no
  readback or install path today; capture is new code on the
  serving path, not a small patch.
- The slot laws differ. The host `KvCache` windowed ring is
  exactly `window` slots, slot = position % window
  (`crates/attention/src/cache.rs`). The resident session's
  windowed ring capacity is `sliding_window + chunk_cap - 1`
  (`crates/wgpu-compute/src/session.rs:237`), slot = position %
  ring_capacity. A naive buffer copy between the two corrupts
  every windowed layer.
- Chunk plans bind the KV buffers (`plans` in the session), so an
  install must go through the reset path that drops them.

The wiring, precisely, for the follow-up lane:

- New method `ResidentSession::install_prefix_snapshot` in
  `crates/wgpu-compute/src/session.rs` (struct at line 4135, `kv`
  field at 4151, `reset()` at 4348 as the shape to follow):
  1. Refuse unless the snapshot geometry matches the session
     (layer count and kinds from `cfg`, row width
     `num_kv_heads * head_dim`); refuse by name, session untouched.
  2. `self.reset()` (fresh `DeviceKv`, plans dropped, position 0).
  3. Per layer, `DeviceKv::ensure_layer`
     (`crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/k6_attention.rs:665`) with
     `appended_total = token_count`, then upload the stored rows
     through the context's buffer-write path into `LayerKv.k` /
     `LayerKv.v` (`k6_attention.rs:602`): global layers take rows
     at slots 0..n in one contiguous write; windowed layers take
     each stored row (absolute position p) at slot
     p % ring_capacity, which is at most two contiguous runs.
  4. `self.position = token_count`; return it. The caller then
     forwards only the unmatched suffix.
- The caller (session factory) consults
  `itak_kv::prefix_store_enabled()` and opens the store from
  `StoreConfig::from_env()` only when the switch is on; with the
  switch off, no store is opened and no lookup happens.
- The capture direction (for `put` after a prefill): per layer,
  read back via `GpuContext::read_f32`
  (`crates/wgpu-compute/src/device.rs:300`), reassemble positions
  in order (global slots 0..position; windowed positions
  max(0, position - window)..position at their ring slots),
  append them into a host `KvCache`, then
  `KvSnapshot::capture`. Fingerprint: the GGUF file's sha256.

## Sizing math for Glimmer

Measured geometry: 52 layers (39 windowed at 2,048, 13 global),
2 KV heads, head dim 128. One row is 256 floats = 1,024 bytes, for
K and again for V: 2,048 bytes per layer-position, 106,496 bytes
per token across all layers before any window eviction. (The
often-quoted 1.83 GB full-context resident figure counts 1,024
bytes per layer-position; the snapshot stores K and V at f32,
2,048 bytes per layer-position.)

- A 4,096-token system-prompt prefix: global layers hold 4,096
  rows, windowed layers hold 2,048, payload 272,629,760 bytes
  (about 260 MiB), plus 16 KiB of token ids and the 72-byte
  preamble. At the measured 159.3 tok/s prefill, reusing it skips
  about 25.7 seconds of prefill per request. Reading 260 MiB back
  from local disk is a tenth of a second class cost.
- Past the window, each extra token costs only the 13 global
  layers: 26,624 bytes per token.
- A full 131,072-token context snapshot: 3,653,238,784 bytes
  (about 3.40 GiB) of payload.
- The default 8 GiB cap therefore holds roughly thirty 4k-token
  prefixes, or two full-context snapshots with room to spare.

All four numbers are pinned by the `glimmer_sizing_math` unit
test against the real Glimmer layer pattern, not just asserted
here.

## Proof in this lane (VM, fixture-level)

- `cargo test -p itak-kv`: 21 passed (15 unit, 5 store
  integration, 1 seam fixture). The fixture runs a small model
  shape (4 layers, mixed windowed/global) two ways, cold and
  store-restored, and requires bitwise-identical attention
  outputs, identical greedy streams, and bitwise-identical
  restored views including window eviction positions.
- Store integration: round-trip, longest-prefix selection among
  nested entries, eviction respecting the cap and LRU order under
  a fake clock, a forged entry (token copy rewritten in place)
  refused while a shorter honest prefix still serves, geometry
  and fingerprint refusals at lookup, torn temp and torn final
  files ignored at open, persistence across reopen.
- Regression suites: attention 60 + 5 doc-tests, wgpu-compute
  277, dflash 24, itak-spec 12, all passing.
- `cargo clippy -p itak-kv --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean,
  `cargo fmt --check` clean, `cargo check --workspace` clean.
- Housekeeping note: the lane's first build hit the VM disk quota
  (many stale lane target dirs); the target dirs of seven merged
  lanes were deleted to free space, and the lane built into the
  merge worktree's shared target dir. No sources outside this lane
  were touched.

## The real-file proof owed

1. The session wiring above, as its own lane, gated by
   `ITAK_KV_PREFIX_STORE` default off.
2. On the card, on the real Glimmer GGUF (sha256
   4cc57c0f51040a226e5a72cc47b7613f7772950e460a665f7083de89f183f60e):
   forward a prefix of at least 4,096 tokens, capture it into the
   store under that fingerprint, restart the session, install the
   snapshot, continue with the same suffix, and require the
   generated stream to match the cold run token for token for at
   least 64 tokens, the same identity shape as the speculative
   harness.
3. The measured wall saving on that run against the 25.7-second
   prediction above, and a cross-process persistence check (entry
   written by one process, hit by another).

===== END FILE: bench/prefix-kv-store-2026-11-07.md =====

===== FILE: bench/proof-tools-verdicts-2026-11-07.md =====
# Proof tools verdict plumbing: the Category F pair of HIGHs, plus their sibling MEDIUMs (2026-11-07)

Lane `lane/proof-tools-verdicts`, from main
2a2030e18b1089708c831217c38dc8a0e7ff4e4c. Code in the first
commit on this lane; this note is the second commit. All proof
runs executed on this VM against this lane's tree (before runs
on the unfixed tree, after runs on the fixed tree, same fixture
files both times); no server jobs.

Source of the work: the cold critic panel of 2026-11-07
(`CRITIC-ENGINE-MERGE.md`, Category F; probes executed by the
mop-up seat). The harnesses that produce this project's golden
and cross-check verdicts could print "pass" on a failing run:
divergence was invisible to the verdict logic, and exit codes
said success regardless. The code the harnesses verify was
checked directly by the correctness seat and is clean; only the
verdict plumbing was broken. Four findings were in scope; each
fix below was proven lying-then-honest by execution, and every
tool was also run on a genuine match to prove no false
divergence was introduced.

## Finding 1 [HIGH]: compare_traces never gates on the first values

`golden/tools/compare_traces.py`, `judge()`: the first-values
metrics (`first_max_diff`, `first_rel_std`) were computed and
printed but never entered `ok`, although the module's own
reading rule says a stage matches "with the first values
tracking".

Repro (the mop-up seat's, rebuilt as a fixture): reference
`embed` tensor `[1,2,3,4]`; our trace line carries the
statistics of the permutation `[4,3,2,1]` (identical mean,
population variance, and max_abs; first values completely
different).

Before:
```
embed            match                  0.000e+00     0.000e+00      0.000e+00   3.000e+00
first divergent stage: None
EXIT=0
```
Fix: `first_rel <= 1e-2` (the same band as the other criteria,
in units of the stream's own standard deviation, exactly as
the seat prescribed) joins the `ok` conjunction in `judge()`.

After:
```
embed            DIVERGENT              0.000e+00     0.000e+00      0.000e+00   3.000e+00  <-- FIRST DIVERGENT (input stage matched: True)
first divergent stage: embed
EXIT=1
```
Regression case: `golden/tools/test_verdict_tools.py` generates
this fixture pair itself and asserts the permuted tensor prints
DIVERGENT; it also pins the clean pair (match, exit 0) and the
NO REF exit below.

## Finding 2 [HIGH]: compare.sh exits 0 on a failing vector set

`bench/q2q3-xcheck/compare.sh`: `run_set` returned diff.py's
status, but nothing read it; each call overwrote the last, the
script's exit status was the final (absent) set's, and an absent
set returned 0.

Repro (real script, real Rust probe from the lane it hardcodes):
a directory holding one present set, `q2k_synth.bin`, with a
deliberately wrong reference (all zeros), and the other seven
sets absent.

Before:
```
q2k_synth: values=256 exact=62 (24.2188%) zero_sign_only=0 nan_mismatch=0 max_abs_diff=45
q3k_synth.bin: absent, skipped
... (six more absent lines)
EXIT=0
```
Fix: per-set results accumulate into PASSED / FAILED / SKIPPED
lists (a failed probe run now counts as a set failure instead
of diffing a stale dump), a per-set summary prints at the end,
and the script exits 1 when any present set failed. The server
half's discipline is `set -euo pipefail`; the local half
deliberately does NOT adopt `-e`, because it must visit every
set to report the per-set summary the panel required. Manual
accumulation reaches the same verdict without aborting the
remaining sets.

After, same directory:
```
---- compare.sh summary ----
FAIL    q2k_synth.bin
SKIPPED q3k_synth.bin
... (six more SKIPPED lines)
sets: 0 passed, 1 failed, 7 skipped
EXIT=1
```
Judgment call, absent sets: an absent set does NOT by itself
fail the run. It is named in the summary and counted, and a
partial staging copied back for a quick check stays usable
(the skip path is a designed behavior that predates the
finding; the seat's fix shape tracks absents separately from
failures). One exception: if NO set was present at all, the
run exits 1 with `compare.sh: no sets were compared; nothing
was verified` on stderr, because a verification that verified
nothing must not report success. Executed: the all-absent run
prints 8 SKIPPED lines and exits 1.

Clean-pair proof: the same script against a directory whose
`q2k_synth_ref.f32` was generated from the probe's own output
prints `exact=256 (100.0000%)`, `PASS q2k_synth.bin`, and
exits 0 with the seven absent sets counted as skipped.

## Finding 3 [MEDIUM]: cosine against a zero tensor, and verdict tools that cannot exit nonzero

`golden/tools/compare_layers.py` `stats()` defined cosine as
1.0 whenever the product of the norms was 0, so a dead-vs-live
checkpoint printed a perfect cosine; and neither
compare_layers.py nor compare_traces.py could exit nonzero on
any divergence, missing reference, or partial trace.

Unit repro (module imported and called, the seat's shape):
```
before: stats(zeros((2,4)), full((2,4), 0.05)) == (0.05, 0.05, 1.0)
after:  stats(zeros((2,4)), full((2,4), 0.05)) == (0.05, 0.05, 0.0)
        stats(zeros((2,4)), zeros((2,4)))      == (0.0, 0.0, 1.0)
```
Fix: `stats()` compares the norms separately: cosine 0.0 when
exactly one norm is zero, 1.0 only when both are zero. In
`main()`, a both-sides-all-zeros checkpoint line carries the
marker `(both sides all zeros)` so the legitimate 1.0 is not
read as agreement between live activations. Both tools now
return their verdict as the exit status: compare_layers exits
1 when any checkpoint is flagged divergent; compare_traces
exits 1 when a first divergent stage is set or any stage
reported NO REF; both exit 0 only on a full match.

Full-run proof (generated 28-layer fixture pair; llama `embd`
all zeros on both sides, llama `L00_attn_norm` all zeros
against Rust 0.05, everything else identical constants):
```
before: L00_attn_norm  cosine 1.000000, no flag,
        first divergent checkpoint: None, EXIT=0
after:  embd           cosine 1.000000  (both sides all zeros)
        L00_attn_norm  cosine 0.000000  <-- DIVERGENT
        first divergent checkpoint: L00_attn_norm, EXIT=1
```
Clean-pair proof: the same generator with no zeroed stems
prints no flags, `first divergent checkpoint: None`, EXIT=0;
the faithful compare_traces fixture prints `match`, EXIT=0.

## Finding 4 [MEDIUM]: diff.py's pass criterion is value-exact under a bit-exact claim

`bench/q2q3-xcheck/diff.py` counted signed-zero-only bit
differences (`zero_sign`) but excluded them from the verdict,
while the harness framing claims the comparison is "byte for
byte" (harness.c header) and diff.py headlines a "bit-exact
match count".

Repro (the seat's): ref `[+0.0, 1.5, -0.0, 2.0]` vs Rust text
`[-0.0, 1.5, +0.0, 2.0]`:
```
before: sztest: values=4 exact=2 (50.0000%) zero_sign_only=2 nan_mismatch=0 max_abs_diff=0, EXIT=0
after:  (identical printed line), EXIT=1
```
Judgment call: the panel offered either failing on
`zero_sign > 0` or restating the claim as value-exact wherever
it is made; the task brief prefers the stricter,
claim-preserving option unless a consumer depends on
value-exact semantics. None does. The only exit-code consumer
is compare.sh, and every recorded run of this harness
(`bench/overnight-q2k-q3k-dequant-2026-11-05.md`, all eight
sets, 223,744 values) reports sign-of-zero-only = 0 with exact
at 100%, so the stricter verdict changes no recorded result;
it makes the "byte for byte" claim true going forward. Fix:
the return condition gains `and zero_sign == 0`, and the
docstring states the bit-exact verdict explicitly. NaN handling
was already bit-strict (any NaN bit difference lands in
`nan_mismatch` and fails) and is now pinned by a regression
case in `bench/q2q3-xcheck/test_diff.py`, alongside the
signed-zero, identical, and real-mismatch cases.

## Gates

- Before/after executions above, on identical fixtures.
- `python3 golden/tools/test_verdict_tools.py`: 8/8 cases pass.
  (One case was corrected during the lane: identical-tensor
  cosine is 0.9999999999999998 in floating point, so the test
  asserts within 1e-12 rather than exact 1.0.)
- `python3 bench/q2q3-xcheck/test_diff.py`: 4/4 cases pass.
- `python3 -m py_compile` on both edited .py files: clean.
  `bash -n` on compare.sh: clean.
- Clean-pair runs of every tool print match and exit 0 (no
  false divergence): compare_traces faithful fixture,
  compare_layers clean fixture, diff.py identical dumps,
  compare.sh probe-generated reference.
- Shared tree untouched and whole: `cargo check --workspace`
  clean; `go test ./...` from platform/ all packages ok.

===== FILE: bench/q2q3-xcheck/compare.sh =====
#!/bin/bash
# Local half of the cross-check: run the Rust probe over every vector
# set copied back from the server staging and diff against ggml's
# reference outputs. Usage: compare.sh <dir-with-bins-and-refs>
#
# Exit status: nonzero if any PRESENT set fails its diff (or its probe
# run fails), or if no set was present at all (a run that compared
# nothing proves nothing). Absent sets are skipped, named in the
# per-set summary, and do not by themselves fail the run, so a partial
# staging copied back for a quick check stays usable.
set -uo pipefail
DIR=${1:?usage: compare.sh <dir>}
cd "$DIR"
WT=~/workspace/lanes/overnight-q2q3
export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"

PASSED=()
FAILED=()
SKIPPED=()

run_set() {
    local ty=$1 bin=$2 block_bytes=$3
    local ref="${bin%.bin}_ref.f32"
    if [ ! -f "$bin" ]; then
        echo "$bin: absent, skipped"
        SKIPPED+=("$bin")
        return 0
    fi
    local size blocks elements
    size=$(stat -c %s "$bin")
    blocks=$((size / block_bytes))
    elements=$((blocks * 256))
    if ! cargo run --release --quiet --manifest-path "$WT/Cargo.toml" \
        -p gguf --example probe -- "$ty" "$bin" "$elements" "$elements" \
        > "${bin%.bin}_rust.txt" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "$bin: probe run failed"
        FAILED+=("$bin (probe run failed)")
        return 0
    fi
    if python3 "$WT/bench/q2q3-xcheck/diff.py" "$ref" "${bin%.bin}_rust.txt" "${bin%.bin}"; then
        PASSED+=("$bin")
    else
        FAILED+=("$bin")
    fi
}

run_set q2_k q2k_synth.bin 84
run_set q3_k q3k_synth.bin 110
run_set q2_k q2k_dsweep.bin 84
run_set q3_k q3k_dsweep.bin 110
run_set q2_k q2k_quant.bin 84
run_set q3_k q3k_quant.bin 110
run_set q2_k q2k_real.bin 84
run_set q3_k q3k_real.bin 110

echo "---- compare.sh summary ----"
for bin in "${PASSED[@]}"; do echo "PASS    $bin"; done
for bin in "${FAILED[@]}"; do echo "FAIL    $bin"; done
for bin in "${SKIPPED[@]}"; do echo "SKIPPED $bin"; done
echo "sets: ${#PASSED[@]} passed, ${#FAILED[@]} failed, ${#SKIPPED[@]} skipped"
if [ "${#FAILED[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    exit 1
fi
if [ "${#PASSED[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "compare.sh: no sets were compared; nothing was verified" >&2
    exit 1
fi
exit 0

===== END FILE: bench/q2q3-xcheck/compare.sh =====

===== FILE: bench/q2q3-xcheck/diff.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compare ggml reference f32 output against the Rust probe dump.

Usage: diff.py <ref.f32> <rust.txt> [label]

The reference file is little-endian f32 binary. The Rust file is the
gguf probe example's text dump (one shortest-round-trip f32 per line),
which parses back to the exact f32 values.

Reports: value count, bit-exact match count, signed-zero-only mismatch
count (bit differs, value compares equal), NaN mismatch count, max abs
diff, and the worst block (256 values per block) by max abs diff.

The verdict is bit-exact, as the harness framing claims ("byte for
byte"): the exit status is 0 only when every value's bits match, so a
signed-zero-only difference fails just as a NaN bit difference does.
"""
import struct
import sys


def main():
    ref_path, rust_path = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    label = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else ref_path

    ref_raw = open(ref_path, "rb").read()
    n = len(ref_raw) // 4
    ref = struct.unpack("<%df" % n, ref_raw)
    ref_bits = struct.unpack("<%dI" % n, ref_raw)

    rust_vals = []
    with open(rust_path) as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if line:
                rust_vals.append(float(line))
    if len(rust_vals) != n:
        print(f"{label}: LENGTH MISMATCH ref={n} rust={len(rust_vals)}")
        return 1
    rust_raw = struct.pack("<%df" % n, *rust_vals)
    rust = struct.unpack("<%df" % n, rust_raw)
    rust_bits = struct.unpack("<%dI" % n, rust_raw)

    exact = 0
    zero_sign = 0
    nan_mismatch = 0
    max_diff = 0.0
    block_max = {}
    for i in range(n):
        a, b = ref[i], rust[i]
        if ref_bits[i] == rust_bits[i]:
            exact += 1
            continue
        if a != a or b != b:  # NaN on either side
            nan_mismatch += 1
            continue
        d = abs(a - b)
        if d == 0.0:
            zero_sign += 1
            continue
        if d > max_diff:
            max_diff = d
        blk = i // 256
        if d > block_max.get(blk, 0.0):
            block_max[blk] = d

    worst = sorted(block_max.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:5]
    print(f"{label}: values={n} exact={exact} ({100.0 * exact / n:.4f}%) "
          f"zero_sign_only={zero_sign} nan_mismatch={nan_mismatch} "
          f"max_abs_diff={max_diff:.6g}")
    for blk, d in worst:
        print(f"  worst block {blk}: max_abs_diff={d:.6g}")
    return 0 if (nan_mismatch == 0 and max_diff == 0.0 and zero_sign == 0) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

===== END FILE: bench/q2q3-xcheck/diff.py =====

===== FILE: bench/q2q3-xcheck/extract_real.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Scan every GGUF under /mnt/models for Q2_K (id 10) and Q3_K (id 11)
tensors and extract up to 48 real blocks per type into
q2k_real.bin / q3k_real.bin, with a manifest of where they came from.

Uses the llama.cpp tree's own gguf-py reader. Only the extracted blocks
are copied out of the (multi-GB) model files, via memmap slices.
"""
import glob
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "/home/server/llama.cpp/gguf-py")
import gguf  # noqa: E402

BLOCK = {10: 84, 11: 110}
NAME = {10: "q2k", 11: "q3k"}
MAX_BLOCKS_PER_TYPE = 48


def tensor_bytes(reader, tensor, want_bytes):
    """Raw bytes from the start of a tensor's data, block aligned."""
    offset = getattr(tensor, "data_offset", None)
    if offset is not None:
        return bytes(reader.data[offset:offset + want_bytes])
    arr = tensor.data
    if arr.dtype.itemsize == want_bytes:
        return arr.reshape(-1)[:1].tobytes()
    return arr.tobytes()[:want_bytes]


def main():
    found = {10: 0, 11: 0}
    outs = {10: bytearray(), 11: bytearray()}
    manifest = []
    for path in sorted(glob.glob("/mnt/models/**/*.gguf", recursive=True)):
        try:
            reader = gguf.GGUFReader(path)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - report and move on
            manifest.append(f"SKIP {path}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
            continue
        for t in reader.tensors:
            tid = int(t.tensor_type)
            if tid in BLOCK and found[tid] < MAX_BLOCKS_PER_TYPE:
                want = (MAX_BLOCKS_PER_TYPE - found[tid]) * BLOCK[tid]
                raw = tensor_bytes(reader, t, want)
                take = len(raw) // BLOCK[tid]
                if take > 0:
                    outs[tid] += raw[:take * BLOCK[tid]]
                    found[tid] += take
                    manifest.append(
                        f"{NAME[tid]}: {path} tensor={t.name} blocks={take}")
    for tid in (10, 11):
        if outs[tid]:
            with open(f"{NAME[tid]}_real.bin", "wb") as f:
                f.write(outs[tid])
        manifest.append(f"TOTAL {NAME[tid]} blocks={found[tid]}")
    with open("real_manifest.txt", "w") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(manifest) + "\n")
    print("\n".join(manifest))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

===== END FILE: bench/q2q3-xcheck/extract_real.py =====

===== FILE: bench/q2q3-xcheck/gen_vectors.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Deterministic test vectors for the Q2_K / Q3_K dequantizer cross-check.

Writes, into the current directory:
  q2k_synth.bin / q3k_synth.bin   hand-built edge-case blocks
  q2k_dsweep.bin / q3k_dsweep.bin blocks sweeping the f16 scale `d`
                                  over every finite exponent pattern
  quant_in.f32                    f32 rows for ggml's reference
                                  quantizers (quantize_row_*_ref)

All f16 scale fields in synthetic blocks are finite (exponent != 0x1F):
NaN/Inf scales would test the f16 conversion table's NaN payload
handling, not the dequantizers, and the two implementations are allowed
to differ there. Everything else (quants, scales, masks) is exercised
over its full byte range.
"""
import math
import random
import struct
import sys

QK = 256


def put_f16(buf, off, bits):
    struct.pack_into("<H", buf, off, bits)


def q2k_block(scales, qs, d, dmin):
    b = bytearray(84)
    b[0:16] = scales
    b[16:80] = qs
    put_f16(b, 80, d)
    put_f16(b, 82, dmin)
    return bytes(b)


def q3k_block(hmask, qs, scales, d):
    b = bytearray(110)
    b[0:32] = hmask
    b[32:96] = qs
    b[96:108] = scales
    put_f16(b, 108, d)
    return bytes(b)


def f16_finite(rng):
    while True:
        b = rng.randrange(0, 65536)
        if ((b >> 10) & 0x1F) != 0x1F:
            return b


def rand_bytes(rng, n):
    return bytes(rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(n))


def main():
    rng = random.Random(20261105)

    # ---------------- Q2_K synthetic edge blocks ----------------
    q2 = []
    q2.append(q2k_block(bytes(16), bytes(64), 0x0000, 0x0000))          # all zero
    q2.append(q2k_block(b"\xff" * 16, b"\xff" * 64, 0x7BFF, 0x7BFF))    # max finite scales, max quants
    q2.append(q2k_block(b"\xff" * 16, b"\xff" * 64, 0x0000, 0x3C00))    # d = 0, dmin = 1
    q2.append(q2k_block(b"\xff" * 16, b"\xff" * 64, 0x3C00, 0x0000))    # d = 1, dmin = 0
    q2.append(q2k_block(bytes((i * 0x11) & 0xFF for i in range(16)),    # nibble ladder scales
                        bytes((i * 37 + 11) & 0xFF for i in range(64)),
                        0x3800, 0x3400))                                # d = 0.5, dmin = 0.25
    q2.append(q2k_block(bytes((i * 17 + 3) & 0xFF for i in range(16)),
                        bytes(0xAA if i % 2 == 0 else 0x55 for i in range(64)),
                        0xC100, 0x3555))                                # d = -2.5, dmin ~ 0.2
    for _ in range(128):                                                # seeded random blocks
        q2.append(q2k_block(rand_bytes(rng, 16), rand_bytes(rng, 64),
                            f16_finite(rng), f16_finite(rng)))
    with open("q2k_synth.bin", "wb") as f:
        f.write(b"".join(q2))

    # ---------------- Q3_K synthetic edge blocks ----------------
    unit_scales = bytes([0x12, 0x34, 0x56, 0x78, 0x9A, 0xBC,
                         0xDE, 0xF0, 0x21, 0x43, 0x65, 0x87])
    q3 = []
    q3.append(q3k_block(bytes(32), bytes(64), bytes(12), 0x0000))       # all zero
    q3.append(q3k_block(b"\xff" * 32, b"\xff" * 64, b"\xff" * 12, 0x7BFF))  # max everything, max finite d
    q3.append(q3k_block(bytes(32), b"\xff" * 64, b"\xff" * 12, 0x3C00))     # mask all clear (negatives), d = 1
    q3.append(q3k_block(b"\xff" * 32, b"\xff" * 64, b"\xff" * 12, 0x3C00))  # mask all set, d = 1
    q3.append(q3k_block(bytes(0xAA if i % 2 == 0 else 0x55 for i in range(32)),
                        bytes((i * 37 + 11) & 0xFF for i in range(64)),
                        unit_scales, 0x3800))                           # alternating mask, unit-test scales, d = 0.5
    q3.append(q3k_block(rand_bytes(rng, 32),
                        bytes((i * 37 + 11) & 0xFF for i in range(64)),
                        bytes(12), 0x2800))                             # scales all zero (factor -32), d = 2^-5
    for _ in range(128):                                                # seeded random blocks
        q3.append(q3k_block(rand_bytes(rng, 32), rand_bytes(rng, 64),
                            rand_bytes(rng, 12), f16_finite(rng)))
    with open("q3k_synth.bin", "wb") as f:
        f.write(b"".join(q3))

    # ---------------- f16 d sweeps ----------------
    # d (and dmin for Q2_K) walk every finite exponent, four mantissa
    # patterns, both signs: 30 * 4 * 2 = 240 blocks per type.
    sweep_bits = []
    for exp in range(0, 31):
        for mant in (0x000, 0x155, 0x2AA, 0x3FF):
            for sign in (0, 1):
                sweep_bits.append((sign << 15) | (exp << 10) | mant)
    scales2 = bytes((i * 0x11) & 0xFF for i in range(16))
    qs2 = bytes((i * 37 + 11) & 0xFF for i in range(64))
    with open("q2k_dsweep.bin", "wb") as f:
        for bits in sweep_bits:
            f.write(q2k_block(scales2, qs2, bits, 0x3C00))
    hmask3 = bytes((i * 91 + 7) & 0xFF for i in range(32))
    qs3 = bytes((i * 53 + 3) & 0xFF for i in range(64))
    scales3 = bytes((i * 29 + 5) & 0xFF for i in range(12))
    with open("q3k_dsweep.bin", "wb") as f:
        for bits in sweep_bits:
            f.write(q3k_block(hmask3, qs3, scales3, bits))

    # ---------------- quantizer inputs ----------------
    rows = []
    r = random.Random(42)
    rows.append([r.uniform(-1, 1) for _ in range(QK)])                  # uniform
    rows.append([(r.uniform(0, 1) + r.uniform(0, 1) + r.uniform(0, 1) - 1.5) * 2
                 for _ in range(QK)])                                   # approx normal
    rows.append([0.0] * QK)                                             # zeros
    rows.append([0.5] * QK)                                             # constant
    rows.append([math.sin(i / 8.0) * 4 for i in range(QK)])             # sine sweep
    rows.append([r.uniform(-100, 100) for _ in range(QK)])              # wide range
    spike = [r.uniform(-1e-4, 1e-4) for _ in range(QK)]
    spike[100] = 50.0
    rows.append(spike)                                                  # tiny + one spike
    with open("quant_in.f32", "wb") as f:
        for row in rows:
            f.write(struct.pack("<%df" % QK, *row))

    print("q2k_synth blocks:", len(q2), " q3k_synth blocks:", len(q3),
          " dsweep blocks per type:", len(sweep_bits),
          " quant rows:", len(rows))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

===== END FILE: bench/q2q3-xcheck/gen_vectors.py =====

===== FILE: bench/q2q3-xcheck/harness.c =====
// Cross-check harness for the Q2_K / Q3_K dequantizer port.
//
// Dequantizes caller-supplied blocks with ggml's own reference row
// functions (dequantize_row_q2_K / dequantize_row_q3_K) and quantizes
// f32 rows with ggml's reference quantizers (quantize_row_q2_K_ref /
// quantize_row_q3_K_ref), so the Rust port in crates/gguf can be
// compared against the exact code it was ported from, byte for byte.
//
// Build, two equivalent routes:
//   (a) link the tree's built libggml-base (what run-server.sh does):
//       gcc -O2 -std=c11 -I<tree>/ggml/include -I<tree>/ggml/src \
//           harness.c -o harness -L<build>/bin -lggml-base -lm \
//           -Wl,-rpath,<build>/bin
//   (b) compile ggml-quants.c standalone, garbage-collecting the
//       unused quantizers (the four functions used here are
//       self-contained; without --gc-sections the link fails on
//       ggml_abort / ggml_row_size from unrelated IQ quantizers):
//       gcc -O2 -std=c11 -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections \
//           -I<tree>/ggml/include -I<tree>/ggml/src \
//           harness.c <tree>/ggml/src/ggml-quants.c -o harness -lm \
//           -Wl,--gc-sections
//
// Modes:
//   harness dequant q2k|q3k <blocks.bin> <out.f32>
//   harness quant   q2k|q3k <in.f32>    <blocks.bin>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#include "ggml-quants.h"

static void die(const char * msg) {
    fprintf(stderr, "harness: %s\n", msg);
    exit(2);
}

static uint8_t * read_all(const char * path, long * out_size) {
    FILE * f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) die("cannot open input");
    if (fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END) != 0) die("seek failed");
    long size = ftell(f);
    if (size < 0) die("tell failed");
    if (fseek(f, 0, SEEK_SET) != 0) die("seek failed");
    uint8_t * buf = malloc(size > 0 ? (size_t) size : 1);
    if (!buf) die("oom");
    if (size > 0 && fread(buf, 1, (size_t) size, f) != (size_t) size) die("read failed");
    fclose(f);
    *out_size = size;
    return buf;
}

static void write_all(const char * path, const void * data, long size) {
    FILE * f = fopen(path, "wb");
    if (!f) die("cannot open output");
    if (size > 0 && fwrite(data, 1, (size_t) size, f) != (size_t) size) die("write failed");
    fclose(f);
}

int main(int argc, char ** argv) {
    if (argc != 5) die("usage: harness <dequant|quant> <q2k|q3k> <in> <out>");
    const int is_q2 = strcmp(argv[2], "q2k") == 0;
    if (!is_q2 && strcmp(argv[2], "q3k") != 0) die("type must be q2k or q3k");

    fprintf(stderr, "sizeof(block_q2_K)=%zu sizeof(block_q3_K)=%zu QK_K=%d\n",
            sizeof(block_q2_K), sizeof(block_q3_K), QK_K);

    long in_size = 0;
    uint8_t * in = read_all(argv[3], &in_size);

    if (strcmp(argv[1], "dequant") == 0) {
        const long block_bytes = is_q2 ? (long) sizeof(block_q2_K) : (long) sizeof(block_q3_K);
        if (in_size % block_bytes != 0) die("input is not a whole number of blocks");
        const long nblocks = in_size / block_bytes;
        float * out = malloc((size_t) (nblocks * QK_K) * sizeof(float));
        if (!out) die("oom");
        if (is_q2) {
            dequantize_row_q2_K((const block_q2_K *) in, out, nblocks * QK_K);
        } else {
            dequantize_row_q3_K((const block_q3_K *) in, out, nblocks * QK_K);
        }
        write_all(argv[4], out, nblocks * QK_K * (long) sizeof(float));
        free(out);
    } else if (strcmp(argv[1], "quant") == 0) {
        const long row_bytes = QK_K * (long) sizeof(float);
        if (in_size % row_bytes != 0) die("input is not a whole number of 256-element rows");
        const long nrows = in_size / row_bytes;
        const long block_bytes = is_q2 ? (long) sizeof(block_q2_K) : (long) sizeof(block_q3_K);
        uint8_t * out = malloc((size_t) (nrows * block_bytes));
        if (!out) die("oom");
        if (is_q2) {
            quantize_row_q2_K_ref((const float *) in, (block_q2_K *) out, nrows * QK_K);
        } else {
            quantize_row_q3_K_ref((const float *) in, (block_q3_K *) out, nrows * QK_K);
        }
        write_all(argv[4], out, nrows * block_bytes);
        free(out);
    } else {
        die("mode must be dequant or quant");
    }

    free(in);
    return 0;
}

===== END FILE: bench/q2q3-xcheck/harness.c =====

#!/bin/bash
# Server half of the Q2_K/Q3_K dequantizer cross-check.
# Run under the shared phase lock:
#   flock -w 14400 /tmp/itak-phase.lock bash ~/overnight-q2q3/run-server.sh
set -euo pipefail
cd ~/overnight-q2q3
exec >> ~/overnight-q2q3/run.log 2>&1
echo "=== run-server.sh start $(date -Is) ==="

# Wait for any cargo/test processes tied to ~/gpu-wave6 to clear.
for i in $(seq 1 240); do
    if pgrep -af "gpu-wave6" | grep -Eq "cargo|rustc"; then
        echo "gpu-wave6 build still running, waiting ($i)"
        sleep 30
    else
        break
    fi
done

TREE=/home/server/llama.cpp
BIN=""
for d in "$TREE/build-vulkan2/bin" "$TREE/build-hip/bin"; do
    if [ -f "$d/libggml-base.so" ]; then BIN=$d; break; fi
done
if [ -z "$BIN" ]; then echo "no libggml-base.so found"; exit 2; fi
echo "libggml-base from: $BIN"

gcc -O2 -std=c11 -I"$TREE/ggml/include" -I"$TREE/ggml/src" \
    harness.c -o harness -L"$BIN" -lggml-base -lm -Wl,-rpath,"$BIN"

python3 gen_vectors.py

./harness dequant q2k q2k_synth.bin q2k_synth_ref.f32
./harness dequant q3k q3k_synth.bin q3k_synth_ref.f32
./harness dequant q2k q2k_dsweep.bin q2k_dsweep_ref.f32
./harness dequant q3k q3k_dsweep.bin q3k_dsweep_ref.f32
./harness quant q2k quant_in.f32 q2k_quant.bin
./harness quant q3k quant_in.f32 q3k_quant.bin
./harness dequant q2k q2k_quant.bin q2k_quant_ref.f32
./harness dequant q3k q3k_quant.bin q3k_quant_ref.f32

python3 extract_real.py
for t in q2k q3k; do
    if [ -f "${t}_real.bin" ]; then
        ./harness dequant "$t" "${t}_real.bin" "${t}_real_ref.f32"
    fi
done

sha256sum harness.c gen_vectors.py extract_real.py *.bin *.f32 > SHA256SUMS
echo "=== SHA256SUMS ==="
cat SHA256SUMS
echo "=== DONE $(date -Is) ==="

===== FILE: bench/q2q3-xcheck/test_diff.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Regression tests for diff.py's bit-exact verdict.

Pins the critic-panel Category F fix (2026-11-07): the exit status is
0 only when every value's bits match. A signed-zero-only difference
(bits differ, values compare equal) fails, as does a NaN whose bit
pattern differs; identical dumps pass.

Usage: test_diff.py; exits 0 when every case passes.
"""

import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
FAILURES = []


def check(name, cond, detail=""):
    print(f"{'PASS' if cond else 'FAIL'}  {name}" + (f"  ({detail})" if detail else ""))
    if not cond:
        FAILURES.append(name)


def run_diff(ref_bytes, rust_lines):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
        td = Path(td)
        (td / "ref.f32").write_bytes(ref_bytes)
        (td / "rust.txt").write_text("".join(f"{v}\n" for v in rust_lines))
        r = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, str(HERE / "diff.py"), str(td / "ref.f32"),
             str(td / "rust.txt"), "test"],
            capture_output=True, text=True)
        return r


def main():
    # Signed zeros: +0.0 vs -0.0 in two positions. Values compare
    # equal, bits differ: the bit-exact verdict must fail.
    r = run_diff(struct.pack("<4f", 0.0, 1.5, -0.0, 2.0),
                 ["-0.0", "1.5", "0.0", "2.0"])
    check("diff.py: signed-zero-only difference exits 1",
          r.returncode == 1 and "zero_sign_only=2" in r.stdout,
          f"rc={r.returncode}")

    # Identical dumps pass.
    r = run_diff(struct.pack("<4f", 1.5, -2.25, 0.0, 3.0),
                 ["1.5", "-2.25", "0.0", "3.0"])
    check("diff.py: identical dumps exit 0",
          r.returncode == 0 and "exact=4 (100.0000%)" in r.stdout,
          f"rc={r.returncode}")

    # A real value mismatch fails.
    r = run_diff(struct.pack("<f", 1.0), ["2.0"])
    check("diff.py: value mismatch exits 1", r.returncode == 1,
          f"rc={r.returncode}")

    # A NaN with a different payload bit pattern fails: the text
    # "nan" packs to the canonical quiet NaN, the reference carries
    # a payload bit.
    r = run_diff(struct.pack("<I", 0x7FC00001), ["nan"])
    check("diff.py: NaN bit difference exits 1",
          r.returncode == 1 and "nan_mismatch=1" in r.stdout,
          f"rc={r.returncode}")

    print(f"\n{len(FAILURES)} failure(s)" if FAILURES else "\nall cases passed")
    return 1 if FAILURES else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

===== END FILE: bench/q2q3-xcheck/test_diff.py =====

===== FILE: bench/quantize-once-2026-11-04.md =====
# Quantize-once (profile candidate C3): one K12 quantize of `h` per layer stage

Branch `lane/quantize-once` over main 72a4b9d. All counts below
are counted from the plan builder in
`crates/wgpu-compute/src/session.rs` (the same code the host
unit tests now pin); nothing here is measured on a GPU yet.
The server run that executes the GPU legs and the prefill pair
is specified at the end and is still owed.

## The change

In an MMQ-served chunk plan, every projection over a layer's
`h` prepared its own K12 plain quantize of that buffer. The
plan builder now prepares ONE shared quantize per layer
stage into a dedicated scratch pair (`q8h_qs` / `q8h_ds`,
kept apart from the general pair so no single-consumer
quantize can clobber it mid-stage), and each member product
binds that pair and carries no quantize of its own
(`ProjCall`'s MMQ variants now hold `Option<K12QuantCall>`;
the shared form is the `None` case). The layer plan encodes
the shared quantize ahead of every member: the attention
stage's right after the attention norm, the FFN stage's
right after the post-attention chain.

Byte-identity is by construction: the quantize is a pure
function of (input buffer, batch, width), every member of a
stage shares all three, and the product kernels bind the
same buffers in both forms, so a member product reads
exactly the bytes its own quantize dispatch would have
written. Membership is guarded: a projection whose input
width differs from the share's prepared width never joins
(it keeps its own quantize over the general pair), and a
member whose product prepare refuses leaves the share
untouched and falls back to the GEMM form, the standing
fallback ladder unchanged. Every refusal keeps its name.

## A correction to the profile's premise, counted from the code

The profile (section 1.4 and candidate C3) derived 78
redundant quantizes per chunk by counting three consumers
of "the identical `h`": the QKV batch, the separate V, and
the FFN pair. The encode order says otherwise. The batch
and V read the `h` the attention norm produced; the
post-attention chain (L8) then OVERWRITES `h` with the FFN
norm's output, and the pair reads that second tensor.
Batch and pair quantize different contents that happen to
share a scratch buffer, so no single quantize can serve
both, and sharing across the chain would change the math.

The true unit is the stage: one `h` content, several
readers. Two shares per layer, never one. The savings
below are counted on that basis.

## Dispatch arithmetic, counted from the plan builder

K12 legs per layer before the change (MMQ serving; every
h projection carried its own quantize):

| Layer class | Attention stage | FFN stage | h legs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full batch, paired (26 of the real layers) | batch = 1 | pair = 1 | 2 |
| Partial batch, paired (26 of the real layers) | batch + V = 2 | pair = 1 | 3 |
| Unbatched, unpaired (no real layer; code path) | Q + K + V + gate = 4 | gate + up = 2 | 6 |

After the change each stage holds ONE shared quantize
regardless of member count, so the removed legs per layer
are: full batch 0, partial batch 1 (the V leg), unbatched
up to 4 (three in the attention stage, one in the FFN
stage). A stage with a single member is neutral by
construction: its one quantize moves from the product to
the layer, and the count does not move (pinned in the host
tests).

Per 64-row chunk on the real file (52 layers, 26 full and
26 partial, the profile's V split): K12 legs in total go
from 234 to 208, and total dispatches drop by the same 26,
from the flash era's derived 679 to 653 (both totals
derived under MMQ serving, not measured). The removed legs
also remove their re-reads of `h`: 26 legs x 1.70 MB
(64 rows x 6656 x 4 B) is about 44 MB per chunk. (The
profile's ~133 MB figure scales with its 78 count and
falls with it.)

At fixture scale the same arithmetic is pinned twice over:
host unit tests pin `layer_dispatch_count` per class
(fixture layers 9 and 8; full batch 13 before and after;
partial 15 to 14; the mixed class 18 to 16; unbatched 23
to 19), and the new mixed-fixture resident test pins the
assembled chunk: 93 dispatches with the shares, 105
before, 69 on a backend with no MMQ set (no quantize legs
exist there at all).

## Why the resident pin (51 per chunk) does not move

The resident fixture's asserted plans are 1-row and 4-row
plans. Below `GEMM_MIN_ROWS` (16) every projection takes
its GEMV form, which consumes f32 activations and quantizes
nothing: those plans contain no K12 legs before the change
and none after. The pin stands at 51, untouched, and the
mixed-fixture test carries the new pins where the MMQ
forms actually engage.

## Decode

Decode plans are 1-row plans: GEMV forms throughout, no
quantize legs, no duplication to remove. Quantize-once
does not apply to decode and decode is untouched; the
mixed test pins the decode delta at exactly 3 x 69
dispatches for three decode chunks, the count the mixed
layers record with no shares anywhere.

## Expected effect (expectation, not a measurement)

26 of 679 dispatches per chunk is 3.8 percent of the
dispatch count, and the legs themselves are small
(1.70 MB read, about 0.81 MB written per leg, single-digit
microseconds at the profile's measured stream rate), so
the traffic saving alone is worth well under a tenth of a
percent of the chunk's chain time. Any real gain has to
come from the 26 removed dependent boundaries; the
profile's decode-era pricing of a boundary (~12-15 us)
would bound that near 0.3-0.4 ms per chunk, about 0.2
percent of the ~194 ms chunk. Expect a small effect,
likely inside run-to-run noise at 1,024 tokens. The
change's certain value is structural: fewer dispatches,
44 MB per chunk of re-reads gone, and an accounting that
now proves the count instead of deriving it per run. The
profile's M6 discipline is the gate: dispatch count down
by the derived amount, outputs token-identical, marginal
recorded honestly even if it does not move.

  After: "so the shipped ceiling default (16) admits exactly the

# Server cache semantics: key distinctness, sampled bypass, template fetch errors (2026-11-07)

Lane `lane/server-cache-semantics`, from main 012396a.
Three findings from the cold critic panel
(`~/workspace/reports/critic-engine-2026-11-07/CRITIC-ENGINE-MERGE.md`,
Category E), all in `platform/internal/server/server.go`: one HIGH
(the cache key's distinctness was untested, seat 5's executed
mutation) and two MEDIUMs (seat 3, code inspection). The two
chat-template HIGHs of Category E landed in the previous lane
(0578b44); this lane closes what remains of the category in the
server package.

## Finding 1 (HIGH, Operability seat): the cache key's distinctness was untested

`chatCacheKey` hashes the full marshaled request, and the comment
beside it shows the collision risk was understood — but the only
cache test repeated one identical request and asserted a hit.
Seat 5 mutated the key to hash only `req.Model` and
`go test ./internal/server/` stayed fully green: a key that stops
covering messages, temperature, or seed (a JSON-tag refactor
would do it silently) serves one caller's completion to every
other caller of the model, green suite throughout.

### What the key actually covers

Read before fixing: `chatCacheKey` marshals the whole
`chatRequest`. Its real inputs are every field of `chatRequest`
(model, messages, tools, stream, max_tokens, temperature, top_p,
stop, seed, top_k, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty) and, one
level down, every field of `chatMessage` (role, content, name,
tool_call_id, tool_calls, reasoning_content, recipient, end_turn),
`chatTool`/`toolFunction` (type, name, description, parameters),
and `chatToolCall`/`toolFunction` (id, type, name, arguments).
Pointer fields marshal distinctly from absent ones.

### Fix: tests, no code change

The key was correct; the proof was missing. Two test layers now
pin it:

- `platform/internal/server/cachekey_internal_test.go` (new,
  in-package because the key is unexported):
  `TestChatCacheKeyFieldByFieldDistinct` moves exactly one input
  at a time from a base request that sets all of them (28
  variants) and requires each variant's key to differ from the
  base key AND from every other variant's key.
  `TestChatCacheKeyStableForIdenticalRequests` pins the other
  half: identical requests key identically, map fields included.
- `platform/internal/server/server_cache_test.go` (new):
  `TestChatCacheDistinctRequestsGetDistinctEntries` posts a base
  request and 11 single-field variants over HTTP (message
  content, role, appended message, max_tokens, present-zero
  temperature, seed, seeded temperature, top_p, top_k, stop,
  model) and asserts for each: `X-Torch-Cache: miss`, the engine
  call count up by exactly one, and the entry count in `/debug`
  cache stats up by exactly one. A final repeat of the base
  request still hits its own entry. All variants stay cacheable
  under the finding-2 semantics, so a miss can only mean the key
  told them apart.

### Mutation-kill proof

Applied seat 5's exact mutation (`json.Marshal(req.Model)` in
place of `json.Marshal(req)`), with the new tests in the tree:

- `TestChatCacheKeyFieldByFieldDistinct`: FAIL — 28 variant arms
  report "key equals the base key" (every non-model field), plus
  pairwise collisions.
- `TestChatCacheDistinctRequestsGetDistinctEntries`: FAIL — the
  first same-model variant is served as a hit.
- `TestChatCompletionAndCache` (the pre-existing test): PASS
  under the mutation — the original hole, reproduced verbatim.

Mutation reverted; all three pass. The reverted tree's diff for
`chatCacheKey` is comment-only (a pointer to these tests).

## Finding 2 (MEDIUM, Failure seat): the cache stored sampled generations

`cache.Set` ran after any successful non-streaming completion
with no temperature/seed guard. Two identical unseeded
temperature > 0 requests share a key, so the second caller got
the first caller's sampled output byte-identical for the TTL —
the variation the temperature was set to obtain, frozen.

### Fix: cache semantics, stated where the cache is defined

New `chatCacheable(req)`: a request is cacheable iff it carries
a seed, or its temperature is absent, or its temperature is
<= 0. In `handleChatCompletions` the gate applies to BOTH sides:
uncacheable requests skip the `cache.Get` and the `cache.Set`
and answer `X-Torch-Cache: skip`; cacheable requests answer
`hit`/`miss` exactly as before. The semantics are documented in
the package header and on `chatCacheable` itself: seeded =
deterministic (same seed, same sample), temperature 0 = greedy,
unseeded temperature > 0 = variation requested, never frozen.

### Evidence

Fails before: against the unmodified handler,
`TestChatUnseededSampledRequestsBypassCache` failed at the first
assertion (first request answered `X-Torch-Cache: miss`, i.e.
the sample was being stored for replay).

Passes after, with a new `sampledEngine` fake whose completion
differs on every call so a replay is visible in the body:
two identical unseeded temperature-0.7 requests return two
distinct completions ("take 1", "take 2"), both `skip`, two
engine calls, zero cache entries. The widening guards pass
before and after, as regression pins:
`TestChatSeededSampledRequestsStillCache` (miss then hit, one
engine call) and `TestChatZeroTemperatureRequestsStillCache`
(same).

## Finding 3 (MEDIUM, Failure seat): a template-fetch error silently flattened, and the flattening was cached

`buildPrompt` returned `flattenMessages(msgs), nil` whenever
`resolveTemplate` returned nil — and `resolveTemplate` returned
nil WITHOUT setting `tplDone` on any fetch error other than
`ErrNoChatTemplate`. So a transient engine hiccup during the
template fetch produced a role-flattened prompt for that request
with no error anywhere, and the handler's unconditional
`cache.Set` then replayed the wrongly-prompted generation for
the TTL — contradicting the handler's own comment that a bad
prompt build is "never a silent fallback". Secondary defect in
the same function: `resolveTemplate` held `tplMu` across the
5-second network fetch, serializing every concurrent chat
request behind one slow fetch.

### Fix: split the outcomes, unlock the fetch

- `resolveTemplate` now returns `(*engine.ChatTemplate, error)`.
  Definitive outcomes are unchanged and still cached: config
  template wins, engine template fetched once,
  `ErrNoChatTemplate` settles as (nil, nil) = flatten. Any other
  fetch error returns a named wrapped error
  ("chat template fetch failed: %w"), is logged, and is NOT
  cached, so the next request retries. `buildPrompt` propagates
  it, so the request takes the handler's existing 502
  `chat_template_error` path: nothing generates, nothing is
  cached.
- `tplMu` now guards the cached outcome only, never the fetch:
  the outcome is read under a short lock, the fetch runs
  unlocked, and the new `cacheTemplateOutcome` records the
  definitive result first-writer-wins, so concurrent fetches
  agree on one outcome. (Concurrent requests may fetch twice;
  that is the stated trade for not serializing chat behind a
  5-second fetch.)

### Evidence

Fails before: `TestChatTemplateFetchFailureIsNamedNotFlattened`
— against the unmodified code the failing-fetch request
answered 200 with the flattened generation (the test wants 502
`chat_template_error`); `TestChatTemplateFetchDoesNotSerializeRequests`
— with one fetch parked inside a blocking fake, a second
request never reached its own fetch within 3 s.

Passes after: the failing-fetch request answers 502
`chat_template_error`, the engine's Generate is never called,
and the cache holds zero entries; once the fake recovers, the
next request renders through the real template (prompt asserted
byte-equal to the ChatML expectation), and a repeat is a cache
hit on that templated generation with the engine called once in
total. The concurrency test's second request reaches its own
fetch while the first is still parked, and both complete 200.

## Gates (lane tree, after all fixes)

From `platform/`:

- `go build ./...` — clean.
- `go test ./...` — all 9 packages pass; `--- PASS` count 123,
  counted as `go test ./... -v | grep -c -- "--- PASS"`
  (baseline at 012396a by the same count: 115; +8 new tests =
  2 key pins + 6 HTTP tests in this lane, no test removed).
- `go test -race ./internal/server/` — clean (the concurrency
  test above runs under it).
- `go vet ./...` — clean.
- `gofmt -l .` — empty.
- `golangci-lint run ./...` (v2.15.0, built with go1.26.9) —
  0 issues. One annotation added on the way: gosec G101
  pattern-matches the literal text `max_tokens` inside the HTTP
  test's request bodies, the same false-positive shape the
  pre-existing `TestChatMaxTokensCapRefusedByName` bodies would
  trip if they sat in a map literal; the variants map carries a
  `//nolint:gosec` with the reason, in the repo's existing
  nolint-with-reason style.
- `cargo check --workspace` from the repo root — clean (the
  tree is shared; no Rust file changed).

## Left alone, deliberately

- The embeddings NIT (server.go handleEmbeddings has no
  server-side generation deadline or input-count cap of its
  own): outside this lane's three findings; bounds exist one
  layer down, per the panel.
- Cache eviction/TTL internals in `internal/cache`: the panel

- The chat-template MEDIUM in `render.go` (dict.items() sorted

# Serving smoke transcript, 2026-10-30 (TODO T-9.8)

End to end proof that the Go platform and the Rust engine serve a real
Glimmer chat completion through our own stack: HTTP in, Unix socket NDJSON
to the engine, CPU forward pass on the real 17 GB model file, streamed
tokens back out as an OpenAI-shaped response.

- Host: ubuntu-server (scratch dir `~/itak-serve/`, sources rsynced from
  this repo; nothing installed system-wide)
- Model: `/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf`
- Code: commit `e40b8ba` (Rust `itak-engine` binary crate) and commit
  `110ed17` (platform `Generate` over the socket)
- Production Glimmer llama-server (Vulkan, 127.0.0.1:8080, pid 683675)
  was never touched; `/health` returned `{"status":"ok"}` before and
  after the smoke (last verified 2026-10-30T05:18Z).
- All times UTC.

## Build

```text
# on ubuntu-server, in ~/itak-serve/
cargo build --release            # produces target/release/itak-engine
                                 # and target/release/examples/glimmer_generate
# on the build VM
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o torchd ./platform/cmd/torchd   # scp'd to ~/itak-serve/torchd
```

## Engine start (2026-10-30T03:38Z)

```text
./target/release/itak-engine \
  --model /mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf \

```

Log: model loaded in 50,486 ms, tensor coverage 731/731
(`itak-loader` `require_complete()`), tokenizer ready, listening on the
socket. RSS about 17.6 GB.

## Platform start

```text
TORCH_API_KEY=test-key ./torchd -engine-socket ~/itak-serve/run/engine.sock \
  -models glimmer -addr 127.0.0.1:19091     # with engine
./torchd -models glimmer -addr 127.0.0.1:19092   # no engine (refusal checks)
```

(Ports 19091/19092 because 8091 on this host is already held by an
unrelated llama-server instance; loopback only either way. `test-key` is
a throwaway smoke credential, not a real key.)

## Fast checks (2026-10-30T03:41Z, all passed)

- `GET /healthz` on :19091: engine `ok: true`, detail
  "socket handshake + ping ok"
- `GET /v1/models` with the key on :19091: lists `glimmer`
- `GET /debug` on :19091: `engine_debug` present, model `glimmer`,
  coverage_expected = coverage_found = 731, context_length 131072,
  generations 0
- Chat with no key: refused 401 (verbatim re-capture below)
- Chat with key on the no-engine instance: refused 503 (below)

Verbatim refusal outputs (re-captured 2026-10-30T05:20:09Z against the
no-engine instance on :19092, same code path):


## Why the smoke prompt is a question, not the plain statement

The platform flattens chat messages to plain text as
`user: <content>\nassistant:`. Probes against a throwaway CPU
llama-server (port 18299, greedy, production untouched) showed what the
plain statement does with that shape:

- content `The capital of France is` flattens to 11 prompt ids
  [200000, 1556, 38, 589, 7963, 323, 11698, 373, 198, 140680, 38] and
  llama.cpp's greedy continuation RESTATES the sentence
  (" The capital of France is Paris.\nParis") instead of continuing it.
  Our engine would do the same; it is the same model. A smoke that
  "begins with Paris" cannot be built on that prompt shape honestly.
- content `Capital of France? One word.` flattens to 12 prompt ids
  [200000, 1556, 38, 20555, 323, 11698, 43, 5615, 2918, 335, 140680, 38]
  and llama.cpp greedy gives ids [13796, 198, 1556, 38], text
  " Paris\nuser:". First generated token is exactly " Paris".

So the smoke asks the question directly, with `max_tokens: 4` and
stop `["\n"]`, which makes the expected completion exactly " Paris"
with finish_reason "stop".

## The smoke generation

Request sent 2026-10-30T03:42:50Z:

```text
$ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19091/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer test-key" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"glimmer",
         "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Capital of France? One word."}],
         "max_tokens":4,"temperature":0,"stop":["\n"]}'
```

Engine log:

```text
[itak-engine] generate start: prompt_tokens=12 max_tokens=4 temperature=0
[itak-engine] prompt ids: [200000, 1556, 38, 20555, 323, 11698, 43, 5615, 2918, 335, 140680, 38]
[muse-glimmer] forward.begin: tokens=12 position=0 layers=52
[muse-glimmer] forward.end: logits=202048 position=12
[itak-engine] generate done: finish_reason=stop generated=2 elapsed_ms=2891315 text=" Paris"
```

Response received 2026-10-30T04:31:01Z (curl exit 0):

```json
{"choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":" Paris","role":"assistant"}}],"created":1793334661,"id":"chatcmpl-4d52a65e1b9eac2a","model":"glimmer","object":"chat.completion"}
http=200 time_total=2891.277553s
```

Reading it plainly: the engine generated 2 tokens. Token 13796
(" Paris") was emitted; token 198 ("\n") matched the stop string, was
held back by the streamer's stop hold-back, and ended the generation
with finish_reason "stop". The completion is exactly " Paris", the
same first token llama.cpp produced for the same flattened prompt.

## Reproduction against the engine alone (glimmer_generate)

The same flattened prompt run through the engine's own example binary
(`glimmer_generate`, greedy, 4 tokens), bypassing the platform entirely.
T-9.8's proof asks that temperature 0 through the platform reproduce
this output.

- Attempt 1 (started 2026-10-30T03:36:44Z): KILLED, exit 137 at
  03:44:08Z, while the platform smoke generation was also running.
  Two 30B CPU jobs on one host pinned swap at 3/3 GB; the kill is
  consistent with the OOM killer (no dmesg access to confirm).
  Lesson recorded: never run two 30B CPU jobs concurrently on this
  host. Its logged prompt ids already matched the smoke's 12 ids.
- Attempt 2 (2026-10-30T05:19:02Z to 06:07:11Z, exit 0), run alone:

  ```text
  prompt_ids=[200000, 1556, 38, 20555, 323, 11698, 43, 5615, 2918, 335, 140680, 38]
  coverage: expected=731 found=731 missing=0
  phase=prefill ms=2752226 prompt_tokens=12
  prefill_top rank=0 id=13796 tok=" Paris" logit=12.998796 prob=0.658840
  gen step=1 id=13796 tok=" Paris" source=prefill
  gen step=2 id=198 tok="\n" ms=41851
  gen step=3 id=1556 tok="user" ms=41892
  gen step=4 id=38 tok=":" ms=42448
  generated_ids=[13796, 198, 1556, 38]
  generated_text=" Paris\nuser:"
  peak_rss_kb=38192312
  ```

  The engine alone produces exactly llama.cpp's greedy ids
  [13796, 198, 1556, 38] for this prompt, and the platform smoke's
  two generated tokens (13796 emitted, 198 stop-triggered) are the
  first two of them. Temperature 0 through the platform reproduces
  the engine-alone output, as T-9.8 requires. Three-way agreement:
  llama.cpp probe, engine alone, platform end to end.

## Incidents and honest edges

- The engine process exited at an unknown time after the smoke
  completed cleanly at 04:31:01Z. No panic or error in its log; the
  platform's health check afterwards reported the socket as a broken
  pipe (verbatim, 2026-10-30T05:20:09Z):

  ```text
  $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:19091/healthz
  {"engine":{"detail":"engine: handshake failed: write frame: write unix @->/home/server/itak-serve/run/engine.sock: write: broken pipe","ok":false},"status":"ok"}
  ```

  Cause unconfirmed (OOM is the leading hypothesis; swap stayed pinned
  at 3/3 GB). Nothing restarted it, because nothing supervises it yet.
  That is TODO T-9.11, and this smoke is its Exhibit A.

- Speed, stated plainly: this request took 2,891 s wall (one 12-row
  prefill plus two single-token forwards on the CPU reference path).
  llama.cpp on CPU answered the same probe prompt in seconds; the
  production Vulkan build does 998 tok/s prefill and 44.31 tok/s
  decode on this model. The CPU engine is a correctness oracle. GPU
  serving is T-9.5/T-9.10 territory and is not claimed here.

===== FILE: bench/shader-autopsy-2026-11-04.md =====
# Shader autopsy, first pass: what ACO actually emitted

Step 1 of the streaming-rate research plan (actions 1 and 3):
before any new kernel is written, look at the compiled form of
every kernel family in the resident path. Tooling:
`bench/shader-autopsy.sh` (this lane). No engine code changed.

## Run

- Where: ubuntu-server, tree staged at `~/gpu-wave5` from
  `git archive` of main `bda7ff55ea57f4a764afddf9ba2e050c59b86916`;
  anchor files (session.rs, compute.rs, k18_small_batch.rs,
  spec_generate_gpu.rs) sha256-verified identical to the
  worktree before the run. Raw output:
  `/tmp/shader-autopsy/2026-11-05-bda7ff55/` on the server
  (dated 2026-11-05 UTC, 2026-11-04 EST).
- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (RADV NAVI31, gfx1100).
- Driver: Mesa 26.0.8-1ubuntu0.3 (mesa-vulkan-drivers),
  Vulkan 1.4.335. Kernel 7.0.0-42. cargo/rustc 1.99.1.
- Dumps: `RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats,asm,cs` (compute stage
  only), private `MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR` per arm so every
  shader compiled cold. RADV's dump headers carry no shader
  name, so attribution is by family-isolated compiles
  (wgpu-compute's `shader_compile` tests, one family per
  run, identical dump env) cross-checked against the
  in-situ dump set of the real verdict run (100 stats
  blocks; the same signatures recur there).
- The dump arm of the verdict harness ran with the opt-in
  families ON (`WGPU_COMPUTE_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS=16`,
  `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMQ_WIDE_MIN_ROWS=32`) so K15/K16/K18
  compile in situ; the perf arms ran at shipped defaults.
  The family-isolation passes were run manually with the
  script's exact flags and are folded into the script as
  phase 3b.

Reported LDS is RADV's allocated figure; it differs from
the WGSL-declared staging constants by driver packing
(deltas from -1,280 to +960 bytes across families), which
is why the isolated compiles, not LDS alone, carry the
attribution. SGPRs read 108 for every shader in every
family: that is ACO's compute allocation, not a
per-kernel signal, and it is not used below.

## The table (family-isolated compiles, Mesa 26.0.8, gfx1100)

| Family | Shaders | VGPR | Spilled VGPR | Scratch (B) | LDS reported (B) | WGSL staging (B) | Code (B) | s_buffer_load per shader |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GEMV K1 (Q4_K) | 9 variants | 48 | 0 | 0 | 1,024-4,096 | partials only | 1,744-5,824 | 2-3 |
| GEMV K2/K3 (Q6_K/Q5_K) | 14 variants | 48-72 | 0 | 0 | 1,024-2,048 | partials only | 1,852-6,316 | 3-8 |
| MMQ K13 (Q4_K, m64) | 1 | 256 | 0 | 0 | 41,984 | 41,216 | 31,824 | 7 |
| MMQ K14 (Q6_K, m64) | 1 | 256 | 0 | 0 | 44,032 | 45,312 | 34,544 | 7 |
| Wide MMQ K15/K16 | 9 | 256 | 1,041-1,213 | 78,080-86,528 | 41,984-62,464 | 41,472-66,048 | 72,576-82,844 | 17 |
| K17 DFlash | 1 main + 3 util | 24 | 0 | 0 | 1,024 | ~512 + scalars | 2,492 | 6 |
| K18 small-batch, tile 32 | 5 | 256 | 0 | 0 | 16,384 | 15,424 / 16,448 | 31,564-34,324 | 7 |
| K18 small-batch, tile 64 | 6 | 256 | 0 | 0 | 26,624 | 25,664 / 26,688 | 31,792-34,512 | 7 |
| GEMM K10/K11 | 9 | 12-60 | 0 | 0 | up to 16,384 in situ | n/a | 220-7,260 | small |

Static instruction features (per big shader): the MMQ and
K18 bodies each carry 1,024 `v_dot4` (the unrolled 4x4
sub-tile dot products) and roughly 600 `ds_load`/`ds_store`
(LDS operand traffic, by design). No shader anywhere uses
a 16-bit or byte global load (`buffer_load_b16`/ubyte
count is 0 in every dump); GEMV's weight stream loads are
`buffer_load_b128` (128-bit) in the unrolled body.

In situ, the real verdict run compiled K18's tile-64
variants only (6 shaders, LDS 26,624, VGPR 256): Glimmer's
tensor widths route tile-64 shapes; tile 32 appears only
in the isolated compile set.

## Verdicts per kernel

- **GEMV (K1/K2/K3): clean.** VGPR 48-72, no spills, no
  scratch, 1-4 KB of LDS (reduction partials only), weight
  loads at full 128-bit width, buffer descriptors fetched
  2-8 times per shader (once per buffer, at setup). The
  compiled form matches the measured behavior: this is
  the fast family and its codegen gives no reason to
  doubt the measurement.
- **MMQ K13/K14: register-saturated, not spilling.**
  VGPR 256 is the architectural per-wave maximum; ACO
  still kept everything in registers (zero spills, zero
  scratch) in 32-35 KB of fully unrolled code. Occupancy
  per CU is at the floor, which costs latency hiding on
  the prefill path, but there is no codegen defect.
- **Wide MMQ K15/K16: convicted.** Every one of the 9
  wide shaders spills: 1,041-1,213 spilled VGPRs and
  78-86 KB of scratch per shader, on top of VGPR 256 and
  42-62 KB of LDS. A kernel that reloads its own register
  spills from memory while trying to stream weights is
  moving far more bytes than the tensor holds. This is
  a compiled-form explanation, from the driver's own
  statistics, for the recorded wide-MMQ behavior (about
  3.5x slower per tensor than K13/K14, one session hang).
  The shipped default (wide out of the ladder) is the
  right call, now with evidence instead of just timings.
- **K17 DFlash: clean.** VGPR 24, no spills, 1 KB LDS,
  2.5 KB code. Nothing in the draft block kernel's
  compiled form is suspect; the draft's cost sits in the
  GEMV-form block forward around it, as measured before.
- **K18 small-batch: no codegen smoking gun; the ceiling
  is structural.** Zero spills, zero scratch, descriptors
  clean (7 fetches), dots and LDS traffic exactly as
  designed. What the stats do show is VGPR 256 at both
  tile sizes: each K18 wave carries the maximum register
  allocation, so resident waves per CU are few, and every
  super-block column pays an LDS stage plus barrier for
  operands the GEMV form reads straight from DRAM. Set
  against the measured flat 70-130 GB/s stream rate, the
  compiled form points at occupancy plus staging latency,
  not at a defect ACO introduced.
- **K10/K11 GEMM and the K4-K8 utility set: clean.**
  Small, unspilled, nothing to chase.

## GEMV vs K18, and the Mesa 15132 question

The research plan named Mesa issue 15132 as a suspect:
on that report, ACO clobbered loop-invariant buffer
descriptors and emitted about 25 percent more buffer
loads (and 184 percent more scalar loads) than the rival
compiler for the same Q4_K GEMV shader. Our dumps do
**not** show that pattern. In every family the buffer
descriptors are fetched a small constant number of times
per shader (GEMV 2-8, MMQ/K18 7, wide 17), true scalar
loads are 4-24 per shader, and there is no per-iteration
descriptor refetch in the unrolled bodies. One invariant
argument reload repeats 16 times in K18's body
(`s_load_b128` at offset 0x30); that is two orders of
magnitude below the 15132 scale and cannot carry the
measured 5-10x stream-rate gap. GEMV's dynamic load
count is at the width minimum by construction (one
128-bit load per 16 bytes of weight stream). For K18
and MMQ the global side is loop-carried staging, so
static counts cannot give a dynamic total; what can be
said is that nothing on the descriptor or scalar side
is inflated. The 15132 mechanism is cleared for this
codebase on this driver. What remains standing, from
the compiled form alone: register-ceiling occupancy in
every staged family, LDS staging latency by design,
and (wide only) the spill storm.

## Blocked: the speculative phase currently device-losts

All three `spec_generate_gpu` runs in this pass (dump
arm and both perf arms, shipped defaults included)
died at the same instruction: spec round 1, inside the
DFlash draft's `forward_block`, with RADV reporting
"The CS has been cancelled because the context is lost.
This context is guilty of a hard recovery", after which
wgpu panicked on the lost device (exit 101). Phase A
completed in every run: plain decode 35.62-37.63 tok/s,
64 chunks, the stream opening with the known golden
tokens [13796, 26, 1573, 373, 290, 2167, 26899, 1212].

This is not a code regression claim: the same harness
at this same SHA passed phase B four times on
2026-11-04 (bench/small-batch-2026-11-04.md, IDENTITY +
GOLDEN in all verdict runs). The changed variable is
the server's tenant mix. Other tenants now hold 6.54 GB
of VRAM (two Qwen3-Embedding servers on 8091, one
Qwen3-4B server on 8092), against about 2.7 GB during
the verdict runs. Phase B's footprint arithmetic:
6.54 GB tenants + 16.76 GB target weights + 1.63 GB
draft weights + KV and activation buffers is about
25.3 GB against the card's 25.75 GB. The working
theory, labeled as theory (dmesg needs sudo, which is
not available non-interactively): allocation pressure
pushes buffers into GTT, the draft block forward
overruns the amdgpu watchdog, and recovery kills the
context. The tenants were not touched; all three
llama-server processes were still alive after each
recovery. Consequence for this pass: no spec tok/s and
no verify-ms could be collected, for any arm.

## cswave32: one data point (phase A only)

`RADV_PERFTEST=cswave32`, shipped defaults, private
shader cache per arm, 64 tokens, depth 6 harness (the
spec phase never ran, above). Plain decode: control
35.70 tok/s, cswave32 35.62 tok/s, identical token
stream, identical dispatch count (28,480). No
measurable movement on the GEMV decode path. This is
a single data point on phase A only, not a verdict on
wave32 for the staged families; that A/B still needs a
phase B that survives, or a per-tensor bench.

## Fixture note

The script's first staged run also executed the
resident_session mixed fixture with K18 enabled (dump
arm env). `resident_session_matches_trait_and_cpu`
failed on exactly one assertion: the dispatch-count
pin at tests/resident_session.rs:398 (318 recorded vs
306 pinned for the shipped ladder). Every token
agreement check ahead of that pin passed, and the
other two resident tests passed. Enabling K18 changes
the graph's dispatch count by design, so the pin
tripping is expected, not a correctness finding. The
script now runs the fixture at shipped defaults.

## Limits of this pass, and the next step

Shader statistics and disassembly are static: they
convict spills, register ceilings, and load widths,
but they cannot time the LDS staging or count dynamic
loads. The dynamic confirmation is step 2 of the plan
(per-dispatch timestamps plus an SQTT capture with
`MESA_VK_TRACE=rgp` and L2 counters on the surviving
kernel), run when phase B can execute on this server
again. Nothing in this pass changes any default:
K18 stays off, wide MMQ stays out of the ladder, and
both stays are now backed by the compiled form, not
only by timings.

===== END FILE: bench/shader-autopsy-2026-11-04.md =====
