#!/bin/bash
# Shader autopsy: read-only diagnosis of the compiled form of
# every kernel family in the resident GPU path, plus the run
# environment, captured before any new kernel is written.
#
# Why: the streaming-rate research (bench plan in
# ~/workspace/research/gpu-streaming-rate-2026-11-04) found the
# shared-weight batched kernels streaming at 70-130 GB/s while
# the per-row GEMV reader reaches several hundred GB/s on the
# same card. Step 1 of that plan is to look at what the driver
# compiler (ACO, via RADV) actually emitted for each family:
# register counts, scratch (spills), LDS per workgroup, and
# load widths in the disassembly, with GEMV (fast) compared
# against K18 (slow). The Mesa issue 15132 pattern (redundant
# buffer loads from aliased multi-view access) is the named
# suspect; the stats and asm dumps are how it gets caught.
#
# What it does:
#   1. Captures the environment (GPU, Mesa/Vulkan driver,
#      toolchain, git SHA, flags) into env.txt.
#   2. Builds the verdict harness (itak-spec's
#      spec_generate_gpu example) and the mixed-fixture
#      resident_session test.
#   3. Dump arm: runs the verdict harness on the real Glimmer
#      files with RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats,asm,cs (compute stage
#      only) and a private MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR, so every
#      shader compiles cold and dumps. The opt-in kernel
#      families are switched ON for this arm only
#      (WGPU_COMPUTE_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS=16 for K18,
#      WGPU_COMPUTE_MMQ_WIDE_MIN_ROWS=32 for K15/K16) so all
#      families appear in one dump set. Also runs the
#      resident_session mixed fixture under dumps at SHIPPED
#      defaults: that test pins the exact dispatch count of
#      the shipped ladder (resident_session.rs), so running
#      it with K18 on trips the count pin by design (318 vs
#      306, observed 2026-11-04) after every token check has
#      already passed.
#   3b. Family isolation: runs wgpu-compute's shader_compile
#      tests one family at a time (K1, K2/K3, K12-K14,
#      K10/K11, K17, K15/K16, K18, K4-K8), each under the
#      same dump env with its own private cache, so every
#      stats block is attributable to exactly one family.
#      RADV's dump headers carry no shader name, and the
#      in-situ LDS values differ from the WGSL staging
#      constants by driver packing, so this isolation is
#      what makes the comparison table exact.
#   4. Perf arms: the same verdict run at shipped defaults
#      (K18 off, wide MMQ off), once plain and once with
#      RADV_PERFTEST=cswave32, each with its own private
#      shader cache. These are single data points, not
#      verdicts; the logs keep the full output either way.
#
# This script changes no engine code and sets no defaults.
# Dumps land on the harness's stderr (RADV writes them
# there); stdout and stderr are kept in separate logs.
#
# Usage:
#   bench/shader-autopsy.sh [MODEL] [DRAFT]
# MODEL/DRAFT default to the recorded Glimmer paths.
# Knobs: AUTOPSY_OUT (default /tmp/shader-autopsy/<date>-<sha>),
# AUTOPSY_NTOK (64), AUTOPSY_DEPTH (6), EXPECTED_SHA (recorded
# in env.txt when the tree has no .git, e.g. an archive stage).
#
# Run on ubuntu-server with the GPU free (the resident
# session takes the card). One arm at a time, sequential.
set -u
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT" || exit 2
export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS="${CARGO_BUILD_JOBS:-4}"

MODEL="${1:-/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf}"
DRAFT="${2:-/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/dflash-Muse-Glimmer-30B-Q4_K_M.gguf}"
NTOK="${AUTOPSY_NTOK:-64}"
DEPTH="${AUTOPSY_DEPTH:-6}"
SHA="$(git rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "${EXPECTED_SHA:-unknown}")"
STAMP="$(date +%F)-$(echo "$SHA" | cut -c1-8)"
OUT="${AUTOPSY_OUT:-/tmp/shader-autopsy/$STAMP}"
mkdir -p "$OUT"
SUMMARY="$OUT/summary.txt"
: > "$SUMMARY"
note() { echo "$*" | tee -a "$SUMMARY"; }

note "=== shader autopsy $(date -Is) ==="
note "tree: $ROOT"
note "out:  $OUT"

# --- 1. environment -------------------------------------------------
{
  echo "date: $(date -Is)"
  echo "host: $(hostname)"
  echo "kernel: $(uname -srm)"
  echo "git_sha: $SHA"
  echo "expected_sha: ${EXPECTED_SHA:-same-as-git}"
  echo "cargo: $(cargo --version 2>/dev/null)"
  echo "rustc: $(rustc --version 2>/dev/null)"
  echo "--- vulkan devices ---"
  vulkaninfo --summary 2>/dev/null | grep -E "deviceName|driverName|driverInfo|apiVersion" \
    || echo "vulkaninfo: not available"
  echo "--- gpu (lspci) ---"
  lspci 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "vga|3d controller|display" || echo "lspci: not available"
  echo "--- mesa package ---"
  dpkg-query -W -f='${Package} ${Version}\n' 'libgl1-mesa-dri' 'mesa-vulkan-drivers' 2>/dev/null \
    || echo "dpkg mesa query: not available"
  echo "--- vram (rocm-smi, if present) ---"
  rocm-smi --showmeminfo vram 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "used|total" || echo "rocm-smi: not available"
  echo "--- run flags ---"
  echo "dump arm:  RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats,asm,cs WGPU_COMPUTE_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS=16 WGPU_COMPUTE_MMQ_WIDE_MIN_ROWS=32"
  echo "perf arms: shipped defaults; arm B adds RADV_PERFTEST=cswave32"
  echo "each arm:  private MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR under $OUT"
  echo "model: $MODEL"
  echo "draft: $DRAFT"
  echo "ntok: $NTOK depth: $DEPTH"
} > "$OUT/env.txt" 2>&1
note "env captured: $OUT/env.txt"

[ -f "$MODEL" ] || { note "SKIP: model not found: $MODEL"; exit 0; }
[ -f "$DRAFT" ] || { note "SKIP: draft not found: $DRAFT"; exit 0; }

# --- 2. build --------------------------------------------------------
note "--- build ---"
cargo build --release -p itak-spec --example spec_generate_gpu 2>&1 | tail -2 | tee -a "$SUMMARY"
GEN="$ROOT/target/release/examples/spec_generate_gpu"
[ -x "$GEN" ] || { note "FAIL: spec_generate_gpu did not build"; exit 1; }
cargo test --release -p wgpu-compute --test resident_session --no-run 2>&1 | tail -2 | tee -a "$SUMMARY"
FIXTURE="$(ls -t "$ROOT"/target/release/deps/resident_session-* 2>/dev/null | grep -v '\.d$' | head -1)"
[ -n "$FIXTURE" ] && [ -x "$FIXTURE" ] || { note "FAIL: resident_session test binary not found"; exit 1; }
note "fixture binary: $FIXTURE"
cargo test --release -p wgpu-compute --test shader_compile --no-run 2>&1 | tail -2 | tee -a "$SUMMARY"
SHADER_COMPILE="$(ls -t "$ROOT"/target/release/deps/shader_compile-* 2>/dev/null | grep -v '\.d$' | head -1)"
[ -n "$SHADER_COMPILE" ] && [ -x "$SHADER_COMPILE" ] || { note "FAIL: shader_compile test binary not found"; exit 1; }
note "shader_compile binary: $SHADER_COMPILE"

# Memory discipline for the model runs on the shared server
# (recorded server rule: arena caps keep the 17 GB load from
# fragmenting the box's tight RAM).
export MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2
export MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_=0

# --- 3. dump arm -----------------------------------------------------
note "--- dump arm (all kernel families on, RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats,asm,cs) ---"
mkdir -p "$OUT/cache-allon"
RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats,asm,cs \
MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR="$OUT/cache-allon" \
WGPU_COMPUTE_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS=16 \
WGPU_COMPUTE_MMQ_WIDE_MIN_ROWS=32 \
  "$GEN" "$MODEL" "$DRAFT" "$NTOK" "$DEPTH" \
  > "$OUT/allon.stdout.log" 2> "$OUT/allon.stderr.log"
note "verdict run exit: $? (dumps in allon.stderr.log, $(wc -c < "$OUT/allon.stderr.log") bytes)"
grep -E "IDENTITY|GOLDEN|SPEED|T-9.6|tok/s" "$OUT/allon.stdout.log" | tail -6 | tee -a "$SUMMARY" || true

mkdir -p "$OUT/cache-fixture"
RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats,asm,cs \
MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR="$OUT/cache-fixture" \
  "$FIXTURE" --nocapture \
  > "$OUT/fixture.stdout.log" 2> "$OUT/fixture.stderr.log"
note "mixed fixture exit: $? (dumps in fixture.stderr.log, $(wc -c < "$OUT/fixture.stderr.log") bytes)"

# --- 3b. family isolation ---------------------------------------------
note "--- family isolation (shader_compile, one family per run) ---"
for fam in k1_shader_compiles k2_k3_shaders_compile k12_k14_mmq_shaders_compile \
           k10_k11_gemm_shaders_compile k17_dflash_shaders_compile \
           k15_k16_mmq_wide_shaders_compile k18_small_batch_shaders_compile \
           k4_to_k8_pipelines_compile; do
  mkdir -p "$OUT/cache-fam-$fam"
  RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats,asm,cs \
  MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR="$OUT/cache-fam-$fam" \
    "$SHADER_COMPILE" "$fam" --nocapture \
    > "$OUT/family-$fam.stdout.log" 2> "$OUT/family-$fam.stderr.log"
  note "family $fam exit: $? stats blocks: $(grep -c 'SHADER STATS' "$OUT/family-$fam.stderr.log")"
done

# --- 4. perf arms (single data points) --------------------------------
run_perf() {
  local arm="$1"; shift
  mkdir -p "$OUT/cache-$arm"
  note "--- perf arm: $arm ($*) ---"
  env MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR="$OUT/cache-$arm" "$@" \
    "$GEN" "$MODEL" "$DRAFT" "$NTOK" "$DEPTH" \
    > "$OUT/perf-$arm.stdout.log" 2> "$OUT/perf-$arm.stderr.log"
  note "perf $arm exit: $?"
  grep -E "plain stream" "$OUT/perf-$arm.stdout.log" | tail -1 | tee -a "$SUMMARY" || true
  grep -E "IDENTITY|GOLDEN|SPEED|T-9.6" "$OUT/perf-$arm.stdout.log" | tail -4 | tee -a "$SUMMARY" || true
  grep -E "verify|draft|round" "$OUT/perf-$arm.stdout.log" | tail -6 | tee -a "$SUMMARY" || true
}
run_perf control
run_perf cswave32 RADV_PERFTEST=cswave32

# --- 5. stats extract ---------------------------------------------------
# Pull every stats block out of the dump logs into one small
# file for hand analysis: a block starts at a line naming
# shader statistics and runs until the next blank line.
python3 - "$OUT" <<'PYEOF' || note "stats extract: python3 pass failed, raw logs hold everything"
import re, sys, pathlib
out = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
pat = re.compile(r"(vgpr|sgpr|spilled|scratch|lds|code size)", re.I)
import glob
names = ["allon.stderr.log", "fixture.stderr.log"] + \
        sorted(p.name for p in out.glob("family-*.stderr.log"))
for name in names:
    src = out / name
    if not src.exists():
        continue
    lines = src.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
    blocks, cur = [], None
    for ln in lines:
        if re.search(r"shader statistics|shader stats", ln, re.I):
            if cur: blocks.append(cur)
            cur = [ln]
        elif cur is not None:
            if ln.strip() == "" :
                blocks.append(cur); cur = None
            elif pat.search(ln):
                cur.append(ln)
    if cur: blocks.append(cur)
    dst = out / (name.replace(".stderr.log", "") + ".stats-extract.txt")
    dst.write_text("\n\n".join("\n".join(b) for b in blocks) + "\n")
    print(f"{name}: {len(blocks)} stats blocks -> {dst.name}")
PYEOF

note "AUTOPSY_DONE"

===== FILE: bench/small-batch-2026-11-04.md =====
# Small-batch products (K18): design, expectations, server proof

## The problem, measured

From bench/spec-gpu-port-2026-11-03.md's round economics
addendum (RX 7900 XTX, main 72a4b9d): below
GEMM_MIN_ROWS (16), the resident session's projections
run GEMV form, one full weight stream per row. The
probe fits rows x 16 GB at about 815 GB/s exactly
(1 row 30 ms, 2 rows 47 ms, 7 rows 140 ms). A depth-6
speculative round pays about 151 ms of verify, most of
it a 7-row forward re-streaming the target seven
times; the DFlash draft's 16-row block forward pays
57.3 ms the same way. Lowering the matrix threshold
to 2 was tested and killed with data: 7-row forwards
got slower (140 to 253 ms) and the dispatch count
roughly doubled, because the GEMM and MMQ tiles are
built for 32 and 64 rows.

## What K18 is

`crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/k18_small_batch.rs`:
the MMQ math at a tile sized for the band.

- One weight stream per dispatch: a workgroup owns a
  tile of 32 or 64 output rows and ALL batch rows in
  the pass (2..=16), stages the tile's packed weight
  words once per super-block column, and applies them
  to every row from workgroup memory. Global weight
  traffic per dispatch is the tensor's bytes, once,
  at any row count in the band.
- The math is K13/K14's, term for term: K12's Q8_1
  activations, exact i32 DP4A dots per sub-block, the
  per-sub-block scale fold (Q4_K's expression for
  Q4_K and Q5_K; Q6_K's per-half fold with the -32
  offset). Per-thread sub-tile is the same 4x4; with
  four batch lanes the workgroup is `tile_n` threads.
- Q5_K's stage assembles each element's 5-bit quant
  into its own byte (ql nibble plus bit `j` of
  `qh[l]`), K14's assembly idiom; it is the only new
  stage. Q4_K's and Q6_K's stages are their MMQ
  siblings' text.
- Staging bytes: Q4_K and Q5_K 15,424 at tile 32
  (fits a default-limits 16 KiB grant), 25,664 at
  tile 64; Q6_K 16,448 at tile 32 (64 bytes over the
  default grant, so Q6_K reports absence there and
  keeps GEMV, the K13/K14 contract), 26,688 at 64.
- Refusals by name: batch outside 1..=16, width not a
  whole number of super-blocks, tile widths outside
  {32, 64}, staging over the device's grant.

## Routing, and the shipped default

One wiring place: `prepare_proj` in session.rs, the
plain-projection ladder every layer projection in
the resident chain goes through (QKV batch, the
plain attention-out form, FFN gate/up). Per family
the ladder is now: matrix forms at 16 rows and up
(unchanged), then K18 inside the configured band,
then GEMV. The band is config in compute.rs, wide-MMQ
style: `WGPU_COMPUTE_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS`, resolved
at backend construction and logged. The shipped
default is 1, which is OFF: no batch qualifies.

The default is deliberate, and it is the wide-MMQ
lesson applied to this lane's own kernel: K15/K16
were numerically correct, entered the ladder, and
then measured 3.5x slower per tensor and hung a real
session. K18's streaming math is sound and its
parity is gated, but nothing about it is measured on
a real card yet, so merged main must not route a
single projection through it until the server proof
below says otherwise. The proof moving the default
is a follow-up commit, not this lane's assumption.

Out of this lane's scope, plainly:

- The gated and SwiGLU projection forms keep their
  own ladders (their quantize is a different K12
  variant); at small rows they still GEMV. The
  verify forward's down projection is one of them,
  so a wired round keeps that tensor's per-row
  streams until a follow-on extends K18's wiring.
- The output head keeps K3's fused finish: the
  block-logits path prepares it directly, not
  through prepare_proj, because the softcap finish
  must not change family with batch. Its 0.92 GB
  stream per row set is not covered here.
- The DFlash draft's block forward composes its own
  GEMV calls inside dflash_session.rs; its 57 ms is
  the same disease in a second patient and is the
  named follow-on after the verify side proves.

## Expectations, labeled

These are arithmetic on recorded measurements, not
results:

- Stream floor: one pass over the target's streamed
  projection bytes (about 16 GB) at the measured
  815 GB/s is about 20 ms, against about 140 ms for
  today's 7-row GEMV set. That is the floor the
  one-stream design aims at.
- Compute cross-check: the recorded MMQ per-tensor
  rate (Q4_K m64 product at 41,133 tok/s on the
  file's largest Q4_K tensor) works out to roughly
  1.4e12 DP4A/s sustained. A 7-row verify set is
  about 2.4e10 DP4A at the model's streamed element
  count, which prices the compute floor in the same
  20 ms class. The two floors agree, which is the
  design's premise: at these row counts neither DRAM
  nor DP4A should dominate if the small tiles hold
  MMQ-class efficiency.
- Landing band, stated as an expectation: the 7-row
  verify projection set lands between 20 and 45 ms
  (from about 140). The risks that could push it out
  of the band are the small workgroups' staging share
  and register pressure in the unrolled inner loop;
  the rows table below exists to measure exactly
  that.
- Round-level honesty: even at the band's low end,
  K18 alone does not close T-9.6's 88.6 bar. The
  draft's 57 ms, the unwired down projection and
  head, and acceptance economics at depth 6
  (1.97 tokens per round at acceptance 0.172) all
  still stand. K18 removes the verify stream
  multiplier, which the round accounting names as
  the largest single term.

## Server proof sequence

On the server (RX 7900 XTX), staged from the lane
tip, one heavy job at a time:

1. Parity gates execute (no skips):
   `cargo test -p wgpu-compute --test k18_small_batch -- --nocapture`
   Four tests: per-family parity at batches
   [1, 2, 3, 7, 15, 16] against the host quantized
   reference at the reassociation bar and against
   the family's GEMV product inside the 5% band
   with the tie-ruled argmax check, plus the deep
   geometry test at width 768 and 230 output rows.
2. Compile leg executes:
   `cargo test -p wgpu-compute --test shader_compile k18_small_batch`
   on the card's full limits (all candidates of all
   three families compile) and the default-limits
   positions (Q4_K/Q5_K build at s32, Q6_K absent).
3. Rows table on the real tensors:
   `cargo run --release -p wgpu-compute --example small_batch_bench`
   Read the gemv vs `k18 s64 + quantize` lines at
   rows 2, 7, and 16 per family, and the mmq line
   at 16. The claim to check: k18 + quantize beats
   gemv at every row from 2 up, by a factor growing
   with rows, and does not lose to mmq at 16 by
   enough to matter (the session routes 16 to mmq
   first anyway).
4. Session verdicts, threshold on vs off:
   `WGPU_COMPUTE_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS=16` in the
   environment, run itak-spec's `spec_generate_gpu`
   against the real target and draft files at
   depth 6 and depth 1, greedy, Stage 1 prompt.
   Control: the same runs with the variable unset.
   IDENTITY and GOLDEN must PASS in both positions;
   compare effective tok/s against the recorded
   baselines (depth 6: 9.21, depth 1: 14.60).
   The construction log must show
   `small batch config: max_rows=16` in the on
   position and `max_rows=1` in the control.
5. If 3 and 4 hold, the follow-up commit moves
   `DEFAULT_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS` to 16 (at batch
   16 the matrix branch still owns the row when MMQ
   exists; 16 only extends K18's reach to devices
   without it) and records the measured rows table
   and verdict numbers in this note.

## Server proof verdict (2026-11-04, RX 7900 XTX, main ef6ca5d)

Correctness: perfect. The k18_small_batch parity gate executed on
the card (worst vs-GEMV band diff 0.0045, argmax full at every
batch), the shader compile leg passed, and all four verdict runs
printed IDENTITY PASS and GOLDEN PASS with no hang and no lost
context.

Performance: a loss, and the default stays OFF.
- Depth 6: control 9.19 tok/s (verify 149.8 ms) against K18 on
  8.13 tok/s (verify 178.0 ms, up 28.2).
- Depth 1: control 14.22 tok/s (verify 55.3 ms) against K18 on
  8.90 tok/s (verify 125.1 ms, up 69.8).
- draft_ms unchanged in the on position, as designed (the draft
  session is not wired to K18).

Mechanism, measured: K18 does stream the weights once (its
per-tensor time is flat in rows), but at about 70 to 130 GB/s,
where GEMV streams the same tensors at up to 676 GB/s. The
one-stream saving only overtakes GEMV's per-row restreaming at
rows 12 and up on the largest tensors, outside the verify band of
2 to 7 rows. The design's staging through workgroup memory is
the rate ceiling. K18 stays in the tree, opt-in by env, with this
table as the baseline any second attempt must beat. The blocker
for T-9.6's speed half is now named at the last level: a shared
weight kernel that streams at GEMV's rate, which neither the
wide MMQ nor K18 achieved.

===== END FILE: bench/small-batch-2026-11-04.md =====

===== FILE: bench/socket-seam-fixes-2026-11-07.md =====
# Socket seam fixes: engine authentication and stale-frame recovery (2026-11-07)

Lane `lane/socket-seam-auth-recovery`, from main 85beb8a.
Two HIGH findings from the cold critic panel
(`~/workspace/reports/critic-engine-2026-11-07/CRITIC-ENGINE-MERGE.md`,
Category D), both on the Go platform's Unix-socket seam to the Rust
engine. The Failure seat's verdict for this path was NO-SHIP on its
own; the Security seat's was DO NOT SHIP until these two are fixed.

## Finding 1 (HIGH, Security seat): the dial never authenticated the engine

`platform/internal/engine/unix.go` (dialRaw/handshake): the platform
checked only that something at the socket path answered `hello_ack`
with proto 1. The protocol shapes are public, and the default path
is the predictable `/tmp/itak-engine.sock`, so a squatter bound
there during a restart window received all prompt traffic and could
forge completions. The Rust engine authenticates its side
(`bind_socket` pins the file to 0600; `check_peer` refuses a peer
whose SO_PEERCRED uid differs); the platform authenticated nothing.

### Fix

Before any dial (the control connection in `DialUnix` and
Generate's per-call connection share `dialRaw`, so no path reaches
the peer unchecked), `checkSocketTrust` stats the socket file and
refuses by name with the new `ErrUntrustedSocket` unless all three
hold: the file is a socket, its owner uid equals this process's
uid, and its permissions are exactly 0600. This mirrors the engine
side's two facts: the mode it pins, and uid equality, which is the
same predicate `check_peer` enforces from the other direction.

Which layers were built, and why: the panel offered the stat check
or SO_PEERCRED via `SyscallConn` + `GetsockoptUcred`, and preferred
both if the ucred read is clean in this codebase's dependency set.
It is not: `platform/go.mod` is standard-library only, and
`GetsockoptUcred` lives in `golang.org/x/sys/unix`, so the peer-cred
read would add the platform's first external dependency for one
syscall. The stat check alone is the panel's stated minimum and is
built. The residual stat-to-dial race is narrower than it looks: a
replacement socket file at the path can only be created by a
same-uid process (or root), because binding requires unlinking or
creating the directory entry, and the engine's path lives where
only the owner can do that in supported deployments; a same-uid
impostor is inside the trust boundary the engine itself accepts
(its peer check passes any same-uid process). The check lives in
`socket_unix.go` (`//go:build unix`), with the pure predicate
`socketTrustOK` split out for unit tests; `socket_other.go` keeps
non-unix builds verifying the arms they can read (socket type and
mode).

Supervisor interaction: `dialUntil` retries ANY dial error until
its deadline and then fails the launch by name, so a trust refusal
surfaces as an error and a restart-budget entry, never as a hang
and never as "engine is serving". The refusal is deliberately NOT
wrapped in `ErrUnavailable`: the retry behavior is identical, but
the supervisor's log line names the trust failure instead of
reading as a slow engine start. `cmd/torchd`'s one-shot `dialEngine`
treats it the same way (starts with the engine marked unavailable
and logs the named error).

One behavior consequence, stated plainly: the platform now refuses
any engine socket not pinned to 0600. The real engine has always
pinned its socket, so supported deployments are unaffected; test
fakes that stand in for the engine now pin theirs too (see Tests).

## Finding 2 (HIGH, Failure seat, probe-proven): stale frame after a timeout

`exchangeAnyLocked` read replies from the shared buffered reader
with no recovery: when an exchange timed out, the engine's late
reply stayed buffered, and the next exchange consumed it as its
own. The seat's executed probe: after a 100 ms-timeout `DebugInfo`
against an engine answering at 400 ms, the first `Health` ate the
stale `debug_info` frame and reported the healthy engine down
(`got op "debug_info", want "pong"`). Worse, two consecutive Embed
calls share the reply op, so a timed-out Embed's late vectors could
be returned to the next Embed caller as its result, silently.

### Fix

The control connection is now retired on any read failure that can
leave its frame stream desynchronized:

- a read timeout (the reply may still be in flight);
- a partial frame consumed before the failure (its remainder is
  in flight);
- an oversized frame (its unread tail is still in the stream);
- a failed write (the peer's state for that frame is unknowable).

`readFrame` now reports whether the failed read consumed a partial
frame, and `exchangeAnyLocked` poisons the client in the cases
above: the connection closes, the client is marked closed, the
failing call keeps its existing named error (`ErrTimeout`,
`ErrFrameTooLarge`, `ErrHandshake` as classified today), and every
later call refuses with `ErrClosed`. A clean refusal before any
byte is consumed (the engine hung up between requests) does NOT
poison: nothing can be stale, and the next exchange fails or
succeeds on its own. Generate's per-call connections are untouched
beyond the shared `readFrame` signature: a generate stream owns
its connection end to end, so no other caller can consume its
frames.

Supervisor interaction: the supervisor's serving path returns
whatever the live client returns, so a poisoned client surfaces
`ErrClosed` by name (Health reports `client closed`, the same
honest state as after an explicit Close) instead of wrong answers.
The supervisor drops its client when the incarnation dies and
redials on the next launch, which is the existing recovery path;
the regression tests pin that a fresh dial on the same socket
serves normally and returns each request its own reply. What does
not exist, before or after this lane: supervisor detection of a
poisoned-but-process-alive client between incarnation deaths (the
engine process is healthy in the timeout scenario, so no death
fires a redial). That is recorded below as an adjacent gap, not
silently claimed as covered.

## Evidence: fails before, passes after

The panel's probe was reproduced first, in its exact shape (fake
engine answers `debug` after 400 ms; caller context 100 ms; then
`Health`), as a scratch test against the unfixed tree:

- Before: `DebugInfo` returns `ErrTimeout`; the next `Health`
  returns `ok=false, "engine: handshake failed: got op
  \"debug_info\", want \"pong\""` — the healthy engine reported
  down by the stale frame. BUG REPRODUCED, matching the seat's
  probe output.
- After: the same probe's `Health` returns `ok=false, "client
  closed"` — the client was retired by the timed-out exchange and
  the stale frame was never consumed. (The scratch probe was
  deleted after serving as the before/after witness; its shape
  lives on as `TestTimeoutPoisonsControlConnection`.)
- Fails-before for the new dial tests cannot be a compile-clean
  run on the unfixed tree (they name the new `ErrUntrustedSocket`),
  so the before-state evidence for Finding 1 is the seat's code
  read plus the behavioral fact the probe relies on: on the
  unfixed tree the squatter-shaped listener (no 0600 pin) dials
  and handshakes successfully — every pre-existing fake-engine
  test did exactly that, which is why the fakes had to learn the
  pin (below).

## Tests

New, in `platform/internal/engine/unix_seam_test.go` and
`socket_unix_test.go`:

- `TestDialRefusesSocketWithLoosePermissions`: a protocol-correct
  listener whose socket file is not pinned to 0600 refuses with
  `ErrUntrustedSocket`, and not as `ErrUnavailable`.
- `TestDialAcceptsOwnerOnlySocket`: the 0600 happy path dials,
  handshakes, and reports healthy.
- `TestDialMissingSocketIsUnavailableNotUntrusted`: the two dial
  failures stay distinct (startup race vs trust refusal).
- `TestDialRefusesNonSocketFile`: a regular file at 0600 refuses.
- `TestSocketTrustOK`: the predicate arm by arm (the uid arm is
  pinned here because a test process cannot fabricate a socket
  file owned by another uid), and `TestCheckSocketTrustArms` runs
  the stat wrapper under the owner's uid (pass) and a foreign uid
  (refuse).
- `TestTimeoutPoisonsControlConnection`: the probe as a
  regression — timeout, then Health reports `client closed`,
  then exchanges refuse with `ErrClosed`.
- `TestEmbedAfterTimeoutNeverReturnsStaleVectors`: a timed-out
  Embed's late reply can never answer the next Embed; a fresh
  dial returns each request its own vectors.

Adjusted, with reasons:

- The fake engines in `engine_test.go` (`fakeEngine`,
  `capturingEngine`, `noTemplateEngine`), `unix_bounds_test.go`
  (`scriptedEngine`), and `supervisor_test.go`'s fake engine
  process now chmod their sockets to 0600 after binding, modeling
  the real engine; without it the new check refuses them, which
  is the check working as designed.
- `TestOversizedReplyFrameRefusedByName`: its secondary surface
  asserted Health's detail would name the frame cap after an
  oversized reply. Under the stale-frame rule the oversized
  frame's tail retires the client, so Health now reports
  `client closed`; the primary assertion (DebugInfo refuses with
  `ErrFrameTooLarge`) is unchanged, and the test now also pins
  that the tail is never consumed as a reply.

# Speculative loop on the GPU-resident stack: the T-9.6 port

Date: 2026-11-03. Branch: `lane/spec-gpu` (base 31634aa). Status:
the port is built and locally gated; the T-9.6 verdict itself is
**not yet proven**, because the two proofs that need a real GPU
(the resident block tests at full execution and the server runner
below) have not run. This note records the design, what is proven
where, the one hard blocker on the speed bar, and the exact server
run still owed. T-9.6 stays open until that run lands.

## What was built

Four commits on the lane branch:

1. `eb72e86` wgpu-compute: resident block logits, layer captures,
   and bounded rewind (session.rs).
2. `62d94dd` wgpu-compute: resident block, capture, and rewind
   tests (tests/resident_block.rs). They do not execute on this
   VM: it enumerates no suitable adapter, so they take the skip
   path here (verified with `--nocapture`: "no suitable adapter
   (enumerated: [])"). They execute on a host with a qualifying
   adapter, the server.
3. `3cc9406` itak-spec: the TargetDriver seam, CpuTarget,
   ResidentTarget, and the stub-driver loop tests.
4. The runner and this note (the commit carrying this file).

## Design decisions

**The loop is generic over a target driver seam; nothing else
moved.** `crates/itak-spec/src/driver.rs` names exactly the
operations the loop performs (config, position, forward,
forward_capturing, forward_block_capturing, checkpoint, rewind,
release). `CpuTarget` wraps the original CPU path unchanged
(model, shared compute, position cache; checkpoint/rewind/release
order preserved), and every pre-existing session test passes
unmodified in behavior (33 tests). `ResidentTarget`
(`resident.rs`) drives the existing `ResidentSession`; the draft
side (`Speculator` seam, `DflashSpeculator`) is untouched.

**The verify forward is the existing resident chain, never a
second forward.** Three additions to `ResidentSession`, all on
the one chain:

- *Block tail.* A verify chunk runs a standalone final norm over
  every row of stream A (the chain leaves every row's final
  residual there; the last layer's close writes it for all rows
  and only additionally emits the standard head input for the
  last row), then the head at the chunk's batch. The head keeps
  the standard head's arithmetic family at any batch: a Q5_K
  head takes K3's fused finishing at batch = rows; Q4_K/Q6_K
  heads take their GEMV prepares plus the K8 finish over the
  flattened rows, instead of `prepare_proj`'s matrix forms,
  because the head is a GEMV at the only size the standard path
  runs (one row) and the block tail must not change families as
  the batch grows. Dispatch accounting swaps the standard head
  segment's share of the plan's count for the block segment's.
- *Captures.* A capturing chunk encodes the chain as one compute
  pass per layer range, with an encoder copy of stream A into a
  capture staging at each named layer's entry (every layer
  enters with its residual in stream A; layer 0's input is the
  post-norm stream, exactly what the CPU model's
  `forward_capturing` returns). Copies are not dispatches and
  are not counted, consistent with the existing readback copies.
  Captures merge across chunks in position order, matching the
  model's contract.
- *Rewind.* `rewind_to(position)` restores the position counter;
  entries past it are never read (views derive from position)
  and are overwritten positionally. Soundness bound, derived
  from the ring geometry: windowed slots are `position % ring`
  with ring = window + MAX_CHUNK_ROWS - 1, so a discarded write
  can alias a committed key inside a later query's window only
  when the discarded span exceeds MAX_CHUNK_ROWS (64). The
  method refuses spans over 64 by name (`session` step);
  `reset()` remains the full-rewind path. A speculative round
  discards at most depth + 1 (default 17), well inside the bound.
  On this driver a checkpoint is therefore just the position at
  checkpoint time and release is a no-op; `resident.rs` says why
  that is sound rather than lazy.

**The draft has no GPU path; it stays on CPU behind the same
seam.** `crates/dflash`'s `DflashModel` is its own CPU
implementation and does not consume the `Compute` trait, so
there is no existing GPU draft to wire. Per the tasking, the
port drives it on the best existing backend (CPU) behind the
unchanged `Speculator` seam and names the consequence below
instead of inventing a draft GPU path inside this item.

**Identity on GPU is empirical, not construction-exact.** On CPU
the speculative stream is token-identical by construction (same
code path). On GPU, identity rests on a multi-row chunk agreeing
with sequential one-row forwards at argmax resolution; the
resident cross-path tests bound that drift at about 1.1e-6 on
logits. One configuration rule follows: chunks of 16+ rows take
the MMQ path, whose Q8_1 activation quantization makes logits
approximate by design (measured band 0.36 to 0.42 percent of
result scale). At the default depth 6 a verify block is 7 rows,
so the proof configuration stays on the GEMV chain end to end.
The runner measures identity on the real files; nothing here
claims it by construction.

## The speed blocker, stated plainly

The T-9.6 bar is effective tok/s at or above 88.6. The verify
side can plausibly reach it (the llama.cpp sweep's depth-6
operating point, 107.39 tok/s at acceptance 0.541, implies the
shape works when drafting is cheap). This build's drafting is
not cheap: the CPU draft block forward measured 9.9 s for a
4-row block on the server (`bench/dflash-e3-2026-10-30.md`), and
spec-loop rounds measured draft time at roughly 31 to 35 s per
16-row block. Against verify rounds that cost tens of
milliseconds on the resident GPU, a CPU draft at seconds per
block puts the effective rate orders of magnitude under the
bar. **Expect the server run to print SPEED: FAIL.** The
identity half of T-9.6 is fully provable by the same run. The
named missing component is a GPU path for the DFlash draft
model (its own item; T-9.7's depth/acceptance sweep should run
on this stack after it exists, since the winning depth depends
on the draft's real cost). The runner's `--bar` flag exists so
that future runs can judge against a revised bar without a code
change; the default stays the recorded 88.6.

## What is proven locally (this VM, no qualifying GPU adapter)

Commands run from the lane worktree with
`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$PWD/target`:

- `cargo test -p itak-spec`: 35 passed, 0 failed. The 33
  pre-existing tests (greedy identity vs plain at depths 1/2/4/6,
  sabotage refusal and latch, creation refusals, call order) pass
  through the refactored seam unchanged. The 2 new stub-driver
  tests prove the loop through the seam without model
  arithmetic: greedy identity between a DFlash session and a
  mode-off session over a deterministic stub driver, and
  per-round rewind targets landing exactly on base + 1 +
  accepted with checkpoint/release pairing (one each per round)
  and cumulative stats equal to the summed round outcomes.
- `cargo test -p wgpu-compute`: whole suite green. The two new
  `resident_block` tests (block logits and captures vs the CPU
  model's block forward at the cross-backend bar; rewind
  soundness and both refusal shapes) **compile and skip** here:
  "no suitable adapter (enumerated: [])". The pre-existing GPU
  tests skip the same way on this VM; nothing GPU-side executed
  locally. This is the honest limit of the local proof.
- `cargo clippy -p wgpu-compute --all-targets` and
  `cargo clippy -p itak-spec --all-targets`: clean (workspace
  lints deny warnings). `cargo fmt` applied per crate.
- The runner builds (`cargo build -p itak-spec --example
  spec_generate_gpu`) and its usage path exits 2 with the usage
  line, mirroring the CPU runner.

## The server run still owed (exactly)

Preconditions: the server GPU free (parent clears it), the lane
branch landed on the server tree, release build.


`cargo test -p wgpu-compute --test resident_block` (both tests
must execute, not skip).

What the run must show to close T-9.6's identity half:
`IDENTITY: PASS` (spec stream token-identical to the plain
resident GPU stream at temperature 0) and `GOLDEN: PASS` (first
8 tokens [13796, 26, 1573, 373, 290, 2167, 26899, 1212]).
The combined line will read "CORRECTNESS PASS, SPEED FAIL"
until a GPU draft path exists; the exit code follows the
correctness contract, the CPU runner's convention, so the two
halves are never confused. If IDENTITY fails, the first
divergence position prints with both streams, and the suspects
in order are: block-tail arithmetic family drift at 7 rows,
capture row misalignment feeding the draft, and ring aliasing
inside the rewind span (the span here is at most 7, far inside
the proven bound, so this should be last).

## Files in this port

  plan segment, segmented capturing encode, `forward_capturing`,
  `forward_block_capturing`, `rewind_to`, module docs.
- `crates/wgpu-compute/tests/resident_block.rs`: the block,
  capture, and rewind pins.
- `crates/itak-spec/src/driver.rs`: the `TargetDriver` trait,
  `CpuTarget`, and the stub-driver loop tests.
- `crates/itak-spec/src/resident.rs`: `ResidentTarget`.

  the driver (default `CpuTarget`); driver accessors.

## Server verdict (2026-11-04, RX 7900 XTX, main 864dffd + the K17 brace fix)

Ran on the real card against the real files, greedy, 64 tokens,
Stage 1 prompt. Plain arm: first 8 tokens
[13796, 26, 1573, 373, 290, 2167, 26899, 1212], 35.66 tok/s decode.

- CPU-draft arm: IDENTITY PASS, GOLDEN PASS. Acceptance 0.172
  through the shared conditioning path.
- GPU-draft arm: IDENTITY PASS, GOLDEN PASS. Effective 4.79 tok/s.
- SPEED: FAIL. 4.79 against the 88.6 bar.

Root cause is one defect, caught independently by the
dflash_session parity gate: the GPU draft's block forward diverges
from the CPU reference (fixture parity fails at block row 0,
argmax 4 vs 248; the fuse stage passes the drift bar and the inject
bookkeeping matches, so the divergence sits in the per-layer chain
or the K17 attention). Acceptance collapses to 0.003 (1 of 351),
and with no accepted drafts the loop pays verify cost for nothing.
Per-round cost with a working draft is fine (62 rounds in about
13.2 s of generate). T-9.6 stays OPEN: correctness is proven on
both arms; the speed half waits on the draft parity fix.

## Draft parity fix and re-verdict (2026-11-04, RX 7900 XTX)

The divergence is found and fixed. Root cause: BlockPlan cached a
single attention-call index, overwritten per layer, so only the
LAST draft layer's attention call received the per-block runtime
values (block start, committed count). Every earlier layer
attended over zero committed positions at block start 0; the
committed KV was written correctly, the earlier layers never
looked at it. Bisection proof: the fixture passes in full at 1
layer and fails at 2. The fix stores every layer's attention index
and rewrites all of them per block (dflash_session.rs, one file).

After the fix: the dflash_session parity gate is 4 of 4 green on
the card, and on the real files the GPU draft's bookkeeping equals
the CPU draft's exactly (32 rounds, 180 proposed, 31 accepted,
acceptance 0.172 in both arms). IDENTITY PASS, GOLDEN PASS.
Effective speed 9.22 tok/s: SPEED STILL FAILS the 88.6 bar. With
a correct draft the blocker is economics, not correctness: at
depth 6 acceptance 0.172 yields 1.97 tokens per round against a
full target verify forward per round, and the loop trails plain
decode (35.45 tok/s the same night). T-9.6 stays OPEN on its
speed half: acceptance economics and verify cost are the work now.

## Round economics (2026-11-04, RX 7900 XTX, main 72a4b9d)

The round is now fully accounted for. Per round at depth 6, from
the loop's own diag: draft 62.1 ms, verify 151.0 ms, residual
about 4 ms (checkpoint, correction walk, rewind, emission).
Submissions, readbacks, captures and rollback are all cleared
with numbers; the 5.66 MB block-logits readback is about 1 ms.

The cost is the projection form. Below GEMM_MIN_ROWS (16),
projections run GEMV: one full weight stream per row. The probe
fits rows x 16 GB at about 815 GB/s exactly (1 row 30 ms, 2 rows
47 ms, 7 rows 140 ms), so a 7-row verify pays seven streams. The
draft's 16-row block has the same disease at smaller scale
(57.3 ms). Lowering the threshold to 2 was tested and killed with
data: 7-row forwards got slower (140 to 253 ms) and the MMQ
dispatch count roughly doubled, because the existing GEMM tiles
are built for 32 and 64 rows. What is missing is a purpose-built
small-batch matrix kernel that streams the weights once for
2 to 16 rows; that is also the prefill chain's missing piece.

One real cut landed: the greedy propose path built vocab-width
one-hot vectors for every proposed token on every round (5.66 MB
of zeros, 2.04 ms of host time) to back a trait view the loop
never reads. The greedy arm now stores no distributions
(speculator.rs). Re-verdict after the cut: depth 6 effective
9.21 tok/s, depth 1 effective 14.60 tok/s, IDENTITY and GOLDEN
PASS on both. SPEED STILL FAILS the 88.6 bar, with the blocker
now precise: about 150 ms verify plus about 58 ms draft per
round, both small-batch projection cost.

# Speculative loop real-file proof: itak-spec against the real Glimmer files (2026-10-30)

Runner: `crates/itak-spec/examples/spec_generate.rs` (release build),
run on ubuntu-server, CPU reference backend throughout. The two phases
ran as separate processes (mode `plain`, then mode `spec` reading the
plain stream back from `plain_stream.txt`), launched by a script file
so no shell layer could mangle the arguments; the running process's
argv was verified NUL-separated in `/proc` before trusting any
output. Staging: `~/spec-run-b-2026-10-30` on the server, built from
commit 499ecce (the crate itself landed in dcaf130). Files:

- Target: `/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf`
- Draft: `/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/dflash-Muse-Glimmer-30B-Q4_K_M.gguf`
  (coverage 58/58 through the loader gate)
- Prompt: "The capital of France is" (ids [200000, 954, 7963, 323,
  11698, 373] with BOS), 16 tokens generated, depth 6, temperature 0.

## Verdict

- IDENTITY: PASS. The speculative stream is token-identical to plain
  greedy over all 16 tokens:
  [13796, 26, 1573, 373, 290, 2167, 26899, 1212, 6996, 310, 11698,
  341, 290, 2167, 26899, 1212].
- GOLDEN: PASS. The first 8 tokens match the verified continuation
  from bench/gpu-proof-2026-10-30.md.

## Plain phase (the baseline)

- Load 8.3 s. Prefill (6 prompt tokens) 1569.0 s.
- Decode 676.5 s for the 15 steps after the first token
  (42.28 s/token as the runner prints it, 45.1 s per step).
- Phase total 2250.5 s; whole process 2258.7 s.

## Speculative phase

- Load 8.6 s. Capturing prefill 1436.1 s, pending = 13796.
- Phase total 10231.7 s (639.48 s/token on the runner's
  total-over-tokens accounting).

| Round | Base | Proposed | Draft (s) | Verify (s) | Rewind | Accepted | First rejection | Emitted |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6 | 6 | 34.7 | 1740.0 | 13 to 8 | 1 | 2 | 2 |
| 2 | 8 | 6 | 35.2 | 1654.5 | 15 to 11 | 2 | 3 | 3 |
| 3 | 11 | 6 | 31.0 | 1643.9 | 18 to 13 | 1 | 2 | 2 |
| 4 | 13 | 6 | 30.3 | 1649.8 | 20 to 16 | 2 | 3 | 3 |
| 5 | 16 | 4 | 30.9 | 1251.8 | 21 to 19 | 2 | 3 | 3 |
| 6 | 19 | 1 | 31.4 | 650.8 | 21 to 21 | 1 | none | 2 |

Session totals: 6 rounds, 29 proposed, 9 accepted, acceptance rate
0.3103, 5 rejections, 5 rollbacks, 2.50 tokens per round, no fallback
latch. Rounds 5 and 6 were budget-capped by the remaining token
count (n = 4, then n = 1); round 6 accepted its whole capped block
and emitted the bonus token. The pending token at every round
boundary matches the plain stream at that position (13796, 1573,
2167, 1212, 11698, 2167), and every rewind lands exactly on
base + 1 + accepted, windowed rings included.

## What the numbers mean

On this backend a block-forward row costs about 250 s (verify totals
divided by rows), while a single-token decode step costs about
45 s: the multi-token path is roughly 5.5x the per-row price of the
single-token path, before speculation's arithmetic even starts. A
7-row verify therefore costs about 1650-1740 s to buy back at most
7 tokens, so the speculative loop cannot win on the CPU reference
backend, and this run does not pretend otherwise (phase totals:
2250.5 s plain vs 10231.7 s speculative for the same 16 tokens).
The mechanism is the deliverable: token identity at temperature 0
against the real files, a real 31 percent acceptance rate from the
trained draft at the sweep's depth 6, and the checkpoint/rewind
round running end to end on the real geometry (52 layers, window
2048 rings included). The speed case belongs to the GPU resident
path, where one submission evaluates the whole block (the remaining
half of TODO T-9.6, and T-9.7's sweep on this stack).

## Incident record (kept because it cost real time)

- The first attempt ran both phases in one process and was
  OOM-killed (kernel log 2026-10-30 13:30 UTC, 59.5 GB anon RSS):
  a duplicated launch put two instances into the same staging
  directory and log file, and their interleaved writes made the
  log unreadable as evidence. The runner was split into per-phase
  processes (commit 499ecce).
- The second attempt's phase B was OOM-killed at 56.9 GB RSS eight
  minutes in (borrowed embedding/head tables are 10.8 GB of f32 and
  the draft's dequantized weights about 10 GB on top of the
  target's footprint). Relaunched with MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 and
  MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_=0, phase B peaked at 44.5 GB early and
  completed; allocator arena retention was roughly 12 GB of the
  earlier peak.
- Two process launches were also corrupted by shell quoting on the
  prompt (word-split through the ssh layer turned mode and stream
  arguments into prompt words). The fix that ended the class:
  launch from a script file and verify /proc/<pid>/cmdline before
  believing a run.
- Intermediate monitoring readouts in this environment proved
  unreliable more than once (numbers that later direct reads of the
  same files contradicted). Every figure in this note was taken
  from a direct read of the final log files.

===== FILE: bench/spec-round-economics-2026-11-06.md =====
# Spec round economics: current cost map and the host-side trim, 2026-11-06

Lane `lane/spec-round-economics`, based on main `a064b5d7`
(code-identical to `c439e3af`, the tree the verdict session
staged: the diff between them over `crates/` and `platform/`
is empty). Question: what does one speculative round cost
now, per component, and what is left of the T-9.6 gap
(88.6 tok/s bar; best arm 19.26 tok/s at depth 1) that the
spec/draft/session layer can still take?

## Evidence

All numbers come from the 2026-11-06 cleared-card verdict
session's own records, server `~/gpu-wave11/logs11/`:

- `exposure.log`: spec phase B, depth 6,
  `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=16`, `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing`.
  Its 46k `[wgpu-compute-diag]` per-dispatch records were
  segmented by the `[diag] spec.round.begin`,
  `spec.propose.end`, and `spec.verify.end` markers into
  propose / verify / tail phases. Cross-checks: the propose
  segment's kernel totals reproduce the draft session's own
  aggregate (`exposure.csv`, the surviving report) to the
  dispatch once the tail-phase inject chain and the initial
  conditioning inject are added back (1,299.8 + 14.8 + ~1.3
  = 1,315.9 ms); the verify segment's dispatch count plus
  the one prefill forward lands within one dispatch of the
  target session's reported 14,717.
- `on-d1.log` / `on-d6.log` / `off-d1.log` / `off-d6.log`:
  the timing-off A/B arms (per-round `draft_ms` /
  `verify_ms` walls, session counters, verdict lines).
- `diag-plain.csv`: the plain `glimmer_generate` run's
  per-kernel aggregate (single-row GEMV streaming rates).

## The cost map

### Depth 6 (exposure run; round wall 166.0 ms = 63 tokens /
32 rounds / 11.86 tok/s effective)

| phase | wall ms | GPU ms | share |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| draft (propose) | 47.8 | 40.6 | 28.8% |
| verify | 114.2 | 102.0 | 68.8% |
| tail (walk + commit) | 4.0 (residual) | 0.5 | 2.4% |

Draft GPU, per round (the block is 16 positions at every
depth; see F3):

| kernel | dispatches | ms | share | weights | eff. rate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| k3_q5k_gemv (head) | 1 | 17.21 | 42.4% | 924.6 MB | 53.7 GB/s |
| k1_q4k_gemv | 25 | 14.00 | 34.5% | 920.1 MB | 65.7 GB/s |
| k2_q6k_gemv | 10 | 8.77 | 21.6% | 578.5 MB | 66.0 GB/s |
| k17_dflash_attend | 5 | 0.36 | 0.9% | - | - |
| norms / rotate / swiglu / gather | 47 | 0.27 | 0.7% | - | - |

Verify GPU, per round (7 rows):

| kernel | dispatches | ms | share |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| k19_q4k_mmv | 100.75 | 36.95 | 36.2% |
| k1_q4k_gemv (unrouted) | 81.25 | 26.60 | 26.1% |
| k2_q6k_gemv (unrouted) | 26.81 | 25.88 | 25.4% |
| k3_q5k_gemv (head, fused finish) | 1 | 7.55 | 7.4% |
| k4_norm_chain | 103 | 2.77 | 2.7% |
| k6_attn_flash | 52 | 1.65 | 1.6% |
| k20_q6k_mmv | 25.19 | 0.33 | 0.3% |
| rest | ~55 | 0.24 | 0.2% |

Timing-off cross-check (`on-d6.log`): round 191.7 ms =
draft 64.0 + verify 123.6 + residual 4.1. The draft wall is
the run-variable part (exposure: 47.8, tight 46-49; on-d6:
mean 64.0, spread 53-71); the kernel totals are the stable
part of the map.

### Depth 1 (the default; `on-d1.log`, timing off)

Round wall 86.1 ms = 63 tokens / 38 rounds / 19.26 tok/s.

| phase | wall ms | share | basis |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| draft (propose) | 45.7 | 53.1% | wall per round; GPU ≈ 40.6 (F3) |
| verify | 38.8 | 45.1% | wall per round (2 rows) |
| residual | 1.6 | 1.9% | round wall minus the two walls |

Control (`off-d1.log`, MMV unset): 97.6 = draft 48.3 +
verify 47.1 + residual 2.2. No timing-on depth-1 phase-B
run exists, so the depth-1 verify has no per-kernel split;
its structure is the depth-6 table's, at 2 rows.

## Findings

**F1. The round is a small-batch weight-streaming problem
on both sides.** The draft streams 2,423 MB of weights per
round in the GEMV batch form at 54-66 GB/s. Verify's
unrouted GEMV share (the gated projection and the SwiGLU
pair, which do not route through `prepare_proj`) costs
52.5 ms at depth 6, and K19, already routed, is still
verify's largest single item at 36.9 ms. Against all of
that, the same tensors in single-row GEMV form (plain
decode, `diag-plain.csv`) stream at 648.5-868.6 GB/s. The
card's ceiling is 960 GB/s; nothing in the round comes
close except the form that cannot batch.

**F2. The single largest kernel cost at the default depth
is the draft head:** one Q5_K GEMV dispatch, 17.21 ms,
42.4% of draft GPU and about 20% of the whole depth-1
round, streaming 924.6 MB at 53.7 GB/s. Plain decode
streams the same tensor shape at 868.6 GB/s (1.06 ms per
token, `diag-plain.csv`). 

**F3. The draft's GPU cost is depth-independent.**
`forward_block` always runs the full 16-token block
(`speculator.rs`: the block is `[pending, mask x 15]`
regardless of depth), so the depth-6 draft kernel table is
also the depth-1 draft's, and the depth-1 round pays the
same ~40.6 GPU ms to obtain one candidate. Truncating the
block is not available: block attention is non-causal, so
a shorter block changes the earlier rows' distributions
(settled in `propose_block`'s docs and in the fixture's
`causal_attention: false`).

**F4. The big costs belong to the existing kernel lanes;
this lane documents and does not duplicate them.** The
draft's projections (F1/F2) want MMV routing inside
`dflash_session.rs`'s own `prepare_proj`: the K19/K20
kernels exist, and the draft head is a plain Q5_K
projection with no fused finish, so the K21 kernel shape
fits it directly (K21's known gap is only the finish the
target's head needs). Verify's unrouted share wants the
same routing extended to `prepare_gated_proj` and
`prepare_swiglu_proj`, and the target head (7.55 ms at
depth 6) wants the K21 finish variant. Both are named
follow-ups of the MMV/K21 lanes with protocols already
written; the numbers above are their sizing.

**F5. The round's synchronization is already minimal.**
Per round: the draft forward is one submission plus one
blocking map; the verify forward is one submission plus
its maps (logits and captures drain together); the commit
is one inject submission with no map. `fuse()` is not on
the GPU commit path (it is the CPU model's public seam
and a parity-test entry; the inject plan encodes the
fusion prefix on-device). Two effective drains per round
is the floor for this sequential loop.

**F6. Host CPU work is the only in-layer remainder, and
two of its three pieces are now trimmed (below).**
Measured on the VM (indicative magnitudes; the server CPU
is faster): the readback byte conversion in `map_staging`
costs 0.61 ms for a full block and is already
memcpy-class (a "faster conversion" variant was
benchmarked and was slower; that hypothesis is dead). The
scalar `sampler::argmax` costs ~0.26 ms per 202,048-wide
row and runs on 1 + (depth + 1) rows per round (propose
rows plus the correction walk's rows). And the draft's
full-block readback moves 3,232,768 values (12.93 MB) per
round while every consumer slices only rows `1..=depth`
(`propose_block`); rows past the slice are computed
(unavoidable, F3) but were also transferred, converted,
and cached for nothing.

**F7. The bar is not reachable from this layer.** At
depth 1, 88.6 tok/s needs an 18.7 ms round (1.66
tokens/round). Draft + verify GPU alone measure ~75 ms.
T-9.6 stands or falls with the kernel lanes' streaming
rates (F4); the trim below is worth a few percent, taken
because it is free.

## What this lane built: the host-side trim

Two changes, both pure overhead removal with identical
outputs, so neither carries a gate (the shipped behavior
is not an arm of either; there is nothing to arm):

1. **Laned `sampler::argmax`** (`crates/itak-spec/src/sampler.rs`).
   Eight interleaved accumulators break the scalar scan's
   dependency chain; the merge applies the scalar rule
   (strictly greater wins; equal value goes to the lower
   index), which keeps the result bit-identical to the old
   scan on every input, NaNs, infinities, signed zeros,
   and denormals included (a NaN never wins a `>`
   comparison, so no accumulator can hold one). Callers:
   the propose slice, the correction walk, the plain step.
   Pinned by `argmax_matches_the_scalar_reference`: the
   pre-change scan kept verbatim in the tests, compared
   over hand-built adversarial rows and a seeded sweep at
   14 lengths including the real 202,048 width. VM
   micro-benchmark (noisy, direction only): 7-row walk
   4.3 ms scalar vs 1.9-2.9 ms laned.

2. **Capped draft block readback**
   (`crates/wgpu-compute/src/dflash_session.rs`,
   `crates/itak-spec/src/speculator.rs`).
   `DflashSession::forward_block_capped` runs the
   identical block (same plan, same submission) and copies
   / maps only the first `row_cap` logit rows;
   `forward_block` delegates to the same path uncapped and
   is byte-identical to before. The speculator computes
   its slice bound (`depth + 1`, clamped by `max_drafts`)
   before the forward and passes it down on the GPU arm;
   the CPU arm computes in-process and is untouched. A cap
   outside `1..=rows` refuses by name
   (`dflash forward_block` step) before any device work;
   the resolution rule is the pure, unit-tested
   `capped_rows`. Per round the readback falls from
   3,232,768 values (12.93 MB) to (depth + 1) rows: depth 1
   404,096 values (1.62 MB), depth 6 1,414,336 (5.66 MB).
   Instrumentation: the `[dflash] forward_block.capped`
   diag event (rows / returned) fires whenever a cap
   bites, and `DflashSessionStats::logits_values_read`
   counts the values that actually crossed, so the server
   A/B reads engagement off the logs instead of trusting
   the wiring. The device test
   `dflash_session_capped_forward_returns_the_full_prefix`
   pins that a capped result is the full forward's exact
   prefix at every cap, plus both refusals.

Expected effect (estimate; the protocol below replaces it
with measurements): depth 1 about 1.5-2.5 ms per round
(~2-3%), depth 6 about 3-5 ms per round (~2-3%), from the
smaller transfer and conversion, the propose argmax over
a cache-resident prefix, and the laned walk.

## VM gates (this lane)

- `cargo test -p itak-spec`: green, 48 tests, including
  `argmax_matches_the_scalar_reference`.
- `cargo test -p wgpu-compute`: green across every binary
  (193 tests in 23 binaries; lib: 102, including
  `capped_rows_accepts_only_true_prefixes`).
  The device tests, the new capped-forward one included,
  skip with a printed reason on this adapterless VM; their
  execution is step 1 of the server protocol.
- `cargo test -p dflash`: green, 24 tests.
- `cargo clippy -p itak-spec -p wgpu-compute -p dflash
  --all-targets`: clean. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`:
  clean.

## Server A/B protocol (parent runs; card time serialized)

Staging: `git archive` the lane head to `~/gpu-wave12` on
ubuntu-server; manifest-diff against the local tree. The
control is main `a064b5d7` (code-identical to the
`~/gpu-wave11` staging; a fresh staging is equally fine).
Build in each tree:
`cargo build --release -p itak-spec --example spec_generate_gpu`
and `cargo test -p wgpu-compute --test dflash_session --release --no-run`.
Serialize every run through
`flock -w 14400 /tmp/itak-phase.lock`; before each arm,
guard `/sys/class/drm/card2/device/mem_info_vram_used`
at driver residue (~33,271,808 B; stop the leg if above
1 GB). Never reboot; never touch the production
llama-server.

1. Device test on the real adapter, lane tree:
   `cargo test -p wgpu-compute --test dflash_session --release dflash_session_capped_forward_returns_the_full_prefix`
   must execute (not skip) and pass.
2. Arms, both trees, the verdict session's own invocation
   (models `/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf`
   and `dflash-Muse-Glimmer-30B-Q4_K_M.gguf`):
   `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=16 spec_generate_gpu <target> <draft> 64 <depth> "The capital of France is" both <stream>`
   at depths 1 and 6, three repetitions each, median taken.
3. Gates per run: `IDENTITY: PASS` and `GOLDEN: PASS` in
   the harness output, and the two arms' spec streams
   token-identical to each other (the harness prints the
   stream; the stream files diff clean).
4. Engagement proof, lane arm only: the log carries
   `[dflash] forward_block.capped rows=16 returned=2`
   (depth 1) / `returned=7` (depth 6) once per round, and
   no such line appears in the control arm.
5. Read: median `draft_ms` and effective tok/s per depth
   against this note's estimate (depth 1 draft down
   ~1.5-2.5 ms; effective up ~2-3%). `verify_ms` is the
   control's twin within noise; if it moves, suspect the
   run, not the change (the change touches no verify code).
6. One MMV-unset pair at depth 1 as a sanity arm: same
   gates, same capped lines.

## Exact server command sequence (ubuntu-server)

Staging follows the loop proof's pattern: a fresh directory built
from the merged commit, launched from a script file, argv verified
in `/proc` before any output is trusted, allocator arenas capped
(the loop proof's OOM lesson).

```sh
# 0. Stage the tree at the merged commit (parent lands the lane,
#    then this runs against main's new HEAD).
mkdir -p ~/spec-sweep-2026-11-03
rsync -a --delete <checkout-of-main-at-merge> ~/spec-sweep-2026-11-03/repo/
cd ~/spec-sweep-2026-11-03/repo && git rev-parse HEAD   # record it in this note

# 1. Build the runner.
export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
cargo build --release -p itak-spec --example spec_sweep

# 2. Write the launch script (never a hand-quoted ssh command line).
cat > ~/spec-sweep-2026-11-03/run.sh <<'EOS'
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
cd "$HOME/spec-sweep-2026-11-03/repo"
export MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2
export MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_=0
exec ./target/release/examples/spec_sweep \
  /mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  /mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/dflash-Muse-Glimmer-30B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  default 16 "The capital of France is"
EOS
chmod +x ~/spec-sweep-2026-11-03/run.sh

# 3. Launch detached, then verify the argv before trusting anything.
nohup ~/spec-sweep-2026-11-03/run.sh > ~/spec-sweep-2026-11-03/sweep.log 2>&1 &
PID=$!
sleep 5
tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/$PID/cmdline; echo

# 4. When the process exits, the table is the tail of the log:
tail -20 ~/spec-sweep-2026-11-03/sweep.log
```

Budget note: the arguments above sweep the default candidate set at
16 tokens per depth, the loop proof's budget. Depth 6 alone took
10,231 s at that budget, so the full set is an overnight-class run
(estimated 8 to 12 hours across depths); that is the honest price of
CPU acceptance numbers on the real 17 GB files. A shorter first
confirmation pass, if wanted, is the same script with `6 16` in
place of `default 16`: it should land near the loop proof's 0.3103
acceptance at depth 6. The configured 128-token budget is for the
GPU fill-in, where a depth costs seconds, and for any future CPU run
with a weekend to spare.

## GPU fill-in (when the T-9.6 GPU lane lands)

Same table, same rows: the GPU lane's runner (its own example wiring
`run_sweep` to a GPU session factory) runs with the identical
arguments except the binary path and the budget (`default 128`).
The acceptance column is expected to agree with the CPU column
within float nondeterminism; the effective tok/s column is where
the serving claim is made or lost, against the recorded anchors:
44.31 tok/s plain llama.cpp Vulkan, 107.39 tok/s at depth 6
llama.cpp DFlash.

| 12 | 64 | 730 | 63 | 0.086 | 1.98 | 127 | 20.6 | 6.17 |
| 16 | - | - | - | REFUSED | - | - | - | - |

Depth 16 refusal (verbatim): "session build for depth 16 failed:
draft depth 16 is out of range for draft block size 16". The
envelope maximum is block minus 1 = 15.

Winner by SPEC 9.4 (smallest depth within 2% of the best
effective rate): the best rate is 16.86 tok/s at depth 1, the band
floor is 16.52, and no other depth enters it. WINNER: depth 1,
measured acceptance 0.615. Recorded as the SpecConfig depth
default (crates/itak-spec/src/config.rs).

Honest context: every depth in this table sits below the same
night's plain decode rate (35.45 tok/s). Depth 1 is the measured
winner of a loop that does not yet beat plain decoding on this
stack; the remaining problem is acceptance economics and verify
cost, which is T-9.6's open speed half, not this item's proof.

# Split-K default flip: fixed factor 4 ships (2026-11-07)

Lane `lane/splitk-default-flip`, from main 333f354.
The MMQ split-K routing config
(`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMQ_SPLITK`) flips its shipped
default from OFF to fixed factor 4. The resolver's
explicit positions, the factor rule (including the
auto rule's arithmetic), the kernels, and the
reduction are unchanged; only the unset position
moved, in the same shape as the MMV ceiling and
K21F head flips (unset resolves to the shipped
default; a present but unrecognized value resolves
to the closed fallback, never to the default).

## Authority

David's standing order, 2026-11-07: "Anything that
makes sense engine go faster should be set to on."
This flip is that order applied to the wave20
split-K verdict.

## The evidence

bench/splitk-mmq-2026-11-07.md shipped the split-K
forms default-OFF with a written flip criterion:
the default moves only if the interleaved prefill
A/B shows a real win at both lengths with no
regression on the unsplit shapes, identity+golden
hold at `auto` and at `=8`, and the autopsy shows
no new spills.

The wave20 consolidated card session
(bench/wave20-session-2026-11-07.md, leg 1, staged
from main 515ce23 on the RX 7900 XTX) ran that
protocol. Reading against the criterion:

- **Prefill A/B, interleaved pairs, DIAG=timing.**
  Walls at 1,022 tokens: off 6,446 / 6,408 ms;
  fixed 4: 5,175 / 5,324 ms (about -18%). Walls at
  8,202 tokens: off 68,476 / 68,571 ms; fixed 4:
  59,047 / 58,877 ms (about -14%). A direct
  unwrapped confirmation run at factor 4
  reproduced the split lines (wall 5,106 ms),
  ruling out a wrapper artifact.
- **No unsplit-shape regression.** At fixed 4 the
  split forms beat the plain kernels on the wide
  shapes too: `k13_q4k_mmq_split` at 59.1 / 58.7
  GB/s vs plain 47.9; `k14_q6k_mmq_split` at 64.0 /
  63.4 GB/s vs plain 35.6 (1,022-token kernel
  lines). The reduction costs 50.2 ms across 3,744
  dispatches at that shape.
- **Correctness legs executed on the card.**
  tests/splitk_mmq.rs: 3 passed. Drift is
  reassociation-class, as the design predicted
  (relative at most about 8.5e-7); the split form
  is not bit-identical to the unsplit product by
  construction and never claimed to be.
- **Identity + golden.** PASS at `=auto` and at
  `=8` (the identity gate runs the flag at its
  admitted extremes; factor 4 sits between them).
  The `=auto` capture manifest carries
  `"mmq_splitk":"auto"` in `resolved_config`.
- **Autopsy: no new spills.** PARTIAL as scoped:
  the K13/K14 family dump showed 0 spilled SGPRs,
  0 spilled VGPRs, 0 scratch across all blocks,
  with the plain LDS figures reproduced exactly.
  Per-form attribution by name was not isolated
  (RADV dump blocks are anonymous); the remaining
  method (a dump run of the splitk_mmq test binary
  itself) is named in the session record.

The criterion is met at fixed factor 4. This lane
is that flip, and nothing else.

## Factor 8 is disqualified; auto is not the default

Both were measured in the same wave20 A/B, and
the record stands so neither is re-proposed as a
default without new evidence:

- **Fixed 8: DISQUALIFIED.** Walls +50% at 1,022
  tokens (10,180 / 9,071 ms) and +88% at 8,202
  (128,771 / 129,251 ms). The mechanism is in the
  kernel lines: at 8,202 the K13 split form itself
  collapses to 27.5 GB/s and `splitk_reduce` alone
  takes 27,538.9 / 27,655.5 ms across 29,952
  dispatches, 22.8% of total GPU time. Factor 8
  remains an admissible EXPLICIT operator value
  (the resolver still accepts `1`..=`8`); the
  disqualification is of 8 as a default, and it
  was already visible in the design note's slice
  math: at 26 blocks, factor 8's slices walk
  4/4/4/4/4/4/2/0, the last slice empty.
- **Auto: marginal, not shipped.** Walls about
  -3.5% at 1,022 and -2% at 8,202. Under auto only
  the KV projections split, and the rule's pick
  for that shape is factor 8, the disqualified
  factor; its small net win survives only because
  the KV shape is a small share of the prefill.
  The auto rule's arithmetic is unchanged by this
  flip; it remains an operator choice for
  shape-targeted runs.

## The change

- `compute::resolve_mmq_splitk` now resolves over
  two named constants: `DEFAULT_MMQ_SPLITK`
  (`MmqSplitK::Fixed(4)`, the shipped default;
  `pub(crate)` because the mode type is) and
  `MMQ_SPLITK_FALLBACK` (`MmqSplitK::Off`, the
  closed fallback). New semantics matrix:

  | value | resolves |
  |---|---|
  | unset | fixed 4 (the shipped default, `DEFAULT_MMQ_SPLITK`) |
  | `off` (trimmed) | OFF (the explicit off; the one-variable rollback) |
  | `auto` (trimmed) | the per-projection auto rule (arithmetic unchanged) |
  | `1`..=`8` (trimmed) | that fixed factor |
  | any other text | OFF, fail-closed (`MMQ_SPLITK_FALLBACK`), logged by name at construction |

  A present-but-malformed value does NOT inherit
  the new default: it resolves to the fallback,
  and `log_mmq_splitk_fallback` names it in the
  construction log ("failing closed to off, NOT
  the shipped default fixed:4"), on the flash /
  K21F fallback pattern. The construction log line
  now reads: `mmq splitk config: mode=<mode> (env
  WGPU_COMPUTE_MMQ_SPLITK: unset is the shipped
  default fixed:4, "off" disables, "auto" is the
  tile-count rule, 1..=8 a fixed factor; rollback
  WGPU_COMPUTE_MMQ_SPLITK=off)`. Resolution still
  happens once at backend construction; the
  `mmq_splitk` accessor and the `mmq_splitk`
  resolved-config pair in both sessions' diag
  manifests are unchanged in shape and now report
  `fixed:4` at unset.
- Routing is untouched: the split still applies
  at the standard rung only, behind
  coopmat/wide/K22/K23, never stacked on the
  prototypes, with the logged fallback to the
  unsplit prepare. `mmq_splitk_factor` is
  unchanged in every arm (Off, Fixed clamp, the
  auto rule's `ceil(64 / tiles)`).
- Doc updates where the old default was stated:
  the env, resolver, accessor docs and the
  construction comment in compute.rs; the
  `mmq_product_q4k` ladder comment in session.rs;
  the split paragraph in the K13 module header.
  bench/splitk-mmq-2026-11-07.md gains an appended
  supersession section (its history stands).

## Pins

- `compute::mmq_splitk_resolution` re-pinned to
  the full new matrix: unset resolves to
  `DEFAULT_MMQ_SPLITK` (pinned equal to
  `MmqSplitK::Fixed(4)`); `off` off; `auto` auto;
