===== FILE: crates/arch-llama/src/diag.rs =====
//! Diagnostic channel for the arch-llama module.
//!
//! Project law: every module ships with diagnostics from birth, and
//! every refusal emits through the diagnostic channel with its reason.
//! This crate keeps the channel a trait so the engine's diag crate can
//! own the real sink later; the two sinks here are the silent default
//! and a stderr sink for local work. Same shape as the muse-glimmer
//! module's channel, so arch modules are interchangeable at the seam.

/// A sink for structured diagnostic events: an event name plus a short
/// detail string. Implementations must be cheap to call on hot paths or
/// document that they are not.
pub trait Diag: Send + Sync {
    /// Record one event.
    fn event(&self, event: &str, detail: &str);
}

/// The default sink: drops every event. Use it when the engine process
/// has not wired a real sink yet; errors still propagate as values, so
/// nothing fails silently even with this sink installed.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct NullDiag;

impl Diag for NullDiag {
    fn event(&self, _event: &str, _detail: &str) {}
}

/// A sink that writes one line per event to stderr, for local runs and
/// test debugging.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct StderrDiag;

impl Diag for StderrDiag {
    fn event(&self, event: &str, detail: &str) {
        eprintln!("[arch-llama] {event}: {detail}");
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::sync::Mutex;

    /// A capturing sink in the itak-engine test shape: records every
    /// event so the test can prove the seam delivers what it is
    /// given, instead of trusting that sink wiring is present in the
    /// source.
    #[derive(Default)]
    struct Capture {
        events: Mutex<Vec<(String, String)>>,
    }

    impl Diag for Capture {
        fn event(&self, event: &str, detail: &str) {
            self.events
                .lock()
                .expect("capture lock")
                .push((event.to_string(), detail.to_string()));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn seam_delivers_events_to_a_sink() {
        let capture = Capture::default();
        capture.event("seam_probe", "detail=fired");
        let events = capture.events.lock().expect("capture lock");
        assert!(
            events
                .iter()
                .any(|(e, d)| e == "seam_probe" && d == "detail=fired"),
            "a sink must receive the events emitted through the seam"
        );
        drop(events);
        // The shipped sinks behave: NullDiag drops silently and
        // StderrDiag writes without panicking.
        NullDiag.event("seam_probe", "detail=dropped");
        StderrDiag.event("seam_probe", "detail=stderr");
    }
}

===== END FILE: crates/arch-llama/src/diag.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/arch-llama/src/error.rs =====
//! Error types for the arch-llama module.
//!
//! Design rule (carried from the 2026-10-29 audit of the original Go
//! engine): every failure is loud and names the thing that failed. The
//! original loader silently substituted pseudo-random weights for any
//! tensor it could not read, dropped Qwen2's attention biases without a
//! word, and invented a 32000-token vocabulary when the real one was
//! missing. Those defect classes are banned here: a missing metadata
//! key, a missing tensor, or a shape that disagrees with the config is
//! a named error, never a fallback value.

use std::fmt;

/// Result alias for arch-llama operations.
pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, LlamaError>;

/// Everything that can go wrong while configuring, loading, or running
/// a llama-family or qwen2-family model.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum LlamaError {
    /// A metadata key the config requires is absent from the file.
    MissingMetadata {
        /// The full GGUF metadata key that was required.
        key: String,
    },
    /// A metadata key is present but its value cannot describe a model
    /// this module can run (impossible head counts, per-layer head
    /// arrays meant for hybrid modules, and so on).
    InvalidMetadata {
        /// The full GGUF metadata key at fault.
        key: String,
        /// What is wrong with the value.
        detail: String,
    },
    /// `general.architecture` names an architecture this module does
    /// not serve. This module serves exactly `llama` and `qwen2`.
    WrongArchitecture {
        /// The architecture string found in the file.
        found: String,
    },
    /// The config's architecture string has no RoPE pairing mapped.
    /// Pairing is per-architecture in llama.cpp's table (see
    /// [`crate::config::RopePairing`]); an unmapped architecture is
    /// refused by name rather than assigned a guessed pairing.
    /// `LlamaConfig::from_file` already refuses architectures
    /// outside the served set, so this fires only for a config
    /// assembled by hand with an unmapped string.
    RopePairingUnknown {
        /// The architecture string with no mapped pairing.
        architecture: String,
    },
    /// A tensor the forward needs is not in the weight source. The old
    /// engine kept random placeholder weights in this situation; here
    /// it is an error, always.
    MissingTensor {
        /// The full GGUF tensor name that was required.
        name: String,
    },
    /// A tensor is present but its dimensions disagree with the shape
    /// the config requires for it.
    ShapeMismatch {
        /// The full GGUF tensor name.
        name: String,
        /// Dimensions the config requires, in GGUF stored order.
        expected: Vec<u64>,
        /// Dimensions the source actually carries, in GGUF stored order.
        actual: Vec<u64>,
    },
    /// A tensor's dimensions imply one element count but its data
    /// holds another, so the tensor cannot be what its name claims.
    TensorDataLength {
        /// The full GGUF tensor name.
        name: String,
        /// Element count implied by the dimensions.
        expected: u64,
        /// Element count actually present in the data.
        actual: usize,
    },
    /// `forward` was called with zero tokens.
    EmptyInput,
    /// A token id is outside the model's vocabulary.
    TokenOutOfRange {
        /// The offending token id.
        token: u32,
        /// The model's vocabulary size.
        vocab_size: u32,
    },
    /// A forward pass would run past the model's context length.
    SequenceTooLong {
        /// Total sequence length the pass would reach.
        total: usize,
        /// The model's context length, from its metadata.
        context_length: u32,
    },
    /// The layers of a KV cache disagree about the next position,
    /// which means the cache was advanced unevenly and cannot be
    /// trusted for this sequence.
    CacheDesync {
        /// The first layer whose position disagreed.
        layer: usize,
        /// The position every layer was expected to be at (layer 0's).
        expected: usize,
        /// The position the disagreeing layer is actually at.
        actual: usize,
    },
    /// The GGUF loader refused something (a tensor it cannot
    /// dequantize, a malformed file, a mistyped metadata value).
    Gguf(gguf::GgufError),
    /// A torch-math primitive refused its inputs.
    Math(torch_math::MathError),
    /// The attention crate refused its inputs or the cache operation.
    Attention(attention::AttentionError),
}

impl fmt::Display for LlamaError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Self::MissingMetadata { key } => {
                write!(f, "required GGUF metadata key is absent: {key}")
            }
            Self::InvalidMetadata { key, detail } => {
                write!(f, "GGUF metadata key {key} is invalid: {detail}")
            }
            Self::WrongArchitecture { found } => write!(
                f,
                "this module serves architectures \"llama\" and \"qwen2\" only, file declares \"{found}\""
            ),
            Self::RopePairingUnknown { architecture } => write!(
                f,
                "no RoPE pairing is mapped for architecture \"{architecture}\"; pairing is per-architecture in llama.cpp and is never guessed"
            ),
            Self::MissingTensor { name } => {
                write!(
                    f,
                    "required tensor is absent from the weight source: {name}"
                )
            }
            Self::ShapeMismatch {
                name,
                expected,
                actual,
            } => write!(
                f,
                "tensor {name}: shape {actual:?} does not match the shape the config requires {expected:?}"
            ),
            Self::TensorDataLength {
                name,
                expected,
                actual,
            } => write!(
                f,
                "tensor {name}: dimensions imply {expected} elements but the data holds {actual}"
            ),
            Self::EmptyInput => write!(f, "forward called with zero tokens"),
            Self::TokenOutOfRange { token, vocab_size } => write!(
                f,
                "token id {token} is outside the vocabulary of {vocab_size}"
            ),
            Self::SequenceTooLong {
                total,
                context_length,
            } => write!(
                f,
                "sequence would reach {total} tokens, past the model's context length of {context_length}"
            ),
            Self::CacheDesync {
                layer,
                expected,
                actual,
            } => write!(
                f,
                "KV cache desync: layer {layer} is at position {actual}, expected {expected}"
            ),
            Self::Gguf(e) => write!(f, "gguf loader: {e}"),
            Self::Math(e) => write!(f, "math: {e}"),
            Self::Attention(e) => write!(f, "attention: {e}"),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for LlamaError {
    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {
        match self {
            Self::Gguf(e) => Some(e),
            Self::Math(e) => Some(e),
            Self::Attention(e) => Some(e),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

impl From<gguf::GgufError> for LlamaError {
    fn from(e: gguf::GgufError) -> Self {
        // A tensor the loader cannot find is this module's own named
        // error, so callers see one vocabulary for the common case.
        match e {
            gguf::GgufError::MissingTensor(name) => Self::MissingTensor { name },
            other => Self::Gguf(other),
        }
    }
}

impl From<torch_math::MathError> for LlamaError {
    fn from(e: torch_math::MathError) -> Self {
        Self::Math(e)
    }
}

impl From<attention::AttentionError> for LlamaError {
    fn from(e: attention::AttentionError) -> Self {
        Self::Attention(e)
    }
}

===== END FILE: crates/arch-llama/src/error.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/arch-llama/src/lib.rs =====
//! Generic dense architecture module for the iTaK Torch Rust
//! engine: the `llama` and `qwen2` families.
//!
//! One crate, one block shape: pre-norm transformer layers with
//! rotary position embedding, grouped-query attention over a real
//! KV cache, and a SwiGLU feed-forward network. That is the shape
//! both families share; what differs is in the files, and this crate
//! reads it from the files: Qwen2's attention biases (which the
//! original Go engine silently dropped) are part of the tensor map,
//! the RMSNorm epsilon and RoPE base come from each file's own
//! metadata, and a model whose `output.weight` is absent runs on its
//! embedding table as a tied head, explicitly, never by substitution
//! for a tensor that failed to read.
//!
//! Status: blueprint stage 2 (ARCHITECTURE.md), the first verified
//! text stage. The conformance models are TinyLlama-1.1B (`llama`)
//! and Qwen2.5-1.5B (`qwen2`), dissected 2026-10-29
//! (`~/workspace/model-teardown/models/`). What is real:
//!
//! - [`LlamaConfig`] parsed from the file's own GGUF metadata,
//!   every required key named when absent, no fabricated defaults.
//! - The full tensor inventory ([`Weights`]) for both families,
//!   including the optional q/k/v biases, loaded through the
//!   [`TensorSource`] seam (the `gguf` crate's file implements it)
//!   with every shape checked against the config.
//! - The forward in [`LlamaModel::forward`]: embedding, per-layer
//!   pre-norm, RoPE, GQA attention against the `attention` crate's
//!   KV cache, SwiGLU FFN, final norm, head. Prefill and incremental
//!   decode are the same code path over the shared cache; the tests
//!   prove their logits agree.
//! - Fail-loud errors everywhere: a missing key, a missing tensor,
//!   or a wrong shape is a named [`LlamaError`], never a substituted
//!   value. That is the audit's central lesson, applied.

#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
#![warn(missing_docs)]

pub mod config;
pub mod diag;
pub mod error;
pub mod model;
pub mod weights;

#[cfg(test)]
mod testkit;

pub use config::{LlamaConfig, RopePairing, ARCHITECTURES};
pub use diag::{Diag, NullDiag, StderrDiag};
pub use error::{LlamaError, Result};
pub use model::{ForwardTrace, LayerTrace, LlamaModel};
pub use weights::{expected_tensor_names, LayerWeights, TensorData, TensorSource, Weights};

===== END FILE: crates/arch-llama/src/lib.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/arch-llama/src/model.rs =====
//! [`LlamaModel`]: config plus weights plus diag, and the forward
//! pass that ties them together.
//!
//! The forward is the architecture as both families run it, per
//! layer: embedding lookup, pre-attention RMSNorm, Q/K/V projections
//! (with the family's biases when loaded), RoPE on Q and K at each
//! position, the new K/V appended to the layer's cache, grouped-query
//! attention over everything the cache holds, output projection,
//! residual add, pre-FFN RMSNorm, SwiGLU FFN, residual add. Then the
//! final norm and the head (untied, or the embedding table when
//! tied). Arithmetic delegates to `torch-math`; attention and KV
//! storage are the `attention` crate's, so the cache is the only way
//! attention can see keys and values, by construction.
//!
//! Prefill and incremental decode are one path: [`forward`] takes
//! any number of tokens and appends them to the cache at the cache's
//! current position, [`step`] is the one-token case. The KV proof
//! test below runs a prompt both ways and requires the logits to
//! agree, which is the property the original engine's design (full
//! re-forward per token against a cache nothing called) could not
//! even state.
//!
//! Validation happens before any cache mutation: token range and
//! the context bound are checked up front, and every tensor shape
//! was checked at load, so a refused pass leaves the cache exactly
//! as it found it.
//!
//! [`forward`]: LlamaModel::forward
//! [`step`]: LlamaModel::step

use std::sync::Arc;

use attention::{gqa_attention, AttentionParams, KvCache, LayerKind};

use crate::config::{LlamaConfig, RopePairing};
use crate::diag::{Diag, NullDiag};
use crate::error::{LlamaError, Result};
use crate::weights::{TensorData, Weights};

/// A llama-family or qwen2-family model ready to run.
pub struct LlamaModel {
    config: LlamaConfig,
    weights: Weights,
    diag: Arc<dyn Diag>,
}

impl LlamaModel {
    /// Assemble a model from its parts, with a silent diagnostic sink.
    pub fn new(config: LlamaConfig, weights: Weights) -> Self {
        LlamaModel {
            config,
            weights,
            diag: Arc::new(NullDiag),
        }
    }

    /// Assemble a model with a diagnostic sink attached. Every pass
    /// emits its begin and end through it.
    pub fn with_diag(config: LlamaConfig, weights: Weights, diag: Arc<dyn Diag>) -> Self {
        LlamaModel {
            config,
            weights,
            diag,
        }
    }

    /// The model's configuration.
    pub fn config(&self) -> &LlamaConfig {
        &self.config
    }

    /// The model's weights.
    pub fn weights(&self) -> &Weights {
        &self.weights
    }

    /// A fresh KV cache for this model: one global store per layer
    /// (both conformance families attend over the full history;
    /// neither file declares a sliding window).
    pub fn new_cache(&self) -> Result<KvCache> {
        let pattern = vec![LayerKind::Global; self.config.block_count as usize];
        Ok(KvCache::new(
            &pattern,
            self.config.kv_heads as usize,
            self.config.head_dim as usize,
        )?)
    }

    /// Run `tokens` through the model starting at the cache's
    /// current position, append their K/V to the cache, and return
    /// the next-token logits for the final position.
    ///
    /// On any refusal the cache is untouched (all validation happens
    /// before the first append) and the error names what failed.
    pub fn forward(&self, tokens: &[u32], cache: &mut KvCache) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        self.forward_inner(tokens, cache, None)
    }

    /// [`forward`](Self::forward) with per-layer intermediates
    /// captured into a [`ForwardTrace`]: the same code path, with
    /// the sub-step buffers cloned out as they pass. Exists for
    /// activation diffing against a reference engine (golden layer
    /// harness); the plain forward pays nothing for it.
    pub fn forward_traced(
        &self,
        tokens: &[u32],
        cache: &mut KvCache,
    ) -> Result<(Vec<f32>, ForwardTrace)> {
        let mut trace = ForwardTrace::default();
        let logits = self.forward_inner(tokens, cache, Some(&mut trace))?;
        Ok((logits, trace))
    }

    fn forward_inner(
        &self,
        tokens: &[u32],
        cache: &mut KvCache,
        mut trace: Option<&mut ForwardTrace>,
    ) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        if tokens.is_empty() {
            return Err(LlamaError::EmptyInput);
        }
        let cfg = &self.config;
        for &token in tokens {
            if token >= cfg.vocab_size {
                return Err(LlamaError::TokenOutOfRange {
                    token,
                    vocab_size: cfg.vocab_size,
                });
            }
        }
        let base = cache.next_position(0)?;
        for layer in 1..cfg.block_count as usize {
            let at = cache.next_position(layer)?;
            if at != base {
                return Err(LlamaError::CacheDesync {
                    layer,
                    expected: base,
                    actual: at,
                });
            }
        }
        let total = base + tokens.len();
        if total > cfg.context_length as usize {
            return Err(LlamaError::SequenceTooLong {
                total,
                context_length: cfg.context_length,
            });
        }
        self.diag.event(
            "forward.begin",
            &format!(
                "tokens={} position={} layers={}",
                tokens.len(),
                base,
                cfg.block_count
            ),
        );

        let rows = tokens.len();
        let hidden = cfg.hidden as usize;
        let mut x = Vec::with_capacity(rows * hidden);
        for &token in tokens {
            let row = token as usize * hidden;
            x.extend_from_slice(&self.weights.embedding.data[row..row + hidden]);
        }
        if let Some(t) = trace.as_deref_mut() {
            t.embd = x.clone();
        }

        let positions: Vec<usize> = (base..base + rows).collect();
        for (index, w) in self.weights.layers.iter().enumerate() {
            let mut lt = trace.as_ref().map(|_| LayerTrace::default());
            let h = rms_rows(&x, hidden, &w.attn_norm.data, cfg.rms_eps)?;
            if let Some(lt) = lt.as_mut() {
                lt.attn_norm = h.clone();
            }
            let mut q = linear(
                &h,
                hidden,
                &w.attn_q,
                cfg.q_width() as usize,
                w.attn_q_bias.as_ref(),
            )?;
            let mut k = linear(
                &h,
                hidden,
                &w.attn_k,
                cfg.k_width() as usize,
                w.attn_k_bias.as_ref(),
            )?;
            let v = linear(
                &h,
                hidden,
                &w.attn_v,
                cfg.v_width() as usize,
                w.attn_v_bias.as_ref(),
            )?;
            if let Some(lt) = lt.as_mut() {
                lt.q_pre_rope = q.clone();
                lt.k_pre_rope = k.clone();
                lt.v = v.clone();
            }
            rope_rows(&mut q, cfg.q_heads as usize, cfg, &positions)?;
            rope_rows(&mut k, cfg.kv_heads as usize, cfg, &positions)?;
            if let Some(lt) = lt.as_mut() {
                lt.q = q.clone();
                lt.k = k.clone();
            }
            let k_w = cfg.k_width() as usize;
            let v_w = cfg.v_width() as usize;
            for (r, &position) in positions.iter().enumerate() {
                cache.append(
                    index,
                    &k[r * k_w..(r + 1) * k_w],
                    &v[r * v_w..(r + 1) * v_w],
                    position,
                )?;
            }
            let view = cache.view(index)?;
            let attn = gqa_attention(
                &q,
                rows,
                cfg.q_heads as usize,
                &positions,
                &view,
                &AttentionParams::new(),
            )?;
            let out = linear(&attn, cfg.q_width() as usize, &w.attn_output, hidden, None)?;
            add_in_place(&mut x, &out);
            if let Some(lt) = lt.as_mut() {
                lt.ffn_inp = x.clone();
            }

            let h = rms_rows(&x, hidden, &w.ffn_norm.data, cfg.rms_eps)?;
            if let Some(lt) = lt.as_mut() {
                lt.ffn_norm = h.clone();
            }
            let gate = linear(&h, hidden, &w.ffn_gate, cfg.ffn_hidden as usize, None)?;
            let up = linear(&h, hidden, &w.ffn_up, cfg.ffn_hidden as usize, None)?;
            let act = torch_math::swiglu(&gate, &up)?;
            let down = linear(&act, cfg.ffn_hidden as usize, &w.ffn_down, hidden, None)?;
            if let Some(lt) = lt.as_mut() {
                lt.ffn_out = down.clone();
            }
            add_in_place(&mut x, &down);
            if let (Some(t), Some(lt)) = (trace.as_deref_mut(), lt.as_mut()) {
                lt.l_out = x.clone();
                t.layers.push(std::mem::take(lt));
            }
        }

        let last = &x[(rows - 1) * hidden..rows * hidden];
        let normed = torch_math::rms_norm(last, &self.weights.final_norm.data, cfg.rms_eps)?;
        if let Some(t) = trace {
            t.result_norm = normed.clone();
        }
        let head = self.weights.head();
        let logits = torch_math::matvec(&head.data, cfg.vocab_size as usize, hidden, &normed)?;

        self.diag.event(
            "forward.end",
            &format!("logits={} position={}", logits.len(), total),
        );
        Ok(logits)
    }

    /// Advance the model by one token: the incremental decode step.
    /// Shares the cache path with [`forward`](Self::forward) exactly;
    /// it exists so call sites read as what they are.
    pub fn step(&self, token: u32, cache: &mut KvCache) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        self.forward(&[token], cache)
    }
}

/// Per-layer intermediates captured by
/// [`LlamaModel::forward_traced`]. Every buffer is in this crate's
/// row convention: `[rows][width]`, one row per input token, in the
/// same flat layout the forward itself uses. Field names follow the
/// reference graph's tensor names (llama.cpp) so a dump of one side
/// lines up against the other by name.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
pub struct LayerTrace {
    /// Output of the pre-attention RMSNorm (`attn_norm`).
    pub attn_norm: Vec<f32>,
    /// Query projection before RoPE (no reference-graph counterpart;
    /// the reference names only the rotated tensor).
    pub q_pre_rope: Vec<f32>,
    /// Key projection before RoPE.
    pub k_pre_rope: Vec<f32>,
    /// Query projection after RoPE (`Qcur`).
    pub q: Vec<f32>,
    /// Key projection after RoPE (`Kcur`).
    pub k: Vec<f32>,
    /// Value projection (`Vcur`).
    pub v: Vec<f32>,
    /// Hidden state after the attention residual add (`ffn_inp`).
    pub ffn_inp: Vec<f32>,
    /// Output of the pre-FFN RMSNorm (`ffn_norm`).
    pub ffn_norm: Vec<f32>,
    /// FFN down-projection output, before its residual add
    /// (`ffn_out`).
    pub ffn_out: Vec<f32>,
    /// Hidden state after the FFN residual add: this layer's output
    /// (`l_out`).
    pub l_out: Vec<f32>,
}

/// One traced forward pass: the embedding rows, one [`LayerTrace`]
/// per layer, and the final norm applied to the last position.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
pub struct ForwardTrace {
    /// Embedding output rows (`inp_embd`).
    pub embd: Vec<f32>,
    /// Per-layer traces, in layer order.
    pub layers: Vec<LayerTrace>,
    /// Final RMSNorm output for the last position (`result_norm`).
    pub result_norm: Vec<f32>,
}

/// RMSNorm applied row by row over a `[rows, width]` buffer.
fn rms_rows(x: &[f32], width: usize, weight: &[f32], eps: f32) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(x.len());
    for row in x.chunks_exact(width) {
        out.extend_from_slice(&torch_math::rms_norm(row, weight, eps)?);
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// One linear projection over every row of a `[rows, in_w]` buffer:
/// `out = x * W^T (+ bias)`, with `weight` in GGUF stored layout
/// (`out_w` rows of `in_w`). Per-row matvec, deliberately: this is
/// the reference path the kernels are later verified against.
fn linear(
    x: &[f32],
    in_w: usize,
    weight: &TensorData,
    out_w: usize,
    bias: Option<&TensorData>,
) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(x.len() / in_w * out_w);
    for row in x.chunks_exact(in_w) {
        let mut projected = torch_math::matvec(&weight.data, out_w, in_w, row)?;
        if let Some(bias) = bias {
            for (o, b) in projected.iter_mut().zip(bias.data.iter()) {
                *o += b;
            }
        }
        out.extend_from_slice(&projected);
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// RoPE applied in place to a `[rows, heads * head_dim]` buffer,
/// one position per row. The channel pairing comes from the file's
/// architecture via [`LlamaConfig::rope_pairing`]: llama-family
/// files rotate adjacent pairs, qwen2 files rotate half-split
/// pairs. Naming one pairing function here for both families is
/// the mistake this dispatch replaces (13643e0 fixed qwen2 by
/// flipping the shared function and regressed llama with it).
fn rope_rows(x: &mut [f32], heads: usize, cfg: &LlamaConfig, positions: &[usize]) -> Result<()> {
    let head_dim = cfg.head_dim as usize;
    let rotary_dim = cfg.rope_dim as usize;
    let width = heads * head_dim;
    let pairing = cfg.rope_pairing()?;
    for (r, &position) in positions.iter().enumerate() {
        for h in 0..heads {
            let start = (r * heads + h) * head_dim;
            let head = &x[start..start + head_dim];
            let rotated = match pairing {
                RopePairing::Interleaved => torch_math::rope_interleaved_partial(
                    head,
                    position,
                    cfg.rope_freq_base,
                    head_dim,
                    rotary_dim,
                )?,
                RopePairing::HalfSplit => torch_math::rope_partial(
                    head,
                    position,
                    cfg.rope_freq_base,
                    head_dim,
                    rotary_dim,
                )?,
            };
            x[start..start + head_dim].copy_from_slice(&rotated);
        }
    }
    debug_assert_eq!(x.len(), positions.len() * width);
    Ok(())
}

/// Residual add. Lengths are equal by construction (both operands
/// come from the same row shape), so this cannot fail.
fn add_in_place(a: &mut [f32], b: &[f32]) {
    debug_assert_eq!(a.len(), b.len());
    for (x, y) in a.iter_mut().zip(b.iter()) {
        *x += y;
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::testkit::{
        build_gguf, deterministic_values, refs, tiny_config, tiny_metadata, BiasMode, FakeSource,
    };
    use gguf::GgufFile;

    fn tiny_model(arch: &str, tied: bool, biases: BiasMode) -> LlamaModel {
        let cfg = tiny_config(arch);
        let source = FakeSource::full(&cfg, tied, biases);
        let weights = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect("tiny weights load");
        LlamaModel::new(cfg, weights)
    }

    fn max_abs_diff(a: &[f32], b: &[f32]) -> f32 {
        assert_eq!(a.len(), b.len());
        a.iter()
            .zip(b.iter())
            .map(|(x, y)| (x - y).abs())
            .fold(0.0f32, f32::max)
    }

    #[test]
    fn tiny_synthetic_model_runs_end_to_end() {
        let model = tiny_model("llama", false, BiasMode::None);
        let mut cache = model.new_cache().expect("cache");
        let logits = model
            .forward(&[3, 1, 4, 1], &mut cache)
            .expect("forward runs");
        assert_eq!(logits.len(), 64);
        assert!(logits.iter().all(|z| z.is_finite()));
        // The cache advanced by the prompt length on every layer.
        for stats in cache.stats() {
            assert_eq!(stats.appended, 4);
            assert_eq!(stats.stored, 4);
        }
    }

    /// Apply one torch-math pairing function head by head, the
    /// manual reference `rope_rows` is checked against.
    fn rotate_manually(
        input: &[f32],
        heads: usize,
        head_dim: usize,
        positions: &[usize],
        f: impl Fn(&[f32], usize) -> Vec<f32>,
    ) -> Vec<f32> {
        let mut out = input.to_vec();
        for (r, &position) in positions.iter().enumerate() {
            for h in 0..heads {
                let start = (r * heads + h) * head_dim;
                let rotated = f(&input[start..start + head_dim], position);
                out[start..start + head_dim].copy_from_slice(&rotated);
            }
        }
        out
    }

    #[test]
    fn rope_rows_dispatches_on_the_config_architecture() {
        // Same buffer, same positions, two configs differing only
        // in the architecture string: llama must come out as the
        // interleaved rotation and qwen2 as the half-split one,
        // each exactly the torch-math function the mapping names.
        // This is the per-arch selection test for the 13643e0
        // regression, which flipped both families with one edit.
        let heads = 2;
        let positions = [1usize, 3];
        let input = deterministic_values(2 * heads * 8, 42);
        let llama_cfg = tiny_config("llama");
        let qwen2_cfg = tiny_config("qwen2");

        let mut llama_out = input.clone();
        rope_rows(&mut llama_out, heads, &llama_cfg, &positions).expect("llama rotates");
        let llama_expected = rotate_manually(&input, heads, 8, &positions, |head, pos| {
            torch_math::rope_interleaved_partial(head, pos, 10_000.0, 8, 8)
                .expect("interleaved rotates")
        });
        assert_eq!(llama_out, llama_expected);

        let mut qwen2_out = input.clone();
        rope_rows(&mut qwen2_out, heads, &qwen2_cfg, &positions).expect("qwen2 rotates");
        let qwen2_expected = rotate_manually(&input, heads, 8, &positions, |head, pos| {
            torch_math::rope_partial(head, pos, 10_000.0, 8, 8).expect("half-split rotates")
        });
        assert_eq!(qwen2_out, qwen2_expected);

        // The two pairings genuinely differ on this input (at
        // positions past 0 rotation is not the identity, and the
        // pairings join different channels), so the equality checks
        // above cannot both pass under a single shared pairing.
        assert!(
            max_abs_diff(&llama_out, &qwen2_out) > 1e-3,
            "pairings must differ: diff {}",
            max_abs_diff(&llama_out, &qwen2_out)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rope_rows_partial_rotary_uses_the_interleaved_subrange_for_llama() {
        // A llama-arch config whose rope_dim is below the head dim:
        // the interleaved pairing applied over the first rope_dim
        // channels, the tail passed through unrotated.
        let heads = 2;
        let positions = [2usize];
        let input = deterministic_values(heads * 8, 7);
        let mut cfg = tiny_config("llama");
        cfg.rope_dim = 4;

        let mut out = input.clone();
        rope_rows(&mut out, heads, &cfg, &positions).expect("partial rotates");
        let expected = rotate_manually(&input, heads, 8, &positions, |head, pos| {
            torch_math::rope_interleaved_partial(head, pos, 10_000.0, 8, 4)
                .expect("interleaved partial rotates")
        });
        assert_eq!(out, expected);
        // Tail channels of every head are the input's, exactly.
        for h in 0..heads {
            assert_eq!(out[h * 8 + 4..h * 8 + 8], input[h * 8 + 4..h * 8 + 8]);
        }
        // And it is not the full-rotary result: channels 4..8 stay
        // put here, where the full form rotates them.
        let mut full_cfg = tiny_config("llama");
        full_cfg.rope_dim = 8;
        let mut full_out = input.clone();
        rope_rows(&mut full_out, heads, &full_cfg, &positions).expect("full rotates");
        assert!(max_abs_diff(&out, &full_out) > 1e-3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn partial_rotary_llama_forward_agrees_prefill_and_incremental() {
        // The whole forward over the partial interleaved path:
        // prefill and one-token steps must still agree, the KV
        // proof restated for the subrange rotation.
        let mut cfg = tiny_config("llama");
        cfg.rope_dim = 4;
        let source = FakeSource::full(&cfg, false, BiasMode::None);
        let weights = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect("weights load");
        let model = LlamaModel::new(cfg, weights);
        let prompt = [5u32, 9, 2, 7];

        let mut prefill_cache = model.new_cache().expect("cache");
        let prefill_logits = model
            .forward(&prompt, &mut prefill_cache)
            .expect("prefill runs");
        assert!(prefill_logits.iter().all(|z| z.is_finite()));

        let mut decode_cache = model.new_cache().expect("cache");
        let mut decode_logits = Vec::new();
        for &token in &prompt {
            decode_logits = model.step(token, &mut decode_cache).expect("step runs");
        }
        assert!(
            max_abs_diff(&prefill_logits, &decode_logits) <= 1e-4,
            "prefill vs incremental diff {}",
            max_abs_diff(&prefill_logits, &decode_logits)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn kv_proof_prefill_and_incremental_decode_agree() {
        let model = tiny_model("qwen2", false, BiasMode::NonZero);
        let prompt = [5u32, 9, 2, 7, 3];

        let mut prefill_cache = model.new_cache().expect("cache");
        let prefill_logits = model
            .forward(&prompt, &mut prefill_cache)
            .expect("prefill runs");

        let mut decode_cache = model.new_cache().expect("cache");
        let mut decode_logits = Vec::new();
        for &token in &prompt {
            decode_logits = model.step(token, &mut decode_cache).expect("step runs");
        }

        let mut chunked_cache = model.new_cache().expect("cache");
        model
            .forward(&prompt[..2], &mut chunked_cache)
            .expect("chunk 1 runs");
        let chunked_logits = model
            .forward(&prompt[2..], &mut chunked_cache)
            .expect("chunk 2 runs");

        // Same math, three ways of feeding it: the logits for the
        // final position must agree to float noise. This is the KV
        // cache proof the old engine could not pass, having no
        // working cache on any path.
        assert!(
            max_abs_diff(&prefill_logits, &decode_logits) <= 1e-4,
            "prefill vs incremental diff {}",
            max_abs_diff(&prefill_logits, &decode_logits)
        );
        assert!(
            max_abs_diff(&prefill_logits, &chunked_logits) <= 1e-4,
            "prefill vs chunked diff {}",
            max_abs_diff(&prefill_logits, &chunked_logits)
        );
        assert_eq!(prefill_cache.next_position(0).expect("pos"), 5);
        assert_eq!(decode_cache.next_position(0).expect("pos"), 5);
    }

    #[test]
    fn tied_head_matches_an_explicit_copy_of_the_embedding() {
        let cfg = tiny_config("llama");
        let tied_source = FakeSource::full(&cfg, true, BiasMode::None);
        let tied_weights = Weights::load(&tied_source, &cfg).expect("tied loads");
        assert!(tied_weights.tied_embeddings);
        let tied_model = LlamaModel::new(cfg.clone(), tied_weights);

        // Same weights, but with output.weight present and holding
        // exactly the embedding table: the tied model's head.
        let mut explicit_source = FakeSource::full(&cfg, true, BiasMode::None);
        let embedding = explicit_source
            .get("token_embd.weight")
            .expect("embedding present")
            .clone();
        explicit_source.set(TensorData {
            name: "output.weight".to_string(),
            shape: embedding.shape.clone(),
            data: embedding.data.clone(),
        });
        let explicit_weights = Weights::load(&explicit_source, &cfg).expect("explicit loads");
        assert!(!explicit_weights.tied_embeddings);
        let explicit_model = LlamaModel::new(cfg, explicit_weights);

        let mut c1 = tied_model.new_cache().expect("cache");
        let mut c2 = explicit_model.new_cache().expect("cache");
        let a = tied_model.forward(&[1, 2, 3], &mut c1).expect("tied runs");
        let b = explicit_model
            .forward(&[1, 2, 3], &mut c2)
            .expect("explicit runs");
        assert!(
            max_abs_diff(&a, &b) <= 1e-5,
            "tied vs explicit-copy diff {}",
            max_abs_diff(&a, &b)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn attention_biases_change_the_output() {
        let plain = tiny_model("llama", false, BiasMode::None);
        let biased = tiny_model("llama", false, BiasMode::NonZero);
        let zeroed = tiny_model("llama", false, BiasMode::Zero);
        let prompt = [2u32, 6, 1];

        let mut c = plain.new_cache().expect("cache");
        let plain_logits = plain.forward(&prompt, &mut c).expect("plain runs");
        let mut c = biased.new_cache().expect("cache");
        let biased_logits = biased.forward(&prompt, &mut c).expect("biased runs");
        let mut c = zeroed.new_cache().expect("cache");
        let zeroed_logits = zeroed.forward(&prompt, &mut c).expect("zeroed runs");

        // Identical weights otherwise: the only difference between
        // the runs is the bias values, so a real difference here is
        // the biases being applied, and zero biases reproducing the
        // bias-free result proves presence alone does nothing.
        assert!(
            max_abs_diff(&plain_logits, &biased_logits) > 1e-3,
            "biases had no effect: diff {}",
            max_abs_diff(&plain_logits, &biased_logits)
        );
        assert!(
            max_abs_diff(&plain_logits, &zeroed_logits) <= 1e-6,
            "zero biases should be inert: diff {}",
            max_abs_diff(&plain_logits, &zeroed_logits)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn forward_refuses_bad_input_without_touching_the_cache() {
        let model = tiny_model("llama", false, BiasMode::None);
        let mut cache = model.new_cache().expect("cache");
        assert!(matches!(
            model.forward(&[], &mut cache),
            Err(LlamaError::EmptyInput)
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            model.forward(&[64], &mut cache),
            Err(LlamaError::TokenOutOfRange { .. })
        ));
        let too_long = vec![1u32; 129];
        assert!(matches!(
            model.forward(&too_long, &mut cache),
            Err(LlamaError::SequenceTooLong { .. })
        ));
        assert_eq!(cache.next_position(0).expect("pos"), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn desynced_cache_is_refused_by_name() {
        let model = tiny_model("llama", false, BiasMode::None);
        let mut cache = model.new_cache().expect("cache");
        // Advance layer 0 only: a cache no honest forward produced.
        let row = vec![0.0f32; 2 * 8];
        cache.append(0, &row, &row, 0).expect("manual append");
        let err = model
            .forward(&[1], &mut cache)
            .expect_err("desync must fail");
        assert!(matches!(err, LlamaError::CacheDesync { layer: 1, .. }));
    }

    #[test]
    fn end_to_end_through_the_real_gguf_loader() {
        // The whole path on the real loader: synthetic GGUF bytes,
        // parsed by the gguf crate, config from the file, weights
        // through its TensorSource implementation, forward on top.
        let cfg = tiny_config("llama");
        let source = FakeSource::full(&cfg, false, BiasMode::None);
        let metadata = tiny_metadata("llama");
        let bytes = build_gguf(&refs(&metadata), &source.into_test_tensors());
        let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(bytes).expect("synthetic file parses");
        let parsed = LlamaConfig::from_file(&file).expect("config parses");
        assert_eq!(parsed, cfg);
        let weights = Weights::load(&file, &parsed).expect("weights load from file");
        let model = LlamaModel::new(parsed, weights);
        let mut cache = model.new_cache().expect("cache");
        let logits = model
            .forward(&[10, 20, 30], &mut cache)
            .expect("forward runs on file-backed weights");
        assert_eq!(logits.len(), 64);
        assert!(logits.iter().all(|z| z.is_finite()));
    }
}

//! Shared fixtures for this crate's tests: a minimal GGUF v3 byte
//! builder (so config and load tests run through the real gguf
//! parser, not a stub), metadata sets carrying the measured values
//! of the two conformance files, and a deterministic value generator
//! for synthetic weights. Test code only; nothing here ships in the
//! library's API surface.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use gguf::MetadataValue;

use crate::config::LlamaConfig;
use crate::error::{LlamaError, Result};
use crate::weights::{TensorData, TensorSource};

/// One tensor to write into a synthetic GGUF: name, dimensions in
/// GGUF stored order, and its F32 values (written as ggml type F32).
pub struct TestTensor {
    /// Tensor name.
    pub name: String,
    /// Dimensions in GGUF stored order (innermost first).
    pub dims: Vec<u64>,
    /// Element values; length must equal the product of `dims`.
    pub values: Vec<f32>,
}

/// Little-endian bytes for F32 values.
pub fn f32_bytes(values: &[f32]) -> Vec<u8> {
    values.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect()
}

fn write_string(out: &mut Vec<u8>, s: &str) {
    out.extend_from_slice(&(s.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(s.as_bytes());
}

fn write_scalar(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: &MetadataValue) {
    match v {
        MetadataValue::UInt8(x) => out.push(*x),
        MetadataValue::Int8(x) => out.push(*x as u8),
        MetadataValue::UInt16(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Int16(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::UInt32(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Int32(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Float32(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Bool(x) => out.push(u8::from(*x)),
        MetadataValue::String(s) => write_string(out, s),
        MetadataValue::UInt64(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Int64(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Float64(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Array(_) => panic!("arrays do not nest in GGUF"),
    }
}

fn write_value(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: &MetadataValue) {
    out.extend_from_slice(&v.type_id().to_le_bytes());
    match v {
        MetadataValue::Array(items) => {
            let elem_type = items.first().map_or(8, MetadataValue::type_id);
            out.extend_from_slice(&elem_type.to_le_bytes());
            out.extend_from_slice(&(items.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
            for item in items {
                write_scalar(out, item);
            }
        }
        scalar => write_scalar(out, scalar),
    }
}

fn align_up(v: u64, a: u64) -> u64 {
    v.div_ceil(a) * a
}

/// Build a complete GGUF v3 file in memory: the given metadata and
/// F32 tensors, tensor data aligned to 32 bytes like a real file.
pub fn build_gguf(metadata: &[(&str, MetadataValue)], tensors: &[TestTensor]) -> Vec<u8> {
    const ALIGNMENT: u64 = 32;
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    out.extend_from_slice(b"GGUF");
    out.extend_from_slice(&3u32.to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&(tensors.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&(metadata.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
    for (key, value) in metadata {
        write_string(&mut out, key);
        write_value(&mut out, value);
    }
    // Tensor directory, with offsets assigned in layout order.
    let mut offset: u64 = 0;
    let mut offsets = Vec::with_capacity(tensors.len());
    for t in tensors {
        offset = align_up(offset, ALIGNMENT);
        offsets.push(offset);
        offset += (t.values.len() * 4) as u64;
    }
    for (t, &off) in tensors.iter().zip(&offsets) {
        assert_eq!(
            t.values.len() as u64,
            t.dims.iter().product::<u64>(),
            "test tensor {} value count disagrees with its dims",
            t.name
        );
        write_string(&mut out, &t.name);
        out.extend_from_slice(&(t.dims.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
        for d in &t.dims {
            out.extend_from_slice(&d.to_le_bytes());
        }
        out.extend_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes()); // ggml type 0: F32
        out.extend_from_slice(&off.to_le_bytes());
    }
    // Pad to the data section, then the tensor bytes at their offsets.
    let data_start = align_up(out.len() as u64, ALIGNMENT);
    out.resize(data_start as usize, 0);
    for (t, &off) in tensors.iter().zip(&offsets) {
        let at = data_start as usize + off as usize;
        if out.len() < at + t.values.len() * 4 {
            out.resize(at + t.values.len() * 4, 0);
        }
        out[at..at + t.values.len() * 4].copy_from_slice(&f32_bytes(&t.values));
    }
    out
}

/// A token array of `n` distinct short strings, standing in for a
/// real vocabulary in metadata fixtures.
pub fn tokens(n: usize) -> MetadataValue {
    MetadataValue::Array(
        (0..n)
            .map(|i| MetadataValue::String(format!("t{i}")))
            .collect(),
    )
}

/// Metadata exactly as measured in the real TinyLlama-1.1B GGUF
/// (census 2026-10-29): llama arch, no attention biases, untied head.
pub fn tinyllama_metadata() -> Vec<(String, MetadataValue)> {
    vec![
        (
            "general.architecture".into(),

/// Metadata for a two-layer synthetic model of the given family:
/// hidden 32, FFN 48, 4 Q heads over 2 KV heads (head dim 8),
/// vocab 64, context 128. Small enough for full forward tests.
pub fn tiny_metadata(arch: &str) -> Vec<(String, MetadataValue)> {
    let p = |suffix: &str| format!("{arch}.{suffix}");
    let mut entries = vec![
        (
            "general.architecture".to_string(),
            MetadataValue::String(arch.to_string()),
        ),
        (
            "general.name".to_string(),
            MetadataValue::String(format!("tiny-{arch}")),
        ),
        (p("block_count"), MetadataValue::UInt32(2)),
        (p("context_length"), MetadataValue::UInt32(128)),
        (p("embedding_length"), MetadataValue::UInt32(32)),
        (p("feed_forward_length"), MetadataValue::UInt32(48)),
        (p("attention.head_count"), MetadataValue::UInt32(4)),
        (p("attention.head_count_kv"), MetadataValue::UInt32(2)),
        (
            p("attention.layer_norm_rms_epsilon"),
            MetadataValue::Float32(1e-6),
        ),
        (p("rope.freq_base"), MetadataValue::Float32(10_000.0)),
        ("tokenizer.ggml.tokens".to_string(), tokens(64)),
    ];
    if arch == "llama" {
        // TinyLlama carries the key; Qwen2.5 does not. Mirror both.
        entries.push((p("rope.dimension_count"), MetadataValue::UInt32(8)));
    }
    entries
}

/// Deterministic pseudo-values in a stable range, so synthetic
/// weights are neither zeros (which hide wiring bugs: every path
/// would output zero) nor random per run (which hides regressions).
/// Values land in [-0.3, 0.3).
pub fn deterministic_values(count: usize, seed: u32) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.wrapping_add(0x9E37_79B9);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            // LCG, Numerical Recipes constants.
            state = state.wrapping_mul(1_664_525).wrapping_add(1_013_904_223);
            let unit = (state >> 8) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32;
            unit * 0.6 - 0.3
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Convert owned metadata fixtures to the borrowed shape
/// [`build_gguf`] takes.
pub fn refs(entries: &[(String, MetadataValue)]) -> Vec<(&str, MetadataValue)> {
    entries
        .iter()
        .map(|(k, v)| (k.as_str(), v.clone()))
        .collect()
}

/// A [`LlamaConfig`] for the tiny synthetic shape [`tiny_metadata`]
/// describes, built directly (config parsing itself is tested
/// through the GGUF byte path in the config module).
pub fn tiny_config(arch: &str) -> LlamaConfig {
    LlamaConfig {
        architecture: arch.to_string(),
        name: Some(format!("tiny-{arch}")),
        block_count: 2,
        context_length: 128,
        hidden: 32,
        ffn_hidden: 48,
        q_heads: 4,
        kv_heads: 2,
        head_dim: 8,
        rope_freq_base: 10_000.0,
        rope_dim: 8,
        rms_eps: 1e-6,
        vocab_size: 64,
    }
}

/// How a [`FakeSource`] fills the attention bias tensors.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BiasMode {
    /// No bias tensors in the source at all.
    None,
    /// Bias tensors present, all zeros (present but inert: proves
    /// the forward applies the values, not just their presence).
    Zero,
    /// Bias tensors present with deterministic nonzero values.
    NonZero,
}

/// An in-memory [`TensorSource`] holding a complete tiny weight set
/// for a config, unless a test removes or replaces tensors.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct FakeSource {
    tensors: HashMap<String, TensorData>,
}

impl FakeSource {
    /// A complete weight set for `cfg`: every tensor the load
    /// requires, plus biases per `biases`, plus the untied head
    /// unless `tied`. Values are deterministic per tensor.
    pub fn full(cfg: &LlamaConfig, tied: bool, biases: BiasMode) -> Self {
        let mut tensors: HashMap<String, TensorData> = HashMap::new();
        // Each tensor's values derive from its NAME, never from
        // insertion order, so two sources that differ only in which
        // optional tensors they carry (biases, the untied head)
        // still hold identical values for every shared tensor. The
        // bias and tied tests rely on exactly that.
        fn seed_of(name: &str) -> u32 {
            // FNV-1a over the name.
            let mut hash = 0x811C_9DC5u32;
            for byte in name.bytes() {
                hash ^= u32::from(byte);
                hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0x0100_0193);
            }
            hash
        }
        let put = |tensors: &mut HashMap<String, TensorData>, name: String, shape: &[u64]| {
            let count: u64 = shape.iter().product();
            let seed = seed_of(&name);
            tensors.insert(
                name.clone(),
                TensorData {
                    name,
                    shape: shape.to_vec(),
                    data: deterministic_values(count as usize, seed),
                },
            );
        };
        let hidden = u64::from(cfg.hidden);
        let vocab = u64::from(cfg.vocab_size);
        let ffn = u64::from(cfg.ffn_hidden);
        let q_w = u64::from(cfg.q_width());
        let k_w = u64::from(cfg.k_width());
        let v_w = u64::from(cfg.v_width());
        put(
            &mut tensors,
            "token_embd.weight".to_string(),
            &[hidden, vocab],
        );
        put(&mut tensors, "output_norm.weight".to_string(), &[hidden]);
        if !tied {
            put(&mut tensors, "output.weight".to_string(), &[hidden, vocab]);
        }
        for layer in 0..cfg.block_count {
            let p = |suffix: &str| format!("blk.{layer}.{suffix}");
            put(&mut tensors, p("attn_norm.weight"), &[hidden]);
            put(&mut tensors, p("attn_q.weight"), &[hidden, q_w]);
            put(&mut tensors, p("attn_k.weight"), &[hidden, k_w]);
            put(&mut tensors, p("attn_v.weight"), &[hidden, v_w]);
            if biases != BiasMode::None {
                for (suffix, width) in [
                    ("attn_q.bias", q_w),
                    ("attn_k.bias", k_w),
                    ("attn_v.bias", v_w),
                ] {
                    let name = p(suffix);
                    let data = match biases {
                        BiasMode::Zero => vec![0.0; width as usize],
                        _ => deterministic_values(width as usize, seed_of(&name)),
                    };
                    tensors.insert(
                        name.clone(),
                        TensorData {
                            name,
                            shape: vec![width],
                            data,
                        },
                    );
                }
            }
            put(&mut tensors, p("attn_output.weight"), &[q_w, hidden]);
            put(&mut tensors, p("ffn_norm.weight"), &[hidden]);
            put(&mut tensors, p("ffn_gate.weight"), &[hidden, ffn]);
            put(&mut tensors, p("ffn_up.weight"), &[hidden, ffn]);
            put(&mut tensors, p("ffn_down.weight"), &[ffn, hidden]);
        }
        FakeSource { tensors }
    }

    /// Remove a tensor, for missing-tensor tests.
    pub fn remove(&mut self, name: &str) {
        self.tensors.remove(name);
    }

    /// Replace or insert a tensor, for shape and tied-head tests.
    pub fn set(&mut self, tensor: TensorData) {
        self.tensors.insert(tensor.name.clone(), tensor);
    }

    /// Look up a tensor the source holds.
    pub fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&TensorData> {
        self.tensors.get(name)
    }

    /// Convert the whole set into [`TestTensor`]s for the GGUF byte
    /// builder, for the end-to-end-through-the-real-loader test.
    pub fn into_test_tensors(self) -> Vec<TestTensor> {
        let mut out: Vec<TestTensor> = self
            .tensors
            .into_values()
            .map(|t| TestTensor {
                name: t.name,
                dims: t.shape,
                values: t.data,
            })
            .collect();
        out.sort_by(|a, b| a.name.cmp(&b.name));
        out
    }
}

impl TensorSource for FakeSource {
    fn tensor(&self, name: &str) -> Result<TensorData> {
        self.tensors
            .get(name)
            .cloned()
            .ok_or_else(|| LlamaError::MissingTensor {
                name: name.to_string(),
            })
    }

    fn has_tensor(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.tensors.contains_key(name)
    }
}

===== END FILE: crates/arch-llama/src/testkit.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/arch-llama/src/weights.rs =====
//! The weight layout of a llama-family or qwen2-family model: every
//! tensor the forward needs, by its exact GGUF name.
//!
//! The per-layer inventory is the one measured in the real files'
//! tensor censuses (2026-10-29), not the shorter list the original
//! engine's Llama-shaped template used. That template never looked
//! up the attention biases, so Qwen2 ran with its biases silently
//! dropped; here the biases are named members of the map. For
//! `qwen2` files they are required (the family's reference graph
//! applies them on every layer, so a qwen2 file without them is not
//! the model it claims to be); for `llama` files they are loaded and
//! applied when present.
//!
//! Loading goes through the [`TensorSource`] trait, which the `gguf`
//! crate's [`GgufFile`] implements below. Every tensor's shape is
//! checked against the config before it is accepted: a tensor of the
//! wrong shape is a named error, not a surprise inside a matmul.
//!
//! The output head: when `output.weight` is present it is the head.
//! When it is absent the model is tied and the head reads the
//! embedding table; that state is recorded on [`Weights`] as
//! `tied_embeddings`, not improvised at call time. (The real
//! Qwen2.5-1.5B GGUF carries an explicit `output.weight` even though
//! the Hugging Face checkpoint ties its embeddings: the converter
//! materialized the head. So this file loads untied, and the tied
//! path serves the files that genuinely omit the head.)

use gguf::GgufFile;

use crate::config::LlamaConfig;
use crate::error::{LlamaError, Result};

/// One tensor handed over by a [`TensorSource`]: its name, its shape
/// in GGUF stored order (innermost dimension first), and its elements
/// dequantized to f32 in stored order.
///
/// The forward's projections consume `data` directly as a row-major
/// matrix whose rows are the output features: GGUF stores a
/// projection of shape `[in, out]` as `out` rows of `in` elements,
/// which is exactly the layout `torch_math::matvec` multiplies.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct TensorData {
    /// Full GGUF tensor name, for example `blk.3.ffn_down.weight`.
    pub name: String,
    /// Dimensions in GGUF stored order (innermost first).
    pub shape: Vec<u64>,
    /// Dequantized elements, in stored order.
    pub data: Vec<f32>,
}

impl TensorData {
    /// Total element count implied by the shape.
    pub fn elements(&self) -> u64 {
        self.shape.iter().product()
    }
}

/// A source of tensors by name: the seam between this module and
/// the loader.
///
/// Implementor contract: return the tensor or fail with
/// [`LlamaError::MissingTensor`]. Never substitute, synthesize, or
/// zero-fill a tensor that was not found; silent placeholders are
/// the defect this rebuild exists to remove.
pub trait TensorSource {
    /// Fetch one tensor by its full GGUF name, dequantized to f32.
    fn tensor(&self, name: &str) -> Result<TensorData>;
    /// Whether a tensor with this name exists in the source. The
    /// load uses it only for the tensors whose presence is a model
    /// property (the untied head, llama-family biases), never to
    /// skip a required tensor quietly.
    fn has_tensor(&self, name: &str) -> bool;
}

impl TensorSource for GgufFile {
    fn tensor(&self, name: &str) -> Result<TensorData> {
        let info = gguf::GgufFile::tensor_info(self, name)?;
        let shape = info.dims().to_vec();
        let data = self.load_f32(name)?;
        Ok(TensorData {
            name: name.to_string(),
            shape,
            data,
        })
    }

    fn has_tensor(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        gguf::GgufFile::has_tensor(self, name)
    }
}

/// The tensors of one transformer layer, in forward order.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct LayerWeights {
    /// `attn_norm.weight`: pre-attention RMSNorm.
    pub attn_norm: TensorData,
    /// `attn_q.weight`: query projection.
    pub attn_q: TensorData,
    /// `attn_k.weight`: key projection.
    pub attn_k: TensorData,
    /// `attn_v.weight`: value projection.
    pub attn_v: TensorData,
    /// `attn_q.bias`: query bias. Required for qwen2, applied when
    /// present for llama, absent otherwise.
    pub attn_q_bias: Option<TensorData>,
    /// `attn_k.bias`: key bias; same rule as the query bias.
    pub attn_k_bias: Option<TensorData>,
    /// `attn_v.bias`: value bias; same rule as the query bias.
    pub attn_v_bias: Option<TensorData>,
    /// `attn_output.weight`: attention output projection.
    pub attn_output: TensorData,
    /// `ffn_norm.weight`: pre-FFN RMSNorm.
    pub ffn_norm: TensorData,
    /// `ffn_gate.weight`: SwiGLU gate projection.
    pub ffn_gate: TensorData,
    /// `ffn_up.weight`: SwiGLU up projection.
    pub ffn_up: TensorData,
    /// `ffn_down.weight`: FFN down projection (the FFN tensors hold
    /// most of both conformance models' bytes; this is the large one).
    pub ffn_down: TensorData,
}

/// The full weight set of a llama-family or qwen2-family model.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Weights {
    /// `token_embd.weight`: the embedding table.
    pub embedding: TensorData,
    /// `output_norm.weight`: final RMSNorm before the head.
    pub final_norm: TensorData,
    /// `output.weight`: the untied output head, when the file
    /// carries one.
    pub output: Option<TensorData>,
    /// Whether the head is tied to the embedding table (recorded
    /// from the absence of `output.weight` at load).
    pub tied_embeddings: bool,
    /// Per-layer weights, in layer order.
    pub layers: Vec<LayerWeights>,
}

/// Per-layer tensor suffixes that [`Weights::load`] always requires,
/// in load order.
const LAYER_SUFFIXES: [&str; 9] = [
    "attn_norm.weight",
    "attn_q.weight",
    "attn_k.weight",
    "attn_v.weight",
    "attn_output.weight",
    "ffn_norm.weight",
    "ffn_gate.weight",
    "ffn_up.weight",
    "ffn_down.weight",
];

/// Per-layer bias suffixes, required for qwen2 and probed for llama.
const BIAS_SUFFIXES: [&str; 3] = ["attn_q.bias", "attn_k.bias", "attn_v.bias"];

/// The name of the output head tensor.
pub const OUTPUT_HEAD_NAME: &str = "output.weight";

/// Every tensor name [`Weights::load`] will always request for
/// `cfg`, in load order. `output.weight` is not in the list: its
/// presence is probed, and its absence is the tied state, not a
/// missing tensor. Exposed so the loader's coverage report can be
/// checked against this module's expectations mechanically.
pub fn expected_tensor_names(cfg: &LlamaConfig) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut names = Vec::with_capacity(
        2 + cfg.block_count as usize * (LAYER_SUFFIXES.len() + BIAS_SUFFIXES.len()),
    );
    names.push("token_embd.weight".to_string());
    names.push("output_norm.weight".to_string());
    for layer in 0..cfg.block_count {
        for suffix in LAYER_SUFFIXES {
            names.push(format!("blk.{layer}.{suffix}"));
        }
        if cfg.attention_biases_required() {
            for suffix in BIAS_SUFFIXES {
                names.push(format!("blk.{layer}.{suffix}"));
            }
        }
    }
    names
}

impl Weights {
    /// Load the full weight set for `cfg` from `source`. The first
    /// missing or misshaped tensor aborts the load with a named
    /// error; a partially loaded model is never returned.
    pub fn load<S: TensorSource>(source: &S, cfg: &LlamaConfig) -> Result<Weights> {
        let hidden = u64::from(cfg.hidden);
        let vocab = u64::from(cfg.vocab_size);
        let ffn = u64::from(cfg.ffn_hidden);
        let q_w = u64::from(cfg.q_width());
        let k_w = u64::from(cfg.k_width());
        let v_w = u64::from(cfg.v_width());

        let embedding = checked(source, "token_embd.weight", &[hidden, vocab])?;
        let final_norm = checked(source, "output_norm.weight", &[hidden])?;
        let output = if source.has_tensor(OUTPUT_HEAD_NAME) {
            Some(checked(source, OUTPUT_HEAD_NAME, &[hidden, vocab])?)
        } else {
            None
        };
        let tied_embeddings = output.is_none();

        let mut layers = Vec::with_capacity(cfg.block_count as usize);
        for index in 0..cfg.block_count {
            let get_checked = |suffix: &str, shape: &[u64]| {
                checked(source, &format!("blk.{index}.{suffix}"), shape)
            };
            let bias = |suffix: &str, width: u64| -> Result<Option<TensorData>> {
                let name = format!("blk.{index}.{suffix}");
                // Required for qwen2 (where a missing bias then
                // fails inside `checked` by name); for llama, loaded
                // when the file carries the tensor.
                if cfg.attention_biases_required() || source.has_tensor(&name) {
                    Ok(Some(checked(source, &name, &[width])?))
                } else {
                    Ok(None)
                }
            };
            layers.push(LayerWeights {
                attn_norm: get_checked(LAYER_SUFFIXES[0], &[hidden])?,
                attn_q: get_checked(LAYER_SUFFIXES[1], &[hidden, q_w])?,
                attn_k: get_checked(LAYER_SUFFIXES[2], &[hidden, k_w])?,
                attn_v: get_checked(LAYER_SUFFIXES[3], &[hidden, v_w])?,
                attn_q_bias: bias(BIAS_SUFFIXES[0], q_w)?,
                attn_k_bias: bias(BIAS_SUFFIXES[1], k_w)?,
                attn_v_bias: bias(BIAS_SUFFIXES[2], v_w)?,
                attn_output: get_checked(LAYER_SUFFIXES[4], &[q_w, hidden])?,
                ffn_norm: get_checked(LAYER_SUFFIXES[5], &[hidden])?,
                ffn_gate: get_checked(LAYER_SUFFIXES[6], &[hidden, ffn])?,
                ffn_up: get_checked(LAYER_SUFFIXES[7], &[hidden, ffn])?,
                ffn_down: get_checked(LAYER_SUFFIXES[8], &[ffn, hidden])?,
            });
        }
        Ok(Weights {
            embedding,
            final_norm,
            output,
            tied_embeddings,
            layers,
        })
    }

    /// The tensor the LM head multiplies: the untied head when the
    /// file carried one, the embedding table when tied.
    pub fn head(&self) -> &TensorData {
        match &self.output {
            Some(head) => head,
            None => &self.embedding,
        }
    }
}

/// Fetch one tensor and verify it against the shape the config
/// requires for it: presence, dimensions, and element count all
/// checked before the tensor is accepted.
fn checked<S: TensorSource>(source: &S, name: &str, expected: &[u64]) -> Result<TensorData> {
    let tensor = source.tensor(name)?;
    if tensor.shape != expected {
        return Err(LlamaError::ShapeMismatch {
            name: name.to_string(),
            expected: expected.to_vec(),
            actual: tensor.shape.clone(),
        });
    }
    let want = tensor.elements();
    if tensor.data.len() as u64 != want {
        return Err(LlamaError::TensorDataLength {
            name: name.to_string(),
            expected: want,
            actual: tensor.data.len(),
        });
    }
    Ok(tensor)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::testkit::{tiny_config, BiasMode, FakeSource};

    #[test]
    fn llama_full_source_loads_untied() {
        let cfg = tiny_config("llama");
        let source = FakeSource::full(&cfg, false, BiasMode::None);
        let weights = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect("full source loads");
        assert_eq!(weights.layers.len(), 2);
        assert!(!weights.tied_embeddings);
        assert!(weights.output.is_some());
        assert!(weights.layers[0].attn_q_bias.is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn qwen2_full_source_loads_with_biases() {
        let cfg = tiny_config("qwen2");
        let source = FakeSource::full(&cfg, false, BiasMode::NonZero);
        let weights = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect("full source loads");
        assert!(weights.layers[1].attn_q_bias.is_some());
        assert!(weights.layers[1].attn_k_bias.is_some());
        assert!(weights.layers[1].attn_v_bias.is_some());
    }

    #[test]
    fn missing_output_head_means_tied_not_missing() {
        let cfg = tiny_config("qwen2");
        let source = FakeSource::full(&cfg, true, BiasMode::NonZero);
        let weights = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect("tied source loads");
        assert!(weights.tied_embeddings);
        assert!(weights.output.is_none());
        // The head falls back to the embedding table itself.
        assert_eq!(weights.head().name, "token_embd.weight");
    }

    #[test]
    fn missing_ffn_down_is_named() {
        let cfg = tiny_config("llama");
        let mut source = FakeSource::full(&cfg, false, BiasMode::None);
        source.remove("blk.1.ffn_down.weight");
        let err = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect_err("missing tensor must fail");
        match err {
            LlamaError::MissingTensor { name } => {
                assert_eq!(name, "blk.1.ffn_down.weight")
            }
            other => panic!("expected MissingTensor, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn qwen2_missing_bias_is_named() {
        let cfg = tiny_config("qwen2");
        let mut source = FakeSource::full(&cfg, false, BiasMode::NonZero);
        source.remove("blk.0.attn_q.bias");
        let err = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect_err("qwen2 without biases must fail");
        match err {
            LlamaError::MissingTensor { name } => assert_eq!(name, "blk.0.attn_q.bias"),
            other => panic!("expected MissingTensor, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn llama_biases_present_are_loaded() {
        let cfg = tiny_config("llama");
        let source = FakeSource::full(&cfg, false, BiasMode::NonZero);
        let weights = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect("loads");
        assert!(weights.layers[0].attn_q_bias.is_some());
    }

    #[test]
    fn wrong_shape_is_named() {
        let cfg = tiny_config("llama");
        let mut source = FakeSource::full(&cfg, false, BiasMode::None);
        source.set(TensorData {
            name: "blk.0.attn_q.weight".to_string(),
            shape: vec![16, 16],
            data: vec![0.0; 256],
        });
        let err = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect_err("wrong shape must fail");
        match err {
            LlamaError::ShapeMismatch {
                name,
                expected,
                actual,
            } => {
                assert_eq!(name, "blk.0.attn_q.weight");
                assert_eq!(expected, vec![32, 32]);
                assert_eq!(actual, vec![16, 16]);
            }
            other => panic!("expected ShapeMismatch, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn expected_names_match_the_load_map() {
        let llama = tiny_config("llama");
        let names = expected_tensor_names(&llama);
        assert_eq!(names.len(), 2 + 2 * 9);
        assert!(!names.iter().any(|n| n.ends_with(".bias")));
        let qwen2 = tiny_config("qwen2");
        let names = expected_tensor_names(&qwen2);
        assert_eq!(names.len(), 2 + 2 * 12);
        assert!(names.contains(&"blk.1.attn_v.bias".to_string()));
    }
}
