===== FILE: crates/cpu-compute/src/lib.rs =====
//! `cpu-compute`: the CPU reference implementation of
//! [`muse_glimmer::Compute`], the arithmetic seam of the Muse
//! Glimmer architecture module.
//!
//! This is the crate the skeleton was waiting for. Where
//! [`muse_glimmer::UnimplementedCompute`] refuses every step by name,
//! [`CpuCompute`] does the real arithmetic: dequantization through
//! the `gguf` crate, dense math through `torch-math`, and grouped-
//! query attention over the `attention` crate's KV cache. It is a
//! correctness reference, not a speed contender: weights are
//! dequantized on every call and attention runs one query row at a
//! time, so the specialized kernels that come later can be verified
//! against simple, obviously-correct code.
//!
//! Two design points the trait forced, stated plainly:
//!
//! - **KV storage lives here, not in the caller's cache.**
//!   [`muse_glimmer::Cache`] is a position contract only (`position`
//!   and `advance`); it has no KV surface, and the forward hands the
//!   compute layer nothing else. So [`CpuCompute`] owns an
//!   `attention::KvCache`, built from the first config it serves,
//!   and cross-checks it against the position contract on every
//!   attention call: if the cache's stored positions and the
//!   caller's position disagree, the step refuses by name instead of
//!   attending to the wrong history. One [`CpuCompute`] serves one
//!   sequence; [`CpuCompute::reset`] abandons it.
//! - **Prefill and decode are the same code path.** Attention
//!   processes one position at a time: rotate, append to the cache,
//!   attend. A multi-token prefill is that loop repeated, and a
//!   decode step is the loop run once, so the two cannot drift
//!   apart. The integration tests prove the property end to end:
//!   incremental decode logits match one-shot prefill logits for the
//!   same sequence.
//! - **Speculative rollback is exposed, not improvised.**
//!   [`CpuCompute::cache_checkpoint`], [`CpuCompute::cache_rewind`],
//!   and [`CpuCompute::cache_release`] pass the `attention` crate's
//!   checkpoint API through to the one place the KV cache lives, so
//!   a speculation driver (SPEC-itak-spec Section 5) rolls this
//!   backend's storage back exactly, ring evictions included.
//!
//! The forward's step order, including the two placements the
//! architecture crate flagged for verification (post norms after
//! each residual add; the gate projection reading the normed
//! attention input), is `muse-glimmer`'s, not this crate's: this
//! crate supplies arithmetic for the steps in the order it is
//! called. Its tests pin the implemented order numerically, with the
//! assumptions named where they bite.

#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
#![warn(missing_docs)]

pub mod cpu;
pub mod diag;

pub use attention::Checkpoint;
pub use cpu::CpuCompute;

===== END FILE: crates/cpu-compute/src/lib.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/cpu-compute/tests/forward_tests.rs =====
//! End-to-end tests of `CpuCompute` driving `GlimmerModel::forward`
//! on a tiny synthetic model (2 layers, hidden 32, vocab 128) whose
//! weights are set by hand in this file. The analytic tests compute
//! their expected logits with test-local f64 math written from the
//! formulas, sharing no code with the backend, so agreement is a
//! real check and not the implementation grading itself.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::Arc;

use cpu_compute::CpuCompute;
use muse_glimmer::{
    Cache, Dtype, GlimmerConfig, GlimmerError, GlimmerModel, LayerKind, PatternSource,
    PositionCache, TensorSource, TensorView, Weights,
};

const HIDDEN: usize = 32;
const FFN: usize = 64;
const VOCAB: usize = 128;
const HEAD_DIM: usize = 8;

/// Deterministic pseudo-random values in [-0.25, 0.25], so the
/// "random" fixtures are identical on every run and every machine.
struct Lcg(u64);

impl Lcg {
    fn next_f32(&mut self) -> f32 {
        self.0 = self
            .0
            .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
            .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
        let v = ((self.0 >> 40) & 0xFF_FFFF) as f32 / (1u64 << 24) as f32;
        (v - 0.5) * 0.5
    }
}

fn rand_vec(rng: &mut Lcg, n: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    (0..n).map(|_| rng.next_f32()).collect()
}

fn ones(n: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    vec![1.0; n]
}

fn zeros(n: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    vec![0.0; n]
}

/// Identity matrix as stored GGUF data: shape [n, n], row o is e_o.
fn identity(n: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut v = vec![0.0; n * n];
    for i in 0..n {
        v[i * n + i] = 1.0;
    }
    v
}

fn scaled_identity(n: usize, s: f32) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut v = vec![0.0; n * n];
    for i in 0..n {
        v[i * n + i] = s;
    }
    v
}

/// Selector matrix: shape [inn, out] with out <= inn, row o is e_o,
/// so the projection keeps the first `out` channels.
fn selector(inn: usize, out: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut v = vec![0.0; inn * out];
    for o in 0..out {
        v[o * inn + o] = 1.0;
    }
    v
}

/// Output head whose row j is e_{j mod hidden}: logit j reads
/// channel j mod hidden of the normed hidden state.
fn head_repeat(hidden: usize, vocab: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut v = vec![0.0; hidden * vocab];
    for j in 0..vocab {
        v[j * hidden + (j % hidden)] = 1.0;
    }
    v
}

fn f32_tensor(name: &str, shape: &[u64], values: Vec<f32>) -> TensorView {
    let data: Vec<u8> = values.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect();
    TensorView {
        name: name.to_string(),
        dtype: Dtype::F32,
        shape: shape.to_vec(),
        data: Arc::from(data.into_boxed_slice()),
    }
}

struct MapSource {
    tensors: HashMap<String, TensorView>,
}

impl TensorSource for MapSource {
    fn tensor(&self, name: &str) -> muse_glimmer::Result<TensorView> {
        self.tensors
            .get(name)
            .cloned()
            .ok_or_else(|| GlimmerError::MissingTensor {
                name: name.to_string(),
            })
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
enum Style {
    /// Attention output and FFN zeroed: the residual stream is only
    /// ever renormalized, so the expected logits are a closed form.
    Analytic,
    /// Identity Q, selector K/V, quarter-identity gate, identity
    /// output projection, zero FFN: attention really mixes positions
    /// and the naive route below can follow it exactly.
    Attention,
    /// Every projection pseudo-random: the full path exercised with
    /// no structure to hide behind.
    Random,
}

fn emb_pattern_a(token: usize, i: usize) -> f32 {
    ((token * 31 + i * 17) % 13) as f32 - 6.0
}

fn emb_pattern_b(token: usize, i: usize) -> f32 {
    ((token * 7 + i * 11) % 9) as f32 - 4.0
}

/// Build the full synthetic weight set for `cfg` in one of the three
/// styles. All shapes are derived from the config, so configs with
/// different head lengths still load.
fn build_source(cfg: &GlimmerConfig, style: Style) -> MapSource {
    let hidden = cfg.hidden as usize;
    let ffn = cfg.ffn_hidden as usize;
    let qw = cfg.q_width() as usize;
    let kw = cfg.k_width() as usize;
    let vw = cfg.v_width() as usize;
    let vocab = cfg.vocab_size as usize;
    let head_dim = cfg.key_length as usize;
    let mut rng = Lcg(0x9e37_79b9_7f4a_7c15);
    let mut tensors: HashMap<String, TensorView> = HashMap::new();
    let put = |tensors: &mut HashMap<String, TensorView>,
               name: String,
               shape: &[u64],
               values: Vec<f32>| {
        tensors.insert(name.clone(), f32_tensor(&name, shape, values));
    };

    let emb_values = match style {
        Style::Analytic => (0..vocab * hidden)
            .map(|e| emb_pattern_a(e / hidden, e % hidden))
            .collect(),
        Style::Attention => (0..vocab * hidden)
            .map(|e| emb_pattern_b(e / hidden, e % hidden))
            .collect(),
        Style::Random => rand_vec(&mut rng, vocab * hidden),
    };
    put(
        &mut tensors,
        "token_embd.weight".to_string(),
        &[hidden as u64, vocab as u64],
        emb_values,
    );
    put(
        &mut tensors,
        "output_norm.weight".to_string(),
        &[hidden as u64],
        ones(hidden),
    );
    let head_values = match style {
        Style::Random => rand_vec(&mut rng, vocab * hidden),
        _ => head_repeat(hidden, vocab),
    };
    put(
        &mut tensors,
        "output.weight".to_string(),
        &[hidden as u64, vocab as u64],
        head_values,
    );

    for layer in 0..cfg.block_count as usize {
        let name = |suffix: &str| format!("blk.{layer}.{suffix}");
        put(
            &mut tensors,
            name("attn_norm.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64],
            ones(hidden),
        );
        let q_values = match style {
            Style::Random => rand_vec(&mut rng, hidden * qw),
            _ => identity(hidden),
        };
        put(
            &mut tensors,
            name("attn_q.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64, qw as u64],
            q_values,
        );
        let k_values = match style {
            Style::Random => rand_vec(&mut rng, hidden * kw),
            _ => selector(hidden, kw),
        };
        put(
            &mut tensors,
            name("attn_k.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64, kw as u64],
            k_values,
        );
        let v_values = match style {
            Style::Random => rand_vec(&mut rng, hidden * vw),
            _ => selector(hidden, vw),
        };
        put(
            &mut tensors,
            name("attn_v.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64, vw as u64],
            v_values,
        );
        put(
            &mut tensors,
            name("attn_q_norm.weight"),
            &[head_dim as u64],
            ones(head_dim),
        );
        put(
            &mut tensors,
            name("attn_k_norm.weight"),
            &[head_dim as u64],
            ones(head_dim),
        );
        let gate_values = match style {
            Style::Analytic => rand_vec(&mut rng, hidden * qw),
            Style::Attention => scaled_identity(hidden, 0.25),
            Style::Random => rand_vec(&mut rng, hidden * qw),
        };
        put(
            &mut tensors,
            name("attn_gate.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64, qw as u64],
            gate_values,
        );
        let out_values = match style {
            Style::Analytic => zeros(qw * hidden),
            Style::Attention => identity(hidden),
            Style::Random => rand_vec(&mut rng, qw * hidden),
        };
        put(
            &mut tensors,
            name("attn_output.weight"),
            &[qw as u64, hidden as u64],
            out_values,
        );
        put(
            &mut tensors,
            name("post_attention_norm.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64],
            ones(hidden),
        );
        put(
            &mut tensors,
            name("ffn_norm.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64],
            ones(hidden),
        );
        let ffn_gate_values = match style {
            Style::Attention => zeros(hidden * ffn),
            _ => rand_vec(&mut rng, hidden * ffn),
        };
        put(
            &mut tensors,
            name("ffn_gate.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64, ffn as u64],
            ffn_gate_values,
        );
        let ffn_up_values = match style {
            Style::Attention => zeros(hidden * ffn),
            _ => rand_vec(&mut rng, hidden * ffn),
        };
        put(
            &mut tensors,
            name("ffn_up.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64, ffn as u64],
            ffn_up_values,
        );
        let ffn_down_values = match style {
            Style::Random => rand_vec(&mut rng, ffn * hidden),
            _ => zeros(ffn * hidden),
        };
        put(
            &mut tensors,
            name("ffn_down.weight"),
            &[ffn as u64, hidden as u64],
            ffn_down_values,
        );
        put(
            &mut tensors,
            name("post_ffw_norm.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64],
            ones(hidden),
        );
    }
    MapSource { tensors }
}

fn test_config(layers: Vec<LayerKind>, sliding_window: u32) -> GlimmerConfig {
    test_config_kv(layers, sliding_window, 8, 8)
}

fn test_config_kv(
    layers: Vec<LayerKind>,
    sliding_window: u32,
    key_length: u32,
    value_length: u32,
) -> GlimmerConfig {
    GlimmerConfig {
        name: Some("synthetic test model".to_string()),
        block_count: layers.len() as u32,
        context_length: 128,
        hidden: HIDDEN as u32,
        ffn_hidden: FFN as u32,
        q_heads: 4,
        kv_heads: 2,
        key_length,
        value_length,
        rope_freq_base: 10_000.0,
        rope_freq_base_swa: 10_000.0,
        rms_eps: 1e-6,
        sliding_window,
        logit_softcap: 20.0,
        logit_scale: 0.5,
        vocab_size: VOCAB as u32,
        layers,
        pattern_source: PatternSource::MeasuredFallback,
    }
}

fn make_model(cfg: &GlimmerConfig, style: Style) -> GlimmerModel {
    let source = build_source(cfg, style);
    let weights = Weights::load(&source, cfg).expect("synthetic weights load");
    GlimmerModel::new(cfg.clone(), weights, Box::new(CpuCompute::new()))
}

/// Test-local RMSNorm (weight 1) in f64, from the formula. Shares no
/// code with the backend or with `torch-math`.
fn rms64(v: &[f64], eps: f64) -> Vec<f64> {
    let ms = v.iter().map(|x| x * x).sum::<f64>() / v.len() as f64;
    let inv = 1.0 / (ms + eps).sqrt();
    v.iter().map(|x| x * inv).collect()
}

fn max_diff(a: &[f32], b: &[f32]) -> f32 {
    a.iter()
        .zip(b.iter())
        .map(|(x, y)| (x - y).abs())
        .fold(0.0, f32::max)
}

#[test]
fn zero_attention_and_ffn_match_hand_computed_logits() {
    // CONVENTIONS PINNED, settled from llama.cpp source in the Run B
    // follow-up (src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp): (1) the embedding
    // output passes a weightless RMSNorm before layer 0; (2) each
    // post norm normalizes the sub-block's OUTPUT and the result is
    // added to the untouched residual, so the residual stream itself
    // is never renormalized; (3) the head scales first, then
    // softcaps. With the attention output projection and the FFN
    // down projection zeroed, both branch outputs are the zero
    // vector, their post norms are zero too, and each layer leaves
    // the stream exactly as it found it. The expected logits below
    // are computed by exactly that reading with test-local math:
    // the embedding row passes TWO norms in total (embedding norm,
    // final norm). The pre-fix conventions (post norms after the
    // adds, no embedding norm, cap before scale) would give five
    // norms and a different finishing curve, and fail here.
    let cfg = test_config(vec![LayerKind::SlidingWindow, LayerKind::SlidingWindow], 16);
    let model = make_model(&cfg, Style::Analytic);
    let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
    let logits = model
        .forward(&[7, 42, 3], &mut cache)
        .expect("forward runs");
    assert_eq!(cache.position(), 3);
    assert_eq!(logits.len(), VOCAB);

    // Last token is 3; its embedding row passes the embedding norm
    // and the final norm, then the repeat-identity head, then the
    // file's scale and softcap (scale 0.5, cap 20, in that order).
    let mut x: Vec<f64> = (0..HIDDEN)
        .map(|i| f64::from(emb_pattern_a(3, i)))
        .collect();
    for _ in 0..2 {
        x = rms64(&x, 1e-6);
    }
    for (j, got) in logits.iter().enumerate() {
        let z = x[j % HIDDEN];
        let want = 20.0 * (0.5 * z / 20.0).tanh();
        assert!(
            (f64::from(*got) - want).abs() < 1e-4,
            "logit {j}: got {got}, want {want}"
        );
    }
}

/// Test-local RoPE in f64: adjacent pairs, pair i turning by
/// position * base^(-2i / dim). This is ggml's NORM pairing, the
/// one llama.cpp selects for muse-glimmer; torch-math's default
/// `rope` is the half-split NEOX pairing the llama/qwen2 families
/// use, and the Glimmer backend must not call that one.
fn rope64(v: &[f64], position: usize, base: f64) -> Vec<f64> {
    let mut out = v.to_vec();
    let dim = v.len() as f64;
    for pair in 0..v.len() / 2 {
        let angle = position as f64 * base.powf(-((2 * pair) as f64) / dim);
        let (s, c) = angle.sin_cos();
        let (a, b) = (out[2 * pair], out[2 * pair + 1]);
        out[2 * pair] = a * c - b * s;
        out[2 * pair + 1] = a * s + b * c;
    }
    out
}

#[test]
fn attention_mixing_matches_a_naive_reference() {
    // CONVENTIONS PINNED, settled from llama.cpp source in the Run B
    // follow-up (src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp): (1) the attention
    // gate projection reads the same normed input as the Q/K/V
    // projections. Here attn_gate is 0.25 * identity, so the gate
    // values are 0.25 * h and the naive route below uses h (the
    // normed input), never the raw stream; the opposite reading
    // produces different numbers and would fail. (2) The embedding
    // output is RMS-normed (weightless) before the layer, and that
    // normed stream, not the raw embedding, is the residual base.
    // (3) The post-attention norm normalizes the branch output
    // (with the reference graph's hardcoded eps 1e-8) before the
    // residual add; the FFN output is zero in this style, so its
    // post norm contributes nothing. (4) RoPE runs on the sliding
    // layer and NOT on the global layer (NoPE), so the naive route
    // runs twice, once per kind, rotating only for the sliding one:
    // a backend that rotates the global layer, or fails to rotate
    // the sliding one, disagrees with one of the two runs.
    // Everything else (QK norms per head, GQA grouping 2:1, causal
    // masking, the gate's sigmoid, the final norm, scale-then-cap)
    // is computed here from the formulas, in f64, sharing no code
    // with the backend.
    let eps = 1e-6f64;
    let post_eps = 1e-8f64; // the reference graph's hardcoded post-norm eps
    let toks = [5usize, 9usize];
    let emb: Vec<Vec<f64>> = toks
        .iter()
        .map(|&t| {
            (0..HIDDEN)
                .map(|i| f64::from(emb_pattern_b(t, i)))
                .collect()
        })
        .collect();
    // The stream entering the layer: embedding rows after the
    // weightless embedding norm.
    let stream: Vec<Vec<f64>> = emb.iter().map(|x| rms64(x, eps)).collect();
    let h: Vec<Vec<f64>> = stream.iter().map(|x| rms64(x, eps)).collect();

    for (kind, rotate) in [(LayerKind::Global, false), (LayerKind::SlidingWindow, true)] {
        let cfg = test_config(vec![kind], 16);
        let model = make_model(&cfg, Style::Attention);
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        let logits = model.forward(&[5, 9], &mut cache).expect("forward runs");
        assert_eq!(cache.position(), 2);

        let q_of = |p: usize, head: usize| -> Vec<f64> {
            let q = rms64(&h[p][head * HEAD_DIM..(head + 1) * HEAD_DIM], eps);
            if rotate {
                rope64(&q, p, 10_000.0)
            } else {
                q
            }
        };
        let k_of = |p: usize, kv: usize| -> Vec<f64> {
            let k = rms64(&h[p][kv * HEAD_DIM..(kv + 1) * HEAD_DIM], eps);
            if rotate {
                rope64(&k, p, 10_000.0)
            } else {
                k
            }
        };
        let v_of =
            |p: usize, kv: usize| -> Vec<f64> { h[p][kv * HEAD_DIM..(kv + 1) * HEAD_DIM].to_vec() };

        // Attention for the last position (p = 1) only; its output
        // is what the returned logits are computed from.
        let p = 1;
        let mut attn = vec![0.0f64; HIDDEN];
        for head in 0..4 {
            let kv = head / 2; // GQA: heads pair up over 2 KV heads.
            let q = q_of(p, head);
            let mut scores = Vec::new();
            for j in 0..=p {
                let k = k_of(j, kv);
                let s: f64 =
                    q.iter().zip(&k).map(|(a, b)| a * b).sum::<f64>() / (HEAD_DIM as f64).sqrt();
                scores.push(s);
            }
            let max = scores.iter().cloned().fold(f64::NEG_INFINITY, f64::max);
            let exps: Vec<f64> = scores.iter().map(|s| (s - max).exp()).collect();
            let sum: f64 = exps.iter().sum();
            for d in 0..HEAD_DIM {
                let mut acc = 0.0;
                for (j, e) in exps.iter().enumerate() {
                    acc += (e / sum) * v_of(j, kv)[d];
                }
                attn[head * HEAD_DIM + d] = acc;
            }
        }
        // Gate: attn_gate = 0.25 * identity over the normed input h.
        let gated: Vec<f64> = attn
            .iter()
            .zip(&h[p])
            .map(|(a, hv)| a / (1.0 + (-(0.25 * hv)).exp()))
            .collect();
        // Output projection is identity. Post norm on the branch,
        // then the residual add against the embedding-normed stream.
        // The FFN branch is zero, so the stream passes it unchanged.
        let post = rms64(&gated, post_eps);
        let after: Vec<f64> = stream[p].iter().zip(&post).map(|(x, g)| x + g).collect();
        let n = rms64(&after, eps); // final norm
        for (j, got) in logits.iter().enumerate() {
            let z = n[j % HIDDEN];
            let want = 20.0 * (0.5 * z / 20.0).tanh();
            assert!(
                (f64::from(*got) - want).abs() < 1e-3,
                "{kind:?} logit {j}: got {got}, want {want}"
            );
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn post_norm_eps_and_placement_are_pinned_by_a_tiny_branch() {
    // The post-norm convention has two halves, both settled from
    // src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp: the norm applies to the branch
    // output BEFORE the residual add, with eps hardcoded to 1e-8
    // (not the file's 1e-5). With an ordinary-size branch the eps
    // half is numerically invisible, so this test shrinks the
    // attention output projection to 1e-4 * identity: the branch RMS
    // lands near sqrt(1e-8), where eps 1e-8 vs eps 1e-6 changes the
    // normalized branch by more than an order of magnitude, and the
    // placement half matters just as much (normalizing the branch
    // rescales it to unit RMS; normalizing the sum would leave it a
    // 1e-4 ripple on the stream). The naive route below computes
    // the expected logits under both eps readings and asserts the
    // backend lands on the 1e-8 one decisively.
    let cfg = test_config(vec![LayerKind::Global], 16);
    let mut source = build_source(&cfg, Style::Attention);
    source.tensors.insert(
        "blk.0.attn_output.weight".to_string(),
        f32_tensor(
            "blk.0.attn_output.weight",
            &[HIDDEN as u64, HIDDEN as u64],
            scaled_identity(HIDDEN, 1e-4),
        ),
    );
    let weights = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect("weights load");
    let model = GlimmerModel::new(cfg, weights, Box::new(CpuCompute::new()));
    let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
    let logits = model.forward(&[5, 9], &mut cache).expect("forward runs");

    let eps = 1e-6f64;
    let toks = [5usize, 9usize];
    let emb: Vec<Vec<f64>> = toks
        .iter()
        .map(|&t| {
            (0..HIDDEN)
                .map(|i| f64::from(emb_pattern_b(t, i)))
                .collect()
        })
        .collect();
    let stream: Vec<Vec<f64>> = emb.iter().map(|x| rms64(x, eps)).collect();
    let h: Vec<Vec<f64>> = stream.iter().map(|x| rms64(x, eps)).collect();
    let p = 1;
    let mut attn = vec![0.0f64; HIDDEN];
    for head in 0..4 {
        let kv = head / 2;
        let q = rms64(&h[p][head * HEAD_DIM..(head + 1) * HEAD_DIM], eps);
        let mut scores = Vec::new();
        for hj in h.iter().take(p + 1) {
            let k = rms64(&hj[kv * HEAD_DIM..(kv + 1) * HEAD_DIM], eps);
            let s: f64 =
                q.iter().zip(&k).map(|(a, b)| a * b).sum::<f64>() / (HEAD_DIM as f64).sqrt();
            scores.push(s);
        }
        let max = scores.iter().cloned().fold(f64::NEG_INFINITY, f64::max);
        let exps: Vec<f64> = scores.iter().map(|s| (s - max).exp()).collect();
        let sum: f64 = exps.iter().sum();
        for d in 0..HEAD_DIM {
            let mut acc = 0.0;
            for (j, e) in exps.iter().enumerate() {
                acc += (e / sum) * h[j][kv * HEAD_DIM + d];
            }
            attn[head * HEAD_DIM + d] = acc;
        }
    }
    let branch: Vec<f64> = attn
        .iter()
        .zip(&h[p])
        .map(|(a, hv)| 1e-4 * a / (1.0 + (-(0.25 * hv)).exp()))
        .collect();
    let expected = |post_eps: f64| -> Vec<f64> {
        let post = rms64(&branch, post_eps);
        let after: Vec<f64> = stream[p].iter().zip(&post).map(|(x, g)| x + g).collect();
        let n = rms64(&after, eps);
        (0..VOCAB)
            .map(|j| 20.0 * (0.5 * n[j % HIDDEN] / 20.0).tanh())
            .collect()
    };
    let to_f32 = |v: &[f64]| v.iter().map(|x| *x as f32).collect::<Vec<f32>>();
    let d_right = max_diff(&logits, &to_f32(&expected(1e-8)));
    let d_wrong = max_diff(&logits, &to_f32(&expected(1e-6)));
    assert!(
        d_right < 2e-3 && d_right * 10.0 < d_wrong,
        "post-norm eps/placement not decisive: distance to the eps-1e-8 reading \
         is {d_right}, to the eps-1e-6 reading is {d_wrong}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn forward_is_deterministic() {
    let cfg = test_config(vec![LayerKind::SlidingWindow, LayerKind::Global], 16);
    let run = || {
        let model = make_model(&cfg, Style::Random);
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        model
            .forward(&[11, 22, 33, 44], &mut cache)
            .expect("forward runs")
    };
    let a = run();
    let b = run();
    assert_eq!(a, b, "same weights and input must give identical logits");
}

#[test]
fn incremental_decode_matches_one_shot_prefill() {
    // THE KV correctness proof. One model consumes the sequence in
    // three calls (2 tokens, 1 token, 2 tokens) against one cache;
    // separate models consume each prefix in a single call. Because
    // CpuCompute's attention appends and attends one position at a
    // time, both routes execute the same operations in the same
    // order, and the logits must agree to float exactness (the 1e-6
    // bound leaves room only for reassociation noise, of which there
    // should be none).
    let cfg = test_config(vec![LayerKind::SlidingWindow, LayerKind::Global], 16);
    let seq = [3u32, 17, 42, 90, 5];

    let mut reference: Vec<Vec<f32>> = Vec::new();
    for len in [2usize, 3, 5] {
        let model = make_model(&cfg, Style::Random);
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        reference.push(
            model
                .forward(&seq[..len], &mut cache)
                .expect("one-shot forward runs"),
        );
    }

    let model = make_model(&cfg, Style::Random);
    let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
    let first = model.forward(&seq[0..2], &mut cache).expect("chunk 1");
    let second = model.forward(&seq[2..3], &mut cache).expect("chunk 2");
    let third = model.forward(&seq[3..5], &mut cache).expect("chunk 3");
    let got = [first, second, third];
    assert_eq!(cache.position(), 5);

    for (i, (g, r)) in got.iter().zip(reference.iter()).enumerate() {
        let d = max_diff(g, r);
        assert!(
            d <= 1e-6,
            "step {i}: incremental logits differ from one-shot prefill by {d}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn incremental_matches_prefill_across_window_eviction() {
    // Same proof, but the sliding layer's window (3) is smaller than
    // the sequence (6), so the ring buffer evicts mid-sequence on
    // both routes. The global layer rides along in the same model.
    let cfg = test_config(vec![LayerKind::SlidingWindow, LayerKind::Global], 3);
    let seq = [9u32, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4];

    let reference = {
        let model = make_model(&cfg, Style::Random);
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        model
            .forward(&seq, &mut cache)
            .expect("one-shot forward runs")
    };

    let model = make_model(&cfg, Style::Random);
    let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
    model.forward(&seq[0..4], &mut cache).expect("chunk 1");
    let got = model.forward(&seq[4..6], &mut cache).expect("chunk 2");
    assert_eq!(cache.position(), 6);

    let d = max_diff(&got, &reference);
    assert!(
        d <= 1e-6,
        "incremental logits differ from one-shot prefill by {d} across window eviction"
    );
}

/// Intermediate-scale config for the decode-sensitivity test: the
/// real model's head geometry (32 Q heads over 2 KV heads, a 16 to
/// 1 grouping), its eps and RoPE base, an every-fourth global layer
/// pattern like the real 52, but only 8 layers and hidden 512 so
/// the test stays inside a debug-build time budget (the reference
/// backend dequantizes per call; at hidden 1024 this test took
/// ~300 s in debug). The existing proofs are 2 layers, 4 heads,
/// head dim 8; run B's freeze appeared at real scale, so this test
/// exists to find which scale axis, if any, kills decode
/// sensitivity in isolation.
fn intermediate_config() -> GlimmerConfig {
    let layers: Vec<LayerKind> = (0..8)
        .map(|i| {
            if i % 4 == 3 {
                LayerKind::Global
            } else {
                LayerKind::SlidingWindow
            }
        })
        .collect();
    GlimmerConfig {
        name: Some("intermediate synthetic".to_string()),
        block_count: 8,
        context_length: 4096,
        hidden: 512,
        ffn_hidden: 1024,
        q_heads: 32,
        kv_heads: 2,
        key_length: 16,
        value_length: 16,
        rope_freq_base: 500_000.0,
        rope_freq_base_swa: 500_000.0,
        rms_eps: 1e-5,
        sliding_window: 2048,
        logit_softcap: 20.0,
        logit_scale: 0.196_116_13,
        vocab_size: 96,
        layers,
        pattern_source: PatternSource::MeasuredFallback,
    }
}

#[test]
fn decode_step_tracks_the_fed_token_at_intermediate_scale() {
    // Run B's second symptom: at decode time the returned top-5 was
    // identical to about 1e-6 regardless of the token fed. This test
    // measures exactly that sensitivity at intermediate scale: same
    // prompt, two different decode tokens, and the max logit
    // difference between the two resulting distributions must be
    // orders of magnitude above the freeze signature. The one-shot
    // cross-check separates "the decode path is broken" from "the
    // model's dynamics are insensitive": a correct decode step must
    // also reproduce the one-shot logits for prompt + token.
    let cfg = intermediate_config();
    let prompt: [u32; 5] = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];

    let decode_after = |token: u32| -> Vec<f32> {
        let model = make_model(&cfg, Style::Random);
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        model.forward(&prompt, &mut cache).expect("prefill");
        model.forward(&[token], &mut cache).expect("decode step")
    };
    let logits_a = decode_after(7);
    let logits_b = decode_after(42);

    let sensitivity = max_diff(&logits_a, &logits_b);
    eprintln!("intermediate-scale decode sensitivity (7 vs 42): {sensitivity}");
    assert!(
        sensitivity > 1e-3,
        "decode sensitivity collapsed: feeding token 7 vs token 42 after the \
         same prompt changed the logits by only {sensitivity} (freeze signature \
         in run B was ~1e-6)"
    );

    // The decode step must equal a one-shot run over prompt + token.
    let one_shot = {
        let model = make_model(&cfg, Style::Random);
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        let mut seq = prompt.to_vec();
        seq.push(7);
        model.forward(&seq, &mut cache).expect("one-shot")
    };
    let lag = max_diff(&logits_a, &one_shot);
    assert!(
        lag <= 1e-5,
        "decode step disagrees with one-shot prompt+token by {lag}: the decode \
         path is not computing the distribution for the position it claims"
    );
}

#[test]
fn unsupported_dtype_refuses_by_name() {
    // A Q4_0 tensor in the FFN down projection: the gguf crate has
    // no Q4_0 dequantizer, so the forward must refuse naming the
    // tensor and the type, never substitute anything.
    let cfg = test_config(vec![LayerKind::SlidingWindow, LayerKind::Global], 16);
    let mut source = build_source(&cfg, Style::Random);
    source.tensors.insert(
        "blk.0.ffn_down.weight".to_string(),
        TensorView {
            name: "blk.0.ffn_down.weight".to_string(),
            dtype: Dtype::Q4_0,
            // A plausible [ffn, hidden] shape, so the shape checks
            // pass and it is the dtype refusal that fires.
            shape: vec![FFN as u64, HIDDEN as u64],
            data: Arc::from(vec![0u8; 4].into_boxed_slice()),
        },
    );
    let weights = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect("weights load");
    let model = GlimmerModel::new(cfg, weights, Box::new(CpuCompute::new()));
    let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
    let err = model
        .forward(&[1, 2], &mut cache)
        .expect_err("Q4_0 must refuse");
    match err {
        GlimmerError::StepFailed { step, detail } => {
            assert_eq!(step, "swiglu_ffn");
            assert!(detail.contains("blk.0.ffn_down.weight"), "{detail}");
            assert!(detail.contains("Q4_0"), "{detail}");
        }
        other => panic!("expected StepFailed, got {other:?}"),
    }
    // A refused pass must not advance the caller's cache.
    assert_eq!(cache.position(), 0);
}

#[test]
fn fresh_cache_against_used_compute_refuses() {
    // The position contract: the backend's KV state is at position 2
    // after a 2-token forward, so handing the same model a fresh
    // cache (position 0) must refuse, not attend to a history the
    // caller does not know about.
    let cfg = test_config(vec![LayerKind::SlidingWindow, LayerKind::Global], 16);
    let model = make_model(&cfg, Style::Random);
    let mut cache_a = PositionCache::new();
    model
        .forward(&[1, 2], &mut cache_a)
        .expect("first forward runs");
    assert_eq!(cache_a.position(), 2);

    let mut cache_b = PositionCache::new();
    let err = model
        .forward(&[3], &mut cache_b)
        .expect_err("diverged caches must refuse");
    match err {
        GlimmerError::StepFailed { step, detail } => {
            assert_eq!(step, "attention");
            assert!(detail.contains("position 2"), "{detail}");
            assert!(detail.contains("position 0"), "{detail}");
        }
        other => panic!("expected StepFailed, got {other:?}"),
    }
}

#[test]
fn mismatched_key_value_length_refuses() {
    // The attention crate stores keys and values at one head
    // dimension; a config with key_length 8 and value_length 4 is
    // refused by name at the attention step.
    let cfg = test_config_kv(vec![LayerKind::Global], 16, 8, 4);
    let model = make_model(&cfg, Style::Random);
    let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
    let err = model
        .forward(&[1], &mut cache)
        .expect_err("mismatched head lengths must refuse");
    match err {
        GlimmerError::StepFailed { step, detail } => {
            assert_eq!(step, "attention");
            assert!(detail.contains("key_length 8"), "{detail}");
            assert!(detail.contains("value_length 4"), "{detail}");
        }
        other => panic!("expected StepFailed, got {other:?}"),
    }
}

/// Block forward (E1) and the speculative round trip (E1 + E2),
/// appended as their own module so the convention proofs above stay
/// untouched. These tests reuse the fixtures above: same weight
/// builder, same configs, same max-diff helper.
mod block_and_spec {
    use super::*;
    use std::rc::Rc;

    use muse_glimmer::{AttentionRequest, Compute, LayerWeights};

    #[test]
    fn block_forward_matches_sequential_single_token_forwards() {
        // E1's core proof: teacher-forcing a block yields, at every
        // row, the distribution a sequential decode produces at that
        // position. Causality is what makes this exact rather than
        // approximate: row i may only depend on tokens 0..=i, and
        // both routes compute it that way.
        let cfg = test_config(vec![LayerKind::SlidingWindow, LayerKind::Global], 16);
        let vocab = cfg.vocab_size as usize;
        let seq = [3u32, 17, 42, 90, 5];

        let model = make_model(&cfg, Style::Random);
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        let block = model
            .forward_block(&seq, &mut cache)
            .expect("block forward runs");
        assert_eq!(block.len(), seq.len() * vocab);
        assert_eq!(cache.position(), seq.len());

        let stepped = make_model(&cfg, Style::Random);
        let mut stepped_cache = PositionCache::new();
        for (i, &token) in seq.iter().enumerate() {
            let logits = stepped
                .forward(&[token], &mut stepped_cache)
                .expect("sequential step runs");
            let row = &block[i * vocab..(i + 1) * vocab];
            let d = max_diff(row, &logits);
            assert!(
                d <= 1e-6,
                "position {i}: block row differs from the sequential forward by {d}"
            );
        }

        // forward is the block's last row: one implementation, two
        // entry points.
        let whole = make_model(&cfg, Style::Random);
        let mut whole_cache = PositionCache::new();
        let last = whole
            .forward(&seq, &mut whole_cache)
            .expect("one-shot forward runs");
        let d = max_diff(&block[(seq.len() - 1) * vocab..], &last);
        assert!(
            d <= 1e-6,
            "forward disagrees with forward_block's last row by {d}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn block_forward_crossing_a_sliding_window_boundary_matches_sequential() {
        // Window 3, sequence 6: the block crosses the ring boundary
        // mid-block, and rows after the crossing were computed
        // against a window the earlier rows never saw. The per-row
        // agreement with the sequential route must survive that.
        let cfg = test_config(vec![LayerKind::SlidingWindow, LayerKind::Global], 3);
        let vocab = cfg.vocab_size as usize;
        let seq = [9u32, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4];

        let model = make_model(&cfg, Style::Random);
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        let block = model
            .forward_block(&seq, &mut cache)
            .expect("block forward runs");

        let stepped = make_model(&cfg, Style::Random);
        let mut stepped_cache = PositionCache::new();
        for (i, &token) in seq.iter().enumerate() {
            let logits = stepped
                .forward(&[token], &mut stepped_cache)
                .expect("sequential step runs");
            let row = &block[i * vocab..(i + 1) * vocab];
            let d = max_diff(row, &logits);
            assert!(
                d <= 1e-6,
                "position {i}: block row differs across the window boundary by {d}"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn block_forward_matches_sequential_at_intermediate_scale() {
        // Same proof at the convention tests' intermediate scale:
        // 8 layers in the real every-fourth pattern, 32 Q heads over
        // 2 KV heads, the real eps and softcap/scale finishing.
        let cfg = intermediate_config();
        let vocab = cfg.vocab_size as usize;
        let seq = [3u32, 17, 42, 90, 5, 23];

        let model = make_model(&cfg, Style::Random);
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        let block = model
            .forward_block(&seq, &mut cache)
            .expect("block forward runs");
        assert_eq!(block.len(), seq.len() * vocab);

        let stepped = make_model(&cfg, Style::Random);
        let mut stepped_cache = PositionCache::new();
        for (i, &token) in seq.iter().enumerate() {
            let logits = stepped
                .forward(&[token], &mut stepped_cache)
                .expect("sequential step runs");
            let row = &block[i * vocab..(i + 1) * vocab];
            let d = max_diff(row, &logits);
            assert!(
                d <= 1e-5,
                "position {i}: block row differs from the sequential forward by {d} at intermediate scale"
            );
        }
    }

    /// A `Compute` that delegates to a shared `CpuCompute`, so a
    /// test can hold the backend next to the model that owns it and
    /// drive the checkpoint API the model cannot see. Test
    /// scaffolding only: every method is a one-line forward.
    struct SharedCompute(Rc<CpuCompute>);

    impl Compute for SharedCompute {
        fn embed(
            &self,
            table: &TensorView,
            tokens: &[u32],
            cfg: &GlimmerConfig,
        ) -> muse_glimmer::Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.0.embed(table, tokens, cfg)
        }

        fn rms_norm(
            &self,
            x: &[f32],
            weight: &TensorView,
            rows: usize,
            eps: f32,
        ) -> muse_glimmer::Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.0.rms_norm(x, weight, rows, eps)
        }

        fn rms_norm_plain(
            &self,
            x: &[f32],
            rows: usize,
            eps: f32,
        ) -> muse_glimmer::Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.0.rms_norm_plain(x, rows, eps)
        }

        fn proj(
            &self,
            x: &[f32],
            weight: &TensorView,
            rows: usize,
        ) -> muse_glimmer::Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.0.proj(x, weight, rows)
        }

        fn attention(
            &self,
            req: &AttentionRequest<'_>,
            cache: &mut dyn Cache,
        ) -> muse_glimmer::Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.0.attention(req, cache)
        }

        fn attn_gate(&self, attn_out: &[f32], gate: &[f32]) -> muse_glimmer::Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.0.attn_gate(attn_out, gate)
        }

        fn add(&self, a: &[f32], b: &[f32]) -> muse_glimmer::Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.0.add(a, b)
        }

        fn swiglu_ffn(
            &self,
            x: &[f32],
            w: &LayerWeights,
            rows: usize,
            cfg: &GlimmerConfig,
        ) -> muse_glimmer::Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.0.swiglu_ffn(x, w, rows, cfg)
        }

        fn lm_head(
            &self,
            x: &[f32],
            head: &TensorView,
            cfg: &GlimmerConfig,
        ) -> muse_glimmer::Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.0.lm_head(x, head, cfg)
        }
    }

    fn make_shared_model(cfg: &GlimmerConfig) -> (GlimmerModel, Rc<CpuCompute>) {
        let compute = Rc::new(CpuCompute::new());
        let source = build_source(cfg, Style::Random);
        let weights = Weights::load(&source, cfg).expect("synthetic weights load");
        let model = GlimmerModel::new(
            cfg.clone(),
            weights,
            Box::new(SharedCompute(compute.clone())),
        );
        (model, compute)
    }

    #[test]
    fn speculative_round_trip_rewind_restores_exact_continuation() {
        // The whole E1 + E2 loop at model scale, on a window-3
        // config: the prompt alone overflows the ring, and the
        // block's appends evict rows held for the committed prefix
        // (SPEC Section 5.1's corruption case, proven byte-exact at
        // the cache level in the attention crate's tests). The round
        // bound equals the window here, the largest round the ring
        // admits exactly. Checkpoint, block forward over three
        // drafted tokens, rewind to keep the first two, release,
        // then continue: the continuation logits must match a route
        // that never speculated, because the rewind restored the
        // cache exactly, kept speculative rows included.
        let cfg = test_config(vec![LayerKind::SlidingWindow, LayerKind::Global], 3);
        let prompt = [3u32, 17, 42, 90];
        let block_tokens = [5u32, 23, 8];
        let continuation = [11u32];

        let reference = {
            let model = make_model(&cfg, Style::Random);
            let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
            model.forward(&prompt, &mut cache).expect("prefill");
            model
                .forward(&block_tokens[..2], &mut cache)
                .expect("kept tokens");
            model
                .forward(&continuation, &mut cache)
                .expect("continuation")
        };

        let (model, compute) = make_shared_model(&cfg);
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        model.forward(&prompt, &mut cache).expect("prefill");
        assert_eq!(cache.position(), 4);
        let checkpoint = compute.cache_checkpoint(3).expect("checkpoint");
        let block = model
            .forward_block(&block_tokens, &mut cache)
            .expect("verify forward");
        assert_eq!(block.len(), block_tokens.len() * VOCAB);
        assert_eq!(cache.position(), 7);
        // Commit: base 4, pending + 1 accepted = keep 2 of the block.
        compute.cache_rewind(&checkpoint, 6).expect("kv rewind");
        cache.rewind_to(6);
        compute.cache_release(&checkpoint).expect("release");
        let got = model
            .forward(&continuation, &mut cache)
            .expect("continuation");
        assert_eq!(cache.position(), 7);

        let d = max_diff(&got, &reference);
        assert!(
            d <= 1e-6,
            "post-rewind continuation differs from the never-speculated route by {d}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rewound_kv_with_unrewound_position_cache_refuses() {
        // The two-truths hazard of SPEC Section 5.4: the KV store is
        // rewound but the position cache is not, so they disagree
        // (2 vs 4). The next forward must refuse by name at the
        // attention step's cross-check, not attend across the gap.
        let cfg = test_config(vec![LayerKind::SlidingWindow, LayerKind::Global], 16);
        let (model, compute) = make_shared_model(&cfg);
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        model.forward(&[3, 17], &mut cache).expect("prefill");
        let checkpoint = compute.cache_checkpoint(2).expect("checkpoint");
        model
            .forward_block(&[42, 90], &mut cache)
            .expect("block forward");
        compute.cache_rewind(&checkpoint, 2).expect("kv rewind");
        compute.cache_release(&checkpoint).expect("release");
        // Deliberately no cache.rewind_to(2) here.
        let err = model
            .forward(&[5], &mut cache)
            .expect_err("diverged position truths must refuse");
        match err {
            GlimmerError::StepFailed { step, detail } => {
                assert_eq!(step, "attention");
                assert!(detail.contains("position 2"), "{detail}");
                assert!(detail.contains("position 4"), "{detail}");
            }
            other => panic!("expected StepFailed, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------
// Captured layer inputs (E3): the additive capture the DFlash draft's
// conditioning consumes. Proven three ways: the capturing pass returns
// bit-identical logits to the plain pass on the same weights; the
// layer-0 capture equals the closed-form weightless RMSNorm of the
// embedding rows; and the block capturing variant captures the same
// rows as the single forward variant.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------

#[test]
fn capturing_forward_is_additive_and_captures_true_layer_inputs() {
    let cfg = test_config(vec![LayerKind::SlidingWindow, LayerKind::Global], 16);
    let tokens = [5u32, 9, 3];

    // Plain forward on one freshly built model.
    let plain = make_model(&cfg, Style::Random);
    let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
    let plain_logits = plain.forward(&tokens, &mut cache).expect("plain forward");
    assert_eq!(cache.position(), 3);

    // Capturing forward on an identically built model.
    let source = build_source(&cfg, Style::Random);
    let weights = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect("weights load");
    let emb_view = source
        .tensors
        .get("token_embd.weight")
        .expect("embedding tensor")
        .clone();
    let model = GlimmerModel::new(cfg.clone(), weights, Box::new(CpuCompute::new()));
    let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
    let (logits, captures) = model
        .forward_capturing(&tokens, &mut cache, &[0, 1])
        .expect("capturing forward");
    assert_eq!(logits, plain_logits, "capture must not change the logits");
    assert_eq!(cache.position(), 3);
    assert_eq!(captures.len(), 2);
    assert_eq!(captures[0].layer, 0);
    assert_eq!(captures[1].layer, 1);

    // Layer 0's input is the embedding output after the weightless
    // RMSNorm: closed form, from the embedding bytes themselves.
    let emb_row = |token: u32| -> Vec<f64> {
        let start = token as usize * HIDDEN * 4;
        emb_view.data[start..start + HIDDEN * 4]
            .chunks_exact(4)
            .map(|b| f64::from(f32::from_le_bytes([b[0], b[1], b[2], b[3]])))
            .collect()
    };
    for (r, &token) in tokens.iter().enumerate() {
        let expected = rms64(&emb_row(token), 1e-6);
        let actual = &captures[0].rows[r * HIDDEN..(r + 1) * HIDDEN];
        for (a, e) in actual.iter().zip(expected.iter()) {
            assert!(
                (f64::from(*a) - e).abs() < 1e-5,
                "layer 0 capture row {r}: got {a}, expected {e}"
            );
        }
    }
    // Layer 1's input is layer 0's output: a different tensor than
    // layer 0's input (the random weights guarantee the layer moved
    // the residual), with the same shape.
    assert_eq!(captures[1].rows.len(), 3 * HIDDEN);
    assert_ne!(captures[1].rows, captures[0].rows);

    // The block variant captures the same rows and its last-row
    // logits equal the single forward's.
    let block_model = make_model(&cfg, Style::Random);
    let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
    let (block_logits, block_captures) = block_model
        .forward_block_capturing(&tokens, &mut cache, &[1, 0])
        .expect("block capturing forward");
    assert_eq!(block_captures, captures);
    let last = &block_logits[(tokens.len() - 1) * VOCAB..tokens.len() * VOCAB];
    assert_eq!(last, plain_logits.as_slice());
}

===== FILE: crates/dflash/src/cache.rs =====
//! [`DflashCache`]: the draft's own KV storage.
//!
//! The draft's cache is filled by the injection pass
//! ([`crate::DflashModel::inject`]) with K/V projected from the
//! fused target conditioning at TARGET positions, and read by the
//! drafting pass. It is not the target's cache, it is not
//! checkpointed by the target-side machinery, and the drafting pass
//! never writes to it: block K/V built while proposing are
//! speculative state, discarded when the block ends (SPEC-itak-spec
//! Section 4 step 7: after a round, the draft's state equals having
//! processed exactly the committed sequence, which arrives through
//! `inject` and nothing else).
//!
//! Storage is one position map per layer over a shared position
//! set (an injection writes every layer at the same positions).
//! Sliding-window eviction is a READ-side mask, applied in the
//! attention step exactly as the reference graph's mask states it
//! (a key at `kp` is visible to a query at `p` when
//! `kp > p - window`): keeping the rows and masking at read time is
//! visibility-identical to the reference's ring eviction, and it
//! keeps overwrite-after-rewind semantics trivially correct.
//! Re-injecting a held position overwrites its rows, matching
//! llama.cpp's cache, which sets the cell at a position when the
//! target reprocesses it.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;

use crate::config::DflashConfig;

/// One position's stored rows for one layer.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct KvRow {
    /// Key row, `[kv_heads * key_length]`, RoPE already applied.
    pub k: Vec<f32>,
    /// Value row, `[kv_heads * value_length]`.
    pub v: Vec<f32>,
}

/// The draft model's KV cache: per-layer position maps over one
/// shared set of committed positions.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct DflashCache {
    layers: Vec<BTreeMap<usize, KvRow>>,
}

impl DflashCache {
    /// An empty cache shaped for `cfg`'s layer count.
    pub fn new(cfg: &DflashConfig) -> Self {
        DflashCache {
            layers: (0..cfg.block_count as usize)
                .map(|_| BTreeMap::new())
                .collect(),
        }
    }

    /// Drop every stored position. The next injection starts a
    /// fresh sequence.
    pub fn reset(&mut self) {
        for layer in &mut self.layers {
            layer.clear();
        }
    }

    /// Number of committed positions held (the same for every
    /// layer; layer 0's map is the count of record).
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.layers.first().map_or(0, BTreeMap::len)
    }

    /// Whether no position has been injected yet.
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.len() == 0
    }

    /// Whether `position` has been injected.
    pub fn contains(&self, position: usize) -> bool {
        self.layers
            .first()
            .is_some_and(|layer| layer.contains_key(&position))
    }

    /// Every held position, ascending.
    pub fn positions(&self) -> Vec<usize> {
        self.layers
            .first()
            .map(|layer| layer.keys().copied().collect())
            .unwrap_or_default()
    }

    /// The stored row for (`layer`, `position`), when present.
    pub fn get(&self, layer: usize, position: usize) -> Option<&KvRow> {
        self.layers.get(layer)?.get(&position)
    }

    /// Iterate one layer's rows in ascending position order.
    pub fn iter_layer(&self, layer: usize) -> impl Iterator<Item = (usize, &KvRow)> {
        self.layers
            .get(layer)
            .into_iter()
            .flat_map(|map| map.iter().map(|(p, row)| (*p, row)))
    }

    /// Store (or overwrite) one position's row on one layer. Called
    /// only by the model's injection pass, which validates widths
    /// and position order before any store happens.
    pub(crate) fn insert(&mut self, layer: usize, position: usize, row: KvRow) {
        if let Some(map) = self.layers.get_mut(layer) {
            map.insert(position, row);
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::testkit::tiny_config;

    fn row(fill: f32) -> KvRow {
        KvRow {
            k: vec![fill; 4],
            v: vec![fill; 4],
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn insert_get_and_overwrite() {
        let cfg = tiny_config();
        let mut cache = DflashCache::new(&cfg);
        assert!(cache.is_empty());
        cache.insert(0, 3, row(1.0));
        cache.insert(0, 1, row(2.0));
        cache.insert(1, 3, row(3.0));
        assert_eq!(cache.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(cache.positions(), vec![1, 3]);
        assert!(cache.contains(3));
        assert!(!cache.contains(2));
        assert_eq!(cache.get(0, 3).expect("row").k, vec![1.0; 4]);
        assert_eq!(cache.get(1, 3).expect("row").v, vec![3.0; 4]);
        // Overwrite replaces, never duplicates.
        cache.insert(0, 3, row(9.0));
        assert_eq!(cache.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(cache.get(0, 3).expect("row").k, vec![9.0; 4]);
        // Ascending iteration regardless of insertion order.
        let seen: Vec<usize> = cache.iter_layer(0).map(|(p, _)| p).collect();
        assert_eq!(seen, vec![1, 3]);
        cache.reset();
        assert!(cache.is_empty());
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/dflash/src/config.rs =====
//! [`DflashConfig`]: the architecture parameters of a DFlash draft
//! model, parsed from GGUF metadata.
//!
//! Every value comes from the file, read through the [`Metadata`]
//! seam under the file's own `dflash` prefixed keys (plus the
//! `general` and `tokenizer` blocks). Nothing is defaulted silently:
//! a missing required key is a [`DflashError::MissingMetadata`]
//! naming the key. The two optional keys carry defined meanings in
//! the reference implementation and are handled explicitly:
//! `dflash.attention.causal` absent means the draft's block
//! attention is non-causal (llama.cpp's graph reads the flag with a
//! false default, src/models/dflash.cpp), and `dflash.hidden_act`
//! absent means silu; any other activation value is refused as an
//! unsupported feature rather than approximated.
//!
//! Measured reference values (the real draft file,
//! `dflash-Muse-Glimmer-30B-Q4_K_M.gguf`, census 2026-10-30 read
//! with this workspace's `gguf` crate): 5 layers, hidden 6656,
//! FFN 19968, 32 Q heads over 8 KV heads, key and value length 128,
//! RoPE base 500000, RMS eps 1e-5, block size 16, target layers
//! [2, 14, 26, 38, 50], sliding window 2048 with an all-true
//! sliding pattern, mask token 201818, vocab 202048, context 131072.

use crate::error::{DflashError, Result};
use crate::metadata::Metadata;

/// The one architecture string this module serves.
pub const ARCHITECTURE: &str = "dflash";

// Metadata keys, spelled exactly as they appear in the real file.
pub(crate) const KEY_ARCHITECTURE: &str = "general.architecture";
pub(crate) const KEY_NAME: &str = "general.name";
pub(crate) const KEY_BLOCK_COUNT: &str = "dflash.block_count";
pub(crate) const KEY_CONTEXT_LENGTH: &str = "dflash.context_length";
pub(crate) const KEY_HIDDEN: &str = "dflash.embedding_length";
pub(crate) const KEY_FFN_HIDDEN: &str = "dflash.feed_forward_length";
pub(crate) const KEY_Q_HEADS: &str = "dflash.attention.head_count";
pub(crate) const KEY_KV_HEADS: &str = "dflash.attention.head_count_kv";
pub(crate) const KEY_KEY_LENGTH: &str = "dflash.attention.key_length";
pub(crate) const KEY_VALUE_LENGTH: &str = "dflash.attention.value_length";
pub(crate) const KEY_ROPE_FREQ_BASE: &str = "dflash.rope.freq_base";
pub(crate) const KEY_RMS_EPS: &str = "dflash.attention.layer_norm_rms_epsilon";
pub(crate) const KEY_BLOCK_SIZE: &str = "dflash.block_size";
pub(crate) const KEY_TARGET_LAYERS: &str = "dflash.target_layers";
pub(crate) const KEY_SLIDING_WINDOW: &str = "dflash.attention.sliding_window";
pub(crate) const KEY_SLIDING_PATTERN: &str = "dflash.attention.sliding_window_pattern";
pub(crate) const KEY_CAUSAL: &str = "dflash.attention.causal";
pub(crate) const KEY_HIDDEN_ACT: &str = "dflash.hidden_act";
pub(crate) const KEY_MASK_TOKEN: &str = "tokenizer.ggml.mask_token_id";
pub(crate) const KEY_VOCAB_TOKENS: &str = "tokenizer.ggml.tokens";

/// Architecture parameters for one DFlash draft model, all read
/// from its GGUF metadata.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct DflashConfig {
    /// Model name from `general.name`, when the file carries one.
    pub name: Option<String>,
    /// Number of draft transformer layers.
    pub block_count: u32,
    /// Maximum context length the draft was built for.
    pub context_length: u32,
    /// Draft hidden size (`embedding_length`).
    pub hidden: u32,
    /// Feed-forward intermediate size.
    pub ffn_hidden: u32,
    /// Query head count.
    pub q_heads: u32,
    /// Key/value head count.
    pub kv_heads: u32,
    /// Per-head key dimension.
    pub key_length: u32,
    /// Per-head value dimension.
    pub value_length: u32,
    /// RoPE frequency base. The draft has a single rope: llama.cpp
    /// uses this base for every layer, sliding or not.
    pub rope_freq_base: f32,
    /// RMSNorm epsilon, from the file.
    pub rms_eps: f32,
    /// Noise block size: the anchor plus at most `block_size - 1`
    /// drafted positions.
    pub block_size: u32,
    /// Target layer indices whose INPUT residual rows condition the
    /// draft, in concatenation order (`dflash.target_layers`;
    /// llama.cpp throws when this key is absent).
    pub target_layers: Vec<u32>,
    /// Sliding-window size in tokens, shared by every sliding layer.
    pub sliding_window: u32,
    /// Per-layer sliding flags, in layer order: `true` means the
    /// layer's attention reads through the sliding window.
    pub sliding_pattern: Vec<bool>,
    /// Whether block attention is causal. Absent key means false
    /// (non-causal block attention), the reference default.
    pub causal_attention: bool,
    /// The mask token id that fills the noise block after the
    /// anchor (`tokenizer.ggml.mask_token_id`).
    pub mask_token_id: u32,
    /// Vocabulary size, from the tokenizer token array length.
    pub vocab_size: u32,
}

impl DflashConfig {
    /// Parse a config from GGUF metadata. Fails loud on the first
    /// missing or impossible value; see the module docs.
    pub fn from_metadata<M: Metadata>(meta: &M) -> Result<Self> {
        let arch = meta
            .get_string(KEY_ARCHITECTURE)
            .ok_or(DflashError::MissingMetadata {
                key: KEY_ARCHITECTURE.to_string(),
            })?;
        if arch != ARCHITECTURE {
            return Err(DflashError::WrongArchitecture { found: arch });
        }

        if let Some(act) = meta.get_string(KEY_HIDDEN_ACT) {
            if act != "silu" {
                return Err(DflashError::UnsupportedFeature {
                    name: KEY_HIDDEN_ACT.to_string(),
                    detail: format!(
                        "hidden activation \"{act}\" is not implemented; this module implements silu (the reference graph's SwiGLU path)"
                    ),
                });
            }
        }

        let block_count = required_u32(meta, KEY_BLOCK_COUNT)?;
        if block_count == 0 {
            return Err(invalid(KEY_BLOCK_COUNT, "block_count is zero"));
        }
        let q_heads = required_u32(meta, KEY_Q_HEADS)?;
        let kv_heads = required_u32(meta, KEY_KV_HEADS)?;
        if q_heads == 0 || kv_heads == 0 {
            return Err(invalid(KEY_KV_HEADS, "head counts must be at least 1"));
        }
        if q_heads % kv_heads != 0 {
            return Err(invalid(
                KEY_KV_HEADS,
                "query head count is not a whole multiple of the KV head count, so grouped-query grouping is impossible",
            ));
        }
        let key_length = required_u32(meta, KEY_KEY_LENGTH)?;
        if key_length < 2 || key_length % 2 != 0 {
            return Err(invalid(
                KEY_KEY_LENGTH,
                "key length must be even and at least 2 for RoPE pairing",
            ));
        }
        let value_length = required_u32(meta, KEY_VALUE_LENGTH)?;
        if value_length == 0 {
            return Err(invalid(KEY_VALUE_LENGTH, "value length is zero"));
        }
        let block_size = required_u32(meta, KEY_BLOCK_SIZE)?;
        if block_size == 0 {
            return Err(invalid(KEY_BLOCK_SIZE, "block_size is zero"));
        }

        let target_layers =
            meta.get_u32_array(KEY_TARGET_LAYERS)
                .ok_or(DflashError::MissingMetadata {
                    key: KEY_TARGET_LAYERS.to_string(),
                })?;
        if target_layers.is_empty() {
            return Err(invalid(
                KEY_TARGET_LAYERS,
                "target layer list is empty; the draft would have no conditioning input",
            ));
        }
        for (i, &layer) in target_layers.iter().enumerate() {
            if target_layers[..i].contains(&layer) {
                return Err(invalid(
                    KEY_TARGET_LAYERS,
                    "target layer list contains a duplicate; each named layer is concatenated once",
                ));
            }
        }

        let sliding_pattern =
            meta.get_bool_array(KEY_SLIDING_PATTERN)
                .ok_or(DflashError::MissingMetadata {
                    key: KEY_SLIDING_PATTERN.to_string(),
                })?;
        if sliding_pattern.len() != block_count as usize {
            return Err(invalid(
                KEY_SLIDING_PATTERN,
                "sliding window pattern length does not equal the block count",
            ));
        }
        let sliding_window = required_u32(meta, KEY_SLIDING_WINDOW)?;
        if sliding_pattern.iter().any(|s| *s) && sliding_window == 0 {
            return Err(invalid(
                KEY_SLIDING_WINDOW,
                "pattern marks sliding layers but the sliding window is zero",
            ));
        }

        let causal_attention = match meta.get_string(KEY_CAUSAL) {
            Some(text) => match text.as_str() {
                "true" => true,
                "false" => false,
                other => {
                    return Err(invalid(
                        KEY_CAUSAL,
                        &format!(
                            "causal flag is the string \"{other}\", expected \"true\" or \"false\""
                        ),
                    ))
                }
            },
            None => meta.get_bool(KEY_CAUSAL).unwrap_or(false),
        };

        let rope_freq_base = required_f32(meta, KEY_ROPE_FREQ_BASE)?;
        if !rope_freq_base.is_finite() || rope_freq_base <= 1.0 {
            return Err(invalid(
                KEY_ROPE_FREQ_BASE,
                "rope frequency base must be finite and greater than 1",
            ));
        }
        let rms_eps = required_f32(meta, KEY_RMS_EPS)?;
        if !rms_eps.is_finite() || rms_eps <= 0.0 {
            return Err(invalid(
                KEY_RMS_EPS,
                "rms epsilon must be finite and greater than 0",
            ));
        }

        let vocab = meta
            .get_array_len(KEY_VOCAB_TOKENS)
            .ok_or(DflashError::MissingMetadata {
                key: KEY_VOCAB_TOKENS.to_string(),
            })?;
        let vocab_size = u32::try_from(vocab)
            .map_err(|_| invalid(KEY_VOCAB_TOKENS, "vocabulary size does not fit in u32"))?;
        if vocab_size == 0 {
            return Err(invalid(KEY_VOCAB_TOKENS, "vocabulary is empty"));
        }
        let mask_token_id = required_u32(meta, KEY_MASK_TOKEN)?;
        if mask_token_id >= vocab_size {
            return Err(invalid(
                KEY_MASK_TOKEN,
                "mask token id is outside the vocabulary",
            ));
        }

        Ok(DflashConfig {
            name: meta.get_string(KEY_NAME),
            block_count,
            context_length: required_u32(meta, KEY_CONTEXT_LENGTH)?,
            hidden: required_u32(meta, KEY_HIDDEN)?,
            ffn_hidden: required_u32(meta, KEY_FFN_HIDDEN)?,
            q_heads,
            kv_heads,
            key_length,
            value_length,
            rope_freq_base,
            rms_eps,
            block_size,
            target_layers,
            sliding_window,
            sliding_pattern,
            causal_attention,
            mask_token_id,
            vocab_size,
        })
    }

    /// Whether draft layer `index` attends through the sliding
    /// window, or `None` when out of range.
    pub fn is_sliding(&self, index: usize) -> Option<bool> {
        self.sliding_pattern.get(index).copied()
    }

    /// Width of the query projection per position.
    pub fn q_width(&self) -> u32 {
        self.q_heads * self.key_length
    }

    /// Width of the key projection per position.
    pub fn k_width(&self) -> u32 {
        self.kv_heads * self.key_length
    }

    /// Width of the value projection per position.
    pub fn v_width(&self) -> u32 {
        self.kv_heads * self.value_length
    }

    /// Width of the attention output per position (the output
    /// projection's input width).
    pub fn attn_out_width(&self) -> u32 {
        self.q_heads * self.value_length
    }

    /// Grouped-query group size: how many Q heads share one KV head.
    pub fn gqa_group(&self) -> u32 {
        self.q_heads / self.kv_heads
    }

    /// The largest number of draft tokens one block can propose:
    /// the block's first position is the anchor, which is not a
    /// draft.
    pub fn max_drafts(&self) -> u32 {
        self.block_size - 1
    }
}

fn required_u32<M: Metadata>(meta: &M, key: &'static str) -> Result<u32> {
    meta.get_u32(key).ok_or(DflashError::MissingMetadata {
        key: key.to_string(),
    })
}

fn required_f32<M: Metadata>(meta: &M, key: &'static str) -> Result<f32> {
    meta.get_f32(key).ok_or(DflashError::MissingMetadata {
        key: key.to_string(),
    })
}

fn invalid(key: &'static str, detail: &str) -> DflashError {
    DflashError::InvalidMetadata {
        key: key.to_string(),
        detail: detail.to_string(),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::testkit::{real_draft_metadata, tiny_metadata};

    #[test]
    fn real_file_metadata_parses_to_measured_values() {
        let cfg = DflashConfig::from_metadata(&real_draft_metadata()).expect("real metadata");
        assert_eq!(cfg.name.as_deref(), Some("Hf_Museglimmer"));
        assert_eq!(cfg.block_count, 5);
        assert_eq!(cfg.context_length, 131_072);
        assert_eq!(cfg.hidden, 6656);
        assert_eq!(cfg.ffn_hidden, 19_968);
        assert_eq!(cfg.q_heads, 32);
        assert_eq!(cfg.kv_heads, 8);
        assert_eq!(cfg.gqa_group(), 4);
        assert_eq!(cfg.key_length, 128);
        assert_eq!(cfg.value_length, 128);
        assert_eq!(cfg.q_width(), 4096);
        assert_eq!(cfg.k_width(), 1024);
        assert!((cfg.rope_freq_base - 500_000.0).abs() < 0.01);
        assert!((cfg.rms_eps - 1e-5).abs() < 1e-9);
        assert_eq!(cfg.block_size, 16);
        assert_eq!(cfg.max_drafts(), 15);
        assert_eq!(cfg.target_layers, vec![2, 14, 26, 38, 50]);
        assert_eq!(cfg.sliding_window, 2048);
        assert_eq!(cfg.sliding_pattern, vec![true; 5]);
        assert!(!cfg.causal_attention);
        assert_eq!(cfg.mask_token_id, 201_818);
        assert_eq!(cfg.vocab_size, 202_048);
    }

    #[test]
    fn tiny_synthetic_config_parses() {
        let cfg = DflashConfig::from_metadata(&tiny_metadata()).expect("tiny metadata");
        assert_eq!(cfg.block_count, 2);
        assert_eq!(cfg.target_layers, vec![0, 1]);
        assert_eq!(cfg.sliding_pattern, vec![true, false]);
        assert_eq!(cfg.is_sliding(0), Some(true));
        assert_eq!(cfg.is_sliding(1), Some(false));
        assert_eq!(cfg.is_sliding(2), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn missing_target_layers_is_a_named_error() {
        // llama.cpp throws on this exact absence; the config must
        // name the key, never invent a conditioning layer.
        let mut meta = real_draft_metadata();
        meta.remove(KEY_TARGET_LAYERS);
        let err = DflashConfig::from_metadata(&meta).expect_err("missing key must fail");
        match err {
            DflashError::MissingMetadata { key } => assert_eq!(key, KEY_TARGET_LAYERS),
            other => panic!("expected MissingMetadata, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn wrong_architecture_is_refused() {
        let mut meta = tiny_metadata();
        meta.insert_string(KEY_ARCHITECTURE, "muse-glimmer");
        let err = DflashConfig::from_metadata(&meta).expect_err("wrong arch must fail");
        match err {
            DflashError::WrongArchitecture { found } => assert_eq!(found, "muse-glimmer"),
            other => panic!("expected WrongArchitecture, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn pattern_length_mismatch_is_invalid() {
        let mut meta = tiny_metadata();
        meta.insert_bool_array(KEY_SLIDING_PATTERN, &[true]);
        let err = DflashConfig::from_metadata(&meta).expect_err("short pattern must fail");
        assert!(matches!(err, DflashError::InvalidMetadata { .. }));
    }

    #[test]
    fn duplicate_target_layer_is_invalid() {
        let mut meta = tiny_metadata();
        meta.insert_u32_array(KEY_TARGET_LAYERS, &[1, 1]);
        let err = DflashConfig::from_metadata(&meta).expect_err("duplicate must fail");
        assert!(matches!(err, DflashError::InvalidMetadata { .. }));
    }

    #[test]
    fn causal_flag_reads_string_and_bool_forms() {
        let mut meta = tiny_metadata();
        meta.insert_string(KEY_CAUSAL, "true");
        let cfg = DflashConfig::from_metadata(&meta).expect("string form parses");
        assert!(cfg.causal_attention);
        let mut meta = tiny_metadata();
        meta.insert_bool(KEY_CAUSAL, true);
        let cfg = DflashConfig::from_metadata(&meta).expect("bool form parses");
        assert!(cfg.causal_attention);
        let mut meta = tiny_metadata();
        meta.insert_string(KEY_CAUSAL, "sometimes");
        let err = DflashConfig::from_metadata(&meta).expect_err("junk flag must fail");
        assert!(matches!(err, DflashError::InvalidMetadata { .. }));
    }

    #[test]
    fn non_silu_activation_is_an_unsupported_feature() {
        let mut meta = tiny_metadata();
        meta.insert_string(KEY_HIDDEN_ACT, "gelu");
        let err = DflashConfig::from_metadata(&meta).expect_err("gelu must refuse");
        assert!(matches!(err, DflashError::UnsupportedFeature { .. }));
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/dflash/src/diag.rs =====
//! Diagnostic channel for the dflash module.
//!
//! Project law: every module ships with diagnostics from birth, and
//! every refusal emits through the diagnostic channel with its reason.
//! This crate keeps the channel a trait so the engine's diag crate can
//! own the real sink later; the two sinks here are the silent default
//! and a stderr sink for local work. Same shape as the other arch
//! modules' channels, so arch modules are interchangeable at the seam.

/// A sink for structured diagnostic events: an event name plus a short
/// detail string. Implementations must be cheap to call on hot paths or
/// document that they are not.
pub trait Diag: Send + Sync {
    /// Record one event.
    fn event(&self, event: &str, detail: &str);
}

/// The default sink: drops every event. Use it when the engine process
/// has not wired a real sink yet; errors still propagate as values, so
/// nothing fails silently even with this sink installed.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct NullDiag;

impl Diag for NullDiag {
    fn event(&self, _event: &str, _detail: &str) {}
}

/// A sink that writes one line per event to stderr, for local runs and
/// test debugging.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct StderrDiag;

impl Diag for StderrDiag {
    fn event(&self, event: &str, detail: &str) {
        eprintln!("[dflash] {event}: {detail}");
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::sync::Mutex;

    /// A capturing sink in the itak-engine test shape: records every
    /// event so the test can prove the seam delivers what it is
    /// given, instead of trusting that sink wiring is present in the
    /// source.
    #[derive(Default)]
    struct Capture {
        events: Mutex<Vec<(String, String)>>,
    }

    impl Diag for Capture {
        fn event(&self, event: &str, detail: &str) {
            self.events
                .lock()
                .expect("capture lock")
                .push((event.to_string(), detail.to_string()));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn seam_delivers_events_to_a_sink() {
        let capture = Capture::default();
        capture.event("seam_probe", "detail=fired");
        let events = capture.events.lock().expect("capture lock");
        assert!(
            events
                .iter()
                .any(|(e, d)| e == "seam_probe" && d == "detail=fired"),
            "a sink must receive the events emitted through the seam"
        );
        drop(events);
        // The shipped sinks behave: NullDiag drops silently and
        // StderrDiag writes without panicking.
        NullDiag.event("seam_probe", "detail=dropped");
        StderrDiag.event("seam_probe", "detail=stderr");
    }
}
