//! The weight layout of a DFlash draft model: every tensor the two
//! passes need, by its exact GGUF name.
//!
//! The inventory is the one measured in the real file's tensor
//! census (2026-10-30): three globals plus eleven tensors per layer,
//! 58 in total. Two structural facts of this arch live here, not in
//! the forward:
//!
//! - The draft carries NO embedding table and NO output head. In
//!   llama.cpp it borrows the target model's through the target
//!   context when its own are absent. [`Weights::load`] therefore
//!   loads `token_embd.weight` and `output.weight` when the file
//!   carries them and records their absence as the borrowed state;
//!   the forward then requires caller-supplied target tensors
//!   ([`crate::TargetTensors`]) and refuses by name without them.
//! - The variant family (DFlash2 selector, DSpark Markov/confidence
//!   heads, a `d2t` vocabulary map) is gated on tensor presence in
//!   llama.cpp's loader. A file carrying any of those tensors is a
//!   different model than this module implements, so the load
//!   refuses it by name instead of silently running the plain graph
//!   over it.
//!
//! Loading goes through the [`TensorSource`] trait, implemented by
//! the loader crate over a parsed GGUF file. Every tensor's shape
//! is checked against the config before it is accepted: a tensor of
//! the wrong shape is a named error, not a surprise inside a matmul.

use crate::config::DflashConfig;
use crate::error::{DflashError, Result};

/// One tensor handed over by a [`TensorSource`]: its name, its shape
/// in GGUF stored order (innermost dimension first), and its elements
/// dequantized to f32 in stored order.
///
/// The forward's projections consume `data` directly as a row-major
/// matrix whose rows are the output features: GGUF stores a
/// projection of shape `[in, out]` as `out` rows of `in` elements,
/// which is exactly the layout `torch_math::matvec` multiplies.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct TensorData {
    /// Full GGUF tensor name, for example `blk.3.ffn_down.weight`.
    pub name: String,
    /// Dimensions in GGUF stored order (innermost first).
    pub shape: Vec<u64>,
    /// Dequantized elements, in stored order.
    pub data: Vec<f32>,
}

impl TensorData {
    /// Total element count implied by the shape.
    pub fn elements(&self) -> u64 {
        self.shape.iter().product()
    }
}

/// A source of tensors by name: the seam between this module and
/// the loader.
///
/// Implementor contract: return the tensor or fail with
/// [`DflashError::MissingTensor`]. Never substitute, synthesize, or
/// zero-fill a tensor that was not found; silent placeholders are
/// the defect this rebuild exists to remove.
pub trait TensorSource {
    /// Fetch one tensor by its full GGUF name, dequantized to f32.
    fn tensor(&self, name: &str) -> Result<TensorData>;
    /// Whether a tensor with this name exists in the source. The
    /// load uses it only for the tensors whose presence is a model
    /// property (the draft's own embedding/head, the optional post
    /// norms, and the variant gates), never to skip a required
    /// tensor quietly.
    fn has_tensor(&self, name: &str) -> bool;
}

/// The tensors of one draft layer, in forward order.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct LayerWeights {
    /// `attn_norm.weight`: pre-attention RMSNorm.
    pub attn_norm: TensorData,
    /// `attn_q.weight`: query projection.
    pub attn_q: TensorData,
    /// `attn_k.weight`: key projection.
    pub attn_k: TensorData,
    /// `attn_v.weight`: value projection.
    pub attn_v: TensorData,
    /// `attn_q_norm.weight`: per-head query RMSNorm.
    pub attn_q_norm: TensorData,
    /// `attn_k_norm.weight`: per-head key RMSNorm.
    pub attn_k_norm: TensorData,
    /// `attn_output.weight`: attention output projection.
    pub attn_output: TensorData,
    /// `post_attention_norm.weight`: optional post-attention
    /// RMSNorm, applied to the attention branch before its residual
    /// add when the file carries it. Absent in the real file.
    pub post_attention_norm: Option<TensorData>,
    /// `ffn_norm.weight`: pre-FFN RMSNorm.
    pub ffn_norm: TensorData,
    /// `ffn_gate.weight`: SwiGLU gate projection.
    pub ffn_gate: TensorData,
    /// `ffn_up.weight`: SwiGLU up projection.
    pub ffn_up: TensorData,
    /// `ffn_down.weight`: FFN down projection.
    pub ffn_down: TensorData,
    /// `post_ffw_norm.weight`: optional post-FFN RMSNorm, same rule
    /// as the post-attention norm. Absent in the real file.
    pub post_ffw_norm: Option<TensorData>,
}

/// The full weight set of a DFlash draft model.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Weights {
    /// `fc.weight`: the conditioning fusion projection, from the
    /// concatenated target layer inputs to the draft hidden size.
    pub fc: TensorData,
    /// `enc.output_norm.weight`: RMSNorm over the fused
    /// conditioning rows.
    pub enc_output_norm: TensorData,
    /// `output_norm.weight`: final RMSNorm before the head.
    pub output_norm: TensorData,
    /// `token_embd.weight` when the draft file carries its own
    /// embedding table; `None` means the target's table is borrowed.
    pub embedding: Option<TensorData>,
    /// `output.weight` when the draft file carries its own head;
    /// `None` means the target's head is borrowed.
    pub output: Option<TensorData>,
    /// The target model's hidden size, derived at load from the
    /// `fc` input width divided by the target layer count. The
    /// conditioning rows the injection pass accepts are
    /// `target_layers.len() * target_hidden` wide.
    pub target_hidden: u32,
    /// Per-layer weights, in layer order.
    pub layers: Vec<LayerWeights>,
}

/// Per-layer tensor suffixes [`Weights::load`] always requires, in
/// load order.
const LAYER_SUFFIXES: [&str; 11] = [
    "attn_norm.weight",
    "attn_q.weight",
    "attn_k.weight",
    "attn_v.weight",
    "attn_q_norm.weight",
    "attn_k_norm.weight",
    "attn_output.weight",
    "ffn_norm.weight",
    "ffn_gate.weight",
    "ffn_up.weight",
    "ffn_down.weight",
];

/// Per-layer optional post-norm suffixes, loaded when present.
const POST_NORM_SUFFIXES: [&str; 2] = ["post_attention_norm.weight", "post_ffw_norm.weight"];

/// Tensor names whose presence marks a DFlash variant this module
/// does not implement (the gates llama.cpp's own loader checks).
const VARIANT_GATES: [(&str, &str); 3] = [
    (
        "d2t",
        "a d2t tensor means the draft predicts a reduced vocabulary that maps to target ids; this module implements the plain full-vocabulary draft",
    ),
    (
        "markov_w1.weight",
        "a markov_w1 tensor marks a DSpark draft (Markov + confidence heads); this module implements plain DFlash",
    ),
    (
        "selector_hidden.weight",
        "a selector_hidden tensor marks a DFlash2 draft (conv + selector lattice); this module implements plain DFlash",
    ),
];

/// Every tensor name [`Weights::load`] will always request for
/// `cfg`, in load order. The draft's own `token_embd.weight` and
/// `output.weight` are not in the list: their presence is probed,
/// and their absence is the borrowed state, not a missing tensor.
/// Exposed so the loader's coverage report can be checked against
/// this module's expectations mechanically.
pub fn expected_tensor_names(cfg: &DflashConfig) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut names = Vec::with_capacity(3 + cfg.block_count as usize * LAYER_SUFFIXES.len());
    names.push("fc.weight".to_string());
    names.push("enc.output_norm.weight".to_string());
    names.push("output_norm.weight".to_string());
    for layer in 0..cfg.block_count {
        for suffix in LAYER_SUFFIXES {
            names.push(format!("blk.{layer}.{suffix}"));
        }
    }
    names
}

/// Tensor names [`Weights::load`] loads when the file carries them:
/// the draft's own embedding table and head, and the per-layer post
/// norms. Reported separately by the loader's coverage check so a
/// file's optional inventory is visible, never silently absorbed.
pub fn optional_tensor_names(cfg: &DflashConfig) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut names = vec!["token_embd.weight".to_string(), "output.weight".to_string()];
    for layer in 0..cfg.block_count {
        for suffix in POST_NORM_SUFFIXES {
            names.push(format!("blk.{layer}.{suffix}"));
        }
    }
    names
}

impl Weights {
    /// Load the full weight set for `cfg` from `source`. The first
    /// missing or misshaped tensor aborts the load with a named
    /// error; a partially loaded model is never returned.
    pub fn load<S: TensorSource>(source: &S, cfg: &DflashConfig) -> Result<Weights> {
        for (gate, detail) in VARIANT_GATES {
            if source.has_tensor(gate) {
                return Err(DflashError::UnsupportedFeature {
                    name: gate.to_string(),
                    detail: detail.to_string(),
                });
            }
        }

        let hidden = u64::from(cfg.hidden);
        let ffn = u64::from(cfg.ffn_hidden);
        let vocab = u64::from(cfg.vocab_size);
        let q_w = u64::from(cfg.q_width());
        let k_w = u64::from(cfg.k_width());
        let v_w = u64::from(cfg.v_width());
        let out_w = u64::from(cfg.attn_out_width());

        // The fc input width is the one shape the config cannot
        // fully pin down (it depends on the TARGET's hidden size),
        // so it is validated structurally here: it must be a whole
        // multiple of the target layer count, and its quotient is
        // the target hidden size every conditioning row must match.
        let fc = source.tensor("fc.weight")?;
        if fc.shape.len() != 2 || fc.shape[1] != hidden {
            return Err(DflashError::ShapeMismatch {
                name: fc.name.clone(),
                expected: vec![0, hidden],
                actual: fc.shape.clone(),
            });
        }
        let cond_in = fc.shape[0];
        let n_target = cfg.target_layers.len() as u64;
        if cond_in == 0 || cond_in % n_target != 0 {
            return Err(DflashError::InvalidMetadata {
                key: "dflash.target_layers".to_string(),
                detail: format!(
                    "fc.weight input width {cond_in} is not a whole multiple of the {} target layers, so the concatenated conditioning rows cannot be its input",
                    cfg.target_layers.len()
                ),
            });
        }
        check_len(&fc)?;
        let target_hidden =
            u32::try_from(cond_in / n_target).map_err(|_| DflashError::InvalidMetadata {
                key: "dflash.target_layers".to_string(),
                detail: "target hidden size derived from fc.weight does not fit in u32".to_string(),
            })?;

        let enc_output_norm = checked(source, "enc.output_norm.weight", &[hidden])?;
        let output_norm = checked(source, "output_norm.weight", &[hidden])?;
        let embedding = if source.has_tensor("token_embd.weight") {
            Some(checked(source, "token_embd.weight", &[hidden, vocab])?)
        } else {
            None
        };
        let output = if source.has_tensor("output.weight") {
            Some(checked(source, "output.weight", &[hidden, vocab])?)
        } else {
            None
        };

        let mut layers = Vec::with_capacity(cfg.block_count as usize);
        for index in 0..cfg.block_count {
            let get = |suffix: &str, shape: &[u64]| {
                checked(source, &format!("blk.{index}.{suffix}"), shape)
            };
            let post = |suffix: &str| -> Result<Option<TensorData>> {
                let name = format!("blk.{index}.{suffix}");
                if source.has_tensor(&name) {
                    Ok(Some(checked(source, &name, &[hidden])?))
                } else {
                    Ok(None)
                }
            };
            layers.push(LayerWeights {
                attn_norm: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[0], &[hidden])?,
                attn_q: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[1], &[hidden, q_w])?,
                attn_k: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[2], &[hidden, k_w])?,
                attn_v: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[3], &[hidden, v_w])?,
                attn_q_norm: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[4], &[u64::from(cfg.key_length)])?,
                attn_k_norm: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[5], &[u64::from(cfg.key_length)])?,
                attn_output: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[6], &[out_w, hidden])?,
                post_attention_norm: post(POST_NORM_SUFFIXES[0])?,
                ffn_norm: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[7], &[hidden])?,
                ffn_gate: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[8], &[hidden, ffn])?,
                ffn_up: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[9], &[hidden, ffn])?,
                ffn_down: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[10], &[ffn, hidden])?,
                post_ffw_norm: post(POST_NORM_SUFFIXES[1])?,
            });
        }
        Ok(Weights {
            fc,
            enc_output_norm,
            output_norm,
            embedding,
            output,
            target_hidden,
            layers,
        })
    }

    /// The row width conditioning features must have: target layer
    /// count times the target hidden size, as loaded from `fc`.
    pub fn conditioning_width(&self) -> usize {
        self.fc.shape[0] as usize
    }
}

/// Fetch one tensor and verify it against the shape the config
/// requires for it: presence, dimensions, and element count all
/// checked before the tensor is accepted.
fn checked<S: TensorSource>(source: &S, name: &str, expected: &[u64]) -> Result<TensorData> {
    let tensor = source.tensor(name)?;
    if tensor.shape != expected {
        return Err(DflashError::ShapeMismatch {
            name: name.to_string(),
            expected: expected.to_vec(),
            actual: tensor.shape.clone(),
        });
    }
    check_len(&tensor)?;
    Ok(tensor)
}

/// A tensor's data must hold exactly the elements its shape claims.
fn check_len(tensor: &TensorData) -> Result<()> {
    let want = tensor.elements();
    if tensor.data.len() as u64 != want {
        return Err(DflashError::TensorDataLength {
            name: tensor.name.clone(),
            expected: want,
            actual: tensor.data.len(),
        });
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::testkit::{tiny_config, FakeSource};

    #[test]
    fn full_source_loads_borrowed() {
        let cfg = tiny_config();
        let source = FakeSource::full(&cfg, false);
        let weights = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect("full source loads");
        assert_eq!(weights.layers.len(), 2);
        assert!(weights.embedding.is_none(), "draft borrows the embedding");
        assert!(weights.output.is_none(), "draft borrows the head");
        // fc input width 16 over 2 target layers: target hidden 8.
        assert_eq!(weights.target_hidden, 8);
        assert_eq!(weights.conditioning_width(), 16);
        assert!(weights.layers[0].post_attention_norm.is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn own_embedding_and_head_load_when_present() {
        let cfg = tiny_config();
        let source = FakeSource::full(&cfg, true);
        let weights = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect("full source loads");
        assert!(weights.embedding.is_some());
        assert!(weights.output.is_some());
    }

    #[test]
    fn missing_ffn_down_is_named() {
        let cfg = tiny_config();
        let mut source = FakeSource::full(&cfg, false);
        source.remove("blk.1.ffn_down.weight");
        let err = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect_err("missing tensor must fail");
        match err {
            DflashError::MissingTensor { name } => assert_eq!(name, "blk.1.ffn_down.weight"),
            other => panic!("expected MissingTensor, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn variant_gate_refuses_by_name() {
        let cfg = tiny_config();
        let mut source = FakeSource::full(&cfg, false);
        source.insert(crate::testkit::tensor(
            "selector_hidden.weight",
            &[4, 4],
            0.0,
        ));
        let err = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect_err("DFlash2 file must refuse");
        match err {
            DflashError::UnsupportedFeature { name, .. } => {
                assert_eq!(name, "selector_hidden.weight")
            }
            other => panic!("expected UnsupportedFeature, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn fc_width_not_a_multiple_of_target_layers_is_invalid() {
        let cfg = tiny_config();
        let mut source = FakeSource::full(&cfg, false);
        source.insert(crate::testkit::tensor("fc.weight", &[15, 8], 0.0));
        let err = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect_err("15 over 2 layers cannot fuse");
        assert!(matches!(err, DflashError::InvalidMetadata { .. }));
    }

    #[test]
    fn wrong_shape_is_named() {
        let cfg = tiny_config();
        let mut source = FakeSource::full(&cfg, false);
        // The tiny config's attn_q is [hidden 8, q_width 8]; a
        // [4, 8] tensor cannot be it.
        source.insert(crate::testkit::tensor("blk.0.attn_q.weight", &[4, 8], 0.0));
        let err = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect_err("wrong shape must fail");
        match err {
            DflashError::ShapeMismatch {
                name,
                expected,
                actual,
            } => {
                assert_eq!(name, "blk.0.attn_q.weight");
                assert_eq!(expected, vec![8, 8]);
                assert_eq!(actual, vec![4, 8]);
            }
            other => panic!("expected ShapeMismatch, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn expected_names_match_the_real_census_count() {
        let cfg = tiny_config();
        let names = expected_tensor_names(&cfg);
        assert_eq!(names.len(), 3 + 2 * 11);
        assert_eq!(names[0], "fc.weight");
        let real = crate::testkit::real_config();
        assert_eq!(expected_tensor_names(&real).len(), 58);
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/gguf/examples/dump.rs =====
//! Dump a GGUF file's header, model config, and tensor inventory.
//!
//! Usage: `cargo run --example dump -- <path.gguf>`
//! Set `GGUF_DEBUG=1` to see the loader's structured diagnostics as it parses.

use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let Some(path) = std::env::args().nth(1) else {
        eprintln!("usage: dump <path.gguf>");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    };
    let file = match gguf::GgufFile::open(Path::new(&path)) {
        Ok(f) => f,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("error: {e}");
            return ExitCode::FAILURE;
        }
    };
    println!("file: {path}");
    println!("version: {}", file.version());
    println!("file_len: {} bytes", file.file_len());
    println!("alignment: {}", file.alignment());
    println!("data_start: {}", file.data_start());
    println!("metadata entries: {}", file.metadata().len());
    match file.architecture() {
        Ok(arch) => println!("architecture: {arch}"),
        Err(e) => println!("architecture: <error: {e}>"),
    }
    match file.model_config() {
        Ok(cfg) => println!("model_config: {cfg:?}"),
        Err(e) => println!("model_config: <error: {e}>"),
    }
    match file.tokenizer() {
        Ok(tok) => println!(
            "tokenizer: {} tokens, bos={:?} eos={:?}",
            tok.tokens.len(),
            tok.bos_token_id,
            tok.eos_token_id
        ),
        Err(e) => println!("tokenizer: <error: {e}>"),
    }
    println!("tensors: {}", file.tensors().len());
    for t in file.tensors() {
        println!(
            "  {} type={} dims={:?} elements={} bytes={:?}",
            t.name(),
            t.type_name(),
            t.dims(),
            t.element_count(),
            t.byte_len()
        );
    }
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

===== FILE: crates/gguf/examples/mmap_rss.rs =====
//! Evidence tool for PLAN T-2.1 (memory-mapped GGUF backing): shows
//! that `GgufFile::open` costs no anonymous RSS proportional to file
//! size, while the pre-T-2.1 path (`std::fs::read` +
//! `GgufFile::from_bytes`) costs the full file size in anonymous RSS.
//! The OOM killer's figure is anon-rss, and the phase B footprint
//! audit (bench/phase-b-footprint-2026-11-05.md) is what this fix
//! answers, so the table splits RSS into anon and file parts.
//!
//! Usage: `cargo run -p gguf --release --example mmap_rss -- [size_mib] [dir]`
//! (default 512, system temp dir). Writes a synthetic GGUF with one
//! F32 tensor of `size_mib` MiB into `dir`, measures this process at
//! each phase, and removes the file at the end. Pass a `dir` on a
//! volume that can hold the file; a small tmpfs will not. Linux only
//! (reads /proc/self/status).

use std::io::Write;
use std::path::PathBuf;

use gguf::GgufFile;

/// (VmRSS, RssAnon, RssFile) in KiB from /proc/self/status.
fn rss_kib() -> (u64, u64, u64) {
    let status = std::fs::read_to_string("/proc/self/status")
        .expect("mmap_rss reads /proc/self/status (Linux)");
    let field = |name: &str| -> u64 {
        status
            .lines()
            .find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix(name))
            .and_then(|rest| rest.trim().strip_suffix("kB"))
            .and_then(|num| num.trim().parse().ok())
            .unwrap_or(0)
    };
    (field("VmRSS:"), field("RssAnon:"), field("RssFile:"))
}

fn report(phase: &str) {
    let (rss, anon, file) = rss_kib();
    println!(
        "{phase:<28} VmRSS {:>8.1} MiB   RssAnon {:>8.1} MiB   RssFile {:>8.1} MiB",
        rss as f64 / 1024.0,
        anon as f64 / 1024.0,
        file as f64 / 1024.0,
    );
}

fn align_up(v: u64, a: u64) -> u64 {
    v.div_ceil(a) * a
}

/// Write a GGUF v3 file holding one F32 tensor of `data_bytes` zero
/// bytes (element count `data_bytes / 4`), streaming the data section
/// in chunks so the writer itself never holds the file in memory.
fn write_big_gguf(path: &PathBuf, data_bytes: u64) {
    let mut header = Vec::new();
    header.extend_from_slice(b"GGUF");
    header.extend_from_slice(&3u32.to_le_bytes());
    header.extend_from_slice(&1u64.to_le_bytes()); // tensor count
    header.extend_from_slice(&1u64.to_le_bytes()); // metadata kv count
                                                   // general.architecture = "rss-probe"
    header.extend_from_slice(&20u64.to_le_bytes());
    header.extend_from_slice(b"general.architecture");
    header.extend_from_slice(&8u32.to_le_bytes()); // value type: string
    header.extend_from_slice(&9u64.to_le_bytes());
    header.extend_from_slice(b"rss-probe");
    // Tensor directory: "big.weight", 1 dim, F32 (type 0), offset 0.
    header.extend_from_slice(&10u64.to_le_bytes());
    header.extend_from_slice(b"big.weight");
    header.extend_from_slice(&1u32.to_le_bytes());
    header.extend_from_slice(&(data_bytes / 4).to_le_bytes());
    header.extend_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes());
    header.extend_from_slice(&0u64.to_le_bytes());
    let data_start = align_up(header.len() as u64, 32);
    header.resize(data_start as usize, 0);

    let mut file = std::fs::File::create(path).unwrap();
    file.write_all(&header).unwrap();
    let chunk = vec![0u8; 8 * 1024 * 1024];
    let mut remaining = data_bytes;
    while remaining > 0 {
        let n = remaining.min(chunk.len() as u64) as usize;
        file.write_all(&chunk[..n]).unwrap();
        remaining -= n as u64;
    }
    file.sync_all().unwrap();
}

fn main() {
    let size_mib: u64 = std::env::args()
        .nth(1)
        .and_then(|a| a.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(512);
    let data_bytes = size_mib * 1024 * 1024;
    let dir = std::env::args()
        .nth(2)
        .map_or_else(std::env::temp_dir, PathBuf::from);
    let path = dir.join(format!("gguf-mmap-rss-{}.gguf", std::process::id()));
    write_big_gguf(&path, data_bytes);
    println!(
        "synthetic GGUF: {} (tensor data {size_mib} MiB)",
        path.display()
    );

    report("start");
    {
        let file = GgufFile::open(&path).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(file.architecture().unwrap(), "rss-probe");
        report("mapped open");
        let tensor = file.tensor_bytes("big.weight").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(tensor.len() as u64, data_bytes);
        // Touch three pages: first, middle, last.
        let probe =
            tensor[0] as u64 + tensor[tensor.len() / 2] as u64 + tensor[tensor.len() - 1] as u64;
        std::hint::black_box(probe);
        report("mapped touch 3 pages");
        // Touch every page of the tensor data.
        let mut sum: u64 = 0;
        for page in tensor.chunks(4096) {
            sum += page[0] as u64;
        }
        std::hint::black_box(sum);
        report("mapped touch every page");
    }
    report("mapped dropped");
    {
        let bytes = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap();
        let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(bytes).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(file.architecture().unwrap(), "rss-probe");
        report("owned read + from_bytes");
    }
    let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&path);
}

===== FILE: crates/gguf/examples/probe.rs =====
//! Dequantize a raw byte range (for example one tensor block extracted
//! from a real GGUF with `dd`) and print the f32 values, one per line.
//! Used to cross-check this crate's dequantizers against reference
//! implementations on real model bytes.
//!
//! Usage: `cargo run --example probe -- <type> <file> <elements> [count]`
//! where type is one of f32, f16, bf16, q8_0, q2_k, q3_k, q4_k, q5_k,
//! q6_k. Values print with Rust's shortest round-trip formatting, so a
//! large `count` gives an exact text dump for diffing against a
//! reference implementation.

use std::process::ExitCode;

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    if args.len() < 4 {
        eprintln!("usage: probe <type> <file> <elements> [count]");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    let ty = match args[1].as_str() {
        "f32" => gguf::GgmlType::F32,
        "f16" => gguf::GgmlType::F16,
        "bf16" => gguf::GgmlType::Bf16,
        "q8_0" => gguf::GgmlType::Q8_0,
        "q2_k" => gguf::GgmlType::Q2K,
        "q3_k" => gguf::GgmlType::Q3K,
        "q4_k" => gguf::GgmlType::Q4K,
        "q5_k" => gguf::GgmlType::Q5K,
        "q6_k" => gguf::GgmlType::Q6K,
        other => {
            eprintln!("unknown type {other}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let data = match std::fs::read(&args[2]) {
        Ok(d) => d,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("read error: {e}");
            return ExitCode::FAILURE;
        }
    };
    let elements: usize = match args[3].parse() {
        Ok(n) => n,
        Err(_) => {
            eprintln!("bad element count {}", args[3]);
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let count: usize = args.get(4).and_then(|s| s.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(16);
    let out = gguf::dequant::dequantize(ty, &data, elements);
    for v in out.iter().take(count) {
        println!("{v:?}");
    }
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

===== FILE: crates/gguf/examples/qkv_probe.rs =====
//! QKV source probe (layer-diff follow-up to integration run A).
//!
//! llama.cpp prefers a fused `attn_qkv.weight` when a GGUF carries
//! one and slices it as contiguous [Q; K; V] row blocks; this crate
//! loads the split `attn_q/k/v.weight` tensors. When a file carries
//! both, the two sources must agree or one of them is not what it
//! claims to be. This probe dequantizes both sources for one layer,
//! applies each to a caller-supplied attn_norm dump (the Rust
//! layer_dump output, proven to match the reference to 1e-6), and
//! writes every candidate Q/K as .bin files for numerical
//! comparison against the reference's Qcur/Kcur dump.
//!
//! Usage:
//!   qkv_probe --model <file.gguf> --attn-norm <L00_attn_norm.bin>
//!             --out <dir> [--layer 0]

use std::env;
use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::ExitCode;

use gguf::GgufFile;

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    match run() {
        Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,
        Err(msg) => {
            eprintln!("qkv_probe: {msg}");
            ExitCode::FAILURE
        }
    }
}

fn next_value(it: &mut impl Iterator<Item = String>, flag: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    it.next()
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("flag {flag} needs a value"))
}

fn write_bin(dir: &Path, name: &str, data: &[f32]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(data.len() * 4);
    for v in data {
        bytes.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
    }
    let path = dir.join(format!("{name}.bin"));
    fs::write(&path, bytes).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))
}

/// out = h * W^T + bias, W in [out][in] row-major (GGUF order).
fn proj(h: &[f32], rows: usize, w: &[f32], out_w: usize, bias: Option<&[f32]>) -> Vec<f32> {
    let in_w = w.len() / out_w;
    let mut out = vec![0.0f32; rows * out_w];
    for r in 0..rows {
        let hr = &h[r * in_w..(r + 1) * in_w];
        for o in 0..out_w {
            let wr = &w[o * in_w..(o + 1) * in_w];
            let mut acc: f32 = hr.iter().zip(wr.iter()).map(|(a, b)| a * b).sum();
            if let Some(b) = bias {
                acc += b[o];
            }
            out[r * out_w + o] = acc;
        }
    }
    out
}

fn run() -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut model = None;
    let mut attn_norm_path = None;
    let mut out_dir = None;
    let mut layer = 0usize;
    let mut it = env::args().skip(1);
    while let Some(arg) = it.next() {
        match arg.as_str() {
            "--model" => model = Some(next_value(&mut it, &arg)?),
            "--attn-norm" => attn_norm_path = Some(next_value(&mut it, &arg)?),
            "--out" => out_dir = Some(next_value(&mut it, &arg)?),
            "--layer" => {
                layer = next_value(&mut it, &arg)?
                    .parse()
                    .map_err(|_| "bad --layer".to_string())?;
            }
            other => return Err(format!("unknown argument {other}")),
        }
    }
    let model = model.ok_or("missing --model")?;
    let attn_norm_path = attn_norm_path.ok_or("missing --attn-norm")?;
    let out_dir = PathBuf::from(out_dir.ok_or("missing --out")?);
    fs::create_dir_all(&out_dir).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

    let file = GgufFile::open(Path::new(&model)).map_err(|e| format!("open: {e}"))?;
    let p = format!("blk.{layer}");
    for suffix in [
        "attn_q.weight",
        "attn_k.weight",
        "attn_v.weight",
        "attn_qkv.weight",
        "attn_q.bias",
        "attn_k.bias",
        "attn_v.bias",
        "attn_qkv.bias",
    ] {
        let name = format!("{p}.{suffix}");
        match file.tensor_info(&name) {
            Ok(info) => eprintln!(
                "{name}: dims={:?} type={} elements={}",
                info.dims(),
                info.type_name(),
                info.element_count()
            ),
            Err(_) => eprintln!("{name}: ABSENT"),
        }
    }

    let raw = fs::read(&attn_norm_path).map_err(|e| format!("{attn_norm_path}: {e}"))?;
    let h: Vec<f32> = raw
        .chunks_exact(4)
        .map(|c| f32::from_le_bytes([c[0], c[1], c[2], c[3]]))
        .collect();
    let hidden = 1536usize;
    let rows = h.len() / hidden;

    let load = |suffix: &str| -> Result<Option<Vec<f32>>, String> {
        let name = format!("{p}.{suffix}");
        if file.has_tensor(&name) {
            Ok(Some(
                file.load_f32(&name).map_err(|e| format!("{name}: {e}"))?,
            ))
        } else {
            Ok(None)
        }
    };
    let wq = load("attn_q.weight")?.ok_or("attn_q.weight absent")?;
    let wk = load("attn_k.weight")?.ok_or("attn_k.weight absent")?;
    let bq = load("attn_q.bias")?;
    let bk = load("attn_k.bias")?;
    let q_w = 1536usize;
    let k_w = 256usize;

    write_bin(
        &out_dir,
        "q_split",
        &proj(&h, rows, &wq, q_w, bq.as_deref()),
    )?;
    write_bin(
        &out_dir,
        "k_split",
        &proj(&h, rows, &wk, k_w, bk.as_deref()),
    )?;

    if let Some(wqkv) = load("attn_qkv.weight")? {
        let total_w = q_w + 2 * k_w;
        let bqkv = load("attn_qkv.bias")?;
        let bias_q: Option<&[f32]> = match (&bqkv, &bq) {
            (Some(b), _) => Some(&b[..q_w]),
            (None, Some(b)) => Some(b.as_slice()),
            (None, None) => None,
        };
        let bias_k: Option<&[f32]> = match (&bqkv, &bk) {
            (Some(b), _) => Some(&b[q_w..q_w + k_w]),
            (None, Some(b)) => Some(b.as_slice()),
            (None, None) => None,
        };
        // Contiguous [Q; K; V] row blocks: the llama.cpp slicing.
        let wq_f = &wqkv[..q_w * hidden];
        let wk_f = &wqkv[q_w * hidden..(q_w + k_w) * hidden];
        write_bin(&out_dir, "q_fused", &proj(&h, rows, wq_f, q_w, bias_q))?;
        write_bin(&out_dir, "k_fused", &proj(&h, rows, wk_f, k_w, bias_k))?;
        // Interleaved GQA slicing: per KV group, [6 Q heads; 1 K; 1 V].
        let group_q = q_w / 2; // 768 rows of Q per KV group
        let stride = group_q + 2 * k_w;
        let mut wq_i = vec![0.0f32; q_w * hidden];
        let mut wk_i = vec![0.0f32; k_w * hidden];
        for g in 0..2usize {
            let src = g * stride * hidden;
            wq_i[g * group_q * hidden..(g + 1) * group_q * hidden]
                .copy_from_slice(&wqkv[src..src + group_q * hidden]);
            let ks = src + group_q * hidden;
            wk_i[g * k_w * hidden..(g + 1) * k_w * hidden]
                .copy_from_slice(&wqkv[ks..ks + k_w * hidden]);
        }
        write_bin(
            &out_dir,
            "q_fused_interleaved",
            &proj(&h, rows, &wq_i, q_w, bias_q),
        )?;
        write_bin(
            &out_dir,
            "k_fused_interleaved",
            &proj(&h, rows, &wk_i, k_w, bias_k),
        )?;
        let _ = total_w;
    }
    eprintln!("qkv_probe: wrote candidates to {}", out_dir.display());
    Ok(())
}

===== END FILE: crates/gguf/examples/qkv_probe.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/gguf/examples/tokenizer_extract.rs =====
//! Extract a GGUF file's embedded tokenizer data to a `.tokdata` file.
//!
//! The tokenizer crate deliberately does not depend on this crate, so
//! conformance work needs the vocabulary in a neutral interchange
//! format. This tool produces it: it opens a GGUF file (which loads the
//! whole file, so run it on the machine that holds the model), reads
//! `tokenizer.ggml.*` through [`GgufFile::tokenizer`] plus the unknown
//! token id from raw metadata, and writes the arrays out framed.
//!
//! Usage: `cargo run --release --example tokenizer_extract -- <model.gguf> <out.tokdata>`
//!
//! # The `.tokdata` format (version 2)
//!
//! Line-oriented ASCII framing; string payloads are length-prefixed raw
//! UTF-8 bytes so any token text survives verbatim:
//!
//! ```text
//! ITAK-TOKDATA-2
//! model <tokenizer.ggml.model, or ->
//! pre <tokenizer.ggml.pre, or ->
//! bos <id, or ->
//! eos <id, or ->
//! unk <id, or ->
//! pad <id, or ->
//! tokens <count>
//! <byte length>\n<raw bytes>\n   (repeated count times)
//! token_types <count, 0 when the file records none>
//! <one signed decimal per line>  (repeated count times)
//! merges <count>
//! <byte length>\n<raw bytes>\n   (repeated count times)
//! scores <count, 0 when the file records none>
//! <one decimal float per line>  (repeated count times)
//! ```
//!
//! Version 1 (written by the first cut of this tool) is identical
//! except for the header line and the missing scores section;
//! readers accept both. Scores ride along because SentencePiece
//! family tokenizers merge by per-token score, and the scores live
//! in `tokenizer.ggml.scores`, a separate array from the merges.

use std::fs::File;
use std::io::{BufWriter, Write};
use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;

use gguf::GgufFile;

fn opt_id(id: Option<u32>) -> String {
    id.map_or_else(|| "-".to_string(), |v| v.to_string())
}

fn write_framed(out: &mut impl Write, s: &str) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    writeln!(out, "{}", s.len())?;
    out.write_all(s.as_bytes())?;
    writeln!(out)
}

fn run(model_path: &str, out_path: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    let file = GgufFile::open(Path::new(model_path)).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let info = file.tokenizer().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let md = file.metadata();
    let model = md
        .opt_string("tokenizer.ggml.model")
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let pre = md
        .opt_string("tokenizer.ggml.pre")
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let unk = md
        .opt_u32("tokenizer.ggml.unknown_token_id")
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

    let mut out = BufWriter::new(File::create(out_path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    let write = |out: &mut BufWriter<File>| -> std::io::Result<()> {
        writeln!(out, "ITAK-TOKDATA-2")?;
        writeln!(out, "model {}", model.unwrap_or("-"))?;
        writeln!(out, "pre {}", pre.unwrap_or("-"))?;
        writeln!(out, "bos {}", opt_id(info.bos_token_id))?;
        writeln!(out, "eos {}", opt_id(info.eos_token_id))?;
        writeln!(out, "unk {}", opt_id(unk))?;
        writeln!(out, "pad {}", opt_id(info.padding_token_id))?;
        writeln!(out, "tokens {}", info.tokens.len())?;
        for token in &info.tokens {
            write_framed(out, token)?;
        }
        match &info.token_types {
            Some(types) => {
                writeln!(out, "token_types {}", types.len())?;
                for ty in types {
                    writeln!(out, "{ty}")?;
                }
            }
            None => writeln!(out, "token_types 0")?,
        }
        let merges: &[String] = info.merges.as_deref().unwrap_or(&[]);
        writeln!(out, "merges {}", merges.len())?;
        for merge in merges {
            write_framed(out, merge)?;
        }
        let scores: &[f32] = info.scores.as_deref().unwrap_or(&[]);
        writeln!(out, "scores {}", scores.len())?;
        for score in scores {
            // f32 Display is the shortest decimal that parses back to
            // the identical value, so the scores survive verbatim.
            writeln!(out, "{score}")?;
        }
        Ok(())
    };
    write(&mut out).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    out.flush().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

    println!(
        "extracted {} tokens, {} merges, {} scores -> {out_path}",
        info.tokens.len(),
        info.merges.as_deref().unwrap_or(&[]).len(),
        info.scores.as_deref().unwrap_or(&[]).len()
    );
    Ok(())
}

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let mut args = std::env::args().skip(1);
    let (Some(model), Some(out)) = (args.next(), args.next()) else {
        eprintln!("usage: tokenizer_extract <model.gguf> <out.tokdata>");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    };
    match run(&model, &out) {
        Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("error: {e}");
            ExitCode::FAILURE
        }
    }
}

===== END FILE: crates/gguf/examples/tokenizer_extract.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/gguf/src/config.rs =====
//! Model configuration read from the file's own metadata.
//!
//! GGUF keys the architecture parameters under the architecture's own
//! name: a file declaring `general.architecture = "qwen2"` stores
//! `qwen2.block_count`, `qwen2.embedding_length`, and so on. This module
//! resolves those keys from the file itself. Nothing here invents values:
//! required fields are hard errors when absent, and the two fields with a
//! genuine format-level convention (KV head count falls back to the query
//! head count; RoPE base may be absent) are explicit `Option`s documenting
//! that convention at the call site.

use crate::error::Result;
use crate::file::GgufFile;

/// The architecture parameters an engine needs before it can build a
/// forward pass, read from one GGUF file.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct ModelConfig {
    /// Architecture string, the file's own declaration (`general.architecture`).
    pub architecture: String,
    /// Transformer block (layer) count, `<arch>.block_count`.
    pub layer_count: u32,
    /// Hidden size, `<arch>.embedding_length`.
    pub hidden_size: u32,
    /// Feed-forward inner size, `<arch>.feed_forward_length`, when present.
    pub ffn_size: Option<u32>,
    /// Query attention heads, `<arch>.attention.head_count`. When a file
    /// stores the count as a per-layer array (hybrid architectures), this
    /// is the maximum and the full array is in `head_count_per_layer`.
    pub head_count: u32,
    /// Per-layer query head counts, when the file stores them as an array.
    pub head_count_per_layer: Option<Vec<u32>>,
    /// Key/value attention heads. GGUF omits `<arch>.attention.head_count_kv`
    /// for full multi-head attention; the fallback to `head_count` is the
    /// format's own convention and is applied here, once, visibly. When a
    /// file stores the count as a per-layer array (hybrid architectures,
    /// where non-attention layers carry 0), this is the maximum, i.e. the
    /// KV head count of the attention layers, and the full array is in
    /// `head_count_kv_per_layer`.
    pub head_count_kv: u32,
    /// Per-layer KV head counts, when the file stores them as an array.
    pub head_count_kv_per_layer: Option<Vec<u32>>,
    /// Context length the model was trained for, `<arch>.context_length`.
    pub context_length: u32,
    /// RoPE frequency base, `<arch>.rope.freq_base` (the spec key; the
    /// `<arch>.attention.rope.freq_base` spelling some converters emit is
    /// accepted as a fallback), when present.
    pub rope_base: Option<f32>,
    /// RMSNorm epsilon, `<arch>.attention.layer_norm_rms_epsilon`, when present.
    pub norm_eps: Option<f32>,
    /// Vocabulary size, from `tokenizer.ggml.tokens` when a tokenizer is
    /// embedded, else `<arch>.vocab_size` when present.
    pub vocab_size: Option<usize>,
}

impl ModelConfig {
    /// Read the configuration from a parsed file's metadata.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Missing or mistyped required keys are hard errors naming the key.
    pub fn from_file(file: &GgufFile) -> Result<Self> {
        let md = file.metadata();
        let arch = file.architecture()?.to_string();
        let key = |suffix: &str| format!("{arch}.{suffix}");

        let layer_count = md.get_u32(&key("block_count"))?;
        let hidden_size = md.get_u32(&key("embedding_length"))?;
        let ffn_size = md.opt_u32(&key("feed_forward_length"))?;
        let (head_count, head_count_per_layer) = read_head_count(md, &key("attention.head_count"))?;
        let head_count = match head_count {
            Some(v) => v,
            None => {
                return Err(
                    crate::error::GgufError::MissingMetadata(key("attention.head_count")).logged(),
                )
            }
        };
        let (kv_scalar, head_count_kv_per_layer) =
            read_head_count(md, &key("attention.head_count_kv"))?;
        let head_count_kv = match kv_scalar {
            Some(v) => v,
            None => head_count,
        };
        let context_length = md.get_u32(&key("context_length"))?;
        let rope_base = match md.opt_f32(&key("rope.freq_base"))? {
            Some(v) => Some(v),
            None => md.opt_f32(&key("attention.rope.freq_base"))?,
        };
        let norm_eps = md.opt_f32(&key("attention.layer_norm_rms_epsilon"))?;
        let vocab_size = match md.get("tokenizer.ggml.tokens") {
            Some(crate::metadata::MetadataValue::Array(items)) => Some(items.len()),
            _ => md.opt_u32(&key("vocab_size"))?.map(|v| v as usize),
        };

        Ok(Self {
            architecture: arch,
            layer_count,
            hidden_size,
            ffn_size,
            head_count,
            head_count_per_layer,
            head_count_kv,
            head_count_kv_per_layer,
            context_length,
            rope_base,
            norm_eps,
            vocab_size,
        })
    }
}

/// Read a head-count key that a file may store either as a scalar or as a
/// per-layer array (hybrid architectures do the latter, with 0 on layers
/// that have no attention). Returns `(scalar, per_layer)`: for array
/// storage the scalar is the array maximum, for scalar storage the array
/// is `None`, and for an absent key both are `None`.
fn read_head_count(
    md: &crate::metadata::Metadata,
    key: &str,
) -> Result<(Option<u32>, Option<Vec<u32>>)> {
    match md.get(key) {
        None => Ok((None, None)),
        Some(crate::metadata::MetadataValue::Array(_)) => {
            let layers = md.get_u32_array(key)?;
            let scalar = layers.iter().max().copied();
            Ok((scalar, Some(layers)))
        }
        Some(_) => Ok((Some(md.get_u32(key)?), None)),
    }
}

/// Tokenizer data embedded in a GGUF file.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct TokenizerInfo {
    /// Token strings by id (`tokenizer.ggml.tokens`).
    pub tokens: Vec<String>,
    /// Token type ids (`tokenizer.ggml.token_type`), when present.
    pub token_types: Option<Vec<i32>>,
    /// Byte-pair merge rules (`tokenizer.ggml.merges`), when present.
    pub merges: Option<Vec<String>>,
    /// Per-token scores (`tokenizer.ggml.scores`), when present.
    /// SentencePiece-family tokenizers merge by these scores, so the
    /// tokenizer crate needs them verbatim; files that were converted
    /// without the array leave this `None` and llama.cpp falls back
    /// to a score of 0.0 for every token.
    pub scores: Option<Vec<f32>>,
    /// Beginning-of-sequence token id (`tokenizer.ggml.bos_token_id`).
    pub bos_token_id: Option<u32>,
    /// End-of-sequence token id (`tokenizer.ggml.eos_token_id`).
    pub eos_token_id: Option<u32>,
    /// Padding token id (`tokenizer.ggml.padding_token_id`).
    pub padding_token_id: Option<u32>,
}

impl TokenizerInfo {
    /// Read tokenizer data from a parsed file's metadata.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// `MissingMetadata` when the file embeds no tokenizer tokens;
    /// mistyped arrays are named mismatches.
    pub fn from_file(file: &GgufFile) -> Result<Self> {
        let md = file.metadata();
        let tokens = md.get_string_array("tokenizer.ggml.tokens")?;
        let token_types = match md.get("tokenizer.ggml.token_type") {
            Some(_) => Some(md.get_i32_array("tokenizer.ggml.token_type")?),
            None => None,
        };
        let merges = match md.get("tokenizer.ggml.merges") {
            Some(_) => Some(md.get_string_array("tokenizer.ggml.merges")?),
            None => None,
        };
        let scores = match md.get("tokenizer.ggml.scores") {
            Some(_) => Some(md.get_f32_array("tokenizer.ggml.scores")?),
            None => None,
        };
        Ok(Self {
            tokens,
            token_types,
            merges,
            scores,
            bos_token_id: md.opt_u32("tokenizer.ggml.bos_token_id")?,
            eos_token_id: md.opt_u32("tokenizer.ggml.eos_token_id")?,
            padding_token_id: md.opt_u32("tokenizer.ggml.padding_token_id")?,
        })
    }
}

impl GgufFile {
    /// Architecture parameters from this file's own metadata.
    pub fn model_config(&self) -> Result<ModelConfig> {
        ModelConfig::from_file(self)
    }

    /// Embedded tokenizer data, when the file carries a tokenizer.
    pub fn tokenizer(&self) -> Result<TokenizerInfo> {
        TokenizerInfo::from_file(self)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::diag;
    use crate::error::GgufError;

    // A minimal in-memory GGUF: header plus the metadata entries
    // pushed by the helpers below, no tensors. Just enough for
    // from_file to walk its required keys in order.
    fn push_u32(b: &mut Vec<u8>, v: u32) {
        b.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
    }

    fn push_u64(b: &mut Vec<u8>, v: u64) {
        b.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
    }

    fn push_string(b: &mut Vec<u8>, s: &str) {
        push_u64(b, s.len() as u64);
        b.extend_from_slice(s.as_bytes());
    }

    fn push_kv_string(b: &mut Vec<u8>, key: &str, value: &str) {
        push_string(b, key);
        push_u32(b, 8); // GGUF string value type
        push_string(b, value);
    }

    fn push_kv_u32(b: &mut Vec<u8>, key: &str, value: u32) {
        push_string(b, key);
        push_u32(b, 4); // GGUF u32 value type
        push_u32(b, value);
    }

    #[test]
    fn missing_head_count_refusal_emits_its_diag_event() {
        // A previously silent path: ModelConfig::from_file
        // constructed its MissingMetadata for an absent head_count
        // key with no diag call anywhere in this module. The file
        // below carries the two required keys from_file reads
        // before head_count, so the refusal is exactly that
        // construction.
        let mut bytes = Vec::new();
        bytes.extend_from_slice(b"GGUF");
        push_u32(&mut bytes, 3); // version
        push_u64(&mut bytes, 0); // tensor count
        push_u64(&mut bytes, 3); // metadata kv count
        push_kv_string(&mut bytes, "general.architecture", "lane-g-arch");
        push_kv_u32(&mut bytes, "lane-g-arch.block_count", 2);
        push_kv_u32(&mut bytes, "lane-g-arch.embedding_length", 8);
        let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(bytes).expect("the synthetic file parses");

        let err =
            ModelConfig::from_file(&file).expect_err("no head_count key anywhere must refuse");
        assert!(
            matches!(&err, GgufError::MissingMetadata(k) if k == "lane-g-arch.attention.head_count"),
            "error: {err}"
        );
        assert!(
            diag::captured_errors().iter().any(|l| {
                l.contains("event=missing_metadata")
                    && l.contains("key=lane-g-arch.attention.head_count")
            }),
            "the config refusal must emit its diag event"
        );
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/gguf/src/dequant.rs =====
//! Dequantization to f32, following mainline ggml's reference row
//! dequantizers exactly (same block layouts, same scale unpacking), so
//! values produced here match what llama.cpp computes from the same bytes.
//!
//! Every function in this module assumes the caller has already validated
//! that `data.len()` is the exact on-disk length for `elements` elements of
//! the type (see `GgmlType::byte_len`); `dequantize` debug-asserts it.

use crate::ggml::GgmlType;

/// Convert an IEEE 754 half-precision bit pattern to f32.
pub fn f16_to_f32(bits: u16) -> f32 {
    let sign = u32::from(bits >> 15);
    let exp = u32::from((bits >> 10) & 0x1f);
    let frac = u32::from(bits & 0x3ff);
    if exp == 0x1f {
        let out = if frac == 0 {
            0x7f80_0000
        } else {
            0x7fc0_0000 | (frac << 13)
        };
        return f32::from_bits((sign << 31) | out);
    }
    if exp == 0 {
        if frac == 0 {
            return f32::from_bits(sign << 31);
        }
        // Subnormal half: value is frac * 2^-24, exact in f32.
        let v = frac as f32 * f32::from_bits(0x3380_0000);
        return if sign == 1 { -v } else { v };
    }
    let out = ((exp + 127 - 15) << 23) | (frac << 13);
    f32::from_bits((sign << 31) | out)
}

/// Convert a bfloat16 bit pattern to f32 (a pure high-half copy).
pub fn bf16_to_f32(bits: u16) -> f32 {
    f32::from_bits(u32::from(bits) << 16)
}

fn read_f16(data: &[u8], byte_offset: usize) -> f32 {
    f16_to_f32(u16::from_le_bytes([
        data[byte_offset],
        data[byte_offset + 1],
    ]))
}

/// Unpack one sub-block's (scale, min) pair from a K-quant scales array.
/// Mirrors ggml's `get_scale_min_k4` exactly: the 12-byte array packs eight
/// 6-bit scales and eight 6-bit mins with the high bits folded into the
/// last four bytes.
fn scale_min_k4(j: usize, scales: &[u8]) -> (u8, u8) {
    if j < 4 {
        (scales[j] & 63, scales[j + 4] & 63)
    } else {
        (
            (scales[j + 4] & 0xF) | ((scales[j - 4] >> 6) << 4),
            (scales[j + 4] >> 4) | ((scales[j] >> 6) << 4),
        )
    }
}

fn dequant_q8_0(data: &[u8], out: &mut [f32]) {
    for (b, block) in data.chunks_exact(34).enumerate() {
        let d = read_f16(block, 0);
        let o = &mut out[b * 32..(b + 1) * 32];
        for (i, slot) in o.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            *slot = d * f32::from(block[2 + i] as i8);
        }
    }
}

/// Port of ggml's `dequantize_row_q2_K` (ggml/src/ggml-quants.c) over the
/// `block_q2_K` layout (ggml/src/ggml-common.h): 16 packed scale/min
/// bytes, 64 two-bit quant bytes, then f16 `d` and f16 `dmin` (note the
/// scales and quants come FIRST in this block, unlike Q4_K..Q6_K).
///
/// Each scale byte serves one 16-element sub-block: low nibble is the
/// scale, high nibble is the min. The block walks two chunks of 128
/// elements; per chunk, four 2-bit planes (shifts 0, 2, 4, 6), and each
/// plane covers two sub-blocks read from `qs[l]` and `qs[l + 16]`.
fn dequant_q2_k(data: &[u8], out: &mut [f32]) {
    for (b, block) in data.chunks_exact(84).enumerate() {
        let scales = &block[0..16];
        let qs = &block[16..80];
        let d = read_f16(block, 80);
        let dmin = read_f16(block, 82);
        let o = &mut out[b * 256..(b + 1) * 256];
        let mut is = 0usize;
        for chunk in 0..2 {
            let q = &qs[chunk * 32..chunk * 32 + 32];
            for (plane, shift) in [0u32, 2, 4, 6].into_iter().enumerate() {
                for sub in 0..2 {
                    let sc = scales[is];
                    is += 1;
                    let dl = d * f32::from(sc & 0xF);
                    let ml = dmin * f32::from(sc >> 4);
                    for l in 0..16 {
                        let qv = (q[sub * 16 + l] >> shift) & 3;
                        o[chunk * 128 + plane * 32 + sub * 16 + l] = dl * f32::from(qv) - ml;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Unpack the 16 six-bit scales of a Q3_K block from its 12 packed bytes.
/// Mirrors the uint32 shuffle at the top of ggml's `dequantize_row_q3_K`
/// (ggml/src/ggml-quants.c) operation for operation: bytes 0..8 supply
/// the low four bits (low nibbles for scales 0..8, high nibbles for
/// scales 8..16) and bytes 8..12 supply the top two bits of every scale.
fn unpack_scales_q3_k(packed: &[u8]) -> [i8; 16] {
    const KMASK1: u32 = 0x0303_0303;
    const KMASK2: u32 = 0x0f0f_0f0f;
    let mut aux = [
        u32::from_le_bytes([packed[0], packed[1], packed[2], packed[3]]),
        u32::from_le_bytes([packed[4], packed[5], packed[6], packed[7]]),
        u32::from_le_bytes([packed[8], packed[9], packed[10], packed[11]]),
        0,
    ];
    let tmp = aux[2];
    aux[2] = ((aux[0] >> 4) & KMASK2) | (((tmp >> 4) & KMASK1) << 4);
    aux[3] = ((aux[1] >> 4) & KMASK2) | (((tmp >> 6) & KMASK1) << 4);
    aux[0] = (aux[0] & KMASK2) | ((tmp & KMASK1) << 4);
    aux[1] = (aux[1] & KMASK2) | (((tmp >> 2) & KMASK1) << 4);
    let mut scales = [0i8; 16];
    for (i, word) in aux.iter().enumerate() {
        for (j, byte) in word.to_le_bytes().into_iter().enumerate() {
            scales[i * 4 + j] = byte as i8;
        }
    }
    scales
}

/// Port of ggml's `dequantize_row_q3_K` (ggml/src/ggml-quants.c) over the
/// `block_q3_K` layout (ggml/src/ggml-common.h): 32 high-bit mask bytes,
/// 64 two-bit quant bytes, 12 packed scale bytes, then f16 `d`.
///
/// The third bit of each value is NOT stored as a plain bit: a SET mask
/// bit means the 2-bit quant stands as-is (values 0..3), a CLEAR mask bit
/// subtracts 4 (values -4..-1). The mask bit index advances one bit per
/// 32-element plane pair and is never reset, so the second 128-element
/// chunk reads bits 4..8 of the same 32 mask bytes while the quant
/// pointer advances by 32 bytes per chunk.
fn dequant_q3_k(data: &[u8], out: &mut [f32]) {
    for (b, block) in data.chunks_exact(110).enumerate() {
        let hmask = &block[0..32];
        let qs = &block[32..96];
        let scales = unpack_scales_q3_k(&block[96..108]);
        let d = read_f16(block, 108);
        let o = &mut out[b * 256..(b + 1) * 256];
        let mut is = 0usize;
        let mut m: u8 = 1;
        for chunk in 0..2 {
            let q = &qs[chunk * 32..chunk * 32 + 32];
            for (plane, shift) in [0u32, 2, 4, 6].into_iter().enumerate() {
                for sub in 0..2 {
                    let dl = d * f32::from(scales[is] - 32);
                    is += 1;
                    for l in 0..16 {
                        let qv = i32::from((q[sub * 16 + l] >> shift) & 3);
                        let sub4 = if hmask[sub * 16 + l] & m != 0 { 0 } else { 4 };
                        let v = (qv - sub4) as f32;
                        o[chunk * 128 + plane * 32 + sub * 16 + l] = dl * v;
                    }
                }
                m <<= 1;
            }
        }
    }
}

fn dequant_q4_k(data: &[u8], out: &mut [f32]) {
    for (b, block) in data.chunks_exact(144).enumerate() {
        let d = read_f16(block, 0);
        let dmin = read_f16(block, 2);
        let scales = &block[4..16];
        let qs = &block[16..144];
        let o = &mut out[b * 256..(b + 1) * 256];
        // Four groups of 64 elements; each group holds two 32-element
        // sub-blocks, low nibbles first, then high nibbles.
        for group in 0..4 {
            let (sc1, m1) = scale_min_k4(2 * group, scales);
            let (sc2, m2) = scale_min_k4(2 * group + 1, scales);
            let d1 = d * f32::from(sc1);
            let dm1 = dmin * f32::from(m1);
            let d2 = d * f32::from(sc2);
            let dm2 = dmin * f32::from(m2);
            for l in 0..32 {
                let byte = qs[group * 32 + l];
                o[group * 64 + l] = d1 * f32::from(byte & 0xF) - dm1;
                o[group * 64 + 32 + l] = d2 * f32::from(byte >> 4) - dm2;
            }
        }
    }
}

fn dequant_q5_k(data: &[u8], out: &mut [f32]) {
    for (b, block) in data.chunks_exact(176).enumerate() {
        let d = read_f16(block, 0);
        let dmin = read_f16(block, 2);
        let scales = &block[4..16];
        let qh = &block[16..48];
        let ql = &block[48..176];
        let o = &mut out[b * 256..(b + 1) * 256];
        // Same 64-element grouping as Q4_K. The fifth bits live in one
        // shared 32-byte qh array for the whole block: group g reads bit
        // 2g (first sub-block) and bit 2g+1 (second) of qh[l], so the byte
        // index stays l and only the masks advance.
        let mut u1: u8 = 1;
        let mut u2: u8 = 2;
        for group in 0..4 {
            let (sc1, m1) = scale_min_k4(2 * group, scales);
            let (sc2, m2) = scale_min_k4(2 * group + 1, scales);
            let d1 = d * f32::from(sc1);
            let dm1 = dmin * f32::from(m1);
            let d2 = d * f32::from(sc2);
            let dm2 = dmin * f32::from(m2);
            for l in 0..32 {
                let low_byte = ql[group * 32 + l];
                let high_byte = qh[l];
                let lo = (low_byte & 0xF) + if high_byte & u1 != 0 { 16 } else { 0 };
                let hi = (low_byte >> 4) + if high_byte & u2 != 0 { 16 } else { 0 };
                o[group * 64 + l] = d1 * f32::from(lo) - dm1;
                o[group * 64 + 32 + l] = d2 * f32::from(hi) - dm2;
            }
            u1 <<= 2;
            u2 <<= 2;
        }
    }
}

fn dequant_q6_k(data: &[u8], out: &mut [f32]) {
    for (b, block) in data.chunks_exact(210).enumerate() {
        let ql = &block[0..128];
        let qh = &block[128..192];
        let sc = &block[192..208];
        let d = read_f16(block, 208);
        let o = &mut out[b * 256..(b + 1) * 256];
        // Two halves of 128 elements. Each half interleaves four 32-element
        // streams (ql low, next-chunk ql low, ql high, next-chunk ql high),
        // and each qh byte carries the top two bits of all four streams for
        // its index: bits 0-1, 2-3, 4-5, 6-7 respectively.
        for half in 0..2 {
            let ql_h = &ql[half * 64..half * 64 + 64];
            let qh_h = &qh[half * 32..half * 32 + 32];
            let sc_h = &sc[half * 8..half * 8 + 8];
            let base = half * 128;
            for l in 0..32 {
                let is = l / 16;
                let q1 = i32::from((ql_h[l] & 0xF) | ((qh_h[l] & 3) << 4)) - 32;
                let q2 = i32::from((ql_h[l + 32] & 0xF) | (((qh_h[l] >> 2) & 3) << 4)) - 32;
                let q3 = i32::from((ql_h[l] >> 4) | (((qh_h[l] >> 4) & 3) << 4)) - 32;
                let q4 = i32::from((ql_h[l + 32] >> 4) | (((qh_h[l] >> 6) & 3) << 4)) - 32;
                o[base + l] = d * f32::from(sc_h[is] as i8) * q1 as f32;
                o[base + 32 + l] = d * f32::from(sc_h[is + 2] as i8) * q2 as f32;
                o[base + 64 + l] = d * f32::from(sc_h[is + 4] as i8) * q3 as f32;
                o[base + 96 + l] = d * f32::from(sc_h[is + 6] as i8) * q4 as f32;
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Dequantize `elements` elements of type `ty` from their exact on-disk
/// bytes into a fresh f32 vector.
pub fn dequantize(ty: GgmlType, data: &[u8], elements: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    debug_assert_eq!(
        ty.byte_len(elements as u64),
        Some(data.len() as u64),
        "caller must pass the exact byte length for the element count"
    );
    let mut out = vec![0.0f32; elements];
    match ty {
        GgmlType::F32 => {
            for (slot, chunk) in out.iter_mut().zip(data.chunks_exact(4)) {
                *slot = f32::from_le_bytes([chunk[0], chunk[1], chunk[2], chunk[3]]);
            }
        }
        GgmlType::F16 => {
            for (slot, chunk) in out.iter_mut().zip(data.chunks_exact(2)) {
                *slot = f16_to_f32(u16::from_le_bytes([chunk[0], chunk[1]]));
            }
        }
        GgmlType::Bf16 => {
            for (slot, chunk) in out.iter_mut().zip(data.chunks_exact(2)) {
                *slot = bf16_to_f32(u16::from_le_bytes([chunk[0], chunk[1]]));
            }
        }
        GgmlType::Q8_0 => dequant_q8_0(data, &mut out),
        GgmlType::Q2K => dequant_q2_k(data, &mut out),
        GgmlType::Q3K => dequant_q3_k(data, &mut out),
        GgmlType::Q4K => dequant_q4_k(data, &mut out),
        GgmlType::Q5K => dequant_q5_k(data, &mut out),
        GgmlType::Q6K => dequant_q6_k(data, &mut out),
    }
    out
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn f16_known_values() {
        assert_eq!(f16_to_f32(0x3c00), 1.0);
        assert_eq!(f16_to_f32(0xc000), -2.0);
        assert_eq!(f16_to_f32(0x3800), 0.5);
        assert_eq!(f16_to_f32(0x0000), 0.0);
        assert_eq!(f16_to_f32(0x7c00), f32::INFINITY);
        assert_eq!(f16_to_f32(0xfc00), f32::NEG_INFINITY);
        // Smallest subnormal half is exactly 2^-24.
        assert_eq!(f16_to_f32(0x0001), 5.960_464_5e-8);
        assert!(f16_to_f32(0x7e00).is_nan());
    }

    #[test]
    fn bf16_known_values() {
        assert_eq!(bf16_to_f32(0x3f80), 1.0);
        assert_eq!(bf16_to_f32(0xc020), -2.5);
        assert_eq!(bf16_to_f32(0x0000), 0.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn scale_min_k4_low_subblocks() {
        let mut scales = [0u8; 12];
        scales[0] = 0b10_000011; // high bits must be masked off for j < 4
        scales[4] = 0b01_000010;
        assert_eq!(scale_min_k4(0, &scales), (3, 2));
    }

    /// Build one Q2_K block from its parts (f16 values as raw bits).
    fn q2_k_block(scales: &[u8; 16], qs: &[u8; 64], d: u16, dmin: u16) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut block = Vec::with_capacity(84);
        block.extend_from_slice(scales);
        block.extend_from_slice(qs);
        block.extend_from_slice(&d.to_le_bytes());
        block.extend_from_slice(&dmin.to_le_bytes());
        block
    }

    /// Build one Q3_K block from its parts (f16 value as raw bits).
    fn q3_k_block(hmask: &[u8; 32], qs: &[u8; 64], scales: &[u8; 12], d: u16) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut block = Vec::with_capacity(110);
        block.extend_from_slice(hmask);
        block.extend_from_slice(qs);
        block.extend_from_slice(scales);
        block.extend_from_slice(&d.to_le_bytes());
        block
    }

    #[test]
    fn q2_k_zero_quants_hit_the_mins() {
        // scale byte s: low nibble 1 (scale), high nibble s (min).
        let mut scales = [0u8; 16];
        for (s, byte) in scales.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            *byte = ((s as u8) << 4) | 1;
        }
        // d = 2.0 (0x4000), dmin = 0.25 (0x3400), all quants zero, so
        // every output is -(dmin * min) = -0.25 * s in sub-block s.
        let block = q2_k_block(&scales, &[0u8; 64], 0x4000, 0x3400);
        let out = dequantize(GgmlType::Q2K, &block, 256);
        for s in 0..16 {
            let base = (s / 8) * 128 + ((s % 8) / 2) * 32 + (s % 2) * 16;
            assert_eq!(out[base], -0.25 * s as f32, "sub-block {s} first");
            assert_eq!(out[base + 15], -0.25 * s as f32, "sub-block {s} last");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn q2_k_planes_chunks_and_subblocks() {
        // d = 1.0, dmin = 0, every scale byte 0x01 (scale 1, min 0), so
        // outputs equal the raw 2-bit quants. 0xE4 = planes 0,1,2,3.
        let mut qs = [0u8; 64];
        qs[0] = 0xE4; // chunk 0, sub-block 0, l = 0
        qs[16] = 0xE4; // chunk 0, sub-block 1, l = 0
        qs[32] = 0xE4; // chunk 1, sub-block 0, l = 0
        let block = q2_k_block(&[0x01u8; 16], &qs, 0x3C00, 0x0000);
        let out = dequantize(GgmlType::Q2K, &block, 256);
        for base in [0usize, 16, 128] {
            assert_eq!(out[base], 0.0);
            assert_eq!(out[base + 32], 1.0);
            assert_eq!(out[base + 64], 2.0);
            assert_eq!(out[base + 96], 3.0);
        }
        assert_eq!(out[1], 0.0);
        assert_eq!(out[200], 0.0);
        assert_eq!(out[255], 0.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn q2_k_max_scale_min_and_quant() {
        // scale 15, min 15, quant 3 everywhere: 0.5*15*3 - 0.5*15 = 15.
        let block = q2_k_block(&[0xFFu8; 16], &[0xFFu8; 64], 0x3800, 0x3800);
        let out = dequantize(GgmlType::Q2K, &block, 256);
        assert!(out.iter().all(|&v| v == 15.0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn q2_k_zero_scales_give_zero() {
        // d and dmin both zero: no scale or min can produce a value.
        let block = q2_k_block(&[0xFFu8; 16], &[0xFFu8; 64], 0x0000, 0x0000);
        let out = dequantize(GgmlType::Q2K, &block, 256);
        assert!(out.iter().all(|&v| v == 0.0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn q3_k_scale_unpack_matches_hand_computation() {
        // Expected values worked byte-by-byte from ggml's uint32 shuffle:
        // bytes 0..8 give the low four bits, bytes 8..12 give the top two
        // bits in four successive 2-bit fields per byte.
        let packed = [
            0x12, 0x34, 0x56, 0x78, 0x9A, 0xBC, 0xDE, 0xF0, 0x21, 0x43, 0x65, 0x87,
        ];
        let expected: [i8; 16] = [18, 52, 22, 56, 10, 12, 30, 16, 33, 3, 37, 7, 9, 27, 29, 47];
        assert_eq!(unpack_scales_q3_k(&packed), expected);
    }

    #[test]
    fn q3_k_mask_clear_subtracts_four() {
        // All scale bytes zero unpack to scale 0, so dl = d * (0 - 32).
        // d = 2^-5 (0x2800) makes dl exactly -1. Quants are all zero.
        let scales = [0u8; 12];
        // Mask clear everywhere: value is (0 - 4), output 4.0 everywhere.
        let block = q3_k_block(&[0u8; 32], &[0u8; 64], &scales, 0x2800);
        let out = dequantize(GgmlType::Q3K, &block, 256);
        assert!(out.iter().all(|&v| v == 4.0));
        // Mask set everywhere: value is 0, output 0.0 everywhere.
        let block = q3_k_block(&[0xFFu8; 32], &[0u8; 64], &scales, 0x2800);
        let out = dequantize(GgmlType::Q3K, &block, 256);
        assert!(out.iter().all(|&v| v == 0.0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn q3_k_planes_and_second_chunk_mask_bits() {
        // Same dl = -1 setup as above; mask fully set so values are the
        // raw quants negated. 0xE4 in qs[0] and qs[32] exercises planes
        // in chunk 0 and chunk 1 (chunk 1 reads mask bits 4..8).
        let mut qs = [0u8; 64];
        qs[0] = 0xE4;
        qs[32] = 0xE4;
        let block = q3_k_block(&[0xFFu8; 32], &qs, &[0u8; 12], 0x2800);
        let out = dequantize(GgmlType::Q3K, &block, 256);
        for base in [0usize, 128] {
            assert_eq!(out[base], 0.0);
            assert_eq!(out[base + 32], -1.0);
            assert_eq!(out[base + 64], -2.0);
            assert_eq!(out[base + 96], -3.0);
        }
        assert_eq!(out[1], 0.0);
        assert_eq!(out[255], 0.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn q3_k_scale_extremes() {
        // All nibbles and 2-bit fields maxed: every scale unpacks to 63,
        // factor (63 - 32) = 31, d = 1.0.
        let block = q3_k_block(&[0xFFu8; 32], &[0xFFu8; 64], &[0xFFu8; 12], 0x3C00);
        let out = dequantize(GgmlType::Q3K, &block, 256);
        assert!(out.iter().all(|&v| v == 93.0));
        // Same quants with the mask clear: value (3 - 4) = -1, output -31.
        let block = q3_k_block(&[0u8; 32], &[0xFFu8; 64], &[0xFFu8; 12], 0x3C00);
        let out = dequantize(GgmlType::Q3K, &block, 256);
        assert!(out.iter().all(|&v| v == -31.0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn scale_min_k4_high_subblocks() {
        // j = 4: sc = (scales[8] & 0xF) | ((scales[0] >> 6) << 4)
        //      m  = (scales[8] >> 4)  | ((scales[4] >> 6) << 4)
        let mut scales = [0u8; 12];
        scales[0] = 0b10_000000;
        scales[4] = 0b01_000000;
        scales[8] = 0b0101_1001;
        assert_eq!(scale_min_k4(4, &scales), (0b10_1001, 0b01_0101));
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/gguf/src/diag.rs =====
//! Structured diagnostics for the GGUF loader.
//!
//! David's rule: debugging is built into every module from birth, not bolted
//! on after a failure. This module is the crate's diagnostic channel:
//!
//! - Enable the debug level with [`set_debug_enabled`] or the
//!   `GGUF_DEBUG` environment variable (checked on every
//!   [`debug_enabled`] call, so a test or a long-running process can
//!   flip it at runtime). The error level ([`error`]) is not gated:
//!   a refusal emits whether or not debug is on.
//! - Output is structured `key=value` lines on stderr, tagged
//!   `[gguf][debug]`, so logs can be grepped and parsed mechanically.
//! - Every parse and load event worth investigating (header values, tensor
//!   directory entries, dequantization runs, and every hard error) passes
//!   through here. Errors are logged at the point they are created, before
//!   they propagate, so the log shows the refusal and its reason even when
//!   the caller only prints the top-level error.

use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};

static DEBUG_ENABLED: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);

/// Turn structured debug logging on or off for the whole process.
pub fn set_debug_enabled(enabled: bool) {
    DEBUG_ENABLED.store(enabled, Ordering::Relaxed);
}

/// Whether debug logging is active: the explicit flag, or `GGUF_DEBUG`
/// present in the environment (any value other than `0`).
pub fn debug_enabled() -> bool {
    if DEBUG_ENABLED.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
        return true;
    }
    match std::env::var("GGUF_DEBUG") {
        Ok(v) => v != "0" && !v.is_empty(),
        Err(_) => false,
    }
}

/// Emit one structured debug line if diagnostics are enabled.
///
/// `event` is a short snake_case name; `fields` are `key=value` fragments the
/// caller has already formatted. Keeping formatting at the call site keeps
/// this channel allocation-light and dependency-free.
pub fn debug(event: &str, fields: &str) {
    if debug_enabled() {
        eprintln!("[gguf][debug] event={event} {fields}");
    }
}

/// Emit a structured line for a hard error, unconditionally.
/// Errors are the refusals the audit law says must be observable,
/// so unlike [`debug`] this is never gated by the debug flag: a
/// refusal that only shows when debug is on is a silent refusal.
/// Every `GgufError` construction inside the crate emits through
/// here exactly once, at the point the error is created (see
/// `GgufError::logged` in error.rs), before it propagates.
pub fn error(event: &str, fields: &str) {
    #[cfg(test)]
    capture(&format!("[gguf][error] event={event} {fields}"));
    eprintln!("[gguf][error] event={event} {fields}");
}

/// Test-only capture of emitted error lines, so unit tests can
/// prove a refusal actually fired its diag event instead of
/// trusting that the call is present in the source. Lines are the
/// exact formatted output; tests assert on their own event names
/// and field values, which are unique per test, so parallel tests
/// sharing this buffer cannot satisfy each other's assertions.
#[cfg(test)]
static CAPTURED: std::sync::Mutex<Vec<String>> = std::sync::Mutex::new(Vec::new());

#[cfg(test)]
fn capture(line: &str) {
    CAPTURED
        .lock()
        .unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())
        .push(line.to_string());
}

/// The error lines captured since the process started (test builds
/// only). Callers compare a snapshot taken before the action under
/// test, or search for field values only their own test produces.
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) fn captured_errors() -> Vec<String> {
    CAPTURED.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner()).clone()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn flag_round_trips() {
        set_debug_enabled(true);
        assert!(debug_enabled());
        set_debug_enabled(false);
        // Env may still enable it in a developer shell; only assert the flag
        // store did not panic and the API is callable in both states.
        let _ = debug_enabled();
    }

    #[test]
    fn error_emits_with_debug_off() {
        // The documented contract: errors are unconditional. With
        // the flag off and regardless of env, the event must land
        // in the capture buffer (the same line stderr receives).
        set_debug_enabled(false);
        error("unconditional_probe", "probe=flag_off");
        assert!(captured_errors()
            .iter()
            .any(|l| l.contains("event=unconditional_probe") && l.contains("probe=flag_off")));
    }
}
