===== FILE: crates/gguf/src/error.rs =====
//! Error types for the GGUF loader.
//!
//! Design rule (from the 2026-10-29 audit of the old Go loader): every
//! failure is loud and names the thing that failed. There is no error path
//! in this crate that substitutes placeholder data.

use std::fmt;

/// Result alias for loader operations.
pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, GgufError>;

/// Everything that can go wrong while parsing or loading a GGUF file.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum GgufError {
    /// Underlying I/O failure (opening or reading the file).
    Io(std::io::Error),
    /// The first four bytes were not the `GGUF` magic.
    BadMagic {
        /// The four bytes actually found.
        found: [u8; 4],
    },
    /// GGUF format version other than 3.
    UnsupportedVersion(u32),
    /// The file ended before a structure was complete.
    Truncated {
        /// What was being read when the file ran out.
        context: &'static str,
        /// Byte offset where the read started.
        offset: u64,
        /// Bytes the read needed.
        needed: u64,
        /// Total file size in bytes.
        file_len: u64,
    },
    /// A metadata key or tensor name was not valid UTF-8.
    InvalidUtf8 {
        /// What the string was (metadata key, tensor name, string value).
        context: &'static str,
    },
    /// A metadata value type id that GGUF does not define.
    UnknownMetadataType(u32),
    /// A string/array length or element count that cannot fit in memory.
    LengthOverflow {
        /// What carried the impossible length.
        context: &'static str,
    },
    /// A tensor was requested by name and is not in the file.
    MissingTensor(String),
    /// A tensor's element count is not a whole number of quantization blocks.
    BadElementCount {
        /// Tensor name.
        tensor: String,
        /// Element count from the tensor directory.
        elements: u64,
        /// Block size of the tensor's type.
        block_size: u64,
    },
    /// A tensor's declared data range falls outside the file.
    TensorOutOfBounds {
        /// Tensor name.
        tensor: String,
        /// Absolute byte offset of the tensor data.
        offset: u64,
        /// Byte length of the tensor data.
        len: u64,
        /// Total file size in bytes.
        file_len: u64,
    },
    /// A tensor uses a type this loader does not dequantize. This is a hard
    /// error by design: the old loader silently substituted random weights
    /// for types it could not read, and that defect class is banned here.
    UnsupportedTensorType {
        /// Tensor name.
        tensor: String,
        /// Mainline ggml type id from the file.
        type_id: u32,
        /// Human-readable type name, or `unknown` for unassigned ids.
        type_name: String,
    },
    /// A structural rule of the GGUF format was violated.
    InvalidFormat {
        /// The structure being parsed.
        context: &'static str,
        /// What was wrong, in plain words.
        detail: String,
    },
    /// A metadata key the caller required is absent.
    MissingMetadata(String),
    /// A metadata key exists but holds a different value type than asked for.
    MetadataTypeMismatch {
        /// Metadata key.
        key: String,
        /// Type the caller asked for.
        expected: &'static str,
        /// Type actually stored in the file.
        found: &'static str,
    },
}

impl fmt::Display for GgufError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Self::Io(e) => write!(f, "io error: {e}"),
            Self::BadMagic { found } => {
                write!(f, "bad magic: expected GGUF, found {found:?}")
            }
            Self::UnsupportedVersion(v) => {
                write!(f, "unsupported GGUF version {v} (this loader reads version 3)")
            }
            Self::Truncated {
                context,
                offset,
                needed,
                file_len,
            } => write!(
                f,
                "file truncated reading {context}: need {needed} bytes at offset {offset}, file is {file_len} bytes"
            ),
            Self::InvalidUtf8 { context } => write!(f, "invalid UTF-8 in {context}"),
            Self::UnknownMetadataType(id) => write!(f, "unknown metadata value type id {id}"),
            Self::LengthOverflow { context } => {
                write!(f, "declared length for {context} overflows addressable memory")
            }
            Self::MissingTensor(name) => write!(f, "tensor not found: {name}"),
            Self::BadElementCount {
                tensor,
                elements,
                block_size,
            } => write!(
                f,
                "tensor {tensor}: element count {elements} is not a multiple of block size {block_size}"
            ),
            Self::TensorOutOfBounds {
                tensor,
                offset,
                len,
                file_len,
            } => write!(
                f,
                "tensor {tensor}: data range [{offset}, {}) exceeds file length {file_len}",
                offset.saturating_add(*len)
            ),
            Self::UnsupportedTensorType {
                tensor,
                type_id,
                type_name,
            } => write!(
                f,
                "tensor {tensor}: unsupported type {type_name} (ggml type id {type_id}); this loader dequantizes F32, F16, BF16, Q8_0, Q2_K, Q3_K, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K only"
            ),
            Self::InvalidFormat { context, detail } => {
                write!(f, "invalid GGUF format in {context}: {detail}")
            }
            Self::MissingMetadata(key) => write!(f, "metadata key not found: {key}"),
            Self::MetadataTypeMismatch {
                key,
                expected,
                found,
            } => write!(
                f,
                "metadata key {key}: expected {expected}, found {found}"
            ),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for GgufError {
    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {
        match self {
            Self::Io(e) => Some(e),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

impl GgufError {
    /// Emit this error through the crate's diagnostic channel and
    /// return it unchanged: the construction seam every error site
    /// in the crate routes through (`GgufError::Variant { .. }
    /// .logged()`), so a refusal is recorded exactly once, at the
    /// point it is created, before it propagates (diag.rs documents
    /// the same contract). The variant-to-event mapping lives in
    /// [`emit`](Self::emit), whose match is exhaustive: adding a
    /// variant fails compilation there until the new variant has
    /// an event name and fields, so a new error cannot be born
    /// silent by forgetting a call at its construction sites.
    pub(crate) fn logged(self) -> Self {
        self.emit();
        self
    }

    /// The one place a variant becomes a diag event. Field shapes
    /// follow the crate's `key=value` convention and, where the
    /// parser had hand-written events before this seam existed,
    /// keep those event names (bad_magic, missing_tensor, ...).
    fn emit(&self) {
        let (event, fields) = match self {
            Self::Io(e) => ("io_error", format!("error={e}")),
            Self::BadMagic { found } => ("bad_magic", format!("found={found:?}")),
            Self::UnsupportedVersion(v) => ("unsupported_version", format!("version={v}")),
            Self::Truncated {
                context,
                offset,
                needed,
                file_len,
            } => (
                "truncated",
                format!("context={context} offset={offset} needed={needed} file_len={file_len}"),
            ),
            Self::InvalidUtf8 { context } => ("invalid_utf8", format!("context={context}")),
            Self::UnknownMetadataType(id) => ("unknown_metadata_type", format!("type_id={id}")),
            Self::LengthOverflow { context } => ("length_overflow", format!("context={context}")),
            Self::MissingTensor(name) => ("missing_tensor", format!("name={name}")),
            Self::BadElementCount {
                tensor,
                elements,
                block_size,
            } => (
                "bad_element_count",
                format!("tensor={tensor} elements={elements} block_size={block_size}"),
            ),
            Self::TensorOutOfBounds {
                tensor,
                offset,
                len,
                file_len,
            } => (
                "tensor_out_of_bounds",
                format!("name={tensor} offset={offset} len={len} file_len={file_len}"),
            ),
            Self::UnsupportedTensorType {
                tensor,
                type_id,
                type_name,
            } => (
                "unsupported_type",
                format!("name={tensor} type_id={type_id} type={type_name}"),
            ),
            Self::InvalidFormat { context, detail } => (
                "invalid_format",
                format!("context={context} detail={detail}"),
            ),
            Self::MissingMetadata(key) => ("missing_metadata", format!("key={key}")),
            Self::MetadataTypeMismatch {
                key,
                expected,
                found,
            } => (
                "metadata_type_mismatch",
                format!("key={key} expected={expected} found={found}"),
            ),
        };
        crate::diag::error(event, &fields);
    }
}

impl From<std::io::Error> for GgufError {
    fn from(e: std::io::Error) -> Self {
        // The conversion is a construction path like any other:
        // an io failure becomes a GgufError here, so it emits
        // here, and the `?` that triggered the conversion does
        // not emit a second time.
        Self::Io(e).logged()
    }
}

===== END FILE: crates/gguf/src/error.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/gguf/src/file.rs =====
//! The GGUF file parser and tensor loader.
//!
//! Parse order follows the format: magic, version, counts, metadata
//! key-values, tensor directory, alignment padding, tensor data. Validation
//! is done once at parse time for everything that can be checked without
//! dequantizing (element counts against block geometry, tensor data ranges
//! against file length), so a malformed file fails at open, not mid-run.
//!
//! Loading is by name and fails loudly: absent tensor, unsupported type,
//! out-of-bounds data are all hard errors. There is deliberately no API
//! that returns placeholder or partially-filled weights.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::fs::File;
use std::path::Path;

use crate::dequant;
use crate::diag;
use crate::error::{GgufError, Result};
use crate::ggml::{type_name, GgmlType};
use crate::metadata::{Metadata, MetadataValue};

const GGUF_MAGIC: &[u8; 4] = b"GGUF";
const SUPPORTED_VERSION: u32 = 3;
const DEFAULT_ALIGNMENT: u32 = 32;

/// One entry of the tensor directory.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct TensorInfo {
    name: String,
    dims: Vec<u64>,
    type_id: u32,
    rel_offset: u64,
    elements: u64,
}

impl TensorInfo {
    /// Tensor name as stored in the file.
    pub fn name(&self) -> &str {
        &self.name
    }

    /// Dimensions as stored in the file. GGUF stores the contiguous
    /// (row) dimension first: `dims()[0]` is the length of one row.
    pub fn dims(&self) -> &[u64] {
        &self.dims
    }

    /// Total element count (product of all dimensions).
    pub fn element_count(&self) -> u64 {
        self.elements
    }

    /// Mainline ggml type id as stored in the file.
    pub fn type_id(&self) -> u32 {
        self.type_id
    }

    /// Human-readable ggml type name (for example `Q4_K`, `BF16`).
    pub fn type_name(&self) -> &'static str {
        type_name(self.type_id)
    }

    /// The type, when this loader can dequantize it.
    pub fn ggml_type(&self) -> Option<GgmlType> {
        GgmlType::from_id(self.type_id)
    }

    /// Offset of the tensor data relative to the start of the tensor data
    /// section, exactly as stored in the directory.
    pub fn relative_offset(&self) -> u64 {
        self.rel_offset
    }

    /// On-disk byte length, when the type is supported and the element
    /// count is a whole number of blocks.
    pub fn byte_len(&self) -> Option<u64> {
        self.ggml_type().and_then(|t| t.byte_len(self.elements))
    }
}

/// Backing store for the file image.
///
/// `Owned` is the in-memory buffer handed to
/// [`GgufFile::from_bytes`]. `Mapped` is the on-disk file mapped by
/// [`GgufFile::open`] (PLAN T-2.1): the image occupies no anonymous
/// memory, so opening a model no longer costs its file size in RAM;
/// pages are faulted in by the kernel as tensors are read and can be
/// evicted under memory pressure. Both forms serve the identical
/// byte slice, so nothing downstream of the parse can tell them
/// apart.
#[derive(Debug)]
enum ImageBacking {
    Owned(Vec<u8>),
    Mapped(memmap2::Mmap),
}

impl ImageBacking {
    /// The whole file image as a byte slice.
    fn as_slice(&self) -> &[u8] {
        match self {
            Self::Owned(bytes) => bytes,
            Self::Mapped(map) => map,
        }
    }
}

/// Memory-map an opened file for read-only access.
///
/// This is the crate's only unsafe call site (see the crate-level
/// lint note in `lib.rs`).
#[allow(unsafe_code)]
fn map_file(file: &File) -> std::io::Result<memmap2::Mmap> {
    // SAFETY: `Mmap::map` is unsafe because the mapping aliases the
    // file's bytes: if another process truncates or rewrites the
    // file while it is mapped, reads of the affected pages can
    // observe changed bytes or fault with SIGBUS past a truncated
    // end instead of returning an error. This loader treats GGUF
    // model files as immutable artifacts for the life of a
    // `GgufFile`: `open` maps the file once, nothing in this crate
    // ever writes through the mapping (it is mapped read-only), and
    // callers must not modify or truncate a file while a `GgufFile`
    // opened from it is alive. That is the standing deployment
    // contract for model files (they are replaced by rename between
    // runs, never edited in place), and it is the same assumption
    // every mmap-backed GGUF reader (llama.cpp included) makes.
    unsafe { memmap2::Mmap::map(file) }
}

/// A parsed GGUF file.
///
/// The file image is either an owned in-memory buffer
/// ([`GgufFile::from_bytes`]) or a memory mapping of the file on
/// disk ([`GgufFile::open`], PLAN T-2.1); the API is the same for
/// both. Everything the engine needs for correctness (typed
/// metadata, per-tensor geometry, checked ranges) is validated
/// here.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct GgufFile {
    backing: ImageBacking,
    version: u32,
    metadata: Metadata,
    tensors: Vec<TensorInfo>,
    index: HashMap<String, usize>,
    alignment: u32,
    data_start: usize,
}

impl GgufFile {
    /// Open and parse a GGUF file from disk.
    ///
    /// The file is memory-mapped, not read into memory (PLAN T-2.1),
    /// so opening a file costs no anonymous RAM proportional to its
    /// size. The file must not be modified or truncated while the
    /// returned `GgufFile` is alive; see [`map_file`] for the full
    /// contract.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// The same named errors as [`GgufFile::from_bytes`] for the
    /// file's contents, plus `Io` when the file cannot be opened or
    /// mapped.
    pub fn open(path: &Path) -> Result<Self> {
        diag::debug("file_open", &format!("path={}", path.display()));
        let file = File::open(path)?;
        if file.metadata()?.len() == 0 {
            // A zero-length file cannot be mapped (and the mapping
            // library refuses it), but it still has a named parse
            // failure: parse the empty image so `open` reports the
            // same `Truncated` error the in-memory path reports.
            return Self::from_bytes(Vec::new());
        }
        let map = map_file(&file)?;
        Self::parse(ImageBacking::Mapped(map))
    }

    /// Parse a GGUF file from an in-memory byte buffer.
    pub fn from_bytes(bytes: Vec<u8>) -> Result<Self> {
        Self::parse(ImageBacking::Owned(bytes))
    }

    /// Parse a GGUF file from its image backing.
    fn parse(backing: ImageBacking) -> Result<Self> {
        let bytes = backing.as_slice();
        let mut reader = Reader::new(bytes);

        let magic = reader.read_bytes(4, "magic")?;
        if magic != GGUF_MAGIC {
            let found = [magic[0], magic[1], magic[2], magic[3]];
            return Err(GgufError::BadMagic { found }.logged());
        }
        let version = reader.read_u32("version")?;
        if version != SUPPORTED_VERSION {
            return Err(GgufError::UnsupportedVersion(version).logged());
        }
        let tensor_count = reader.read_u64("tensor_count")?;
        let metadata_count = reader.read_u64("metadata_kv_count")?;
        diag::debug(
            "parse_header",
            &format!("version={version} tensors={tensor_count} metadata_kv={metadata_count}"),
        );

        let mut entries = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..metadata_count {
            let key = reader.read_string("metadata key")?;
            let value = read_metadata_value(&mut reader)?;
            entries.push((key, value));
        }
        let metadata = Metadata::from_entries(entries);

        let mut tensors = Vec::new();
        let mut index = HashMap::new();
        for _ in 0..tensor_count {
            let name = reader.read_string("tensor name")?;
            let n_dims = reader.read_u32("tensor dimension count")?;
            if !(1..=4).contains(&n_dims) {
                return Err(GgufError::InvalidFormat {
                    context: "tensor directory",
                    detail: format!("tensor {name}: dimension count {n_dims} outside 1..=4"),
                }
                .logged());
            }
            let mut dims = Vec::with_capacity(n_dims as usize);
            let mut elements: u64 = 1;
            for _ in 0..n_dims {
                let d = reader.read_u64("tensor dimension")?;
                dims.push(d);
                // ok_or_else, not ok_or: the error must be
                // constructed (and so emitted, via .logged()) only
                // on the failure path, never for a product that fit.
                elements = elements.checked_mul(d).ok_or_else(|| {
                    GgufError::LengthOverflow {
                        context: "tensor element count",
                    }
                    .logged()
                })?;
            }
            let type_id = reader.read_u32("tensor type")?;
            let rel_offset = reader.read_u64("tensor offset")?;
            if let Some(ty) = GgmlType::from_id(type_id) {
                if ty.byte_len(elements).is_none() {
                    return Err(GgufError::BadElementCount {
                        tensor: name,
                        elements,
                        block_size: ty.block_size(),
                    }
                    .logged());
                }
            }
            diag::debug(
                "tensor_dir",
                &format!(
                    "name={name} type={} dims={dims:?} elements={elements} rel_offset={rel_offset}",
                    type_name(type_id)
                ),
            );
            let slot = tensors.len();
            if index.insert(name.clone(), slot).is_some() {
                return Err(GgufError::InvalidFormat {
                    context: "tensor directory",
                    detail: format!("duplicate tensor name {name}"),
                }
                .logged());
            }
            tensors.push(TensorInfo {
                name,
                dims,
                type_id,
                rel_offset,
                elements,
            });
        }

        let alignment = match metadata.opt_u32("general.alignment")? {
            Some(a) => a,
            None => DEFAULT_ALIGNMENT,
        };
        if alignment == 0 || !alignment.is_power_of_two() || alignment > (1 << 20) {
            return Err(GgufError::InvalidFormat {
                context: "header",
                detail: format!(
                    "general.alignment {alignment} is not a power of two within 1..=1048576"
                ),
            }
            .logged());
        }
        let header_len = reader.position() as u64;
        let data_start_u = align_up(header_len, u64::from(alignment));
        let data_start = usize::try_from(data_start_u).map_err(|_| {
            GgufError::LengthOverflow {
                context: "tensor data offset",
            }
            .logged()
        })?;

        // Bounds-check every supported tensor's data range against the file.
        let file_len = bytes.len() as u64;
        for tensor in &tensors {
            if let Some(len) = tensor.byte_len() {
                // ok_or_else for the same reason as the element
                // count above: construction (and emission) belongs
                // to the failure path only.
                let offset = data_start_u.checked_add(tensor.rel_offset).ok_or_else(|| {
                    GgufError::LengthOverflow {
                        context: "tensor data offset",
                    }
                    .logged()
                })?;
                let in_bounds = offset.checked_add(len).is_some_and(|end| end <= file_len);
                if !in_bounds {
                    return Err(GgufError::TensorOutOfBounds {
                        tensor: tensor.name.clone(),
                        offset,
                        len,
                        file_len,
                    }
                    .logged());
                }
            }
        }

        diag::debug(
            "parse_done",
            &format!(
                "tensors={} metadata_kv={} alignment={alignment} data_start={data_start} file_len={file_len}",
                tensors.len(),
                metadata.len()
            ),
        );

        Ok(Self {
            backing,
            version,
            metadata,
            tensors,
            index,
            alignment,
            data_start,
        })
    }

    /// The whole file image, whichever backing form it has.
    fn bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
        self.backing.as_slice()
    }

    /// GGUF format version (always 3 for a successfully parsed file).
    pub fn version(&self) -> u32 {
        self.version
    }

    /// The metadata section.
    pub fn metadata(&self) -> &Metadata {
        &self.metadata
    }

    /// The architecture string (`general.architecture`), the file's own
    /// declaration of what it is.
    pub fn architecture(&self) -> Result<&str> {
        self.metadata.get_string("general.architecture")
    }

    /// Alignment used for the tensor data section.
    pub fn alignment(&self) -> u32 {
        self.alignment
    }

    /// Absolute byte offset where the tensor data section begins.
    pub fn data_start(&self) -> usize {
        self.data_start
    }

    /// Total file size in bytes.
    pub fn file_len(&self) -> usize {
        self.bytes().len()
    }

    /// All tensor directory entries, in file order.
    pub fn tensors(&self) -> &[TensorInfo] {
        &self.tensors
    }

    /// Tensor names, in file order.
    pub fn tensor_names(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
        self.tensors.iter().map(TensorInfo::name)
    }

    /// Whether a tensor with this name exists.
    pub fn has_tensor(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.index.contains_key(name)
    }

    /// Directory entry for a tensor, or a hard `MissingTensor` error.
    pub fn tensor_info(&self, name: &str) -> Result<&TensorInfo> {
        match self.index.get(name) {
            Some(&slot) => Ok(&self.tensors[slot]),
            None => Err(GgufError::MissingTensor(name.to_string()).logged()),
        }
    }

    /// The raw stored bytes of a tensor.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// `MissingTensor` when absent; `UnsupportedTensorType` when the type
    /// is not one this loader sizes and dequantizes (a raw read of an
    /// unsized type would be a guess, so it is refused too).
    pub fn tensor_bytes(&self, name: &str) -> Result<&[u8]> {
        let info = self.tensor_info(name)?;
        self.tensor_bytes_for(info)
    }

    fn tensor_bytes_for(&self, info: &TensorInfo) -> Result<&[u8]> {
        let len = match info.byte_len() {
            Some(len) => len,
            None => {
                return Err(GgufError::UnsupportedTensorType {
                    tensor: info.name.clone(),
                    type_id: info.type_id,
                    type_name: type_name(info.type_id).to_string(),
                }
                .logged());
            }
        };
        let start = self.data_start + info.rel_offset as usize;
        let end = start + len as usize;
        // Ranges were checked at parse time against the image length;
        // this slice can only fail if the image was mutated behind the
        // API, which the backing forms do not allow from safe code (for
        // the mapped form it would take another process rewriting the
        // file, excluded by the contract on `open`).
        Ok(&self.bytes()[start..end])
    }

    /// Load a tensor fully dequantized to f32.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// `MissingTensor` when absent, `UnsupportedTensorType` when the
    /// stored type is not F32, F16, BF16, Q8_0, Q2_K, Q3_K, Q4_K, Q5_K, or
    /// Q6_K. No
    /// partial or placeholder data is ever returned.
    pub fn load_f32(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        let info = self.tensor_info(name)?;
        self.load_f32_for(info)
    }

    /// [`load_f32`](Self::load_f32) from a directory entry directly.
    pub fn load_f32_for(&self, info: &TensorInfo) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        let ty = match info.ggml_type() {
            Some(ty) => ty,
            None => {
                return Err(GgufError::UnsupportedTensorType {
                    tensor: info.name.clone(),
                    type_id: info.type_id,
                    type_name: type_name(info.type_id).to_string(),
                }
                .logged());
            }
        };
        let raw = self.tensor_bytes_for(info)?;
        let elements = usize::try_from(info.elements).map_err(|_| {
            GgufError::LengthOverflow {
                context: "tensor element count",
            }
            .logged()
        })?;
        diag::debug(
            "tensor_load",
            &format!(
                "name={} type={} elements={elements} bytes={}",
                info.name,
                info.type_name(),
                raw.len()
            ),
        );
        Ok(dequant::dequantize(ty, raw, elements))
    }
}

fn align_up(value: u64, alignment: u64) -> u64 {
    value.div_ceil(alignment) * alignment
}

/// Byte cursor over the file with format-aware truncation errors.
struct Reader<'a> {
    bytes: &'a [u8],
    pos: usize,
}

impl<'a> Reader<'a> {
    fn new(bytes: &'a [u8]) -> Self {
        Self { bytes, pos: 0 }
    }

    fn position(&self) -> usize {
        self.pos
    }

    fn remaining(&self) -> usize {
        self.bytes.len() - self.pos
    }

    fn read_bytes(&mut self, n: usize, context: &'static str) -> Result<&'a [u8]> {
        if self.remaining() < n {
            return Err(GgufError::Truncated {
                context,
                offset: self.pos as u64,
                needed: n as u64,
                file_len: self.bytes.len() as u64,
            }
            .logged());
        }
        let out = &self.bytes[self.pos..self.pos + n];
        self.pos += n;
        Ok(out)
    }

    fn read_u8(&mut self, context: &'static str) -> Result<u8> {
        Ok(self.read_bytes(1, context)?[0])
    }

    fn read_i8(&mut self, context: &'static str) -> Result<i8> {
        Ok(self.read_u8(context)? as i8)
    }

    fn read_u16(&mut self, context: &'static str) -> Result<u16> {
        let b = self.read_bytes(2, context)?;
        Ok(u16::from_le_bytes([b[0], b[1]]))
    }

    fn read_i16(&mut self, context: &'static str) -> Result<i16> {
        Ok(self.read_u16(context)? as i16)
    }

    fn read_u32(&mut self, context: &'static str) -> Result<u32> {
        let b = self.read_bytes(4, context)?;
        Ok(u32::from_le_bytes([b[0], b[1], b[2], b[3]]))
    }

    fn read_i32(&mut self, context: &'static str) -> Result<i32> {
        Ok(self.read_u32(context)? as i32)
    }

    fn read_u64(&mut self, context: &'static str) -> Result<u64> {
        let b = self.read_bytes(8, context)?;
        Ok(u64::from_le_bytes([
            b[0], b[1], b[2], b[3], b[4], b[5], b[6], b[7],
        ]))
    }

    fn read_i64(&mut self, context: &'static str) -> Result<i64> {
        Ok(self.read_u64(context)? as i64)
    }

    fn read_f32(&mut self, context: &'static str) -> Result<f32> {
        Ok(f32::from_bits(self.read_u32(context)?))
    }

    fn read_f64(&mut self, context: &'static str) -> Result<f64> {
        Ok(f64::from_bits(self.read_u64(context)?))
    }

    fn read_bool(&mut self, context: &'static str) -> Result<bool> {
        Ok(self.read_u8(context)? != 0)
    }

    fn read_string(&mut self, context: &'static str) -> Result<String> {
        let len = self.read_u64("string length")?;
        let len =
            usize::try_from(len).map_err(|_| GgufError::LengthOverflow { context }.logged())?;
        let raw = self.read_bytes(len, context)?;
        String::from_utf8(raw.to_vec()).map_err(|_| GgufError::InvalidUtf8 { context }.logged())
    }
}

/// Read one metadata value, dispatching on its GGUF value-type id.
fn read_metadata_value(reader: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<MetadataValue> {
    let type_id = reader.read_u32("metadata value type")?;
    let value = match type_id {
        0 => MetadataValue::UInt8(reader.read_u8("metadata u8")?),
        1 => MetadataValue::Int8(reader.read_i8("metadata i8")?),
        2 => MetadataValue::UInt16(reader.read_u16("metadata u16")?),
        3 => MetadataValue::Int16(reader.read_i16("metadata i16")?),
        4 => MetadataValue::UInt32(reader.read_u32("metadata u32")?),
        5 => MetadataValue::Int32(reader.read_i32("metadata i32")?),
        6 => MetadataValue::Float32(reader.read_f32("metadata f32")?),
        7 => MetadataValue::Bool(reader.read_bool("metadata bool")?),
        8 => MetadataValue::String(reader.read_string("metadata string")?),
        9 => {
            let elem_type = reader.read_u32("metadata array element type")?;
            let len = reader.read_u64("metadata array length")?;
            // Every element costs at least one byte on disk; a declared
            // length larger than the rest of the file is impossible.
            if len > reader.remaining() as u64 {
                return Err(GgufError::Truncated {
                    context: "metadata array",
                    offset: reader.position() as u64,
                    needed: len,
                    file_len: reader.bytes.len() as u64,
                }
                .logged());
            }
            let mut items = Vec::new();
            for _ in 0..len {
                items.push(read_metadata_scalar(reader, elem_type)?);
            }
            MetadataValue::Array(items)
        }
        10 => MetadataValue::UInt64(reader.read_u64("metadata u64")?),
        11 => MetadataValue::Int64(reader.read_i64("metadata i64")?),
        12 => MetadataValue::Float64(reader.read_f64("metadata f64")?),
        other => return Err(GgufError::UnknownMetadataType(other).logged()),
    };
    Ok(value)
}

/// Read one array element (arrays cannot nest in GGUF).
fn read_metadata_scalar(reader: &mut Reader<'_>, type_id: u32) -> Result<MetadataValue> {
    let value = match type_id {
        0 => MetadataValue::UInt8(reader.read_u8("array u8")?),
        1 => MetadataValue::Int8(reader.read_i8("array i8")?),
        2 => MetadataValue::UInt16(reader.read_u16("array u16")?),
        3 => MetadataValue::Int16(reader.read_i16("array i16")?),
        4 => MetadataValue::UInt32(reader.read_u32("array u32")?),
        5 => MetadataValue::Int32(reader.read_i32("array i32")?),
        6 => MetadataValue::Float32(reader.read_f32("array f32")?),
        7 => MetadataValue::Bool(reader.read_bool("array bool")?),
        8 => MetadataValue::String(reader.read_string("array string")?),
        10 => MetadataValue::UInt64(reader.read_u64("array u64")?),
        11 => MetadataValue::Int64(reader.read_i64("array i64")?),
        12 => MetadataValue::Float64(reader.read_f64("array f64")?),
        other => return Err(GgufError::UnknownMetadataType(other).logged()),
    };
    Ok(value)
}

===== FILE: crates/gguf/src/ggml.rs =====
//! ggml tensor types, using MAINLINE ggml type ids.
//!
//! The old Go loader died on this table: it mapped id 30 to I2_S, but in
//! mainline ggml id 30 is BF16, so every BF16 tensor decoded as 2-bit
//! ternary garbage. The ids below are the mainline `ggml_type` enum values
//! and are pinned by unit tests so the collision can never come back.
//!
//! Only the types this loader can dequantize to f32 are modeled as
//! supported: F32, F16, BF16, Q8_0, Q2_K, Q3_K, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K. Any
//! other id is reported by name in a hard error (see [`type_name`])
//! instead of being silently skipped.

/// A ggml tensor element type this loader supports.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u32)]
pub enum GgmlType {
    /// 32-bit float, stored raw.
    F32 = 0,
    /// 16-bit IEEE half float.
    F16 = 1,
    /// 8-bit integer blocks of 32 with one f16 scale per block.
    Q8_0 = 8,
    /// K-quant 2-bit, 256-element super-blocks.
    Q2K = 10,
    /// K-quant 3-bit, 256-element super-blocks.
    Q3K = 11,
    /// K-quant 4-bit, 256-element super-blocks.
    Q4K = 12,
    /// K-quant 5-bit, 256-element super-blocks.
    Q5K = 13,
    /// K-quant 6-bit, 256-element super-blocks.
    Q6K = 14,
    /// Brain float 16. Mainline ggml id 30. NOT I2_S.
    Bf16 = 30,
}

impl GgmlType {
    /// Look up a supported type by its mainline ggml id. Returns `None` for
    /// every other id, including ids that name real ggml types this loader
    /// does not dequantize (Q8_1, IQ2_XXS, and friends).
    pub fn from_id(id: u32) -> Option<Self> {
        match id {
            0 => Some(Self::F32),
            1 => Some(Self::F16),
            8 => Some(Self::Q8_0),
            10 => Some(Self::Q2K),
            11 => Some(Self::Q3K),
            12 => Some(Self::Q4K),
            13 => Some(Self::Q5K),
            14 => Some(Self::Q6K),
            30 => Some(Self::Bf16),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The mainline ggml type id.
    pub fn id(self) -> u32 {
        self as u32
    }

    /// Elements per quantization block. Unquantized types have block size 1.
    pub fn block_size(self) -> u64 {
        match self {
            Self::F32 | Self::F16 | Self::Bf16 => 1,
            Self::Q8_0 => 32,
            Self::Q2K | Self::Q3K | Self::Q4K | Self::Q5K | Self::Q6K => 256,
        }
    }

    /// Bytes one block occupies in the file.
    pub fn block_bytes(self) -> u64 {
        match self {
            Self::F32 => 4,
            Self::F16 | Self::Bf16 => 2,
            // f16 scale + 32 x i8
            Self::Q8_0 => 2 + 32,
            // 16 packed scale/min bytes + 64 two-bit quant bytes + f16 d + f16 dmin
            Self::Q2K => 16 + 64 + 2 + 2,
            // 32 high-bit mask bytes + 64 two-bit quant bytes + 12 scale bytes + f16 d
            Self::Q3K => 32 + 64 + 12 + 2,
            // f16 d + f16 dmin + 12 scale bytes + 128 nibble bytes
            Self::Q4K => 2 + 2 + 12 + 128,
            // f16 d + f16 dmin + 12 scale bytes + 32 high-bit bytes + 128 nibble bytes
            Self::Q5K => 2 + 2 + 12 + 32 + 128,
            // 128 low-nibble bytes + 64 high-bit bytes + 16 i8 scales + f16 d
            Self::Q6K => 128 + 64 + 16 + 2,
        }
    }

    /// On-disk byte length of a tensor with `elements` elements, or `None`
    /// when the count is not a whole number of blocks.
    pub fn byte_len(self, elements: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        let block = self.block_size();
        if elements % block != 0 {
            return None;
        }
        (elements / block).checked_mul(self.block_bytes())
    }
}

/// Human-readable name for ANY mainline ggml type id, supported or not, so
/// hard errors can name what the file actually contains. Returns `unknown`
/// for ids mainline ggml has not assigned.
///
/// The trap from the old loader is called out here: I2_S in Microsoft's
/// bitnet.cpp fork is id 36 there, but has no mainline id; mainline id 30
/// is BF16 and is what this function reports.
pub fn type_name(id: u32) -> &'static str {
    match id {
        0 => "F32",
        1 => "F16",
        2 => "Q4_0",
        3 => "Q4_1",
        6 => "Q5_0",
        7 => "Q5_1",
        8 => "Q8_0",
        9 => "Q8_1",
        10 => "Q2_K",
        11 => "Q3_K",
        12 => "Q4_K",
        13 => "Q5_K",
        14 => "Q6_K",
        15 => "Q8_K",
        16 => "IQ2_XXS",
        17 => "IQ2_XS",
        18 => "IQ3_XXS",
        19 => "IQ1_S",
        20 => "IQ4_NL",
        21 => "IQ3_S",
        22 => "IQ2_S",
        23 => "IQ4_XS",
        24 => "I8",
        25 => "I16",
        26 => "I32",
        27 => "I64",
        28 => "F64",
        29 => "IQ1_M",
        30 => "BF16",
        34 => "TQ1_0",
        35 => "TQ2_0",
        39 => "MXFP4",
        _ => "unknown",
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn mainline_ids_are_pinned() {
        // The exact collision that corrupted BF16 tensors in the old loader.
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::Bf16.id(), 30);
        assert_eq!(type_name(30), "BF16");
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::from_id(30), Some(GgmlType::Bf16));
        // Q2_K and Q3_K gained readers on 2026-11-05 (cross-checked
        // against ggml's reference row dequantizers; see
        // bench/overnight-q2k-q3k-dequant-2026-11-05.md). This pin
        // replaces the audit-era assertion that id 11 must stay
        // unsupported: support is now deliberate, and the ids are pinned
        // so they cannot drift.
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::Q2K.id(), 10);
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::Q3K.id(), 11);
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::from_id(10), Some(GgmlType::Q2K));
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::from_id(11), Some(GgmlType::Q3K));
        assert_eq!(type_name(10), "Q2_K");
        assert_eq!(type_name(11), "Q3_K");
        // Types still without readers must stay hard errors, not support.
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::from_id(9), None); // Q8_1
        assert_eq!(type_name(9), "Q8_1");
    }

    #[test]
    fn block_geometry_matches_ggml() {
        // Q2_K/Q3_K sizes are ggml's static_asserts on block_q2_K and
        // block_q3_K in ggml-common.h (QK_K = 256): 84 and 110 bytes.
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::Q2K.block_bytes(), 84);
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::Q3K.block_bytes(), 110);
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::Q2K.block_size(), 256);
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::Q3K.block_size(), 256);
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::Q2K.byte_len(256), Some(84));
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::Q3K.byte_len(512), Some(220));
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::Q2K.byte_len(255), None);
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::Q3K.byte_len(128), None);
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::Q4K.block_bytes(), 144);
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::Q5K.block_bytes(), 176);
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::Q6K.block_bytes(), 210);
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::Q8_0.block_bytes(), 34);
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::Q4K.byte_len(256), Some(144));
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::Q4K.byte_len(255), None);
        assert_eq!(GgmlType::F32.byte_len(7), Some(28));
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/gguf/src/lib.rs =====
//! Strict GGUF v3 loading for the iTaK Torch rebuild.
//!
//! This crate replaces the original Go GGUF loader, which the 2026-10-29
//! audit found had three defect classes this crate is built to make
//! impossible:
//!
//! 1. **Missing dequantizers.** The Go loader had no Q3_K, Q5_K, or Q8_1
//!    readers. Here the supported set (F32, F16, BF16, Q8_0, Q2_K, Q3_K,
//!    Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K) dequantizes with ggml-exact math, and every other
//!    type is a hard error naming the tensor and the type.
//! 2. **A type-id collision.** The Go loader treated mainline ggml type
//!    id 30 as I2_S; mainline id 30 is BF16. The id table in [`ggml`] is
//!    mainline and pinned by tests.
//! 3. **Silent placeholder weights.** The Go loader substituted
//!    pseudo-random weights for anything it could not read. This crate has
//!    no placeholder path: a tensor that is absent, unreadable, or of an
//!    unsupported type is an error, full stop.
//!
//! Diagnostics are built in from birth (David's rule): structured
//! `key=value` debug lines flow through [`diag`] whenever `GGUF_DEBUG` is
//! set or [`diag::set_debug_enabled`] is called, and every hard error is
//! logged at the point of refusal.
//!
//! Quick start:
//!
//! ```no_run
//! use std::path::Path;
//! let file = gguf::GgufFile::open(Path::new("model.gguf")).unwrap();
//! println!("arch: {}", file.architecture().unwrap());
//! let config = file.model_config().unwrap();
//! let weights = file.load_f32("token_embd.weight").unwrap();
//! ```

// Unsafe is denied crate-wide, with exactly one exception: the
// memory-map call in `file::map_file` (PLAN T-2.1), which carries an
// item-level allow and a safety contract. Every other unsafe block in
// this crate is a lint error.
#![deny(unsafe_code)]

pub mod config;
pub mod dequant;
pub mod diag;
pub mod error;
pub mod file;
pub mod ggml;
pub mod metadata;

pub use config::{ModelConfig, TokenizerInfo};
pub use error::{GgufError, Result};
pub use file::{GgufFile, TensorInfo};
pub use ggml::GgmlType;
pub use metadata::{Metadata, MetadataValue};

===== END FILE: crates/gguf/src/lib.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/gguf/src/metadata.rs =====
//! GGUF metadata: the key-value section between the header and the tensor
//! directory. Values keep the exact type the file stored; the typed getters
//! on [`Metadata`] widen only where the conversion is lossless and report a
//! named mismatch everywhere else.

use crate::error::{GgufError, Result};

/// One metadata value, mirroring the GGUF value-type enum.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum MetadataValue {
    /// Type 0.
    UInt8(u8),
    /// Type 1.
    Int8(i8),
    /// Type 2.
    UInt16(u16),
    /// Type 3.
    Int16(i16),
    /// Type 4.
    UInt32(u32),
    /// Type 5.
    Int32(i32),
    /// Type 6.
    Float32(f32),
    /// Type 7.
    Bool(bool),
    /// Type 8.
    String(String),
    /// Type 9. GGUF arrays are homogeneous; elements share one value type.
    Array(Vec<MetadataValue>),
    /// Type 10.
    UInt64(u64),
    /// Type 11.
    Int64(i64),
    /// Type 12.
    Float64(f64),
}

impl MetadataValue {
    /// Short type name used in mismatch errors.
    pub fn type_name(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::UInt8(_) => "u8",
            Self::Int8(_) => "i8",
            Self::UInt16(_) => "u16",
            Self::Int16(_) => "i16",
            Self::UInt32(_) => "u32",
            Self::Int32(_) => "i32",
            Self::Float32(_) => "f32",
            Self::Bool(_) => "bool",
            Self::String(_) => "string",
            Self::Array(_) => "array",
            Self::UInt64(_) => "u64",
            Self::Int64(_) => "i64",
            Self::Float64(_) => "f64",
        }
    }

    /// The GGUF value-type id for this variant.
    pub fn type_id(&self) -> u32 {
        match self {
            Self::UInt8(_) => 0,
            Self::Int8(_) => 1,
            Self::UInt16(_) => 2,
            Self::Int16(_) => 3,
            Self::UInt32(_) => 4,
            Self::Int32(_) => 5,
            Self::Float32(_) => 6,
            Self::Bool(_) => 7,
            Self::String(_) => 8,
            Self::Array(_) => 9,
            Self::UInt64(_) => 10,
            Self::Int64(_) => 11,
            Self::Float64(_) => 12,
        }
    }

    /// Lossless view as u64, for the unsigned and small signed integers.
    fn as_u64(&self) -> Option<u64> {
        match self {
            Self::UInt8(v) => Some(u64::from(*v)),
            Self::UInt16(v) => Some(u64::from(*v)),
            Self::UInt32(v) => Some(u64::from(*v)),
            Self::UInt64(v) => Some(*v),
            Self::Int8(v) => u64::try_from(i64::from(*v)).ok(),
            Self::Int16(v) => u64::try_from(i64::from(*v)).ok(),
            Self::Int32(v) => u64::try_from(i64::from(*v)).ok(),
            Self::Int64(v) => u64::try_from(*v).ok(),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// Lossless view as i64.
    fn as_i64(&self) -> Option<i64> {
        match self {
            Self::UInt8(v) => Some(i64::from(*v)),
            Self::UInt16(v) => Some(i64::from(*v)),
            Self::UInt32(v) => Some(i64::from(*v)),
            Self::UInt64(v) => i64::try_from(*v).ok(),
            Self::Int8(v) => Some(i64::from(*v)),
            Self::Int16(v) => Some(i64::from(*v)),
            Self::Int32(v) => Some(i64::from(*v)),
            Self::Int64(v) => Some(*v),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// View as f64: exact for f32/f64, and for integers up to 2^53.
    fn as_f64(&self) -> Option<f64> {
        match self {
            Self::Float32(v) => Some(f64::from(*v)),
            Self::Float64(v) => Some(*v),
            _ => self
                .as_i64()
                .map(|v| v as f64)
                .or_else(|| self.as_u64().map(|v| v as f64)),
        }
    }
}

/// The full metadata section of one GGUF file, in file order.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct Metadata {
    entries: Vec<(String, MetadataValue)>,
}

impl Metadata {
    pub(crate) fn from_entries(entries: Vec<(String, MetadataValue)>) -> Self {
        Self { entries }
    }

    /// Number of key-value pairs.
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.entries.len()
    }

    /// Whether the section is empty.
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.entries.is_empty()
    }

    /// Iterate keys and values in file order.
    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&str, &MetadataValue)> {
        self.entries.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.as_str(), v))
    }

    /// Raw lookup; `None` when the key is absent.
    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&MetadataValue> {
        self.entries.iter().find(|(k, _)| k == key).map(|(_, v)| v)
    }

    /// Raw lookup that fails loudly when the key is absent.
    pub fn require(&self, key: &str) -> Result<&MetadataValue> {
        self.get(key)
            .ok_or_else(|| GgufError::MissingMetadata(key.to_string()).logged())
    }

    /// The typed getters' shared refusal: the key is absent, or it
    /// holds a different type than the getter reads. This helper is
    /// a construction seam of its own (every getter's mismatch
    /// leaves through it), so the emission lives here, once.
    fn mismatch(&self, key: &str, expected: &'static str) -> GgufError {
        let err = match self.get(key) {
            None => GgufError::MissingMetadata(key.to_string()),
            Some(v) => GgufError::MetadataTypeMismatch {
                key: key.to_string(),
                expected,
                found: v.type_name(),
            },
        };
        err.logged()
    }

    /// Integer read as u32. Accepts any integer type whose value fits.
    pub fn get_u32(&self, key: &str) -> Result<u32> {
        let v = self.get_u64(key)?;
        u32::try_from(v).map_err(|_| self.mismatch(key, "u32"))
    }

    /// Integer read as u64. Accepts any integer type whose value fits.
    pub fn get_u64(&self, key: &str) -> Result<u64> {
        match self.require(key)?.as_u64() {
            Some(v) => Ok(v),
            None => Err(self.mismatch(key, "u64")),
        }
    }

    /// Integer read as i64. Accepts any integer type whose value fits.
    pub fn get_i64(&self, key: &str) -> Result<i64> {
        match self.require(key)?.as_i64() {
            Some(v) => Ok(v),
            None => Err(self.mismatch(key, "i64")),
        }
    }

    /// Float read as f32. Accepts f32 and f64 storage.
    pub fn get_f32(&self, key: &str) -> Result<f32> {
        match self.require(key)? {
            MetadataValue::Float32(v) => Ok(*v),
            MetadataValue::Float64(v) => Ok(*v as f32),
            _ => Err(self.mismatch(key, "f32")),
        }
    }

    /// Float read as f64. Accepts f32 and f64 storage.
    pub fn get_f64(&self, key: &str) -> Result<f64> {
        match self.require(key)?.as_f64() {
            Some(v) => Ok(v),
            None => Err(self.mismatch(key, "f64")),
        }
    }

    /// Strict bool read.
    pub fn get_bool(&self, key: &str) -> Result<bool> {
        match self.require(key)? {
            MetadataValue::Bool(v) => Ok(*v),
            _ => Err(self.mismatch(key, "bool")),
        }
    }

    /// Strict string read.
    pub fn get_string(&self, key: &str) -> Result<&str> {
        match self.require(key)? {
            MetadataValue::String(v) => Ok(v.as_str()),
            _ => Err(self.mismatch(key, "string")),
        }
    }

    /// Optional string read: `Ok(None)` when absent, error when present
    /// with the wrong type.
    pub fn opt_string(&self, key: &str) -> Result<Option<&str>> {
        match self.get(key) {
            None => Ok(None),
            Some(MetadataValue::String(v)) => Ok(Some(v.as_str())),
            Some(_) => Err(self.mismatch(key, "string")),
        }
    }

    /// Optional u32 read: `Ok(None)` when absent.
    pub fn opt_u32(&self, key: &str) -> Result<Option<u32>> {
        match self.get(key) {
            None => Ok(None),
            Some(_) => self.get_u32(key).map(Some),
        }
    }

    /// Optional f32 read: `Ok(None)` when absent.
    pub fn opt_f32(&self, key: &str) -> Result<Option<f32>> {
        match self.get(key) {
            None => Ok(None),
            Some(_) => self.get_f32(key).map(Some),
        }
    }

    /// Optional array read: `Ok(None)` when absent, error when
    /// present with the wrong type. The array sibling of the
    /// `opt_*` scalar reads, for optional array probes (a draft
    /// model's sliding-window pattern, for example) whose absence
    /// is a legitimate answer and must not build the strict
    /// getter's missing-key refusal.
    pub fn opt_array(&self, key: &str) -> Result<Option<&Vec<MetadataValue>>> {
        match self.get(key) {
            None => Ok(None),
            Some(MetadataValue::Array(v)) => Ok(Some(v)),
            Some(_) => Err(self.mismatch(key, "array")),
        }
    }

    /// Array read: the raw element list.
    pub fn get_array(&self, key: &str) -> Result<&Vec<MetadataValue>> {
        match self.require(key)? {
            MetadataValue::Array(v) => Ok(v),
            _ => Err(self.mismatch(key, "array")),
        }
    }

    /// Array of strings read (tokenizer vocabularies, merges, and friends).
    pub fn get_string_array(&self, key: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
        let arr = self.get_array(key)?;
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(arr.len());
        for item in arr {
            match item {
                MetadataValue::String(s) => out.push(s.clone()),
                other => {
                    return Err(GgufError::MetadataTypeMismatch {
                        key: key.to_string(),
                        expected: "array of string",
                        found: other.type_name(),
                    }
                    .logged())
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(out)
    }

    /// Array of i32 read (token type ids and similar small tables).
    pub fn get_i32_array(&self, key: &str) -> Result<Vec<i32>> {
        let arr = self.get_array(key)?;
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(arr.len());
        for item in arr {
            match item.as_i64().and_then(|v| i32::try_from(v).ok()) {
                Some(v) => out.push(v),
                None => {
                    return Err(GgufError::MetadataTypeMismatch {
                        key: key.to_string(),
                        expected: "array of i32",
                        found: item.type_name(),
                    }
                    .logged())
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(out)
    }

    /// Array of u32 read (for example per-layer head counts in hybrid
    /// architectures).
    pub fn get_u32_array(&self, key: &str) -> Result<Vec<u32>> {
        let arr = self.get_array(key)?;
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(arr.len());
        for item in arr {
            match item.as_u64().and_then(|v| u32::try_from(v).ok()) {
                Some(v) => out.push(v),
                None => {
                    return Err(GgufError::MetadataTypeMismatch {
                        key: key.to_string(),
                        expected: "array of u32",
                        found: item.type_name(),
                    }
                    .logged())
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(out)
    }

    /// Array of f32 read (for example RoPE scaling factor tables).
    pub fn get_f32_array(&self, key: &str) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        let arr = self.get_array(key)?;
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(arr.len());
        for item in arr {
            match item {
                MetadataValue::Float32(v) => out.push(*v),
                MetadataValue::Float64(v) => out.push(*v as f32),
                other => {
                    return Err(GgufError::MetadataTypeMismatch {
                        key: key.to_string(),
                        expected: "array of f32",
                        found: other.type_name(),
                    }
                    .logged())
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(out)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::diag;

    #[test]
    fn type_mismatch_refusal_emits_its_diag_event() {
        // A previously silent path: the typed getters' mismatch
        // helper constructed MetadataTypeMismatch with no diag
        // call anywhere near it. The refusal must now be on the
        // diagnostic channel, proven against the captured events,
        // not against the source. The probe key is unique to this
        // test, so no parallel test's events can satisfy the
        // assertion.
        let md = Metadata::from_entries(vec![(
            "lane_g_probe.count".to_string(),
            MetadataValue::String("not a number".to_string()),
        )]);
        let err = md
            .get_u32("lane_g_probe.count")
            .expect_err("a string value is not a u32");
        assert!(
            matches!(err, GgufError::MetadataTypeMismatch { .. }),
            "error: {err}"
        );
        assert!(
            diag::captured_errors().iter().any(|l| {
                l.contains("event=metadata_type_mismatch") && l.contains("key=lane_g_probe.count")
            }),
            "the mismatch refusal must emit its diag event"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn missing_key_refusal_emits_its_diag_event() {
        let md = Metadata::from_entries(vec![]);
        let err = md
            .require("lane_g_probe.absent")
            .expect_err("an absent key refuses");
        assert!(matches!(err, GgufError::MissingMetadata(_)), "error: {err}");
        assert!(
            diag::captured_errors().iter().any(|l| {
                l.contains("event=missing_metadata") && l.contains("key=lane_g_probe.absent")
            }),
            "the missing-key refusal must emit its diag event"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn opt_getters_are_silent_when_the_key_is_absent() {
        // The optional reads exist for probes whose absence is a
        // legitimate answer (an arch's optional override key, for
        // example). They must answer Ok(None) without constructing
        // the MissingMetadata refusal, so no missing_metadata event
        // fires for the probe key. The key is unique to this test.
        let md = Metadata::from_entries(vec![]);
        assert_eq!(md.opt_f32("lane_opt_probe.absent").unwrap(), None);
        assert_eq!(md.opt_u32("lane_opt_probe.absent").unwrap(), None);
        assert_eq!(md.opt_string("lane_opt_probe.absent").unwrap(), None);
        assert_eq!(md.opt_array("lane_opt_probe.absent").unwrap(), None);
        assert!(
            !diag::captured_errors()
                .iter()
                .any(|l| l.contains("lane_opt_probe.absent")),
            "an absent optional key must not emit any diag error"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn opt_getter_still_refuses_a_wrong_type_loudly() {
        // Silence is for absence only: a present key holding the
        // wrong kind of value refuses through the same mismatch seam
        // as the strict getters, event included.
        let md = Metadata::from_entries(vec![(
            "lane_opt_probe.wrong_type".to_string(),
            MetadataValue::String("not a float".to_string()),
        )]);
        let err = md
            .opt_f32("lane_opt_probe.wrong_type")
            .expect_err("a string value is not an f32");
        assert!(
            matches!(err, GgufError::MetadataTypeMismatch { .. }),
            "error: {err}"
        );
        assert!(
            diag::captured_errors().iter().any(|l| {
                l.contains("event=metadata_type_mismatch")
                    && l.contains("key=lane_opt_probe.wrong_type")
            }),
            "the wrong-type refusal must emit its diag event"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn opt_array_round_trips_a_present_array() {
        // The present-and-correct case: the elements come back
        // untouched, in file order.
        let md = Metadata::from_entries(vec![(
            "lane_opt_probe.pattern".to_string(),
            MetadataValue::Array(vec![
                MetadataValue::Bool(true),
                MetadataValue::Bool(false),
                MetadataValue::Bool(true),
            ]),
        )]);
        let items = md
            .opt_array("lane_opt_probe.pattern")
            .unwrap()
            .expect("a present array reads as Some");
        assert_eq!(items.len(), 3);
        assert!(matches!(items[0], MetadataValue::Bool(true)));
        assert!(matches!(items[1], MetadataValue::Bool(false)));
        assert!(matches!(items[2], MetadataValue::Bool(true)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn opt_array_still_refuses_a_wrong_type_loudly() {
        // The array sibling of the scalar rule above: silence is
        // for absence only. A present key holding a non-array
        // value refuses through the mismatch seam, event
        // included. The probe key is unique to this test.
        let md = Metadata::from_entries(vec![(
            "lane_opt_probe.wrong_type_array".to_string(),
            MetadataValue::String("not an array".to_string()),
        )]);
        let err = md
            .opt_array("lane_opt_probe.wrong_type_array")
            .expect_err("a string value is not an array");
        assert!(
            matches!(err, GgufError::MetadataTypeMismatch { .. }),
            "error: {err}"
        );
        assert!(
            diag::captured_errors().iter().any(|l| {
                l.contains("event=metadata_type_mismatch")
                    && l.contains("key=lane_opt_probe.wrong_type_array")
            }),
            "the wrong-type refusal must emit its diag event"
        );
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/gguf/tests/open.rs =====
//! `GgufFile::open` (memory-mapped, PLAN T-2.1) must be
//! indistinguishable from `GgufFile::from_bytes` (owned buffer) on
//! every observable: parsed metadata, tensor directory, raw tensor
//! bytes, dequantized values, and the named error for every failure
//! the in-memory path names. The tiny GGUF writer is adapted from
//! `tests/synthetic.rs`.

use std::path::PathBuf;

use gguf::{GgufError, GgufFile, MetadataValue};

// ---------- tiny GGUF writer (adapted from tests/synthetic.rs) ----------

struct TestTensor {
    name: String,
    dims: Vec<u64>,
    type_id: u32,
    data: Vec<u8>,
}

fn tensor(name: &str, dims: &[u64], type_id: u32, data: Vec<u8>) -> TestTensor {
    TestTensor {
        name: name.to_string(),
        dims: dims.to_vec(),
        type_id,
        data,
    }
}

fn write_string(out: &mut Vec<u8>, s: &str) {
    out.extend_from_slice(&(s.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(s.as_bytes());
}

fn write_scalar(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: &MetadataValue) {
    match v {
        MetadataValue::UInt32(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::String(s) => write_string(out, s),
        _ => panic!("this writer only carries the value kinds these tests use"),
    }
}

fn write_value(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: &MetadataValue) {
    out.extend_from_slice(&v.type_id().to_le_bytes());
    write_scalar(out, v);
}

fn align_up(v: u64, a: u64) -> u64 {
    v.div_ceil(a) * a
}

fn build(metadata: &[(&str, MetadataValue)], tensors: &[TestTensor], alignment: u64) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    out.extend_from_slice(b"GGUF");
    out.extend_from_slice(&3u32.to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&(tensors.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&(metadata.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
    for (k, v) in metadata {
        write_string(&mut out, k);
        write_value(&mut out, v);
    }
    let mut offsets = Vec::new();
    let mut cursor = 0u64;
    for t in tensors {
        let aligned = align_up(cursor, alignment);
        offsets.push(aligned);
        cursor = aligned + t.data.len() as u64;
    }
    for (t, off) in tensors.iter().zip(&offsets) {
        write_string(&mut out, &t.name);
        out.extend_from_slice(&(t.dims.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
        for d in &t.dims {
            out.extend_from_slice(&d.to_le_bytes());
        }
        out.extend_from_slice(&t.type_id.to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&off.to_le_bytes());
    }
    let data_start = align_up(out.len() as u64, alignment);
    out.resize(data_start as usize, 0);
    for (t, off) in tensors.iter().zip(&offsets) {
        out.resize((data_start + off) as usize, 0);
        out.extend_from_slice(&t.data);
    }
    out
}

// ---------- temp file handling ----------

/// A temp file that removes itself on drop, so a failing assert does
/// not litter the temp directory.
struct TempFile(PathBuf);

impl TempFile {
    fn write(name: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> Self {
        let path =
            std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("gguf-open-test-{}-{name}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::write(&path, bytes).unwrap();
        Self(path)
    }
}

impl Drop for TempFile {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&self.0);
    }
}

// ---------- the fixture ----------

fn fixture_bytes() -> Vec<u8> {
    let f32_data: Vec<u8> = [1.0f32, -2.5, 3.25, 0.0]
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes())
        .collect();
    // F16: 1.0 (0x3c00) and 0.5 (0x3800).
    let f16_data: Vec<u8> = [0x3c00u16, 0x3800]
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes())
        .collect();
    build(
        &[
            (
                "general.architecture",
                MetadataValue::String("testarch".into()),
            ),
            ("test.count", MetadataValue::UInt32(42)),
        ],
        &[
            tensor("a.weight", &[4], 0, f32_data),
            tensor("b.weight", &[2], 1, f16_data),
        ],
        32,
    )
}

// ---------- parity ----------

#[test]
fn open_matches_from_bytes_on_every_observable() {
    let bytes = fixture_bytes();
    let tmp = TempFile::write("parity.gguf", &bytes);

    let mapped = GgufFile::open(&tmp.0).unwrap();
    let owned = GgufFile::from_bytes(bytes).unwrap();

    assert_eq!(mapped.version(), owned.version());
    assert_eq!(mapped.file_len(), owned.file_len());
    assert_eq!(mapped.data_start(), owned.data_start());
    assert_eq!(mapped.alignment(), owned.alignment());
    assert_eq!(mapped.architecture().unwrap(), "testarch");
    assert_eq!(mapped.metadata().get_u32("test.count").unwrap(), 42);
    assert_eq!(
        mapped.tensor_names().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        owned.tensor_names().collect::<Vec<_>>()
    );
    for name in owned.tensor_names() {
        assert_eq!(
            mapped.tensor_bytes(name).unwrap(),
            owned.tensor_bytes(name).unwrap(),
            "raw bytes differ for {name}"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mapped.load_f32(name).unwrap(),
            owned.load_f32(name).unwrap(),
            "dequantized values differ for {name}"
        );
    }
    assert_eq!(
        mapped.load_f32("a.weight").unwrap(),
        vec![1.0, -2.5, 3.25, 0.0]
    );
    assert_eq!(mapped.load_f32("b.weight").unwrap(), vec![1.0, 0.5]);
    let err = mapped.tensor_bytes("nope.weight").unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(err, GgufError::MissingTensor(_)));
}

// ---------- named failures, identical on both paths ----------

#[test]
fn open_missing_file_is_io_not_found() {
    let path = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
        "gguf-open-test-{}-does-not-exist.gguf",
        std::process::id()
    ));
    let err = GgufFile::open(&path).unwrap_err();
    match err {
        GgufError::Io(e) => assert_eq!(e.kind(), std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound),
        other => panic!("expected Io(NotFound), got {other:?}"),
    }
}

#[test]
fn open_empty_file_fails_like_from_bytes() {
    let tmp = TempFile::write("empty.gguf", &[]);
    let open_err = GgufFile::open(&tmp.0).unwrap_err();
    let bytes_err = GgufFile::from_bytes(Vec::new()).unwrap_err();
    // The in-memory path names this Truncated("magic"); a zero-length
    // file cannot be mapped, and open must not let that turn into a
    // different (Io) failure.
    assert!(matches!(
        open_err,
        GgufError::Truncated {
            context: "magic",
            ..
        }
    ));
    assert_eq!(open_err.to_string(), bytes_err.to_string());
}

#[test]
fn open_bad_magic_fails_like_from_bytes() {
    let mut bytes = fixture_bytes();
    bytes[0] = b'X';
    let tmp = TempFile::write("bad-magic.gguf", &bytes);
    let open_err = GgufFile::open(&tmp.0).unwrap_err();
    let bytes_err = GgufFile::from_bytes(bytes).unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(open_err, GgufError::BadMagic { .. }));
    assert_eq!(open_err.to_string(), bytes_err.to_string());
}

#[test]
fn open_truncated_file_fails_like_from_bytes() {
    let full = fixture_bytes();
    // Two cut points: inside the header (directory incomplete) and
    // inside the tensor data (directory fine, data out of bounds).
    for cut in [full.len() / 3, full.len() - 2] {
        let truncated = &full[..cut];
        let tmp = TempFile::write(&format!("truncated-{cut}.gguf"), truncated);
        let open_err = GgufFile::open(&tmp.0).unwrap_err();
        let bytes_err = GgufFile::from_bytes(truncated.to_vec()).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            open_err.to_string(),
            bytes_err.to_string(),
            "error differs at cut {cut}"
        );
    }
}
