===== FILE: crates/gguf/tests/synthetic.rs =====
//! End-to-end tests over synthetic GGUF files built by a tiny writer in
//! this module. Dequantization expectations are hand-computed from the
//! ggml block layouts, not produced by the code under test.

use gguf::{GgufError, GgufFile, MetadataValue};

// ---------- tiny GGUF writer ----------

struct TestTensor {
    name: String,
    dims: Vec<u64>,
    type_id: u32,
    data: Vec<u8>,
}

fn tensor(name: &str, dims: &[u64], type_id: u32, data: Vec<u8>) -> TestTensor {
    TestTensor {
        name: name.to_string(),
        dims: dims.to_vec(),
        type_id,
        data,
    }
}

fn write_string(out: &mut Vec<u8>, s: &str) {
    out.extend_from_slice(&(s.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(s.as_bytes());
}

fn write_scalar(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: &MetadataValue) {
    match v {
        MetadataValue::UInt8(x) => out.push(*x),
        MetadataValue::Int8(x) => out.push(*x as u8),
        MetadataValue::UInt16(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Int16(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::UInt32(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Int32(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Float32(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Bool(x) => out.push(u8::from(*x)),
        MetadataValue::String(s) => write_string(out, s),
        MetadataValue::UInt64(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Int64(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Float64(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Array(_) => panic!("nested arrays are not valid GGUF"),
    }
}

fn write_value(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: &MetadataValue) {
    out.extend_from_slice(&v.type_id().to_le_bytes());
    match v {
        MetadataValue::Array(items) => {
            let elem_type = items.first().map_or(8, MetadataValue::type_id);
            out.extend_from_slice(&elem_type.to_le_bytes());
            out.extend_from_slice(&(items.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
            for item in items {
                write_scalar(out, item);
            }
        }
        _ => write_scalar(out, v),
    }
}

fn align_up(v: u64, a: u64) -> u64 {
    v.div_ceil(a) * a
}

/// Build a complete GGUF v3 file. Tensor data offsets are aligned the way
/// real writers align them.
fn build(metadata: &[(&str, MetadataValue)], tensors: &[TestTensor], alignment: u64) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    out.extend_from_slice(b"GGUF");
    out.extend_from_slice(&3u32.to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&(tensors.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&(metadata.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
    for (k, v) in metadata {
        write_string(&mut out, k);
        write_value(&mut out, v);
    }
    let mut offsets = Vec::new();
    let mut cursor = 0u64;
    for t in tensors {
        let aligned = align_up(cursor, alignment);
        offsets.push(aligned);
        cursor = aligned + t.data.len() as u64;
    }
    for (t, off) in tensors.iter().zip(&offsets) {
        write_string(&mut out, &t.name);
        out.extend_from_slice(&(t.dims.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
        for d in &t.dims {
            out.extend_from_slice(&d.to_le_bytes());
        }
        out.extend_from_slice(&t.type_id.to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&off.to_le_bytes());
    }
    let data_start = align_up(out.len() as u64, alignment);
    out.resize(data_start as usize, 0);
    for (t, off) in tensors.iter().zip(&offsets) {
        out.resize((data_start + off) as usize, 0);
        out.extend_from_slice(&t.data);
    }
    out
}

fn f16le(bits: u16) -> [u8; 2] {
    bits.to_le_bytes()
}

const F16_ONE: u16 = 0x3c00;
const F16_TWO: u16 = 0x4000;
const F16_HALF: u16 = 0x3800;

// ---------- header and metadata ----------

#[test]
fn header_and_metadata_parse() {
    let bytes = build(
        &[
            (
                "general.architecture",
                MetadataValue::String("testarch".into()),
            ),
            ("general.name", MetadataValue::String("Tiny Test".into())),
            ("test.count", MetadataValue::UInt32(42)),
            ("test.delta", MetadataValue::Int32(-7)),
            ("test.ratio", MetadataValue::Float32(0.25)),
            ("test.flag", MetadataValue::Bool(true)),
            (
                "test.tags",
                MetadataValue::Array(vec![
                    MetadataValue::String("a".into()),
                    MetadataValue::String("bc".into()),
                ]),
            ),
        ],
        &[],
        32,
    );
    let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(bytes).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(file.version(), 3);
    assert_eq!(file.architecture().unwrap(), "testarch");
    let md = file.metadata();
    assert_eq!(md.get_string("general.name").unwrap(), "Tiny Test");
    assert_eq!(md.get_u32("test.count").unwrap(), 42);
    assert_eq!(md.get_i64("test.delta").unwrap(), -7);
    assert_eq!(md.get_f32("test.ratio").unwrap(), 0.25);
    assert!(md.get_bool("test.flag").unwrap());
    assert_eq!(
        md.get_string_array("test.tags").unwrap(),
        vec!["a".to_string(), "bc".to_string()]
    );
}

#[test]
fn missing_and_mistyped_metadata_are_named_errors() {
    let bytes = build(
        &[("general.architecture", MetadataValue::String("x".into()))],
        &[],
        32,
    );
    let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(bytes).unwrap();
    let err = file.metadata().get_u32("nope.key").unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(err, GgufError::MissingMetadata(k) if k == "nope.key"));
    let err = file.metadata().get_u32("general.architecture").unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(err, GgufError::MetadataTypeMismatch { .. }));
}

#[test]
fn bad_magic_and_wrong_version_are_rejected() {
    let mut bad = build(&[], &[], 32);
    bad[0] = b'X';
    assert!(matches!(
        GgufFile::from_bytes(bad),
        Err(GgufError::BadMagic { .. })
    ));
    let mut v2 = build(&[], &[], 32);
    v2[4..8].copy_from_slice(&2u32.to_le_bytes());
    assert!(matches!(
        GgufFile::from_bytes(v2),
        Err(GgufError::UnsupportedVersion(2))
    ));
}

#[test]
fn truncated_file_fails() {
    let bytes = build(
        &[("general.architecture", MetadataValue::String("x".into()))],
        &[tensor("w", &[4], 0, vec![0u8; 16])],
        32,
    );
    let cut = bytes[..bytes.len() / 2].to_vec();
    assert!(GgufFile::from_bytes(cut).is_err());
}

#[test]
fn tensor_data_past_eof_is_rejected_at_parse() {
    let mut bytes = build(&[], &[tensor("w", &[4], 0, vec![0u8; 16])], 32);
    bytes.truncate(bytes.len() - 10);
    let err = GgufFile::from_bytes(bytes).unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(err, GgufError::TensorOutOfBounds { .. }));
}

// ---------- model config ----------

fn config_metadata(with_kv: bool) -> Vec<(String, MetadataValue)> {
    let mut v: Vec<(String, MetadataValue)> = vec![
        (
            "general.architecture".into(),
            MetadataValue::String("testarch".into()),
        ),
        ("testarch.block_count".into(), MetadataValue::UInt32(4)),
        (
            "testarch.embedding_length".into(),
            MetadataValue::UInt32(128),
        ),
        (
            "testarch.feed_forward_length".into(),
            MetadataValue::UInt32(256),
        ),
        (
            "testarch.attention.head_count".into(),
            MetadataValue::UInt32(8),
        ),
        (
            "testarch.context_length".into(),
            MetadataValue::UInt32(2048),
        ),
        (
            "testarch.rope.freq_base".into(),
            MetadataValue::Float32(500_000.0),
        ),
        (
            "tokenizer.ggml.tokens".into(),
            MetadataValue::Array(vec![
                MetadataValue::String("<unk>".into()),
                MetadataValue::String("a".into()),
                MetadataValue::String("b".into()),
            ]),
        ),
        (
            "tokenizer.ggml.bos_token_id".into(),
            MetadataValue::UInt32(0),
        ),
        (
            "tokenizer.ggml.eos_token_id".into(),
            MetadataValue::UInt32(1),
        ),
    ];
    if with_kv {
        v.push((
            "testarch.attention.head_count_kv".into(),
            MetadataValue::UInt32(2),
        ));
    }
    v
}

#[test]
fn model_config_reads_the_files_own_keys() {
    let owned = config_metadata(true);
    let refs: Vec<(&str, MetadataValue)> =
        owned.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.as_str(), v.clone())).collect();
    let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&refs, &[], 32)).unwrap();
    let cfg = file.model_config().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(cfg.architecture, "testarch");
    assert_eq!(cfg.layer_count, 4);
    assert_eq!(cfg.hidden_size, 128);
    assert_eq!(cfg.ffn_size, Some(256));
    assert_eq!(cfg.head_count, 8);
    assert_eq!(cfg.head_count_kv, 2);
    assert_eq!(cfg.context_length, 2048);
    assert_eq!(cfg.rope_base, Some(500_000.0));
    assert_eq!(cfg.vocab_size, Some(3));
    let tok = file.tokenizer().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(tok.tokens.len(), 3);
    assert_eq!(tok.bos_token_id, Some(0));
    assert_eq!(tok.eos_token_id, Some(1));
}

#[test]
fn kv_head_count_falls_back_to_query_heads() {
    let owned = config_metadata(false);
    let refs: Vec<(&str, MetadataValue)> =
        owned.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.as_str(), v.clone())).collect();
    let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&refs, &[], 32)).unwrap();
    let cfg = file.model_config().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(cfg.head_count_kv, cfg.head_count);
}

#[test]
fn per_layer_kv_head_counts_from_hybrid_files() {
    // Real shape from a granitehybrid GGUF: head_count_kv is an array with
    // the KV count on attention layers and 0 on SSM layers.
    let mut owned = config_metadata(false);
    owned.push((
        "testarch.attention.head_count_kv".into(),
        MetadataValue::Array(vec![
            MetadataValue::Int32(0),
            MetadataValue::Int32(0),
            MetadataValue::Int32(4),
            MetadataValue::Int32(0),
        ]),
    ));
    let refs: Vec<(&str, MetadataValue)> =
        owned.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.as_str(), v.clone())).collect();
    let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&refs, &[], 32)).unwrap();
    let cfg = file.model_config().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(cfg.head_count_kv, 4);
    assert_eq!(cfg.head_count_kv_per_layer, Some(vec![0, 0, 4, 0]));
    assert_eq!(cfg.head_count_per_layer, None);
}

#[test]
fn alignment_comes_from_metadata() {
    let bytes = build(
        &[
            ("general.architecture", MetadataValue::String("x".into())),
            ("general.alignment", MetadataValue::UInt32(64)),
        ],
        &[tensor("w", &[2], 0, vec![0u8; 8])],
        64,
    );
    let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(bytes).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(file.alignment(), 64);
    assert_eq!(file.data_start() % 64, 0);
    assert_eq!(file.load_f32("w").unwrap().len(), 2);
}

// ---------- dequantization, hand-computed ----------

#[test]
fn dequant_f32_f16_bf16() {
    let f32_data: Vec<u8> = [1.5f32, -0.25]
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes())
        .collect();
    let f16_data: Vec<u8> = [F16_ONE, 0xbc00, F16_HALF]
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|b| f16le(*b))
        .collect();
    // BF16: 1.0 = 0x3f80, -2.5 = 0xc020.
    let bf16_data: Vec<u8> = [0x3f80u16, 0xc020]
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|b| b.to_le_bytes())
        .collect();
    let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(build(
        &[],
        &[
            tensor("f32w", &[2], 0, f32_data),
            tensor("f16w", &[3], 1, f16_data),
            tensor("bf16w", &[2], 30, bf16_data),
        ],
        32,
    ))
    .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(file.load_f32("f32w").unwrap(), vec![1.5, -0.25]);
    assert_eq!(file.load_f32("f16w").unwrap(), vec![1.0, -1.0, 0.5]);
    assert_eq!(file.load_f32("bf16w").unwrap(), vec![1.0, -2.5]);
}

#[test]
fn bf16_id_30_is_not_i2_s() {
    // Regression for the old loader's fatal collision: mainline id 30 is
    // BF16. If this ever decodes as anything else, the test goes red.
    let data: Vec<u8> = [0x3f80u16].iter().flat_map(|b| b.to_le_bytes()).collect();
    let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&[], &[tensor("w", &[1], 30, data)], 32)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(file.tensor_info("w").unwrap().type_name(), "BF16");
    assert_eq!(file.load_f32("w").unwrap(), vec![1.0]);
}

#[test]
fn dequant_q8_0() {
    let mut data = Vec::new();
    data.extend_from_slice(&f16le(F16_HALF)); // d = 0.5
    let mut qs = [0i8; 32];
    qs[0] = 2;
    qs[1] = -4;
    qs[31] = 100;
    data.extend(qs.iter().map(|q| *q as u8));
    let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&[], &[tensor("w", &[32], 8, data)], 32)).unwrap();
    let out = file.load_f32("w").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(out[0], 1.0);
    assert_eq!(out[1], -2.0);
    assert_eq!(out[31], 50.0);
    assert!(out[2..31].iter().all(|v| *v == 0.0));
}

#[test]
fn dequant_q4_k() {
    // Hand-computed: d = 2.0, dmin = 0.5.
    // Sub-block 0: scale 3, min 2 -> factor 6.0, offset 1.0.
    // Sub-block 1: scale 1, min 0 -> factor 2.0, offset 0.0.
    let mut block = Vec::new();
    block.extend_from_slice(&f16le(F16_TWO));
    block.extend_from_slice(&f16le(F16_HALF));
    let mut scales = [0u8; 12];
    scales[0] = 3;
    scales[4] = 2;
    scales[1] = 1;
    scales[5] = 0;
    block.extend_from_slice(&scales);
    let mut qs = [0u8; 128];
    qs[0] = 0x21;
    qs[1] = 0x43;
    block.extend_from_slice(&qs);
    assert_eq!(block.len(), 144);
    let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&[], &[tensor("w", &[256], 12, block)], 32)).unwrap();
    let out = file.load_f32("w").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(out[0], 5.0); // 6*1 - 1
    assert_eq!(out[1], 17.0); // 6*3 - 1
    assert_eq!(out[2], -1.0); // 6*0 - 1
    assert_eq!(out[32], 4.0); // 2*2 - 0 (high nibble of qs[0])
    assert_eq!(out[33], 8.0); // 2*4 - 0 (high nibble of qs[1])
    assert_eq!(out[64], 0.0); // sub-block 2 has zero scale and min
}

#[test]
fn dequant_q5_k() {
    // Hand-computed: d = 1.0, dmin = 0. Sub-block 0 scale 2, sub-block 1
    // scale 1. ql[0] = 0x53, qh[0] = 0x01 sets element 0's fifth bit.
    let mut block = Vec::new();
    block.extend_from_slice(&f16le(F16_ONE));
    block.extend_from_slice(&f16le(0));
    let mut scales = [0u8; 12];
    scales[0] = 2;
    scales[1] = 1;
    block.extend_from_slice(&scales);
    let mut qh = [0u8; 32];
    qh[0] = 0x01;
    block.extend_from_slice(&qh);
    let mut ql = [0u8; 128];
    ql[0] = 0x53;
    block.extend_from_slice(&ql);
    assert_eq!(block.len(), 176);
    let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&[], &[tensor("w", &[256], 13, block)], 32)).unwrap();
    let out = file.load_f32("w").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(out[0], 38.0); // 2 * (3 + 16)
    assert_eq!(out[32], 5.0); // 1 * 5 (high nibble, no fifth bit)
    assert_eq!(out[1], 0.0);
}

#[test]
fn dequant_q6_k() {
    // Hand-computed: d = 1.0. Scales: sc[0]=2, sc[2]=1, sc[4]=3, sc[6]=1.
    // ql[0] = 0x23, ql[32] = 0x05, qh[0] = 0x41 (bit 0 for stream 1,
    // bit 6 for stream 4).
    let mut block = vec![0u8; 210];
    block[0] = 0x23; // ql[0]
    block[32] = 0x05; // ql[32]
    block[128] = 0x41; // qh[0]
    block[192] = 2; // sc[0]
    block[194] = 1; // sc[2]
    block[196] = 3; // sc[4]
    block[198] = 1; // sc[6]
    block[208..210].copy_from_slice(&f16le(F16_ONE));
    let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&[], &[tensor("w", &[256], 14, block)], 32)).unwrap();
    let out = file.load_f32("w").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(out[0], -26.0); // sc0 * ((3 | 1<<4) - 32) = 2 * -13
    assert_eq!(out[32], -27.0); // sc2 * (5 - 32)
    assert_eq!(out[64], -90.0); // sc4 * (2 - 32) = 3 * -30
    assert_eq!(out[96], -16.0); // sc6 * ((0 | 1<<4) - 32) = 1 * -16
}

#[test]
fn two_dim_tensor_directory_and_load() {
    let data: Vec<u8> = (0..8).flat_map(|i| (i as f32).to_le_bytes()).collect();
    let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&[], &[tensor("w", &[4, 2], 0, data)], 32)).unwrap();
    let info = file.tensor_info("w").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(info.dims(), &[4, 2]);
    assert_eq!(info.element_count(), 8);
    let out = file.load_f32("w").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(out, (0..8).map(|i| i as f32).collect::<Vec<_>>());
}

// ---------- fail-loud behavior ----------

#[test]
fn missing_tensor_is_a_hard_error() {
    let file =
        GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&[], &[tensor("a.weight", &[1], 0, vec![0; 4])], 32)).unwrap();
    let err = file.load_f32("b.weight").unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(&err, GgufError::MissingTensor(n) if n == "b.weight"));
    assert!(err.to_string().contains("b.weight"));
}

#[test]
fn unsupported_types_are_hard_errors_that_name_the_type() {
    // Q4_0 (2) and Q8_1 (9): real ggml types this loader does not
    // dequantize. They must fail loudly here, never decode as something
    // else. (Q3_K stood in this list until 2026-11-05, when it gained a
    // cross-checked reader; see q2_k_and_q3_k_tensors_load below.)
    for (type_id, name) in [(2u32, "Q4_0"), (9, "Q8_1")] {
        let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(build(
            &[],
            &[tensor("w", &[256], type_id, vec![0u8; 64])],
            32,
        ))
        .unwrap();
        let err = file.load_f32("w").unwrap_err();
        match err {
            GgufError::UnsupportedTensorType {
                ref tensor,
                type_id: id,
                ref type_name,
            } => {
                assert_eq!(tensor, "w");
                assert_eq!(id, type_id);
                assert_eq!(type_name, name);
            }
            other => panic!("expected UnsupportedTensorType, got {other:?}"),
        }
        assert!(err.to_string().contains(name));
    }
    // An id mainline ggml has not assigned is named by number.
    let file =
        GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&[], &[tensor("w", &[8], 99, vec![0u8; 32])], 32)).unwrap();
    let err = file.load_f32("w").unwrap_err();
    assert!(err.to_string().contains("99"));
}

#[test]
fn q2_k_and_q3_k_tensors_load() {
    // Q2_K (10): one 256-element block, 84 bytes. Scale bytes 0x01
    // (scale 1, min 0), d = 1.0 at bytes 80..82, qs[0] = 3, so the first
    // value is 3.0 and the rest of the block is 0.0.
    let mut q2 = vec![0u8; 84];
    q2[0..16].fill(0x01);
    q2[16] = 3;
    q2[80] = 0x00;
    q2[81] = 0x3C;
    let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&[], &[tensor("w", &[256], 10, q2)], 32)).unwrap();
    let out = file.load_f32("w").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(out.len(), 256);
    assert_eq!(out[0], 3.0);
    assert!(out[1..].iter().all(|&v| v == 0.0));

    // Q3_K (11): one 256-element block, 110 zero bytes. d = 0 forces
    // every output to 0.0 regardless of quants and scales.
    let file =
        GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&[], &[tensor("w", &[256], 11, vec![0u8; 110])], 32)).unwrap();
    let out = file.load_f32("w").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(out.len(), 256);
    assert!(out.iter().all(|&v| v == 0.0));
}

#[test]
fn bad_element_count_is_rejected_at_parse() {
    // 100 elements is not a whole number of 256-element Q4_K blocks.
    let err = GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&[], &[tensor("w", &[100], 12, vec![0u8; 144])], 32))
        .unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(err, GgufError::BadElementCount { .. }));
}

===== FILE: crates/itak-engine/src/diag.rs =====
//! The engine's diagnostic channel.
//!
//! David's rule: debugging is built into every module from birth,
//! not bolted on after a failure. Until this module landed, the
//! engine's channel was the free-standing `log_line` helper in
//! main.rs; this module is that channel with the shape the sibling
//! crates use, so engine logs read the same across the workspace:
//!
//! - An emit function ([`emit`] for lifecycle and job events,
//!   [`error`] for refusals and failures) taking a named event and
//!   a detail string.
//! - A sink seam ([`Diag`], mirroring the arch crates' trait of the
//!   same name): the process sink is stderr by default
//!   ([`StderrDiag`]), and tests can install a capturing sink
//!   through [`set_sink`] to prove a refusal emitted its event.
//! - Named event kinds, catalogued here. Lifecycle and job events:
//!   `model_load_begin`, `model_loaded`, `stale_socket_removed`,
//!   `serving`, `concurrency`, `hello`, `generate_start`,
//!   `generate_prompt_ids`, `generate_done`, `generate_failed`,
//!   `generate_aborted`. Refusals and failures emit through
//!   [`error`] under their protocol code (`peer_refused`,
//!   `protocol_mismatch`, `bad_frame`, `bad_request`,
//!   `model_not_found`, `engine_busy`, `engine_died`,
//!   `context_overflow`, `no_chat_template`, `unknown_op`) or, for
//!   failures with no wire code, `model_load_failed`,
//!   `socket_bind_failed`, `accept_failed`, `connection_failed`,
//!   `connection_read_failed`.
//!
//! Both levels are unconditional. The engine's stderr is its
//! operator log (the platform supervisor forwards it), and a
//! refusal hidden behind a debug flag is exactly the failure mode
//! the audit law exists to prevent; this process has no
//! debug-level chatter to gate. The one content gate the engine
//! keeps, the operator's `--log-content` for full prompt ids and
//! completion text, stays at its call sites and is orthogonal to
//! this channel.
//!
//! The stderr sink prints the detail with the engine's historical
//! `[itak-engine {secs}]` prefix, byte for byte the lines the
//! engine has always logged, so existing log readers see one
//! shape. The event name rides the channel for sinks that record
//! structure: the capturing test sink today, a structured sink
//! whenever the platform grows one.

use std::sync::{Arc, OnceLock, RwLock};
use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

/// A sink for the engine's diagnostic events: a named event plus a
/// detail string. Implementations must be cheap to call, because
/// any thread in the process may emit at any time.
pub trait Diag: Send + Sync {
    /// Record one event.
    fn event(&self, event: &str, detail: &str);
}

/// The default sink: one timestamped line per event on stderr, in
/// the format the engine has always logged.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct StderrDiag;

impl Diag for StderrDiag {
    fn event(&self, _event: &str, detail: &str) {
        let secs = SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
            .map(|d| d.as_secs())
            .unwrap_or(0);
        eprintln!("[itak-engine {secs}] {detail}");
    }
}

static SINK: OnceLock<RwLock<Arc<dyn Diag>>> = OnceLock::new();

fn sink_slot() -> &'static RwLock<Arc<dyn Diag>> {
    SINK.get_or_init(|| RwLock::new(Arc::new(StderrDiag)))
}

fn current_sink() -> Arc<dyn Diag> {
    let slot = sink_slot().read().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
    Arc::clone(&slot)
}

/// Install a different process sink. The seam exists for tests,
/// which install a capturing sink to prove a refusal emitted its
/// named event; production runs on the stderr default.
#[cfg(test)]
pub fn set_sink(sink: Arc<dyn Diag>) {
    *sink_slot().write().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner()) = sink;
}

/// Serializes tests that swap the process sink. The sink is
/// process-global, so two swapping tests running in parallel would
/// capture (and restore over) each other's events; a test that
/// installs a sink holds this lock for its whole install, drive,
/// read, restore sequence.
#[cfg(test)]
pub static SINK_TEST_LOCK: std::sync::Mutex<()> = std::sync::Mutex::new(());

/// Emit a lifecycle or job event through the diagnostic channel.
pub fn emit(event: &str, detail: &str) {
    current_sink().event(event, detail);
}

/// Emit a refusal or failure through the diagnostic channel, under
/// its protocol code where the wire has one. Unconditional, like
/// every error path in this workspace: a refusal that only shows
/// under a debug flag is a silent refusal.
pub fn error(event: &str, detail: &str) {
    current_sink().event(event, detail);
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::sync::Mutex;

    #[test]
    fn stderr_sink_event_does_not_panic() {
        StderrDiag.event("test_event", "detail=present");
    }

    #[test]
    fn emit_routes_to_the_installed_sink() {
        // A capturing sink defined here, the same way the engine's
        // connection tests capture: install, emit, read back.
        #[derive(Default)]
        struct Capture {
            events: Mutex<Vec<(String, String)>>,
        }
        impl Diag for Capture {
            fn event(&self, event: &str, detail: &str) {
                self.events
                    .lock()
                    .expect("capture lock")
                    .push((event.to_string(), detail.to_string()));
            }
        }
        let _guard = SINK_TEST_LOCK.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        let capture = Arc::new(Capture::default());
        set_sink(capture.clone());
        emit("lifecycle_probe", "detail=one");
        error("refusal_probe", "detail=two");
        set_sink(Arc::new(StderrDiag));
        let events = capture.events.lock().expect("capture lock");
        assert!(events
            .iter()
            .any(|(e, d)| e == "lifecycle_probe" && d == "detail=one"));
        assert!(events
            .iter()
            .any(|(e, d)| e == "refusal_probe" && d == "detail=two"));
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/itak-engine/src/engine.rs =====
//! The engine workers: one loaded model, a configured number of
//! serving slots (TODO T-9.14).
//!
//! Each slot is a worker thread because the CPU compute backend
//! serves exactly one sequence (its KV state is per-sequence and
//! not Sync). Connection threads hand jobs over a bounded mpsc
//! channel and forward the streamed events; jobs beyond the slots
//! queue in the channel up to its configured capacity, and a
//! submission past capacity is refused by name (`engine_busy`)
//! instead of queueing without limit. Each job builds a fresh
//! [`GlimmerModel`] from the shared, already-loaded weights (a clone
//! of Arc-backed tensor views, so it is cheap) with a fresh
//! [`CpuCompute`] and a fresh [`PositionCache`], which is the
//! per-sequence isolation the backend contract requires: slots
//! share the weights and nothing mutable.
//!
//! Every failure inside a job is a named [`GenEvent::Error`], never
//! a fabricated token: a bad prompt, a context overflow, and a
//! forward refusal are distinct codes the platform maps to distinct
//! HTTP answers. A panic inside a job is contained by the worker
//! loop (`catch_unwind` in [`run_worker`]): the job completes on
//! its channel with the `engine_died` code and the slot keeps
//! serving, instead of the dead worker stranding the caller on a
//! channel that never completes.

use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::mpsc::{Receiver, Sender};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::Instant;

use cpu_compute::CpuCompute;
use muse_glimmer::{Compute, GlimmerConfig, GlimmerModel, PositionCache, StderrDiag, Weights};
use tokenizer::{TokenType, Tokenizer, TokenizerData};

use crate::sampler::{Sampler, SamplerConfig};
use crate::streamer::Streamer;

/// Operator configuration for the engine process. Every value comes
/// from a flag or an environment variable (see main.rs); nothing
/// about a deployment is compiled in.
pub struct EngineConfig {
    /// Path to the GGUF file to load.
    pub model_path: PathBuf,
    /// Advertised model name override; None derives the name from
    /// the file (metadata name, else file stem).
    pub model_name: Option<String>,
}

/// Static facts about the loaded model, shared with connection
/// threads for the hello detail and the debug self-report.
pub struct ModelInfo {
    /// The name requests must address (or leave empty).
    pub name: String,
    /// The file the model was loaded from.
    pub path: String,
    /// The file's own architecture string.
    pub architecture: String,
    /// Transformer layer count.
    pub layers: usize,
    /// Hidden width.
    pub hidden: u32,
    /// Vocabulary size.
    pub vocab: usize,
    /// Context length from the file's metadata.
    pub context_length: u32,
    /// Coverage gate result: tensors the arch module requires.
    pub coverage_expected: usize,
    /// Coverage gate result: tensors found and verified.
    pub coverage_found: usize,
    /// The model's own chat template from the GGUF metadata
    /// (`tokenizer.chat_template`); None when the file carries
    /// none, which the chat_template op refuses by name.
    pub chat_template: Option<String>,
    /// The BOS token's text ("" when the tokenizer has no BOS), for
    /// the template's `bos_token` variable.
    pub bos_token: String,
    /// The EOS token's text ("" when the tokenizer has no EOS).
    pub eos_token: String,
}

/// Live counters for the debug self-report.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Stats {
    /// Generations completed (a terminal event was sent).
    pub generations: u64,
    /// Tokens generated across all jobs.
    pub tokens_generated: u64,
    /// Prompt tokens of the most recent job.
    pub last_prompt_tokens: usize,
    /// Generated tokens of the most recent job.
    pub last_generated_tokens: usize,
    /// Cache position reached by the most recent job (prompt plus
    /// generated tokens processed into the KV cache).
    pub last_cache_position: usize,
    /// Generations running right now (one per busy slot).
    pub active: usize,
    /// Jobs accepted and waiting for a slot.
    pub queued: usize,
    /// Embedding batches completed.
    pub embeddings: u64,
}

/// One event on a job's reply channel.
pub enum GenEvent {
    /// A piece of completion text and the token that produced it.
    Token {
        /// Decoded text (may be empty when the token's bytes do not
        /// yet complete a character).
        text: String,
        /// The sampled token id.
        token_id: u32,
    },
    /// The generation ended; no more events follow.
    Done {
        /// "stop" (EOS or stop string) or "length" (max_tokens).
        finish_reason: String,
    },
    /// The generation refused or failed, by name.
    Error {
        /// Protocol error code (see protocol.rs).
        code: String,
        /// Human-readable detail.
        message: String,
    },
}

/// One unit of work handed from a connection thread to a worker:
/// a generation, or an embedding batch (TODO T-9.15). Both ride the
/// same bounded queue, so the concurrency contract covers both.
pub enum Work {
    /// A generation job.
    Generate(Job),
    /// An embedding job.
    Embed(EmbedJob),
}

/// The outcome of an embedding batch: one vector per input, in
/// order, or the named failure as (code, message).
pub type EmbedOutcome = Result<Vec<Vec<f32>>, (String, String)>;

/// One embedding job: a batch of texts and the channel the vectors
/// (or the named failure) go back on.
pub struct EmbedJob {
    /// The input texts, in order.
    pub inputs: Vec<String>,
    /// Per-input token cap from the operator's configuration
    /// (--max-embed-tokens); an input tokenizing past it refuses
    /// the batch by name instead of occupying a slot without bound.
    pub max_tokens_per_input: usize,
    /// Where the outcome goes.
    pub reply: Sender<EmbedOutcome>,
}

/// One generation job handed from a connection thread to the worker.
pub struct Job {
    /// Requested model name (already checked against the loaded
    /// model by the connection thread).
    pub prompt: String,
    /// Requested token cap; None for the configured default.
    pub max_tokens: Option<usize>,
    /// Sampling temperature; 0 is greedy.
    pub temperature: f64,
    /// Nucleus mass cap.
    pub top_p: f64,
    /// Stop strings.
    pub stop: Vec<String>,
    /// Sampling seed for this job (ignored when greedy). The
    /// connection thread resolves the request's optional seed
    /// against the clock before the job is queued.
    pub seed: u64,
    /// Top-k candidate cap; None or 0 disables truncation.
    pub top_k: Option<usize>,
    /// Presence penalty (OpenAI form); 0 disables.
    pub presence_penalty: f64,
    /// Frequency penalty (OpenAI form); 0 disables.
    pub frequency_penalty: f64,
    /// Whether this job's full prompt ids and generated text may
    /// be written to the engine log (the operator's --log-content).
    /// Off by default: the log lines carry counts and timings.
    pub log_content: bool,
    /// Where events go.
    pub reply: Sender<GenEvent>,
}

/// The loaded model, shared by the worker threads. Passed from
/// [`load`] to [`run_worker`]; its fields stay private because the
/// workers are the only consumers. Cloning is cheap: the weights
/// are Arc-backed tensor views and the tokenizer is shared behind
/// an Arc, so each slot clones the handle set, not the model.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Loaded {
    cfg: GlimmerConfig,
    weights: Weights,
    tokenizer: Arc<Tokenizer>,
    add_bos: bool,
}

/// Adapts the gguf crate's parsed tokenizer info into the tokenizer
/// crate's input data. Same thin adapter as the loader's conformance
/// harness and generation example; it lives in binary code, not in
/// either library.
fn data_from_info(
    info: &gguf::TokenizerInfo,
    model: Option<String>,
    unknown: Option<u32>,
) -> TokenizerData {
    TokenizerData {
        model,
        tokens: info.tokens.clone(),
        token_types: info
            .token_types
            .as_ref()
            .map(|types| types.iter().map(|&t| TokenType::from_gguf(t)).collect())
            .unwrap_or_default(),
        merges: info.merges.clone().unwrap_or_default(),
        scores: info.scores.clone(),
        bos_token_id: info.bos_token_id,
        eos_token_id: info.eos_token_id,
        unknown_token_id: unknown,
        padding_token_id: info.padding_token_id,
    }
}

/// Load the model file end to end: parse, config from the file's own
/// metadata, the coverage gate (any missing tensor fails the load by
/// name), weights, and the tokenizer. Called once at startup; a load
/// failure is fatal to the process, because a model that did not
/// load completely must not serve at all.
pub fn load(config: &EngineConfig) -> Result<(Arc<ModelInfo>, Loaded), String> {
    let path = &config.model_path;
    let file = gguf::GgufFile::open(path).map_err(|e| format!("open {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    let cfg = itak_loader::load_config(&file).map_err(|e| format!("load config: {e}"))?;
    let report = itak_loader::coverage(&file, &cfg);
    report
        .require_complete()
        .map_err(|e| format!("coverage gate: {e}"))?;
    let coverage_expected = report.expected_count();
    let coverage_found = report.found_count();
    let weights =
        itak_loader::load_weights(&file, &cfg).map_err(|e| format!("load weights: {e}"))?;

    let tinfo = file
        .tokenizer()
        .map_err(|e| format!("tokenizer info: {e}"))?;
    let tok_model = file
        .metadata()
        .opt_string("tokenizer.ggml.model")
        .map_err(|e| format!("tokenizer model key: {e}"))?
        .map(str::to_string);
    let tokenizer = Tokenizer::new(data_from_info(&tinfo, tok_model, None))
        .map_err(|e| format!("build tokenizer: {e}"))?;
    let add_bos = file
        .metadata()
        .get_bool("tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token")
        .unwrap_or(false);

    let architecture = file
        .metadata()
        .opt_string("general.architecture")
        .map_err(|e| format!("architecture key: {e}"))?
        .unwrap_or(muse_glimmer::ARCHITECTURE)
        .to_string();
    let name = config
        .model_name
        .clone()
        .or_else(|| cfg.name.clone())
        .or_else(|| path.file_stem().map(|s| s.to_string_lossy().into_owned()))
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "model".to_string());
    let chat_template = file
        .metadata()
        .opt_string("tokenizer.chat_template")
        .map_err(|e| format!("chat template key: {e}"))?
        .map(str::to_string);
    // The template's special-token variables, as text. A special
    // token that does not decode is reported as empty rather than
    // failing the load: the template op can still serve the
    // template, and a template that needs the text will render
    // visibly wrong instead of silently half-loading the model.
    let token_text = |id: Option<u32>| -> String {
        match id {
            Some(id) => tokenizer
                .decode_bytes(&[id])
                .ok()
                .and_then(|bytes| String::from_utf8(bytes).ok())
                .unwrap_or_default(),
            None => String::new(),
        }
    };
    let info = ModelInfo {
        name,
        path: path.display().to_string(),
        architecture,
        layers: cfg.layers.len(),
        hidden: cfg.hidden,
        vocab: cfg.vocab_size as usize,
        context_length: cfg.context_length,
        coverage_expected,
        coverage_found,
        chat_template,
        bos_token: token_text(tokenizer.bos_id()),
        eos_token: token_text(tokenizer.eos_id()),
    };
    Ok((
        Arc::new(info),
        Loaded {
            cfg,
            weights,
            tokenizer: Arc::new(tokenizer),
            add_bos,
        },
    ))
}

/// The worker loop: receive jobs and run them, until every sender
/// is gone (the process is shutting down). One worker thread is one
/// serving slot (TODO T-9.14): `slots` workers share the job queue
/// behind a mutex, and each job builds its own model instance,
/// compute backend, and position cache from the shared weights, so
/// concurrent jobs share nothing mutable. The queue in front of the
/// slots is bounded by the channel capacity the caller chose; a
/// submission past it is refused by the connection thread with the
/// `engine_busy` code, never queued without limit and never run
/// concurrently inside another job's state.
///
/// Each job runs under `catch_unwind`. A panic anywhere inside a
/// job (a tokenizer edge, a forward bug, a sampler fault) used to
/// kill the worker thread with the job's reply sender still
/// uncompleted inside it, stranding the caller on a channel that
/// would never deliver a terminal event (panel B1/B4). The loop
/// now completes the job by name instead: the panic is recorded on
/// the diag channel and the job's channel receives the
/// `engine_died` outcome, the same code the connection thread
/// reports when a worker is gone. The slot then takes the next
/// job; the weights and stats it shares are behind the same
/// poison-tolerant locks the rest of the engine uses.
pub fn run_worker(
    loaded: Loaded,
    stats: Arc<Mutex<Stats>>,
    default_max_tokens: usize,
    jobs: Arc<Mutex<Receiver<Work>>>,
) {
    loop {
        let work = {
            let rx = jobs.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
            rx.recv()
        };
        match work {
            Ok(Work::Generate(job)) => {
                let reply = job.reply.clone();
                let contained = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
                    run_job(&loaded, &stats, default_max_tokens, job)
                }));
                if contained.is_err() {
                    crate::diag::error(
                        "engine_died",
                        "generation job panicked in the worker; completed as engine_died",
                    );
                    let _ = reply.send(GenEvent::Error {
                        code: "engine_died".to_string(),
                        message: "engine worker panicked during generation".to_string(),
                    });
                }
            }
            Ok(Work::Embed(job)) => {
                let reply = job.reply.clone();
                let contained = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
                    run_embed(&loaded, &stats, job)
                }));
                if contained.is_err() {
                    crate::diag::error(
                        "engine_died",
                        "embedding job panicked in the worker; completed as engine_died",
                    );
                    let _ = reply.send(Err((
                        "engine_died".to_string(),
                        "engine worker panicked during embedding".to_string(),
                    )));
                }
            }
            Err(_) => return,
        }
    }
}

/// Run one embedding batch: tokenize each input (with BOS exactly
/// when the file's metadata says the family takes one, the same
/// rule generations follow), look the tokens up in the model's own
/// embedding table through the compute backend's embed step, mean
/// pool the rows, and L2-normalize. The result is a bag-of-embeddings
/// vector: an honest product of the model's table, named as such,
/// not a hidden-state pooling the engine does not do.
fn run_embed(loaded: &Loaded, stats: &Arc<Mutex<Stats>>, job: EmbedJob) {
    {
        let mut st = stats.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        st.queued = st.queued.saturating_sub(1);
    }
    let outcome = embed_batch(loaded, &job.inputs, job.max_tokens_per_input);
    if let Err((code, message)) = &outcome {
        // The batch's refusal is recorded under its protocol code
        // (the per-input cap's bad_request lands here) before the
        // outcome goes back to the connection thread.
        crate::diag::error(code, message);
    }
    if outcome.is_ok() {
        let mut st = stats.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        st.embeddings += 1;
    }
    let _ = job.reply.send(outcome);
}

fn embed_batch(
    loaded: &Loaded,
    inputs: &[String],
    max_tokens_per_input: usize,
) -> Result<Vec<Vec<f32>>, (String, String)> {
    let compute = CpuCompute::new();
    let hidden = loaded.cfg.hidden as usize;
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(inputs.len());
    for input in inputs {
        let body = loaded
            .tokenizer
            .encode(input)
            .map_err(|e| ("bad_request".to_string(), format!("tokenize input: {e}")))?;
        let ids = assemble_prompt_ids(&body, loaded.add_bos, loaded.tokenizer.bos_id());
        if ids.is_empty() {
            return Err((
                "bad_request".to_string(),
                "input produced no tokens".to_string(),
            ));
        }
        check_embed_input(ids.len(), max_tokens_per_input)?;
        let rows = compute
            .embed(&loaded.weights.embedding, &ids, &loaded.cfg)
            .map_err(|e| ("forward_failed".to_string(), format!("embed lookup: {e}")))?;
        let pooled = mean_pool(&rows, hidden, ids.len());
        out.push(l2_normalize(&pooled).ok_or_else(|| {
            (
                "forward_failed".to_string(),
                "embedding pooled to a zero vector".to_string(),
            )
        })?);
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// The per-input token cap refusal for an embedding batch,
/// factored out so its shape is unit-testable without a loaded
/// model. Before the cap existed, one batch could carry any number
/// of inputs of any length onto a shared worker slot and starve
/// generation indefinitely (adjudication, embed path unbounded);
/// the batch count half of the cap is enforced by the connection
/// thread in main.rs, this is the per-input half.
fn check_embed_input(tokens: usize, max_tokens: usize) -> Result<(), (String, String)> {
    if tokens > max_tokens {
        return Err((
            "bad_request".to_string(),
            format!("embed input of {tokens} tokens exceeds the per-input maximum of {max_tokens}"),
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Mean of `n` rows of width `hidden`, laid out contiguously.
fn mean_pool(rows: &[f32], hidden: usize, n: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut out = vec![0.0f32; hidden];
    for row in 0..n {
        for (j, acc) in out.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            *acc += rows[row * hidden + j];
        }
    }
    if n > 0 {
        let scale = 1.0 / n as f32;
        for acc in out.iter_mut() {
            *acc *= scale;
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Scale a vector to unit length; None when it has no length.
fn l2_normalize(v: &[f32]) -> Option<Vec<f32>> {
    let norm = v.iter().map(|x| x * x).sum::<f32>().sqrt();
    if norm == 0.0 || !norm.is_finite() {
        return None;
    }
    Some(v.iter().map(|x| x / norm).collect())
}

/// Assemble the id sequence a job runs on: the tokenized body,
/// with the BOS id prepended when the file's metadata asks for
/// one AND the body does not already begin with it. A rendered
/// chat template starts with the bos_token text, which tokenizes
/// to the BOS id itself; prepending again would put two BOS ids
/// at the head of every chat prompt, where llama.cpp's tokenizer
/// drops the duplicate (TODO T-9.16, found live by the T-9.17
/// proof run: the engine logged [200000, 200000, ...] for the
/// Glimmer file's own template).
fn assemble_prompt_ids(body: &[u32], add_bos: bool, bos: Option<u32>) -> Vec<u32> {
    let mut ids: Vec<u32> = Vec::with_capacity(body.len() + 1);
    if add_bos {
        if let Some(bos) = bos {
            if body.first() != Some(&bos) {
                ids.push(bos);
            }
        }
    }
    ids.extend_from_slice(body);
    ids
}

/// Test-only panic trigger: a generation job carrying this prompt
/// panics inside the worker, so the containment test can prove a
/// panicking job completes as `engine_died` instead of stranding
/// its caller. Compiled only into test builds; no production path
/// can set it off.
#[cfg(test)]
const TEST_PANIC_PROMPT: &str = "__itak_engine_worker_panic_test__";

fn run_job(loaded: &Loaded, stats: &Arc<Mutex<Stats>>, default_max_tokens: usize, job: Job) {
    let Job {
        prompt,
        max_tokens,
        temperature,
        top_p,
        stop,
        seed,
        top_k,
        presence_penalty,
        frequency_penalty,
        log_content,
        reply,
    } = job;
    #[cfg(test)]
    if prompt == TEST_PANIC_PROMPT {
        panic!("test-injected worker panic");
    }
    // The job leaves the queue the moment a slot takes it, however
    // it ends from here (including the early named failures below).
    {
        let mut st = stats.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        st.queued = st.queued.saturating_sub(1);
    }
    let fail = |code: &str, message: String| {
        // Every named job failure is recorded on the diagnostic
        // channel under its protocol code as it is reported: the
        // tokenize bad_request, the empty-prompt bad_request, and
        // the context_overflow refusal all leave through here.
        crate::diag::error(code, &message);
        let _ = reply.send(GenEvent::Error {
            code: code.to_string(),
            message,
        });
    };

    // Tokenize: the engine owns the tokenizer, so the prompt the
    // model sees is the prompt the conformance proofs cover. BOS is
    // added exactly when the file's metadata says the family does,
    // and never twice: a prompt that already begins with the BOS
    // token (a chat template rendering its bos_token, TODO T-9.16)
    // keeps the one it carries, the same dedupe llama.cpp's
    // tokenizer performs (llama-vocab.cpp: add_bos with the first
    // real token already BOS drops the duplicate).
    let body = match loaded.tokenizer.encode(&prompt) {
        Ok(ids) => ids,
        Err(e) => return fail("bad_request", format!("tokenize prompt: {e}")),
    };
    let ids = assemble_prompt_ids(&body, loaded.add_bos, loaded.tokenizer.bos_id());
    if ids.is_empty() {
        return fail("bad_request", "prompt produced no tokens".to_string());
    }
    let max_tokens = max_tokens.filter(|&n| n > 0).unwrap_or(default_max_tokens);
    let context = loaded.cfg.context_length as usize;
    // checked_add, not addition: a max_tokens near usize::MAX (the
    // configured default is operator input too) must refuse as a
    // context overflow, never wrap the sum under the context length
    // and admit an unbounded generation (adjudication H-1).
    let fits = matches!(ids.len().checked_add(max_tokens), Some(total) if total <= context);
    if !fits {
        return fail(
            "context_overflow",
            format!(
                "prompt of {} tokens plus max_tokens {} exceeds the context length {}",
                ids.len(),
                max_tokens,
                context
            ),
        );
    }
    crate::diag::emit(
        "generate_start",
        &format!(
            "generate start: prompt_tokens={} max_tokens={} temperature={} top_p={}",
            ids.len(),
            max_tokens,
            temperature,
            top_p
        ),
    );
    // The full id list is content, not diagnostics: token ids are
    // reversible to prompt text with the model's own tokenizer, so
    // it is logged only under the operator's --log-content. It is
    // also one unbounded line per job (a max-context prompt is on
    // the order of a megabyte on one line), which is half of how
    // the supervisor's stderr pump wedged (adjudication H-2).
    if log_content {
        crate::diag::emit("generate_prompt_ids", &format!("prompt ids: {ids:?}"));
    }

    {
        let mut st = stats.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        st.active += 1;
        st.last_prompt_tokens = ids.len();
        st.last_generated_tokens = 0;
        st.last_cache_position = ids.len();
    }
    let started = Instant::now();
    let outcome = generate_inner(
        loaded,
        &ids,
        max_tokens,
        SamplerConfig {
            temperature,
            top_p,
            top_k: top_k.unwrap_or(0),
            presence_penalty,
            frequency_penalty,
            seed,
        },
        stop,
        &reply,
    );
    let mut st = stats.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
    st.active = st.active.saturating_sub(1);
    match outcome {
        JobOutcome::Done {
            finish_reason,
            generated,
            text,
        } => {
            st.generations += 1;
            st.tokens_generated += generated as u64;
            st.last_generated_tokens = generated;
            st.last_cache_position = ids.len() + generated;
            drop(st);
            crate::diag::emit(
                "generate_done",
                &done_log_line(
                    &finish_reason,
                    generated,
                    started.elapsed().as_millis(),
                    &text,
                    log_content,
                ),
            );
            let _ = reply.send(GenEvent::Done { finish_reason });
        }
        JobOutcome::Failed { code, message } => {
            drop(st);
            // The job's failure record is this line (the forward
            // and detokenize refusals land here, named in its
            // fields); the error frame is sent directly rather
            // than through fail(), which would record it twice.
            crate::diag::emit(
                "generate_failed",
                &format!("generate failed: code={} message={}", code, message),
            );
            let _ = reply.send(GenEvent::Error { code, message });
        }
        JobOutcome::Aborted { generated } => {
            st.last_generated_tokens = generated;
            drop(st);
            crate::diag::emit("generate_aborted", "generate aborted: client disconnected");
        }
    }
}

/// The generate-done log line. The completion text is user
/// content, so by default the line carries the finish reason, the
/// count, and the elapsed time only; the full text is included
/// solely under the operator's --log-content, the same gate as the
/// prompt id dump in run_job. The stable prefix and field order
/// are unchanged either way, so log readers see one shape.
fn done_log_line(
    finish_reason: &str,
    generated: usize,
    elapsed_ms: u128,
    text: &str,
    log_content: bool,
) -> String {
    if log_content {
        format!(
            "generate done: finish_reason={finish_reason} generated={generated} elapsed_ms={elapsed_ms} text={text:?}"
        )
    } else {
        format!(
            "generate done: finish_reason={finish_reason} generated={generated} elapsed_ms={elapsed_ms}"
        )
    }
}

enum JobOutcome {
    Done {
        finish_reason: String,
        generated: usize,
        text: String,
    },
    Failed {
        code: String,
        message: String,
    },
    Aborted {
        generated: usize,
    },
}

/// The token loop itself: prefill once, then one forward per sampled
/// token against the position cache (the incremental decode the
/// blueprint requires; there is no full re-forward anywhere here).
fn generate_inner(
    loaded: &Loaded,
    ids: &[u32],
    max_tokens: usize,
    sampler_cfg: SamplerConfig,
    stop: Vec<String>,
    reply: &Sender<GenEvent>,
) -> JobOutcome {
    let model = GlimmerModel::with_diag(
        loaded.cfg.clone(),
        loaded.weights.clone(),
        Box::new(CpuCompute::new()),
        Arc::new(StderrDiag),
    );
    let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
    let mut sampler = Sampler::new(sampler_cfg);
    // The prompt counts toward the penalties (the OpenAI form), so
    // it is observed before the first pick.
    sampler.observe(ids);
    let mut streamer = Streamer::new(stop);
    let eos = loaded.tokenizer.eos_id();

    let mut logits = match model.forward(ids, &mut cache) {
        Ok(logits) => logits,
        Err(e) => {
            return JobOutcome::Failed {
                code: "forward_failed".to_string(),
                message: format!("prefill: {e}"),
            }
        }
    };
    let mut generated = 0usize;
    let mut last_token = 0u32;
    loop {
        let token = sampler.pick(&logits);
        if Some(token) == eos {
            if !flush(reply, &mut streamer, last_token) {
                return JobOutcome::Aborted { generated };
            }
            return JobOutcome::Done {
                finish_reason: "stop".to_string(),
                generated,
                text: streamer.text().to_string(),
            };
        }
        generated += 1;
        last_token = token;
        let bytes = match loaded.tokenizer.decode_bytes(&[token]) {
            Ok(bytes) => bytes,
            Err(e) => {
                return JobOutcome::Failed {
                    code: "detokenize_failed".to_string(),
                    message: format!("token {token}: {e}"),
                }
            }
        };
        for chunk in streamer.push(&bytes) {
            if reply
                .send(GenEvent::Token {
                    text: chunk,
                    token_id: token,
                })
                .is_err()
            {
                return JobOutcome::Aborted { generated };
            }
        }
        if streamer.stopped() {
            return JobOutcome::Done {
                finish_reason: "stop".to_string(),
                generated,
                text: streamer.text().to_string(),
            };
        }
        if generated >= max_tokens {
            if !flush(reply, &mut streamer, last_token) {
                return JobOutcome::Aborted { generated };
            }
            return JobOutcome::Done {
                finish_reason: "length".to_string(),
                generated,
                text: streamer.text().to_string(),
            };
        }
        match model.forward(&[token], &mut cache) {
            Ok(next) => logits = next,
            Err(e) => {
                return JobOutcome::Failed {
                    code: "forward_failed".to_string(),
                    message: format!("decode step {generated}: {e}"),
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Send the streamer's held-back tail as final token text,
/// attributed to the last generated token (the bytes are its tail).
/// Returns false when the client has gone away.
fn flush(reply: &Sender<GenEvent>, streamer: &mut Streamer, last_token: u32) -> bool {
    for chunk in streamer.finish() {
        if reply
            .send(GenEvent::Token {
                text: chunk,
                token_id: last_token,
            })
            .is_err()
        {
            return false;
        }
    }
    true
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn prompt_ids_prepend_bos_once_and_only_when_asked() {
        // Plain body: BOS goes on the front.
        assert_eq!(
            assemble_prompt_ids(&[954, 7963], true, Some(200000)),
            vec![200000, 954, 7963]
        );
        // A body already starting with BOS (a rendered chat
        // template) keeps exactly one.
        assert_eq!(
            assemble_prompt_ids(&[200000, 200022, 15651], true, Some(200000)),
            vec![200000, 200022, 15651]
        );
        // The family does not add BOS: the body stands as-is.
        assert_eq!(assemble_prompt_ids(&[954], false, Some(200000)), vec![954]);
        // No BOS id known: nothing to prepend.
        assert_eq!(assemble_prompt_ids(&[954], true, None), vec![954]);
        // Empty body with BOS asked: the lone BOS is the prompt.
        assert_eq!(assemble_prompt_ids(&[], true, Some(200000)), vec![200000]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn done_log_line_carries_content_only_under_the_flag() {
        let plain = done_log_line("stop", 7, 1234, "the completion text", false);
        assert!(plain.contains("finish_reason=stop"), "line: {plain}");
        assert!(plain.contains("generated=7"), "line: {plain}");
        assert!(plain.contains("elapsed_ms=1234"), "line: {plain}");
        assert!(
            !plain.contains("completion text"),
            "content must not reach the default log line: {plain}"
        );
        let full = done_log_line("stop", 7, 1234, "the completion text", true);
        assert!(full.contains("the completion text"), "line: {full}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn embed_input_cap_refuses_by_name() {
        assert!(check_embed_input(8192, 8192).is_ok());
        let (code, message) = check_embed_input(8193, 8192).expect_err("past the cap refuses");
        assert_eq!(code, "bad_request");
        assert!(message.contains("8193"), "message: {message}");
        assert!(message.contains("8192"), "message: {message}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn mean_pool_averages_rows() {
        // Two rows of width 3.
        let rows = [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 3.0, 2.0, 1.0];
        assert_eq!(mean_pool(&rows, 3, 2), vec![2.0, 2.0, 2.0]);
        assert_eq!(mean_pool(&rows, 3, 1), vec![1.0, 2.0, 3.0]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn l2_normalize_makes_unit_vectors_and_refuses_zero() {
        let v = l2_normalize(&[3.0, 4.0]).expect("normalizes");
        assert!((v[0] - 0.6).abs() < 1e-6 && (v[1] - 0.8).abs() < 1e-6);
        let norm: f32 = v.iter().map(|x| x * x).sum::<f32>().sqrt();
        assert!((norm - 1.0).abs() < 1e-6);
        assert!(l2_normalize(&[0.0, 0.0]).is_none());
    }

    /// Stable fixture values in [-0.25, 0.25): the same LCG the
    /// spec fixtures use, so the synthetic weights are identical
    /// on every run.
    fn fixture_values(state: &mut u64, n: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
        (0..n)
            .map(|_| {
                *state = state
                    .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                    .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
                let v = ((*state >> 40) & 0xFF_FFFF) as f32 / (1u64 << 24) as f32;
                (v - 0.5) * 0.5
            })
            .collect()
    }

    fn put_fixture_tensor(
        tensors: &mut std::collections::HashMap<String, muse_glimmer::TensorView>,
        name: String,
        shape: &[u64],
        values: Vec<f32>,
    ) {
        let data: Vec<u8> = values.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect();
        tensors.insert(
            name.clone(),
            muse_glimmer::TensorView {
                name,
                dtype: muse_glimmer::Dtype::F32,
                shape: shape.to_vec(),
                data: std::sync::Arc::from(data.into_boxed_slice()),
            },
        );
    }

    struct FixtureSource {
        tensors: std::collections::HashMap<String, muse_glimmer::TensorView>,
    }

    impl muse_glimmer::TensorSource for FixtureSource {
        fn tensor(&self, name: &str) -> muse_glimmer::Result<muse_glimmer::TensorView> {
            self.tensors.get(name).cloned().ok_or_else(|| {
                muse_glimmer::GlimmerError::MissingTensor {
                    name: name.to_string(),
                }
            })
        }
    }

    /// A small synthetic [`Loaded`] (4 layers, hidden 32, vocab
    /// 128: the spec fixtures' geometry) so the worker test drives
    /// the real [`run_worker`] on an honest value. No generation
    /// runs against it: the panic job dies on the test hook before
    /// tokenizing, and the survival probe is an empty embedding
    /// batch, which completes without touching the model.
    fn tiny_loaded() -> Loaded {
        use muse_glimmer::{LayerKind, PatternSource};
        let hidden = 32usize;
        let ffn = 64usize;
        let vocab = 128usize;
        let qw = 32usize; // q_heads 4 * key_length 8
        let kw = 16usize; // kv_heads 2 * key_length 8
        let vw = 16usize; // kv_heads 2 * value_length 8
        let head_dim = 8usize;
        let cfg = GlimmerConfig {
            name: Some("synthetic worker-test target".to_string()),
            block_count: 4,
            context_length: 256,
            hidden: hidden as u32,
            ffn_hidden: ffn as u32,
            q_heads: 4,
            kv_heads: 2,
            key_length: 8,
            value_length: 8,
            rope_freq_base: 10_000.0,
            rope_freq_base_swa: 10_000.0,
            rms_eps: 1e-6,
            sliding_window: 16,
            logit_softcap: 20.0,
            logit_scale: 0.5,
            vocab_size: vocab as u32,
            layers: vec![
                LayerKind::SlidingWindow,
                LayerKind::Global,
                LayerKind::SlidingWindow,
                LayerKind::Global,
            ],
            pattern_source: PatternSource::MeasuredFallback,
        };
        let mut state: u64 = 0x5eed_0001;
        let mut tensors: std::collections::HashMap<String, muse_glimmer::TensorView> =
            std::collections::HashMap::new();
        put_fixture_tensor(
            &mut tensors,
            "token_embd.weight".to_string(),
            &[hidden as u64, vocab as u64],
            fixture_values(&mut state, vocab * hidden),
        );
        put_fixture_tensor(
            &mut tensors,
            "output_norm.weight".to_string(),
            &[hidden as u64],
            vec![1.0; hidden],
        );
        put_fixture_tensor(
            &mut tensors,
            "output.weight".to_string(),
            &[hidden as u64, vocab as u64],
            fixture_values(&mut state, vocab * hidden),
        );
        for layer in 0..4usize {
            let name = |suffix: &str| format!("blk.{layer}.{suffix}");
            put_fixture_tensor(
                &mut tensors,
                name("attn_norm.weight"),
                &[hidden as u64],
                vec![1.0; hidden],
            );
            put_fixture_tensor(
                &mut tensors,
                name("attn_q.weight"),
                &[hidden as u64, qw as u64],
                fixture_values(&mut state, hidden * qw),
            );
            put_fixture_tensor(
                &mut tensors,
                name("attn_k.weight"),
                &[hidden as u64, kw as u64],
                fixture_values(&mut state, hidden * kw),
            );
            put_fixture_tensor(
                &mut tensors,
                name("attn_v.weight"),
                &[hidden as u64, vw as u64],
                fixture_values(&mut state, hidden * vw),
            );
            put_fixture_tensor(
                &mut tensors,
                name("attn_q_norm.weight"),
                &[head_dim as u64],
                vec![1.0; head_dim],
            );
            put_fixture_tensor(
                &mut tensors,
                name("attn_k_norm.weight"),
                &[head_dim as u64],
                vec![1.0; head_dim],
            );
            put_fixture_tensor(
                &mut tensors,
                name("attn_gate.weight"),
                &[hidden as u64, qw as u64],
                fixture_values(&mut state, hidden * qw),
            );
            put_fixture_tensor(
                &mut tensors,
                name("attn_output.weight"),
                &[qw as u64, hidden as u64],
                fixture_values(&mut state, qw * hidden),
            );
            put_fixture_tensor(
                &mut tensors,
                name("post_attention_norm.weight"),
                &[hidden as u64],
                vec![1.0; hidden],
            );
            put_fixture_tensor(
                &mut tensors,
                name("ffn_norm.weight"),
                &[hidden as u64],
                vec![1.0; hidden],
            );
            put_fixture_tensor(
                &mut tensors,
                name("ffn_gate.weight"),
                &[hidden as u64, ffn as u64],
                fixture_values(&mut state, hidden * ffn),
            );
            put_fixture_tensor(
                &mut tensors,
                name("ffn_up.weight"),
                &[hidden as u64, ffn as u64],
                fixture_values(&mut state, hidden * ffn),
            );
            put_fixture_tensor(
                &mut tensors,
                name("ffn_down.weight"),
                &[ffn as u64, hidden as u64],
                fixture_values(&mut state, ffn * hidden),
            );
            put_fixture_tensor(
                &mut tensors,
                name("post_ffw_norm.weight"),
                &[hidden as u64],
                vec![1.0; hidden],
            );
        }
        let weights =
            Weights::load(&FixtureSource { tensors }, &cfg).expect("synthetic weights load");
        let tokenizer = Tokenizer::new(TokenizerData {
            model: Some("gpt2".to_string()),
            tokens: (0..vocab).map(|i| format!("tok{i}")).collect(),
            token_types: Vec::new(),
            merges: Vec::new(),
            scores: None,
            bos_token_id: None,
            eos_token_id: None,
            unknown_token_id: None,
            padding_token_id: None,
        })
        .expect("synthetic tokenizer builds");
        Loaded {
            cfg,
            weights,
            tokenizer: Arc::new(tokenizer),
            add_bos: false,
        }
    }

    /// The panic containment contract (panel B1/B4): a job that
    /// panics inside the worker completes its channel with the
    /// named `engine_died` outcome instead of hanging its caller,
    /// the panic is recorded on the diag channel, and the slot
    /// keeps serving afterwards.
    #[test]
    fn worker_panic_completes_the_job_as_engine_died() {
        use std::sync::mpsc::channel;
        use std::time::Duration;

        #[derive(Default)]
        struct Capture {
            events: Mutex<Vec<(String, String)>>,
        }
        impl crate::diag::Diag for Capture {
            fn event(&self, event: &str, detail: &str) {
                self.events
                    .lock()
                    .expect("capture lock")
                    .push((event.to_string(), detail.to_string()));
            }
        }
        // The diag sink is process-global; hold the lock the diag
        // tests use for the whole install, drive, read sequence.
        let _guard = crate::diag::SINK_TEST_LOCK
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        let capture = Arc::new(Capture::default());
        crate::diag::set_sink(capture.clone());

        let (job_tx, job_rx) = channel::<Work>();
        let stats = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Stats::default()));
        let worker = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            run_worker(tiny_loaded(), stats, 8, Arc::new(Mutex::new(job_rx)))
        });

        let (reply_tx, reply_rx) = channel::<GenEvent>();
        job_tx
            .send(Work::Generate(Job {
                prompt: TEST_PANIC_PROMPT.to_string(),
                max_tokens: None,
                temperature: 0.0,
                top_p: 1.0,
                stop: Vec::new(),
                seed: 0,
                top_k: None,
                presence_penalty: 0.0,
                frequency_penalty: 0.0,
                log_content: false,
                reply: reply_tx,
            }))
            .expect("queue the panic job");
        let event = reply_rx
            .recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10))
            .expect("a panicking job must still complete its channel");
        match event {
            GenEvent::Error { code, .. } => assert_eq!(code, "engine_died"),
            GenEvent::Token { .. } => panic!("a panicking job produced a token"),
            GenEvent::Done { .. } => panic!("a panicking job reported done"),
        }

        // The slot survived: an empty embedding batch completes
        // normally on the same worker.
        let (embed_tx, embed_rx) = channel::<EmbedOutcome>();
        job_tx
            .send(Work::Embed(EmbedJob {
                inputs: Vec::new(),
                max_tokens_per_input: 8,
                reply: embed_tx,
            }))
            .expect("queue the survival probe");
        let outcome = embed_rx
            .recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10))
            .expect("the worker must keep serving after a contained panic");
        assert!(outcome.is_ok(), "survival probe failed: {outcome:?}");

        drop(job_tx);
        worker.join().expect("worker exits when the queue closes");

        let events = capture.events.lock().expect("capture lock");
        assert!(
            events.iter().any(|(event, _)| event == "engine_died"),
            "the panic must emit its diag event, got {events:?}"
        );
        drop(events);
        crate::diag::set_sink(Arc::new(crate::diag::StderrDiag));
    }

    #[test]
    fn pooled_cosine_ranks_the_related_pair_first() {
        // The T-9.15 ranking shape at the pooling level: rows are
        // token embeddings; two inputs sharing a token direction
        // must land closer than an unrelated one.
        let cat = mean_pool(&[1.0, 0.1, 0.9, 0.2], 2, 2); // tokens A, B
        let cats = mean_pool(&[1.0, 0.1, 0.8, 0.3], 2, 2); // tokens A, B'
        let car = mean_pool(&[-0.9, 1.0, -1.0, 0.8], 2, 2); // unrelated
        let cos = |a: &[f32], b: &[f32]| -> f32 {
            let an = l2_normalize(a).expect("a");
            let bn = l2_normalize(b).expect("b");
            an.iter().zip(bn.iter()).map(|(x, y)| x * y).sum()
        };
        assert!(
            cos(&cat, &cats) > cos(&cat, &car),
            "related {} should beat unrelated {}",
            cos(&cat, &cats),
            cos(&cat, &car)
        );
    }
}
