//! Minimal JSON for the socket protocol.
//!
//! The workspace carries no external dependencies, and the NDJSON
//! protocol between the platform and this engine needs only objects,
//! arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and null. This module is a
//! small recursive-descent parser and a serializer for exactly that,
//! with the string escapes (including `\uXXXX` surrogate pairs) the
//! tokenizer's token text can contain. Anything outside the grammar
//! is a named parse error with the byte offset, never a panic.

/// A parsed JSON value. Objects keep insertion order.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum Value {
    /// JSON null.
    Null,
    /// JSON true or false.
    Bool(bool),
    /// A JSON number, held as f64 (token ids and counts in this
    /// protocol are far below 2^53, so the representation is exact).
    Num(f64),
    /// A JSON string, fully unescaped.
    Str(String),
    /// A JSON array.
    Arr(Vec<Value>),
    /// A JSON object as ordered key/value pairs.
    Obj(Vec<(String, Value)>),
}

impl Value {
    /// Look up `key` on an object value; None for any other shape.
    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&Value> {
        match self {
            Value::Obj(pairs) => pairs.iter().find(|(k, _)| k == key).map(|(_, v)| v),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The string contents, if this value is a string.
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        match self {
            Value::Str(s) => Some(s),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The numeric value, if this value is a number.
    pub fn as_f64(&self) -> Option<f64> {
        match self {
            Value::Num(n) => Some(*n),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The numeric value as usize, if it is a non-negative integer
    /// in range. Fractional or negative numbers return None, and so
    /// does anything above u32::MAX: counts in this protocol are
    /// token counts and batch sizes, and a value near usize::MAX is
    /// not a count but an attempt to wrap a caller's length
    /// arithmetic (adjudication H-1, where a max_tokens of 2^64
    /// saturated this conversion to usize::MAX and wrapped the
    /// engine's context check).
    pub fn as_usize(&self) -> Option<usize> {
        match self {
            Value::Num(n) if *n >= 0.0 && n.fract() == 0.0 && *n <= u32::MAX as f64 => {
                Some(*n as usize)
            }
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The elements, if this value is an array.
    pub fn as_arr(&self) -> Option<&[Value]> {
        match self {
            Value::Arr(items) => Some(items),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// Build an object value from key/value pairs.
pub fn obj(pairs: Vec<(&str, Value)>) -> Value {
    Value::Obj(pairs.into_iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.to_string(), v)).collect())
}

/// Serialize a value as compact JSON. Strings escape the quote, the
/// backslash, and control characters; all other characters pass
/// through as UTF-8, which is valid JSON.
pub fn stringify(value: &Value) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    write_value(value, &mut out);
    out
}

fn write_value(value: &Value, out: &mut String) {
    match value {
        Value::Null => out.push_str("null"),
        Value::Bool(b) => out.push_str(if *b { "true" } else { "false" }),
        Value::Num(n) => write_num(*n, out),
        Value::Str(s) => write_str(s, out),
        Value::Arr(items) => {
            out.push('[');
            for (i, item) in items.iter().enumerate() {
                if i > 0 {
                    out.push(',');
                }
                write_value(item, out);
            }
            out.push(']');
        }
        Value::Obj(pairs) => {
            out.push('{');
            for (i, (k, v)) in pairs.iter().enumerate() {
                if i > 0 {
                    out.push(',');
                }
                write_str(k, out);
                out.push(':');
                write_value(v, out);
            }
            out.push('}');
        }
    }
}

fn write_num(n: f64, out: &mut String) {
    if n.is_nan() || n.is_infinite() {
        // Not representable in JSON; the protocol never produces
        // these, and null is the least wrong rendering.
        out.push_str("null");
    } else if n.fract() == 0.0 && n.abs() <= 9_007_199_254_740_992.0 {
        out.push_str(&(n as i64).to_string());
    } else {
        out.push_str(&n.to_string());
    }
}

fn write_str(s: &str, out: &mut String) {
    out.push('"');
    for c in s.chars() {
        match c {
            '"' => out.push_str("\\\""),
            '\\' => out.push_str("\\\\"),
            '\n' => out.push_str("\\n"),
            '\r' => out.push_str("\\r"),
            '\t' => out.push_str("\\t"),
            '\u{08}' => out.push_str("\\b"),
            '\u{0c}' => out.push_str("\\f"),
            c if (c as u32) < 0x20 => {
                out.push_str(&format!("\\u{:04x}", c as u32));
            }
            c => out.push(c),
        }
    }
    out.push('"');
}

/// Parse one complete JSON document. Trailing non-whitespace is an
/// error, so a truncated or doubled frame cannot slip through.
pub fn parse(input: &str) -> Result<Value, String> {
    let mut p = Parser {
        bytes: input.as_bytes(),
        pos: 0,
    };
    p.skip_ws();
    let value = p.parse_value(0)?;
    p.skip_ws();
    if p.pos != p.bytes.len() {
        return Err(format!("trailing data at byte {}", p.pos));
    }
    Ok(value)
}

/// The deepest nesting the parser accepts. Protocol frames nest a
/// handful of levels, so 128 is generous headroom; past it the
/// input is not a frame but an attack on the recursive parser's
/// call stack (20,000 nested arrays overflowed the stack and
/// aborted the whole engine process, adjudication CB), and it is
/// refused with a named parse error instead.
const MAX_DEPTH: usize = 128;

struct Parser<'a> {
    bytes: &'a [u8],
    pos: usize,
}

impl Parser<'_> {
    fn skip_ws(&mut self) {
        while let Some(b) = self.bytes.get(self.pos) {
            if matches!(b, b' ' | b'\t' | b'\n' | b'\r') {
                self.pos += 1;
            } else {
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    fn peek(&self) -> Result<u8, String> {
        self.bytes
            .get(self.pos)
            .copied()
            .ok_or_else(|| "unexpected end of input".to_string())
    }

    fn parse_value(&mut self, depth: usize) -> Result<Value, String> {
        if depth > MAX_DEPTH {
            return Err(format!(
                "nesting deeper than {MAX_DEPTH} levels at byte {}",
                self.pos
            ));
        }
        match self.peek()? {
            b'{' => self.parse_obj(depth),
            b'[' => self.parse_arr(depth),
            b'"' => Ok(Value::Str(self.parse_string()?)),
            b't' => self.parse_lit("true", Value::Bool(true)),
            b'f' => self.parse_lit("false", Value::Bool(false)),
            b'n' => self.parse_lit("null", Value::Null),
            b'-' | b'0'..=b'9' => self.parse_num(),
            other => Err(format!(
                "unexpected character {:?} at byte {}",
                other as char, self.pos
            )),
        }
    }

    fn parse_lit(&mut self, lit: &str, value: Value) -> Result<Value, String> {
        if self.bytes[self.pos..].starts_with(lit.as_bytes()) {
            self.pos += lit.len();
            Ok(value)
        } else {
            Err(format!("invalid literal at byte {}", self.pos))
        }
    }

    fn parse_num(&mut self) -> Result<Value, String> {
        let start = self.pos;
        if self.peek()? == b'-' {
            self.pos += 1;
        }
        while let Some(b) = self.bytes.get(self.pos) {
            if matches!(b, b'0'..=b'9' | b'.' | b'e' | b'E' | b'+' | b'-') {
                self.pos += 1;
            } else {
                break;
            }
        }
        let text = std::str::from_utf8(&self.bytes[start..self.pos])
            .map_err(|_| format!("invalid number at byte {start}"))?;
        text.parse::<f64>()
            .map(Value::Num)
            .map_err(|_| format!("invalid number {text:?} at byte {start}"))
    }

    fn parse_string(&mut self) -> Result<String, String> {
        // Caller has peeked the opening quote.
        self.pos += 1;
        let mut out = String::new();
        loop {
            let b = self.peek()?;
            match b {
                b'"' => {
                    self.pos += 1;
                    return Ok(out);
                }
                b'\\' => {
                    self.pos += 1;
                    let esc = self.peek()?;
                    self.pos += 1;
                    match esc {
                        b'"' => out.push('"'),
                        b'\\' => out.push('\\'),
                        b'/' => out.push('/'),
                        b'b' => out.push('\u{08}'),
                        b'f' => out.push('\u{0c}'),
                        b'n' => out.push('\n'),
                        b'r' => out.push('\r'),
                        b't' => out.push('\t'),
                        b'u' => {
                            let hi = self.parse_hex4()?;
                            if (0xd800..0xdc00).contains(&hi) {
                                // High surrogate: a low surrogate must
                                // follow as a second \u escape.
                                if self.bytes.get(self.pos) == Some(&b'\\')
                                    && self.bytes.get(self.pos + 1) == Some(&b'u')
                                {
                                    self.pos += 2;
                                    let lo = self.parse_hex4()?;
                                    if !(0xdc00..0xe000).contains(&lo) {
                                        return Err(format!(
                                            "invalid low surrogate at byte {}",
                                            self.pos
                                        ));
                                    }
                                    let c = 0x1_0000
                                        + (((hi - 0xd800) as u32) << 10)
                                        + (lo - 0xdc00) as u32;
                                    out.push(char::from_u32(c).ok_or("invalid surrogate pair")?);
                                } else {
                                    return Err(format!("unpaired surrogate at byte {}", self.pos));
                                }
                            } else if (0xdc00..0xe000).contains(&hi) {
                                return Err(format!("unpaired low surrogate at byte {}", self.pos));
                            } else {
                                out.push(
                                    char::from_u32(hi as u32).ok_or("invalid unicode escape")?,
                                );
                            }
                        }
                        other => {
                            return Err(format!(
                                "invalid escape {:?} at byte {}",
                                other as char, self.pos
                            ))
                        }
                    }
                }
                0x00..=0x1f => {
                    return Err(format!(
                        "raw control character in string at byte {}",
                        self.pos
                    ))
                }
                _ => {
                    // Copy one UTF-8 encoded character verbatim. The
                    // input is a &str, so the bytes are valid UTF-8
                    // and the lead byte gives the length.
                    let len = utf8_len(b);
                    let end = self.pos + len;
                    let chunk = std::str::from_utf8(&self.bytes[self.pos..end])
                        .map_err(|_| format!("invalid utf-8 at byte {}", self.pos))?;
                    out.push_str(chunk);
                    self.pos = end;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    fn parse_hex4(&mut self) -> Result<u16, String> {
        let mut value: u16 = 0;
        for _ in 0..4 {
            let b = self.peek()?;
            self.pos += 1;
            let digit = match b {
                b'0'..=b'9' => b - b'0',
                b'a'..=b'f' => b - b'a' + 10,
                b'A'..=b'F' => b - b'A' + 10,
                _ => return Err(format!("invalid hex digit at byte {}", self.pos - 1)),
            };
            value = value * 16 + digit as u16;
        }
        Ok(value)
    }

    fn parse_obj(&mut self, depth: usize) -> Result<Value, String> {
        self.pos += 1; // '{'
        let mut pairs = Vec::new();
        self.skip_ws();
        if self.peek()? == b'}' {
            self.pos += 1;
            return Ok(Value::Obj(pairs));
        }
        loop {
            self.skip_ws();
            if self.peek()? != b'"' {
                return Err(format!("object key must be a string at byte {}", self.pos));
            }
            let key = self.parse_string()?;
            self.skip_ws();
            if self.peek()? != b':' {
                return Err(format!("expected ':' at byte {}", self.pos));
            }
            self.pos += 1;
            self.skip_ws();
            let value = self.parse_value(depth + 1)?;
            pairs.push((key, value));
            self.skip_ws();
            match self.peek()? {
                b',' => self.pos += 1,
                b'}' => {
                    self.pos += 1;
                    return Ok(Value::Obj(pairs));
                }
                _ => return Err(format!("expected ',' or '}}' at byte {}", self.pos)),
            }
        }
    }

    fn parse_arr(&mut self, depth: usize) -> Result<Value, String> {
        self.pos += 1; // '['
        let mut items = Vec::new();
        self.skip_ws();
        if self.peek()? == b']' {
            self.pos += 1;
            return Ok(Value::Arr(items));
        }
        loop {
            self.skip_ws();
            items.push(self.parse_value(depth + 1)?);
            self.skip_ws();
            match self.peek()? {
                b',' => self.pos += 1,
                b']' => {
                    self.pos += 1;
                    return Ok(Value::Arr(items));
                }
                _ => return Err(format!("expected ',' or ']' at byte {}", self.pos)),
            }
        }
    }
}

fn utf8_len(lead: u8) -> usize {
    match lead {
        0x00..=0x7f => 1,
        0xc0..=0xdf => 2,
        0xe0..=0xef => 3,
        _ => 4,
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn round_trip_protocol_shapes() {
        let frame = obj(vec![
            ("op", Value::Str("generate".into())),
            ("max_tokens", Value::Num(4.0)),
            ("temperature", Value::Num(0.5)),
            ("stop", Value::Arr(vec![Value::Str("\n".into())])),
            ("done", Value::Bool(false)),
            ("nothing", Value::Null),
        ]);
        let text = stringify(&frame);
        let back = parse(&text).expect("own output parses");
        assert_eq!(back, frame);
        assert_eq!(back.get("op").and_then(Value::as_str), Some("generate"));
        assert_eq!(back.get("max_tokens").and_then(Value::as_usize), Some(4));
    }

    #[test]
    fn escapes_and_unicode() {
        let v = parse(r#"{"s":"a\"b\\c\ndé😀"}"#).expect("parses");
        assert_eq!(
            v.get("s").and_then(Value::as_str),
            Some("a\"b\\c\nd\u{e9}\u{1f600}")
        );
        // The serializer escapes what JSON requires and leaves the
        // rest as UTF-8; the result parses back to the same string.
        let text = stringify(&v);
        let back = parse(&text).expect("reserializes");
        assert_eq!(back, v);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_garbage_with_offsets() {
        for bad in ["", "{", "{\"a\":}", "{\"a\":1} extra", "[1,]", "\"open"] {
            assert!(parse(bad).is_err(), "expected error for {bad:?}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn numbers_keep_integer_shape() {
        assert_eq!(stringify(&Value::Num(13796.0)), "13796");
        assert_eq!(stringify(&Value::Num(0.5)), "0.5");
        assert_eq!(parse("1e3").expect("parses"), Value::Num(1000.0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn usize_conversion_rejects_values_past_u32() {
        // Adjudication H-1's input exactly: 2^64 used to saturate to
        // usize::MAX here. No protocol count may.
        let at = parse("4294967295").expect("parses");
        assert_eq!(at.as_usize(), Some(4_294_967_295));
        for too_big in ["4294967296", "18446744073709551616", "1e30"] {
            let v = parse(too_big).expect("parses");
            assert_eq!(v.as_usize(), None, "{too_big} must not become a count");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn deep_nesting_is_a_named_error_not_a_stack_overflow() {
        // The adjudication's executed attack: 20,000 nested arrays,
        // about 40 KB of input, aborted the engine process with a
        // stack overflow before the depth cap. It must now be an
        // ordinary parse error.
        let attack = format!("{}{}", "[".repeat(20_000), "]".repeat(20_000));
        let err = parse(&attack).expect_err("the attack input must not parse");
        assert!(err.contains("nesting deeper"), "error: {err}");
        // Objects nest through the same counter.
        let obj_attack = format!("{}1{}", "{\"a\":".repeat(500), "}".repeat(500));
        assert!(parse(&obj_attack).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn nesting_within_the_limit_still_parses() {
        let deep = format!("{}1{}", "[".repeat(100), "]".repeat(100));
        assert!(parse(&deep).is_ok(), "100 levels is legitimate depth");
    }
}

===== END FILE: crates/itak-engine/src/json.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/itak-engine/src/main.rs =====
//! itak-engine: the Rust half of the iTaK Torch rebuild.
//!
//! Owns one loaded model and serves the platform's socket protocol
//! (see protocol.rs, the one definition of the wire format): hello,
//! ping, debug, and generate with streamed token events. The model
//! runs on a configured number of worker threads (slots) because the
//! CPU compute backend serves one sequence per instance; jobs queue
//! in a bounded channel and submissions past its capacity are
//! refused with the `engine_busy` code (TODO T-9.14).
//!
//! Configuration is flags, each with an environment fallback, and
//! nothing is compiled in:
//!
//! - `--model PATH` / `ITAK_ENGINE_MODEL`: the GGUF file (required).
//! - `--socket PATH` / `ITAK_ENGINE_SOCKET`: the Unix socket to bind
//!   (default `/tmp/itak-engine.sock`).
//! - `--model-name NAME` / `ITAK_ENGINE_MODEL_NAME`: the name
//!   requests must address; default is the file's own metadata name.
//! - `--default-max-tokens N` / `ITAK_ENGINE_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS`:
//!   generation cap when a request omits max_tokens (default 128).
//! - `--slots N` / `ITAK_ENGINE_SLOTS`: concurrent generations
//!   (default 1).
//! - `--max-queued N` / `ITAK_ENGINE_MAX_QUEUED`: generations that
//!   may wait for a slot before submissions refuse as engine_busy
//!   (default 8).
//! - `--max-frame-bytes N` / `ITAK_ENGINE_MAX_FRAME_BYTES`: the
//!   largest protocol frame, in bytes, a connection will read
//!   before refusing it as bad_frame and closing (default
//!   4194304).
//! - `--max-embed-inputs N` / `ITAK_ENGINE_MAX_EMBED_INPUTS`: the
//!   largest embed batch, in inputs, one frame may carry (default
//!   256).
//! - `--max-embed-tokens N` / `ITAK_ENGINE_MAX_EMBED_TOKENS`: the
//!   largest single embed input, in tokens (default 8192).
//! - `--log-content` / `ITAK_ENGINE_LOG_CONTENT` (1 or true): also
//!   log the full prompt token ids and generated text of every job.
//!   Default off: job logs carry counts, finish reasons, and
//!   timings only, because prompts and completions are user content
//!   and the supervisor forwards this stderr into the platform log.
//!
//! A model that fails to load (including the tensor coverage gate)
//! exits the process non-zero with the named error: a partial model
//! never serves.

mod diag;
mod engine;
mod json;
mod protocol;
mod sampler;
mod streamer;

use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader, Read, Write};
use std::os::unix::fs::{FileTypeExt, PermissionsExt};
use std::os::unix::io::AsRawFd;
use std::os::unix::net::{UnixListener, UnixStream};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::mpsc::{channel, sync_channel, SyncSender, TrySendError};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::{Instant, SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

use engine::{EmbedJob, EmbedOutcome, EngineConfig, GenEvent, Job, ModelInfo, Stats, Work};
use json::Value;

fn main() {
    std::process::exit(run());
}

fn run() -> i32 {
    let config = match parse_args() {
        Ok(config) => config,
        Err(code) => return code,
    };
    let socket_path = config.socket_path.clone();
    let engine_config = EngineConfig {
        model_path: config.model_path.clone(),
        model_name: config.model_name.clone(),
    };
    diag::emit(
        "model_load_begin",
        &format!(
            "loading model {} (this takes seconds: parse, coverage gate, weights)",
            config.model_path.display()
        ),
    );
    let load_started = Instant::now();
    let (info, loaded) = match engine::load(&engine_config) {
        Ok(pair) => pair,
        Err(e) => {
            diag::error("model_load_failed", &format!("model load FAILED: {e}"));
            return 1;
        }
    };
    diag::emit(
        "model_loaded",
        &format!(
            "model loaded in {} ms: name={} arch={} layers={} hidden={} vocab={} context={} coverage={}/{}",
            load_started.elapsed().as_millis(),
            info.name,
            info.architecture,
            info.layers,
            info.hidden,
            info.vocab,
            info.context_length,
            info.coverage_found,
            info.coverage_expected
        ),
    );

    let stats = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Stats::default()));
    // The queue capacity is the concurrency contract (TODO T-9.14):
    // `slots` jobs run at once, up to `max_queued` more wait, and a
    // submission past that is refused with the engine_busy code.
    let capacity = config.slots + config.max_queued;
    let (job_tx, job_rx) = sync_channel::<Work>(capacity);
    let job_rx = Arc::new(Mutex::new(job_rx));
    let default_max_tokens = config.default_max_tokens;
    for slot in 0..config.slots {
        let worker_stats = Arc::clone(&stats);
        let worker_jobs = Arc::clone(&job_rx);
        let worker_loaded = loaded.clone();
        std::thread::spawn(move || {
            engine::run_worker(worker_loaded, worker_stats, default_max_tokens, worker_jobs);
        });
        let _ = slot;
    }

    let listener = match bind_socket(&socket_path) {
        Ok(listener) => listener,
        Err(e) => {
            diag::error("socket_bind_failed", &e);
            return 1;
        }
    };
    diag::emit(
        "serving",
        &format!(
            "serving on {} (protocol {})",
            socket_path.display(),
            protocol::PROTO_VERSION
        ),
    );

    diag::emit(
        "concurrency",
        &format!(
            "concurrency: slots={} max_queued={} (submissions past capacity refuse as engine_busy)",
            config.slots, config.max_queued
        ),
    );
    let started = Instant::now();
    for conn in listener.incoming() {
        match conn {
            Ok(stream) => {
                let tx = job_tx.clone();
                let info = Arc::clone(&info);
                let stats = Arc::clone(&stats);
                let limits = Limits {
                    slots: config.slots,
                    max_queued: config.max_queued,
                    max_frame_bytes: config.max_frame_bytes,
                    max_embed_inputs: config.max_embed_inputs,
                    max_embed_tokens: config.max_embed_tokens,
                    log_content: config.log_content,
                };
                std::thread::spawn(move || handle_conn(stream, tx, info, stats, started, limits));
            }
            Err(e) => diag::error("accept_failed", &format!("accept failed: {e}")),
        }
    }
    0
}

/// Bind the serving socket.
///
/// A stale socket file from a previous incarnation is removed, but
/// anything else found at the path is never deleted: the path is
/// operator-controlled (--socket / ITAK_ENGINE_SOCKET), and a
/// mistyped path must not erase a real file, so a non-socket is a
/// named startup refusal. After the bind, the socket file is pinned
/// to owner-only permissions (0600): the socket is the engine's
/// control plane, and the file mode is the first half of its access
/// control (the peer credential check in handle_conn is the second).
fn bind_socket(socket_path: &Path) -> Result<UnixListener, String> {
    if socket_path.exists() {
        let is_socket = std::fs::metadata(socket_path)
            .map(|m| m.file_type().is_socket())
            .unwrap_or(false);
        if !is_socket {
            return Err(format!(
                "{} exists and is not a socket; refusing to remove it",
                socket_path.display()
            ));
        }
        diag::emit(
            "stale_socket_removed",
            &format!("removing stale socket file {}", socket_path.display()),
        );
        std::fs::remove_file(socket_path)
            .map_err(|e| format!("cannot remove stale socket: {e}"))?;
    }
    let listener = UnixListener::bind(socket_path)
        .map_err(|e| format!("bind {} failed: {e}", socket_path.display()))?;
    std::fs::set_permissions(socket_path, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o600))
        .map_err(|e| format!("cannot set socket permissions: {e}"))?;
    Ok(listener)
}

/// The engine's configured bounds, carried to connection threads
/// so refusals can name the state that refused: the concurrency
/// contract (slots and queue depth), the frame size cap, and the
/// embed batch caps.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Limits {
    slots: usize,
    max_queued: usize,
    max_frame_bytes: usize,
    max_embed_inputs: usize,
    max_embed_tokens: usize,
    log_content: bool,
}

struct CliConfig {
    model_path: PathBuf,
    socket_path: PathBuf,
    model_name: Option<String>,
    default_max_tokens: usize,
    slots: usize,
    max_queued: usize,
    max_frame_bytes: usize,
    max_embed_inputs: usize,
    max_embed_tokens: usize,
    log_content: bool,
}

fn parse_args() -> Result<CliConfig, i32> {
    let mut model: Option<String> = std::env::var("ITAK_ENGINE_MODEL").ok();
    let mut socket: Option<String> = std::env::var("ITAK_ENGINE_SOCKET").ok();
    let mut name: Option<String> = std::env::var("ITAK_ENGINE_MODEL_NAME").ok();
    let mut default_max: Option<String> = std::env::var("ITAK_ENGINE_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS").ok();
    let mut slots: Option<String> = std::env::var("ITAK_ENGINE_SLOTS").ok();
    let mut max_queued: Option<String> = std::env::var("ITAK_ENGINE_MAX_QUEUED").ok();
    let mut max_frame: Option<String> = std::env::var("ITAK_ENGINE_MAX_FRAME_BYTES").ok();
    let mut max_embed_inputs: Option<String> = std::env::var("ITAK_ENGINE_MAX_EMBED_INPUTS").ok();
    let mut max_embed_tokens: Option<String> = std::env::var("ITAK_ENGINE_MAX_EMBED_TOKENS").ok();
    // A boolean flag, not a value flag: the presence of
    // --log-content, or ITAK_ENGINE_LOG_CONTENT=1/true, turns it on.
    let mut log_content = std::env::var("ITAK_ENGINE_LOG_CONTENT")
        .map(|v| v == "1" || v.eq_ignore_ascii_case("true"))
        .unwrap_or(false);
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < args.len() {
        if args[i] == "--log-content" {
            log_content = true;
            i += 1;
            continue;
        }
        let (slot, label) = match args[i].as_str() {
            "--model" => (&mut model, "--model"),
            "--socket" => (&mut socket, "--socket"),
            "--model-name" => (&mut name, "--model-name"),
            "--default-max-tokens" => (&mut default_max, "--default-max-tokens"),
            "--slots" => (&mut slots, "--slots"),
            "--max-queued" => (&mut max_queued, "--max-queued"),
            "--max-frame-bytes" => (&mut max_frame, "--max-frame-bytes"),
            "--max-embed-inputs" => (&mut max_embed_inputs, "--max-embed-inputs"),
            "--max-embed-tokens" => (&mut max_embed_tokens, "--max-embed-tokens"),
            "--help" | "-h" => {
                eprintln!(
                    "usage: itak-engine --model PATH [--socket PATH] [--model-name NAME] [--default-max-tokens N] [--slots N] [--max-queued N] [--max-frame-bytes N] [--max-embed-inputs N] [--max-embed-tokens N] [--log-content]"
                );
                return Err(0);
            }
            other => {
                eprintln!("itak-engine: unknown argument {other:?} (try --help)");
                return Err(2);
            }
        };
        i += 1;
        match args.get(i) {
            Some(value) => *slot = Some(value.clone()),
            None => {
                eprintln!("itak-engine: {label} needs a value");
                return Err(2);
            }
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    let model = match model {
        Some(model) if !model.is_empty() => model,
        _ => {
            eprintln!("itak-engine: no model given: pass --model PATH or set ITAK_ENGINE_MODEL");
            return Err(2);
        }
    };
    let parse_count =
        |text: Option<String>, label: &str, default: usize, min: usize| -> Result<usize, i32> {
            match text {
                Some(text) => match text.parse::<usize>() {
                    Ok(n) if n >= min => Ok(n),
                    _ => {
                        eprintln!("itak-engine: {label} must be an integer >= {min}");
                        Err(2)
                    }
                },
                None => Ok(default),
            }
        };
    let default_max_tokens = parse_count(default_max, "--default-max-tokens", 128, 1)?;
    let slots = parse_count(slots, "--slots", 1, 1)?;
    let max_queued = parse_count(max_queued, "--max-queued", 8, 0)?;
    let max_frame_bytes = parse_count(max_frame, "--max-frame-bytes", 4_194_304, 1024)?;
    let max_embed_inputs = parse_count(max_embed_inputs, "--max-embed-inputs", 256, 1)?;
    let max_embed_tokens = parse_count(max_embed_tokens, "--max-embed-tokens", 8192, 1)?;
    Ok(CliConfig {
        model_path: PathBuf::from(model),
        socket_path: PathBuf::from(socket.unwrap_or_else(|| "/tmp/itak-engine.sock".to_string())),
        model_name: name,
        default_max_tokens,
        slots,
        max_queued,
        max_frame_bytes,
        max_embed_inputs,
        max_embed_tokens,
        log_content,
    })
}

/// The uid of the process on the other end of a connected Unix
/// stream, from the kernel (SO_PEERCRED): not a claim the peer
/// makes, so it cannot be spoofed by anything the peer sends.
fn peer_uid(stream: &UnixStream) -> Option<u32> {
    // SAFETY: cred is writable storage of exactly the size passed
    // in len; getsockopt with SO_PEERCRED on a Unix stream socket
    // fills it and reports failure by return code, checked here.
    let mut cred: libc::ucred = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
    let mut len = std::mem::size_of::<libc::ucred>() as libc::socklen_t;
    let rc = unsafe {
        libc::getsockopt(
            stream.as_raw_fd(),
            libc::SOL_SOCKET,
            libc::SO_PEERCRED,
            &mut cred as *mut libc::ucred as *mut libc::c_void,
            &mut len,
        )
    };
    if rc == 0 {
        Some(cred.uid)
    } else {
        None
    }
}

/// Refuse a connection whose peer runs under a different uid than
/// the engine itself. The platform and the engine run as the same
/// user in every supported deployment; a peer under any other uid
/// is not the platform, whatever frames it sends. This is the
/// second half of the socket's access control, behind the 0600
/// file mode from bind_socket.
fn check_peer(stream: &UnixStream) -> Result<(), String> {
    // SAFETY: geteuid takes no arguments and cannot fail.
    let own = unsafe { libc::geteuid() };
    match peer_uid(stream) {
        Some(uid) if uid == own => Ok(()),
        Some(uid) => Err(format!("peer uid {uid} is not the engine's uid {own}")),
        None => Err("cannot read the peer's credentials".to_string()),
    }
}

/// Send a named refusal frame and record the refusal on the
/// diagnostic channel under the same code, at the point of
/// refusal: every refusal the engine makes is observable in its
/// log with the code the client was told, not just on the wire.
/// Returns what [`send`] returns (false means the peer is gone).
fn refuse(writer: &mut UnixStream, code: &str, message: &str) -> bool {
    diag::error(code, message);
    send(writer, &protocol::error_frame(code, message))
}

fn handle_conn(
    stream: UnixStream,
    jobs: SyncSender<Work>,
    info: Arc<ModelInfo>,
    stats: Arc<Mutex<Stats>>,
    started: Instant,
    limits: Limits,
) {
    let mut writer = match stream.try_clone() {
        Ok(writer) => writer,
        Err(e) => {
            diag::error(
                "connection_failed",
                &format!("connection clone failed: {e}"),
            );
            return;
        }
    };
    if let Err(msg) = check_peer(&stream) {
        diag::error("peer_refused", &format!("connection refused: {msg}"));
        let _ = send(&mut writer, &protocol::error_frame("peer_refused", &msg));
        return;
    }
    let mut reader = BufReader::new(stream);
    let mut line = String::new();
    // The handshake is a gate, not a convention: until a hello with
    // a matching protocol version completes, no other op is served.
    // Before this, hello was one dispatch arm among six and the
    // version was checked only when the client volunteered it, so
    // any local process could skip the handshake entirely.
    let mut greeted = false;
    loop {
        line.clear();
        // The frame cap is a hard bound on memory: read at most one
        // byte past the cap, which is exactly enough to prove the
        // frame is over it. Before this, read_line grew the buffer
        // until the peer sent a newline or the process ran out of
        // memory, whichever came first (adjudication CB).
        let read = reader
            .by_ref()
            .take((limits.max_frame_bytes + 1) as u64)
            .read_line(&mut line);
        match read {
            Ok(0) => return, // client closed
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(e) => {
                diag::error(
                    "connection_read_failed",
                    &format!("connection read failed: {e}"),
                );
                return;
            }
        }
        if line.len() > limits.max_frame_bytes {
            let msg = format!(
                "frame exceeds the maximum frame size of {} bytes",
                limits.max_frame_bytes
            );
            let _ = refuse(&mut writer, "bad_frame", &msg);
            return;
        }
        let trimmed = line.trim_end();
        if trimmed.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let frame = match json::parse(trimmed) {
            Ok(frame) => frame,
            Err(e) => {
                if !refuse(&mut writer, "bad_frame", &e) {
                    return;
                }
                continue;
            }
        };
        let op = frame.get("op").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
        if op != "hello" && !greeted {
            let msg = format!("first frame on a connection must be hello, not {op:?}");
            let _ = refuse(&mut writer, "protocol_mismatch", &msg);
            return;
        }
        match op {
            "hello" => {
                // The version is required, not volunteered: the
                // platform's client always sends it, and a hello
                // without one has not identified what it speaks.
                // A refused handshake closes the connection; there
                // is nothing to retry on the same socket.
                match frame.get("proto").and_then(Value::as_f64) {
                    Some(v) if v == protocol::PROTO_VERSION => {}
                    Some(v) => {
                        let msg = format!(
                            "protocol version {v} not spoken here; this engine speaks {}",
                            protocol::PROTO_VERSION
                        );
                        let _ = refuse(&mut writer, "protocol_mismatch", &msg);
                        return;
                    }
                    None => {
                        let _ = refuse(
                            &mut writer,
                            "protocol_mismatch",
                            "hello frame carries no proto version",
                        );
                        return;
                    }
                }
                greeted = true;
                let detail = format!(
                    "itak-engine {} model={} arch={}",
                    env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),
                    info.name,
                    info.architecture
                );
                diag::emit("hello", &detail);
                if !send(&mut writer, &protocol::hello_ack(&detail)) {
                    return;
                }
            }
            "ping" => {
                let detail = format!("model={} busy={}", info.name, stats_busy(&stats));
                if !send(&mut writer, &protocol::pong(&detail)) {
                    return;
                }
            }
            "debug" => {
                let frame = debug_info(&info, &stats, started.elapsed().as_secs(), limits);
                if !send(&mut writer, &frame) {
                    return;
                }
            }
            "generate" => {
                if !handle_generate(&frame, &mut writer, &jobs, &info, &stats, limits) {
                    return;
                }
            }
            "embed" => {
                if !handle_embed(&frame, &mut writer, &jobs, &info, &stats, limits) {
                    return;
                }
            }
            "chat_template" => {
                let alive = match &info.chat_template {
                    Some(template) => send(
                        &mut writer,
                        &protocol::chat_template_frame(template, &info.bos_token, &info.eos_token),
                    ),
                    None => refuse(
                        &mut writer,
                        "no_chat_template",
                        "the model file carries no tokenizer.chat_template",
                    ),
                };
                if !alive {
                    return;
                }
            }
            other => {
                let msg = format!("unknown op {other:?}");
                if !refuse(&mut writer, "unknown_op", &msg) {
                    return;
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Run one generate frame to its terminal frame. Returns false when
/// the connection is dead and the handler should stop.
fn handle_generate(
    frame: &Value,
    writer: &mut UnixStream,
    jobs: &SyncSender<Work>,
    info: &Arc<ModelInfo>,
    stats: &Arc<Mutex<Stats>>,
    limits: Limits,
) -> bool {
    let req = match protocol::parse_generate(frame) {
        Ok(req) => req,
        Err(e) => {
            return refuse(writer, "bad_request", &e);
        }
    };
    if !req.model.is_empty() && req.model != info.name {
        let msg = format!(
            "this engine serves model {:?}, not {:?}",
            info.name, req.model
        );
        return refuse(writer, "model_not_found", &msg);
    }
    let (reply_tx, reply_rx) = channel::<GenEvent>();
    // A request seed makes the sampled run reproducible; only a
    // request without one is seeded from the clock (TODO T-9.13).
    let seed = req.seed.unwrap_or_else(|| {
        SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
            .map(|d| d.as_nanos() as u64)
            .unwrap_or(0x2545_f491)
    });
    let job = Job {
        prompt: req.prompt,
        max_tokens: req.max_tokens,
        temperature: req.temperature,
        top_p: req.top_p,
        stop: req.stop,
        seed,
        top_k: req.top_k,
        presence_penalty: req.presence_penalty,
        frequency_penalty: req.frequency_penalty,
        log_content: limits.log_content,
        reply: reply_tx,
    };
    // The bounded queue is the concurrency contract: a submission
    // past capacity refuses by name instead of queueing without
    // limit, and the refusal names the state that refused it.
    match jobs.try_send(Work::Generate(job)) {
        Ok(()) => {
            let mut st = stats.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
            st.queued += 1;
        }
        Err(TrySendError::Full(_)) => {
            let msg = format!(
                "engine busy: {} slot(s) running and the queue is full (max_queued {})",
                limits.slots, limits.max_queued
            );
            return refuse(writer, "engine_busy", &msg);
        }
        Err(TrySendError::Disconnected(_)) => {
            return refuse(writer, "engine_died", "the engine worker is gone");
        }
    }
    loop {
        match reply_rx.recv() {
            Ok(GenEvent::Token { text, token_id }) => {
                if !send(writer, &protocol::token_event(&text, token_id, false, None)) {
                    return false;
                }
            }
            Ok(GenEvent::Done { finish_reason }) => {
                return send(
                    writer,
                    &protocol::token_event("", 0, true, Some(&finish_reason)),
                );
            }
            Ok(GenEvent::Error { code, message }) => {
                // The worker already recorded this failure on the
                // diagnostic channel when it named it; the
                // connection only relays the frame.
                return send(writer, &protocol::error_frame(&code, &message));
            }
            Err(_) => {
                // The worker dropped the job without a terminal
                // event: it died, and the platform should hear that
                // by name, not as a silent close. The worker emitted
                // nothing, so the connection side records it.
                return refuse(
                    writer,
                    "engine_died",
                    "the engine worker stopped mid-generation",
                );
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Run one embed frame to its reply frame: queue the batch behind
/// the same bounded contract as generations, wait for the worker's
/// vectors, and answer with the embeddings frame or the named
/// error. Returns false when the connection is dead.
fn handle_embed(
    frame: &Value,
    writer: &mut UnixStream,
    jobs: &SyncSender<Work>,
    info: &Arc<ModelInfo>,
    stats: &Arc<Mutex<Stats>>,
    limits: Limits,
) -> bool {
    let (model, inputs) = match protocol::parse_embed(frame) {
        Ok(pair) => pair,
        Err(e) => {
            return refuse(writer, "bad_request", &e);
        }
    };
    if !model.is_empty() && model != info.name {
        let msg = format!("this engine serves model {:?}, not {:?}", info.name, model);
        return refuse(writer, "model_not_found", &msg);
    }
    // The batch cap is enforced here, before the batch can occupy
    // a slot: a frame may be large (up to --max-frame-bytes) and a
    // batch of tiny inputs inside it is still unbounded work
    // without this. The per-input token half rides the job and is
    // enforced by the worker after tokenization.
    if inputs.len() > limits.max_embed_inputs {
        let msg = format!(
            "embed batch of {} inputs exceeds the maximum of {}",
            inputs.len(),
            limits.max_embed_inputs
        );
        return refuse(writer, "bad_request", &msg);
    }
    let (reply_tx, reply_rx) = channel::<EmbedOutcome>();
    let job = EmbedJob {
        inputs,
        max_tokens_per_input: limits.max_embed_tokens,
        reply: reply_tx,
    };
    match jobs.try_send(Work::Embed(job)) {
        Ok(()) => {
            let mut st = stats.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
            st.queued += 1;
        }
        Err(TrySendError::Full(_)) => {
            let msg = format!(
                "engine busy: {} slot(s) running and the queue is full (max_queued {})",
                limits.slots, limits.max_queued
            );
            return refuse(writer, "engine_busy", &msg);
        }
        Err(TrySendError::Disconnected(_)) => {
            return refuse(writer, "engine_died", "the engine worker is gone");
        }
    }
    match reply_rx.recv() {
        Ok(Ok(vectors)) => send(writer, &protocol::embeddings_frame(&info.name, &vectors)),
        // The worker recorded the failure on the diagnostic
        // channel when it named it; this only relays the frame.
        Ok(Err((code, message))) => send(writer, &protocol::error_frame(&code, &message)),
        Err(_) => refuse(
            writer,
            "engine_died",
            "the engine worker stopped mid-embedding",
        ),
    }
}

fn stats_busy(stats: &Arc<Mutex<Stats>>) -> bool {
    stats.lock().map(|st| st.active > 0).unwrap_or(false)
}

/// The debug self-report: what is loaded, how its coverage gate
/// went, and what it has served. This is the engine's half of the
/// platform's /debug view. The concurrency fields (slots, active,
/// queued, max_queued) are how an operator sees the T-9.14 contract
/// and which jobs hold it.
fn debug_info(
    info: &ModelInfo,
    stats: &Arc<Mutex<Stats>>,
    uptime_secs: u64,
    limits: Limits,
) -> Value {
    let st = stats.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
    json::obj(vec![
        ("op", Value::Str("debug_info".into())),
        ("proto", Value::Num(protocol::PROTO_VERSION)),
        (
            "engine",
            Value::Str(format!("itak-engine {}", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"))),
        ),
        ("model", Value::Str(info.name.clone())),
        ("model_path", Value::Str(info.path.clone())),
        ("architecture", Value::Str(info.architecture.clone())),
        ("layers", Value::Num(info.layers as f64)),
        ("hidden", Value::Num(f64::from(info.hidden))),
        ("vocab", Value::Num(info.vocab as f64)),
        ("context_length", Value::Num(f64::from(info.context_length))),
        (
            "coverage_expected",
            Value::Num(info.coverage_expected as f64),
        ),
        ("coverage_found", Value::Num(info.coverage_found as f64)),
        ("busy", Value::Bool(st.active > 0)),
        (
            "has_chat_template",
            Value::Bool(info.chat_template.is_some()),
        ),
        ("slots", Value::Num(limits.slots as f64)),
        ("active", Value::Num(st.active as f64)),
        ("queued", Value::Num(st.queued as f64)),
        ("max_queued", Value::Num(limits.max_queued as f64)),
        ("generations", Value::Num(st.generations as f64)),
        ("embeddings", Value::Num(st.embeddings as f64)),
        ("tokens_generated", Value::Num(st.tokens_generated as f64)),
        (
            "last_prompt_tokens",
            Value::Num(st.last_prompt_tokens as f64),
        ),
        (
            "last_generated_tokens",
            Value::Num(st.last_generated_tokens as f64),
        ),
        (
            "last_cache_position",
            Value::Num(st.last_cache_position as f64),
        ),
        ("uptime_secs", Value::Num(uptime_secs as f64)),
    ])
}

/// Write one frame as a line and flush (token events must not sit in
/// a buffer; streaming is the point). False means the peer is gone.
fn send(writer: &mut UnixStream, frame: &Value) -> bool {
    let mut line = json::stringify(frame);
    line.push('\n');
    writer.write_all(line.as_bytes()).is_ok() && writer.flush().is_ok()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::io::Read;

    fn test_info() -> Arc<ModelInfo> {
        Arc::new(ModelInfo {
            name: "fake".to_string(),
            path: "fake.gguf".to_string(),
            architecture: "muse-glimmer".to_string(),
            layers: 1,
            hidden: 8,
            vocab: 16,
            context_length: 128,
            coverage_expected: 1,
            coverage_found: 1,
            chat_template: None,
            bos_token: String::new(),
            eos_token: String::new(),
        })
    }

    fn dummy_job() -> Job {
        // Nobody ever runs this job; it only occupies queue space.
        let (reply_tx, _reply_rx) = channel::<GenEvent>();
        Job {
            prompt: "x".to_string(),
            max_tokens: None,
            temperature: 0.0,
            top_p: 0.0,
            stop: Vec::new(),
            seed: 1,
            top_k: None,
            presence_penalty: 0.0,
            frequency_penalty: 0.0,
            log_content: false,
            reply: reply_tx,
        }
    }

    fn temp_socket_path(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {
        let nanos = SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
            .map(|d| d.as_nanos())
            .unwrap_or(0);
        std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
            "itak-engine-test-{tag}-{}-{nanos}.sock",
            std::process::id()
        ))
    }

    #[test]
    fn stale_regular_file_is_never_deleted() {
        // The attack/accident shape: --socket points at a real file.
        // Startup must refuse by name and leave the file untouched.
        let path = temp_socket_path("notasock");
        std::fs::write(&path, b"precious").expect("write file");
        let err = match bind_socket(&path) {
            Ok(_) => panic!("bind must refuse a non-socket path"),
            Err(e) => e,
        };
        assert!(err.contains("not a socket"), "error: {err}");
        assert_eq!(
            std::fs::read(&path).expect("file still there"),
            b"precious",
            "the file must survive the refused startup"
        );
        std::fs::remove_file(&path).expect("cleanup");
    }

    #[test]
    fn bound_socket_is_owner_only() {
        let path = temp_socket_path("mode");
        let listener = bind_socket(&path).expect("bind");
        let mode = std::fs::metadata(&path)
            .expect("metadata")
            .permissions()
            .mode();
        assert_eq!(mode & 0o777, 0o600, "socket mode: {mode:o}");
        drop(listener);
        std::fs::remove_file(&path).expect("cleanup");
    }

    #[test]
    fn stale_socket_file_is_removed_and_rebound() {
        let path = temp_socket_path("stale");
        let first = bind_socket(&path).expect("first bind");
        drop(first);
        // The socket file outlives the listener; the next bind must
        // clear it and serve, not fail with AddrInUse.
        let second = bind_socket(&path).expect("second bind clears the stale socket");
        drop(second);
        std::fs::remove_file(&path).expect("cleanup");
    }

    /// Run handle_conn on a thread over a stream pair and hand back
    /// the client end. The job receiver stays alive in the caller so
    /// the channel the connection holds never disconnects mid-test.
    fn serve_conn() -> (
        BufReader<UnixStream>,
        std::sync::mpsc::Receiver<Work>,
        std::thread::JoinHandle<()>,
    ) {
        serve_conn_with_frame_cap(4_194_304)
    }

    fn serve_conn_with_frame_cap(
        max_frame_bytes: usize,
    ) -> (
        BufReader<UnixStream>,
        std::sync::mpsc::Receiver<Work>,
        std::thread::JoinHandle<()>,
    ) {
        serve_conn_with_limits(Limits {
            slots: 1,
            max_queued: 0,
            max_frame_bytes,
            max_embed_inputs: 256,
            max_embed_tokens: 8192,
            log_content: false,
        })
    }

    fn serve_conn_with_limits(
        limits: Limits,
    ) -> (
        BufReader<UnixStream>,
        std::sync::mpsc::Receiver<Work>,
        std::thread::JoinHandle<()>,
    ) {
        let (engine_side, client_side) = UnixStream::pair().expect("stream pair");
        client_side
            .set_read_timeout(Some(std::time::Duration::from_secs(10)))
            .expect("read timeout");
        let (tx, rx) = sync_channel::<Work>(4);
        let stats = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Stats::default()));
        let handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            handle_conn(engine_side, tx, test_info(), stats, Instant::now(), limits);
        });
        (BufReader::new(client_side), rx, handle)
    }

    fn write_frame(client: &mut BufReader<UnixStream>, text: &str) {
        let stream = client.get_mut();
        stream.write_all(text.as_bytes()).expect("write frame");
        stream.write_all(b"\n").expect("write newline");
        stream.flush().expect("flush");
    }

    fn read_reply(client: &mut BufReader<UnixStream>) -> String {
        let mut line = String::new();
        let n = client.read_line(&mut line).expect("read reply");
        assert!(n > 0, "expected a reply frame, got EOF");
        line
    }

    fn assert_closed_after_refusal(client: &mut BufReader<UnixStream>) {
        let mut line = String::new();
        let n = client.read_line(&mut line).expect("read after refusal");
        assert_eq!(n, 0, "the connection must close after the refusal");
    }

    #[test]
    fn peer_check_accepts_the_same_uid() {
        // Both ends of a stream pair are this process, so the peer
        // uid is the engine's own: the check passes. A peer under a
        // different uid cannot be produced inside one test process;
        // that half is the kernel's SO_PEERCRED answer, exercised
        // here only in its accepting direction.
        let (a, _b) = UnixStream::pair().expect("stream pair");
        check_peer(&a).expect("same-uid peer is accepted");
        assert_eq!(peer_uid(&a), Some(unsafe { libc::geteuid() }));
    }

    #[test]
    fn op_before_hello_is_refused_and_the_connection_closes() {
        // The adjudication's attack shape: a local process skips the
        // handshake and goes straight for an op.
        let (mut client, _rx, handle) = serve_conn();
        write_frame(&mut client, r#"{"op":"ping"}"#);
        let reply = read_reply(&mut client);
        assert!(reply.contains("\"protocol_mismatch\""), "reply: {reply}");
        assert_closed_after_refusal(&mut client);
        drop(client);
        handle.join().expect("conn thread");
    }

    #[test]
    fn hello_without_proto_is_refused_and_the_connection_closes() {
        let (mut client, _rx, handle) = serve_conn();
        write_frame(&mut client, r#"{"op":"hello"}"#);
        let reply = read_reply(&mut client);
        assert!(reply.contains("\"protocol_mismatch\""), "reply: {reply}");
        assert!(reply.contains("no proto"), "reply: {reply}");
        assert_closed_after_refusal(&mut client);
        drop(client);
        handle.join().expect("conn thread");
    }

    #[test]
    fn hello_with_wrong_proto_is_refused_and_the_connection_closes() {
        let (mut client, _rx, handle) = serve_conn();
        write_frame(&mut client, r#"{"op":"hello","proto":99}"#);
        let reply = read_reply(&mut client);
        assert!(reply.contains("\"protocol_mismatch\""), "reply: {reply}");
        assert_closed_after_refusal(&mut client);
        drop(client);
        handle.join().expect("conn thread");
    }

    #[test]
    fn hello_then_ping_answers() {
        let (mut client, _rx, handle) = serve_conn();
        write_frame(&mut client, r#"{"op":"hello","proto":1,"client":"test"}"#);
        let reply = read_reply(&mut client);
        assert!(reply.contains("\"hello_ack\""), "reply: {reply}");
        write_frame(&mut client, r#"{"op":"ping"}"#);
        let reply = read_reply(&mut client);
        assert!(reply.contains("\"pong\""), "reply: {reply}");
        drop(client);
        handle.join().expect("conn thread");
    }

    #[test]
    fn oversized_frame_is_refused_and_the_connection_closes() {
        // The adjudication's attack shape: a frame far past the cap.
        // The engine must refuse it by name at the cap, not buffer it.
        let (mut client, _rx, handle) = serve_conn_with_frame_cap(64);
        write_frame(&mut client, r#"{"op":"hello","proto":1}"#);
        let reply = read_reply(&mut client);
        assert!(reply.contains("\"hello_ack\""), "reply: {reply}");
        // One combined write, not write_frame's two calls: the engine
        // refuses and closes the moment it has read cap+1 bytes, and
        // under full-suite load that close can land between the helper's
        // payload and newline writes, failing the newline write with
        // EPIPE even though the refusal behaved exactly as specified.
        client
            .get_mut()
            .write_all(format!("{}\n", "a".repeat(500)).as_bytes())
            .expect("write oversized frame");
        let reply = read_reply(&mut client);
        assert!(reply.contains("\"bad_frame\""), "reply: {reply}");
        assert_closed_after_refusal(&mut client);
        drop(client);
        handle.join().expect("conn thread");
    }

    #[test]
    fn unterminated_frame_is_refused_at_the_cap() {
        // The OOM shape exactly: no newline ever arrives. The read
        // must stop one byte past the cap and refuse, not grow.
        let (mut client, _rx, handle) = serve_conn_with_frame_cap(64);
        write_frame(&mut client, r#"{"op":"hello","proto":1}"#);
        let reply = read_reply(&mut client);
        assert!(reply.contains("\"hello_ack\""), "reply: {reply}");
        let stream = client.get_mut();
        stream
            .write_all(&[b'x'; 500])
            .expect("write unterminated bytes");
        stream.flush().expect("flush");
        let reply = read_reply(&mut client);
        assert!(reply.contains("\"bad_frame\""), "reply: {reply}");
        assert_closed_after_refusal(&mut client);
        drop(client);
        handle.join().expect("conn thread");
    }

    #[test]
    fn wrapping_max_tokens_is_refused_by_name_over_the_wire() {
        // Adjudication H-1's frame, end to end: the refusal is the
        // named bad_request and the connection stays usable.
        let (mut client, _rx, handle) = serve_conn();
        write_frame(&mut client, r#"{"op":"hello","proto":1}"#);
        let reply = read_reply(&mut client);
        assert!(reply.contains("\"hello_ack\""), "reply: {reply}");
        write_frame(
            &mut client,
            r#"{"op":"generate","prompt":"x","max_tokens":18446744073709551616}"#,
        );
        let reply = read_reply(&mut client);
        assert!(reply.contains("\"bad_request\""), "reply: {reply}");
        write_frame(&mut client, r#"{"op":"ping"}"#);
        let reply = read_reply(&mut client);
        assert!(reply.contains("\"pong\""), "reply: {reply}");
        drop(client);
        handle.join().expect("conn thread");
    }

    #[test]
    fn oversized_embed_batch_is_refused_by_name() {
        // The embed attack shape: one frame carrying a batch far
        // past the cap. The refusal happens before any slot is
        // occupied, and names the cap.
        let (mut client, _rx, handle) = serve_conn_with_limits(Limits {
            slots: 1,
            max_queued: 0,
            max_frame_bytes: 4_194_304,
            max_embed_inputs: 2,
            max_embed_tokens: 8192,
            log_content: false,
        });
        write_frame(&mut client, r#"{"op":"hello","proto":1}"#);
        let reply = read_reply(&mut client);
        assert!(reply.contains("\"hello_ack\""), "reply: {reply}");
        write_frame(&mut client, r#"{"op":"embed","input":["a","b","c"]}"#);
        let reply = read_reply(&mut client);
        assert!(reply.contains("\"bad_request\""), "reply: {reply}");
        assert!(reply.contains("maximum of 2"), "reply: {reply}");
        drop(client);
        handle.join().expect("conn thread");
    }

    #[test]
    fn full_queue_refuses_engine_busy_by_name() {
        // Capacity 1 and it is already full: the next submission is
        // refused with the engine_busy code, not queued, not run.
        let (tx, _rx) = sync_channel::<Work>(1);
        tx.try_send(Work::Generate(dummy_job()))
            .expect("fill the queue");
        let (mut a, mut b) = UnixStream::pair().expect("stream pair");
        let frame = crate::json::parse(r#"{"op":"generate","prompt":"hello"}"#).expect("frame");
        let stats = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Stats::default()));
        let ok = handle_generate(
            &frame,
            &mut a,
            &tx,
            &test_info(),
            &stats,
            Limits {
                slots: 1,
                max_queued: 0,
                max_frame_bytes: 4_194_304,
                max_embed_inputs: 256,
                max_embed_tokens: 8192,
                log_content: false,
            },
        );
        assert!(ok, "the connection survives a busy refusal");
        drop(a);
        let mut text = String::new();
        b.read_to_string(&mut text).expect("read reply");
        assert!(text.contains("\"engine_busy\""), "reply: {text}");
        // The refused job was not counted as queued.
        let st = stats.lock().expect("stats");
        assert_eq!(st.queued, 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn op_before_hello_refusal_emits_its_diag_event() {
        // The diagnostic half of the handshake gate: the refusal
        // is not only on the wire, it is on the engine's diagnostic
        // channel under its protocol code. Captured through the
        // sink seam (see diag.rs); the lock keeps the other sink
        // swapping test from interleaving with this one.
        #[derive(Default)]
        struct Capture {
            events: Mutex<Vec<(String, String)>>,
        }
        impl diag::Diag for Capture {
            fn event(&self, event: &str, detail: &str) {
                self.events
                    .lock()
                    .expect("capture lock")
                    .push((event.to_string(), detail.to_string()));
            }
        }
        let _guard = diag::SINK_TEST_LOCK
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        let capture = Arc::new(Capture::default());
        diag::set_sink(capture.clone());
        let (mut client, _rx, handle) = serve_conn();
        write_frame(&mut client, r#"{"op":"ping"}"#);
        let reply = read_reply(&mut client);
        assert!(reply.contains("\"protocol_mismatch\""), "reply: {reply}");
        drop(client);
        handle.join().expect("conn thread");
        diag::set_sink(Arc::new(diag::StderrDiag));
        let events = capture.events.lock().expect("capture lock");
        assert!(
            events.iter().any(|(event, detail)| {
                event == "protocol_mismatch" && detail.contains("first frame on a connection")
            }),
            "the refusal must emit its named diag event; captured: {events:?}"
        );
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/itak-engine/src/protocol.rs =====
//! The platform-to-engine socket protocol, defined once, here.
//!
//! Transport: a Unix domain socket, one JSON object per line
//! (NDJSON). The Go platform's client is
//! `platform/internal/engine/unix.go`; SERVING.md carries the same
//! definition in prose. Both sides implement this file's shapes and
//! nothing else.
//!
//! Frames from the platform:
//!
//! - `{"op":"hello","proto":1,"client":"torch-platform"}`: first
//!   frame on every connection.
//! - `{"op":"ping"}`: health probe.
//! - `{"op":"debug"}`: self-report request.
//! - `{"op":"chat_template"}`: ask for the model's own chat
//!   template. The reply is a `chat_template` frame carrying the
//!   template text from the GGUF metadata plus the `bos_token` and
//!   `eos_token` texts the template's variables refer to; a model
//!   whose file carries no template gets an `error` frame with
//!   code `no_chat_template` (TODO T-9.16). The platform renders
//!   the template; the engine only serves it, so the prompt the
//!   model sees is built from the file's own format string.
//! - `{"op":"embed","model":"...","input":["...","..."]}`: embed
//!   one or more texts. The reply is one `embeddings` frame (below)
//!   or an `error` frame. The vectors are mean-pooled token
//!   embeddings from the model's own embedding table (the same
//!   lookup the forward pass starts from), L2-normalized, in input
//!   order (TODO T-9.15).
//! - `{"op":"generate","model":"...","prompt":"...","max_tokens":N,
//!   "temperature":F,"top_p":F,"stop":["..."]}`: one generation.
//!   `max_tokens` absent or 0 means the engine's configured default;
//!   `temperature` absent or 0 is greedy; `top_p` absent, 0, or 1
//!   disables nucleus truncation. Optional sampling parity fields
//!   (TODO T-9.13): `seed` (integer; a seeded sampled run is
//!   reproducible, absent means the engine seeds from the clock),
//!   `top_k` (integer; absent or 0 disables top-k truncation), and
//!   `presence_penalty` / `frequency_penalty` (numbers; absent or 0
//!   disables the penalty).
//!
//! Frames from the engine:
//!
//! - `{"op":"hello_ack","proto":1,"detail":"..."}`: handshake reply.
//!   A peer speaking another protocol version gets an `error` frame
//!   with code `protocol_mismatch` instead, so its handshake fails by
//!   name rather than by hang.
//! - `{"op":"pong","detail":"..."}`.
//! - `{"op":"debug_info", ...}`: model identity, coverage, and
//!   counters; see `debug_info` below for the field set.
//! - `{"op":"token","text":"...","token_id":N,"done":false}`: one
//!   streamed piece of the completion. A generation ends with a
//!   final token frame with `done` true and `finish_reason` set to
//!   `stop` (EOS or a stop string) or `length` (max_tokens reached);
//!   its text is empty and the completion text is the concatenation
//!   of the earlier frames' text.
//! - `{"op":"error","code":"...","message":"..."}`: a named refusal.
//!   Codes the platform maps to a client error (HTTP 400):
//!   `bad_request`, `context_overflow`, `model_not_found`,
//!   `protocol_mismatch`. Codes it maps to a gateway error (502):
//!   `forward_failed`, `detokenize_failed`, `engine_died`,
//!   `unknown_op`, `bad_frame`, `internal`. And `engine_busy` maps
//!   to 503: every slot is running and the bounded job queue is
//!   full (TODO T-9.14). One code is not an op refusal at all:
//!   `peer_refused` is sent once, before the handshake, when the
//!   connecting process runs under a different uid than the engine
//!   (the kernel reports the peer's credentials, SO_PEERCRED), and
//!   the connection closes immediately; a correct deployment, where
//!   the platform and the engine run as the same user, never sees
//!   it.

use crate::json::{obj, Value};

/// The protocol version both sides speak. The Go client refuses a
/// hello_ack carrying any other value.
pub const PROTO_VERSION: f64 = 1.0;

/// A parsed generate request.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct GenerateRequest {
    /// Model name the platform asked for; empty means no preference.
    pub model: String,
    /// The flattened prompt text.
    pub prompt: String,
    /// Requested cap on generated tokens; None for the default.
    pub max_tokens: Option<usize>,
    /// Sampling temperature; 0 is greedy.
    pub temperature: f64,
    /// Nucleus mass cap; values outside (0, 1) disable truncation.
    pub top_p: f64,
    /// Stop strings.
    pub stop: Vec<String>,
    /// Request seed for reproducible sampled runs; None means the
    /// engine seeds from the clock.
    pub seed: Option<u64>,
    /// Top-k candidate cap; None or 0 disables truncation.
    pub top_k: Option<usize>,
    /// Presence penalty (OpenAI form); 0 disables.
    pub presence_penalty: f64,
    /// Frequency penalty (OpenAI form); 0 disables.
    pub frequency_penalty: f64,
}

/// Parse a generate frame. A missing or mistyped prompt is the only
/// hard failure; the numeric fields fall back to their documented
/// defaults so an older platform frame still generates.
pub fn parse_generate(frame: &Value) -> Result<GenerateRequest, String> {
    let prompt = frame
        .get("prompt")
        .and_then(Value::as_str)
        .ok_or_else(|| "generate frame has no string prompt".to_string())?
        .to_string();
    let model = frame
        .get("model")
        .and_then(Value::as_str)
        .unwrap_or("")
        .to_string();
    let max_tokens = match frame.get("max_tokens") {
        // A present max_tokens must be a real count. Falling back
        // to the default on a malformed one would silently accept
        // exactly the frames adjudication H-1 is about (2^64, which
        // used to saturate and wrap the context check), so a
        // present-but-invalid value is a named refusal instead.
        Some(value) => Some(
            value
                .as_usize()
                .ok_or_else(|| "max_tokens is not a valid token count".to_string())?,
        ),
        None => None,
    };
    let temperature = frame
        .get("temperature")
        .and_then(Value::as_f64)
        .unwrap_or(0.0);
    let top_p = frame.get("top_p").and_then(Value::as_f64).unwrap_or(0.0);
    let stop = frame
        .get("stop")
        .and_then(Value::as_arr)
        .map(|items| {
            items
                .iter()
                .filter_map(Value::as_str)
                .map(str::to_string)
                .collect()
        })
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let seed = frame
        .get("seed")
        .and_then(Value::as_usize)
        .map(|n| n as u64);
    let top_k = frame.get("top_k").and_then(Value::as_usize);
    let presence_penalty = frame
        .get("presence_penalty")
        .and_then(Value::as_f64)
        .unwrap_or(0.0);
    let frequency_penalty = frame
        .get("frequency_penalty")
        .and_then(Value::as_f64)
        .unwrap_or(0.0);
    Ok(GenerateRequest {
        model,
        prompt,
        max_tokens,
        temperature,
        top_p,
        stop,
        seed,
        top_k,
        presence_penalty,
        frequency_penalty,
    })
}

/// A parsed embed request: the model name (empty means no
/// preference) and the input texts, in order.
pub fn parse_embed(frame: &Value) -> Result<(String, Vec<String>), String> {
    let model = frame
        .get("model")
        .and_then(Value::as_str)
        .unwrap_or("")
        .to_string();
    let items = frame
        .get("input")
        .and_then(Value::as_arr)
        .ok_or_else(|| "embed frame has no input array".to_string())?;
    if items.is_empty() {
        return Err("embed frame has an empty input array".to_string());
    }
    let mut inputs = Vec::with_capacity(items.len());
    for item in items {
        match item.as_str() {
            Some(s) if !s.is_empty() => inputs.push(s.to_string()),
            _ => return Err("embed input entries must be non-empty strings".to_string()),
        }
    }
    Ok((model, inputs))
}

/// The embeddings reply: one vector per input, in input order.
pub fn embeddings_frame(model: &str, vectors: &[Vec<f32>]) -> Value {
    obj(vec![
        ("op", Value::Str("embeddings".into())),
        ("model", Value::Str(model.into())),
        (
            "embeddings",
            Value::Arr(
                vectors
                    .iter()
                    .map(|v| Value::Arr(v.iter().map(|&x| Value::Num(f64::from(x))).collect()))
                    .collect(),
            ),
        ),
    ])
}

/// The chat template reply: the template text and the special
/// token texts its variables refer to.
pub fn chat_template_frame(template: &str, bos_token: &str, eos_token: &str) -> Value {
    obj(vec![
        ("op", Value::Str("chat_template".into())),
        ("template", Value::Str(template.into())),
        ("bos_token", Value::Str(bos_token.into())),
        ("eos_token", Value::Str(eos_token.into())),
    ])
}

/// The handshake reply.
pub fn hello_ack(detail: &str) -> Value {
    obj(vec![
        ("op", Value::Str("hello_ack".into())),
        ("proto", Value::Num(PROTO_VERSION)),
        ("detail", Value::Str(detail.into())),
    ])
}

/// The health reply.
pub fn pong(detail: &str) -> Value {
    obj(vec![
        ("op", Value::Str("pong".into())),
        ("detail", Value::Str(detail.into())),
    ])
}

/// One streamed token event, or the terminal event when `done`.
pub fn token_event(text: &str, token_id: u32, done: bool, finish_reason: Option<&str>) -> Value {
    let mut pairs = vec![
        ("op", Value::Str("token".into())),
        ("text", Value::Str(text.into())),
        ("token_id", Value::Num(f64::from(token_id))),
        ("done", Value::Bool(done)),
    ];
    if let Some(reason) = finish_reason {
        pairs.push(("finish_reason", Value::Str(reason.into())));
    }
    obj(pairs)
}

/// A named refusal.
pub fn error_frame(code: &str, message: &str) -> Value {
    obj(vec![
        ("op", Value::Str("error".into())),
        ("code", Value::Str(code.into())),
        ("message", Value::Str(message.into())),
    ])
}

    }

    }

        // Adjudication H-1's frame: max_tokens of 2^64 saturated to
        // usize::MAX and wrapped the engine's context check into
        // admitting an unbounded generation. It is now a parse
        // refusal, which the connection maps to bad_request.
        let frame = parse(r#"{"op":"generate","prompt":"x","max_tokens":18446744073709551616}"#)
            .expect("frame");

        assert!(err.contains("max_tokens"), "error: {err}");
    }

        let frame =

        let (model, inputs) = parse_embed(&frame).expect("request");
        assert_eq!(model, "glimmer");
        assert_eq!(inputs, vec!["a".to_string(), "b c".to_string()]);

        for bad in [

            assert!(parse_embed(&frame).is_err(), "expected error for {bad}");
        }
    }

    #[test]

        let text = crate::json::stringify(&frame);
        let back = parse(&text).expect("own output parses");
        assert_eq!(back.get("op").and_then(Value::as_str), Some("embeddings"));
        let vecs = back
            .get("embeddings")
            .and_then(Value::as_arr)
            .expect("vecs");
        assert_eq!(vecs.len(), 2);
    }
}
