//! Sampling over the forward's finished logits.
//!
//! The protocol carries temperature, top-p, top-k, a seed, and the
//! presence/frequency penalties from the platform's request; this
//! module is where they are honored. Temperature at or below zero
//! is greedy (argmax, lowest id on ties), which is the temperature-0
//! behavior the golden-output proofs rely on. Penalties are applied
//! first, in the OpenAI form: a token's logit drops by
//! `frequency_penalty * count + presence_penalty * (count > 0)`,
//! where the count covers the prompt tokens (fed via
//! [`Sampler::observe`]) and every token this sampler has already
//! picked. Above zero temperature, the penalized logits are
//! truncated to the top-k set when top-k is set, softened with a
//! numerically stable softmax in f64, truncated again to the
//! smallest nucleus whose mass reaches top-p (top-p outside (0, 1)
//! disables truncation), and one token is drawn from the
//! renormalized nucleus with a seeded xorshift64* generator. The
//! seed is an explicit input so a sampled run is reproducible end
//! to end (TODO T-9.13); the server seeds from the clock only when
//! the request carries no seed.

use std::collections::HashMap;

/// One generation's sampling parameters, all from the request.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub struct SamplerConfig {
    /// Sampling temperature; at or below 0 the sampler is greedy.
    pub temperature: f64,
    /// Nucleus mass cap; outside (0, 1) disables truncation.
    pub top_p: f64,
    /// Candidate set cap; 0 disables top-k truncation.
    pub top_k: usize,
    /// Flat logit penalty for any prior occurrence (OpenAI form).
    pub presence_penalty: f64,
    /// Per-occurrence logit penalty (OpenAI form).
    pub frequency_penalty: f64,
    /// Generator seed; any value is accepted (zero is remapped,
    /// xorshift has no zero state). Ignored when greedy.
    pub seed: u64,
}

impl Default for SamplerConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        SamplerConfig {
            temperature: 0.0,
            top_p: 0.0,
            top_k: 0,
            presence_penalty: 0.0,
            frequency_penalty: 0.0,
            seed: 0,
        }
    }
}

/// Greedy and stochastic token selection over one logits row, with
/// repetition state for the penalties.
pub struct Sampler {
    cfg: SamplerConfig,
    state: u64,
    counts: HashMap<u32, u32>,
}

impl Sampler {
    /// A sampler for one generation.
    pub fn new(cfg: SamplerConfig) -> Self {
        Sampler {
            cfg,
            state: if cfg.seed == 0 {
                0x9e37_79b9_7f4a_7c15
            } else {
                cfg.seed
            },
            counts: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Whether this sampler ignores its generator and takes argmax.
    pub fn is_greedy(&self) -> bool {
        self.cfg.temperature <= 0.0
    }

    /// Feed tokens into the penalty counts without sampling them:
    /// the prompt, so a penalty request counts prompt repetitions
    /// the way OpenAI's form specifies.
    pub fn observe(&mut self, tokens: &[u32]) {
        for &t in tokens {
            *self.counts.entry(t).or_insert(0) += 1;
        }
    }

    /// The penalized logit for one token id.
    fn adjusted(&self, id: u32, logit: f32) -> f64 {
        let count = self.counts.get(&id).copied().unwrap_or(0);
        if count == 0 || (self.cfg.presence_penalty == 0.0 && self.cfg.frequency_penalty == 0.0) {
            return f64::from(logit);
        }
        let mut z = f64::from(logit);
        z -= self.cfg.frequency_penalty * f64::from(count);
        if count > 0 {
            z -= self.cfg.presence_penalty;
        }
        z
    }

    /// Pick the next token id from a finished logits row. The pick
    /// joins the penalty counts, so a repeated pick costs more
    /// under the penalties than the first one did.
    pub fn pick(&mut self, logits: &[f32]) -> u32 {
        let token = self.select(logits);
        *self.counts.entry(token).or_insert(0) += 1;
        token
    }

    fn select(&mut self, logits: &[f32]) -> u32 {
        if logits.is_empty() {
            return 0;
        }
        // Penalized logits, in id order.
        let adjusted: Vec<f64> = logits
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(i, &z)| self.adjusted(i as u32, z))
            .collect();
        if self.is_greedy() || logits.len() <= 1 {
            return argmax(&adjusted);
        }
        // Candidate set: top-k by penalized logit when top-k is
        // set and smaller than the row, else the whole row.
        let mut candidates: Vec<u32> = (0..logits.len() as u32).collect();
        if self.cfg.top_k > 0 && self.cfg.top_k < candidates.len() {
            candidates.sort_by(|&a, &b| {
                adjusted[b as usize]
                    .partial_cmp(&adjusted[a as usize])
                    .unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)
                    .then(a.cmp(&b))
            });
            candidates.truncate(self.cfg.top_k);
            candidates.sort_unstable();
        }
        // Stable softmax in f64 over the candidates.
        let temp = self.cfg.temperature;
        let max = candidates
            .iter()
            .map(|&id| adjusted[id as usize])
            .fold(f64::NEG_INFINITY, f64::max);
        let mut probs: Vec<(u32, f64)> = candidates
            .iter()
            .map(|&id| (id, ((adjusted[id as usize] - max) / temp).exp()))
            .collect();
        let total: f64 = probs.iter().map(|(_, p)| p).sum();
        for (_, p) in probs.iter_mut() {
            *p /= total;
        }
        // Nucleus truncation on the probability-sorted order.
        let mut order: Vec<usize> = (0..probs.len()).collect();
        order.sort_by(|&a, &b| {
            probs[b]
                .1
                .partial_cmp(&probs[a].1)
                .unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)
                .then(probs[a].0.cmp(&probs[b].0))
        });
        let mut keep = probs.len();
        if self.cfg.top_p > 0.0 && self.cfg.top_p < 1.0 {
            let mut cumulative = 0.0;
            for (rank, &idx) in order.iter().enumerate() {
                cumulative += probs[idx].1;
                if cumulative >= self.cfg.top_p {
                    keep = rank + 1;
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        let kept_mass: f64 = order[..keep].iter().map(|&idx| probs[idx].1).sum();
        let draw = self.next_f64() * kept_mass;
        let mut cumulative = 0.0;
        for &idx in &order[..keep] {
            cumulative += probs[idx].1;
            if draw < cumulative {
                return probs[idx].0;
            }
        }
        // Floating-point edge: the draw rounded up to the kept mass.
        probs[order[keep - 1]].0
    }

    fn next_u64(&mut self) -> u64 {
        // xorshift64* (Marsaglia): full period over nonzero states.
        let mut x = self.state;
        x ^= x >> 12;
        x ^= x << 25;
        x ^= x >> 27;
        self.state = x;
        x.wrapping_mul(0x2545_f491_4f6c_dd1d)
    }

    fn next_f64(&mut self) -> f64 {
        // 53 random bits, uniform on [0, 1).
        (self.next_u64() >> 11) as f64 / (1u64 << 53) as f64
    }
}

/// The lowest id holding the maximum logit (llama.cpp's greedy tie
/// behavior, and what the reference harness's top-1 records show).
fn argmax(logits: &[f64]) -> u32 {
    let mut best = 0u32;
    let mut best_val = f64::NEG_INFINITY;
    for (i, &z) in logits.iter().enumerate() {
        if z > best_val {
            best_val = z;
            best = i as u32;
        }
    }
    best
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn cfg(temperature: f64, top_p: f64, seed: u64) -> SamplerConfig {
        SamplerConfig {
            temperature,
            top_p,
            seed,
            ..SamplerConfig::default()
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn greedy_picks_argmax_with_lowest_id_ties() {
        let mut s = Sampler::new(cfg(0.0, 0.0, 42));
        assert_eq!(s.pick(&[1.0, 3.0, 3.0, 2.0]), 1);
        assert_eq!(s.pick(&[-5.0, -9.0]), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn tiny_top_p_collapses_to_argmax() {
        // The first token's mass alone exceeds a tiny top-p for any
        // seed, so the nucleus is a single token.
        for seed in 0..16 {
            let mut s = Sampler::new(cfg(1.0, 1e-9, seed));
            assert_eq!(s.pick(&[0.0, 10.0, 0.0, 0.0]), 1, "seed {seed}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn seeded_sampling_is_deterministic() {
        let logits = [0.3, 1.2, -0.5, 2.0, 0.0, 0.7];
        let mut a = Sampler::new(cfg(0.8, 0.9, 1234));
        let mut b = Sampler::new(cfg(0.8, 0.9, 1234));
        for _ in 0..32 {
            assert_eq!(a.pick(&logits), b.pick(&logits));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn seeded_runs_match_across_a_whole_sequence() {
        // The T-9.13 determinism shape: two samplers with the same
        // full option set (seed, top-k, top-p, both penalties) fed
        // the same sequence of logits rows produce identical token
        // streams, penalty state included.
        let rows: Vec<Vec<f32>> = (0..24)
            .map(|i| {
                vec![
                    (i % 7) as f32 * 0.3,
                    1.1 - (i % 3) as f32 * 0.2,
                    0.4,
                    2.0 - (i % 5) as f32 * 0.35,
                    -0.6,
                ]
            })
            .collect();
        let full = SamplerConfig {
            temperature: 0.9,
            top_p: 0.95,
            top_k: 4,
            presence_penalty: 0.3,
            frequency_penalty: 0.2,
            seed: 777,
        };
        let run = |c: SamplerConfig| -> Vec<u32> {
            let mut s = Sampler::new(c);
            s.observe(&[3, 3, 1]);
            rows.iter().map(|row| s.pick(row)).collect()
        };
        assert_eq!(run(full), run(full));
        // A different seed diverges somewhere in the sequence with
        // overwhelming probability; if it ever does not, the seed
        // is not actually reaching the generator.
        let other = SamplerConfig { seed: 778, ..full };
        assert_ne!(run(full), run(other));
    }

    #[test]
    fn hot_sampling_spreads_across_tokens() {
        // At a huge temperature the distribution is near uniform, so
        // a run of seeded draws cannot sit on one token.
        let logits = [0.0, 0.1, -0.1, 0.05];
        let mut seen = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
        for seed in 0..200u64 {
            let mut s = Sampler::new(cfg(1.0e6, 1.0, seed.wrapping_mul(7919) + 1));
            seen.insert(s.pick(&logits));
        }
        assert!(seen.len() >= 3, "only saw {seen:?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn peaked_distribution_dominates_at_moderate_temperature() {
        let logits = [0.0, 20.0, 0.0];
        for seed in 0..16 {
            let mut s = Sampler::new(cfg(1.0, 1.0, seed * 31 + 7));
            assert_eq!(s.pick(&logits), 1, "seed {seed}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn top_k_one_is_greedy_even_sampled() {
        let logits = [0.3, 1.2, -0.5, 2.0, 0.0];
        for seed in 0..16 {
            let mut c = cfg(1.3, 1.0, seed);
            c.top_k = 1;
            let mut s = Sampler::new(c);
            assert_eq!(s.pick(&logits), 3, "seed {seed}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn frequency_penalty_pushes_the_pick_off_a_repeated_token() {
        // Token 0 leads by 0.1; after 5 observations under a 0.5
        // frequency penalty its adjusted logit drops by 2.5, so the
        // greedy pick moves to token 1. Without the penalty the
        // same history changes nothing.
        let logits = [2.0, 1.9, 0.0];
        let mut plain = Sampler::new(cfg(0.0, 0.0, 1));
        plain.observe(&[0, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
        assert_eq!(plain.pick(&logits), 0);

        let mut c = cfg(0.0, 0.0, 1);
        c.frequency_penalty = 0.5;
        let mut penalized = Sampler::new(c);
        penalized.observe(&[0, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
        assert_eq!(penalized.pick(&logits), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn presence_penalty_costs_a_token_once_regardless_of_count() {
        // Token 0 leads by 0.4. A presence penalty of 0.5 moves the
        // pick after a single observation, and further observations
        // do not move it more (contrast with frequency above).
        let logits = [2.0, 1.6, 0.0];
        let mut c = cfg(0.0, 0.0, 1);
        c.presence_penalty = 0.5;
        let mut once = Sampler::new(c);
        once.observe(&[0]);
        assert_eq!(once.pick(&logits), 1);
        let mut many = Sampler::new(c);
        many.observe(&[0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
        assert_eq!(many.pick(&logits), 1);
        // And with the weaker penalty the single hit is not enough.
        let mut weak = Sampler::new(SamplerConfig {
            presence_penalty: 0.3,
            ..c
        });
        weak.observe(&[0, 0, 0]);
        assert_eq!(weak.pick(&logits), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn picked_tokens_join_the_penalty_counts() {
        // Greedy with a frequency penalty over a constant row must
        // rotate: each pick makes its token costlier until another
        // token wins. Without the penalty the same row repeats.
        let logits = [1.0, 0.95, 0.9];
        let mut c = cfg(0.0, 0.0, 1);
        c.frequency_penalty = 0.2;
        let mut s = Sampler::new(c);
        assert_eq!(s.pick(&logits), 0);
        assert_eq!(s.pick(&logits), 1); // 0 now costs 0.2, sits at 0.8
        assert_eq!(s.pick(&logits), 2); // then 1 also sits at 0.75
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/itak-engine/src/streamer.rs =====
//! Incremental detokenization for streamed token events.
//!
//! Token bytes arrive one token at a time. A token can end in the
//! middle of a multi-byte UTF-8 character, and a stop string can
//! span two tokens, so emission is a state machine, not a per-token
//! decode:
//!
//! - Bytes accumulate until they form valid UTF-8; only complete
//!   characters are decoded (an invalid byte, which the tokenizer
//!   never produces from real vocabularies, is replaced lossily
//!   rather than stalling the stream).
//! - Decoded text accumulates in full; a stop string found anywhere
//!   in it ends the generation with the text truncated at the stop
//!   string's start.
//! - Before emitting, the longest suffix of the un-emitted text that
//!   is a proper prefix of some stop string is held back, so a stop
//!   string is never half-emitted before it completes.
//!
//! [`Streamer::finish`] flushes whatever is held when the generation
//! ends for another reason (EOS, length), so no text is lost.

/// Streaming text assembler for one generation.
pub struct Streamer {
    stops: Vec<String>,
    /// Bytes not yet decodable as UTF-8.
    pending: Vec<u8>,
    /// All decoded text so far.
    text: String,
    /// Bytes of `text` already handed to the caller.
    emitted: usize,
    /// Set once a stop string matched; the generation is over.
    stopped: bool,
}

impl Streamer {
    /// A streamer with the request's stop strings. Empty stop
    /// strings are dropped (an empty stop would match everywhere).
    pub fn new(stops: Vec<String>) -> Self {
        Streamer {
            stops: stops.into_iter().filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).collect(),
            pending: Vec::new(),
            text: String::new(),
            emitted: 0,
            stopped: false,
        }
    }

    /// Whether a stop string has matched.
    pub fn stopped(&self) -> bool {
        self.stopped
    }

    /// The full decoded text so far, truncated at a matched stop
    /// string. This is the completion text the events add up to.
    pub fn text(&self) -> &str {
        &self.text
    }

    /// Feed one token's raw bytes. Returns the text chunks to emit
    /// now (usually zero or one). After a stop match, further feeds
    /// are ignored and return nothing.
    pub fn push(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<String> {
        if self.stopped {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        self.pending.extend_from_slice(bytes);
        self.decode_pending();
        self.check_stop_and_emit()
    }

    /// Flush everything decodable at the end of a generation that
    /// finished for a reason other than a stop string.
    pub fn finish(&mut self) -> Vec<String> {
        if self.stopped {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        if !self.pending.is_empty() {
            // A truncated final character: emit it lossily rather
            // than dropping bytes the model produced.
            let rest = String::from_utf8_lossy(&self.pending).into_owned();
            self.pending.clear();
            self.text.push_str(&rest);
        }
        let tail = self.text[self.emitted..].to_string();
        self.emitted = self.text.len();
        if tail.is_empty() {
            Vec::new()
        } else {
            vec![tail]
        }
    }

    fn decode_pending(&mut self) {
        loop {
            if self.pending.is_empty() {
                return;
            }
            match std::str::from_utf8(&self.pending) {
                Ok(s) => {
                    let s = s.to_string();
                    self.pending.clear();
                    self.text.push_str(&s);
                    return;
                }
                Err(e) => {
                    let valid = e.valid_up_to();
                    match e.error_len() {
                        None => {
                            // Incomplete trailing character: keep
                            // its bytes pending, emit the valid part.
                            if valid > 0 {
                                let s =
                                    String::from_utf8_lossy(&self.pending[..valid]).into_owned();
                                self.text.push_str(&s);
                                self.pending.drain(..valid);
                            }
                            return;
                        }
                        Some(bad) => {
                            // A byte that can never complete: lossy
                            // replacement for the span, then continue
                            // with the rest.
                            let end = valid + bad;
                            let s = String::from_utf8_lossy(&self.pending[..end]).into_owned();
                            self.text.push_str(&s);
                            self.pending.drain(..end);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    fn check_stop_and_emit(&mut self) -> Vec<String> {
        // A stop occurrence always starts at or after `emitted`:
        // hold-back guarantees an earlier start would have been
        // caught before its first byte was emitted.
        let mut stop_at: Option<usize> = None;
        for stop in &self.stops {
            if let Some(idx) = self.text[self.emitted..].find(stop.as_str()) {
                let at = self.emitted + idx;
                stop_at = Some(stop_at.map_or(at, |prev: usize| prev.min(at)));
            }
        }
        if let Some(at) = stop_at {
            let chunk = self.text[self.emitted..at].to_string();
            self.text.truncate(at);
            self.emitted = at;
            self.stopped = true;
            return if chunk.is_empty() {
                Vec::new()
            } else {
                vec![chunk]
            };
        }
        let hold = self.holdback_len();
        let end = self.text.len() - hold;
        if end > self.emitted {
            let chunk = self.text[self.emitted..end].to_string();
            self.emitted = end;
            vec![chunk]
        } else {
            Vec::new()
        }
    }

    /// Length of the longest suffix of the un-emitted text that is a
    /// proper prefix of some stop string.
    fn holdback_len(&self) -> usize {
        let tail = &self.text[self.emitted..];
        let mut best = 0;
        for stop in &self.stops {
            // Proper prefixes only: a full-length match is handled
            // by the stop check, not by holding back.
            let max_k = stop.len().min(tail.len());
            for k in (1..max_k).rev() {
                if stop.is_char_boundary(k)
                    && tail.is_char_boundary(tail.len() - k)
                    && tail.ends_with(&stop[..k])
                {
                    best = best.max(k);
                    break;
                }
            }
            // Also consider k == tail length when the whole tail is
            // a proper prefix of the stop string.
            if tail.len() < stop.len() && stop.starts_with(tail) && !tail.is_empty() {
                best = best.max(tail.len());
            }
        }
        best
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn collect(streamer: &mut Streamer, feeds: &[&[u8]]) -> String {
        let mut out = String::new();
        for feed in feeds {
            for chunk in streamer.push(feed) {
                out.push_str(&chunk);
            }
        }
        for chunk in streamer.finish() {
            out.push_str(&chunk);
        }
        out
    }

    #[test]
    fn plain_ascii_streams_through() {
        let mut s = Streamer::new(vec![]);
        let out = collect(&mut s, &[b" Paris", b". It", b" is"]);
        assert_eq!(out, " Paris. It is");
        assert_eq!(s.text(), " Paris. It is");
    }

    #[test]
    fn multibyte_character_split_across_tokens() {
        // U+00E9 (e-acute) is 0xC3 0xA9: fed one byte per token.
        let mut s = Streamer::new(vec![]);
        assert!(s.push(&[0xc3]).is_empty());
        let out = collect(&mut s, &[&[0xa9]]);
        assert_eq!(out, "\u{e9}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn stop_string_split_across_tokens() {
        let mut s = Streamer::new(vec!["STOP".to_string()]);
        let mut out = String::new();
        for chunk in s.push(b"abc ST") {
            out.push_str(&chunk);
        }
        // "ST" is a stop prefix: only "abc " may be out so far.
        assert_eq!(out, "abc ");
        assert!(!s.stopped());
        for chunk in s.push(b"OP and more") {
            out.push_str(&chunk);
        }
        assert!(s.stopped());
        assert_eq!(out, "abc ");
        assert_eq!(s.text(), "abc ");
    }

    #[test]
    fn stop_at_token_boundary_and_empty_stop_ignored() {
        let mut s = Streamer::new(vec![String::new(), "END".to_string()]);
        let out = collect(&mut s, &[b"hello ", b"END", b"trailing"]);
        assert_eq!(out, "hello ");
        assert!(s.stopped());
    }

    #[test]
    fn held_back_prefix_flushes_on_finish() {
        let mut s = Streamer::new(vec!["STOP".to_string()]);
        let mut out = String::new();
        for chunk in s.push(b"abc ST") {
            out.push_str(&chunk);
        }
        assert_eq!(out, "abc ");
        for chunk in s.finish() {
            out.push_str(&chunk);
        }
        assert_eq!(out, "abc ST");
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/itak-kv/src/config.rs =====
//! Store configuration: where the prefix store lives and how big
//! it may grow, resolved from the environment in the codebase's
//! fail-closed style (named env vars, exact spellings, malformed
//! values logged and fallen back, never silently widened).
//!
//! - `ITAK_KV_PREFIX_STORE`: the master switch for the session
//!   seam. Only the exact value `1` enables; unset or anything else
//!   is off. Default off.
//! - `ITAK_KV_PREFIX_DIR`: the store root directory. Unset means
//!   `$HOME/.cache/itak/prefix-kv` (or a `prefix-kv` directory
//!   under the system temp dir when `HOME` is unset).
//! - `ITAK_KV_PREFIX_MAX_BYTES`: the store's byte cap. Unset or
//!   malformed means [`DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES`]; the cap is a config
//!   value with a default, never a compiled-in limit on callers,
//!   who may always pass their own [`StoreConfig`].

use std::path::PathBuf;

/// Env var naming the store root directory.
pub const DIR_ENV: &str = "ITAK_KV_PREFIX_DIR";
/// Env var naming the store byte cap.
pub const MAX_BYTES_ENV: &str = "ITAK_KV_PREFIX_MAX_BYTES";
/// Env var switching the prefix store seam on.
pub const ENABLE_ENV: &str = "ITAK_KV_PREFIX_STORE";

/// Default byte cap for the store: 8 GiB. At Glimmer geometry a
/// stored prefix costs about 104 KiB per token before the sliding
/// windows saturate (see the crate's bench note), so the default
/// holds roughly thirty 4k-token prefixes or two full-context
/// snapshots.
pub const DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES: u64 = 8 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024;

/// Whether the prefix store seam is enabled, resolved from a raw
/// env value: only the exact string `"1"` (after trimming) turns
/// it on. This is the codebase's fail-closed switch shape (the
/// K21F head switch resolves the same way): unset, `"0"`, `"true"`,
/// and every other value are off.
#[must_use]
pub fn prefix_store_enabled_from(raw: Option<&str>) -> bool {
    matches!(raw.map(str::trim), Some("1"))
}

/// Whether the prefix store seam is enabled in this process.
#[must_use]
pub fn prefix_store_enabled() -> bool {
    prefix_store_enabled_from(std::env::var(ENABLE_ENV).ok().as_deref())
}

/// Resolve the byte cap from a raw env value: a parsable positive
/// integer wins; unset means the default; a present but malformed
/// or zero value falls back to the default and is logged by name
/// (a cap is a bound, not a gate, so the fallback is the named
/// default rather than the closed position a switch would take).
#[must_use]
pub fn max_bytes_from(raw: Option<&str>) -> u64 {
    match raw.map(str::trim) {
        None => DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES,
        Some(text) => match text.parse::<u64>() {
            Ok(bytes) if bytes > 0 => bytes,
            _ => {
                crate::diag!(
                    "{MAX_BYTES_ENV} value {text:?} is not a positive byte count; \
                     falling back to the default cap {DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES}"
                );
                DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES
            }
        },
    }
}

/// The default store root when [`DIR_ENV`] is unset.
#[must_use]
pub fn default_root() -> PathBuf {
    if let Some(home) = std::env::var_os("HOME") {
        if !home.is_empty() {
            return PathBuf::from(home)
                .join(".cache")
                .join("itak")
                .join("prefix-kv");
        }
    }
    std::env::temp_dir().join("itak-prefix-kv")
}

/// Fully resolved store configuration.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct StoreConfig {
    /// Root directory holding one file per entry.
    pub root: PathBuf,
    /// Byte cap across all entries; LRU eviction enforces it.
    pub max_bytes: u64,
}

impl StoreConfig {
    /// A config with an explicit root and the default cap.
    pub fn new(root: PathBuf) -> Self {
        StoreConfig {
            root,
            max_bytes: DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES,
        }
    }

    /// Resolve the config from the process environment.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn from_env() -> Self {
        let root = std::env::var_os(DIR_ENV)
            .filter(|value| !value.is_empty())
            .map(PathBuf::from)
            .unwrap_or_else(default_root);
        let max_bytes = max_bytes_from(std::env::var(MAX_BYTES_ENV).ok().as_deref());
        StoreConfig { root, max_bytes }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn enable_switch_is_exact_one_only() {
        assert!(prefix_store_enabled_from(Some("1")));
        assert!(prefix_store_enabled_from(Some(" 1 ")));
        assert!(!prefix_store_enabled_from(None));
        assert!(!prefix_store_enabled_from(Some("0")));
        assert!(!prefix_store_enabled_from(Some("true")));
        assert!(!prefix_store_enabled_from(Some("11")));
        assert!(!prefix_store_enabled_from(Some("")));
    }

    #[test]
    fn cap_resolution() {
        assert_eq!(max_bytes_from(None), DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES);
        assert_eq!(max_bytes_from(Some("1024")), 1024);
        assert_eq!(max_bytes_from(Some(" 2048 ")), 2048);
        assert_eq!(max_bytes_from(Some("0")), DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES);
        assert_eq!(max_bytes_from(Some("-5")), DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES);
        assert_eq!(max_bytes_from(Some("lots")), DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES);
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/itak-kv/src/diag.rs =====
//! Diagnostics for the itak-kv crate.
//!
//! Debug logging behind a runtime flag (off by default), per the
//! standing rule that every module ships with a way to see what it
//! did and why it refused. Enable with [`set_debug_enabled`] or the
//! `ITAK_KV_DEBUG` environment variable (checked on every
//! [`debug_enabled`] call, the gguf shape, so a shipped binary can
//! turn the seam on with no code change). Lines go to stderr with a
//! fixed `[itak-kv::diag]` prefix so they can be grepped out of a
//! server log. For programmatic diagnosis without any logging,
//! [`crate::PrefixStore::stats`] returns the store's state directly.

use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};

static DEBUG_ENABLED: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);

/// Turn debug logging on or off at runtime.
pub fn set_debug_enabled(enabled: bool) {
    DEBUG_ENABLED.store(enabled, Ordering::Relaxed);
}

/// Whether debug logging is currently on: the explicit flag, or
/// `ITAK_KV_DEBUG` present in the environment (any value other
/// than `0` or empty).
pub fn debug_enabled() -> bool {
    if DEBUG_ENABLED.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
        return true;
    }
    match std::env::var("ITAK_KV_DEBUG") {
        Ok(v) => v != "0" && !v.is_empty(),
        Err(_) => false,
    }
}

/// Emit one already-formatted diagnostic line: the [`crate::diag`]
/// macro's single output path, so test builds capture exactly what
/// stderr receives and can prove the seam fired.
pub fn emit_debug(formatted: &str) {
    #[cfg(test)]
    capture(&format!("[itak-kv::diag] {formatted}"));
    eprintln!("[itak-kv::diag] {formatted}");
}

/// Test-only capture of emitted debug lines, so unit tests can prove
/// the seam actually fired instead of trusting that the macro call is
/// present in the source (the gguf channel's shape). Lines are the
/// exact formatted output; tests assert on their own probe strings,
/// which are unique per test, so parallel tests sharing this buffer
/// cannot satisfy each other's assertions.
#[cfg(test)]
static CAPTURED: std::sync::Mutex<Vec<String>> = std::sync::Mutex::new(Vec::new());

#[cfg(test)]
fn capture(line: &str) {
    CAPTURED
        .lock()
        .unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())
        .push(line.to_string());
}

/// The debug lines captured since the process started (test builds
/// only).
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) fn captured_lines() -> Vec<String> {
    CAPTURED.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner()).clone()
}

/// Emit one structured diagnostic line to stderr when debug is on.
///
/// Usage: `crate::diag!("put tokens={} bytes={}", n, bytes)`.
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! diag {
    ($($arg:tt)*) => {
        if $crate::diag::debug_enabled() {
            $crate::diag::emit_debug(&::std::format!($($arg)*));
        }
    };
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Serializes this crate's diag tests: the flag and the env var
    /// are process-global, so two tests flipping them in parallel
    /// would satisfy (or break) each other's assertions.
    static DIAG_TEST_LOCK: std::sync::Mutex<()> = std::sync::Mutex::new(());

    #[test]
    fn env_twin_enables_debug() {
        let _guard = DIAG_TEST_LOCK.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        set_debug_enabled(false);
        std::env::remove_var("ITAK_KV_DEBUG");
        assert!(!debug_enabled());
        std::env::set_var("ITAK_KV_DEBUG", "1");
        assert!(
            debug_enabled(),
            "ITAK_KV_DEBUG=1 must enable debug (the gguf env-twin contract)"
        );
        std::env::set_var("ITAK_KV_DEBUG", "0");
        assert!(!debug_enabled(), "ITAK_KV_DEBUG=0 must not enable debug");
        std::env::set_var("ITAK_KV_DEBUG", "");
        assert!(
            !debug_enabled(),
            "an empty ITAK_KV_DEBUG must not enable debug"
        );
        std::env::remove_var("ITAK_KV_DEBUG");
        assert!(!debug_enabled());
    }
    #[test]
    fn seam_fires_when_on_and_is_silent_when_off() {
        let _guard = DIAG_TEST_LOCK.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        std::env::remove_var("ITAK_KV_DEBUG");
        set_debug_enabled(false);
        crate::diag!("silent probe itak_kv_off_probe");
        assert!(
            !captured_lines()
                .iter()
                .any(|l| l.contains("itak_kv_off_probe")),
            "the seam must stay silent while debug is off"
        );
        set_debug_enabled(true);
        crate::diag!("firing probe itak_kv_on_probe");
        set_debug_enabled(false);
        assert!(
            captured_lines()
                .iter()
                .any(|l| l.contains("[itak-kv::diag]") && l.contains("itak_kv_on_probe")),
            "the seam must emit its prefixed line while debug is on"
        );
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/itak-kv/src/error.rs =====
//! Named errors for the itak-kv crate. Every fallible operation
//! returns one of these; nothing in this crate panics on a corrupt
//! file, a mismatched geometry, or a forged entry supplied by a
//! caller or read back from disk.

use std::fmt;

use attention::AttentionError;

/// Everything that can go wrong in the snapshot codec or the
/// prefix store.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum KvError {
    /// The attention crate refused an operation while capturing or
    /// restoring a snapshot.
    Attention(AttentionError),
    /// A token prefix of length zero was offered to the store; an
    /// empty prefix matches everything and stores nothing, so it is
    /// refused rather than indexed.
    EmptyPrefix,
    /// A snapshot's token count disagrees with the token list it was
    /// offered under.
    TokenCountMismatch {
        /// Token count inside the snapshot.
        snapshot: usize,
        /// Token count in the offered token list.
        tokens: usize,
    },
    /// The token ids stored in an entry do not hash to the entry's
    /// key: the entry is forged or corrupt and is never applied.
    PrefixHashMismatch {
        /// The key the entry is filed under.
        stored: u64,
        /// The hash of the token ids the entry actually carries.
        computed: u64,
    },
    /// An entry's preamble token count disagrees with the token
    /// count inside its snapshot payload.
    SnapshotTokenMismatch {
        /// Token count in the entry preamble.
        entry: usize,
        /// Token count inside the snapshot.
        snapshot: usize,
    },
    /// A byte stream does not start with the expected magic.
    BadMagic {
        /// Which format was being read ("snapshot" or "entry").
        what: &'static str,
    },
    /// A byte stream carries a format version this build does not
    /// read.
    UnsupportedVersion {
        /// Which format was being read ("snapshot" or "entry").
        what: &'static str,
        /// The version found in the stream.
        version: u32,
    },
    /// A byte stream ends before its own header says it should.
    Truncated {
        /// Which format was being read.
        what: &'static str,
        /// Bytes the header requires.
        expected: usize,
        /// Bytes actually present.
        actual: usize,
    },
    /// A snapshot's trailing checksum does not match its contents.
    ChecksumMismatch {
        /// The checksum stored in the stream.
        stored: u64,
        /// The checksum computed over the stream.
        computed: u64,
    },
    /// A snapshot's per-layer rows do not add up against its own
    /// header (token count, windows, row widths).
    InconsistentSnapshot {
        /// What does not add up.
        detail: String,
    },
    /// A snapshot's geometry differs from the geometry the caller
    /// requires (layer pattern, KV heads, or head dimension).
    GeometryMismatch {
        /// What differs.
        detail: String,
    },
    /// A snapshot's model fingerprint differs from the fingerprint
    /// the caller requires.
    FingerprintMismatch {
        /// The fingerprint the caller requires.
        expected: String,
        /// The fingerprint the snapshot carries.
        actual: String,
    },
    /// A live cache cannot be snapshotted because its layers do not
    /// agree on one position (a cache is snapshotted as one
    /// sequence, so every layer must have appended the same number
    /// of positions).
    IncoherentCache {
        /// What disagrees.
        detail: String,
    },
    /// One entry is larger than the store's whole byte cap; it is
    /// refused at `put` time instead of evicting everything else
    /// and still not fitting.
    EntryTooLarge {
        /// The entry's size in bytes.
        bytes: u64,
        /// The store's byte cap.
        cap: u64,
    },
    /// A configuration value (env override or caller argument) is
    /// unusable as given.
    InvalidConfig {
        /// What is wrong with it.
        detail: String,
    },
    /// A filesystem operation failed.
    Io {
        /// What the code was doing when it failed.
        context: String,
        /// The operating system's message.
        message: String,
    },
}

impl KvError {
    /// Wrap an `io::Error` with the operation that produced it.
    pub(crate) fn io(context: impl Into<String>, error: std::io::Error) -> Self {
        KvError::Io {
            context: context.into(),
            message: error.to_string(),
        }
    }
}

impl From<AttentionError> for KvError {
    fn from(error: AttentionError) -> Self {
        KvError::Attention(error)
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for KvError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            KvError::Attention(e) => write!(f, "attention: {e}"),
            KvError::EmptyPrefix => write!(f, "empty token prefix refused"),
            KvError::TokenCountMismatch { snapshot, tokens } => write!(
                f,
                "snapshot covers {snapshot} tokens but was offered under {tokens} token ids"
            ),
            KvError::PrefixHashMismatch { stored, computed } => write!(
                f,
                "stored token ids hash to {computed:#018x}, not the entry key {stored:#018x}; entry refused"
            ),
            KvError::SnapshotTokenMismatch { entry, snapshot } => write!(
                f,
                "entry preamble covers {entry} tokens but its snapshot covers {snapshot}"
            ),
            KvError::BadMagic { what } => write!(f, "{what}: bad magic"),
            KvError::UnsupportedVersion { what, version } => {
                write!(f, "{what}: unsupported format version {version}")
            }
            KvError::Truncated {
                what,
                expected,
                actual,
            } => write!(f, "{what}: truncated, needs {expected} bytes, has {actual}"),
            KvError::ChecksumMismatch { stored, computed } => write!(
                f,
                "snapshot checksum mismatch: stored {stored:#018x}, computed {computed:#018x}"
            ),
            KvError::InconsistentSnapshot { detail } => {
                write!(f, "inconsistent snapshot: {detail}")
            }
            KvError::GeometryMismatch { detail } => write!(f, "geometry mismatch: {detail}"),
            KvError::FingerprintMismatch { expected, actual } => write!(
                f,
                "model fingerprint mismatch: need {expected}, snapshot carries {actual}"
            ),
            KvError::IncoherentCache { detail } => write!(f, "incoherent cache: {detail}"),
            KvError::EntryTooLarge { bytes, cap } => {
                write!(f, "entry of {bytes} bytes exceeds the store cap of {cap} bytes")
            }
            KvError::InvalidConfig { detail } => write!(f, "invalid config: {detail}"),
            KvError::Io { context, message } => write!(f, "{context}: {message}"),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for KvError {}

===== END FILE: crates/itak-kv/src/error.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/itak-kv/src/hash.rs =====
//! Prefix keying: FNV-1a 64 over the token ids, the same hash the
//! diag capture fingerprints use elsewhere in this workspace.
//!
//! The hash is an INDEX, never a proof. Two different token
//! sequences may share a key (a collision), so every entry also
//! stores its full token-id list, and a lookup only ever hits after
//! comparing the stored ids against the query's prefix token for
//! token. A collision therefore costs a wasted candidate read; it
//! can never produce a wrong hit. A stored id list whose hash does
//! not reproduce the entry's key is treated as forged or corrupt
//! and refused by name ([`crate::KvError::PrefixHashMismatch`]).

/// FNV-1a 64 offset basis.
const FNV_OFFSET: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;
/// FNV-1a 64 prime.
const FNV_PRIME: u64 = 0x0000_0100_0000_01b3;

/// An alternate offset basis for the discriminator hash, so an
/// entry filename depends on two independent hashes of the same
/// token list.
const ALT_OFFSET: u64 = 0x8422_2325_cbf2_9ce4;

/// FNV-1a 64 over raw bytes, from an explicit offset basis.
fn fnv1a(bytes: &[u8], basis: u64) -> u64 {
    let mut hash = basis;
    for &byte in bytes {
        hash ^= u64::from(byte);
        hash = hash.wrapping_mul(FNV_PRIME);
    }
    hash
}

/// Feed one token id into a running FNV-1a state (little-endian
/// bytes, matching the on-disk token encoding).
fn fnv1a_token(mut hash: u64, token: u32) -> u64 {
    for byte in token.to_le_bytes() {
        hash ^= u64::from(byte);
        hash = hash.wrapping_mul(FNV_PRIME);
    }
    hash
}

/// The prefix key for a token-id sequence.
#[must_use]
pub fn prefix_hash(tokens: &[u32]) -> u64 {
    tokens.iter().fold(FNV_OFFSET, |h, &t| fnv1a_token(h, t))
}

/// A second, independent hash of the same token list, used as the
/// filename discriminator so two colliding prefixes do not fight
/// over one filename.
#[must_use]
pub fn prefix_discriminator(tokens: &[u32]) -> u64 {
    tokens.iter().fold(ALT_OFFSET, |h, &t| fnv1a_token(h, t))
}

/// FNV-1a 64 over a byte slice (the snapshot payload checksum).
#[must_use]
pub fn checksum(bytes: &[u8]) -> u64 {
    fnv1a(bytes, FNV_OFFSET)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn hash_is_order_and_value_sensitive() {
        assert_ne!(prefix_hash(&[1, 2, 3]), prefix_hash(&[3, 2, 1]));
        assert_ne!(prefix_hash(&[1, 2, 3]), prefix_hash(&[1, 2, 4]));
        assert_ne!(prefix_hash(&[1, 2]), prefix_hash(&[1, 2, 0]));
        assert_eq!(prefix_hash(&[]), FNV_OFFSET);
    }

    #[test]
    fn discriminator_is_a_distinct_hash() {
        let tokens = [7_u32, 8, 9, 10];
        assert_ne!(prefix_hash(&tokens), prefix_discriminator(&tokens));
        // And it is deterministic: the same list names the same file.
        assert_eq!(prefix_discriminator(&tokens), prefix_discriminator(&tokens));
    }

    #[test]
    fn checksum_matches_fnv1a_of_empty_and_nonempty() {
        assert_eq!(checksum(&[]), FNV_OFFSET);
        assert_ne!(checksum(b"itkv"), checksum(b"itkw"));
    }
}

//! itak-kv: KV storage contracts for the iTaK Torch rebuild
//! (TODO T-2.4).
//!
//! The `attention` crate owns the in-memory KV cache. This crate
//! owns everything that makes KV state outlive a process:
//!
//! - [`snapshot`]: the versioned [`KvSnapshot`] format. A snapshot
//!   is the KV state of exactly one sequence prefix, captured from
//!   an `attention` [`KvCache`](attention::KvCache), serializable
//!   to bytes with a trailing checksum, and restorable into a
//!   fresh cache with named refusals for anything corrupt,
//!   truncated, or geometrically foreign.
//! - [`store`]: [`PrefixStore`], the persistent tiered prefix-KV
//!   store. Entries are keyed by the hash of a token-id prefix,
//!   carry the full token-id list so a hit is verified token for
//!   token (never trusted from the hash alone), are written
//!   atomically, and are evicted least-recently-used under a byte
//!   cap that is configuration with a default, not a constant.
//!   Lookup returns the longest stored prefix of a query.
//! - [`config`]: the environment resolution for the store (root
//!   directory, byte cap, and the fail-closed master switch the
//!   session seam will consult).
//!
//! The session wiring (a `ResidentSession` restore path that
//! installs a snapshot into device KV and continues from the
//! first unmatched token) is specified in
//! `bench/prefix-kv-store-2026-11-07.md`; this crate provides the
//! store, the format, the switch, and the KV-state-level restore
//! ([`KvSnapshot::restore`]) that the wiring consumes.
//!
//! Everything is f32 reference data, no unsafe, named errors
//! instead of panics on anything read from disk, and debug logging
//! behind a flag (see [`diag`]).

#![forbid(unsafe_code)]

pub mod config;
pub mod diag;
pub mod error;
pub mod hash;
pub mod snapshot;
pub mod store;

pub use config::{
    default_root, max_bytes_from, prefix_store_enabled, prefix_store_enabled_from, StoreConfig,
    DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES, DIR_ENV, ENABLE_ENV, MAX_BYTES_ENV,
};
pub use error::KvError;
pub use hash::{checksum, prefix_discriminator, prefix_hash};
pub use snapshot::{KvGeometry, KvSnapshot, LayerSnapshot, SNAPSHOT_FORMAT_VERSION};
pub use store::{now_unix, EntryMeta, PrefixHit, PrefixStore, StoreStats, ENTRY_FORMAT_VERSION};
