===== FILE: crates/itak-kv/src/snapshot.rs =====
//! The versioned KV snapshot format: the KV state of exactly one
//! sequence prefix, serializable to bytes and restorable into a
//! fresh [`KvCache`].
//!
//! A snapshot covers positions `0..token_count` of one sequence.
//! Per layer it stores only the rows still visible at that point:
//! every row for a global layer, and the last `window` rows for a
//! windowed layer (older rows were evicted by the ring and no
//! consumer can ever see them again, so storing them would be
//! dead weight). Each layer block names its `first_position`, so
//! the restore side replays appends in true position order.
//!
//! Byte layout (all integers little-endian):
//!
//! ```text
//! magic "ITKV"            [4]u8
//! format_version          u32   (= 1)
//! fingerprint_len         u32, then that many UTF-8 bytes
//! token_count             u64
//! num_kv_heads            u32
//! head_dim                u32
//! layer_count             u32
//! per layer: kind u8 (0 global, 1 windowed), 3 reserved zero
//!            bytes, window u64 (0 for global), first_position
//!            u64, row_count u64
//! per layer: keys   (row_count * kv_heads * head_dim) f32
//!            values (same count) f32
//! checksum                u64   FNV-1a 64 over all preceding bytes
//! ```
//!
//! Decoding is strict and total: bad magic, an unknown version, a
//! short buffer, a checksum mismatch, or per-layer rows that do
//! not add up against the header each refuse by name, and a
//! snapshot is only ever handed out whole. Restoring builds a
//! fresh cache and returns it only when every append succeeded,
//! so a refused snapshot leaves nothing partially applied.

use attention::{KvCache, LayerKind};

use crate::error::KvError;
use crate::hash;

/// Snapshot format magic.
const MAGIC: &[u8; 4] = b"ITKV";
/// Bytes one layer header costs on the wire: kind tag (1),
/// reserved (3), window (8), first_position (8), row_count (8).
/// The decoder bounds the declared layer count against this
/// before the count is allowed to size an allocation.
const LAYER_HEADER_LEN: usize = 28;
/// The snapshot format version this build writes and reads.
pub const SNAPSHOT_FORMAT_VERSION: u32 = 1;

/// The layer geometry a snapshot is bound to: the layer pattern
/// plus the KV width every layer shares. A snapshot restores only
/// into this exact geometry.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct KvGeometry {
    /// One entry per layer, in layer order.
    pub layers: Vec<LayerKind>,
    /// KV heads per layer.
    pub num_kv_heads: usize,
    /// Dimension of each KV head.
    pub head_dim: usize,
}

impl KvGeometry {
    /// Floats in one position's row for one of K or V:
    /// `[num_kv_heads][head_dim]` laid out flat.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn row_floats(&self) -> usize {
        self.num_kv_heads * self.head_dim
    }

    /// The row width as a checked product. `num_kv_heads` and
    /// `head_dim` arrive from file bytes on the decode path, and
    /// their product can overflow `usize`; every consumer that
    /// trusts the width against stored data (the decoder, the
    /// validator) goes through here and refuses by name instead
    /// of wrapping in release builds or panicking in debug
    /// builds. [`KvGeometry::row_floats`] stays for geometry
    /// built from a live cache, whose fields the cache itself
    /// already bounded.
    fn row_floats_checked(&self) -> Result<usize, KvError> {
        self.num_kv_heads
            .checked_mul(self.head_dim)
            .ok_or_else(|| KvError::InconsistentSnapshot {
                detail: format!(
                    "KV row width overflows: {} heads of dim {} have no usize product",
                    self.num_kv_heads, self.head_dim
                ),
            })
    }

    /// Payload bytes one token of prefix adds before any window
    /// saturates: every layer stores one K row and one V row per
    /// token. Saturating: this is a sizing estimate over geometry
    /// fields, and a foreign geometry must saturate the estimate,
    /// never wrap or panic it.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn bytes_per_token(&self) -> u64 {
        let per_layer = (self.row_floats() as u64).saturating_mul(8);
        per_layer.saturating_mul(self.layers.len() as u64)
    }

    /// Payload bytes a snapshot of a `tokens`-long prefix carries
    /// under this geometry: global layers store every row,
    /// windowed layers store at most `window` rows. Saturating,
    /// for the same reason as [`KvGeometry::bytes_per_token`].
    #[must_use]
    pub fn stored_bytes_for(&self, tokens: usize) -> u64 {
        let per_row = (self.row_floats() as u64).saturating_mul(8);
        let rows: u64 = self.layers.iter().fold(0_u64, |total, kind| {
            let layer_rows = match kind {
                LayerKind::Global => tokens as u64,
                LayerKind::Windowed { window } => tokens.min(*window) as u64,
            };
            total.saturating_add(layer_rows)
        });
        rows.saturating_mul(per_row)
    }

    /// The geometry of a live cache.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn of_cache(cache: &KvCache) -> Self {
        let layers = (0..cache.layer_count())
            .map(|layer| {
                cache
                    .layer_kind(layer)
                    .expect("layer index from the cache's own count")
            })
            .collect();
        KvGeometry {
            layers,
            num_kv_heads: cache.num_kv_heads(),
            head_dim: cache.head_dim(),
        }
    }
}

/// One layer's stored rows inside a snapshot: the visible rows at
/// capture time, oldest first, each row `row_floats` long for keys
/// and the same for values.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct LayerSnapshot {
    /// Absolute position of the first stored row.
    pub first_position: usize,
    /// Key rows, oldest first, flattened.
    pub keys: Vec<f32>,
    /// Value rows, oldest first, flattened.
    pub values: Vec<f32>,
}

impl LayerSnapshot {
    /// Stored row count, given the geometry's row width.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn rows(&self, row_floats: usize) -> usize {
        self.keys.len().checked_div(row_floats).unwrap_or(0)
    }
}

/// A whole-sequence-prefix KV snapshot.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct KvSnapshot {
    /// The geometry the rows belong to.
    pub geometry: KvGeometry,
    /// Opaque model identity (for example the GGUF file's SHA-256
    /// hex). Recorded at capture; a restore may require an exact
    /// match so KV from one model is never served to another.
    pub model_fingerprint: String,
    /// Positions the snapshot covers: `0..token_count`.
    pub token_count: usize,
    /// One block per layer, in layer order.
    pub layers: Vec<LayerSnapshot>,
}

impl KvSnapshot {
    /// Check the snapshot against its own header: layer count,
    /// per-layer first positions and row counts implied by the
    /// token count and windows, and exact row widths. Called by
    /// both the encoder and the decoder, so a snapshot that exists
    /// in memory has already passed the same checks a file must.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`KvError::InconsistentSnapshot`] naming the first
    /// disagreement.
    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), KvError> {
        let geometry = &self.geometry;
        if self.layers.len() != geometry.layers.len() {
            return Err(inconsistent(format!(
                "snapshot carries {} layer blocks but its geometry has {} layers",
                self.layers.len(),
                geometry.layers.len()
            )));
        }
        if geometry.num_kv_heads == 0 || geometry.head_dim == 0 {
            return Err(inconsistent(
                "geometry has a zero KV head count or head dimension".to_string(),
            ));
        }
        let row = geometry.row_floats_checked()?;
        for (index, (kind, layer)) in geometry.layers.iter().zip(&self.layers).enumerate() {
            let expected_rows = match kind {
                LayerKind::Global => self.token_count,
                LayerKind::Windowed { window } => self.token_count.min(*window),
            };
            let expected_first = self.token_count - expected_rows;
            if layer.first_position != expected_first {
                return Err(inconsistent(format!(
                    "layer {index}: first stored position is {} but {expected_first} follows \
                     from token count {} and kind {kind:?}",
                    layer.first_position, self.token_count
                )));
            }
            // Checked: token_count and the row width both arrive
            // from file bytes, and their product can reach 2^64,
            // where an unchecked multiply wrapped release builds
            // to a length that matched the stored rows (accepting
            // a forged snapshot) and panicked debug builds.
            let expected_floats = expected_rows.checked_mul(row).ok_or_else(|| {
                inconsistent(format!(
                    "layer {index}: {expected_rows} rows of {row} floats overflow \
                     the float count"
                ))
            })?;
            if layer.keys.len() != expected_floats || layer.values.len() != expected_floats {
                return Err(inconsistent(format!(
                    "layer {index}: holds {} key and {} value floats but {expected_rows} rows \
                     of {row} floats were expected",
                    layer.keys.len(),
                    layer.values.len()
                )));
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Capture a snapshot of a live cache. Every layer must have
    /// appended the same number of positions (the cache is one
    /// sequence); a cache mid-round with divergent layer positions
    /// is refused by name instead of being frozen half-way.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`KvError::IncoherentCache`] on divergent layer positions,
    /// or an attention refusal while reading a layer view.
    pub fn capture(cache: &KvCache, model_fingerprint: impl Into<String>) -> Result<Self, KvError> {
        let geometry = KvGeometry::of_cache(cache);
        let token_count = cache.next_position(0)?;
        let row = geometry.row_floats();
        let mut layers = Vec::with_capacity(geometry.layers.len());
        for index in 0..geometry.layers.len() {
            let appended = cache.next_position(index)?;
            if appended != token_count {
                return Err(KvError::IncoherentCache {
                    detail: format!(
                        "layer 0 has appended {token_count} positions but layer {index} has \
                         appended {appended}; a snapshot is one sequence"
                    ),
                });
            }
            let view = cache.view(index)?;
            let visible = view.len();
            let mut keys = Vec::with_capacity(visible * row);
            let mut values = Vec::with_capacity(visible * row);
            for slot in 0..visible {
                for head in 0..geometry.num_kv_heads {
                    let key = view
                        .key(slot, head)
                        .ok_or_else(|| KvError::IncoherentCache {
                            detail: format!("layer {index} view has no key row at slot {slot}"),
                        })?;
                    let value = view
                        .value(slot, head)
                        .ok_or_else(|| KvError::IncoherentCache {
                            detail: format!("layer {index} view has no value row at slot {slot}"),
                        })?;
                    keys.extend_from_slice(key);
                    values.extend_from_slice(value);
                }
            }
            layers.push(LayerSnapshot {
                first_position: token_count - visible,
                keys,
                values,
            });
        }
        let snapshot = KvSnapshot {
            geometry,
            model_fingerprint: model_fingerprint.into(),
            token_count,
            layers,
        };
        snapshot.validate()?;
        crate::diag!(
            "snapshot captured tokens={} layers={} payload_bytes={}",
            snapshot.token_count,
            snapshot.layers.len(),
            snapshot.geometry.stored_bytes_for(snapshot.token_count)
        );
        Ok(snapshot)
    }

    /// Restore the snapshot into a fresh cache. Each layer is
    /// installed through the attention crate's bulk-restore
    /// constructor ([`KvCache::restore_bulk`]), which writes the
    /// stored rows directly into their ring slots: no append
    /// replay, and in particular no zero rows replayed for the
    /// positions a windowed layer has already evicted (the
    /// replay this replaces cost roughly 160 MB of host-side
    /// zero traffic at a 4k-token Glimmer prefix, and
    /// seconds-scale work at full context). The bulk state is
    /// exactly the replay's state (see the constructor's own
    /// contract), and the fresh cache is returned only on full
    /// success.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`KvError::InconsistentSnapshot`] on a self-disagreeing
    /// snapshot, or an attention refusal while building the cache.
    pub fn restore(&self) -> Result<KvCache, KvError> {
        self.validate()?;
        let geometry = &self.geometry;
        let mut cache = KvCache::new(&geometry.layers, geometry.num_kv_heads, geometry.head_dim)?;
        for (index, layer) in self.layers.iter().enumerate() {
            cache.restore_bulk(index, layer.first_position, &layer.keys, &layer.values)?;
        }
        crate::diag!(
            "snapshot restored tokens={} layers={}",
            self.token_count,
            self.layers.len()
        );
        Ok(cache)
    }

    /// Restore after requiring an exact geometry and model
    /// fingerprint match: the store's trust check, so KV captured
    /// for one model or layer geometry is never served to another.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`KvError::GeometryMismatch`] or
    /// [`KvError::FingerprintMismatch`] naming the difference,
    /// then whatever [`KvSnapshot::restore`] refuses.
    pub fn restore_checked(
        &self,
        expected_geometry: &KvGeometry,
        expected_fingerprint: &str,
    ) -> Result<KvCache, KvError> {
        if self.geometry != *expected_geometry {
            return Err(KvError::GeometryMismatch {
                detail: format!(
                    "snapshot geometry ({} layers, {} KV heads, head dim {}) differs from the \
                     required geometry ({} layers, {} KV heads, head dim {})",
                    self.geometry.layers.len(),
                    self.geometry.num_kv_heads,
                    self.geometry.head_dim,
                    expected_geometry.layers.len(),
                    expected_geometry.num_kv_heads,
                    expected_geometry.head_dim,
                ),
            });
        }
        if self.model_fingerprint != expected_fingerprint {
            return Err(KvError::FingerprintMismatch {
                expected: expected_fingerprint.to_string(),
                actual: self.model_fingerprint.clone(),
            });
        }
        self.restore()
    }

    /// Serialize to the versioned byte format (see the module
    /// docs). Validates first: bytes that cannot be produced by a
    /// coherent snapshot are never written.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`KvError::InconsistentSnapshot`] on a self-disagreeing
    /// snapshot.
    pub fn to_bytes(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, KvError> {
        self.validate()?;
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        out.extend_from_slice(MAGIC);
        out.extend_from_slice(&SNAPSHOT_FORMAT_VERSION.to_le_bytes());
        let fingerprint = self.model_fingerprint.as_bytes();
        out.extend_from_slice(&(fingerprint.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(fingerprint);
        out.extend_from_slice(&(self.token_count as u64).to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&(self.geometry.num_kv_heads as u32).to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&(self.geometry.head_dim as u32).to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&(self.geometry.layers.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
        for (kind, layer) in self.geometry.layers.iter().zip(&self.layers) {
            let (tag, window) = match kind {
                LayerKind::Global => (0_u8, 0_u64),
                LayerKind::Windowed { window } => (1_u8, *window as u64),
            };
            out.push(tag);
            out.extend_from_slice(&[0, 0, 0]);
            out.extend_from_slice(&window.to_le_bytes());
            out.extend_from_slice(&(layer.first_position as u64).to_le_bytes());
            out.extend_from_slice(&(layer.rows(self.geometry.row_floats()) as u64).to_le_bytes());
        }
        for layer in &self.layers {
            for value in &layer.keys {
                out.extend_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
            }
            for value in &layer.values {
                out.extend_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
            }
        }
        let sum = hash::checksum(&out);
        out.extend_from_slice(&sum.to_le_bytes());
        Ok(out)
    }

    /// Decode the versioned byte format. Strict: any disagreement
    /// refuses the whole snapshot by name.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`KvError::BadMagic`], [`KvError::UnsupportedVersion`],
    /// [`KvError::Truncated`], [`KvError::ChecksumMismatch`], or
    /// [`KvError::InconsistentSnapshot`].
    pub fn from_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, KvError> {
        let mut reader = Reader::new(bytes);
        if reader.take(4)? != MAGIC {
            return Err(KvError::BadMagic { what: "snapshot" });
        }
        let version = reader.u32()?;
        if version != SNAPSHOT_FORMAT_VERSION {
            return Err(KvError::UnsupportedVersion {
                what: "snapshot",
                version,
            });
        }
        let fingerprint_len = reader.u32()? as usize;
        let fingerprint_bytes = reader.take(fingerprint_len)?;
        let model_fingerprint = String::from_utf8(fingerprint_bytes.to_vec()).map_err(|_| {
            KvError::InconsistentSnapshot {
                detail: "model fingerprint is not valid UTF-8".to_string(),
            }
        })?;
        let token_count = reader.u64_usize("token count")?;
        let num_kv_heads = reader.u32()? as usize;
        let head_dim = reader.u32()? as usize;
        let layer_count = reader.u32()? as usize;
        // Every layer header costs LAYER_HEADER_LEN bytes on the
        // wire, so a count that cannot fit in the bytes remaining
        // is impossible (the same argument the GGUF parser uses
        // for metadata arrays). The refusal must land here, before
        // the count sizes any allocation: an unvalidated count of
        // u32::MAX otherwise demands tens of gigabytes up front
        // and aborts the process, which no error handler can
        // catch, ahead of every other trust check in the format.
        if layer_count > reader.remaining() / LAYER_HEADER_LEN {
            return Err(inconsistent(format!(
                "snapshot declares {layer_count} layers but only {} bytes remain, \
                 not enough for the layer headers alone",
                reader.remaining()
            )));
        }
        let mut kinds = Vec::with_capacity(layer_count);
        let mut blocks = Vec::with_capacity(layer_count);
        for _ in 0..layer_count {
            let tag = reader.take(1)?[0];
            let reserved = reader.take(3)?;
            if reserved != [0, 0, 0] {
                return Err(inconsistent(
                    "layer header reserved bytes are not zero".to_string(),
                ));
            }
            let window = reader.u64()?;
            let first_position = reader.u64_usize("first position")?;
            let row_count = reader.u64_usize("row count")?;
            let kind = match tag {
                0 => LayerKind::Global,
                1 => LayerKind::windowed(usize::try_from(window).map_err(|_| {
                    KvError::InconsistentSnapshot {
                        detail: "window does not fit in usize".to_string(),
                    }
                })?)
                .map_err(|_| KvError::InconsistentSnapshot {
                    detail: "windowed layer carries a zero window".to_string(),
                })?,
                other => {
                    return Err(inconsistent(format!(
                        "layer kind tag {other} is not a known kind"
                    )))
                }
            };
            kinds.push(kind);
            blocks.push((first_position, row_count));
        }
        let geometry = KvGeometry {
            layers: kinds,
            num_kv_heads,
            head_dim,
        };
        let row = geometry.row_floats_checked()?;
        let mut layers = Vec::with_capacity(layer_count);
        for (first_position, row_count) in blocks {
            let floats =
                row_count
                    .checked_mul(row)
                    .ok_or_else(|| KvError::InconsistentSnapshot {
                        detail: "layer row count overflows the row width".to_string(),
                    })?;
            let keys = reader.f32s(floats)?;
            let values = reader.f32s(floats)?;
            layers.push(LayerSnapshot {
                first_position,
                keys,
                values,
            });
        }
        let stored_checksum = reader.u64()?;
        if reader.remaining() != 0 {
            return Err(inconsistent(format!(
                "{} trailing bytes after the checksum",
                reader.remaining()
            )));
        }
        let computed = hash::checksum(&bytes[..bytes.len() - 8]);
        if stored_checksum != computed {
            return Err(KvError::ChecksumMismatch {
                stored: stored_checksum,
                computed,
            });
        }
        let snapshot = KvSnapshot {
            geometry,
            model_fingerprint,
            token_count,
            layers,
        };
        snapshot.validate()?;
        Ok(snapshot)
    }
}

fn inconsistent(detail: String) -> KvError {
    KvError::InconsistentSnapshot { detail }
}

/// A strict little-endian cursor over a snapshot byte stream.
struct Reader<'a> {
    bytes: &'a [u8],
    at: usize,
}

impl<'a> Reader<'a> {
    fn new(bytes: &'a [u8]) -> Self {
        Reader { bytes, at: 0 }
    }

    fn remaining(&self) -> usize {
        self.bytes.len() - self.at
    }

    fn take(&mut self, n: usize) -> Result<&'a [u8], KvError> {
        if self.remaining() < n {
            return Err(KvError::Truncated {
                what: "snapshot",
                expected: self.at + n,
                actual: self.bytes.len(),
            });
        }
        let slice = &self.bytes[self.at..self.at + n];
        self.at += n;
        Ok(slice)
    }

    fn u32(&mut self) -> Result<u32, KvError> {
        let bytes = self.take(4)?;
        Ok(u32::from_le_bytes(
            bytes.try_into().expect("take(4) yields 4 bytes"),
        ))
    }

    fn u64(&mut self) -> Result<u64, KvError> {
        let bytes = self.take(8)?;
        Ok(u64::from_le_bytes(
            bytes.try_into().expect("take(8) yields 8 bytes"),
        ))
    }

    fn u64_usize(&mut self, what: &str) -> Result<usize, KvError> {
        let value = self.u64()?;
        usize::try_from(value).map_err(|_| KvError::InconsistentSnapshot {
            detail: format!("{what} does not fit in usize"),
        })
    }

    fn f32s(&mut self, count: usize) -> Result<Vec<f32>, KvError> {
        let byte_count = count
            .checked_mul(4)
            .ok_or_else(|| KvError::InconsistentSnapshot {
                detail: "float count overflows the byte count".to_string(),
            })?;
        let bytes = self.take(byte_count)?;
        Ok(bytes
            .chunks_exact(4)
            .map(|chunk| f32::from_le_bytes(chunk.try_into().expect("chunks of 4")))
            .collect())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn geometry() -> KvGeometry {
        KvGeometry {
            layers: vec![
                LayerKind::Windowed { window: 4 },
                LayerKind::Global,
                LayerKind::Windowed { window: 4 },
            ],
            num_kv_heads: 2,
            head_dim: 3,
        }
    }

    fn filled_cache(tokens: usize) -> KvCache {
        let geometry = geometry();
        let mut cache = KvCache::new(&geometry.layers, geometry.num_kv_heads, geometry.head_dim)
            .expect("fixture geometry builds");
        let row = geometry.row_floats();
        for position in 0..tokens {
            for layer in 0..geometry.layers.len() {
                let k: Vec<f32> = (0..row)
                    .map(|i| (position * 100 + layer * 10 + i) as f32 / 7.0)
                    .collect();
                let v: Vec<f32> = (0..row)
                    .map(|i| -((position * 50 + layer * 5 + i) as f32) / 3.0)
                    .collect();
                cache
                    .append(layer, &k, &v, position)
                    .expect("in-order appends");
            }
        }
        cache
    }

    #[test]
    fn bytes_round_trip() {
        let cache = filled_cache(10);
        let snapshot = KvSnapshot::capture(&cache, "model-a").expect("capture");
        let bytes = snapshot.to_bytes().expect("encode");
        let decoded = KvSnapshot::from_bytes(&bytes).expect("decode");
        assert_eq!(decoded, snapshot);
    }

    #[test]
    fn restore_rebuilds_the_same_views() {
        let cache = filled_cache(10);
        let snapshot = KvSnapshot::capture(&cache, "model-a").expect("capture");
        let restored = snapshot.restore().expect("restore");
        for layer in 0..3 {
            assert_eq!(
                restored.next_position(layer).expect("position"),
                cache.next_position(layer).expect("position")
            );
            let want = cache.view(layer).expect("view");
            let got = restored.view(layer).expect("view");
            assert_eq!(got.len(), want.len());
            for slot in 0..want.len() {
                assert_eq!(got.position_at(slot), want.position_at(slot));
                for head in 0..2 {
                    assert_eq!(got.key(slot, head), want.key(slot, head));
                    assert_eq!(got.value(slot, head), want.value(slot, head));
                }
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn restore_can_continue_appending() {
        let cache = filled_cache(6);
        let snapshot = KvSnapshot::capture(&cache, "model-a").expect("capture");
        let mut restored = snapshot.restore().expect("restore");
        let row = geometry().row_floats();
        let k = vec![1.5; row];
        let v = vec![-2.5; row];
        for layer in 0..3 {
            restored.append(layer, &k, &v, 6).expect("append at 6");
        }
        assert_eq!(restored.next_position(0).expect("position"), 7);
    }

    #[test]
    fn capture_refuses_a_divergent_cache() {
        // A cache whose layers disagree on position cannot be built
        // through balanced appends; simulate by appending to one
        // layer only.
        let geometry = geometry();
        let mut cache = KvCache::new(&geometry.layers, geometry.num_kv_heads, geometry.head_dim)
            .expect("builds");
        let row = geometry.row_floats();
        cache
            .append(0, &vec![0.0; row], &vec![0.0; row], 0)
            .expect("append");
        let error = KvSnapshot::capture(&cache, "model-a").expect_err("must refuse");
        assert!(matches!(error, KvError::IncoherentCache { .. }), "{error}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn decode_refuses_corruption() {
        let cache = filled_cache(5);
        let snapshot = KvSnapshot::capture(&cache, "model-a").expect("capture");
        let mut bytes = snapshot.to_bytes().expect("encode");
        // Flip a payload byte: the checksum must catch it.
        let at = bytes.len() - 12;
        bytes[at] ^= 0xff;
        let error = KvSnapshot::from_bytes(&bytes).expect_err("must refuse");
        assert!(matches!(error, KvError::ChecksumMismatch { .. }), "{error}");
        // Truncation refuses by name too.
        let error = KvSnapshot::from_bytes(&bytes[..8]).expect_err("must refuse");
        assert!(matches!(error, KvError::Truncated { .. }), "{error}");
        // Bad magic refuses by name.
        let mut bad = snapshot.to_bytes().expect("encode");
        bad[0] = b'X';
        let error = KvSnapshot::from_bytes(&bad).expect_err("must refuse");
        assert!(matches!(error, KvError::BadMagic { .. }), "{error}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn restore_checked_refuses_geometry_and_fingerprint() {
        let cache = filled_cache(4);
        let snapshot = KvSnapshot::capture(&cache, "model-a").expect("capture");
        let mut other = geometry();
        other.head_dim = 9;
        let error = snapshot
            .restore_checked(&other, "model-a")
            .expect_err("must refuse");
        assert!(matches!(error, KvError::GeometryMismatch { .. }), "{error}");
        let error = snapshot
            .restore_checked(&geometry(), "model-b")
            .expect_err("must refuse");
        assert!(
            matches!(error, KvError::FingerprintMismatch { .. }),
            "{error}"
        );
        snapshot
            .restore_checked(&geometry(), "model-a")
            .expect("matching checks restore");
    }

    #[test]
    fn decode_refuses_a_layer_count_that_cannot_fit_the_buffer() {
        // Critic panel regression (security seat, executed probe):
        // a 32-byte header declaring layer_count = u32::MAX made
        // the decoder pre-allocate ~68.7 GB from the unvalidated
        // count and the process ABORTED (an allocation failure is
        // not a catchable error). The count must be refused by
        // name before it sizes any allocation: every layer header
        // costs 28 bytes on the wire, so a count larger than the
        // remaining bytes divided by 28 is impossible.
        let mut bytes = Vec::new();
        bytes.extend_from_slice(MAGIC);
        bytes.extend_from_slice(&SNAPSHOT_FORMAT_VERSION.to_le_bytes());
        bytes.extend_from_slice(&0_u32.to_le_bytes()); // fingerprint len
        bytes.extend_from_slice(&0_u64.to_le_bytes()); // token count
        bytes.extend_from_slice(&1_u32.to_le_bytes()); // KV heads
        bytes.extend_from_slice(&1_u32.to_le_bytes()); // head dim
        bytes.extend_from_slice(&u32::MAX.to_le_bytes()); // layer count
        assert_eq!(bytes.len(), 32);
        let error = KvSnapshot::from_bytes(&bytes).expect_err("must refuse by name");
        assert!(
            matches!(error, KvError::InconsistentSnapshot { .. }),
            "{error}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn decode_refuses_geometry_whose_row_products_overflow() {
        // Critic panel regression (failure seat, executed probe):
        // token_count 2^32 with heads x dim = 2^32 and zero stored
        // rows was ACCEPTED by release builds (the expected-rows
        // product in validate() wrapped to exactly the stored
        // length) and PANICKED debug builds ("attempt to multiply
        // with overflow"), so the two profiles disagreed about
        // validity. Both profiles must refuse by name: the row
        // width and the expected float counts are checked
        // products, never wrapped ones.
        let build = |heads: u32, dim: u32, token_count: u64| {
            let mut bytes = Vec::new();
            bytes.extend_from_slice(MAGIC);
            bytes.extend_from_slice(&SNAPSHOT_FORMAT_VERSION.to_le_bytes());
            bytes.extend_from_slice(&1_u32.to_le_bytes()); // fingerprint len
            bytes.push(b'x');
            bytes.extend_from_slice(&token_count.to_le_bytes());
            bytes.extend_from_slice(&heads.to_le_bytes());
            bytes.extend_from_slice(&dim.to_le_bytes());
            bytes.extend_from_slice(&1_u32.to_le_bytes()); // one layer
            bytes.push(0); // global layer
            bytes.extend_from_slice(&[0, 0, 0]); // reserved
            bytes.extend_from_slice(&0_u64.to_le_bytes()); // window
            bytes.extend_from_slice(&0_u64.to_le_bytes()); // first position
            bytes.extend_from_slice(&0_u64.to_le_bytes()); // row count
            let sum = crate::hash::checksum(&bytes);
            bytes.extend_from_slice(&sum.to_le_bytes());
            bytes
        };
        // expected_rows * row = 2^32 * 2^32 = 2^64 overflows.
        let error =
            KvSnapshot::from_bytes(&build(65536, 65536, 1 << 32)).expect_err("must refuse by name");
        assert!(
            matches!(error, KvError::InconsistentSnapshot { .. }),
            "{error}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn validate_refuses_geometry_whose_row_width_overflows() {
        // The row width itself: two u32 wire fields cannot
        // overflow a 64-bit usize product, but a snapshot built
        // in memory (the fields are public, and validate() is
        // the gate restore() trusts) can carry heads x dim with
        // no usize product. validate() must refuse that by name
        // too, not wrap (release) or panic (debug).
        let foreign = KvSnapshot {
            geometry: KvGeometry {
                layers: vec![LayerKind::Global],
                num_kv_heads: 1 << 32,
                head_dim: 1 << 32,
            },
            model_fingerprint: "x".to_string(),
            token_count: 0,
            layers: vec![LayerSnapshot {
                first_position: 0,
                keys: Vec::new(),
                values: Vec::new(),
            }],
        };
        let error = foreign.validate().expect_err("must refuse by name");
        assert!(
            matches!(error, KvError::InconsistentSnapshot { .. }),
            "{error}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn glimmer_sizing_math() {
        // The recorded Glimmer geometry: 52 layers (39 windowed at
        // 2048, 13 global), 2 KV heads, head dim 128.
        let layers = attention::glimmer_layer_pattern();
        let geometry = KvGeometry {
            layers,
            num_kv_heads: 2,
            head_dim: 128,
        };
        // 52 layers * 2 (K and V) * 256 floats * 4 bytes.
        assert_eq!(geometry.bytes_per_token(), 106_496);
        // A 4096-token prefix: global layers hold 4096 rows,
        // windowed layers hold 2048.
        assert_eq!(geometry.stored_bytes_for(4096), 272_629_760);
        // Full context: 13 * 131072 + 39 * 2048 stored rows.
        assert_eq!(geometry.stored_bytes_for(131_072), 3_653_238_784);
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/itak-kv/src/store.rs =====
//! The persistent prefix store: one file per entry under a root
//! directory, entries keyed by token prefix, the whole store
//! bounded by a byte cap with LRU eviction.
//!
//! Entry file layout (all integers little-endian):
//!
//! ```text
//! preamble, fixed 72 bytes:
//!   magic "ITKVPENT"        [8]u8
//!   format_version          u32   (= 1)
//!   reserved                u32   (zero)
//!   created_unix            u64
//!   last_used_unix          u64   (offset 24; rewritten in place
//!                                  on a verified hit)
//!   prefix_hash             u64
//!   token_count             u64
//!   tokens_bytes            u64   (= 4 * token_count)
//!   payload_bytes           u64   (the snapshot's byte length)
//!   reserved                u64   (zero)
//! token ids                 token_count * u32
//! snapshot bytes            payload_bytes (see snapshot.rs)
//! ```
//!
//! Trust model: the filename and the preamble are an index, never
//! a proof. A lookup candidate is only a hit after the stored
//! token ids hash back to the entry's key AND equal the query's
//! prefix token for token AND the snapshot payload decodes (its
//! own checksum and self-consistency checks) AND its token count
//! matches the preamble AND, when the caller requires them, its
//! geometry and model fingerprint match. Any failure refuses that
//! entry by name in the diag log and moves to the next-longest
//! candidate; a forged or corrupt entry is never applied and
//! never stops a shorter honest prefix from serving.
//!
//! Writes are atomic: the entry is written to a `.tmp-` file in
//! the same directory, synced, and renamed over its final name.
//! A torn temp file left by a crashed writer is ignored by the
//! scanner (it never carries the `.kv` suffix) and a torn final
//! file fails its decode checks and is refused by name.
//!
//! Last-used is the preamble stamp, updated by an 8-byte in-place
//! write on a verified hit (never a content rewrite: entries can
//! be gigabytes). Eviction runs after every `put`: while the
//! store is over its cap, the least recently used entry other
//! than the one just written is deleted. An entry that alone
//! exceeds the cap is refused at `put` time.
//!
//! The index is built by scanning the directory at `open` and is
//! maintained by this instance's own `put`/`lookup` calls; files
//! another process writes after `open` are not seen until the
//! store is reopened. That is the session model: a serving
//! process opens the store once at startup.

use std::fs;
use std::io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

use crate::config::StoreConfig;
use crate::error::KvError;
use crate::hash;
use crate::snapshot::{KvGeometry, KvSnapshot};

/// Entry file magic.
const ENTRY_MAGIC: &[u8; 8] = b"ITKVPENT";
/// The entry format version this build writes and reads.
pub const ENTRY_FORMAT_VERSION: u32 = 1;
/// Fixed preamble length in bytes.
const PREAMBLE_LEN: usize = 72;
/// Byte offset of the last-used stamp inside the preamble.
const LAST_USED_OFFSET: u64 = 24;
/// Entry filename suffix.
const ENTRY_SUFFIX: &str = ".kv";
/// Temp filename prefix; temp files are never indexed.
const TEMP_PREFIX: &str = ".tmp-";

/// One indexed entry: everything the store knows without opening
/// the payload.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct EntryMeta {
    /// Filename inside the store root.
    pub file_name: String,
    /// The prefix key (hash of the stored token ids).
    pub prefix_hash: u64,
    /// Token count of the stored prefix.
    pub token_count: usize,
    /// Total file size in bytes (the eviction accounting unit).
    pub bytes: u64,
    /// Creation stamp (unix seconds, caller-supplied clock).
    pub created_unix: u64,
    /// Last verified-hit stamp (unix seconds).
    pub last_used_unix: u64,
}

/// A verified lookup result: the matched prefix and its snapshot.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct PrefixHit {
    /// How many leading tokens of the query the entry covers.
    pub token_count: usize,
    /// The stored token ids (equal to the query's first
    /// `token_count` ids; returned so callers can log exactly what
    /// was trusted).
    pub tokens: Vec<u32>,
    /// The decoded, verified KV snapshot for those positions.
    pub snapshot: KvSnapshot,
}

/// Point-in-time store state, for diagnostics.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct StoreStats {
    /// Indexed entries.
    pub entries: usize,
    /// Sum of indexed entry file sizes.
    pub total_bytes: u64,
    /// The byte cap in force.
    pub max_bytes: u64,
}

/// The current unix time in seconds (the production clock for
/// entry stamps; tests pass their own).
#[must_use]
pub fn now_unix() -> u64 {
    SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_secs())
        .unwrap_or(0)
}

/// The persistent prefix store.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct PrefixStore {
    root: PathBuf,
    max_bytes: u64,
    entries: Vec<EntryMeta>,
}

impl PrefixStore {
    /// Open (creating if needed) the store described by `config`,
    /// scanning the root and indexing every well-formed entry.
    /// Malformed final files are refused by name in the diag log
    /// and left on disk, unindexed; temp files are ignored.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`KvError::InvalidConfig`] on a zero cap, or
    /// [`KvError::Io`] when the root cannot be created or read.
    pub fn open(config: &StoreConfig) -> Result<Self, KvError> {
        if config.max_bytes == 0 {
            return Err(KvError::InvalidConfig {
                detail: "the store byte cap is zero".to_string(),
            });
        }
        fs::create_dir_all(&config.root)
            .map_err(|e| KvError::io(format!("create store root {}", config.root.display()), e))?;
        let mut store = PrefixStore {
            root: config.root.clone(),
            max_bytes: config.max_bytes,
            entries: Vec::new(),
        };
        store.rescan()?;
        crate::diag!(
            "prefix store opened root={} entries={} bytes={} cap={}",
            store.root.display(),
            store.entries.len(),
            store.total_bytes(),
            store.max_bytes
        );
        Ok(store)
    }

    /// The store root directory.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn root(&self) -> &Path {
        &self.root
    }

    /// Indexed entries, longest prefix first.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn entries(&self) -> Vec<EntryMeta> {
        let mut entries = self.entries.clone();
        entries.sort_by_key(|e| std::cmp::Reverse(e.token_count));
        entries
    }

    /// Point-in-time store state.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn stats(&self) -> StoreStats {
        StoreStats {
            entries: self.entries.len(),
            total_bytes: self.total_bytes(),
            max_bytes: self.max_bytes,
        }
    }

    fn total_bytes(&self) -> u64 {
        self.entries.iter().map(|e| e.bytes).sum()
    }

    /// Rebuild the index from the directory. Public so a long-lived
    /// store can pick up entries another writer added.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`KvError::Io`] when the root cannot be listed.
    pub fn rescan(&mut self) -> Result<(), KvError> {
        let mut entries = Vec::new();
        let listing = fs::read_dir(&self.root)
            .map_err(|e| KvError::io(format!("list store root {}", self.root.display()), e))?;
        for item in listing {
            let item = item.map_err(|e| KvError::io("read store root entry".to_string(), e))?;
            let file_name = item.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
            if file_name.starts_with(TEMP_PREFIX) || !file_name.ends_with(ENTRY_SUFFIX) {
                continue;
            }
            match read_preamble(&item.path()) {
                Ok(meta) => entries.push(meta),
                Err(error) => {
                    crate::diag!("prefix store refuses entry {file_name}: {error}");
                }
            }
        }
        self.entries = entries;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Store `snapshot` under the prefix `tokens`, stamped `now`.
    /// Replaces any existing entry carrying the same token list.
    /// Afterwards, evicts least-recently-used entries until the
    /// store is within its cap.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`KvError::EmptyPrefix`], [`KvError::TokenCountMismatch`],
    /// [`KvError::EntryTooLarge`] when the entry alone exceeds the
    /// cap, a snapshot encode refusal, or [`KvError::Io`].
    pub fn put(&mut self, tokens: &[u32], snapshot: &KvSnapshot, now: u64) -> Result<(), KvError> {
        if tokens.is_empty() {
            return Err(KvError::EmptyPrefix);
        }
        if snapshot.token_count != tokens.len() {
            return Err(KvError::TokenCountMismatch {
                snapshot: snapshot.token_count,
                tokens: tokens.len(),
            });
        }
        let payload = snapshot.to_bytes()?;
        let key = hash::prefix_hash(tokens);
        let entry_bytes = (PREAMBLE_LEN + tokens.len() * 4 + payload.len()) as u64;
        if entry_bytes > self.max_bytes {
            return Err(KvError::EntryTooLarge {
                bytes: entry_bytes,
                cap: self.max_bytes,
            });
        }
        let file_name = self.pick_file_name(tokens, key)?;
        let path = self.root.join(&file_name);
        // Atomic write: temp file in the same directory, sync,
        // rename over the final name.
        let temp_name = format!("{TEMP_PREFIX}{file_name}-{}", std::process::id());
        let temp_path = self.root.join(&temp_name);
        let preamble = encode_preamble(&Preamble {
            created_unix: now,
            last_used_unix: now,
            prefix_hash: key,
            token_count: tokens.len(),
            payload_bytes: payload.len() as u64,
        });
        {
            let mut file = fs::File::create(&temp_path)
                .map_err(|e| KvError::io(format!("create temp entry {temp_name}"), e))?;
            file.write_all(&preamble)
                .and_then(|()| {
                    for token in tokens {
                        file.write_all(&token.to_le_bytes())?;
                    }
                    file.write_all(&payload)
                })
                .and_then(|()| file.sync_all())
                .map_err(|e| KvError::io(format!("write temp entry {temp_name}"), e))?;
        }
        fs::rename(&temp_path, &path)
            .map_err(|e| KvError::io(format!("rename entry {file_name}"), e))?;
        crate::diag!(
            "prefix store put tokens={} bytes={entry_bytes} file={file_name}",
            tokens.len()
        );
        // Replace any prior index record for this file, then index
        // the new entry.
        self.entries.retain(|e| e.file_name != file_name);
        self.entries.push(EntryMeta {
            file_name,
            prefix_hash: key,
            token_count: tokens.len(),
            bytes: entry_bytes,
            created_unix: now,
            last_used_unix: now,
        });
        self.evict_except(&self.entries.last().expect("just pushed").file_name.clone())
    }

    /// Find the longest stored prefix of `query` and return its
    /// verified snapshot, or `None` when no stored prefix matches.
    /// When `expected_geometry` / `expected_fingerprint` are given,
    /// a candidate whose snapshot disagrees is refused by name and
    /// the search continues to shorter prefixes. A verified hit
    /// restamps the entry's last-used time to `now` (an 8-byte
    /// in-place write).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`KvError::Io`] when a candidate file cannot be read at
    /// all; verification failures of individual candidates are
    /// named refusals in the diag log, not errors.
    pub fn lookup(
        &mut self,
        query: &[u32],
        expected_geometry: Option<&KvGeometry>,
        expected_fingerprint: Option<&str>,
        now: u64,
    ) -> Result<Option<PrefixHit>, KvError> {
        let mut candidates: Vec<EntryMeta> = self
            .entries
            .iter()
            .filter(|e| e.token_count <= query.len())
            .cloned()
            .collect();
        candidates.sort_by_key(|e| std::cmp::Reverse(e.token_count));
        for candidate in candidates {
            match self.verify_candidate(&candidate, query, expected_geometry, expected_fingerprint)
            {
                Ok(Some(hit)) => {
                    self.touch(&candidate.file_name, now)?;
                    if let Some(meta) = self
                        .entries
                        .iter_mut()
                        .find(|e| e.file_name == candidate.file_name)
                    {
                        meta.last_used_unix = now;
                    }
                    crate::diag!(
                        "prefix store hit tokens={} file={}",
                        hit.token_count,
                        candidate.file_name
                    );
                    return Ok(Some(hit));
                }
                Ok(None) => {}
                Err(error) => {
                    crate::diag!(
                        "prefix store refuses entry {}: {error}",
                        candidate.file_name
                    );
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(None)
    }

    /// Read and fully verify one candidate against the query.
    /// `Ok(None)` means the entry is well-formed but is not a
    /// prefix of the query (a hash collision or a different branch
    /// of the prefix tree); `Err` means the entry failed a trust
    /// check and was refused by name.
    fn verify_candidate(
        &self,
        meta: &EntryMeta,
        query: &[u32],
        expected_geometry: Option<&KvGeometry>,
        expected_fingerprint: Option<&str>,
    ) -> Result<Option<PrefixHit>, KvError> {
        let path = self.root.join(&meta.file_name);
        let bytes = fs::read(&path)
            .map_err(|e| KvError::io(format!("read entry {}", meta.file_name), e))?;
        let preamble = parse_preamble(&bytes)?;
        if preamble.prefix_hash != meta.prefix_hash || preamble.token_count != meta.token_count {
            return Err(KvError::InconsistentSnapshot {
                detail: format!(
                    "entry {} changed between scan and read (index hash {:#x} / {} tokens, \
                     file hash {:#x} / {} tokens)",
                    meta.file_name,
                    meta.prefix_hash,
                    meta.token_count,
                    preamble.prefix_hash,
                    preamble.token_count
                ),
            });
        }
        let tokens_end = PREAMBLE_LEN + preamble.token_count * 4;
        if bytes.len() < tokens_end {
            return Err(KvError::Truncated {
                what: "entry",
                expected: tokens_end,
                actual: bytes.len(),
            });
        }
        let mut tokens = Vec::with_capacity(preamble.token_count);
        for chunk in bytes[PREAMBLE_LEN..tokens_end].chunks_exact(4) {
            tokens.push(u32::from_le_bytes(chunk.try_into().expect("chunks of 4")));
        }
        // Trust check 1: the stored ids must hash back to the key.
        let computed = hash::prefix_hash(&tokens);
        if computed != preamble.prefix_hash {
            return Err(KvError::PrefixHashMismatch {
                stored: preamble.prefix_hash,
                computed,
            });
        }
        // Prefix check: not an error, just not this query's branch.
        if tokens.as_slice() != &query[..tokens.len()] {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        // Trust check 2: the payload must decode whole and agree
        // with the preamble.
        let payload = &bytes[tokens_end..];
        if payload.len() as u64 != preamble.payload_bytes {
            return Err(KvError::Truncated {
                what: "entry payload",
                expected: preamble.payload_bytes as usize,
                actual: payload.len(),
            });
        }
        let snapshot = KvSnapshot::from_bytes(payload)?;
        if snapshot.token_count != preamble.token_count {
            return Err(KvError::SnapshotTokenMismatch {
                entry: preamble.token_count,
                snapshot: snapshot.token_count,
            });
        }
        // Trust check 3: caller-required geometry and fingerprint.
        if let Some(geometry) = expected_geometry {
            if snapshot.geometry != *geometry {
                return Err(KvError::GeometryMismatch {
                    detail: format!(
                        "entry {} snapshot geometry differs from the required geometry",
                        meta.file_name
                    ),
                });
            }
        }
        if let Some(fingerprint) = expected_fingerprint {
            if snapshot.model_fingerprint != fingerprint {
                return Err(KvError::FingerprintMismatch {
                    expected: fingerprint.to_string(),
                    actual: snapshot.model_fingerprint.clone(),
                });
            }
        }
        Ok(Some(PrefixHit {
            token_count: preamble.token_count,
            tokens,
            snapshot,
        }))
    }

    /// Choose the filename for a put: the hash/length/discriminator
    /// name, unless another entry with different tokens already
    /// owns it (a double hash collision), in which case a counter
    /// suffix disambiguates.
    fn pick_file_name(&self, tokens: &[u32], key: u64) -> Result<String, KvError> {
        let disc = hash::prefix_discriminator(tokens);
        let base = format!("{key:016x}-{}-{disc:016x}", tokens.len());
        for counter in 0..1024_u32 {
            let name = if counter == 0 {
                format!("{base}{ENTRY_SUFFIX}")
            } else {
                format!("{base}-c{counter}{ENTRY_SUFFIX}")
            };
            match self.entries.iter().find(|e| e.file_name == name) {
                None => {
                    // The name may still exist on disk from a writer
                    // this instance has not indexed; check the ids.
                    let path = self.root.join(&name);
                    if path.exists() {
                        if let Ok(existing) = read_entry_tokens(&path) {
                            if existing == tokens {
                                return Ok(name);
                            }
                            continue;
                        }
                    }
                    return Ok(name);
                }
                Some(meta) => {
                    let path = self.root.join(&name);
                    if let Ok(existing) = read_entry_tokens(&path) {
                        if existing == tokens {
                            return Ok(name);
                        }
                    }
                    let _ = meta;
                    continue;
                }
            }
        }
        Err(KvError::InvalidConfig {
            detail: format!(
                "no free filename for prefix hash {key:#x} after 1024 collisions; \
                 the store directory is not behaving like a prefix store"
            ),
        })
    }

    /// Rewrite one entry's last-used stamp in place.
    fn touch(&self, file_name: &str, now: u64) -> Result<(), KvError> {
        let path = self.root.join(file_name);
        let mut file = fs::OpenOptions::new()
            .write(true)
            .open(&path)
            .map_err(|e| KvError::io(format!("open entry {file_name} to restamp"), e))?;
        file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(LAST_USED_OFFSET))
            .and_then(|_| file.write_all(&now.to_le_bytes()))
            .map_err(|e| KvError::io(format!("restamp entry {file_name}"), e))?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Evict least-recently-used entries (never `keep`) until the
    /// store is within its cap.
    fn evict_except(&mut self, keep: &str) -> Result<(), KvError> {
        while self.total_bytes() > self.max_bytes {
            let victim = self
                .entries
                .iter()
                .filter(|e| e.file_name != keep)
                .min_by(|a, b| {
                    a.last_used_unix
                        .cmp(&b.last_used_unix)
                        .then_with(|| a.file_name.cmp(&b.file_name))
                })
                .map(|e| e.file_name.clone());
            let Some(victim) = victim else {
                // Only the kept entry remains and it alone fits by
                // construction (put refuses oversize entries), so
                // this is unreachable unless the cap shrank after
                // the fact; stop rather than evict the new entry.
                break;
            };
            let path = self.root.join(&victim);
            fs::remove_file(&path).map_err(|e| KvError::io(format!("evict entry {victim}"), e))?;
            self.entries.retain(|e| e.file_name != victim);
            crate::diag!("prefix store evicted {victim} (LRU, over cap)");
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// The decoded entry preamble.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Preamble {
    created_unix: u64,
    last_used_unix: u64,
    prefix_hash: u64,
    token_count: usize,
    payload_bytes: u64,
}

fn encode_preamble(preamble: &Preamble) -> [u8; PREAMBLE_LEN] {
    let mut out = [0_u8; PREAMBLE_LEN];
    out[0..8].copy_from_slice(ENTRY_MAGIC);
    out[8..12].copy_from_slice(&ENTRY_FORMAT_VERSION.to_le_bytes());
    out[16..24].copy_from_slice(&preamble.created_unix.to_le_bytes());
    out[24..32].copy_from_slice(&preamble.last_used_unix.to_le_bytes());
    out[32..40].copy_from_slice(&preamble.prefix_hash.to_le_bytes());
    out[40..48].copy_from_slice(&(preamble.token_count as u64).to_le_bytes());
    out[48..56].copy_from_slice(&((preamble.token_count * 4) as u64).to_le_bytes());
    out[56..64].copy_from_slice(&preamble.payload_bytes.to_le_bytes());
    out
}

fn parse_preamble(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Preamble, KvError> {
    if bytes.len() < PREAMBLE_LEN {
        return Err(KvError::Truncated {
            what: "entry",
            expected: PREAMBLE_LEN,
            actual: bytes.len(),
        });
    }
    if &bytes[0..8] != ENTRY_MAGIC {
        return Err(KvError::BadMagic { what: "entry" });
    }
    let version = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[8..12].try_into().expect("4 bytes"));
    if version != ENTRY_FORMAT_VERSION {
        return Err(KvError::UnsupportedVersion {
            what: "entry",
            version,
        });
    }
    let field = |at: usize| u64::from_le_bytes(bytes[at..at + 8].try_into().expect("8 bytes"));
    let token_count = usize::try_from(field(40)).map_err(|_| KvError::InconsistentSnapshot {
        detail: "entry token count does not fit in usize".to_string(),
    })?;
    let tokens_bytes = field(48);
    let expected_tokens_bytes = (token_count as u64).saturating_mul(4);
    if tokens_bytes != expected_tokens_bytes {
        return Err(KvError::InconsistentSnapshot {
            detail: format!(
                "entry tokens_bytes is {tokens_bytes} but token count {token_count} \
                 implies {expected_tokens_bytes}"
            ),
        });
    }
    Ok(Preamble {
        created_unix: field(16),
        last_used_unix: field(24),
        prefix_hash: field(32),
        token_count,
        payload_bytes: field(56),
    })
}

/// Read just the preamble of an entry file into index metadata.
fn read_preamble(path: &Path) -> Result<EntryMeta, KvError> {
    let mut file =
        fs::File::open(path).map_err(|e| KvError::io(format!("open {}", path.display()), e))?;
    let mut head = [0_u8; PREAMBLE_LEN];
    file.read_exact(&mut head)
        .map_err(|e| KvError::io(format!("read preamble of {}", path.display()), e))?;
    let preamble = parse_preamble(&head)?;
    let bytes = file
        .metadata()
        .map_err(|e| KvError::io(format!("stat {}", path.display()), e))?
        .len();
    Ok(EntryMeta {
        file_name: path
            .file_name()
            .map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
            .unwrap_or_default(),
        prefix_hash: preamble.prefix_hash,
        token_count: preamble.token_count,
        bytes,
        created_unix: preamble.created_unix,
        last_used_unix: preamble.last_used_unix,
    })
}

/// Read an entry's stored token ids (preamble + token region).
fn read_entry_tokens(path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<u32>, KvError> {
    let bytes = fs::read(path).map_err(|e| KvError::io(format!("read {}", path.display()), e))?;
    let preamble = parse_preamble(&bytes)?;
    let end = PREAMBLE_LEN + preamble.token_count * 4;
    if bytes.len() < end {
        return Err(KvError::Truncated {
            what: "entry",
            expected: end,
            actual: bytes.len(),
        });
    }
    Ok(bytes[PREAMBLE_LEN..end]
        .chunks_exact(4)
        .map(|chunk| u32::from_le_bytes(chunk.try_into().expect("chunks of 4")))
        .collect())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::config::StoreConfig;
    use attention::{KvCache, LayerKind};

    fn temp_root(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {
        let root =
            std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("itak-kv-store-test-{}-{}", std::process::id(), tag));
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
        root
    }

    fn geometry() -> KvGeometry {
        KvGeometry {
            layers: vec![LayerKind::Windowed { window: 4 }, LayerKind::Global],
            num_kv_heads: 2,
            head_dim: 3,
        }
    }

    fn snapshot_for(tokens: &[u32], fingerprint: &str) -> KvSnapshot {
        let geometry = geometry();
        let mut cache = KvCache::new(&geometry.layers, geometry.num_kv_heads, geometry.head_dim)
            .expect("builds");
        let row = geometry.row_floats();
        for (position, &token) in tokens.iter().enumerate() {
            for layer in 0..geometry.layers.len() {
                let k: Vec<f32> = (0..row)
                    .map(|i| (token as f32) + (position * 10 + layer + i) as f32 / 11.0)
                    .collect();
                let v: Vec<f32> = (0..row)
                    .map(|i| -((token as f32) + (position + layer * 3 + i) as f32 / 5.0))
                    .collect();
                cache.append(layer, &k, &v, position).expect("append");
            }
        }
        KvSnapshot::capture(&cache, fingerprint).expect("capture")
    }

    fn open_store(root: &Path, cap: u64) -> PrefixStore {
        PrefixStore::open(&StoreConfig {
            root: root.to_path_buf(),
            max_bytes: cap,
        })
        .expect("store opens")
    }

    #[test]
    fn open_refuses_a_planted_garbage_entry_by_name() {
        // Critic panel regression (failure seat): a planted
        // 72-byte entry whose token_count is u64::MAX and whose
        // tokens_bytes disagrees made parse_preamble's refusal
        // message evaluate token_count * 4 unchecked, which
        // PANICKED debug builds during open/rescan (release
        // wrapped and printed a wrong number). The message now
        // formats the saturating product the check already
        // computed, so both profiles refuse the entry by name and
        // the store opens with it unindexed.
        let root = temp_root("planted");
        fs::create_dir_all(&root).expect("root");
        let mut bytes = vec![0_u8; PREAMBLE_LEN];
        bytes[0..8].copy_from_slice(ENTRY_MAGIC);
        bytes[8..12].copy_from_slice(&ENTRY_FORMAT_VERSION.to_le_bytes());
        bytes[40..48].copy_from_slice(&u64::MAX.to_le_bytes()); // token count
        bytes[48..56].copy_from_slice(&0_u64.to_le_bytes()); // tokens_bytes: disagrees
        fs::write(root.join("planted.kv"), &bytes).expect("plant");
        let store = open_store(&root, 1 << 30);
        assert!(store.entries().is_empty());
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
    }

    #[test]
    fn put_lookup_round_trip() {
        let root = temp_root("roundtrip");
        let mut store = open_store(&root, 1 << 30);
        let tokens = vec![10_u32, 20, 30, 40, 50];
        let snapshot = snapshot_for(&tokens, "model-a");
        store.put(&tokens, &snapshot, 100).expect("put");
        let hit = store
            .lookup(&[10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70], None, None, 200)
            .expect("lookup")
            .expect("hit");
        assert_eq!(hit.token_count, 5);
        assert_eq!(hit.tokens, tokens);
        assert_eq!(hit.snapshot, snapshot);
        // The hit restamped last-used in the index and on disk.
        assert_eq!(store.entries()[0].last_used_unix, 200);
        let reopened = open_store(&root, 1 << 30);
        assert_eq!(reopened.entries()[0].last_used_unix, 200);
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
    }

    #[test]
    fn longest_prefix_wins_among_nested_entries() {
        let root = temp_root("nested");
        let mut store = open_store(&root, 1 << 30);
        let short = vec![1_u32, 2];
        let mid = vec![1_u32, 2, 3, 4];
        let long = vec![1_u32, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6];
        store
            .put(&short, &snapshot_for(&short, "model-a"), 1)
            .expect("put short");
        store
            .put(&mid, &snapshot_for(&mid, "model-a"), 2)
            .expect("put mid");
        store
            .put(&long, &snapshot_for(&long, "model-a"), 3)
            .expect("put long");
        // A query extending the longest entry hits the longest.
        let hit = store
            .lookup(&[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8], None, None, 10)
            .expect("lookup")
            .expect("hit");
        assert_eq!(hit.token_count, 6);
        // A query that branches after 4 tokens hits the mid entry.
        let hit = store
            .lookup(&[1, 2, 3, 4, 99], None, None, 11)
            .expect("lookup")
            .expect("hit");
        assert_eq!(hit.token_count, 4);
        // A query that branches after 2 tokens hits the short one.
        let hit = store
            .lookup(&[1, 2, 77], None, None, 12)
            .expect("lookup")
            .expect("hit");
        assert_eq!(hit.token_count, 2);
        // No shared prefix at all misses cleanly.
        assert!(store
            .lookup(&[9, 9], None, None, 13)
            .expect("lookup")
            .is_none());
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
    }

    #[test]
    fn put_refuses_mismatched_and_oversize() {
        let root = temp_root("refusals");
        let mut store = open_store(&root, 1 << 30);
        let tokens = vec![1_u32, 2, 3];
        let other = snapshot_for(&[7, 8], "model-a");
        let error = store.put(&tokens, &other, 1).expect_err("must refuse");
        assert!(
            matches!(error, KvError::TokenCountMismatch { .. }),
            "{error}"
        );
        let error = store.put(&[], &other, 1).expect_err("must refuse");
        assert!(matches!(error, KvError::EmptyPrefix), "{error}");
        // A cap smaller than one entry refuses the put by name.
        let root2 = temp_root("oversize");
        let mut small = open_store(&root2, 128);
        let snap = snapshot_for(&tokens, "model-a");
        let error = small.put(&tokens, &snap, 1).expect_err("must refuse");
        assert!(matches!(error, KvError::EntryTooLarge { .. }), "{error}");
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root2);
    }
}

//! Store-level integration tests: LRU eviction under the byte
//! cap, the forged-entry trust guard, geometry and fingerprint
//! refusals at lookup, torn files, and persistence across reopen.

use std::fs;
use std::path::PathBuf;

use attention::{KvCache, LayerKind};
use itak_kv::{KvGeometry, KvSnapshot, PrefixStore, StoreConfig};

fn temp_root(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {
    let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("itak-kv-it-{}-{}", std::process::id(), tag));
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
    root
}

fn geometry() -> KvGeometry {
    KvGeometry {
        layers: vec![LayerKind::Windowed { window: 4 }, LayerKind::Global],
        num_kv_heads: 2,
        head_dim: 3,
    }
}

fn snapshot_for(tokens: &[u32], fingerprint: &str) -> KvSnapshot {
    let geometry = geometry();
    let mut cache =
        KvCache::new(&geometry.layers, geometry.num_kv_heads, geometry.head_dim).expect("builds");
    let row = geometry.row_floats();
    for (position, &token) in tokens.iter().enumerate() {
        for layer in 0..geometry.layers.len() {
            let k: Vec<f32> = (0..row)
                .map(|i| (token as f32) + (position * 10 + layer + i) as f32 / 11.0)
                .collect();
            let v: Vec<f32> = (0..row)
                .map(|i| -((token as f32) + (position + layer * 3 + i) as f32 / 5.0))
                .collect();
            cache.append(layer, &k, &v, position).expect("append");
        }
    }
    KvSnapshot::capture(&cache, fingerprint).expect("capture")
}

fn open_store(root: &std::path::Path, cap: u64) -> PrefixStore {
    PrefixStore::open(&StoreConfig {
        root: root.to_path_buf(),
        max_bytes: cap,
    })
    .expect("store opens")
}

#[test]
fn eviction_respects_the_cap_and_lru_order() {
    let root = temp_root("evict");
    let a = vec![1_u32, 1, 1, 1];
    let b = vec![2_u32, 2, 2, 2];
    let c = vec![3_u32, 3, 3, 3];
    // Measure one entry's size with an uncapped store, then set
    // the cap to hold two entries plus slack, never three.
    let mut probe = open_store(&root, u64::MAX);
    probe.put(&a, &snapshot_for(&a, "m"), 1).expect("put a");
    let entry_bytes = probe.stats().total_bytes;
    drop(probe);
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);

    let cap = entry_bytes * 2 + entry_bytes / 2;
    let mut store = open_store(&root, cap);
    store.put(&a, &snapshot_for(&a, "m"), 1).expect("put a");
    store.put(&b, &snapshot_for(&b, "m"), 2).expect("put b");
    // Touch A so B becomes the least recently used.
    assert!(store
        .lookup(&[1, 1, 1, 1, 9], None, None, 3)
        .expect("lookup")
        .is_some());
    // Putting C pushes the store over the cap; B must go.
    store.put(&c, &snapshot_for(&c, "m"), 4).expect("put c");
    let stats = store.stats();
    assert!(stats.total_bytes <= cap, "over cap: {stats:?}");
    assert_eq!(stats.entries, 2);
    assert!(
        store.lookup(&b, None, None, 5).expect("lookup").is_none(),
        "the LRU entry (b) must be evicted"
    );
    assert!(store.lookup(&a, None, None, 6).expect("lookup").is_some());
    assert!(store.lookup(&c, None, None, 7).expect("lookup").is_some());
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
}

#[test]
fn forged_entry_is_refused_and_shorter_honest_prefix_still_serves() {
    let root = temp_root("forged");
    let mut store = open_store(&root, 1 << 30);
    let short = vec![5_u32, 6];
    let long = vec![5_u32, 6, 7, 8];
    store
        .put(&short, &snapshot_for(&short, "m"), 1)
        .expect("put short");
    store
        .put(&long, &snapshot_for(&long, "m"), 2)
        .expect("put long");
    // Forge the long entry: rewrite its stored token ids in place
    // (same length) so they no longer hash to the entry's key and
    // no longer match the query either.
    let long_meta = store
        .entries()
        .into_iter()
        .find(|e| e.token_count == 4)
        .expect("long entry indexed");
    let path = root.join(&long_meta.file_name);
    let mut bytes = fs::read(&path).expect("read entry");
    // Token region starts after the fixed 72-byte preamble.
    bytes[72] = 0xef;
    bytes[73] = 0xbe;
    bytes[74] = 0xad;
    bytes[75] = 0xde;
    fs::write(&path, &bytes).expect("forge entry");
    // Reopen so the index is rebuilt from disk, then query through
    // the forged entry's prefix: the long entry must be refused
    // and the honest short entry must serve.
    let mut store = open_store(&root, 1 << 30);
    let hit = store
        .lookup(&[5, 6, 7, 8, 9], None, None, 3)
        .expect("lookup")
        .expect("the honest short prefix serves");
    assert_eq!(hit.token_count, 2);
    assert_eq!(hit.tokens, short);
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
}

#[test]
fn geometry_and_fingerprint_requirements_refuse_at_lookup() {
    let root = temp_root("geom");
    let mut store = open_store(&root, 1 << 30);
    let tokens = vec![3_u32, 1, 4];
    store
        .put(&tokens, &snapshot_for(&tokens, "model-a"), 1)
        .expect("put");
    let mut foreign = geometry();
    foreign.head_dim = 12;
    assert!(store
        .lookup(&tokens, Some(&foreign), None, 2)
        .expect("lookup")
        .is_none());
    assert!(store
        .lookup(&tokens, None, Some("model-b"), 3)
        .expect("lookup")
        .is_none());
    let hit = store
        .lookup(&tokens, Some(&geometry()), Some("model-a"), 4)
        .expect("lookup")
        .expect("matching requirements hit");
    assert_eq!(hit.token_count, 3);
    // And the hit's snapshot restores under the checked path.
    hit.snapshot
        .restore_checked(&geometry(), "model-a")
        .expect("restore checked");
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
}

#[test]
fn torn_temp_and_torn_final_files_are_ignored() {
    let root = temp_root("torn");
    fs::create_dir_all(&root).expect("mkdir");
    // A torn temp file from a crashed writer: never indexed.
    fs::write(root.join(".tmp-deadbeef-123.kv"), b"half an entry").expect("write temp");
    // A torn final file: indexed never, refused by name at scan.
    fs::write(root.join("0123456789abcdef-4-0.kv"), b"ITKV").expect("write torn");
    let mut store = open_store(&root, 1 << 30);
    assert_eq!(store.stats().entries, 0);
    // The store still works normally afterwards.
    let tokens = vec![8_u32, 8];
    store
        .put(&tokens, &snapshot_for(&tokens, "m"), 1)
        .expect("put");
    assert!(store
        .lookup(&[8, 8, 8], None, None, 2)
        .expect("lookup")
        .is_some());
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
}

#[test]
fn entries_survive_reopen() {
    let root = temp_root("persist");
    let tokens = vec![42_u32, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47];
    {
        let mut store = open_store(&root, 1 << 30);
        store
            .put(&tokens, &snapshot_for(&tokens, "m"), 10)
            .expect("put");
    }
    let mut store = open_store(&root, 1 << 30);
    let hit = store
        .lookup(&[42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 48], None, None, 20)
        .expect("lookup")
        .expect("hit after reopen");
    assert_eq!(hit.snapshot.token_count, 6);
    let restored = hit.snapshot.restore().expect("restore");
    assert_eq!(restored.next_position(0).expect("position"), 6);
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
}
