===== FILE: crates/itak-kv/tests/restore_fixture.rs =====
//! The seam fixture: a small model shape where a "cold" run
//! (append the prefix, then continue) and a "restored" run
//! (append the prefix, snapshot it through the store, restore
//! into a fresh cache, then continue) must produce bitwise
//! identical attention outputs and identical greedy streams.
//!
//! The surface here is the KV-state level (attention crate math),
//! which is the level this lane wires; the ResidentSession wiring
//! that consumes the same restore is specified in
//! bench/prefix-kv-store-2026-11-07.md.

use std::fs;
use std::path::PathBuf;

use attention::{gqa_attention, AttentionParams, KvCache, LayerKind};
use itak_kv::{KvGeometry, KvSnapshot, PrefixStore, StoreConfig};

const Q_HEADS: usize = 4;
const LOGITS: usize = 16;

/// Small deterministic PRNG stream keyed by a seed word.
fn lcg(seed: u64) -> impl Iterator<Item = f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    std::iter::from_fn(move || {
        state = state
            .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
            .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
        Some(((state >> 40) as u32 as f32) / (1_u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5)
    })
}

fn geometry() -> KvGeometry {
    KvGeometry {
        layers: vec![
            LayerKind::Windowed { window: 4 },
            LayerKind::Global,
            LayerKind::Global,
            LayerKind::Windowed { window: 4 },
        ],
        num_kv_heads: 2,
        head_dim: 8,
    }
}

/// One position's K and V rows for one layer, a pure function of
/// (layer, position, token): the "model" of this fixture.
fn rows(geometry: &KvGeometry, layer: usize, position: usize, token: u32) -> (Vec<f32>, Vec<f32>) {
    let row = geometry.row_floats();
    let seed = (layer as u64) << 40 | (position as u64) << 16 | u64::from(token);
    let mut stream = lcg(seed);
    let k: Vec<f32> = stream.by_ref().take(row).collect();
    let v: Vec<f32> = stream.take(row).collect();
    (k, v)
}

fn append_token(cache: &mut KvCache, geometry: &KvGeometry, position: usize, token: u32) {
    for layer in 0..geometry.layers.len() {
        let (k, v) = rows(geometry, layer, position, token);
        cache.append(layer, &k, &v, position).expect("append");
    }
}

/// Fixed pseudo-head: project the concatenated per-layer
/// attention outputs for the newest position into LOGITS values.
fn logits_for(cache: &KvCache, geometry: &KvGeometry, position: usize, token: u32) -> Vec<f32> {
    let head_dim = geometry.head_dim;
    let q_len = Q_HEADS * head_dim;
    let seed = 0x5eed_u64 ^ ((position as u64) << 20) ^ u64::from(token);
    let q: Vec<f32> = lcg(seed).take(q_len).collect();
    let mut logits = vec![0.0_f32; LOGITS];
    for layer in 0..geometry.layers.len() {
        let view = cache.view(layer).expect("view");
        let out = gqa_attention(&q, 1, Q_HEADS, &[position], &view, &AttentionParams::new())
            .expect("attention");
        for (o, slot) in logits.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            for (i, &value) in out.iter().enumerate() {
                let w = (((o * 31 + i * 7 + layer * 3) % 13) as f32) / 7.0 - 0.8;
                *slot += w * value;
            }
        }
    }
    logits
}

fn argmax(values: &[f32]) -> u32 {
    values
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .max_by(|a, b| a.1.partial_cmp(b.1).expect("no NaNs in fixture"))
        .map(|(i, _)| i as u32)
        .expect("nonempty")
}

/// Run the continuation against a prepared cache and record the
/// per-step logits and greedy picks. The continuation tokens are
/// chosen by the fixture (not by the picks) so both runs walk the
/// same positions; the picks are the stream under test.
fn continue_run(
    cache: &mut KvCache,
    geometry: &KvGeometry,
    start: usize,
    continuation: &[u32],
) -> (Vec<Vec<f32>>, Vec<u32>) {
    let mut all_logits = Vec::new();
    let mut stream = Vec::new();
    for (step, &token) in continuation.iter().enumerate() {
        let position = start + step;
        append_token(cache, geometry, position, token);
        let logits = logits_for(cache, geometry, position, token);
        stream.push(argmax(&logits));
        all_logits.push(logits);
    }
    (all_logits, stream)
}

#[test]
fn restored_cache_continues_bitwise_identically() {
    let geometry = geometry();
    let prefix: Vec<u32> = vec![11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 77, 88, 99];
    let continuation: Vec<u32> = vec![5, 4, 3, 2, 1];

    // Cold run: prefix and continuation in one cache.
    let mut cold =
        KvCache::new(&geometry.layers, geometry.num_kv_heads, geometry.head_dim).expect("builds");
    for (position, &token) in prefix.iter().enumerate() {
        append_token(&mut cold, &geometry, position, token);
    }
    let (cold_logits, cold_stream) =
        continue_run(&mut cold, &geometry, prefix.len(), &continuation);

    // Restored run: prefix only, snapshot through the store,
    // restore, compare state, then continue.
    let root: PathBuf =
        std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("itak-kv-fixture-{}", std::process::id()));
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
    let mut store = PrefixStore::open(&StoreConfig {
        root: root.clone(),
        max_bytes: 1 << 30,
    })
    .expect("store opens");
    let mut warm =
        KvCache::new(&geometry.layers, geometry.num_kv_heads, geometry.head_dim).expect("builds");
    for (position, &token) in prefix.iter().enumerate() {
        append_token(&mut warm, &geometry, position, token);
    }
    let snapshot = KvSnapshot::capture(&warm, "fixture-model").expect("capture");
    store.put(&prefix, &snapshot, 100).expect("put");
    let query: Vec<u32> = prefix.iter().chain(&continuation).copied().collect();
    let hit = store
        .lookup(&query, Some(&geometry), Some("fixture-model"), 200)
        .expect("lookup")
        .expect("hit");
    assert_eq!(hit.token_count, prefix.len());
    let mut restored = hit
        .snapshot
        .restore_checked(&geometry, "fixture-model")
        .expect("restore checked");

    // State equality against the cold cache's prefix state: the
    // cold cache has already continued, so compare against a
    // fresh prefix-only cache instead.
    let mut prefix_only =
        KvCache::new(&geometry.layers, geometry.num_kv_heads, geometry.head_dim).expect("builds");
    for (position, &token) in prefix.iter().enumerate() {
        append_token(&mut prefix_only, &geometry, position, token);
    }
    for layer in 0..geometry.layers.len() {
        let want = prefix_only.view(layer).expect("view");
        let got = restored.view(layer).expect("view");
        assert_eq!(got.len(), want.len(), "layer {layer} visible rows");
        for slot in 0..want.len() {
            assert_eq!(got.position_at(slot), want.position_at(slot));
            for head in 0..geometry.num_kv_heads {
                assert_eq!(got.key(slot, head), want.key(slot, head));
                assert_eq!(got.value(slot, head), want.value(slot, head));
            }
        }
        assert_eq!(
            restored.next_position(layer).expect("position"),
            prefix.len()
        );
    }

    let (restored_logits, restored_stream) =
        continue_run(&mut restored, &geometry, prefix.len(), &continuation);
    assert_eq!(restored_stream, cold_stream);
    assert_eq!(restored_logits, cold_logits);
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
}

===== FILE: crates/itak-loader/FORWARD-DIFF-PLAN.md =====
# Forward diff: localizing Run B's first-token divergence

Companion to INTEGRATION-RUN-B.md. Run B proved the pipeline runs
and that the numerics diverge from llama.cpp at the first generated
token (our top-1: 290 " the", p 4.4e-5; reference: 13796 " Paris",
p 0.396), with our top-5 holding 1.6e-4 of the mass against the
reference's 0.62. This file is the plan that turns that end-to-end
fact into a named layer and a named defect, plus the tooling built
for it.

## What was built

- `muse_glimmer::trace` (crates/muse-glimmer/src/trace.rs): a
  `TraceSink` trait, a `NullTrace` default, statistics
  (`stats_of`: mean, population variance, max abs, first N values,
  computed in f64), and a `TraceLog` collector that reduces each
  capture to one line of a stable text format (version 1, specified
  in the module docs).
- `GlimmerModel::forward_traced`: the ordinary forward, same code
  path, additionally capturing the residual stream at these stage
  boundaries: `embed`, `layer.<i>.mid` (after the attention half,
  post-attention norm applied), `layer.<i>.out` (after the full
  layer), `final_norm`, `logits`. Each capture also emits a
  `trace.capture` event on the model's diagnostic channel. Unit
  tests prove the stage order, the shapes, the statistics, the
  line format byte-for-byte, and that traced and untraced forwards
  return identical logits.
- `examples/glimmer_layer_trace.rs` (this crate): the runnable
  tool. It tokenizes the golden `factual_capital` prompt exactly as
  Run B did, prints the prompt ids and whether they match Run B's
  `[200000, 954, 7963, 323, 11698, 373]`, enforces the coverage
  gate, runs one traced prefill, and prints (or with `--out`,
  files) the 107 trace lines (1 embed + 52 x (mid, out) +
  final_norm + logits), followed by the prefill top-5 in Run B's
  format as a self-check: if the traced run's top-5 does not
  reproduce Run B's position-1 table exactly, the trace is not
  measuring the same forward and nothing downstream of it counts.

Run it on the server, beside the model file, the same way Run B
ran (release build; one prefill is minutes-class on cpu-compute):

```sh
cargo run --release -p itak-loader --example glimmer_layer_trace -- \
    /mnt/models/<glimmer-30b>.gguf --out our-trace.txt
```

## What reference data the diff needs, exactly

A llama.cpp dump of the same stage boundaries, for the same GGUF,
the same prompt ids, CPU only, reduced to the same statistics:

1. The residual stream after the embedding lookup, all 6 positions
   (maps to our `embed`).
2. Per layer 0..51: the residual stream after the attention half
   (the tensor the reference graph feeds its FFN norm) and after
   the full layer (maps to `layer.<i>.mid` and `layer.<i>.out`).
   Last position is the must-have; all positions are wanted (a
   position-dependent error, e.g. RoPE geometry, is invisible in a
   last-row-only diff).
3. The final norm's output for the last position and the finished
   logits (maps to `final_norm` and `logits`).

How to obtain it: llama-server exposes none of this; the practical
route is a small runner (or a patched llama-cli) built against the
same llama.cpp tree Run B used (build-vulkan2), registering the
`cb_eval` callback in `llama_context_params` to copy out the named
graph tensors as the graph executes. The tensor names to capture
are whatever that tree's muse-glimmer graph calls its per-layer
residual, post-attention, and layer-output tensors; mapping our
stage names to its tensor names is a by-eye job against the graph
construction source for this architecture, and that same source
read settles hypothesis 1 (norm convention) and hypothesis 4/5
(placement, RoPE geometry) on paper, possibly before any dump is
needed.

## What exists today: nothing to diff against yet

Searched this repo on 2026-10-29: there is no llama.cpp activation
dump for Glimmer anywhere in it. `golden/` holds token-level
fixtures only (llama-server completions for TinyLlama-1.1B and
Qwen2.5-1.5B, consumed by the arch-llama crate), no per-layer
tensors for any model, and no `.npy`/`.bin` activation artifacts.
The raw Run B record on the server (`~/itak-run-b/`) holds logits-
level comparisons (top-5 tables), not graph intermediates.

Consequence, stated plainly: **the first divergent layer cannot be
named from data that exists today.** Our side of the diff (the
tool above) is built and tested; the reference side is one
llama.cpp runner away. Any number quoted before that dump exists
would be invented, so none is.

## How the diff reads, once both sides exist

Compare stage by stage in capture order, last-row statistics
first, whole-tensor statistics second:

- A stage is "matching" when mean and variance agree to roughly
  1e-2 relative and the first values track: f32 dequantization and
  summation-order noise live well under that, and a structural
  error (wrong norm form, wrong placement, missing scale) moves
  the statistics by far more.
- The first stage whose inputs matched but whose output does not
  is the defect's home. `embed` splits embedding handling from
  everything else; `layer.<i>.mid` vs `layer.<i>.out` splits each
  layer's attention half from its FFN half; `final_norm` and
  `logits` isolate the finishing math (already largely cleared by
  Run B's item 6).

## Ordered hypotheses

Run B's diagnosis order, with the stage that decides each:

0. **Embedding handling** (decided by `embed` alone). If the
   reference graph scales the embedding output (a Gemma-family
   habit: multiply by sqrt(hidden)) and ours does not, every layer
   downstream is wrong by a constant input scale and no layer
   diff will localize below `embed`. Cheapest test in the plan:
   one stage.
1. **Norm convention** (Run B item 1; decided by `layer.0.mid`).
   Our forward applies plain `x * w` RMSNorm everywhere; the
   file's norm weights are centered oddly for that reading
   (output_norm mean +0.017, block norms centered at +0.67..+1.34).
   If the reference uses the `(1 + w)` form, our layer 0 output is
   already systematically mis-scaled, and the error compounds 52
   times. Also settleable from the graph source alone.
2. **Post-norm placement and attention-gate placement** (Run B
   item 3; decided by the mid/out split). Ours applies the post
   norms after each residual add and reads the gate from the
   normed input. If the reference places either differently, the
   divergence appears between `.mid` and `.out` (or inside the
   attention half) at layer 0, not as a smooth scale drift.
3. **QK-norm placement/convention** (Run B item 4; attention half
   only). A pure attention temperature shift: it degrades but
   cannot alone un-concentrate the mass. If stages match through
   `layer.0.mid`'s inputs yet the attention output is off, this
   and item 4 are the suspects; separating them needs a Q/K
   capture point, a small extension of the trace sink, deliberately
   not built until the layer is named.
4. **RoPE geometry** (Run B item 5). The file carries no
   `rope.dimension_count`, so ours rotates the full head dim; the
   reference could hardcode partial rotation for this arch. Its
   signature is position-dependent: whole-tensor statistics drift
   while the first position stays clean, which is exactly why the
   trace keeps both views.
5. **Finishing math** (Run B item 6): excluded as the argmax
   cause (monotone map cannot reorder), kept in the diff only as
   the `logits` stage confirmation.
6. **Decode-path KV handling** (Run B's second symptom, the
   decode-time freeze): NOT addressed by this tool, by design.
   The freeze lives in single-token decode steps after a correct
   or incorrect prefill; a prefill trace cannot see it. The same
   sink and line format extend directly: capture the same stages
   on each decode forward and diff step-over-step self-consistency
   (Run B showed the distribution frozen to 1e-6 across steps
   feeding different tokens; a traced decode makes the frozen
   stage visible). That is the follow-up once the prefill error is
   named, or in parallel if the lanes split that way.

## Gates run for this deliverable

- `cargo test -p muse-glimmer`: 29 passed, 0 failed (6 new trace
  tests: statistics, empty/constant inputs, byte-exact line
  format, collector order and last-row extraction, degenerate
  shapes, traced-stage order and shapes).
- `cargo test -p itak-loader`: 9 passed plus 1 doc test; the
  example builds under the workspace lint gates.
- `cargo clippy -p muse-glimmer -p itak-loader --all-targets`:
  clean under the workspace deny-warnings lints.
- `cargo test --workspace`: every suite green, 0 failed.

===== END FILE: crates/itak-loader/FORWARD-DIFF-PLAN.md =====

===== FILE: crates/itak-loader/INTEGRATION-RUN-B.md =====
# Integration run B: Glimmer's first generation on the new stack

Run 2026-10-29. Runner: `examples/glimmer_generate.rs` in this crate.
Raw record on the server in `~/itak-run-b/` (`run.log`, `run.err`,
`ref-completion.json`, `ref-table.txt`).

## Verdict

Divergence at the first generated token. The pipeline works
mechanically end to end on the real 30B file: parse, coverage gate,
tokenizer, forward, KV cache, greedy loop, no refusals, no
placeholder paths. The forward's numerics do not yet match
llama.cpp: on identical prompt ids its argmax is wrong and its
probability mass is unconcentrated, and a second symptom appears at
decode time (the distribution stops tracking the fed token). No
parameter was tuned to force a match; this note is the evidence.

## Setup

- Prompt: `factual_capital`, the shortest factual prompt in
  `golden/prompts.jsonl`: "The capital of France is".
- Prompt ids, from the tokenizer crate (the file's
  `tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token` is true, so BOS 200000 is
  prepended; the encode itself is the T-2.3-proven one):
  `[200000, 954, 7963, 323, 11698, 373]`.
- Reference: llama.cpp (build-vulkan2) `llama-server`, CPU only
  (`-ngl 0`, 8 threads), port 18299, the same GGUF with no mmproj
  and no draft model. The prompt was posted to `/completion` as a
  token id array, so both engines consumed byte-identical input;
  tokenization cannot explain any difference. Temperature 0,
  `n_predict` 8, `n_probs` 5, `ignore_eos` true. The production
  GPU server on port 8080 was never touched (health-checked before
  and after).
- Ours: the full crate chain (`gguf`, `itak-loader`,
  `tokenizer`, `muse-glimmer` forward on `cpu-compute`), release
  build, run on the server. `cpu-compute` is single-threaded; the
  process sat at 99.9% of one core throughout.

## Reference result (llama.cpp)

Generated ids: `[13796, 26, 1573, 373, 290, 2167, 26899, 1212]`,
text " Paris. It is the most populous". Timings: prompt 795 ms for
6 tokens, decode 314 ms per token.

Top-5 per position (id, token, probability):

| Pos | Sampled | Top-5 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 13796 | 13796 " Paris" 0.3962; 262 " a" 0.0961; 290 " the" 0.0513; 1085 " one" 0.0462; 5711 " known" 0.0323 |
| 2 | 26 | 26 "." 0.4721; 24 "," 0.2480; 1574 ".␊␊" 0.1338; 341 " and" 0.0559; 335 ".␊" 0.0239 |
| 3 | 1573 | 1573 " It" 0.2794; 589 " The" 0.1993; 13796 " Paris" 0.1496; 1394 " This" 0.0278; 220 " " 0.0252 |
| 4 | 373 | 373 " is" 0.8585; 947 " has" 0.0574; 1082 "'s" 0.0470; 812 " was" 0.0098; 23374 " lies" 0.0074 |
| 5 | 290 | 290 " the" 0.3078; 262 " a" 0.1228; 1085 " one" 0.1172; 5711 " known" 0.1113; 1437 " also" 0.1089 |
| 6 | 2167 | 2167 " most" 0.3561; 13467 " largest" 0.2767; 21989 " biggest" 0.0324; 5376 " center" 0.0312; 7963 " capital" 0.0311 |
| 7 | 26899 | 26899 " popul" 0.5940; 70785 " populated" 0.2413; 25600 " visited" 0.0551; 7559 " popular" 0.0337; 24093 " famous" 0.0202 |
| 8 | 1212 | 1212 "ous" 0.9996; 11381 "ously" 0.0001; 66950 "ousand" 0.00004; 474 "ou" 0.00004; 5364 "ouse" 0.00003 |

## Our result

Generated ids: `[290, 290, 15, 15, 15, 15, 15, 15]`, decoded text
" the the######".

Position 1 (the one position where both engines saw the identical
sequence) top-5, from the forward's finished logits:

| Rank | Id | Token | Logit | Prob |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 290 | " the" | 1.223680 | 0.000044 |
| 1 | 341 | " and" | 0.842154 | 0.000030 |
| 2 | 26 | "." | 0.798573 | 0.000029 |
| 3 | 373 | " is" | 0.771220 | 0.000028 |
| 4 | 262 | " a" | 0.762244 | 0.000028 |

The comparison at position 1:

- Argmax differs: ours 290, reference 13796. Greedy decoding makes
  this a hard mismatch, not a sampling artifact.
- Overlap is partial: our rank 0 is the reference's rank 2 (290),
  our rank 4 is its rank 1 runner-up (262); its top token (13796)
  is not in our top-5.
- The internal spread of the top-5 is similar (about 2.5 nats on
  both sides). The divergence is mass concentration: the
  reference's top-5 holds 0.62 of the probability, ours holds
  1.6e-4. In our forward the vocabulary bulk is not suppressed
  relative to the top, which means the final hidden state's
  direction is wrong enough that the head cannot separate the
  answer from the bulk, while still ranking plausible function
  words first. The failure is upstream of the head, in the layer
  stack, not in the finishing math or the sampler.

Positions 2 to 8 are not continuations of the same sequence (each
engine conditions on its own tokens), so they are reported as our
engine's behavior, not as per-position diffs.

## Second symptom: the decode-time freeze

- Step 2 (feeding 290 at position 6) returned a top-5 identical to
  the prefill's to all six printed decimals on every entry.
- Steps 3 to 8 returned one shared top-5 (15 "#" 0.009546; 1898;
  442; 13266; 2694), identical to six decimals across steps that
  fed different tokens (290, then 15) at advancing positions. The
  single variation observed anywhere is 1e-6 in step 5's rank-4
  logit.
- Reading: at decode time the returned distribution is, to about
  1e-6 of its own scale, independent of the token being fed and of
  the position. The new token's contribution is attenuated to
  noise, or the decode path reads a state that stopped tracking
  the input after the first decode step. The synthetic
  incremental-vs-prefill proof in `cpu-compute` (2 layers, 4
  heads, head dim 8, window 16 and 3) does not expose this; the
  real config is 52 layers, 32 Q heads over 2 KV heads, head dim
  128, window 2048.

## Timings and resources (ours)

- Open file: 4,720 ms. Weight load through the coverage gate:
  5,441 ms (731 tensors, 16,743,567,360 bytes served).
- Prefill, 6 tokens, multi-row path: 1,532,787 ms (about 25.5
  minutes).
- Decode steps 2 to 8: 45,174; 45,641; 44,637; 43,906; 43,988;
  42,844; 43,720 ms. About 44 to 46 s per token, roughly 34x
  cheaper per token than the prefill path.
- Peak RSS: 38,190,400 KiB (about 36.4 GiB): the file image, the
  served tensor copies, and transient f32 dequantization buffers.
  There is no resident f32 weight copy; weights dequantize per
  projection call, as the crate documents.
- Prefill cost suspects, in order: the per-projection strided
  transpose in `cpu-compute`'s `proj` for rows > 1, the full
  dequantize of every tensor on every call, then the f64 matmul.
  Reference contrast: llama.cpp on 8 threads did the same prefill
  in 795 ms and decode at 314 ms per token. This backend is a
  correctness reference; the timings quantify how much the
  specialized kernels have to win.

## Diagnosis, ordered

1. **Norm convention.** Measured through our own loader
   (`load_f32`), the file's norm weights have an unusual profile:
   `output_norm.weight` mean +0.017, std 3.13, range [-4.94,
   +4.38] (centered on zero); per-layer norms centered higher
   (`blk.0.attn_norm` +1.34, `blk.51.attn_norm` +1.30,
   `blk.0.ffn_norm` +1.17, `blk.0.post_attention_norm` +0.67);
   `blk.0.attn_q_norm` is a constant vector (all 128 entries
   exactly 3.87) and `blk.0.attn_k_norm` a constant 1.0. Our
   forward applies plain `x * w` RMSNorm everywhere. If
   llama.cpp's muse-glimmer graph uses the Gemma-style `(1 + w)`
   form, every norm in all 52 layers is wrong in ours, which fits
   a near-total loss of signal. The stats alone do not prove the
   convention (block norms center above 1, the final norm at 0),
   so this is the first thing to settle against the llama.cpp
   graph source for this architecture, not a conclusion.
2. **Attention/KV handling at real scale** (the freeze, above).
   Something in the decode path (position handling, head mapping,
   ring state) behaves differently at 32/2 heads and 52 layers
   than at the synthetic scale where the proofs pass.
3. **The two flagged placements** from the architecture module:
   post norms after each residual add, and the attention gate
   reading the normed input. Still unverified against the
   reference graph; either being wrong degrades the output but
   would not obviously un-concentrate the mass on its own.
4. **QK norm application.** Ours norms Q and K per head after the
   projections, before RoPE. With constant-vector norm weights,
   any convention error here is a pure attention temperature
   shift; it cannot by itself produce the observed bulk behavior.
5. **RoPE geometry.** The file's metadata has no
   `rope.dimension_count` key (checked), so full 128-dimension
   rotation matches the file's surface. llama.cpp could still
   hardcode partial rotation for this architecture in source;
   lower suspicion, settled by the same source read as item 1.
6. **Softcap/scale order is excluded as the argmax cause.** The
   finishing map is monotone, so it cannot reorder candidates;
   and the mass-concentration gap is a property of the head's
   input direction, not of the finishing scalars.

## What this run established

- The complete crate chain runs the real 30B model end to end
  with the coverage gate enforced and no refusals: Glimmer's
  first generation on the new stack exists, and it is wrong in a
  precisely measured way.
- The next step that localizes the error: dump our per-layer
  activations for this prompt and diff them against llama.cpp's
  graph intermediates for the same ids, after settling the norm
  convention from the llama.cpp muse-glimmer graph source. One
  layer's first divergence will name the defect; guessing further
  from end-to-end numbers will not.


## Follow-up (2026-10-29 evening): conventions settled from source, forward fixed, Stage 1 re-run

The conventions were settled by reading llama.cpp's own source on
the server: `src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp` (the graph),
`conversion/muse_glimmer.py` (the converter), plus
`llama-graph.cpp` (`build_norm`), `llama-model.cpp`
(`llama_model_rope_type`, n_rot defaults), and `llama-hparams.cpp`
(SWA pattern). No convention below is a guess; each carries its
citation. Commits: a777db6 (muse-glimmer), 1956b27 (torch-math),
082d7fd (cpu-compute). Raw record of the re-run on the server in
`~/itak-run-c/` (`run.log`, `run.err`).

### Verdict of the re-run

The divergence is gone. Our generated ids are
`[13796, 26, 1573, 373, 290, 2167, 26899, 1212]`, exactly the
reference ids, all 8 positions, and the per-position probabilities
track the reference to within 0.015 (f32 reference math vs
llama.cpp kernel accumulation). The decode freeze is gone with
it: every decode step's distribution answers the fed token and
matches the reference step for step.

### Settled conventions

Wrong in our code, fixed:

1. **Post-norm placement and eps.** The reference applies each
   post norm to the sub-block's branch output, then adds the
   untouched residual: `x = x + rms_norm(branch, post_w)` with a
   hardcoded eps of 1e-8 (`muse-glimmer.cpp`: `post_norm_eps =
   1e-8f`, applied at the attention and FFN branches). Ours
   normalized the sum `residual + branch` at the file eps 1e-5,
   renormalizing the whole residual stream 104 times per token.
   Fixed in `muse-glimmer::model` (`POST_NORM_EPS`).
2. **Embedding norm missing.** The graph runs a weightless
   RMSNorm over the embedding output before layer 0
   (`muse-glimmer.cpp`: `build_norm(inpL, nullptr, nullptr, ...)`,
   which is plain `ggml_rms_norm` in `llama-graph.cpp`). Ours fed
   raw embeddings into layer 0. Added as a distinct
   `Compute::rms_norm_plain` step, called right after `embed`.
   There is no embedding scale factor anywhere in the graph.
3. **RoPE on the wrong layers.** RoPE runs on the sliding-window
   layers ONLY; the 13 global layers are NoPE
   (`muse-glimmer.cpp`: "RoPE runs on the SWA layers, NoPE on
   full ones"). Ours rotated every layer. `CpuCompute::attention`
   now rotates only `LayerKind::SlidingWindow`, at the SWA base
   (`rope.freq_base_swa` when the file carries it, else the train
   base, per `llama-model.cpp`; the config now resolves and stores
   it. This file carries no SWA key, so 500000 either way.)
4. **RoPE pairing.** llama.cpp's rope type for this arch is
   `LLAMA_ROPE_TYPE_NORM` (`llama-model.cpp`), ggml's adjacent-pair
   mode, and the converter unpermuted Q/K into that layout
   (`muse_glimmer.py`: `permute` with `qk_order = NORM`). A new
   `torch_math::rope_interleaved` implements that pairing under
   its own name, and the Glimmer backend calls it; the half-split
   NEOX form stays in `torch_math::rope` for the llama/qwen2
   families, whose reference uses it (sibling fix 13643e0, from
   the Qwen2.5 layer diff). The pairings pair different channels
   and are not interchangeable.
5. **Head finishing order.** The graph scales first, then
   softcaps: `ggml_scale` by `logit_scale`, then `build_softcap`
   (`cap * tanh(z / cap)`), `muse-glimmer.cpp` head block. Ours
   capped then scaled. Monotone either way, so this never moved
   argmax (Run B diagnosis item 6 was right); it did move every
   probability. The unit test that pinned the wrong order is
   rewritten with knee values that tell the orders apart
   (z = 20, cap = 20, scale = 0.5: 9.2423 settled, 7.6159 wrong).

Already matching the source, verified and left alone:

- **RMSNorm form is plain `x * w` everywhere in the graph.**
  Run B diagnosis item 1 is settled as NOT a graph-side error:
  the Gemma-style (1 + w) shift was folded into the stored
  weights at conversion for the four per-layer norms only
  (`muse_glimmer.py`: `norm_shift` returns 1.0 for names ending
  `layernorm.weight`, 0.0 otherwise; the final norm was
  deliberately unshifted, which is why `output_norm` centers on
  zero while block norms center near 1). All other norms (pre,
  QK, final, embedding) use the file eps 1e-5 via `build_norm`.
- **Attention gate.** Gate projection reads the same normed
  pre-attention input as Q/K/V; `sigmoid(gate)` multiplies the
  attention output elementwise before the output projection
  (`muse-glimmer.cpp`). Ours already did exactly this.
- **QK norms.** Per-head RMSNorm over head_dim with the stored
  weights, after the projections, before RoPE. The stored
  weights are synthesized by the converter (q_norm = constant
  `qk_scale_factor` = 3.87, matching the measured constant
  vector; k_norm = ones), so plain application is correct.
- **RoPE geometry.** Full head_dim rotation (n_rot = 128; the
  file carries no `rope.dimension_count` and no `rope.freq_base_swa`
  key, both confirmed by a full metadata strings scan; defaults
  in `llama-model.cpp`), base 500000, and the SWA pattern
  (globals at il % 4 == 3) matches our derived pattern.

### Decode freeze: what it was

No discrete cache bug exists. A new intermediate-scale test
(8 layers with globals at 3 and 7, 32 Q heads over 2 KV heads,
head dim 16, hidden 512, the real eps, base, cap, and scale;
`cpu-compute/tests/forward_tests.rs`) measures decode
sensitivity directly: prefill a prompt, then feed token 7 vs
token 42 and compare logits, plus a one-shot equivalence check.
Sensitivity was healthy at that scale (above the 1e-3 assertion
floor; the freeze signature in Run B was about 1e-6) both before
and after the fixes, and the cache position cross-check, the
attention crate's absolute-position masks and views, and the
incremental-vs-one-shot proofs all hold at every scale tested.
The freeze was the convention errors compounding over 52 layers:
post norms renormalizing the residual stream after every
sub-block (each new token's contribution repeatedly rescaled
against the whole stream), a missing embedding norm, and RoPE
rotating the global layers' Q/K with position garbage. Two more
regression tests pin the fixed conventions decisively: a
tiny-branch test (attention output scaled 1e-4, so the branch
RMS sits near sqrt(1e-8)) separates the post-norm eps and
placement readings by more than an order of magnitude, and the
naive-reference attention proof now runs for both layer kinds,
rotating only the sliding one.

Gates: `cargo test --workspace` 196 passed, 0 failed, and
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` clean, both on the
final tree (including `attention_mixing_matches_a_naive_reference`,
re-confirmed green after the sibling RoPE commits landed; it had
failed transiently mid-flight while these edits and the sibling
pairing flip crossed in the shared tree).

===== FILE: crates/itak-loader/examples/dflash_block.rs =====
//! E3 real-file proof: the DFlash draft module end to end against
//! the real files on the server.
//!
//! Usage: `dflash_block <draft.gguf> <target.gguf> [prompt] [block_len]`
//!
//! Phases, each timed and printed as it completes:
//!
//! 1. Census: the draft file's metadata and full tensor inventory,
//!    read with this workspace's `gguf` crate.
//! 2. Config + coverage + weights for the draft through
//!    `itak-loader`'s dflash bridge, coverage gate enforced.
//! 3. Target forward with captured layer inputs (the additive
//!    `forward_capturing` variant) over the prompt, on the CPU
//!    reference backend: this is the conditioning source.
//! 4. Injection of the captured rows into the draft's own cache.
//! 5. One noise block forward through the draft, borrowing the
//!    target's embedding table and output head, reporting
//!    per-position top-1 tokens and checking every logit is finite.
//!
//! This is a correctness runner, not a benchmark: the CPU reference
//! dequantizes as it goes, so the target forward is minutes-class.
//! Timings are reported honestly, per phase.

use std::io::Write;
use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Instant;

use cpu_compute::CpuCompute;
use dflash::{DflashCache, DflashModel, StderrDiag, TargetTensors};
use muse_glimmer::{GlimmerModel, PositionCache};
use tokenizer::{TokenType, Tokenizer, TokenizerData};

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let (Some(draft_path), Some(target_path)) = (args.get(1), args.get(2)) else {
        eprintln!("usage: dflash_block <draft.gguf> <target.gguf> [prompt] [block_len]");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    };
    let prompt = args.get(3).map_or("The capital", String::as_str);
    let block_len: usize = args.get(4).map_or(4, |a| a.parse().unwrap_or(4));
    match run(draft_path, target_path, prompt, block_len) {
        Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,
        Err(msg) => {
            eprintln!("FAIL: {msg}");
            ExitCode::FAILURE
        }
    }
}

fn phase(label: &str, t: Instant) {
    println!("[{label}] {:.1}s", t.elapsed().as_secs_f64());
    let _ = std::io::stdout().flush();
}

/// Same thin tokenizer adapter as the other integration runners.
fn data_from_info(
    info: &gguf::TokenizerInfo,
    model: Option<String>,
    unknown: Option<u32>,
) -> TokenizerData {
    TokenizerData {
        model,
        tokens: info.tokens.clone(),
        token_types: info
            .token_types
            .as_ref()
            .map(|types| types.iter().map(|&t| TokenType::from_gguf(t)).collect())
            .unwrap_or_default(),
        merges: info.merges.clone().unwrap_or_default(),
        scores: info.scores.clone(),
        bos_token_id: info.bos_token_id,
        eos_token_id: info.eos_token_id,
        unknown_token_id: unknown,
        padding_token_id: info.padding_token_id,
    }
}

fn run(draft_path: &str, target_path: &str, prompt: &str, block_len: usize) -> Result<(), String> {
    let total = Instant::now();

    // Phase 1: census of the draft file with our gguf crate.
    let t = Instant::now();
    let draft_file = gguf::GgufFile::open(Path::new(draft_path)).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!(
        "draft file: {} tensors, {} metadata entries",
        draft_file.tensor_names().count(),
        draft_file.metadata().len()
    );
    for name in draft_file.tensor_names() {
        let info = draft_file.tensor_info(name).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        println!("  {name} {:?} {}", info.dims(), info.type_name());
    }
    phase("census", t);

    // Phase 2: draft config, coverage gate, weights.
    let t = Instant::now();
    let dcfg = itak_loader::load_dflash_config(&draft_file).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!(
        "draft config: layers={} hidden={} ffn={} q_heads={} kv_heads={} key={} value={} \
         rope_base={} eps={} block_size={} target_layers={:?} window={} pattern={:?} \
         causal={} mask_token={} vocab={} context={}",
        dcfg.block_count,
        dcfg.hidden,
        dcfg.ffn_hidden,
        dcfg.q_heads,
        dcfg.kv_heads,
        dcfg.key_length,
        dcfg.value_length,
        dcfg.rope_freq_base,
        dcfg.rms_eps,
        dcfg.block_size,
        dcfg.target_layers,
        dcfg.sliding_window,
        dcfg.sliding_pattern,
        dcfg.causal_attention,
        dcfg.mask_token_id,
        dcfg.vocab_size,
        dcfg.context_length
    );
    let report = itak_loader::coverage_dflash(&draft_file, &dcfg);
    println!(
        "coverage: expected={} found={} missing={} unexpected={}",
        report.expected_count(),
        report.found_count(),
        report.missing().len(),
        report.unexpected().len()
    );
    if !report.unexpected().is_empty() {
        println!("  unexpected: {:?}", report.unexpected());
    }
    report.require_complete().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let dweights =
        itak_loader::load_dflash_weights(&draft_file, &dcfg).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!(
        "draft weights: layers={} target_hidden={} conditioning_width={} own_embedding={} own_output={}",
        dweights.layers.len(),
        dweights.target_hidden,
        dweights.conditioning_width(),
        dweights.embedding.is_some(),
        dweights.output.is_some()
    );
    // The draft runs with its diagnostic sink attached, so its
    // refusals and passes are observable in this proof's output.
    let draft = DflashModel::with_diag(dcfg.clone(), dweights, Arc::new(StderrDiag));
    phase("draft load", t);

    // Phase 3: target forward with captured layer inputs.
    let t = Instant::now();
    let target_file = gguf::GgufFile::open(Path::new(target_path)).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let gcfg = itak_loader::load_config(&target_file).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let gweights = itak_loader::load_weights(&target_file, &gcfg).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let info = target_file.tokenizer().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let tok_model = target_file
        .metadata()
        .opt_string("tokenizer.ggml.model")
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
        .map(str::to_string);
    let tokenizer =
        Tokenizer::new(data_from_info(&info, tok_model, None)).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let mut prompt_ids = tokenizer.encode(prompt).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let add_bos = target_file
        .metadata()
        .get_bool("tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token")
        .unwrap_or(false);
    if add_bos {
        if let Some(bos) = info.bos_token_id {
            prompt_ids.insert(0, bos);
        }
    }
    println!("prompt {prompt:?} -> ids {prompt_ids:?}");
    let target = GlimmerModel::new(gcfg.clone(), gweights, Box::new(CpuCompute::new()));
    let capture_layers: Vec<usize> = dcfg.target_layers.iter().map(|&l| l as usize).collect();
    let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
    let (logits, captures) = target
        .forward_capturing(&prompt_ids, &mut cache, &capture_layers)
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!(
        "target forward: {} positions, {} captures of [{}][{}]",
        prompt_ids.len(),
        captures.len(),
        prompt_ids.len(),
        gcfg.hidden
    );
    for cap in &captures {
        assert_eq!(cap.rows.len(), prompt_ids.len() * gcfg.hidden as usize);
        println!("  captured layer {} input rows", cap.layer);
    }
    let anchor = logits
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .max_by(|a, b| a.1.partial_cmp(b.1).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal))
        .map(|(i, _)| i as u32)
        .ok_or("empty target logits")?;
    println!(
        "anchor (target argmax): {anchor} {:?}",
        info.tokens[anchor as usize]
    );
    phase("target forward + capture", t);

    // Phase 4: assemble conditioning features in target_layers
    // order and inject them at the prompt positions.
    let t = Instant::now();
    let hidden = gcfg.hidden as usize;
    let n_pos = prompt_ids.len();
    let width = draft.weights().conditioning_width();
    let mut features = vec![0.0f32; n_pos * width];
    for (k, cap) in captures.iter().enumerate() {
        for p in 0..n_pos {
            features[p * width + k * hidden..p * width + (k + 1) * hidden]
                .copy_from_slice(&cap.rows[p * hidden..(p + 1) * hidden]);
        }
    }
    let positions: Vec<usize> = (0..n_pos).collect();
    let mut dcache = DflashCache::new(&dcfg);
    draft
        .inject(&mut dcache, &features, &positions)
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!("injected positions: {:?}", dcache.positions());
    phase("inject", t);

    // Phase 5: one noise block through the draft.
    let t = Instant::now();
    let source = itak_loader::DflashTensorSource::new(&target_file);
    let emb =
        dflash::TensorSource::tensor(&source, "token_embd.weight").map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let head = dflash::TensorSource::tensor(&source, "output.weight").map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let target_tensors = TargetTensors {
        embedding: Some(&emb),
        output: Some(&head),
    };
    let block: Vec<u32> = draft
        .noise_block(anchor)
        .into_iter()
        .take(block_len)
        .collect();
    println!("noise block: {block:?} at start position {n_pos}");
    let logits = draft
        .forward_block(&dcache, &block, n_pos, &target_tensors)
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    assert_eq!(logits.len(), block.len() * dcfg.vocab_size as usize);
    let vocab = dcfg.vocab_size as usize;
    for (i, row) in logits.chunks_exact(vocab).enumerate() {
        assert!(
            row.iter().all(|z| z.is_finite()),
            "non-finite logit in block row {i}"
        );
        let (top, z) = row
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .max_by(|a, b| a.1.partial_cmp(b.1).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal))
            .ok_or("empty logit row")?;
        println!(
            "  block position {}: top-1 = {} {:?} (logit {:.4})",
            n_pos + i,
            top,
            info.tokens[top],
            z
        );
    }
    phase("draft block forward", t);

    println!("PASS: E3 real-file draft block forward complete");
    phase("total", total);
    Ok(())
}

===== END FILE: crates/itak-loader/examples/dflash_block.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/itak-loader/examples/glimmer_generate.rs =====
//! Integration run B: Glimmer's first generation on the new Rust
//! stack (TODO: integration stage), driven end to end through the
//! real crates: `gguf` parses the file, `itak-loader` loads config
//! and weights behind the coverage gate, the `tokenizer` crate
//! tokenizes, and `muse-glimmer`'s forward runs on `cpu-compute`.
//!
//! Usage: `glimmer_generate <path-to-gguf> <prompt> [n_tokens] [--ids-only] [--gpu|--gpu-trait|--gpu-argmax]`
//!
//! `--gpu` runs the device-resident session in `wgpu-compute`:
//! weights upload once, activations and KV never leave the
//! card, and each forward chunk is one command-buffer chain
//! with only the finished logits read back (the fast path; see
//! `wgpu-compute`'s session module). `--gpu-argmax` runs the
//! same resident session with the on-device argmax tail: each
//! chunk reads back eight bytes (the winning index and its
//! logit, reduced on the GPU) instead of the logits vector,
//! so its per-step lines carry the winner and its raw logit
//! rather than a top-5. `--gpu-trait` selects the older trait
//! path over the same backend (per-step host round trips
//! through `GlimmerModel`), kept as the reference and for
//! comparison runs. The default is the `cpu-compute`
//! reference. Same model, same output contract on all paths.
//!
//! The prompt ids are printed before any weight work happens, so the
//! identical id sequence can be handed to a reference engine (the
//! llama.cpp comparison this run exists for). `--ids-only` stops
//! there: tokenize and exit, no weight load, no forward.
//!
//! Output is line-oriented and flushed per step, so a long CPU run
//! shows its progress token by token: phase timings, the prompt ids,
//! and per generated position the top-5 candidates (id, raw token
//! text, logit, softmax probability over the full vocabulary) plus
//! the greedy pick and its wall time.
//!
//! This is a correctness runner, not a benchmark: `cpu-compute`
//! dequantizes weights on every projection, so a 30B token is
//! minutes-class. Timings are reported honestly, per token.

use std::io::Write;
use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Instant;

use muse_glimmer::{GlimmerModel, PositionCache, StderrDiag};
use tokenizer::{TokenType, Tokenizer, TokenizerData};

/// EXPERIMENT ONLY (overnight logit-scale run, 2026-11-05): the
/// environment variable `ITAK_EXPERIMENT_LOGIT_SCALE`, when set to a
/// positive finite number, replaces the file's `logit_scale` in the
/// config this example hands to the model. Unset (the default) the
/// file value is used untouched. This exists to measure how sensitive
/// Glimmer's output distribution is to the scale (TODO T-9.3 residue);
/// it is not a shipped knob and no library code reads it.
fn experiment_logit_scale(raw: Option<&str>, file_value: f32) -> Result<f32, String> {
    let Some(raw) = raw else {
        return Ok(file_value);
    };
    let forced: f32 = raw
        .parse()
        .map_err(|_| format!("ITAK_EXPERIMENT_LOGIT_SCALE: not a number: {raw:?}"))?;
    if !forced.is_finite() || forced <= 0.0 {
        return Err(format!(
            "ITAK_EXPERIMENT_LOGIT_SCALE: must be positive and finite, got {forced}"
        ));
    }
    Ok(forced)
}

/// Diagnostics on one finished (scaled, softcapped) logit vector:
/// the finished range, the implied pre-softcap range recovered by
/// inverting `cap * tanh(w / cap)` (entries saturated to the cap in
/// f32 are counted, and the recovered max is then a lower bound),
/// the implied raw lm_head range (pre-softcap divided by the scale),
/// and how many of the top 100 finished logits sit beyond
/// `0.9 * cap`, the saturation yardstick of the experiment note.
fn print_logit_stats(label: &str, logits: &[f32], cfg: &muse_glimmer::GlimmerConfig) {
    let cap = cfg.logit_softcap;
    let scale = cfg.logit_scale;
    let fin_min = logits.iter().copied().fold(f32::INFINITY, f32::min);
    let fin_max = logits.iter().copied().fold(f32::NEG_INFINITY, f32::max);
    let mut sorted: Vec<f32> = logits.to_vec();
    sorted.sort_unstable_by(|a, b| b.partial_cmp(a).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
    let top100 = &sorted[..sorted.len().min(100)];
    let beyond = top100.iter().filter(|&&z| z > 0.9 * cap).count();
    let saturated = logits.iter().filter(|&&z| z >= cap).count();
    // Invert the softcap on the entries that did not saturate to the
    // cap in f32; the recovered range is over those entries only.
    let mut pre_min = f32::INFINITY;
    let mut pre_max = f32::NEG_INFINITY;
    for &z in logits {
        if z < cap && z > -cap {
            let w = cap * (z / cap).atanh();
            pre_min = pre_min.min(w);
            pre_max = pre_max.max(w);
        }
    }
    println!(
        "{label} stats: finished_range=[{fin_min:.4},{fin_max:.4}] \
         presoftcap_range=[{pre_min:.4},{pre_max:.4}] saturated_to_cap={saturated} \
         raw_range=[{:.4},{:.4}] top100_beyond_0.9cap={beyond}",
        pre_min / scale,
        pre_max / scale,
    );
    std::io::stdout().flush().ok();
}

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let (Some(path), Some(prompt)) = (args.get(1), args.get(2)) else {
        eprintln!(
            "usage: glimmer_generate <path-to-gguf> <prompt> [n_tokens] [--ids-only] \
             [--gpu|--gpu-trait|--gpu-argmax]"
        );
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    };
    let ids_only = args.iter().any(|a| a == "--ids-only");
    let gpu = args.iter().any(|a| a == "--gpu");
    let gpu_trait = args.iter().any(|a| a == "--gpu-trait");
    let gpu_argmax = args.iter().any(|a| a == "--gpu-argmax");
    let n_tokens: usize = args
        .get(3)
        .filter(|a| !a.starts_with("--"))
        .map_or(8, |a| a.parse().unwrap_or(8));
    match run(path, prompt, n_tokens, ids_only, gpu, gpu_trait, gpu_argmax) {
        Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,
        Err(msg) => {
            eprintln!("FAIL: {msg}");
            ExitCode::FAILURE
        }
    }
}

/// Adapts the gguf crate's parsed tokenizer info into the tokenizer
/// crate's input data. Same thin adapter as the conformance harness
/// (TODO T-2.3); it lives in harness code, not in either library.
fn data_from_info(
    info: &gguf::TokenizerInfo,
    model: Option<String>,
    unknown: Option<u32>,
) -> TokenizerData {
    TokenizerData {
        model,
        tokens: info.tokens.clone(),
        token_types: info
            .token_types
            .as_ref()
            .map(|types| types.iter().map(|&t| TokenType::from_gguf(t)).collect())
            .unwrap_or_default(),
        merges: info.merges.clone().unwrap_or_default(),
        scores: info.scores.clone(),
        bos_token_id: info.bos_token_id,
        eos_token_id: info.eos_token_id,
        unknown_token_id: unknown,
        padding_token_id: info.padding_token_id,
    }
}

/// The `k` highest logits as (id, logit, softmax probability over
/// the whole vocabulary), best first. Probabilities are computed in
/// f64 from the forward's finished (softcapped, scaled) logits.
fn top_k(logits: &[f32], k: usize) -> Vec<(u32, f32, f64)> {
    let max = logits.iter().copied().fold(f32::NEG_INFINITY, f32::max);
    let denom: f64 = logits
        .iter()
        .map(|&z| f64::from(z - max).exp())
        .sum::<f64>();
    let mut idx: Vec<u32> = (0..logits.len() as u32).collect();
    idx.sort_unstable_by(|&a, &b| {
        logits[b as usize]
            .partial_cmp(&logits[a as usize])
            .unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)
    });
    idx.truncate(k);
    idx.iter()
        .map(|&id| {
            let z = logits[id as usize];
            (id, z, f64::from(z - max).exp() / denom)
        })
        .collect()
}

fn print_top(label: &str, top: &[(u32, f32, f64)], vocab: &[String]) {
    for (rank, (id, logit, prob)) in top.iter().enumerate() {
        println!(
            "{label} rank={rank} id={id} tok={:?} logit={logit:.6} prob={prob:.6}",
            vocab[*id as usize]
        );
    }
    std::io::stdout().flush().ok();
}

fn peak_rss_kb() -> Option<u64> {
    let status = std::fs::read_to_string("/proc/self/status").ok()?;
    status
        .lines()
        .find(|l| l.starts_with("VmHWM:"))
        .and_then(|l| l.split_whitespace().nth(1))
        .and_then(|v| v.parse().ok())
}

fn run(
    path: &str,
    prompt: &str,
    n_tokens: usize,
    ids_only: bool,
    gpu: bool,
    gpu_trait: bool,
    gpu_argmax: bool,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let t_open = Instant::now();
    let file = gguf::GgufFile::open(Path::new(path)).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!("phase=open_file ms={}", t_open.elapsed().as_millis());
    println!("file: {path} bytes={}", file.file_len());

    let mut cfg = itak_loader::load_config(&file).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    // EXPERIMENT ONLY: see `experiment_logit_scale`. Defaults to the
    // file value; shipped behavior is unchanged.
    let file_scale = cfg.logit_scale;
    cfg.logit_scale = experiment_logit_scale(
        std::env::var("ITAK_EXPERIMENT_LOGIT_SCALE").ok().as_deref(),
        file_scale,
    )?;
    if cfg.logit_scale != file_scale {
        println!(
            "experiment: logit_scale overridden file={file_scale} forced={}",
            cfg.logit_scale
        );
    }
    println!(
        "config: layers={} hidden={} vocab={} bos={:?} logit_scale={} logit_softcap={}",
        cfg.block_count,
        cfg.hidden,
        cfg.vocab_size,
        file.tokenizer().map(|t| t.bos_token_id).unwrap_or(None),
        cfg.logit_scale,
        cfg.logit_softcap
    );

    // Tokenize before any weight work: the printed id sequence is
    // the exact input both engines are compared on.
    let info = file.tokenizer().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let tok_model = file
        .metadata()
        .opt_string("tokenizer.ggml.model")
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
        .map(str::to_string);
    let tokenizer =
        Tokenizer::new(data_from_info(&info, tok_model, None)).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let body = tokenizer.encode(prompt).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let add_bos = file
        .metadata()
        .get_bool("tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token")
        .unwrap_or(false);
    let mut ids: Vec<u32> = Vec::new();
    if add_bos {
        if let Some(bos) = info.bos_token_id {
            ids.push(bos);
        }
    }
    ids.extend_from_slice(&body);
    println!("prompt: {prompt:?}");
    println!("add_bos_token={add_bos} encode_ids={body:?}");
    println!("prompt_ids={ids:?}");
    std::io::stdout().flush().ok();
    if ids_only {
        println!("ids_only: stopping before weight load");
        return Ok(());
    }

    let report = itak_loader::coverage(&file, &cfg);
    report.require_complete().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!(
        "coverage: expected={} found={} missing={}",
        report.expected_count(),
        report.found_count(),
        report.missing().len()
    );

    let t_load = Instant::now();
    let weights = itak_loader::load_weights(&file, &cfg).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!("phase=load_weights ms={}", t_load.elapsed().as_millis());

    let vocab = info.tokens.clone();
    if gpu || gpu_argmax {
        return run_resident(
            &cfg, &weights, &ids, n_tokens, &vocab, &tokenizer, gpu_argmax,
        );
    }
    let t_backend = Instant::now();
    let backend: Box<dyn muse_glimmer::Compute> = if gpu_trait {
        Box::new(wgpu_compute::WgpuCompute::new().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?)
    } else {
        Box::new(cpu_compute::CpuCompute::new())
    };
    println!(
        "phase=backend_open backend={} ms={}",
        if gpu_trait { "wgpu-trait" } else { "cpu" },
        t_backend.elapsed().as_millis()
    );
    let model = GlimmerModel::with_diag(cfg, weights, backend, Arc::new(StderrDiag));
    let mut cache = PositionCache::new();

    let mut generated: Vec<u32> = Vec::new();
    let t_prefill = Instant::now();
    let logits = model.forward(&ids, &mut cache).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let prefill_ms = t_prefill.elapsed().as_millis();
    let top = top_k(&logits, 5);
    println!("phase=prefill ms={prefill_ms} prompt_tokens={}", ids.len());
    print_top("prefill_top", &top, &vocab);
    print_logit_stats("prefill", &logits, model.config());
    let mut next = top[0].0;
    generated.push(next);
    println!(
        "gen step=1 id={next} tok={:?} source=prefill",
        vocab[next as usize]
    );
    std::io::stdout().flush().ok();

    for step in 2..=n_tokens {
        let t_step = Instant::now();
        let logits = model
            .forward(&[next], &mut cache)
            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let ms = t_step.elapsed().as_millis();
        let top = top_k(&logits, 5);
        print_top(&format!("step{step}_top"), &top, &vocab);
        next = top[0].0;
        generated.push(next);
        println!(
            "gen step={step} id={next} tok={:?} ms={ms}",
            vocab[next as usize]
        );
        std::io::stdout().flush().ok();
    }

    let decoded = tokenizer.decode(&generated).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!("generated_ids={generated:?}");
    println!("generated_text={decoded:?}");
    if let Some(kb) = peak_rss_kb() {
        println!("peak_rss_kb={kb}");
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The `--gpu` path: the device-resident session. Same output
/// contract as the model path (phase lines, top-5 per step,
/// per-token wall times, generated ids and text), plus the
/// session build timing and the session's counters at the end
/// (submissions and readbacks per chunk are the numbers the
/// resident path exists to fix).
fn run_resident(
    cfg: &muse_glimmer::GlimmerConfig,
    weights: &muse_glimmer::Weights,
    ids: &[u32],
    n_tokens: usize,
    vocab: &[String],
    tokenizer: &Tokenizer,
    argmax_tail: bool,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let t_backend = Instant::now();
    let backend = wgpu_compute::WgpuCompute::new().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!(
        "phase=backend_open backend={} ms={}",
        if argmax_tail {
            "resident-argmax"
        } else {
            "resident"
        },
        t_backend.elapsed().as_millis()
    );
    let t_session = Instant::now();
    let mut session =
        wgpu_compute::ResidentSession::new(&backend, cfg, weights).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!("phase=session_build ms={}", t_session.elapsed().as_millis());

    let mut generated: Vec<u32> = Vec::new();
    let t_prefill = Instant::now();
    let mut next = if argmax_tail {
        let (top, logit) = session.forward_argmax(ids).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let prefill_ms = t_prefill.elapsed().as_millis();
        println!("phase=prefill ms={prefill_ms} prompt_tokens={}", ids.len());
        println!("prefill_argmax id={top} logit={logit:.6}");
        top
    } else {
        let logits = session.forward(ids).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let prefill_ms = t_prefill.elapsed().as_millis();
        let top = top_k(&logits, 5);
        println!("phase=prefill ms={prefill_ms} prompt_tokens={}", ids.len());
        print_top("prefill_top", &top, vocab);
        top[0].0
    };
    generated.push(next);
    println!(
        "gen step=1 id={next} tok={:?} source=prefill",
        vocab[next as usize]
    );
    std::io::stdout().flush().ok();

    for step in 2..=n_tokens {
        let t_step = Instant::now();
        if argmax_tail {
            let (top, logit) = session.forward_argmax(&[next]).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            let ms = t_step.elapsed().as_millis();
            next = top;
            generated.push(next);
            println!(
                "gen step={step} id={next} tok={:?} ms={ms} argmax_logit={logit:.6}",
                vocab[next as usize]
            );
        } else {
            let logits = session.forward(&[next]).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            let ms = t_step.elapsed().as_millis();
            let top = top_k(&logits, 5);
            print_top(&format!("step{step}_top"), &top, vocab);
            next = top[0].0;
            generated.push(next);
            println!(
                "gen step={step} id={next} tok={:?} ms={ms}",
                vocab[next as usize]
            );
        }
        std::io::stdout().flush().ok();
    }

    let decoded = tokenizer.decode(&generated).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!("generated_ids={generated:?}");
    println!("generated_text={decoded:?}");
    let stats = session.stats();
    println!(
        "phase=session_stats forwards={} chunks={} submissions={} aux_submissions={} \
         readbacks={} argmax_readbacks={} dispatches={} tokens={}",
        stats.forwards,
        stats.chunks,
        stats.submissions,
        stats.aux_submissions,
        stats.readbacks,
        stats.argmax_readbacks,
        stats.dispatches,
        stats.tokens
    );
    if let Some(kb) = peak_rss_kb() {
        println!("peak_rss_kb={kb}");
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod experiment_tests {
    use super::experiment_logit_scale;

    #[test]
    fn unset_env_keeps_the_file_value() {
        assert_eq!(experiment_logit_scale(None, 0.196_116_13), Ok(0.196_116_13));
    }

    #[test]
    fn set_env_forces_the_scale() {
        assert_eq!(experiment_logit_scale(Some("1.0"), 0.196_116_13), Ok(1.0));
        assert_eq!(experiment_logit_scale(Some("0.5"), 0.196_116_13), Ok(0.5));
    }

    #[test]
    fn bad_env_values_refuse() {
        assert!(experiment_logit_scale(Some("bogus"), 0.196_116_13).is_err());
        assert!(experiment_logit_scale(Some("0"), 0.196_116_13).is_err());
        assert!(experiment_logit_scale(Some("-1.0"), 0.196_116_13).is_err());
        assert!(experiment_logit_scale(Some("inf"), 0.196_116_13).is_err());
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/itak-loader/examples/glimmer_inventory.rs =====
//! Inventory check against a real GGUF file: parse the Glimmer config
//! from the file's own metadata through the itak-loader adapters, check
//! the file's tensor inventory against the muse-glimmer module's
//! expected names, and settle the one name the skeleton flagged as
//! convention-assumed (`output_norm.weight`) against the real file.
//!
//! Usage: `glimmer_inventory <path-to-gguf> [--full]`
//!
//! Default mode reads metadata and the tensor directory only, plus the
//! one `output_norm.weight` fetch through the TensorSource seam.
//! `--full` additionally loads the entire weight set through
//! [`itak_loader::load_weights`] (the real model is 15.59 GiB; the
//! host needs the RAM for the file image plus the served copies).
//! Exit status is 0 only when the config parses and coverage is
//! complete.

use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;

use muse_glimmer::{LayerWeights, TensorSource, TensorView};

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let Some(path) = args.get(1) else {
        eprintln!("usage: glimmer_inventory <path-to-gguf> [--full]");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    };
    let full = args.iter().any(|a| a == "--full");
    match run(path, full) {
        Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,
        Err(msg) => {
            eprintln!("FAIL: {msg}");
            ExitCode::FAILURE
        }
    }
}

fn run(path: &str, full: bool) -> Result<(), String> {
    let file = gguf::GgufFile::open(Path::new(path)).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!("file: {path}");
    println!("file bytes: {}", file.file_len());
    println!("tensors in file: {}", file.tensors().len());

    let cfg = itak_loader::load_config(&file).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!(
        "config: name={:?} layers={} context={} hidden={} ffn={} q_heads={} kv_heads={} key_len={} value_len={} window={} vocab={}",
        cfg.name,
        cfg.block_count,
        cfg.context_length,
        cfg.hidden,
        cfg.ffn_hidden,
        cfg.q_heads,
        cfg.kv_heads,
        cfg.key_length,
        cfg.value_length,
        cfg.sliding_window,
        cfg.vocab_size
    );
    println!(
        "config: rope_base={} rms_eps={} logit_softcap={} logit_scale={} pattern_source={:?} global_layers={} sliding_layers={}",
        cfg.rope_freq_base,
        cfg.rms_eps,
        cfg.logit_softcap,
        cfg.logit_scale,
        cfg.pattern_source,
        cfg.global_layer_count(),
        cfg.sliding_layer_count()
    );
    println!("global layer indices: {:?}", cfg.global_layer_indices());

    // Cross-check: the gguf crate's own generic config reader must
    // agree with the arch module's parse of the same metadata.
    let generic = file.model_config().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!(
        "cross-check gguf ModelConfig: arch={} layers={} hidden={} vocab={:?}",
        generic.architecture, generic.layer_count, generic.hidden_size, generic.vocab_size
    );
    if generic.layer_count != cfg.block_count
        || generic.hidden_size != cfg.hidden
        || generic.vocab_size != Some(cfg.vocab_size as usize)
    {
        return Err("arch module config and gguf ModelConfig disagree".to_string());
    }

    let report = itak_loader::coverage(&file, &cfg);
    println!(
        "coverage: expected={} found={} missing={} unexpected={}",
        report.expected_count(),
        report.found_count(),
        report.missing().len(),
        report.unexpected().len()
    );
    for name in report.missing() {
        println!("  MISSING {name}");
    }
    for name in report.unexpected() {
        println!("  UNEXPECTED {name}");
    }

    // The convention-assumed name, settled against the real file,
    // fetched through the TensorSource seam itself.
    let source = itak_loader::GgufTensorSource::new(&file);
    match source.tensor("output_norm.weight") {
        Ok(view) => println!(
            "output_norm.weight: PRESENT dtype={:?} shape={:?} elements={} bytes={}",
            view.dtype,
            view.shape,
            view.elements(),
            view.data.len()
        ),
        Err(e) => println!("output_norm.weight: NOT SERVED: {e}"),
    }

    report.require_complete().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

    if full {
        let weights = itak_loader::load_weights(&file, &cfg).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let mut tensors = 3usize;
        let mut bytes = weights.embedding.data.len()
            + weights.final_norm.data.len()
            + weights.output.data.len();
        for layer in &weights.layers {
            tensors += 14;
            bytes += layer_bytes(layer);
        }
        println!(
            "full load: {} layers, {} tensors, {} bytes served through TensorSource",
            weights.layers.len(),
            tensors,
            bytes
        );
        println!(
            "output head: name={} dtype={:?} shape={:?}",
            weights.output.name, weights.output.dtype, weights.output.shape
        );
        println!(
            "final norm (output_norm.weight): dtype={:?} shape={:?}",
            weights.final_norm.dtype, weights.final_norm.shape
        );
    }

    println!("VERDICT: config loaded from the real file; coverage complete");
    Ok(())
}

fn layer_bytes(layer: &LayerWeights) -> usize {
    let views: [&TensorView; 14] = [
        &layer.attn_norm,
        &layer.attn_q,
        &layer.attn_k,
        &layer.attn_v,
        &layer.attn_q_norm,
        &layer.attn_k_norm,
        &layer.attn_output,
        &layer.attn_gate,
        &layer.post_attention_norm,
        &layer.ffn_norm,
        &layer.ffn_gate,
        &layer.ffn_up,
        &layer.ffn_down,
        &layer.post_ffw_norm,
    ];
    views.iter().map(|v| v.data.len()).sum()
}

===== FILE: crates/itak-loader/examples/glimmer_layer_trace.rs =====
//! Per-layer activation trace for the muse-glimmer forward: the
//! localization tool for Integration Run B's first-token divergence
//! (see INTEGRATION-RUN-B.md and FORWARD-DIFF-PLAN.md in this
//! crate).
//!
//! Usage: `glimmer_layer_trace <path-to-gguf> [prompt]
//! [--first-n N] [--out <path>] [--ids-only]`
//!
//! The prompt defaults to the golden `factual_capital` prompt,
//! "The capital of France is", tokenized exactly as Run B tokenized
//! it (BOS prepended per the file's own metadata), so the ids are
//! the byte-identical input both engines consumed. The run is one
//! traced prefill over those ids: no decode steps, because the
//! divergence Run B measured is already total at prefill position 1.
//!
//! Output is the stable trace line format (version 1, documented in
//! the `muse_glimmer::trace` module): header lines naming the tool,
//! the model shape, and the prompt ids, then one line per stage
//! (`embed`, `layer.<i>.mid`, `layer.<i>.out`, `final_norm`,
//! `logits`) carrying whole-tensor and last-row statistics, then the
//! prefill top-5 in Run B's table format for a direct cross-check
//! against its position-1 numbers. `--out` writes the trace lines
//! to a file instead of stdout so the dump can be committed next to
//! a reference dump and diffed. `--ids-only` stops after printing
//! the prompt ids, before any weight work.
//!
//! This is a correctness tool, not a benchmark: one 30B prefill on
//! `cpu-compute` is minutes-class, exactly as Run B measured.

use std::io::Write;
use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Instant;

use muse_glimmer::{GlimmerModel, PositionCache, StderrDiag, TraceLog};
use tokenizer::{TokenType, Tokenizer, TokenizerData};

/// The prompt ids Integration Run B fed both engines, from
/// INTEGRATION-RUN-B.md. The dump is only comparable to Run B (and
/// to a reference dump) when the ids match these.
const RUN_B_IDS: [u32; 6] = [200000, 954, 7963, 323, 11698, 373];

/// The golden `factual_capital` prompt (golden/prompts.jsonl).
const GOLDEN_PROMPT: &str = "The capital of France is";

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let Some(path) = args.get(1) else {
        eprintln!(
            "usage: glimmer_layer_trace <path-to-gguf> [prompt] [--first-n N] [--out <path>] [--ids-only]"
        );
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    };
    let prompt = args
        .get(2)
        .filter(|a| !a.starts_with("--"))
        .map_or(GOLDEN_PROMPT, String::as_str);
    let first_n: usize = parse_flag(&args, "--first-n").map_or(8, |v| v.parse().unwrap_or(8));
    let out = parse_flag(&args, "--out");
    let ids_only = args.iter().any(|a| a == "--ids-only");
    match run(path, prompt, first_n, out, ids_only) {
        Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,
        Err(msg) => {
            eprintln!("FAIL: {msg}");
            ExitCode::FAILURE
        }
    }
}

/// The value following `--name` in the argument list, if present.
fn parse_flag<'a>(args: &'a [String], name: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {
    args.windows(2)
        .find(|w| w[0] == name)
        .map(|w| w[1].as_str())
}

/// Adapts the gguf crate's parsed tokenizer info into the tokenizer
/// crate's input data. Same thin adapter as the other runners in
/// this crate; it lives in harness code, not in either library.
fn data_from_info(
    info: &gguf::TokenizerInfo,
    model: Option<String>,
    unknown: Option<u32>,
) -> TokenizerData {
    TokenizerData {
        model,
        tokens: info.tokens.clone(),
        token_types: info
            .token_types
            .as_ref()
            .map(|types| types.iter().map(|&t| TokenType::from_gguf(t)).collect())
            .unwrap_or_default(),
        merges: info.merges.clone().unwrap_or_default(),
        scores: info.scores.clone(),
        bos_token_id: info.bos_token_id,
        eos_token_id: info.eos_token_id,
        unknown_token_id: unknown,
        padding_token_id: info.padding_token_id,
    }
}

/// The `k` highest logits as (id, logit, softmax probability over
/// the whole vocabulary), best first. Same helper as
/// glimmer_generate, so the top-5 prints are directly comparable.
fn top_k(logits: &[f32], k: usize) -> Vec<(u32, f32, f64)> {
    let max = logits.iter().copied().fold(f32::NEG_INFINITY, f32::max);
    let denom: f64 = logits
        .iter()
        .map(|&z| f64::from(z - max).exp())
        .sum::<f64>();
    let mut idx: Vec<u32> = (0..logits.len() as u32).collect();
    idx.sort_unstable_by(|&a, &b| {
        logits[b as usize]
            .partial_cmp(&logits[a as usize])
            .unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)
    });
    idx.truncate(k);
    idx.iter()
        .map(|&id| {
            let z = logits[id as usize];
            (id, z, f64::from(z - max).exp() / denom)
        })
        .collect()
}

fn run(
    path: &str,
    prompt: &str,
    first_n: usize,
    out: Option<&str>,
    ids_only: bool,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let file = gguf::GgufFile::open(Path::new(path)).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!("trace_header v=1 tool=glimmer_layer_trace");
    println!("file: {path} bytes={}", file.file_len());

    let cfg = itak_loader::load_config(&file).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!(
        "config: layers={} hidden={} vocab={}",
        cfg.block_count, cfg.hidden, cfg.vocab_size
    );

    // Tokenize before any weight work, exactly as Run B did: the
    // printed ids are the contract the reference dump must match.
    let info = file.tokenizer().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let tok_model = file
        .metadata()
        .opt_string("tokenizer.ggml.model")
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
        .map(str::to_string);
    let tokenizer =
        Tokenizer::new(data_from_info(&info, tok_model, None)).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let body = tokenizer.encode(prompt).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let add_bos = file
        .metadata()
        .get_bool("tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token")
        .unwrap_or(false);
    let mut ids: Vec<u32> = Vec::new();
    if add_bos {
        if let Some(bos) = info.bos_token_id {
            ids.push(bos);
        }
    }
    ids.extend_from_slice(&body);
    println!("prompt: {prompt:?}");
    println!("prompt_ids={ids:?}");
    println!("run_b_ids_match={}", ids.as_slice() == RUN_B_IDS);
    std::io::stdout().flush().ok();
    if ids_only {
        println!("ids_only: stopping before weight load");
        return Ok(());
    }

    let report = itak_loader::coverage(&file, &cfg);
    report.require_complete().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!(
        "coverage: expected={} found={} missing={}",
        report.expected_count(),
        report.found_count(),
        report.missing().len()
    );

    let t_load = Instant::now();
    let weights = itak_loader::load_weights(&file, &cfg).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!("phase=load_weights ms={}", t_load.elapsed().as_millis());

    let vocab = info.tokens.clone();
    let model = GlimmerModel::with_diag(
        cfg,
        weights,
        Box::new(cpu_compute::CpuCompute::new()),
        Arc::new(StderrDiag),
    );
    let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
    let mut log = TraceLog::new(first_n);

    let t_prefill = Instant::now();
    let logits = model
        .forward_traced(&ids, &mut cache, &mut log)
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!(
        "phase=traced_prefill ms={} prompt_tokens={} stages={}",
        t_prefill.elapsed().as_millis(),
        ids.len(),
        log.records().len()
    );

    let lines = log.lines();
    match out {
        Some(out_path) => {
            let mut text = lines.join("\n");
            text.push('\n');
            std::fs::write(out_path, text).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            println!("trace_out={out_path} lines={}", lines.len());
        }
        None => {
            for line in &lines {
                println!("{line}");
            }
        }
    }
    std::io::stdout().flush().ok();

    // Cross-check against Run B's position-1 table: the traced
    // prefill must reproduce its top-5 exactly, or the trace itself
    // is not measuring the same forward.
    for (rank, (id, logit, prob)) in top_k(&logits, 5).iter().enumerate() {
        println!(
            "prefill_top rank={rank} id={id} tok={:?} logit={logit:.6} prob={prob:.6}",
            vocab[*id as usize]
        );
    }
    std::io::stdout().flush().ok();
    Ok(())
}
