===== FILE: crates/itak-loader/examples/prefill_profile.rs =====
//! Prefill profile harness: where does Glimmer prefill time
//! actually go, per kernel, on the resident GPU path?
//!
//! Usage: `prefill_profile <path-to-gguf> <prompt>`
//!
//! Loads the real file exactly like `glimmer_generate`
//! (gguf parse, `itak-loader` config and weights behind the
//! coverage gate, the same tokenizer adapter), builds the
//! device-resident session in `wgpu-compute`, then feeds the
//! prompt through `ResidentSession::forward` in slices of
//! `PREFILL_PROFILE_SLICE` tokens (default 64, the session's
//! chunk cap), draining the diag timestamp recorder after
//! every slice so no dispatch window is ever lost to the
//! recorder's 2,048-window cap.
//!
//! With `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing` set, the run is timed per
//! dispatch: at the end the per-kernel summary table is
//! printed and written to the path in `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG_OUT`
//! (the same env the diag smoke collector uses), and the raw
//! per-dispatch records land beside it as
//! `<out>.records.csv` for shape-level analysis. With the
//! diag env unset the recorder does not exist, the encode
//! path is the shipped byte-identical off path, and the run
//! is the timing-off control: same binary, same slices, only
//! the `phase=prefill` wall time is comparable.
//!
//! Wall-time caveat, stated once here and in the bench note:
//! in timing mode each slice boundary pays a drain (a resolve
//! submit plus a blocking map), which serializes the pipeline
//! between slices. The per-kernel GPU durations are measured
//! on the device and are unaffected; the timing-mode wall
//! `phase=prefill` is therefore an upper bound, and the
//! off-mode wall is the prefill wall of record.

use std::io::Write;
use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;
use std::time::Instant;

use tokenizer::{TokenType, Tokenizer, TokenizerData};
use wgpu_compute::timestamps::{render_summary, DIAG_OUT_ENV};

/// Adapts the gguf crate's parsed tokenizer info into the tokenizer
/// crate's input data. Same thin adapter as `glimmer_generate`
/// (TODO T-2.3); it lives in harness code, not in either library.
fn data_from_info(
    info: &gguf::TokenizerInfo,
    model: Option<String>,
    unknown: Option<u32>,
) -> TokenizerData {
    TokenizerData {
        model,
        tokens: info.tokens.clone(),
        token_types: info
            .token_types
            .as_ref()
            .map(|types| types.iter().map(|&t| TokenType::from_gguf(t)).collect())
            .unwrap_or_default(),
        merges: info.merges.clone().unwrap_or_default(),
        scores: info.scores.clone(),
        bos_token_id: info.bos_token_id,
        eos_token_id: info.eos_token_id,
        unknown_token_id: unknown,
        padding_token_id: info.padding_token_id,
    }
}

/// Slice-size resolution: the env override applies only inside
/// 1..=1024; anything else falls back to 64, the session's chunk
/// cap and the bench protocol's row count.
fn resolve_slice_rows(raw: Option<&str>) -> usize {
    raw.and_then(|v| v.parse().ok())
        .filter(|&v| (1..=1024).contains(&v))
        .unwrap_or(64)
}

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let (Some(path), Some(prompt)) = (args.get(1), args.get(2)) else {
        eprintln!("usage: prefill_profile <path-to-gguf> <prompt>");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    };
    match run(path, prompt) {
        Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,
        Err(msg) => {
            eprintln!("FAIL: {msg}");
            ExitCode::FAILURE
        }
    }
}

fn run(path: &str, prompt: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    let slice_rows = resolve_slice_rows(std::env::var("PREFILL_PROFILE_SLICE").ok().as_deref());

    let file = gguf::GgufFile::open(Path::new(path)).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!("file: {path} bytes={}", file.file_len());
    let cfg = itak_loader::load_config(&file).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!(
        "config: layers={} hidden={} vocab={}",
        cfg.block_count, cfg.hidden, cfg.vocab_size
    );

    // Tokenize before any weight work, exactly like
    // glimmer_generate, so the prompt id sequence is the bench
    // protocol's own.
    let info = file.tokenizer().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let tok_model = file
        .metadata()
        .opt_string("tokenizer.ggml.model")
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
        .map(str::to_string);
    let tokenizer =
        Tokenizer::new(data_from_info(&info, tok_model, None)).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let body = tokenizer.encode(prompt).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let add_bos = file
        .metadata()
        .get_bool("tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token")
        .unwrap_or(false);
    let mut ids: Vec<u32> = Vec::new();
    if add_bos {
        if let Some(bos) = info.bos_token_id {
            ids.push(bos);
        }
    }
    ids.extend_from_slice(&body);
    println!("prompt_tokens={} slice_rows={slice_rows}", ids.len());
    std::io::stdout().flush().ok();

    let report = itak_loader::coverage(&file, &cfg);
    report.require_complete().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let t_load = Instant::now();
    let weights = itak_loader::load_weights(&file, &cfg).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!("phase=load_weights ms={}", t_load.elapsed().as_millis());

    let t_backend = Instant::now();
    let backend = wgpu_compute::WgpuCompute::new().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!(
        "phase=backend_open backend=resident ms={}",
        t_backend.elapsed().as_millis()
    );
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let recorder = ctx.diag_recorder().cloned();
    let timing = recorder.is_some();
    println!(
        "diag: mode={} recorder={}",
        if timing { "timing" } else { "off" },
        if timing { "present" } else { "absent" }
    );
    if std::env::var("WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG").is_ok_and(|v| v == "timing") && !timing {
        return Err(
            "WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing requested but no diag recorder exists \
             (device granted no timestamp features); refusing to profile blind"
                .to_string(),
        );
    }

    let t_session = Instant::now();
    let mut session =
        wgpu_compute::ResidentSession::new(&backend, &cfg, &weights).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    println!("phase=session_build ms={}", t_session.elapsed().as_millis());
    std::io::stdout().flush().ok();

    let t_prefill = Instant::now();
    let mut last_logits: Vec<f32> = Vec::new();
    let mut drained_total = 0usize;
    for (i, slice) in ids.chunks(slice_rows).enumerate() {
        let t_slice = Instant::now();
        last_logits = session.forward(slice).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let slice_ms = t_slice.elapsed().as_millis();
        let mut drained = 0usize;
        if let Some(rec) = &recorder {
            drained = rec
                .drain(&ctx.device, &ctx.queue)
                .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            drained_total += drained;
        }
        println!(
            "slice={} tokens={} ms={} drained={}",
            i,
            slice.len(),
            slice_ms,
            drained
        );
        std::io::stdout().flush().ok();
    }
    let prefill_ms = t_prefill.elapsed().as_millis();
    println!("phase=prefill ms={prefill_ms} prompt_tokens={}", ids.len());

    // Sanity anchor only (this harness is a profiler, not a
    // correctness gate): the winning first token and its logit.
    if let Some((pos, _)) = last_logits
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .max_by(|a, b| a.1.partial_cmp(b.1).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal))
    {
        println!("prefill_argmax id={pos} logit={:.6}", last_logits[pos]);
    }

    let stats = session.stats();
    println!(
        "phase=session_stats forwards={} chunks={} submissions={} aux_submissions={} \
         readbacks={} argmax_readbacks={} dispatches={} tokens={}",
        stats.forwards,
        stats.chunks,
        stats.submissions,
        stats.aux_submissions,
        stats.readbacks,
        stats.argmax_readbacks,
        stats.dispatches,
        stats.tokens
    );

    if let Some(rec) = &recorder {
        let records = rec.take_records();
        println!(
            "diag_records={} drained_total={} dropped={}",
            records.len(),
            drained_total,
            rec.dropped()
        );
        let table = render_summary(&records);
        print!("{table}");
        std::io::stdout().flush().ok();
        if let Some(out_path) = std::env::var_os(DIAG_OUT_ENV) {
            let out_path = out_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
            std::fs::write(&out_path, &table)
                .map_err(|e| format!("writing diag summary to {out_path}: {e}"))?;
            let mut raw =
                String::from("index,kernel,rows,cols,quant,weight_bytes,shape,duration_ns\n");
            for r in &records {
                raw.push_str(&format!(
                    "{},{},{},{},{},{},{},{}\n",
                    r.index,
                    r.kernel,
                    r.rows,
                    r.cols,
                    r.quant,
                    r.weight_bytes,
                    r.shape.replace(',', ";"),
                    r.duration_ns
                ));
            }
            let raw_path = format!("{out_path}.records.csv");
            std::fs::write(&raw_path, raw)
                .map_err(|e| format!("writing diag records to {raw_path}: {e}"))?;
            println!("diag_out={out_path} records_out={raw_path}");
        } else {
            println!("diag_out=unset (summary printed only)");
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod slice_tests {
    use super::resolve_slice_rows;

    /// The slice-size resolution rule, pinned: the env override
    /// applies only inside 1..=1024; anything else falls back to
    /// the 64-row chunk cap the bench protocol runs at.
    #[test]
    fn slice_resolution() {
        assert_eq!(resolve_slice_rows(None), 64);
        assert_eq!(resolve_slice_rows(Some("64")), 64);
        assert_eq!(resolve_slice_rows(Some("128")), 128);
        assert_eq!(resolve_slice_rows(Some("0")), 64);
        assert_eq!(resolve_slice_rows(Some("4096")), 64);
        assert_eq!(resolve_slice_rows(Some("bogus")), 64);
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/itak-loader/src/adapter.rs =====
//! The adapters: muse-glimmer's [`Metadata`] and [`TensorSource`]
//! traits implemented over a parsed [`GgufFile`].
//!
//! The two traits have different error shapes and the adapters respect
//! both. [`Metadata`] returns `Option`: `None` means absent or a
//! genuinely different kind of value, per the trait contract. The
//! `gguf` crate's getters fail loud with named errors; the adapter
//! translates, and when a key is present but unreadable as the
//! requested kind it says so on the diag channel, because that is the
//! fact a debugging session needs and the `Option` has no room for it.
//! Integer coercion (any stored width into `u32`) is the `gguf`
//! getter's own lossless widening, not a second implementation here.
//!
//! [`TensorSource`] returns the arch module's `Result`: absent tensors
//! map to [`GlimmerError::MissingTensor`], and present-but-undeliverable
//! tensors (a ggml type the `gguf` crate cannot size or read) map to
//! [`GlimmerError::TensorUnreadable`] with the loader's reason attached.
//! Neither adapter ever invents a value: no default metadata, no
//! placeholder bytes.

use std::sync::Arc;

use gguf::{GgufError, GgufFile, MetadataValue};
use muse_glimmer::{
    Dtype, GlimmerError, Metadata, Result as GlimmerResult, TensorSource, TensorView,
};

use crate::diag;

/// muse-glimmer's [`Metadata`] trait over one parsed GGUF file.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct GgufMetadata<'a> {
    file: &'a GgufFile,
}

impl<'a> GgufMetadata<'a> {
    /// Wrap a parsed file.
    pub fn new(file: &'a GgufFile) -> Self {
        Self { file }
    }

    /// The wrapped file.
    pub fn file(&self) -> &'a GgufFile {
        self.file
    }

    /// A present key whose value cannot be read as the requested kind
    /// is worth a diag line even though the trait answer is `None`.
    fn note_unreadable(&self, key: &str, err: &GgufError) {
        if self.file.metadata().get(key).is_some() {
            diag::debug("metadata_unreadable", &format!("key={key} reason={err}"));
        }
    }
}

impl Metadata for GgufMetadata<'_> {
    // The scalar getters route through the `gguf` crate's `opt_*`
    // reads, never the strict getters: the strict getters build their
    // refusal through `require`, which logs a `missing_metadata`
    // error event for a merely absent key. Absence is a legitimate
    // answer to an optional probe (llama.cpp reads
    // `rope.freq_base_swa` exactly that way: an optional override
    // over the train base), so it must stay silent. A present key
    // holding the wrong kind of value still refuses inside the
    // `opt_*` read, and that refusal is logged there and noted here.
    fn get_string(&self, key: &str) -> Option<String> {
        match self.file.metadata().opt_string(key) {
            Ok(v) => v.map(str::to_string),
            Err(e) => {
                self.note_unreadable(key, &e);
                None
            }
        }
    }

    fn get_u32(&self, key: &str) -> Option<u32> {
        match self.file.metadata().opt_u32(key) {
            Ok(v) => v,
            Err(e) => {
                self.note_unreadable(key, &e);
                None
            }
        }
    }

    fn get_f32(&self, key: &str) -> Option<f32> {
        match self.file.metadata().opt_f32(key) {
            Ok(v) => v,
            Err(e) => {
                self.note_unreadable(key, &e);
                None
            }
        }
    }

    fn get_array_len(&self, key: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        match self.file.metadata().get(key) {
            Some(MetadataValue::Array(items)) => Some(items.len()),
            Some(_) => {
                diag::debug(
                    "metadata_unreadable",
                    &format!("key={key} reason=stored value is not an array"),
                );
                None
            }
            None => None,
        }
    }

    fn get_bool_array(&self, key: &str) -> Option<Vec<bool>> {
        // Raw lookup, like get_array_len: absence is silent, and a
        // present value of the wrong shape earns the diag line here
        // (the strict array getters would log absence as an error,
        // which an optional probe must not do).
        match self.file.metadata().get(key) {
            Some(MetadataValue::Array(items)) => {
                let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(items.len());
                for item in items {
                    match item {
                        MetadataValue::Bool(v) => out.push(*v),
                        other => {
                            diag::debug(
                                "metadata_unreadable",
                                &format!(
                                    "key={key} reason=array element is {}, not bool",
                                    other.type_name()
                                ),
                            );
                            return None;
                        }
                    }
                }
                Some(out)
            }
            Some(_) => {
                diag::debug(
                    "metadata_unreadable",
                    &format!("key={key} reason=stored value is not an array"),
                );
                None
            }
            None => None,
        }
    }
}

/// muse-glimmer's [`TensorSource`] trait over one parsed GGUF file.
///
/// Tensor bytes are copied out of the file image into an [`Arc`]:
/// [`TensorView`] owns its bytes by contract, and the `gguf` crate's
/// borrowed slices cannot outlive the file through that API. The copy
/// is one memcpy per tensor at load time; nothing in the token loop
/// touches this path.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct GgufTensorSource<'a> {
    file: &'a GgufFile,
}

impl<'a> GgufTensorSource<'a> {
    /// Wrap a parsed file.
    pub fn new(file: &'a GgufFile) -> Self {
        Self { file }
    }

    /// The wrapped file.
    pub fn file(&self) -> &'a GgufFile {
        self.file
    }
}

impl TensorSource for GgufTensorSource<'_> {
    fn tensor(&self, name: &str) -> GlimmerResult<TensorView> {
        let info = self
            .file
            .tensor_info(name)
            .map_err(|e| map_tensor_error(name, e))?;
        let bytes = self
            .file
            .tensor_bytes(name)
            .map_err(|e| map_tensor_error(name, e))?;
        diag::debug(
            "tensor_served",
            &format!(
                "name={name} type={} elements={} bytes={}",
                info.type_name(),
                info.element_count(),
                bytes.len()
            ),
        );
        Ok(TensorView {
            name: name.to_string(),
            dtype: Dtype::from_ggml_id(info.type_id()),
            shape: info.dims().to_vec(),
            data: Arc::from(bytes),
        })
    }
}

/// Translate a `gguf` refusal into the arch module's vocabulary:
/// absent is `MissingTensor`, everything else is `TensorUnreadable`
/// with the loader's own words kept as the detail.
fn map_tensor_error(name: &str, err: GgufError) -> GlimmerError {
    match err {
        GgufError::MissingTensor(_) => GlimmerError::MissingTensor {
            name: name.to_string(),
        },
        other => GlimmerError::TensorUnreadable {
            name: name.to_string(),
            detail: other.to_string(),
        },
    }
}

/// dflash's [`Metadata`](dflash::Metadata) trait over one parsed
/// GGUF file. Same translation discipline as [`GgufMetadata`]: an
/// unreadable-but-present key earns a diag line, never a fabricated
/// value.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct DflashMetadata<'a> {
    file: &'a GgufFile,
}

impl<'a> DflashMetadata<'a> {
    /// Wrap a parsed file.
    pub fn new(file: &'a GgufFile) -> Self {
        Self { file }
    }

    /// The wrapped file.
    pub fn file(&self) -> &'a GgufFile {
        self.file
    }

    fn note_unreadable(&self, key: &str, err: &GgufError) {
        if self.file.metadata().get(key).is_some() {
            diag::debug("metadata_unreadable", &format!("key={key} reason={err}"));
        }
    }
}

impl dflash::Metadata for DflashMetadata<'_> {
    fn get_string(&self, key: &str) -> Option<String> {
        match self.file.metadata().get_string(key) {
            Ok(v) => Some(v.to_string()),
            Err(e) => {
                self.note_unreadable(key, &e);
                None
            }
        }
    }

    fn get_u32(&self, key: &str) -> Option<u32> {
        match self.file.metadata().get_u32(key) {
            Ok(v) => Some(v),
            Err(e) => {
                self.note_unreadable(key, &e);
                None
            }
        }
    }

    fn get_f32(&self, key: &str) -> Option<f32> {
        match self.file.metadata().get_f32(key) {
            Ok(v) => Some(v),
            Err(e) => {
                self.note_unreadable(key, &e);
                None
            }
        }
    }

    fn get_bool(&self, key: &str) -> Option<bool> {
        match self.file.metadata().get_bool(key) {
            Ok(v) => Some(v),
            Err(e) => {
                self.note_unreadable(key, &e);
                None
            }
        }
    }

    fn get_u32_array(&self, key: &str) -> Option<Vec<u32>> {
        match self.file.metadata().get_u32_array(key) {
            Ok(v) => Some(v),
            Err(e) => {
                self.note_unreadable(key, &e);
                None
            }
        }
    }

    fn get_bool_array(&self, key: &str) -> Option<Vec<bool>> {
        // Through the `opt_*` read, like the scalar fix on
        // [`GgufMetadata`]: the strict `get_array` builds its
        // refusal through `require`, which logs a
        // `missing_metadata` error event for a merely absent
        // key, and absence is a legitimate answer to this probe
        // (the caller turns `None` into its own named refusal).
        // A present key holding a non-array value still refuses
        // inside the `opt_*` read, logged there and noted here;
        // a non-bool element earns the diag line below.
        match self.file.metadata().opt_array(key) {
            Ok(None) => None,
            Ok(Some(items)) => {
                let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(items.len());
                for item in items {
                    match item {
                        MetadataValue::Bool(v) => out.push(*v),
                        other => {
                            diag::debug(
                                "metadata_unreadable",
                                &format!(
                                    "key={key} reason=array element is {}, not bool",
                                    other.type_name()
                                ),
                            );
                            return None;
                        }
                    }
                }
                Some(out)
            }
            Err(e) => {
                self.note_unreadable(key, &e);
                None
            }
        }
    }

    fn get_array_len(&self, key: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        match self.file.metadata().get(key) {
            Some(MetadataValue::Array(items)) => Some(items.len()),
            Some(_) => {
                diag::debug(
                    "metadata_unreadable",
                    &format!("key={key} reason=stored value is not an array"),
                );
                None
            }
            None => None,
        }
    }
}

/// dflash's [`TensorSource`](dflash::TensorSource) trait over one
/// parsed GGUF file. Unlike the muse-glimmer adapter, which serves
/// raw stored views, this one serves tensors dequantized to f32
/// (the dflash module's `TensorData` contract) through the `gguf`
/// crate's own loader, so dtype support is exactly the `gguf`
/// crate's and anything else refuses by name.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct DflashTensorSource<'a> {
    file: &'a GgufFile,
}

impl<'a> DflashTensorSource<'a> {
    /// Wrap a parsed file.
    pub fn new(file: &'a GgufFile) -> Self {
        Self { file }
    }

    /// The wrapped file.
    pub fn file(&self) -> &'a GgufFile {
        self.file
    }
}

impl dflash::TensorSource for DflashTensorSource<'_> {
    fn tensor(&self, name: &str) -> dflash::Result<dflash::TensorData> {
        let info = self
            .file
            .tensor_info(name)
            .map_err(|e| map_dflash_tensor_error(name, e))?;
        let data = self
            .file
            .load_f32(name)
            .map_err(|e| map_dflash_tensor_error(name, e))?;
        diag::debug(
            "tensor_served",
            &format!(
                "name={name} type={} elements={}",
                info.type_name(),
                info.element_count()
            ),
        );
        Ok(dflash::TensorData {
            name: name.to_string(),
            shape: info.dims().to_vec(),
            data,
        })
    }

    fn has_tensor(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.file.has_tensor(name)
    }
}

/// Translate a `gguf` refusal into the dflash module's vocabulary.
fn map_dflash_tensor_error(name: &str, err: GgufError) -> dflash::DflashError {
    match err {
        GgufError::MissingTensor(_) => dflash::DflashError::MissingTensor {
            name: name.to_string(),
        },
        other => dflash::DflashError::TensorUnreadable {
            name: name.to_string(),
            detail: other.to_string(),
        },
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/itak-loader/src/coverage.rs =====
//! The tensor inventory check: a file's tensor names against the arch
//! module's expected names.
//!
//! This is the mechanical form of the audit's central lesson. The
//! original engine loaded models through a Llama-shaped template and
//! never noticed the tensors it had not looked up; here the arch
//! module publishes its full expectation
//! ([`muse_glimmer::expected_tensor_names`]) and this module checks a
//! real file against it, name by name, before a single byte of weight
//! data moves. A miss fails by name, all of them at once.
//!
//! Names the file carries beyond the expectation are reported as
//! `unexpected`, not treated as failures: files legitimately carry
//! tensors a given arch module does not consume (a vision tower beside
//! the language model, for instance), and hiding them would be its own
//! kind of silence. They are printed so a human can judge them.

use std::collections::HashSet;

use gguf::GgufFile;
use muse_glimmer::{expected_tensor_names, GlimmerConfig};

use crate::diag;
use crate::error::{LoaderError, Result};

/// The outcome of one inventory check.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct CoverageReport {
    expected: Vec<String>,
    present: Vec<String>,
    missing: Vec<String>,
    unexpected: Vec<String>,
}

impl CoverageReport {
    /// Every name the arch module expects, in its load order.
    pub fn expected(&self) -> &[String] {
        &self.expected
    }

    /// Expected names found in the file, in expected order.
    pub fn present(&self) -> &[String] {
        &self.present
    }

    /// Expected names absent from the file, in expected order.
    pub fn missing(&self) -> &[String] {
        &self.missing
    }

    /// Names the file carries that the arch module does not expect,
    /// in file order.
    pub fn unexpected(&self) -> &[String] {
        &self.unexpected
    }

    /// How many names the arch module expects.
    pub fn expected_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.expected.len()
    }

    /// How many expected names the file has.
    pub fn found_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.present.len()
    }

    /// True when every expected name is present.
    pub fn is_complete(&self) -> bool {
        self.missing.is_empty()
    }

    /// The gate form of the check: `Ok` when complete, otherwise a
    /// [`LoaderError::MissingTensors`] naming every miss.
    pub fn require_complete(&self) -> Result<()> {
        if self.missing.is_empty() {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            diag::debug(
                "coverage_incomplete",
                &format!("missing={}", self.missing.join(",")),
            );
            Err(LoaderError::MissingTensors(self.missing.clone()))
        }
    }
}

/// Run the inventory check of `file` against the expectation derived
/// from `cfg`.
pub fn coverage(file: &GgufFile, cfg: &GlimmerConfig) -> CoverageReport {
    coverage_for(file, expected_tensor_names(cfg))
}

/// Run the inventory check of `file` against the dflash module's
/// expectation derived from `cfg`. The module's optional tensors
/// (its own embedding table and head, the per-layer post norms) join
/// the expectation when the file carries them, so `unexpected`
/// keeps its meaning: names nobody accounted for, which for this
/// arch includes the variant gates the load refuses by name.
pub fn coverage_dflash(file: &GgufFile, cfg: &dflash::DflashConfig) -> CoverageReport {
    let mut expected = dflash::expected_tensor_names(cfg);
    for name in dflash::optional_tensor_names(cfg) {
        if file.has_tensor(&name) {
            expected.push(name);
        }
    }
    coverage_for(file, expected)
}

/// The shared inventory check over an explicit expectation list.
fn coverage_for(file: &GgufFile, expected: Vec<String>) -> CoverageReport {
    let mut present = Vec::new();
    let mut missing = Vec::new();
    for name in &expected {
        if file.has_tensor(name) {
            present.push(name.clone());
        } else {
            missing.push(name.clone());
        }
    }
    let expected_set: HashSet<&str> = expected.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();
    let unexpected: Vec<String> = file
        .tensor_names()
        .filter(|name| !expected_set.contains(name))
        .map(str::to_string)
        .collect();
    diag::debug(
        "coverage",
        &format!(
            "expected={} found={} missing={} unexpected={}",
            expected.len(),
            present.len(),
            missing.len(),
            unexpected.len()
        ),
    );
    CoverageReport {
        expected,
        present,
        missing,
        unexpected,
    }
}

===== END FILE: crates/itak-loader/src/coverage.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/itak-loader/src/diag.rs =====
//! Structured diagnostics for the loader bridge.
//!
//! David's rule: debugging is built into every module from birth, not
//! bolted on after a failure. This module is the crate's diagnostic
//! channel, mirroring the `gguf` crate's channel so engine logs read
//! the same across crates:
//!
//! - Enable with [`set_debug_enabled`] or the `ITAK_LOADER_DEBUG`
//!   environment variable (checked on every [`debug_enabled`] call, so
//!   a test or a long-running process can flip it at runtime).
//! - Output is structured `key=value` lines on stderr, tagged
//!   `[itak-loader][debug]`, so logs can be grepped and parsed
//!   mechanically.
//! - The events worth investigating pass through here: config loads,
//!   coverage verdicts, tensors served, and every coercion the metadata
//!   adapter had to refuse (a key that is present but holds the wrong
//!   kind of value is exactly the fact a debugging session needs, and
//!   the `Metadata` trait's `Option` return has no room to carry it).

use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};

static DEBUG_ENABLED: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);

/// Turn structured debug logging on or off for the whole process.
pub fn set_debug_enabled(enabled: bool) {
    DEBUG_ENABLED.store(enabled, Ordering::Relaxed);
}

/// Whether debug logging is active: the explicit flag, or
/// `ITAK_LOADER_DEBUG` present in the environment (any value other
/// than `0`).
pub fn debug_enabled() -> bool {
    if DEBUG_ENABLED.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
        return true;
    }
    match std::env::var("ITAK_LOADER_DEBUG") {
        Ok(v) => v != "0" && !v.is_empty(),
        Err(_) => false,
    }
}

/// Emit one structured debug line if diagnostics are enabled.
///
/// `event` is a short snake_case name; `fields` are `key=value`
/// fragments the caller has already formatted. Keeping formatting at
/// the call site keeps this channel allocation-light and
/// dependency-free.
pub fn debug(event: &str, fields: &str) {
    if debug_enabled() {
        eprintln!("[itak-loader][debug] event={event} {fields}");
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn flag_round_trips() {
        set_debug_enabled(true);
        assert!(debug_enabled());
        set_debug_enabled(false);
        // Env may still enable it in a developer shell; only assert the
        // flag store did not panic and the API is callable in both
        // states.
        let _ = debug_enabled();
    }
}

===== END FILE: crates/itak-loader/src/diag.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/itak-loader/src/error.rs =====
//! Error types for the loader bridge.
//!
//! Design rule (carried from the 2026-10-29 audit of the original Go
//! engine): every failure is loud and names the thing that failed. The
//! coverage failure names every missing tensor, not just the first,
//! because an inventory check that dribbles out one name per run is a
//! debugging tax.

use std::fmt;

use gguf::GgufError;
use muse_glimmer::GlimmerError;

/// Result alias for loader operations.
pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, LoaderError>;

/// Everything that can go wrong while bridging a GGUF file into an
/// architecture module.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum LoaderError {
    /// The tensor inventory check found expected tensors absent from
    /// the file. Carries the complete missing list, in the arch
    /// module's expected order.
    MissingTensors(Vec<String>),
    /// The architecture module refused something (bad config, a tensor
    /// it could not take). Passed through unwrapped in kind so callers
    /// can match on the arch module's own error variants.
    Glimmer(GlimmerError),
    /// The dflash module refused something. Same pass-through rule
    /// as [`LoaderError::Glimmer`].
    Dflash(dflash::DflashError),
    /// The GGUF loader refused something (parse or read failure).
    Gguf(GgufError),
}

impl fmt::Display for LoaderError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            LoaderError::MissingTensors(names) => write!(
                f,
                "tensor inventory incomplete: {} expected tensor(s) absent: {}",
                names.len(),
                names.join(", ")
            ),
            LoaderError::Glimmer(e) => write!(f, "{e}"),
            LoaderError::Dflash(e) => write!(f, "{e}"),
            LoaderError::Gguf(e) => write!(f, "{e}"),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for LoaderError {
    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {
        match self {
            LoaderError::MissingTensors(_) => None,
            LoaderError::Glimmer(e) => Some(e),
            LoaderError::Dflash(e) => Some(e),
            LoaderError::Gguf(e) => Some(e),
        }
    }
}

impl From<GlimmerError> for LoaderError {
    fn from(e: GlimmerError) -> Self {
        Self::Glimmer(e)
    }
}

impl From<dflash::DflashError> for LoaderError {
    fn from(e: dflash::DflashError) -> Self {
        Self::Dflash(e)
    }
}

impl From<GgufError> for LoaderError {
    fn from(e: GgufError) -> Self {
        Self::Gguf(e)
    }
}

===== END FILE: crates/itak-loader/src/error.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/itak-loader/src/lib.rs =====
//! itak-loader: the bridge between the `gguf` crate and the
//! architecture modules (ARCHITECTURE.md module grid, TODO T-2.1).
//!
//! The arch modules (here `muse-glimmer`) never parse files. They read
//! metadata through their [`Metadata`](muse_glimmer::Metadata) trait
//! and weights through their
//! [`TensorSource`](muse_glimmer::TensorSource) trait. This crate is
//! the implementor of those traits over a parsed
//! [`gguf::GgufFile`], plus the inventory check that verifies a file
//! against the arch module's published expectation before any weight
//! bytes move:
//!
//! - [`load_config`] parses a [`GlimmerConfig`] from a real file's
//!   metadata, end to end, with the arch module's fail-loud key naming
//!   intact.
//! - [`coverage`] compares the file's tensor names against
//!   [`muse_glimmer::expected_tensor_names`]; [`CoverageReport::
//!   require_complete`](CoverageReport::require_complete) fails by
//!   name on any miss, all misses at once.
//! - [`load_weights`] runs the coverage gate first, then loads the
//!   full weight set through the [`TensorSource`] adapter. A partially
//!   loaded model is never returned.
//!
//! Diagnostics are built in from birth (David's rule): structured
//! `key=value` debug lines flow through [`diag`] whenever
//! `ITAK_LOADER_DEBUG` is set or [`diag::set_debug_enabled`] is
//! called.
//!
//! Quick start:
//!
//! ```no_run
//! use std::path::Path;
//! let file = gguf::GgufFile::open(Path::new("model.gguf")).unwrap();
//! let cfg = itak_loader::load_config(&file).unwrap();
//! let report = itak_loader::coverage(&file, &cfg);
//! report.require_complete().unwrap();
//! let weights = itak_loader::load_weights(&file, &cfg).unwrap();
//! println!("{} layers loaded", weights.layers.len());
//! ```

#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
#![warn(missing_docs)]

pub mod adapter;
pub mod coverage;
pub mod diag;
pub mod error;

pub use adapter::{DflashMetadata, DflashTensorSource, GgufMetadata, GgufTensorSource};
pub use coverage::{coverage, coverage_dflash, CoverageReport};
pub use error::{LoaderError, Result};

use dflash::DflashConfig;
use gguf::GgufFile;
use muse_glimmer::{GlimmerConfig, Weights};

/// Parse the Muse Glimmer config from a parsed GGUF file's metadata.
///
/// # Errors
/// The arch module's own errors, unwrapped: a missing key is
/// [`GlimmerError::MissingMetadata`](muse_glimmer::GlimmerError)
/// naming the key, a wrong `general.architecture` is a refusal naming
/// what the file declares.
pub fn load_config(file: &GgufFile) -> muse_glimmer::Result<GlimmerConfig> {
    let cfg = GlimmerConfig::from_metadata(&GgufMetadata::new(file))?;
    diag::debug(
        "config_loaded",
        &format!(
            "arch={} layers={} hidden={} vocab={} pattern_source={:?}",
            muse_glimmer::ARCHITECTURE,
            cfg.block_count,
            cfg.hidden,
            cfg.vocab_size,
            cfg.pattern_source
        ),
    );
    Ok(cfg)
}

/// Load the full Glimmer weight set from a parsed GGUF file, gated on
/// the inventory check: coverage runs first and fails by name on any
/// miss, so the error lists every absent tensor instead of whichever
/// one the load order happened to reach first.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`LoaderError::MissingTensors`] when the inventory is incomplete;
/// the arch module's errors (as [`LoaderError::Glimmer`]) when a
/// present tensor cannot be delivered as stored.
pub fn load_weights(file: &GgufFile, cfg: &GlimmerConfig) -> Result<Weights> {
    coverage(file, cfg).require_complete()?;
    let weights = Weights::load(&GgufTensorSource::new(file), cfg)?;
    diag::debug(
        "weights_loaded",
        &format!("layers={}", weights.layers.len()),
    );
    Ok(weights)
}

/// Parse the DFlash draft config from a parsed GGUF file's metadata
/// (SPEC-itak-spec E3).
///
/// # Errors
/// The dflash module's own errors, unwrapped: a missing key is
/// [`DflashError::MissingMetadata`](dflash::DflashError) naming the
/// key, a wrong `general.architecture` is a refusal naming what the
/// file declares.
pub fn load_dflash_config(file: &GgufFile) -> dflash::Result<DflashConfig> {
    let cfg = DflashConfig::from_metadata(&DflashMetadata::new(file))?;
    diag::debug(
        "dflash_config_loaded",
        &format!(
            "arch={} layers={} hidden={} vocab={} block_size={} target_layers={:?}",
            dflash::ARCHITECTURE,
            cfg.block_count,
            cfg.hidden,
            cfg.vocab_size,
            cfg.block_size,
            cfg.target_layers
        ),
    );
    Ok(cfg)
}

/// Load the full DFlash weight set from a parsed GGUF file, gated
/// on the inventory check exactly as [`load_weights`] gates the
/// target's: coverage runs first and fails by name on any miss.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`LoaderError::MissingTensors`] when the inventory is incomplete;
/// the dflash module's errors (as [`LoaderError::Dflash`]) when a
/// present tensor cannot be delivered as stored, or when the file
/// carries a variant this module refuses.
pub fn load_dflash_weights(file: &GgufFile, cfg: &DflashConfig) -> Result<dflash::Weights> {
    coverage_dflash(file, cfg).require_complete()?;
    let weights = dflash::Weights::load(&DflashTensorSource::new(file), cfg)?;
    diag::debug(
        "dflash_weights_loaded",
        &format!(
            "layers={} target_hidden={} conditioning_width={}",
            weights.layers.len(),
            weights.target_hidden,
            weights.conditioning_width()
        ),
    );
    Ok(weights)
}

===== END FILE: crates/itak-loader/src/lib.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/itak-loader/tests/wiring.rs =====
//! End-to-end wiring tests over synthetic GGUF files: real bytes in,
//! config, tensors, and coverage out, through the same adapters the
//! engine will use. The tiny GGUF writer is adapted from the `gguf`
//! crate's synthetic tests; expectations here are the muse-glimmer
//! module's measured inventory, not the writer's opinion.

use gguf::{GgufFile, MetadataValue};
use itak_loader::{
    coverage, load_config, load_dflash_config, load_weights, DflashMetadata, GgufTensorSource,
    LoaderError,
};
use muse_glimmer::layer::SWA_PATTERN_KEY;
use muse_glimmer::{Dtype, GlimmerError, LayerKind, PatternSource, TensorSource};

// ---------- tiny GGUF writer (adapted from crates/gguf/tests) ----------

struct TestTensor {
    name: String,
    dims: Vec<u64>,
    type_id: u32,
    data: Vec<u8>,
}

fn tensor(name: &str, dims: &[u64], type_id: u32, data: Vec<u8>) -> TestTensor {
    TestTensor {
        name: name.to_string(),
        dims: dims.to_vec(),
        type_id,
        data,
    }
}

fn write_string(out: &mut Vec<u8>, s: &str) {
    out.extend_from_slice(&(s.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(s.as_bytes());
}

fn write_scalar(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: &MetadataValue) {
    match v {
        MetadataValue::UInt8(x) => out.push(*x),
        MetadataValue::Int8(x) => out.push(*x as u8),
        MetadataValue::UInt16(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Int16(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::UInt32(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Int32(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Float32(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Bool(x) => out.push(u8::from(*x)),
        MetadataValue::String(s) => write_string(out, s),
        MetadataValue::UInt64(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Int64(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Float64(x) => out.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes()),
        MetadataValue::Array(_) => panic!("nested arrays are not valid GGUF"),
    }
}

fn write_value(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: &MetadataValue) {
    out.extend_from_slice(&v.type_id().to_le_bytes());
    match v {
        MetadataValue::Array(items) => {
            let elem_type = items.first().map_or(8, MetadataValue::type_id);
            out.extend_from_slice(&elem_type.to_le_bytes());
            out.extend_from_slice(&(items.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
            for item in items {
                write_scalar(out, item);
            }
        }
        _ => write_scalar(out, v),
    }
}

fn align_up(v: u64, a: u64) -> u64 {
    v.div_ceil(a) * a
}

fn build(metadata: &[(&str, MetadataValue)], tensors: &[TestTensor]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let alignment = 32u64;
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    out.extend_from_slice(b"GGUF");
    out.extend_from_slice(&3u32.to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&(tensors.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&(metadata.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
    for (k, v) in metadata {
        write_string(&mut out, k);
        write_value(&mut out, v);
    }
    let mut offsets = Vec::new();
    let mut cursor = 0u64;
    for t in tensors {
        let aligned = align_up(cursor, alignment);
        offsets.push(aligned);
        cursor = aligned + t.data.len() as u64;
    }
    for (t, off) in tensors.iter().zip(&offsets) {
        write_string(&mut out, &t.name);
        out.extend_from_slice(&(t.dims.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
        for d in &t.dims {
            out.extend_from_slice(&d.to_le_bytes());
        }
        out.extend_from_slice(&t.type_id.to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&off.to_le_bytes());
    }
    let data_start = align_up(out.len() as u64, alignment);
    out.resize(data_start as usize, 0);
    for (t, off) in tensors.iter().zip(&offsets) {
        out.resize((data_start + off) as usize, 0);
        out.extend_from_slice(&t.data);
    }
    out
}

/// The 14 per-layer suffixes of the measured inventory.
const SUFFIXES: [&str; 14] = [
    "attn_norm.weight",
    "attn_q.weight",
    "attn_k.weight",
    "attn_v.weight",
    "attn_q_norm.weight",
    "attn_k_norm.weight",
    "attn_output.weight",
    "attn_gate.weight",
    "post_attention_norm.weight",
    "ffn_norm.weight",
    "ffn_gate.weight",
    "ffn_up.weight",
    "ffn_down.weight",
    "post_ffw_norm.weight",
];

fn tiny_metadata() -> Vec<(String, MetadataValue)> {
    let s = |v: &str| MetadataValue::String(v.to_string());
    let u = MetadataValue::UInt32;
    let f = MetadataValue::Float32;
    let tokens: Vec<MetadataValue> = (0..128).map(|i| s(&format!("t{i}"))).collect();
    vec![
        ("general.architecture".into(), s("muse-glimmer")),
        ("general.name".into(), s("Tiny Glimmer")),
        ("muse-glimmer.block_count".into(), u(2)),
        ("muse-glimmer.context_length".into(), u(128)),
        ("muse-glimmer.embedding_length".into(), u(32)),
        ("muse-glimmer.feed_forward_length".into(), u(64)),
        ("muse-glimmer.attention.head_count".into(), u(4)),
        ("muse-glimmer.attention.head_count_kv".into(), u(2)),
        ("muse-glimmer.attention.key_length".into(), u(8)),
        ("muse-glimmer.attention.value_length".into(), u(8)),
        ("muse-glimmer.rope.freq_base".into(), f(10_000.0)),
        (
            "muse-glimmer.attention.layer_norm_rms_epsilon".into(),
            f(1e-6),
        ),
        ("muse-glimmer.attention.sliding_window".into(), u(16)),
        ("muse-glimmer.final_logit_softcapping".into(), f(20.0)),
        ("muse-glimmer.logit_scale".into(), f(1.0)),
        ("tokenizer.ggml.tokens".into(), MetadataValue::Array(tokens)),
    ]
}

fn refs(metadata: &[(String, MetadataValue)]) -> Vec<(&str, MetadataValue)> {
    metadata
        .iter()
        .map(|(k, v)| (k.as_str(), v.clone()))
        .collect()
}

/// Every expected tensor of the tiny model. All F32 `[4]` except one
/// Q4_K tensor, so dtype mapping is exercised on the serve path.
fn tiny_tensors() -> Vec<TestTensor> {
    let mut out = vec![
        tensor("token_embd.weight", &[4], 0, vec![0u8; 16]),
        tensor("output_norm.weight", &[4], 0, vec![0u8; 16]),
        tensor("output.weight", &[4], 0, vec![0u8; 16]),
    ];
    for layer in 0..2 {
        for suffix in SUFFIXES {
            let name = format!("blk.{layer}.{suffix}");
            if name == "blk.0.attn_q.weight" {
                out.push(tensor(&name, &[256], 12, vec![0u8; 144]));
            } else {
                out.push(tensor(&name, &[4], 0, vec![0u8; 16]));
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

fn tiny_file() -> GgufFile {
    let md = tiny_metadata();
    GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&refs(&md), &tiny_tensors())).expect("tiny file parses")
}

#[test]
fn config_loads_end_to_end_from_gguf_bytes() {
    let file = tiny_file();
    let cfg = load_config(&file).expect("config loads");
    assert_eq!(cfg.block_count, 2);
    assert_eq!(cfg.hidden, 32);
    assert_eq!(cfg.ffn_hidden, 64);
    assert_eq!(cfg.q_heads, 4);
    assert_eq!(cfg.kv_heads, 2);
    assert_eq!(cfg.gqa_group(), 2);
    assert_eq!(cfg.vocab_size, 128);
    assert_eq!(cfg.name.as_deref(), Some("Tiny Glimmer"));
    // The tiny file carries no pattern key and no SWA rope base: both
    // optional reads fall back the way llama.cpp does (measured
    // pattern; train base), and say so in the config.
    assert_eq!(cfg.pattern_source, PatternSource::MeasuredFallback);
    assert!((cfg.rope_freq_base_swa - 10_000.0).abs() < f32::EPSILON);
}

#[test]
fn bool_array_pattern_drives_the_config() {
    // The shape the real Glimmer file stores: an array of bools, one
    // per layer, true for sliding-window. It must win over the
    // measured fallback and drive the layer kinds directly.
    let mut md = tiny_metadata();
    md.push((
        SWA_PATTERN_KEY.into(),
        MetadataValue::Array(vec![MetadataValue::Bool(true), MetadataValue::Bool(false)]),
    ));
    let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&refs(&md), &tiny_tensors())).unwrap();
    let cfg = load_config(&file).expect("config loads");
    assert_eq!(cfg.pattern_source, PatternSource::Metadata);
    assert_eq!(
        cfg.layers,
        vec![LayerKind::SlidingWindow, LayerKind::Global]
    );
}

#[test]

    ));

}

#[test]
fn non_array_pattern_value_falls_back_to_the_measured_pattern() {

#[test]
fn metadata_adapter_coerces_stored_integer_widths() {
    // The real world stores counts at whatever width the writer chose;
    // the trait contract is coercion, and the gguf getter owns it.
    let mut md = tiny_metadata();
    for (k, v) in &mut md {
        if k == "muse-glimmer.block_count" {
            *v = MetadataValue::UInt64(2);
        }
        if k == "muse-glimmer.rope.freq_base" {
            *v = MetadataValue::Float64(10_000.0);
        }
    }
    let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&refs(&md), &tiny_tensors())).unwrap();
    let cfg = load_config(&file).expect("wide storage still parses");
    assert_eq!(cfg.block_count, 2);
    assert!((cfg.rope_freq_base - 10_000.0).abs() < 0.01);
}

#[test]
fn unsupported_type_is_unreadable_not_missing() {
    // Q8_1 (mainline id 9): present in the directory, but the gguf
    // crate cannot size or read it. The seam must say unreadable, with
    // the type named, never missing and never placeholder bytes.
    let mut tensors = tiny_tensors();
    for t in &mut tensors {
        if t.name == "blk.0.attn_q.weight" {
            t.type_id = 9;
            t.data = vec![0u8; 64];
        }
    }
    let md = tiny_metadata();
    let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&refs(&md), &tensors)).unwrap();
    let source = GgufTensorSource::new(&file);
    let err = source.tensor("blk.0.attn_q.weight").unwrap_err();
    match err {
        GlimmerError::TensorUnreadable { name, detail } => {
            assert_eq!(name, "blk.0.attn_q.weight");
            assert!(detail.contains("Q8_1"), "detail names the type: {detail}");
        }
        other => panic!("expected TensorUnreadable, got {other:?}"),
    }
}

#[test]

    assert_eq!(report.found_count(), 31);
    assert!(report.is_complete());
    assert!(report.unexpected().is_empty());
    report.require_complete().expect("complete coverage passes");
    let weights = load_weights(&file, &cfg).expect("weights load");
    assert_eq!(weights.layers.len(), 2);
    assert_eq!(weights.output.name, "output.weight");

}

#[test]
fn coverage_names_every_missing_tensor() {
    let omit = ["output.weight", "blk.1.ffn_down.weight"];
    let tensors: Vec<TestTensor> = tiny_tensors()
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|t| !omit.contains(&t.name.as_str()))
        .collect();
    let md = tiny_metadata();
    let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&refs(&md), &tensors)).unwrap();
    let cfg = load_config(&file).unwrap();
    let report = coverage(&file, &cfg);
    assert_eq!(report.found_count(), 29);
    assert_eq!(
        report.missing(),
        ["output.weight", "blk.1.ffn_down.weight"].as_slice()
    );
    let err = report.require_complete().unwrap_err();
    assert!(err.to_string().contains("output.weight"));
    assert!(err.to_string().contains("blk.1.ffn_down.weight"));
    // load_weights is gated on the same check and fails the same way.
    let err = load_weights(&file, &cfg).unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(err, LoaderError::MissingTensors(_)));
    assert!(err.to_string().contains("blk.1.ffn_down.weight"));
}

/// A complete tiny DFlash metadata set: every key

#[test]
fn absent_dflash_bool_array_key_probes_none_quietly() {
    use dflash::Metadata as _;

    // The adapter-level probe of an absent optional key
    // answers None. Quiet is by construction: the probe
    // routes through gguf's `opt_array`, which returns
    // Ok(None) for absence without building the strict
    // getter's MissingMetadata refusal (the refusal and its
    // missing_metadata diag event are what the scalar fix
    // removed for the Glimmer adapter; the gguf crate's own
    // tests pin opt_array's silence and its wrong-type
    // loudness against the captured diag events).
    let file = tiny_dflash_file();
    let meta = DflashMetadata::new(&file);
    assert_eq!(meta.get_bool_array("dflash.attention.no_such_key"), None);
    // And through the config path, absence of the pattern
    // key surfaces as the config's own named refusal, not
    // as an adapter-level error.
    let md: Vec<(String, MetadataValue)> = tiny_dflash_metadata()
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|(k, _)| k != DFLASH_PATTERN_KEY)
        .collect();
    let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&refs(&md), &[])).unwrap();
    let err = load_dflash_config(&file).unwrap_err();
    match err {
        dflash::DflashError::MissingMetadata { key } => assert_eq!(key, DFLASH_PATTERN_KEY),
        other => panic!("expected MissingMetadata naming the pattern key, got {other:?}"),
    }
}

#[test]
fn wrong_typed_dflash_pattern_key_refuses_by_name() {
    // A present pattern key holding a non-array value must
    // refuse, and the refusal names the key: the adapter
    // returns None (the gguf opt read logs the type mismatch
    // at its own seam), and the config converts None into
    // its MissingMetadata refusal for exactly this key.
    let mut md = tiny_dflash_metadata();
    for (k, v) in &mut md {
        if k == DFLASH_PATTERN_KEY {
            *v = MetadataValue::String("not an array".to_string());
        }
    }
    let file = GgufFile::from_bytes(build(&refs(&md), &[])).unwrap();
    let err = load_dflash_config(&file).unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        err.to_string().contains(DFLASH_PATTERN_KEY),
        "the refusal must name the key in its message too: {err}"
    );
    match err {
        dflash::DflashError::MissingMetadata { key } => assert_eq!(key, DFLASH_PATTERN_KEY),
        other => panic!("expected MissingMetadata naming the pattern key, got {other:?}"),
    }
}
