===== FILE: crates/itak-spec/src/driver.rs =====
//! The target driver seam: the one surface the speculative loop
//! drives its target through (TODO T-9.6).
//!
//! The loop's bookkeeping (checkpoint, verify block, rewind to the
//! committed count) was written against the CPU target path. This
//! trait names exactly the operations the loop performs, no more,
//! so another target backend can sit under the identical loop:
//! [`CpuTarget`] wraps the original CPU path (model, shared
//! compute, position cache) unchanged, and `ResidentTarget` (in
//! `resident`) drives the GPU-resident session of `wgpu-compute`.
//! The draft side is untouched by this seam: drafting stays behind
//! the `Speculator` trait in `speculator`, on whichever backend the
//! draft model itself runs.
//!
//! The contract every driver keeps, because the loop's proof
//! obligation rests on it:
//!
//! - `forward` advances the position by `tokens.len()` and returns
//!   the finished logits of the last token.
//! - `forward_block_capturing` advances by `tokens.len()` and
//!   returns every row's finished logits, row-major
//!   `[tokens][vocab]`, row `i` the distribution for the token
//!   following the prefix extended by `tokens[..=i]`, plus the
//!   named layers' input rows in position order.
//! - `checkpoint` snapshots the KV state before a verify block;
//!   `rewind` restores it to an earlier committed position;
//!   `release` drops the snapshot. A driver whose KV addressing
//!   makes rewind exact by construction (position-addressed
//!   slots, views derived from the position) may implement
//!   checkpoint and release as bookkeeping only, and must say so
//!   in its own docs.

use std::rc::Rc;

use cpu_compute::{Checkpoint, CpuCompute};
use muse_glimmer::{
    Cache, GlimmerConfig, GlimmerModel, LayerInputCapture, PositionCache, Result as GlimmerResult,
};

/// The target operations the speculative loop performs. See the
/// module docs for the contract each method keeps.
pub trait TargetDriver {
    /// Opaque snapshot of the driver's KV state, taken before a
    /// verify block so a refused or partially accepted round can
    /// restore it.
    type Checkpoint;

    /// The target model's configuration (the session validates
    /// the draft against it at creation).
    fn config(&self) -> &GlimmerConfig;

    /// The committed position: tokens forwarded and not rewound.
    fn position(&self) -> usize;

    /// Forward `tokens`, returning the last token's finished
    /// logits.
    fn forward(&mut self, tokens: &[u32]) -> GlimmerResult<Vec<f32>>;

    /// Forward `tokens`, returning the last token's finished
    /// logits plus the named layers' input rows.
    fn forward_capturing(
        &mut self,
        tokens: &[u32],
        capture_layers: &[usize],
    ) -> GlimmerResult<(Vec<f32>, Vec<LayerInputCapture>)>;

    /// Forward `tokens` as one block, returning every row's
    /// finished logits plus the named layers' input rows.
    fn forward_block_capturing(
        &mut self,
        tokens: &[u32],
        capture_layers: &[usize],
    ) -> GlimmerResult<(Vec<f32>, Vec<LayerInputCapture>)>;

    /// Snapshot the KV state ahead of a verify block of at most
    /// `rows` tokens.
    fn checkpoint(&mut self, rows: usize) -> GlimmerResult<Self::Checkpoint>;

    /// Restore the KV state to the committed position `to`,
    /// under the snapshot `checkpoint` took.
    fn rewind(&mut self, checkpoint: &Self::Checkpoint, to: usize) -> GlimmerResult<()>;

    /// Drop the snapshot `checkpoint` took (the round committed
    /// or was rolled back; the snapshot is spent either way).
    fn release(&mut self, checkpoint: &Self::Checkpoint) -> GlimmerResult<()>;

    /// Record one completed speculative round: the draft's
    /// proposed token ids and how many of them the target
    /// accepted. The loop calls this exactly once per
    /// completed round, at the point where both are in hand
    /// (the round's outcome carries counts only, never the
    /// ids). Record only: an implementation must not let
    /// this change sampling, acceptance, or control flow,
    /// and drivers with nothing to record (the default, the
    /// CPU driver included) do nothing. The resident driver
    /// forwards it to the session's capture diag, where it
    /// lands only at the capture level.
    fn note_spec_round(&mut self, _proposed: &[u32], _accepted: usize) {}
}

/// The CPU target driver: the loop's original target path,
/// unchanged. The model forwards through the shared compute (see
/// [`crate::SharedCompute`]); checkpoints, rewind, and release go
/// to that same compute, and the position cache rewinds between
/// the compute rewind and the release, exactly the order the
/// loop always used.
pub struct CpuTarget {
    model: GlimmerModel,
    compute: Rc<CpuCompute>,
    cache: PositionCache,
}

impl CpuTarget {
    /// Wrap a CPU target model and the compute it forwards
    /// through. The compute must be the same [`CpuCompute`] the
    /// model was built with (through [`crate::SharedCompute`]):
    /// the checkpoint machinery lives on it.
    pub fn new(model: GlimmerModel, compute: Rc<CpuCompute>) -> Self {
        CpuTarget {
            model,
            compute,
            cache: PositionCache::new(),
        }
    }

    /// The wrapped model.
    pub fn model(&self) -> &GlimmerModel {
        &self.model
    }

    /// The shared compute the model forwards through.
    pub fn compute(&self) -> &Rc<CpuCompute> {
        &self.compute
    }

    /// The position cache paired with the compute's KV state.
    pub fn cache(&self) -> &PositionCache {
        &self.cache
    }
}

impl TargetDriver for CpuTarget {
    type Checkpoint = Checkpoint;

    fn config(&self) -> &GlimmerConfig {
        self.model.config()
    }

    fn position(&self) -> usize {
        self.cache.position()
    }

    fn forward(&mut self, tokens: &[u32]) -> GlimmerResult<Vec<f32>> {
        self.model.forward(tokens, &mut self.cache)
    }

    fn forward_capturing(
        &mut self,
        tokens: &[u32],
        capture_layers: &[usize],
    ) -> GlimmerResult<(Vec<f32>, Vec<LayerInputCapture>)> {
        self.model
            .forward_capturing(tokens, &mut self.cache, capture_layers)
    }

    fn forward_block_capturing(
        &mut self,
        tokens: &[u32],
        capture_layers: &[usize],
    ) -> GlimmerResult<(Vec<f32>, Vec<LayerInputCapture>)> {
        self.model
            .forward_block_capturing(tokens, &mut self.cache, capture_layers)
    }

    fn checkpoint(&mut self, rows: usize) -> GlimmerResult<Checkpoint> {
        self.compute.cache_checkpoint(rows)
    }

    fn rewind(&mut self, checkpoint: &Checkpoint, to: usize) -> GlimmerResult<()> {
        self.compute.cache_rewind(checkpoint, to)?;
        self.cache.rewind_to(to);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn release(&mut self, checkpoint: &Checkpoint) -> GlimmerResult<()> {
        self.compute.cache_release(checkpoint)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use std::cell::{Cell, RefCell};
    use std::rc::Rc;
    use std::sync::Arc;

    use muse_glimmer::{GlimmerConfig, GlimmerError, LayerInputCapture};

    use super::TargetDriver;
    use crate::config::SpecConfig;
    use crate::diag::NullDiag;
    use crate::session::SpecSession;
    use crate::speculator::SharedCompute;
    use crate::testkit;

    /// A deterministic stub target for loop-bookkeeping tests:
    /// each token's finished logits depend only on that token
    /// (a bigram-style rule), so a block forward agrees with
    /// sequential forwards by construction and greedy identity
    /// between a speculative and a plain session over the stub
    /// is a property of the LOOP, not of any model arithmetic.
    /// Its KV is the vector of forwarded tokens; a rewind
    /// truncates it. Checkpoint, rewind, and release calls are
    /// recorded for the accounting assertions.
    /// The stub's spec-round record log: one (proposed ids,
    /// accepted count) entry per completed round, shared
    /// with the owning test.
    type SpecRoundNotes = Rc<RefCell<Vec<(Vec<u32>, usize)>>>;

    struct StubTarget {
        config: GlimmerConfig,
        kv: Vec<u32>,
        checkpoints: Rc<RefCell<Vec<usize>>>,
        rewinds: Rc<RefCell<Vec<usize>>>,
        releases: Rc<Cell<usize>>,
        spec_rounds: SpecRoundNotes,
    }

    /// A stub checkpoint: the KV length it saw, plus the row
    /// budget it was taken for. A round's rewind target lands
    /// anywhere in `[base, base + rows]`: the committed count
    /// after a partial acceptance sits inside the forwarded
    /// block, past the checkpoint's own length (the CPU
    /// checkpoint budgets the same span).
    struct StubCheckpoint {
        base: usize,
        rows: usize,
    }

    /// The stub's recorded seam calls, shared with the test
    /// that owns the stub.
    struct StubRecorders {
        checkpoints: Rc<RefCell<Vec<usize>>>,
        rewinds: Rc<RefCell<Vec<usize>>>,
        releases: Rc<Cell<usize>>,
        spec_rounds: SpecRoundNotes,
    }

    impl StubTarget {
        fn new() -> (StubTarget, StubRecorders) {
            let recorders = StubRecorders {
                checkpoints: Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new())),
                rewinds: Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new())),
                releases: Rc::new(Cell::new(0)),
                spec_rounds: Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new())),
            };
            (
                StubTarget {
                    config: testkit::target_config(),
                    kv: Vec::new(),
                    checkpoints: recorders.checkpoints.clone(),
                    rewinds: recorders.rewinds.clone(),
                    releases: recorders.releases.clone(),
                    spec_rounds: recorders.spec_rounds.clone(),
                },
                recorders,
            )
        }

        /// The stub's finished logits for one token: a one-hot
        /// row at a deterministic successor, so the greedy pick
        /// is a pure function of the token.
        fn row(&self, token: u32) -> Vec<f32> {
            let vocab = self.config.vocab_size as usize;
            let mut row = vec![0.0f32; vocab];
            row[(token as usize * 31 + 17) % vocab] = 1.0;
            row
        }

        /// Deterministic capture rows for `tokens` at `layer`:
        /// one row of hidden width per token.
        fn capture_rows(&self, tokens: &[u32], layer: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
            let hidden = self.config.hidden as usize;
            let mut rows = Vec::with_capacity(tokens.len() * hidden);
            for &token in tokens {
                let value = token as f32 * 0.001 + layer as f32;
                rows.extend(std::iter::repeat_n(value, hidden));
            }
            rows
        }

        fn captures(&self, tokens: &[u32], layers: &[usize]) -> Vec<LayerInputCapture> {
            layers
                .iter()
                .map(|&layer| LayerInputCapture {
                    layer,
                    rows: self.capture_rows(tokens, layer),
                })
                .collect()
        }
    }

    impl TargetDriver for StubTarget {
        type Checkpoint = StubCheckpoint;

        fn config(&self) -> &GlimmerConfig {
            &self.config
        }

        fn position(&self) -> usize {
            self.kv.len()
        }

        fn forward(&mut self, tokens: &[u32]) -> Result<Vec<f32>, GlimmerError> {
            self.kv.extend_from_slice(tokens);
            Ok(self.row(*tokens.last().expect("forward needs a token")))
        }

        fn forward_capturing(
            &mut self,
            tokens: &[u32],
            capture_layers: &[usize],
        ) -> Result<(Vec<f32>, Vec<LayerInputCapture>), GlimmerError> {
            let captures = self.captures(tokens, capture_layers);
            self.kv.extend_from_slice(tokens);
            Ok((
                self.row(*tokens.last().expect("forward needs a token")),
                captures,
            ))
        }

        fn forward_block_capturing(
            &mut self,
            tokens: &[u32],
            capture_layers: &[usize],
        ) -> Result<(Vec<f32>, Vec<LayerInputCapture>), GlimmerError> {
            let captures = self.captures(tokens, capture_layers);
            let mut logits = Vec::with_capacity(tokens.len() * self.config.vocab_size as usize);
            for &token in tokens {
                logits.extend_from_slice(&self.row(token));
            }
            self.kv.extend_from_slice(tokens);
            Ok((logits, captures))
        }

        fn checkpoint(&mut self, rows: usize) -> Result<StubCheckpoint, GlimmerError> {
            self.checkpoints.borrow_mut().push(rows);
            Ok(StubCheckpoint {
                base: self.kv.len(),
                rows,
            })
        }

        fn rewind(&mut self, checkpoint: &StubCheckpoint, to: usize) -> Result<(), GlimmerError> {
            assert!(
                (checkpoint.base..=checkpoint.base + checkpoint.rows).contains(&to),
                "rewind target {to} outside the checkpoint span [{}, {}]",
                checkpoint.base,
                checkpoint.base + checkpoint.rows
            );
            self.rewinds.borrow_mut().push(to);
            self.kv.truncate(to);
            Ok(())
        }

        fn release(&mut self, _checkpoint: &StubCheckpoint) -> Result<(), GlimmerError> {
            self.releases.set(self.releases.get() + 1);
            Ok(())
        }

        fn note_spec_round(&mut self, proposed: &[u32], accepted: usize) {
            self.spec_rounds
                .borrow_mut()
                .push((proposed.to_vec(), accepted));
        }
    }

    fn fixture_draft(block_size: u32) -> crate::speculator::DflashSpeculator {
        let compute = Rc::new(cpu_compute::CpuCompute::new());
        let fixture = testkit::build_target(Box::new(SharedCompute(compute)));
        testkit::build_speculator(&fixture, block_size)
    }

    const PROMPT: &[u32] = &[3, 17, 42];

    /// The driver seam carries the full loop: a DFlash session
    /// over the stub driver emits exactly the stream a mode-off
    /// session over a fresh stub emits (greedy identity through
    /// the seam, proven without any model arithmetic), and the
    /// draft really proposed.
    #[test]
    fn stub_driver_carries_the_loop_with_greedy_identity() {
        let config = SpecConfig {
            depth: 2,
            ..SpecConfig::default()
        };
        let (stub, _) = StubTarget::new();
        let mut spec = SpecSession::new(
            stub,
            Some(fixture_draft(5)),
            config.clone(),
            Arc::new(NullDiag),
        )
        .expect("spec session over stub builds");
        spec.begin(PROMPT).expect("begin");
        let stream = spec.generate(16, &[]).expect("spec generate");

        let (plain_stub, _) = StubTarget::new();
        let mut plain = SpecSession::new(
            plain_stub,
            None,
            crate::config::SpecConfig {
                mode: crate::config::SpecMode::Off,
                ..config
            },
            Arc::new(NullDiag),
        )
        .expect("plain session over stub builds");
        plain.begin(PROMPT).expect("begin");
        let plain_stream = plain.generate(16, &[]).expect("plain generate");

        assert_eq!(
            stream, plain_stream,
            "greedy identity through the driver seam"
        );
        assert_eq!(stream.len(), 16);
        let stats = spec.stats();
        assert!(stats.proposed > 0, "the draft proposed through the seam");
        assert!(stats.accepted <= stats.proposed);
        assert_eq!(spec.cache_position(), PROMPT.len() + 15);
    }

    /// The same seam carries the n-gram proposer: a session built
    /// through `new_ngram` over the stub stays token-identical to
    /// the plain stub session, and because the stub's stream is a
    /// deterministic successor iteration (eventually periodic),
    /// the proposer both speaks and gets accepted once the orbit
    /// repeats a pair. This is the acceptance shape to expect on
    /// repetitive real text; the fixture-target numbers live in
    /// `bench/ngram-spec-2026-11-07.md`.
    #[test]
    fn stub_driver_carries_ngram_with_greedy_identity() {
        let config = SpecConfig {
            mode: crate::config::SpecMode::Ngram,
            depth: 4,
            ..SpecConfig::default()
        };
        let (stub, _) = StubTarget::new();
        let proposer = crate::NgramProposer::new(crate::NgramConfig::default(), testkit::VOCAB)
            .expect("proposer builds");
        let mut spec =
            SpecSession::new_ngram(stub, Some(proposer), config.clone(), Arc::new(NullDiag))
                .expect("n-gram session over stub builds");
        spec.begin(PROMPT).expect("begin");
        let stream = spec.generate(300, &[]).expect("spec generate");

        let (plain_stub, _) = StubTarget::new();
        let mut plain = SpecSession::new(
            plain_stub,
            None,
            SpecConfig {
                mode: crate::config::SpecMode::Off,
                ..config
            },
            Arc::new(NullDiag),
        )
        .expect("plain session over stub builds");
        plain.begin(PROMPT).expect("begin");
        let plain_stream = plain.generate(300, &[]).expect("plain generate");

        assert_eq!(
            stream, plain_stream,
            "n-gram greedy identity through the driver seam"
        );
        assert_eq!(stream.len(), 300);
        let stats = spec.stats();
        assert!(stats.proposed > 0, "the proposer spoke through the seam");
        assert!(
            stats.accepted > 0,
            "the periodic stub stream accepts n-gram proposals"
        );
        assert!(stats.accepted <= stats.proposed);
        assert_eq!(spec.cache_position(), PROMPT.len() + 299);
    }

    /// Rewind correctness and acceptance accounting, observed at
    /// the seam: after every round the stub's KV length equals
    /// the session's committed position and the round outcome's
    /// cache position; every recorded rewind target equals its
    /// round's base + 1 + accepted (recovered from the outcome
    /// and the running position); checkpoints and releases pair
    /// up one for one; and the cumulative stats equal the sum of
    /// the round outcomes.
    #[test]
    fn stub_driver_rewinds_land_on_the_committed_count() {
        let config = SpecConfig {
            depth: 3,
            ..SpecConfig::default()
        };
        let (stub, rec) = StubTarget::new();
        let mut session =
            SpecSession::new(stub, Some(fixture_draft(5)), config, Arc::new(NullDiag))
                .expect("spec session over stub builds");
        session.begin(PROMPT).expect("begin");

        let mut base = PROMPT.len();
        let mut sum_proposed = 0usize;
        let mut sum_accepted = 0usize;
        let mut rounds = 0usize;
        while session.cache_position() < PROMPT.len() + 20 && rounds < 40 {
            let outcome = session.round().expect("round");
            rounds += 1;
            sum_proposed += outcome.proposed;
            sum_accepted += outcome.accepted;
            // The stub's own KV is inside the driver; the session's
            // committed position and the outcome must agree, and
            // the last rewind of the round must have landed on it.
            assert_eq!(outcome.cache_position, base + 1 + outcome.accepted);
            assert_eq!(session.cache_position(), outcome.cache_position);
            let log = rec.rewinds.borrow();
            assert_eq!(
                log.last().copied(),
                Some(outcome.cache_position),
                "round {rounds}: rewind landed on the committed count"
            );
            drop(log);
            base = outcome.cache_position;
            if outcome.stopped {
                break;
            }
        }
        assert!(rounds > 0);
        let stats = session.stats();
        assert_eq!(stats.rounds, rounds);
        assert_eq!(stats.proposed, sum_proposed, "proposed accounting");
        assert_eq!(stats.accepted, sum_accepted, "accepted accounting");
        assert_eq!(
            rec.checkpoints.borrow().len(),
            rounds,
            "one checkpoint per speculative round"
        );
        assert!(
            rec.checkpoints.borrow().iter().all(|&rows| rows >= 2),
            "verify blocks always carry at least the anchor and one draft"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            rec.releases.get(),
            rounds,
            "every checkpoint is released exactly once"
        );
        assert_eq!(rec.rewinds.borrow().len(), rounds, "one rewind per round");
    }

    /// The capture wiring at the seam: the loop hands the
    /// driver exactly one spec-round record per completed
    /// round, carrying that round's REAL proposed ids and
    /// accepted count. The record's length is the round's
    /// proposed count, its count is the round's accepted
    /// count, and its accepted prefix is exactly the tokens
    /// the round emitted from the proposal (the session's
    /// default config names no stop tokens, so emission is
    /// never truncated). This is the call the resident
    /// driver forwards to its session's capture
    /// accumulator; here the stub records it so the wiring
    /// itself is pinned without a device.
    #[test]
    fn stub_driver_receives_one_spec_round_record_per_round() {
        let config = SpecConfig {
            depth: 3,
            ..SpecConfig::default()
        };
        let (stub, rec) = StubTarget::new();
        let mut session =
            SpecSession::new(stub, Some(fixture_draft(5)), config, Arc::new(NullDiag))
                .expect("spec session over stub builds");
        session.begin(PROMPT).expect("begin");

        let mut outcomes = Vec::new();
        while session.cache_position() < PROMPT.len() + 12 && outcomes.len() < 20 {
            let outcome = session.round().expect("round");
            let stopped = outcome.stopped;
            outcomes.push(outcome);
            if stopped {
                break;
            }
        }
        assert!(!outcomes.is_empty(), "at least one round ran");
        assert!(
            outcomes.iter().all(|o| o.proposed > 0),
            "every round here is speculative: {outcomes:?}"
        );
        let notes = rec.spec_rounds.borrow();
        assert_eq!(
            notes.len(),
            outcomes.len(),
            "one record per completed round"
        );
        for (round, (note, outcome)) in notes.iter().zip(outcomes.iter()).enumerate() {
            assert_eq!(
                note.0.len(),
                outcome.proposed,
                "round {round}: the record carries the round's proposed ids"
            );
            assert_eq!(
                note.1, outcome.accepted,
                "round {round}: the record carries the round's accepted count"
            );
            assert_eq!(
                &note.0[..outcome.accepted],
                &outcome.emitted[..outcome.accepted],
                "round {round}: the recorded ids are the round's real proposal, \
                 whose accepted prefix is what the round emitted"
            );
        }
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/itak-spec/src/error.rs =====
//! Named refusals for the speculative decoding loop (SPEC-itak-spec Section
//! 6.1). Every variant is a state the loop refuses by name; nothing in this
//! crate fails silently, panics on bad input, or falls back without an event.

use dflash::DflashError;
use muse_glimmer::GlimmerError;

/// Every way session creation or a round can refuse, named.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum SpecError {
    /// The chosen drafting mode's machinery is not available on this
    /// session. Medusa needs its heads loader, which is not in this
    /// crate yet. N-gram's machinery exists ([`crate::NgramProposer`])
    /// but is attached only through `SpecSession::new_ngram`; asking
    /// the DFlash constructor for mode `ngram` refuses here instead of
    /// silently running something else.
    ModeUnavailable {
        /// The mode name as it appears in configuration (`ngram`, `medusa`).
        mode: &'static str,
    },
    /// A drafting mode was selected but no draft source was attached:
    /// no draft model for DFlash mode, no proposer for n-gram mode.
    DraftNotLoaded,
    /// The attached draft declares an architecture other than `dflash`.
    DraftArchMismatch {
        /// The architecture string the draft file declares.
        found: String,
    },
    /// The draft model failed to build from its file.
    DraftLoadFailed {
        /// Why the load failed.
        detail: String,
    },
    /// The caller's speculation envelope (rounds, cache budget) does not
    /// match what this session was configured with.
    EnvelopeMismatch {
        /// The envelope field that differs.
        field: &'static str,
        /// What the session was configured with.
        expected: usize,
        /// What the caller asked for.
        actual: usize,
    },
    /// A Medusa heads artifact carries an unsupported format version.
    ArtifactVersionUnsupported {
        /// The version the artifact declares.
        found: u32,
        /// The newest version this build reads.
        supported: u32,
    },
    /// Medusa heads loaded but are all zeros: drafting with them would be
    /// drafting with noise, so the session refuses instead.
    ZeroInitializedHeads,
    /// The configured draft depth is zero or beyond what one draft block
    /// (or the target's largest legal block) can propose.
    DepthOutOfRange {
        /// The configured depth.
        n_max: usize,
        /// The draft block size, which bounds the depth.
        block_size: usize,
    },
    /// A KV checkpoint is already live; rounds never nest checkpoints.
    CheckpointBusy,
    /// The cache position after a round disagrees with what the loop
    /// committed: the loop and the cache have drifted apart, and the
    /// session refuses to continue on a lying cache.
    CacheOutOfSync {
        /// The position the loop committed to.
        expected: usize,
        /// The position the cache reports.
        actual: usize,
    },
    /// Grammar-constrained sampling and speculation are both active. The
    /// correction walk assumes the full vocabulary; enabling both refuses
    /// until the grammar-aware walk exists.
    GrammarConflict,
    /// The target's verify forward refused mid-round. Under the default
    /// error policy the cache has already been rewound to the round's base
    /// and the checkpoint released when this surfaces.
    VerifyRefused {
        /// The target-side refusal.
        source: Box<GlimmerError>,
    },
    /// The draft side refused: a block forward, a conditioning injection,
    /// or a commit-time sync failure in the draft's own cache.
    DraftRefused {
        /// The draft-side refusal.
        source: Box<DflashError>,
    },
    /// A target forward outside the verify step refused (prefill, or a
    /// plain non-speculative step).
    TargetRefused {
        /// The target-side refusal.
        source: Box<GlimmerError>,
    },
    /// A target KV checkpoint, rewind, or release refused.
    CacheRefused {
        /// Which cache operation refused (`checkpoint`, `rewind`, `release`).
        op: &'static str,
        /// The cache-side refusal.
        source: Box<GlimmerError>,
    },
    /// The draft and the target disagree on a shared geometric fact, so
    /// captures and distributions could never line up.
    DraftTargetMismatch {
        /// The field that disagrees (`vocab_size`, `target_layer`).
        field: &'static str,
        /// The target's value.
        expected: usize,
        /// The draft's value.
        actual: usize,
    },
    /// One round needs `depth + 1` checkpoint slots (the pending token plus
    /// the drafts) but the round budget allows fewer.
    RoundBoundTooSmall {
        /// The configured depth.
        depth: usize,
        /// The configured per-round token bound.
        max_round_tokens: usize,
    },
    /// The session was driven out of order: a round before `begin`, a
    /// second `begin`, a round after the session stopped, or a draft commit
    /// whose staged captures do not cover the committed tokens.
    SessionState {
        /// What was wrong with the call order or staged state.
        detail: String,
    },
    /// A sampler entry point was handed inputs that violate its stated
    /// contract: an empty logit row, a correction walk whose target rows
    /// do not cover the proposal plus the bonus row, or a proposal token
    /// outside the rows it indexes. The sampler refuses by name instead
    /// of panicking on the indexing (panel B4, executed probes).
    SamplerContract {
        /// The entry point that refused (`distribution`,
        /// `correct_greedy`, `correct_sampled`).
        entry: &'static str,
        /// What was wrong with the inputs.
        detail: String,
    },
    /// The depth sweep's configuration is unusable: an empty candidate
    /// set, a zero or duplicated candidate depth, an unparsable depth
    /// list, or a zero per-depth token budget. The sweep refuses by name
    /// instead of measuring nothing and calling it a table (T-9.7).
    SweepConfigInvalid {
        /// What was wrong with the sweep configuration.
        detail: String,
    },
}

impl std::fmt::Display for SpecError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            SpecError::ModeUnavailable { mode } => {
                write!(f, "drafting mode {mode} is not available in this build")
            }
            SpecError::DraftNotLoaded => {
                write!(f, "speculation mode requires a loaded draft model")
            }
            SpecError::DraftArchMismatch { found } => {
                write!(f, "draft architecture is {found}, expected dflash")
            }
            SpecError::DraftLoadFailed { detail } => {
                write!(f, "draft model failed to load: {detail}")
            }
            SpecError::EnvelopeMismatch {
                field,
                expected,
                actual,
            } => write!(
                f,
                "speculation envelope mismatch on {field}: session has {expected}, caller asked {actual}"
            ),
            SpecError::ArtifactVersionUnsupported { found, supported } => write!(
                f,
                "draft artifact version {found} is not supported (newest supported: {supported})"
            ),
            SpecError::ZeroInitializedHeads => {
                write!(f, "draft heads are zero-initialized; refusing to draft with noise")
            }
            SpecError::DepthOutOfRange { n_max, block_size } => write!(
                f,
                "draft depth {n_max} is out of range for draft block size {block_size}"
            ),
            SpecError::CheckpointBusy => {
                write!(f, "a KV checkpoint is already live; rounds never nest checkpoints")
            }
            SpecError::CacheOutOfSync { expected, actual } => write!(
                f,
                "cache position {actual} does not match the committed position {expected}"
            ),
            SpecError::GrammarConflict => write!(
                f,
                "grammar-constrained sampling and speculation cannot run together yet"
            ),
            SpecError::VerifyRefused { source } => {
                write!(f, "verify forward refused: {source}")
            }
            SpecError::DraftRefused { source } => {
                write!(f, "draft refused: {source}")
            }
            SpecError::TargetRefused { source } => {
                write!(f, "target forward refused: {source}")
            }
            SpecError::CacheRefused { op, source } => {
                write!(f, "cache {op} refused: {source}")
            }
            SpecError::DraftTargetMismatch {
                field,
                expected,
                actual,
            } => write!(
                f,
                "draft/target mismatch on {field}: target has {expected}, draft has {actual}"
            ),
            SpecError::RoundBoundTooSmall {
                depth,
                max_round_tokens,
            } => write!(
                f,
                "round bound {max_round_tokens} cannot hold depth {depth} plus the pending token"
            ),
            SpecError::SessionState { detail } => write!(f, "session state error: {detail}"),
            SpecError::SamplerContract { entry, detail } => {
                write!(f, "sampler contract refused at {entry}: {detail}")
            }
            SpecError::SweepConfigInvalid { detail } => {
                write!(f, "sweep configuration invalid: {detail}")
            }
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for SpecError {}

/// The loop's result type.
pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, SpecError>;

//! itak-spec: the speculative decoding loop of the iTaK Torch engine
//! (SPEC-itak-spec). A [`SpecSession`] runs block drafting against
//! the Glimmer target with exact-output verification: DFlash block
//! drafting from a separate draft model, or n-gram prompt-lookup
//! drafting ([`NgramProposer`]) from the sequence itself, with no
//! draft model at all.
//!
//! One round, per the spec's Section 4: the draft proposes up to `depth`
//! tokens from the last committed position; the target verifies the whole
//! block in one `forward_block` under a KV checkpoint; the correction
//! walk in [`sampler`] accepts the prefix the target agrees with and
//! emits one correction or bonus token; the cache rewinds to the
//! committed count; the draft is told exactly the newly committed tokens
//! and receives their captured layer-input rows as conditioning.
//!
//! The T-9.7 depth sweep ([`sweep`]) re-measures the depth default on
//! this stack: it drives sessions through a caller-supplied factory,
//! so it runs against whatever backend the sessions were built on.
//!
//! The guarantee that matters: at temperature 0 the emitted sequence is
//! token-identical to non-speculative greedy generation from the same
//! target. The sampled arm implements the spec's rejection-sampling
//! correction exactly, so sampled emission matches the target's
//! distribution. Depth defaults to 6, the operating point the llama.cpp
//! sweep measured on 2026-10-30 (`bench/gpu-proof-2026-10-30.md`), and is
//! configuration, never a constant. Diagnostics and cumulative stats are
//! built in from birth ([`diag`], [`SpecStats`]).
//!
//! Known gaps, named rather than papered over: Medusa drafting
//! refuses with `ModeUnavailable` (its machinery is not in this
//! crate); grammar-constrained speculation refuses with `GrammarConflict`. The
//! loop drives its target through the [`driver::TargetDriver`] seam:
//! the CPU driver ([`CpuTarget`]) proves the mechanism, and the
//! GPU-resident driver ([`ResidentTarget`], TODO T-9.6) runs the
//! identical loop against the resident GPU forward. The draft model
//! has no GPU path in this workspace, so drafting runs on the CPU
//! stack behind the same `Speculator` seam on both drivers (the
//! bench note `bench/spec-gpu-port-2026-11-03.md` records what that
//! costs the speed bar).

#![forbid(unsafe_code)]

pub mod config;
pub mod diag;
pub mod driver;
pub mod error;
pub mod ngram;
pub mod resident;
pub mod rng;
pub mod sampler;
pub mod session;
pub mod speculator;
pub mod sweep;

#[cfg(test)]
mod testkit;

pub use config::{DraftBackend, OnVerifyError, SpecConfig, SpecMode};
pub use diag::{Diag, NullDiag, StderrDiag};
pub use driver::{CpuTarget, TargetDriver};
pub use error::{Result, SpecError};
pub use ngram::{NgramConfig, NgramProposer};
pub use resident::ResidentTarget;
pub use rng::Rng;
pub use session::{RoundOutcome, SpecSession, SpecStats};
pub use speculator::{
    BlockProposal, DflashSpeculator, DraftArm, DraftDist, Proposal, SharedCompute, Speculator,
};
pub use sweep::{run_sweep, DepthRow, SweepConfig, SweepError, SweepReport};

===== FILE: crates/itak-spec/src/ngram.rs =====
//! N-gram prompt-lookup drafting (SPEC-itak-spec Section 6.2, the
//! `ngram` mode): the no-training self-drafting proposer.
//!
//! The proposer holds no model and runs no forward. It keeps the
//! committed token history and, at propose time, looks up the
//! sequence's own suffix: find the most recent prior occurrence of
//! the last `L` tokens (the longest `L` that occurs at all, down to
//! a configured floor) and propose the tokens that followed that
//! occurrence. Repetitive text (code, logs, templated prose, lists)
//! repeats itself, so the continuation is often exactly what the
//! target is about to emit; the session's verifier accepts the
//! prefix it agrees with and corrects the rest, so a wrong guess
//! costs a round, never a token. On non-repetitive text the lookup
//! finds little or nothing and the proposer stays out of the way.
//!
//! Cost: pure CPU, microseconds at session-scale histories. The
//! search is a backward scan from the most recent end (the first
//! hit is the answer, per the ranking rule below), bounded by a
//! configured window so a no-match round cannot scan an unbounded
//! history. No GPU or model types appear here; the only geometry
//! the proposer knows is the target's vocabulary width, which its
//! one-hot proposal distributions are built at (the same reason
//! `DflashConfig` carries `vocab_size`).
//!
//! Ranking, when several occurrences of a suffix exist: the longest
//! match wins; among occurrences of that match, the most recent
//! wins. Recency is the standard prompt-lookup choice: later text
//! is the better predictor of what the sequence does next, and it
//! makes the scan a first-hit search instead of a census.
//!
//! The sampled arm's distributions are one-hot rows at the proposed
//! tokens. That is not an approximation: a one-hot is a genuine
//! distribution, drawing from it yields the proposed token with
//! probability 1, and the rejection-sampling walk in
//! [`crate::sampler::correct_sampled`] divides the target row by it
//! exactly (accept with probability `p(token)`, reject into the
//! normalized residual `(p - q)+`). The greedy arm carries no
//! distributions, like the DFlash greedy arm.
//!
//! Every operational limit is configuration with a default
//! ([`NgramConfig`]), per the build law; nothing is compiled in.

use crate::error::{Result, SpecError};
use crate::speculator::{BlockProposal, DraftArm, DraftDist, Proposal, Speculator};
use crate::SpecMode;

/// Configuration for [`NgramProposer`]. All limits are configuration
/// with defaults, never compiled constants.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct NgramConfig {
    /// The longest suffix tried first. The lookup walks down from
    /// here to `min_match_len`; the first length with any prior
    /// occurrence wins.
    pub max_match_len: usize,
    /// The shortest suffix allowed to propose. Shorter matches are
    /// too weak a signal (a 1-token suffix matches almost anywhere)
    /// and are refused by construction, not by ranking.
    pub min_match_len: usize,
    /// Maximum tokens one proposal can carry; the proposer's
    /// `max_depth`, and the bound session depth is validated
    /// against.
    pub max_proposals: usize,
    /// How far back from the sequence end an occurrence's start may
    /// sit and still count, in tokens. Bounds the no-match scan;
    /// `0` searches the whole history.
    pub search_window_tokens: usize,
    /// Committed history retained, in tokens; older tokens are
    /// dropped from the front as commits arrive. `0` retains
    /// everything. Dropped history can no longer be matched
    /// against, which is the honest cost of the bound.
    pub max_history_tokens: usize,
}

impl Default for NgramConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        NgramConfig {
            max_match_len: 8,
            min_match_len: 2,
            max_proposals: 16,
            search_window_tokens: 65_536,
            max_history_tokens: 1_048_576,
        }
    }
}

impl NgramConfig {
    /// Refuse a configuration the lookup cannot honor, by name.
    fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {
        let refuse = |detail: String| SpecError::SessionState { detail };
        if self.max_proposals == 0 {
            return Err(refuse(
                "n-gram config: max_proposals must be at least 1".to_string(),
            ));
        }
        if self.min_match_len == 0 {
            return Err(refuse(
                "n-gram config: min_match_len must be at least 1".to_string(),
            ));
        }
        if self.max_match_len < self.min_match_len {
            return Err(refuse(format!(
                "n-gram config: max_match_len {} is below min_match_len {}",
                self.max_match_len, self.min_match_len
            )));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// The n-gram prompt-lookup proposer. Implements the crate's
/// [`Speculator`] seam plus an inherent `propose_block` mirroring
/// `DflashSpeculator::propose_block`, so the session dispatches to
/// either draft source through one shape.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct NgramProposer {
    config: NgramConfig,
    /// The target vocabulary width the one-hot distributions are
    /// built at, validated against the target at session creation.
    vocab_size: usize,
    /// Committed tokens in order: exactly the sequence the session
    /// has committed, which at propose time is everything except
    /// `pending` (the trait's commit contract).
    history: Vec<u32>,
    /// Backing store for the trait's borrowed view.
    last_tokens: Vec<u32>,
    /// One-hot rows backing the trait's borrowed view.
    last_probs: Vec<Vec<f32>>,
}

impl NgramProposer {
    /// Build a proposer over `config` for a target with
    /// `vocab_size` tokens. Refuses an invalid configuration by
    /// name.
    pub fn new(config: NgramConfig, vocab_size: usize) -> Result<Self> {
        config.validate()?;
        if vocab_size == 0 {
            return Err(SpecError::SessionState {
                detail: "n-gram proposer: vocab_size must be at least 1".to_string(),
            });
        }
        Ok(NgramProposer {
            config,
            vocab_size,
            history: Vec::new(),
            last_tokens: Vec::new(),
            last_probs: Vec::new(),
        })
    }

    /// The configuration this proposer runs under.
    pub fn config(&self) -> &NgramConfig {
        &self.config
    }

    /// The vocabulary width the proposal distributions are built at.
    pub fn vocab_size(&self) -> usize {
        self.vocab_size
    }

    /// How many committed tokens the history currently holds. At
    /// every round boundary this equals the target's cache position
    /// minus the one pending token.
    pub fn committed_len(&self) -> usize {
        self.history.len()
    }

    /// The lookup, shared by both proposal entry points. `pending`
    /// is the last emitted token, not yet committed: the searched
    /// sequence is `history + [pending]`, indexed virtually so a
    /// long history is never copied per proposal.
    fn lookup(&self, pending: u32, n: usize) -> Vec<u32> {
        let want = n.min(self.config.max_proposals);
        if want == 0 {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        let seq_len = self.history.len() + 1;
        let at = |i: usize| -> u32 {
            if i < self.history.len() {
                self.history[i]
            } else {
                pending
            }
        };
        // A match needs at least one continuation token after the
        // occurrence, so the suffix itself can span at most
        // seq_len - 1 tokens.
        let longest = self.config.max_match_len.min(seq_len.saturating_sub(1));
        if longest < self.config.min_match_len {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        for len in (self.config.min_match_len..=longest).rev() {
            let suffix_start = seq_len - len;
            // The latest start that still has a continuation token.
            let mut start = seq_len - len - 1;
            // The window bounds how far back a start may sit.
            let window_floor = if self.config.search_window_tokens == 0 {
                0
            } else {
                (seq_len - len - 1).saturating_sub(self.config.search_window_tokens - 1)
            };
            loop {
                if (0..len).all(|k| at(start + k) == at(suffix_start + k)) {
                    let cont_start = start + len;
                    let cont_end = (cont_start + want).min(seq_len);
                    return (cont_start..cont_end).map(at).collect();
                }
                if start == window_floor {
                    break;
                }
                start -= 1;
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }

    /// One-hot rows at `tokens`, refusing a token outside the
    /// vocabulary by name rather than indexing past the row.
    fn one_hot_rows(&self, tokens: &[u32]) -> Result<Vec<Vec<f32>>> {
        tokens
            .iter()
            .map(|&t| {
                if (t as usize) >= self.vocab_size {
                    return Err(SpecError::SessionState {
                        detail: format!(
                            "n-gram proposer: token {t} is outside the vocabulary of {} \
                             the distributions are built at",
                            self.vocab_size
                        ),
                    });
                }
                let mut row = vec![0.0f32; self.vocab_size];
                row[t as usize] = 1.0;
                Ok(row)
            })
            .collect()
    }

    /// Propose up to `n` tokens after `pending` by prompt lookup,
    /// the inherent entry the session drives (the DFlash
    /// speculator's `propose_block` shape). The draw source is
    /// accepted for signature parity and never consumed: drawing
    /// from a one-hot distribution yields its token with
    /// probability 1, so the proposal is deterministic on both
    /// arms.
    pub fn propose_block(
        &mut self,
        pending: u32,
        n: usize,
        arm: DraftArm,
        _rng: &mut dyn FnMut() -> f64,
    ) -> Result<Proposal> {
        let tokens = self.lookup(pending, n);
        let dists = match arm {
            DraftArm::Greedy => Vec::new(),
            DraftArm::Sampled { .. } => self.one_hot_rows(&tokens)?,
        };
        self.last_probs = match arm {
            // The greedy arm keeps no distributions on the hot
            // path (the DFlash rule); the trait shim rebuilds the
            // one-hot view from the tokens on demand.
            DraftArm::Greedy => Vec::new(),
            DraftArm::Sampled { .. } => dists.clone(),
        };
        self.last_tokens.clone_from(&tokens);
        Ok(Proposal { tokens, dists })
    }
}

impl Speculator for NgramProposer {
    fn mode(&self) -> SpecMode {
        SpecMode::Ngram
    }

    fn max_depth(&self) -> usize {
        self.config.max_proposals
    }

    fn propose(&mut self, pending: u32, n: usize) -> Result<BlockProposal<'_>> {
        let mut no_draws = || 0.0f64;
        let proposal = self.propose_block(pending, n, DraftArm::Greedy, &mut no_draws)?;
        let _ = proposal;
        if self.last_probs.is_empty() {
            // Greedy proposals carry no stored distributions (see
            // propose_block); the trait's contract is a one-hot
            // view of the proposed tokens, built here on the
            // shim's cold path, exactly the DFlash shim's shape.
            self.last_probs = self.one_hot_rows(&self.last_tokens)?;
        }
        let dists = self
            .last_probs
            .iter()
            .map(|row| DraftDist { probs: row })
            .collect();
        Ok(BlockProposal {
            tokens: &self.last_tokens,
            dists,
        })
    }

    fn commit(&mut self, tokens: &[u32]) -> Result<()> {
        self.history.extend_from_slice(tokens);
        if self.config.max_history_tokens > 0 && self.history.len() > self.config.max_history_tokens
        {
            let excess = self.history.len() - self.config.max_history_tokens;
            self.history.drain(..excess);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    // note_captures keeps the trait default: the proposer conditions
    // on tokens only, so captured layer rows are ignored by design.
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    const VOCAB: usize = 128;

    fn proposer(config: NgramConfig) -> NgramProposer {
        NgramProposer::new(config, VOCAB).expect("valid config")
    }

    fn greedy(prop: &mut NgramProposer, pending: u32, n: usize) -> Vec<u32> {
        let mut no_draws = || 0.0f64;
        prop.propose_block(pending, n, DraftArm::Greedy, &mut no_draws)
            .expect("greedy proposal")
            .tokens
    }

    #[test]
    fn config_validation_refuses_by_name() {
        let bad = NgramConfig {
            max_proposals: 0,
            ..NgramConfig::default()
        };
        assert!(matches!(
            NgramProposer::new(bad, VOCAB),
            Err(SpecError::SessionState { .. })
        ));
        let bad = NgramConfig {
            min_match_len: 0,
            ..NgramConfig::default()
        };
        assert!(NgramProposer::new(bad, VOCAB).is_err());
        let bad = NgramConfig {
            max_match_len: 1,
            min_match_len: 3,
            ..NgramConfig::default()
        };
        assert!(NgramProposer::new(bad, VOCAB).is_err());
        assert!(NgramProposer::new(NgramConfig::default(), 0).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn no_match_returns_empty() {
        // Every token distinct: no suffix of length >= 2 can occur
        // twice, so the proposer stays silent.
        let mut prop = proposer(NgramConfig::default());
        prop.commit(&[10, 20, 30, 40, 50]).expect("commit");
        assert!(greedy(&mut prop, 60, 4).is_empty());
        // A sequence too short to hold a match plus a continuation
        // is silent too.
        let mut prop = proposer(NgramConfig::default());
        prop.commit(&[7]).expect("commit");
        assert!(greedy(&mut prop, 7, 4).is_empty());
        // And n = 0 proposes nothing by construction.
        let mut prop = proposer(NgramConfig::default());
        prop.commit(&[1, 2, 1]).expect("commit");
        assert!(greedy(&mut prop, 2, 0).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn longest_match_wins_over_shorter() {
        // Sequence (history + pending): [1, 2, 3, 4, 9, 8, 3, 4, 7,
        // 1, 2, 3, 4]. The 4-gram suffix [1, 2, 3, 4] occurs at
        // index 0, followed by 9. The shorter 2-gram suffix [3, 4]
        // occurs more recently (index 6), followed by 7. The
        // longest match wins: the proposal follows the 4-gram's
        // continuation, not the fresher 2-gram's.
        let mut prop = proposer(NgramConfig::default());
        prop.commit(&[1, 2, 3, 4, 9, 8, 3, 4, 7, 1, 2, 3])
            .expect("commit");
        assert_eq!(greedy(&mut prop, 4, 4), vec![9, 8, 3, 4]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn most_recent_occurrence_wins_among_equal_matches() {
        // The 2-gram [1, 2] occurs followed by 5 (older, index 0)
        // and by 6 (most recent, index 4); no longer suffix
        // matches, so recency decides and 6 leads the proposal.
        let mut prop = proposer(NgramConfig::default());
        prop.commit(&[1, 2, 5, 8, 1, 2, 6, 7, 1]).expect("commit");
        assert_eq!(greedy(&mut prop, 2, 4), vec![6, 7, 1, 2]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn continuation_is_capped_by_depth_and_by_what_follows() {
        let mut prop = proposer(NgramConfig::default());
        prop.commit(&[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 1]).expect("commit");
        // Depth caps the proposal.
        assert_eq!(greedy(&mut prop, 2, 3), vec![3, 4, 5]);
        // A deeper ask returns the whole recorded continuation,
        // which runs to the end of the sequence (the pending
        // token's own position included: it is a recorded token).
        assert_eq!(greedy(&mut prop, 2, 16), vec![3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 1, 2]);
        // max_proposals caps below the ask.
        let mut capped = proposer(NgramConfig {
            max_proposals: 2,
            ..NgramConfig::default()
        });
        capped.commit(&[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 1]).expect("commit");
        assert_eq!(greedy(&mut capped, 2, 16), vec![3, 4]);
        assert_eq!(capped.max_depth(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn min_match_len_is_a_floor_not_a_ranking() {
        // Only a 1-token repeat exists ([2] occurs, followed by
        // different tokens); the default floor of 2 refuses it.
        let mut prop = proposer(NgramConfig::default());
        prop.commit(&[1, 2, 3, 2, 4, 2]).expect("commit");
        assert!(greedy(&mut prop, 5, 4).is_empty());
        // Lowering the floor to 1 lets the most recent [2] speak:
        // followed by 4.
        let cfg = NgramConfig {
            min_match_len: 1,
            ..NgramConfig::default()
        };
        let mut prop = proposer(cfg);
        prop.commit(&[1, 2, 3, 2]).expect("commit");
        assert_eq!(greedy(&mut prop, 4, 1), Vec::<u32>::new());
        prop.commit(&[4]).expect("commit");
        // Sequence is now [1, 2, 3, 2, 4] + pending 2: the most
        // recent prior [2] was followed by 4.
        assert_eq!(greedy(&mut prop, 2, 1), vec![4]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn search_window_bounds_how_far_back_a_match_may_sit() {
        // The only occurrence of [1, 2] sits at the very start; a
        // window of 4 tokens back from the end cannot see it.
        let cfg = NgramConfig {
            search_window_tokens: 4,
            ..NgramConfig::default()
        };
        let mut prop = proposer(cfg);
        prop.commit(&[1, 2, 3, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 1])
            .expect("commit");
        assert!(greedy(&mut prop, 2, 4).is_empty());
        // The same history with the window open finds it.
        let mut prop = proposer(NgramConfig::default());
        prop.commit(&[1, 2, 3, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 1])
            .expect("commit");
        assert_eq!(greedy(&mut prop, 2, 4), vec![3, 10, 11, 12]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn commit_appends_and_history_bound_trims_oldest() {
        let cfg = NgramConfig {
            max_history_tokens: 5,
            ..NgramConfig::default()
        };
        let mut prop = proposer(cfg);
        prop.commit(&[1, 2, 3]).expect("commit");
        assert_eq!(prop.committed_len(), 3);
        prop.commit(&[4, 5, 6, 7]).expect("commit");
        assert_eq!(prop.committed_len(), 5);
        // The retained history is the newest five: [3, 4, 5, 6, 7].
        // A match against the trimmed-away [1, 2] prefix is gone.
        assert!(greedy(&mut prop, 2, 4).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn note_captures_is_a_no_op() {
        let mut prop = proposer(NgramConfig::default());
        prop.commit(&[1, 2, 3]).expect("commit");
        prop.note_captures(0, &[]).expect("captures ignored");
        assert_eq!(prop.committed_len(), 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn trait_view_agrees_with_propose_block_and_dists_are_one_hot() {
        let mut prop = proposer(NgramConfig::default());
        prop.commit(&[4, 5, 6, 4, 5]).expect("commit");
        let owned = greedy(&mut prop, 6, 3);
        let view = prop.propose(6, 3).expect("trait propose");
        assert_eq!(view.tokens, owned.as_slice());
        assert_eq!(view.dists.len(), owned.len());
        for (dist, &token) in view.dists.iter().zip(owned.iter()) {
            assert_eq!(dist.probs.len(), VOCAB);
            assert_eq!(dist.probs[token as usize], 1.0);
            assert_eq!(dist.probs.iter().sum::<f32>(), 1.0);
        }
        assert_eq!(prop.mode(), SpecMode::Ngram);
        assert_eq!(prop.max_depth(), NgramConfig::default().max_proposals);
    }

    #[test]
    fn sampled_arm_carries_one_hot_dists_and_the_same_tokens() {
        let mut prop = proposer(NgramConfig::default());
        prop.commit(&[4, 5, 6, 4, 5]).expect("commit");
        let mut no_draws = || 0.0f64;
        let sampled = prop
            .propose_block(6, 3, DraftArm::Sampled { temperature: 0.7 }, &mut no_draws)
            .expect("sampled proposal");
        assert_eq!(sampled.tokens, vec![4, 5, 6]);
        assert_eq!(sampled.dists.len(), 3);
        for (row, &token) in sampled.dists.iter().zip(sampled.tokens.iter()) {
            assert_eq!(row[token as usize], 1.0);
            assert_eq!(row.iter().sum::<f32>(), 1.0);
        }
        // Greedy carries no distributions (the walk never reads
        // them on that arm).
        let greedy_prop = prop
            .propose_block(6, 3, DraftArm::Greedy, &mut no_draws)
            .expect("greedy proposal");
        assert_eq!(greedy_prop.tokens, sampled.tokens);
        assert!(greedy_prop.dists.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn out_of_vocab_proposal_refuses_on_the_sampled_arm_by_name() {
        // A token outside the distribution width can only arrive
        // from a caller lying about the vocabulary; the proposer
        // refuses by name instead of indexing past the row.
        let mut prop = proposer(NgramConfig::default());
        prop.commit(&[1, 2, 900, 1]).expect("commit");
        let mut no_draws = || 0.0f64;
        let err = prop
            .propose_block(2, 2, DraftArm::Sampled { temperature: 1.0 }, &mut no_draws)
            .expect_err("out-of-vocab token must refuse");
        assert!(matches!(err, SpecError::SessionState { .. }), "{err}");
    }

    /// Lockstep acceptance simulation against a recorded stream:
    /// the session's greedy rule replayed at the proposer level.
    /// `history` starts as the stream's prompt; each round proposes
    /// after `pending`, the oracle stream accepts the matching
    /// prefix, and the round commits `[pending, accepted...]` and
    /// emits one further oracle token (the correction), exactly the
    /// session's accounting. Returns (proposed, accepted).
    fn simulate(stream: &[u32], prompt_len: usize, depth: usize) -> (usize, usize) {
        let mut prop = proposer(NgramConfig::default());
        prop.commit(&stream[..prompt_len]).expect("commit prompt");
        let mut pending = stream[prompt_len];
        let mut pos = prompt_len + 1;
        let (mut proposed, mut accepted_total) = (0usize, 0usize);
        while pos < stream.len() {
            let tokens = greedy(&mut prop, pending, depth);
            proposed += tokens.len();
            let mut accepted = 0;
            while accepted < tokens.len()
                && pos + accepted < stream.len()
                && tokens[accepted] == stream[pos + accepted]
            {
                accepted += 1;
            }
            accepted_total += accepted;
            // Commit [pending, accepted drafts...]; the correction
            // token at pos + accepted becomes the next pending.
            let mut committed = vec![pending];
            committed.extend_from_slice(&stream[pos..pos + accepted]);
            prop.commit(&committed).expect("commit round");
            if pos + accepted >= stream.len() {
                break;
            }
            pending = stream[pos + accepted];
            pos += accepted + 1;
        }
        (proposed, accepted_total)
    }

    // ----- Session-level tests: the proposer inside the loop -----

    use std::rc::Rc;

    #[test]
    fn session_creation_refusals_are_named() {
        // No proposer attached under n-gram mode.
        let err =
            SpecSession::new_ngram(fixture_target(), None, ngram_config(4), Arc::new(NullDiag))
                .err()

        assert!(matches!(err, SpecError::DraftNotLoaded), "{err}");

        // A proposer attached under the DFlash mode: the pairing
        // is refused by name, never silently reinterpreted.

        )
        .err()

                    field: "vocab_size",

                    actual: 64
                }
            ),

        );

        let too_deep = SpecConfig {

        .expect("round bound must refuse");

        );
    }

    /// The verifier property, n-gram arm: at temperature 0 the
    /// speculative stream equals plain greedy token for token,
    /// across prompt shapes, including the repetitive shape where
    /// the proposer speaks often and the prose shape where it
    /// mostly stays silent.
    #[test]
    fn session_greedy_matches_plain_across_prompt_shapes() {
        let prompts: Vec<Vec<u32>> = vec![repetitive_prompt(), prose_prompt(), vec![7]];
        for prompt in &prompts {
            for depth in [1usize, 4] {
                let mut session =
                    testkit::build_ngram_session(ngram_config(depth), NgramConfig::default());
                session.begin(prompt).expect("begin");
                let stream = session.generate(48, &[]).expect("generate");
                assert_eq!(
                    stream,
                    testkit::plain_greedy(prompt, 48),
                    "n-gram identity, prompt {prompt:?} depth {depth}"
                );
                let stats = session.stats();
                assert!(stats.accepted <= stats.proposed);
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn session_sampled_is_reproducible_per_seed() {
        let run = || {
            let config = SpecConfig {
                mode: SpecMode::Ngram,
                depth: 3,
                temperature: 0.7,
                seed: 42,
                ..SpecConfig::default()
            };
            let mut session = testkit::build_ngram_session(config, NgramConfig::default());
            session.begin(&[10, 20, 30, 40, 10, 20]).expect("begin");
            session.generate(32, &[]).expect("generate")
        };
        let stream = run();
        assert_eq!(stream.len(), 32);
        assert!(stream.iter().all(|&t| (t as usize) < VOCAB));
        assert_eq!(stream, run(), "same seed, same sampled stream");
    }

    /// The fixture acceptance measurement (the harness whose
    /// numbers `bench/ngram-spec-2026-11-07.md` reports): greedy
    /// n-gram sessions over the synthetic fixture target, on a
    /// repetitive prompt and a prose prompt, at three depths.
    /// Identity is asserted hard; the rates are printed for the
    /// record (run with `-- --nocapture` to read them).
    #[test]
    fn fixture_acceptance_measurement() {
        for (name, prompt) in [
            ("repetitive", repetitive_prompt()),
            ("prose", prose_prompt()),
        ] {
            for depth in [1usize, 4, 6] {
                let mut session =
                    testkit::build_ngram_session(ngram_config(depth), NgramConfig::default());
                session.begin(&prompt).expect("begin");
                let stream = session.generate(96, &[]).expect("generate");
                assert_eq!(stream, testkit::plain_greedy(&prompt, 96));
                let stats = session.finish();
                eprintln!(
                    "FIXTURE_ACCEPTANCE fixture={name} depth={depth} rounds={} proposed={} \
                     accepted={} acceptance_rate={:.4} tokens_emitted={}",
                    stats.rounds,
                    stats.proposed,
                    stats.accepted,
                    stats.acceptance_rate(),
                    stats.tokens_emitted
                );
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn lockstep_simulation_accepts_repetition_and_stays_quiet_on_novelty() {
        // A stream built from a repeating sentence accepts almost
        // everything after the first cycle.
        let sentence: Vec<u32> = (0..12).map(|i| 10 + i).collect();
        let mut repetitive = sentence.clone();
        for _ in 0..7 {
            repetitive.extend_from_slice(&sentence);
        }
        let (proposed, accepted) = simulate(&repetitive, 12, 6);
        assert!(proposed > 0, "repetitive stream must propose");
        assert!(
            accepted as f64 / proposed as f64 > 0.9,
            "repetitive acceptance {accepted}/{proposed}"
        );
        // A stream of distinct tokens never repeats a 2-gram, so
        // nothing is proposed and nothing can be accepted wrongly.
        let novel: Vec<u32> = (0..96).collect();
        let (proposed, accepted) = simulate(&novel, 16, 6);
        assert_eq!((proposed, accepted), (0, 0));
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/itak-spec/src/resident.rs =====
//! The GPU-resident target driver (TODO T-9.6): the speculative
//! loop over [`wgpu_compute::ResidentSession`], the one
//! GPU-resident forward of the workspace. The session's chain,
//! KV, and head are reused exactly as they stand; this driver
//! only names the loop's operations over them.
//!
//! Checkpoint and release are bookkeeping here, and that is
//! sound rather than lazy: the resident KV is addressed by
//! absolute position (windowed layers by `position % ring`),
//! every attention view derives from the position a chunk ends
//! at, and entries past the current position are never read, so
//! restoring an earlier committed position is the position
//! restore itself ([`wgpu_compute::ResidentSession::rewind_to`],
//! whose span bound the driver's rewind inherits). A checkpoint
//! is therefore the position at checkpoint time, and releasing
//! it has nothing to free. The verify block size is not a
//! driver input either: the resident plan machinery sizes
//! itself per chunk.

use muse_glimmer::{GlimmerConfig, LayerInputCapture, Result as GlimmerResult};
use wgpu_compute::ResidentSession;

use crate::driver::TargetDriver;

/// A [`TargetDriver`] over a GPU-resident session. The session
/// owns the device KV; this wrapper owns nothing else.
pub struct ResidentTarget<'a> {
    session: ResidentSession<'a>,
}

impl<'a> ResidentTarget<'a> {
    /// Wrap a resident session as the loop's target driver.
    pub fn new(session: ResidentSession<'a>) -> Self {
        ResidentTarget { session }
    }

    /// The wrapped resident session (its stats are the serving
    /// counters the bench reads).
    pub fn session(&self) -> &ResidentSession<'a> {
        &self.session
    }

    /// The wrapped resident session, mutably (a caller resetting
    /// between runs goes through here).
    pub fn session_mut(&mut self) -> &mut ResidentSession<'a> {
        &mut self.session
    }
}

impl TargetDriver for ResidentTarget<'_> {
    /// The position at checkpoint time: restoring it is the
    /// whole checkpoint contract on a position-addressed KV
    /// (see the module docs).
    type Checkpoint = usize;

    fn config(&self) -> &GlimmerConfig {
        self.session.config()
    }

    fn position(&self) -> usize {
        self.session.position()
    }

    fn forward(&mut self, tokens: &[u32]) -> GlimmerResult<Vec<f32>> {
        self.session.forward(tokens)
    }

    fn forward_capturing(
        &mut self,
        tokens: &[u32],
        capture_layers: &[usize],
    ) -> GlimmerResult<(Vec<f32>, Vec<LayerInputCapture>)> {
        self.session.forward_capturing(tokens, capture_layers)
    }

    fn forward_block_capturing(
        &mut self,
        tokens: &[u32],
        capture_layers: &[usize],
    ) -> GlimmerResult<(Vec<f32>, Vec<LayerInputCapture>)> {
        self.session.forward_block_capturing(tokens, capture_layers)
    }

    fn checkpoint(&mut self, _rows: usize) -> GlimmerResult<usize> {
        Ok(self.session.position())
    }

    fn rewind(&mut self, _checkpoint: &usize, to: usize) -> GlimmerResult<()> {
        self.session.rewind_to(to)
    }

    fn release(&mut self, _checkpoint: &usize) -> GlimmerResult<()> {
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Forward the completed round to the resident
    /// session's capture accumulator: at the capture diag
    /// level the session fingerprints the proposed ids and
    /// records the accepted count; at every other level the
    /// session records nothing, so this is a pure
    /// observation with no effect on the round.
    fn note_spec_round(&mut self, proposed: &[u32], accepted: usize) {
        let _ = self.session.note_spec_round(proposed, accepted);
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/itak-spec/src/rng.rs =====
//! The loop's random source (SPEC-itak-spec open question Q6, settled by
//! this crate: the session owns one seeded generator, injected at
//! construction through [`crate::SpecConfig::seed`], never global state).
//!
//! The generator is xorshift64*, the same one the engine's sampler uses
//! (`crates/itak-engine/src/sampler.rs`), so a seed means the same stream
//! of draws in both places. Greedy rounds draw nothing; the generator only
//! advances when temperature sampling actually consumes a draw, which
//! keeps greedy runs perfectly reproducible regardless of the seed.

/// A seeded xorshift64* generator.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Rng {
    state: u64,
}

impl Rng {
    /// Seed the generator. A zero seed is remapped to a fixed nonzero
    /// constant, exactly as the engine sampler does, so seed 0 is still a
    /// well-defined reproducible stream.
    pub fn new(seed: u64) -> Self {
        let state = if seed == 0 {
            0x9e37_79b9_7f4a_7c15
        } else {
            seed
        };
        Rng { state }
    }

    /// The next 64-bit value.
    pub fn next_u64(&mut self) -> u64 {
        let mut x = self.state;
        x ^= x >> 12;
        x ^= x << 25;
        x ^= x >> 27;
        self.state = x;
        x.wrapping_mul(0x2545_f491_4f6c_dd1d)
    }

    /// The next draw in `[0, 1)` with 53 bits of precision.
    pub fn next_f64(&mut self) -> f64 {
        (self.next_u64() >> 11) as f64 / (1u64 << 53) as f64
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn same_seed_same_stream() {
        let mut a = Rng::new(42);
        let mut b = Rng::new(42);
        for _ in 0..64 {
            assert_eq!(a.next_u64(), b.next_u64());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn different_seeds_different_streams() {
        let mut a = Rng::new(1);
        let mut b = Rng::new(2);
        let sa: Vec<u64> = (0..8).map(|_| a.next_u64()).collect();
        let sb: Vec<u64> = (0..8).map(|_| b.next_u64()).collect();
        assert_ne!(sa, sb);
    }

    #[test]
    fn zero_seed_is_remapped_and_deterministic() {
        let mut a = Rng::new(0);
        let mut b = Rng::new(0);
        for _ in 0..16 {
            let x = a.next_f64();
            assert_eq!(x, b.next_f64());
            assert!((0.0..1.0).contains(&x));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn draws_stay_in_unit_interval() {
        let mut r = Rng::new(7);
        for _ in 0..10_000 {
            let x = r.next_f64();
            assert!((0.0..1.0).contains(&x), "draw {x} escaped [0, 1)");
        }
    }
}
