===== FILE: crates/itak-spec/src/sampler.rs =====
//! Distribution construction and the correction walk (SPEC-itak-spec
//! Section 4): pure functions, no model, no cache, so the math is testable
//! in isolation (TODO T-3.7).
//!
//! Indexing contract, settled against the E3 real-file run
//! (`bench/dflash-e3-2026-10-30.md`): the target's block forward returns one
//! finished distribution per input position; row `p[i]` is the distribution
//! the target assigns to the token AFTER position `i`, so `p[i]` judges
//! draft token `t[i + 1]`. The draft's noise block obeys the same shape:
//! draft row `k` (0-based) is the draft distribution for draft token
//! `t[k + 1]` (1-based). The walk below takes proposal tokens `t[0..n]`
//! (0-based slice of the 1-based `t[1..=n]`), proposal distributions
//! `q[0..n]` aligned with them, and target rows `p[0..=n]`.
//!
//! The walk, exactly as the spec states it:
//!
//! - Greedy (temperature 0): accept `t[i]` iff it equals the target's
//!   argmax at `p[i - 1]`. At the first mismatch, emit the target's argmax
//!   at that row as the replacement. On full acceptance, emit the target's
//!   argmax at `p[n]` as the bonus. The emitted stream is then
//!   token-identical to non-speculative greedy generation.
//! - Sampled: draw `r` uniform in `[0, 1)`; accept `t[i]` iff
//!   `r < min(1, p(t[i]) / q(t[i]))`. At the first rejection `j`, emit a
//!   replacement drawn from `norm(max(0, p[j - 1] - q[j]))`. On full
//!   acceptance, emit a bonus drawn from `p[n]`. This is the standard
//!   speculative-sampling correction: the emitted distribution equals the
//!   target's, token for token in distribution.
//!
//! Distribution construction mirrors the engine sampler
//! (`crates/itak-engine/src/sampler.rs`) so both paths mean the same thing
//! by a temperature: a numerically stable softmax over `(z - max) / T` in
//! f64, nucleus truncation that sorts by probability descending with ties
//! broken by the lower token id, and argmax ties broken by the lowest id.
//!
//! Contract: every public entry point states the shape it needs (a
//! non-empty logit row; a walk whose target rows cover the proposal
//! plus the bonus row; proposal tokens inside the rows they index)
//! and refuses a violating input by name with
//! [`SpecError::SamplerContract`] instead of panicking on the
//! indexing. Behavior on contract-respecting inputs is unchanged.

use crate::error::{Result, SpecError};

/// The greedy choice over a finished logit row: the largest logit, lowest
/// token id on ties (the engine sampler's tie rule).
///
/// The scan runs eight interleaved accumulators so the comparison
/// chain is not one long dependency, then merges them with the
/// exact scalar rule. The merge is what keeps the result
/// bit-identical to the naive scan: an accumulator only ever holds
/// a value some element actually had (a NaN never wins a `>`
/// comparison, so no accumulator can hold one), a later accumulator
/// displaces an earlier one only on a strictly greater value or an
/// equal value at a lower index, and -0.0 and 0.0 compare equal, so
/// the first of them wins, as in the scalar scan. Rows under the
/// lane count take the scalar scan itself. The equivalence is
/// pinned by `argmax_matches_the_scalar_reference` in the tests,
/// over adversarial rows (ties across lanes, NaNs, infinities,
/// signed zeros, denormals).
pub fn argmax(logits: &[f32]) -> u32 {
    /// Interleaved scan lanes: lane `j` visits indices
    /// `j, j + LANES, j + 2 * LANES, ...` in increasing order.
    const LANES: usize = 8;
    if logits.len() < LANES {
        let mut best = 0usize;
        let mut best_val = f32::NEG_INFINITY;
        for (i, &v) in logits.iter().enumerate() {
            if v > best_val {
                best_val = v;
                best = i;
            }
        }
        return best as u32;
    }
    // Each lane's sentinel index is its own first index, so a lane
    // whose elements never beat the sentinel (all NaN or all
    // negative infinity) reports its first index, exactly what the
    // scalar scan reports for that lane's elements in isolation.
    let mut lanes: [(f32, usize); LANES] = std::array::from_fn(|j| (f32::NEG_INFINITY, j));
    let mut i = 0usize;
    while i + LANES <= logits.len() {
        for (j, lane) in lanes.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            let v = logits[i + j];
            if v > lane.0 {
                *lane = (v, i + j);
            }
        }
        i += LANES;
    }
    // The tail folds into lane 0 in index order; lane 0's set is
    // then its strided indices followed by the tail indices, all
    // in increasing order, so its scalar-rule best is unaffected.
    while i < logits.len() {
        let v = logits[i];
        if v > lanes[0].0 {
            lanes[0] = (v, i);
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    let mut best = lanes[0];
    for lane in &lanes[1..] {
        if lane.0 > best.0 || (lane.0 == best.0 && lane.1 < best.1) {
            best = *lane;
        }
    }
    best.1 as u32
}

/// Build a probability distribution from finished logits at a temperature.
///
/// Temperature at or below zero returns the one-hot distribution at the
/// argmax, which is the honest greedy distribution. Positive temperatures
/// apply the stable softmax; `top_p` in `(0, 1)` then nucleus-truncates
/// and renormalizes; any other `top_p` disables truncation.
///
/// An empty logit row refuses by name: there is no distribution over
/// zero tokens, and the greedy path used to panic indexing it.
pub fn distribution(logits: &[f32], temperature: f32, top_p: f32) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
    if logits.is_empty() {
        return Err(SpecError::SamplerContract {
            entry: "distribution",
            detail: "logit row is empty; a distribution needs at least one token".to_string(),
        });
    }
    if temperature <= 0.0 {
        let mut out = vec![0.0f32; logits.len()];
        out[argmax(logits) as usize] = 1.0;
        return Ok(out);
    }
    let t = f64::from(temperature);
    let max = logits.iter().copied().fold(f32::NEG_INFINITY, f32::max);
    let mut probs: Vec<f64> = logits
        .iter()
        .map(|&z| ((f64::from(z) - f64::from(max)) / t).exp())
        .collect();
    let sum: f64 = probs.iter().sum();
    if sum > 0.0 {
        for p in &mut probs {
            *p /= sum;
        }
    }
    if top_p > 0.0 && top_p < 1.0 {
        nucleus_truncate(&mut probs, f64::from(top_p));
    }
    Ok(probs.iter().map(|&p| p as f32).collect())
}

/// Nucleus truncation in place: keep the smallest set of highest-probability
/// tokens whose cumulative mass reaches `top_p`, zero the rest, renormalize.
fn nucleus_truncate(probs: &mut [f64], top_p: f64) {
    let mut order: Vec<usize> = (0..probs.len()).collect();
    order.sort_by(|&a, &b| {
        probs[b]
            .partial_cmp(&probs[a])
            .unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)
            .then(a.cmp(&b))
    });
    let mut cumulative = 0.0f64;
    let mut keep = vec![false; probs.len()];
    for &idx in &order {
        keep[idx] = true;
        cumulative += probs[idx];
        if cumulative >= top_p {
            break;
        }
    }
    let mut kept_sum = 0.0f64;
    for (i, p) in probs.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        if keep[i] {
            kept_sum += *p;
        } else {
            *p = 0.0;
        }
    }
    if kept_sum > 0.0 {
        for p in probs.iter_mut() {
            *p /= kept_sum;
        }
    }
}

/// Draw one token from a probability row using a uniform draw in `[0, 1)`.
/// The row need not be perfectly normalized; the draw is scaled by the
/// row's actual mass.
pub fn sample_from(probs: &[f32], r: f64) -> u32 {
    let total: f64 = probs.iter().map(|&p| f64::from(p)).sum();
    if total <= 0.0 {
        return argmax(probs);
    }
    let target = r * total;
    let mut cumulative = 0.0f64;
    for (i, &p) in probs.iter().enumerate() {
        cumulative += f64::from(p);
        if target < cumulative {
            return i as u32;
        }
    }
    // Float edge: the draw landed past the accumulated mass. Fall back to
    // the last token carrying any mass.
    for (i, &p) in probs.iter().enumerate().rev() {
        if p > 0.0 {
            return i as u32;
        }
    }
    argmax(probs)
}

/// Draw from the normalized residual `norm(max(0, p - q))`, the correction
/// distribution at a rejection. If the residual has no mass (reachable
/// only through float rounding on a genuine rejection, where
/// `p(t) < q(t)` already guarantees mass somewhere else in exact math),
/// the draw falls back to `p` itself; that guard is numerical, not a
/// change to the correction rule.
pub fn sample_residual(p: &[f32], q: &[f32], r: f64) -> u32 {
    let residual: Vec<f64> = p
        .iter()
        .zip(q.iter())
        .map(|(&pi, &qi)| (f64::from(pi) - f64::from(qi)).max(0.0))
        .collect();
    let total: f64 = residual.iter().sum();
    if total <= 0.0 {
        return sample_from(p, r);
    }
    let target = r * total;
    let mut cumulative = 0.0f64;
    for (i, &m) in residual.iter().enumerate() {
        cumulative += m;
        if target < cumulative {
            return i as u32;
        }
    }
    sample_from(p, r)
}

/// The outcome of one correction walk.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct WalkOutcome {
    /// How many leading draft tokens were accepted.
    pub accepted: usize,
    /// The token the walk emits after the accepted prefix: the replacement
    /// at the first rejection, or the bonus on full acceptance.
    pub token: u32,
    /// The 1-based index of the first rejected draft token (`j` in the
    /// spec's walk), or `None` on full acceptance.
    pub first_rejection: Option<usize>,
}

/// The greedy walk. `p_argmax` holds the target's argmax at rows
/// `p[0..=n]` (one more row than the proposal: the last row supplies the
/// bonus). `proposal` holds the draft tokens `t[1..=n]`.
///
/// Pure prefix matching against the target's own greedy choices, which is
/// what makes the temperature-0 identity hold by construction.
///
/// Fewer than `proposal.len() + 1` target rows refuses by name: prefix
/// matching reads one row per proposal token, and full acceptance reads
/// the bonus row after them.
pub fn correct_greedy(p_argmax: &[u32], proposal: &[u32]) -> Result<WalkOutcome> {
    let n = proposal.len();
    if p_argmax.len() < n + 1 {
        return Err(SpecError::SamplerContract {
            entry: "correct_greedy",
            detail: format!(
                "walk over {} proposal tokens needs {} target rows (one per token plus the bonus row), got {}",
                n,
                n + 1,
                p_argmax.len()
            ),
        });
    }
    let mut accepted = 0;
    while accepted < n && proposal[accepted] == p_argmax[accepted] {
        accepted += 1;
    }
    if accepted == n {
        Ok(WalkOutcome {
            accepted,
            token: p_argmax[n],
            first_rejection: None,
        })
    } else {
        Ok(WalkOutcome {
            accepted,
            token: p_argmax[accepted],
            first_rejection: Some(accepted + 1),
        })
    }
}

/// The sampled walk (rejection sampling, SPEC-itak-spec Sections 4 and
/// T-3.2). `p_rows` holds the target distributions at rows `p[0..=n]`,
/// `q_rows` the draft distributions aligned with `proposal`. `rng` yields
/// uniform draws in `[0, 1)`; a full-acceptance walk consumes `n + 1`
/// draws (one per proposal token plus the bonus), a walk rejected at `j`
/// consumes `j + 1` (the rejections draws plus the residual draw).
///
/// Missing rows refuse by name: `p_rows` must cover the proposal plus
/// the bonus row and `q_rows` the proposal, and every proposal token
/// must index inside the rows it is judged against.
pub fn correct_sampled(
    p_rows: &[&[f32]],
    q_rows: &[&[f32]],
    proposal: &[u32],
    rng: &mut dyn FnMut() -> f64,
) -> Result<WalkOutcome> {
    let n = proposal.len();
    if p_rows.len() < n + 1 {
        return Err(SpecError::SamplerContract {
            entry: "correct_sampled",
            detail: format!(
                "walk over {n} proposal tokens needs {} target rows (one per token plus the bonus row), got {}",
                n + 1,
                p_rows.len()
            ),
        });
    }
    if q_rows.len() < n {
        return Err(SpecError::SamplerContract {
            entry: "correct_sampled",
            detail: format!(
                "walk over {n} proposal tokens needs {n} draft rows, got {}",
                q_rows.len()
            ),
        });
    }
    for k in 0..n {
        let token = proposal[k] as usize;
        if token >= p_rows[k].len() || token >= q_rows[k].len() {
            return Err(SpecError::SamplerContract {
                entry: "correct_sampled",
                detail: format!(
                    "proposal token {} at position {k} is outside its target row of {} entries or its draft row of {} entries",
                    proposal[k],
                    p_rows[k].len(),
                    q_rows[k].len()
                ),
            });
        }
    }
    for k in 0..n {
        let token = proposal[k] as usize;
        let p_t = f64::from(p_rows[k][token]);
        let q_t = f64::from(q_rows[k][token]);
        let ratio = if q_t > 0.0 {
            p_t / q_t
        } else if p_t > 0.0 {
            f64::INFINITY
        } else {
            0.0
        };
        let r = rng();
        if r < ratio.min(1.0) {
            continue;
        }
        let replacement = sample_residual(p_rows[k], q_rows[k], rng());
        return Ok(WalkOutcome {
            accepted: k,
            token: replacement,
            first_rejection: Some(k + 1),
        });
    }
    let bonus = sample_from(p_rows[n], rng());
    Ok(WalkOutcome {
        accepted: n,
        token: bonus,
        first_rejection: None,
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// A scripted draw source: the walk must consume draws in order.
    fn scripted(draws: &[f64]) -> (Vec<f64>, usize) {
        (draws.to_vec(), 0)
    }

    #[test]
    fn argmax_breaks_ties_by_lowest_id() {
        assert_eq!(argmax(&[1.0, 3.0, 3.0, 2.0]), 1);
        assert_eq!(argmax(&[-5.0, -1.0]), 1);
    }

    /// The pre-optimization scan, verbatim: the reference the
    /// laned implementation must match bit for bit (the returned
    /// index, on every input, not just well-behaved ones).
    fn argmax_scalar_reference(logits: &[f32]) -> u32 {
        let mut best = 0usize;
        let mut best_val = f32::NEG_INFINITY;
        for (i, &v) in logits.iter().enumerate() {
            if v > best_val {
                best_val = v;
                best = i;
            }
        }
        best as u32
    }

    /// A deterministic xorshift64* source for the equivalence
    /// sweep (no external crates, same sequence every run).
    struct SweepRng(u64);

    impl SweepRng {
        fn next_u64(&mut self) -> u64 {
            let mut x = self.0;
            x ^= x >> 12;
            x ^= x << 25;
            x ^= x >> 27;
            self.0 = x;
            x.wrapping_mul(0x2545_F491_4F6C_DD1D)
        }

        /// Draw from a pool chosen to stress the tie and
        /// special-value rules: small integers (frequent exact
        /// ties), signed zeros, infinities, NaN, denormals, and
        /// wide-magnitude values.
        fn next_logit(&mut self) -> f32 {
            const POOL: &[f32] = &[
                0.0,
                -0.0,
                1.0,
                -1.0,
                2.0,
                3.0,
                f32::INFINITY,
                f32::NEG_INFINITY,
                f32::NAN,
                f32::MIN_POSITIVE,
                -f32::MIN_POSITIVE,
                1e30,
                -1e30,
            ];
            let r = self.next_u64();
            if r % 3 == 0 {
                POOL[((r >> 8) as usize) % POOL.len()]
            } else {
                ((r >> 16) % 2001) as f32 * 0.01 - 10.0
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn argmax_matches_the_scalar_reference() {
        // Hand-built adversarial rows: maxima duplicated across
        // lane boundaries, all-special rows, signed-zero pairs.
        let fixed: Vec<Vec<f32>> = vec![
            Vec::new(),
            vec![f32::NAN; 64],
            vec![f32::NEG_INFINITY; 65],
            vec![0.0, -0.0],
            vec![-0.0, 0.0],
            {
                let mut v = vec![1.0; 64];
                v[63] = 2.0;
                v
            },
            {
                let mut v = vec![1.0; 64];
                v[0] = 2.0;
                v[56] = 2.0;
                v
            },
            {
                let mut v = vec![f32::NAN; 100];
                v[99] = -1.0;
                v
            },
        ];
        for row in &fixed {
            assert_eq!(
                argmax(row),
                argmax_scalar_reference(row),
                "fixed row {row:?}"
            );
        }
        // Randomized sweep across sizes that cross the lane and
        // tail boundaries, at the real vocabulary width included.
        let mut rng = SweepRng(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
        for &len in &[
            1usize, 7, 8, 9, 15, 16, 17, 63, 64, 65, 100, 999, 4096, 202_048,
        ] {
            for _ in 0..24 {
                let row: Vec<f32> = (0..len).map(|_| rng.next_logit()).collect();
                assert_eq!(
                    argmax(&row),
                    argmax_scalar_reference(&row),
                    "argmax diverged from the scalar reference at len {len}"
                );
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn distribution_at_zero_temperature_is_one_hot() {
        let d = distribution(&[0.0, 2.0, 1.0], 0.0, 1.0).expect("distribution");
        assert_eq!(d, vec![0.0, 1.0, 0.0]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn distribution_softmax_matches_hand_math() {
        // logits [0, ln 2] at T=1: exp gives [1, 2], normalized [1/3, 2/3].
        let d = distribution(&[0.0, std::f32::consts::LN_2], 1.0, 1.0).expect("distribution");
        assert!((d[0] - 1.0 / 3.0).abs() < 1e-6, "got {d:?}");
        assert!((d[1] - 2.0 / 3.0).abs() < 1e-6, "got {d:?}");
        // Temperature 2 flattens: exp([0, ln2 / 2]) = [1, sqrt(2)].
        let d2 = distribution(&[0.0, std::f32::consts::LN_2], 2.0, 1.0).expect("distribution");
        let sqrt2 = std::f64::consts::SQRT_2;
        let expect0 = (1.0 / (1.0 + sqrt2)) as f32;
        assert!((d2[0] - expect0).abs() < 1e-6, "got {d2:?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn distribution_nucleus_truncates_and_renormalizes() {
        // Probs before truncation: [0.5, 0.3, 0.2] via logits ln of those.
        let logits = [0.5f32.ln(), 0.3f32.ln(), 0.2f32.ln()];
        let d = distribution(&logits, 1.0, 0.6).expect("distribution");
        // Top token alone is 0.5 < 0.6, so the nucleus is {0, 1} with mass
        // 0.8, renormalized to [0.625, 0.375, 0].
        assert!((d[0] - 0.625).abs() < 1e-5, "got {d:?}");
        assert!((d[1] - 0.375).abs() < 1e-5, "got {d:?}");
        assert_eq!(d[2], 0.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn greedy_walk_accepts_the_matching_prefix() {
        // Target argmaxes per row p[0..=3]; proposal matches twice, then
        // diverges: replacement is the target argmax at the mismatch row.
        let p_argmax = [10, 20, 30, 40];
        let out = correct_greedy(&p_argmax, &[10, 20, 99]).expect("walk");
        assert_eq!(out.accepted, 2);
        assert_eq!(out.token, 30);
        assert_eq!(out.first_rejection, Some(3));
    }

    #[test]
    fn greedy_walk_full_acceptance_takes_the_bonus() {
        let p_argmax = [10, 20, 30, 40];
        let out = correct_greedy(&p_argmax, &[10, 20, 30]).expect("walk");
        assert_eq!(out.accepted, 3);
        assert_eq!(out.token, 40);
        assert_eq!(out.first_rejection, None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn greedy_walk_first_token_mismatch() {
        let p_argmax = [10, 20];
        let out = correct_greedy(&p_argmax, &[77]).expect("walk");
        assert_eq!(out.accepted, 0);
        assert_eq!(out.token, 10);
        assert_eq!(out.first_rejection, Some(1));
    }

    #[test]
    fn greedy_walk_empty_proposal_is_all_bonus() {
        let out = correct_greedy(&[55], &[]).expect("walk");
        assert_eq!(out.accepted, 0);
        assert_eq!(out.token, 55);
        assert_eq!(out.first_rejection, None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn sampled_walk_accepts_when_the_draw_beats_the_ratio() {
        // p = [0.5, 0.5], q = [0.25, 0.75]; proposal token 1 has
        // p/q = 2/3. Draw 0.5 accepts; the bonus then comes from p[1].
        let p0: &[f32] = &[0.5, 0.5];
        let p1: &[f32] = &[0.1, 0.9];
        let q0: &[f32] = &[0.25, 0.75];
        let (draws, mut used) = scripted(&[0.5, 0.5]);
        let mut rng = || {
            let d = draws[used];
            used += 1;
            d
        };
        let out = correct_sampled(&[p0, p1], &[q0], &[1], &mut rng).expect("walk");
        assert_eq!(out.accepted, 1);
        assert_eq!(out.first_rejection, None);
        // Bonus draw 0.5 against p1 = [0.1, 0.9] lands on token 1.
        assert_eq!(out.token, 1);
        assert_eq!(used, 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn sampled_walk_rejection_draws_from_the_residual() {
        // Same setup; draw 0.7 > 2/3 rejects. Residual max(0, p - q) =
        // [0.25, 0], normalized [1, 0]: the replacement is token 0 for
        // any residual draw.
        let p0: &[f32] = &[0.5, 0.5];
        let p1: &[f32] = &[0.1, 0.9];
        let q0: &[f32] = &[0.25, 0.75];
        let (draws, mut used) = scripted(&[0.7, 0.99]);
        let mut rng = || {
            let d = draws[used];
            used += 1;
            d
        };
        let out = correct_sampled(&[p0, p1], &[q0], &[1], &mut rng).expect("walk");
        assert_eq!(out.accepted, 0);
        assert_eq!(out.token, 0);
        assert_eq!(out.first_rejection, Some(1));
        assert_eq!(used, 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn sampled_walk_certain_token_always_accepts() {
        // q puts all mass on the proposed token and p agrees: ratio is 1,
        // and even a draw of 0.999 accepts (r < min(1, ratio) = 1).
        let p0: &[f32] = &[0.0, 1.0];
        let p1: &[f32] = &[1.0, 0.0];
        let q0: &[f32] = &[0.0, 1.0];
        let (draws, mut used) = scripted(&[0.999, 0.0]);
        let mut rng = || {
            let d = draws[used];
            used += 1;
            d
        };
        let out = correct_sampled(&[p0, p1], &[q0], &[1], &mut rng).expect("walk");
        assert_eq!(out.accepted, 1);
        assert_eq!(out.token, 0);
    }

    // The four contract violations the panel's probes panicked on,
    // one per probe site: each now refuses by name instead.

    #[test]
    fn distribution_refuses_empty_logits_by_name() {
        // Probe site: the one-hot write over an empty row (greedy path).
        let err = distribution(&[], 0.0, 1.0).expect_err("empty logits must refuse");
        assert!(
            matches!(
                err,
                SpecError::SamplerContract {
                    entry: "distribution",
                    ..
                }
            ),
            "got {err:?}"
        );
        // The sampled path refuses the same input the same way.
        let err = distribution(&[], 1.0, 1.0).expect_err("empty logits must refuse");
        assert!(
            matches!(
                err,
                SpecError::SamplerContract {
                    entry: "distribution",
                    ..
                }
            ),
            "got {err:?}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn greedy_walk_refuses_rows_shorter_than_the_proposal_by_name() {
        // Probe site: prefix matching reads one target row past the
        // end when the rows run out mid-proposal.
        let err = correct_greedy(&[10], &[10, 20]).expect_err("short rows must refuse");
        assert!(
            matches!(
                err,
                SpecError::SamplerContract {
                    entry: "correct_greedy",
                    ..
                }
            ),
            "got {err:?}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn greedy_walk_refuses_a_missing_bonus_row_by_name() {
        // Probe site: full acceptance reads the bonus row at index n.
        let err = correct_greedy(&[10, 20], &[10, 20]).expect_err("missing bonus row must refuse");
        assert!(
            matches!(
                err,
                SpecError::SamplerContract {
                    entry: "correct_greedy",
                    ..
                }
            ),
            "got {err:?}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn sampled_walk_refuses_a_missing_bonus_row_by_name() {
        // Probe site: the full-acceptance bonus draw reads p_rows[n].
        let p0: &[f32] = &[0.5, 0.5];
        let q0: &[f32] = &[0.25, 0.75];
        let mut rng = || 0.0f64;
        let err = correct_sampled(&[p0], &[q0], &[1], &mut rng)
            .expect_err("missing bonus row must refuse");
        assert!(
            matches!(
                err,
                SpecError::SamplerContract {
                    entry: "correct_sampled",
                    ..
                }
            ),
            "got {err:?}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn sampled_walk_refuses_an_out_of_range_proposal_token_by_name() {
        // Same entry point, the other indexing the walk performs: a
        // proposal token outside the rows it is judged against.
        let p0: &[f32] = &[0.5, 0.5];
        let p1: &[f32] = &[0.5, 0.5];
        let q0: &[f32] = &[0.25, 0.75];
        let mut rng = || 0.0f64;
        let err = correct_sampled(&[p0, p1], &[q0], &[7], &mut rng)
            .expect_err("out-of-range token must refuse");
        assert!(
            matches!(
                err,
                SpecError::SamplerContract {
                    entry: "correct_sampled",
                    ..
                }
            ),
            "got {err:?}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn residual_distribution_is_the_normalized_positive_part() {
        // p = [0.2, 0.3, 0.5], q = [0.5, 0.25, 0.25]: residual is
        // [0, 0.05, 0.25], normalized [0, 1/6, 5/6].
        let p: &[f32] = &[0.2, 0.3, 0.5];
        let q: &[f32] = &[0.5, 0.25, 0.25];
        assert_eq!(sample_residual(p, q, 0.1), 1);
        assert_eq!(sample_residual(p, q, 0.5), 2);
        assert_eq!(sample_residual(p, q, 0.0), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn sample_from_uses_cumulative_mass_in_id_order() {
        let probs: &[f32] = &[0.25, 0.25, 0.5];
        assert_eq!(sample_from(probs, 0.0), 0);
        assert_eq!(sample_from(probs, 0.3), 1);
        assert_eq!(sample_from(probs, 0.9), 2);
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/itak-spec/src/session.rs =====
//! The speculative session: one target, one draft, and the round
//! structure of SPEC-itak-spec Section 4.
//!
//! The loop invariant: the emitted stream is always `committed + pending`,
//! where `committed` is exactly the target cache's position and `pending`
//! is the last emitted token, not yet forwarded. A round proposes drafts
//! after `pending`, verifies `[pending, drafts...]` in one block forward
//! under a KV checkpoint, runs the correction walk from
//! [`crate::sampler`], rewinds the cache to the committed count, and tells
//! the draft exactly the newly committed tokens. At temperature 0 the
//! emitted stream is token-identical to non-speculative greedy generation;
//! that identity is the crate's standing proof obligation and is tested on
//! synthetic configs and on the real Glimmer files.
//!
//! The target sits behind the [`crate::driver::TargetDriver`] seam:
//! the session is generic over the driver, defaulting to the CPU
//! driver ([`crate::CpuTarget`]) the loop was proven on, so the
//! GPU-resident driver runs the identical loop (TODO T-9.6).

use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Instant;

use muse_glimmer::LayerInputCapture;

use crate::config::{OnVerifyError, SpecConfig, SpecMode};
use crate::diag::Diag;
use crate::driver::{CpuTarget, TargetDriver};
use crate::error::{Result, SpecError};
use crate::ngram::NgramProposer;
use crate::rng::Rng;
use crate::sampler;
use crate::speculator::{cache_refused, DflashSpeculator, DraftArm, Proposal, Speculator};

/// Cumulative session statistics, pullable at any time (the
/// `spec_stats()` readout of SPEC-itak-spec Section 6.4).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SpecStats {
    /// Rounds run, including plain (non-speculative) rounds.
    pub rounds: usize,
    /// Draft tokens proposed across all rounds, including a latched
    /// round's discarded proposal (it was proposed, then the verify
    /// refused; the count stays honest).
    pub proposed: usize,
    /// Draft tokens accepted across all rounds.
    pub accepted: usize,
    /// Rounds whose correction walk rejected at least one draft token.
    pub rejections: usize,
    /// Rounds in which at least one speculatively forwarded position was
    /// discarded: partial acceptance, zero acceptance, or a verify
    /// refusal rollback.
    pub rollbacks: usize,
    /// Tokens emitted by rounds (the initial pending token from `begin`
    /// is not counted; it was emitted by the prefill).
    pub tokens_emitted: usize,
    /// Whether speculation has latched off after a verify refusal.
    pub fallback_latched: bool,
}

impl SpecStats {
    /// Accepted over proposed, in `[0, 1]`; zero when nothing was proposed.
    pub fn acceptance_rate(&self) -> f64 {
        if self.proposed == 0 {
            0.0
        } else {
            self.accepted as f64 / self.proposed as f64
        }
    }

    /// Round-emitted tokens per round; zero before the first round.
    pub fn tokens_per_round(&self) -> f64 {
        if self.rounds == 0 {
            0.0
        } else {
            self.tokens_emitted as f64 / self.rounds as f64
        }
    }
}

/// What one round did (SPEC-itak-spec Section 6.2).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RoundOutcome {
    /// Tokens this round emitted (stop-truncated when `stopped`).
    pub emitted: Vec<u32>,
    /// Draft tokens proposed this round.
    pub proposed: usize,
    /// Draft tokens accepted this round.
    pub accepted: usize,
    /// 1-based index of the first rejected draft token, if any.
    pub first_rejection: Option<usize>,
    /// Target cache position after the round's commit.
    pub cache_position: usize,
    /// Whether a stop token ended the session in this round.
    pub stopped: bool,
}

/// The draft source attached to a session: the seam that admits a
/// second proposer next to the DFlash speculator. The round loop
/// drives either source through this one dispatch shape (the
/// inherent `propose_block` both types carry, plus the
/// [`Speculator`] trait's commit and capture calls), so the loop
/// itself never learns which drafter it runs. Private on purpose:
/// construction goes through `SpecSession::new` (DFlash) and
/// `SpecSession::new_ngram` (n-gram), which each validate their
/// own pairing of mode and source.
enum DraftSource {
    /// The DFlash block drafter (a separate draft model).
    Dflash(DflashSpeculator),
    /// The n-gram prompt-lookup proposer (no model; see
    /// [`crate::ngram`]).
    Ngram(NgramProposer),
}

impl DraftSource {
    /// Maximum draft tokens one block can propose.
    fn max_depth(&self) -> usize {
        match self {
            DraftSource::Dflash(spec) => spec.max_depth(),
            DraftSource::Ngram(prop) => prop.max_depth(),
        }
    }

    /// Propose up to `n` tokens after `pending` (see
    /// `DflashSpeculator::propose_block` for the row contract).
    fn propose_block(
        &mut self,
        pending: u32,
        n: usize,
        arm: DraftArm,
        rng: &mut dyn FnMut() -> f64,
    ) -> Result<Proposal> {
        match self {
            DraftSource::Dflash(spec) => spec.propose_block(pending, n, arm, rng),
            DraftSource::Ngram(prop) => prop.propose_block(pending, n, arm, rng),
        }
    }

    /// Hand the source the target rows a forward captured. The
    /// n-gram source keeps the trait default (captures ignored):
    /// it conditions on tokens only.
    fn note_captures(
        &mut self,
        base_position: usize,
        captures: &[LayerInputCapture],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        match self {
            DraftSource::Dflash(spec) => spec.note_captures(base_position, captures),
            DraftSource::Ngram(prop) => prop.note_captures(base_position, captures),
        }
    }

    /// Tell the source exactly the newly committed tokens.
    fn commit(&mut self, tokens: &[u32]) -> Result<()> {
        match self {
            DraftSource::Dflash(spec) => spec.commit(tokens),
            DraftSource::Ngram(prop) => prop.commit(tokens),
        }
    }
}

/// A speculative decoding session over one target model, driven
/// through the [`TargetDriver`] seam. The default driver is the
/// CPU target path ([`CpuTarget`]).
pub struct SpecSession<D: TargetDriver = CpuTarget> {
    driver: D,
    speculator: Option<DraftSource>,
    capture_layers: Vec<usize>,
    config: SpecConfig,
    diag: Arc<dyn Diag>,
    rng: Rng,
    pending: u32,
    begun: bool,
    ended: bool,
    poisoned: Option<String>,
    latched_off: bool,
    stats: SpecStats,
}

impl<D: TargetDriver> SpecSession<D> {
    /// Create a session, validating everything up front (SPEC-itak-spec
    /// Section 6.1): mode availability, draft presence and agreement with
    /// the target, depth against the draft block and the round bound, and
    /// the grammar conflict. Any refusal emits `spec.refused` and returns
    /// the named error; a session that exists is a session whose rounds
    /// can run.
    ///
    /// `driver` is the target behind the [`TargetDriver`] seam: for
    /// the CPU path, a [`CpuTarget`] wrapping the model and the
    /// compute it forwards through (see [`crate::SharedCompute`]).
    pub fn new(
        driver: D,
        draft: Option<DflashSpeculator>,
        config: SpecConfig,
        diag: Arc<dyn Diag>,
    ) -> Result<Self> {
        Self::new_inner(driver, draft.map(DraftSource::Dflash), config, diag)
    }

    /// Create a session drafting with the n-gram prompt-lookup
    /// proposer instead of a draft model (SPEC-itak-spec Section
    /// 6.2, mode `ngram`): the no-training self-drafting arm. Same
    /// validation discipline as [`Self::new`]: the proposer must be
    /// present and agree with the target's vocabulary, and depth
    /// must fit the proposer's maximum proposals and the round
    /// bound. There are no capture layers: the proposer conditions
    /// on tokens only. The DFlash constructor keeps refusing mode
    /// `ngram` with `ModeUnavailable`; the proposer is attached
    /// here, not there.
    pub fn new_ngram(
        driver: D,
        draft: Option<NgramProposer>,
        config: SpecConfig,
        diag: Arc<dyn Diag>,
    ) -> Result<Self> {
        Self::new_inner(driver, draft.map(DraftSource::Ngram), config, diag)
    }

    /// Shared creation: validate the mode against the attached
    /// draft source, then the source's geometry against the
    /// target. Mode `off` needs no source and validates nothing
    /// about one.
    fn new_inner(
        driver: D,
        draft: Option<DraftSource>,
        config: SpecConfig,
        diag: Arc<dyn Diag>,
    ) -> Result<Self> {
        let refuse = |err: SpecError| -> SpecError {
            diag.event("spec.refused", &format!("error={err}"));
            err
        };
        if config.grammar_active {
            return Err(refuse(SpecError::GrammarConflict));
        }
        if config.mode == SpecMode::Medusa {
            return Err(refuse(SpecError::ModeUnavailable {
                mode: config.mode.name(),
            }));
        }
        let mut capture_layers: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
        if config.mode == SpecMode::Ngram {
            match &draft {
                Some(DraftSource::Ngram(prop)) => {
                    let tcfg = driver.config();
                    if prop.vocab_size() != tcfg.vocab_size as usize {
                        return Err(refuse(SpecError::DraftTargetMismatch {
                            field: "vocab_size",
                            expected: tcfg.vocab_size as usize,
                            actual: prop.vocab_size(),
                        }));
                    }
                    if config.depth == 0 || config.depth > prop.max_depth() {
                        return Err(refuse(SpecError::DepthOutOfRange {
                            n_max: config.depth,
                            block_size: prop.max_depth() + 1,
                        }));
                    }
                    if config.depth + 1 > config.max_round_tokens {
                        return Err(refuse(SpecError::RoundBoundTooSmall {
                            depth: config.depth,
                            max_round_tokens: config.max_round_tokens,
                        }));
                    }
                }
                // The n-gram machinery is attached through
                // new_ngram only; a DFlash speculator under mode
                // ngram means the mode is not available on this
                // session, the constructor's historical refusal.
                Some(DraftSource::Dflash(_)) => {
                    return Err(refuse(SpecError::ModeUnavailable {
                        mode: config.mode.name(),
                    }));
                }
                None => return Err(refuse(SpecError::DraftNotLoaded)),
            }
        }
        if config.mode == SpecMode::Dflash {
            let spec = match &draft {
                Some(DraftSource::Dflash(spec)) => spec,
                Some(DraftSource::Ngram(_)) => {
                    return Err(refuse(SpecError::SessionState {
                        detail: "mode dflash needs a DFlash speculator; the attached draft \
                                 source is an n-gram proposer (build the session through \
                                 new_ngram with mode ngram)"
                            .to_string(),
                    }));
                }
                None => return Err(refuse(SpecError::DraftNotLoaded)),
            };
            let dcfg = spec.config();
            let tcfg = driver.config();
            if dcfg.vocab_size != tcfg.vocab_size {
                return Err(refuse(SpecError::DraftTargetMismatch {
                    field: "vocab_size",
                    expected: tcfg.vocab_size as usize,
                    actual: dcfg.vocab_size as usize,
                }));
            }
            if dcfg.target_layers.is_empty() {
                return Err(refuse(SpecError::DraftTargetMismatch {
                    field: "target_layers",
                    expected: 1,
                    actual: 0,
                }));
            }
            for &layer in &dcfg.target_layers {
                if layer as usize >= tcfg.block_count as usize {
                    return Err(refuse(SpecError::DraftTargetMismatch {
                        field: "target_layer",
                        expected: tcfg.block_count as usize,
                        actual: layer as usize,
                    }));
                }
                capture_layers.push(layer as usize);
            }
            if config.depth == 0 || config.depth > spec.max_depth() {
                return Err(refuse(SpecError::DepthOutOfRange {
                    n_max: config.depth,
                    block_size: dcfg.block_size as usize,
                }));
            }
            if config.depth + 1 > config.max_round_tokens {
                return Err(refuse(SpecError::RoundBoundTooSmall {
                    depth: config.depth,
                    max_round_tokens: config.max_round_tokens,
                }));
            }
        }
        let rng = Rng::new(config.seed);
        let session = SpecSession {
            driver,
            speculator: draft,
            capture_layers,
            config,
            diag,
            rng,
            pending: 0,
            begun: false,
            ended: false,
            poisoned: None,
            latched_off: false,
            stats: SpecStats::default(),
        };
        if session.config.mode == SpecMode::Off {
            session.diag.event(
                "spec.disabled",
                "mode=off plain generation, no draft attached",
            );
            session
                .diag
                .event("spec.session.begin", "mode=off depth=0 draft=none");
        } else {
            session.diag.event(
                "spec.session.begin",
                &format!(
                    "mode={} depth={} max_round_tokens={} temperature={}",
                    session.config.mode.name(),
                    session.config.depth,
                    session.config.max_round_tokens,
                    session.config.temperature
                ),
            );
        }
        Ok(session)
    }

    /// The configuration this session was created with.
    pub fn config(&self) -> &SpecConfig {
        &self.config
    }

    /// The target driver behind the seam (a resident driver's
    /// session counters are the serving numbers a bench reads).
    pub fn driver(&self) -> &D {
        &self.driver
    }

    /// The target driver behind the seam, mutably.
    pub fn driver_mut(&mut self) -> &mut D {
        &mut self.driver
    }

    /// Cumulative statistics so far.
    pub fn stats(&self) -> SpecStats {
        self.stats
    }

    /// The `spec_stats()` readout: the same statistics [`Self::stats`]
    /// returns, named as the spec names it for the engine to expose later.
    pub fn spec_stats(&self) -> SpecStats {
        self.stats
    }

    /// Whether speculation has latched off after a verify refusal.
    pub fn is_latched(&self) -> bool {
        self.latched_off
    }

    /// The last emitted token, not yet forwarded (valid after `begin`).
    pub fn pending(&self) -> u32 {
        self.pending
    }

    /// The target cache's committed position.
    pub fn cache_position(&self) -> usize {
        self.driver.position()
    }

    /// Prefill the prompt and draw the first token. Returns the pending
    /// token: the first element of the generated stream. The prompt's
    /// captured layer inputs are injected into the draft here, so the
    /// draft starts the first round conditioned on exactly the prompt.
    pub fn begin(&mut self, prompt: &[u32]) -> Result<u32> {
        if self.begun {
            return Err(SpecError::SessionState {
                detail: "begin called twice".to_string(),
            });
        }
        let logits = match self.speculator.as_mut() {
            Some(DraftSource::Dflash(spec)) if self.config.mode == SpecMode::Dflash => {
                let (logits, captures) = self
                    .driver
                    .forward_capturing(prompt, &self.capture_layers)
                    .map_err(|e| SpecError::TargetRefused {
                        source: Box::new(e),
                    })?;
                spec.note_captures(0, &captures)?;
                spec.commit(prompt)?;
                logits
            }
            Some(DraftSource::Ngram(prop)) if self.config.mode == SpecMode::Ngram => {
                // No captures exist to stage: the proposer
                // conditions on tokens only, so begin is a plain
                // prefill plus the prompt commit that seeds its
                // lookup history with exactly the prompt.
                let logits = self
                    .driver
                    .forward(prompt)
                    .map_err(|e| SpecError::TargetRefused {
                        source: Box::new(e),
                    })?;
                prop.commit(prompt)?;
                logits
            }
            _ => self
                .driver
                .forward(prompt)
                .map_err(|e| SpecError::TargetRefused {
                    source: Box::new(e),
                })?,
        };
        self.pending = self.draw(&logits)?;
        self.begun = true;
        Ok(self.pending)
    }

    /// Run one round against the configured stop set.
    pub fn round(&mut self) -> Result<RoundOutcome> {
        let stops: HashSet<u32> = self.config.eos_tokens.iter().copied().collect();
        self.round_internal(None, &stops)
    }

    /// Generate up to `max_new_tokens` tokens, stopping early at any stop
    /// token (the config's `eos_tokens` plus `extra_stops`). The returned
    /// stream starts with the pending token from `begin`; its length is
    /// exactly `max_new_tokens` unless a stop token ended the session.
    /// Round sizes are budget-capped so the stream never overshoots.
    pub fn generate(&mut self, max_new_tokens: usize, extra_stops: &[u32]) -> Result<Vec<u32>> {
        if !self.begun {
            return Err(SpecError::SessionState {
                detail: "generate called before begin".to_string(),
            });
        }
        if max_new_tokens == 0 {
            return Ok(Vec::new());
        }
        let mut stops: HashSet<u32> = self.config.eos_tokens.iter().copied().collect();
        stops.extend(extra_stops.iter().copied());
        let mut stream = vec![self.pending];
        if stops.contains(&self.pending) {
            self.ended = true;
            return Ok(stream);
        }
        while stream.len() < max_new_tokens && !self.ended {
            let cap = max_new_tokens - stream.len() - 1;
            let outcome = self.round_internal(Some(cap), &stops)?;
            stream.extend_from_slice(&outcome.emitted);
        }
        Ok(stream)
    }

    /// End the session, emitting `spec.session.end`, and return the final
    /// statistics.
    pub fn finish(self) -> SpecStats {
        self.diag.event(
            "spec.session.end",
            &format!(
                "rounds={} proposed={} accepted={} acceptance_rate={:.4} tokens_emitted={} fallback_latched={}",
                self.stats.rounds,
                self.stats.proposed,
                self.stats.accepted,
                self.stats.acceptance_rate(),
                self.stats.tokens_emitted,
                self.stats.fallback_latched
            ),
        );
        self.stats
    }

    /// Draw one token from a finished target logit row under the session's
    /// sampling configuration.
    fn draw(&mut self, logits: &[f32]) -> Result<u32> {
        if self.config.temperature <= 0.0 {
            Ok(sampler::argmax(logits))
        } else {
            let dist = sampler::distribution(logits, self.config.temperature, self.config.top_p)?;
            Ok(sampler::sample_from(&dist, self.rng.next_f64()))
        }
    }

    fn round_internal(&mut self, cap: Option<usize>, stops: &HashSet<u32>) -> Result<RoundOutcome> {
        if !self.begun {
            return Err(SpecError::SessionState {
                detail: "round called before begin".to_string(),
            });
        }
        if self.ended {
            return Err(SpecError::SessionState {
                detail: "round called after a stop token ended the session".to_string(),
            });
        }
        if let Some(detail) = &self.poisoned {
            return Err(SpecError::SessionState {
                detail: format!("session is poisoned by an earlier failure: {detail}"),
            });
        }
        self.stats.rounds += 1;
        let round_no = self.stats.rounds;
        let base = self.driver.position();
        self.diag.event(
            "spec.round.begin",
            &format!("round={round_no} base={base} pending={}", self.pending),
        );
        if self.config.mode == SpecMode::Off || self.latched_off || self.speculator.is_none() {
            return self.plain_step(round_no, base, 0, stops);
        }
        self.speculative_round(round_no, base, cap, stops)
    }

    /// One plain step: forward the pending token, draw the next. Used for
    /// mode-off sessions and as the latched fallback's round completion.
    /// The draft is never touched here: mode-off sessions have no live
    /// draft, and a latched session has abandoned its draft for good.
    fn plain_step(
        &mut self,
        round_no: usize,
        base: usize,
        proposed_count: usize,
        stops: &HashSet<u32>,
    ) -> Result<RoundOutcome> {
        let pending = self.pending;
        let logits = self
            .driver
            .forward(&[pending])
            .map_err(|e| SpecError::TargetRefused {
                source: Box::new(e),
            })?;
        let token = self.draw(&logits)?;
        self.pending = token;
        let emitted = vec![token];
        let mut stopped = false;
        if stops.contains(&token) {
            stopped = true;
            self.ended = true;
        }
        self.stats.proposed += proposed_count;
        self.stats.tokens_emitted += emitted.len();
        self.diag.event(
            "spec.cache.commit",
            &format!("round={round_no} position={}", base + 1),
        );
        self.diag.event(
            "spec.round.accept",
            &format!(
                "round={round_no} proposed={proposed_count} accepted=0 first_rejection=none emitted={} plain=true",
                emitted.len()
            ),
        );
        Ok(RoundOutcome {
            emitted,
            proposed: proposed_count,
            accepted: 0,
            first_rejection: None,
            cache_position: base + 1,
            stopped,
        })
    }

    /// Roll the target cache back to `to` and release the checkpoint.
    /// Any failure here poisons the session: cache state is no longer
    /// provably the committed prefix.
    fn rewind_and_release(&mut self, checkpoint: &D::Checkpoint, to: usize) -> Result<()> {
        if let Err(e) = self.driver.rewind(checkpoint, to) {
            let err = cache_refused("rewind", e);
            self.poisoned = Some(err.to_string());
            return Err(err);
        }
        if let Err(e) = self.driver.release(checkpoint) {
            let err = cache_refused("release", e);
            self.poisoned = Some(err.to_string());
            return Err(err);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn speculative_round(
        &mut self,
        round_no: usize,
        base: usize,
        cap: Option<usize>,
        stops: &HashSet<u32>,
    ) -> Result<RoundOutcome> {
        let pending = self.pending;
        let greedy = self.config.temperature <= 0.0;
        let mut n = self.config.depth.min(
            self.speculator
                .as_ref()
                .expect("speculative round requires a draft")
                .max_depth(),
        );
        if let Some(cap) = cap {
            n = n.min(cap);
        }

        // Step 2: propose. The draft conditions on everything committed so
        // far; its cache already holds exactly that prefix.
        let arm = if greedy {
            DraftArm::Greedy
        } else {
            DraftArm::Sampled {
                temperature: self
                    .config
                    .draft_temperature
                    .unwrap_or(self.config.temperature),
            }
        };
        let t0 = Instant::now();
        let proposal = {
            // Disjoint field borrows: the draft handle and the generator
            // are separate fields, so the draw closure can borrow the
            // generator while the speculator is borrowed too.
            let spec = self.speculator.as_mut().expect("checked above");
            let mut draw = || self.rng.next_f64();
            spec.propose_block(pending, n, arm, &mut draw)?
        };
        let draft_ms = t0.elapsed().as_millis();
        let n = proposal.tokens.len();
        self.diag.event(
            "spec.propose.end",
            &format!("round={round_no} proposed={n} draft_ms={draft_ms}"),
        );

        // Step 3: checkpoint, then one block forward over
        // [pending, drafts...] with the conditioning layers captured.
        let checkpoint = self
            .driver
            .checkpoint(n + 1)
            .map_err(|e| cache_refused("checkpoint", e))?;
        let mut verify_tokens = Vec::with_capacity(n + 1);
        verify_tokens.push(pending);
        verify_tokens.extend_from_slice(&proposal.tokens);
        let t0 = Instant::now();
        let verified = self
            .driver
            .forward_block_capturing(&verify_tokens, &self.capture_layers);
        let verify_ms = t0.elapsed().as_millis();
        let (logits, captures) = match verified {
            Ok(pair) => pair,
            Err(e) => {
                // Step 8: roll back before anything else observes the
                // half-forwarded block, then apply the error policy.
                self.rewind_and_release(&checkpoint, base)?;
                self.stats.rollbacks += 1;
                self.diag.event(
                    "spec.cache.rewind",
                    &format!("round={round_no} from={base} to={base} reason=verify_refused"),
                );
                return match self.config.on_verify_error {
                    OnVerifyError::Refuse => {
                        let err = SpecError::VerifyRefused {
                            source: Box::new(e),
                        };
                        self.diag
                            .event("spec.refused", &format!("round={round_no} error={err}"));
                        Err(err)
                    }
                    OnVerifyError::LatchOff => {
                        self.latched_off = true;
                        self.stats.fallback_latched = true;
                        self.diag.event(
                            "spec.fallback.latched",
                            &format!("round={round_no} reason={e}"),
                        );
                        self.plain_step(round_no, base, n, stops)
                    }
                };
            }
        };
        self.diag.event(
            "spec.verify.end",
            &format!("round={round_no} verify_ms={verify_ms}"),
        );

        // Stage the fresh captures for the commit. If staging refuses,
        // the round cannot commit honestly: roll the target back too.
        if let Err(e) = self
            .speculator
            .as_mut()
            .expect("checked above")
            .note_captures(base, &captures)
        {
            self.rewind_and_release(&checkpoint, base)?;
            return Err(e);
        }

        // Step 4: the correction walk over finished distributions.
        let vocab = self.driver.config().vocab_size as usize;
        let walk = if greedy {
            let p_argmax: Vec<u32> = logits.chunks_exact(vocab).map(sampler::argmax).collect();
            sampler::correct_greedy(&p_argmax, &proposal.tokens)?
        } else {
            let p_rows: Vec<Vec<f32>> = logits
                .chunks_exact(vocab)
                .map(|row| sampler::distribution(row, self.config.temperature, self.config.top_p))
                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
            let p_refs: Vec<&[f32]> = p_rows.iter().map(Vec::as_slice).collect();
            let q_refs: Vec<&[f32]> = proposal.dists.iter().map(Vec::as_slice).collect();
            let mut rng = || self.rng.next_f64();
            sampler::correct_sampled(&p_refs, &q_refs, &proposal.tokens, &mut rng)?
        };
        let accepted = walk.accepted;
        let keep = base + 1 + accepted;

        // Step 5: commit. Rewind both position views to the committed
        // count, release the checkpoint, then tell the draft exactly the
        // newly committed tokens.
        self.rewind_and_release(&checkpoint, keep)?;
        self.diag.event(
            "spec.cache.rewind",
            &format!("round={round_no} from={} to={keep}", base + n + 1),
        );
        self.diag.event(
            "spec.cache.commit",
            &format!("round={round_no} position={keep}"),
        );
        if self.driver.position() != keep {
            let err = SpecError::CacheOutOfSync {
                expected: keep,
                actual: self.driver.position(),
            };
            self.poisoned = Some(err.to_string());
            self.diag
                .event("spec.refused", &format!("round={round_no} error={err}"));
            return Err(err);
        }
        if keep < base + n + 1 {
            self.stats.rollbacks += 1;
        }
        let committed = &verify_tokens[..1 + accepted];
        if let Err(e) = self
            .speculator
            .as_mut()
            .expect("checked above")
            .commit(committed)
        {
            self.poisoned = Some(e.to_string());
            return Err(e);
        }

        // Emission, with stop truncation (Section 4, step 6).
        let mut emitted: Vec<u32> = Vec::with_capacity(accepted + 1);
        emitted.extend_from_slice(&proposal.tokens[..accepted]);
        emitted.push(walk.token);
        let mut stopped = false;
        for (i, token) in emitted.iter().enumerate() {
            if stops.contains(token) {
                emitted.truncate(i + 1);
                stopped = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if stopped {
            self.ended = true;
        }
        self.pending = walk.token;
        self.stats.proposed += n;
        self.stats.accepted += accepted;
        if walk.first_rejection.is_some() {
            self.stats.rejections += 1;
        }
        self.stats.tokens_emitted += emitted.len();
        self.diag.event(
            "spec.round.accept",
            &format!(
                "round={round_no} proposed={n} accepted={accepted} first_rejection={} emitted={}",
                walk.first_rejection
                    .map(|j| j.to_string())
                    .unwrap_or_else(|| "none".to_string()),
                emitted.len()
            ),
        );
        // Capture wiring, record only: hand the completed
        // round's real proposed ids and accepted count to
        // the driver's record seam, here where both are
        // still in hand (RoundOutcome below carries counts
        // only). The resident driver forwards them to its
        // session's capture accumulator; every other driver
        // records nothing. Placed after the commit, so a
        // round that fails anywhere above is never recorded
        // as completed, and the call itself feeds nothing
        // back into sampling, acceptance, or control flow.
        self.driver.note_spec_round(&proposal.tokens, accepted);
        Ok(RoundOutcome {
            emitted,
            proposed: n,
            accepted,
            first_rejection: walk.first_rejection,
            cache_position: keep,
            stopped,
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use std::rc::Rc;
    use std::sync::Arc;

    use cpu_compute::CpuCompute;

    use super::*;
    use crate::config::SpecMode;
    use crate::diag::NullDiag;
    use crate::speculator::SharedCompute;
    use crate::testkit;

    const PROMPT_A: &[u32] = &[3, 17, 42];
    const PROMPT_B: &[u32] = &[100, 5, 5, 9, 71];
    const PROMPT_C: &[u32] = &[7];

    fn greedy_config(depth: usize) -> SpecConfig {
        SpecConfig {
            depth,
            ..SpecConfig::default()
        }
    }

    /// THE proof obligation (SPEC-itak-spec Sections 4 and 9, TODO
    /// T-3.6): at temperature 0 the speculative stream equals the plain
    /// greedy stream token for token, at several depths and prompts.
    #[test]
    fn greedy_speculation_matches_plain_generation() {
        for (block_size, depths) in [(5u32, &[1usize, 2, 4][..]), (8, &[6][..])] {
            for &depth in depths {
                for prompt in [PROMPT_A, PROMPT_B, PROMPT_C] {
                    let mut session = testkit::build_session(greedy_config(depth), block_size);
                    let pending = session.begin(prompt).expect("begin");
                    let stream = session.generate(24, &[]).expect("generate");
                    let plain = testkit::plain_greedy(prompt, 24);
                    assert_eq!(pending, plain[0], "pending is the first plain token");
                    assert_eq!(
                        stream, plain,
                        "depth {depth} prompt {prompt:?}: speculative stream diverged"
                    );
                    let stats = session.spec_stats();
                    assert_eq!(stats, session.stats());
                    assert!(stats.proposed > 0, "draft must propose");
                    assert!(stats.accepted <= stats.proposed);
                    assert_eq!(stats.tokens_emitted, 23);
                    assert!((0.0..=1.0).contains(&stats.acceptance_rate()));
                    assert_eq!(session.cache_position(), prompt.len() + 23);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// The depth knob observably changes behavior: same output, more
    /// proposals per round at the larger depth.
    #[test]
    fn depth_knob_changes_proposal_volume_not_output() {
        let run = |depth: usize| {
            let mut session = testkit::build_session(greedy_config(depth), 5);
            session.begin(PROMPT_A).expect("begin");
            let stream = session.generate(24, &[]).expect("generate");
            (stream, session.stats())
        };
        let (stream_1, stats_1) = run(1);
        let (stream_4, stats_4) = run(4);
        assert_eq!(stream_1, stream_4);
        assert!(
            stats_4.proposed > stats_1.proposed,
            "depth 4 proposed {} vs depth 1 proposed {}",
            stats_4.proposed,
            stats_1.proposed
        );
    }

    /// A stop token truncates the stream at itself, inclusive, and ends
    /// the session (Section 4, step 6).
    #[test]
    fn stop_token_truncates_the_stream() {
        let plain = testkit::plain_greedy(PROMPT_A, 24);
        let mut config = greedy_config(2);
        config.eos_tokens = vec![plain[2]];
        let mut session = testkit::build_session(config, 5);
        session.begin(PROMPT_A).expect("begin");
        let stream = session.generate(24, &[]).expect("generate");
        assert_eq!(stream, plain[..3].to_vec());
        assert!(matches!(
            session.round(),
            Err(SpecError::SessionState { .. })
        ));
    }

    /// Temperature sampling runs the full correction walk and is
    /// reproducible under a fixed seed (the seed knob's behavior test).
    #[test]
    fn sampled_generation_is_reproducible_per_seed() {
        let run = |seed: u64| {
            let config = SpecConfig {
                depth: 3,
                temperature: 0.7,
                seed,
                ..SpecConfig::default()
            };
            let mut session = testkit::build_session(config, 5);
            session.begin(PROMPT_B).expect("begin");
            let stream = session.generate(24, &[]).expect("generate");
            (stream, session.stats())
        };
        let (stream_a, stats_a) = run(1234);
        let (stream_b, _) = run(1234);
        assert_eq!(stream_a, stream_b, "same seed, same stream");
        assert_eq!(stream_a.len(), 24);
        assert!(stream_a.iter().all(|&t| (t as usize) < testkit::VOCAB));
        assert!(stats_a.proposed > 0);
        let (stream_c, _) = run(99);
        assert_ne!(stream_a, stream_c, "different seed, different stream");
    }

    /// With the refuse policy, a one-shot verify failure surfaces as
    /// VerifyRefused with cache and pending untouched, and the session
    /// then completes with the identical stream.
    #[test]
    fn verify_refusal_surfaces_and_the_session_recovers() {
        let config = greedy_config(2);
        let (mut session, armed) = testkit::build_sabotage_session(config);
        let pending = session.begin(PROMPT_A).expect("begin");
        armed.set(true);
        let err = session.round().expect_err("round must refuse");
        assert!(matches!(err, SpecError::VerifyRefused { .. }), "got {err}");
        assert_eq!(session.cache_position(), PROMPT_A.len());
        assert_eq!(session.pending(), pending);
        assert_eq!(session.stats().rollbacks, 1);
        let stream = session.generate(16, &[]).expect("generate after refusal");
        assert_eq!(stream, testkit::plain_greedy(PROMPT_A, 16));
    }

    /// With the latch policy, the same failure latches speculation off
    /// (visibly, in the stats) and the round still emits the correct
    /// plain token; the rest of the stream stays identical.
    #[test]
    fn verify_refusal_latches_off_when_configured() {
        let mut config = greedy_config(2);
        config.on_verify_error = OnVerifyError::LatchOff;
        let (mut session, armed) = testkit::build_sabotage_session(config);
        session.begin(PROMPT_A).expect("begin");
        armed.set(true);
        let outcome = session.round().expect("latched round completes plainly");
        let plain = testkit::plain_greedy(PROMPT_A, 16);
        assert!(session.is_latched());
        assert!(session.stats().fallback_latched);
        assert_eq!(outcome.emitted, vec![plain[1]]);
        assert_eq!(outcome.proposed, 2, "the discarded proposal is counted");
        let rest = session.generate(15, &[]).expect("generate after latch");
        assert_eq!(rest, plain[1..16].to_vec());
        assert_eq!(session.stats().proposed, 2, "no proposals after the latch");
    }

    /// Mode off generates plainly through the same session accounting.
    #[test]
    fn mode_off_generates_plainly() {
        let compute = Rc::new(CpuCompute::new());
        let fixture = testkit::build_target(Box::new(SharedCompute(compute.clone())));
        let config = SpecConfig {
            mode: SpecMode::Off,
            ..SpecConfig::default()
        };
        let mut session = SpecSession::new(
            CpuTarget::new(fixture.model, compute),
            None,
            config,
            Arc::new(NullDiag),
        )
        .expect("mode-off session builds");
        session.begin(PROMPT_A).expect("begin");
        let stream = session.generate(16, &[]).expect("generate");
        assert_eq!(stream, testkit::plain_greedy(PROMPT_A, 16));
        assert_eq!(session.stats().proposed, 0);
    }

    fn try_new(config: SpecConfig, draft: Option<DflashSpeculator>) -> Result<SpecSession> {
        let compute = Rc::new(CpuCompute::new());
        let fixture = testkit::build_target(Box::new(SharedCompute(compute.clone())));
        SpecSession::new(
            CpuTarget::new(fixture.model, compute),
            draft,
            config,
            Arc::new(NullDiag),
        )
    }

    fn fixture_draft(block_size: u32) -> DflashSpeculator {
        let compute = Rc::new(CpuCompute::new());
        let fixture = testkit::build_target(Box::new(SharedCompute(compute)));
        testkit::build_speculator(&fixture, block_size)
    }

    /// Creation validates everything up front and refuses by name
    /// (Section 6.1): one test per refusal in the table this crate can
    /// produce.
    #[test]
    fn creation_refusals_are_named() {
        // DraftNotLoaded.
        let err = try_new(SpecConfig::default(), None)
            .err()
            .expect("no draft");
        assert!(matches!(err, SpecError::DraftNotLoaded), "got {err}");
        // ModeUnavailable.
        let config = SpecConfig {
            mode: SpecMode::Ngram,
            ..SpecConfig::default()
        };
        let err = try_new(config, Some(fixture_draft(5)))
            .err()
            .expect("ngram");
        assert!(
            matches!(err, SpecError::ModeUnavailable { .. }),
            "got {err}"
        );
        // GrammarConflict.
        let config = SpecConfig {
            grammar_active: true,
            ..SpecConfig::default()
        };
        let err = try_new(config, Some(fixture_draft(5)))
            .err()
            .expect("grammar");
        assert!(matches!(err, SpecError::GrammarConflict), "got {err}");
        // DepthOutOfRange: zero, and beyond the block's draft count.
        let config = SpecConfig {
            depth: 0,
            ..SpecConfig::default()
        };
        let err = try_new(config, Some(fixture_draft(5)))
            .err()
            .expect("depth 0");
        assert!(
            matches!(err, SpecError::DepthOutOfRange { .. }),
            "got {err}"
        );
        // Block 5 proposes at most 4, so depth 5 is out of range.
        let config = SpecConfig {
            depth: 5,
            ..SpecConfig::default()
        };
        let err = try_new(config, Some(fixture_draft(5)))
            .err()
            .expect("depth 5 of block 5");
        assert!(
            matches!(err, SpecError::DepthOutOfRange { .. }),
            "got {err}"
        );
        // RoundBoundTooSmall: depth 4 needs a bound of at least 5.
        let config = SpecConfig {
            depth: 4,
            max_round_tokens: 4,
            ..SpecConfig::default()
        };
        let err = try_new(config, Some(fixture_draft(5)))
            .err()
            .expect("bound");
        assert!(
            matches!(err, SpecError::RoundBoundTooSmall { .. }),
            "got {err}"
        );
    }

    /// Call-order discipline: rounds need a begin, and begin runs once.
    #[test]
    fn call_order_is_enforced() {
        let mut session = testkit::build_session(greedy_config(2), 5);
        assert!(matches!(
            session.round(),
            Err(SpecError::SessionState { .. })
        ));
        session.begin(PROMPT_A).expect("begin");
        assert!(matches!(
            session.begin(PROMPT_A),
            Err(SpecError::SessionState { .. })
        ));
    }
}
