//! Speculators: the drafting side of the loop (SPEC-itak-spec Section
//! 6.2), plus the shared compute handle a session needs to reach the
//! target's KV checkpoint machinery.
//!
//! The [`Speculator`] trait is the seam every drafting mode plugs into.
//! Its shape is fixed; the concrete DFlash implementation adds one
//! inherent method, [`DflashSpeculator::propose_block`], which returns the
//! owned per-position distributions the sampled correction walk needs
//! (the trait's borrowed view carries greedy material only, matching the
//! spec's contract).

use std::rc::Rc;

use cpu_compute::{Checkpoint, CpuCompute};
use dflash::{DflashCache, DflashConfig, DflashModel, TargetTensors, TensorData};
use muse_glimmer::{
    AttentionRequest, Cache, Compute, GlimmerConfig, GlimmerError, LayerInputCapture, LayerWeights,
    Result as GlimmerResult, TensorView,
};
use wgpu_compute::DflashSession;

use crate::error::{Result, SpecError};
use crate::sampler;

/// A compute handle shared between a [`muse_glimmer::GlimmerModel`] and its session.
///
/// The target model owns its compute privately, but the loop must call
/// `cache_checkpoint` / `cache_rewind` / `cache_release` on the same
/// [`CpuCompute`] the model forwards through. This wrapper is the bridge:
/// build one `Rc<CpuCompute>`, hand a `SharedCompute` clone to the model
/// as its `Box<dyn Compute>`, and keep the `Rc` for the session.
pub struct SharedCompute(pub Rc<CpuCompute>);

impl Compute for SharedCompute {
    fn embed(
        &self,
        table: &TensorView,
        tokens: &[u32],
        cfg: &GlimmerConfig,
    ) -> GlimmerResult<Vec<f32>> {
        self.0.embed(table, tokens, cfg)
    }
    fn rms_norm(
        &self,
        x: &[f32],
        weight: &TensorView,
        rows: usize,
        eps: f32,
    ) -> GlimmerResult<Vec<f32>> {
        self.0.rms_norm(x, weight, rows, eps)
    }
    fn rms_norm_plain(&self, x: &[f32], rows: usize, eps: f32) -> GlimmerResult<Vec<f32>> {
        self.0.rms_norm_plain(x, rows, eps)
    }
    fn proj(&self, x: &[f32], weight: &TensorView, rows: usize) -> GlimmerResult<Vec<f32>> {
        self.0.proj(x, weight, rows)
    }
    fn attention(&self, req: &AttentionRequest, cache: &mut dyn Cache) -> GlimmerResult<Vec<f32>> {
        self.0.attention(req, cache)
    }
    fn attn_gate(&self, attn_out: &[f32], gate: &[f32]) -> GlimmerResult<Vec<f32>> {
        self.0.attn_gate(attn_out, gate)
    }
    fn add(&self, a: &[f32], b: &[f32]) -> GlimmerResult<Vec<f32>> {
        self.0.add(a, b)
    }
    fn swiglu_ffn(
        &self,
        x: &[f32],
        w: &LayerWeights,
        rows: usize,
        cfg: &GlimmerConfig,
    ) -> GlimmerResult<Vec<f32>> {
        self.0.swiglu_ffn(x, w, rows, cfg)
    }
    fn lm_head(
        &self,
        x: &[f32],
        head: &TensorView,
        cfg: &GlimmerConfig,
    ) -> GlimmerResult<Vec<f32>> {
        self.0.lm_head(x, head, cfg)
    }
}

/// Re-exported so session code names the checkpoint type through one path.
pub type TargetCheckpoint = Checkpoint;

/// One proposal distribution, borrowed from the speculator's buffers.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct DraftDist<'a> {
    /// Probabilities over the vocabulary for one draft position.
    pub probs: &'a [f32],
}

/// A block of draft tokens with their distributions, borrowed from the
/// speculator's last proposal.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct BlockProposal<'a> {
    /// The proposed tokens, in order (`t[1..=n]` in spec indexing).
    pub tokens: &'a [u32],
    /// One distribution per proposed token, aligned with `tokens`. The
    /// vector itself is owned because the borrowed rows live in the
    /// speculator's probability buffer; the spec fixes this shape (tokens
    /// plus per-token distributions), not the container spelling.
    pub dists: Vec<DraftDist<'a>>,
}

/// The drafting seam (SPEC-itak-spec Section 6.2). Implementations own
/// their draft model and cache; the session owns the target and the round
/// structure.
pub trait Speculator {
    /// The drafting mode this speculator implements.
    fn mode(&self) -> crate::SpecMode;

    /// Maximum draft tokens one block can propose.
    fn max_depth(&self) -> usize;

    /// Propose up to `n` tokens after `pending`, the last emitted token.
    /// The result borrows the speculator's internal buffers and is valid
    /// until the next `propose` or `commit` call.
    fn propose(&mut self, pending: u32, n: usize) -> Result<BlockProposal<'_>>;

    /// Tell the draft that exactly these tokens were committed, in order,
    /// so its state equals having processed exactly the committed sequence
    /// (Section 4, step 7).
    fn commit(&mut self, tokens: &[u32]) -> Result<()>;

    /// Hand the draft the target layer-input rows a forward just captured,
    /// tagged by absolute position. Modes that condition on target hidden
    /// states (DFlash) stage them for the next `commit`; modes that do not
    /// ignore them. The default implementation ignores them.
    fn note_captures(
        &mut self,
        _base_position: usize,
        _captures: &[LayerInputCapture],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Which arm of the correction walk a proposal is materialized for. The
/// greedy arm reads only argmaxes; the sampled arm needs the full draft
/// distributions at a temperature.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub enum DraftArm {
    /// Greedy: proposal tokens are the draft rows' argmaxes.
    Greedy,
    /// Sampled: proposal tokens are drawn from the draft distributions at
    /// this temperature, and the distributions themselves are returned.
    Sampled {
        /// Draft temperature (already resolved: follow-target applied).
        temperature: f32,
    },
}

/// An owned block proposal: tokens plus, for the sampled arm, the full
/// per-position draft distributions the walk divides by.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Proposal {
    /// The proposed tokens, in order.
    pub tokens: Vec<u32>,
    /// Per-position draft distributions, aligned with `tokens`. Empty on
    /// the greedy arm, where the walk never reads distributions.
    pub dists: Vec<Vec<f32>>,
}

/// The draft's execution arm: the same semantics on two
/// device paths. Every piece of loop bookkeeping (capture
/// staging, commit consumption, proposal slicing) lives on
/// [`DflashSpeculator`] itself and is shared; the arm only
/// answers the two passes (inject, forward block) and the
/// committed length.
/// The CPU arm's payload, boxed inside the enum so the
/// two arms' sizes stay comparable.
struct CpuDraft {
    /// The loaded draft model.
    model: DflashModel,
    /// The draft's private KV cache.
    cache: DflashCache,
    /// The borrowed target embedding table.
    embedding: TensorData,
    /// The borrowed target output head.
    output: TensorData,
}

enum DraftBackendImpl {
    /// The CPU reference implementation, with its private
    /// cache and the borrowed target tensors as f32 data.
    Cpu(Box<CpuDraft>),
    /// The device-resident GPU session. The session borrows
    /// its backend at `'static`: the runner leaks the
    /// backend for the process lifetime, the same
    /// discipline it already applies to the target's
    /// resident session. Boxed, like the CPU payload, so
    /// the arms' sizes stay comparable.
    Gpu {
        /// The resident draft session.
        session: Box<DflashSession<'static>>,
    },
}

/// The DFlash speculator: a draft execution arm, the draft
/// config and conditioning geometry both arms agree on,
/// and the staging area for captured conditioning rows.
///
/// Draft sync contract (Section 4, step 7, and Section 10 Q1/Q2 as
/// settled): the draft's cache holds exactly the committed positions
/// `0..len`. Captures from a target forward are staged by
/// [`DflashSpeculator::note_captures`] keyed to their absolute positions;
/// [`Speculator::commit`] injects the staged rows for exactly the newly
/// committed positions and drops the rest of the stage. The draft cache is
/// never checkpointed by the target's machinery; this staging is its whole
/// rollback story, and it is exact because a position's conditioning row
/// depends only on the committed prefix that produced it.
pub struct DflashSpeculator {
    backend: DraftBackendImpl,
    /// The draft config (identical for both arms; the CPU
    /// arm's model and the GPU arm's session were both
    /// built from it).
    config: DflashConfig,
    /// Conditioning row width, from the loaded `fc`.
    conditioning_width: usize,
    /// Target hidden size, derived from `fc` at load.
    target_hidden: usize,
    /// Staged conditioning rows: `(absolute position, fused row)` pairs in
    /// increasing position order, plus the position the stage starts at.
    staged: Vec<(usize, Vec<f32>)>,
    staged_from: Option<usize>,
    /// Last proposal buffers, backing the trait's borrowed view.
    last_tokens: Vec<u32>,
    last_probs: Vec<Vec<f32>>,
}

impl DflashSpeculator {
    /// Assemble a speculator from a loaded draft model and the target
    /// tensors it borrows (the CPU arm). The caller (session creation)
    /// validates the draft against the target; this constructor only
    /// takes ownership.
    pub fn new(model: DflashModel, embedding: TensorData, output: TensorData) -> Self {
        let config = model.config().clone();
        let conditioning_width = model.weights().conditioning_width();
        let target_hidden = model.weights().target_hidden as usize;
        let cache = DflashCache::new(model.config());
        DflashSpeculator {
            backend: DraftBackendImpl::Cpu(Box::new(CpuDraft {
                model,
                cache,
                embedding,
                output,
            })),
            config,
            conditioning_width,
            target_hidden,
            staged: Vec::new(),
            staged_from: None,
            last_tokens: Vec::new(),
            last_probs: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Assemble a speculator over a device-resident draft
    /// session (the GPU arm, selected by
    /// [`crate::DraftBackend::Gpu`]). The session was built
    /// from the same draft config and weights the CPU arm
    /// would load; every loop-visible behavior (staging,
    /// commit, proposal slicing, refusals) is the shared
    /// code above the arm.
    pub fn gpu(session: DflashSession<'static>) -> Self {
        let config = session.config().clone();
        let conditioning_width = session.conditioning_width();
        let target_hidden = session.target_hidden() as usize;
        DflashSpeculator {
            backend: DraftBackendImpl::Gpu {
                session: Box::new(session),
            },
            config,
            conditioning_width,
            target_hidden,
            staged: Vec::new(),
            staged_from: None,
            last_tokens: Vec::new(),
            last_probs: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// The draft config this speculator serves (either arm).
    pub fn config(&self) -> &DflashConfig {
        &self.config
    }

    /// The draft model of the CPU arm. The GPU arm has no
    /// `DflashModel` to hand back; session creation reads
    /// [`DflashSpeculator::config`] instead, which both
    /// arms answer.
    pub fn model(&self) -> Option<&DflashModel> {
        match &self.backend {
            DraftBackendImpl::Cpu(cpu) => Some(&cpu.model),
            DraftBackendImpl::Gpu { .. } => None,
        }
    }

    /// Run the noise block for `pending` on the active
    /// arm and return its first `row_cap` rows of logits.
    ///
    /// The cap is a host-transfer hint, not a block shape:
    /// the block always runs whole (its attention is
    /// non-causal), and the caller slices only rows
    /// `1..=row_cap - 1` from the result, so rows past the
    /// cap are never consumed. The GPU arm therefore reads
    /// back just the prefix
    /// ([`wgpu_compute::DflashSession::forward_block_capped`]);
    /// the CPU arm computes in-process, has no transfer to
    /// trim, and returns the full block as before.
    fn forward_block_logits(&mut self, pending: u32, row_cap: usize) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        let block = {
            let mut block = vec![self.config.mask_token_id; self.config.block_size as usize];
            block[0] = pending;
            block
        };
        let start = self.committed_len();
        match &mut self.backend {
            DraftBackendImpl::Cpu(cpu) => {
                let borrowed = TargetTensors {
                    embedding: Some(&cpu.embedding),
                    output: Some(&cpu.output),
                };
                cpu.model
                    .forward_block(&cpu.cache, &block, start, &borrowed)
                    .map_err(|e| SpecError::DraftRefused {
                        source: Box::new(e),
                    })
            }
            DraftBackendImpl::Gpu { session } => session
                .forward_block_capped(&block, start, row_cap.min(block.len()))
                .map_err(|e| SpecError::DraftRefused {
                    source: Box::new(e),
                }),
        }
    }

    /// Inject fused conditioning rows on the active arm.
    fn inject(&mut self, features: &[f32], positions: &[usize]) -> Result<()> {
        match &mut self.backend {
            DraftBackendImpl::Cpu(cpu) => cpu
                .model
                .inject(&mut cpu.cache, features, positions)
                .map_err(|e| SpecError::DraftRefused {
                    source: Box::new(e),
                }),
            DraftBackendImpl::Gpu { session } => {
                session
                    .inject(features, positions)
                    .map_err(|e| SpecError::DraftRefused {
                        source: Box::new(e),
                    })
            }
        }
    }

    /// How many committed positions the draft's cache currently holds.
    /// At every round boundary this equals the target's cache position.
    pub fn committed_len(&self) -> usize {
        match &self.backend {
            DraftBackendImpl::Cpu(cpu) => cpu.cache.len(),
            DraftBackendImpl::Gpu { session } => session.committed_len(),
        }
    }

    /// Run one full noise block after `pending` and return up to `n`
    /// proposals. The block always runs at the draft's full block size:
    /// block attention is non-causal, so a truncated block would change
    /// the earlier rows' distributions; the session slices the result.
    /// The slice bound is known before the forward, so it goes in as
    /// the readback cap: rows past it never cross to the host on the
    /// GPU arm.
    ///
    /// Row semantics (settled by the E3 run): block row `k` is the draft
    /// distribution for the draft token at block position `k + 1`, with
    /// the anchor (`pending`) at block position 0.
    pub fn propose_block(
        &mut self,
        pending: u32,
        n: usize,
        arm: DraftArm,
        rng: &mut dyn FnMut() -> f64,
    ) -> Result<Proposal> {
        let want = n.min(self.config.max_drafts() as usize);
        // Rows 0..=want are the only rows sliced below: row 0
        // is the anchor's own, rows 1..=want back the drafts.
        let logits = self.forward_block_logits(pending, want + 1)?;
        let vocab = self.config.vocab_size as usize;
        let mut tokens = Vec::with_capacity(want);
        let mut dists: Vec<Vec<f32>> = Vec::new();
        for k in 0..want {
            // Forward row k + 1 is the distribution for draft token
            // k + 1: row 0 belongs to the anchor's own position and is
            // not itself a draft (the model's forward_block contract).
            let row = &logits[(k + 1) * vocab..(k + 2) * vocab];
            match arm {
                DraftArm::Greedy => tokens.push(sampler::argmax(row)),
                DraftArm::Sampled { temperature } => {
                    let dist = sampler::distribution(row, temperature, 1.0)?;
                    tokens.push(sampler::sample_from(&dist, rng()));
                    dists.push(dist);
                }
            }
        }
        // The sampled arm's distributions back the trait's
        // borrowed view, so they are kept. The greedy arm's
        // one-hot view is NOT materialized here: at the real
        // vocab it is megabytes of zeros per round on the
        // loop's hot path (measured at about 2 ms of a
        // 217 ms round), and the one consumer, the trait
        // shim below, rebuilds it from the tokens on demand.
        self.last_probs = match arm {
            DraftArm::Greedy => Vec::new(),
            DraftArm::Sampled { .. } => dists.clone(),
        };
        self.last_tokens.clone_from(&tokens);
        Ok(Proposal { tokens, dists })
    }
}

impl Speculator for DflashSpeculator {
    fn mode(&self) -> crate::SpecMode {
        crate::SpecMode::Dflash
    }

    fn max_depth(&self) -> usize {
        self.config.max_drafts() as usize
    }

    fn propose(&mut self, pending: u32, n: usize) -> Result<BlockProposal<'_>> {
        let mut no_draws = || 0.0f64;
        let proposal = self.propose_block(pending, n, DraftArm::Greedy, &mut no_draws)?;
        let _ = proposal;
        if self.last_probs.is_empty() {
            // Greedy proposals carry no stored distributions
            // (see propose_block); the trait's contract is a
            // one-hot view of the proposed tokens, built here
            // on the shim's cold path.
            let vocab = self.config.vocab_size as usize;
            self.last_probs = self
                .last_tokens
                .iter()
                .map(|&t| {
                    let mut one_hot = vec![0.0f32; vocab];
                    one_hot[t as usize] = 1.0;
                    one_hot
                })
                .collect();
        }
        let dists = self
            .last_probs
            .iter()
            .map(|row| DraftDist { probs: row })
            .collect();
        Ok(BlockProposal {
            tokens: &self.last_tokens,
            dists,
        })
    }

    fn commit(&mut self, tokens: &[u32]) -> Result<()> {
        let from = self.committed_len();
        if tokens.is_empty() {
            self.staged.clear();
            self.staged_from = None;
            return Ok(());
        }
        let staged_from = self.staged_from.ok_or_else(|| SpecError::SessionState {
            detail: format!(
                "draft commit of {} tokens at position {from} has no staged captures",
                tokens.len()
            ),
        })?;
        if staged_from != from || self.staged.len() < tokens.len() {
            return Err(SpecError::SessionState {
                detail: format!(
                    "draft commit at position {from} needs {} staged rows from {from}, \
                     stage holds {} rows from {staged_from}",
                    tokens.len(),
                    self.staged.len()
                ),
            });
        }
        let width = self.conditioning_width;
        let mut features = Vec::with_capacity(tokens.len() * width);
        let mut positions = Vec::with_capacity(tokens.len());
        for i in 0..tokens.len() {
            let (position, row) = &self.staged[i];
            if *position != from + i || row.len() != width {
                return Err(SpecError::SessionState {
                    detail: format!(
                        "staged capture {i} is position {position} width {}, expected position {} width {width}",
                        row.len(),
                        from + i
                    ),
                });
            }
            features.extend_from_slice(row);
            positions.push(*position);
        }
        // The stage is consumed either way: a failed injection leaves the
        // draft desynced, which the session surfaces as a refusal rather
        // than retrying against stale rows.
        self.staged.clear();
        self.staged_from = None;
        self.inject(&features, &positions)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    fn note_captures(
        &mut self,
        base_position: usize,
        captures: &[LayerInputCapture],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        if self.staged_from.is_some() {
            return Err(SpecError::SessionState {
                detail: "captures staged twice without a commit between them".to_string(),
            });
        }
        if captures.is_empty() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        // Concatenate each position's per-layer rows in target_layers
        // order: exactly the flat conditioning layout inject consumes.
        let target_hidden = self.target_hidden;
        let width = self.conditioning_width;
        let rows = captures[0].rows.len() / target_hidden;
        let mut staged = Vec::with_capacity(rows);
        for i in 0..rows {
            let mut row = Vec::with_capacity(width);
            for capture in captures {
                row.extend_from_slice(&capture.rows[i * target_hidden..(i + 1) * target_hidden]);
            }
            staged.push((base_position + i, row));
        }
        self.staged = staged;
        self.staged_from = Some(base_position);
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Wrap a target-side refusal from the session's cache operations.
pub(crate) fn cache_refused(op: &'static str, source: GlimmerError) -> SpecError {
    SpecError::CacheRefused {
        op,
        source: Box::new(source),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::testkit;

    fn captures(positions: usize, layers: &[usize]) -> Vec<LayerInputCapture> {
        let target_hidden = testkit::TARGET_HIDDEN;
        layers
            .iter()
            .map(|&layer| LayerInputCapture {
                layer,
                rows: (0..positions * target_hidden)
                    .map(|i| (i % 7) as f32 * 0.01)
                    .collect(),
            })
            .collect()
    }

    /// The draft sync contract: commit consumes exactly the staged rows
    /// for the committed positions; the draft's cache then holds exactly
    /// the committed prefix, and stale or missing stages refuse by name.
    #[test]
    fn commit_consumes_exactly_the_staged_prefix() {
        let compute = std::rc::Rc::new(CpuCompute::new());
        let fixture = testkit::build_target(Box::new(SharedCompute(compute)));
        let mut spec = testkit::build_speculator(&fixture, 5);

        // Commit with nothing staged refuses.
        assert!(matches!(
            spec.commit(&[1, 2]),
            Err(SpecError::SessionState { .. })
        ));

        // Stage 4 positions, commit 3: the draft holds exactly 3.
        spec.note_captures(0, &captures(4, &[1, 3])).expect("stage");
        spec.commit(&[10, 11, 12]).expect("commit prefix");
        assert_eq!(spec.committed_len(), 3);

        // A stage that does not start at the committed length refuses.
        spec.note_captures(9, &captures(2, &[1, 3])).expect("stage");
        assert!(matches!(
            spec.commit(&[13]),
            Err(SpecError::SessionState { .. })
        ));
        assert_eq!(spec.committed_len(), 3, "a refused commit changes nothing");
    }

    /// One agreement probe between the trait's borrowed view and the
    /// owned block proposal: for the same speculator state, pending
    /// token, and depth, the view's tokens must equal the block
    /// proposal's tokens one for one, and each of the view's
    /// distributions must be the one-hot row at exactly its token.
    fn assert_proposals_agree(spec: &mut DflashSpeculator, pending: u32, n: usize) {
        let (view_tokens, view_argmax): (Vec<u32>, Vec<u32>) = {
            let view = spec.propose(pending, n).expect("trait propose");
            let argmaxes = view
                .dists
                .iter()
                .map(|dist| {
                    let mass: f32 = dist.probs.iter().sum();
                    assert!(
                        (mass - 1.0).abs() < 1e-6,
                        "greedy dists are one-hot, mass {mass}"
                    );
                    sampler::argmax(dist.probs)
                })
                .collect();
            (view.tokens.to_vec(), argmaxes)
        };
        assert_eq!(
            view_argmax, view_tokens,
            "view dists must be one-hot at the view tokens (pending {pending}, n {n})"
        );
        let mut no_draws = || 0.0f64;
        let block = spec
            .propose_block(pending, n, DraftArm::Greedy, &mut no_draws)
            .expect("block propose");
        assert_eq!(
            view_tokens, block.tokens,
            "trait view and block proposal diverge (pending {pending}, n {n})"
        );
    }

    /// The GPU arm's shared bookkeeping: a speculator built
    /// over a resident draft session stages, commits, and
    /// proposes through exactly the code the CPU arm uses,
    /// and its committed length tracks the GPU session's.
    /// Adapter-guarded like every GPU test in the workspace:
    /// skips with a printed reason where no adapter
    /// qualifies. The fixture is the smallest draft the
    /// GEMV kernels accept (every projection input a whole
    /// number of Q4_K blocks).
    #[test]
    fn gpu_arm_shares_the_speculator_bookkeeping() {
        use muse_glimmer::{Dtype, GlimmerError, TensorSource as GlimmerSource, TensorView};
        use std::collections::HashMap;
        use std::sync::Arc as StdArc;
        use wgpu_compute::{
            DflashRawWeights, DflashSession, DflashSessionConfig, WgpuCompute, WgpuError,
        };

        let backend = match WgpuCompute::new() {
            Ok(b) => b,
            Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
                eprintln!(
                    "skipping gpu arm speculator test: no suitable adapter (enumerated: [{}])",
                    seen.join("; ")
                );
                return;
            }
            Err(e) => panic!("backend construction failed unexpectedly: {e}"),
        };
        let backend: &'static WgpuCompute = Box::leak(Box::new(backend));

        // Deterministic small-magnitude Q4_K / F32 tensors,
        // the parity fixture's by-construction style.
        fn q4k(name: &str, inn: usize, out: usize, seed: u8) -> TensorView {
            let blocks = inn * out / 256;
            let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(blocks * 144);
            for b in 0..blocks {
                data.extend_from_slice(
                    &wgpu_compute::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::f32_to_f16_bits(0.005).to_le_bytes(),
                );
                data.extend_from_slice(
                    &wgpu_compute::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::f32_to_f16_bits(0.002).to_le_bytes(),
                );
                for i in 0..12 {
                    data.push(seed.wrapping_add(i as u8) & 0x07);
                }
                for i in 0..128 {
                    data.push(seed.wrapping_add((b + i) as u8));
                }
            }
            TensorView {
                name: name.to_string(),
                dtype: Dtype::Q4K,
                shape: vec![inn as u64, out as u64],
                data: StdArc::from(data.into_boxed_slice()),
            }
        }
        fn f32t(name: &str, n: usize, center: f32) -> TensorView {
            let data: Vec<u8> = (0..n)
                .flat_map(|i| (center + (i % 5) as f32 * 0.01).to_le_bytes())
                .collect();
            TensorView {
                name: name.to_string(),
                dtype: Dtype::F32,
                shape: vec![n as u64],
                data: StdArc::from(data.into_boxed_slice()),
            }
        }
        struct MapSource {
            tensors: HashMap<String, TensorView>,
        }
        impl GlimmerSource for MapSource {
            fn tensor(&self, name: &str) -> muse_glimmer::Result<TensorView> {
                self.tensors
                    .get(name)
                    .cloned()
                    .ok_or_else(|| GlimmerError::MissingTensor {
                        name: name.to_string(),
                    })
            }
        }

        let cfg = dflash::DflashConfig {
            name: None,
            block_count: 2,
            context_length: 64,
            hidden: 256,
            ffn_hidden: 256,
            q_heads: 2,
            kv_heads: 1,
            key_length: 128,
            value_length: 128,
            rope_freq_base: 10_000.0,
            rms_eps: 1e-5,
            block_size: 2,
            target_layers: vec![0, 1],
            sliding_window: 2048,
            sliding_pattern: vec![false, false],
            causal_attention: false,
            mask_token_id: 255,
            vocab_size: 256,
        };
        let mut tensors: HashMap<String, TensorView> = HashMap::new();
        let mut put = |v: TensorView| {
            tensors.insert(v.name.clone(), v);
        };
        put(q4k("fc.weight", 512, 256, 1));
        put(f32t("enc.output_norm.weight", 256, 1.0));
        put(f32t("output_norm.weight", 256, 1.0));
        for layer in 0..2 {
            let p = |s: &str| format!("blk.{layer}.{s}");
            put(f32t(&p("attn_norm.weight"), 256, 1.0));
            put(q4k(&p("attn_q.weight"), 256, 256, 2));
            put(q4k(&p("attn_k.weight"), 256, 128, 3));
            put(q4k(&p("attn_v.weight"), 256, 128, 4));
            put(f32t(&p("attn_q_norm.weight"), 128, 1.0));
            put(f32t(&p("attn_k_norm.weight"), 128, 1.0));
            put(q4k(&p("attn_output.weight"), 256, 256, 5));
            put(f32t(&p("ffn_norm.weight"), 256, 1.0));
            put(q4k(&p("ffn_gate.weight"), 256, 256, 6));
            put(q4k(&p("ffn_up.weight"), 256, 256, 7));
            put(q4k(&p("ffn_down.weight"), 256, 256, 8));
        }
        let raw = DflashRawWeights::load(&MapSource { tensors }, &cfg).expect("raw loads");
        let embedding = q4k("token_embd.weight", 256, 256, 9);
        let output = q4k("output.weight", 256, 256, 10);
        let session = DflashSession::new(
            backend,
            &cfg,
            &raw,
            Some(&embedding),
            Some(&output),
            DflashSessionConfig { kv_capacity: 32 },
        )
        .expect("draft session builds");
        let mut spec = DflashSpeculator::gpu(session);
        assert_eq!(spec.config().block_size, 2);
        assert!(spec.model().is_none(), "the GPU arm has no CPU model");
        assert_eq!(spec.committed_len(), 0);

        // Commit with nothing staged refuses, arm-independent.
        assert!(matches!(
            spec.commit(&[1]),
            Err(SpecError::SessionState { .. })
        ));

        // Stage three positions of two-layer captures and
        // commit them: the GPU session's held set advances
        // through the shared staging code.
        let caps: Vec<LayerInputCapture> = [0usize, 1]
            .iter()
            .map(|&layer| LayerInputCapture {
                layer,
                rows: (0..3 * 256).map(|i| (i % 7) as f32 * 0.01).collect(),
            })
            .collect();
        spec.note_captures(0, &caps).expect("stage");
        spec.commit(&[10, 11, 12]).expect("gpu commit");
        assert_eq!(spec.committed_len(), 3);

        // A proposal runs the GPU forward and returns
        // in-vocabulary tokens at the requested depth.
        let mut no_draws = || 0.0f64;
        let proposal = spec
            .propose_block(12, 1, DraftArm::Greedy, &mut no_draws)
            .expect("gpu propose");
        assert_eq!(proposal.tokens.len(), 1);
        assert!(proposal.tokens[0] < cfg.vocab_size);
        assert_eq!(spec.committed_len(), 3, "proposing commits nothing");
    }

    /// The trait's borrowed proposal view agrees with the owned block
    /// proposal the session consumes: the same tokens, compared
    /// directly. The discarding shape of the trait view is accepted
    /// design (the panel merge ruled it so); this test is the guard
    /// that keeps the two proposal paths from drifting apart
    /// silently, which a lengths-and-mass check cannot do.
    #[test]
    fn trait_proposal_matches_block_proposal() {
        let compute = std::rc::Rc::new(CpuCompute::new());
        let fixture = testkit::build_target(Box::new(SharedCompute(compute)));

        // A fresh speculator, nothing committed yet.
        let mut fresh = testkit::build_speculator(&fixture, 5);
        assert_proposals_agree(&mut fresh, 0, 2);
        assert_proposals_agree(&mut fresh, 127, 3);

        // A speculator with a committed prefix, probed below, at,
        // and past its maximum depth.
        let mut spec = testkit::build_speculator(&fixture, 5);
        spec.note_captures(0, &captures(3, &[1, 3])).expect("stage");
        spec.commit(&[4, 5, 6]).expect("commit");
        assert_proposals_agree(&mut spec, 6, 1);
        assert_proposals_agree(&mut spec, 6, 3);
        assert_proposals_agree(&mut spec, 6, 4);
        assert_proposals_agree(&mut spec, 9, 2);
        assert_proposals_agree(&mut spec, 6, 5);

        assert_eq!(spec.max_depth(), 4);
        assert_eq!(spec.mode(), crate::SpecMode::Dflash);
    }
}

//! The draft-depth sweep (TODO T-9.7): run the speculative loop once
//! per candidate depth, log acceptance per depth, and name the winning
//! depth as the recorded default.
//!
//! Everything operational here is configuration with a default, never a
//! compiled-in constant (David's law): the candidate set and the
//! per-depth token budget live in [`SweepConfig`], and the depth each
//! session runs at is [`crate::SpecConfig::depth`], the same field
//! serving uses. The sweep only ever overrides that field on a clone of
//! the caller's base configuration.
//!
//! The runner is backend-agnostic by construction. It names no compute
//! backend and no model type: the caller hands it a factory that builds
//! a ready [`SpecSession`] for a given configuration, and the runner
//! drives `begin` / `generate` / `finish` and does the accounting. The
//! CPU example (`examples/spec_sweep.rs`) wires the factory to the CPU
//! reference backend today; when the GPU-resident loop lands (TODO
//! T-9.6's speed half), its lane wires the same runner to a factory
//! that builds the session over the GPU compute path, and the sweep,
//! the table, and the winner rule do not change.
//!
//! The measured wall is the `generate` call only: model loads and the
//! prompt prefill are excluded, so effective tok/s compares depths, not
//! disk speed. A depth whose session stops early (a stop token in the
//! base configuration) is measured on the tokens it actually emitted;
//! the row says how many, so a short row is never mistaken for a full
//! one.

use std::fmt;
use std::time::Instant;

use crate::config::SpecConfig;
use crate::diag::Diag;
use crate::driver::TargetDriver;
use crate::error::{Result, SpecError};
use crate::session::{SpecSession, SpecStats};

/// The default candidate depths, ascending: exactly the set the
/// 2026-10-30 llama.cpp sweep measured (`bench/gpu-proof-2026-10-30.
/// md`), from the floor to the real draft's block size (16).
/// Keeping the set identical makes the two tables comparable cell
/// for cell. The set is a sweep menu, not a default: this stack's
/// own sweep (T-9.7, `bench/spec-sweep-gpu-fixed-2026-11-04.md`)
/// picked depth 1, which is [`SpecConfig`]'s standing default;
/// the 6 in the set is the llama.cpp operating point that sweep
/// measured, not a default of this stack. A default, not a
/// constant: any caller can replace the set wholesale through
/// [`SweepConfig`].
pub const DEFAULT_CANDIDATE_DEPTHS: &[usize] = &[1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16];

/// The default winner band: the recorded operating-point rule (SPEC
/// 9.4, applied in `bench/gpu-proof-2026-10-30.md`) picks the smallest
/// depth within 2% of the best measured speed, because the speed curve
/// is flat near its peak and the shallower round is the cheaper one to
/// be wrong about.
pub const DEFAULT_WINNER_BAND: f64 = 0.02;

/// The default generation budget per depth: enough rounds at every
/// candidate depth for the acceptance rate to settle, small enough for
/// a bench run to finish.
pub const DEFAULT_TOKENS_PER_DEPTH: usize = 128;

/// What a sweep measures: the candidate depths and the per-depth
/// generation budget. Validated before anything runs
/// ([`SweepConfig::validate`]); an unusable configuration refuses by
/// name instead of producing an empty table.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct SweepConfig {
    /// Candidate draft depths, in the order they are measured. Each
    /// must be at least 1 and appear at most once. A depth beyond the
    /// draft's block size is not refused here (the sweep does not know
    /// the draft); session creation refuses it by name when its turn
    /// comes, and the sweep stops there.
    pub depths: Vec<usize>,
    /// Tokens generated per depth (the `generate` budget handed to
    /// each session). Must be at least 1.
    pub tokens_per_depth: usize,
    /// The winner band, as a fraction in `[0, 1)`: the chosen default
    /// is the smallest depth whose effective tok/s is within this
    /// fraction of the best depth's. Default: 0.02 (SPEC 9.4's rule).
    pub winner_band: f64,
}

impl Default for SweepConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        SweepConfig {
            depths: DEFAULT_CANDIDATE_DEPTHS.to_vec(),
            tokens_per_depth: DEFAULT_TOKENS_PER_DEPTH,
            winner_band: DEFAULT_WINNER_BAND,
        }
    }
}

impl SweepConfig {
    /// Parse a comma-separated candidate list (`"1,2,4,6"`), whitespace
    /// tolerant. Refuses by name: an empty list or entry, a non-numeric
    /// entry, a zero depth, or a duplicate.
    pub fn parse_depths(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<usize>> {
        let invalid = |detail: String| SpecError::SweepConfigInvalid { detail };
        let mut depths = Vec::new();
        for part in text.split(',') {
            let part = part.trim();
            if part.is_empty() {
                return Err(invalid(format!("depth list {text:?} has an empty entry")));
            }
            let depth: usize = part
                .parse()
                .map_err(|_| invalid(format!("depth {part:?} in {text:?} is not a number")))?;
            depths.push(depth);
        }
        let config = SweepConfig {
            depths,
            ..SweepConfig::default()
        };
        config.validate()?;
        Ok(config.depths)
    }

    /// Check the configuration is measurable: a non-empty candidate
    /// set of positive, distinct depths and a positive token budget.
    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {
        let invalid = |detail: String| SpecError::SweepConfigInvalid { detail };
        if self.depths.is_empty() {
            return Err(invalid("candidate depth set is empty".to_string()));
        }
        if self.tokens_per_depth == 0 {
            return Err(invalid("tokens_per_depth is zero".to_string()));
        }
        if !(0.0..1.0).contains(&self.winner_band) {
            return Err(invalid(format!(
                "winner_band {} is outside [0, 1)",
                self.winner_band
            )));
        }
        for (i, &depth) in self.depths.iter().enumerate() {
            if depth == 0 {
                return Err(invalid("candidate depth 0 is not a depth".to_string()));
            }
            if self.depths[..i].contains(&depth) {
                return Err(invalid(format!("candidate depth {depth} appears twice")));
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// One measured depth: the session's own cumulative statistics plus the
/// generate wall they were produced under. All rates derive from the
/// counts, so a row can be rebuilt from a [`SpecStats`] and a wall time
/// without running anything (which is how the accounting is tested).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct DepthRow {
    /// The draft depth this row measured.
    pub depth: usize,
    /// Rounds the session ran.
    pub rounds: usize,
    /// Draft tokens proposed across all rounds.
    pub proposed: usize,
    /// Draft tokens accepted across all rounds.
    pub accepted: usize,
    /// `accepted / proposed`, in `[0, 1]`; zero when nothing proposed.
    pub acceptance_rate: f64,
    /// Round-emitted tokens per round.
    pub tokens_per_round: f64,
    /// Tokens emitted by rounds (the prefill's pending token excluded,
    /// exactly as [`SpecStats`] counts).
    pub tokens_emitted: usize,
    /// Wall seconds of the `generate` call (loads and prefill excluded).
    pub wall_secs: f64,
    /// `tokens_emitted / wall_secs`: the depth's effective speed.
    pub tok_per_sec: f64,
    /// Whether speculation latched off during this depth's session.
    pub fallback_latched: bool,
}

impl DepthRow {
    /// Build a row from a finished session's statistics and the wall
    /// time its generation took.
    pub fn from_stats(depth: usize, stats: &SpecStats, wall_secs: f64) -> DepthRow {
        let tok_per_sec = if wall_secs > 0.0 {
            stats.tokens_emitted as f64 / wall_secs
        } else {
            0.0
        };
        DepthRow {
            depth,
            rounds: stats.rounds,
            proposed: stats.proposed,
            accepted: stats.accepted,
            acceptance_rate: stats.acceptance_rate(),
            tokens_per_round: stats.tokens_per_round(),
            tokens_emitted: stats.tokens_emitted,
            wall_secs,
            tok_per_sec,
            fallback_latched: stats.fallback_latched,
        }
    }
}

/// The outcome of a sweep: one row per measured depth, in the order
/// they were measured, plus the winner band they were judged under
/// (carried from the [`SweepConfig`] that ran, so a filed report can
/// be re-judged by hand).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct SweepReport {
    /// The measured rows.
    pub rows: Vec<DepthRow>,
    /// The winner band fraction the chosen default is picked under.
    pub winner_band: f64,
}

impl Default for SweepReport {
    fn default() -> Self {
        SweepReport {
            rows: Vec::new(),
            winner_band: DEFAULT_WINNER_BAND,
        }
    }
}

impl SweepReport {
    /// The winning depth's row, by the recorded operating-point rule
    /// (SPEC 9.4): the smallest depth whose effective tok/s is within
    /// `winner_band` of the best depth's. The speed curve is flat near
    /// its peak, so the band keeps clock jitter from crowning a deep,
    /// expensive round over a shallow one that measured the same.
    /// `None` when no depth was measured.
    pub fn winner(&self) -> Option<&DepthRow> {
        let best = self
            .rows
            .iter()
            .map(|row| row.tok_per_sec)
            .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max);
        let floor = best * (1.0 - self.winner_band);
        self.rows
            .iter()
            .filter(|row| row.tok_per_sec >= floor)
            .min_by_key(|row| row.depth)
    }

    /// The winning depth, if any depth was measured.
    pub fn chosen_depth(&self) -> Option<usize> {
        self.winner().map(|row| row.depth)
    }

    /// The sweep table as markdown, in the shape the T-9.7 bench note
    /// files: one row per depth, then the chosen-default line naming
    /// the depth to record in [`crate::SpecConfig`] with its measured
    /// acceptance rate.
    pub fn render_table(&self) -> String {
        let mut out = String::new();
        out.push_str(
            "| Depth | Rounds | Proposed | Accepted | Acceptance rate | Tokens/round | Emitted | Wall (s) | Effective tok/s |\n",
        );
        out.push_str(
            "|------:|-------:|---------:|---------:|----------------:|-------------:|--------:|---------:|----------------:|\n",
        );
        for row in &self.rows {
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "| {} | {} | {} | {} | {:.3} | {:.2} | {} | {:.1} | {:.2} |\n",
                row.depth,
                row.rounds,
                row.proposed,
                row.accepted,
                row.acceptance_rate,
                row.tokens_per_round,
                row.tokens_emitted,
                row.wall_secs,
                row.tok_per_sec
            ));
        }
        match self.winner() {
            Some(w) => out.push_str(&format!(
                "\nChosen default depth: **{}** (acceptance rate {:.3}, effective {:.2} tok/s).\n",
                w.depth, w.acceptance_rate, w.tok_per_sec
            )),
            None => {
                out.push_str("\nChosen default depth: none (no depths measured).\n");
            }
        }
        out
    }
}

/// Why a sweep stopped, named. The loop's own refusals keep their
/// [`SpecError`] name; a factory that cannot build a session for a
/// depth (a model load, a backend init) reports in its own words, and
/// the sweep adds the depth it stopped at.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum SweepError {
    /// The loop refused: bad sweep configuration, a session creation
    /// refusal, or a round refusal.
    Spec(SpecError),
    /// The session factory failed to build for this depth.
    Build {
        /// The depth whose session never existed.
        depth: usize,
        /// The factory's own description of the failure.
        detail: String,
    },
}

impl fmt::Display for SweepError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            SweepError::Spec(err) => write!(f, "{err}"),
            SweepError::Build { depth, detail } => {
                write!(f, "session build for depth {depth} failed: {detail}")
            }
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for SweepError {}

impl From<SpecError> for SweepError {
    fn from(err: SpecError) -> Self {
        SweepError::Spec(err)
    }
}

/// Run the sweep: for each candidate depth, build a session from
/// `factory` (handed the base configuration with only its depth
/// overridden), prefill `prompt`, generate `tokens_per_depth` tokens
/// under a wall clock, and fold the finished session's statistics into
/// a row.
///
/// The first refusal stops the sweep and is returned by name: a table
/// with a silent hole in it would be a lie about the depths it skipped.
/// Every step emits through `diag` (`spec.sweep.begin`, one
/// `spec.sweep.row` per depth, `spec.sweep.end`, and `spec.sweep.
/// refused` on the way out).
pub fn run_sweep<D, F>(
    sweep: &SweepConfig,
    base: &SpecConfig,
    prompt: &[u32],
    mut factory: F,
    diag: &dyn Diag,
) -> std::result::Result<SweepReport, SweepError>
where
    D: TargetDriver,
    F: FnMut(&SpecConfig) -> std::result::Result<SpecSession<D>, String>,
{
    if let Err(err) = sweep.validate() {
        diag.event("spec.sweep.refused", &format!("error={err}"));
        return Err(err.into());
    }
    diag.event(
        "spec.sweep.begin",
        &format!(
            "depths={:?} tokens_per_depth={} prompt_tokens={}",
            sweep.depths,
            sweep.tokens_per_depth,
            prompt.len()
        ),
    );
    let mut rows = Vec::with_capacity(sweep.depths.len());
    for &depth in &sweep.depths {
        let mut config = base.clone();
        config.depth = depth;
        let row = measure_depth(&mut factory, &config, prompt, sweep.tokens_per_depth);
        match row {
            Ok(row) => {
                diag.event(
                    "spec.sweep.row",
                    &format!(
                        "depth={} rounds={} proposed={} accepted={} acceptance_rate={:.4} tokens_per_round={:.2} wall_s={:.3} tok_per_sec={:.2} fallback_latched={}",
                        row.depth,
                        row.rounds,
                        row.proposed,
                        row.accepted,
                        row.acceptance_rate,
                        row.tokens_per_round,
                        row.wall_secs,
                        row.tok_per_sec,
                        row.fallback_latched
                    ),
                );
                rows.push(row);
            }
            Err(err) => {
                diag.event("spec.sweep.refused", &format!("depth={depth} error={err}"));
                return Err(err);
            }
        }
    }
    let report = SweepReport {
        rows,
        winner_band: sweep.winner_band,
    };
    match report.winner() {
        Some(w) => diag.event(
            "spec.sweep.end",
            &format!(
                "chosen_depth={} acceptance_rate={:.4} tok_per_sec={:.2}",
                w.depth, w.acceptance_rate, w.tok_per_sec
            ),
        ),
        None => diag.event("spec.sweep.end", "chosen_depth=none"),
    }
    Ok(report)
}

/// Build, run, and account one depth. Split from [`run_sweep`] so the
/// per-depth failure handling reads as one named refusal path.
fn measure_depth<D, F>(
    factory: &mut F,
    config: &SpecConfig,
    prompt: &[u32],
    tokens: usize,
) -> std::result::Result<DepthRow, SweepError>
where
    D: TargetDriver,
    F: FnMut(&SpecConfig) -> std::result::Result<SpecSession<D>, String>,
{
    let mut session = factory(config).map_err(|detail| SweepError::Build {
        depth: config.depth,
        detail,
    })?;
    session.begin(prompt)?;
    let started = Instant::now();
    session.generate(tokens, &[])?;
    let wall_secs = started.elapsed().as_secs_f64();
    let stats = session.finish();
    Ok(DepthRow::from_stats(config.depth, &stats, wall_secs))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use std::rc::Rc;
    use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

    use cpu_compute::CpuCompute;

    use super::*;
    use crate::diag::Diag;
    use crate::speculator::SharedCompute;
    use crate::testkit;
    use crate::NullDiag;

    const PROMPT: &[u32] = &[3, 17, 42];

    /// A diag sink that keeps every event, so tests can prove the
    /// sweep's evidence actually crossed the seam.
    #[derive(Debug, Default)]
    struct RecDiag(Mutex<Vec<String>>);

    impl Diag for RecDiag {
        fn event(&self, name: &str, detail: &str) {
            self.0
                .lock()
                .expect("recording diag lock")
                .push(format!("{name} {detail}"));
        }
    }

    impl RecDiag {
        fn saw(&self, needle: &str) -> bool {
            self.0
                .lock()
                .expect("recording diag lock")
                .iter()
                .any(|line| line.contains(needle))
        }
    }

    /// The CPU-fixture factory: the same wiring the example uses for
    /// the real files, over the synthetic geometry (draft block 16, so
    /// every candidate depth up to the default set's max is legal).
    fn fixture_factory(config: &SpecConfig) -> std::result::Result<SpecSession, String> {
        Ok(testkit::build_session(config.clone(), 16))
    }

    /// The fallible twin of [`fixture_factory`]: session creation
    /// refusals surface as the factory's error text instead of the
    /// testkit builder's expect, so a test can watch the sweep stop.
    fn try_fixture_factory(config: &SpecConfig) -> std::result::Result<SpecSession, String> {
        let compute = Rc::new(CpuCompute::new());
        let fixture = testkit::build_target(Box::new(SharedCompute(compute.clone())));
        let speculator = testkit::build_speculator(&fixture, 16);
        SpecSession::new(
            crate::driver::CpuTarget::new(fixture.model, compute),
            Some(speculator),
            config.clone(),
            Arc::new(NullDiag),
        )
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())
    }

    fn fabricated_row(depth: usize, tok_per_sec: f64, acceptance_rate: f64) -> DepthRow {
        DepthRow {
            depth,
            rounds: 10,
            proposed: 100,
            accepted: (acceptance_rate * 100.0) as usize,
            acceptance_rate,
            tokens_per_round: 5.0,
            tokens_emitted: 50,
            wall_secs: 1.0,
            tok_per_sec,
            fallback_latched: false,
        }
    }

    fn close(a: f64, b: f64) -> bool {
        (a - b).abs() < 1e-12
    }

    #[test]
    fn default_config_is_valid_and_covers_the_operating_point() {
        let config = SweepConfig::default();
        config
            .validate()
            .expect("the default sweep config validates");
        assert!(config.depths.contains(&1), "the standing default is swept");
        assert!(
            config.depths.contains(&6),
            "the llama.cpp operating point is swept"
        );
        assert!(config.depths.contains(&16), "the draft block max is swept");
        assert_eq!(config.tokens_per_depth, DEFAULT_TOKENS_PER_DEPTH);
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_depths_reads_lists() {
        assert_eq!(
            SweepConfig::parse_depths("1,2,4,6").expect("list parses"),
            vec![1, 2, 4, 6]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            SweepConfig::parse_depths(" 6 ").expect("single parses"),
            vec![6]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            SweepConfig::parse_depths("1, 2 , 12").expect("spaces parse"),
            vec![1, 2, 12]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_depths_refuses_bad_input() {
        for text in ["", " ", "0", "3,0", "x", "1,,2", "4,4", "1,", "-3", "2.5"] {
            let err = SweepConfig::parse_depths(text).expect_err(&format!("{text:?} must refuse"));
            assert!(
                matches!(err, SpecError::SweepConfigInvalid { .. }),
                "{text:?} refused with {err:?}, want SweepConfigInvalid"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn validate_refuses_empty_zero_duplicate_and_zero_budget() {
        let cases = [
            SweepConfig {
                depths: vec![],
                tokens_per_depth: 8,
                winner_band: DEFAULT_WINNER_BAND,
            },
            SweepConfig {
                depths: vec![0],
                tokens_per_depth: 8,
                winner_band: DEFAULT_WINNER_BAND,
            },
            SweepConfig {
                depths: vec![2, 2],
                tokens_per_depth: 8,
                winner_band: DEFAULT_WINNER_BAND,
            },
            SweepConfig {
                depths: vec![2],
                tokens_per_depth: 0,
                winner_band: DEFAULT_WINNER_BAND,
            },
            SweepConfig {
                depths: vec![2],
                tokens_per_depth: 8,
                winner_band: 1.0,
            },
        ];
        for config in cases {
            assert!(
                matches!(config.validate(), Err(SpecError::SweepConfigInvalid { .. })),
                "{config:?} must refuse validation"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn row_math_comes_from_the_counts() {
        let stats = SpecStats {
            rounds: 4,
            proposed: 24,
            accepted: 9,
            rejections: 3,
            rollbacks: 3,
            tokens_emitted: 13,
            fallback_latched: false,
        };
        let row = DepthRow::from_stats(6, &stats, 2.0);
        assert_eq!(row.depth, 6);
        assert!(close(row.acceptance_rate, 0.375), "9/24 = 0.375");
        assert!(close(row.tokens_per_round, 3.25), "13/4 = 3.25");
        assert!(close(row.tok_per_sec, 6.5), "13 tokens over 2 s = 6.5");
        let idle = DepthRow::from_stats(1, &SpecStats::default(), 0.0);
        assert!(close(idle.acceptance_rate, 0.0), "no proposals, no rate");
        assert!(close(idle.tok_per_sec, 0.0), "no wall, no speed");
    }

    #[test]
    fn winner_follows_the_spec_9_4_band_rule() {
        // Outright speed: depth 2 sits outside the 2% band under the
        // best (60 * 0.98 = 58.8), so the fast deep row wins despite
        // its poor acceptance.
        let report = SweepReport {
            rows: vec![
                fabricated_row(2, 50.0, 0.90),
                fabricated_row(16, 60.0, 0.10),
            ],
            winner_band: DEFAULT_WINNER_BAND,
        };
        assert_eq!(
            report.chosen_depth(),
            Some(16),
            "outside the band, best speed wins"
        );

        // Inside the band: 49.5 is within 2% of 50 (floor 49.0), so
        // the smallest depth in the band is the pick.
        let report = SweepReport {
            rows: vec![fabricated_row(8, 50.0, 0.90), fabricated_row(4, 49.5, 0.80)],
            winner_band: DEFAULT_WINNER_BAND,
        };
        assert_eq!(
            report.chosen_depth(),
            Some(4),
            "inside the band, the smallest depth wins"
        );

        // Just outside the band: 48.0 < 49.0, so depth 4 does not
        // qualify and the best row stands.
        let report = SweepReport {
            rows: vec![fabricated_row(8, 50.0, 0.90), fabricated_row(4, 48.0, 0.95)],
            winner_band: DEFAULT_WINNER_BAND,
        };
        assert_eq!(report.chosen_depth(), Some(8), "outside the band, no steal");

        assert_eq!(SweepReport::default().chosen_depth(), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn table_rendering_has_the_bench_note_shape() {
        let report = SweepReport {
            rows: vec![fabricated_row(4, 50.0, 0.9), fabricated_row(6, 60.0, 0.5)],
            winner_band: DEFAULT_WINNER_BAND,
        };
        let table = report.render_table();
        assert!(table.contains("| Depth | Rounds | Proposed | Accepted |"));
        assert_eq!(
            table.lines().filter(|l| l.starts_with('|')).count(),
            4,
            "header, separator, and one line per depth"
        );
        assert!(
            table.contains("Chosen default depth: **6**"),
            "the winner line names the chosen depth: {table}"
        );
        let empty = SweepReport::default().render_table();
        assert!(empty.contains("Chosen default depth: none"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn sweep_matches_direct_session_accounting() {
        let sweep = SweepConfig {
            depths: vec![1, 2],
            tokens_per_depth: 12,
            winner_band: DEFAULT_WINNER_BAND,
        };
        let base = SpecConfig::default();
        let diag = RecDiag::default();
        let report = run_sweep(&sweep, &base, PROMPT, fixture_factory, &diag)
            .expect("the fixture sweep runs");
        assert_eq!(report.rows.len(), 2);
        for row in &report.rows {
            // The same session, run directly at the same configuration,
            // must produce the identical counts: the sweep's accounting
            // is the session's accounting, not a second set of books.
            let mut config = base.clone();
            config.depth = row.depth;
            let mut session = testkit::build_session(config, 16);
            session.begin(PROMPT).expect("direct begin");
            session
                .generate(sweep.tokens_per_depth, &[])
                .expect("direct generate");
            let stats = session.finish();
            assert_eq!(row.rounds, stats.rounds, "depth {} rounds", row.depth);
            assert_eq!(row.proposed, stats.proposed, "depth {} proposed", row.depth);
            assert_eq!(row.accepted, stats.accepted, "depth {} accepted", row.depth);
            assert_eq!(
                row.tokens_emitted, stats.tokens_emitted,
                "depth {} emitted",
                row.depth
            );
            assert!(
                close(row.acceptance_rate, stats.acceptance_rate()),
                "depth {} acceptance rate is the stats rate",
                row.depth
            );
            assert!(row.wall_secs > 0.0, "a real wall was measured");
            assert!(row.tok_per_sec > 0.0, "tokens moved, so speed is real");
        }
        assert!(diag.saw("spec.sweep.begin"));
        assert!(diag.saw("spec.sweep.row depth=1"));
        assert!(diag.saw("spec.sweep.row depth=2"));
        assert!(diag.saw("spec.sweep.end chosen_depth="));
    }

    #[test]
    fn sweep_refuses_a_depth_beyond_the_draft_block_by_name() {
        let sweep = SweepConfig {
            depths: vec![99],
            tokens_per_depth: 4,
            winner_band: DEFAULT_WINNER_BAND,
        };
        let diag = RecDiag::default();
        let err = run_sweep(
            &sweep,
            &SpecConfig::default(),
            PROMPT,
            try_fixture_factory,
            &diag,
        )
        .expect_err("depth 99 cannot build against a block of 16");
        match err {
            SweepError::Build { depth, detail } => {
                assert_eq!(depth, 99);
                assert!(
                    detail.contains("draft depth 99 is out of range"),
                    "the session's named refusal survives the factory: {detail}"
                );
            }
            other => panic!("want a Build refusal for depth 99, got {other}"),
        }
        assert!(diag.saw("spec.sweep.refused depth=99"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn sweep_reports_a_factory_failure_with_its_depth() {
        let sweep = SweepConfig {
            depths: vec![3],
            tokens_per_depth: 4,
            winner_band: DEFAULT_WINNER_BAND,
        };
        let diag = RecDiag::default();
        let err = run_sweep(
            &sweep,
            &SpecConfig::default(),
            PROMPT,
            |_| -> std::result::Result<SpecSession, String> {
                Err("no backend in this test".to_string())
            },
            &diag,
        )
        .expect_err("a factory failure stops the sweep");
        match err {
            SweepError::Build { depth, detail } => {
                assert_eq!(depth, 3);
                assert!(detail.contains("no backend"));
            }
            other => panic!("want a Build refusal, got {other}"),
        }
        assert!(diag.saw("spec.sweep.refused depth=3"));
    }
}

//! Synthetic fixtures for this crate's tests: a small random-weight
//! Glimmer target (4 layers, hidden 32, vocab 128, window 16) and a small
//! random-weight DFlash draft with compatible geometry (hidden 32, the
//! same width as the target, exactly as the real draft file declares;
//! target layers [1, 3] of the target, conditioning width 64), wired the
//! real files wire: the draft borrows the target's embedding table and
//! head. Plus a sabotage compute that fails one attention call on command,
//! for the verify-refusal paths. Test code only.

use std::cell::Cell;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::rc::Rc;
use std::sync::Arc;

use cpu_compute::CpuCompute;
use dflash::{
    DflashConfig, DflashModel, TensorData, TensorSource as DraftSource, Weights as DraftWeights,
};
use muse_glimmer::{
    Cache, Dtype, GlimmerConfig, GlimmerError, GlimmerModel, LayerKind, PatternSource,
    PositionCache, TensorSource as TargetSource, TensorView, Weights as TargetWeights,
};

use crate::diag::NullDiag;
use crate::driver::CpuTarget;
use crate::sampler;
use crate::session::SpecSession;
use crate::speculator::{DflashSpeculator, SharedCompute};
use crate::SpecConfig;

/// Target hidden size in the fixtures.
pub const TARGET_HIDDEN: usize = 32;
/// Target vocabulary in the fixtures.
pub const VOCAB: usize = 128;
/// Draft mask token in the fixtures.
pub const MASK_TOKEN: u32 = 126;

/// Deterministic pseudo-random values in [-0.25, 0.25] (the same LCG the
/// cpu-compute forward tests use, so fixtures are stable everywhere).
pub struct Lcg(pub u64);

impl Lcg {
    /// Next pseudo-random value.
    pub fn next_f32(&mut self) -> f32 {
        self.0 = self
            .0
            .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
            .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
        let v = ((self.0 >> 40) & 0xFF_FFFF) as f32 / (1u64 << 24) as f32;
        (v - 0.5) * 0.5
    }
}

fn rand_vec(rng: &mut Lcg, n: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    (0..n).map(|_| rng.next_f32()).collect()
}

fn ones(n: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    vec![1.0; n]
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- target

/// The synthetic target's configuration.
pub fn target_config() -> GlimmerConfig {
    GlimmerConfig {
        name: Some("synthetic spec target".to_string()),
        block_count: 4,
        context_length: 256,
        hidden: TARGET_HIDDEN as u32,
        ffn_hidden: 64,
        q_heads: 4,
        kv_heads: 2,
        key_length: 8,
        value_length: 8,
        rope_freq_base: 10_000.0,
        rope_freq_base_swa: 10_000.0,
        rms_eps: 1e-6,
        sliding_window: 16,
        logit_softcap: 20.0,
        logit_scale: 0.5,
        vocab_size: VOCAB as u32,
        layers: vec![
            LayerKind::SlidingWindow,
            LayerKind::Global,
            LayerKind::SlidingWindow,
            LayerKind::Global,
        ],
        pattern_source: PatternSource::MeasuredFallback,
    }
}

struct TargetMapSource {
    tensors: HashMap<String, TensorView>,
}

impl TargetSource for TargetMapSource {
    fn tensor(&self, name: &str) -> muse_glimmer::Result<TensorView> {
        self.tensors
            .get(name)
            .cloned()
            .ok_or_else(|| GlimmerError::MissingTensor {
                name: name.to_string(),
            })
    }
}

fn f32_tensor(name: &str, shape: &[u64], values: Vec<f32>) -> TensorView {
    let data: Vec<u8> = values.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect();
    TensorView {
        name: name.to_string(),
        dtype: Dtype::F32,
        shape: shape.to_vec(),
        data: Arc::from(data.into_boxed_slice()),
    }
}

/// A built target plus the borrowed tensors the draft speculator needs,
/// in `dflash::TensorData` form (the same values the target loaded).
pub struct TargetFixture {
    /// The target model, forwarding through the given compute.
    pub model: GlimmerModel,
    /// The target's embedding table, token-major rows.
    pub embedding: TensorData,
    /// The target's LM head, token-major rows.
    pub output: TensorData,
}

/// Build the synthetic target over `compute`.
pub fn build_target(compute: Box<dyn muse_glimmer::Compute>) -> TargetFixture {
    let cfg = target_config();
    let hidden = cfg.hidden as usize;
    let ffn = cfg.ffn_hidden as usize;
    let qw = cfg.q_width() as usize;
    let kw = cfg.k_width() as usize;
    let vw = cfg.v_width() as usize;
    let vocab = cfg.vocab_size as usize;
    let head_dim = cfg.key_length as usize;
    let mut rng = Lcg(0x5eed_0001);
    let mut tensors: HashMap<String, TensorView> = HashMap::new();
    let mut put = |name: String, shape: &[u64], values: Vec<f32>| {
        tensors.insert(name.clone(), f32_tensor(&name, shape, values));
    };
    let emb_values = rand_vec(&mut rng, vocab * hidden);
    put(
        "token_embd.weight".to_string(),
        &[hidden as u64, vocab as u64],
        emb_values.clone(),
    );
    put(
        "output_norm.weight".to_string(),
        &[hidden as u64],
        ones(hidden),
    );
    let head_values = rand_vec(&mut rng, vocab * hidden);
    put(
        "output.weight".to_string(),
        &[hidden as u64, vocab as u64],
        head_values.clone(),
    );
    for layer in 0..cfg.block_count as usize {
        let name = |suffix: &str| format!("blk.{layer}.{suffix}");
        put(name("attn_norm.weight"), &[hidden as u64], ones(hidden));
        put(
            name("attn_q.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64, qw as u64],
            rand_vec(&mut rng, hidden * qw),
        );
        put(
            name("attn_k.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64, kw as u64],
            rand_vec(&mut rng, hidden * kw),
        );
        put(
            name("attn_v.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64, vw as u64],
            rand_vec(&mut rng, hidden * vw),
        );
        put(
            name("attn_q_norm.weight"),
            &[head_dim as u64],
            ones(head_dim),
        );
        put(
            name("attn_k_norm.weight"),
            &[head_dim as u64],
            ones(head_dim),
        );
        put(
            name("attn_gate.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64, qw as u64],
            rand_vec(&mut rng, hidden * qw),
        );
        put(
            name("attn_output.weight"),
            &[qw as u64, hidden as u64],
            rand_vec(&mut rng, qw * hidden),
        );
        put(
            name("post_attention_norm.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64],
            ones(hidden),
        );
        put(name("ffn_norm.weight"), &[hidden as u64], ones(hidden));
        put(
            name("ffn_gate.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64, ffn as u64],
            rand_vec(&mut rng, hidden * ffn),
        );
        put(
            name("ffn_up.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64, ffn as u64],
            rand_vec(&mut rng, hidden * ffn),
        );
        put(
            name("ffn_down.weight"),
            &[ffn as u64, hidden as u64],
            rand_vec(&mut rng, ffn * hidden),
        );
        put(name("post_ffw_norm.weight"), &[hidden as u64], ones(hidden));
    }
    let source = TargetMapSource { tensors };
    let weights = TargetWeights::load(&source, &cfg).expect("synthetic target weights load");
    TargetFixture {
        model: GlimmerModel::new(cfg, weights, compute),
        embedding: TensorData {
            name: "token_embd.weight".to_string(),
            shape: vec![hidden as u64, vocab as u64],
            data: emb_values,
        },
        output: TensorData {
            name: "output.weight".to_string(),
            shape: vec![hidden as u64, vocab as u64],
            data: head_values,
        },
    }
}

/// The plain greedy reference: prompt through a fresh target, then
/// single-token argmax steps. This is what speculative output must equal
/// at temperature 0.
pub fn plain_greedy(prompt: &[u32], count: usize) -> Vec<u32> {
    let fixture = build_target(Box::new(CpuCompute::new()));
    let model = fixture.model;
    let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
    let mut logits = model.forward(prompt, &mut cache).expect("plain prefill");
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(count);
    for i in 0..count {
        let token = sampler::argmax(&logits);
        out.push(token);
        if i + 1 < count {
            logits = model.forward(&[token], &mut cache).expect("plain step");
        }
    }
    out
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------- draft

/// The synthetic draft's configuration at a given block size.
pub fn draft_config(block_size: u32) -> DflashConfig {
    DflashConfig {
        name: Some("synthetic spec draft".to_string()),
        block_count: 2,
        context_length: 256,
        hidden: 32,
        ffn_hidden: 64,
        q_heads: 2,
        kv_heads: 1,
        key_length: 16,
        value_length: 16,
        rope_freq_base: 10_000.0,
        rms_eps: 1e-5,
        block_size,
        target_layers: vec![1, 3],
        sliding_window: 16,
        sliding_pattern: vec![true, false],
        causal_attention: false,
        mask_token_id: MASK_TOKEN,
        vocab_size: VOCAB as u32,
    }
}

struct DraftMapSource {
    tensors: HashMap<String, TensorData>,
}

impl DraftSource for DraftMapSource {
    fn tensor(&self, name: &str) -> dflash::Result<TensorData> {
        self.tensors
            .get(name)
            .cloned()
            .ok_or_else(|| dflash::DflashError::MissingTensor {
                name: name.to_string(),
            })
    }

    fn has_tensor(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.tensors.contains_key(name)
    }
}

/// Build the synthetic draft speculator borrowing `fixture`'s tensors.
pub fn build_speculator(fixture: &TargetFixture, block_size: u32) -> DflashSpeculator {
    let cfg = draft_config(block_size);
    let hidden = cfg.hidden as usize;
    let ffn = cfg.ffn_hidden as usize;
    let qw = cfg.q_width() as usize;
    let kw = cfg.k_width() as usize;
    let vw = cfg.v_width() as usize;
    let out_w = cfg.attn_out_width() as usize;
    let head_dim = cfg.key_length as usize;
    let cond_in = cfg.target_layers.len() * TARGET_HIDDEN;
    let mut rng = Lcg(0x5eed_0002);
    let mut tensors: HashMap<String, TensorData> = HashMap::new();
    let mut put = |name: String, shape: &[u64], values: Vec<f32>| {
        tensors.insert(
            name.clone(),
            TensorData {
                name,
                shape: shape.to_vec(),
                data: values,
            },
        );
    };
    put(
        "fc.weight".to_string(),
        &[cond_in as u64, hidden as u64],
        rand_vec(&mut rng, cond_in * hidden),
    );
    put(
        "enc.output_norm.weight".to_string(),
        &[hidden as u64],
        ones(hidden),
    );
    put(
        "output_norm.weight".to_string(),
        &[hidden as u64],
        ones(hidden),
    );
    for layer in 0..cfg.block_count as usize {
        let name = |suffix: &str| format!("blk.{layer}.{suffix}");
        put(name("attn_norm.weight"), &[hidden as u64], ones(hidden));
        put(
            name("attn_q.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64, qw as u64],
            rand_vec(&mut rng, hidden * qw),
        );
        put(
            name("attn_k.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64, kw as u64],
            rand_vec(&mut rng, hidden * kw),
        );
        put(
            name("attn_v.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64, vw as u64],
            rand_vec(&mut rng, hidden * vw),
        );
        put(
            name("attn_q_norm.weight"),
            &[head_dim as u64],
            ones(head_dim),
        );
        put(
            name("attn_k_norm.weight"),
            &[head_dim as u64],
            ones(head_dim),
        );
        put(
            name("attn_output.weight"),
            &[out_w as u64, hidden as u64],
            rand_vec(&mut rng, out_w * hidden),
        );
        put(name("ffn_norm.weight"), &[hidden as u64], ones(hidden));
        put(
            name("ffn_gate.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64, ffn as u64],
            rand_vec(&mut rng, hidden * ffn),
        );
        put(
            name("ffn_up.weight"),
            &[hidden as u64, ffn as u64],
            rand_vec(&mut rng, hidden * ffn),
        );
        put(
            name("ffn_down.weight"),
            &[ffn as u64, hidden as u64],
            rand_vec(&mut rng, ffn * hidden),
        );
    }
    let source = DraftMapSource { tensors };
    let weights = DraftWeights::load(&source, &cfg).expect("synthetic draft weights load");
    let model = DflashModel::new(cfg, weights);
    DflashSpeculator::new(model, fixture.embedding.clone(), fixture.output.clone())
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------- session

/// A session over the standard fixtures at the given draft block size.
pub fn build_session(config: SpecConfig, block_size: u32) -> SpecSession {
    let compute = Rc::new(CpuCompute::new());
    let fixture = build_target(Box::new(SharedCompute(compute.clone())));
    let speculator = build_speculator(&fixture, block_size);
    SpecSession::new(
        CpuTarget::new(fixture.model, compute),
        Some(speculator),
        config,
        Arc::new(NullDiag),
    )
    .expect("fixture session builds")
}

/// Build a session over the standard fixture target drafting with
/// the n-gram proposer under `ngram` config. The caller's
/// `SpecConfig` carries mode `ngram` and the depth.
pub fn build_ngram_session(config: SpecConfig, ngram: crate::NgramConfig) -> SpecSession {
    let compute = Rc::new(CpuCompute::new());
    let fixture = build_target(Box::new(SharedCompute(compute.clone())));
    let proposer = crate::NgramProposer::new(ngram, VOCAB).expect("fixture proposer builds");
    SpecSession::new_ngram(
        CpuTarget::new(fixture.model, compute),
        Some(proposer),
        config,
        Arc::new(NullDiag),
    )
    .expect("fixture n-gram session builds")
}

/// A compute that delegates to a shared [`CpuCompute`] but, while armed,
/// fails exactly the next attention call and then disarms itself. Used to
/// force a one-shot verify refusal mid-round.
pub struct SabotageCompute {
    inner: Rc<CpuCompute>,
    armed: Rc<Cell<bool>>,
}

impl muse_glimmer::Compute for SabotageCompute {
    fn embed(
        &self,
        table: &muse_glimmer::TensorView,
        tokens: &[u32],
        cfg: &GlimmerConfig,
    ) -> muse_glimmer::Result<Vec<f32>> {
        self.inner.embed(table, tokens, cfg)
    }
    fn rms_norm(
        &self,
        x: &[f32],
        weight: &muse_glimmer::TensorView,
        rows: usize,
        eps: f32,
    ) -> muse_glimmer::Result<Vec<f32>> {
        self.inner.rms_norm(x, weight, rows, eps)
    }
    fn rms_norm_plain(&self, x: &[f32], rows: usize, eps: f32) -> muse_glimmer::Result<Vec<f32>> {
        self.inner.rms_norm_plain(x, rows, eps)
    }
    fn proj(
        &self,
        x: &[f32],
        weight: &muse_glimmer::TensorView,
        rows: usize,
    ) -> muse_glimmer::Result<Vec<f32>> {
        self.inner.proj(x, weight, rows)
    }
    fn attention(
        &self,
        req: &muse_glimmer::AttentionRequest,
        cache: &mut dyn Cache,
    ) -> muse_glimmer::Result<Vec<f32>> {
        if self.armed.get() {
            self.armed.set(false);
            return Err(GlimmerError::StepFailed {
                step: "attention",
                detail: "sabotaged attention for the refusal test".to_string(),
            });
        }
        self.inner.attention(req, cache)
    }
    fn attn_gate(&self, attn_out: &[f32], gate: &[f32]) -> muse_glimmer::Result<Vec<f32>> {
        self.inner.attn_gate(attn_out, gate)
    }
    fn add(&self, a: &[f32], b: &[f32]) -> muse_glimmer::Result<Vec<f32>> {
        self.inner.add(a, b)
    }
    fn swiglu_ffn(
        &self,
        x: &[f32],
        w: &muse_glimmer::LayerWeights,
        rows: usize,
        cfg: &GlimmerConfig,
    ) -> muse_glimmer::Result<Vec<f32>> {
        self.inner.swiglu_ffn(x, w, rows, cfg)
    }
    fn lm_head(
        &self,
        x: &[f32],
        head: &muse_glimmer::TensorView,
        cfg: &GlimmerConfig,
    ) -> muse_glimmer::Result<Vec<f32>> {
        self.inner.lm_head(x, head, cfg)
    }
}

/// A session whose target compute can be armed to refuse one attention
/// call. Returns the session and the arming switch.
pub fn build_sabotage_session(config: SpecConfig) -> (SpecSession, Rc<Cell<bool>>) {
    let compute = Rc::new(CpuCompute::new());
    let armed = Rc::new(Cell::new(false));
    let sabotage = SabotageCompute {
        inner: compute.clone(),
        armed: armed.clone(),
    };
    let fixture = build_target(Box::new(sabotage));
    let speculator = build_speculator(&fixture, 5);
    let session = SpecSession::new(
        CpuTarget::new(fixture.model, compute),
        Some(speculator),
        config,
        Arc::new(NullDiag),
    )
    .expect("sabotage fixture session builds");
    (session, armed)
}
