===== FILE: crates/muse-glimmer/src/metadata.rs =====
//! Read access to GGUF metadata, abstracted behind a trait.
//!
//! The config parser never touches a GGUF file directly. It reads through
//! [`Metadata`], which the loader crate (TODO T-2.1, `itak-loader` in
//! this workspace) implements over the `gguf` crate's parsed file.
//! Keeping the parser behind this seam means config logic is testable
//! with an in-memory map and the loader can be dropped in without
//! touching this crate.
//!
//! Implementor contract: GGUF stores integers at several widths. The
//! getters coerce any integer width the file used into the requested
//! type, and return `None` only when the key is absent or holds a value
//! of a genuinely different kind (a string where a number was required).

use std::collections::HashMap;

/// Typed read access to a GGUF file's metadata block.
pub trait Metadata {
    /// String value for `key`, or `None` when absent.
    fn get_string(&self, key: &str) -> Option<String>;
    /// Unsigned 32-bit value for `key`, coerced from any integer width
    /// the file used, or `None` when absent.
    fn get_u32(&self, key: &str) -> Option<u32>;
    /// 32-bit float value for `key`, coerced from any float width the
    /// file used, or `None` when absent.
    fn get_f32(&self, key: &str) -> Option<f32>;
    /// Element count of the array stored at `key`, or `None` when absent.
    /// The config reads the vocabulary size from the length of the
    /// tokenizer token array, which is how GGUF carries it.
    fn get_array_len(&self, key: &str) -> Option<usize>;
    /// Elements of the bool array stored at `key`, or `None` when
    /// absent or not a bool array. The sliding-window pattern key is
    /// carried this way: one bool per layer, `true` for a
    /// sliding-window layer, exactly llama.cpp's `is_swa` semantics
    /// (src/llama-model.cpp: `load_swa_pattern` reads the array form
    /// of the key before any other shape).
    fn get_bool_array(&self, key: &str) -> Option<Vec<bool>>;
}

/// In-memory [`Metadata`] for tests and tools. Not a file parser: it
/// holds exactly what the caller put in it, which is what makes missing
/// key tests honest (a key that was not inserted is absent, full stop).
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct MapMetadata {
    strings: HashMap<String, String>,
    u32s: HashMap<String, u32>,
    f32s: HashMap<String, f32>,
    array_lens: HashMap<String, usize>,
    bool_arrays: HashMap<String, Vec<bool>>,
}

impl MapMetadata {
    /// An empty metadata map.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    /// Insert a string value.
    pub fn insert_string(&mut self, key: &str, value: &str) {
        self.strings.insert(key.to_string(), value.to_string());
    }

    /// Insert an unsigned 32-bit value.
    pub fn insert_u32(&mut self, key: &str, value: u32) {
        self.u32s.insert(key.to_string(), value);
    }

    /// Insert a 32-bit float value.
    pub fn insert_f32(&mut self, key: &str, value: f32) {
        self.f32s.insert(key.to_string(), value);
    }

    /// Insert an array length.
    pub fn insert_array_len(&mut self, key: &str, len: usize) {
        self.array_lens.insert(key.to_string(), len);
    }

    /// Insert a bool array.
    pub fn insert_bool_array(&mut self, key: &str, values: Vec<bool>) {
        self.bool_arrays.insert(key.to_string(), values);
    }

    /// Remove a key from every map, for missing-key tests.
    pub fn remove(&mut self, key: &str) {
        self.strings.remove(key);
        self.u32s.remove(key);
        self.f32s.remove(key);
        self.array_lens.remove(key);
        self.bool_arrays.remove(key);
    }
}

impl Metadata for MapMetadata {
    fn get_string(&self, key: &str) -> Option<String> {
        self.strings.get(key).cloned()
    }

    fn get_u32(&self, key: &str) -> Option<u32> {
        self.u32s.get(key).copied()
    }

    fn get_f32(&self, key: &str) -> Option<f32> {
        self.f32s.get(key).copied()
    }

    fn get_array_len(&self, key: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        self.array_lens.get(key).copied()
    }

    fn get_bool_array(&self, key: &str) -> Option<Vec<bool>> {
        self.bool_arrays.get(key).cloned()
    }
}

===== END FILE: crates/muse-glimmer/src/metadata.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/muse-glimmer/src/model.rs =====
//! [`GlimmerModel`]: config plus weights plus compute, and the forward
//! pass that ties them together.
//!
//! The forward follows the reference graph in llama.cpp
//! (src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp); its conventions were settled from
//! that source in the Run B follow-up (see
//! crates/itak-loader/INTEGRATION-RUN-B.md):
//!
//! - Embedding rows pass a WEIGHTLESS RMSNorm (eps = the file's)
//!   before layer 0; there is no embedding scale factor.
//! - Per layer: pre-attention norm, Q/K/V projections, per-head Q
//!   and K norms, attention of the layer's kind, and the sigmoid
//!   attention gate, whose projection reads the same normed input
//!   as Q/K/V and which multiplies the attention output before the
//!   output projection.
//! - Each sub-block's output passes its POST norm (eps hardcoded
//!   1e-8 in the reference graph) BEFORE the residual add:
//!   `x = x + post_norm(branch)`. The residual stream itself is
//!   never renormalized.
//! - Every stored-norm multiplication is plain `x * w`. The
//!   Gemma-style (1 + w) shift was folded into the four per-layer
//!   norm weights at conversion time (conversion/muse_glimmer.py:
//!   `norm_shift`); the final norm was deliberately left unshifted,
//!   which is why its stored weights center on zero.
//! - RoPE runs on the sliding-window layers only, at the SWA base,
//!   in ggml's NORM (interleaved, adjacent-pair) mode; the global
//!   layers are NoPE.
//! - The head is: final norm, untied lm_head, multiply by
//!   `logit_scale`, then softcap `cap * tanh(z / cap)`.
//!
//! Input validation (non-empty, token range) is done here, for real,
//! before any compute step runs. Everything else delegates to
//! [`Compute`]; with [`UnimplementedCompute`] installed, the first step
//! refuses by name, which is the correct skeleton behavior.

use std::sync::Arc;

use crate::cache::Cache;
use crate::compute::{AttentionRequest, Compute};
use crate::config::GlimmerConfig;
use crate::diag::{Diag, NullDiag};
use crate::error::{GlimmerError, Result};
use crate::trace::{NullTrace, TraceSink};
use crate::weights::Weights;

/// Epsilon for the two post norms (post-attention, post-FFN). The
/// reference graph hardcodes 1e-8 for these, independent of the
/// file's RMS epsilon used by every other norm
/// (src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp: `post_norm_eps`).
pub(crate) const POST_NORM_EPS: f32 = 1e-8;

/// The residual stream entering one layer during a forward pass,
/// captured by the captured-states forward variants
/// ([`GlimmerModel::forward_capturing`] and
/// [`GlimmerModel::forward_block_capturing`]).
///
/// `rows` is row-major `[tokens][hidden]`: the exact values the
/// layer's pre-attention norm read during this pass, which for
/// layer 0 is the embedding output after its weightless RMSNorm and
/// for every later layer is the previous layer's output. This is
/// the tensor llama.cpp's target graph exposes as `t_layer_inp`
/// (src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp) and the conditioning input the
/// DFlash draft consumes at the layers its own metadata names
/// (SPEC-itak-spec Q1, settled 2026-10-30).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct LayerInputCapture {
    /// The layer whose input this is.
    pub layer: usize,
    /// Row-major `[tokens][hidden]` residual rows entering `layer`.
    pub rows: Vec<f32>,
}

/// A Muse Glimmer model ready (structurally) to run.
pub struct GlimmerModel {
    config: GlimmerConfig,
    weights: Weights,
    compute: Box<dyn Compute>,
    diag: Arc<dyn Diag>,
}

impl GlimmerModel {
    /// Assemble a model from its parts, with a silent diagnostic sink.
    pub fn new(config: GlimmerConfig, weights: Weights, compute: Box<dyn Compute>) -> Self {
        GlimmerModel {
            config,
            weights,
            compute,
            diag: Arc::new(NullDiag),
        }
    }

    /// Assemble a model with a diagnostic sink attached. Every refusal
    /// and every completed pass emits through it.
    pub fn with_diag(
        config: GlimmerConfig,
        weights: Weights,
        compute: Box<dyn Compute>,
        diag: Arc<dyn Diag>,
    ) -> Self {
        GlimmerModel {
            config,
            weights,
            compute,
            diag,
        }
    }

    /// The model's configuration.
    pub fn config(&self) -> &GlimmerConfig {
        &self.config
    }

    /// The input validation both forward entry points share, run
    /// for real before any compute step: non-empty, every token in
    /// vocabulary.
    fn validate_tokens(&self, tokens: &[u32]) -> Result<()> {
        if tokens.is_empty() {
            return Err(GlimmerError::EmptyInput);
        }
        for &token in tokens {
            if token >= self.config.vocab_size {
                return Err(GlimmerError::TokenOutOfRange {
                    token,
                    vocab_size: self.config.vocab_size,
                });
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Run one forward pass over `tokens` and return the next-token
    /// logits for the final position, softcapped and scaled per the
    /// file's own `final_logit_softcapping` and `logit_scale`.
    ///
    /// On success the cache advances by `tokens.len()`; on any refusal
    /// the cache is untouched and the error names the step or input
    /// that failed.
    pub fn forward(&self, tokens: &[u32], cache: &mut dyn Cache) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        self.validate_tokens(tokens)?;
        self.diag.event(
            "forward.begin",
            &format!(
                "tokens={} position={} layers={}",
                tokens.len(),
                cache.position(),
                self.config.block_count
            ),
        );

        let (x, _) = self.forward_rows(tokens, cache, &[], &mut NullTrace)?;
        let logits = self.finish_last(&x, tokens.len(), &mut NullTrace)?;

        cache.advance(tokens.len());
        self.diag.event(
            "forward.end",
            &format!("logits={} position={}", logits.len(), cache.position()),
        );
        Ok(logits)
    }

    /// The same forward as [`forward`](Self::forward), additionally
    /// reporting the residual stream at every stage boundary to
    /// `sink` (see the [`trace`](crate::trace) module for the stage
    /// list and line format). This is the per-layer diff path: run
    /// both engines over the same prompt ids, reduce both to the
    /// same statistics, and the first stage whose statistics
    /// disagree names the layer that broke. The logits returned are
    /// the ordinary forward's, through the same code: every other
    /// entry point passes a [`NullTrace`] into the shared body.
    pub fn forward_traced(
        &self,
        tokens: &[u32],
        cache: &mut dyn Cache,
        sink: &mut dyn TraceSink,
    ) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        self.validate_tokens(tokens)?;
        self.diag.event(
            "forward_traced.begin",
            &format!(
                "tokens={} position={} layers={}",
                tokens.len(),
                cache.position(),
                self.config.block_count
            ),
        );

        let (x, _) = self.forward_rows(tokens, cache, &[], sink)?;
        let logits = self.finish_last(&x, tokens.len(), sink)?;

        cache.advance(tokens.len());
        self.diag.event(
            "forward_traced.end",
            &format!("logits={} position={}", logits.len(), cache.position()),
        );
        Ok(logits)
    }

    /// One trace capture: hand the stage to the sink and note it on
    /// the diagnostic channel, so a traced run's stages are visible
    /// in the diag stream as well as in the dump.
    fn capture(
        &self,
        sink: &mut dyn TraceSink,
        stage: &str,
        tensor: &[f32],
        rows: usize,
        cols: usize,
    ) {
        sink.capture(stage, tensor, rows, cols);
        self.diag.event("trace.capture", stage);
    }

    /// [`GlimmerModel::forward`] plus captured layer inputs: runs the
    /// identical pass and additionally returns, for each layer index
    /// in `capture_layers`, the residual rows that entered that
    /// layer ([`LayerInputCapture`], in ascending layer order).
    ///
    /// Capture is additive by construction: the layer loop's math,
    /// step order, and cache contract are `forward`'s, and the only
    /// extra work is cloning the residual at the named layers. The
    /// speculation stack's DFlash proposer consumes these rows
    /// (SPEC-itak-spec Q1); nothing in the verified forward path
    /// depends on them.
    ///
    /// A capture index at or past the layer count is refused with
    /// [`GlimmerError::CaptureLayerOutOfRange`] before any compute
    /// runs, and (like every refusal) leaves the cache untouched.
    pub fn forward_capturing(
        &self,
        tokens: &[u32],
        cache: &mut dyn Cache,
        capture_layers: &[usize],
    ) -> Result<(Vec<f32>, Vec<LayerInputCapture>)> {
        self.validate_tokens(tokens)?;
        self.validate_capture(capture_layers)?;
        self.diag.event(
            "forward_capturing.begin",
            &format!(
                "tokens={} position={} capture={capture_layers:?}",
                tokens.len(),
                cache.position()
            ),
        );

        let (x, captures) = self.forward_rows(tokens, cache, capture_layers, &mut NullTrace)?;
        let logits = self.finish_last(&x, tokens.len(), &mut NullTrace)?;

        cache.advance(tokens.len());
        self.diag.event(
            "forward_capturing.end",
            &format!(
                "logits={} captured={} position={}",
                logits.len(),
                captures.len(),
                cache.position()
            ),
        );
        Ok((logits, captures))
    }

    /// Block forward with per-position logits (SPEC-itak-spec
    /// Section 3, dependency E1): run `tokens` through the same layer
    /// loop [`GlimmerModel::forward`] runs, and return the finished
    /// logits for EVERY position in the block, row-major
    /// `[block][vocab]`, each row softcapped and scaled exactly as
    /// `forward` finishes its single row. Row `i` is the distribution
    /// for the token following the prefix extended by
    /// `tokens[..=i]`, which is what a speculative verify round
    /// consumes.
    ///
    /// This is not a second forward: `forward` is this method's
    /// block-of-one case read at the last row (plus the positions the
    /// block already consumed). The cache contract is `forward`'s:
    /// on success the cache advances by `tokens.len()`; on any
    /// refusal the cache is untouched and the error names the step
    /// or input that failed.
    pub fn forward_block(&self, tokens: &[u32], cache: &mut dyn Cache) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        self.validate_tokens(tokens)?;
        self.diag.event(
            "forward_block.begin",
            &format!(
                "tokens={} position={} layers={}",
                tokens.len(),
                cache.position(),
                self.config.block_count
            ),
        );

        let (x, _) = self.forward_rows(tokens, cache, &[], &mut NullTrace)?;
        let out = self.finish_block(&x, tokens.len())?;

        cache.advance(tokens.len());
        self.diag.event(
            "forward_block.end",
            &format!(
                "rows={} logits={} position={}",
                tokens.len(),
                out.len(),
                cache.position()
            ),
        );
        Ok(out)
    }

    /// [`GlimmerModel::forward_block`] plus captured layer inputs:
    /// the block variant of [`GlimmerModel::forward_capturing`], for
    /// a verify round that also feeds a DFlash proposer. Same
    /// additive-capture contract and same refusal rules.
    pub fn forward_block_capturing(
        &self,
        tokens: &[u32],
        cache: &mut dyn Cache,
        capture_layers: &[usize],
    ) -> Result<(Vec<f32>, Vec<LayerInputCapture>)> {
        self.validate_tokens(tokens)?;
        self.validate_capture(capture_layers)?;
        self.diag.event(
            "forward_block_capturing.begin",
            &format!(
                "tokens={} position={} capture={capture_layers:?}",
                tokens.len(),
                cache.position()
            ),
        );

        let (x, captures) = self.forward_rows(tokens, cache, capture_layers, &mut NullTrace)?;
        let out = self.finish_block(&x, tokens.len())?;

        cache.advance(tokens.len());
        self.diag.event(
            "forward_block_capturing.end",
            &format!(
                "rows={} logits={} captured={} position={}",
                tokens.len(),
                out.len(),
                captures.len(),
                cache.position()
            ),
        );
        Ok((out, captures))
    }

    /// Every capture index must name a real layer. Checked before
    /// any compute runs so a bad request cannot consume cache
    /// positions or backend state.
    fn validate_capture(&self, capture_layers: &[usize]) -> Result<()> {
        for &layer in capture_layers {
            if layer >= self.config.block_count as usize {
                return Err(GlimmerError::CaptureLayerOutOfRange {
                    layer,
                    block_count: self.config.block_count,
                });
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// The head application `forward` performs: final norm and
    /// lm_head over the LAST row of the final hidden states, then
    /// the file's softcap and scale.
    fn finish_last(&self, x: &[f32], rows: usize, sink: &mut dyn TraceSink) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        let cfg = &self.config;
        let c = &*self.compute;
        let hidden = cfg.hidden as usize;
        let last = &x[(rows - 1) * hidden..rows * hidden];
        let normed = c.rms_norm(last, &self.weights.final_norm, 1, cfg.rms_eps)?;
        self.capture(sink, "final_norm", &normed, 1, hidden);
        let mut logits = c.lm_head(&normed, &self.weights.output, cfg)?;
        softcap_scale(&mut logits, cfg.logit_softcap, cfg.logit_scale);
        let vocab = logits.len();
        self.capture(sink, "logits", &logits, 1, vocab);
        Ok(logits)
    }

    /// The head application `forward_block` performs: final norm,
    /// lm_head, softcap and scale for EVERY row, row-major
    /// `[rows][vocab]`.
    fn finish_block(&self, x: &[f32], rows: usize) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        let cfg = &self.config;
        let c = &*self.compute;
        let hidden = cfg.hidden as usize;
        let vocab = cfg.vocab_size as usize;
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(rows * vocab);
        for r in 0..rows {
            let row = &x[r * hidden..(r + 1) * hidden];
            let normed = c.rms_norm(row, &self.weights.final_norm, 1, cfg.rms_eps)?;
            let mut logits = c.lm_head(&normed, &self.weights.output, cfg)?;
            softcap_scale(&mut logits, cfg.logit_softcap, cfg.logit_scale);
            out.extend_from_slice(&logits);
        }
        Ok(out)
    }

    /// The shared body of all forward entry points: embedding,
    /// the weightless embedding norm, and the per-layer loop,
    /// returning the final hidden states `[tokens.len(), hidden]`
    /// plus any requested layer-input captures.
    /// Reads and appends KV through `cache` (via the compute
    /// backend's attention step) but does not advance the position
    /// contract: the entry points advance it once their head
    /// application has succeeded, so a refused pass leaves the cache
    /// untouched.
    ///
    /// Capture is a clone of the residual at the top of the named
    /// layers' iterations, taken before that layer's pre-attention
    /// norm reads it. It performs no compute calls, so a capturing
    /// pass makes exactly the step sequence a plain pass makes.
    fn forward_rows(
        &self,
        tokens: &[u32],
        cache: &mut dyn Cache,
        capture_layers: &[usize],
        sink: &mut dyn TraceSink,
    ) -> Result<(Vec<f32>, Vec<LayerInputCapture>)> {
        let cfg = &self.config;
        let rows = tokens.len();
        let c = &*self.compute;
        let mut captures: Vec<LayerInputCapture> = Vec::new();

        let mut x = c.embed(&self.weights.embedding, tokens, cfg)?;
        // The reference graph normalizes the embedding output with a
        // weightless RMSNorm before the first layer
        // (src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp: build_norm with no weight).
        x = c.rms_norm_plain(&x, rows, cfg.rms_eps)?;
        self.capture(sink, "embed", &x, rows, cfg.hidden as usize);

        for (index, (kind, w)) in cfg
            .layers
            .iter()
            .zip(self.weights.layers.iter())
            .enumerate()
        {
            if capture_layers.contains(&index) {
                captures.push(LayerInputCapture {
                    layer: index,
                    rows: x.clone(),
                });
            }
            let residual = x;

            let h = c.rms_norm(&residual, &w.attn_norm, rows, cfg.rms_eps)?;
            let q = c.proj(&h, &w.attn_q, rows)?;
            let k = c.proj(&h, &w.attn_k, rows)?;
            let v = c.proj(&h, &w.attn_v, rows)?;
            let q = c.rms_norm(&q, &w.attn_q_norm, rows * cfg.q_heads as usize, cfg.rms_eps)?;
            let k = c.rms_norm(
                &k,
                &w.attn_k_norm,
                rows * cfg.kv_heads as usize,
                cfg.rms_eps,
            )?;
            let attn = c.attention(
                &AttentionRequest {
                    q: &q,
                    k: &k,
                    v: &v,
                    layer: index,
                    kind: *kind,
                    cfg,
                },
                cache,
            )?;
            let gate = c.proj(&h, &w.attn_gate, rows)?;
            let attn = c.attn_gate(&attn, &gate)?;
            let out = c.proj(&attn, &w.attn_output, rows)?;
            // Post norm on the branch output, THEN the residual add:
            // the reference graph normalizes the sub-block output
            // (hardcoded eps 1e-8) and adds the untouched residual.
            let out = c.rms_norm(&out, &w.post_attention_norm, rows, POST_NORM_EPS)?;
            let after_attn = c.add(&residual, &out)?;
            self.capture(
                sink,
                &format!("layer.{index}.mid"),
                &after_attn,
                rows,
                cfg.hidden as usize,
            );

            let residual = after_attn;
            let h = c.rms_norm(&residual, &w.ffn_norm, rows, cfg.rms_eps)?;
            let ffn = c.swiglu_ffn(&h, w, rows, cfg)?;
            let ffn = c.rms_norm(&ffn, &w.post_ffw_norm, rows, POST_NORM_EPS)?;
            x = c.add(&residual, &ffn)?;
            self.capture(
                sink,
                &format!("layer.{index}.out"),
                &x,
                rows,
                cfg.hidden as usize,
            );
        }

        Ok((x, captures))
    }
}

/// The file's logit finishing, applied in place: multiply by the
/// logit scale FIRST, then softcap `cap * tanh(z / cap)` when the cap
/// is positive. The reference graph applies them in exactly this
/// order (src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp: `ggml_scale`, then
/// `build_softcap`). The order is invisible to argmax (both maps are
/// monotone) but changes every probability. Plain scalar math on the
/// logit vector, implemented here rather than delegated, and unit
/// tested below.
pub fn softcap_scale(logits: &mut [f32], cap: f32, scale: f32) {
    for z in logits.iter_mut() {
        *z *= scale;
        if cap > 0.0 {
            *z = cap * (*z / cap).tanh();
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::cache::PositionCache;
    use crate::compute::UnimplementedCompute;
    use crate::metadata::Metadata;
    use crate::testkit::tiny_metadata;
    use crate::weights::{Dtype, TensorSource, TensorView};
    use std::cell::RefCell;
    use std::collections::HashMap;

    /// Source that hands out a dummy tensor for any expected name.
    struct AnySource {
        names: HashMap<String, ()>,
    }

    impl TensorSource for AnySource {
        fn tensor(&self, name: &str) -> Result<TensorView> {
            if self.names.contains_key(name) {
                Ok(TensorView {
                    name: name.to_string(),
                    dtype: Dtype::F32,
                    shape: vec![1],
                    data: Arc::from(vec![0u8; 4].into_boxed_slice()),
                })
            } else {
                Err(GlimmerError::MissingTensor {
                    name: name.to_string(),
                })
            }
        }
    }

    fn tiny_model(compute: Box<dyn Compute>) -> (GlimmerModel, GlimmerConfig) {
        let meta = tiny_metadata();
        let cfg = GlimmerConfig::from_metadata(&meta).expect("tiny config");
        let names = crate::weights::expected_tensor_names(&cfg)
            .into_iter()
            .map(|n| (n, ()))
            .collect();
        let weights = Weights::load(&AnySource { names }, &cfg).expect("tiny weights");
        (GlimmerModel::new(cfg.clone(), weights, compute), cfg)
    }

    /// A compute stub that records its call order and returns zeros of
    /// plausible length. It verifies the forward's STRUCTURE: which
    /// steps run, in what order, for a two-layer model. It asserts
    /// nothing about numerics, which are the kernel crate's to prove.
    /// The call log is shared with the test through an `Rc` so the test
    /// can read it after the stub moves into the model.
    struct RecordingCompute {
        calls: std::rc::Rc<RefCell<Vec<&'static str>>>,
    }

    impl RecordingCompute {
        fn record(&self, step: &'static str) {
            self.calls.borrow_mut().push(step);
        }
    }

    impl Compute for RecordingCompute {
        fn embed(
            &self,
            _table: &TensorView,
            tokens: &[u32],
            cfg: &GlimmerConfig,
        ) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.record("embed");
            Ok(vec![0.0; tokens.len() * cfg.hidden as usize])
        }

        fn rms_norm(
            &self,
            x: &[f32],
            _weight: &TensorView,
            _rows: usize,
            _eps: f32,
        ) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.record("rms_norm");
            Ok(vec![0.0; x.len()])
        }

        fn rms_norm_plain(&self, x: &[f32], _rows: usize, _eps: f32) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.record("rms_norm_plain");
            Ok(vec![0.0; x.len()])
        }

        fn proj(&self, x: &[f32], _weight: &TensorView, _rows: usize) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.record("proj");
            Ok(vec![0.0; x.len()])
        }

        fn attention(
            &self,
            req: &AttentionRequest<'_>,
            _cache: &mut dyn Cache,
        ) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.record("attention");
            Ok(vec![0.0; req.q.len()])
        }

        fn attn_gate(&self, attn_out: &[f32], _gate: &[f32]) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.record("attn_gate");
            Ok(attn_out.to_vec())
        }

        fn add(&self, a: &[f32], _b: &[f32]) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.record("add");
            Ok(a.to_vec())
        }

        fn swiglu_ffn(
            &self,
            x: &[f32],
            _w: &crate::weights::LayerWeights,
            _rows: usize,
            _cfg: &GlimmerConfig,
        ) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.record("swiglu_ffn");
            Ok(vec![0.0; x.len()])
        }

        fn lm_head(&self, _x: &[f32], _head: &TensorView, cfg: &GlimmerConfig) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.record("lm_head");
            Ok(vec![0.0; cfg.vocab_size as usize])
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn unimplemented_compute_refuses_at_embed_by_name() {
        let (model, _cfg) = tiny_model(Box::new(UnimplementedCompute));
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        let err = model
            .forward(&[1, 2, 3], &mut cache)
            .expect_err("skeleton compute must refuse");
        assert_eq!(
            err.to_string(),
            "forward step is not implemented yet: embed"
        );
        assert!(matches!(err, GlimmerError::Unimplemented { step: "embed" }));
        // A refused pass must not advance the cache.
        assert_eq!(cache.position(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn forward_validates_input_before_any_compute() {
        let (model, cfg) = tiny_model(Box::new(UnimplementedCompute));
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        assert!(matches!(
            model.forward(&[], &mut cache),
            Err(GlimmerError::EmptyInput)
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            model.forward(&[cfg.vocab_size], &mut cache),
            Err(GlimmerError::TokenOutOfRange { .. })
        ));
        let meta_vocab = tiny_metadata().get_array_len("tokenizer.ggml.tokens");
        assert_eq!(meta_vocab, Some(128));
    }

    #[test]
    fn forward_walks_the_full_layer_structure_in_order() {
        let calls = std::rc::Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));
        let compute = Box::new(RecordingCompute {
            calls: calls.clone(),
        });
        let (model, _cfg) = tiny_model(compute);
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        let logits = model
            .forward(&[1, 2], &mut cache)
            .expect("recording compute completes the walk");
        assert_eq!(logits.len(), 128);
        assert!(logits.iter().all(|z| *z == 0.0));
        assert_eq!(cache.position(), 2);

        let one_layer: [&str; 16] = [
            "rms_norm", // attn pre-norm
            "proj",     // q
            "proj",     // k
            "proj",     // v
            "rms_norm", // q norm
            "rms_norm", // k norm
            "attention",
            "proj", // gate
            "attn_gate",
            "proj",     // output
            "rms_norm", // post-attention norm (branch, before the add)
            "add",
            "rms_norm", // ffn pre-norm
            "swiglu_ffn",
            "rms_norm", // post-ffn norm (branch, before the add)
            "add",
        ];
        let mut expected: Vec<&str> = vec!["embed", "rms_norm_plain"];
        expected.extend(one_layer);
        expected.extend(one_layer);
        expected.extend(["rms_norm", "lm_head"]);
        assert_eq!(calls.borrow().as_slice(), expected.as_slice());
    }

    #[test]
    fn forward_traced_captures_every_stage_in_order() {
        let calls = std::rc::Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));
        let compute = Box::new(RecordingCompute {
            calls: calls.clone(),
        });
        let (model, _cfg) = tiny_model(compute);
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        let mut log = crate::trace::TraceLog::new(4);
        let logits = model
            .forward_traced(&[1, 2], &mut cache, &mut log)
            .expect("traced forward completes the walk");
        assert_eq!(logits.len(), 128);
        assert_eq!(cache.position(), 2);

        let stages: Vec<&str> = log.records().iter().map(|r| r.stage.as_str()).collect();
        assert_eq!(
            stages,
            [
                "embed",
                "layer.0.mid",
                "layer.0.out",
                "layer.1.mid",
                "layer.1.out",
                "final_norm",
                "logits",
            ]
        );
        // The recording compute returns zeros, so every captured
        // statistic is zero and the shapes track the tiny config:
        // 2 rows of hidden 32 in the stream, 1 row at the finish.
        let embed = &log.records()[0];
        assert_eq!((embed.rows, embed.cols, embed.full.n), (2, 32, 64));
        assert_eq!(embed.full.mean, 0.0);
        let head = &log.records()[6];
        assert_eq!((head.rows, head.cols, head.full.n), (1, 128, 128));

        // The traced and untraced paths are the same code: a plain
        // forward over the same stub gives the same logits.
        let calls2 = std::rc::Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));
        let (model2, _cfg2) = tiny_model(Box::new(RecordingCompute { calls: calls2 }));
        let mut cache2 = PositionCache::new();
        let plain = model2
            .forward(&[1, 2], &mut cache2)
            .expect("plain forward completes the walk");
        assert_eq!(logits, plain);
    }

    #[test]
    fn forward_block_heads_every_row_through_the_same_loop() {
        let calls = std::rc::Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));
        let compute = Box::new(RecordingCompute {
            calls: calls.clone(),
        });
        let (model, _cfg) = tiny_model(compute);
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        let logits = model
            .forward_block(&[1, 2], &mut cache)
            .expect("recording compute completes the block walk");
        // [block][vocab] row-major: 2 rows of 128.
        assert_eq!(logits.len(), 2 * 128);
        assert_eq!(cache.position(), 2);

        // The layer walk is forward's, unchanged; what the block
        // adds is one (final norm, lm_head) pair per row, after it.
        let recorded = calls.borrow();
        let walk = &recorded[..recorded.len() - 4];
        let one_layer: [&str; 16] = [
            "rms_norm",
            "proj",
            "proj",
            "proj",
            "rms_norm",
            "rms_norm",
            "attention",
            "proj",
            "attn_gate",
            "proj",
            "rms_norm",
            "add",
            "rms_norm",
            "swiglu_ffn",
            "rms_norm",
            "add",
        ];
        let mut expected_walk: Vec<&str> = vec!["embed", "rms_norm_plain"];
        expected_walk.extend(one_layer);
        expected_walk.extend(one_layer);
        assert_eq!(walk, expected_walk.as_slice());
        assert_eq!(
            &recorded[recorded.len() - 4..],
            ["rms_norm", "lm_head", "rms_norm", "lm_head"].as_slice()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn forward_block_of_one_returns_forward_shape() {
        let calls = std::rc::Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));
        let compute = Box::new(RecordingCompute {
            calls: calls.clone(),
        });
        let (model, _cfg) = tiny_model(compute);
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        let block = model
            .forward_block(&[7], &mut cache)
            .expect("block of one runs");
        assert_eq!(block.len(), 128);
        assert_eq!(cache.position(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn forward_block_refuses_like_forward() {
        let (model, cfg) = tiny_model(Box::new(UnimplementedCompute));
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        assert!(matches!(
            model.forward_block(&[], &mut cache),
            Err(GlimmerError::EmptyInput)
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            model.forward_block(&[cfg.vocab_size], &mut cache),
            Err(GlimmerError::TokenOutOfRange { .. })
        ));
        let err = model
            .forward_block(&[1, 2, 3], &mut cache)
            .expect_err("skeleton compute must refuse");
        assert!(matches!(err, GlimmerError::Unimplemented { step: "embed" }));
        assert_eq!(cache.position(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn capturing_forward_makes_the_identical_step_sequence() {
        // Plain forward on one recording stub...
        let plain_calls = std::rc::Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));
        let (model, _cfg) = tiny_model(Box::new(RecordingCompute {
            calls: plain_calls.clone(),
        }));
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        let plain_logits = model.forward(&[1, 2], &mut cache).expect("plain forward");
        assert_eq!(cache.position(), 2);

        // ...and the capturing variant on a second one. Capture may
        // clone residuals; it may not add, drop, or reorder a single
        // compute step, and its logits and cache advance must match.
        let cap_calls = std::rc::Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));
        let (model, cfg) = tiny_model(Box::new(RecordingCompute {
            calls: cap_calls.clone(),
        }));
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        let (logits, captures) = model
            .forward_capturing(&[1, 2], &mut cache, &[1, 0])
            .expect("capturing forward");
        assert_eq!(logits, plain_logits);
        assert_eq!(cache.position(), 2);
        assert_eq!(
            cap_calls.borrow().as_slice(),
            plain_calls.borrow().as_slice()
        );
        // Captures come back in ascending layer order regardless of
        // request order, one per requested layer, each holding the
        // full [tokens][hidden] residual block.
        assert_eq!(captures.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(captures[0].layer, 0);
        assert_eq!(captures[1].layer, 1);
        for cap in &captures {
            assert_eq!(cap.rows.len(), 2 * cfg.hidden as usize);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn capturing_block_forward_captures_and_heads_every_row() {
        let calls = std::rc::Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));
        let (model, _cfg) = tiny_model(Box::new(RecordingCompute {
            calls: calls.clone(),
        }));
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        let (logits, captures) = model
            .forward_block_capturing(&[1, 2], &mut cache, &[0])
            .expect("capturing block forward");
        assert_eq!(logits.len(), 2 * 128);
        assert_eq!(captures.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(captures[0].layer, 0);
        assert_eq!(cache.position(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn capture_out_of_range_refuses_before_any_compute() {
        let calls = std::rc::Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));
        let (model, _cfg) = tiny_model(Box::new(RecordingCompute {
            calls: calls.clone(),
        }));
        let mut cache = PositionCache::new();
        // The tiny model has 2 layers; layer 2 does not exist.
        let err = model
            .forward_capturing(&[1], &mut cache, &[2])
            .expect_err("layer 2 of 2 must refuse");
        assert!(matches!(
            err,
            GlimmerError::CaptureLayerOutOfRange {
                layer: 2,
                block_count: 2
            }
        ));
        assert!(calls.borrow().is_empty(), "no compute step may run");
        assert_eq!(cache.position(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn softcap_scale_matches_the_formula() {
        let mut logits = vec![0.0, 20.0, -20.0, 1000.0];
        softcap_scale(&mut logits, 20.0, 0.5);
        assert_eq!(logits[0], 0.0);
        // Scale first, then cap: 20 * tanh(0.5 * 20 / 20)
        // = 20 * tanh(0.5) = 9.2423431. The opposite order would
        // give 0.5 * 20 * tanh(1) = 7.6159416, so this value tells
        // the two conventions apart.
        assert!((logits[1] - 9.242_343).abs() < 1e-5);
        assert!((logits[2] + 9.242_343).abs() < 1e-5);
        // Saturates at the cap itself, 20, because the scale is
        // applied before the cap, not after it.
        assert!((logits[3] - 20.0).abs() < 1e-4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn softcap_scale_with_no_cap_just_scales() {
        let mut logits = vec![2.0, -4.0];
        softcap_scale(&mut logits, 0.0, 0.25);
        assert_eq!(logits, vec![0.5, -1.0]);
    }
}

//! Shared fixtures for this crate's tests: metadata maps carrying the

/// Metadata exactly as measured in the real Muse-Glimmer-30B GGUF
/// (census 2026-10-29). Building the config from these values is the
/// closest a unit test gets to the real file without a 15 GiB fixture.
pub fn real_glimmer_metadata() -> MapMetadata {
    let mut m = MapMetadata::new();
    m.insert_string(KEY_ARCHITECTURE, "muse-glimmer");
    m.insert_string(KEY_NAME, "Muse Glimmer Hf");
    m.insert_u32(KEY_BLOCK_COUNT, 52);
    m.insert_u32(KEY_CONTEXT_LENGTH, 131_072);
    m.insert_u32(KEY_HIDDEN, 6656);
    m.insert_u32(KEY_FFN_HIDDEN, 19_968);
    m.insert_u32(KEY_Q_HEADS, 32);
    m.insert_u32(KEY_KV_HEADS, 2);
    m.insert_u32(KEY_KEY_LENGTH, 128);
    m.insert_u32(KEY_VALUE_LENGTH, 128);
    m.insert_f32(KEY_ROPE_FREQ_BASE, 500_000.0);
    m.insert_f32(KEY_RMS_EPS, 1e-5);
    m.insert_u32(KEY_SLIDING_WINDOW, 2048);
    // The pattern array exactly as stored in the real file's header
    // (read 2026-11-05): ARRAY of BOOL, `[true, true, true, false]`
    // repeated 13 times. The literal 52 values are quoted in
    // layer.rs's tests, which pin this construction to them.
    m.insert_bool_array(SWA_PATTERN_KEY, (0..52).map(|i| i % 4 != 3).collect());
    m.insert_f32(KEY_LOGIT_SOFTCAP, 20.0);
    m.insert_f32(KEY_LOGIT_SCALE, 0.196_116_13);
    m.insert_array_len(KEY_VOCAB_TOKENS, 202_048);
    m
}

===== FILE: crates/muse-glimmer/src/trace.rs =====
//! Per-layer activation tracing for the forward pass: the tooling
//! that localizes a forward numerics error to the first divergent
//! layer instead of guessing from end-to-end logits.
//!
//! [`GlimmerModel::forward_traced`](crate::GlimmerModel::forward_traced)
//! runs the ordinary forward and reports the residual stream at fixed
//! stage boundaries to a [`TraceSink`]:
//!
//! - `embed`: the residual stream entering layer 0: the embedding
//!   output after the graph's weightless embedding norm.
//! - `layer.<i>.mid`: layer `i`'s residual stream after the attention
//!   half (the post-attention norm applied to the attention branch
//!   output, then the residual add), entering the FFN half.
//! - `layer.<i>.out`: layer `i`'s residual stream after the full
//!   layer (the post-FFN norm applied to the FFN branch output, then
//!   the residual add).
//! - `final_norm`: the final norm's output for the last position.
//! - `logits`: the finished logits (softcapped and scaled).
//!
//! A sink receives the raw tensor plus its row/column shape. The
//! residual-stream stages are `rows x hidden`; `final_norm` and
//! `logits` are single rows. [`TraceLog`] is the collecting sink: it
//! reduces every capture to a [`TraceRecord`] of statistics (mean,
//! variance, max abs, first values) over the whole tensor and over
//! the last row separately, and formats records in the stable text
//! format below so two runs, or our run and a reference dump reduced
//! to the same statistics, can be diffed line by line.
//!
//! ## Line format (version 1)
//!
//! ```text
//! trace v=1 stage=<stage> rows=<r> cols=<c> n=<count> mean=<e> var=<e> max_abs=<e> last_mean=<e> last_var=<e> last_max_abs=<e> first=[<f>,...] last_first=[<f>,...]
//! ```
//!
//! Statistics are printed with `{:.6e}`, first values with `{:.6}`,
//! comma-separated with no spaces. Variance is the population
//! variance. The last-row fields describe the final position's
//! vector, the one the head reads; the whole-tensor fields catch
//! position-dependent errors (for example a RoPE geometry mistake)
//! that a last-row-only view would hide. A record whose stage is
//! missing on one side of a diff, or whose statistics first disagree
//! at some layer, is the localization signal this module exists to
//! produce.

/// Statistics over a slice of activations, computed in f64 so the
/// reduction itself is never the noise source.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct VecStats {
    /// Number of values reduced.
    pub n: usize,
    /// Arithmetic mean.
    pub mean: f64,
    /// Population variance.
    pub var: f64,
    /// Largest absolute value.
    pub max_abs: f64,
    /// The first `first_n` values, in order (fewer if the slice is
    /// shorter).
    pub first: Vec<f32>,
}

/// Reduce `data` to its statistics, keeping the first `first_n`
/// values verbatim. An empty slice reduces to zeros with `n = 0`.
pub fn stats_of(data: &[f32], first_n: usize) -> VecStats {
    if data.is_empty() {
        return VecStats {
            n: 0,
            mean: 0.0,
            var: 0.0,
            max_abs: 0.0,
            first: Vec::new(),
        };
    }
    let mut sum = 0.0f64;
    let mut sumsq = 0.0f64;
    let mut max_abs = 0.0f64;
    for &v in data {
        let v = f64::from(v);
        sum += v;
        sumsq += v * v;
        if v.abs() > max_abs {
            max_abs = v.abs();
        }
    }
    let n = data.len() as f64;
    let mean = sum / n;
    // E[x^2] - mean^2 can go negligibly negative on constant input;
    // clamp at zero rather than emit a negative variance.
    let var = (sumsq / n - mean * mean).max(0.0);
    VecStats {
        n: data.len(),
        mean,
        var,
        max_abs,
        first: data.iter().take(first_n).copied().collect(),
    }
}

/// A receiver for forward-pass stage captures. Implementations must
/// be cheap or document their cost: the forward calls
/// [`TraceSink::capture`] once per stage boundary.
pub trait TraceSink {
    /// One stage boundary: `stage` names the point in the pass,
    /// `tensor` is the row-major `rows x cols` activation there.
    fn capture(&mut self, stage: &str, tensor: &[f32], rows: usize, cols: usize);
}

/// The default sink: drops every capture. The untraced
/// [`GlimmerModel::forward`](crate::GlimmerModel::forward) runs
/// through this sink, so the traced and untraced paths are the same
/// code.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct NullTrace;

impl TraceSink for NullTrace {
    fn capture(&mut self, _stage: &str, _tensor: &[f32], _rows: usize, _cols: usize) {}
}

/// One reduced capture: stage name, shape, and the statistics of
/// the whole tensor and of its last row.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct TraceRecord {
    /// Stage name as captured (for example `layer.17.out`).
    pub stage: String,
    /// Row count of the captured tensor.
    pub rows: usize,
    /// Column count of the captured tensor.
    pub cols: usize,
    /// Statistics over the whole tensor.
    pub full: VecStats,
    /// Statistics over the last row (the final position).
    pub last_row: VecStats,
}

impl TraceRecord {
    /// This record in the stable version-1 line format documented
    /// at the top of this module.
    pub fn to_line(&self) -> String {
        format!(
            "trace v=1 stage={} rows={} cols={} n={} mean={:.6e} var={:.6e} max_abs={:.6e} \
             last_mean={:.6e} last_var={:.6e} last_max_abs={:.6e} first=[{}] last_first=[{}]",
            self.stage,
            self.rows,
            self.cols,
            self.full.n,
            self.full.mean,
            self.full.var,
            self.full.max_abs,
            self.last_row.mean,
            self.last_row.var,
            self.last_row.max_abs,
            format_first(&self.full.first),
            format_first(&self.last_row.first),
        )
    }
}

fn format_first(values: &[f32]) -> String {
    values
        .iter()
        .map(|v| format!("{v:.6}"))
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join(",")
}

/// A collecting [`TraceSink`]: reduces every capture on arrival and
/// keeps the records in capture order. This is the sink the
/// layer-trace tooling dumps.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct TraceLog {
    first_n: usize,
    records: Vec<TraceRecord>,
}

impl TraceLog {
    /// A log keeping the first `first_n` values of every tensor and
    /// of every last row.
    pub fn new(first_n: usize) -> Self {
        TraceLog {
            first_n,
            records: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// The records so far, in capture order.
    pub fn records(&self) -> &[TraceRecord] {
        &self.records
    }

    /// All records in the stable line format, one per line.
    pub fn lines(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        self.records.iter().map(TraceRecord::to_line).collect()
    }
}

impl TraceSink for TraceLog {
    fn capture(&mut self, stage: &str, tensor: &[f32], rows: usize, cols: usize) {
        let last_row: &[f32] = if cols > 0 && tensor.len() >= cols {
            &tensor[tensor.len() - cols..]
        } else {
            &[]
        };
        self.records.push(TraceRecord {
            stage: stage.to_string(),
            rows,
            cols,
            full: stats_of(tensor, self.first_n),
            last_row: stats_of(last_row, self.first_n),
        });
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn stats_of_a_known_vector() {
        // [1, 2, 3, 4]: mean 2.5, population variance 1.25, max 4.
        let s = stats_of(&[1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0], 2);
        assert_eq!(s.n, 4);
        assert!((s.mean - 2.5).abs() < 1e-12);
        assert!((s.var - 1.25).abs() < 1e-12);
        assert!((s.max_abs - 4.0).abs() < 1e-12);
        assert_eq!(s.first, vec![1.0, 2.0]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn stats_of_negative_and_empty_inputs() {
        let s = stats_of(&[-3.0, 1.0], 8);
        assert_eq!(s.n, 2);
        assert!((s.max_abs - 3.0).abs() < 1e-12);
        // "first" saturates at the available length, never pads.
        assert_eq!(s.first, vec![-3.0, 1.0]);

        let empty = stats_of(&[], 8);
        assert_eq!(empty.n, 0);
        assert_eq!(empty.mean, 0.0);
        assert_eq!(empty.var, 0.0);
        assert!(empty.first.is_empty());

        // Constant input has exactly zero variance (no negative
        // clamp artifact leaking through).
        let flat = stats_of(&[2.0, 2.0, 2.0], 1);
        assert_eq!(flat.var, 0.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn record_line_format_is_stable() {
        let record = TraceRecord {
            stage: "embed".to_string(),
            rows: 2,
            cols: 2,
            full: stats_of(&[1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0], 2),
            last_row: stats_of(&[3.0, 4.0], 2),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            record.to_line(),
            "trace v=1 stage=embed rows=2 cols=2 n=4 mean=2.500000e0 var=1.250000e0 \
             max_abs=4.000000e0 last_mean=3.500000e0 last_var=2.500000e-1 \
             last_max_abs=4.000000e0 first=[1.000000,2.000000] last_first=[3.000000,4.000000]"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn trace_log_reduces_and_keeps_capture_order() {
        let mut log = TraceLog::new(1);
        log.capture("embed", &[1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0], 2, 2);
        log.capture("logits", &[0.5, -0.5], 1, 2);
        let records = log.records();
        assert_eq!(records.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(records[0].stage, "embed");
        // Last row of a 2x2 tensor is its second half.
        assert_eq!(records[0].last_row.first, vec![3.0]);
        assert!((records[0].last_row.mean - 3.5).abs() < 1e-12);
        assert_eq!(records[1].stage, "logits");
        assert_eq!(records[1].rows, 1);
        assert_eq!(log.lines().len(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn trace_log_survives_a_degenerate_shape() {
        // A capture whose cols exceed the tensor must not panic;
        // the last-row view degrades to empty statistics.
        let mut log = TraceLog::new(4);
        log.capture("odd", &[1.0], 1, 8);
        let record = &log.records()[0];
        assert_eq!(record.full.n, 1);
        assert_eq!(record.last_row.n, 0);
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/muse-glimmer/src/weights.rs =====
//! The weight layout of a Muse Glimmer model: every tensor the forward
//! needs, by its exact GGUF name.
//!
//! The per-layer inventory is the one measured in the real file's tensor
//! census (2026-10-29), not the shorter list a Llama-shaped template
//! would guess. Beyond the familiar q/k/v/o projections, gate/up/down,
//! and two norms, the real layers also carry Q and K norms (applied per
//! head after the projections), an attention gate projection, and post
//! norms after both residual adds. A template that never looks those
//! names up silently runs without them; that is the original engine's
//! defect, designed out here: [`Weights::load`] requires every name, and
//! a missing one is a [`GlimmerError::MissingTensor`] naming it.
//!
//! Loading goes through the [`TensorSource`] trait. The loader crate
//! (TODO T-2.1, `itak-loader` in this workspace) implements it over the
//! `gguf` crate's parsed file; this crate never parses files.
//!
//! The output head is untied: `output.weight` is a tensor of its own in
//! the file. If it is absent, load fails. Substituting the embedding
//! table for a missing head is a silent behavior change and is never
//! done here.

use std::sync::Arc;

use crate::config::GlimmerConfig;
use crate::error::Result;

/// Element type of a tensor, as declared by its GGUF type id.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Dtype {
    /// ggml type 0.
    F32,
    /// ggml type 1.
    F16,
    /// ggml type 2.
    Q4_0,
    /// ggml type 8.
    Q8_0,
    /// ggml type 12.
    Q4K,
    /// ggml type 13.
    Q5K,
    /// ggml type 14.
    Q6K,
    /// ggml type 30 (mainline assignment; the original Go loader read
    /// this id as a 2-bit type and corrupted every BF16 tensor, which is
    /// why the mapping lives in exactly one place).
    Bf16,
    /// A type id this module does not name. Carried, not hidden: the
    /// compute layer decides whether it can work with the tensor, and
    /// refuses by name when it cannot.
    Unknown(u32),
}

impl Dtype {
    /// Map a mainline ggml type id to a [`Dtype`].
    pub fn from_ggml_id(id: u32) -> Dtype {
        match id {
            0 => Dtype::F32,
            1 => Dtype::F16,
            2 => Dtype::Q4_0,
            8 => Dtype::Q8_0,
            12 => Dtype::Q4K,
            13 => Dtype::Q5K,
            14 => Dtype::Q6K,
            30 => Dtype::Bf16,
            other => Dtype::Unknown(other),
        }
    }
}

/// One tensor handed over by a [`TensorSource`]: its name, type, shape
/// in GGUF stored order, and its raw bytes.
///
/// The bytes sit behind an [`Arc`] because weight sets are large (the
/// real model is 15.59 GiB) and views get cloned as they move between
/// the loader, this module, and the compute layer. Dequantization is the
/// compute layer's job; this type is deliberately just the measured
/// facts about the tensor.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct TensorView {
    /// Full GGUF tensor name, for example `blk.3.ffn_down.weight`.
    pub name: String,
    /// Element type.
    pub dtype: Dtype,
    /// Dimensions in GGUF stored order (innermost first).
    pub shape: Vec<u64>,
    /// Raw tensor bytes, exactly as stored in the file.
    pub data: Arc<[u8]>,
}

impl TensorView {
    /// Total element count implied by the shape.
    pub fn elements(&self) -> u64 {
        self.shape.iter().product()
    }
}

/// A source of tensors by name: the seam between this module and the
/// loader.
///
/// Implementor contract: return the tensor or fail loud. Absent names
/// fail with [`GlimmerError::MissingTensor`]; names that are present but
/// cannot be delivered as stored fail with
/// [`GlimmerError::TensorUnreadable`]. Never substitute, synthesize, or
/// zero-fill a tensor that was not found; silent placeholders are the
/// defect this rebuild exists to remove.
pub trait TensorSource {
    /// Fetch one tensor by its full GGUF name.
    fn tensor(&self, name: &str) -> Result<TensorView>;
}

/// The tensors of one transformer layer, in forward order.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct LayerWeights {
    /// `attn_norm.weight`: pre-attention RMSNorm.
    pub attn_norm: TensorView,
    /// `attn_q.weight`: query projection.
    pub attn_q: TensorView,
    /// `attn_k.weight`: key projection.
    pub attn_k: TensorView,
    /// `attn_v.weight`: value projection.
    pub attn_v: TensorView,
    /// `attn_q_norm.weight`: per-head RMSNorm on the query projection.
    pub attn_q_norm: TensorView,
    /// `attn_k_norm.weight`: per-head RMSNorm on the key projection.
    pub attn_k_norm: TensorView,
    /// `attn_output.weight`: attention output projection.
    pub attn_output: TensorView,
    /// `attn_gate.weight`: projection producing the gate that scales the
    /// attention output (gated attention, present in the real file).
    pub attn_gate: TensorView,
    /// `post_attention_norm.weight`: RMSNorm after the attention
    /// residual add.
    pub post_attention_norm: TensorView,
    /// `ffn_norm.weight`: pre-FFN RMSNorm.
    pub ffn_norm: TensorView,
    /// `ffn_gate.weight`: SwiGLU gate projection.
    pub ffn_gate: TensorView,
    /// `ffn_up.weight`: SwiGLU up projection.
    pub ffn_up: TensorView,
    /// `ffn_down.weight`: FFN down projection (75 percent of the model's
    /// bytes live in the FFN tensors; this is the large one).
    pub ffn_down: TensorView,
    /// `post_ffw_norm.weight`: RMSNorm after the FFN residual add.
    pub post_ffw_norm: TensorView,
}

/// The full weight set of a Muse Glimmer model.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Weights {
    /// `token_embd.weight`: the embedding table.
    pub embedding: TensorView,
    /// `output_norm.weight`: final RMSNorm before the head.
    pub final_norm: TensorView,
    /// `output.weight`: the untied output head (Q5_K in the real file).
    pub output: TensorView,
    /// Per-layer weights, in layer order.
    pub layers: Vec<LayerWeights>,
}

/// Per-layer tensor suffixes in forward order, exactly as measured in
/// the real file's census.
const LAYER_SUFFIXES: [&str; 14] = [
    "attn_norm.weight",
    "attn_q.weight",
    "attn_k.weight",
    "attn_v.weight",
    "attn_q_norm.weight",
    "attn_k_norm.weight",
    "attn_output.weight",
    "attn_gate.weight",
    "post_attention_norm.weight",
    "ffn_norm.weight",
    "ffn_gate.weight",
    "ffn_up.weight",
    "ffn_down.weight",
    "post_ffw_norm.weight",
];

/// Every tensor name [`Weights::load`] will request for `cfg`, in load
/// order. Exposed so the loader's tensor inventory (TODO T-2.1) can be
/// checked against this module's expectations mechanically, instead of
/// by reading two codebases side by side. Verified against the real
/// file on 2026-10-29 through the `itak-loader` inventory check: all
/// 731 expected names present, zero unexpected, and
/// `output_norm.weight` confirmed as the file's final-norm tensor
/// (F32, shape [6656]), not merely a naming-convention assumption.
pub fn expected_tensor_names(cfg: &GlimmerConfig) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut names = Vec::with_capacity(3 + cfg.block_count as usize * LAYER_SUFFIXES.len());
    names.push("token_embd.weight".to_string());
    names.push("output_norm.weight".to_string());
    names.push("output.weight".to_string());
    for layer in 0..cfg.block_count {
        for suffix in LAYER_SUFFIXES {
            names.push(format!("blk.{layer}.{suffix}"));
        }
    }
    names
}

impl Weights {
    /// Load the full weight set for `cfg` from `source`. The first
    /// missing tensor aborts the load with a named error; a partially
    /// loaded model is never returned.
    pub fn load<S: TensorSource>(source: &S, cfg: &GlimmerConfig) -> Result<Weights> {
        let embedding = source.tensor("token_embd.weight")?;
        let final_norm = source.tensor("output_norm.weight")?;
        let output = source.tensor("output.weight")?;
        let mut layers = Vec::with_capacity(cfg.block_count as usize);
        for index in 0..cfg.block_count {
            let get = |suffix: &str| source.tensor(&format!("blk.{index}.{suffix}"));
            layers.push(LayerWeights {
                attn_norm: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[0])?,
                attn_q: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[1])?,
                attn_k: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[2])?,
                attn_v: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[3])?,
                attn_q_norm: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[4])?,
                attn_k_norm: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[5])?,
                attn_output: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[6])?,
                attn_gate: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[7])?,
                post_attention_norm: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[8])?,
                ffn_norm: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[9])?,
                ffn_gate: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[10])?,
                ffn_up: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[11])?,
                ffn_down: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[12])?,
                post_ffw_norm: get(LAYER_SUFFIXES[13])?,
            });
        }
        Ok(Weights {
            embedding,
            final_norm,
            output,
            layers,
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::config::GlimmerConfig;
    use crate::error::GlimmerError;
    use crate::testkit::tiny_metadata;
    use std::collections::HashMap;

    /// A tensor source backed by a name set: every expected name is
    /// present unless the test removed it.
    struct FakeSource {
        present: HashMap<String, ()>,
    }

    impl FakeSource {
        fn full(cfg: &GlimmerConfig) -> Self {
            let present = expected_tensor_names(cfg)
                .into_iter()
                .map(|n| (n, ()))
                .collect();
            FakeSource { present }
        }
    }

    impl TensorSource for FakeSource {
        fn tensor(&self, name: &str) -> Result<TensorView> {
            if self.present.contains_key(name) {
                Ok(TensorView {
                    name: name.to_string(),
                    dtype: Dtype::F32,
                    shape: vec![1],
                    data: Arc::from(vec![0u8; 4].into_boxed_slice()),
                })
            } else {
                Err(GlimmerError::MissingTensor {
                    name: name.to_string(),
                })
            }
        }
    }

    fn tiny_cfg() -> GlimmerConfig {
        GlimmerConfig::from_metadata(&tiny_metadata()).expect("tiny config")
    }

    #[test]
    fn expected_names_cover_globals_and_every_layer() {
        let cfg = tiny_cfg();
        let names = expected_tensor_names(&cfg);
        assert_eq!(names.len(), 3 + 2 * 14);
        assert_eq!(names[0], "token_embd.weight");
        assert!(names.contains(&"blk.1.post_ffw_norm.weight".to_string()));
        assert!(names.contains(&"blk.0.attn_gate.weight".to_string()));
        assert!(names.contains(&"blk.0.attn_q_norm.weight".to_string()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn full_source_loads() {
        let cfg = tiny_cfg();
        let source = FakeSource::full(&cfg);
        let weights = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect("full source loads");
        assert_eq!(weights.layers.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(weights.output.name, "output.weight");
    }

    #[test]
    fn missing_ffn_down_is_named() {
        let cfg = tiny_cfg();
        let mut source = FakeSource::full(&cfg);
        source.present.remove("blk.1.ffn_down.weight");
        let err = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect_err("missing tensor must fail");
        match err {
            GlimmerError::MissingTensor { name } => {
                assert_eq!(name, "blk.1.ffn_down.weight")
            }
            other => panic!("expected MissingTensor, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn missing_output_head_is_not_replaced_by_embedding() {
        let cfg = tiny_cfg();
        let mut source = FakeSource::full(&cfg);
        source.present.remove("output.weight");
        let err = Weights::load(&source, &cfg).expect_err("missing head must fail");
        assert!(matches!(err, GlimmerError::MissingTensor { .. }));
    }

    #[test]
    fn dtype_ids_match_mainline_ggml() {
        assert_eq!(Dtype::from_ggml_id(0), Dtype::F32);
        assert_eq!(Dtype::from_ggml_id(12), Dtype::Q4K);
        assert_eq!(Dtype::from_ggml_id(13), Dtype::Q5K);
        assert_eq!(Dtype::from_ggml_id(14), Dtype::Q6K);
        assert_eq!(Dtype::from_ggml_id(30), Dtype::Bf16);
        assert_eq!(Dtype::from_ggml_id(99), Dtype::Unknown(99));
    }

    #[test]
    fn tensor_view_counts_elements() {
        let view = TensorView {
            name: "x".to_string(),
            dtype: Dtype::Q4K,
            shape: vec![6656, 202_048],
            data: Arc::from(Vec::new().into_boxed_slice()),
        };
        assert_eq!(view.elements(), 6656 * 202_048);
    }
}

# Tokenizer conformance: TODO T-2.3 proof

**Byte-level family result: 16 of 16 bench prompts token-identical
to the reference tokenizer on Glimmer's real vocabulary; 16 of 16
decode round-trips exact.** Run 2026-10-29 against David's
production Glimmer llama-server. The first run was 14/16 and caught
a real pre-tokenizer defect, documented below; the fix is part of
the same landing.

**SentencePiece family result: 15 of 15 golden prompts
token-identical to llama.cpp on TinyLlama's real vocabulary, and
decode reproduces all 15 fixture completion texts exactly.** That
proof is `tests/spm_golden.rs` against the golden fixture; see the
SentencePiece section at the end of this file.

## Inputs

- **Vocabulary**: extracted from the production model file
  `/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf`
  on the server with the gguf crate's `tokenizer_extract` example
  (the file is 15 GiB and the parser loads it whole, so extraction
  runs where the model lives; the resulting `.tokdata` is 9.7 MB).
  The file declares `tokenizer.ggml.model = "gpt2"` and
  `tokenizer.ggml.pre = "llama4"`; 202,048 tokens, 439,802 merges,
  bos 200000, eos 200001, pad 200018, no unknown token id.
- **Reference tokenizations**: `conformance/make_reference.py`, run
  on the server against the production llama-server's `/tokenize`
  endpoint with `add_special: false` (pure tokenization, no BOS/EOS
  injection, matching `Tokenizer::encode`). The generated reference
  is committed as `conformance/glimmer.tokref`. The server was only
  ever read through its normal API; it was not restarted or
  reconfigured.
- **Comparison**: `cargo run --release -p tokenizer --example
  conformance -- <glimmer.tokdata> conformance/glimmer.tokref`. The
  example adapts `gguf::TokenizerInfo` into `TokenizerData` (the
  gguf crate is a dev-dependency of the harness only; the library
  stays decoupled), encodes every prompt, compares id sequences
  exactly, and decodes the reference ids back to the prompt text.

## The prompt set

Sixteen prompts chosen to stress the known divergence edges:

| # | Stresses | Tokens | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | plain prose, single spaces | 17 | exact |
| 1 | double spaces | 15 | exact |
| 2 | punctuation clusters, quotes, ellipsis, em dash | 18 | exact |
| 3 | a 20-digit run | 16 | exact |
| 4 | decimals, date, time, leading zeros | 27 | exact |
| 5 | contractions, incl. double `you'd've` | 30 | exact (was the failure, below) |
| 6 | accented Latin (French, Spanish) | 27 | exact |
| 7 | CJK sentences (Japanese, Chinese) | 17 | exact |
| 8 | Latin and CJK mixed | 16 | exact |
| 9 | a Rust code snippet | 35 | exact |
| 10 | newline runs, space indent, tab, trailing newline | 16 | exact |
| 11 | leading and trailing spaces | 7 | exact |
| 12 | leading blank lines | 7 | exact |
| 13 | currency, symbols, arrow, emoji | 29 | exact |
| 14 | camelCase, snake_case, dunder identifiers | 18 | exact |
| 15 | leading apostrophe word, `90's`, double contraction | 20 | exact |

## The one mismatch, and the fix

First run: case 5 diverged at token index 1.

```text
prompt:    "I don't know if we'll make it, ..."
reference: [53, 5863, 2609, 563, 31519, 2170, 536, 24, 1108, 28661, ...]
ours:      [53, 2360, 2050, 2609, 563, 675, 8961, 2170, 536, 24, ...]
```

Reference token 5863 is `Ġdon't`, a single token. Ours produced
2360 `Ġdon` + 2050 `'t`, and the same split repeated at every
contraction in the prompt (`we'll`, `they're`, `isn't`, `we'd`,
`she's`). Cause class: **pre-tokenizer split**. This crate had
implemented the llama-3 pattern, in which the contraction is a
standalone first alternative, so `don't` was split before BPE and
the merged token was unreachable.

The reference build's own source settles what the right pattern
is: in `llama-vocab.cpp`, `tokenizer_pre == "llama4"` maps to
`LLAMA_VOCAB_PRE_TYPE_GPT4O`, whose pattern carries the contraction
as an optional suffix of the word alternatives
(`(?:'s|'t|'re|'ve|'m|'ll|'d)?`). There is no standalone
contraction alternative; a contraction that follows no word (the
`'ve` of `you'd've`, the `'s` of `90's`) is produced by the
prefix-char word branch.

Fix, in `src/pretokenize.rs`: the standalone contraction branch is
gone, and every word piece absorbs one trailing contraction
(`word_end`). The crate docs in `src/lib.rs` now state the GPT-4o
pattern instead of the llama-3 one. Regression tests cover
`don't`, `you'd've`, `'tis`, `90's`, `dogs'`, and `DON'T`, and
case 15 of the bench set exercises the same shapes against the
reference. After the fix: 16/16 exact, and all pre-existing crate
tests still pass.

## What this does not prove

- The prompt set contains no literal special-token text (for
  example `<|im_start|>` typed as prose), and the comparison ran
  with `add_special: false`; special-token matching and BOS/EOS
  policy are covered by the crate's unit tests, not by this run.
- The documented scanner deviations in `src/lib.rs` stand:
  `\p{L}` is `char::is_alphabetic` (the pattern's `\p{M}` mark
  class is not modeled separately), and a whitespace run mixing
  newlines and spaces can split at a different point than a true
  regex engine in rare multi-newline cases. No case in this set
  exercised either gap into a divergence.

## SentencePiece family: TinyLlama proof

Integration Run A (`golden/RESULTS-integration-a.md`) found the
byte-level family tokenizing TinyLlama-1.1B into near-byte pieces:
that file's vocabulary is SentencePiece BPE, a different family.
The family is now implemented in `src/spm.rs` as a direct port of
llama.cpp's SPM path, with every rule cited to `llama-vocab.cpp` in
the llama.cpp checkout the fixtures were generated with (0.7.0-dev,
build 137, commit a7af149):

- Spaces escape to `▁` (`llama_escape_whitespace`) and one space is
  prefixed at the start of the text and after every special token
  (the SPM case of `llama_vocab::impl::tokenize`; the SPM type
  defaults set `add_space_prefix = true`). The file's
  `tokenizer.ggml.add_space_prefix` key can override that default
  in llama.cpp; the crate does not plumb the key yet, and TinyLlama
  does not carry it.
- Symbols start as single codepoints, lengths from the
  `unicode_len_utf8` high-nibble table (`src/unicode.cpp`).
- Adjacent pairs merge one at a time from a priority queue keyed by
  the combined token's score from `tokenizer.ggml.scores`
  (`llm_bigram_spm::comparator`: highest score, ties to the
  smallest left index). TinyLlama carries the scores array (32,000
  entries); a file without it gets all-zero scores in llama.cpp,
  which reduces the queue to leftmost-first merging, and the crate
  mirrors that too. The merges array in the file does not drive
  this family and is not parsed for it.
- Leftover symbols re-segment down to `<0xXX>` byte tokens
  (`byte_to_token`), the byte-fallback path the accented and code
  prompts exercise through pieces like the newline byte token.
- Decode is the SPM case of `token_to_piece`: unescape `▁`, byte
  tokens contribute their byte, specials render literally. The
  encoder's space prefix returns as one leading space on decode;
  llama.cpp removes it only in its whole-sequence detokenizer, not
  in per-token pieces, so this crate keeps it and the tests assert
  it explicitly.

Proof, `tests/spm_golden.rs`, against data extracted from the real
GGUF on the server (`conformance/tinyllama.tokdata`, format version
2, which adds the scores section): the golden fixture's
`llama-tokenize` prompt ids are reproduced exactly for all 15
prompts (`[bos] + encode(prompt)`), decode of the prompt ids
reproduces each prompt with exactly the one leading space, and
decode of the fixture completion ids reproduces all 15 completion
texts. The `examples/conformance.rs` harness, fed the same tokdata
and a fixture-derived `.tokref`, also reports 15/15 prompts
token-identical; its decode round-trip line differs by exactly
that leading space, because the harness's identity expectation was
written for the byte-level family.

One rule the source did not fully settle: llama.cpp partitions
text around special tokens with its own special-token table, while
this crate matches control / user-defined token texts (shared with
the byte-level family). No golden prompt contains a special token
as prose, so the fixture cannot distinguish the two; the synthetic
tests in `tests/spm_family.rs` pin the crate's behavior.

===== FILE: crates/tokenizer/conformance/make_reference.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the tokenizer conformance reference from a live llama-server.

This is the bench prompt set for TODO T-2.3: sixteen prompts chosen to
stress the edges where BPE tokenizers diverge (spacing, punctuation
clusters, long digit runs, contractions, accents, CJK, code, newline
runs, boundary whitespace, symbols). Each prompt is sent to the
reference server's /tokenize endpoint with add_special disabled, so the
comparison is pure tokenization with no BOS/EOS injection, matching
`tokenizer::Tokenizer::encode`.

Usage:
    LLAMA_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:8080 python3 make_reference.py [out.tokref]

The output is the `.tokref` format (version 1) read by the tokenizer
crate's `conformance` example:

    ITAK-TOKREF-1
    cases <count>
    <prompt byte length>\n<prompt bytes>\n
    ids <count>
    <space-separated token ids>
    (repeated per case)

Run it against David's production Glimmer server on the server itself;
the committed glimmer.tokref was generated exactly that way.
"""

import json
import os
import sys
import urllib.request

BASE = os.environ.get("LLAMA_BASE", "http://127.0.0.1:8080")

PROMPTS = [
    # Plain prose with ordinary single spacing.
    "The capital of France is Paris, and it is known for the Eiffel Tower.",
    # Double spaces between words.
    "Hello  world, this  sentence has  double spaces in  it.",
    # Punctuation clusters, quotes, ellipsis character.
    "Wait... what?! Really?? She paused\u2026 then said: 'stop' \u2014 twice.",
    # A digit run far past the 1-to-3 digit split rule.
    "The invoice total came to 12345678901234567890 dollars exactly.",
    # Mixed digits: decimals, a date, a time, leading zeros.
    "Version 3.14159 shipped on 2026-10-29 at 13:37:35 with build 007.",
    # Contractions, including the double contraction you'd've.
    "I don't know if we'll make it, but they're saying it isn't over yet; "
    "you'd've thought we'd have learned, and I'm not sure she's ready.",
    # Accented Latin text across several languages.
    "Le caf\u00e9 na\u00eff servait un r\u00e9sum\u00e9 avec la pi\u00f1ata "
    "et le jalape\u00f1o, fa\u00e7ade d\u00e9j\u00e0 vu, se\u00f1or.",
    # CJK sentences (Japanese and Chinese).
    "\u4eba\u5de5\u77e5\u80fd\u306f\u672a\u6765\u3067\u3059\u3002"
    "\u6771\u4eac\u306f\u65e5\u672c\u306e\u9996\u90fd\u3067\u3059\u3002"
    "\u5317\u4eac\u4e5f\u662f\u9996\u90fd\u3002",
    # Latin and CJK mixed in one line.
    "Tokyo \u6771\u4eac is a city, and \u5317\u4eac (Beijing) is another one.",
    # A Rust code snippet: brackets, operators, a format string.
    'fn main() { let xs: Vec<u32> = (0..10).map(|i| i * i).collect(); '
    'println!("{:?}", xs); }',
    # Newline-heavy: blank lines, space indent, a tab, trailing newline.
    "first line\n\n\n    indented by four\n\ttabbed line\nlast line\n",
    # Leading and trailing spaces around short text.
    "   leading spaces and trailing spaces   ",
    # Text that starts with blank lines.
    "\n\n  hello after blank lines\n\n",
    # Currency, symbols, an arrow, an emoji.
    "Total: $5, \u20ac10, \u00a33.50 (\u00b10.5\u00b0C) \u2192 ship it "
    "\U0001f680 today \u00a9 2026.",
    # Identifier shapes: camelCase, snake_case, digits, dunder.
    "getUserById calls max_token_count on the HTTPServer2 instance __privately.",
    # Contraction placement stress: a leading apostrophe word, a
    # digit-adjacent contraction, a double contraction, all in prose.
    "'Tis the season, the 90's are back, and you'd've agreed, hadn't you?",
]


def tokenize(content: str) -> list:
    body = json.dumps({"content": content, "add_special": False}).encode("utf-8")
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        BASE + "/tokenize", data=body, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
        return json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))["tokens"]


def main() -> int:
    out_path = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "glimmer.tokref"
    cases = []
    for i, prompt in enumerate(PROMPTS):
        ids = tokenize(prompt)
        cases.append((prompt, ids))
        print(f"case {i}: {len(ids)} tokens")
    with open(out_path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(b"ITAK-TOKREF-1\n")
        f.write(f"cases {len(cases)}\n".encode("ascii"))
        for prompt, ids in cases:
            raw = prompt.encode("utf-8")
            f.write(f"{len(raw)}\n".encode("ascii"))
            f.write(raw + b"\n")
            f.write(f"ids {len(ids)}\n".encode("ascii"))
            f.write((" ".join(str(t) for t in ids) + "\n").encode("ascii"))
    print(f"wrote {len(cases)} cases -> {out_path}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

===== END FILE: crates/tokenizer/conformance/make_reference.py =====
