===== FILE: crates/torch-math/src/rope.rs =====
//! Rotary position embedding (RoPE). The old Go native engine had no
//! RoPE anywhere in its forward path, so position information never
//! entered the model at all. This module is the correction, written
//! against the conventions llama.cpp uses (the project's reference):
//!
//! - The head vector is treated as `rotary_dim / 2` half-split pairs
//!   `(x[i], x[i + rotary_dim / 2])`: the GPT-NeoX pairing, which is
//!   ggml's `GGML_ROPE_TYPE_NEOX`, the mode llama.cpp applies for
//!   the qwen2 family (`llama_model_rope_type` in
//!   src/llama-model.cpp). It is NOT the llama family's mode: llama
//!   (and muse-glimmer) map to the adjacent NORM pairing in
//!   [`crate::rope_interleaved`]. Pairing is per-architecture, and
//!   arch modules select it from the file, never from this
//!   function's name. (An earlier version of this module paired
//!   adjacent channels `(x[2i], x[2i + 1])` while claiming the same
//!   name; the layer-by-layer activation diff against llama.cpp on
//!   Qwen2.5-1.5B, 2026-10-29, proved that pairing wrong for qwen2
//!   and this one right: with the input to layer 0 identical,
//!   half-split rotation of the pre-RoPE projections reproduces the
//!   reference Qcur/Kcur to the quant noise floor, adjacent pairing
//!   diverges by two orders of magnitude more. The same fix
//!   generalized to llama files regressed TinyLlama's golden run
//!   from 6/15 to 0/15, because llama's pairing was the adjacent
//!   one all along; see `crates/arch-llama/src/config.rs` for the
//!   per-architecture mapping.)
//! - Pair `i` rotates by `position * base^(-2i / rotary_dim)`.
//! - `base` is a parameter: the classic value is `10000`, long-context
//!   models use more (Glimmer and Qwen2.5 use `500000`, Llama 3 uses
//!   `500000`, Mistral uses `1000000` in some releases). It is read
//!   from each model's config, never assumed.
//!
//! Partial rotary (only the first `rotary_dim` channels rotate, as in
//! some Phi and Gemma configurations) is supported by [`rope_partial`];
//! the remaining channels pass through unchanged. The frequency
//! denominator is `rotary_dim`, matching llama.cpp's partial-rotary
//! convention; for the full form [`rope`] the two are equal anyway.

use crate::{dbg_log, MathError, Result};

/// Apply RoPE to one head vector of length `head_dim` at `position`,
/// rotating every channel. Equivalent to [`rope_partial`] with
/// `rotary_dim == head_dim`.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// - [`MathError::LengthMismatch`] if `input.len() != head_dim`.
/// - [`MathError::InvalidConfig`] if `head_dim` is odd or less than 2,
///   or if `base` is not finite and greater than 1.
pub fn rope(input: &[f32], position: usize, base: f32, head_dim: usize) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
    rope_partial(input, position, base, head_dim, head_dim)
}

/// Apply RoPE to the first `rotary_dim` channels of one head vector of
/// length `head_dim` at `position`; channels at or beyond `rotary_dim`
/// are copied through unchanged.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// - [`MathError::LengthMismatch`] if `input.len() != head_dim`.
/// - [`MathError::InvalidConfig`] if `head_dim` or `rotary_dim` is odd
///   or less than 2, if `rotary_dim > head_dim`, or if `base` is not
///   finite and greater than 1.
pub fn rope_partial(
    input: &[f32],
    position: usize,
    base: f32,
    head_dim: usize,
    rotary_dim: usize,
) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
    if head_dim < 2 || head_dim % 2 != 0 {
        return Err(MathError::InvalidConfig {
            op: "rope",
            param: "head_dim",
            reason: "head_dim must be even and >= 2",
        });
    }
    if input.len() != head_dim {
        return Err(MathError::LengthMismatch {
            op: "rope",
            expected: head_dim,
            actual: input.len(),
        });
    }
    if rotary_dim < 2 || rotary_dim % 2 != 0 || rotary_dim > head_dim {
        return Err(MathError::InvalidConfig {
            op: "rope",
            param: "rotary_dim",
            reason: "rotary_dim must be even, >= 2, and <= head_dim",
        });
    }
    if !base.is_finite() || base <= 1.0 {
        return Err(MathError::InvalidConfig {
            op: "rope",
            param: "base",
            reason: "base must be finite and > 1",
        });
    }
    dbg_log!("rope position={position} base={base} head_dim={head_dim} rotary_dim={rotary_dim}");
    let mut out = input.to_vec();
    // Angles are computed in f64: at long contexts the product
    // position * base^(-2i/d) loses real precision in f32, and the
    // reference implementation is the one that must not drift.
    // Pairing is half-split (GPT-NeoX / ggml NEOX): pair i joins
    // channel i with channel i + rotary_dim/2.
    let pos = position as f64;
    let base64 = f64::from(base);
    let half = rotary_dim / 2;
    for i in 0..half {
        let exponent = -((2 * i) as f64) / (rotary_dim as f64);
        let angle = pos * base64.powf(exponent);
        let (sin, cos) = angle.sin_cos();
        let (x, y) = (f64::from(input[i]), f64::from(input[i + half]));
        out[i] = (x * cos - y * sin) as f32;
        out[i + half] = (x * sin + y * cos) as f32;
    }
    Ok(out)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::test_util::{assert_close, assert_vec_close};

    #[test]
    fn position_zero_is_identity() {
        // Every angle is 0 at position 0, and rotation by 0 is exact.
        let input = [0.3, -1.2, 2.5, 0.7];
        let out = rope(&input, 0, 500_000.0, 4).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out, input.to_vec());
    }

    #[test]
    fn known_rotations() {
        // head_dim 4, base 10000, half-split pairing: pair 0 joins
        // channels (0, 2) and turns at rate 1, pair 1 joins (1, 3)
        // at rate 10000^(-1/2) = 0.01. At position 1 the input
        // [1, 0, 1, 0] puts (1, 1) in pair 0 and (0, 0) in pair 1,
        // so pair 0 becomes (cos 1 - sin 1, sin 1 + cos 1) written
        // back to channels 0 and 2, and pair 1 stays zero. (These
        // values distinguish the half-split pairing from the
        // adjacent pairing, which would rotate (1, 0) and (1, 0)
        // separately; the layer diff against llama.cpp settled
        // which one the reference uses.)
        let out = rope(&[1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0], 1, 10_000.0, 4).unwrap();
        assert_vec_close(
            &out,
            &[
                -0.301_168_68, // cos(1) - sin(1), channel 0
                0.0,           // channel 1 (pair 1 was zero)
                1.381_773_3,   // sin(1) + cos(1), channel 2
                0.0,           // channel 3 (pair 1 was zero)
            ],
            1e-5,
        );
        // Pair 1 in isolation: [0, 1, 0, 0] is (1, 0) in pair 1,
        // which turns at rate 0.01 into channels 1 and 3.
        let out = rope(&[0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0], 1, 10_000.0, 4).unwrap();
        assert_vec_close(
            &out,
            &[
                0.0,
                0.999_950_000_416_665_3, // cos(0.01)
                0.0,
                0.009_999_833_334_166_664, // sin(0.01)
            ],
            1e-5,
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rotation_preserves_norm() {
        // RoPE is an orthogonal transform per pair, so the vector's
        // sum of squares is invariant at any position and base.
        let input = [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0];
        let out = rope(&input, 7, 500_000.0, 4).unwrap();
        let before: f64 = input.iter().map(|v| f64::from(*v) * f64::from(*v)).sum();
        let after: f64 = out.iter().map(|v| f64::from(*v) * f64::from(*v)).sum();
        assert_close(after as f32, before, 0.01);
    }

    #[test]
    fn partial_rotary_leaves_the_tail_untouched() {
        let input = [1.0, 0.0, 9.0, -4.0];
        let out = rope_partial(&input, 3, 10_000.0, 4, 2).unwrap();
        // Channels 2 and 3 are beyond rotary_dim and pass through.
        assert_eq!(out[2], 9.0);
        assert_eq!(out[3], -4.0);
        // Channel pair 0 did rotate (angle 3 radians on [1, 0]).
        assert_close(out[0], -0.989_992_496_600_445_4, 1e-5); // cos(3)
        assert_close(out[1], 0.141_120_008_059_867_2, 1e-5); // sin(3)
    }

    #[test]
    fn base_is_a_parameter() {
        // With base 500000 and head_dim 4, pair 1 (channels 1 and 3)
        // turns at rate 500000^(-1/2) = 0.00141421..., far slower
        // than base 10000.
        let out = rope(&[0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0], 1, 500_000.0, 4).unwrap();
        assert_close(out[3], 0.001_414_213_5, 1e-6); // sin(500000^-0.5)
        assert_close(out[1], 0.999_999_0, 1e-6); // cos(500000^-0.5)
    }

    #[test]
    fn length_mismatch_is_an_error() {
        assert_eq!(
            rope(&[1.0, 0.0], 0, 10_000.0, 4),
            Err(MathError::LengthMismatch {
                op: "rope",
                expected: 4,
                actual: 2
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn bad_config_is_an_error() {
        // Odd head_dim.
        assert!(matches!(
            rope(&[1.0, 0.0, 1.0], 0, 10_000.0, 3),
            Err(MathError::InvalidConfig {
                param: "head_dim",
                ..
            })
        ));
        // rotary_dim beyond head_dim.
        assert!(matches!(
            rope_partial(&[1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0], 0, 10_000.0, 4, 8),
            Err(MathError::InvalidConfig {
                param: "rotary_dim",
                ..
            })
        ));
        // Base of 1 would make every frequency 1.
        assert!(matches!(
            rope(&[1.0, 0.0], 0, 1.0, 2),
            Err(MathError::InvalidConfig { param: "base", .. })
        ));
    }
}

===== END FILE: crates/torch-math/src/rope.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/torch-math/src/rope_interleaved.rs =====
//! RoPE with interleaved (adjacent) pairing, kept in its own module
//! because it is a DIFFERENT convention from [`crate::rope`]'s
//! half-split pairing, not a variant of it:
//!
//! - Pair `i` joins channels `(2i, 2i + 1)` and rotates by
//!   `position * base^(-2i / head_dim)`.
//! - This is ggml's `GGML_ROPE_TYPE_NORM`, the mode llama.cpp
//!   selects for muse-glimmer (`llama_model_rope_type` in
//!   src/llama-model.cpp) and GPT-J-style models. Glimmer's
//!   converter unpermutes the Q/K projections into exactly this
//!   layout at conversion time (conversion/muse_glimmer.py:
//!   `permute` with `qk_order = NORM`), so the stored weights
//!   assume it.
//! - The pairings are not interchangeable: they pair different
//!   channels at the same rates, and a model converted for one is
//!   garbage under the other. The Run B follow-up (2026-10-29)
//!   found the Glimmer backend one edit away from the half-split
//!   form; giving each pairing its own named function is the
//!   structural fix, so a backend states its architecture's
//!   pairing at the call site.
//!
//! Partial rotary (only the first `rotary_dim` channels rotate, as
//! in llama-architecture files whose `rope.dimension_count` is
//! below the head dimension) is supported by
//! [`rope_interleaved_partial`]; the remaining channels pass
//! through unchanged. The frequency denominator is `rotary_dim`,
//! the same partial-rotary convention [`crate::rope_partial`]
//! documents for the half-split form; for the full form
//! [`rope_interleaved`] the two are equal anyway.

use crate::{dbg_log, MathError, Result};

/// Apply RoPE with interleaved (adjacent) pairing to one head vector
/// of length `head_dim` at `position`: pair `i` joins channels
/// `(2i, 2i + 1)` and rotates by `position * base^(-2i / head_dim)`.
/// Equivalent to [`rope_interleaved_partial`] with
/// `rotary_dim == head_dim`.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// - [`MathError::LengthMismatch`] if `input.len() != head_dim`.
/// - [`MathError::InvalidConfig`] if `head_dim` is odd or less than 2,
///   or if `base` is not finite and greater than 1.
pub fn rope_interleaved(
    input: &[f32],
    position: usize,
    base: f32,
    head_dim: usize,
) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
    rope_interleaved_partial(input, position, base, head_dim, head_dim)
}

/// Apply RoPE with interleaved (adjacent) pairing to the first
/// `rotary_dim` channels of one head vector of length `head_dim` at
/// `position`; channels at or beyond `rotary_dim` are copied through
/// unchanged. Pair `i` joins channels `(2i, 2i + 1)` and rotates by
/// `position * base^(-2i / rotary_dim)`.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// - [`MathError::LengthMismatch`] if `input.len() != head_dim`.
/// - [`MathError::InvalidConfig`] if `head_dim` or `rotary_dim` is
///   odd or less than 2, if `rotary_dim > head_dim`, or if `base`
///   is not finite and greater than 1.
pub fn rope_interleaved_partial(
    input: &[f32],
    position: usize,
    base: f32,
    head_dim: usize,
    rotary_dim: usize,
) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
    if head_dim < 2 || head_dim % 2 != 0 {
        return Err(MathError::InvalidConfig {
            op: "rope_interleaved",
            param: "head_dim",
            reason: "head_dim must be even and >= 2",
        });
    }
    if input.len() != head_dim {
        return Err(MathError::LengthMismatch {
            op: "rope_interleaved",
            expected: head_dim,
            actual: input.len(),
        });
    }
    if rotary_dim < 2 || rotary_dim % 2 != 0 || rotary_dim > head_dim {
        return Err(MathError::InvalidConfig {
            op: "rope_interleaved",
            param: "rotary_dim",
            reason: "rotary_dim must be even, >= 2, and <= head_dim",
        });
    }
    if !base.is_finite() || base <= 1.0 {
        return Err(MathError::InvalidConfig {
            op: "rope_interleaved",
            param: "base",
            reason: "base must be finite and > 1",
        });
    }
    dbg_log!(
        "rope_interleaved_partial position={position} base={base} head_dim={head_dim} rotary_dim={rotary_dim}"
    );
    let mut out = input.to_vec();
    // Angles in f64, as in the half-split form: at long contexts the
    // product position * base^(-2i/d) loses real precision in f32.
    let pos = position as f64;
    let base64 = f64::from(base);
    for i in 0..rotary_dim / 2 {
        let exponent = -((2 * i) as f64) / (rotary_dim as f64);
        let angle = pos * base64.powf(exponent);
        let (sin, cos) = angle.sin_cos();
        let (x, y) = (f64::from(input[2 * i]), f64::from(input[2 * i + 1]));
        out[2 * i] = (x * cos - y * sin) as f32;
        out[2 * i + 1] = (x * sin + y * cos) as f32;
    }
    Ok(out)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::test_util::{assert_close, assert_vec_close};

    #[test]
    fn known_rotations() {
        // head_dim 4, base 10000, adjacent pairing: pair 0 joins
        // channels (0, 1) and turns at rate 1, pair 1 joins (2, 3)
        // at rate 10000^(-1/2) = 0.01. At position 1 the input
        // [1, 0, 1, 0] puts (1, 0) in both pairs, so the output is
        // (cos 1, sin 1, cos 0.01, sin 0.01). The half-split form on
        // the same input gives (-0.301, 0, 1.382, 0) instead, so
        // these values tell the pairings apart.
        let input = [1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0];
        let out = rope_interleaved(&input, 1, 10_000.0, 4).unwrap();
        assert_vec_close(
            &out,
            &[
                0.540_302_305_868_139_8,   // cos(1), channel 0
                0.841_470_984_807_896_5,   // sin(1), channel 1
                0.999_950_000_416_665_3,   // cos(0.01), channel 2
                0.009_999_833_334_166_664, // sin(0.01), channel 3
            ],
            1e-5,
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rotation_preserves_norm_and_zero_position() {
        let input = [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0];
        assert_eq!(
            rope_interleaved(&input, 0, 500_000.0, 4).unwrap(),
            input.to_vec()
        );
        let out = rope_interleaved(&input, 7, 500_000.0, 4).unwrap();
        let before: f64 = input.iter().map(|v| f64::from(*v) * f64::from(*v)).sum();
        let after: f64 = out.iter().map(|v| f64::from(*v) * f64::from(*v)).sum();
        assert_close(after as f32, before, 0.01);
    }

    #[test]
    fn partial_rotary_rotates_adjacent_pairs_and_passes_the_tail() {
        // head_dim 8, rotary_dim 4, base 10000, position 1: adjacent
        // pair 0 joins channels (0, 1) at rate 1, pair 1 joins
        // (2, 3) at rate 10000^(-2/4) = 0.01, and channels 4..8 are
        // beyond rotary_dim and pass through. The half-split
        // partial on the same input pairs (0, 2) and (1, 3)
        // instead, turning channel 0 with (cos 1 - sin 1), so
        // these values tell the pairings apart in the partial case
        // as well.
        let input = [1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 9.0, -4.0, 7.0, 3.0];
        let out = rope_interleaved_partial(&input, 1, 10_000.0, 8, 4).unwrap();
        assert_vec_close(
            &out,
            &[
                0.540_302_305_868_139_8,   // cos(1), channel 0
                0.841_470_984_807_896_5,   // sin(1), channel 1
                0.999_950_000_416_665_3,   // cos(0.01), channel 2
                0.009_999_833_334_166_664, // sin(0.01), channel 3
                9.0,                       // tail, untouched
                -4.0,
                7.0,
                3.0,
            ],
            1e-5,
        );
        // The half-split partial form on the same input must NOT
        // produce this: pairings differ, not just names.
        let neox = crate::rope_partial(&input, 1, 10_000.0, 8, 4).unwrap();
        assert!(
            out.iter().zip(&neox).any(|(a, b)| (a - b).abs() > 0.1),
            "interleaved and half-split partials must differ on this input"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn partial_with_full_rotary_dim_equals_the_full_form() {
        let input = [0.3, -1.2, 2.5, 0.7, 1.1, -0.4, 0.9, 2.2];
        let partial = rope_interleaved_partial(&input, 5, 500_000.0, 8, 8).unwrap();
        let full = rope_interleaved(&input, 5, 500_000.0, 8).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(partial, full);
    }

    #[test]
    fn bad_config_is_an_error() {
        assert_eq!(
            rope_interleaved(&[1.0, 0.0], 0, 10_000.0, 4),
            Err(MathError::LengthMismatch {
                op: "rope_interleaved",
                expected: 4,
                actual: 2
            })
        );
        // Partial form refuses an impossible rotary_dim by name.
        assert!(matches!(
            rope_interleaved_partial(&[1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0], 0, 10_000.0, 4, 8),
            Err(MathError::InvalidConfig {
                param: "rotary_dim",
                ..
            })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            rope_interleaved_partial(&[1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0], 0, 10_000.0, 4, 3),
            Err(MathError::InvalidConfig {
                param: "rotary_dim",
                ..
            })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            rope_interleaved(&[1.0, 0.0, 1.0], 0, 10_000.0, 3),
            Err(MathError::InvalidConfig {
                param: "head_dim",
                ..
            })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            rope_interleaved(&[1.0, 0.0], 0, 1.0, 2),
            Err(MathError::InvalidConfig { param: "base", .. })
        ));
    }
}

# K4-K8 results: the wgpu Compute surface completed and proven

Date: 2026-10-30. Machine: ubuntu-server, AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX
(RADV NAVI31, Vulkan). Command:
`cargo test -p wgpu-compute --release -- --nocapture`.
Full log: `~/k4-k8-server-run3.log` on the server.

## Verdict

Every `muse_glimmer::Compute` step now runs on the device.
Final run: all suites green (lib 24, cross-backend 1, K1
synthetic 3, K2/K3 synthetic 3, K4-K8 kernels 7, shader compile
2). The production Glimmer llama-server on the same machine was
health-checked before and after (`{"status":"ok"}`, pid 683675,
untouched throughout).

## Numbers (max abs diff vs the CPU reference, per test)

K4 norms and add:
- rms_norm, eps 1e-5 and eps 1e-8: 5.960e-8
- rms_norm_plain: 1.192e-7
- fused norm_residual vs the trait composition (norm, then
  add): 0.0 exactly
- residual add: exact (asserted equal)

K5 RoPE and KV append:
- rotate vs `torch_math::rope_interleaved` (rows at positions
  5..8, 32 heads x 128, base 500000): 3.055e-7
- append: windowed (window 4) rows landed in ring slots 2, 3;
  global rows in slots 6, 7; contents asserted equal

K6 attention vs `cpu-compute`'s attention step, same Q/K/V
stream through both backends (3-token prefill plus 4 decode
steps, 3 layers: sliding, global, sliding; window 4, so the
ring evicts during the run): all 15 chunk/layer outputs within
8.941e-8.

K7 activations:
- attn_gate through the trait: 2.980e-8
- swiglu vs `torch_math::swiglu`: 2.980e-8

K8 embedding gather vs `cpu-compute`'s embed, every dtype both
backends accept: F32, F16, BF16, Q8_0, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K all
0.0 exactly (the in-kernel dequantizers restate gguf's
reference decoders operation for operation).

K8 head finish vs `muse_glimmer::softcap_scale` over the real
202,048-wide vocab (scale 0.19611613, cap 20.0): 2.384e-6.

## Cross-backend harness (tests/cross_backend.rs)

Synthetic 6-layer Glimmer (sliding x3, global, sliding,
global), real head geometry (32 Q / 2 KV, head dim 128),
hidden 512, FFN 1024, vocab 1024, window 4; all projections,
embedding, and head K-quantized (Q4_K; head Q5_K), norms F32;
byte-identical weights through both backends. Prompt of 4
tokens, then 5 greedy decode steps (9 positions through a
window of 4):

- steps 0-5 max abs logit diff: 2.3842e-7, 2.3842e-7,
  2.3842e-7, 3.5763e-7, 3.5763e-7, 2.3842e-7
- top-1 agreed at every step; worst diff 3.5763e-7 against the
  stated pass bound of 0.5

## Defects found by the proof (and fixed)

1. The K8 gather shaders widened f16 through a nested
   `pack2x16float` call, which is a WGSL type error
   (`pack2x16float` takes `vec2<f32>`). The first server run
   failed at pipeline creation with the validator's message.
   Fixed to the direct `unpack2x16float(bits).x` form in both
   K8 shaders.
2. The K4 fused-vs-composed test called `norm_residual` with
   its residual and branch arguments swapped (2.621e0 diff).
   The kernel was correct; the test call was fixed, and the
   fused form now matches the composition exactly (0.0).
3. An earlier draft of the K8 Q6_K decoder indexed the wrong
   ql bytes and qh bit pairs for streams 2 and 3; caught by
   restating gguf's reference dequantizer stream by stream
   before the server run. The shipped decoder matches
   cpu-compute exactly (0.0) on Q6_K gathers.

## Local gates (this workstation, no suitable adapter)

- `cargo test --workspace`: all suites pass; the GPU tests
  skip with printed reasons by design (llvmpipe does not count
  as an adapter, BACKEND.md Section 6).
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`: clean under the
  workspace's deny-all lints.

## Notes for the next step

- K8's `finish` kernel (scale-then-softcap) is proven but
  deliberately not wired into `lm_head`: the model applies
  `softcap_scale` on the host today, and applying it twice
  would be a bug. It is the epilogue the K3 head GEMV grows
  when the forward becomes device-resident.
- K4's fused `norm_residual` is likewise proven against the
  trait composition and held for the device-resident forward;
  the trait path composes `rms_norm` + `add`.
- Per-call host<->device transfers remain the trait seam's
  cost (weights are cached device-side by name; activations
  move per call), as documented in `compute.rs`.

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/adapter_features.rs =====
//! Adapter feature readout: the diag-capture checklist's open
//! evaluation (2026-11-04 visibility research, carried into
//! bench/diag-capture-2026-11-06.md) asks whether
//! `wgpu::Features::PIPELINE_STATISTICS_QUERY` is offered on
//! gfx1100 under RADV, and, if it is, whether a device can be
//! opened with it and a pipeline-statistics query set created
//! without disturbing anything else.
//!
//! This example answers both from the adapter at runtime: it
//! enumerates every adapter wgpu can see, prints the facts the
//! backend's own detect path records plus the two feature bits
//! the session cares about (timestamp queries, which the diag
//! recorder already uses, and pipeline statistics), and, when
//! pipeline statistics are offered, tries to open a device
//! with the feature and create a query set for two stages.
//! Every refusal is printed by name; the exit code is 0 when
//! the readout itself completed, whatever the answers are
//! (the answers are data, not pass/fail).
//!
//! Usage: `adapter_features`

use std::process::ExitCode;

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let instance = wgpu::Instance::new(&wgpu::InstanceDescriptor {
        backends: wgpu::Backends::VULKAN,
        ..Default::default()
    });
    let adapters = instance.enumerate_adapters(wgpu::Backends::VULKAN);
    if adapters.is_empty() {
        println!("adapter_features: no Vulkan adapters enumerated");
        return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
    }
    for (i, adapter) in adapters.iter().enumerate() {
        let info = adapter.get_info();
        let features = adapter.features();
        let psq = features.contains(wgpu::Features::PIPELINE_STATISTICS_QUERY);
        let tsq = features.contains(wgpu::Features::TIMESTAMP_QUERY);
        println!(
            "adapter[{i}] name={:?} backend={:?} device_type={:?} driver={:?} driver_info={:?}",
            info.name, info.backend, info.device_type, info.driver, info.driver_info
        );
        println!("adapter[{i}] features: timestamp_query={tsq} pipeline_statistics_query={psq}");
        if psq {
            match pollster::block_on(adapter.request_device(&wgpu::DeviceDescriptor {
                label: Some("adapter_features probe"),
                required_features: wgpu::Features::PIPELINE_STATISTICS_QUERY,
                required_limits: adapter.limits(),
                ..Default::default()
            })) {
                Ok((device, _queue)) => {
                    let _query_set = device.create_query_set(&wgpu::QuerySetDescriptor {
                        label: Some("adapter_features pipeline statistics"),
                        ty: wgpu::QueryType::PipelineStatistics(
                            wgpu::PipelineStatisticsTypes::VERTEX_SHADER_INVOCATIONS
                                | wgpu::PipelineStatisticsTypes::COMPUTE_SHADER_INVOCATIONS,
                        ),
                        count: 1,
                    });
                    println!(
                        "adapter[{i}] probe device opened with PIPELINE_STATISTICS_QUERY; \
                         pipeline-statistics query set created (count 1)"
                    );
                }
                Err(e) => {
                    println!("adapter[{i}] probe device refused: {e}");
                }
            }
        }
    }
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/calibrate_profile.rs =====
//! Calibration: measure this machine's own MMV band
//! table on the local adapter and write it as a
//! calibration profile (see [`wgpu_compute::profile`]),
//! replacing the shipped table's one-card provenance
//! with this card's own sweep.
//!
//! Method: the same two arms the shipped table was
//! derived from (bench/mmv-band-routing-2026-11-06.md,
//! bench/mmv-sweep.sh), run back to back in one
//! process through the session's own routing ladder
//! ([`ProjBench`], so the variant measured is the
//! variant a forward would dispatch):
//!
//! - Control arm: the MMV ceiling pinned closed
//!   (`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=1`), K18 and the
//!   chunked form pinned off: every cell measures the
//!   GEMV ladder.
//! - MMV arm: the ceiling open at the kernels' full
//!   band and every band cell pinned to the full band
//!   (`2-16`), so every cell the kernels admit
//!   measures the register-streaming form itself,
//!   not the shipped table's opinion of it.
//!
//! A row is a win for the MMV form under the shipped
//! derivation's rule
//! ([`wgpu_compute::profile::mmv_row_win`]): its
//! MMV-arm median is under 0.98x its control median
//! ([`wgpu_compute::profile::mmv_wins`]), both arms'
//! outputs agree with the direct GEMV form (a
//! disagreeing cell is no measurement), and the row
//! is one the MMV form can dispatch at all. That
//! third clause matters: the MMV arm pins its bands
//! to 2-16, so at batch 1 both arms dispatch the
//! identical GEMV form and a sub-0.98x median there
//! is inter-arm drift, not a form win (the wave19
//! session's derived table carried batch 1 in three
//! cells on exactly that drift; the exclusion lives
//! in the shared derivation helpers, not in this
//! tool's printing). Wins adjacent in the sweep group
//! into the cell's ranges
//! ([`wgpu_compute::profile::derive_band_ranges`]).
//! The arms pin every measured knob in the
//! environment, so a profile already on disk cannot
//! contaminate the measurement: env wins over
//! profile per cell by the resolution precedence.
//!
//! The run prints its evidence before its conclusion:
//! one line per measured row (both arms' medians, the
//! ratio, the agreement, the verdict) ahead of the
//! derived table, and the same lines are written into
//! the profile file as comments, so any derived cell
//! can be checked against the numbers that produced
//! it without re-running the sweep.
//!
//! The profile is keyed to the adapter and driver
//! that produced it and written to `--out PATH`, or
//! to the standard profile location
//! ([`wgpu_compute::profile::profile_path`]) when no
//! `--out` is given. On a machine with no suitable
//! adapter the run refuses by name and writes
//! nothing: there is no hardware to calibrate. A run
//! below the verdict repetition floor also refuses
//! to write: a profile outlives its run and steers
//! future routing, so it is not derived from a smoke.
//!
//! Usage:
//!   calibrate_profile [--out PATH] [--reps N] [--warmup N]

use std::process::ExitCode;
use std::time::Instant;

use muse_glimmer::Dtype;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k12_q8_quant::{ds_vec4s, qs_words};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::{K1Pipeline, K1Weights};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k2_q6k_gemv::{K2Pipeline, K2Weights};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k3_q5k_gemv::{K3Pipeline, K3Weights};
use wgpu_compute::profile::{
    derive_band_ranges, format_band_cell, mmv_row_win, write_profile_with_evidence, AdapterKey,
    CalibrationProfile, RowEvidence,
};
use wgpu_compute::timestamps::DispatchMeta;
use wgpu_compute::{
    DetectPolicy, GpuContext, ProjBench, ProjBenchCall, WgpuCompute, WgpuError, MMV_MAX_BATCH,
};

/// Input width of every swept projection: the model's
/// hidden size (the sweep harness's matrix).
const IN: usize = 6656;

/// The swept shapes as (label, output width): the
/// same three the shipped table was derived from.
const SHAPES: [(&str, usize); 3] = [("attn", 6656), ("ffn", 19968), ("kv", 256)];

/// The swept families as (profile name, dtype).
const FAMILIES: [(&str, Dtype); 3] = [
    ("q4k", Dtype::Q4K),
    ("q5k", Dtype::Q5K),
    ("q6k", Dtype::Q6K),
];

/// The row sweep, identical to the sweep harness's:
/// the whole verify band, the batch-9 cliff point,
/// and the matrix threshold at 16.
const ROWS: [u32; 11] = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 12, 16];

const DEFAULT_REPS: u32 = 25;
const MIN_VERDICT_REPS: u32 = 20;
const DEFAULT_WARMUP: u32 = 3;

/// The nine band env names, composed from the family
/// and shape names exactly as the backend composes
/// its lookups.
fn band_env_names() -> Vec<String> {
    let mut names = Vec::new();
    for (family, _) in FAMILIES {
        for (shape, _) in SHAPES {
            names.push(format!(
                "WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_{}_{}_ROWS",
                family.to_uppercase(),
                shape.to_uppercase()
            ));
        }
    }
    names
}

/// Pin the process environment for one arm. The two
/// arms differ only in the MMV gate and band cells;
/// every other routing knob the ladder reads is
/// pinned to its shipped-off position in both, so the
/// only variable between arms is the MMV form itself.
fn set_arm_env(mmv_arm: bool) {
    // The ladder's other rungs stay out of both arms.
    std::env::set_var("WGPU_COMPUTE_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS", "1");
    std::env::set_var("WGPU_COMPUTE_CHUNKED_GEMV_MAX_ROWS", "1");
    std::env::remove_var("WGPU_COMPUTE_WIDE_MIN_ROWS");
    if mmv_arm {
        std::env::set_var("WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS", "16");
        for name in band_env_names() {
            std::env::set_var(name, "2-16");
        }
    } else {
        std::env::set_var("WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS", "1");
        for name in band_env_names() {
            std::env::remove_var(name);
        }
    }
}

fn arg(args: &[String], flag: &str) -> Option<String> {
    args.windows(2).find(|w| w[0] == flag).map(|w| w[1].clone())
}

fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            ((state >> 40) as u32) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

fn lcg_bytes(seed: u8, count: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state.wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(17);
            state
        })
        .collect()
}

/// A synthetic Q4_K tensor's raw bytes (144-byte
/// blocks), the sweep harness's fixture shape:
/// rotating (d, dmin) f16 headers over LCG payloads.
fn synthetic_q4k(in_elems: usize, out_rows: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let blocks_per_row = in_elems / 256;
    let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(out_rows * blocks_per_row * 144);
    let headers: [(u16, u16); 4] = [
        (0x3c00, 0x3400),
        (0x3800, 0x0000),
        (0x4000, 0x2e66),
        (0x3e00, 0x3800),
    ];
    for row in 0..out_rows {
        for blk in 0..blocks_per_row {
            let (d, dmin) = headers[(row + blk) % headers.len()];
            let mut block = [0u8; 144];
            block[0..2].copy_from_slice(&d.to_le_bytes());
            block[2..4].copy_from_slice(&dmin.to_le_bytes());
            block[4..144].copy_from_slice(&lcg_bytes((row * 7 + blk * 13 + 5) as u8, 140)[..]);
            data.extend_from_slice(&block);
        }
    }
    data
}

/// A synthetic Q5_K tensor's raw bytes (176-byte
/// blocks, same fixture discipline as Q4_K).
fn synthetic_q5k(in_elems: usize, out_rows: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let blocks_per_row = in_elems / 256;
    let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(out_rows * blocks_per_row * 176);
    let headers: [(u16, u16); 4] = [
        (0x3c00, 0x3400),
        (0x3800, 0x0000),
        (0x4000, 0x2e66),
        (0x3e00, 0x3800),
    ];
    for row in 0..out_rows {
        for blk in 0..blocks_per_row {
            let (d, dmin) = headers[(row + blk) % headers.len()];
            let mut block = [0u8; 176];
            block[0..2].copy_from_slice(&d.to_le_bytes());
            block[2..4].copy_from_slice(&dmin.to_le_bytes());
            block[4..176].copy_from_slice(&lcg_bytes((row * 7 + blk * 13 + 5) as u8, 172)[..]);
            data.extend_from_slice(&block);
        }
    }
    data
}

/// A synthetic Q6_K tensor's raw bytes (210-byte
/// blocks, the f16 super-scale at offset 208).
fn synthetic_q6k(in_elems: usize, out_rows: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let blocks_per_row = in_elems / 256;
    let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(out_rows * blocks_per_row * 210);
    let ds: [u16; 3] = [0x3c00, 0x3800, 0x4000];
    for row in 0..out_rows {
        for blk in 0..blocks_per_row {
            let mut block = lcg_bytes((row * 11 + blk * 7 + 3) as u8, 210);
            block[208..210].copy_from_slice(&ds[(row + blk) % ds.len()].to_le_bytes());
            data.extend_from_slice(&block);
        }
    }
    data
}

fn quant_name(quant: Dtype) -> &'static str {
    match quant {
        Dtype::Q4K => "Q4_K",
        Dtype::Q5K => "Q5_K",
        Dtype::Q6K => "Q6_K",
        _ => "other",
    }
}

/// The agreement rule between a routed output and
/// the GEMV control output, the sweep harness's own
/// (mirroring the crate's kernel tests): a form that
/// quantizes its activation answers to the 5%
/// quantization band, an f32 form to the tight
/// reassociation bound.
fn agree(got: &[f32], want: &[f32], quantized: bool) -> bool {
    let scale = want.iter().fold(0.0f32, |a, w| a.max(w.abs()));
    let max_diff = got
        .iter()
        .zip(want.iter())
        .fold(0.0f32, |a, (g, w)| a.max((g - w).abs()));
    if quantized {
        max_diff / scale.max(1.0) <= 0.05
    } else {
        max_diff <= 2e-3 + 5e-5 * scale
    }
}

fn median(sorted: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    let n = sorted.len();
    if n % 2 == 1 {
        sorted[n / 2]
    } else {
        (sorted[n / 2 - 1] + sorted[n / 2]) / 2.0
    }
}

/// The GEMV control weights, one family at a time,
/// uploaded from the same synthetic bytes the routed
/// handle holds.
enum GemvWeights {
    Q4K(K1Weights),
    Q6K(K2Weights),
    Q5K(K3Weights),
}

/// Time one cell on the wall clock: warmup passes
/// untimed, then one submit-plus-poll per repetition.
/// Returns the median ms. (The sweep harness's
/// timing loop, kept identical so the two tools'
/// medians are the same measurement.)
fn time_wall(ctx: &GpuContext, call: &ProjBenchCall, warmup: u32, reps: u32) -> f64 {
    let run_one = |ctx: &GpuContext| {
        let mut encoder = ctx
            .device
            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                label: Some("calibrate pass"),
            });
        {
            let mut pass = encoder.begin_compute_pass(&wgpu::ComputePassDescriptor {
                label: Some("calibrate"),
                timestamp_writes: None,
            });
            call.encode_into(&mut pass);
        }
        ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
    };
    for _ in 0..warmup {
        run_one(ctx);
    }
    ctx.device
        .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
        .expect("poll after warmup");
    let mut times: Vec<f64> = Vec::with_capacity(reps as usize);
    for _ in 0..reps {
        let start = Instant::now();
        run_one(ctx);
        ctx.device
            .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
            .expect("poll in timed loop");
        times.push(start.elapsed().as_secs_f64() * 1e3);
    }
    times.sort_by(|a, b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap());
    median(&times)
}

/// Time one cell with the diag timestamps system, or
/// `None` when the records do not line up with the
/// repetition count (the caller re-times on the wall
/// clock and says so). Returns the median ms.
fn time_diag(
    ctx: &GpuContext,
    call: &ProjBenchCall,
    meta: DispatchMeta,
    warmup: u32,
    reps: u32,
) -> Option<f64> {
    let recorder = ctx.diag_recorder()?;
    let dropped_before = recorder.dropped();
    let run_one = |ctx: &GpuContext, stamp: bool| {
        let stamp = if stamp {
            ctx.diag_stamp(meta.clone())
        } else {
            None
        };
        let mut encoder = ctx
            .device
            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                label: Some("calibrate pass"),
            });
        {
            let mut pass = encoder.begin_compute_pass(&wgpu::ComputePassDescriptor {
                label: Some("calibrate"),
                timestamp_writes: None,
            });
            let slot = stamp.as_ref().and_then(|s| s.begin(&mut pass));
            call.encode_into(&mut pass);
            if let (Some(s), Some(slot)) = (stamp.as_ref(), slot) {
                s.end(&mut pass, slot);
            }
        }
        ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
    };
    for _ in 0..warmup {
        run_one(ctx, false);
    }
    ctx.device
        .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
        .expect("poll after warmup");
    for _ in 0..reps {
        run_one(ctx, true);
    }
    ctx.device
        .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
        .expect("poll after timed loop");
    recorder.drain(&ctx.device, &ctx.queue).expect("diag drain");
    if recorder.dropped() != dropped_before {
        return None;
    }
    let records = recorder.take_records();
    if records.len() != reps as usize {
        return None;
    }
    let mut times: Vec<f64> = records.iter().map(|r| r.duration_ns as f64 / 1e6).collect();
    times.sort_by(|a, b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap());
    Some(median(&times))
}

/// One arm's measurements: per (family, shape, row)
/// the routed variant's median ms and whether its
/// output agreed with the direct GEMV form.
struct Arm {
    medians: [[Vec<f64>; 3]; 3],
    agrees: [[Vec<bool>; 3]; 3],
}

/// Run one arm: every cell of the matrix through the
/// routing ladder of the backend this process just
/// constructed under the arm's env.
fn measure_arm(backend: &WgpuCompute, warmup: u32, reps: u32) -> Arm {
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let timing_diag = ctx.diag_recorder().is_some();
    let k1 = K1Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k1 pipeline");
    let k2 = K2Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k2 pipeline");
    let k3 = K3Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k3 pipeline");
    let max_rows = *ROWS.iter().max().unwrap() as usize;
    let input = lcg_input(7, max_rows * IN);
    let in_buf = ctx.upload_f32("calibrate input", &input);
    let qs_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("calibrate qs", (qs_words(max_rows, IN) * 4) as u64);
    let ds_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("calibrate ds", (ds_vec4s(max_rows, IN) * 16) as u64);

    let blank = |fill: f64| -> [[Vec<f64>; 3]; 3] {
        [
            [
                vec![fill; ROWS.len()],
                vec![fill; ROWS.len()],
                vec![fill; ROWS.len()],
            ],
            [
                vec![fill; ROWS.len()],
                vec![fill; ROWS.len()],
                vec![fill; ROWS.len()],
            ],
            [
                vec![fill; ROWS.len()],
                vec![fill; ROWS.len()],
                vec![fill; ROWS.len()],
            ],
        ]
    };
    let mut medians = blank(0.0);
    let mut agrees = [
        [
            vec![false; ROWS.len()],
            vec![false; ROWS.len()],
            vec![false; ROWS.len()],
        ],
        [
            vec![false; ROWS.len()],
            vec![false; ROWS.len()],
            vec![false; ROWS.len()],
        ],
        [
            vec![false; ROWS.len()],
            vec![false; ROWS.len()],
            vec![false; ROWS.len()],
        ],
    ];

    for (fi, (_, quant)) in FAMILIES.iter().enumerate() {
        for (si, (shape_label, out)) in SHAPES.iter().enumerate() {
            let name = format!("calibrate {} {shape_label}", quant_name(*quant));
            let raw = match quant {
                Dtype::Q4K => synthetic_q4k(IN, *out),
                Dtype::Q5K => synthetic_q5k(IN, *out),
                Dtype::Q6K => synthetic_q6k(IN, *out),
                _ => unreachable!("families are the three K quants"),
            };
            let bench = ProjBench::upload(backend, &name, *quant, &raw, IN, *out)
                .expect("proj bench upload");
            let gemv_w = match quant {
                Dtype::Q4K => {
                    GemvWeights::Q4K(k1.upload(ctx, &name, &raw, IN, *out).expect("k1 upload"))
                }
                Dtype::Q6K => {
                    GemvWeights::Q6K(k2.upload(ctx, &name, &raw, IN, *out).expect("k2 upload"))
                }
                Dtype::Q5K => {
                    GemvWeights::Q5K(k3.upload(ctx, &name, &raw, IN, *out).expect("k3 upload"))
                }
                _ => unreachable!("families are the three K quants"),
            };
            let weight_bytes = bench.byte_len() as u64;
            let out_variant =
                ctx.scratch_buffer("calibrate out variant", (max_rows * out * 4) as u64);
            let out_control =
                ctx.scratch_buffer("calibrate out control", (max_rows * out * 4) as u64);

            for (ri, rows_n) in ROWS.iter().enumerate() {
                let run_control = |ctx: &GpuContext| {
                    let mut encoder =
                        ctx.device
                            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                                label: Some("calibrate control pass"),
                            });
                    {
                        let mut pass = encoder.begin_compute_pass(&wgpu::ComputePassDescriptor {
                            label: Some("calibrate control"),
                            timestamp_writes: None,
                        });
                        match &gemv_w {
                            GemvWeights::Q4K(w) => k1
                                .prepare(ctx, w, &in_buf, &out_control, *rows_n)
                                .expect("k1 prepare")
                                .encode_into(&mut pass),
                            GemvWeights::Q6K(w) => k2
                                .prepare(ctx, w, &in_buf, &out_control, *rows_n)
                                .expect("k2 prepare")
                                .encode_into(&mut pass),
                            GemvWeights::Q5K(w) => k3
                                .prepare(ctx, w, &in_buf, &out_control, *rows_n)
                                .expect("k3 prepare")
                                .encode_into(&mut pass),
                        }
                    }
                    ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
                };
                run_control(ctx);
                ctx.device
                    .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
                    .expect("poll after control");
                let control = ctx
                    .read_f32(&out_control, *rows_n as usize * out)
                    .expect("control readback");

                let call = bench
                    .prepare(
                        backend,
                        &in_buf,
                        &qs_buf,
                        &ds_buf,
                        &out_variant,
                        *rows_n as usize,
                    )
                    .expect("proj bench prepare");
                {
                    let mut encoder =
                        ctx.device
                            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                                label: Some("calibrate check pass"),
                            });
                    {
                        let mut pass = encoder.begin_compute_pass(&wgpu::ComputePassDescriptor {
                            label: Some("calibrate check"),
                            timestamp_writes: None,
                        });
                        call.encode_into(&mut pass);
                    }
                    ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
                }
                ctx.device
                    .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
                    .expect("poll after check");
                let got = ctx
                    .read_f32(&out_variant, *rows_n as usize * out)
                    .expect("variant readback");
                agrees[fi][si][ri] = agree(&got, &control, call.quantized());

                let meta = DispatchMeta {
                    kernel: call.kernel_name(),
                    rows: u64::from(*rows_n),
                    cols: IN as u64,
                    quant: quant_name(*quant),
                    weight_bytes,
                    shape: format!("calibrate {shape_label}"),
                };
                let median_ms = if timing_diag {
                    match time_diag(ctx, &call, meta, warmup, reps) {
                        Some(t) => t,
                        None => time_wall(ctx, &call, warmup, reps),
                    }
                } else {
                    time_wall(ctx, &call, warmup, reps)
                };
                medians[fi][si][ri] = median_ms;
            }
        }
    }
    Arm { medians, agrees }
}

/// Open the backend for one arm, or refuse by name:
/// calibration needs the hardware it calibrates for,
/// so no suitable adapter is a refusal (exit 1), not
/// a skip, and nothing is written.
fn open_backend(arm: &str) -> Result<WgpuCompute, ExitCode> {
    match WgpuCompute::with_policy(&DetectPolicy::default()) {
        Ok(backend) => Ok(backend),
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            eprintln!(
                "REFUSED: no suitable GPU on this machine to calibrate \
                 (arm {arm}; enumerated: [{}]); nothing written",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            Err(ExitCode::from(1))
        }
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("backend construction failed (arm {arm}): {e}");
            Err(ExitCode::from(2))
        }
    }
}

fn run() -> Result<(), ExitCode> {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let reps: u32 = arg(&args, "--reps")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_REPS);
    let warmup: u32 = arg(&args, "--warmup")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_WARMUP);
    if reps < MIN_VERDICT_REPS {
        eprintln!(
            "REFUSED: reps {reps} is below the {MIN_VERDICT_REPS}-repetition \
             verdict floor; a profile is not derived from a smoke. \
             Pass --reps {DEFAULT_REPS} (the default) for a verdict run; \
             nothing written"
        );
        return Err(ExitCode::from(1));
    }
    // Diag timestamps are the timing method when the
    // device grants them (the sweep harness's method);
    // set the mode unless the caller already chose one.
    if std::env::var_os("WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG").is_none() {
        std::env::set_var("WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG", "timing");
    }

    set_arm_env(false);
    let control_backend = open_backend("control")?;
    let key = AdapterKey::from_facts(&control_backend.context().adapter);
    let adapter_name = control_backend.context().adapter.name.clone();
    println!("adapter: {adapter_name}");
    println!("arm control: GEMV ladder (MMV ceiling pinned closed)");
    let control = measure_arm(&control_backend, warmup, reps);
    drop(control_backend);

    set_arm_env(true);
    let mmv_backend = open_backend("mmv")?;
    println!("arm mmv: register-streaming forms (ceiling and bands pinned open)");
    let mmv = measure_arm(&mmv_backend, warmup, reps);
    drop(mmv_backend);

    let mut profile = CalibrationProfile::new(key);
    profile.mmv_max_rows = Some(MMV_MAX_BATCH);
    // Derive every cell first, gathering the per-row
    // evidence as the verdicts are computed, so the
    // evidence prints before the table it produces.
    let mut evidence: Vec<RowEvidence> = Vec::new();
    let mut cells: Vec<(&str, &str, String)> = Vec::new();
    for (fi, (family, _)) in FAMILIES.iter().enumerate() {
        for (si, (shape, _)) in SHAPES.iter().enumerate() {
            let wins: Vec<bool> = ROWS
                .iter()
                .enumerate()
                .map(|(ri, &rows_n)| {
                    let row = RowEvidence {
                        family,
                        shape,
                        rows: rows_n,
                        control_ms: control.medians[fi][si][ri],
                        mmv_ms: mmv.medians[fi][si][ri],
                        agrees: control.agrees[fi][si][ri] && mmv.agrees[fi][si][ri],
                    };
                    evidence.push(row);
                    mmv_row_win(row.rows, row.mmv_ms, row.control_ms, row.agrees)
                })
                .collect();
            cells.push((
                family,
                shape,
                format_band_cell(&derive_band_ranges(&ROWS, &wins)),
            ));
        }
    }
    println!(
        "calibration evidence (one line per measured row; verdicts by \
         wgpu_compute::profile::mmv_row_win):"
    );
    for row in &evidence {
        println!("{}", row.line());
    }
    println!(
        "derived band table (win = MMV median < 0.98x control, both arms agreeing, \
         row inside the kernels' band):"
    );
    for (family, shape, cell) in cells {
        println!("  {family} {shape}: {cell}");
        let placed = profile.set_band_cell_named(family, shape, cell);
        assert!(placed, "family and shape names are the table's own");
    }

    let out_path = match arg(&args, "--out") {
        Some(p) => std::path::PathBuf::from(p),
        None => match wgpu_compute::profile::profile_path() {
            Some(p) => p,
            None => {
                eprintln!(
                    "REFUSED: no profile location resolves (no --out, no \
                     WGPU_COMPUTE_PROFILE_PATH, no XDG_CONFIG_HOME or HOME); \
                     nothing written"
                );
                return Err(ExitCode::from(1));
            }
        },
    };
    if let Err(e) = write_profile_with_evidence(&out_path, &profile, &evidence) {
        eprintln!(
            "REFUSED: writing the profile to {} failed: {e}",
            out_path.display()
        );
        return Err(ExitCode::from(1));
    }
    println!(
        "wrote {} (keyed to [{}])",
        out_path.display(),
        profile.key.describe()
    );
    Ok(())
}

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    match run() {
        Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,
        Err(code) => code,
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/diag_diff.rs =====
//! Diff two diag capture runs: the mechanical answer to
//! "where did the wrong run go wrong".
//!
//! Each argument is a `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG_OUT` prefix from a
//! run made with `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=capture`. The tool reads
//! the two sidecars capture writes beside that prefix
//! (`<prefix>.capture.csv` and `<prefix>.manifest.json`) and
//! compares them:
//!
//! - Manifests first: every field that differs, is missing,
//!   or is extra is printed, so "were these even the same
//!   run" (same build, same adapter and driver, same
//!   resolved configuration, same model file) is answered
//!   before any data is compared.
//! - Then the capture records, position by position: the
//!   first record whose kind, value count, fingerprint,
//!   argmax, or accepted count differs is the divergence,
//!   printed with both runs' records. Everything before it
//!   provably computed the same values.
//!
//! Exit codes: 0 when the runs are identical, 1 when any
//! manifest field or capture record differs, 2 on a usage
//! or read error.
//!
//! Usage: diag_diff <diag_out A> <diag_out B>

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::ExitCode;

use wgpu_compute::{
    capture_sidecar_path, diff_capture_records, diff_manifest_fields, manifest_fields,
    manifest_sidecar_path, parse_capture_csv,
};

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
    if args.len() != 2 {
        eprintln!("usage: diag_diff <diag_out A> <diag_out B>");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    match run(&PathBuf::from(&args[0]), &PathBuf::from(&args[1])) {
        Ok(differs) => {
            if differs {
                ExitCode::from(1)
            } else {
                ExitCode::SUCCESS
            }
        }
        Err(message) => {
            eprintln!("diag_diff: {message}");
            ExitCode::from(2)
        }
    }
}

fn run(a_prefix: &Path, b_prefix: &Path) -> Result<bool, String> {
    let mut differs = false;

    // Manifests: the same-run question.
    let a_manifest = read_optional(&manifest_sidecar_path(a_prefix))?;
    let b_manifest = read_optional(&manifest_sidecar_path(b_prefix))?;
    match (&a_manifest, &b_manifest) {
        (Some(a), Some(b)) => {
            let diffs = diff_manifest_fields(&manifest_fields(a), &manifest_fields(b));
            if diffs.is_empty() {
                println!("manifests: identical");
            } else {
                differs = true;
                println!("manifests: {} field(s) differ:", diffs.len());
                for line in diffs {
                    println!("  {line}");
                }
            }
        }
        (None, None) => println!("manifests: neither run wrote one"),
        (Some(_), None) => {
            differs = true;
            println!("manifests: only the first run wrote one");
        }
        (None, Some(_)) => {
            differs = true;
            println!("manifests: only the second run wrote one");
        }
    }

    // Capture records: the first-divergence question.
    let a_records = read_records(&capture_sidecar_path(a_prefix))?;
    let b_records = read_records(&capture_sidecar_path(b_prefix))?;
    let diff = diff_capture_records(&a_records, &b_records);
    match &diff.divergence {
        None => println!("capture records: identical ({} compared)", diff.compared),
        Some(div) => {
            differs = true;
            println!(
                "capture records: first divergence at seq {} (field {}), after {} agreeing record(s)",
                div.seq,
                div.field,
                diff.compared - 1
            );
            match &div.a {
                Some(r) => println!("  first : {}", r.to_csv_row()),
                None => println!("  first : (no record)"),
            }
            match &div.b {
                Some(r) => println!("  second: {}", r.to_csv_row()),
                None => println!("  second: (no record)"),
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(differs)
}

/// Read a sidecar that may legitimately be absent; absence
/// is `Ok(None)`, any other failure is an error.
fn read_optional(path: &Path) -> Result<Option<String>, String> {
    match std::fs::read_to_string(path) {
        Ok(text) => Ok(Some(text)),
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(None),
        Err(e) => Err(format!("reading {} failed: {e}", path.display())),
    }
}

/// Read and parse a capture CSV sidecar; absence here is an
/// error (a capture run always writes one at finish).
fn read_records(path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<wgpu_compute::CaptureRecord>, String> {
    let text = std::fs::read_to_string(path)
        .map_err(|e| format!("reading {} failed: {e}", path.display()))?;
    parse_capture_csv(&text)
}
