===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/dp4a_probe.rs =====
//! Integer-dot throughput probe: the evidence for whether
//! WGSL's packed i8 dot actually reaches the hardware's
//! integer dot instruction on this backend (RADV's
//! `v_dot4_i32_i8`), rather than naga decomposing it into
//! scalar integer multiplies.
//!
//! Three register-loop kernels, identical launch geometry
//! and trip counts, so their rates are directly comparable:
//!
//! - `packed`: one `dot4I8Packed` per step (4 int MACs).
//! - `unpack`: `unpack4xI8` into a `vec4<i32>` and a vector
//!   dot per step (the same 4 int MACs, if the compiler keeps
//!   them vectorized; if it scalarizes them, this collapses).
//! - `fp32`: one fused multiply-add per step (1 FMA = 2
//!   FLOPs), the FP32 reference rate.
//!
//! A packed rate near 4x the fp32 FMA rate (per step) means
//! the integer dot instruction is doing the work: the
//! 7900 XTX issues one DP4A per lane per clock alongside the
//! FP32 pipes. A packed rate near the fp32 rate means the
//! "integer path" is scalar multiplies in disguise, and the
//! MMQ kernels' measured rate must be read with that in
//! mind. The loop bodies mix the step index into the inputs
//! so nothing constant-folds, and each thread writes one
//! word at the end so nothing dead-code-eliminates.
//!
//! Usage: dp4a_probe [--iters N] [--steps N]

use std::process::ExitCode;
use std::time::Instant;

use wgpu_compute::{DetectPolicy, WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

fn arg(args: &[String], flag: &str) -> Option<String> {
    args.windows(2).find(|w| w[0] == flag).map(|w| w[1].clone())
}

const SHADER: &str = "
@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read_write> sink: array<i32, 1048576>;

const STEPS: u32 = __STEPS__u;

@compute @workgroup_size(256)
fn packed_main(@builtin(global_invocation_id) gid: vec3<u32>) {
    let idx = gid.x;
    var a: u32 = 0x01020304u + idx;
    var b: u32 = 0x05060708u;
    var acc: i32 = 0;
    for (var i = 0u; i < STEPS; i++) {
        a = a * 1664525u + 1013904223u;
        acc += dot4I8Packed(a, b);
    }
    sink[idx] = acc;
}

@compute @workgroup_size(256)
fn unpack_main(@builtin(global_invocation_id) gid: vec3<u32>) {
    let idx = gid.x;
    var a: u32 = 0x01020304u + idx;
    let b = vec4<i32>(5, 6, 7, 8);
    var acc: i32 = 0;
    for (var i = 0u; i < STEPS; i++) {
        a = a * 1664525u + 1013904223u;
        acc += dot(unpack4xI8(a), b);
    }
    sink[idx] = acc;
}

@compute @workgroup_size(256)
fn fp32_main(@builtin(global_invocation_id) gid: vec3<u32>) {
    let idx = gid.x;
    var a: f32 = 1.0009765625 + f32(idx) * 0.0000001;
    var acc: f32 = 0.0;
    for (var i = 0u; i < STEPS; i++) {
        acc = a * acc + 1.0000001;
        a = a * 1.0000001 + 0.0000001;
    }
    sink[idx] = i32(acc);
}
";

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let iters: u32 = arg(&args, "--iters")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(20);
    let steps: u32 = arg(&args, "--steps")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(4096);
    let backend = match WgpuCompute::with_policy(&DetectPolicy::default()) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            println!(
                "SKIP: no suitable GPU on this machine (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
        }
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("backend construction failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    println!("adapter: {}", ctx.adapter.name);
    let threads: u64 = 1_048_576;
    let workgroups = (threads / 256) as u32;
    let src = SHADER.replace("__STEPS__", &steps.to_string());
    let module = ctx
        .device
        .create_shader_module(wgpu::ShaderModuleDescriptor {
            label: Some("dp4a probe"),
            source: wgpu::ShaderSource::Wgsl(src.into()),
        });
    let sink = ctx.scratch_buffer("dp4a sink", threads * 4);
    let layout = ctx
        .device
        .create_bind_group_layout(&wgpu::BindGroupLayoutDescriptor {
            label: Some("dp4a probe layout"),
            entries: &[wgpu::BindGroupLayoutEntry {
                binding: 0,
                visibility: wgpu::ShaderStages::COMPUTE,
                ty: wgpu::BindingType::Buffer {
                    ty: wgpu::BufferBindingType::Storage { read_only: false },
                    has_dynamic_offset: false,
                    min_binding_size: None,
                },
                count: None,
            }],
        });
    let bind_group = ctx.device.create_bind_group(&wgpu::BindGroupDescriptor {
        label: Some("dp4a probe bind group"),
        layout: &layout,
        entries: &[wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
            binding: 0,
            resource: sink.as_entire_binding(),
        }],
    });
    let pipe_layout = ctx
        .device
        .create_pipeline_layout(&wgpu::PipelineLayoutDescriptor {
            label: Some("dp4a probe pipeline layout"),
            bind_group_layouts: &[&layout],
            push_constant_ranges: &[],
        });
    for (name, entry) in [
        ("packed dot4I8Packed", "packed_main"),
        ("unpack vec4<i32> dot", "unpack_main"),
        ("fp32 fma", "fp32_main"),
    ] {
        let pipeline = ctx
            .device
            .create_compute_pipeline(&wgpu::ComputePipelineDescriptor {
                label: Some(name),
                layout: Some(&pipe_layout),
                module: &module,
                entry_point: Some(entry),
                compilation_options: wgpu::PipelineCompilationOptions::default(),
                cache: None,
            });
        let run = |ctx: &wgpu_compute::GpuContext| {
            let mut encoder = ctx
                .device
                .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                    label: Some("dp4a probe pass"),
                });
            {
                let mut pass = encoder.begin_compute_pass(&wgpu::ComputePassDescriptor {
                    label: Some("dp4a probe"),
                    timestamp_writes: None,
                });
                pass.set_pipeline(&pipeline);
                pass.set_bind_group(0, &bind_group, &[]);
                pass.dispatch_workgroups(workgroups, 1, 1);
            }
            ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
        };
        for _ in 0..3 {
            run(ctx);
        }
        ctx.device
            .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
            .expect("poll after warmup");
        let start = Instant::now();
        for _ in 0..iters {
            run(ctx);
        }
        ctx.device
            .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
            .expect("poll after timed loop");
        let secs = start.elapsed().as_secs_f64() / f64::from(iters);
        let steps_done = threads * u64::from(steps);
        if name.starts_with("fp32") {
            let tflops = steps_done as f64 * 2.0 / secs / 1e12;
            println!("{name:<22} {:>8.3} ms  {tflops:>7.2} TFLOPS", secs * 1e3);
        } else {
            let tops = steps_done as f64 * 4.0 / secs / 1e12;
            println!(
                "{name:<22} {:>8.3} ms  {tops:>7.2} TOPS (int8 MAC)",
                secs * 1e3
            );
        }
    }
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

===== END FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/dp4a_probe.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/k10_bench.rs =====
//! K10/K11 prefill GEMM bench: hold the real file's largest
//! Q4_K and Q6_K tensors resident, run each projection shape
//! at a prefill batch through the GEMV kernels and through
//! the GEMM variants, and report per-tensor pass time,
//! tokens/s (batch rows per second), and the effective weight
//! stream. The GEMV at batch 1 doubles as the window canary:
//! its GB/s is the number BACKEND.md's healthy windows put at
//! ~816 (Q4_K) and ~832 (Q6_K), so a slow window shows itself
//! before any GEMM verdict is read from it.
//!
//! Usage:
//!   k10_bench [--model PATH] [--batch N] [--iters N]
//!             [--warmup N] [--budget-mib N]
//!
//! The resident set is capped by --budget-mib for the same
//! coexistence reason as k1_bench; the default 512 MiB fits
//! the largest tensors of both families (an FFN gate at
//! 74.8 MB, an FFN down at 109.4 MB) with room to spare.

use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;
use std::time::Instant;

use gguf::{GgmlType, GgufFile};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k10_q4k_gemm::{GemmShape, K10Call, K10Pipeline};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k11_q6k_gemm::{K11Call, K11Pipeline};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::{K1Call, K1Pipeline, K1Weights, ACT_NONE};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k2_q6k_gemv::{K2Call, K2Pipeline, K2Weights};
use wgpu_compute::{DetectPolicy, WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

fn arg(args: &[String], flag: &str) -> Option<String> {
    args.windows(2).find(|w| w[0] == flag).map(|w| w[1].clone())
}

fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            ((state >> 40) as u32) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

/// One encodable projection dispatch, whichever kernel built
/// it; the bench times compositions, not types.
enum BenchCall {
    K1(K1Call),
    K2(K2Call),
    K10(K10Call),
    K11(K11Call),
}

impl BenchCall {
    fn encode_into(&self, pass: &mut wgpu::ComputePass<'_>) {
        match self {
            BenchCall::K1(c) => c.encode_into(pass),
            BenchCall::K2(c) => c.encode_into(pass),
            BenchCall::K10(c) => c.encode_into(pass),
            BenchCall::K11(c) => c.encode_into(pass),
        }
    }
}

struct TensorBench {
    name: String,
    family: &'static str,
    bytes: u64,
    inn: usize,
    out: usize,
    calls: Vec<(String, BenchCall)>,
}

fn time_calls(ctx: &wgpu_compute::GpuContext, calls: &[BenchCall], warmup: u32, iters: u32) -> f64 {
    let run_pass = |ctx: &wgpu_compute::GpuContext| {
        let mut encoder = ctx
            .device
            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                label: Some("k10 bench pass"),
            });
        {
            let mut pass = encoder.begin_compute_pass(&wgpu::ComputePassDescriptor {
                label: Some("k10 bench"),
                timestamp_writes: None,
            });
            for c in calls {
                c.encode_into(&mut pass);
            }
        }
        ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
    };
    for _ in 0..warmup {
        run_pass(ctx);
    }
    ctx.device
        .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
        .expect("poll after warmup");
    let start = Instant::now();
    for _ in 0..iters {
        run_pass(ctx);
    }
    ctx.device
        .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
        .expect("poll after timed loop");
    start.elapsed().as_secs_f64() / f64::from(iters)
}

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let model = arg(&args, "--model").unwrap_or_else(|| {
        "/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf".to_string()
    });
    let batch: u32 = arg(&args, "--batch")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(64);
    let iters: u32 = arg(&args, "--iters")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(10);
    let warmup: u32 = arg(&args, "--warmup")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(2);
    let budget: u64 = arg(&args, "--budget-mib")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse::<u64>().ok())
        .unwrap_or(512)
        * 1024
        * 1024;

    let file = match GgufFile::open(Path::new(&model)) {
        Ok(f) => f,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("cannot open {model}: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    // The largest tensor of each family, plus the largest
    // Q4_K tensor whose output is attention-width (the QKV
    // batch's shape class), greedily under the budget.
    let mut by_size: Vec<(String, GgmlType, u64, usize, usize)> = file
        .tensors()
        .iter()
        .filter(|t| matches!(t.ggml_type(), Some(GgmlType::Q4K | GgmlType::Q6K)))
        .filter_map(|t| {
            let bytes = t.byte_len()?;
            let dims = t.dims();
            Some((
                t.name().to_string(),
                t.ggml_type()?,
                bytes,
                dims[0] as usize,
                dims[1] as usize,
            ))
        })
        .collect();
    by_size.sort_by_key(|c| std::cmp::Reverse(c.2));
    let mut chosen: Vec<(String, GgmlType, u64, usize, usize)> = Vec::new();
    let mut seen_families: Vec<GgmlType> = Vec::new();
    let mut total: u64 = 0;
    for cand in &by_size {
        let new_family = !seen_families.contains(&cand.1);
        if !new_family && chosen.len() >= 3 {
            continue;
        }
        if total + cand.2 > budget {
            continue;
        }
        total += cand.2;
        seen_families.push(cand.1);
        chosen.push(cand.clone());
        if chosen.len() >= 4 {
            break;
        }
    }
    if chosen.is_empty() {
        eprintln!("no Q4_K/Q6_K tensor fits the budget");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }

    let backend = match WgpuCompute::with_policy(&DetectPolicy::default()) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            println!(
                "SKIP: no suitable GPU on this machine (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
        }
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("backend construction failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    println!("adapter: {}", ctx.adapter.name);
    println!("batch: {batch}, iters {iters} (+{warmup} warmup)");

    let k1 = K1Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k1 pipeline");
    let k2 = K2Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k2 pipeline");
    let gemm_shapes = [
        GemmShape::new(64, 256),
        GemmShape::new(64, 128),
        GemmShape::new(32, 128),
        GemmShape::new(32, 256),
    ];
    let mut k10s: Vec<(String, K10Pipeline)> = Vec::new();
    let mut k11s: Vec<(String, K11Pipeline)> = Vec::new();
    for shape in gemm_shapes {
        match K10Pipeline::with_shape_act(&ctx.device, shape, ACT_NONE) {
            Ok(p) => k10s.push((shape.name(), p)),
            Err(e) => println!("k10 {} unavailable: {e}", shape.name()),
        }
        match K11Pipeline::with_shape_act(&ctx.device, shape, ACT_NONE) {
            Ok(p) => k11s.push((shape.name(), p)),
            Err(e) => println!("k11 {} unavailable: {e}", shape.name()),
        }
    }

    let mut benches: Vec<TensorBench> = Vec::new();
    // Keep the weight handles alive beside their calls.
    let mut keep_q4: Vec<K1Weights> = Vec::new();
    let mut keep_q6: Vec<K2Weights> = Vec::new();
    for (name, ty, bytes, inn, out) in &chosen {
        let raw = file.tensor_bytes(name).expect("tensor bytes");
        let input = lcg_input(7, batch as usize * inn);
        let in_buf = ctx.upload_f32("bench input", &input);
        let out_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("bench output", (batch as usize * out * 4) as u64);
        let mut calls: Vec<(String, BenchCall)> = Vec::new();
        match ty {
            GgmlType::Q4K => {
                let w = k1.upload(ctx, name, raw, *inn, *out).expect("k1 upload");
                calls.push((
                    "gemv".to_string(),
                    BenchCall::K1(
                        k1.prepare(ctx, &w, &in_buf, &out_buf, batch)
                            .expect("k1 prepare"),
                    ),
                ));
                for (label, g) in &k10s {
                    calls.push((
                        format!("gemm {label}"),
                        BenchCall::K10(
                            g.prepare(ctx, &w, &in_buf, &out_buf, batch)
                                .expect("k10 prepare"),
                        ),
                    ));
                }
                keep_q4.push(w);
            }
            GgmlType::Q6K => {
                let w = k2.upload(ctx, name, raw, *inn, *out).expect("k2 upload");
                calls.push((
                    "gemv".to_string(),
                    BenchCall::K2(
                        k2.prepare(ctx, &w, &in_buf, &out_buf, batch)
                            .expect("k2 prepare"),
                    ),
                ));
                for (label, g) in &k11s {
                    calls.push((
                        format!("gemm {label}"),
                        BenchCall::K11(
                            g.prepare(ctx, &w, &in_buf, &out_buf, batch)
                                .expect("k11 prepare"),
                        ),
                    ));
                }
                keep_q6.push(w);
            }
            _ => unreachable!(),
        }
        benches.push(TensorBench {
            name: name.clone(),
            family: if *ty == GgmlType::Q4K { "Q4_K" } else { "Q6_K" },
            bytes: *bytes,
            inn: *inn,
            out: *out,
            calls,
        });
    }
    // The weight handles stay in scope until every timed pass
    // has run (their buffers back the calls' bind groups).
    let _residency = (keep_q4, keep_q6);

    for bench in &benches {
        println!(
            "\n{} [{} x {}] {}: {} bytes",
            bench.name, bench.inn, bench.out, bench.family, bench.bytes
        );
        for (label, call) in &bench.calls {
            let secs = time_calls(ctx, std::slice::from_ref(call), warmup, iters);
            let ms = secs * 1e3;
            let tok_s = f64::from(batch) / secs;
            let stream_once = bench.bytes as f64 / secs / 1e9;
            let stream_per_row = stream_once * f64::from(batch);
            println!(
                "  {label:<12} {ms:9.3} ms/pass  {tok_s:9.1} tok/s  stream {stream_once:8.1} GB/s (x1)  {stream_per_row:9.1} GB/s (x{batch})"
            );
        }
    }
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

===== END FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/k10_bench.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/k1_bench.rs =====
//! K1 streaming bench (BACKEND.md Section 7, tier 1 shape):
//! hold a set of the real file's largest Q4_K tensors resident,
//! dispatch the GEMV over all of them per iteration, and report
//! the effective streaming bandwidth against llama.cpp's measured
//! 708 GB/s and the 637 GB/s ash decision trigger.
//!
//! Usage:
//!   k1_bench [--model PATH] [--budget-mib N] [--iters N] [--warmup N]
//!            [--variant NAME] [--wg N]
//!
//! `--variant` selects the K1 shape (see `K1Shape::from_name`:
//! `v2` is the first landing's kernel; `r2`, `r4sgf16`, ... are
//! the llama-family tunings; `shipped` is whatever
//! `K1Pipeline::new` would build on this device). `--wg`
//! overrides the workgroup size of a llama-family shape.
//!
//! The resident set is capped by --budget-mib because this bench
//! runs beside whatever already holds VRAM on the card (on the
//! server, the production llama-server). The default 160 MiB is
//! sized for that coexistence and is roughly twice the card's
//! 96 MiB Infinity Cache, so the stream genuinely comes from
//! VRAM; the tool prints the card's VRAM state it found so the
//! report carries its own constraint. A full-model residency run
//! (14.89 GiB) needs the card to itself and is a separate,
//! scheduled measurement.

use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;
use std::time::Instant;

use gguf::{GgmlType, GgufFile};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::{pack_input_f16, K1Call, K1Pipeline, K1Shape, K1Weights};
use wgpu_compute::{DetectPolicy, WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

/// llama.cpp Vulkan's measured effective bandwidth on this card
/// (BACKEND.md Section 1): the number to match.
const LLAMA_CPP_GBS: f64 = 708.0;
/// The ash decision trigger (BACKEND.md Section 8): below 90
/// percent of llama.cpp's number after tuning, evaluate raw
/// Vulkan.
const ASH_TRIGGER_GBS: f64 = 637.0;

fn arg(args: &[String], flag: &str) -> Option<String> {
    args.windows(2).find(|w| w[0] == flag).map(|w| w[1].clone())
}

/// Deterministic pseudo-random f32s in [-0.5, 0.5) via a 64-bit
/// LCG, matching `k1_check`.
fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            ((state >> 40) as u32) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Best-effort VRAM accounting from sysfs, printed so the bench
/// report states the card's occupancy it ran under.
fn vram_state() -> Option<String> {
    // Only the discrete card exposes mem_info files; skip every
    // card that does not rather than giving up at the first one.
    for card in 0..8 {
        let base = format!("/sys/class/drm/card{card}/device");
        let Ok(total) = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("{base}/mem_info_vram_total")) else {
            continue;
        };
        let Ok(used) = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("{base}/mem_info_vram_used")) else {
            continue;
        };
        let (Ok(total), Ok(used)) = (total.trim().parse::<u64>(), used.trim().parse::<u64>())
        else {
            continue;
        };
        return Some(format!(
            "card{card} VRAM: {used} of {total} bytes in use ({} free)",
            total - used
        ));
    }
    None
}

struct Resident {
    // The weights handle is never read after setup; it is kept so
    // the buffer's residency is explicit in this tool's own
    // accounting, beside the bind group that references it.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    weights: K1Weights,
    call: K1Call,
}

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let model = arg(&args, "--model").unwrap_or_else(|| {
        "/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf".to_string()
    });
    let budget_mib: u64 = arg(&args, "--budget-mib")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(160);
    let iters: u32 = arg(&args, "--iters")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(25);
    let warmup: u32 = arg(&args, "--warmup")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(3);
    let variant = arg(&args, "--variant").unwrap_or_else(|| "shipped".to_string());
    let wg_override: Option<u32> = arg(&args, "--wg").and_then(|s| s.parse().ok());
    let budget = budget_mib * 1024 * 1024;

    let file = match GgufFile::open(Path::new(&model)) {
        Ok(f) => f,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("cannot open {model}: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    // Largest Q4_K tensors first, greedily packed under the
    // budget. Glimmer's Q4_K population is dominated by the
    // 74,760,192-byte FFN gate/up tensors.
    let mut candidates: Vec<(String, u64, usize, usize)> = file
        .tensors()
        .iter()
        .filter(|t| t.ggml_type() == Some(GgmlType::Q4K))
        .filter_map(|t| {
            let bytes = t.byte_len()?;
            let dims = t.dims();
            Some((
                t.name().to_string(),
                bytes,
                dims[0] as usize,
                dims[1] as usize,
            ))
        })
        .collect();
    candidates.sort_by_key(|c| std::cmp::Reverse(c.1));
    let mut chosen: Vec<(String, u64, usize, usize)> = Vec::new();
    let mut total_bytes: u64 = 0;
    for candidate in candidates {
        if total_bytes + candidate.1 > budget {
            continue;
        }
        total_bytes += candidate.1;
        chosen.push(candidate);
    }
    if chosen.is_empty() {
        eprintln!("no Q4_K tensor fits the {budget_mib} MiB budget");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }

    let backend = match WgpuCompute::with_policy(&DetectPolicy::default()) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            println!(
                "SKIP: no suitable GPU on this machine (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
        }
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("backend construction failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let mut shape = if variant == "shipped" {
        wgpu_compute::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::shipped_shape(ctx.device.features())
    } else {
        match K1Shape::from_name(&variant) {
            Some(s) => s,
            None => {
                eprintln!(
                    "unknown variant {variant:?} (expected v2, r<rows>[sg][f16], or shipped)"
                );
                return ExitCode::from(2);
            }
        }
    };
    if let Some(wg) = wg_override {
        shape.workgroup = wg;
    }
    let pipeline = match K1Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape) {
        Ok(p) => p,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("k1 pipeline for shape {} failed: {e}", shape.name());
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    println!("adapter: {}", ctx.adapter.name);
    println!(
        "shape: {} (rows {}, workgroup {}, subgroup {}, f16 activations {}, legacy {})",
        shape.name(),
        shape.rows,
        shape.workgroup,
        shape.subgroup,
        shape.f16_activations,
        shape.legacy
    );
    if let Some(state) = vram_state() {
        println!("{state}");
    }
    println!(
        "resident set: {} tensors, {} bytes streamed per iteration",
        chosen.len(),
        total_bytes
    );

    let mut resident: Vec<Resident> = Vec::new();
    for (name, _bytes, inn, out) in &chosen {
        let bytes = file.tensor_bytes(name).expect("tensor bytes");
        let weights = match pipeline.upload(ctx, name, bytes, *inn, *out) {
            Ok(w) => w,
            Err(e) => {
                eprintln!("upload of {name} failed: {e}");
                return ExitCode::from(2);
            }
        };
        let input = lcg_input(7, *inn);
        let in_bytes: Vec<u8> = if shape.input_is_f16() {
            pack_input_f16(&input)
        } else {
            input.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect()
        };
        let input_buffer = ctx.device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
            label: Some("bench input"),
            size: in_bytes.len() as u64,
            usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::STORAGE | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
            mapped_at_creation: false,
        });
        ctx.queue.write_buffer(&input_buffer, 0, &in_bytes);
        let output_buffer = ctx.device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
            label: Some("bench output"),
            size: (*out * 4) as u64,
            usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::STORAGE,
            mapped_at_creation: false,
        });
        let call = match pipeline.prepare(ctx, &weights, &input_buffer, &output_buffer, 1) {
            Ok(c) => c,
            Err(e) => {
                eprintln!("prepare for {name} failed: {e}");
                return ExitCode::from(2);
            }
        };
        println!("  {name}: {} bytes [{inn} x {out}]", weights.byte_len);
        resident.push(Resident { weights, call });
    }

    let run_pass = |ctx: &wgpu_compute::GpuContext| {
        let mut encoder = ctx
            .device
            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                label: Some("k1 bench pass"),
            });
        for r in &resident {
            r.call.encode(&mut encoder);
        }
        ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
    };

    for _ in 0..warmup {
        run_pass(ctx);
    }
    if ctx
        .device
        .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
        .is_err()
    {
        eprintln!("device poll failed after warmup");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    let start = Instant::now();
    for _ in 0..iters {
        run_pass(ctx);
    }
    if ctx
        .device
        .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
        .is_err()
    {
        eprintln!("device poll failed after timed loop");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    let elapsed = start.elapsed().as_secs_f64();
    let streamed = total_bytes as f64 * f64::from(iters);
    let gbs = streamed / elapsed / 1e9;
    println!(
        "iters {iters} (+{warmup} warmup): {streamed:.0} bytes in {elapsed:.3} s = {gbs:.1} GB/s"
    );
    println!("reference: llama.cpp Vulkan {LLAMA_CPP_GBS:.0} GB/s; ash trigger {ASH_TRIGGER_GBS:.0} GB/s");
    if gbs >= LLAMA_CPP_GBS {
        println!(
            "verdict: at or above llama.cpp's measured bandwidth; wgpu stays, no ash question"
        );
    } else if gbs >= ASH_TRIGGER_GBS {
        println!(
            "verdict: above the ash trigger ({:.1}% of llama.cpp); wgpu stays per BACKEND.md Section 8",
            100.0 * gbs / LLAMA_CPP_GBS
        );
    } else {
        println!(
            "verdict: BELOW the ash trigger ({:.1}% of llama.cpp); BACKEND.md Section 8's ash evaluation trigger fires",
            100.0 * gbs / LLAMA_CPP_GBS
        );
    }
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

===== END FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/k1_bench.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/k1_check.rs =====
//! K1 correctness on the real file: run one real Q4_K tensor
//! through the wgpu backend's `proj` and compare against the CPU
//! reference (the `gguf` crate's dequantizer plus `torch-math`'s
//! matvec), the same cross-check style the `gguf` crate's own
//! real-file proofs use.
//!
//! Usage:
//!   k1_check [--model PATH] [--tensor NAME] [--seed N] [--variant NAME]
//!
//! Defaults: the Glimmer Q4_K_M file on the server and its first
//! FFN gate tensor. Run it on the machine whose GPU is under test
//! (the 7900 XTX server): the default selection policy refuses
//! machines without a discrete Vulkan GPU, and this tool reports
//! that as a SKIP (exit 0), not a failure. A real mismatch exits 1.
//!
//! `--variant` selects the K1 shape under test (see
//! `K1Shape::from_name`); the default is the shipped shape for
//! the device, i.e. exactly what `Compute::proj` would run.

use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;

use gguf::{GgmlType, GgufFile};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::{shipped_shape, K1Pipeline, K1Shape};
use wgpu_compute::{DetectPolicy, WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

/// Deterministic pseudo-random f32s in [-0.5, 0.5): a 64-bit LCG,
/// so the check input is reproducible without a rand dependency.
fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            let bits = (state >> 40) as u32;
            bits as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

fn arg(args: &[String], flag: &str) -> Option<String> {
    args.windows(2).find(|w| w[0] == flag).map(|w| w[1].clone())
}

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let model = arg(&args, "--model").unwrap_or_else(|| {
        "/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf".to_string()
    });
    let tensor = arg(&args, "--tensor").unwrap_or_else(|| "blk.0.ffn_gate.weight".to_string());
    let seed: u64 = arg(&args, "--seed")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(42);
    let variant = arg(&args, "--variant").unwrap_or_else(|| "shipped".to_string());

    let file = match GgufFile::open(Path::new(&model)) {
        Ok(f) => f,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("cannot open {model}: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let info = match file.tensor_info(&tensor) {
        Ok(i) => i.clone(),
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("tensor {tensor} not readable in {model}: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    if info.ggml_type() != Some(GgmlType::Q4K) {
        eprintln!(
            "tensor {tensor} is {}, not Q4_K; K1 checks Q4_K tensors only",
            info.type_name()
        );
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    let dims = info.dims().to_vec();
    let (inn, out) = (dims[0] as usize, dims[1] as usize);
    let bytes = match file.tensor_bytes(&tensor) {
        Ok(b) => b.to_vec(),
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("cannot read bytes of {tensor}: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    println!(
        "tensor {tensor}: [{inn} x {out}] Q4_K, {} bytes",
        bytes.len()
    );

    let input = lcg_input(seed, inn);
    // CPU reference: gguf's dequantizer is ggml-exact, and matvec
    // sums in row order; the GPU sums in a tree, so the comparison
    // tolerance is relative to the output's own scale.
    let weights = gguf::dequant::dequantize(GgmlType::Q4K, &bytes, inn * out);
    let expected = torch_math::matvec(&weights, out, inn, &input).expect("cpu reference matvec");

    let backend = match WgpuCompute::with_policy(&DetectPolicy::default()) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            println!(
                "SKIP: no suitable GPU on this machine (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
        }
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("backend construction failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    println!("adapter: {}", ctx.adapter.name);

    let shape = if variant == "shipped" {
        shipped_shape(ctx.device.features())
    } else {
        match K1Shape::from_name(&variant) {
            Some(s) => s,
            None => {
                eprintln!(
                    "unknown variant {variant:?} (expected v2, r<rows>[sg][f16], or shipped)"
                );
                return ExitCode::from(2);
            }
        }
    };
    println!(
        "shape: {} (rows {}, workgroup {}, subgroup {}, f16 activations {}, legacy {})",
        shape.name(),
        shape.rows,
        shape.workgroup,
        shape.subgroup,
        shape.f16_activations,
        shape.legacy
    );
    let pipeline = match K1Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape) {
        Ok(p) => p,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("k1 pipeline for shape {} failed: {e}", shape.name());
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let weights = match pipeline.upload(ctx, &tensor, &bytes, inn, out) {
        Ok(w) => w,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("upload of {tensor} failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let got = match pipeline.run(ctx, &weights, &input) {
        Ok(g) => g,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("gpu run failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };

    let mut max_abs = 0.0f32;
    let mut scale = 0.0f32;
    let mut dot = 0.0f64;
    let mut norm_g = 0.0f64;
    let mut norm_e = 0.0f64;
    for (g, e) in got.iter().zip(expected.iter()) {
        max_abs = max_abs.max((g - e).abs());
        scale = scale.max(e.abs());
        dot += f64::from(*g) * f64::from(*e);
        norm_g += f64::from(*g) * f64::from(*g);
        norm_e += f64::from(*e) * f64::from(*e);
    }
    let cosine = dot / (norm_g.sqrt() * norm_e.sqrt());
    let rel = max_abs / scale.max(1.0);
    println!(
        "outputs {out}: max_abs_err {max_abs:.6} at output scale {scale:.3} (rel {rel:.3e}), cosine {cosine:.9}"
    );
    // f32 reassociation between a sequential CPU sum and the GPU
    // tree reduction lands near 1e-6 relative; the bound leaves
    // two orders of headroom and still catches any layout error,
    // which would be off by whole dequantized values.
    if rel < 1e-4 && cosine > 0.999_999 {
        println!("K1 CHECK PASS");
        ExitCode::SUCCESS
    } else {
        println!("K1 CHECK FAIL");
        ExitCode::from(1)
    }
}

===== END FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/k1_check.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/k1_fixture_dump.rs =====
//! K1 fixture dump for cross-language kernel benches (bench
//! tooling for the Mojo kernel test, bench/mojo-kernel-test-
//! 2026-11-07.md; not part of the engine and not a shipped path).
//!
//! Writes the fixture files a non-Rust K1 port needs to run the
//! SAME math on the SAME data as `k1_check`:
//!   weights_q4k.bin  raw Q4_K bytes of the tensor, file order
//!   input_f32.bin    the check's deterministic LCG input (f32 LE)
//!   ref_f32.bin      CPU reference output (gguf dequantizer plus
//!                    torch-math matvec, the harness's own path)
//!   gpu_f32.bin      the shipped wgpu K1 pipeline's output
//!   fixture.txt      shapes and the gpu-vs-ref cosine/rel line in
//!                    exactly the format `k1_check` prints
//!
//! Usage:
//!   k1_fixture_dump --out DIR [--model PATH] [--tensor NAME]
//!                   [--seed N]
//!
//! Defaults match `k1_check`: the Glimmer Q4_K_M file, its first
//! FFN gate tensor, seed 42, shipped K1 shape. On a machine with
//! no suitable GPU the tool reports SKIP (exit 0) after writing
//! the CPU-side files, like `k1_check`.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::ExitCode;

use gguf::{GgmlType, GgufFile};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::{shipped_shape, K1Pipeline};
use wgpu_compute::{DetectPolicy, WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

/// Deterministic pseudo-random f32s in [-0.5, 0.5): the same
/// 64-bit LCG `k1_check` uses, so the input is bit-identical.
fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            let bits = (state >> 40) as u32;
            bits as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

fn arg(args: &[String], flag: &str) -> Option<String> {
    args.windows(2).find(|w| w[0] == flag).map(|w| w[1].clone())
}

fn f32_bytes(values: &[f32]) -> Vec<u8> {
    values.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect()
}

fn write_file(dir: &Path, name: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    let path = dir.join(name);
    std::fs::write(&path, bytes).map_err(|e| format!("cannot write {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    println!("wrote {} ({} bytes)", path.display(), bytes.len());
    Ok(path)
}

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let Some(out_dir) = arg(&args, "--out") else {
        eprintln!("usage: k1_fixture_dump --out DIR [--model PATH] [--tensor NAME] [--seed N]");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    };
    let out_dir = PathBuf::from(out_dir);
    if let Err(e) = std::fs::create_dir_all(&out_dir) {
        eprintln!("cannot create {}: {e}", out_dir.display());
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    let model = arg(&args, "--model").unwrap_or_else(|| {
        "/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf".to_string()
    });
    let tensor = arg(&args, "--tensor").unwrap_or_else(|| "blk.0.ffn_gate.weight".to_string());
    let seed: u64 = arg(&args, "--seed")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(42);

    let file = match GgufFile::open(Path::new(&model)) {
        Ok(f) => f,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("cannot open {model}: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let info = match file.tensor_info(&tensor) {
        Ok(i) => i.clone(),
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("tensor {tensor} not readable in {model}: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    if info.ggml_type() != Some(GgmlType::Q4K) {
        eprintln!(
            "REFUSAL k1_fixture_dump: tensor {tensor} is {}, not Q4_K",
            info.type_name()
        );
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    let dims = info.dims().to_vec();
    let (inn, out) = (dims[0] as usize, dims[1] as usize);
    let bytes = match file.tensor_bytes(&tensor) {
        Ok(b) => b.to_vec(),
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("cannot read bytes of {tensor}: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    println!(
        "tensor {tensor}: [{inn} x {out}] Q4_K, {} bytes",
        bytes.len()
    );

    let input = lcg_input(seed, inn);
    let weights = gguf::dequant::dequantize(GgmlType::Q4K, &bytes, inn * out);
    let expected = torch_math::matvec(&weights, out, inn, &input).expect("cpu reference matvec");

    for (name, data) in [
        ("weights_q4k.bin", bytes.as_slice()),
        ("input_f32.bin", &f32_bytes(&input)),
        ("ref_f32.bin", &f32_bytes(&expected)),
    ] {
        if let Err(e) = write_file(&out_dir, name, data) {
            eprintln!("{e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    }

    let backend = match WgpuCompute::with_policy(&DetectPolicy::default()) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            println!(
                "SKIP: no suitable GPU on this machine (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
        }
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("backend construction failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    println!("adapter: {}", ctx.adapter.name);
    let shape = shipped_shape(ctx.device.features());
    println!(
        "shape: {} (rows {}, workgroup {}, subgroup {}, f16 activations {}, legacy {})",
        shape.name(),
        shape.rows,
        shape.workgroup,
        shape.subgroup,
        shape.f16_activations,
        shape.legacy
    );
    let pipeline = match K1Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape) {
        Ok(p) => p,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("k1 pipeline for shape {} failed: {e}", shape.name());
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let uploaded = match pipeline.upload(ctx, &tensor, &bytes, inn, out) {
        Ok(w) => w,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("upload of {tensor} failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let got = match pipeline.run(ctx, &uploaded, &input) {
        Ok(g) => g,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("gpu run failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    if let Err(e) = write_file(&out_dir, "gpu_f32.bin", &f32_bytes(&got)) {
        eprintln!("{e}");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }

    let mut max_abs = 0.0f32;
    let mut scale = 0.0f32;
    let mut dot = 0.0f64;
    let mut norm_g = 0.0f64;
    let mut norm_e = 0.0f64;
    for (g, e) in got.iter().zip(expected.iter()) {
        max_abs = max_abs.max((g - e).abs());
        scale = scale.max(e.abs());
        dot += f64::from(*g) * f64::from(*e);
        norm_g += f64::from(*g) * f64::from(*g);
        norm_e += f64::from(*e) * f64::from(*e);
    }
    let cosine = dot / (norm_g.sqrt() * norm_e.sqrt());
    let rel = max_abs / scale.max(1.0);
    let summary = format!(
        "tensor {tensor}: [{inn} x {out}] Q4_K, {} bytes\n\
         outputs {out}: max_abs_err {max_abs:.6} at output scale {scale:.3} (rel {rel:.3e}), cosine {cosine:.9}\n",
        bytes.len()
    );
    print!("{summary}");
    if let Err(e) = write_file(&out_dir, "fixture.txt", summary.as_bytes()) {
        eprintln!("{e}");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    if rel < 1e-4 && cosine > 0.999_999 {
        println!("K1 FIXTURE PASS");
        ExitCode::SUCCESS
    } else {
        println!("K1 FIXTURE FAIL");
        ExitCode::from(1)
    }
}
