===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/k2_bench.rs =====
//! K2 streaming bench (BACKEND.md Section 7, tier 1 shape):
//! hold a set of the real file's largest Q6_K tensors resident,
//! dispatch the GEMV over all of them per iteration, and report
//! the effective streaming bandwidth against llama.cpp's measured
//! 708 GB/s and the 637 GB/s ash decision trigger.
//!
//! Usage:
//!   k2_bench [--model PATH] [--budget-mib N] [--iters N] [--warmup N]
//!            [--variant NAME] [--wg N]
//!
//! `--variant` selects the K2 shape (see `K2Shape::from_name`:
//! `r<rows>[sg]`; `shipped` is whatever `K2Pipeline::new` would
//! build on this device). `--wg` overrides the workgroup size.
//!
//! Stream accounting is on the raw file bytes (210 per block),
//! the useful stream llama.cpp's 708 GB/s is also measured on;
//! the device buffers hold 212 bytes per block (the padded
//! layout in the K2 module docs), so device traffic is 212/210
//! of the counted stream. The tool prints both numbers.
//!
//! The resident set is capped by --budget-mib because this bench
//! runs beside whatever already holds VRAM on the card (on the
//! server, the production llama-server). The default 160 MiB is
//! sized for that coexistence and is roughly twice the card's
//! 96 MiB Infinity Cache, so the stream genuinely comes from
//! VRAM; the tool prints the card's VRAM state it found so the
//! report carries its own constraint.

use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;
use std::time::Instant;

use gguf::{GgmlType, GgufFile};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k2_q6k_gemv::{K2Call, K2Pipeline, K2Shape, K2Weights};
use wgpu_compute::{DetectPolicy, WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

/// llama.cpp Vulkan's measured effective bandwidth on this card
/// (BACKEND.md Section 1): the number to match.
const LLAMA_CPP_GBS: f64 = 708.0;
/// The ash decision trigger (BACKEND.md Section 8): below 90
/// percent of llama.cpp's number after tuning, evaluate raw
/// Vulkan.
const ASH_TRIGGER_GBS: f64 = 637.0;

fn arg(args: &[String], flag: &str) -> Option<String> {
    args.windows(2).find(|w| w[0] == flag).map(|w| w[1].clone())
}

/// Deterministic pseudo-random f32s in [-0.5, 0.5) via a 64-bit
/// LCG, matching `k2_check`.
fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            ((state >> 40) as u32) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Best-effort VRAM accounting from sysfs, printed so the bench
/// report states the card's occupancy it ran under.
fn vram_state() -> Option<String> {
    // Only the discrete card exposes mem_info files; skip every
    // card that does not rather than giving up at the first one.
    for card in 0..8 {
        let base = format!("/sys/class/drm/card{card}/device");
        let Ok(total) = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("{base}/mem_info_vram_total")) else {
            continue;
        };
        let Ok(used) = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("{base}/mem_info_vram_used")) else {
            continue;
        };
        let (Ok(total), Ok(used)) = (total.trim().parse::<u64>(), used.trim().parse::<u64>())
        else {
            continue;
        };
        return Some(format!(
            "card{card} VRAM: {used} of {total} bytes in use ({} free)",
            total - used
        ));
    }
    None
}

struct Resident {
    // The weights handle is never read after setup; it is kept so
    // the buffer's residency is explicit in this tool's own
    // accounting, beside the bind group that references it.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    weights: K2Weights,
    call: K2Call,
}

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let model = arg(&args, "--model").unwrap_or_else(|| {
        "/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf".to_string()
    });
    let budget_mib: u64 = arg(&args, "--budget-mib")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(160);
    let iters: u32 = arg(&args, "--iters")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(25);
    let warmup: u32 = arg(&args, "--warmup")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(3);
    let variant = arg(&args, "--variant").unwrap_or_else(|| "shipped".to_string());
    let wg_override: Option<u32> = arg(&args, "--wg").and_then(|s| s.parse().ok());
    let budget = budget_mib * 1024 * 1024;

    let file = match GgufFile::open(Path::new(&model)) {
        Ok(f) => f,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("cannot open {model}: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    // Largest Q6_K tensors first, greedily packed under the
    // budget. Glimmer's Q6_K population is the FFN down tensors
    // (about 104 MiB each) plus the small attention V tensors.
    let mut candidates: Vec<(String, u64, usize, usize)> = file
        .tensors()
        .iter()
        .filter(|t| t.ggml_type() == Some(GgmlType::Q6K))
        .filter_map(|t| {
            let bytes = t.byte_len()?;
            let dims = t.dims();
            Some((
                t.name().to_string(),
                bytes,
                dims[0] as usize,
                dims[1] as usize,
            ))
        })
        .collect();
    candidates.sort_by_key(|c| std::cmp::Reverse(c.1));
    let mut chosen: Vec<(String, u64, usize, usize)> = Vec::new();
    let mut total_bytes: u64 = 0;
    for candidate in candidates {
        if total_bytes + candidate.1 > budget {
            continue;
        }
        total_bytes += candidate.1;
        chosen.push(candidate);
    }
    if chosen.is_empty() {
        eprintln!("no Q6_K tensor fits the {budget_mib} MiB budget");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }

    let backend = match WgpuCompute::with_policy(&DetectPolicy::default()) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            println!(
                "SKIP: no suitable GPU on this machine (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
        }
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("backend construction failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let mut shape = if variant == "shipped" {
        wgpu_compute::kernels::k2_q6k_gemv::shipped_shape(ctx.device.features())
    } else {
        match K2Shape::from_name(&variant) {
            Some(s) => s,
            None => {
                eprintln!("unknown variant {variant:?} (expected r<rows>[sg] or shipped)");
                return ExitCode::from(2);
            }
        }
    };
    if let Some(wg) = wg_override {
        shape.workgroup = wg;
    }
    let pipeline = match K2Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape) {
        Ok(p) => p,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("k2 pipeline for shape {} failed: {e}", shape.name());
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    println!("adapter: {}", ctx.adapter.name);
    println!(
        "shape: {} (rows {}, workgroup {}, subgroup {})",
        shape.name(),
        shape.rows,
        shape.workgroup,
        shape.subgroup
    );
    if let Some(state) = vram_state() {
        println!("{state}");
    }
    println!(
        "resident set: {} tensors, {} raw bytes streamed per iteration ({} device bytes at the 212/210 padded stride)",
        chosen.len(),
        total_bytes,
        total_bytes * 212 / 210
    );

    let mut resident: Vec<Resident> = Vec::new();
    for (name, _bytes, inn, out) in &chosen {
        let bytes = file.tensor_bytes(name).expect("tensor bytes");
        let weights = match pipeline.upload(ctx, name, bytes, *inn, *out) {
            Ok(w) => w,
            Err(e) => {
                eprintln!("upload of {name} failed: {e}");
                return ExitCode::from(2);
            }
        };
        let input = lcg_input(7, *inn);
        let in_bytes: Vec<u8> = input.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect();
        let input_buffer = ctx.device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
            label: Some("bench input"),
            size: in_bytes.len() as u64,
            usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::STORAGE | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
            mapped_at_creation: false,
        });
        ctx.queue.write_buffer(&input_buffer, 0, &in_bytes);
        let output_buffer = ctx.device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
            label: Some("bench output"),
            size: (*out * 4) as u64,
            usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::STORAGE,
            mapped_at_creation: false,
        });
        let call = match pipeline.prepare(ctx, &weights, &input_buffer, &output_buffer, 1) {
            Ok(c) => c,
            Err(e) => {
                eprintln!("prepare for {name} failed: {e}");
                return ExitCode::from(2);
            }
        };
        println!("  {name}: {} raw bytes [{inn} x {out}]", weights.byte_len);
        resident.push(Resident { weights, call });
    }

    let run_pass = |ctx: &wgpu_compute::GpuContext| {
        let mut encoder = ctx
            .device
            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                label: Some("k2 bench pass"),
            });
        for r in &resident {
            r.call.encode(&mut encoder);
        }
        ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
    };

    for _ in 0..warmup {
        run_pass(ctx);
    }
    if ctx
        .device
        .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
        .is_err()
    {
        eprintln!("device poll failed after warmup");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    let start = Instant::now();
    for _ in 0..iters {
        run_pass(ctx);
    }
    if ctx
        .device
        .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
        .is_err()
    {
        eprintln!("device poll failed after timed loop");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    let elapsed = start.elapsed().as_secs_f64();
    let streamed = total_bytes as f64 * f64::from(iters);
    let gbs = streamed / elapsed / 1e9;
    println!(
        "iters {iters} (+{warmup} warmup): {streamed:.0} raw bytes in {elapsed:.3} s = {gbs:.1} GB/s"
    );
    println!("reference: llama.cpp Vulkan {LLAMA_CPP_GBS:.0} GB/s; ash trigger {ASH_TRIGGER_GBS:.0} GB/s");
    if gbs >= LLAMA_CPP_GBS {
        println!(
            "verdict: at or above llama.cpp's measured bandwidth; wgpu stays, no ash question"
        );
    } else if gbs >= ASH_TRIGGER_GBS {
        println!(
            "verdict: above the ash trigger ({:.1}% of llama.cpp); wgpu stays per BACKEND.md Section 8",
            100.0 * gbs / LLAMA_CPP_GBS
        );
    } else {
        println!(
            "verdict: BELOW the ash trigger ({:.1}% of llama.cpp); BACKEND.md Section 8's ash evaluation trigger fires",
            100.0 * gbs / LLAMA_CPP_GBS
        );
    }
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

===== END FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/k2_bench.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/k2_check.rs =====
//! K2 correctness on the real file: run one real Q6_K tensor
//! through the wgpu backend and compare against the CPU
//! reference (the `gguf` crate's dequantizer plus `torch-math`'s
//! matvec), the same cross-check style as `k1_check`.
//!
//! Usage:
//!   k2_check [--model PATH] [--tensor NAME] [--seed N] [--variant NAME]
//!
//! Defaults: the Glimmer Q4_K_M file on the server and its first
//! FFN down tensor (the largest Q6_K population: the down
//! projection of every layer). Run it on the machine whose GPU
//! is under test (the 7900 XTX server): the default selection
//! policy refuses machines without a discrete Vulkan GPU, and
//! this tool reports that as a SKIP (exit 0), not a failure. A
//! real mismatch exits 1.
//!
//! `--variant` selects the K2 shape under test (see
//! `K2Shape::from_name`); the default is the shipped shape for
//! the device, i.e. exactly what `Compute::proj` would run.
//!
//! Note the stream accounting: the file's Q6_K blocks are 210
//! bytes and the device layout pads each to 212 (see the K2
//! module docs); the CPU reference and the byte counts printed
//! here are on the raw file bytes.

use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;

use gguf::{GgmlType, GgufFile};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k2_q6k_gemv::{shipped_shape, K2Pipeline, K2Shape};
use wgpu_compute::{DetectPolicy, WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

/// Deterministic pseudo-random f32s in [-0.5, 0.5): a 64-bit LCG,
/// so the check input is reproducible without a rand dependency.
fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            let bits = (state >> 40) as u32;
            bits as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

fn arg(args: &[String], flag: &str) -> Option<String> {
    args.windows(2).find(|w| w[0] == flag).map(|w| w[1].clone())
}

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let model = arg(&args, "--model").unwrap_or_else(|| {
        "/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf".to_string()
    });
    let tensor = arg(&args, "--tensor").unwrap_or_else(|| "blk.0.ffn_down.weight".to_string());
    let seed: u64 = arg(&args, "--seed")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(42);
    let variant = arg(&args, "--variant").unwrap_or_else(|| "shipped".to_string());

    let file = match GgufFile::open(Path::new(&model)) {
        Ok(f) => f,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("cannot open {model}: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let info = match file.tensor_info(&tensor) {
        Ok(i) => i.clone(),
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("tensor {tensor} not readable in {model}: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    if info.ggml_type() != Some(GgmlType::Q6K) {
        eprintln!(
            "tensor {tensor} is {}, not Q6_K; K2 checks Q6_K tensors only",
            info.type_name()
        );
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    let dims = info.dims().to_vec();
    let (inn, out) = (dims[0] as usize, dims[1] as usize);
    let bytes = match file.tensor_bytes(&tensor) {
        Ok(b) => b.to_vec(),
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("cannot read bytes of {tensor}: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    println!(
        "tensor {tensor}: [{inn} x {out}] Q6_K, {} bytes",
        bytes.len()
    );

    let input = lcg_input(seed, inn);
    // CPU reference: gguf's dequantizer is ggml-exact, and matvec
    // sums in row order; the GPU sums in a tree, so the comparison
    // tolerance is relative to the output's own scale.
    let weights = gguf::dequant::dequantize(GgmlType::Q6K, &bytes, inn * out);
    let expected = torch_math::matvec(&weights, out, inn, &input).expect("cpu reference matvec");

    let backend = match WgpuCompute::with_policy(&DetectPolicy::default()) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            println!(
                "SKIP: no suitable GPU on this machine (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
        }
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("backend construction failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    println!("adapter: {}", ctx.adapter.name);

    let shape = if variant == "shipped" {
        shipped_shape(ctx.device.features())
    } else {
        match K2Shape::from_name(&variant) {
            Some(s) => s,
            None => {
                eprintln!("unknown variant {variant:?} (expected r<rows>[sg] or shipped)");
                return ExitCode::from(2);
            }
        }
    };
    println!(
        "shape: {} (rows {}, workgroup {}, subgroup {})",
        shape.name(),
        shape.rows,
        shape.workgroup,
        shape.subgroup
    );
    let pipeline = match K2Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape) {
        Ok(p) => p,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("k2 pipeline for shape {} failed: {e}", shape.name());
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let weights = match pipeline.upload(ctx, &tensor, &bytes, inn, out) {
        Ok(w) => w,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("upload of {tensor} failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let got = match pipeline.run(ctx, &weights, &input) {
        Ok(g) => g,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("gpu run failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };

    let mut max_abs = 0.0f32;
    let mut scale = 0.0f32;
    let mut dot = 0.0f64;
    let mut norm_g = 0.0f64;
    let mut norm_e = 0.0f64;
    for (g, e) in got.iter().zip(expected.iter()) {
        max_abs = max_abs.max((g - e).abs());
        scale = scale.max(e.abs());
        dot += f64::from(*g) * f64::from(*e);
        norm_g += f64::from(*g) * f64::from(*g);
        norm_e += f64::from(*e) * f64::from(*e);
    }
    let cosine = dot / (norm_g.sqrt() * norm_e.sqrt());
    let rel = max_abs / scale.max(1.0);
    println!(
        "outputs {out}: max_abs_err {max_abs:.6} at output scale {scale:.3} (rel {rel:.3e}), cosine {cosine:.9}"
    );
    // f32 reassociation between a sequential CPU sum and the GPU
    // tree reduction lands near 1e-6 relative; the bound leaves
    // two orders of headroom and still catches any layout error,
    // which would be off by whole dequantized values.
    if rel < 1e-4 && cosine > 0.999_999 {
        println!("K2 CHECK PASS");
        ExitCode::SUCCESS
    } else {
        println!("K2 CHECK FAIL");
        ExitCode::from(1)
    }
}

===== END FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/k2_check.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/k3_bench.rs =====
//! K3 streaming bench (BACKEND.md Section 7, tier 1 shape):
//! hold the real file's Q5_K output head resident, dispatch the
//! GEMV per iteration, and report the effective streaming
//! bandwidth against llama.cpp's measured 708 GB/s and the
//! 637 GB/s ash decision trigger.
//!
//! Usage:
//!   k3_bench [--model PATH] [--budget-mib N] [--iters N] [--warmup N]
//!            [--variant NAME] [--wg N]
//!
//! `--variant` selects the K3 shape (see `K3Shape::from_name`:
//! `r<rows>[sg]`; `shipped` is whatever `K3Pipeline::new` would
//! build on this device). `--wg` overrides the workgroup size.
//!
//! Glimmer has exactly one Q5_K tensor, the 202,048-row head at
//! 924,571,648 bytes. When the budget cannot hold it whole, the
//! bench streams the leading whole rows that fit (rows are
//! contiguous: 26 blocks of 176 bytes each) and prints the slice
//! geometry loudly, so a sliced number is never mistaken for a
//! whole-head number. The default 160 MiB budget slices; run
//! with --budget-mib 1024 or more to hold the whole head when
//! the card has the room.

use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;
use std::time::Instant;

use gguf::{GgmlType, GgufFile};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k3_q5k_gemv::{K3Call, K3Pipeline, K3Shape, K3Weights};
use wgpu_compute::{DetectPolicy, WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

/// llama.cpp Vulkan's measured effective bandwidth on this card
/// (BACKEND.md Section 1): the number to match.
const LLAMA_CPP_GBS: f64 = 708.0;
/// The ash decision trigger (BACKEND.md Section 8): below 90
/// percent of llama.cpp's number after tuning, evaluate raw
/// Vulkan.
const ASH_TRIGGER_GBS: f64 = 637.0;
/// Bytes per head row: 6,656 inputs is 26 Q5_K blocks of 176.
const ROW_BYTES: u64 = 26 * 176;

fn arg(args: &[String], flag: &str) -> Option<String> {
    args.windows(2).find(|w| w[0] == flag).map(|w| w[1].clone())
}

/// Deterministic pseudo-random f32s in [-0.5, 0.5) via a 64-bit
/// LCG, matching `k3_check`.
fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            ((state >> 40) as u32) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Best-effort VRAM accounting from sysfs, printed so the bench
/// report states the card's occupancy it ran under.
fn vram_state() -> Option<String> {
    // Only the discrete card exposes mem_info files; skip every
    // card that does not rather than giving up at the first one.
    for card in 0..8 {
        let base = format!("/sys/class/drm/card{card}/device");
        let Ok(total) = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("{base}/mem_info_vram_total")) else {
            continue;
        };
        let Ok(used) = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("{base}/mem_info_vram_used")) else {
            continue;
        };
        let (Ok(total), Ok(used)) = (total.trim().parse::<u64>(), used.trim().parse::<u64>())
        else {
            continue;
        };
        return Some(format!(
            "card{card} VRAM: {used} of {total} bytes in use ({} free)",
            total - used
        ));
    }
    None
}

struct Resident {
    // The weights handle is never read after setup; it is kept so
    // the buffer's residency is explicit in this tool's own
    // accounting, beside the bind group that references it.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    weights: K3Weights,
    call: K3Call,
}

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let model = arg(&args, "--model").unwrap_or_else(|| {
        "/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf".to_string()
    });
    let budget_mib: u64 = arg(&args, "--budget-mib")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(160);
    let iters: u32 = arg(&args, "--iters")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(25);
    let warmup: u32 = arg(&args, "--warmup")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(3);
    let variant = arg(&args, "--variant").unwrap_or_else(|| "shipped".to_string());
    let wg_override: Option<u32> = arg(&args, "--wg").and_then(|s| s.parse().ok());
    let budget = budget_mib * 1024 * 1024;

    let file = match GgufFile::open(Path::new(&model)) {
        Ok(f) => f,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("cannot open {model}: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    // The one Q5_K tensor: the output head.
    let head = file
        .tensors()
        .iter()
        .find(|t| t.ggml_type() == Some(GgmlType::Q5K));
    let Some(head) = head else {
        eprintln!("no Q5_K tensor in {model}");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    };
    let name = head.name().to_string();
    let dims = head.dims();
    let (inn, full_rows) = (dims[0] as usize, dims[1] as usize);
    let full_bytes = match head.byte_len() {
        Some(b) => b,
        None => {
            eprintln!("tensor {name} has no byte length");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    if full_bytes != full_rows as u64 * ROW_BYTES || inn != 6_656 {
        eprintln!(
            "tensor {name} geometry [{inn} x {full_rows}] at {full_bytes} bytes is not the expected head shape"
        );
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    let rows = if full_bytes <= budget {
        full_rows
    } else {
        (budget / ROW_BYTES) as usize
    };
    if rows == 0 {
        eprintln!("budget {budget_mib} MiB cannot hold even one head row");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    let total_bytes = rows as u64 * ROW_BYTES;

    let backend = match WgpuCompute::with_policy(&DetectPolicy::default()) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            println!(
                "SKIP: no suitable GPU on this machine (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
        }
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("backend construction failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let mut shape = if variant == "shipped" {
        wgpu_compute::kernels::k3_q5k_gemv::shipped_shape(ctx.device.features())
    } else {
        match K3Shape::from_name(&variant) {
            Some(s) => s,
            None => {
                eprintln!("unknown variant {variant:?} (expected r<rows>[sg] or shipped)");
                return ExitCode::from(2);
            }
        }
    };
    if let Some(wg) = wg_override {
        shape.workgroup = wg;
    }
    let pipeline = match K3Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape) {
        Ok(p) => p,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("k3 pipeline for shape {} failed: {e}", shape.name());
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    println!("adapter: {}", ctx.adapter.name);
    println!(
        "shape: {} (rows {}, workgroup {}, subgroup {})",
        shape.name(),
        shape.rows,
        shape.workgroup,
        shape.subgroup
    );
    if let Some(state) = vram_state() {
        println!("{state}");
    }
    if rows == full_rows {
        println!("resident set: the whole head {name}, {total_bytes} bytes streamed per iteration [{inn} x {rows}]");
    } else {
        println!(
            "resident set: SLICE of {name}: leading {rows} of {full_rows} rows, {total_bytes} bytes streamed per iteration [{inn} x {rows}] (budget {budget_mib} MiB cannot hold the whole {full_bytes}-byte head)"
        );
    }

    let all_bytes = match file.tensor_bytes(&name) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("cannot read bytes of {name}: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let slice = &all_bytes[..total_bytes as usize];
    let weights = match pipeline.upload(ctx, &name, slice, inn, rows) {
        Ok(w) => w,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("upload of {name} failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let input = lcg_input(7, inn);
    let in_bytes: Vec<u8> = input.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect();
    let input_buffer = ctx.device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
        label: Some("bench input"),
        size: in_bytes.len() as u64,
        usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::STORAGE | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
        mapped_at_creation: false,
    });
    ctx.queue.write_buffer(&input_buffer, 0, &in_bytes);
    let output_buffer = ctx.device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
        label: Some("bench output"),
        size: (rows * 4) as u64,
        usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::STORAGE,
        mapped_at_creation: false,
    });
    let call = match pipeline.prepare(ctx, &weights, &input_buffer, &output_buffer, 1) {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("prepare for {name} failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let resident = Resident { weights, call };

    let run_pass = |ctx: &wgpu_compute::GpuContext| {
        let mut encoder = ctx
            .device
            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                label: Some("k3 bench pass"),
            });
        resident.call.encode(&mut encoder);
        ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
    };

    for _ in 0..warmup {
        run_pass(ctx);
    }
    if ctx
        .device
        .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
        .is_err()
    {
        eprintln!("device poll failed after warmup");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    let start = Instant::now();
    for _ in 0..iters {
        run_pass(ctx);
    }
    if ctx
        .device
        .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
        .is_err()
    {
        eprintln!("device poll failed after timed loop");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    let elapsed = start.elapsed().as_secs_f64();
    let streamed = total_bytes as f64 * f64::from(iters);
    let gbs = streamed / elapsed / 1e9;
    println!(
        "iters {iters} (+{warmup} warmup): {streamed:.0} bytes in {elapsed:.3} s = {gbs:.1} GB/s"
    );
    println!("reference: llama.cpp Vulkan {LLAMA_CPP_GBS:.0} GB/s; ash trigger {ASH_TRIGGER_GBS:.0} GB/s");
    if gbs >= LLAMA_CPP_GBS {
        println!(
            "verdict: at or above llama.cpp's measured bandwidth; wgpu stays, no ash question"
        );
    } else if gbs >= ASH_TRIGGER_GBS {
        println!(
            "verdict: above the ash trigger ({:.1}% of llama.cpp); wgpu stays per BACKEND.md Section 8",
            100.0 * gbs / LLAMA_CPP_GBS
        );
    } else {
        println!(
            "verdict: BELOW the ash trigger ({:.1}% of llama.cpp); BACKEND.md Section 8's ash evaluation trigger fires",
            100.0 * gbs / LLAMA_CPP_GBS
        );
    }
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

===== END FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/k3_bench.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/k3_check.rs =====
//! K3 correctness on the real file: run the real Q5_K output
//! head through the wgpu backend and compare against the CPU
//! reference (the `gguf` crate's dequantizer plus `torch-math`'s
//! matvec), the same cross-check style as `k1_check`. The head
//! is 202,048 rows, so this is also the two-dimensional
//! dispatch's real-file proof (101,024 workgroups at the
//! shipped two-rows-per-workgroup shape, past the 65,535
//! per-dimension cap).
//!
//! Usage:
//!   k3_check [--model PATH] [--tensor NAME] [--seed N] [--variant NAME]
//!
//! Defaults: the Glimmer Q4_K_M file on the server and its
//! output head. Run it on the machine whose GPU is under test
//! (the 7900 XTX server): the default selection policy refuses
//! machines without a discrete Vulkan GPU, and this tool
//! reports that as a SKIP (exit 0), not a failure. A real
//! mismatch exits 1. The CPU reference dequantizes the whole
//! head (about 5.4 GB of f32), so this tool wants a machine
//! with the RAM for it; the server has it.
//!
//! `--variant` selects the K3 shape under test (see
//! `K3Shape::from_name`); the default is the shipped shape for
//! the device, i.e. exactly what `Compute::lm_head` would run.

use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;

use gguf::{GgmlType, GgufFile};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k3_q5k_gemv::{shipped_shape, K3Pipeline, K3Shape};
use wgpu_compute::{DetectPolicy, WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

/// Deterministic pseudo-random f32s in [-0.5, 0.5): a 64-bit LCG,
/// so the check input is reproducible without a rand dependency.
fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            let bits = (state >> 40) as u32;
            bits as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

fn arg(args: &[String], flag: &str) -> Option<String> {
    args.windows(2).find(|w| w[0] == flag).map(|w| w[1].clone())
}

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let model = arg(&args, "--model").unwrap_or_else(|| {
        "/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf".to_string()
    });
    let tensor = arg(&args, "--tensor").unwrap_or_else(|| "output.weight".to_string());
    let seed: u64 = arg(&args, "--seed")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(42);
    let variant = arg(&args, "--variant").unwrap_or_else(|| "shipped".to_string());

    let file = match GgufFile::open(Path::new(&model)) {
        Ok(f) => f,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("cannot open {model}: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let info = match file.tensor_info(&tensor) {
        Ok(i) => i.clone(),
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("tensor {tensor} not readable in {model}: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    if info.ggml_type() != Some(GgmlType::Q5K) {
        eprintln!(
            "tensor {tensor} is {}, not Q5_K; K3 checks Q5_K tensors only",
            info.type_name()
        );
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    let dims = info.dims().to_vec();
    let (inn, out) = (dims[0] as usize, dims[1] as usize);
    let bytes = match file.tensor_bytes(&tensor) {
        Ok(b) => b.to_vec(),
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("cannot read bytes of {tensor}: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    println!(
        "tensor {tensor}: [{inn} x {out}] Q5_K, {} bytes",
        bytes.len()
    );

    let input = lcg_input(seed, inn);
    // CPU reference: gguf's dequantizer is ggml-exact, and matvec
    // sums in row order; the GPU sums in a tree, so the comparison
    // tolerance is relative to the output's own scale.
    let weights = gguf::dequant::dequantize(GgmlType::Q5K, &bytes, inn * out);
    let expected = torch_math::matvec(&weights, out, inn, &input).expect("cpu reference matvec");

    let backend = match WgpuCompute::with_policy(&DetectPolicy::default()) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            println!(
                "SKIP: no suitable GPU on this machine (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
        }
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("backend construction failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    println!("adapter: {}", ctx.adapter.name);

    let shape = if variant == "shipped" {
        shipped_shape(ctx.device.features())
    } else {
        match K3Shape::from_name(&variant) {
            Some(s) => s,
            None => {
                eprintln!("unknown variant {variant:?} (expected r<rows>[sg] or shipped)");
                return ExitCode::from(2);
            }
        }
    };
    println!(
        "shape: {} (rows {}, workgroup {}, subgroup {})",
        shape.name(),
        shape.rows,
        shape.workgroup,
        shape.subgroup
    );
    let pipeline = match K3Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape) {
        Ok(p) => p,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("k3 pipeline for shape {} failed: {e}", shape.name());
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let weights = match pipeline.upload(ctx, &tensor, &bytes, inn, out) {
        Ok(w) => w,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("upload of {tensor} failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let got = match pipeline.run(ctx, &weights, &input) {
        Ok(g) => g,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("gpu run failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };

    let mut max_abs = 0.0f32;
    let mut scale = 0.0f32;
    let mut dot = 0.0f64;
    let mut norm_g = 0.0f64;
    let mut norm_e = 0.0f64;
    for (g, e) in got.iter().zip(expected.iter()) {
        max_abs = max_abs.max((g - e).abs());
        scale = scale.max(e.abs());
        dot += f64::from(*g) * f64::from(*e);
        norm_g += f64::from(*g) * f64::from(*g);
        norm_e += f64::from(*e) * f64::from(*e);
    }
    let cosine = dot / (norm_g.sqrt() * norm_e.sqrt());
    let rel = max_abs / scale.max(1.0);
    println!(
        "outputs {out}: max_abs_err {max_abs:.6} at output scale {scale:.3} (rel {rel:.3e}), cosine {cosine:.9}"
    );
    // f32 reassociation between a sequential CPU sum and the GPU
    // tree reduction lands near 1e-6 relative; the bound leaves
    // two orders of headroom and still catches any layout error,
    // which would be off by whole dequantized values.
    if rel < 1e-4 && cosine > 0.999_999 {
        println!("K3 CHECK PASS");
        ExitCode::SUCCESS
    } else {
        println!("K3 CHECK FAIL");
        ExitCode::from(1)
    }
}

===== END FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/k3_check.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/mmq_bench.rs =====
//! MMQ prefill bench (K12 quantizer + K13/K14 integer-dot
//! product kernels) against the same real-file tensors and
//! the same discipline as `k10_bench`: the largest Q4_K and
//! Q6_K tensors resident, each projection shape run through
//! the GEMV replay, the shipped f32 GEMM (t32x128), and the
//! MMQ at both tile shapes, with the K12 quantize pass timed
//! both alone and composed into the MMQ total. The GEMV at
//! batch 1 doubles as the window canary (~816 GB/s Q4_K,
//! ~832 GB/s Q6_K in a healthy window).
//!
//! The wide-tile double-buffered MMQ (K15 for Q4_K, K16 for
//! Q6_K) runs in the same per-tensor table at every tile
//! candidate the device can build, labeled `mmq wide w<N>`:
//! the per-tensor half of the wide-tile proof, whose
//! session-level half (marginal and gross prefill tok/s at
//! 1,024 tokens, old ladder vs wide ladder) runs through
//! `bench/mmq-wide-bench.sh`.
//!
//! Usage:
//!   mmq_bench [--model PATH] [--batch N] [--iters N]
//!             [--warmup N] [--budget-mib N]

use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;
use std::time::Instant;

use gguf::{GgmlType, GgufFile};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k10_q4k_gemm::{GemmShape, K10Call, K10Pipeline};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k11_q6k_gemm::{K11Call, K11Pipeline};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k12_q8_quant::{K12QuantCall, K12QuantPipeline};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k13_q4k_mmq::{K13Call, K13Pipeline, MmqShape};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k14_q6k_mmq::{K14Call, K14Pipeline};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k15_q4k_mmq_wide::{
    K15Call, K15Pipeline, WideMmqShape, WIDE_TILE_CANDIDATES,
};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k16_q6k_mmq_wide::{K16Call, K16Pipeline};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::{K1Call, K1Pipeline, K1Weights, ACT_NONE};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k2_q6k_gemv::{K2Call, K2Pipeline, K2Weights};
use wgpu_compute::{DetectPolicy, WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

fn arg(args: &[String], flag: &str) -> Option<String> {
    args.windows(2).find(|w| w[0] == flag).map(|w| w[1].clone())
}

fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            ((state >> 40) as u32) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

/// One encodable dispatch, whichever kernel built it; the
/// bench times compositions, not types.
enum BenchCall {
    K1(K1Call),
    K2(K2Call),
    K10(K10Call),
    K11(K11Call),
    K12(K12QuantCall),
    K13(K13Call),
    K14(K14Call),
    K15(K15Call),
    K16(K16Call),
}

impl BenchCall {
    fn encode_into(&self, pass: &mut wgpu::ComputePass<'_>) {
        match self {
            BenchCall::K1(c) => c.encode_into(pass),
            BenchCall::K2(c) => c.encode_into(pass),
            BenchCall::K10(c) => c.encode_into(pass),
            BenchCall::K11(c) => c.encode_into(pass),
            BenchCall::K12(c) => c.encode_into(pass),
            BenchCall::K13(c) => c.encode_into(pass),
            BenchCall::K14(c) => c.encode_into(pass),
            BenchCall::K15(c) => c.encode_into(pass),
            BenchCall::K16(c) => c.encode_into(pass),
        }
    }
}

fn time_calls(ctx: &wgpu_compute::GpuContext, calls: &[BenchCall], warmup: u32, iters: u32) -> f64 {
    let run_pass = |ctx: &wgpu_compute::GpuContext| {
        let mut encoder = ctx
            .device
            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                label: Some("mmq bench pass"),
            });
        {
            let mut pass = encoder.begin_compute_pass(&wgpu::ComputePassDescriptor {
                label: Some("mmq bench"),
                timestamp_writes: None,
            });
            for c in calls {
                c.encode_into(&mut pass);
            }
        }
        ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
    };
    for _ in 0..warmup {
        run_pass(ctx);
    }
    ctx.device
        .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
        .expect("poll after warmup");
    let start = Instant::now();
    for _ in 0..iters {
        run_pass(ctx);
    }
    ctx.device
        .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
        .expect("poll after timed loop");
    start.elapsed().as_secs_f64() / f64::from(iters)
}

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let model = arg(&args, "--model").unwrap_or_else(|| {
        "/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf".to_string()
    });
    let batch: u32 = arg(&args, "--batch")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(64);
    let iters: u32 = arg(&args, "--iters")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(10);
    let warmup: u32 = arg(&args, "--warmup")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(2);
    let budget: u64 = arg(&args, "--budget-mib")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse::<u64>().ok())
        .unwrap_or(512)
        * 1024
        * 1024;

    let file = match GgufFile::open(Path::new(&model)) {
        Ok(f) => f,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("cannot open {model}: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    // Same selection as k10_bench: the largest tensor of
    // each family first, then more under the budget.
    let mut by_size: Vec<(String, GgmlType, u64, usize, usize)> = file
        .tensors()
        .iter()
        .filter(|t| matches!(t.ggml_type(), Some(GgmlType::Q4K | GgmlType::Q6K)))
        .filter_map(|t| {
            let bytes = t.byte_len()?;
            let dims = t.dims();
            Some((
                t.name().to_string(),
                t.ggml_type()?,
                bytes,
                dims[0] as usize,
                dims[1] as usize,
            ))
        })
        .collect();
    by_size.sort_by_key(|c| std::cmp::Reverse(c.2));
    let mut chosen: Vec<(String, GgmlType, u64, usize, usize)> = Vec::new();
    let mut seen_families: Vec<GgmlType> = Vec::new();
    let mut total: u64 = 0;
    for cand in &by_size {
        let new_family = !seen_families.contains(&cand.1);
        if !new_family && chosen.len() >= 3 {
            continue;
        }
        if total + cand.2 > budget {
            continue;
        }
        total += cand.2;
        seen_families.push(cand.1);
        chosen.push(cand.clone());
        if chosen.len() >= 4 {
            break;
        }
    }
    if chosen.is_empty() {
        eprintln!("no Q4_K/Q6_K tensor fits the budget");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }

    let backend = match WgpuCompute::with_policy(&DetectPolicy::default()) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            println!(
                "SKIP: no suitable GPU on this machine (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
        }
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("backend construction failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    println!("adapter: {}", ctx.adapter.name);
    println!("batch: {batch}, iters {iters} (+{warmup} warmup)");

    let k1 = K1Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k1 pipeline");
    let k2 = K2Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k2 pipeline");
    let k10 = K10Pipeline::with_shape_act(&ctx.device, GemmShape::new(32, 128), ACT_NONE)
        .expect("k10 t32x128");
    let k11 = K11Pipeline::with_shape_act(&ctx.device, GemmShape::new(32, 128), ACT_NONE)
        .expect("k11 t32x128");
    let k12 = K12QuantPipeline::new(&ctx.device, ACT_NONE).expect("k12 pipeline");
    let mut mmq4: Vec<(MmqShape, K13Pipeline)> = Vec::new();
    let mut mmq6: Vec<(MmqShape, K14Pipeline)> = Vec::new();
    for shape in [MmqShape::new(32), MmqShape::new(64)] {
        match K13Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape) {
            Ok(p) => mmq4.push((shape, p)),
            Err(e) => println!("k13 {} unavailable: {e}", shape.name()),
        }
        match K14Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape) {
            Ok(p) => mmq6.push((shape, p)),
            Err(e) => println!("k14 {} unavailable: {e}", shape.name()),
        }
    }
    // The wide set: every candidate the device can build,
    // widest first (the shipped shape is the first entry on
    // a device whose grant sorts the same way; on the
    // 64 KiB server card that is w128 for K15 and w112 for
    // K16, whose w128 staging set is 512 bytes over).
    let mut wide4: Vec<(WideMmqShape, K15Pipeline)> = Vec::new();
    let mut wide6: Vec<(WideMmqShape, K16Pipeline)> = Vec::new();
    for cand in WIDE_TILE_CANDIDATES {
        let shape = WideMmqShape::new(cand);
        match K15Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape) {
            Ok(p) => wide4.push((shape, p)),
            Err(e) => println!("k15 {} unavailable: {e}", shape.name()),
        }
        match K16Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape) {
            Ok(p) => wide6.push((shape, p)),
            Err(e) => println!("k16 {} unavailable: {e}", shape.name()),
        }
    }

    let mut keep_q4: Vec<K1Weights> = Vec::new();
    let mut keep_q6: Vec<K2Weights> = Vec::new();
    for (name, ty, bytes, inn, out) in &chosen {
        let raw = file.tensor_bytes(name).expect("tensor bytes");
        let input = lcg_input(7, batch as usize * inn);
        let in_buf = ctx.upload_f32("bench input", &input);
        let out_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("bench output", (batch as usize * out * 4) as u64);
        let qs_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer(
            "bench qs",
            (wgpu_compute::kernels::k12_q8_quant::qs_words(batch as usize, *inn) * 4) as u64,
        );
        let ds_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer(
            "bench ds",
            (wgpu_compute::kernels::k12_q8_quant::ds_vec4s(batch as usize, *inn) * 16) as u64,
        );
        let quant = BenchCall::K12(
            k12.prepare(ctx, &in_buf, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, batch, *inn)
                .expect("k12 prepare"),
        );
        println!(
            "\n{name} ({ty:?}, {inn}x{out}, {:.1} MB)",
            *bytes as f64 / 1e6
        );
        let report = |label: &str, secs: f64| {
            let rows_s = f64::from(batch) / secs;
            let stream = *bytes as f64 / secs / 1e9;
            println!(
                "  {label:<22} {:>9.3} ms  {:>9.0} tok/s  {:>7.1} GB/s stream",
                secs * 1e3,
                rows_s,
                stream
            );
        };
        match ty {
            GgmlType::Q4K => {
                let w = k1.upload(ctx, name, raw, *inn, *out).expect("k1 upload");
                let gemv = [BenchCall::K1(
                    k1.prepare(ctx, &w, &in_buf, &out_buf, batch)
                        .expect("k1 prepare"),
                )];
                report("gemv replay", time_calls(ctx, &gemv, warmup, iters));
                let gemm = [BenchCall::K10(
                    k10.prepare(ctx, &w, &in_buf, &out_buf, batch)
                        .expect("k10 prepare"),
                )];
                report("gemm t32x128", time_calls(ctx, &gemm, warmup, iters));
                report("k12 quantize", time_calls(ctx, &[quant], warmup, iters));
                for (shape, mmq) in &mmq4 {
                    let prod = [BenchCall::K13(
                        mmq.prepare(ctx, &w, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, &out_buf, batch)
                            .expect("k13 prepare"),
                    )];
                    let prod_s = time_calls(ctx, &prod, warmup, iters);
                    report(&format!("mmq {} product", shape.name()), prod_s);
                    let quant2 = BenchCall::K12(
                        k12.prepare(ctx, &in_buf, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, batch, *inn)
                            .expect("k12 prepare"),
                    );
                    let total = [
                        quant2,
                        BenchCall::K13(
                            mmq.prepare(ctx, &w, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, &out_buf, batch)
                                .expect("k13 prepare"),
                        ),
                    ];
                    let total_s = time_calls(ctx, &total, warmup, iters);
                    report(&format!("mmq {} + quantize", shape.name()), total_s);
                }
                for (shape, wide) in &wide4 {
                    let prod = [BenchCall::K15(
                        wide.prepare(ctx, &w, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, &out_buf, batch)
                            .expect("k15 prepare"),
                    )];
                    let prod_s = time_calls(ctx, &prod, warmup, iters);
                    report(&format!("mmq wide {} product", shape.name()), prod_s);
                    let quant2 = BenchCall::K12(
                        k12.prepare(ctx, &in_buf, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, batch, *inn)
                            .expect("k12 prepare"),
                    );
                    let total = [
                        quant2,
                        BenchCall::K15(
                            wide.prepare(ctx, &w, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, &out_buf, batch)
                                .expect("k15 prepare"),
                        ),
                    ];
                    let total_s = time_calls(ctx, &total, warmup, iters);
                    report(&format!("mmq wide {} + quantize", shape.name()), total_s);
                }
                keep_q4.push(w);
            }
            GgmlType::Q6K => {
                let w = k2.upload(ctx, name, raw, *inn, *out).expect("k2 upload");
                let gemv = [BenchCall::K2(
                    k2.prepare(ctx, &w, &in_buf, &out_buf, batch)
                        .expect("k2 prepare"),
                )];
                report("gemv replay", time_calls(ctx, &gemv, warmup, iters));
                let gemm = [BenchCall::K11(
                    k11.prepare(ctx, &w, &in_buf, &out_buf, batch)
                        .expect("k11 prepare"),
                )];
                report("gemm t32x128", time_calls(ctx, &gemm, warmup, iters));
                report("k12 quantize", time_calls(ctx, &[quant], warmup, iters));
                for (shape, mmq) in &mmq6 {
                    let prod = [BenchCall::K14(
                        mmq.prepare(ctx, &w, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, &out_buf, batch)
                            .expect("k14 prepare"),
                    )];
                    let prod_s = time_calls(ctx, &prod, warmup, iters);
                    report(&format!("mmq {} product", shape.name()), prod_s);
                    let quant2 = BenchCall::K12(
                        k12.prepare(ctx, &in_buf, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, batch, *inn)
                            .expect("k12 prepare"),
                    );
                    let total = [
                        quant2,
                        BenchCall::K14(
                            mmq.prepare(ctx, &w, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, &out_buf, batch)
                                .expect("k14 prepare"),
                        ),
                    ];
                    let total_s = time_calls(ctx, &total, warmup, iters);
                    report(&format!("mmq {} + quantize", shape.name()), total_s);
                }
                for (shape, wide) in &wide6 {
                    let prod = [BenchCall::K16(
                        wide.prepare(ctx, &w, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, &out_buf, batch)
                            .expect("k16 prepare"),
                    )];
                    let prod_s = time_calls(ctx, &prod, warmup, iters);
                    report(&format!("mmq wide {} product", shape.name()), prod_s);
                    let quant2 = BenchCall::K12(
                        k12.prepare(ctx, &in_buf, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, batch, *inn)
                            .expect("k12 prepare"),
                    );
                    let total = [
                        quant2,
                        BenchCall::K16(
                            wide.prepare(ctx, &w, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, &out_buf, batch)
                                .expect("k16 prepare"),
                        ),
                    ];
                    let total_s = time_calls(ctx, &total, warmup, iters);
                    report(&format!("mmq wide {} + quantize", shape.name()), total_s);
                }
                keep_q6.push(w);
            }
            _ => unreachable!("selection filtered to Q4_K/Q6_K"),
        }
    }
    let _ = (keep_q4, keep_q6);
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}
