===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/mmv_sweep.rs =====
//! Small-batch sweep harness: every projection
//! variant the session's routing ladder can choose,
//! measured head to head over the verify band at the
//! real Glimmer shapes, one CSV per run.
//!
//! Each run drives single projections through
//! [`ProjBench`], which prepares through the session's
//! own `prepare_proj` ladder, so the variant measured
//! is the variant a forward would dispatch under the
//! process environment as it stands: shipped GEMV/MM
//! forms as control, K18 under
//! `WGPU_COMPUTE_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS`, the MMV
//! register-streaming forms under
//! `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS`, the chunked forms
//! under their env, wide MMQ under
//! `WGPU_COMPUTE_WIDE_MIN_ROWS`. The harness sets no
//! routing env itself; it records the active routing
//! env into every CSV row's `variant_env` column.
//! `bench/mmv-sweep.sh` runs the arm matrix.
//!
//! The cell matrix is the autotune table the research
//! plan calls for: quant family (Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K) x
//! shape (attention-sized 6656 out, FFN-up 19968 out,
//! KV-sized 256 out, all from hidden 6656; the KV
//! width is `GlimmerConfig::k_width()`, KV heads times
//! key length, 2 x 128) x rows {1..=9, 12, 16}.
//!
//! Measurement discipline: warmup dispatches are
//! excluded, every cell gets at least 20 timed
//! repetitions at the default settings, and the CSV
//! reports median and min. GPU time comes from the
//! diag timestamps system (one stamp around the whole
//! projection composition) when the context carries a
//! recorder (`WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing` and a device
//! that granted the timestamp features); otherwise
//! each repetition is bracketed on the wall clock
//! around submit plus poll, and the run says which
//! method it used on stdout and in its log. A cell
//! whose stamp records do not line up with its
//! repetition count is re-timed on the wall clock,
//! with the substitution printed.
//!
//! Correctness guard: every cell's variant output is
//! compared against the GEMV form's output for the
//! same inputs, prepared directly from the kernel
//! pipelines, before anything is timed. Agreement uses
//! the crate's own kernel-test rules
//! (tests/k18_small_batch.rs): a form that quantizes
//! its activation answers to the 5% quantization band
//! (`check_quant_band`), an f32 form to the tight
//! reassociation bound (`check_close`). A disagreeing
//! cell is marked `agree=0` in the CSV, never silently
//! timed as if it agreed.
//!
//! Usage:
//!   mmv_sweep --out PATH [--label NAME] [--reps N]
//!             [--warmup N] [--rows 1,2,7] [--quants Q4_K,Q6_K]
//!             [--outs 6656,19968,256]
//!   mmv_sweep --enumerate   (print the cell matrix, no GPU)

use std::fmt::Write as _;
use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;
use std::time::Instant;

use muse_glimmer::Dtype;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k12_q8_quant::{ds_vec4s, qs_words};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::{K1Pipeline, K1Weights};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k2_q6k_gemv::{K2Pipeline, K2Weights};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k3_q5k_gemv::{K3Pipeline, K3Weights};
use wgpu_compute::timestamps::DispatchMeta;
use wgpu_compute::{DetectPolicy, GpuContext, ProjBench, ProjBenchCall, WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

/// Input width of every swept projection: the model's
/// hidden size.
const IN: usize = 6656;

/// The swept shapes as (label, output width). The KV
/// width is the config's `k_width()` (KV heads times
/// key length, 2 x 128 = 256), read from
/// crates/muse-glimmer/src/config.rs, whose real-file
/// test pins it.
const SHAPES: [(&str, usize); 3] = [("attn", 6656), ("ffn", 19968), ("kv", 256)];

/// The row sweep: the whole verify band (a depth-1
/// round verifies 2 rows, depth 6 verifies 7), the
/// batch-9 cliff point from the NUM_COLS dose-response,
/// and the matrix threshold at 16.
const ROWS: [u32; 11] = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 12, 16];

/// Timed repetitions per cell at the default: the
/// floor the measurement discipline sets. A run below
/// it is a smoke, and says so.
const DEFAULT_REPS: u32 = 25;
const MIN_VERDICT_REPS: u32 = 20;
const DEFAULT_WARMUP: u32 = 3;

/// Routing env the harness watches and stamps into
/// its output. It sets none of them.
const ROUTING_VARS: [&str; 5] = [
    "WGPU_COMPUTE_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS",
    "WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS",
    "WGPU_COMPUTE_WIDE_MIN_ROWS",
    "WGPU_COMPUTE_CHUNK_ROWS",
    "WGPU_COMPUTE_CHUNK_MAX_ROWS",
];

fn arg(args: &[String], flag: &str) -> Option<String> {
    args.windows(2).find(|w| w[0] == flag).map(|w| w[1].clone())
}

fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            ((state >> 40) as u32) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

fn lcg_bytes(seed: u8, count: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state.wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(17);
            state
        })
        .collect()
}

/// A synthetic Q4_K tensor's raw bytes (144-byte
/// blocks), the kernel tests' fixture shape: rotating
/// (d, dmin) f16 headers over LCG payloads
/// (tests/k18_small_batch.rs).
fn synthetic_q4k(in_elems: usize, out_rows: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let blocks_per_row = in_elems / 256;
    let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(out_rows * blocks_per_row * 144);
    let headers: [(u16, u16); 4] = [
        (0x3c00, 0x3400),
        (0x3800, 0x0000),
        (0x4000, 0x2e66),
        (0x3e00, 0x3800),
    ];
    for row in 0..out_rows {
        for blk in 0..blocks_per_row {
            let (d, dmin) = headers[(row + blk) % headers.len()];
            let mut block = [0u8; 144];
            block[0..2].copy_from_slice(&d.to_le_bytes());
            block[2..4].copy_from_slice(&dmin.to_le_bytes());
            block[4..144].copy_from_slice(&lcg_bytes((row * 7 + blk * 13 + 5) as u8, 140)[..]);
            data.extend_from_slice(&block);
        }
    }
    data
}

/// A synthetic Q5_K tensor's raw bytes (176-byte
/// blocks, same fixture discipline as Q4_K).
fn synthetic_q5k(in_elems: usize, out_rows: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let blocks_per_row = in_elems / 256;
    let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(out_rows * blocks_per_row * 176);
    let headers: [(u16, u16); 4] = [
        (0x3c00, 0x3400),
        (0x3800, 0x0000),
        (0x4000, 0x2e66),
        (0x3e00, 0x3800),
    ];
    for row in 0..out_rows {
        for blk in 0..blocks_per_row {
            let (d, dmin) = headers[(row + blk) % headers.len()];
            let mut block = [0u8; 176];
            block[0..2].copy_from_slice(&d.to_le_bytes());
            block[2..4].copy_from_slice(&dmin.to_le_bytes());
            block[4..176].copy_from_slice(&lcg_bytes((row * 7 + blk * 13 + 5) as u8, 172)[..]);
            data.extend_from_slice(&block);
        }
    }
    data
}

/// A synthetic Q6_K tensor's raw bytes (210-byte
/// blocks, the f16 super-scale at offset 208).
fn synthetic_q6k(in_elems: usize, out_rows: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let blocks_per_row = in_elems / 256;
    let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(out_rows * blocks_per_row * 210);
    let ds: [u16; 3] = [0x3c00, 0x3800, 0x4000];
    for row in 0..out_rows {
        for blk in 0..blocks_per_row {
            let mut block = lcg_bytes((row * 11 + blk * 7 + 3) as u8, 210);
            block[208..210].copy_from_slice(&ds[(row + blk) % ds.len()].to_le_bytes());
            data.extend_from_slice(&block);
        }
    }
    data
}

/// Bytes of one synthetic tensor of `quant` at
/// `IN` x `out`: block geometry only, for the
/// enumeration listing. Run-mode weight bytes come
/// from the uploaded handle, not from here.
fn geometry_bytes(quant: Dtype, out: usize) -> usize {
    let block_bytes = match quant {
        Dtype::Q4K => 144,
        Dtype::Q5K => 176,
        Dtype::Q6K => 210,
        _ => 0,
    };
    IN / 256 * out * block_bytes
}

fn quant_name(quant: Dtype) -> &'static str {
    match quant {
        Dtype::Q4K => "Q4_K",
        Dtype::Q5K => "Q5_K",
        Dtype::Q6K => "Q6_K",
        _ => "other",
    }
}

/// The routing env stamp: the run's label plus every
/// watched routing variable that is set, or `env:none`
/// when none is. Semicolon-joined so the CSV column
/// never grows a comma.
fn variant_env_stamp(label: &str) -> String {
    let mut set: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for var in ROUTING_VARS {
        if let Ok(v) = std::env::var(var) {
            set.push(format!("{var}={v}"));
        }
    }
    if set.is_empty() {
        format!("{label}|env:none")
    } else {
        format!("{label}|{}", set.join(";"))
    }
}

/// The agreement rule between a variant output and
/// the GEMV control output, mirroring the crate's
/// kernel tests (tests/k18_small_batch.rs): a form
/// that quantizes its activation answers to the 5%
/// quantization band (`check_quant_band`), an f32 form
/// to the tight reassociation bound (`check_close`).
/// Returns (agrees, max abs diff).
fn agree(got: &[f32], want: &[f32], quantized: bool) -> (bool, f32) {
    let scale = want.iter().fold(0.0f32, |a, w| a.max(w.abs()));
    let max_diff = got
        .iter()
        .zip(want.iter())
        .fold(0.0f32, |a, (g, w)| a.max((g - w).abs()));
    if quantized {
        (max_diff / scale.max(1.0) <= 0.05, max_diff)
    } else {
        (max_diff <= 2e-3 + 5e-5 * scale, max_diff)
    }
}

fn median(sorted: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    let n = sorted.len();
    if n % 2 == 1 {
        sorted[n / 2]
    } else {
        (sorted[n / 2 - 1] + sorted[n / 2]) / 2.0
    }
}

/// The GEMV control weights, one family at a time,
/// uploaded from the same synthetic bytes the routed
/// handle holds.
enum GemvWeights {
    Q4K(K1Weights),
    Q6K(K2Weights),
    Q5K(K3Weights),
}

/// Time one cell on the wall clock: warmup passes
/// untimed, then one submit-plus-poll per repetition.
/// Returns (median ms, min ms).
fn time_wall(ctx: &GpuContext, call: &ProjBenchCall, warmup: u32, reps: u32) -> (f64, f64) {
    let run_one = |ctx: &GpuContext| {
        let mut encoder = ctx
            .device
            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                label: Some("mmv sweep pass"),
            });
        {
            let mut pass = encoder.begin_compute_pass(&wgpu::ComputePassDescriptor {
                label: Some("mmv sweep"),
                timestamp_writes: None,
            });
            call.encode_into(&mut pass);
        }
        ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
    };
    for _ in 0..warmup {
        run_one(ctx);
    }
    ctx.device
        .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
        .expect("poll after warmup");
    let mut times: Vec<f64> = Vec::with_capacity(reps as usize);
    for _ in 0..reps {
        let start = Instant::now();
        run_one(ctx);
        ctx.device
            .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
            .expect("poll in timed loop");
        times.push(start.elapsed().as_secs_f64() * 1e3);
    }
    times.sort_by(|a, b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap());
    (median(&times), times[0])
}

/// Time one cell with the diag timestamps system: one
/// stamp around the whole projection composition per
/// repetition, warmup passes unstamped. Returns
/// (median ms, min ms), or `None` when the records do
/// not line up with the repetition count (the caller
/// re-times on the wall clock and says so).
fn time_diag(
    ctx: &GpuContext,
    call: &ProjBenchCall,
    meta: DispatchMeta,
    warmup: u32,
    reps: u32,
) -> Option<(f64, f64)> {
    let recorder = ctx.diag_recorder()?;
    let dropped_before = recorder.dropped();
    let run_one = |ctx: &GpuContext, stamp: bool| {
        let stamp = if stamp {
            ctx.diag_stamp(meta.clone())
        } else {
            None
        };
        let mut encoder = ctx
            .device
            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                label: Some("mmv sweep pass"),
            });
        {
            let mut pass = encoder.begin_compute_pass(&wgpu::ComputePassDescriptor {
                label: Some("mmv sweep"),
                timestamp_writes: None,
            });
            let slot = stamp.as_ref().and_then(|s| s.begin(&mut pass));
            call.encode_into(&mut pass);
            if let (Some(s), Some(slot)) = (stamp.as_ref(), slot) {
                s.end(&mut pass, slot);
            }
        }
        ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
    };
    for _ in 0..warmup {
        run_one(ctx, false);
    }
    ctx.device
        .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
        .expect("poll after warmup");
    for _ in 0..reps {
        run_one(ctx, true);
    }
    ctx.device
        .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
        .expect("poll after timed loop");
    recorder.drain(&ctx.device, &ctx.queue).expect("diag drain");
    if recorder.dropped() != dropped_before {
        return None;
    }
    let records = recorder.take_records();
    if records.len() != reps as usize {
        return None;
    }
    let mut times: Vec<f64> = records.iter().map(|r| r.duration_ns as f64 / 1e6).collect();
    times.sort_by(|a, b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap());
    Some((median(&times), times[0]))
}

fn parse_filter<T: std::str::FromStr>(raw: Option<String>) -> Option<Vec<T>> {
    raw.map(|s| {
        s.split(',')
            .filter_map(|p| p.trim().parse::<T>().ok())
            .collect()
    })
}

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let quants_all = [Dtype::Q4K, Dtype::Q5K, Dtype::Q6K];

    if args.iter().any(|a| a == "--enumerate") {
        println!("cell matrix: in={IN}, shapes (label, out) = {SHAPES:?}");
        println!("variant_env,kernel,quant,rows,out_cols,median_ms,min_ms,weight_bytes,gbps_median,agree");
        for quant in quants_all {
            for (_, out) in SHAPES {
                for rows in ROWS {
                    println!(
                        "enumerate,enumerate,{},{rows},{out},,,{},,",
                        quant_name(quant),
                        geometry_bytes(quant, out),
                    );
                }
            }
        }
        println!(
            "cells per run: {}",
            quants_all.len() * SHAPES.len() * ROWS.len()
        );
        return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
    }

    let out_path = match arg(&args, "--out") {
        Some(p) => p,
        None => {
            eprintln!("--out PATH is required in run mode (or pass --enumerate)");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let label = arg(&args, "--label").unwrap_or_else(|| "unlabeled".to_string());
    let reps: u32 = arg(&args, "--reps")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_REPS);
    let warmup: u32 = arg(&args, "--warmup")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_WARMUP);
    let rows_filter = parse_filter::<u32>(arg(&args, "--rows"));
    let outs_filter = parse_filter::<usize>(arg(&args, "--outs"));
    let quants_filter: Option<Vec<String>> = arg(&args, "--quants").map(|s| {
        s.split(',')
            .map(|p| p.trim().to_string())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
    });
    let rows: Vec<u32> = ROWS
        .iter()
        .copied()
        .filter(|r| rows_filter.as_ref().is_none_or(|f| f.contains(r)))
        .collect();
    let shapes: Vec<(&str, usize)> = SHAPES
        .iter()
        .copied()
        .filter(|(_, o)| outs_filter.as_ref().is_none_or(|f| f.contains(o)))
        .collect();
    let quants: Vec<Dtype> = quants_all
        .iter()
        .copied()
        .filter(|q| {
            quants_filter
                .as_ref()
                .is_none_or(|f| f.iter().any(|n| n == quant_name(*q)))
        })
        .collect();
    if rows.is_empty() || shapes.is_empty() || quants.is_empty() {
        eprintln!("filters selected no cells");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    if reps < MIN_VERDICT_REPS {
        println!(
            "note: reps {reps} is below the {MIN_VERDICT_REPS}-repetition verdict floor; this run is a smoke, not a verdict run"
        );
    }

    let stamp = variant_env_stamp(&label);
    println!("variant_env: {stamp}");
    println!("reps {reps} (+{warmup} warmup), rows {rows:?}");

    let backend = match WgpuCompute::with_policy(&DetectPolicy::default()) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            println!(
                "SKIP: no suitable GPU on this machine (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
        }
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("backend construction failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    println!("adapter: {}", ctx.adapter.name);
    let timing_method = if ctx.diag_recorder().is_some() {
        "diag_timestamps"
    } else {
        "wall_clock"
    };
    println!("timing_method: {timing_method}");

    let k1 = K1Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k1 pipeline");
    let k2 = K2Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k2 pipeline");
    let k3 = K3Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k3 pipeline");

    let max_rows = *rows.iter().max().unwrap() as usize;
    let input = lcg_input(7, max_rows * IN);
    let in_buf = ctx.upload_f32("sweep input", &input);
    let qs_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("sweep qs", (qs_words(max_rows, IN) * 4) as u64);
    let ds_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("sweep ds", (ds_vec4s(max_rows, IN) * 16) as u64);

    let mut csv = String::from(
        "variant_env,kernel,quant,rows,out_cols,median_ms,min_ms,weight_bytes,gbps_median,agree\n",
    );
    let mut disagreements = 0u32;

    for quant in &quants {
        for (shape_label, out) in &shapes {
            let name = format!("sweep {} {shape_label}", quant_name(*quant));
            let raw = match quant {
                Dtype::Q4K => synthetic_q4k(IN, *out),
                Dtype::Q5K => synthetic_q5k(IN, *out),
                Dtype::Q6K => synthetic_q6k(IN, *out),
                _ => unreachable!("quants filtered to the three K families"),
            };
            let bench = ProjBench::upload(&backend, &name, *quant, &raw, IN, *out)
                .expect("proj bench upload");
            let gemv_w = match quant {
                Dtype::Q4K => {
                    GemvWeights::Q4K(k1.upload(ctx, &name, &raw, IN, *out).expect("k1 upload"))
                }
                Dtype::Q6K => {
                    GemvWeights::Q6K(k2.upload(ctx, &name, &raw, IN, *out).expect("k2 upload"))
                }
                Dtype::Q5K => {
                    GemvWeights::Q5K(k3.upload(ctx, &name, &raw, IN, *out).expect("k3 upload"))
                }
                _ => unreachable!("quants filtered to the three K families"),
            };
            let weight_bytes = bench.byte_len() as u64;
            let out_variant = ctx.scratch_buffer("sweep out variant", (max_rows * out * 4) as u64);
            let out_control = ctx.scratch_buffer("sweep out control", (max_rows * out * 4) as u64);

            for rows_n in &rows {
                // The GEMV control output for this cell,
                // prepared directly from the kernel
                // pipelines, before anything is timed.
                let run_control = |ctx: &GpuContext| {
                    let mut encoder =
                        ctx.device
                            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                                label: Some("mmv sweep control pass"),
                            });
                    {
                        let mut pass = encoder.begin_compute_pass(&wgpu::ComputePassDescriptor {
                            label: Some("mmv sweep control"),
                            timestamp_writes: None,
                        });
                        match &gemv_w {
                            GemvWeights::Q4K(w) => k1
                                .prepare(ctx, w, &in_buf, &out_control, *rows_n)
                                .expect("k1 prepare")
                                .encode_into(&mut pass),
                            GemvWeights::Q6K(w) => k2
                                .prepare(ctx, w, &in_buf, &out_control, *rows_n)
                                .expect("k2 prepare")
                                .encode_into(&mut pass),
                            GemvWeights::Q5K(w) => k3
                                .prepare(ctx, w, &in_buf, &out_control, *rows_n)
                                .expect("k3 prepare")
                                .encode_into(&mut pass),
                        }
                    }
                    ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
                };
                run_control(ctx);
                ctx.device
                    .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
                    .expect("poll after control");
                let control = ctx
                    .read_f32(&out_control, *rows_n as usize * out)
                    .expect("control readback");

                // The routed variant for this cell.
                let call = bench
                    .prepare(
                        &backend,
                        &in_buf,
                        &qs_buf,
                        &ds_buf,
                        &out_variant,
                        *rows_n as usize,
                    )
                    .expect("proj bench prepare");
                {
                    let mut encoder =
                        ctx.device
                            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                                label: Some("mmv sweep check pass"),
                            });
                    {
                        let mut pass = encoder.begin_compute_pass(&wgpu::ComputePassDescriptor {
                            label: Some("mmv sweep check"),
                            timestamp_writes: None,
                        });
                        call.encode_into(&mut pass);
                    }
                    ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
                }
                ctx.device
                    .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
                    .expect("poll after check");
                let got = ctx
                    .read_f32(&out_variant, *rows_n as usize * out)
                    .expect("variant readback");
                let (agrees, max_diff) = agree(&got, &control, call.quantized());
                if !agrees {
                    disagreements += 1;
                    eprintln!(
                        "DISAGREE {} {shape_label} rows {rows_n}: kernel {} max abs diff {max_diff:.4} (quantized form: {})",
                        quant_name(*quant),
                        call.kernel_name(),
                        call.quantized(),
                    );
                }

                let meta = DispatchMeta {
                    kernel: call.kernel_name(),
                    rows: u64::from(*rows_n),
                    cols: IN as u64,
                    quant: quant_name(*quant),
                    weight_bytes,
                    shape: format!("sweep {shape_label}"),
                };
                let (median_ms, min_ms) = if timing_method == "diag_timestamps" {
                    match time_diag(ctx, &call, meta, warmup, reps) {
                        Some(t) => t,
                        None => {
                            eprintln!(
                                "note: diag records did not line up for {} {shape_label} rows {rows_n}; re-timed on the wall clock",
                                quant_name(*quant),
                            );
                            time_wall(ctx, &call, warmup, reps)
                        }
                    }
                } else {
                    time_wall(ctx, &call, warmup, reps)
                };
                let gbps = if median_ms > 0.0 {
                    weight_bytes as f64 / (median_ms / 1e3) / 1e9
                } else {
                    0.0
                };
                writeln!(
                    csv,
                    "{stamp},{},{},{rows_n},{out},{median_ms:.4},{min_ms:.4},{weight_bytes},{gbps:.2},{}",
                    call.kernel_name(),
                    quant_name(*quant),
                    u8::from(agrees),
                )
                .expect("csv line");
                println!(
                    "{} {shape_label} rows {rows_n:>2}: {:<18} median {median_ms:>9.4} ms  min {min_ms:>9.4} ms  {gbps:>8.2} GB/s  agree {}",
                    quant_name(*quant),
                    call.kernel_name(),
                    u8::from(agrees),
                );
            }
        }
    }

    std::fs::write(Path::new(&out_path), &csv).expect("write csv");
    println!("wrote {out_path} ({disagreements} disagreeing cells)");
    if disagreements > 0 {
        eprintln!(
            "warning: {disagreements} cells disagreed with the GEMV control and are marked agree=0"
        );
    }
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

===== END FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/mmv_sweep.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/small_batch_bench.rs =====
//! Small-batch bench (K18 against the GEMV forms it
//! would replace, and the MMQ forms at the band's top):
//! the largest real-file tensor of each quant family,
//! swept over the row counts the speculative loop runs
//! at (1..=16), with the K12 quantize pass timed both
//! alone and composed into the K18 total.
//!
//! The question is the round economics one
//! (bench/spec-gpu-port-2026-11-03.md): below 16 rows
//! the session's projections stream the weights once
//! per row in GEMV form. The GEMV rows in this table
//! are that cost, per tensor; the K18 rows are one
//! weight stream per dispatch however many rows ride
//! it. The stream column is tensor bytes per second
//! (so a GEMV line at R rows reads up to R times the
//! card's DRAM rate: it is re-reading), and the ms
//! column is the verdict.
//!
//! Usage:
//!   small_batch_bench [--model PATH] [--iters N]
//!                     [--warmup N] [--budget-mib N]

use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;
use std::time::Instant;

use gguf::{GgmlType, GgufFile};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k12_q8_quant::{K12QuantCall, K12QuantPipeline};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k13_q4k_mmq::{K13Call, K13Pipeline, MmqShape};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k14_q6k_mmq::{K14Call, K14Pipeline};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k18_small_batch::{
    K18Call, K18Q4KPipeline, K18Q5KPipeline, K18Q6KPipeline,
};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::{K1Call, K1Pipeline, K1Weights, ACT_NONE};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k2_q6k_gemv::{K2Call, K2Pipeline, K2Weights};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k3_q5k_gemv::{K3Call, K3Pipeline, K3Weights};
use wgpu_compute::{DetectPolicy, GpuContext, WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

fn arg(args: &[String], flag: &str) -> Option<String> {
    args.windows(2).find(|w| w[0] == flag).map(|w| w[1].clone())
}

fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            ((state >> 40) as u32) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

/// The row sweep: the band K18 serves, with the
/// working points of the speculative loop (2 for a
/// depth-1 round's verify, 7 for depth 6, 16 for the
/// draft block) called out in the set.
const ROWS: [u32; 10] = [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 12, 15, 16];

/// One encodable dispatch, whichever kernel built it;
/// the bench times compositions, not types.
enum BenchCall {
    K1(K1Call),
    K2(K2Call),
    K3(K3Call),
    K12(K12QuantCall),
    K13(K13Call),
    K14(K14Call),
    K18(K18Call),
}

impl BenchCall {
    fn encode_into(&self, pass: &mut wgpu::ComputePass<'_>) {
        match self {
            BenchCall::K1(c) => c.encode_into(pass),
            BenchCall::K2(c) => c.encode_into(pass),
            BenchCall::K3(c) => c.encode_into(pass),
            BenchCall::K12(c) => c.encode_into(pass),
            BenchCall::K13(c) => c.encode_into(pass),
            BenchCall::K14(c) => c.encode_into(pass),
            BenchCall::K18(c) => c.encode_into(pass),
        }
    }
}

fn time_calls(ctx: &GpuContext, calls: &[BenchCall], warmup: u32, iters: u32) -> f64 {
    let run_pass = |ctx: &GpuContext| {
        let mut encoder = ctx
            .device
            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                label: Some("small batch bench pass"),
            });
        {
            let mut pass = encoder.begin_compute_pass(&wgpu::ComputePassDescriptor {
                label: Some("small batch bench"),
                timestamp_writes: None,
            });
            for c in calls {
                c.encode_into(&mut pass);
            }
        }
        ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
    };
    for _ in 0..warmup {
        run_pass(ctx);
    }
    ctx.device
        .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
        .expect("poll after warmup");
    let start = Instant::now();
    for _ in 0..iters {
        run_pass(ctx);
    }
    ctx.device
        .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
        .expect("poll after timed loop");
    start.elapsed().as_secs_f64() / f64::from(iters)
}

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let model = arg(&args, "--model").unwrap_or_else(|| {
        "/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf".to_string()
    });
    let iters: u32 = arg(&args, "--iters")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(10);
    let warmup: u32 = arg(&args, "--warmup")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(2);
    let budget: u64 = arg(&args, "--budget-mib")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse::<u64>().ok())
        .unwrap_or(1536)
        * 1024
        * 1024;

    let file = match GgufFile::open(Path::new(&model)) {
        Ok(f) => f,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("cannot open {model}: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    // The largest tensor of each family, under the
    // budget: the Q5_K pick is the untied output head,
    // the single biggest small-batch stream in a
    // verify forward.
    let mut by_size: Vec<(String, GgmlType, u64, usize, usize)> = file
        .tensors()
        .iter()
        .filter(|t| {
            matches!(
                t.ggml_type(),
                Some(GgmlType::Q4K | GgmlType::Q6K | GgmlType::Q5K)
            )
        })
        .filter_map(|t| {
            let bytes = t.byte_len()?;
            let dims = t.dims();
            Some((
                t.name().to_string(),
                t.ggml_type()?,
                bytes,
                dims[0] as usize,
                dims[1] as usize,
            ))
        })
        .collect();
    by_size.sort_by_key(|c| std::cmp::Reverse(c.2));
    let mut chosen: Vec<(String, GgmlType, u64, usize, usize)> = Vec::new();
    let mut seen_families: Vec<GgmlType> = Vec::new();
    let mut total: u64 = 0;
    for cand in &by_size {
        if seen_families.contains(&cand.1) {
            continue;
        }
        if total + cand.2 > budget {
            continue;
        }
        total += cand.2;
        seen_families.push(cand.1);
        chosen.push(cand.clone());
        if chosen.len() >= 3 {
            break;
        }
    }
    if chosen.is_empty() {
        eprintln!("no Q4_K/Q6_K/Q5_K tensor fits the budget");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }

    let backend = match WgpuCompute::with_policy(&DetectPolicy::default()) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            println!(
                "SKIP: no suitable GPU on this machine (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
        }
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("backend construction failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    println!("adapter: {}", ctx.adapter.name);
    println!("rows: {ROWS:?}, iters {iters} (+{warmup} warmup)");

    let k1 = K1Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k1 pipeline");
    let k2 = K2Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k2 pipeline");
    let k3 = K3Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k3 pipeline");
    let k12 = K12QuantPipeline::new(&ctx.device, ACT_NONE).expect("k12 pipeline");
    let small4 = K18Q4KPipeline::for_device(&ctx.device)
        .expect("k18 q4k probe")
        .expect("k18 q4k pipeline on the bench device");
    let small6 = K18Q6KPipeline::for_device(&ctx.device)
        .expect("k18 q6k probe")
        .expect("k18 q6k pipeline on the bench device");
    let small5 = K18Q5KPipeline::for_device(&ctx.device)
        .expect("k18 q5k probe")
        .expect("k18 q5k pipeline on the bench device");
    println!(
        "k18 shipped shapes: q4k {} q6k {} q5k {}",
        small4.shape().name(),
        small6.shape().name(),
        small5.shape().name()
    );
    // The MMQ comparison at the band's top (16 rows):
    // the standard tiles, whose showing at small rows
    // is the reason K18 exists.
    let mmq4 = K13Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, MmqShape::new(64))
        .ok()
        .or_else(|| K13Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, MmqShape::new(32)).ok());
    let mmq6 = K14Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, MmqShape::new(64))
        .ok()
        .or_else(|| K14Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, MmqShape::new(32)).ok());

    let mut keep_q4: Vec<K1Weights> = Vec::new();
    let mut keep_q6: Vec<K2Weights> = Vec::new();
    let mut keep_q5: Vec<K3Weights> = Vec::new();
    for (name, ty, bytes, inn, out) in &chosen {
        let raw = file.tensor_bytes(name).expect("tensor bytes");
        println!(
            "\n{name} ({ty:?}, {inn}x{out}, {:.1} MB)",
            *bytes as f64 / 1e6
        );
        let report = |label: &str, rows: u32, secs: f64| {
            let rows_s = f64::from(rows) / secs;
            let stream = *bytes as f64 / secs / 1e9;
            println!(
                "  rows {rows:>2}  {label:<22} {:>9.3} ms  {:>9.0} tok/s  {:>7.1} GB/s of tensor",
                secs * 1e3,
                rows_s,
                stream
            );
        };
        // Buffers are sized at the sweep's top and the
        // prepares slice them per row count (every
        // prepare validates sizes as minimums).
        let max_rows = 16usize;
        let input = lcg_input(7, max_rows * inn);
        let in_buf = ctx.upload_f32("bench input", &input);
        let out_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("bench output", (max_rows * out * 4) as u64);
        let qs_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer(
            "bench qs",
            (wgpu_compute::kernels::k12_q8_quant::qs_words(max_rows, *inn) * 4) as u64,
        );
        let ds_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer(
            "bench ds",
            (wgpu_compute::kernels::k12_q8_quant::ds_vec4s(max_rows, *inn) * 16) as u64,
        );
        match ty {
            GgmlType::Q4K => {
                let w = k1.upload(ctx, name, raw, *inn, *out).expect("k1 upload");
                for rows in ROWS {
                    let gemv = [BenchCall::K1(
                        k1.prepare(ctx, &w, &in_buf, &out_buf, rows)
                            .expect("k1 prepare"),
                    )];
                    report("gemv", rows, time_calls(ctx, &gemv, warmup, iters));
                    let quant = BenchCall::K12(
                        k12.prepare(ctx, &in_buf, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, rows, *inn)
                            .expect("k12 prepare"),
                    );
                    let prod = [BenchCall::K18(
                        small4
                            .prepare(ctx, &w, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, &out_buf, rows)
                            .expect("k18 q4k prepare"),
                    )];
                    let prod_s = time_calls(ctx, &prod, warmup, iters);
                    report(
                        &format!("k18 {} product", small4.shape().name()),
                        rows,
                        prod_s,
                    );
                    let total = [
                        quant,
                        BenchCall::K18(
                            small4
                                .prepare(ctx, &w, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, &out_buf, rows)
                                .expect("k18 q4k prepare"),
                        ),
                    ];
                    report(
                        &format!("k18 {} + quantize", small4.shape().name()),
                        rows,
                        time_calls(ctx, &total, warmup, iters),
                    );
                    if rows == 16 {
                        if let Some(mmq) = &mmq4 {
                            let prod = [BenchCall::K13(
                                mmq.prepare(ctx, &w, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, &out_buf, rows)
                                    .expect("k13 prepare"),
                            )];
                            report(
                                &format!("mmq {} product", mmq.shape().name()),
                                rows,
                                time_calls(ctx, &prod, warmup, iters),
                            );
                        }
                    }
                }
                keep_q4.push(w);
            }
            GgmlType::Q6K => {
                let w = k2.upload(ctx, name, raw, *inn, *out).expect("k2 upload");
                for rows in ROWS {
                    let gemv = [BenchCall::K2(
                        k2.prepare(ctx, &w, &in_buf, &out_buf, rows)
                            .expect("k2 prepare"),
                    )];
                    report("gemv", rows, time_calls(ctx, &gemv, warmup, iters));
                    let quant = BenchCall::K12(
                        k12.prepare(ctx, &in_buf, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, rows, *inn)
                            .expect("k12 prepare"),
                    );
                    let prod = [BenchCall::K18(
                        small6
                            .prepare(ctx, &w, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, &out_buf, rows)
                            .expect("k18 q6k prepare"),
                    )];
                    let prod_s = time_calls(ctx, &prod, warmup, iters);
                    report(
                        &format!("k18 {} product", small6.shape().name()),
                        rows,
                        prod_s,
                    );
                    let total = [
                        quant,
                        BenchCall::K18(
                            small6
                                .prepare(ctx, &w, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, &out_buf, rows)
                                .expect("k18 q6k prepare"),
                        ),
                    ];
                    report(
                        &format!("k18 {} + quantize", small6.shape().name()),
                        rows,
                        time_calls(ctx, &total, warmup, iters),
                    );
                    if rows == 16 {
                        if let Some(mmq) = &mmq6 {
                            let prod = [BenchCall::K14(
                                mmq.prepare(ctx, &w, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, &out_buf, rows)
                                    .expect("k14 prepare"),
                            )];
                            report(
                                &format!("mmq {} product", mmq.shape().name()),
                                rows,
                                time_calls(ctx, &prod, warmup, iters),
                            );
                        }
                    }
                }
                keep_q6.push(w);
            }
            GgmlType::Q5K => {
                let w = k3.upload(ctx, name, raw, *inn, *out).expect("k3 upload");
                for rows in ROWS {
                    let gemv = [BenchCall::K3(
                        k3.prepare(ctx, &w, &in_buf, &out_buf, rows)
                            .expect("k3 prepare"),
                    )];
                    report("gemv", rows, time_calls(ctx, &gemv, warmup, iters));
                    let quant = BenchCall::K12(
                        k12.prepare(ctx, &in_buf, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, rows, *inn)
                            .expect("k12 prepare"),
                    );
                    let prod = [BenchCall::K18(
                        small5
                            .prepare(ctx, &w, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, &out_buf, rows)
                            .expect("k18 q5k prepare"),
                    )];
                    let prod_s = time_calls(ctx, &prod, warmup, iters);
                    report(
                        &format!("k18 {} product", small5.shape().name()),
                        rows,
                        prod_s,
                    );
                    let total = [
                        quant,
                        BenchCall::K18(
                            small5
                                .prepare(ctx, &w, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, &out_buf, rows)
                                .expect("k18 q5k prepare"),
                        ),
                    ];
                    report(
                        &format!("k18 {} + quantize", small5.shape().name()),
                        rows,
                        time_calls(ctx, &total, warmup, iters),
                    );
                }
                keep_q5.push(w);
            }
            _ => unreachable!("selection filtered to Q4_K/Q6_K/Q5_K"),
        }
    }
    let _ = (keep_q4, keep_q6, keep_q5);
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/stream_probe.rs =====
//! Tier 1 stream probe (BACKEND.md Section 7): what does the
//! wgpu stack itself stream at on this card, before any
//! dequantization math? It runs over the largest Q4_K tensor of
//! the real file, held resident.
//!
//! The probe uses K1's grid shape (one workgroup per output
//! row, lanes striding the row's words, LDS reduction) but sums
//! words instead of dequantizing, which isolates the grid and
//! the access pattern from the dequant arithmetic: on the server
//! it streamed at 746.9 GB/s where the first K1 shader managed
//! 148.6 GB/s, which is how the K1 gap was attributed to load
//! instructions inside the kernel rather than to the stack.
//!
//! Usage: stream_probe [--model PATH] [--iters N]
//!
//! This is a measurement tool for the backend's bench record, not
//! a kernel: its outputs are checksums nobody reads.

use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;
use std::time::Instant;

use gguf::{GgmlType, GgufFile};
use wgpu_compute::{DetectPolicy, WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

const ROW_SHADER: &str = r#"
struct Params {
    words_per_row: u32,
    out_rows: u32,
    grid_x: u32,
}

@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> weights: array<u32>;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read_write> output: array<u32>;
@group(0) @binding(2) var<uniform> params: Params;

var<workgroup> partials: array<u32, 128>;

@compute @workgroup_size(128)
fn main(@builtin(workgroup_id) wid: vec3<u32>,
        @builtin(local_invocation_id) lid: vec3<u32>) {
    let flat = wid.y * params.grid_x + wid.x;
    if (flat >= params.out_rows) {
        return;
    }
    let lane = lid.x;
    let row0 = flat * params.words_per_row;
    var acc = 0u;
    for (var i = lane; i < params.words_per_row; i += 128u) {
        acc += weights[row0 + i];
    }
    partials[lane] = acc;
    workgroupBarrier();
    var stride = 64u;
    while (stride > 0u) {
        if (lane < stride) {
            partials[lane] += partials[lane + stride];
        }
        workgroupBarrier();
        stride >>= 1u;
    }
    if (lane == 0u) {
        output[flat] = partials[0];
    }
}
"#;

fn arg(args: &[String], flag: &str) -> Option<String> {
    args.windows(2).find(|w| w[0] == flag).map(|w| w[1].clone())
}

fn grid(total: u64) -> (u32, u32) {
    let x = total.min(65_535) as u32;
    (x, total.div_ceil(u64::from(x)) as u32)
}

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let model = arg(&args, "--model").unwrap_or_else(|| {
        "/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf".to_string()
    });
    let iters: u32 = arg(&args, "--iters")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(2000);

    let file = match GgufFile::open(Path::new(&model)) {
        Ok(f) => f,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("cannot open {model}: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let mut tensors: Vec<(String, u64, usize, usize)> = file
        .tensors()
        .iter()
        .filter(|t| t.ggml_type() == Some(GgmlType::Q4K))
        .filter_map(|t| {
            Some((
                t.name().to_string(),
                t.byte_len()?,
                t.dims()[0] as usize,
                t.dims()[1] as usize,
            ))
        })
        .collect();
    tensors.sort_by_key(|c| std::cmp::Reverse(c.1));
    let (name, bytes_len, inn, out) = tensors[0].clone();
    let bytes = file.tensor_bytes(&name).expect("tensor bytes").to_vec();

    let backend = match WgpuCompute::with_policy(&DetectPolicy::default()) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            println!(
                "SKIP: no suitable GPU on this machine (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
        }
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("backend construction failed: {e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    println!("adapter: {}", ctx.adapter.name);
    println!("tensor {name}: {bytes_len} bytes [{inn} x {out}]");

    let weights = ctx.device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
        label: Some("probe weights"),
        size: bytes_len,
        usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::STORAGE | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
        mapped_at_creation: false,
    });
    ctx.queue.write_buffer(&weights, 0, &bytes);
    let output = ctx.device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
        label: Some("probe output"),
        size: 202_048 * 4,
        usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::STORAGE,
        mapped_at_creation: false,
    });

    let shader = ROW_SHADER;
    let words_per_row = (bytes_len / 4 / out as u64) as u32;
    let mut params_bytes = Vec::new();
    params_bytes.extend_from_slice(&words_per_row.to_le_bytes());
    params_bytes.extend_from_slice(&(out as u32).to_le_bytes());
    let dispatch = grid(out as u64);
    params_bytes.extend_from_slice(&dispatch.0.to_le_bytes());
    params_bytes.extend_from_slice(&1u32.to_le_bytes()); // pad to 16 bytes

    let params = ctx.device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
        label: Some("probe params"),
        size: params_bytes.len() as u64,
        usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::UNIFORM | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
        mapped_at_creation: false,
    });
    ctx.queue.write_buffer(&params, 0, &params_bytes);
    let module = ctx
        .device
        .create_shader_module(wgpu::ShaderModuleDescriptor {
            label: Some("stream probe shader"),
            source: wgpu::ShaderSource::Wgsl(shader.into()),
        });
    let pipeline = ctx
        .device
        .create_compute_pipeline(&wgpu::ComputePipelineDescriptor {
            label: Some("stream probe pipeline"),
            layout: None,
            module: &module,
            entry_point: Some("main"),
            compilation_options: wgpu::PipelineCompilationOptions::default(),
            cache: None,
        });
    let bind_group = ctx.device.create_bind_group(&wgpu::BindGroupDescriptor {
        label: Some("probe bind group"),
        layout: &pipeline.get_bind_group_layout(0),
        entries: &[
            wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                binding: 0,
                resource: weights.as_entire_binding(),
            },
            wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                binding: 1,
                resource: output.as_entire_binding(),
            },
            wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                binding: 2,
                resource: params.as_entire_binding(),
            },
        ],
    });

    let run_pass = |ctx: &wgpu_compute::GpuContext| {
        let mut encoder = ctx
            .device
            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                label: Some("probe pass"),
            });
        {
            let mut pass = encoder.begin_compute_pass(&wgpu::ComputePassDescriptor {
                label: Some("probe"),
                timestamp_writes: None,
            });
            pass.set_pipeline(&pipeline);
            pass.set_bind_group(0, &bind_group, &[]);
            pass.dispatch_workgroups(dispatch.0, dispatch.1, 1);
        }
        ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
    };

    for _ in 0..50 {
        run_pass(ctx);
    }
    if ctx
        .device
        .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
        .is_err()
    {
        eprintln!("device poll failed after warmup");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    let start = Instant::now();
    for _ in 0..iters {
        run_pass(ctx);
    }
    if ctx
        .device
        .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
        .is_err()
    {
        eprintln!("device poll failed after timed loop");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    let elapsed = start.elapsed().as_secs_f64();
    let streamed = bytes_len as f64 * f64::from(iters);
    println!(
        "row mode: {iters} iters, {streamed:.0} bytes in {elapsed:.3} s = {:.1} GB/s",
        streamed / elapsed / 1e9
    );
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

===== END FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/examples/stream_probe.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/src/compute.rs =====
//! [`WgpuCompute`]: the wgpu backend behind `muse_glimmer::Compute`.
//!
//! What runs on the device: `proj` (and through it `lm_head`)
//! for Q4_K, Q6_K, and Q5_K tensors, through kernels K1, K2,
//! and K3 respectively, selected by the tensor's dtype; the
//! norms and the residual add through K4; `attention` end to
//! end, with K5 rotating Q and K on the sliding layers and
//! appending the rotated keys and the values into this
//! backend's own resident KV buffers, and K6 running the
//! scores and the online-softmax reduce over them (the host
//! mirror in the backend's KV state holds the same rows, so
//! the device buffers and the `Cache` trait's position
//! contract cannot drift apart); `swiglu_ffn` end to end
//! (K1 gate and up, K7 activation, K2 down) with `attn_gate`
//! through K7; and the embedding gather through K8. Nothing
//! is silently substituted: BACKEND.md Section 6 puts per-op
//! CPU fallback at load time as the caller's disclosed
//! composition decision, so this backend never detours a
//! step to the CPU behind the caller's back.
//!
//! The device-resident forward (the session in
//! `crate::session`, with the DFlash draft session beside
//! it) is the crate's other half: it keeps the whole forward
//! on the device and routes its projections through the
//! wider kernel ladder (the K9 to K24 products, the split-K
//! reducer, and the cooperative-matrix variants) under the
//! routing switches resolved in this module. The shipped
//! defaults at this writing: the MMV ceiling is 16, staged
//! flash is on, the K21F head route is on, the cooperative
//! matrix rung is on with K24 selected, split-K is fixed
//! factor 4, and F16 KV storage is off; each switch keeps
//! its named env override and its fail-closed fallback.
//!
//! Data path, stated plainly: weight tensors upload once and are
//! cached by name (per-tensor device buffers, BACKEND.md
//! Section 5); each `proj` call uploads its input rows and reads
//! its output rows back, because the trait's currency is host
//! slices. When the forward itself becomes device-resident, the
//! per-call transfers are what go away; the kernels and the cache
//! stay.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use muse_glimmer::{

    Result, TensorView,
};

use crate::detect::{detect, DetectPolicy};

use crate::kernels::k15_q4k_mmq_wide::K15Pipeline;
use crate::kernels::k16_q6k_mmq_wide::K16Pipeline;

use crate::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::{K1Pipeline, K1Weights, ACT_GATED, ACT_NONE, ACT_SWIGLU};

/// Environment variable naming the wide-MMQ row threshold
/// override: the chunk row count at or past which the
/// session prefers the wide-tile double-buffered MMQ
/// products (K15/K16) over the standard ones (K13/K14).
/// Operational config, not a compiled constant: set it
/// past the batch cap (64) to take the wide form out of
/// the ladder entirely (the A/B control position the
/// prefill bench script uses), or lower it to widen the
/// wide form's reach. An unparsable value falls back to
/// [`DEFAULT_WIDE_MIN_ROWS`], with the fallback logged.
pub const WIDE_MIN_ROWS_ENV: &str = "WGPU_COMPUTE_MMQ_WIDE_MIN_ROWS";

/// The wide-MMQ row threshold when the environment does
/// not override it: past the chunk cap, so the wide form
/// is OUT of the ladder by default. The server proof of
/// 2026-11-04 (bench/mmq-wide-tile-2026-11-03.md) found
/// the wide kernels numerically correct but about 3.5x
/// slower per tensor than the standard MMQ, and the wide
/// ladder hung the real session outright (GPU context
/// lost). The standard MMQ is the shipping position; the
/// wide form stays in the tree for future work and can be
/// opted into with the env override.
pub const DEFAULT_WIDE_MIN_ROWS: u32 = 65;

/// Resolve the wide-MMQ row threshold from the raw
/// environment value: a plain u32, or the default when
/// unset or unparsable.
fn resolve_wide_min_rows(raw: Option<&str>) -> u32 {
    match raw {
        Some(s) => s.trim().parse::<u32>().unwrap_or(DEFAULT_WIDE_MIN_ROWS),
        None => DEFAULT_WIDE_MIN_ROWS,
    }
}

/// Environment variable naming the small-batch product
/// threshold override: the largest batch row count at
/// which the session prefers the small-batch products
/// (K18) over the GEMV forms, inside the band from 2
/// rows up. Operational config, not a compiled
/// constant: set it to 15 or 16 to enable K18 across
/// its measured band (the kernel itself refuses past
/// [`crate::kernels::k18_small_batch::SMALL_MAX_BATCH`]),
/// or leave it at the default to keep K18 out of the
/// ladder entirely. An unparsable value falls back to
/// [`DEFAULT_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS`], with the fallback
/// logged at construction.
pub const SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS_ENV: &str = "WGPU_COMPUTE_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS";

/// The small-batch row threshold when the environment
/// does not override it: 1, which is OFF, since the
/// ladder only routes batches of 2 or more rows to
/// K18. The shipped default follows the wide-MMQ
/// precedent: an unproven kernel does not enter the
/// ladder by default. The server proof that can move
/// this value is sequenced in
/// bench/small-batch-2026-11-04.md.
pub const DEFAULT_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS: u32 = 1;

/// Resolve the small-batch row threshold from the raw
/// environment value: a plain u32, or the default when
/// unset or unparsable.
fn resolve_small_batch_max_rows(raw: Option<&str>) -> u32 {
    match raw {
        Some(s) => s
            .trim()
            .parse::<u32>()
            .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS),
        None => DEFAULT_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS,
    }
}

/// Environment variable naming the register-streaming
/// small-batch (MMV) threshold override: the largest
/// batch row count at which the session prefers the
/// register-streaming products (K19 for Q4_K, K20
/// for Q6_K, K21 for Q5_K) over the K18 and GEMV
/// forms, inside the band
/// from 2 rows up. Operational config, not a compiled
/// constant: the shipped default (16) enables the MMV
/// forms across their band (each kernel itself refuses
/// past its cap); set it to 1 to keep them out of the
/// ladder entirely, or to any value in between to clip
/// the band from above. The ceiling is only
/// the outer gate: the band routing table below
/// ([`MmvBands`]) narrows it per family and shape to
/// the cells the 2026-11-06 sweep measured as wins.
/// An unparsable value falls back to the closed
/// ceiling ([`MMV_MAX_ROWS_FALLBACK`]), never to the
/// shipped default, with the resolved value logged at
/// construction.
pub const MMV_MAX_ROWS_ENV: &str = "WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS";

/// The MMV row threshold when the environment does not
/// override it: 16, the kernels' full band, so the MMV
/// forms are in the ladder wherever the band table
/// admits the batch. This default shipped at 1 (OFF:
/// the ladder only routes batches of 2 or more rows)
/// under the wide-MMQ and K18 precedent, that an
/// unproven kernel does not enter the ladder by
/// default. The server proofs sequenced in
/// bench/mmv-prototype-2026-11-05.md (Q4_K),
/// bench/mmv-q6k-2026-11-05.md (Q6_K) and
/// bench/mmv-q5k-2026-11-05.md (Q5_K), then the band
/// table of bench/mmv-band-routing-2026-11-06.md,
/// discharged that burden, and the baseline session's
/// card protocol (bench/baseline-session-2026-11-06.md
/// leg (d)) passed at this ceiling at both depths with
/// identity, golden, and byte-identical streams in
/// every arm; the default moved to 16 on 2026-11-06.
/// Rollback is one env value:
/// `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=1` restores the pre-flip
/// ladder exactly.
pub const DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS: u32 = 16;

/// The MMV ceiling a present but unparsable env value
/// resolves to: 1, closed. The fallback is deliberately
/// NOT the shipped default: a typo in the environment
/// must never widen routing, so the malformed case
/// keeps the fail-closed value it resolved to before
/// the default moved.
const MMV_MAX_ROWS_FALLBACK: u32 = 1;

/// Resolve the MMV row threshold from the raw
/// environment value: a plain u32; the shipped default
/// when unset; the closed fallback when present but
/// unparsable. Production resolution goes through
/// [`resolve_mmv_max_rows_with_profile`]; this is the
/// tests' handle on the env layer alone.
#[cfg(test)]
fn resolve_mmv_max_rows(raw: Option<&str>) -> u32 {
    resolve_mmv_max_rows_with_profile(raw, None)
}

/// Resolve the MMV row threshold with the calibration
/// profile's layer in its precedence place: an env
/// value, when present, decides on its own (a present
/// but unparsable value still falls to the closed
/// fallback, never to the profile: a typo must not
/// widen routing through any layer); with the env
/// unset, the loaded profile's ceiling applies when
/// it states one; only then the shipped default.
fn resolve_mmv_max_rows_with_profile(raw: Option<&str>, profile_ceiling: Option<u32>) -> u32 {
    match raw {
        Some(s) => s.trim().parse::<u32>().unwrap_or(MMV_MAX_ROWS_FALLBACK),
        None => profile_ceiling.unwrap_or(DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS),
    }
}

/// The quant family an MMV routing decision belongs
/// to: the register-streaming products are one per
/// family (K19 for Q4_K, K20 for Q6_K, K21 for Q5_K),
/// and the 2026-11-06 sweep measured each family's
/// cells separately, so the routing table below is
/// keyed by family first.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum MmvFamily {
    Q4K,
    Q5K,
    Q6K,
}

impl MmvFamily {
    /// The family's short name, as it appears in the
    /// band env names and the construction log.
    pub(crate) fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            MmvFamily::Q4K => "q4k",
            MmvFamily::Q5K => "q5k",
            MmvFamily::Q6K => "q6k",
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn index(self) -> usize {
        match self {
            MmvFamily::Q4K => 0,
            MmvFamily::Q5K => 1,
            MmvFamily::Q6K => 2,
        }
    }
}

/// The shape class of a projection, as the sweep
/// measured it: the three output widths at the
/// model's hidden width (attn 6656, ffn 19968,
/// kv 256). Real projections are classified by
/// relative geometry in [`mmv_shape_of`], since a
/// session sees more widths than the sweep's three
/// (the Q projection at 4096 out, the down
/// projection at 19968 in).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum MmvShape {
    /// Output near the input width (attention-sized).
    Attn,
    /// Output a wide multiple of the input (FFN up).
    Ffn,
    /// Output a small fraction of the input (K/V).
    Kv,
}

impl MmvShape {
    /// The shape class's short name, as it appears
    /// in the band env names and the logs.
    pub(crate) fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            MmvShape::Attn => "attn",
            MmvShape::Ffn => "ffn",
            MmvShape::Kv => "kv",
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn index(self) -> usize {
        match self {
            MmvShape::Attn => 0,
            MmvShape::Ffn => 1,
            MmvShape::Kv => 2,
        }
    }
}

/// Classify a projection's geometry into the
/// sweep's shape classes: a projection whose output
/// is at most an eighth of its input width is a KV
/// projection (Glimmer: 256 out of 6656 in); one
/// whose output is at least twice its input width
/// is an FFN projection (19968 out of 6656 in);
/// everything else is attention-class. The measured
/// cells sit far from both boundaries (256 is 1/26
/// of 6656, 19968 is 3x), so every real projection
/// classifies unambiguously; a geometry the sweep
/// did not measure (the Q projection at 4096 out,
/// the down projection at 19968 in) lands in the
/// attention class, the disclosure
/// bench/mmv-band-routing-2026-11-06.md records.
pub(crate) fn mmv_shape_of(in_features: usize, out_rows: usize) -> MmvShape {
    if out_rows * 8 <= in_features {
        MmvShape::Kv
    } else if out_rows >= 2 * in_features {
        MmvShape::Ffn
    } else {
        MmvShape::Attn
    }
}

/// The env name carrying the band cell for one
/// (family, shape) pair: the batch-row ranges in
/// which that family's register-streaming product
/// serves that shape class, in the syntax
/// [`parse_mmv_band`] reads. Operational config,
/// not a compiled constant, like every routing
/// threshold in this module. Set a cell to "1" to
/// close it entirely.
fn mmv_band_env(family: MmvFamily, shape: MmvShape) -> &'static str {
    match (family, shape) {
        (MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Attn) => "WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_Q4K_ATTN_ROWS",
        (MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Ffn) => "WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_Q4K_FFN_ROWS",
        (MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Kv) => "WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_Q4K_KV_ROWS",
        (MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvShape::Attn) => "WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_Q5K_ATTN_ROWS",
        (MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvShape::Ffn) => "WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_Q5K_FFN_ROWS",
        (MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvShape::Kv) => "WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_Q5K_KV_ROWS",
        (MmvFamily::Q6K, MmvShape::Attn) => "WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_Q6K_ATTN_ROWS",
        (MmvFamily::Q6K, MmvShape::Ffn) => "WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_Q6K_FFN_ROWS",
        (MmvFamily::Q6K, MmvShape::Kv) => "WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_Q6K_KV_ROWS",
    }
}

/// The shipped band cell for one (family, shape)
/// pair, in the same syntax the env override uses,
/// so the default and the override share one parse
/// path. Every range here is derived cell by cell
/// from the 2026-11-06 sweep table in
/// bench/mmv-band-routing-2026-11-06.md: a batch is
/// in the cell only where the sweep measured the
/// MMV form beating the GEMV control there (a tie
/// or a loss falls through to the ladder), so the
/// ranges are the measured win map and nothing
/// else.
fn default_mmv_band(family: MmvFamily, shape: MmvShape) -> &'static str {
    match (family, shape) {
        (MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Attn) => "6-12",
        (MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Ffn) => "2,4-12",
        (MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Kv) => "2-3",
        (MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvShape::Attn) => "2-16",
        (MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvShape::Ffn) => "3-16",
        (MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvShape::Kv) => "16",
        (MmvFamily::Q6K, MmvShape::Attn) => "2-12",
        (MmvFamily::Q6K, MmvShape::Ffn) => "2-12",
        (MmvFamily::Q6K, MmvShape::Kv) => "12",
    }
}

/// Parse one band cell: comma-separated inclusive
/// ranges, each a single row ("16") or a span
/// ("6-12"), whitespace ignored. Parsed ranges are
/// intersected with the kernels' own band
/// ([`MMV_MIN_BATCH`]..=[`MMV_MAX_BATCH`]); a range
/// missing the band entirely drops out, so "1" is
/// a valid cell that routes nothing. Any malformed
/// item (empty, non-numeric, a reversed span) makes
/// the whole value unparsable: `None`, and the
/// caller falls back to the shipped cell, the
/// fail-closed direction every resolver in this
/// module takes.
fn parse_mmv_band(raw: &str) -> Option<Vec<(u32, u32)>> {
    let mut ranges = Vec::new();
    for item in raw.split(',') {
        let item = item.trim();
        if item.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        let (lo, hi) = match item.split_once('-') {
            Some((a, b)) => (a.trim().parse::<u32>().ok()?, b.trim().parse::<u32>().ok()?),
            None => {
                let v = item.parse::<u32>().ok()?;
                (v, v)
            }
        };
        if lo > hi {
            return None;
        }
        let lo = lo.max(MMV_MIN_BATCH);
        let hi = hi.min(MMV_MAX_BATCH);
        if lo <= hi {
            ranges.push((lo, hi));
        }
    }
    Some(ranges)
}

/// The resolved MMV routing table: one band cell
/// per (family, shape) pair. The table only ever
/// narrows the global [`MMV_MAX_ROWS_ENV`] ceiling:
/// a family's product serves a projection when the
/// batch is under the ceiling AND inside the cell,
/// so the shipped ceiling default (16) admits exactly
/// the measured-win cells instead of the whole band
/// whose middle the dose-response sweep convicted
/// (bench/mmv-verdict-2026-11-05.md, step 4).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct MmvBands {
    /// `cells[family.index()][shape.index()]`: the
    /// inclusive batch-row ranges the family's
    /// product serves for that shape class.
    cells: [[Vec<(u32, u32)>; 3]; 3],
}

impl MmvBands {
    /// Whether the family's register-streaming
    /// product serves this shape class at `batch`
    /// rows under the resolved global `ceiling`.
    pub(crate) fn routes(
        &self,
        ceiling: u32,
        family: MmvFamily,
        shape: MmvShape,
        batch: u32,
    ) -> bool {
        batch >= MMV_MIN_BATCH
            && batch <= ceiling
            && self.cells[family.index()][shape.index()]
                .iter()
                .any(|&(lo, hi)| lo <= batch && batch <= hi)
    }

    /// The table in the band syntax, for the
    /// construction log: the effective policy is
    /// always printable from the resolved config.
    fn describe(&self) -> String {
        let mut out = String::new();
        for family in [MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvFamily::Q6K] {
            if !out.is_empty() {
                out.push(' ');
            }
            out.push_str(family.name());
            out.push('[');
            for (i, shape) in [MmvShape::Attn, MmvShape::Ffn, MmvShape::Kv]
                .into_iter()
                .enumerate()
            {
                if i > 0 {
                    out.push(' ');
                }
                out.push_str(shape.name());
                out.push(' ');
                out.push_str(&fmt_mmv_band(&self.cells[family.index()][shape.index()]));
            }
            out.push(']');
        }
        out
    }
}

/// One band cell in the syntax [`parse_mmv_band`]
/// reads, for logs: "6-12", "2,4-12", "16", or
/// "none" when the cell routes nothing.
fn fmt_mmv_band(ranges: &[(u32, u32)]) -> String {
    if ranges.is_empty() {
        return "none".to_string();
    }
    ranges
        .iter()
        .map(|&(lo, hi)| {
            if lo == hi {
                lo.to_string()
            } else {
                format!("{lo}-{hi}")
            }
        })
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join(",")
}

/// The shipped routing table: every cell at its
/// [`default_mmv_band`]. Production resolution goes
/// through [`resolve_mmv_bands`] with the real env;
/// this is the tests' handle on the defaults alone.
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) fn default_mmv_bands() -> MmvBands {
    resolve_mmv_bands(|_| None)
}

/// Resolve the routing table: each cell from its
/// env override when set and parsable, else the
/// shipped cell. The defaults parse through the
/// same path as an override; a shipped cell that
/// stopped parsing is a bug, and the `expect` says
/// so at construction instead of routing silently.
/// `get` is the env lookup, passed in so tests
/// resolve against a table of their own.
#[cfg(test)]
fn resolve_mmv_bands(get: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<String>) -> MmvBands {
    resolve_mmv_bands_with_profile(get, None)
}

/// Resolve the routing table with the calibration
/// profile's layer in its precedence place: each cell
/// comes from its env override when set and parsable,
/// else from the loaded profile's cell for the pair
/// when it states one and it parses, else the shipped
/// cell. The layers share one parse path, so a cell
/// means the same thing whichever layer stated it;
/// an unparsable value at any layer falls through to
/// the next rather than disabling or widening the
/// cell, and the fallbacks are logged at construction
/// ([`log_mmv_band_fallbacks`],
/// [`log_mmv_profile_cell_fallbacks`]).
fn resolve_mmv_bands_with_profile(
    get: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<String>,
    profile: Option<&crate::profile::CalibrationProfile>,
) -> MmvBands {
    let mut cells: [[Vec<(u32, u32)>; 3]; 3] = Default::default();
    for family in [MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvFamily::Q6K] {
        for shape in [MmvShape::Attn, MmvShape::Ffn, MmvShape::Kv] {
            let parsed = get(mmv_band_env(family, shape))
                .and_then(|raw| parse_mmv_band(&raw))
                .or_else(|| {
                    profile
                        .and_then(|p| p.band_cell(family, shape))
                        .and_then(parse_mmv_band)
                })
                .or_else(|| parse_mmv_band(default_mmv_band(family, shape)));
            cells[family.index()][shape.index()] =
                parsed.expect("the shipped MMV band cells parse");
        }
    }
    MmvBands { cells }
}

/// Log, per cell, when an env override is present
/// but unparsable and a lower layer therefore
/// applies: a silent fallback in a routing table
/// is how a typo becomes a mystery cliff. The line
/// names the layer that actually governs the cell,
/// the profile's cell when a loaded profile states
/// one, else the shipped cell.
fn log_mmv_band_fallbacks(profile: Option<&crate::profile::CalibrationProfile>) {
    for family in [MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvFamily::Q6K] {
        for shape in [MmvShape::Attn, MmvShape::Ffn, MmvShape::Kv] {
            let env = mmv_band_env(family, shape);
            if let Ok(raw) = std::env::var(env) {
                if parse_mmv_band(&raw).is_none() {
                    match profile.and_then(|p| p.band_cell(family, shape)) {
                        Some(cell) => dbg_log!(
                            "mmv band env {env}={raw:?} is unparsable; \
                             the profile cell ({cell}) applies"
                        ),
                        None => dbg_log!(
                            "mmv band env {env}={raw:?} is unparsable; \
                             the shipped cell ({}) applies",
                            default_mmv_band(family, shape)
                        ),
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Log, per cell, when a loaded profile states a
/// cell the band parser refuses and the shipped cell
/// therefore applies: a profile is hand-editable, so
/// its typos get the same named-fallback treatment
/// as the env's.
fn log_mmv_profile_cell_fallbacks(profile: Option<&crate::profile::CalibrationProfile>) {
    let Some(profile) = profile else {
        return;
    };
    for family in [MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvFamily::Q6K] {
        for shape in [MmvShape::Attn, MmvShape::Ffn, MmvShape::Kv] {
            if let Some(cell) = profile.band_cell(family, shape) {
                if parse_mmv_band(cell).is_none() {
                    dbg_log!(
                        "mmv profile cell {} {} ({cell:?}) is unparsable; \
                         the shipped cell ({}) applies",
                        family.name(),
                        shape.name(),
                        default_mmv_band(family, shape)
                    );
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Load the calibration profile for this context's
/// adapter at construction, and state the outcome on
/// the diag channel either way: the loaded profile
/// (with its key, which the backend keeps for the
/// capture manifest), or `None` with the reason
/// logged (no path resolves, no file there, or a file
/// that failed verification). A rejected profile is
/// never half-applied: the shipped defaults govern,
/// exactly as on an uncalibrated machine.
fn load_construction_profile(
    ctx: &crate::device::GpuContext,
) -> (Option<crate::profile::CalibrationProfile>, Option<String>) {
    use crate::profile::{load_profile, profile_path, AdapterKey, ProfileLoad};
    let key = AdapterKey::from_facts(&ctx.adapter);
    let Some(path) = profile_path() else {
        dbg_log!(
            "mmv profile: no profile path resolves (no {}, \
             XDG_CONFIG_HOME, or HOME); shipped defaults apply",
            crate::profile::PROFILE_PATH_ENV
        );
        return (None, None);
    };
    match load_profile(&path, &key) {
        ProfileLoad::Loaded(profile) => {
            let profile = *profile;
            dbg_log!(
                "mmv profile: loaded [{}] from {}",
                profile.key.describe(),
                path.display()
            );
            let describe = profile.key.describe();
            (Some(profile), Some(describe))
        }
        ProfileLoad::Absent => {
            dbg_log!(
                "mmv profile: none at {}; shipped defaults apply",
                path.display()
            );
            (None, None)
        }
        ProfileLoad::Rejected(why) => {
            dbg_log!("mmv profile: {why}; shipped defaults apply");
            (None, None)
        }
    }
}

/// Environment variable naming the chunked-GEMV row
/// threshold override: the largest batch row count at
/// which the session serves a plain projection as
/// several windowed GEMV dispatches at power-of-two row
/// counts (the chunked form) instead of one GEMV dispatch
/// at the batch's own count, inside the band from 2 rows
/// up to below the matrix threshold. Operational config,
/// not a compiled constant: set it to 15 to enable the
/// chunked form across the whole speculative verify band,
/// or leave it at the default to keep the ladder's GEMV
/// rung exactly as shipped. An unparsable value falls
/// back to [`DEFAULT_CHUNKED_GEMV_MAX_ROWS`], with the
/// fallback logged at construction.
pub const CHUNKED_GEMV_MAX_ROWS_ENV: &str = "WGPU_COMPUTE_CHUNKED_GEMV_MAX_ROWS";

/// The chunked-GEMV row threshold when the environment
/// does not override it: 1, which is OFF, since the
/// ladder only routes batches of 2 or more rows to the
/// chunked form. The shipped default follows the K18
/// precedent: an unproven dispatch shape does not enter
/// the ladder by default. The head-to-head proof that
/// can move this value is sequenced in
/// bench/chunked-gemv-2026-11-05.md.
pub const DEFAULT_CHUNKED_GEMV_MAX_ROWS: u32 = 1;

/// Resolve the chunked-GEMV row threshold from the raw
/// environment value: a plain u32, or the default when
/// unset or unparsable.
fn resolve_chunked_gemv_max_rows(raw: Option<&str>) -> u32 {
    match raw {
        Some(s) => s
            .trim()
            .parse::<u32>()
            .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_CHUNKED_GEMV_MAX_ROWS),
        None => DEFAULT_CHUNKED_GEMV_MAX_ROWS,
    }
}

/// Environment variable naming the K22 (Q4_K MMQ,
/// register-organization prototype) routing switch: the
/// exact value `1` makes the resident session prefer the
/// K22 product over the standard K13 product for Q4_K MMQ
/// projections. Operational config, not a compiled
/// constant, and deliberately fail-closed: an unset
/// variable, or any other value, keeps K22 out of the
/// ladder entirely, so the shipped ladder is byte-for-byte
/// the ladder every existing proof ran on. The shipped
/// default follows the wide-MMQ and K18 precedent: an
/// unproven kernel does not enter the ladder by default.
/// The server proof that can move this switch's default
/// is sequenced in bench/k22-mmq-2026-11-05.md.
pub const K22_MMQ_ENV: &str = "WGPU_COMPUTE_K22_MMQ";

/// Resolve the K22 routing switch from the raw
/// environment value: only the exact value `1` (after
/// trimming) enables it; everything else is off.
fn resolve_k22_mmq(raw: Option<&str>) -> bool {
    matches!(raw.map(str::trim), Some("1"))
}

/// Environment variable naming the staged-flash routing
/// switch: it decides whether the resident session runs
/// multi-row attention calls through K6's staged flash
/// form (K/V blocks of 32 keys staged in workgroup memory,
/// 8 query rows per workgroup; see
/// `crate::kernels::k6_attention::FLASH_STAGED_SHADER`)
/// instead of the shipped flash form. Operational config,
/// not a compiled constant. The staged form is the
/// DEFAULT: an unset variable resolves to on, and the
/// exact value `1` (after trimming) also resolves to on,
/// so a value that meant on before the default flip still
/// means on. The exact value `0` is the explicit off and
/// the one-variable rollback to the shipped form. Any
/// other value fails closed to off, with the refusal
/// logged by name at construction: a typo must never
/// silently select a form. Single-row calls keep the
/// shipped form in every switch position (a one-row
/// workgroup would stage a KV block for one active row
/// of eight); that exclusion is routing, not part of the
/// switch. The default flipped on the interleaved card
/// evidence in bench/flash-host-cost-2026-11-06.md,
/// which discharged the decision rule written in
/// bench/flash-rework-2026-11-06.md; the flip itself is
/// recorded in bench/flash-default-flip-2026-11-07.md.
pub const FLASH_STAGED_ENV: &str = "WGPU_COMPUTE_FLASH_STAGED";

/// Resolve the staged-flash routing switch from the raw
/// environment value: unset is ON (the shipped default),
/// the exact value `1` (after trimming) is ON, the exact
/// value `0` is the explicit OFF, and any other value
/// fails closed to OFF. The caller logs the refusal for
/// an unrecognized value at construction
/// ([`log_flash_staged_fallback`]), so the fail-closed
/// position is visible in the run log, never silent.
fn resolve_flash_staged(raw: Option<&str>) -> bool {
    match raw.map(str::trim) {
        None | Some("1") => true,
        Some("0") => false,
        Some(_) => false,
    }
}

/// Whether a raw staged-flash env value is one the
/// resolver recognizes (`1` or `0` after trimming, or
/// unset). An unrecognized value resolves off; the
/// construction log names it, following the MMV band
/// fallback pattern: a silent fallback in a routing
/// switch is how a typo becomes a mystery regression.
fn flash_staged_value_recognized(raw: Option<&str>) -> bool {
