                     when a sequence is abandoned (a forward that failed midway leaves the KV state \
                     ahead of the cache and also needs a reset)",
                    req.layer
                ),
            ));
        }

        let head_dim = cfg.key_length as usize;
        let q_heads = cfg.q_heads as usize;
        let kv_heads = cfg.kv_heads as usize;
        let window = match req.kind {
            LayerKind::Global => None,
            LayerKind::SlidingWindow => Some(cfg.sliding_window as usize),
        };

        // Rotate Q and K in place on the device, sliding layers
        // only, at the SWA base; global layers are NoPE and pass
        // through unrotated (src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp).
        let q_buf = self.ctx.upload_f32("attention q", req.q);
        let k_buf = self.ctx.upload_f32("attention k", req.k);
        if req.kind == LayerKind::SlidingWindow {
            self.k5
                .rotate(
                    &self.ctx,
                    &q_buf,
                    rows,
                    q_heads,
                    head_dim,
                    start,
                    cfg.rope_freq_base_swa,
                )
                .map_err(|e| step_failed(step, e.to_string()))?;
            self.k5
                .rotate(
                    &self.ctx,
                    &k_buf,
                    rows,
                    kv_heads,
                    head_dim,
                    start,
                    cfg.rope_freq_base_swa,
                )
                .map_err(|e| step_failed(step, e.to_string()))?;
        }
        // The rotated keys come back exactly once: the host
        // mirror appends what the device computed, so the mirror
        // (positions, cross-checks, tests) and the device buffers
        // can never drift apart in what they hold.
        let k_rot = self
            .ctx
            .read_f32(&k_buf, req.k.len())
            .map_err(|e| step_failed(step, e.to_string()))?;
        for i in 0..rows {
            state
                .host_mut()
                .append(
                    req.layer,
                    &k_rot[i * k_width..(i + 1) * k_width],
                    &req.v[i * v_width..(i + 1) * v_width],
                    start + i,
                )
                .map_err(|e| step_failed(step, e.to_string()))?;
        }
        let (stored, first_pos) = {
            let view = state
                .host()
                .view(req.layer)
                .map_err(|e| step_failed(step, e.to_string()))?;
            let first = view.position_at(0).ok_or_else(|| {
                step_failed(
                    step,
                    "the layer's cache view is empty right after an append",
                )
            })?;
            (view.len(), first)
        };
        let appended_total = state
            .host()
            .next_position(req.layer)
            .map_err(|e| step_failed(step, e.to_string()))?;
        let layer_kv = state.ensure_layer(&self.ctx, req.layer, k_width, appended_total, step)?;
        // K5's second half: append the rotated K rows and the V
        // rows into the layer's resident buffers, at the slots
        // the cache semantics assign.
        let v_buf = self.ctx.upload_f32("attention v", req.v);
        self.k5
            .append(
                &self.ctx,
                &k_buf,
                &v_buf,
                &layer_kv.k,
                &layer_kv.v,
                rows,
                k_width,
                start,
                window,
            )
            .map_err(|e| step_failed(step, e.to_string()))?;
        // K6: scores plus the online-softmax reduce over the
        // resident buffers.
        let geom = AttendGeom {
            rows,
            q_heads,
            kv_heads,
            head_dim,
            stored,
            first_pos,
            start_pos: start,
            window,
            // The trait state's ring holds exactly one window,
            // so its slot modulus is the window itself.
            ring: window,
        };
        let scores = self
            .k6
            .scores(&self.ctx, &q_buf, layer_kv, &geom)
            .map_err(|e| step_failed(step, e.to_string()))?;
        let out = self
            .k6
            .reduce(&self.ctx, &scores, layer_kv, &geom)
            .map_err(|e| step_failed(step, e.to_string()))?;
        dbg_log!(
            "attention layer={} kind={:?} start={} rows={} stored={}",
            req.layer,
            req.kind,
            start,
            rows,
            stored
        );
        Ok(out)
    }

    fn attn_gate(&self, attn_out: &[f32], gate: &[f32]) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        self.k7
            .attn_gate(&self.ctx, attn_out, gate)
            .map_err(|e| step_failed("attn_gate", e.to_string()))
    }

    fn add(&self, a: &[f32], b: &[f32]) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        self.k4
            .add(&self.ctx, a, b)
            .map_err(|e| step_failed("add", e.to_string()))
    }

    fn swiglu_ffn(
        &self,
        x: &[f32],
        w: &LayerWeights,
        rows: usize,
        _cfg: &GlimmerConfig,
    ) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        let step = "swiglu_ffn";
        // The FFN end to end: gate and up through K1 (Q4_K in the
        // real file), the activation through K7, and the down
        // projection through K2 (Q6_K).
        let gate = self.proj_impl(x, &w.ffn_gate, rows, step)?;
        let up = self.proj_impl(x, &w.ffn_up, rows, step)?;
        let act = self
            .k7
            .swiglu(&self.ctx, &gate, &up)
            .map_err(|e| step_failed(step, e.to_string()))?;
        self.proj_impl(&act, &w.ffn_down, rows, step)
    }

    fn lm_head(&self, x: &[f32], head: &TensorView, cfg: &GlimmerConfig) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        let step = "lm_head";
        if head.shape.len() != 2 {
            return Err(step_failed(
                step,
                format!(
                    "output head {} has shape {:?}, expected [hidden, vocab] in GGUF stored order",
                    head.name, head.shape
                ),
            ));
        }
        let (inn, vocab) = (head.shape[0] as usize, head.shape[1] as usize);
        if inn != x.len() {
            return Err(step_failed(
                step,
                format!(
                    "output head {} reads {inn} inputs but the normed hidden state holds {}",
                    head.name,
                    x.len()
                ),
            ));
        }
        if vocab != cfg.vocab_size as usize {
            return Err(step_failed(
                step,
                format!(
                    "output head {} produces {vocab} logits but the config's vocabulary is {}",
                    head.name, cfg.vocab_size
                ),
            ));
        }
        self.proj_impl(x, head, 1, step)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn wide_min_rows_resolution() {
        // Unset: the default.
        assert_eq!(resolve_wide_min_rows(None), DEFAULT_WIDE_MIN_ROWS);
        // Plain values pass through, including the two
        // bench positions: 1 (wide everywhere the matrix
        // path runs) and 65 (past the batch cap: wide out
        // of the ladder, the A/B control).
        assert_eq!(resolve_wide_min_rows(Some("1")), 1);
        assert_eq!(resolve_wide_min_rows(Some("65")), 65);
        assert_eq!(resolve_wide_min_rows(Some(" 48 ")), 48);
        // Unparsable values fall back to the default rather
        // than failing backend construction.
        assert_eq!(resolve_wide_min_rows(Some("wide")), DEFAULT_WIDE_MIN_ROWS);
        assert_eq!(resolve_wide_min_rows(Some("")), DEFAULT_WIDE_MIN_ROWS);
        assert_eq!(resolve_wide_min_rows(Some("-3")), DEFAULT_WIDE_MIN_ROWS);
    }

    #[test]
    fn small_batch_max_rows_resolution() {
        // Unset: the default, which is off (1 routes
        // nothing, since the ladder's band starts at 2).
        assert_eq!(
            resolve_small_batch_max_rows(None),
            DEFAULT_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS
        );
        assert_eq!(DEFAULT_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS, 1);
        // Plain values pass through, including the
        // proof positions: 15 (the routed band under
        // GEMM_MIN_ROWS) and 16 (the kernel's full
        // band).
        assert_eq!(resolve_small_batch_max_rows(Some("15")), 15);
        assert_eq!(resolve_small_batch_max_rows(Some("16")), 16);
        assert_eq!(resolve_small_batch_max_rows(Some(" 0 ")), 0);
        // Unparsable values fall back to the default
        // rather than failing backend construction.
        assert_eq!(
            resolve_small_batch_max_rows(Some("small")),
            DEFAULT_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS
        );
        assert_eq!(
            resolve_small_batch_max_rows(Some("")),
            DEFAULT_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS
        );
        assert_eq!(
            resolve_small_batch_max_rows(Some("-2")),
            DEFAULT_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn mmv_max_rows_resolution() {
        // Unset: the shipped default, 16, the kernels'
        // full band. The default moved from 1 (off) to
        // 16 on the baseline session's card verdict
        // (bench/baseline-session-2026-11-06.md leg
        // (d): cap 16 beat the unset control at both
        // depths, 21.73 vs 17.39 and 16.33 vs 10.14,
        // with identity and golden green in every arm).
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmv_max_rows(None), DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS);
        assert_eq!(DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS, 16);
        // Plain values pass through, including the
        // proof positions: 15 (the routed band under
        // GEMM_MIN_ROWS) and 16 (the kernels' full
        // band). The explicit close still closes: a set
        // "1" wins over the shipped default.
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmv_max_rows(Some("1")), 1);
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmv_max_rows(Some("15")), 15);
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmv_max_rows(Some("16")), 16);
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmv_max_rows(Some(" 0 ")), 0);
        // Unparsable values fall back to the CLOSED
        // ceiling, not the shipped default, rather than
        // failing backend construction: a typo in the
        // env must never widen routing. This is the
        // fail-closed behavior the malformed case had
        // before the default moved, kept deliberately.
        assert_eq!(MMV_MAX_ROWS_FALLBACK, 1);
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmv_max_rows(Some("mmv")), MMV_MAX_ROWS_FALLBACK);
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmv_max_rows(Some("")), MMV_MAX_ROWS_FALLBACK);
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmv_max_rows(Some("-2")), MMV_MAX_ROWS_FALLBACK);
    }

    #[test]
    fn mmv_band_parse_forms() {
        // Single rows, spans, and lists, whitespace
        // tolerated.
        assert_eq!(parse_mmv_band("16"), Some(vec![(16, 16)]));
        assert_eq!(parse_mmv_band("6-12"), Some(vec![(6, 12)]));
        assert_eq!(parse_mmv_band("2,4-12"), Some(vec![(2, 2), (4, 12)]));
        assert_eq!(parse_mmv_band(" 2 , 4 - 12 "), Some(vec![(2, 2), (4, 12)]));
        // Ranges are intersected with the kernels'
        // own band (2..=16): a span reaching past it
        // clamps, and a span missing it entirely
        // drops out, so "1" is a valid cell that
        // routes nothing.
        assert_eq!(parse_mmv_band("0-99"), Some(vec![(2, 16)]));
        assert_eq!(parse_mmv_band("1"), Some(vec![]));
        assert_eq!(parse_mmv_band("17-20"), Some(vec![]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn mmv_band_parse_rejects_malformed() {
        // Any malformed item poisons the whole
        // value: resolution then falls back to the
        // shipped cell rather than guessing a band.
        for raw in [
            "",
            "x",
            "2-",
            "-3",
            "5-2",
            "2,,3",
            "2-3-4",
            "1.5",
            "99999999999999999999",
        ] {
            assert_eq!(parse_mmv_band(raw), None, "input {raw:?}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn mmv_band_resolution_falls_back_to_the_shipped_cell() {
        // Unset: the shipped cell.
        let bands = resolve_mmv_bands(|_| None);
        assert!(bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Attn, 6));
        assert!(!bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Attn, 2));
        // A parsable override replaces exactly its
        // own cell; the rest of the table is the
        // shipped one.
        let bands = resolve_mmv_bands(|name| {
            (name == mmv_band_env(MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Attn)).then(|| "2-3".to_string())
        });
        assert!(bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Attn, 2));
        assert!(!bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Attn, 6));
        assert!(bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q6K, MmvShape::Attn, 6));
        // An unparsable override falls back to the
        // shipped cell: it neither disables nor
        // widens the cell.
        let bands = resolve_mmv_bands(|name| {
            (name == mmv_band_env(MmvFamily::Q6K, MmvShape::Kv)).then(|| "junk".to_string())
        });
        assert!(bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q6K, MmvShape::Kv, 12));
        assert!(!bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q6K, MmvShape::Kv, 6));
        // An override of "1" closes its cell.
        let bands = resolve_mmv_bands(|name| {
            (name == mmv_band_env(MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvShape::Attn)).then(|| "1".to_string())
        });
        assert!(!bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvShape::Attn, 7));
    }

    #[test]
    fn mmv_profile_layer_sits_between_env_and_shipped() {
        use crate::profile::{AdapterKey, CalibrationProfile};
        // A profile measured on some other sweep: it
        // opens Q4_K KV at batch 12 (a batch the
        // shipped cell "2-3" leaves closed), narrows
        // Q4_K attention to "2-3" (the shipped cell is
        // "6-12"), and states an unparsable Q5_K KV
        // cell, which must fall through to the shipped
        // "16" rather than poison the table.
        let mut profile = CalibrationProfile::new(AdapterKey {
            name: "test adapter".to_string(),
            backend: "Vulkan".to_string(),
            driver: "test driver".to_string(),
            driver_info: "test driver info".to_string(),
        });
        profile.set_band_cell(MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Kv, "12".to_string());
        profile.set_band_cell(MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Attn, "2-3".to_string());
        profile.set_band_cell(MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvShape::Kv, "junk".to_string());

        // No env: the profile governs the cells it
        // states, the shipped table the rest.
        let bands = resolve_mmv_bands_with_profile(|_| None, Some(&profile));
        assert!(bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Kv, 12));
        assert!(!bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Kv, 4));
        assert!(bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Attn, 2));
        assert!(!bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Attn, 6));
        assert!(bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvShape::Kv, 16));
        assert!(!bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvShape::Kv, 2));
        assert!(bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q6K, MmvShape::Attn, 6));

        // An env override beats the profile for the
        // same cell, and only that cell.
        let bands = resolve_mmv_bands_with_profile(
            |name| {
                (name == mmv_band_env(MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Attn)).then(|| "6-9".to_string())
            },
            Some(&profile),
        );
        assert!(bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Attn, 6));
        assert!(!bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Attn, 2));
        assert!(bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Kv, 12));

        // An unparsable env value falls through to the
        // profile layer, not past it: the profile is
        // the next statement of the cell's value.
        let bands = resolve_mmv_bands_with_profile(
            |name| {
                (name == mmv_band_env(MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Attn)).then(|| "junk".to_string())
            },
            Some(&profile),
        );
        assert!(bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Attn, 2));
        assert!(!bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Attn, 6));

        // The ceiling resolves in the same precedence:
        // env over profile over shipped, and a present
        // but unparsable env value still lands on the
        // closed fallback without ever reaching the
        // profile.
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmv_max_rows_with_profile(None, Some(4)), 4);
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmv_max_rows_with_profile(None, None), 16);
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmv_max_rows_with_profile(Some("9"), Some(4)), 9);
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmv_max_rows_with_profile(Some("junk"), Some(4)), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn mmv_shape_classification() {
        // The sweep's measured geometries.
        assert_eq!(mmv_shape_of(6656, 6656), MmvShape::Attn);
        assert_eq!(mmv_shape_of(6656, 19968), MmvShape::Ffn);
        assert_eq!(mmv_shape_of(6656, 256), MmvShape::Kv);
        // The real model's other projections land in
        // the attention class: Q (4096 out), O (4096
        // in), down (19968 in).
        assert_eq!(mmv_shape_of(6656, 4096), MmvShape::Attn);
        assert_eq!(mmv_shape_of(4096, 6656), MmvShape::Attn);
        assert_eq!(mmv_shape_of(19968, 6656), MmvShape::Attn);
        // The class boundaries themselves: an output
        // at exactly an eighth of the input is KV, at
        // exactly double is FFN.
        assert_eq!(mmv_shape_of(2048, 256), MmvShape::Kv);
        assert_eq!(mmv_shape_of(6656, 832), MmvShape::Kv);
        assert_eq!(mmv_shape_of(6656, 833), MmvShape::Attn);
        assert_eq!(mmv_shape_of(6656, 13312), MmvShape::Ffn);
        assert_eq!(mmv_shape_of(6656, 202048), MmvShape::Ffn);
    }

    #[test]
    fn mmv_default_bands_match_the_measured_win_map() {
        // The shipped table against the verdict of
        // the 2026-11-06 sweep, cell by cell
        // (bench/results/mmv-sweep-20261106-212335/,
        // derived in
        // bench/mmv-band-routing-2026-11-06.md). Each
        // row is batches 2..=16 in order, true where
        // the family's product routes under a fully
        // open ceiling. A cell the sweep measured as
        // a tie or a loss for the MMV arm is false;
        // rows the sweep did not measure (10, 11, 13,
        // 14, 15) are true only where two measured
        // wins bracket them (Q5_K's run to 16; Q4_K
        // and Q6_K end at 12, their last measured
        // win, since row 16 on those families is the
        // MMQ rung in both arms and carries no MMV
        // measurement).
        let bands = default_mmv_bands();
        let expected: [(MmvFamily, MmvShape, [bool; 15]); 9] = [
            (
                MmvFamily::Q4K,
                MmvShape::Attn,
                [
                    false, false, false, false, true, true, true, true, true, true, true, false,
                    false, false, false,
                ],
            ),
            (
                MmvFamily::Q4K,
                MmvShape::Ffn,
                [
                    true, false, true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true, false,
                    false, false, false,
                ],
            ),
            (
                MmvFamily::Q4K,
                MmvShape::Kv,
                [
                    true, true, false, false, false, false, false, false, false, false, false,
                    false, false, false, false,
                ],
            ),
            (MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvShape::Attn, [true; 15]),
            (
                MmvFamily::Q5K,
                MmvShape::Ffn,
                [
                    false, true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true,
                    true, true,
                ],
            ),
            (
                MmvFamily::Q5K,
                MmvShape::Kv,
                [
                    false, false, false, false, false, false, false, false, false, false, false,
                    false, false, false, true,
                ],
            ),
            (
                MmvFamily::Q6K,
                MmvShape::Attn,
                [
                    true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true, false, false,
                    false, false,
                ],
            ),
            (
                MmvFamily::Q6K,
                MmvShape::Ffn,
                [
                    true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true, false, false,
                    false, false,
                ],
            ),
            (
                MmvFamily::Q6K,
                MmvShape::Kv,
                [
                    false, false, false, false, false, false, false, false, false, false, true,
                    false, false, false, false,
                ],
            ),
        ];
        for (family, shape, table) in expected {
            for (i, &want) in table.iter().enumerate() {
                let batch = i as u32 + 2;
                assert_eq!(
                    bands.routes(16, family, shape, batch),
                    want,
                    "{} {} batch {batch}",
                    family.name(),
                    shape.name()
                );
            }
        }
        // The construction log prints this same
        // table in band syntax.
        assert!(bands
            .describe()
            .contains("q4k[attn 6-12 ffn 2,4-12 kv 2-3]"));
        assert!(bands.describe().contains("q5k[attn 2-16 ffn 3-16 kv 16]"));
        assert!(bands.describe().contains("q6k[attn 2-12 ffn 2-12 kv 12]"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn mmv_routes_ceiling_composition() {
        let bands = default_mmv_bands();
        // The explicit close (ceiling 1) routes nothing,
        // whatever the table says.
        for family in [MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvFamily::Q6K] {
            for shape in [MmvShape::Attn, MmvShape::Ffn, MmvShape::Kv] {
                for batch in 2..=16 {
                    assert!(
                        !bands.routes(1, family, shape, batch),
                        "{} {} batch {batch} routed under the closed ceiling",
                        family.name(),
                        shape.name()
                    );
                }
            }
        }
        // The shipped ceiling is the kernels' full band
        // (16 since the 2026-11-06 flip, on the baseline
        // session's card verdict,
        // bench/baseline-session-2026-11-06.md leg (d)),
        // so at the default the ceiling itself clips
        // nothing and routing is exactly the band
        // table's: measured wins route, measured losses
        // and holes do not.
        assert_eq!(DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS, 16);
        assert!(bands.routes(DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS, MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Attn, 6));
        assert!(!bands.routes(DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS, MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Attn, 2));
        assert!(!bands.routes(DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS, MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Ffn, 3));
        assert!(bands.routes(DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS, MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Kv, 2));
        assert!(!bands.routes(DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS, MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Kv, 12));
        assert!(bands.routes(DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS, MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvShape::Kv, 16));
        assert!(bands.routes(DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS, MmvFamily::Q6K, MmvShape::Kv, 12));
        assert!(!bands.routes(DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS, MmvFamily::Q6K, MmvShape::Attn, 16));
        // A ceiling clips cells from above: at cap 4
        // the Q4_K attention cell (6-12) admits
        // nothing, while Q6_K attention admits its
        // measured wins at rows 2..=4 and no further.
        assert!(!bands.routes(4, MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvShape::Attn, 6));
        assert!(bands.routes(4, MmvFamily::Q6K, MmvShape::Attn, 4));
        assert!(!bands.routes(4, MmvFamily::Q6K, MmvShape::Attn, 5));
        // The session dose positions: at cap 12 the
        // Q5_K KV cell (16 only) is still closed; at
        // cap 16 it opens.
        assert!(!bands.routes(12, MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvShape::Kv, 16));
        assert!(bands.routes(16, MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvShape::Kv, 16));
        // Batch 1 never routes (the kernels' band
        // starts at 2), even under a huge ceiling, and
        // neither does a batch past the kernels' cap.
        assert!(!bands.routes(u32::MAX, MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvShape::Attn, 1));
        assert!(!bands.routes(u32::MAX, MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvShape::Attn, 17));
    }

    #[test]
    fn k22_mmq_switch_resolution() {
        // Unset: off. The shipped ladder is the ladder
        // with K22 nowhere in it.
        assert!(!resolve_k22_mmq(None));
        // The exact value "1" (trimmed) is the only
        // enabling position: the switch is fail-closed by
        // design, so a typo routes the proven kernel, not
        // the prototype.
        assert!(resolve_k22_mmq(Some("1")));
        assert!(resolve_k22_mmq(Some(" 1 ")));
        assert!(!resolve_k22_mmq(Some("0")));
        assert!(!resolve_k22_mmq(Some("true")));
        assert!(!resolve_k22_mmq(Some("")));
        assert!(!resolve_k22_mmq(Some("11")));
    }

    #[test]
    fn flash_staged_switch_resolution() {
        // Unset: ON. The default flipped on the
        // interleaved card evidence in
        // bench/flash-host-cost-2026-11-06.md: cache-
        // controlled arms show the staged form winning
        // the prefill wall at 1,022 tokens (about 6,150
        // ms on against 6,490 ms off) and at every
        // longer shape measured, with the wall delta
        // matching the kernel delta and identical
        // session stats, discharging the decision rule
        // in bench/flash-rework-2026-11-06.md. The flip
        // is recorded in
        // bench/flash-default-flip-2026-11-07.md.
        assert!(resolve_flash_staged(None));
        // The exact value "1" (trimmed) still means on:
        // a value that enabled the staged form before
        // the flip enables it after.
        assert!(resolve_flash_staged(Some("1")));
        assert!(resolve_flash_staged(Some(" 1 ")));
        // The exact value "0" (trimmed) is the explicit
        // off, the one-variable rollback to the shipped
        // flash form.
        assert!(!resolve_flash_staged(Some("0")));
        assert!(!resolve_flash_staged(Some(" 0 ")));
        // Any other value fails closed to off: a typo
        // never silently selects a form, and the refusal
        // is logged by name at construction.
        assert!(!resolve_flash_staged(Some("true")));
        assert!(!resolve_flash_staged(Some("")));
        assert!(!resolve_flash_staged(Some("11")));
        assert!(!resolve_flash_staged(Some("on")));
        assert_eq!(FLASH_STAGED_ENV, "WGPU_COMPUTE_FLASH_STAGED");
    }

    #[test]
    fn flash_staged_value_recognition() {
        // The recognized set is exactly the positions
        // the resolver gives meaning to: unset, "1",
        // "0" (either after trimming). Everything else
        // is the unrecognized set the construction log
        // names when it fails closed.
        assert!(flash_staged_value_recognized(None));
        assert!(flash_staged_value_recognized(Some("1")));
        assert!(flash_staged_value_recognized(Some(" 1 ")));
        assert!(flash_staged_value_recognized(Some("0")));
        assert!(flash_staged_value_recognized(Some(" 0 ")));
        assert!(!flash_staged_value_recognized(Some("true")));
        assert!(!flash_staged_value_recognized(Some("")));
        assert!(!flash_staged_value_recognized(Some("11")));
        assert!(!flash_staged_value_recognized(Some("on")));
    }

    #[test]
    fn k21f_head_switch_resolution() {
        // Unset: ON (the shipped default). The route
        // earned the default back under the guard's
        // written reopen criterion: the wave18 card
        // retest (bench/k21f-retest-2026-11-07.md) ran
        // the mask-fixed kernel on the real file with
        // the switch on and recorded IDENTITY and
        // GOLDEN PASS at depths 1 and 6, with the
        // finish output bit-identical to K3's at the
        // real head geometry. Before that proof the
        // default was off (the guard, bench/k21f-
        // default-guard-2026-11-07.md, after the
        // defaults-confirmation identity failure).
        // (This assertion also pins DEFAULT_K21F_HEAD
        // itself: the unset arm returns the constant.)
        assert!(resolve_k21f_head(None));
        // The exact value "1" (trimmed) is on: the
        // value that meant on under the guard still
        // means on after the flip.
        assert!(resolve_k21f_head(Some("1")));
        assert!(resolve_k21f_head(Some(" 1 ")));
        // The exact value "0" (trimmed) is the
        // explicit off: the one-variable rollback to
        // the K3 fused head.
        assert!(!resolve_k21f_head(Some("0")));
        assert!(!resolve_k21f_head(Some(" 0 ")));
        // Anything else fails closed to the fallback,
        // never to the shipped default: a typo must
        // not silently widen routing (the MMV
        // ceiling's fallback discipline).
        assert!(!resolve_k21f_head(Some("true")));
        assert!(!resolve_k21f_head(Some("")));
        assert!(!resolve_k21f_head(Some("11")));
        // (These arms pin K21F_HEAD_FALLBACK the same
        // way: the unrecognized arm returns it.)
        assert!(!resolve_k21f_head(Some("on")));
        assert_eq!(K21F_HEAD_ENV, "WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD");
    }

    #[test]

    #[test]
    fn mmq_splitk_resolution() {
        // Unset: the shipped default, fixed factor 4.
        // The wave20 card session (bench/wave20-session-
        // 2026-11-07.md, leg 1) discharged the flip
        // criterion in bench/splitk-mmq-2026-11-07.md at
        // this factor: prefill walls -18% at 1,022
        // tokens and -14% at 8,202, the split forms
        // faster than plain on the wide shapes too,
        // identity and golden held, no new spills.
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmq_splitk(None), DEFAULT_MMQ_SPLITK);
        assert_eq!(DEFAULT_MMQ_SPLITK, MmqSplitK::Fixed(4));
        // The explicit off (the one-variable rollback to
        // the pre-flip unsplit ladder).
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmq_splitk(Some("off")), MmqSplitK::Off);
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmq_splitk(Some(" off ")), MmqSplitK::Off);
        // The auto rule (measured marginal in wave20,
        // about -3.5% / -2%: an operator choice, not
        // the default).
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmq_splitk(Some("auto")), MmqSplitK::Auto);
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmq_splitk(Some(" auto ")), MmqSplitK::Auto);
        // Fixed factors across the admitted range keep
        // their meaning. Factor 8 stays admissible as
        // an explicit choice; wave20 disqualified it as
        // a default (+50% / +88% walls), which is a
        // defaults judgment, not a resolver refusal.
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmq_splitk(Some("1")), MmqSplitK::Fixed(1));
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmq_splitk(Some("4")), MmqSplitK::Fixed(4));
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmq_splitk(Some(" 8 ")), MmqSplitK::Fixed(8));
        // Everything else fails closed to the fallback
        // (off), NEVER to the shipped default: zero,
        // past the ceiling, booleans, words, empty. A
        // typo must not silently widen routing to
        // fixed:4 (the MMV flip's deliberate split).
        assert_eq!(MMQ_SPLITK_FALLBACK, MmqSplitK::Off);
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmq_splitk(Some("0")), MMQ_SPLITK_FALLBACK);
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmq_splitk(Some("9")), MMQ_SPLITK_FALLBACK);
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmq_splitk(Some("true")), MMQ_SPLITK_FALLBACK);
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmq_splitk(Some("on")), MMQ_SPLITK_FALLBACK);
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmq_splitk(Some("")), MMQ_SPLITK_FALLBACK);
        assert_eq!(resolve_mmq_splitk(Some("-2")), MMQ_SPLITK_FALLBACK);
        assert_eq!(MMQ_SPLITK_ENV, "WGPU_COMPUTE_MMQ_SPLITK");
    }

    #[test]
    fn mmq_splitk_factor_rule() {
        // Off never splits.
        assert_eq!(mmq_splitk_factor(MmqSplitK::Off, 4, 26), 1);
        assert_eq!(mmq_splitk_factor(MmqSplitK::Off, 512, 26), 1);
        // Fixed: the factor itself, capped at the block
        // count (past it the extra slices are empty) and
        // floored at 1. Fixed(1) is an explicit no-split.
        assert_eq!(mmq_splitk_factor(MmqSplitK::Fixed(4), 4, 26), 4);
        assert_eq!(mmq_splitk_factor(MmqSplitK::Fixed(8), 4, 3), 3);
        assert_eq!(mmq_splitk_factor(MmqSplitK::Fixed(1), 4, 26), 1);
        // Auto: target roughly 64 workgroups. The KV
        // shape (4 tiles, 26 blocks) takes the full 8;
        // a 32-tile projection doubles; anything at or
        // past 64 tiles stays unsplit.
        assert_eq!(mmq_splitk_factor(MmqSplitK::Auto, 4, 26), 8);
        assert_eq!(mmq_splitk_factor(MmqSplitK::Auto, 32, 26), 2);
        assert_eq!(mmq_splitk_factor(MmqSplitK::Auto, 64, 26), 1);
        assert_eq!(mmq_splitk_factor(MmqSplitK::Auto, 312, 26), 1);
        // Auto never exceeds the block count either: a
        // 4-tile projection over a single super-block
        // cannot split.
        assert_eq!(mmq_splitk_factor(MmqSplitK::Auto, 4, 1), 1);
        assert_eq!(mmq_splitk_factor(MmqSplitK::Auto, 8, 2), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn k21_finish_pipeline_is_registered() {
        // Registration proof: a backend that
        // constructs carries the finish-carrying K21
        // pipeline, under the same shipped shape as
        // plain K21 (the finish changes the store, not
        // the tile). Skips where no adapter qualifies
        // (this VM); executes on the card, where the
        // construction-time compile of the band-floor
        // finish variant is itself part of the gate.
        let backend = match WgpuCompute::new() {
            Ok(b) => b,
            Err(crate::error::WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
                eprintln!(
                    "skipping k21 finish registration test: no suitable adapter \
                     (enumerated: [{}])",
                    seen.join("; ")
                );
                return;
            }
            Err(e) => panic!("backend construction failed unexpectedly: {e}"),
        };
        assert_eq!(backend.k21_finish().shape(), backend.k21().shape());
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/src/coopmat_bridge.rs =====
//! The coopmat device bridge: how a device that can run
//! cooperative-matrix shaders is opened inside a backend
//! whose framework cannot create one.
//!
//! wgpu 27 exposes no cooperative matrix support at any
//! layer (no feature bit, no WGSL syntax, no Naga IR
//! type; bench/coopmat-feasibility-2026-11-06.md pins
//! the greps), and its own Vulkan device creation can
//! never enable VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix: the device
//! extension list is computed from the requested wgpu
//! features alone. A passthrough SPIR-V module declaring
//! the coopmat capability against such a device is a
//! spec violation, not a shortcut.
//!
//! The bridge is wgpu-hal's own sanctioned interop, used
//! end to end: the hal adapter's `open_with_callback`
//! creates the device exactly as the stock path does
//! (same extension computation, same feature selection,
//! same queue family), and a [`CreateDeviceCallback`]
//! adds the one extension wgpu cannot name plus its
//! feature struct to the create chain; the resulting
//! hal device is then wrapped by the safe
//! `Adapter::create_device_from_hal`, requesting
//! EXPERIMENTAL_PASSTHROUGH_SHADERS so coopmat SPIR-V
//! can enter through `create_shader_module_passthrough`.
//! The callback's own contract is the design's: "You
//! must not remove anything from this list, but you may
//! add to it."
//!
//! Gating: the bridge is entered when the
//! environment names it ([`COOPMAT_BRIDGE_ENV`], exact
//! value `1`), or when the variable is unset and the
//! coopmat routing default implies it (the default
//! flipped on in bench/coopmat-default-flip-2026-11-07.md;
//! a present bridge value decides on its own, so an
//! explicit `0` still names a deliberate stock-device
//! run). With neither in force, `GpuContext::open`
//! runs the shipped `request_device` path untouched.
//! The bridge is fail-closed in the other direction
//! too: every probe below (extension exposed, feature
//! bit true, the s8 x s8 to s32 16x16x16 subgroup
//! property row present) must pass before any device
//! is created, and any refusal is returned as a named
//! string; the caller logs it on the diag channel and
//! opens the stock device instead, so a machine
//! without coopmat serves exactly as it did before
//! this module existed, with the refusal on record. The coopmat kernel
//! module reads [`GpuContext::coopmat`] and exists only
//! when this bridge actually delivered a device: a
//! routing request against a stock device refuses by
//! name there, never silently.
//!
//! The required property row is the one the llama
//! parity spec pins for `mul_mmq_cm1` on this card
//! family (bench/llama-parity-specs-2026-11-06.md):
//! subgroup scope, 16x16x16, signed 8-bit A and B,
//! signed 32-bit accumulate, the shape ggml's
//! `coopmat_int_support` requires. The step-0 probe on
//! the RX 7900 XTX found that row among its 14 rows;
//! see bench/coopmat-build-2026-11-06.md.
//!
//! [`CreateDeviceCallback`]: wgpu_hal::vulkan::CreateDeviceCallback
//! [`GpuContext::coopmat`]: crate::device::GpuContext::coopmat

use crate::diag::dbg_log;

/// Environment variable naming the coopmat device
/// bridge switch: the exact value `1` opens the GPU
/// device through the bridge in this module (ash
/// device creation with VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix
/// enabled, handed to wgpu through its hal interop).
/// Operational config, not a compiled constant. The
/// explicit switch is fail-closed: the exact value `1`
/// opens the bridge and any other present value keeps
/// the shipped `request_device` path, so a deliberate
/// stock-device run stays nameable. An UNSET variable
/// no longer decides alone: it defers to the coopmat
/// routing default ([`coopmat_bridge_requested`]),
/// which the wave20 card verdict flipped on
/// (bench/coopmat-default-flip-2026-11-07.md). The
/// server proof that moved the routing default is
/// bench/wave20-session-2026-11-07.md, leg 2; the
/// bridge's own build record is
/// bench/coopmat-build-2026-11-06.md.
pub const COOPMAT_BRIDGE_ENV: &str = "WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT_BRIDGE";

/// Resolve the bridge switch from the raw environment
/// value: only the exact value `1` (after trimming)
/// enables it; everything else is off.
pub fn resolve_coopmat_bridge(raw: Option<&str>) -> bool {
    matches!(raw.map(str::trim), Some("1"))
}

/// Whether this process asked for the bridged device:
/// the bridge is explicitly named by
/// [`COOPMAT_BRIDGE_ENV`], or the coopmat routing
/// default implies it (see
/// [`crate::compute::DEFAULT_COOPMAT`]). The explicit
/// position keeps its exact meaning: a present value
/// decides the bridge on its own (`1` opens it,
/// anything else refuses it, logged by name however
/// the decision lands), so
/// `WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT_BRIDGE=0` stays a deliberate
/// stock-device run even with the routing default on.
/// With the variable unset, the implied position
/// follows the one routing question the bridge exists
/// to serve: with the coopmat rung's default ON the
/// device opens through the bridge so the rung can
/// engage, and the bridge's own probes still decide
/// whether a coopmat device exists at all; with the
/// routing default OFF (`WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT=0`)
/// nothing asks for a bridged device and the stock
/// open serves, byte-for-byte as before the flip.
/// The flip that made the routing default is
/// recorded in bench/coopmat-default-flip-2026-11-07.md.
pub fn coopmat_bridge_requested() -> bool {
    match std::env::var(COOPMAT_BRIDGE_ENV).ok() {
        Some(raw) => {
            let requested = resolve_coopmat_bridge(Some(raw.as_str()));
            dbg_log!(
                "coopmat bridge env {COOPMAT_BRIDGE_ENV}={raw:?} present: the explicit \
                 value decides, bridge requested={requested}"
            );
            requested
        }
        None => crate::compute::resolve_coopmat(None),
    }
}

/// What the bridge probe confirmed about the device it
/// opened. Recorded on [`GpuContext`](crate::device::GpuContext)
/// at construction; the coopmat kernel module gates its
/// own existence on this being present.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct CoopmatInfo {
    /// Cooperative matrix property rows the driver
    /// reported for the physical device (14 on the
    /// server's RADV gfx1100 at the step-0 probe).
    pub property_rows: u32,
    /// The physical device's subgroup size, read from
    /// VkPhysicalDeviceSubgroupProperties in the same
    /// probe (64 on the server's RADV). The coopmat
    /// shader's workgroup geometry is compiled for a
    /// fixed subgroup size, so the kernel constructor
    /// checks this value and refuses by name on a
    /// mismatch.
    pub subgroup_size: u32,
}

/// Open a device on `adapter` through the bridge,
/// requesting the features in `desc` (which the caller
/// has already extended with
/// EXPERIMENTAL_PASSTHROUGH_SHADERS). On success the
/// returned context info certifies that the probes
/// passed and the device really carries the extension.
///
/// # Safety contract
///
/// This function is the crate's one `#[allow(unsafe_code)]`
/// site, and every unsafe call in it is one of the
/// following, each with its contract:
///
/// - `Adapter::as_hal` and the hal adapter's accessors:
///   the adapter came from this process's own Vulkan
///   instance enumeration (detect enumerates VULKAN
///   only), so the Vulkan hal adapter exists; the
///   returned guard borrows the adapter and is held
///   until the hal device is wrapped.
/// - The ash probes (`enumerate_device_extension_
///   properties`, `get_physical_device_features2`, the
///   KHR property query): read-only queries against the
///   hal adapter's own physical device handle, through
///   the hal instance's own ash function tables
///   (`shared_instance().raw_instance()`). The one
///   object built from this crate's own ash `Entry` is
///   the KHR extension's function table; an ash `Entry`
///   is only a loader handle for `vkGetInstanceProcAddr`
///   against the same libvulkan, never a second
///   instance.
/// - The create callback's chain edit: the callback
///   adds VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix to the extension
///   list (add-only, as the callback contract requires)
///   and chains a `VkPhysicalDeviceCooperativeMatrix
///   FeaturesKHR` with cooperativeMatrix = true into
///   the create info. The feature struct is a local of
///   this function; the callback runs synchronously
///   inside `open_with_callback`, and the device is
///   created inside that same call, so the struct
///   outlives every use of the chain. The extensions
///   and features wgpu-hal computed are not modified
///   in any other way, so the device the bridge returns
///   differs from the stock device by exactly the
///   coopmat extension and feature.
/// - `Adapter::create_device_from_hal`: the hal device
///   came from this same hal adapter's
///   `open_with_callback`, and `desc` requests exactly
///   the feature set the hal device was opened with,
///   so the subset clause of its contract holds.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// A named refusal string for every probe failure,
/// extension absence, or hal failure; the caller logs
/// it and falls back to the stock device.
#[allow(unsafe_code)]
pub(crate) fn open_bridged(
    adapter: &wgpu::Adapter,
    desc: &wgpu::DeviceDescriptor<'_>,
) -> Result<(wgpu::Device, wgpu::Queue, CoopmatInfo), String> {
    use ash::vk;
    use std::ffi::CStr;

    // SAFETY: per the module contract above; each call
    // is annotated at its site.
    unsafe {
        let Some(hal_guard) = adapter.as_hal::<wgpu_hal::vulkan::Api>() else {
            return Err("the selected adapter has no Vulkan hal adapter".to_string());
        };
        let hal = &*hal_guard;
        let ash_instance = hal.shared_instance().raw_instance();
        let physical = hal.raw_physical_device();

        // Probe 1: the extension must be exposed.
        let extensions = ash_instance
            .enumerate_device_extension_properties(physical)
            .map_err(|e| format!("device extension enumeration failed: {e:?}"))?;
        let cm_ext_name = ash::khr::cooperative_matrix::NAME;
        let exposed = extensions.iter().any(|e| {
            // Extension names are NUL-terminated per the
            // Vulkan spec; the array is 256 bytes.
            CStr::from_ptr(e.extension_name.as_ptr()) == cm_ext_name
        });
        if !exposed {
            return Err(
                "VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix is not exposed by this physical device".to_string(),
            );
        }

        // Probe 2: the feature bit, and the subgroup
        // size. The subgroup properties chain into the
        // properties query, not the features query; the
        // two structs live in different pNext families.
        let mut cm_features = vk::PhysicalDeviceCooperativeMatrixFeaturesKHR::default();
        let mut features2 = vk::PhysicalDeviceFeatures2::default().push_next(&mut cm_features);
        ash_instance.get_physical_device_features2(physical, &mut features2);
        let mut subgroup_props = vk::PhysicalDeviceSubgroupProperties::default();
        let mut props2 = vk::PhysicalDeviceProperties2::default().push_next(&mut subgroup_props);
        ash_instance.get_physical_device_properties2(physical, &mut props2);
        if cm_features.cooperative_matrix == 0 {
            return Err(
                "VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix is exposed but its cooperativeMatrix \
                 feature is false on this physical device"
                    .to_string(),
            );
        }
        let subgroup_size = subgroup_props.subgroup_size;

        // Probe 3: the property rows must carry the one
        // shape the kernel is built for: s8 inputs, s32
        // accumulate, 16x16x16, subgroup scope.
        let entry = ash::Entry::load()
            .map_err(|e| format!("loading the Vulkan loader for the probe failed: {e}"))?;
        let cm_fn = ash::khr::cooperative_matrix::Instance::new(&entry, ash_instance);
        let rows = cm_fn
            .get_physical_device_cooperative_matrix_properties(physical)
            .map_err(|e| format!("cooperative matrix property query failed: {e:?}"))?;
        let required_row = rows.iter().any(|r| {
            r.m_size == 16
                && r.n_size == 16
                && r.k_size == 16
                && r.a_type == vk::ComponentTypeKHR::SINT8
                && r.b_type == vk::ComponentTypeKHR::SINT8
                && r.c_type == vk::ComponentTypeKHR::SINT32
                && r.result_type == vk::ComponentTypeKHR::SINT32
                && r.scope == vk::ScopeKHR::SUBGROUP
        });
        if !required_row {
            return Err(format!(
                "no s8 x s8 to s32 16x16x16 subgroup cooperative matrix row \
                 among the {} rows this device reports",
                rows.len()
            ));
        }
        dbg_log!(
            "coopmat bridge probe: extension exposed, feature on, {} property rows, \
             s8 x s8 to s32 16x16x16 subgroup row present, subgroup size {subgroup_size}",
            rows.len()
        );

        // Device creation: wgpu-hal's own open, with the
        // callback adding exactly the coopmat extension
        // and its feature struct. `cm_enable` outlives
        // the call: the callback runs and the device is
        // created synchronously inside open_with_callback.
        let mut cm_enable =
            vk::PhysicalDeviceCooperativeMatrixFeaturesKHR::default().cooperative_matrix(true);
        let cm_enable_ref = &mut cm_enable;
        let callback: Box<wgpu_hal::vulkan::CreateDeviceCallback> = Box::new(
            move |args: wgpu_hal::vulkan::CreateDeviceCallbackArgs<'_, '_, '_>| {
                args.extensions.push(ash::khr::cooperative_matrix::NAME);
                let info = std::mem::take(args.create_info);
                *args.create_info = info.push_next(&mut *cm_enable_ref);
            },
        );
        let open_device = hal
            .open_with_callback(desc.required_features, &desc.memory_hints, Some(callback))
            .map_err(|e| format!("hal device open through the bridge failed: {e:?}"))?;
        let (device, queue) = adapter
            .create_device_from_hal::<wgpu_hal::vulkan::Api>(open_device, desc)
            .map_err(|e| format!("wrapping the bridged hal device failed: {e}"))?;
        Ok((
            device,
            queue,
            CoopmatInfo {
                property_rows: rows.len() as u32,
                subgroup_size,
            },
        ))
    }
}

/// Create a shader module from precompiled SPIR-V words
/// through wgpu's passthrough path, on a device this
/// bridge opened. This is the second and last unsafe
/// site in the crate, and it lives here so the unsafe
/// surface stays in one module.
///
/// # Safety contract
///
/// `create_shader_module_passthrough` is unsafe because
/// wgpu validates nothing: the words are fed to the
/// driver as-is. The contract this caller upholds:
///
/// - The words come from a checked-in artifact compiled
///   from the in-repo GLSL source by the recorded
///   rebuild script and validated with spirv-val at
///   build time (kernels/coopmat/rebuild.sh); they are
///   never assembled, patched, or generated at runtime.
/// - The device came from [`open_bridged`]: its probes
///   confirmed VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix is enabled, so
///   the cooperative matrix capability the module
///   declares is legal on it. Calling this on a stock
///   device would be a spec violation; the kernel
///   module gates its construction on
///   [`GpuContext::coopmat`](crate::device::GpuContext::coopmat)
///   being present, which only a bridged device sets.
#[allow(unsafe_code)]
pub(crate) fn passthrough_shader_module(
    device: &wgpu::Device,
    label: &str,
    spirv_words: &[u32],
) -> wgpu::ShaderModule {
    let desc = wgpu::ShaderModuleDescriptorPassthrough {
        label: Some(label),
        spirv: Some(std::borrow::Cow::Borrowed(spirv_words)),
        ..Default::default()
    };
    // SAFETY: per the contract above.
    unsafe { device.create_shader_module_passthrough(desc) }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn bridge_switch_is_fail_closed() {
        assert!(resolve_coopmat_bridge(Some("1")));
        assert!(resolve_coopmat_bridge(Some(" 1 ")));
        assert!(!resolve_coopmat_bridge(None));
        assert!(!resolve_coopmat_bridge(Some("0")));
        assert!(!resolve_coopmat_bridge(Some("")));
        assert!(!resolve_coopmat_bridge(Some("true")));
        assert!(!resolve_coopmat_bridge(Some("11")));
    }
}

//! Adapter selection: the policy from BACKEND.md Section 2 and the
//! `detect()` that applies it.
//!
//! Selection is a policy, not a driver default. This host class
//! exposes three Vulkan adapters at once (the discrete 7900 XTX, an
//! Intel iGPU, and llvmpipe), and `PowerPreference::HighPerformance`
//! picking the right one is driver behavior, not a contract. So the
//! ranking is written down here, as a pure function over adapter
//! facts that the unit tests can pin:
//!
//! - Only Vulkan adapters are candidates (DECISIONS 2026-10-26:
//!   Vulkan is the GPU path; ROCm and HIP are parked).
//! - A discrete GPU always qualifies and always wins.
//! - An integrated or "other" adapter qualifies only when the
//!   policy explicitly allows non-discrete GPUs (BACKEND.md
//!   Section 6, level L1: entered by configuration, never by
//!   preference drift).
//! - A CPU-type adapter (llvmpipe) never qualifies, under any
//!   policy: BACKEND.md Section 6 counts a software adapter as no
//!   adapter, because it would report success while running slower
//!   than this workspace's own CPU backend.
//!
//! When nothing qualifies, detection fails with
//! [`WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter`] listing every adapter seen. The
//! CPU backend is the caller's fallback (level L4), chosen by the
//! caller, not smuggled in here.

use crate::device::GpuContext;
use crate::error::{Result, WgpuError};

use crate::diag::dbg_log;

/// The facts about one adapter that the ranking reads. Kept as a
/// plain struct (not a live `wgpu::Adapter`) so the policy is
/// testable without hardware.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct AdapterFacts {
    /// Adapter name as the driver reports it.
    pub name: String,
    /// wgpu backend the adapter came from.
    pub backend: wgpu::Backend,
    /// wgpu device type classification.
    pub device_type: wgpu::DeviceType,
    /// Driver name string as the adapter reports it
    /// (`AdapterInfo.driver`); carried so a diag capture
    /// manifest can state the exact stack a run executed on.
    pub driver: String,
    /// Driver info string as the adapter reports it
    /// (`AdapterInfo.driver_info`), the version-bearing half
    /// of the driver identity.
    pub driver_info: String,
}

impl AdapterFacts {
    /// The facts of a live adapter.
    fn of(adapter: &wgpu::Adapter) -> Self {
        let info = adapter.get_info();
        AdapterFacts {
            name: info.name,
            backend: info.backend,
            device_type: info.device_type,
            driver: info.driver,
            driver_info: info.driver_info,
        }
    }

    /// One-line description for refusals and the diag channel.
    fn describe(&self) -> String {
        format!(
            "{} (backend {:?}, type {:?})",
            self.name, self.backend, self.device_type
        )
    }
}

/// Adapter selection policy. The default is the production stance:
/// discrete Vulkan or nothing.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct DetectPolicy {
    /// Allow integrated and other non-discrete Vulkan adapters when
    /// no discrete GPU qualifies (BACKEND.md Section 6, level L1).
    pub allow_non_discrete: bool,
}

/// Rank class of one adapter under `policy`; lower wins, `None`
/// disqualifies the adapter outright.
fn rank_class(facts: &AdapterFacts, policy: &DetectPolicy) -> Option<u8> {
    if facts.backend != wgpu::Backend::Vulkan {
        return None;
    }
    match facts.device_type {
        wgpu::DeviceType::DiscreteGpu => Some(0),
        wgpu::DeviceType::IntegratedGpu | wgpu::DeviceType::Other => {
            if policy.allow_non_discrete {
                Some(1)
            } else {
                None
            }
        }
        // A software rasterizer counts as no adapter (BACKEND.md
        // Section 6), and a virtual GPU is a host decision this
        // policy does not make silently either.
        wgpu::DeviceType::Cpu | wgpu::DeviceType::VirtualGpu => None,
    }
}

/// The index of the adapter the policy selects, or `None` when no
/// adapter qualifies. Pure: the unit tests pin the ranking here.
#[must_use]
pub fn rank_adapters(facts: &[AdapterFacts], policy: &DetectPolicy) -> Option<usize> {
    let mut best: Option<(u8, usize)> = None;
    for (index, adapter) in facts.iter().enumerate() {
        if let Some(class) = rank_class(adapter, policy) {
            if best.is_none_or(|(best_class, _)| class < best_class) {
                best = Some((class, index));
            }
        }
    }
    best.map(|(_, index)| index)
}

/// Enumerate this machine's Vulkan adapters, apply the policy, and
/// open a device on the winner with the adapter's own limits (not
/// wgpu's defaults: a default-limits device caps buffers far below
/// what RADV grants, BACKEND.md Section 2).
///
/// # Errors
///
/// [`WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter`] when the policy qualifies
/// nothing; [`WgpuError::DeviceRequest`] when the winning adapter
/// cannot create a device; [`WgpuError::LimitShortfall`] when the
/// granted limits fall below this crate's kernel floor.
pub fn detect(policy: &DetectPolicy) -> Result<GpuContext> {
    let instance = wgpu::Instance::new(&wgpu::InstanceDescriptor {
        backends: wgpu::Backends::VULKAN,
        ..Default::default()
    });
    let adapters = instance.enumerate_adapters(wgpu::Backends::VULKAN);
    let facts: Vec<AdapterFacts> = adapters.iter().map(AdapterFacts::of).collect();
    for adapter in &facts {
        dbg_log!("adapter seen: {}", adapter.describe());
    }
    let Some(index) = rank_adapters(&facts, policy) else {
        return Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter {
            seen: facts.iter().map(AdapterFacts::describe).collect(),
            allow_non_discrete: policy.allow_non_discrete,
        });
    };
    let chosen = &facts[index];
    dbg_log!("adapter selected: {}", chosen.describe());
    GpuContext::open(&adapters[index], chosen.clone())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn facts(name: &str, backend: wgpu::Backend, device_type: wgpu::DeviceType) -> AdapterFacts {
        AdapterFacts {
            name: name.to_string(),
            backend,
            device_type,
            driver: String::new(),
            driver_info: String::new(),
        }
    }

    fn server_trio() -> Vec<AdapterFacts> {
        // The three adapters the BACKEND.md probe measured on the
        // real host, in probe order.
        vec![
            facts(
                "AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (RADV NAVI31)",
                wgpu::Backend::Vulkan,
                wgpu::DeviceType::DiscreteGpu,
            ),
            facts(
                "Intel(R) UHD Graphics 770 (ADL-S GT1)",
                wgpu::Backend::Vulkan,
                wgpu::DeviceType::IntegratedGpu,
            ),
            facts(
                "llvmpipe (LLVM 21.1.8, 256 bits)",
                wgpu::Backend::Vulkan,
                wgpu::DeviceType::Cpu,
            ),
        ]
    }

    #[test]
    fn discrete_vulkan_wins_on_the_server_trio() {
        let policy = DetectPolicy::default();
        assert_eq!(rank_adapters(&server_trio(), &policy), Some(0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn llvmpipe_alone_is_no_adapter() {
        let trio = server_trio();
        let only_pipe = &trio[2..];
        assert_eq!(rank_adapters(only_pipe, &DetectPolicy::default()), None);
        // Even the permissive policy never selects a CPU adapter.
        let permissive = DetectPolicy {
            allow_non_discrete: true,
        };
        assert_eq!(rank_adapters(only_pipe, &permissive), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn integrated_needs_the_explicit_policy() {
        let trio = server_trio();
        let no_discrete = &trio[1..];
        assert_eq!(rank_adapters(no_discrete, &DetectPolicy::default()), None);
        let permissive = DetectPolicy {
            allow_non_discrete: true,
        };
        assert_eq!(rank_adapters(no_discrete, &permissive), Some(0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn non_vulkan_discrete_is_not_a_candidate() {
        let metal_card = vec![facts(
            "Some GPU",
            wgpu::Backend::Metal,
            wgpu::DeviceType::DiscreteGpu,
        )];
        assert_eq!(rank_adapters(&metal_card, &DetectPolicy::default()), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn first_discrete_wins_ties() {
        let two = vec![
            facts(
                "Card A",
                wgpu::Backend::Vulkan,
                wgpu::DeviceType::DiscreteGpu,
            ),
            facts(
                "Card B",
                wgpu::Backend::Vulkan,
                wgpu::DeviceType::DiscreteGpu,
            ),
        ];
        assert_eq!(rank_adapters(&two, &DetectPolicy::default()), Some(0));
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/src/device.rs =====
//! An opened GPU device: the selected adapter's identity, the
//! `wgpu` device and queue, and the granted limits the kernels are
//! checked against.
//!
//! The device is created with the ADAPTER's limits, not wgpu's
//! defaults (BACKEND.md Section 2: a default-limits device caps
//! buffers far below what RADV grants). The granted limits are then
//! verified against this crate's floor before any kernel runs: the
//! largest K1 tensor (an FFN gate at 74.8 MB) must bind whole, and
//! the dispatch scheme needs real workgroup range. A shortfall is a
//! named error here, BACKEND.md Section 6's fallback event, never a
//! surprise mid-load.

use crate::detect::AdapterFacts;
use crate::error::{Result, WgpuError};
use crate::timestamps::{DiagMode, DiagRecorder, DiagStamp, DispatchMeta};

use crate::diag::dbg_log;

use std::sync::Arc;

/// Floor for `max_storage_buffer_binding_size`: the largest tensor
/// any kernel binds whole is K3's output head at 924,571,648 bytes
/// (about 0.86 GiB); the floor rounds that up to 1 GiB so a device
/// that cannot bind the head whole refuses up front, at device
/// opening, instead of mid-load. (The K1-only floor was 128 MiB,
/// sized to an FFN gate at 74,760,192 bytes; K3 landing is what
/// raised it, as this constant's earlier note anticipated. The
/// RADV adapter grants 2 GiB.)
pub const MIN_BINDING_BYTES: u64 = 1024 * 1024 * 1024;

/// Floor for `max_compute_workgroups_per_dimension`: the K1 grid
/// scheme addresses rows through two dimensions and needs only a
/// modest first dimension, but a token floor of 1 workgroup would
/// make the scheme meaningless; 4,096 is far below every real
/// adapter (RADV grants 65,535) and far above a broken one.
pub const MIN_WORKGROUPS_PER_DIMENSION: u32 = 4_096;

/// One opened GPU: adapter identity plus device and queue.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct GpuContext {
    /// The adapter the policy selected, as facts.
    pub adapter: AdapterFacts,
    /// The opened device, created with the adapter's limits.
    pub device: wgpu::Device,
    /// The device's submission queue.
    pub queue: wgpu::Queue,
    /// Granted `max_buffer_size`, recorded for upload checks and
    /// the residency accounting in the bench reports.
    pub max_buffer_size: u64,
    /// Granted `max_storage_buffer_binding_size`.
    pub max_binding_size: u64,
    /// Features the device was actually granted (the subset of
    /// the adapter's features this crate asked for: SUBGROUP and
    /// SHADER_F16, the two the tuned K1 shapes select on).
    /// Kernels read this, through `device.features()`, at
    /// pipeline construction; a shape whose feature is absent
    /// refuses by name there.
    pub features: wgpu::Features,
    /// Per-dispatch GPU timestamp recorder, present only when
    /// the diag mode requests timestamps (`timing`, or
    /// `capture` which implies timing; env
    /// `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG`) and the device granted the
    /// timestamp features. `None` in the default world: no
    /// query set, no resolve buffers, and every prepared call
    /// carries no stamp, so the encode path is byte-identical
    /// to the uninstrumented one.
    pub diag: Option<Arc<DiagRecorder>>,
    /// Coopmat capability of this device, present only
    /// when the device was opened through the coopmat
    /// bridge ([`crate::coopmat_bridge`]) and its probes
    /// confirmed VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix with the
    /// s8 x s8 to s32 16x16x16 subgroup row. `None` on every
    /// stock device: the coopmat kernel module gates its
    /// own existence on this field, and a routing request
    /// against a stock device refuses by name there.
    pub coopmat: Option<crate::coopmat_bridge::CoopmatInfo>,
}

impl GpuContext {
    /// Open a device on `adapter` with the adapter's own limits and
    /// verify the granted limits against this crate's floor.
    pub(crate) fn open(adapter: &wgpu::Adapter, facts: AdapterFacts) -> Result<Self> {
        // Ask for the features the tuned kernels select on, when
        // the adapter offers them (BACKEND.md Section 2 measured
        // both present on the server stack). Asking only for what
        // the adapter has keeps device creation infallible on
        // lesser stacks; the kernels then fall back by name at
        // pipeline construction (see shipped_shape).
        let diag_mode = DiagMode::from_env();
        let mut wanted = wgpu::Features::SUBGROUP | wgpu::Features::SHADER_F16;
        if diag_mode.requests_timestamps() {
            // Diagnosis runs (timing, and capture which implies
            // it) ask for the timestamp features too; verdict
            // runs (mode off) request exactly what they always
            // have, so their device is unchanged.
            wanted |=
                wgpu::Features::TIMESTAMP_QUERY | wgpu::Features::TIMESTAMP_QUERY_INSIDE_PASSES;
        }
        let required_features = adapter.features() & wanted;
        let make_desc = |required_features: wgpu::Features| wgpu::DeviceDescriptor {
            label: Some("wgpu-compute device"),
            required_features,
            required_limits: adapter.limits(),
            ..Default::default()
        };
        // The coopmat bridge is entered when its
        // switch names it, or when the switch is unset
        // and the coopmat routing default implies it
        // (coopmat_bridge::coopmat_bridge_requested;
        // the routing default flipped on in
        // bench/coopmat-default-flip-2026-11-07.md):
        // the bridged open asks for the same features
        // plus passthrough shaders, on a device
        // carrying VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix. Any
        // bridge refusal is named on the diag channel
        // and the stock device serves instead, so a
        // machine without coopmat behaves exactly as
        // it did before the bridge existed. With the
        // switch explicitly off and the routing switch
        // closed, the request below is the shipped
        // one, unchanged.
        let mut coopmat = None;
        let (device, queue) = if crate::coopmat_bridge::coopmat_bridge_requested() {
            let bridged_features = required_features
                | (adapter.features() & wgpu::Features::EXPERIMENTAL_PASSTHROUGH_SHADERS);
            match crate::coopmat_bridge::open_bridged(adapter, &make_desc(bridged_features)) {
                Ok((device, queue, info)) => {
                    coopmat = Some(info);
                    (device, queue)
                }
                Err(refusal) => {
                    dbg_log!("coopmat bridge refused: {refusal}; the stock device serves");
                    pollster::block_on(adapter.request_device(&make_desc(required_features)))
                        .map_err(|e| WgpuError::DeviceRequest {
                            detail: e.to_string(),
                        })?
                }
            }
        } else {
            pollster::block_on(adapter.request_device(&make_desc(required_features))).map_err(
                |e| WgpuError::DeviceRequest {
                    detail: e.to_string(),
                },
            )?
        };
        let features = device.features();
        dbg_log!(
            "device features granted: subgroup={} shader_f16={}",
            features.contains(wgpu::Features::SUBGROUP),
            features.contains(wgpu::Features::SHADER_F16)
        );
        if let Some(info) = coopmat {
            dbg_log!(
                "coopmat bridge device open: {} cooperative matrix property rows, \
                 subgroup size {}",
                info.property_rows,
                info.subgroup_size
            );
        }
        let limits = device.limits();
        // wgpu reports the binding cap as u32; this crate's
        // accounting is u64 throughout, so widen once, here.
        let binding_size = u64::from(limits.max_storage_buffer_binding_size);
        dbg_log!(
            "device opened on {}: max_buffer_size={} max_binding={} max_workgroups_per_dim={}",
            facts.name,
            limits.max_buffer_size,
            binding_size,
            limits.max_compute_workgroups_per_dimension
        );
        if binding_size < MIN_BINDING_BYTES {
            return Err(WgpuError::LimitShortfall {
                what: "max_storage_buffer_binding_size",
                required: MIN_BINDING_BYTES,
                granted: binding_size,
            });
        }
        if limits.max_compute_workgroups_per_dimension < MIN_WORKGROUPS_PER_DIMENSION {
            return Err(WgpuError::LimitShortfall {
                what: "max_compute_workgroups_per_dimension",
                required: u64::from(MIN_WORKGROUPS_PER_DIMENSION),
                granted: u64::from(limits.max_compute_workgroups_per_dimension),
            });
        }
        if limits.max_buffer_size < binding_size {
            return Err(WgpuError::LimitShortfall {
                what: "max_buffer_size (below the granted binding size)",
                required: binding_size,
                granted: limits.max_buffer_size,
            });
        }
        // The diag recorder exists only when timestamps were
        // requested (timing mode, or capture which implies it)
        // on a device that granted both timestamp features. The
        // conversion period is the queue's own, read here at
        // runtime; no value is assumed. A timing request the
        // device cannot serve is named in the diag log and the
        // context simply carries no recorder.
        let diag = if diag_mode.wants_recorder(features) {
            let period = queue.get_timestamp_period();
            dbg_log!("diag timing on: timestamp period {period} ns");
            Some(Arc::new(DiagRecorder::new(&device, period)))
        } else {
            if diag_mode.requests_timestamps() {
                dbg_log!(
                    "diag {} requested but the device did not grant \
                     TIMESTAMP_QUERY + TIMESTAMP_QUERY_INSIDE_PASSES; \
                     instrumentation off",
                    diag_mode.name()
                );
            }
            None
        };
        Ok(GpuContext {
            adapter: facts,
            max_buffer_size: limits.max_buffer_size,
            max_binding_size: binding_size,
            features,
            device,
            queue,
            diag,
            coopmat,
        })
    }

    /// The diag timestamp recorder, when this context carries
    /// one (timing mode on a capable device).
    #[must_use]
    pub fn diag_recorder(&self) -> Option<&Arc<DiagRecorder>> {
        self.diag.as_ref()
    }

    /// A timestamp stamp for one dispatch, when this context
    /// carries a recorder; kernel `prepare` methods call this
    /// so a prepared call stamps itself in `encode_into`.
    /// `None` (no recorder) leaves the call uninstrumented.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn diag_stamp(&self, meta: DispatchMeta) -> Option<DiagStamp> {
        self.diag
            .as_ref()
            .map(|rec| DiagStamp::new(Arc::clone(rec), meta))
    }

    /// Create a storage buffer of `size` bytes with copy access in
    /// both directions: the scratch shape every one-shot kernel in
    /// this crate allocates for its inputs and outputs. (The
    /// resident weight buffers of BACKEND.md Section 5 are created
    /// by the kernels that own them; this helper is for the
    /// per-call activations the `Compute` trait hands over as host
    /// slices.)
    pub fn scratch_buffer(&self, label: &str, size: u64) -> wgpu::Buffer {
        self.device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
            label: Some(label),
            size: size.max(4),
            usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::STORAGE
                | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST
                | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_SRC,
            mapped_at_creation: false,
        })
    }

    /// Upload raw bytes into a fresh storage buffer (see
    /// [`GpuContext::scratch_buffer`]).
    pub fn upload_bytes(&self, label: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> wgpu::Buffer {
        let buffer = self.scratch_buffer(label, bytes.len() as u64);
        self.queue.write_buffer(&buffer, 0, bytes);
        buffer
    }

    /// Upload f32 values into a fresh storage buffer.
    pub fn upload_f32(&self, label: &str, data: &[f32]) -> wgpu::Buffer {
        let bytes: Vec<u8> = data.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect();
        self.upload_bytes(label, &bytes)
    }

    /// Upload u32 values into a fresh storage buffer.
    pub fn upload_u32(&self, label: &str, data: &[u32]) -> wgpu::Buffer {
        let bytes: Vec<u8> = data.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect();
        self.upload_bytes(label, &bytes)
    }

    /// Create a uniform buffer from raw parameter bytes (the
    /// kernels' `Params` structs, laid out by hand in each kernel
    /// module).
    pub fn uniform_buffer(&self, label: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> wgpu::Buffer {
        let buffer = self.device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
            label: Some(label),
            size: (bytes.len() as u64).max(4),
            usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::UNIFORM | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
            mapped_at_creation: false,
        });
        self.queue.write_buffer(&buffer, 0, bytes);
        buffer
    }

    /// Read `count` f32 values back from a storage buffer: copy to
    /// a staging buffer, map, collect. This is the readback half of
    /// the trait's host-slice currency, shared by every one-shot
    /// kernel (K1's `run` keeps its own copy because the bench
    /// holds its buffers resident across iterations).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::Readback`] when the map fails or never fires.
    pub fn read_f32(&self, buffer: &wgpu::Buffer, count: usize) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        self.read_f32_at(buffer, 0, count)
    }

    /// Read `count` f32 values back from a storage buffer,
    /// starting at element `first_float`: the ranged form of
    /// [`GpuContext::read_f32`], for callers whose data does
    /// not start at the buffer's head (the resident session's
    /// KV capture reads a windowed layer's visible rows out of
    /// the middle of its ring buffer). Same staging, copy, and
    /// map path; a zero `count` reads nothing and submits
    /// nothing.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::Readback`] when the map fails or never fires.
    pub fn read_f32_at(
        &self,
        buffer: &wgpu::Buffer,
        first_float: usize,
        count: usize,
    ) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        if count == 0 {
            return Ok(Vec::new());
        }
        let bytes = (count * 4) as u64;
        let staging = self.device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
            label: Some("readback staging"),
            size: bytes.max(4),
            usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST | wgpu::BufferUsages::MAP_READ,
            mapped_at_creation: false,
        });
        let mut encoder = self
            .device
            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                label: Some("readback copy"),
            });
        encoder.copy_buffer_to_buffer(buffer, (first_float * 4) as u64, &staging, 0, bytes);
        self.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
        self.map_staging(&staging, count)
    }

    /// Map a staging buffer filled by a copy the CALLER encoded
    /// and submitted (the device-resident session copies its
    /// logits into its own staging buffer inside the forward's
    /// single submission, then maps through here), collecting
    /// `count` f32 values. The caller owns the staging buffer's
    /// size and usage (`COPY_DST | MAP_READ`).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::Readback`] when the map fails or never fires.
    pub fn map_staging(&self, staging: &wgpu::Buffer, count: usize) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        let slice = staging.slice(..);
        let (tx, rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
        slice.map_async(wgpu::MapMode::Read, move |result| {
            let _ = tx.send(result);
        });
        self.device
            .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
            .map_err(|e| WgpuError::Readback {
                detail: e.to_string(),
            })?;
        rx.recv()
            .map_err(|_| WgpuError::Readback {
                detail: "map callback never fired".to_string(),
            })?
            .map_err(|e| WgpuError::Readback {
                detail: e.to_string(),
            })?;
        let mapped = slice.get_mapped_range();
        let out: Vec<f32> = mapped
            .chunks_exact(4)
            .take(count)
            .map(|c| f32::from_le_bytes([c[0], c[1], c[2], c[3]]))
            .collect();
        drop(mapped);
        staging.unmap();
        Ok(out)
    }

    /// Verify a whole-tensor upload of `bytes` fits this device,
    /// naming the tensor and both numbers when it does not. This is
    /// the residency check the per-tensor buffer strategy
    /// (BACKEND.md Section 5) needs: one buffer per tensor, bound
    /// whole, or a refusal by name.
    pub fn check_tensor_fits(&self, name: &str, bytes: u64) -> Result<()> {
        if bytes > self.max_buffer_size {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: name.to_string(),
                detail: format!(
                    "tensor holds {bytes} bytes but the device caps a buffer at {}",
                    self.max_buffer_size
                ),
            });
        }
        if bytes > self.max_binding_size {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: name.to_string(),
                detail: format!(
                    "tensor holds {bytes} bytes but a single binding caps at {}",
                    self.max_binding_size
                ),
            });
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/src/dflash_session.rs =====
//! The DFlash draft model as a device-resident session:
//! the GPU counterpart of `dflash::DflashModel`, composed
//! in the resident pattern [`crate::session::ResidentSession`]
//! established for the Glimmer target (weights uploaded
//! once, position-addressed resident KV, one command chain
//! per pass, logits readback appended to the same encoder).
//!
//! The semantics are the CPU implementation's, step for
//! step; `crates/dflash` is the spec and the correctness
//! oracle:
//!
//! - **Injection** ([`DflashSession::inject`]): conditioning
//!   rows (the target's layer inputs at `dflash.target_layers`,
//!   concatenated per position) are fused by the `fc`
//!   projection and the encoder output RMSNorm; per layer,
//!   K/V projections of the fused rows, the per-head RMSNorm
//!   and NEOX RoPE on K, stored in the layer's resident KV
//!   buffers AT THEIR ABSOLUTE POSITIONS. The resident KV
//!   is a flat position-addressed space, not a ring: the
//!   CPU cache is a position-keyed map whose reads filter
//!   by mask, and the flat layout is that map's exact
//!   device shape (the sliding window is a read-side mask
//!   here, as it is in the CPU implementation).
//! - **Drafting** ([`DflashSession::forward_block`]): the
//!   noise block is gathered from the (borrowed) embedding
//!   table and run through the draft layers; attention
//!   reads the committed positions plus the block's own
//!   rows under the config's causal flag and per-layer
//!   sliding window (K17); the final RMSNorm and the
//!   (borrowed) output head produce the logits. No logit
//!   scale or softcap: the draft applies none. The pass
//!   never writes the resident KV, exactly like the CPU
//!   drafting pass never writes the cache.
//!
//! Composition: projections walk the same small-batch
//! ladder the resident session walks below its matrix
