        self.write_positions_array();
        self.stats.injects += 1;
        self.diag.event(
            "inject.end",
            &format!("cached_positions={}", self.held.len()),
        );
        Ok(())
    }

    /// The conditioning fusion on its own (the CPU model's
    /// public seam): `fc` projection followed by the
    /// encoder output RMSNorm, read back to the host.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`DflashError::ConditioningWidth`] on a feature
    /// slice that is not `rows` rows of the conditioning
    /// width; [`DflashError::StepFailed`] for device-side
    /// failures.
    pub fn fuse(&mut self, features: &[f32], rows: usize) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        let width = self.conditioning_width;
        if features.len() != rows * width {
            return Err(DflashError::ConditioningWidth {
                expected: width,
                actual: reported_width(features.len(), rows),
            });
        }
        if rows == 0 {
            return Ok(Vec::new());
        }
        let hidden = self.cfg.hidden as usize;
        let ctx = self.backend.context();
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(rows * hidden);
        let mut offset = 0;
        while offset < rows {
            let crows = INJECT_CHUNK_ROWS.min(rows - offset);
            let chunk = &features[offset * width..(offset + crows) * width];
            let bytes: Vec<u8> = chunk.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect();
            ctx.queue.write_buffer(&self.scratch.features, 0, &bytes);
            if !self.inject_plans.contains_key(&crows) {
                let plan = self.build_inject_plan(crows)?;
                self.inject_plans.insert(crows, plan);
            }
            let plan = &self.inject_plans[&crows];
            let mut encoder = ctx
                .device
                .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                    label: Some("dflash fuse chain"),
                });
            {
                let mut pass = encoder.begin_compute_pass(&wgpu::ComputePassDescriptor {
                    label: Some("dflash fuse prefix"),
                    timestamp_writes: None,
                });
                for call in &plan.prefix {
                    call.encode_into(&mut pass);
                }
            }
            encoder.copy_buffer_to_buffer(
                &self.scratch.fused_n,
                0,
                &self.scratch.fuse_staging,
                0,
                (crows * hidden * 4) as u64,
            );
            ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
            self.stats.submissions += 1;
            let part = ctx
                .map_staging(&self.scratch.fuse_staging, crows * hidden)
                .map_err(|e| we(STEP_SESSION, e))?;
            out.extend_from_slice(&part);
            self.stats.readbacks += 1;
            self.drain_diag();
            offset += crows;
        }
        Ok(out)
    }

    /// Run one block through the draft and return
    /// per-position logits, row-major
    /// `[tokens.len()][vocab]`: the GPU form of
    /// `DflashModel::forward_block`, same validation order,
    /// same row meaning (row `i` is the distribution for
    /// the token following block position
    /// `start_position + i`). The pass never writes the
    /// resident KV.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// The CPU pass's errors in its order
    /// ([`DflashError::EmptyInput`],
    /// [`DflashError::BlockTooLong`],
    /// [`DflashError::TokenOutOfRange`],
    /// [`DflashError::SequenceTooLong`]);
    /// [`DflashError::StepFailed`] for device-side
    /// failures. (The borrowed-table refusals the CPU pass
    /// raises here were already settled at construction;
    /// see the module docs.)
    pub fn forward_block(&mut self, tokens: &[u32], start_position: usize) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        self.run_block(tokens, start_position, None)
    }

    /// Run one block through the draft and read back only
    /// the first `row_cap` rows of its logits: the prefix
    /// variant of [`Self::forward_block`] for a caller that
    /// consumes a bounded prefix of the block (the
    /// speculative loop slices at most `depth + 1` rows:
    /// the anchor's row plus one per draft it may propose).
    ///
    /// The device still runs the full block: block
    /// attention is non-causal, so a truncated block would
    /// change the earlier rows' distributions. Only the
    /// staging copy and the host map shrink, so the
    /// returned rows are the full forward's first `row_cap`
    /// rows, bit for bit, in the same row-major layout.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`DflashError::StepFailed`] under the
    /// `dflash forward_block` step when `row_cap` is not a
    /// true prefix of the block (`1..=tokens.len()`); the
    /// CPU pass's errors, in its order, otherwise.
    pub fn forward_block_capped(
        &mut self,
        tokens: &[u32],
        start_position: usize,
        row_cap: usize,
    ) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        self.run_block(tokens, start_position, Some(row_cap))
    }

    /// The block pass behind both public forwards: the
    /// CPU pass's validations in its order, the one
    /// submission, and the readback of the resolved prefix
    /// (the whole block when uncapped).
    fn run_block(
        &mut self,
        tokens: &[u32],
        start_position: usize,
        row_cap: Option<usize>,
    ) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        let cfg = &self.cfg;
        if tokens.is_empty() {
            return Err(DflashError::EmptyInput);
        }
        if tokens.len() > cfg.block_size as usize {
            return Err(DflashError::BlockTooLong {
                len: tokens.len(),
                block_size: cfg.block_size,
            });
        }
        for &token in tokens {
            if token >= cfg.vocab_size {
                return Err(DflashError::TokenOutOfRange {
                    token,
                    vocab_size: cfg.vocab_size,
                });
            }
        }
        let total = start_position + tokens.len();
        if total > cfg.context_length as usize {
            return Err(DflashError::SequenceTooLong {
                total,
                context_length: cfg.context_length,
            });
        }
        let rows = tokens.len();
        let read_rows = match row_cap {
            None => rows,
            Some(cap) => capped_rows(rows, cap).ok_or_else(|| DflashError::StepFailed {
                step: STEP_BLOCK,
                detail: format!(
                    "row cap {cap} is not a prefix of the {rows}-row block; \
                     the cap sizes the readback only, never the block"
                ),
            })?,
        };
        self.diag.event(
            "forward_block.begin",
            &format!(
                "tokens={} start={} cached={}",
                tokens.len(),
                start_position,
                self.held.len()
            ),
        );
        if read_rows < rows {
            self.diag.event(
                "forward_block.capped",
                &format!("rows={rows} returned={read_rows}"),
            );
        }
        let vocab = cfg.vocab_size as usize;
        let ctx = self.backend.context();
        let token_bytes: Vec<u8> = tokens.iter().flat_map(|t| t.to_le_bytes()).collect();
        ctx.queue
            .write_buffer(&self.scratch.tokens, 0, &token_bytes);
        let position_bytes: Vec<u8> = (0..rows)
            .flat_map(|i| ((start_position + i) as u32).to_le_bytes())
            .collect();
        ctx.queue
            .write_buffer(&self.scratch.block_positions, 0, &position_bytes);
        if !self.block_plans.contains_key(&rows) {
            let plan = self.build_block_plan(rows)?;
            self.block_plans.insert(rows, plan);
        }
        let plan = &self.block_plans[&rows];
        let mut encoder = ctx
            .device
            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                label: Some("dflash block forward"),
            });
        plan.encode(
            &mut encoder,
            ctx,
            start_position,
            self.held.len(),
            BlockReadback {
                logits: &self.scratch.logits,
                staging: &self.scratch.staging,
                rows: read_rows,
            },
        );
        ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
        self.stats.submissions += 1;
        let logits = ctx
            .map_staging(&self.scratch.staging, read_rows * vocab)
            .map_err(|e| we(STEP_BLOCK, e))?;
        self.stats.blocks += 1;
        self.stats.readbacks += 1;
        self.stats.logits_values_read += logits.len() as u64;
        self.drain_diag();
        self.capture_block(&logits);
        self.diag
            .event("forward_block.end", &format!("logits={}", logits.len()));
        Ok(logits)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn contiguous_runs_group_only_true_runs() {
        assert_eq!(contiguous_runs(&[]), Vec::<(usize, usize)>::new());
        assert_eq!(contiguous_runs(&[0, 1, 2, 3]), vec![(0, 4)]);
        assert_eq!(
            contiguous_runs(&[0, 1, 4, 5, 9]),
            vec![(0, 2), (2, 2), (4, 1)]
        );
        assert_eq!(contiguous_runs(&[7]), vec![(0, 1)]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn reported_width_matches_the_cpu_helper() {
        assert_eq!(reported_width(24, 4), 6);
        assert_eq!(reported_width(24, 0), 24);
        assert_eq!(reported_width(25, 4), 6);
    }

    #[test]
    fn capped_rows_accepts_only_true_prefixes() {
        assert_eq!(capped_rows(16, 1), Some(1));
        assert_eq!(capped_rows(16, 2), Some(2));
        assert_eq!(capped_rows(16, 16), Some(16));
        assert_eq!(capped_rows(16, 0), None);
        assert_eq!(capped_rows(16, 17), None);
        assert_eq!(capped_rows(0, 1), None);
        assert_eq!(capped_rows(1, 1), Some(1));
    }

    #[test]
    fn session_config_default_is_the_documented_capacity() {
        assert_eq!(DflashSessionConfig::default().kv_capacity, 8192);
    }

    /// A minimal draft config for the capture wiring pins:
    /// three layers deep, block size 4, the fixture's shape
    /// discipline in miniature.
    fn capture_test_cfg() -> DflashConfig {
        DflashConfig {
            name: None,
            block_count: 3,
            context_length: 128,
            hidden: 256,
            ffn_hidden: 512,
            q_heads: 4,
            kv_heads: 2,
            key_length: 64,
            value_length: 64,
            rope_freq_base: 10_000.0,
            rms_eps: 1e-5,
            block_size: 4,
            target_layers: vec![0, 2],
            sliding_window: 3,
            sliding_pattern: vec![true, false, true],
            causal_attention: false,
            mask_token_id: 511,
            vocab_size: 512,
        }
    }

    /// The manifest's session section states the draft's
    /// own shape: kind, depth (the layer count), and block
    /// size first, then the target shape the draft serves.
    #[test]
    fn capture_session_pairs_state_the_draft_shape() {
        let pairs = DflashSession::capture_session_pairs(&capture_test_cfg(), 512, 256, 64);
        let expected: Vec<(String, String)> = [
            ("kind", "dflash"),
            ("depth", "3"),
            ("block_size", "4"),
            ("hidden", "256"),
            ("vocab", "512"),
            ("context_length", "128"),
            ("target_hidden", "256"),
            ("conditioning_width", "512"),
            ("kv_capacity", "64"),
        ]
        .iter()
        .map(|(k, v)| (k.to_string(), v.to_string()))
        .collect();
        assert_eq!(pairs, expected);
    }

    /// The exact calls the constructor and the block exit
    /// make, driven against a timing-mode accumulator (the
    /// resident path's pin, restated for the draft
    /// session): no manifest begins, the block record
    /// returns nothing, no capture rows exist, and the
    /// finish writes the timing report with NO capture
    /// sidecars beside it.
    #[test]
    fn capture_wiring_is_inert_in_timing_mode() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
            "wgpu-compute-dflash-capture-timing-{}",
            std::process::id()
        ));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).expect("temp dir");
        let out = dir.join("timing.csv");
        let manifest = RunManifest {
            session: DflashSession::capture_session_pairs(&capture_test_cfg(), 512, 256, 64),
            ..RunManifest::default()
        };
        let mut acc = DiagAccumulator::with_mode(Some(out.clone()), DiagMode::Timing);
        acc.begin_manifest(manifest);
        assert!(acc.manifest_json().is_none(), "timing begins no manifest");
        assert!(acc
            .record_forward(CaptureRecord::KIND_BLOCK, &[1.0, 2.0])
            .is_none());
        assert!(acc.record_spec_round(&[7, 8], 1).is_none());
        assert!(acc.capture_records().is_empty());
        assert!(acc.write_report(0));
        assert!(!crate::timestamps::manifest_sidecar_path(&out).exists());
        assert!(!crate::timestamps::capture_sidecar_path(&out).exists());
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }

    /// The same calls at capture level: the manifest
    /// begins with the draft's pairs inside it, and the
    /// block forward's logits land as one `block` record.
    #[test]
    fn capture_wiring_records_the_block_in_capture_mode() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
            "wgpu-compute-dflash-capture-capture-{}",
            std::process::id()
        ));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).expect("temp dir");
        let out = dir.join("capture.csv");
        let manifest = RunManifest {
            session: DflashSession::capture_session_pairs(&capture_test_cfg(), 512, 256, 64),
            ..RunManifest::default()
        };
        let mut acc = DiagAccumulator::with_mode(Some(out.clone()), DiagMode::Capture);
        acc.begin_manifest(manifest);
        let json = acc.manifest_json().expect("capture begins a manifest");
        assert!(json.contains("\"kind\":\"dflash\""), "manifest: {json}");
        assert!(json.contains("\"depth\":\"3\""), "manifest: {json}");
        assert!(json.contains("\"block_size\":\"4\""), "manifest: {json}");
        let record = acc
            .record_forward(CaptureRecord::KIND_BLOCK, &[0.0, 1.0, 0.5])
            .expect("capture records the block");
        assert_eq!(record.kind, CaptureRecord::KIND_BLOCK);
        assert_eq!(record.values, 3);
        assert_eq!(acc.capture_record_count(), 1);
        assert!(acc.write_report(0));
        let capture_text = std::fs::read_to_string(crate::timestamps::capture_sidecar_path(&out))
            .expect("capture sidecar written");
        let parsed =
            crate::timestamps::parse_capture_csv(&capture_text).expect("capture sidecar parses");
        assert_eq!(parsed.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(parsed[0].kind, CaptureRecord::KIND_BLOCK);
        assert!(crate::timestamps::manifest_sidecar_path(&out).exists());
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }

    /// The draft ladder's resolution, pinned against
    /// the shipped band table at the draft's own
    /// geometries. The Glimmer draft is hidden-6656
    /// like its target, so the shape representatives
    /// are the sweep's: attention (6656 out), FFN
    /// (19968 out), KV (256 out), and the head
    /// (202048 out, FFN class by relative geometry).
    /// `cands` resolves with the shipped bands and the
    /// given ceilings in [`proj_candidates`] order
    /// (mmv ceiling, small ceiling, chunked ceiling).
    fn cands(
        ceilings: (u32, u32, u32),
        family: MmvFamily,
        in_features: usize,
        out_rows: usize,
        batch: u32,
    ) -> Vec<ProjForm> {
        proj_candidates(
            &crate::compute::default_mmv_bands(),
            ceilings.0,
            ceilings.1,
            ceilings.2,
            family,
            in_features,
            out_rows,
            batch,
        )
    }

    const DRAFT_ATTN: (usize, usize) = (6656, 6656);
    const DRAFT_FFN: (usize, usize) = (6656, 19968);
    const DRAFT_KV: (usize, usize) = (6656, 256);
    const DRAFT_HEAD: (usize, usize) = (6656, 202048);

    #[test]
    fn draft_ladder_ships_open_at_default_ceilings() {
        // The shipped defaults since the 2026-11-06
        // flip (bench/baseline-session-2026-11-06.md
        // leg (d)): the MMV ceiling resolves to 16,
        // the small and chunked ceilings stay 1. At
        // those ceilings the ladder carries exactly the
        // band table's MMV admissions and nothing else.
        // The ceilings are read from the constants, so
        // this pins the shipped resolution itself, not
        // a copy of it.
        let defaults = (
            crate::compute::DEFAULT_MMV_MAX_ROWS,
            crate::compute::DEFAULT_SMALL_BATCH_MAX_ROWS,
            crate::compute::DEFAULT_CHUNKED_GEMV_MAX_ROWS,
        );
        assert_eq!(defaults, (16, 1, 1));
        // The draft head at the block batch routes to
        // K21 through the Q5_K FFN cell: the route the
        // baseline session's leg (e) priced at 10 ms a
        // round of draft time.
        assert_eq!(
            cands(defaults, MmvFamily::Q5K, DRAFT_HEAD.0, DRAFT_HEAD.1, 16),
            vec![ProjForm::Mmv]
        );
        // Measured in-band admissions across families.
        assert_eq!(
            cands(defaults, MmvFamily::Q4K, DRAFT_ATTN.0, DRAFT_ATTN.1, 7),
            vec![ProjForm::Mmv]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            cands(defaults, MmvFamily::Q6K, DRAFT_KV.0, DRAFT_KV.1, 12),
            vec![ProjForm::Mmv]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            cands(defaults, MmvFamily::Q5K, DRAFT_KV.0, DRAFT_KV.1, 16),
            vec![ProjForm::Mmv]
        );
        // The table's exclusions stay exclusions at the
        // shipped default: Q4_K and Q6_K admit nothing
        // at the block batch, the Q4_K FFN hole at
        // row 3 stays a hole, the Q5_K KV cell admits
        // only row 16, and single rows and past-band
        // batches stay the GEMV's.
        for family in [MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvFamily::Q6K] {
            for (inf, out) in [DRAFT_ATTN, DRAFT_FFN, DRAFT_KV] {
                assert_eq!(
                    cands(defaults, family, inf, out, 16),
                    Vec::<ProjForm>::new(),
                    "{family:?} in {inf} out {out} batch 16"
                );
            }
        }
        assert_eq!(
            cands(defaults, MmvFamily::Q4K, DRAFT_FFN.0, DRAFT_FFN.1, 3),
            Vec::<ProjForm>::new()
        );
        assert_eq!(
            cands(defaults, MmvFamily::Q5K, DRAFT_KV.0, DRAFT_KV.1, 12),
            Vec::<ProjForm>::new()
        );
        for family in [MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvFamily::Q6K] {
            for (inf, out) in [DRAFT_ATTN, DRAFT_FFN, DRAFT_KV, DRAFT_HEAD] {
                for batch in [1, 64] {
                    assert_eq!(
                        cands(defaults, family, inf, out, batch),
                        Vec::<ProjForm>::new(),
                        "{family:?} in {inf} out {out} batch {batch}"
                    );
                }
            }
        }
        // The explicit close still closes everything:
        // with every ceiling at 1 no rung applies at
        // any batch, so the GEMV form serves exactly as
        // the pre-ladder draft served.
        for family in [MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvFamily::Q6K] {
            for (inf, out) in [DRAFT_ATTN, DRAFT_FFN, DRAFT_KV, DRAFT_HEAD] {
                for batch in [2, 3, 7, 12, 16, 64] {
                    assert_eq!(
                        cands((1, 1, 1), family, inf, out, batch),
                        Vec::<ProjForm>::new(),
                        "{family:?} in {inf} out {out} batch {batch}"
                    );
                }
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn draft_head_routes_to_mmv_at_block_batch() {
        // The cost map's fattest dispatch: the Q5_K
        // head at the block's 16 rows, ceiling open.
        // The Q5_K cells admit 16 in every shape class
        // (attn 2-16, ffn 3-16, kv exactly 16), so the
        // head takes K21.
        assert_eq!(
            cands((16, 1, 1), MmvFamily::Q5K, DRAFT_HEAD.0, DRAFT_HEAD.1, 16),
            vec![ProjForm::Mmv]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            cands((16, 1, 1), MmvFamily::Q5K, DRAFT_ATTN.0, DRAFT_ATTN.1, 16),
            vec![ProjForm::Mmv]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            cands((16, 1, 1), MmvFamily::Q5K, DRAFT_KV.0, DRAFT_KV.1, 16),
            vec![ProjForm::Mmv]
        );
        // The Q5_K KV cell is exactly row 16: at 12
        // nothing routes.
        assert_eq!(
            cands((16, 1, 1), MmvFamily::Q5K, DRAFT_KV.0, DRAFT_KV.1, 12),
            Vec::<ProjForm>::new()
        );
        // The global gate still rules: ceiling 1
        // closes the head like everything else.
        assert_eq!(
            cands((1, 1, 1), MmvFamily::Q5K, DRAFT_HEAD.0, DRAFT_HEAD.1, 16),
            Vec::<ProjForm>::new()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn draft_block_batch_leaves_q4k_q6k_on_the_lower_ladder() {
        // At the block's 16 rows the shipped Q4_K and
        // Q6_K cells admit nothing (their measured
        // cells end at 12; the sweep never measured
        // MMV at 16, where MMQ served both arms), so
        // with the lower ceilings also closed the GEMV
        // form serves, and the exclusion is policy, not
        // a kernel limit (the kernels serve 16).
        for family in [MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvFamily::Q6K] {
            for (inf, out) in [DRAFT_ATTN, DRAFT_FFN, DRAFT_KV] {
                assert_eq!(
                    cands((16, 1, 1), family, inf, out, 16),
                    Vec::<ProjForm>::new(),
                    "{family:?} in {inf} out {out}"
                );
            }
        }
        // Inside the measured band they route: Q4_K
        // attention at 7, Q6_K attention and KV at 12.
        assert_eq!(
            cands((16, 1, 1), MmvFamily::Q4K, DRAFT_ATTN.0, DRAFT_ATTN.1, 7),
            vec![ProjForm::Mmv]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            cands((16, 1, 1), MmvFamily::Q6K, DRAFT_ATTN.0, DRAFT_ATTN.1, 12),
            vec![ProjForm::Mmv]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            cands((16, 1, 1), MmvFamily::Q6K, DRAFT_KV.0, DRAFT_KV.1, 12),
            vec![ProjForm::Mmv]
        );
        // The Q4_K FFN cell has a measured hole at
        // row 3 ("2,4-12"): 3 falls through, 4 routes.
        assert_eq!(
            cands((16, 1, 1), MmvFamily::Q4K, DRAFT_FFN.0, DRAFT_FFN.1, 3),
            Vec::<ProjForm>::new()
        );
        assert_eq!(
            cands((16, 1, 1), MmvFamily::Q4K, DRAFT_FFN.0, DRAFT_FFN.1, 4),
            vec![ProjForm::Mmv]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn draft_ladder_orders_rungs_and_bounds_the_lower_ones() {
        // All ceilings open: the order is MMV, then
        // K18, then chunked, and a batch the MMV cell
        // excludes still reaches the lower rungs.
        assert_eq!(
            cands((16, 16, 15), MmvFamily::Q5K, DRAFT_ATTN.0, DRAFT_ATTN.1, 7),
            vec![ProjForm::Mmv, ProjForm::Small, ProjForm::Chunked]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            cands((16, 16, 15), MmvFamily::Q4K, DRAFT_KV.0, DRAFT_KV.1, 12),
            vec![ProjForm::Small, ProjForm::Chunked]
        );
        // The chunked rung keeps the resident bound:
        // at 16 rows the matrix threshold owns the
        // ladder, so even a wide-open chunked ceiling
        // admits nothing there.
        assert_eq!(
            cands((16, 1, 64), MmvFamily::Q4K, DRAFT_KV.0, DRAFT_KV.1, 16),
            Vec::<ProjForm>::new()
        );
        // Single rows are the GEMV's at every setting.
        for family in [MmvFamily::Q4K, MmvFamily::Q5K, MmvFamily::Q6K] {
            assert_eq!(
                cands((16, 16, 64), family, DRAFT_ATTN.0, DRAFT_ATTN.1, 1),
                Vec::<ProjForm>::new()
            );
        }
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/src/diag.rs =====
//! Debug logging seam for this crate, mirroring `cpu-compute`'s:
//! structured lines to stderr behind a flag, off by default. This is
//! the crate's built-in way to pull its bug information out (David's
//! rule: debugging built into every module from birth).
//!
//! Enable with [`set_debug`] or the `WGPU_COMPUTE_DEBUG` environment variable
//! (checked on every [`debug_enabled`] call, the gguf shape, so a
//! shipped binary can turn the seam on with no code change).
//!
//! This flag gates only these `dbg_log` lines. Per-dispatch kernel
//! timing is a separate, already-wired system (`WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG`,
//! see `timestamps.rs`); the two are not the same switch.

use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};

static DEBUG_ENABLED: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);

/// Enable or disable debug logging to stderr. When on, the backend
/// logs adapter enumeration and selection, tensor uploads, and
/// dispatches under a `[wgpu-compute]` prefix.
pub fn set_debug(enabled: bool) {
    DEBUG_ENABLED.store(enabled, Ordering::Relaxed);
}

/// Whether debug logging is currently enabled: the explicit flag,
/// or `WGPU_COMPUTE_DEBUG` present in the environment (any value other than
/// `0` or empty). See [`set_debug`].
#[must_use]
pub fn debug_enabled() -> bool {
    if DEBUG_ENABLED.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
        return true;
    }
    match std::env::var("WGPU_COMPUTE_DEBUG") {
        Ok(v) => v != "0" && !v.is_empty(),
        Err(_) => false,
    }
}

/// Emit one already-formatted diagnostic line: the `dbg_log`
/// macro's single output path, so test builds capture exactly what
/// stderr receives and can prove the seam fired.
pub fn emit_debug(formatted: &str) {
    #[cfg(test)]
    capture(&format!("[wgpu-compute] {formatted}"));
    eprintln!("[wgpu-compute] {formatted}");
}

/// Test-only capture of emitted debug lines, so unit tests can prove
/// the seam actually fired instead of trusting that the macro call is
/// present in the source (the gguf channel's shape). Lines are the
/// exact formatted output; tests assert on their own probe strings,
/// which are unique per test, so parallel tests sharing this buffer
/// cannot satisfy each other's assertions.
#[cfg(test)]
static CAPTURED: std::sync::Mutex<Vec<String>> = std::sync::Mutex::new(Vec::new());

#[cfg(test)]
fn capture(line: &str) {
    CAPTURED
        .lock()
        .unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())
        .push(line.to_string());
}

/// The debug lines captured since the process started (test builds
/// only).
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) fn captured_lines() -> Vec<String> {
    CAPTURED.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner()).clone()
}

/// Internal logging macro: silent unless the debug flag is on.
macro_rules! dbg_log {
    ($($arg:tt)*) => {
        if $crate::diag::debug_enabled() {
            $crate::diag::emit_debug(&::std::format!($($arg)*));
        }
    };
}
pub(crate) use dbg_log;

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Serializes this crate's diag tests: the flag and the env var
    /// are process-global, so two tests flipping them in parallel
    /// would satisfy (or break) each other's assertions.
    static DIAG_TEST_LOCK: std::sync::Mutex<()> = std::sync::Mutex::new(());

    #[test]
    fn env_twin_enables_debug() {
        let _guard = DIAG_TEST_LOCK.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        set_debug(false);
        std::env::remove_var("WGPU_COMPUTE_DEBUG");
        assert!(!debug_enabled());
        std::env::set_var("WGPU_COMPUTE_DEBUG", "1");
        assert!(
            debug_enabled(),
            "WGPU_COMPUTE_DEBUG=1 must enable debug (the gguf env-twin contract)"
        );
        std::env::set_var("WGPU_COMPUTE_DEBUG", "0");
        assert!(
            !debug_enabled(),
            "WGPU_COMPUTE_DEBUG=0 must not enable debug"
        );
        std::env::set_var("WGPU_COMPUTE_DEBUG", "");
        assert!(
            !debug_enabled(),
            "an empty WGPU_COMPUTE_DEBUG must not enable debug"
        );
        std::env::remove_var("WGPU_COMPUTE_DEBUG");
        assert!(!debug_enabled());
    }
    #[test]
    fn seam_fires_when_on_and_is_silent_when_off() {
        let _guard = DIAG_TEST_LOCK.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        std::env::remove_var("WGPU_COMPUTE_DEBUG");
        set_debug(false);
        crate::diag::dbg_log!("silent probe wgpu_compute_debug_off_probe");
        assert!(
            !captured_lines()
                .iter()
                .any(|l| l.contains("wgpu_compute_debug_off_probe")),
            "the seam must stay silent while debug is off"
        );
        set_debug(true);
        crate::diag::dbg_log!("firing probe wgpu_compute_debug_on_probe");
        set_debug(false);
        assert!(
            captured_lines()
                .iter()
                .any(|l| l.contains("[wgpu-compute]") && l.contains("wgpu_compute_debug_on_probe")),
            "the seam must emit its prefixed line while debug is on"
        );
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/src/error.rs =====
//! Error types for the wgpu backend.
//!
//! Same rule as the rest of the rebuild: every failure is loud and
//! names the thing that failed. Device selection failures list every
//! adapter that was seen and why none qualified; tensor refusals
//! carry the tensor name and both byte counts; a kernel that has not
//! landed yet is a named refusal, never a substituted result.

use std::fmt;

/// Everything that can go wrong while selecting a device, uploading
/// a tensor, or running a kernel in this crate.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum WgpuError {
    /// No adapter satisfied the selection policy. `seen` describes
    /// every adapter wgpu enumerated, so the refusal shows whether
    /// the card was absent, present but the wrong kind, or present
    /// only as a software rasterizer (which BACKEND.md Section 6
    /// counts as no adapter at all).
    NoSuitableAdapter {
        /// One line per enumerated adapter: name, backend, type.
        seen: Vec<String>,
        /// Whether the policy in force allowed non-discrete GPUs.
        allow_non_discrete: bool,
    },
    /// The selected adapter could not produce a device.
    DeviceRequest {
        /// The wgpu failure, in its own words.
        detail: String,
    },
    /// The granted device limits fall below what a kernel or a
    /// tensor requires. This is BACKEND.md Section 6's fallback
    /// event, surfaced as an error instead of a surprise mid-load.
    LimitShortfall {
        /// Which limit fell short.
        what: &'static str,
        /// Bytes (or units) the work requires.
        required: u64,
        /// What the device actually granted.
        granted: u64,
    },
    /// A tensor's declared geometry and its bytes disagree, or its
    /// shape is not one the addressed kernel can run.
    InvalidTensor {
        /// The full GGUF tensor name.
        name: String,
        /// What is wrong, with both numbers where numbers differ.
        detail: String,
    },
    /// Shader compilation or pipeline creation failed.
    Pipeline {
        /// The wgpu failure, in its own words.
        detail: String,
    },
    /// A buffer map (readback) failed or returned an error.
    Readback {
        /// The wgpu failure, in its own words.
        detail: String,
    },
}

impl fmt::Display for WgpuError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter {
                seen,
                allow_non_discrete,
            } => {
                write!(
                    f,
                    "no suitable GPU adapter (allow_non_discrete={allow_non_discrete}); enumerated: [{}]",
                    seen.join("; ")
                )
            }
            WgpuError::DeviceRequest { detail } => {
                write!(f, "request_device failed: {detail}")
            }
            WgpuError::LimitShortfall {
                what,
                required,
                granted,
            } => {
                write!(
                    f,
                    "device limit {what} too small: need {required}, granted {granted}"
                )
            }
            WgpuError::InvalidTensor { name, detail } => {
                write!(f, "tensor {name} is not runnable as given: {detail}")
            }
            WgpuError::Pipeline { detail } => {
                write!(f, "shader or pipeline creation failed: {detail}")
            }
            WgpuError::Readback { detail } => {
                write!(f, "buffer readback failed: {detail}")
            }
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for WgpuError {}

/// Result alias for wgpu backend operations.
pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, WgpuError>;

===== END FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/src/error.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/coopmat/README.md =====
# Cooperative-matrix SPIR-V artifacts

The `.spv` files in this folder are checked in on purpose, and this note
is how they are produced and verified.

## Why binaries are checked in

The K23 and K24 cooperative-matrix kernels load precompiled SPIR-V
(`include_bytes!` in `crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/k23_q4k_coopmat.rs`
and `k24_q4k_coopmat.rs`) because the wgpu/Naga path cannot compile or
validate this module: wgpu 27 has no cooperative-matrix IR. The GLSL
sources (`.comp`) sit beside the artifacts and are the source of truth;
the binaries are build outputs that the repo carries because the runtime
needs them as-is.

## How they are built

- `rebuild.sh` rebuilds the K23 artifact; `rebuild-k24.sh` does the
  same for K24. Both compile with `glslangValidator -V
  --target-env vulkan1.3`, the conservative floor for the KHR
  cooperative-matrix extension on this backend's Vulkan 1.4 devices.

## How they are verified

Each rebuild script:

1. validates the fresh artifact with `spirv-val`,
2. disassembles it with `spirv-dis` into the checked-in
   `.spv.dis.txt` beside the artifact, and
3. refuses to pass unless the disassembly contains the four cooperative
   matrix ops the kernels exist for: `OpTypeCooperativeMatrixKHR`,
   `OpCooperativeMatrixLoadKHR`, `OpCooperativeMatrixMulAddKHR`, and
   `OpCooperativeMatrixStoreKHR`.

On top of that, the Rust wrappers carry unit tests
(`spirv_artifact_carries_coopmat_ops`) that walk the checked-in
artifact's instruction stream and require the same ops, so a stale or
swapped binary fails the workspace test gate without a rebuild.

===== END FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/coopmat/README.md =====

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/coopmat/k23_q4k_coopmat.comp =====
// K23: Q4_K x Q8_1 integer cooperative-matrix MMQ.
//
// Modeled on llama.cpp's mul_mmq_cm1.comp and the Q4_K
// parts of mul_mmq_cm1_funcs.glsl (ggml-org/llama.cpp,
// MIT), the shader ggml's Vulkan backend selects for
// Q4_K x Q8_1 products on RDNA3/4 when
// VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix is present and the device
// reports a subgroup-scope s8 x s8 to s32 16x16x16
// cooperative matrix shape (ggml-vulkan.cpp's
// coopmat_int_support). bench/llama-parity-specs-2026-11-06.md
// pins those references; bench/coopmat-build-2026-11-06.md
// records this port.
//
// What is transcribed, and what is adapted:
//
// - Staging follows mul_mmq_cm1 verbatim in structure.
//   Two shared tiles, split the way llama splits them:
//   the weight side stages de-interleaved raw nibble
//   codes in rows of QPITCH = BK_STEP * (BK / 4) + 4 =
//   36 u32 words (the +4 is llama's bank skew), with the
//   per-sub-block (d * scale, -(dmin * min)) pairs in a
//   separate vec2 array (llama's buf_a_dm); the
//   activation side stages K12's Q8_1 words the same
//   way, with the (d, d * sum) pairs in two float arrays
//   (llama's buf_b_d and buf_b_s; this repo's K12 writes
//   the sum pre-scaled by d, the same convention ggml's
//   MMQ quantizer uses, and K13's epilogue proves it).
//   Nibbles are stored raw (0..15 as int8 bytes): the
//   -dmin * min correction term absorbs the unsigned
//   offset, exactly as llama's block_a_to_shmem does
//   for Q4_K.
// - The scale algebra is llama's Q4_K cm1_accumulate
//   identity, per 32-element sub-block ks:
//     out += dot_i32 * (d_b * sc) * d_a
//          + (-(dmin_b * mn)) * (d_a * sum_q)
//   where dot_i32 is the integer coopmat product of the
//   raw codes over the sub-block.
// - Tiles: BK 32 with BK_STEP 4 (one staged chunk is
//   128 K elements), TM = TN = TK = 16, as in llama.
//   The workgroup tile differs from llama's BM 128 x
//   BN 128: this backend's MMQ band caps the batch at
//   64 (K13's MMQ_MAX_BATCH contract), so the tile is
//   128 output rows x 64 batch rows, two subgroups
//   across the output side and two across the batch
//   side, each subgroup owning 64 x 32 outputs.
// - The accumulator epilogue is a deliberate
//   simplification, disclosed here rather than hidden:
//   llama extracts the int32 accumulator's elements
//   per thread (cm_elem_row and the wave-size-dependent
//   magic-bias path in mul_mmq_cm1.comp). This shader
//   instead coopMatStores each 16x16 int32 tile into a
//   per-subgroup shared tile and folds it into f32 sums
//   with scalar reads, which is layout-exact by the
//   cooperative matrix memory-layout rules and carries
//   no wave-size element-mapping assumptions. The
//   extraction form is the named follow-up if the
//   measured profile convicts the fold.
//
// Device assumptions, all gated before this module can
// exist: the s8 x s8 to s32 16x16x16 subgroup property
// row (bridge probe), subgroup size 64 (the kernel
// constructor refuses any other), RADV on RDNA3 (the
// only stack the lane protocol measures).
//
// Shape contract (the Rust prepare enforces it):
// in_features % 256 == 0, batch in 1..=64. Rows past
// out_rows or batch stage zeros and store nothing.
//
// Rebuild: see rebuild.sh in this directory. The .spv
// is a checked-in build artifact; Naga cannot validate
// it (wgpu 27 has no coopmat IR), so correctness rests
// on the on-card numeric gate, as the feasibility note
// disclosed.

#version 450

#extension GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix : require
#extension GL_KHR_shader_subgroup_basic : require
#extension GL_KHR_memory_scope_semantics : enable
#extension GL_EXT_shader_explicit_arithmetic_types : enable
#extension GL_EXT_control_flow_attributes : enable

layout(local_size_x = 256, local_size_y = 1, local_size_z = 1) in;

layout(set = 0, binding = 0) readonly buffer Weights { uint data_w[]; };
layout(set = 0, binding = 1) readonly buffer QsIn { uint data_qs[]; };
layout(set = 0, binding = 2) readonly buffer DsIn { vec4 data_ds[]; };
layout(set = 0, binding = 3) buffer OutBuf { float data_out[]; };
layout(set = 0, binding = 4) uniform Params {
    uint blocks_per_row; // Q4_K super-blocks per weight row
    uint out_rows;
    uint batch;
    uint blocks32;       // 32-element blocks per row
} p;

const uint BK = 32;
const uint BK_STEP = 4;
const uint QPITCH = BK_STEP * (BK / 4) + 4; // 36
const uint W_ROWS = 128;  // output rows per workgroup
const uint X_ROWS = 64;   // batch rows per workgroup
const uint WM = 64;       // output rows per subgroup
const uint WN = 32;       // batch rows per subgroup
const uint TM = 16;
const uint TN = 16;
const uint TK = 16;

shared uint buf_w_qs[W_ROWS * QPITCH];
shared vec2 buf_w_dm[W_ROWS * BK_STEP];
shared uint buf_x_qs[X_ROWS * QPITCH];
shared float buf_x_d[X_ROWS * BK_STEP];
shared float buf_x_s[X_ROWS * BK_STEP];
shared int buf_tile[4 * TM * TN];

// One of the 12 packed scale bytes of a Q4_K
// super-block (K13's scale_byte, transcribed).
uint scale_byte(uint sw0, uint sw1, uint sw2, uint i) {
    uint w = (i < 4u) ? sw0 : ((i < 8u) ? sw1 : sw2);
    return (w >> (8u * (i % 4u))) & 0xffu;
}

// ggml get_scale_min_k4: sub-block j's (scale, min)
// 6-bit pair (K13's scale_min_k4, transcribed).
uvec2 scale_min_k4(uint j, uint sw0, uint sw1, uint sw2) {
    if (j < 4u) {
        return uvec2(scale_byte(sw0, sw1, sw2, j) & 63u,
                     scale_byte(sw0, sw1, sw2, j + 4u) & 63u);
    }
    return uvec2((scale_byte(sw0, sw1, sw2, j + 4u) & 0xfu)
                     | ((scale_byte(sw0, sw1, sw2, j - 4u) >> 6u) << 4u),
                 (scale_byte(sw0, sw1, sw2, j + 4u) >> 4u)
                     | ((scale_byte(sw0, sw1, sw2, j) >> 6u) << 4u));
}

void main() {
    const uint tid = gl_LocalInvocationIndex;
    const uint sg = gl_SubgroupID;
    const uint inv = gl_SubgroupInvocationID;

    const uint wg_out0 = gl_WorkGroupID.x * W_ROWS;
    const uint wg_batch0 = gl_WorkGroupID.y * X_ROWS;

    // Subgroup tile assignment (llama's warp_r / warp_c
    // over the weight side and the activation side).
    const uint warp_r = sg % (W_ROWS / WM);
    const uint warp_c = sg / (W_ROWS / WM);
    const uint a_row0 = warp_r * WM;
    const uint b_col0 = warp_c * WN;

    // This thread's fixed slice of the subgroup tile:
    // batch column b_in_warp, output rows of one parity
    // class. sums[i] accumulates output (2 * i + opar,
    // b_in_warp) of the subgroup tile.
    const uint b_in_warp = inv % WN;
    const uint opar = inv / WN;
    float sums[32];
    for (uint i = 0; i < 32u; i++) {
        sums[i] = 0.0;
    }

    // Weight staging assignment (llama's loadr_a /
    // loadc_a): each thread owns one row quarter; two
    // row passes cover the 128-row tile.
    const uint loadr = tid % (BK / 8u);
    const uint loadc = tid / (BK / 8u);
    const uint loadstride = 256u * 8u / BK; // 64 rows per pass

    for (uint kb0 = 0; kb0 < p.blocks32; kb0 += BK_STEP) {
        // ---- Stage the weight tile for this chunk.
        [[unroll]] for (uint li = 0; li < W_ROWS / loadstride; li++) {
            const uint row = loadc + li * loadstride;
            const uint grow = wg_out0 + row;
            const bool valid = grow < p.out_rows;
            [[unroll]] for (uint ks = 0; ks < BK_STEP; ks++) {
                const uint sb = kb0 + ks;
                const uint base = row * QPITCH + ks * (BK / 4u);
                if (valid) {
                    const uint super_blk = sb >> 3;
                    const uint sub = sb & 7u;
                    const uint g = sub >> 1;
                    const uint bw = (grow * p.blocks_per_row + super_blk) * 36u;
                    const uint raw0 = data_w[bw + 4u + g * 8u + loadr * 2u];
                    const uint raw1 = data_w[bw + 4u + g * 8u + loadr * 2u + 1u];
                    if ((sub & 1u) == 0u) {
                        buf_w_qs[base + loadr * 2u] = raw0 & 0x0F0F0F0Fu;
                        buf_w_qs[base + loadr * 2u + 1u] = raw1 & 0x0F0F0F0Fu;
                    } else {
                        buf_w_qs[base + loadr * 2u] = (raw0 >> 4) & 0x0F0F0F0Fu;
                        buf_w_qs[base + loadr * 2u + 1u] = (raw1 >> 4) & 0x0F0F0F0Fu;
                    }
                    if (loadr == 0u) {
                        const vec2 dm = unpackHalf2x16(data_w[bw]);
                        const uvec2 sm = scale_min_k4(sub, data_w[bw + 1u],
                                                      data_w[bw + 2u], data_w[bw + 3u]);
                        buf_w_dm[ks * W_ROWS + row] =
                            vec2(dm.x * float(sm.x), -(dm.y * float(sm.y)));
                    }
                } else {
                    buf_w_qs[base + loadr * 2u] = 0u;
                    buf_w_qs[base + loadr * 2u + 1u] = 0u;
                    if (loadr == 0u) {
                        buf_w_dm[ks * W_ROWS + row] = vec2(0.0);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        // ---- Stage the activation tile for this chunk:
        // each thread owns one batch row's word pairs.
        {
            const uint row = tid / 4u;
            const uint part = tid % 4u;
            const uint grow = wg_batch0 + row;
            const bool valid = grow < p.batch;
            [[unroll]] for (uint ks = 0; ks < BK_STEP; ks++) {
                const uint kb = kb0 + ks;
                const uint base = row * QPITCH + ks * (BK / 4u) + part * 2u;
                if (valid) {
                    const uint src = (grow * p.blocks32 + kb) * 8u;
                    buf_x_qs[base] = data_qs[src + part * 2u];
                    buf_x_qs[base + 1u] = data_qs[src + part * 2u + 1u];
                    if (part == 0u) {
                        const vec4 ds = data_ds[grow * p.blocks32 + kb];
                        buf_x_d[ks * X_ROWS + row] = ds.x;
                        buf_x_s[ks * X_ROWS + row] = ds.y;
                    }
                } else {
                    buf_x_qs[base] = 0u;
                    buf_x_qs[base + 1u] = 0u;
                    if (part == 0u) {
                        buf_x_d[ks * X_ROWS + row] = 0.0;
                        buf_x_s[ks * X_ROWS + row] = 0.0;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        barrier();

        // ---- The integer coopmat product, one staged
        // chunk: BK_STEP sub-blocks, each folded into
        // the f32 sums with its own scale pair.
        [[unroll]] for (uint ks = 0; ks < BK_STEP; ks++) {
            const float xd = buf_x_d[ks * X_ROWS + b_col0 + b_in_warp];
            const float xs = buf_x_s[ks * X_ROWS + b_col0 + b_in_warp];
            [[unroll]] for (uint r = 0; r < WM / TM; r++) {
                [[unroll]] for (uint c = 0; c < WN / TN; c++) {
                    coopmat<int32_t, gl_ScopeSubgroup, TM, TN, gl_MatrixUseAccumulator> acc =
                        coopmat<int32_t, gl_ScopeSubgroup, TM, TN, gl_MatrixUseAccumulator>(0);
                    [[unroll]] for (uint h = 0; h < BK / TK; h++) {
                        coopmat<int8_t, gl_ScopeSubgroup, TM, TK, gl_MatrixUseA> ca;
                        coopMatLoad(ca, buf_w_qs,
                                    (a_row0 + r * TM) * QPITCH + ks * (BK / 4u) + h * (TK / 4u),
                                    QPITCH, gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutRowMajor);
                        coopmat<int8_t, gl_ScopeSubgroup, TK, TN, gl_MatrixUseB> cb;
                        coopMatLoad(cb, buf_x_qs,
                                    (b_col0 + c * TN) * QPITCH + ks * (BK / 4u) + h * (TK / 4u),
                                    QPITCH, gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutColumnMajor);
                        acc = coopMatMulAdd(ca, cb, acc);
                    }
                    coopMatStore(acc, buf_tile, sg * (TM * TN), TN,
                                 gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutRowMajor);
                    subgroupBarrier();
                    // Fold this tile: the threads whose
                    // batch column falls in this tile's
                    // half each fold their eight rows.
                    if (b_in_warp >= c * TN && b_in_warp < (c + 1u) * TN) {
                        const uint bl = b_in_warp - c * TN;
                        [[unroll]] for (uint ol = opar; ol < TM; ol += 2u) {
                            const uint o = r * TM + ol;
                            const int v = buf_tile[sg * (TM * TN) + ol * TN + bl];
                            const vec2 dm = buf_w_dm[ks * W_ROWS + a_row0 + o];
                            sums[r * (TM / 2u) + (ol >> 1)] +=
                                float(v) * dm.x * xd + dm.y * xs;
                        }
                    }
                    subgroupBarrier();
                }
            }
        }
        barrier();
    }

    // ---- Store this thread's slice, guarded per
    // element (K13's store form, transposed ownership).
    for (uint i = 0; i < 32u; i++) {
        const uint grow_out = wg_out0 + a_row0 + 2u * i + opar;
        const uint grow_batch = wg_batch0 + b_col0 + b_in_warp;
        if (grow_out < p.out_rows && grow_batch < p.batch) {
            data_out[grow_batch * p.out_rows + grow_out] = sums[i];
        }
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/coopmat/k24_q4k_coopmat.comp =====
// K24: Q4_K x Q8_1 integer cooperative-matrix MMQ, v2.
//
// The register-resident form of K23 (the v1 coopmat
// kernel in k23_q4k_coopmat.comp, same directory). The
// staging, the tile geometry, the buffer contract, and
// the accumulate identity are K23's, unchanged; the
// product loop is rebuilt on llama.cpp's mul_mmq_cm1
// Q4_K branch structure (ggml-org/llama.cpp, MIT;
// bench/llama-parity-specs-2026-11-06.md pins the
// reference, bench/coopmat-v2-2026-11-07.md records
// the autopsy that motivated this form and the card
// protocol that judges it).
//
// What changed against K23, and why:
//
// - Fragments are preloaded once per 32-element
//   sub-block into register arrays (llama's cache_a /
//   cache_b "preload up front" structure). K23 reloaded
//   the A fragment once per column tile and the B
//   fragment once per row tile, 32 cooperative loads
//   per sub-block on the critical path between the
//   muladds; this form loads 12 and reuses them from
//   registers.
// - The accumulator fold is in-register. K23 stored
//   every 16x16 int32 tile into a shared fold tile and
//   folded it back with scalar reads: 32 coopMatStores
//   and 64 subgroup barriers per staged chunk, with
//   half of each subgroup idle in every fold. This
//   form reads the accumulator's elements directly
//   (acc[e]) and folds them into the per-thread f32
//   sums with llama's cm1_accumulate identity in its
//   plain (non-magic-bias) shape:
//     sums += dot_i32 * (d_b * sc) * d_a
//           + (-(dmin_b * mn)) * (d_a * sum_q)
//   No shared fold tile, no coopMatStore, no subgroup
//   barrier anywhere in the shader.
//
// The element mapping the register fold stands on:
// element e of this thread's 16x16 int32 accumulator
// sits at row cm_elem_row(e), column
// gl_SubgroupInvocationID % TN of the tile. This is
// NOT llama's mapping: llama runs its cm1 on AMD at
// wave32 (ggml-vulkan.cpp's cm1_use_wave32, which
// forces a 32-wide subgroup through pipeline creation,
// a control the wgpu passthrough path does not have),
// where the row is (inv / 16) + 2e. This shader is
// compiled for the 64-wide subgroup the crate's bridge
// probes and the Rust constructor requires, and at
// wave64 on GFX11 (RDNA3) Mesa's cooperative matrix
// lowering (radv_nir_lower_cooperative_matrix) places
// accumulator element e at row (inv / 16) + 4e, column
// inv % 16: its load, store, and element-coordinate
// lowerings all compute base_row = inv / 16,
// row_iter = e * wave_size / 16 = 4e, inner_idx =
// inv & 15, and the accumulator length is
// 16 * 16 / 64 = 4 elements per thread (CM_ELEMS).
// The mapping is a GFX11 hardware-layout fact the
// driver lowering transcribes, not a tuning choice.
// GFX11.5/12 (RDNA3.5/RDNA4) take a different branch
// of that lowering and are out of scope here, exactly
// as they are for K23; the on-card numeric gate in
// the lane protocol is the proof on the target card.
//
// What deliberately did not change:
//
// - Staging is K23's transcription of llama's split
//   layout, byte for byte: raw nibble codes at QPITCH
//   36 with the +4 bank skew, (d * scale, -(dmin *
//   min)) vec2 pairs on the weight side, K12's Q8_1
//   words with (d, d * sum) split float arrays on the
//   activation side.
// - The tile is K23's: 128 output rows x 64 batch
//   rows per workgroup, 256 threads, four subgroups
//   of 64 owning 64 x 32 each, BK 32 staged in
//   BK_STEP 4 chunks of 128 K elements. llama's cm1
//   runs a 128 x 128 tile at wave32 with 512 threads;
//   the batch cap of this backend's MMQ band (64,
//   K13's MMQ_MAX_BATCH contract) fixes the batch
//   side here, and the subgroup width is the
//   passthrough's, not a free choice.
// - No magic bias: llama's accumulator bias trick is
//   its wave32-off path (USE_MAGIC_BIAS = WARP != 32
//   selects it, and llama's AMD configuration runs
//   WARP 32, so the shipped fast path does not use it
//   either). The sub-block integer dot is bounded by
//   32 * 15 * 127 = 60960 in magnitude, far inside
//   f32's exact-integer range, so the plain
//   float(acc[e]) conversion is exact.
// - No staging prefetch split: llama overlaps the
//   next chunk's loads with this chunk's compute
//   (its PREFETCH_BLOCK / STORE_BLOCK_TO_LDS split).
//   That is a staging-side change, a different design
//   story from this kernel's register-resident
//   product loop; the bench note names it as the
//   recorded next step if the card convicts staging.
//
// Device assumptions, all gated before this module
// can exist (the Rust constructor enforces them): the
// s8 x s8 to s32 16x16x16 subgroup property row
// (bridge probe), subgroup size 64, RADV on RDNA3
// (GFX11; the only stack the lane protocol measures).
//
// Shape contract (the Rust prepare enforces it):
// in_features % 256 == 0, batch in 1..=64. Rows past
// out_rows or batch stage zeros and store nothing.
//
// Rebuild: see rebuild.sh in this directory. The .spv
// is a checked-in build artifact; Naga cannot validate
// it (wgpu 27 has no coopmat IR), so correctness rests
// on the on-card numeric gate, as the feasibility note
// disclosed for K23.

#version 450

#extension GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix : require
#extension GL_KHR_shader_subgroup_basic : require
#extension GL_KHR_memory_scope_semantics : enable
#extension GL_EXT_shader_explicit_arithmetic_types : enable
#extension GL_EXT_control_flow_attributes : enable

layout(local_size_x = 256, local_size_y = 1, local_size_z = 1) in;

layout(set = 0, binding = 0) readonly buffer Weights { uint data_w[]; };
layout(set = 0, binding = 1) readonly buffer QsIn { uint data_qs[]; };
layout(set = 0, binding = 2) readonly buffer DsIn { vec4 data_ds[]; };
layout(set = 0, binding = 3) buffer OutBuf { float data_out[]; };
layout(set = 0, binding = 4) uniform Params {
    uint blocks_per_row; // Q4_K super-blocks per weight row
    uint out_rows;
    uint batch;
    uint blocks32;       // 32-element blocks per row
} p;

const uint BK = 32;
const uint BK_STEP = 4;
const uint QPITCH = BK_STEP * (BK / 4) + 4; // 36
const uint W_ROWS = 128;  // output rows per workgroup
const uint X_ROWS = 64;   // batch rows per workgroup
const uint WM = 64;       // output rows per subgroup
const uint WN = 32;       // batch rows per subgroup
const uint TM = 16;
const uint TN = 16;
const uint TK = 16;
const uint CMS_PER_ROW = WM / TM; // 4 coopmat tiles down the subgroup tile
const uint CMS_PER_COL = WN / TN; // 2 coopmat tiles across it
const uint K_SUB = BK / TK;       // 2 K steps per 32-element sub-block
// Accumulator elements per thread at the compiled
// subgroup size 64: (TM * TN) / 64. Mesa's GFX11
// lowering computes the same length for a 32-bit
// accumulator (radv_nir_cmat_length).
const uint CM_ELEMS = (TM * TN) / 64u; // 4

shared uint buf_w_qs[W_ROWS * QPITCH];
shared vec2 buf_w_dm[W_ROWS * BK_STEP];
shared uint buf_x_qs[X_ROWS * QPITCH];
shared float buf_x_d[X_ROWS * BK_STEP];
shared float buf_x_s[X_ROWS * BK_STEP];

// One of the 12 packed scale bytes of a Q4_K
// super-block (K13's scale_byte, transcribed).
uint scale_byte(uint sw0, uint sw1, uint sw2, uint i) {
    uint w = (i < 4u) ? sw0 : ((i < 8u) ? sw1 : sw2);
    return (w >> (8u * (i % 4u))) & 0xffu;
}

// ggml get_scale_min_k4: sub-block j's (scale, min)
// 6-bit pair (K13's scale_min_k4, transcribed).
uvec2 scale_min_k4(uint j, uint sw0, uint sw1, uint sw2) {
    if (j < 4u) {
        return uvec2(scale_byte(sw0, sw1, sw2, j) & 63u,
                     scale_byte(sw0, sw1, sw2, j + 4u) & 63u);
    }
    return uvec2((scale_byte(sw0, sw1, sw2, j + 4u) & 0xfu)
                     | ((scale_byte(sw0, sw1, sw2, j - 4u) >> 6u) << 4u),
                 (scale_byte(sw0, sw1, sw2, j + 4u) >> 4u)
                     | ((scale_byte(sw0, sw1, sw2, j) >> 6u) << 4u));
}

// The tile row of accumulator element e for this
// thread, at subgroup size 64 on GFX11: Mesa's
// lowering places it at base_row + e * (wave_size /
// 16) with base_row = inv / 16 (see the header). The
// element's column is inv % TN, fixed per thread.
uint cm_elem_row(uint e) {
    return (gl_SubgroupInvocationID / TN) + 4u * e;
}

void main() {
    const uint tid = gl_LocalInvocationIndex;
    const uint sg = gl_SubgroupID;
    const uint inv = gl_SubgroupInvocationID;

    const uint wg_out0 = gl_WorkGroupID.x * W_ROWS;
    const uint wg_batch0 = gl_WorkGroupID.y * X_ROWS;

    // Subgroup tile assignment (llama's warp_r / warp_c
    // over the weight side and the activation side).
    const uint warp_r = sg % (W_ROWS / WM);
    const uint warp_c = sg / (W_ROWS / WM);
    const uint a_row0 = warp_r * WM;
    const uint b_col0 = warp_c * WN;

    // This thread's fixed accumulator column in every
    // 16-wide tile (llama's elem_col0). sums is indexed
    // [tile (r, c)][element e], llama's layout: element
    // e of tile (r, c) is this thread's partial for
    // output (a_row0 + r * TM + cm_elem_row(e),
    // b_col0 + c * TN + elem_col0) of the subgroup tile.
    const uint elem_col0 = inv % TN;
    float sums[CMS_PER_ROW * CMS_PER_COL * CM_ELEMS];
    for (uint i = 0; i < CMS_PER_ROW * CMS_PER_COL * CM_ELEMS; i++) {
        sums[i] = 0.0;
    }

    // Weight staging assignment (llama's loadr_a /
    // loadc_a): each thread owns one row quarter; two
    // row passes cover the 128-row tile.
    const uint loadr = tid % (BK / 8u);
    const uint loadc = tid / (BK / 8u);
    const uint loadstride = 256u * 8u / BK; // 64 rows per pass

    for (uint kb0 = 0; kb0 < p.blocks32; kb0 += BK_STEP) {
        // ---- Stage the weight tile for this chunk.
        [[unroll]] for (uint li = 0; li < W_ROWS / loadstride; li++) {
            const uint row = loadc + li * loadstride;
            const uint grow = wg_out0 + row;
            const bool valid = grow < p.out_rows;
            [[unroll]] for (uint ks = 0; ks < BK_STEP; ks++) {
                const uint sb = kb0 + ks;
                const uint base = row * QPITCH + ks * (BK / 4u);
                if (valid) {
                    const uint super_blk = sb >> 3;
                    const uint sub = sb & 7u;
                    const uint g = sub >> 1;
                    const uint bw = (grow * p.blocks_per_row + super_blk) * 36u;
                    const uint raw0 = data_w[bw + 4u + g * 8u + loadr * 2u];
                    const uint raw1 = data_w[bw + 4u + g * 8u + loadr * 2u + 1u];
                    if ((sub & 1u) == 0u) {
                        buf_w_qs[base + loadr * 2u] = raw0 & 0x0F0F0F0Fu;
                        buf_w_qs[base + loadr * 2u + 1u] = raw1 & 0x0F0F0F0Fu;
                    } else {
                        buf_w_qs[base + loadr * 2u] = (raw0 >> 4) & 0x0F0F0F0Fu;
                        buf_w_qs[base + loadr * 2u + 1u] = (raw1 >> 4) & 0x0F0F0F0Fu;
                    }
                    if (loadr == 0u) {
                        const vec2 dm = unpackHalf2x16(data_w[bw]);
                        const uvec2 sm = scale_min_k4(sub, data_w[bw + 1u],
                                                      data_w[bw + 2u], data_w[bw + 3u]);
                        buf_w_dm[ks * W_ROWS + row] =
                            vec2(dm.x * float(sm.x), -(dm.y * float(sm.y)));
                    }
                } else {
                    buf_w_qs[base + loadr * 2u] = 0u;
                    buf_w_qs[base + loadr * 2u + 1u] = 0u;
                    if (loadr == 0u) {
                        buf_w_dm[ks * W_ROWS + row] = vec2(0.0);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        // ---- Stage the activation tile for this chunk:
        // each thread owns one batch row's word pairs.
        {
            const uint row = tid / 4u;
            const uint part = tid % 4u;
            const uint grow = wg_batch0 + row;
            const bool valid = grow < p.batch;
            [[unroll]] for (uint ks = 0; ks < BK_STEP; ks++) {
                const uint kb = kb0 + ks;
                const uint base = row * QPITCH + ks * (BK / 4u) + part * 2u;
                if (valid) {
                    const uint src = (grow * p.blocks32 + kb) * 8u;
                    buf_x_qs[base] = data_qs[src + part * 2u];
                    buf_x_qs[base + 1u] = data_qs[src + part * 2u + 1u];
                    if (part == 0u) {
                        const vec4 ds = data_ds[grow * p.blocks32 + kb];
                        buf_x_d[ks * X_ROWS + row] = ds.x;
                        buf_x_s[ks * X_ROWS + row] = ds.y;
                    }
                } else {
                    buf_x_qs[base] = 0u;
                    buf_x_qs[base + 1u] = 0u;
                    if (part == 0u) {
                        buf_x_d[ks * X_ROWS + row] = 0.0;
                        buf_x_s[ks * X_ROWS + row] = 0.0;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        barrier();

        // ---- The integer coopmat product, one staged
        // chunk: BK_STEP sub-blocks. Per sub-block the
        // fragments are preloaded into register arrays
        // once, then every (r, c) tile's product folds
        // in-register (llama's Q4_K cm1 branch shape).
        [[unroll]] for (uint ks = 0; ks < BK_STEP; ks++) {
            // Preload all A/B fragments up front (ILP).
            coopmat<int8_t, gl_ScopeSubgroup, TM, TK, gl_MatrixUseA>
                cache_a[CMS_PER_ROW * K_SUB];
            coopmat<int8_t, gl_ScopeSubgroup, TK, TN, gl_MatrixUseB>
                cache_b[CMS_PER_COL * K_SUB];

            [[unroll]] for (uint r = 0; r < CMS_PER_ROW; r++) {
                [[unroll]] for (uint h = 0; h < K_SUB; h++) {
                    coopMatLoad(cache_a[r * K_SUB + h], buf_w_qs,
                                (a_row0 + r * TM) * QPITCH + ks * (BK / 4u) + h * (TK / 4u),
                                QPITCH, gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutRowMajor);
                }
            }
            [[unroll]] for (uint c = 0; c < CMS_PER_COL; c++) {
                [[unroll]] for (uint h = 0; h < K_SUB; h++) {
                    coopMatLoad(cache_b[c * K_SUB + h], buf_x_qs,
                                (b_col0 + c * TN) * QPITCH + ks * (BK / 4u) + h * (TK / 4u),
                                QPITCH, gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutColumnMajor);
                }
            }

            // This thread's activation scale pair per
            // column tile: (d, d * sum) for its own
            // element column.
            float scale_b[CMS_PER_COL];
            float bs[CMS_PER_COL];
            [[unroll]] for (uint c = 0; c < CMS_PER_COL; c++) {
                scale_b[c] = buf_x_d[ks * X_ROWS + b_col0 + c * TN + elem_col0];
                bs[c] = buf_x_s[ks * X_ROWS + b_col0 + c * TN + elem_col0];
            }

            [[unroll]] for (uint r = 0; r < CMS_PER_ROW; r++) {
                // This thread's weight scale pairs for
                // its element rows in this row tile:
                // (d * sc, -(dmin * mn)) per element.
                float scale_a[CM_ELEMS];
                float ma[CM_ELEMS];
                [[unroll]] for (uint e = 0; e < CM_ELEMS; e++) {
                    const vec2 dm = buf_w_dm[ks * W_ROWS + a_row0 + r * TM + cm_elem_row(e)];
                    scale_a[e] = dm.x;
                    ma[e] = dm.y;
                }

                [[unroll]] for (uint c = 0; c < CMS_PER_COL; c++) {
                    coopmat<int32_t, gl_ScopeSubgroup, TM, TN, gl_MatrixUseAccumulator> acc =
                        coopmat<int32_t, gl_ScopeSubgroup, TM, TN, gl_MatrixUseAccumulator>(0);
                    [[unroll]] for (uint h = 0; h < K_SUB; h++) {
                        acc = coopMatMulAdd(cache_a[r * K_SUB + h],
                                            cache_b[c * K_SUB + h], acc);
                    }
                    // The in-register fold: llama's
                    // cm1_accumulate, plain path.
                    const uint tile_idx = r * CMS_PER_COL + c;
                    [[unroll]] for (uint e = 0; e < CM_ELEMS; e++) {
                        sums[tile_idx * CM_ELEMS + e] =
                            sums[tile_idx * CM_ELEMS + e]
                            + fma(float(acc[e]) * scale_a[e], scale_b[c],
                                  ma[e] * bs[c]);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        barrier();
    }

    // ---- Store: each thread stores its own elements,
    // guarded per element (llama's cm1 store form).
    [[unroll]] for (uint r = 0; r < CMS_PER_ROW; r++) {
        [[unroll]] for (uint c = 0; c < CMS_PER_COL; c++) {
            const uint tile_idx = r * CMS_PER_COL + c;
            [[unroll]] for (uint e = 0; e < CM_ELEMS; e++) {
                const uint grow_out = wg_out0 + a_row0 + r * TM + cm_elem_row(e);
                const uint grow_batch = wg_batch0 + b_col0 + c * TN + elem_col0;
                if (grow_out < p.out_rows && grow_batch < p.batch) {
                    data_out[grow_batch * p.out_rows + grow_out] =
                        sums[tile_idx * CM_ELEMS + e];
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

         %26 = OpLabel
        %135 = OpLoad %uint %gl_SubgroupInvocationID
        %137 = OpUDiv %uint %135 %uint_16
        %138 = OpLoad %uint %e
        %139 = OpIMul %uint %uint_4 %138
        %140 = OpIAdd %uint %137 %139
               OpReturnValue %140
               OpFunctionEnd

===== END FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/coopmat/k24_q4k_coopmat.spv.dis.txt =====

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/coopmat/rebuild-k24.sh =====
#!/bin/sh
# Rebuild the checked-in K24 coopmat SPIR-V artifact
# from its GLSL source, and prove the artifact carries
# the cooperative matrix ops it exists for (and does
# NOT carry the one it exists to remove).
#
# Requires glslangValidator, spirv-dis, and spirv-val
# (Vulkan SDK or distribution packages; on
# ubuntu-server all three are system tools in
# /usr/bin). The compile target is vulkan1.3: the
# coopmat extension is a 1.3-era KHR extension and the
# backend's devices are Vulkan 1.4, so 1.3 is the
# conservative floor the module is built against.
#
# The disassembly is written next to the artifact and
# checked in with it: Naga cannot validate this module
# (wgpu 27 has no coopmat IR), so the in-repo
# inspection record is part of the build's evidence.
#
# K24's structural claim is the absence of
# OpCooperativeMatrixStoreKHR: the v2 fold is
# in-register (bench/coopmat-v2-2026-11-07.md), so a
# store op in the artifact means the fold regressed
# to the K23 LDS round-trip and the rebuild fails.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

glslangValidator -V --target-env vulkan1.3 \
    -o k24_q4k_coopmat.spv k24_q4k_coopmat.comp
spirv-val k24_q4k_coopmat.spv
spirv-dis k24_q4k_coopmat.spv > k24_q4k_coopmat.spv.dis.txt

for op in OpTypeCooperativeMatrixKHR OpCooperativeMatrixLoadKHR \
          OpCooperativeMatrixMulAddKHR; do
    if ! grep -q "$op" k24_q4k_coopmat.spv.dis.txt; then
        echo "rebuild: $op missing from the disassembly" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
done
if grep -q "OpCooperativeMatrixStoreKHR" k24_q4k_coopmat.spv.dis.txt; then
    echo "rebuild: OpCooperativeMatrixStoreKHR present; the v2 fold must stay in-register" >&2
    exit 1
fi
echo "rebuild: k24_q4k_coopmat.spv OK (coopmat load/muladd present, no coopmat store)"

===== END FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/coopmat/rebuild-k24.sh =====
