===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/k19_q4k_mmv.rs =====
//! K19: the Q4_K small-batch product in llama.cpp's
//! `mul_mat_vec` register-streaming shape, built for
//! the same row band K18 serves (2..=16 batch rows) as
//! a structural counter-proposal to it.
//!
//! Why this kernel exists is a measurement, stated in
//! bench/shader-autopsy-2026-11-04.md,
//! bench/small-batch-2026-11-04.md, and
//! bench/mmv-prototype-2026-11-05.md: both of this
//! crate's earlier attempts
//! at one weight stream per dispatch (the wide MMQ,
//! K15/K16, and the small-batch MMQ, K18) stage weight
//! tiles in workgroup memory, and both stream far
//! below the GEMV rate (K18 at about 70 to 130 GB/s
//! against GEMV's up to 676 GB/s on the same tensors).
//! The shader autopsy (bench/shader-autopsy-2026-11-
//! 04.md) cleared the GEMV's compiled form and the
//! compiler with it; what the two slow kernels share
//! and the fast one lacks is the LDS weight staging.
//! llama.cpp's fast small-batch Vulkan path makes the
//! opposite choice: `mul_mat_vec` dequantizes weights
//! in registers and never stages them (sources read
//! from the server's llama.cpp tree,
//! `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/vulkan-shaders/mul_mat_vec.
//! comp` and `mul_mat_vec_base.glsl`), and its column
//! count scales with the batch (llama.cpp issue
//! #25356's dose-response: the stock NUM_COLS cap of 8
//! cliffs at batch 9, 125.0 down to 19.7 t/s; a cap of
//! 16 gives 131.5 at batch 9 and 158.5 at batch 16).
//!
//! The shape, term for term with that source:
//!
//! - The batch lives INSIDE the workgroup (llama's
//!   `NUM_COLS`), specialized as a literal in the
//!   generated shader per batch count, so the
//!   accumulator array is fully unrolled at generation
//!   time and every index is a compile-time constant:
//!   `temp[NUM_COLS][NUM_ROWS]` in the source is
//!   `acc[rows * batch]` here, one register accumulator
//!   per (output row, batch row) pair.
//! - A workgroup covers [`MmvShape::rows`] output rows
//!   (llama's `NUM_ROWS`; 2, the value ggml-vulkan
//!   picks for K-quants on RDNA3 and the tile K1 ships)
//!   times the whole batch. The weight tile a workgroup
//!   touches is those rows only, so the tensor streams
//!   from device memory once per dispatch however many
//!   batch rows ride it: the property K18 was built
//!   for, reached without its staging.
//! - Per super-block, the sixteen-thread group
//!   assignment, the packed scale extraction, and the
//!   dot math are K1's llama-family text verbatim (K1
//!   is itself a port of `mul_mat_vec_q4_k.comp`): each
//!   thread owns sixteen elements, dequantizes them
//!   into registers (four `vec4`s), and dots them
//!   against every batch row's activation quads in
//!   turn. The activations are re-read per output row
//!   from the input buffer (they are the small side:
//!   the whole batch's activations are hundreds of KB
//!   against the weight stream's GBs, and they ride
//!   the cache); the weights are loaded and
//!   dequantized exactly once per workgroup.
//! - The reduction is K1's: a segmented subgroup
//!   butterfly inside each sixteen-thread group plus a
//!   workgroup-memory finish (ggml's HYBRID mode), or
//!   a pure workgroup-memory tree where the device
//!   grants no subgroup feature. The only workgroup
//!   memory in the shader is those reduction partials,
//!   exactly the exception llama.cpp's own reduction
//!   makes (`tmpsh` in `mul_mat_vec_base.glsl`).
//! - The input is the resident f32 activation buffer
//!   itself, the GEMV's currency: no K12 quantize
//!   dispatch rides in front (K18 and the MMQ forms
//!   pay one), and the output layout is the GEMV's
//!   `[batch][out_rows]`, so a plan can swap this form
//!   for K1's without moving a byte.
//!
//! What WGSL could not carry from the GLSL source,
//! named precisely (details in the bench note):
//! llama's `temp` is indexed by specialization
//! constants (`constant_id`), which WGSL expresses
//! only as pipeline-overridable `override` values or,
//! as here, generation-time literals; and llama's K
//! loop reads its input vector through a second
//! register file of pre-loaded quads shared across
//! rows, where this port re-reads the quads per row
//! from the storage buffer and relies on the cache,
//! the same trade K1's port already made. Neither
//! changes the streaming structure; both are noted so
//! the card verdict can be read against them.
//!
//! Routing is the session's, and it is config: the
//! session prefers K19 inside the band only up to the
//! backend's `mmv_max_rows` threshold (env
//! `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS`, shipped default 16,
//! the full band, narrowed per shape by the band
//! routing table). The default shipped at 1 (off: no
//! batch qualified) under the wide-MMQ and K18
//! precedent, that an unproven kernel never enters the
//! ladder by default; the proof sequence in
//! bench/mmv-prototype-2026-11-05.md and the baseline
//! session's card verdict
//! (bench/baseline-session-2026-11-06.md leg (d))
//! discharged it, and the default moved on 2026-11-06.
//! Setting the env to 1 restores the old posture
//! exactly.

use std::cell::RefCell;
use std::collections::HashMap;

use crate::device::GpuContext;
use crate::error::{Result, WgpuError};
use crate::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::{grid_dims, K1Weights};

use crate::diag::dbg_log;

/// Elements per Q4_K super-block.
const BLOCK_ELEMS: usize = 256;

/// Batch rows one K19 dispatch covers at most: the
/// top of the small-batch band, and the column cap
/// llama.cpp's dose-response argues for (issue
/// #25356, cited in the module docs). The kernel is
/// specialized per batch count from [`MMV_MIN_BATCH`]
/// to this cap; batches past it are the GEMM ladder's,
/// not this kernel's.
pub const MMV_MAX_BATCH: u32 = 16;

/// The band's floor: one row is decode, and decode is
/// the GEMV's (llama.cpp dispatches a single column
/// through the same shader family; this crate already
/// has a proven kernel there, and the prototype's
/// question starts where the batch does).
pub const MMV_MIN_BATCH: u32 = 2;

/// The parallel shape a K19 pipeline runs: K1's
/// llama-family geometry (sixteen-thread groups over
/// super-blocks, [`Self::workgroup`] threads), with the
/// batch specialized per variant rather than carried
/// in the shape.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MmvShape {
    /// Output rows one workgroup covers (llama.cpp's
    /// NUM_ROWS).
    pub rows: u32,
    /// Threads per workgroup; a multiple of sixteen
    /// (one sixteen-thread group per super-block in
    /// flight).
    pub workgroup: u32,
    /// Reduce with the segmented subgroup butterfly
    /// (needs the device's SUBGROUP feature) instead of
    /// the pure workgroup-memory tree.
    pub subgroup: bool,
}

impl MmvShape {
    /// A shape with the given tile geometry and the
    /// workgroup-memory reduction.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn new(rows: u32, workgroup: u32) -> MmvShape {
        MmvShape {
            rows,
            workgroup,
            subgroup: false,
        }
    }

    /// This shape with the subgroup reduction.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn with_subgroup(self) -> MmvShape {
        MmvShape {
            subgroup: true,
            ..self
        }
    }

    /// The bench/check name: `r<rows>` with an `sg`
    /// suffix for the subgroup reduction.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn name(&self) -> String {
        let mut name = format!("r{}", self.rows);
        if self.subgroup {
            name.push_str("sg");
        }
        name
    }

    /// Check the shape against a device's granted
    /// features and the geometry rules, naming what is
    /// missing.
    fn validate(&self, features: wgpu::Features) -> Result<()> {
        if !(1..=4).contains(&self.rows) {
            return Err(WgpuError::Pipeline {
                detail: format!(
                    "k19 shape {}: rows per workgroup {} is outside 1..=4",
                    self.name(),
                    self.rows
                ),
            });
        }
        if self.workgroup == 0 || self.workgroup % 16 != 0 || self.workgroup > 256 {
            return Err(WgpuError::Pipeline {
                detail: format!(
                    "k19 shape {}: workgroup size {} is not a multiple of 16 in 16..=256",
                    self.name(),
                    self.workgroup
                ),
            });
        }
        if self.subgroup && !features.contains(wgpu::Features::SUBGROUP) {
            return Err(WgpuError::Pipeline {
                detail: format!(
                    "k19 shape {} needs the SUBGROUP device feature, which this device was not granted",
                    self.name()
                ),
            });
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// The shape [`K19Pipeline::new`] builds for a device
/// with the given granted features: two rows per
/// workgroup of 128 (K1's shipped geometry and
/// ggml-vulkan's K-quant choice on RDNA3), with the
/// subgroup reduction when the device grants it.
#[must_use]
pub fn shipped_shape(features: wgpu::Features) -> MmvShape {
    let base = MmvShape::new(2, 128);
    if features.contains(wgpu::Features::SUBGROUP) {
        base.with_subgroup()
    } else {
        base
    }
}

/// IEEE 754 half to f32, shared WGSL text (K1's,
/// mirroring gguf::dequant::f16_to_f32 for every value
/// a weight file can hold).
const F16_TO_F32_WGSL: &str = r#"
// IEEE 754 half to f32, mirroring gguf::dequant::f16_to_f32 for
// every value a weight file can hold (normals, subnormals, zero;
// inf and NaN payloads keep their class).
fn f16_to_f32(h: u32) -> f32 {
    let sign = (h >> 15u) & 1u;
    let exp = (h >> 10u) & 31u;
    let frac = h & 1023u;
    if (exp == 31u) {
        return bitcast<f32>((sign << 31u) | 0x7f800000u | (frac << 13u));
    }
    if (exp == 0u) {
        let v = f32(frac) * 5.960464477539063e-08;
        if (sign == 1u) { return -v; }
        return v;
    }
    return bitcast<f32>((sign << 31u) | ((exp + 112u) << 23u) | (frac << 13u));
}
"#;

/// The K19 shader for `shape` at `batch`, generated
/// with the tile geometry and the batch as literals:
/// the (row, batch) accumulator array is fully
/// unrolled at generation time, so every accumulator
/// index is a compile-time constant and the array can
/// live in registers (the structural point of the
/// prototype; a runtime-indexed local array in WGSL
/// is free to spill to function memory, which would
/// quietly rebuild the staging this kernel exists to
/// avoid). The per-thread element assignment, packed
/// scale extraction, and dot math are K1's llama-family
/// text (see the module docs).
fn mmv_shader(shape: &MmvShape, batch: u32) -> String {
    let rows = shape.rows;
    let wg = shape.workgroup;
    let groups = wg / 16;
    let slices = rows * batch;
    let partials_len = if shape.subgroup { slices * groups } else { wg };

    // The main loop's body, unrolled per output row of
    // the tile and per batch row: per row, the header,
    // the packed scale extraction, and the dequantized
    // register quads; per (row, batch), the activation
    // quads and K1's dot math into the pair's own
    // accumulator.
    let mut body = String::new();
    for r in 0..rows {
        body.push_str(&format!(
            "        {{\n            let row = row0 + {r}u;\n            if (row < params.out_rows) {{\n"
        ));
        body.push_str(
            "                let bw = (row * params.blocks_per_row + blk) * 36u;\n                let hw = weights[bw];\n                let d = f16_to_f32(hw & 0xffffu);\n                let dmin = f16_to_f32(hw >> 16u);\n                let s16 = (weights[bw + 1u] >> (16u * half)) & 0xffffu;\n                let m16 = (weights[bw + 2u] >> (16u * half)) & 0xffffu;\n                let h16 = (weights[bw + 3u] >> (16u * half)) & 0xffffu;\n                let lo = (m16 << 16u) | s16;\n                let sc_lo = vec4<f32>(unpack4xU8(lo & 0x3f3f3f3fu));\n                let hi = (((h16 << 12u) | h16) & 0x0f0f0f0fu) | ((lo & 0xc0c0c0c0u) >> 2u);\n                let sc_hi = vec4<f32>(unpack4xU8(hi));\n                let w0 = weights[bw + w0_off];\n                let w1 = weights[bw + w0_off + 16u];\n                let qa = vec4<f32>(unpack4xU8(w0 & 0x0f0f0f0fu));\n                let qb = vec4<f32>(unpack4xU8((w0 >> 4u) & 0x0f0f0f0fu));\n                let qc = vec4<f32>(unpack4xU8(w1 & 0x0f0f0f0fu));\n                let qd = vec4<f32>(unpack4xU8((w1 >> 4u) & 0x0f0f0f0fu));\n",
        );
        for b in 0..batch {
            let acc_idx = r * batch + b;
            body.push_str(&format!(
                "                {{\n                    let xb0 = ({b}u * params.blocks_per_row + blk) * 64u;\n                    let xa = input[xb0 + yv];\n                    let xbq = input[xb0 + yv + 8u];\n                    let xc = input[xb0 + yv + 32u];\n                    let xd = input[xb0 + yv + 40u];\n                    let sa = dot(xa, vec4<f32>(1.0));\n                    let sb = dot(xbq, vec4<f32>(1.0));\n                    let sc_ = dot(xc, vec4<f32>(1.0));\n                    let sd = dot(xd, vec4<f32>(1.0));\n                    acc[{acc_idx}] += d * (sc_lo.x * dot(qa, xa) + sc_lo.y * dot(qb, xbq)\n                            + sc_hi.x * dot(qc, xc) + sc_hi.y * dot(qd, xd))\n                        - dmin * (sc_lo.z * sa + sc_lo.w * sb + sc_hi.z * sc_ + sc_hi.w * sd);\n                }}\n"
            ));
        }
        body.push_str("            }\n        }\n");
    }

    // The reduction, generated per accumulator slice
    // for the same reason as the body: constant
    // indices throughout.
    let reduction = if shape.subgroup {
        let mut red = String::new();
        for s in 0..slices {
            red.push_str(&format!(
                "    {{ var v = acc[{s}]; v += subgroupShuffleXor(v, 1u); v += subgroupShuffleXor(v, 2u); v += subgroupShuffleXor(v, 4u); v += subgroupShuffleXor(v, 8u); acc[{s}] = v; }}\n"
            ));
        }
        red.push_str("    if (t == 0u) {\n");
        for s in 0..slices {
            red.push_str(&format!(
                "        partials[{idx} * {groups}u + group] = acc[{s}];\n",
                idx = s
            ));
        }
        red.push_str("    }\n    workgroupBarrier();\n    if (lane == 0u) {\n");
        for s in 0..slices {
            let r = s / batch;
            let b = s % batch;
            red.push_str(&format!(
                "        {{ var sum = 0.0; for (var g = 0u; g < {groups}u; g++) {{ sum += partials[{s} * {groups}u + g]; }} if (row0 + {r}u < params.out_rows) {{ output[{b}u * params.out_rows + row0 + {r}u] = sum; }} }}\n"
            ));
        }
        red.push_str("    }\n");
        red
    } else {
        let half_wg = wg / 2;
        let mut red = String::new();
        for s in 0..slices {
            let r = s / batch;
            let b = s % batch;
            red.push_str(&format!(
                "    partials[lane] = acc[{s}];\n    workgroupBarrier();\n    {{ var stride = {half_wg}u; while (stride > 0u) {{ if (lane < stride) {{ partials[lane] += partials[lane + stride]; }} workgroupBarrier(); stride >>= 1u; }} }}\n    if (lane == 0u && row0 + {r}u < params.out_rows) {{ output[{b}u * params.out_rows + row0 + {r}u] = partials[0]; }}\n"
            ));
        }
        red
    };

    format!(
        r#"struct Params {{
    blocks_per_row: u32,
    out_rows: u32,
    grid_x: u32,
}}

@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> weights: array<u32>;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read> input: array<vec4<f32>>;
@group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read_write> output: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(3) var<uniform> params: Params;

// Reduction partials only: the one workgroup array in
// the shader, carrying per-group (or per-lane) sums to
// the finish. No weight or activation tile is staged
// anywhere; weights dequantize in registers and the
// activations are read from the input buffer per row.
var<workgroup> partials: array<f32, {partials_len}>;
{F16_TO_F32_WGSL}
@compute @workgroup_size({wg})
fn main(@builtin(workgroup_id) wid: vec3<u32>,
        @builtin(local_invocation_id) lid: vec3<u32>) {{
    let row_groups = (params.out_rows + {rows}u - 1u) / {rows}u;
    let flat = wid.y * params.grid_x + wid.x;
    // Whole-workgroup early out: every lane shares
    // `flat`, so the exit is uniform and the barriers
    // in the reduction stay legal.
    if (flat >= row_groups) {{
        return;
    }}
    let row0 = flat * {rows}u;
    let lane = lid.x;
    let group = lane / 16u;
    let t = lane % 16u;
    let half = t / 8u;
    let l0 = 4u * (t % 8u);
    // This thread's qs words within a super-block (the
    // qs plane starts at word 4, after the four header
    // words; the second word sits 64 bytes later) and
    // its first activation quad within the block's
    // 64-quad span: K1's assignment, verbatim.
    let w0_off = 4u + 8u * half + l0 / 4u;
    let yv = 16u * half + l0 / 4u;

    var acc = array<f32, {slices}>();
    for (var blk = group; blk < params.blocks_per_row; blk += {groups}u) {{
{body}    }}
{reduction}}}
"#
    )
}

/// One prepared K19 dispatch: a bind group plus grid
/// dimensions, built once for a (weights, input,
/// output, batch) combination and encodable any number
/// of times.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct K19Call {
    pipeline: wgpu::ComputePipeline,
    bind_group: wgpu::BindGroup,
    grid: (u32, u32),
    /// Diag timestamp stamp (see `crate::timestamps`);
    /// `None` unless the context carries a recorder.
    diag: Option<crate::timestamps::DiagStamp>,
}

impl K19Call {
    /// Record this call's dispatch into `encoder`.
    pub fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut wgpu::CommandEncoder) {
        let mut pass = encoder.begin_compute_pass(&wgpu::ComputePassDescriptor {
            label: Some("k19 q4_k mmv"),
            timestamp_writes: None,
        });
        self.encode_into(&mut pass);
    }

    /// Record this dispatch into an already-open compute
    /// `pass`: the composition form the device-resident
    /// session uses to chain a whole forward into one
    /// pass.
    pub fn encode_into(&self, pass: &mut wgpu::ComputePass<'_>) {
        let slot = self.diag.as_ref().and_then(|d| d.begin(pass));
        pass.set_pipeline(&self.pipeline);
        pass.set_bind_group(0, &self.bind_group, &[]);
        pass.dispatch_workgroups(self.grid.0, self.grid.1, 1);
        if let (Some(d), Some(s)) = (&self.diag, slot) {
            d.end(pass, s);
        }
    }
}

/// The compiled K19 pipeline set: one shader variant
/// per batch count in the band, compiled lazily and
/// cached (the batch is a generation literal, so each
/// batch count is its own module; a session warms the
/// counts it will run through [`K19Pipeline::
/// precompile`] at plan time). Compilation of the
/// band-floor variant happens at construction, so a
/// WGSL defect in the family fails at backend
/// construction like every other kernel's.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct K19Pipeline {
    shape: MmvShape,
    variants: RefCell<HashMap<u32, wgpu::ComputePipeline>>,
}

impl K19Pipeline {
    /// Compile the shipped shape for `device` (see
    /// [`shipped_shape`]).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::Pipeline`] on a shape the device
    /// cannot run or a shader wgpu rejects.
    pub fn new(device: &wgpu::Device) -> Result<Self> {
        Self::with_shape(device, shipped_shape(device.features()))
    }

    /// Compile an explicit [`MmvShape`] on `device`.
    /// The shape is validated against the device's
    /// granted features first: a shape the device
    /// cannot run is a named refusal here, not a shader
    /// validation failure later.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::Pipeline`] on a shape the device
    /// cannot run or a shader wgpu rejects.
    pub fn with_shape(device: &wgpu::Device, shape: MmvShape) -> Result<Self> {
        shape.validate(device.features())?;
        let this = K19Pipeline {
            shape,
            variants: RefCell::new(HashMap::new()),
        };
        // The construction smoke check: the band-floor
        // variant compiles now, so the family's WGSL is
        // proven on this device before any plan routes
        // here.
        this.precompile(device, MMV_MIN_BATCH)?;
        dbg_log!("k19 pipeline built: shape {}", shape.name());
        Ok(this)
    }

    /// The shape this pipeline runs.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn shape(&self) -> MmvShape {
        self.shape
    }

    /// Compile (or fetch from the cache) the variant
    /// for `batch`: the session's plan builder calls
    /// this ahead of the first prepare at a batch count
    /// so Naga's translation cost stays out of the
    /// token loop, and `prepare` calls it on demand
    /// regardless.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::InvalidTensor`] when `batch` is
    /// outside the band; [`WgpuError::Pipeline`] when
    /// wgpu rejects the variant's shader.
    pub fn precompile(&self, device: &wgpu::Device, batch: u32) -> Result<()> {
        self.variant(device, batch).map(|_| ())
    }

    /// The cached variant for `batch`, compiling it on
    /// first use.
    fn variant(&self, device: &wgpu::Device, batch: u32) -> Result<wgpu::ComputePipeline> {
        if !(MMV_MIN_BATCH..=MMV_MAX_BATCH).contains(&batch) {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: "k19 call".to_string(),
                detail: format!(
                    "batch {batch} is outside {MMV_MIN_BATCH}..={MMV_MAX_BATCH} \
                     (the register-streaming small-batch band)"
                ),
            });
        }
        if let Some(p) = self.variants.borrow().get(&batch) {
            return Ok(p.clone());
        }
        let module = device.create_shader_module(wgpu::ShaderModuleDescriptor {
            label: Some("k19 q4_k mmv shader"),
            source: wgpu::ShaderSource::Wgsl(mmv_shader(&self.shape, batch).into()),
        });
        let pipeline = device.create_compute_pipeline(&wgpu::ComputePipelineDescriptor {
            label: Some("k19 q4_k mmv pipeline"),
            layout: None,
            module: &module,
            entry_point: Some("main"),
            compilation_options: wgpu::PipelineCompilationOptions::default(),
            cache: None,
        });
        dbg_log!(
            "k19 variant compiled: shape {} batch {batch}",
            self.shape.name()
        );
        self.variants.borrow_mut().insert(batch, pipeline.clone());
        Ok(pipeline)
    }

    /// Prepare a dispatch of `weights` over a batch of
    /// f32 input rows: `input` holds `batch *
    /// weights.in_features` f32 and `output` holds
    /// `batch * weights.out_rows` f32, both in the GEMV's
    /// `[batch][width]` layout, so a plan can swap this
    /// form for K1's without moving a byte.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::InvalidTensor`] when the batch is
    /// outside the band or a buffer is smaller than the
    /// geometry addresses.
    pub fn prepare(
        &self,
        ctx: &GpuContext,
        weights: &K1Weights,
        input: &wgpu::Buffer,
        output: &wgpu::Buffer,
        batch: u32,
    ) -> Result<K19Call> {
        let pipeline = self.variant(&ctx.device, batch)?;
        let need_in = u64::from(batch) * weights.in_features as u64 * 4;
        let need_out = u64::from(batch) * weights.out_rows as u64 * 4;
        if input.size() < need_in || output.size() < need_out {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: "k19 call".to_string(),
                detail: format!(
                    "buffer sizes (in {}, out {}) are below the geometry's needs \
                     ({need_in}, {need_out})",
                    input.size(),
                    output.size()
                ),
            });
        }
        let total = (weights.out_rows as u64).div_ceil(u64::from(self.shape.rows));
        let grid = grid_dims(total);
        let blocks_per_row = (weights.in_features / BLOCK_ELEMS) as u32;
        let params: [u32; 3] = [blocks_per_row, weights.out_rows as u32, grid.0];
        let param_bytes: Vec<u8> = params.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect();
        let params_buffer = ctx.device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
            label: Some("k19 params"),
            size: param_bytes.len() as u64,
            usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::UNIFORM | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
            mapped_at_creation: false,
        });
        ctx.queue.write_buffer(&params_buffer, 0, &param_bytes);
        let entries = vec![
            wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                binding: 0,
                resource: weights.buffer().as_entire_binding(),
            },
            wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                binding: 1,
                resource: input.as_entire_binding(),
            },
            wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                binding: 2,
                resource: output.as_entire_binding(),
            },
            wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                binding: 3,
                resource: params_buffer.as_entire_binding(),
            },
        ];
        let bind_group = ctx.device.create_bind_group(&wgpu::BindGroupDescriptor {
            label: Some("k19 bind group"),
            layout: &pipeline.get_bind_group_layout(0),
            entries: &entries,
        });
        Ok(K19Call {
            pipeline,
            bind_group,
            grid,
            diag: ctx.diag_stamp(crate::timestamps::DispatchMeta {
                kernel: "k19_q4k_mmv",
                rows: weights.out_rows as u64,
                cols: weights.in_features as u64,
                quant: "Q4_K",
                weight_bytes: weights.byte_len,
                shape: format!("batch={batch} grid={}x{}", grid.0, grid.1),
            }),
        })
    }

    /// Convenience one-shot: run the product over host
    /// f32 rows and read the result back. The batch is
    /// the input's row count. The check/bench data path;
    /// the resident session prepares against its own
    /// buffers instead.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::InvalidTensor`] when the input is
    /// not a whole number of rows or its row count is
    /// outside the band; [`WgpuError::Readback`] when
    /// the result cannot be mapped back.
    pub fn run(&self, ctx: &GpuContext, weights: &K1Weights, input: &[f32]) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        if input.is_empty() || input.len() % weights.in_features != 0 {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: "k19 input".to_string(),
                detail: format!(
                    "input holds {} elements, not a whole number of {}-wide rows",
                    input.len(),
                    weights.in_features
                ),
            });
        }
        let batch = (input.len() / weights.in_features) as u32;
        let input_buffer = ctx.upload_f32("k19 input", input);
        let out_elems = batch as usize * weights.out_rows;
        let output_buffer = ctx.device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
            label: Some("k19 output"),
            size: (out_elems * 4) as u64,
            usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::STORAGE | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_SRC,
            mapped_at_creation: false,
        });
        let call = self.prepare(ctx, weights, &input_buffer, &output_buffer, batch)?;
        let mut encoder = ctx
            .device
            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                label: Some("k19 run"),
            });
        call.encode(&mut encoder);
        ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
        let out = ctx.read_f32(&output_buffer, out_elems)?;
        dbg_log!(
            "k19 run: batch={batch} out_rows={} bytes_streamed={}",
            weights.out_rows,
            weights.byte_len
        );
        Ok(out)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn shape_names_and_validation() {
        assert_eq!(MmvShape::new(2, 128).name(), "r2");
        assert_eq!(MmvShape::new(2, 128).with_subgroup().name(), "r2sg");
        assert_eq!(
            shipped_shape(wgpu::Features::empty()),
            MmvShape::new(2, 128)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            shipped_shape(wgpu::Features::SUBGROUP),
            MmvShape::new(2, 128).with_subgroup()
        );
        let err = MmvShape::new(9, 128)
            .validate(wgpu::Features::all())
            .unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            err.to_string().contains("outside 1..=4"),
            "refusal names the row range: {err}"
        );
        let err = MmvShape::new(2, 100)
            .validate(wgpu::Features::all())
            .unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            err.to_string().contains("not a multiple of 16"),
            "refusal names the workgroup rule: {err}"
        );
        let err = MmvShape::new(2, 128)
            .with_subgroup()
            .validate(wgpu::Features::empty())
            .unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            err.to_string().contains("SUBGROUP"),
            "refusal names the missing feature: {err}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn band_edges_are_named_constants() {
        assert_eq!(MMV_MIN_BATCH, 2);
        assert_eq!(MMV_MAX_BATCH, 16);
    }

    #[test]
    fn shader_specializes_the_batch_and_stages_no_weights() {
        for batch in [2, 7, 16] {
            for shape in [MmvShape::new(2, 128), MmvShape::new(2, 128).with_subgroup()] {
                let shader = mmv_shader(&shape, batch);
                // The accumulator array is sized by the
                // literal slice count, and every dot
                // lands in a constant-indexed slot.
                let slices = 2 * batch;
                assert!(
                    shader.contains(&format!("array<f32, {slices}>()")),
                    "batch {batch}: accumulator array is specialized"
                );
                assert!(shader.contains(&format!("acc[{}]", slices - 1)));
                assert!(shader.contains("@workgroup_size(128)"));
                // The one workgroup array is the
                // reduction partials: no weight tile,
                // no activation tile, no staged array
                // sized by the tensor geometry.
                assert_eq!(shader.matches("var<workgroup>").count(), 1);
                assert!(shader.contains("var<workgroup> partials: array<f32,"));
                assert!(!shader.contains("w_qs"));
                assert!(!shader.contains("x_qs"));
                // K1's packed scale extraction and word
                // assignment ride along verbatim.
                assert!(shader.contains("0x3f3f3f3fu"));
                assert!(shader.contains("let w0_off = 4u + 8u * half + l0 / 4u;"));
                // The dequantized quads exist as named
                // register values.
                assert!(shader.contains("let qa = vec4<f32>(unpack4xU8(w0 & 0x0f0f0f0fu));"));
            }
        }
        // The subgroup variant shuffles inside the
        // sixteen; the tree variant never names a
        // subgroup builtin.
        let sg = mmv_shader(&MmvShape::new(2, 128).with_subgroup(), 4);
        assert!(sg.contains("subgroupShuffleXor"));
        let tree = mmv_shader(&MmvShape::new(2, 128), 4);
        assert!(!tree.contains("subgroupShuffleXor"));
        assert!(tree.contains("partials[lane] = acc[0];"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_variant_validates_under_naga() {
        // The strongest shader gate a machine with no
        // GPU adapter at all can run: every generated
        // variant (the full band, both reductions) must
        // parse and validate under Naga, the same
        // front end wgpu feeds the driver with. This
        // proves the WGSL is well-formed and well-typed;
        // it does not prove a driver's compiler accepts
        // it or keeps the accumulators in registers,
        // which is the server protocol's step 0 and
        // step 1 (bench/mmv-prototype-2026-11-05.md).
        for batch in MMV_MIN_BATCH..=MMV_MAX_BATCH {
            for shape in [MmvShape::new(2, 128), MmvShape::new(2, 128).with_subgroup()] {
                let src = mmv_shader(&shape, batch);
                let module = naga::front::wgsl::parse_str(&src).unwrap_or_else(|e| {
                    panic!(
                        "shape {} batch {batch}: WGSL parse failed: {}",
                        shape.name(),
                        e.emit_to_string(&src)
                    )
                });
                naga::valid::Validator::new(
                    naga::valid::ValidationFlags::all(),
                    naga::valid::Capabilities::all(),
                )
                .validate(&module)
                .unwrap_or_else(|e| {
                    panic!(
                        "shape {} batch {batch}: Naga validation failed: {e:?}",
                        shape.name()
                    )
                });
            }
        }
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/k1_q4k_gemv.rs =====
//! K1: Q4_K dequantize-and-multiply GEMV (BACKEND.md Section 3).
//!
//! The bulk of the decode stream: 77.3 percent of Glimmer's bytes
//! per token are Q4_K (FFN gate and up, attention Q and K
//! projections, the embedding table's rows through `proj`-shaped
//! calls). This kernel's GB/s is effectively the backend's GB/s.
//!
//! The shader reads the ggml block layout directly from the
//! tensor's raw bytes (144 bytes per 256-element super-block: f16
//! `d`, f16 `dmin`, 12 packed scale/min bytes, 128 nibble bytes),
//! expanding values in registers and never materializing a
//! dequantized weight anywhere, per BACKEND.md Section 4. The
//! dequantization arithmetic mirrors `gguf::dequant::dequant_q4_k`
//! term for term, including `get_scale_min_k4`'s 6-bit unpacking, so
//! GPU results can be checked against the CPU reference within
//! float reassociation noise.
//!
//! Two parallel shapes live here behind [`K1Shape`]:
//!
//! - The legacy shape (the first landing's v2): one workgroup of
//!   32 lanes per output row, one lane per super-block, everything
//!   as `vec4`. It measured 216.5 GB/s on the server (BACKEND.md's
//!   results section), against a 746.9 GB/s stream probe through
//!   the same stack: correct, and the baseline the tuning pass
//!   started from. The tuned llama shape below replaced it as
//!   the shipped kernel (816.5 GB/s in the tuning pass's healthy
//!   window; the full record is BACKEND.md's second
//!   BACKEND-RESULTS section).
//! - The llama shape, a port of llama.cpp's Vulkan
//!   `mul_mat_vec_q4_k.comp` structure (the shader ggml-vulkan
//!   compiles for Q4_K GEMV; sources read from the server's
//!   llama.cpp tree, `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/vulkan-shaders/`):
//!   sixteen threads cooperate on one super-block, each thread
//!   owning sixteen elements (two u32 words of nibbles, unpacked
//!   with the byte-unpack trick instead of per-element shifts);
//!   the eight sub-block scale/min pairs are extracted with
//!   llama.cpp's packed construction (three u16 lanes and two
//!   `unpack4xU8`s per thread-half) instead of twelve byte
//!   extractions; a workgroup covers several output rows so the
//!   activation quads each thread loads serve every row in the
//!   tile (llama.cpp's NUM_ROWS, which is 2 for K-quants on RDNA3
//!   per `ggml-vulkan.cpp`'s `rm_kq`); and the reduction is
//!   either a workgroup-memory tree or, when the device granted
//!   the subgroup feature, a segmented shuffle butterfly inside
//!   each sixteen-thread group plus a short shared-memory finish
//!   (ggml's HYBRID reduction mode, with the subgroup forced to
//!   the block-group width there by construction and here by the
//!   xor masks staying inside the aligned sixteen).
//!
//!   The f16 variant additionally rides the activations as
//!   `vec4<f16>` and takes the sixteen-element dot products in
//!   f16 (the packed form llama.cpp's `mul_mat_vec_q4_k_f16_f32`
//!   pipeline uses for the activation side), converting each
//!   per-sub-block dot to f32 before the scale combine, so the
//!   accumulation across blocks and the row reduction stay f32.
//!   That is strictly tighter than llama.cpp's f16 pipeline,
//!   whose running `temp` is f16 throughout; whether it holds
//!   this crate's check tolerance is a measured question, and
//!   the answer is recorded in BACKEND.md's results.
//!
//! What is deliberately NOT here: shared-memory dequant staging.
//! A GEMV consumes every dequantized value exactly once, so
//! staging weights in workgroup memory buys a barrier and a
//! round trip for zero reuse; the values that ARE reused (the
//! activation quads and their sums, across the rows of a tile)
//! already live in registers. llama.cpp's GEMV stages nothing
//! either (its shared memory carries reduction partials, as
//! here); its GEMM path is the one that stages, for reuse
//! GEMV does not have. Scale staging fails the same test: all
//! sixteen lanes extract their scale bytes in parallel in the
//! same instruction slots a single staging lane would spend
//! serially, so the packed extraction above is the cooperative
//! form of the same idea.
//!
//! The grid is two-dimensional because one dispatch dimension
//! caps at 65,535 workgroups (BACKEND.md Section 2): the flat
//! workgroup index wraps over `grid_x`, which matters for the
//! 202,048-row head class of shapes even though K1's own widest
//! tensor (FFN at 19,968 rows) fits in one dimension.

use crate::device::GpuContext;
use crate::error::{Result, WgpuError};

use crate::diag::dbg_log;

/// Elements per Q4_K super-block.
const BLOCK_ELEMS: usize = 256;
/// Bytes per Q4_K super-block.
const BLOCK_BYTES: usize = 144;
/// wgpu's per-dimension dispatch cap on this stack.
const MAX_WORKGROUPS_PER_DIM: u32 = 65_535;

/// The parallel shape a K1 pipeline runs.
///
/// The legacy shape is the first landing's kernel, kept verbatim
/// for A/B measurement. The llama shapes share one generated
/// shader family, parameterized by rows per workgroup, workgroup
/// size, the reduction, and the activation precision.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct K1Shape {
    /// Output rows one workgroup covers (llama.cpp's NUM_ROWS).
    /// Ignored by the legacy shape, which covers one row.
    pub rows: u32,
    /// Threads per workgroup; a multiple of sixteen (one
    /// sixteen-thread group per super-block in flight). Ignored
    /// by the legacy shape, which runs 32.
    pub workgroup: u32,
    /// Reduce with the segmented subgroup butterfly (needs the
    /// device's SUBGROUP feature) instead of the pure
    /// workgroup-memory tree.
    pub subgroup: bool,
    /// Ride activations as f16 and take the per-sub-block dots
    /// in f16 (needs the device's SHADER_F16 feature).
    pub f16_activations: bool,
    /// The first landing's shader, unchanged.
    pub legacy: bool,
}

impl K1Shape {
    /// The first landing's shipped shape (v2, vec4 traffic).
    pub const LEGACY: K1Shape = K1Shape {
        rows: 1,
        workgroup: 32,
        subgroup: false,
        f16_activations: false,
        legacy: true,
    };

    /// A llama-family shape with the given tile geometry and the
    /// workgroup-memory reduction, f32 activations.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn llama(rows: u32, workgroup: u32) -> K1Shape {
        K1Shape {
            rows,
            workgroup,
            subgroup: false,
            f16_activations: false,
            legacy: false,
        }
    }

    /// This shape with the subgroup reduction.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn with_subgroup(self) -> K1Shape {
        K1Shape {
            subgroup: true,
            ..self
        }
    }

    /// This shape with f16 activations.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn with_f16(self) -> K1Shape {
        K1Shape {
            f16_activations: true,
            ..self
        }
    }

    /// Whether the input buffer this shape reads holds packed
    /// f16 (two bytes per element) instead of f32.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn input_is_f16(&self) -> bool {
        self.f16_activations && !self.legacy
    }

    /// The bench/check name of this shape: `v2` for the legacy
    /// kernel, else `r<rows>` with `sg` and `f16` suffixes for
    /// the reduction and the activation precision (workgroup
    /// size is a separate bench flag, defaulting to 128).
    #[must_use]
    pub fn name(&self) -> String {
        if self.legacy {
            return "v2".to_string();
        }
        let mut name = format!("r{}", self.rows);
        if self.subgroup {
            name.push_str("sg");
        }
        if self.f16_activations {
            name.push_str("f16");
        }
        name
    }

    /// Parse a bench/check shape name (see [`K1Shape::name`]),
    /// with workgroup size 128 (llama.cpp's large-workgroup
    /// variant on this card: subgroup16 times four).
    #[must_use]
    pub fn from_name(name: &str) -> Option<K1Shape> {
        if name == "v2" {
            return Some(K1Shape::LEGACY);
        }
        let rest = name.strip_prefix('r')?;
        let (digits, suffix) = rest.split_at(
            rest.find(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_digit())
                .unwrap_or(rest.len()),
        );
        let rows: u32 = digits.parse().ok()?;
        let mut shape = K1Shape::llama(rows, 128);
        match suffix {
            "" => {}
            "sg" => shape.subgroup = true,
            "f16" => shape.f16_activations = true,
            "sgf16" => {
                shape.subgroup = true;
                shape.f16_activations = true;
            }
            _ => return None,
        }
        Some(shape)
    }

    /// Check the shape against a device's granted features and
    /// the geometry rules, naming what is missing.
    fn validate(&self, features: wgpu::Features) -> Result<()> {
        if self.legacy {
            return Ok(());
        }
        if !(1..=8).contains(&self.rows) {
            return Err(WgpuError::Pipeline {
                detail: format!(
                    "k1 shape {}: rows per workgroup {} is outside 1..=8",
                    self.name(),
                    self.rows
                ),
            });
        }
        if self.workgroup == 0 || self.workgroup % 16 != 0 || self.workgroup > 256 {
            return Err(WgpuError::Pipeline {
                detail: format!(
                    "k1 shape {}: workgroup size {} is not a multiple of 16 in 16..=256",
                    self.name(),
                    self.workgroup
                ),
            });
        }
        if self.subgroup && !features.contains(wgpu::Features::SUBGROUP) {
            return Err(WgpuError::Pipeline {
                detail: format!(
                    "k1 shape {} needs the SUBGROUP device feature, which this device was not granted",
                    self.name()
                ),
            });
        }
        if self.f16_activations && !features.contains(wgpu::Features::SHADER_F16) {
            return Err(WgpuError::Pipeline {
                detail: format!(
                    "k1 shape {} needs the SHADER_F16 device feature, which this device was not granted",
                    self.name()
                ),
            });
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// The shape [`K1Pipeline::new`] builds for a device with the
/// given granted features: the best measured shape the features
/// allow, falling back step by step to shapes that need less.
/// The measurements behind the choice are recorded in
/// BACKEND.md's BACKEND-RESULTS sections: the winner is two
/// rows per workgroup of 128 with the subgroup reduction
/// (816.5 GB/s on the server, 115 percent of llama.cpp's
/// measured 708), which is also the configuration ggml-vulkan
/// itself picks for K-quants on RDNA3 (`rm_kq` 2, large
/// workgroup, hybrid reduction). The f16 shapes are never
/// shipped: they measured slower than their f32 twins and
/// their real-tensor error (rel 5.9e-4) breaks this crate's
/// check tolerance (rel 1e-4), so they remain bench-only
/// variants behind explicit names.
#[must_use]
pub fn shipped_shape(features: wgpu::Features) -> K1Shape {
    if features.contains(wgpu::Features::SUBGROUP) {
        K1Shape::llama(2, 128).with_subgroup()
    } else {
        K1Shape::llama(2, 128)
    }
}

/// Round-to-nearest-even f32 to f16 bit pattern, for packing
/// activations for the f16 shapes. Exact inverse of
/// `gguf::dequant::f16_to_f32` up to the rounding it names.
#[must_use]
pub fn f32_to_f16_bits(x: f32) -> u16 {
    let bits = x.to_bits();
    let sign = ((bits >> 16) & 0x8000) as u16;
    let exp = ((bits >> 23) & 0xff) as i32;
    let frac = bits & 0x7f_ffff;
    if exp == 0xff {
        // Inf keeps its class; NaN becomes a quiet NaN half.
        return sign | if frac == 0 { 0x7c00 } else { 0x7e00 };
    }
    let mut e = exp - 112; // the f16 exponent field if normal
    if e >= 0x1f {
        return sign | 0x7c00; // overflow rounds to inf
    }
    if e <= 0 {
        // Subnormal half (or zero): value is m * 2^-24 with m a
        // 10-bit field; shift the 24-bit significand down with
        // round-to-nearest-even on the dropped bits.
        if e < -10 {
            return sign;
        }
        let m = frac | 0x80_0000;
        let shift = (14 - e) as u32;
        let rem = m & ((1u32 << shift) - 1);
        let halfway = 1u32 << (shift - 1);
        let mut out = m >> shift;
        if rem > halfway || (rem == halfway && (out & 1) == 1) {
            out += 1;
        }
        return sign | (out as u16);
    }
    // Normal half: drop 13 mantissa bits, round to nearest even.
    let mut kept = frac >> 13;
    let rem = frac & 0x1fff;
    if rem > 0x1000 || (rem == 0x1000 && (kept & 1) == 1) {
        kept += 1;
        if kept == 0x400 {
            kept = 0;
            e += 1;
            if e >= 0x1f {
                return sign | 0x7c00;
            }
        }
    }
    sign | ((e as u16) << 10) | (kept as u16)
}

/// Pack f32 activations as little-endian f16 bytes, the input
/// buffer layout the f16 shapes read.
#[must_use]
pub fn pack_input_f16(input: &[f32]) -> Vec<u8> {
    input
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|v| f32_to_f16_bits(*v).to_le_bytes())
        .collect()
}

/// The legacy K1 shader (v2), in WGSL. See BACKEND.md's results
/// section for its tuning history; it is kept verbatim so the
/// tuned shapes bench against the exact kernel that shipped.
const SHADER_V2: &str = r#"
struct Params {
    blocks_per_row: u32,
    out_rows: u32,
    grid_x: u32,
    batch: u32,
}

@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> weights: array<vec4<u32>>;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read> input: array<vec4<f32>>;
@group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read_write> output: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(3) var<uniform> params: Params;

var<workgroup> partials: array<f32, 32>;

// IEEE 754 half to f32, mirroring gguf::dequant::f16_to_f32 for
// every value a weight file can hold (normals, subnormals, zero;
// inf and NaN payloads keep their class).
fn f16_to_f32(h: u32) -> f32 {
    let sign = (h >> 15u) & 1u;
    let exp = (h >> 10u) & 31u;
    let frac = h & 1023u;
    if (exp == 31u) {
        return bitcast<f32>((sign << 31u) | 0x7f800000u | (frac << 13u));
    }
    if (exp == 0u) {
        // Subnormal half: value is frac * 2^-24, exact in f32.
        let v = f32(frac) * 5.960464477539063e-08;
        if (sign == 1u) { return -v; }
        return v;
    }
    return bitcast<f32>((sign << 31u) | ((exp + 112u) << 23u) | (frac << 13u));
}

// One of the 12 packed scale bytes of a super-block.
fn scale_byte(sw: array<u32, 3>, i: u32) -> u32 {
    return (sw[i / 4u] >> (8u * (i % 4u))) & 0xffu;
}

// ggml get_scale_min_k4: sub-block j's (scale, min) 6-bit pair.
fn scale_min_k4(j: u32, sw: array<u32, 3>) -> vec2<u32> {
    if (j < 4u) {
        return vec2<u32>(scale_byte(sw, j) & 63u, scale_byte(sw, j + 4u) & 63u);
    }
    return vec2<u32>(
        (scale_byte(sw, j + 4u) & 0xfu) | ((scale_byte(sw, j - 4u) >> 6u) << 4u),
        (scale_byte(sw, j + 4u) >> 4u) | ((scale_byte(sw, j) >> 6u) << 4u),
    );
}

@compute @workgroup_size(32)
fn main(@builtin(workgroup_id) wid: vec3<u32>,
        @builtin(local_invocation_id) lid: vec3<u32>) {
    let flat = wid.y * params.grid_x + wid.x;
    // Whole-workgroup early out: every lane shares `flat`, so the
    // exit is uniform and the barriers below stay legal.
    if (flat >= params.out_rows * params.batch) {
        return;
    }
    let out_row = flat % params.out_rows;
    let batch_row = flat / params.out_rows;
    let lane = lid.x;

    // One lane per super-block (striding when a row has more
    // blocks than lanes). A block is nine vec4 words: header,
    // then eight of nibbles. The activation span of a block is
    // 64 vec4s, and every output row of a batch row reads the
    // same input vector.
    let row_block0 = out_row * params.blocks_per_row;
    let x_row_base = batch_row * params.blocks_per_row * 64u;

    var acc = 0.0;
    for (var blk = lane; blk < params.blocks_per_row; blk += 32u) {
        let bw = (row_block0 + blk) * 9u;
        let hdr = weights[bw];
        let d = f16_to_f32(hdr.x & 0xffffu);
        let dmin = f16_to_f32((hdr.x >> 16u) & 0xffffu);
        let sw = array<u32, 3>(hdr.y, hdr.z, hdr.w);
        let x_base = x_row_base + blk * 64u;
        // Four groups of 64 elements. Group g's nibble bytes are
        // vec4s 2g and 2g+1 after the header; within a byte, the
        // low nibble is element l and the high nibble element
        // l + 32 of the group, exactly ggml's grouping.
        for (var grp = 0u; grp < 4u; grp++) {
            let sm1 = scale_min_k4(2u * grp, sw);
            let sm2 = scale_min_k4(2u * grp + 1u, sw);
            let d1 = d * f32(sm1.x);
            let dm1 = dmin * f32(sm1.y);
            let d2 = d * f32(sm2.x);
            let dm2 = dmin * f32(sm2.y);
            var sum_qx_lo = 0.0;
            var sum_x_lo = 0.0;
            var sum_qx_hi = 0.0;
            var sum_x_hi = 0.0;
            // A group is 32 nibble bytes in two vec4s. Byte l of
            // the group pairs with activation l (low nibble) and
            // l + 32 (high nibble). The low span of a half is 16
            // activations = 4 vec4s; the high span sits 8 vec4s
            // later. All loop bounds are literal so the compiler
            // unrolls and the vec4 loads stay single instructions.
            for (var half = 0u; half < 2u; half++) {
                let qv = weights[bw + 1u + grp * 2u + half];
                for (var c = 0u; c < 4u; c++) {
                    let word = qv[c];
                    let xv_lo = input[x_base + grp * 16u + half * 4u + c];
                    let xv_hi = input[x_base + grp * 16u + 8u + half * 4u + c];
                    for (var j = 0u; j < 4u; j++) {
                        let qbyte = (word >> (8u * j)) & 0xffu;
                        let x_lo = xv_lo[j];
                        let x_hi = xv_hi[j];
                        sum_qx_lo += f32(qbyte & 0xfu) * x_lo;
                        sum_x_lo += x_lo;
                        sum_qx_hi += f32(qbyte >> 4u) * x_hi;
                        sum_x_hi += x_hi;
                    }
                }
            }
            acc += d1 * sum_qx_lo - dm1 * sum_x_lo + d2 * sum_qx_hi - dm2 * sum_x_hi;
        }
    }

    partials[lane] = acc;
    workgroupBarrier();
    var stride = 16u;
    while (stride > 0u) {
        if (lane < stride) {
            partials[lane] += partials[lane + stride];
        }
        workgroupBarrier();
        stride >>= 1u;
    }
    if (lane == 0u) {
        output[batch_row * params.out_rows + out_row] = partials[0];
    }
}
"#;

/// Activation modes for the llama-family shader, baked in as
/// a literal at generation time: the plain GEMV, the
/// attention-gate form (the activation quads are multiplied by
/// the branch-stable sigmoid of a second input stream before
/// any dot product is taken, which is K7's gate multiply
/// folded into the projection that consumes it), and the
/// SwiGLU form (the quads become `silu(gate) * up` elementwise,
/// K7's SwiGLU folded into the down projection that consumes
/// it). Folding is exact, not approximate: the transform is
/// per-element, applied to the same f32 values K7 would have
/// read from the materialized activation buffer, with K7's
/// own expressions, and every sum the kernel takes (the dots
/// and the activation sums) is taken over the transformed
/// quads, exactly as the unfused composition computes them
/// over the transformed rows.
pub const ACT_NONE: u32 = 0;
/// Attention-gate activation: `a * sigmoid(b)`, K7's
/// branch-stable sigmoid.
pub const ACT_GATED: u32 = 1;
/// SwiGLU activation: `silu(g) * u`, K7's quotient form.
pub const ACT_SWIGLU: u32 = 2;

/// The llama-family K1 shader for `shape`, generated with the
/// tile geometry as literals so the compiler unrolls the row
/// loop and sizes the reduction arrays exactly. The body follows
/// llama.cpp's `mul_mat_vec_q4_k.comp` (cited in the module
/// docs): thread `t` of a sixteen-thread group owns elements
/// `l0..l0+3` of sub-blocks `2h`, `2h+1`, `2h+4`, `2h+5` of each
/// super-block it strides, where `h = t / 8` is the block half
/// and `l0 = 4 * (t % 8)` the byte offset within the half's
/// 64-byte span (the qs plane starts at byte 16 of the block,
/// word 4). (llama.cpp interleaves the same assignment
/// differently across its lanes; the set of (word, activation)
/// pairs per thread is identical, and consecutive lanes here
/// read consecutive words.)
///
/// The activation mode (see [`ACT_GATED`]
/// and [`ACT_SWIGLU`]). The activated variants read a second
/// input stream at binding 4, addressed by the `b_stride_elems`
/// and `b_off_elems` uniforms: stream B's row for batch row
/// `r` starts at element `r * b_stride_elems + b_off_elems`,
/// and its width equals the weights' input width, so B is
/// either a standalone activation buffer (stride = its width,
/// offset 0), a segment of a wider concatenated buffer (the
/// batched QKV layout's gate segment), or the second half of
/// a paired gate/up buffer (stride = twice the width, offset
/// = the width, binding the same buffer as stream A). Stream
/// A's own row stride is the `a_stride_blocks` uniform, which
/// the plain form sets to the weights' blocks per row and the
/// paired SwiGLU form sets to twice that.
fn llama_shader_act(shape: &K1Shape, act: u32) -> String {
    let rows = shape.rows;
    let wg = shape.workgroup;
    let groups = wg / 16;
    // Reduction scratch: the tree variant keeps one partial per
    // lane per row; the subgroup variant only the per-group sums.
    let partials_len = if shape.subgroup {
        rows * groups
    } else {
        rows * wg
    };
    let enable_f16 = if shape.f16_activations {
        "enable f16;\n"
    } else {
        ""
    };
    let input_decl = if shape.f16_activations {
        "array<vec4<f16>>"
    } else {
        "array<vec4<f32>>"
    };
    // Per-sub-block dot products and activation sums, in the
    // activation precision, named for the four sub-blocks this
    // thread owns (A and B from the first qs word's low and high
    // nibbles, C and D from the second word's).
    let dot_math = if shape.f16_activations {
        r#"
            let qa = vec4<f16>(unpack4xU8(w0 & 0x0f0f0f0fu));
            let qb = vec4<f16>(unpack4xU8((w0 >> 4u) & 0x0f0f0f0fu));
            let qc = vec4<f16>(unpack4xU8(w1 & 0x0f0f0f0fu));
            let qd = vec4<f16>(unpack4xU8((w1 >> 4u) & 0x0f0f0f0fu));
            acc[r] += d * (sc_lo.x * f32(dot(qa, xa)) + sc_lo.y * f32(dot(qb, xbq))
                         + sc_hi.x * f32(dot(qc, xc)) + sc_hi.y * f32(dot(qd, xd)))
                    - dmin * (sc_lo.z * f32(sa) + sc_lo.w * f32(sb)
                            + sc_hi.z * f32(sc_) + sc_hi.w * f32(sd));"#
    } else {
        r#"
            let qa = vec4<f32>(unpack4xU8(w0 & 0x0f0f0f0fu));
            let qb = vec4<f32>(unpack4xU8((w0 >> 4u) & 0x0f0f0f0fu));
            let qc = vec4<f32>(unpack4xU8(w1 & 0x0f0f0f0fu));
            let qd = vec4<f32>(unpack4xU8((w1 >> 4u) & 0x0f0f0f0fu));
            acc[r] += d * (sc_lo.x * dot(qa, xa) + sc_lo.y * dot(qb, xbq)
                         + sc_hi.x * dot(qc, xc) + sc_hi.y * dot(qd, xd))
                    - dmin * (sc_lo.z * sa + sc_lo.w * sb
                            + sc_hi.z * sc_ + sc_hi.w * sd);"#
    };
    let one = if shape.f16_activations {
        "vec4<f16>(1.0h)"
    } else {
        "vec4<f32>(1.0)"
    };
    let reduction = if shape.subgroup {
        format!(
            r#"
    // Segmented butterfly inside each sixteen-thread group
    // (the xor masks never cross the aligned sixteen, so each
    // group reduces its own partials inside whatever hardware
    // subgroup width the device runs), then one shared-memory
    // finish across groups: ggml's HYBRID reduction.
    for (var r = 0u; r < {rows}u; r++) {{
        var v = acc[r];
        v += subgroupShuffleXor(v, 1u);
        v += subgroupShuffleXor(v, 2u);
        v += subgroupShuffleXor(v, 4u);
        v += subgroupShuffleXor(v, 8u);
        acc[r] = v;
    }}
    if (t == 0u) {{
        for (var r = 0u; r < {rows}u; r++) {{
            partials[r * {groups}u + group] = acc[r];
        }}
    }}
    workgroupBarrier();
    if (lane == 0u) {{
        for (var r = 0u; r < {rows}u; r++) {{
            if (row0 + r < params.out_rows) {{
                var s = 0.0;
                for (var g = 0u; g < {groups}u; g++) {{
                    s += partials[r * {groups}u + g];
                }}
                output[batch_row * params.out_rows + row0 + r] = s;
            }}
        }}
    }}"#
        )
    } else {
        format!(
            r#"
    for (var r = 0u; r < {rows}u; r++) {{
        partials[r * {wg}u + lane] = acc[r];
    }}
    workgroupBarrier();
    var stride = {half_wg}u;
    while (stride > 0u) {{
        if (lane < stride) {{
            for (var r = 0u; r < {rows}u; r++) {{
                partials[r * {wg}u + lane] += partials[r * {wg}u + lane + stride];
            }}
        }}
        workgroupBarrier();
        stride >>= 1u;
    }}
    if (lane == 0u) {{
        for (var r = 0u; r < {rows}u; r++) {{
            if (row0 + r < params.out_rows) {{
                output[batch_row * params.out_rows + row0 + r] = partials[r * {wg}u];
            }}
        }}
    }}"#,
            half_wg = wg / 2
        )
    };

    // The activation fusion's pieces, empty for the plain
    // GEMV: a second input binding with K7's exact scalar
    // forms, the per-component apply over a quad, and the
    // transform block that rewrites the loaded quads before
    // any sum is taken over them.
    let act_decls = if act == ACT_NONE {
        ""
    } else {
        r#"
@group(0) @binding(4) var<storage, read> input_b: array<vec4<f32>>;

// Logistic sigmoid, K7's branch-stable form (cpu-compute's):
// the exponential's argument is never positive.
fn sigmoid1(x: f32) -> f32 {
    if (x >= 0.0) {
        return 1.0 / (1.0 + exp(-x));
    }
    let e = exp(x);
    return e / (1.0 + e);
}
"#
    };
    let act_apply = match act {
        ACT_GATED => {
            r#"
fn act_apply(a: vec4<f32>, b: vec4<f32>) -> vec4<f32> {
    return vec4<f32>(a.x * sigmoid1(b.x), a.y * sigmoid1(b.y),
                     a.z * sigmoid1(b.z), a.w * sigmoid1(b.w));
}
"#
        }
        ACT_SWIGLU => {
            r#"
// SiLU, K7's quotient form: x * sigmoid(x) as the single
// quotient the reference computes.
fn silu1(x: f32) -> f32 {
    return x / (1.0 + exp(-x));
}

fn act_apply(g: vec4<f32>, u: vec4<f32>) -> vec4<f32> {
    return vec4<f32>(silu1(g.x) * u.x, silu1(g.y) * u.y,
                     silu1(g.z) * u.z, silu1(g.w) * u.w);
}
"#
        }
        _ => "",
    };
    let decl = if act == ACT_NONE { "let" } else { "var" };
    let act_transform = if act == ACT_NONE {
        ""
    } else {
        r#"        let bb0 = (batch_row * params.b_stride_elems + params.b_off_elems) / 4u + blk * 64u;
        xa = act_apply(xa, input_b[bb0 + yv]);
        xbq = act_apply(xbq, input_b[bb0 + yv + 8u]);
        xc = act_apply(xc, input_b[bb0 + yv + 32u]);
        xd = act_apply(xd, input_b[bb0 + yv + 40u]);
"#
    };

    format!(
        r#"{enable_f16}struct Params {{
    blocks_per_row: u32,
    out_rows: u32,
    grid_x: u32,
    batch: u32,
    a_stride_blocks: u32,
    b_stride_elems: u32,
    b_off_elems: u32,
}}

@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> weights: array<u32>;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read> input: {input_decl};
@group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read_write> output: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(3) var<uniform> params: Params;
{act_decls}{act_apply}

var<workgroup> partials: array<f32, {partials_len}>;

// IEEE 754 half to f32, mirroring gguf::dequant::f16_to_f32 for
// every value a weight file can hold (normals, subnormals, zero;
// inf and NaN payloads keep their class).
fn f16_to_f32(h: u32) -> f32 {{
    let sign = (h >> 15u) & 1u;
    let exp = (h >> 10u) & 31u;
    let frac = h & 1023u;
    if (exp == 31u) {{
        return bitcast<f32>((sign << 31u) | 0x7f800000u | (frac << 13u));
    }}
    if (exp == 0u) {{
        let v = f32(frac) * 5.960464477539063e-08;
        if (sign == 1u) {{ return -v; }}
        return v;
    }}
    return bitcast<f32>((sign << 31u) | ((exp + 112u) << 23u) | (frac << 13u));
}}

@compute @workgroup_size({wg})
fn main(@builtin(workgroup_id) wid: vec3<u32>,
        @builtin(local_invocation_id) lid: vec3<u32>) {{
    let row_groups = (params.out_rows + {rows}u - 1u) / {rows}u;
    let flat = wid.y * params.grid_x + wid.x;
    // Whole-workgroup early out: every lane shares `flat`, so
    // the exit is uniform and the barriers below stay legal.
    if (flat >= params.batch * row_groups) {{
        return;
    }}
    let batch_row = flat / row_groups;
    let row0 = (flat % row_groups) * {rows}u;
    let lane = lid.x;
    let group = lane / 16u;
    let t = lane % 16u;
    let half = t / 8u;
    let l0 = 4u * (t % 8u);
    // This thread's qs words within a super-block (the qs plane
    // starts at word 4, after the four header words; the second
    // word sits 64 bytes later) and its first activation quad
    // within the block's 64-quad span.
    let w0_off = 4u + 8u * half + l0 / 4u;
    let yv = 16u * half + l0 / 4u;

    var acc = array<f32, {rows}>();
    for (var blk = group; blk < params.blocks_per_row; blk += {groups}u) {{
        // Activation quads and their sums are per-block, shared
        // by every row of the tile: loaded once, used {rows}
        // times. A pairs with sub-block 2h, B with 2h+1 (the
        // first word's high nibbles, 32 elements later), C and
        // D with 2h+4 and 2h+5 (the second word, 128 later).
        let xb0 = (batch_row * params.a_stride_blocks + blk) * 64u;
        {decl} xa = input[xb0 + yv];
        {decl} xbq = input[xb0 + yv + 8u];
        {decl} xc = input[xb0 + yv + 32u];
        {decl} xd = input[xb0 + yv + 40u];
{act_transform}        let sa = dot(xa, {one});
        let sb = dot(xbq, {one});
        let sc_ = dot(xc, {one});
        let sd = dot(xd, {one});
        for (var r = 0u; r < {rows}u; r++) {{
            let row = row0 + r;
            if (row >= params.out_rows) {{
                continue;
            }}
            let bw = (row * params.blocks_per_row + blk) * 36u;
            let hw = weights[bw];
            let d = f16_to_f32(hw & 0xffffu);
            let dmin = f16_to_f32(hw >> 16u);
            // llama.cpp's packed scale extraction
            // (mul_mat_vec_q4_k.comp): the three u16 lanes of
            // the scale bytes for this thread's half, combined
            // into (scaleA, scaleB, minA, minB) and (scaleC,
            // scaleD, minC, minD) with two byte unpacks. The
            // values equal get_scale_min_k4(2h), (2h+1), (2h+4),
            // (2h+5) exactly; the packing is the point.
            let s16 = (weights[bw + 1u] >> (16u * half)) & 0xffffu;
            let m16 = (weights[bw + 2u] >> (16u * half)) & 0xffffu;
            let h16 = (weights[bw + 3u] >> (16u * half)) & 0xffffu;
            let lo = (m16 << 16u) | s16;
            let sc_lo = vec4<f32>(unpack4xU8(lo & 0x3f3f3f3fu));
            let hi = (((h16 << 12u) | h16) & 0x0f0f0f0fu) | ((lo & 0xc0c0c0c0u) >> 2u);
            let sc_hi = vec4<f32>(unpack4xU8(hi));
            let w0 = weights[bw + w0_off];
            let w1 = weights[bw + w0_off + 16u];
            {dot_math}
        }}
    }}
{reduction}
}}
"#
    )
}

/// Grid dimensions `(x, y)` for `total` workgroups under the
/// per-dimension cap: x takes as many as it may, y takes the rest,
/// and the shader recovers the flat index as `y * grid_x + x`.
#[must_use]
pub fn grid_dims(total: u64) -> (u32, u32) {
    if total == 0 {
        return (0, 0);
    }
    let x = total.min(u64::from(MAX_WORKGROUPS_PER_DIM)) as u32;
    let y = total.div_ceil(u64::from(x));
    (x, y.min(u64::from(u32::MAX)) as u32)
}

/// A contiguous row window into a projection's input and
/// output buffers, in bytes: a windowed GEMV prepare
/// ([`K1Pipeline::prepare_rows`] and its K2/K3 siblings)
/// binds exactly this window, so the kernel's row 0 is the
/// window's first row and its batch is the window's row
/// count. The window changes only which rows a dispatch
/// covers; the per-row math is the shipped kernel's,
/// untouched.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct RowWindow {
    /// First row of the window within the caller's buffers.
    pub first_row: u32,
    /// Byte offset of the window's first input row.
    pub in_offset: u64,
    /// Byte length of the window's input rows.
    pub in_bytes: u64,
    /// Byte offset of the window's first output row.
    pub out_offset: u64,
    /// Byte length of the window's output rows.
    pub out_bytes: u64,
}

impl RowWindow {
    /// The input binding for this window: the buffer from
    /// the window's offset, for exactly the window's bytes.
    pub fn in_binding<'a>(&self, buffer: &'a wgpu::Buffer) -> wgpu::BindingResource<'a> {
        wgpu::BindingResource::Buffer(wgpu::BufferBinding {
            buffer,
            offset: self.in_offset,
            size: std::num::NonZeroU64::new(self.in_bytes),
        })
    }

    /// The output binding for this window (see
    /// [`RowWindow::in_binding`]).
    pub fn out_binding<'a>(&self, buffer: &'a wgpu::Buffer) -> wgpu::BindingResource<'a> {
        wgpu::BindingResource::Buffer(wgpu::BufferBinding {
            buffer,
            offset: self.out_offset,
            size: std::num::NonZeroU64::new(self.out_bytes),
        })
    }

    /// The diag shape suffix naming the window's first
    /// row, so a chunked dispatch is distinguishable from
    /// a whole-batch one in the timestamp report.
    pub fn stamp_suffix(&self) -> String {
        format!(" win@{}", self.first_row)
    }
}

/// Resolve and validate a row window over a projection's
/// buffers: rows `row_start..row_start + rows` of a tensor
/// with `in_features` input elements per row (at
/// `in_elem_bytes` bytes each) and `out_rows` f32 outputs
/// per row, inside `input` and `output`. Shared by the
/// three GEMV pipelines' windowed prepares.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// [`WgpuError::InvalidTensor`] naming `name` when the
/// window is empty, when it runs past either buffer, or
/// when a window offset is not a multiple of the device's
/// minimum storage-binding offset alignment (a window is
/// a buffer binding, so its offsets carry the binding
/// alignment rule; geometries whose row stride is not a
/// multiple of it cannot be windowed and refuse here, by
/// name, for the caller's fallback to serve whole).
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
pub fn resolve_row_window(
    device: &wgpu::Device,
    name: &str,
    in_features: usize,
    in_elem_bytes: u64,
    out_rows: usize,
    input: &wgpu::Buffer,
    output: &wgpu::Buffer,
    row_start: u32,
    rows: u32,
) -> Result<RowWindow> {
    if rows == 0 {
        return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
            name: format!("{name} call"),
            detail: "row window is empty".to_string(),
        });
    }
    let in_row = in_features as u64 * in_elem_bytes;
    let out_row = out_rows as u64 * 4;
    let end = u64::from(row_start) + u64::from(rows);
    if end * in_row > input.size() || end * out_row > output.size() {
        return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
            name: format!("{name} call"),
            detail: format!(
                "row window {row_start}..{end} runs past the buffers \
                 (input {} bytes at {in_row} per row, output {} bytes at {out_row} per row)",
                input.size(),
                output.size()
            ),
        });
    }
    let align = u64::from(device.limits().min_storage_buffer_offset_alignment);
    let in_offset = u64::from(row_start) * in_row;
    let out_offset = u64::from(row_start) * out_row;
    if in_offset % align != 0 || out_offset % align != 0 {
        return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
            name: format!("{name} call"),
            detail: format!(
                "row window at row {row_start} has binding offsets \
                 (input {in_offset}, output {out_offset}) that are not multiples \
                 of the device's {align}-byte storage binding alignment"
            ),
        });
    }
    Ok(RowWindow {
        first_row: row_start,
        in_offset,
        in_bytes: u64::from(rows) * in_row,
        out_offset,
        out_bytes: u64::from(rows) * out_row,
    })
}

/// A Q4_K weight tensor resident on the device: one storage buffer
/// holding the tensor's raw GGUF bytes, bound whole per dispatch
/// (BACKEND.md Section 5's per-tensor buffer strategy).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct K1Weights {
    /// Whole-tensor byte length, for the bench's stream accounting.
    pub byte_len: u64,
    /// Input width (elements per row); a whole number of blocks.
    pub in_features: usize,
    /// Output rows.
    pub out_rows: usize,
    buffer: wgpu::Buffer,
}

impl K1Weights {
    /// The resident device buffer holding the tensor's raw
    /// bytes, for the sibling kernel that consumes the same
    /// upload through its own pipelines (K10, the Q4_K GEMM:
    /// a model's weights live on the device exactly once, in
    /// whichever form the session uploaded them, and both the
    /// GEMV and the GEMM bind that one buffer).
    pub(crate) fn buffer(&self) -> &wgpu::Buffer {
        &self.buffer
    }
}

/// Stream geometry for an activation dispatch (see
/// [`K1Pipeline::prepare_act`]): element strides and the
/// second stream's segment offset, all in elements and all
/// whole Q4_K blocks.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct K1ActGeom {
    /// Row stride of stream A, in elements.
    pub a_stride_elems: usize,
    /// Row stride of stream B, in elements.
    pub b_stride_elems: usize,
    /// Element offset of stream B's segment within its row.
    pub b_off_elems: usize,
}

/// One prepared K1 dispatch set: a bind group plus grid dimensions,
/// built once for a (weights, input, output, batch) combination and
/// encodable any number of times. The bench encodes the same call
/// repeatedly; `run` encodes it once.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct K1Call {
    pipeline: wgpu::ComputePipeline,
    bind_group: wgpu::BindGroup,
    grid: (u32, u32),
    /// Diag timestamp stamp (see `crate::timestamps`); `None`
    /// unless the context carries a recorder.
    diag: Option<crate::timestamps::DiagStamp>,
}

impl K1Call {
    /// Record this call's dispatch into `encoder`.
    pub fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut wgpu::CommandEncoder) {
        let mut pass = encoder.begin_compute_pass(&wgpu::ComputePassDescriptor {
            label: Some("k1 q4_k gemv"),
            timestamp_writes: None,
        });
        self.encode_into(&mut pass);
    }

    /// Record this dispatch into an already-open compute
    /// `pass`: the composition form the device-resident
    /// session uses to chain a whole forward into one pass
    /// per segment (wgpu inserts the hazard barriers
    /// between dispatches inside the pass).
    pub fn encode_into(&self, pass: &mut wgpu::ComputePass<'_>) {
        let slot = self.diag.as_ref().and_then(|d| d.begin(pass));
        pass.set_pipeline(&self.pipeline);
        pass.set_bind_group(0, &self.bind_group, &[]);
        pass.dispatch_workgroups(self.grid.0, self.grid.1, 1);
        if let (Some(d), Some(s)) = (&self.diag, slot) {
            d.end(pass, s);
        }
    }
}

/// The compiled K1 pipeline, in one [`K1Shape`] and one
/// activation mode. Compilation happens once, at backend
/// construction, so Naga translation cost stays out of the
/// token loop (BACKEND.md Section 4).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct K1Pipeline {
    pipeline: wgpu::ComputePipeline,
    shape: K1Shape,
    act: u32,
}

impl K1Pipeline {
    /// Compile the shipped shape for `device` (see
    /// [`shipped_shape`]: the best measured shape the device's
    /// granted features allow).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::Pipeline`] if wgpu rejects the module or the
    /// pipeline. (wgpu reports shader errors through its error
    /// handling rather than a return value on some paths; the
    /// crate's conformance tests compile this pipeline on whatever
    /// adapter a machine offers, which is where a WGSL defect
    /// would surface first.)
    pub fn new(device: &wgpu::Device) -> Result<Self> {
        Self::with_shape(device, shipped_shape(device.features()))
    }

    /// Compile an explicit [`K1Shape`] on `device`. The shape is
    /// validated against the device's granted features first: a
    /// shape the device cannot run is a named refusal here, not
    /// a shader validation failure later.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::Pipeline`] on a shape the device cannot run
    /// or a shader wgpu rejects.
    pub fn with_shape(device: &wgpu::Device, shape: K1Shape) -> Result<Self> {
        Self::with_shape_act(device, shape, ACT_NONE)
    }

    /// Compile an explicit [`K1Shape`] with an activation mode
    /// (see [`ACT_GATED`] and [`ACT_SWIGLU`]): the fused form
    /// that applies K7's elementwise math to the activation
    /// quads inside the GEMV. Activation modes exist only for
    /// the llama family with f32 activations: the legacy shader
    /// is kept verbatim, and the f16 shapes' dots are taken in
    /// f16, where an f32 elementwise stage has no exact place.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::Pipeline`] on a shape the device cannot run,
    /// an unknown activation mode, or a mode combined with the
    /// legacy or f16-activation shapes.
    pub fn with_shape_act(device: &wgpu::Device, shape: K1Shape, act: u32) -> Result<Self> {
        shape.validate(device.features())?;
        if act > ACT_SWIGLU {
            return Err(WgpuError::Pipeline {
                detail: format!("k1 activation mode {act} is not one this kernel defines"),
            });
        }
        if act != ACT_NONE && (shape.legacy || shape.f16_activations) {
            return Err(WgpuError::Pipeline {
                detail: format!(
                    "k1 activation mode {act} needs the llama family with f32 activations; \
                     shape {} does not qualify",
                    shape.name()
                ),
            });
        }
        let source: String = if shape.legacy {
            SHADER_V2.to_string()
        } else {
            llama_shader_act(&shape, act)
        };
        let module = device.create_shader_module(wgpu::ShaderModuleDescriptor {
            label: Some("k1 q4_k gemv shader"),
            source: wgpu::ShaderSource::Wgsl(source.into()),
        });
        let pipeline = device.create_compute_pipeline(&wgpu::ComputePipelineDescriptor {
            label: Some("k1 q4_k gemv pipeline"),
            layout: None,
            module: &module,
            entry_point: Some("main"),
            compilation_options: wgpu::PipelineCompilationOptions::default(),
            cache: None,
        });
        dbg_log!("k1 pipeline built: shape {} act {act}", shape.name());
        Ok(K1Pipeline {
            pipeline,
            shape,
            act,
        })
    }

    /// The shape this pipeline runs.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn shape(&self) -> K1Shape {
        self.shape
    }

    /// The activation mode this pipeline runs ([`ACT_NONE`],
    /// [`ACT_GATED`], or [`ACT_SWIGLU`]).
    #[must_use]
    pub fn act(&self) -> u32 {
        self.act
    }

    /// Upload a Q4_K tensor's raw bytes into a fresh device buffer.
    /// The geometry is validated against the bytes before anything
    /// is uploaded: a mismatch is a refusal naming the tensor,
    /// never a truncated or padded upload.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::InvalidTensor`] on any geometry or byte-count
    /// disagreement; [`WgpuError::LimitShortfall`] through
    /// [`GpuContext::check_tensor_fits`] when the device cannot
    /// hold or bind the tensor whole.
    pub fn upload(
        &self,
        ctx: &GpuContext,
        name: &str,
        bytes: &[u8],
        in_features: usize,
        out_rows: usize,
    ) -> Result<K1Weights> {
        if in_features == 0 || in_features % BLOCK_ELEMS != 0 {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: name.to_string(),
                detail: format!(
                    "input width {in_features} is not a positive whole number of {BLOCK_ELEMS}-element Q4_K blocks"
                ),
            });
        }
        if out_rows == 0 {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: name.to_string(),
                detail: "output row count is zero".to_string(),
            });
        }
        let expected = (in_features / BLOCK_ELEMS) * BLOCK_BYTES * out_rows;
        if bytes.len() != expected {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: name.to_string(),
                detail: format!(
                    "tensor holds {} bytes but [{in_features}, {out_rows}] of Q4_K needs {expected}",
                    bytes.len()
                ),
            });
        }
        ctx.check_tensor_fits(name, bytes.len() as u64)?;
        let buffer = ctx.device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
            label: Some(name),
            size: bytes.len() as u64,
            usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::STORAGE | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
            mapped_at_creation: false,
        });
        ctx.queue.write_buffer(&buffer, 0, bytes);
        dbg_log!(
            "k1 upload {name}: {} bytes [{in_features} x {out_rows}]",
            bytes.len()
        );
        Ok(K1Weights {
            byte_len: bytes.len() as u64,
            in_features,
            out_rows,
            buffer,
        })
    }

    /// Upload several Q4_K tensors that share an input width
    /// into ONE device buffer, concatenated along the output
    /// rows: a single dispatch over the concatenated weights
    /// computes every part's rows, because the kernel addresses
    /// weights by output row and knows nothing of tensor
    /// boundaries. Each output row's arithmetic is the row's
    /// own standalone dispatch's, unchanged; what the caller
    /// saves is the dispatch count (the batched QKV and gate+up
    /// projections of the resident forward). Each part is
    /// `(raw bytes, in_features, out_rows)` and validated
    /// exactly as [`K1Pipeline::upload`] validates.
    ///
