//! K4: RMSNorm fused with the residual add (BACKEND.md Section 3).
//!
//! The bytes are trivial (the 6,656-wide hidden vector, twice per
//! layer); the point is fusion, so the hidden vector is not
//! re-read from VRAM between the residual add and the norm. One
//! shader, mode-selected by a uniform, covers every norm the
//! forward calls:
//!
//! - **Weighted** ([`K4Pipeline::rms_norm`]): `x / sqrt(mean(x^2) +
//!   eps) * w`, plain `x * w` scaling. This is the pre norms (at
//!   the file's eps), the per-head Q and K norms (width = head
//!   dim, rows = positions times heads), and the final norm.
//! - **Plain** ([`K4Pipeline::rms_norm_plain`]): the weightless
//!   form the reference graph applies to the embedding output
//!   before layer 0 (src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp: build_norm with
//!   a null weight). A distinct mode, not a ones weight the
//!   caller would have to invent, mirroring the trait.
//! - **Weighted + residual** ([`K4Pipeline::norm_residual`]): the
//!   fused post-norm step, `residual + norm(branch)`, the shape
//!   BACKEND.md's fusion note describes: the branch output is
//!   normalized (at the reference graph's hardcoded post-norm eps
//!   1e-8, passed in as `eps` like every other value here) and the
//!   untouched residual is added in the same pass. The `Compute`
//!   trait hands the forward separate `rms_norm` and `add` steps,
//!   so the trait path composes the two halves of this module;
//!   the fused entry point is the one a device-resident forward
//!   calls, and it is proven against that composition in the
//!   crate's tests.
//!
//! The residual add also lives here as its own tiny kernel
//! ([`K4Pipeline::add`]): BACKEND.md names K4 "RMSNorm fused with
//! residual add", so the add is this module's second half, not a
//! kernel of its own.
//!
//! Numerical note: the CPU reference accumulates the mean of
//! squares in f64; this kernel accumulates in f32 across the
//! workgroup. The difference is reassociation-class noise, far
//! below the cross-backend tolerance the crate's tests assert,
//! and it is stated here rather than hidden.

use crate::device::GpuContext;
use crate::error::{Result, WgpuError};

use crate::diag::dbg_log;

/// Threads per workgroup: one workgroup normalizes one row,
/// lanes striding over the row's channels.
const WORKGROUP: u32 = 256;

/// The norm shader. `mode`: 0 weighted, 1 plain (weightless),
/// 2 weighted with the residual added. The weight and residual
/// bindings are always present; modes that do not read them bind
/// a one-element dummy buffer instead.
const NORM_SHADER: &str = r#"
struct Params {
    width: u32,
    total_rows: u32,
    grid_x: u32,
    mode: u32,
    eps: f32,
}

@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> x: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read> weight: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read> residual: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(3) var<storage, read_write> out: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(4) var<uniform> params: Params;

var<workgroup> partials: array<f32, 256>;
var<workgroup> inv_rms_shared: f32;

@compute @workgroup_size(256)
fn norm_main(@builtin(workgroup_id) wid: vec3<u32>,
             @builtin(local_invocation_id) lid: vec3<u32>) {
    let row = wid.y * params.grid_x + wid.x;
    // Whole-workgroup early out: every lane shares `row`, so the
    // exit is uniform and the barriers below stay legal.
    if (row >= params.total_rows) {
        return;
    }
    let lane = lid.x;
    let base = row * params.width;

    var ss = 0.0;
    for (var i = lane; i < params.width; i += 256u) {
        let v = x[base + i];
        ss += v * v;
    }
    partials[lane] = ss;
    workgroupBarrier();
    var stride = 128u;
    while (stride > 0u) {
        if (lane < stride) {
            partials[lane] += partials[lane + stride];
        }
        workgroupBarrier();
        stride >>= 1u;
    }
    if (lane == 0u) {
        inv_rms_shared = inverseSqrt(partials[0] / f32(params.width) + params.eps);
    }
    workgroupBarrier();
    let inv = inv_rms_shared;

    for (var i = lane; i < params.width; i += 256u) {
        var y = x[base + i] * inv;
        if (params.mode != 1u) {
            y = y * weight[i];
        }
        if (params.mode == 2u) {
            y = residual[base + i] + y;
        }
        out[base + i] = y;
    }
}
"#;

/// The residual add shader: one thread per element.
const ADD_SHADER: &str = r#"
struct AddParams {
    n: u32,
    grid_x: u32,
}

@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> a: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read> b: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read_write> out: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(3) var<uniform> params: AddParams;

@compute @workgroup_size(256)
fn add_main(@builtin(workgroup_id) wid: vec3<u32>,
            @builtin(local_invocation_id) lid: vec3<u32>) {
    let flat = (wid.y * params.grid_x + wid.x) * 256u + lid.x;
    if (flat < params.n) {
        out[flat] = a[flat] + b[flat];
    }
}
"#;

/// Mode values for the norm shader's `mode` uniform.
mod mode {
    pub const WEIGHTED: u32 = 0;
    pub const PLAIN: u32 = 1;
    pub const WEIGHTED_RESIDUAL: u32 = 2;
}

/// The chain shader: two norm stages and the residual add
/// between them in ONE dispatch, the fusion the resident
/// forward's half-layer boundaries call for. Stage one is the
/// fused post-norm (`stream = residual + norm(branch) *
/// w_post`, at the post-norm eps); stage two is the next
/// pre-norm over the result (`h = norm(stream) * w_pre`, at
/// the file eps). The two stages chain with nothing between
/// them in the forward, and fusing them is exact: the lane
/// keeps its strided share of the intermediate row in
/// registers between the stages, so stage two reduces over
/// precisely the f32 values stage one wrote (it writes them
/// to `out_stream` in the same pass, for the consumers that
/// need the stream itself). Each stage's reduction is the
/// norm shader's own distribution and partials tree, and each
/// stage's per-element math is its mode's, term for term.
///
/// The register residency bounds the width: a lane holds
/// `ceil(width / 256)` elements, capped at 32, so widths up
/// to 8192 chain (the real hidden width is 6656, 26 per
/// lane); wider rows refuse by name at prepare time.
const CHAIN_SHADER: &str = r#"
struct ChainParams {
    width: u32,
    total_rows: u32,
    grid_x: u32,
    eps_post: f32,
    eps_pre: f32,
}

@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> residual: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read> branch: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read> w_post: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(3) var<storage, read> w_pre: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(4) var<storage, read_write> out_stream: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(5) var<storage, read_write> out_normed: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(6) var<uniform> params: ChainParams;

var<workgroup> partials: array<f32, 256>;
var<workgroup> inv_shared: f32;

@compute @workgroup_size(256)
fn chain_main(@builtin(workgroup_id) wid: vec3<u32>,
              @builtin(local_invocation_id) lid: vec3<u32>) {
    let row = wid.y * params.grid_x + wid.x;
    // Whole-workgroup early out: every lane shares `row`, so
    // the exit is uniform and the barriers below stay legal.
    if (row >= params.total_rows) {
        return;
    }
    let lane = lid.x;
    let base = row * params.width;

    // Stage one's reduction over the branch row.
    var ss = 0.0;
    for (var i = lane; i < params.width; i += 256u) {
        let v = branch[base + i];
        ss += v * v;
    }
    partials[lane] = ss;
    workgroupBarrier();
    var stride = 128u;
    while (stride > 0u) {
        if (lane < stride) {
            partials[lane] += partials[lane + stride];
        }
        workgroupBarrier();
        stride >>= 1u;
    }
    if (lane == 0u) {
        inv_shared = inverseSqrt(partials[0] / f32(params.width) + params.eps_post);
    }
    workgroupBarrier();
    let inv_post = inv_shared;

    // The intermediate row: written to the stream output and
    // kept in registers for stage two's reduction.
    var s_vals: array<f32, 32>;
    var ss2 = 0.0;
    var n = 0u;
    for (var i = lane; i < params.width; i += 256u) {
        var y = branch[base + i] * inv_post;
        y = y * w_post[i];
        let s = residual[base + i] + y;
        s_vals[n] = s;
        out_stream[base + i] = s;
        ss2 += s * s;
        n += 1u;
    }
    partials[lane] = ss2;
    workgroupBarrier();
    stride = 128u;
    while (stride > 0u) {
        if (lane < stride) {
            partials[lane] += partials[lane + stride];
        }
        workgroupBarrier();
        stride >>= 1u;
    }
    if (lane == 0u) {
        inv_shared = inverseSqrt(partials[0] / f32(params.width) + params.eps_pre);
    }
    workgroupBarrier();
    let inv_pre = inv_shared;

    var m = 0u;
    for (var i = lane; i < params.width; i += 256u) {
        var y = s_vals[m] * inv_pre;
        y = y * w_pre[i];
        out_normed[base + i] = y;
        m += 1u;
    }
}
"#;

/// Largest row width the chain shader serves: 256 lanes
/// holding at most 32 strided elements each.
pub const CHAIN_MAX_WIDTH: usize = 256 * 32;

/// The close shader: the last layer's post-FFN norm and
/// residual add, with the head's final norm folded in. Stage
/// one is the chain shader's first stage (the stream takes
/// the residual plus the post-normed branch, at the
/// post-norm eps); the LAST row's workgroup then runs the
/// final norm over its register-resident stream row (the
/// head input is the final-normed stream, at the file eps)
/// in the same dispatch, so the separate final-norm
/// dispatch and the last-row copy both disappear from the
/// resident forward's tail. The math is the two stages'
/// composition exactly, under the chain shader's
/// register-residency width bound.
const CLOSE_SHADER: &str = r#"
struct CloseParams {
    width: u32,
    total_rows: u32,
    grid_x: u32,
    eps_post: f32,
    eps_final: f32,
}

@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> residual: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read> branch: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read> w_post: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(3) var<storage, read> w_final: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(4) var<storage, read_write> out_stream: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(5) var<storage, read_write> out_head: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(6) var<uniform> params: CloseParams;

var<workgroup> partials: array<f32, 256>;
var<workgroup> inv_shared: f32;

@compute @workgroup_size(256)
fn close_main(@builtin(workgroup_id) wid: vec3<u32>,
              @builtin(local_invocation_id) lid: vec3<u32>) {
    let row = wid.y * params.grid_x + wid.x;
    // Whole-workgroup early out: every lane shares `row`, so
    // the exit is uniform and the barriers below stay legal.
    if (row >= params.total_rows) {
        return;
    }
    let lane = lid.x;
    let base = row * params.width;

    var ss = 0.0;
    for (var i = lane; i < params.width; i += 256u) {
        let v = branch[base + i];
        ss += v * v;
    }
    partials[lane] = ss;
    workgroupBarrier();
    var stride = 128u;
    while (stride > 0u) {
        if (lane < stride) {
            partials[lane] += partials[lane + stride];
        }
        workgroupBarrier();
        stride >>= 1u;
    }
    if (lane == 0u) {
        inv_shared = inverseSqrt(partials[0] / f32(params.width) + params.eps_post);
    }
    workgroupBarrier();
    let inv_post = inv_shared;

    var s_vals: array<f32, 32>;
    var ss2 = 0.0;
    var n = 0u;
    for (var i = lane; i < params.width; i += 256u) {
        var y = branch[base + i] * inv_post;
        y = y * w_post[i];
        let s = residual[base + i] + y;
        s_vals[n] = s;
        out_stream[base + i] = s;
        ss2 += s * s;
        n += 1u;
    }

    // Only the last row feeds the head; other rows are done.
    if (row != params.total_rows - 1u) {
        return;
    }
    partials[lane] = ss2;
    workgroupBarrier();
    stride = 128u;
    while (stride > 0u) {
        if (lane < stride) {
            partials[lane] += partials[lane + stride];
        }
        workgroupBarrier();
        stride >>= 1u;
    }
    if (lane == 0u) {
        inv_shared = inverseSqrt(partials[0] / f32(params.width) + params.eps_final);
    }
    workgroupBarrier();
    let inv_final = inv_shared;

    var m = 0u;
    for (var i = lane; i < params.width; i += 256u) {
        var y = s_vals[m] * inv_final;
        y = y * w_final[i];
        out_head[i] = y;
        m += 1u;
    }
}
"#;

/// One prepared K4 dispatch: a bind group plus grid dimensions,
/// built once for a fixed (buffers, rows, width, mode, eps)
/// combination and encodable any number of times into any
/// command encoder. This is the device-resident forward's unit
/// of composition (see [`crate::session`]): the one-shot entry
/// points below prepare, encode, submit, and read back; the
/// resident path prepares once per shape and encodes the whole
/// forward into a single submission.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct K4Call {
    pipeline: wgpu::ComputePipeline,
    bind_group: wgpu::BindGroup,
    grid: (u32, u32),
    /// Diag timestamp stamp (see `crate::timestamps`); `None`
    /// unless the context carries a recorder.
    diag: Option<crate::timestamps::DiagStamp>,
}

impl K4Call {
    /// Record this call's dispatch into `encoder`.
    pub fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut wgpu::CommandEncoder) {
        let mut pass = encoder.begin_compute_pass(&wgpu::ComputePassDescriptor {
            label: Some("k4 dispatch"),
            timestamp_writes: None,
        });
        self.encode_into(&mut pass);
    }

    /// Record this dispatch into an already-open compute
    /// `pass`: the composition form the device-resident
    /// session uses to chain a whole forward into one pass
    /// per segment (wgpu inserts the hazard barriers
    /// between dispatches inside the pass).
    pub fn encode_into(&self, pass: &mut wgpu::ComputePass<'_>) {
        let slot = self.diag.as_ref().and_then(|d| d.begin(pass));
        pass.set_pipeline(&self.pipeline);
        pass.set_bind_group(0, &self.bind_group, &[]);
        pass.dispatch_workgroups(self.grid.0, self.grid.1, 1);
        if let (Some(d), Some(s)) = (&self.diag, slot) {
            d.end(pass, s);
        }
    }
}

/// The compiled K4 pipelines (norm, add, and the two-stage
/// chain), plus the dummy buffer the norm shader binds for
/// inputs a mode does not read.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct K4Pipeline {
    norm: wgpu::ComputePipeline,
    add: wgpu::ComputePipeline,
    chain: wgpu::ComputePipeline,
    close: wgpu::ComputePipeline,
    dummy: wgpu::Buffer,
}

impl K4Pipeline {
    /// Compile both K4 pipelines on `device`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::Pipeline`] when wgpu rejects a shader.
    pub fn new(device: &wgpu::Device) -> Result<Self> {
        let norm_module = device.create_shader_module(wgpu::ShaderModuleDescriptor {
            label: Some("k4 rmsnorm shader"),
            source: wgpu::ShaderSource::Wgsl(NORM_SHADER.into()),
        });
        let norm = device.create_compute_pipeline(&wgpu::ComputePipelineDescriptor {
            label: Some("k4 rmsnorm pipeline"),
            layout: None,
            module: &norm_module,
            entry_point: Some("norm_main"),
            compilation_options: wgpu::PipelineCompilationOptions::default(),
            cache: None,
        });
        let add_module = device.create_shader_module(wgpu::ShaderModuleDescriptor {
            label: Some("k4 residual add shader"),
            source: wgpu::ShaderSource::Wgsl(ADD_SHADER.into()),
        });
        let add = device.create_compute_pipeline(&wgpu::ComputePipelineDescriptor {
            label: Some("k4 residual add pipeline"),
            layout: None,
            module: &add_module,
            entry_point: Some("add_main"),
            compilation_options: wgpu::PipelineCompilationOptions::default(),
            cache: None,
        });
        let chain_module = device.create_shader_module(wgpu::ShaderModuleDescriptor {
            label: Some("k4 norm chain shader"),
            source: wgpu::ShaderSource::Wgsl(CHAIN_SHADER.into()),
        });
        let chain = device.create_compute_pipeline(&wgpu::ComputePipelineDescriptor {
            label: Some("k4 norm chain pipeline"),
            layout: None,
            module: &chain_module,
            entry_point: Some("chain_main"),
            compilation_options: wgpu::PipelineCompilationOptions::default(),
            cache: None,
        });
        let dummy = device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
            label: Some("k4 dummy binding"),
            size: 4,
            usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::STORAGE,
            mapped_at_creation: false,
        });
        let close_module = device.create_shader_module(wgpu::ShaderModuleDescriptor {
            label: Some("k4 norm close shader"),
            source: wgpu::ShaderSource::Wgsl(CLOSE_SHADER.into()),
        });
        let close = device.create_compute_pipeline(&wgpu::ComputePipelineDescriptor {
            label: Some("k4 norm close pipeline"),
            layout: None,
            module: &close_module,
            entry_point: Some("close_main"),
            compilation_options: wgpu::PipelineCompilationOptions::default(),
            cache: None,
        });
        dbg_log!("k4 pipelines built");
        Ok(K4Pipeline {
            norm,
            add,
            chain,
            close,
            dummy,
        })
    }

    /// Prepare a norm dispatch over device buffers: `x` read,
    /// `out` written, `weight` and `residual` bound when the mode
    /// reads them (a dummy binding otherwise). `rows` rows of
    /// `width` channels; the caller validates shapes, exactly as
    /// the one-shot entry points do before they call this.
    // One argument per bound input plus the mode and eps: the
    // parameter list is the bind group's shape, kept flat on
    // purpose for this private helper.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    fn prepare_norm(
        &self,
        ctx: &GpuContext,
        x: &wgpu::Buffer,
        weight: Option<&wgpu::Buffer>,
        residual: Option<&wgpu::Buffer>,
        out: &wgpu::Buffer,
        rows: usize,
        width: usize,
        mode_value: u32,
        eps: f32,
    ) -> K4Call {
        let grid = crate::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::grid_dims(rows as u64);
        let params: [u32; 5] = [width as u32, rows as u32, grid.0, mode_value, eps.to_bits()];
        let param_bytes: Vec<u8> = params.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect();
        let params_buf = ctx.uniform_buffer("k4 norm params", &param_bytes);
        let dummy = self.dummy.clone();
        let bind_group = ctx.device.create_bind_group(&wgpu::BindGroupDescriptor {
            label: Some("k4 norm bind group"),
            layout: &self.norm.get_bind_group_layout(0),
            entries: &[
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 0,
                    resource: x.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 1,
                    resource: weight.unwrap_or(&dummy).as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 2,
                    resource: residual.unwrap_or(&dummy).as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 3,
                    resource: out.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 4,
                    resource: params_buf.as_entire_binding(),
                },
            ],
        });
        K4Call {
            pipeline: self.norm.clone(),
            bind_group,
            grid,
            diag: ctx.diag_stamp(crate::timestamps::DispatchMeta {
                kernel: "k4_rmsnorm",
                rows: rows as u64,
                cols: width as u64,
                quant: "",
                weight_bytes: weight.map_or(0, |w| w.size()),
                shape: format!("mode={mode_value} rows={rows} width={width}"),
            }),
        }
    }

    /// Prepare a weighted RMSNorm over device buffers:
    /// `x / sqrt(mean(x^2) + eps) * w` per row, `x` holding
    /// `rows` rows of the weight's width, written to `out`.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn prepare_rms_norm(
        &self,
        ctx: &GpuContext,
        x: &wgpu::Buffer,
        weight: &wgpu::Buffer,
        out: &wgpu::Buffer,
        rows: usize,
        width: usize,
        eps: f32,
    ) -> K4Call {
        self.prepare_norm(
            ctx,
            x,
            Some(weight),
            None,
            out,
            rows,
            width,
            mode::WEIGHTED,
            eps,
        )
    }

    /// Prepare a weightless RMSNorm over device buffers (the
    /// post-embedding form): `x / sqrt(mean(x^2) + eps)` per row.
    pub fn prepare_rms_norm_plain(
        &self,
        ctx: &GpuContext,
        x: &wgpu::Buffer,
        out: &wgpu::Buffer,
        rows: usize,
        width: usize,
        eps: f32,
    ) -> K4Call {
        self.prepare_norm(ctx, x, None, None, out, rows, width, mode::PLAIN, eps)
    }

    /// Prepare the fused post-norm step over device buffers:
    /// `residual + rms_norm(branch) * w` per row in one pass,
    /// written to `out` (which aliases neither input).
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn prepare_norm_residual(
        &self,
        ctx: &GpuContext,
        residual: &wgpu::Buffer,
        branch: &wgpu::Buffer,
        weight: &wgpu::Buffer,
        out: &wgpu::Buffer,
        rows: usize,
        width: usize,
        eps: f32,
    ) -> K4Call {
        self.prepare_norm(
            ctx,
            branch,
            Some(weight),
            Some(residual),
            out,
            rows,
            width,
            mode::WEIGHTED_RESIDUAL,
            eps,
        )
    }

    /// Prepare a two-stage norm chain over device buffers
    /// (see [`CHAIN_SHADER`]): stage one writes
    /// `out_stream = residual + rms_norm(branch) * w_post` at
    /// `eps_post`; stage two writes
    /// `out_normed = rms_norm(out_stream) * w_pre` at
    /// `eps_pre`, reducing over the register-resident
    /// intermediate row. Neither output aliases an input.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::InvalidTensor`] when `width` is zero or
    /// past [`CHAIN_MAX_WIDTH`] (the register-residency bound;
    /// wider rows keep the two-dispatch composition).
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn prepare_norm_chain(
        &self,
        ctx: &GpuContext,
        residual: &wgpu::Buffer,
        branch: &wgpu::Buffer,
        w_post: &wgpu::Buffer,
        w_pre: &wgpu::Buffer,
        out_stream: &wgpu::Buffer,
        out_normed: &wgpu::Buffer,
        rows: usize,
        width: usize,
        eps_post: f32,
        eps_pre: f32,
    ) -> Result<K4Call> {
        if width == 0 || width > CHAIN_MAX_WIDTH {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: "k4 norm chain".to_string(),
                detail: format!(
                    "width {width} is outside 1..={CHAIN_MAX_WIDTH}: the chain holds the \
                     intermediate row in registers, 32 strided elements per lane at most"
                ),
            });
        }
        let grid = crate::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::grid_dims(rows as u64);
        let params: [u32; 5] = [
            width as u32,
            rows as u32,
            grid.0,
            eps_post.to_bits(),
            eps_pre.to_bits(),
        ];
        let param_bytes: Vec<u8> = params.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect();
        let params_buf = ctx.uniform_buffer("k4 chain params", &param_bytes);
        let bind_group = ctx.device.create_bind_group(&wgpu::BindGroupDescriptor {
            label: Some("k4 chain bind group"),
            layout: &self.chain.get_bind_group_layout(0),
            entries: &[
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 0,
                    resource: residual.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 1,
                    resource: branch.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 2,
                    resource: w_post.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 3,
                    resource: w_pre.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 4,
                    resource: out_stream.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 5,
                    resource: out_normed.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 6,
                    resource: params_buf.as_entire_binding(),
                },
            ],
        });
        Ok(K4Call {
            pipeline: self.chain.clone(),
            bind_group,
            grid,
            diag: ctx.diag_stamp(crate::timestamps::DispatchMeta {
                kernel: "k4_norm_chain",
                rows: rows as u64,
                cols: width as u64,
                quant: "",
                weight_bytes: w_post.size() + w_pre.size(),
                shape: format!("rows={rows} width={width}"),
            }),
        })
    }

    /// Prepare a close dispatch over device buffers (see
    /// [`CLOSE_SHADER`]): `out_stream = residual +
    /// rms_norm(branch) * w_post` at `eps_post` for every
    /// row, and for the last row additionally
    /// `out_head = rms_norm(out_stream last row) * w_final`
    /// at `eps_final`, from the register-resident row.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::InvalidTensor`] when `width` is zero or
    /// past [`CHAIN_MAX_WIDTH`].
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn prepare_norm_close(
        &self,
        ctx: &GpuContext,
        residual: &wgpu::Buffer,
        branch: &wgpu::Buffer,
        w_post: &wgpu::Buffer,
        w_final: &wgpu::Buffer,
        out_stream: &wgpu::Buffer,
        out_head: &wgpu::Buffer,
        rows: usize,
        width: usize,
        eps_post: f32,
        eps_final: f32,
    ) -> Result<K4Call> {
        if width == 0 || width > CHAIN_MAX_WIDTH {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: "k4 norm close".to_string(),
                detail: format!(
                    "width {width} is outside 1..={CHAIN_MAX_WIDTH}: the close holds the \
                     intermediate row in registers, 32 strided elements per lane at most"
                ),
            });
        }
        let grid = crate::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::grid_dims(rows as u64);
        let params: [u32; 5] = [
            width as u32,
            rows as u32,
            grid.0,
            eps_post.to_bits(),
            eps_final.to_bits(),
        ];
        let param_bytes: Vec<u8> = params.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect();
        let params_buf = ctx.uniform_buffer("k4 close params", &param_bytes);
        let bind_group = ctx.device.create_bind_group(&wgpu::BindGroupDescriptor {
            label: Some("k4 close bind group"),
            layout: &self.close.get_bind_group_layout(0),
            entries: &[
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 0,
                    resource: residual.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 1,
                    resource: branch.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 2,
                    resource: w_post.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 3,
                    resource: w_final.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 4,
                    resource: out_stream.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 5,
                    resource: out_head.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 6,
                    resource: params_buf.as_entire_binding(),
                },
            ],
        });
        Ok(K4Call {
            pipeline: self.close.clone(),
            bind_group,
            grid,
            diag: ctx.diag_stamp(crate::timestamps::DispatchMeta {
                kernel: "k4_norm_close",
                rows: rows as u64,
                cols: width as u64,
                quant: "",
                weight_bytes: w_post.size() + w_final.size(),
                shape: format!("rows={rows} width={width}"),
            }),
        })
    }

    /// Prepare a residual add over device buffers: `a + b`
    /// elementwise into `out`, `n` elements.
    pub fn prepare_add(
        &self,
        ctx: &GpuContext,
        a: &wgpu::Buffer,
        b: &wgpu::Buffer,
        out: &wgpu::Buffer,
        n: usize,
    ) -> K4Call {
        let total = (n as u64).div_ceil(u64::from(WORKGROUP));
        let grid = crate::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::grid_dims(total);
        let params: [u32; 2] = [n as u32, grid.0];
        let param_bytes: Vec<u8> = params.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect();
        let params_buf = ctx.uniform_buffer("k4 add params", &param_bytes);
        let bind_group = ctx.device.create_bind_group(&wgpu::BindGroupDescriptor {
            label: Some("k4 add bind group"),
            layout: &self.add.get_bind_group_layout(0),
            entries: &[
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 0,
                    resource: a.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 1,
                    resource: b.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 2,
                    resource: out.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 3,
                    resource: params_buf.as_entire_binding(),
                },
            ],
        });
        K4Call {
            pipeline: self.add.clone(),
            bind_group,
            grid,
            diag: ctx.diag_stamp(crate::timestamps::DispatchMeta {
                kernel: "k4_add",
                rows: n as u64,
                cols: 1,
                quant: "",
                weight_bytes: 0,
                shape: format!("n={n}"),
            }),
        }
    }

    /// Shared norm body: upload, dispatch one workgroup per row,
    /// read back. `weight` and `residual` are bound only by the
    /// modes that read them; the caller validates shapes.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    fn run_norm(
        &self,
        ctx: &GpuContext,
        x: &[f32],
        weight: Option<&[f32]>,
        residual: Option<&[f32]>,
        rows: usize,
        width: usize,
        mode_value: u32,
        eps: f32,
    ) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        let x_buf = ctx.upload_f32("k4 norm input", x);
        let w_buf = weight.map(|w| ctx.upload_f32("k4 norm weight", w));
        let r_buf = residual.map(|r| ctx.upload_f32("k4 norm residual", r));
        let out_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("k4 norm output", (x.len() * 4) as u64);
        let call = self.prepare_norm(
            ctx,
            &x_buf,
            w_buf.as_ref(),
            r_buf.as_ref(),
            &out_buf,
            rows,
            width,
            mode_value,
            eps,
        );
        let mut encoder = ctx
            .device
            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                label: Some("k4 norm run"),
            });
        call.encode(&mut encoder);
        ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
        dbg_log!("k4 norm: rows={rows} width={width} mode={mode_value} eps={eps}");
        ctx.read_f32(&out_buf, x.len())
    }

    /// Weighted RMSNorm: `x / sqrt(mean(x^2) + eps) * w` per row.
    /// `x` holds `rows` rows of `weight.len()` channels.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::InvalidTensor`] when `x` is not a whole number
    /// of weight-wide rows; [`WgpuError::Readback`] on map failure.
    pub fn rms_norm(
        &self,
        ctx: &GpuContext,
        x: &[f32],
        weight: &[f32],
        rows: usize,
        eps: f32,
    ) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        let width = check_rows("rms_norm", x, rows, weight.len())?;
        self.run_norm(ctx, x, Some(weight), None, rows, width, mode::WEIGHTED, eps)
    }

    /// Weightless RMSNorm: `x / sqrt(mean(x^2) + eps)` per row.
    /// `rows` divides `x` evenly; the width is `x.len() / rows`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::InvalidTensor`] when `rows` does not divide
    /// `x`; [`WgpuError::Readback`] on map failure.
    pub fn rms_norm_plain(
        &self,
        ctx: &GpuContext,
        x: &[f32],
        rows: usize,
        eps: f32,
    ) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        if rows == 0 || x.is_empty() || x.len() % rows != 0 {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: "rms_norm_plain input".to_string(),
                detail: format!(
                    "input holds {} elements, not a whole number of {rows} rows",
                    x.len()
                ),
            });
        }
        let width = x.len() / rows;
        self.run_norm(ctx, x, None, None, rows, width, mode::PLAIN, eps)
    }

    /// The fused post-norm step: `residual + rms_norm(branch) * w`
    /// per row, in one pass. `eps` is the caller's: the reference
    /// graph's post norms pass its hardcoded 1e-8.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::InvalidTensor`] on any shape disagreement;
    /// [`WgpuError::Readback`] on map failure.
    pub fn norm_residual(
        &self,
        ctx: &GpuContext,
        residual: &[f32],
        branch: &[f32],
        weight: &[f32],
        rows: usize,
        eps: f32,
    ) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        if residual.len() != branch.len() {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: "norm_residual input".to_string(),
                detail: format!(
                    "residual holds {} elements but the branch holds {}",
                    residual.len(),
                    branch.len()
                ),
            });
        }
        let width = check_rows("norm_residual", branch, rows, weight.len())?;
        self.run_norm(
            ctx,
            branch,
            Some(weight),
            Some(residual),
            rows,
            width,
            mode::WEIGHTED_RESIDUAL,
            eps,
        )
    }

    /// Residual add of two equal-length activations.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::InvalidTensor`] when the lengths differ;
    /// [`WgpuError::Readback`] on map failure.
    pub fn add(&self, ctx: &GpuContext, a: &[f32], b: &[f32]) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        if a.len() != b.len() {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: "add input".to_string(),
                detail: format!(
                    "residual operands hold {} and {} elements",
                    a.len(),
                    b.len()
                ),
            });
        }
        if a.is_empty() {
            return Ok(Vec::new());
        }
        let a_buf = ctx.upload_f32("k4 add a", a);
        let b_buf = ctx.upload_f32("k4 add b", b);
        let out_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("k4 add output", (a.len() * 4) as u64);
        let call = self.prepare_add(ctx, &a_buf, &b_buf, &out_buf, a.len());
        let mut encoder = ctx
            .device
            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                label: Some("k4 add run"),
            });
        call.encode(&mut encoder);
        ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
        dbg_log!("k4 add: n={}", a.len());
        ctx.read_f32(&out_buf, a.len())
    }
}

/// Validate that `x` is exactly `rows` rows of `width`, returning
/// the width. Shared by the weighted entry points.
fn check_rows(step: &'static str, x: &[f32], rows: usize, width: usize) -> Result<usize> {
    if rows == 0 || width == 0 || x.len() != rows * width {
        return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
            name: "k4 input".to_string(),
            detail: format!(
                "{step}: input holds {} elements but {rows} rows of width {width} need {}",
                x.len(),
                rows * width
            ),
        });
    }
    Ok(width)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn norm_shader_names_its_entry_point_and_modes() {
        // CPU-side guard: the shader carries both entry points the
        // pipelines bind, and the mode uniform the host selects.
        assert!(NORM_SHADER.contains("fn norm_main"));
        assert!(NORM_SHADER.contains("mode: u32"));
        assert!(ADD_SHADER.contains("fn add_main"));
        assert!(CHAIN_SHADER.contains("fn chain_main"));
        assert!(CLOSE_SHADER.contains("fn close_main"));
        // The chain's two epsilons are separate uniforms: the
        // post stage's hardcoded 1e-8 must not leak into the
        // pre stage's file eps.
        assert!(CHAIN_SHADER.contains("eps_post"));
        assert!(CHAIN_SHADER.contains("eps_pre"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn check_rows_rejects_mismatched_shapes() {
        assert!(check_rows("rms_norm", &[0.0; 6], 2, 3).is_ok());
        assert!(check_rows("rms_norm", &[0.0; 6], 2, 4).is_err());
        assert!(check_rows("rms_norm", &[0.0; 6], 0, 3).is_err());
        assert!(check_rows("rms_norm", &[0.0; 6], 2, 0).is_err());
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/k5_rope_kv.rs =====
//! K5: RoPE rotation plus KV append (BACKEND.md Section 3).
//!
//! Two entry points, used back to back by the attention step:
//!
//! - **Rotate** ([`K5Pipeline::rotate`]): in-place interleaved
//!   (adjacent-pair, ggml NORM) RoPE over the rows of a projection
//!   buffer, one row per sequence position, each head of
//!   `head_dim` channels rotated at its absolute position. The
//!   pairing and the angle law are `torch-math`'s
//!   `rope_interleaved` exactly: pair `i` joins channels
//!   `(2i, 2i + 1)` and turns by `position * base^(-2i / head_dim)`.
//!   The base is a parameter (the SWA base the config resolved,
//!   `rope_freq_base_swa` with its train-base fallback), never a
//!   constant. Rotation runs on the sliding-window layers only;
//!   the global layers are NoPE and the caller simply does not
//!   call this kernel for them.
//! - **Append** ([`K5Pipeline::append`]): copy the rotated K rows
//!   and the V rows from their per-call staging buffers into the
//!   layer's resident KV buffers (K6's storage, see
//!   [`crate::kernels::k6_attention`]), at the slot the cache
//!   semantics assign: the position itself for global layers,
//!   `position % window` (the ring slot) for sliding layers. The
//!   slot law is the `attention` crate's `slot_of`, restated in
//!   the shader.
//!
//! Numerical note: `torch-math` computes its angles in f64; the
//! shader computes in f32 (`pow`, `sin`, `cos`). At Glimmer's
//! positions and base the two agree to float noise far below the
//! cross-backend tolerance the crate's tests assert; the
//! difference is stated here rather than hidden, the same
//! disclosure K4 makes for its f32 sum of squares.
//!
//! The rotation is deliberately NOT fused into the projection
//! epilogue in this landing (BACKEND.md allows either): the
//! `Compute` trait hands the attention step whole Q/K/V buffers,
//! so a standalone rotate over those buffers is the honest shape
//! of the seam as it exists today.

use crate::device::GpuContext;
use crate::error::{Result, WgpuError};

use crate::diag::dbg_log;

/// Threads per workgroup for both K5 kernels.
const WORKGROUP: u32 = 256;

/// The rotate shader: one thread per (row, head, pair).
const ROTATE_SHADER: &str = r#"
struct RotateParams {
    width: u32,
    head_dim: u32,
    total_pairs: u32,
    start_position: u32,
    base: f32,
    grid_x: u32,
}

@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read_write> data: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<uniform> params: RotateParams;

@compute @workgroup_size(256)
fn rotate_main(@builtin(workgroup_id) wid: vec3<u32>,
               @builtin(local_invocation_id) lid: vec3<u32>) {
    let flat = (wid.y * params.grid_x + wid.x) * 256u + lid.x;
    if (flat >= params.total_pairs) {
        return;
    }
    let pairs_per_row = params.width / 2u;
    let row = flat / pairs_per_row;
    let within = flat % pairs_per_row;
    let pairs_per_head = params.head_dim / 2u;
    let head = within / pairs_per_head;
    let pair = within % pairs_per_head;

    let position = f32(params.start_position + row);
    let angle = position * pow(params.base, -2.0 * f32(pair) / f32(params.head_dim));
    let c = cos(angle);
    let s = sin(angle);
    let i0 = row * params.width + head * params.head_dim + 2u * pair;
    let a = data[i0];
    let b = data[i0 + 1u];
    data[i0] = a * c - b * s;
    data[i0 + 1u] = a * s + b * c;
}
"#;

/// The append shader: one thread per element of the appended
/// rows. `window` is 0 for global layers (slot = position) and
/// the ring size for sliding layers (slot = position % window).
const APPEND_SHADER: &str = r#"
struct AppendParams {
    kv_width: u32,
    total: u32,
    start_position: u32,
    window: u32,
    grid_x: u32,
}

@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> k_src: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read> v_src: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read_write> k_dst: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(3) var<storage, read_write> v_dst: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(4) var<uniform> params: AppendParams;

@compute @workgroup_size(256)
fn append_main(@builtin(workgroup_id) wid: vec3<u32>,
               @builtin(local_invocation_id) lid: vec3<u32>) {
    let flat = (wid.y * params.grid_x + wid.x) * 256u + lid.x;
    if (flat >= params.total) {
        return;
    }
    let row = flat / params.kv_width;
    let channel = flat % params.kv_width;
    let position = params.start_position + row;
    var slot = position;
    if (params.window != 0u) {
        slot = position % params.window;
    }
    let dst = slot * params.kv_width + channel;
    k_dst[dst] = k_src[flat];
    v_dst[dst] = v_src[flat];
}
"#;

/// One prepared rotate dispatch, encodable any number of times
/// into any command encoder. The start position is the one
/// parameter a sequence changes per forward, so the call keeps
/// its uniform buffer and rewrites that one word through
/// [`K5RotateCall::set_start_position`]; everything else (the
/// buffer, the geometry, the base) is fixed at prepare time.
/// This is the device-resident forward's unit of composition
/// (see [`crate::session`]); the one-shot entry points prepare,
/// encode, and submit.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct K5RotateCall {
    pipeline: wgpu::ComputePipeline,
    bind_group: wgpu::BindGroup,
    params: wgpu::Buffer,
    grid: (u32, u32),
    /// Diag timestamp stamp (see `crate::timestamps`); `None`
    /// unless the context carries a recorder.
    diag: Option<crate::timestamps::DiagStamp>,
}

impl K5RotateCall {
    /// Record this call's dispatch into `encoder`.
    pub fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut wgpu::CommandEncoder) {
        let mut pass = encoder.begin_compute_pass(&wgpu::ComputePassDescriptor {
            label: Some("k5 rope rotate"),
            timestamp_writes: None,
        });
        self.encode_into(&mut pass);
    }

    /// Record this dispatch into an already-open compute
    /// `pass`: the composition form the device-resident
    /// session uses to chain a whole forward into one pass
    /// per segment (wgpu inserts the hazard barriers
    /// between dispatches inside the pass).
    pub fn encode_into(&self, pass: &mut wgpu::ComputePass<'_>) {
        let slot = self.diag.as_ref().and_then(|d| d.begin(pass));
        pass.set_pipeline(&self.pipeline);
        pass.set_bind_group(0, &self.bind_group, &[]);
        pass.dispatch_workgroups(self.grid.0, self.grid.1, 1);
        if let (Some(d), Some(s)) = (&self.diag, slot) {
            d.end(pass, s);
        }
    }

    /// Point the rotation at a new absolute start position (the
    /// prepared call's rows sit at `start_position + row`). The
    /// rewrite rides the queue, so it lands in submission order:
    /// call it while no submission using this call is in flight
    /// (the resident session is synchronous per forward, so this
    /// is its natural state).
    pub fn set_start_position(&self, ctx: &GpuContext, start_position: usize) {
        // RotateParams word 3, after width, head_dim, total_pairs.
        ctx.queue
            .write_buffer(&self.params, 12, &(start_position as u32).to_le_bytes());
    }
}

/// One prepared append dispatch, the rotate call's sibling: the
/// start position rewrites through
/// [`K5AppendCall::set_start_position`], the rest is fixed at
/// prepare time.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct K5AppendCall {
    pipeline: wgpu::ComputePipeline,
    bind_group: wgpu::BindGroup,
    params: wgpu::Buffer,
    grid: (u32, u32),
    /// Diag timestamp stamp (see `crate::timestamps`); `None`
    /// unless the context carries a recorder.
    diag: Option<crate::timestamps::DiagStamp>,
}

impl K5AppendCall {
    /// Record this call's dispatch into `encoder`.
    pub fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut wgpu::CommandEncoder) {
        let mut pass = encoder.begin_compute_pass(&wgpu::ComputePassDescriptor {
            label: Some("k5 kv append"),
            timestamp_writes: None,
        });
        self.encode_into(&mut pass);
    }

    /// Record this dispatch into an already-open compute
    /// `pass`: the composition form the device-resident
    /// session uses to chain a whole forward into one pass
    /// per segment (wgpu inserts the hazard barriers
    /// between dispatches inside the pass).
    pub fn encode_into(&self, pass: &mut wgpu::ComputePass<'_>) {
        let slot = self.diag.as_ref().and_then(|d| d.begin(pass));
        pass.set_pipeline(&self.pipeline);
        pass.set_bind_group(0, &self.bind_group, &[]);
        pass.dispatch_workgroups(self.grid.0, self.grid.1, 1);
        if let (Some(d), Some(s)) = (&self.diag, slot) {
            d.end(pass, s);
        }
    }

    /// Point the append at a new absolute start position (the
    /// prepared rows land at slots for `start_position + row`).
    /// Same queue-ordering contract as
    /// [`K5RotateCall::set_start_position`].
    pub fn set_start_position(&self, ctx: &GpuContext, start_position: usize) {
        // AppendParams word 2, after kv_width and total.
        ctx.queue
            .write_buffer(&self.params, 8, &(start_position as u32).to_le_bytes());
    }
}

/// The compiled K5 pipelines (rotate and append).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct K5Pipeline {
    rotate: wgpu::ComputePipeline,
    append: wgpu::ComputePipeline,
}

impl K5Pipeline {
    /// Compile both K5 pipelines on `device`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::Pipeline`] when wgpu rejects a shader.
    pub fn new(device: &wgpu::Device) -> Result<Self> {
        let build = |source: &str, entry: &'static str, label: &'static str| {
            let module = device.create_shader_module(wgpu::ShaderModuleDescriptor {
                label: Some(label),
                source: wgpu::ShaderSource::Wgsl(source.into()),
            });
            device.create_compute_pipeline(&wgpu::ComputePipelineDescriptor {
                label: Some(label),
                layout: None,
                module: &module,
                entry_point: Some(entry),
                compilation_options: wgpu::PipelineCompilationOptions::default(),
                cache: None,
            })
        };
        let rotate = build(ROTATE_SHADER, "rotate_main", "k5 rope rotate");
        let append = build(APPEND_SHADER, "append_main", "k5 kv append");
        dbg_log!("k5 pipelines built");
        Ok(K5Pipeline { rotate, append })
    }

    /// Prepare a rotate dispatch over `buffer` in place: `rows`
    /// rows of `heads * head_dim` channels, row `r` at absolute
    /// position `start_position + r` (rewritable through the
    /// returned call), interleaved pairing, the given base.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::InvalidTensor`] when the geometry is unusable
    /// (odd or zero head dim, zero rows).
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn prepare_rotate(
        &self,
        ctx: &GpuContext,
        buffer: &wgpu::Buffer,
        rows: usize,
        heads: usize,
        head_dim: usize,
        start_position: usize,
        base: f32,
    ) -> Result<K5RotateCall> {
        if rows == 0 || heads == 0 || head_dim < 2 || head_dim % 2 != 0 {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: "k5 rotate".to_string(),
                detail: format!(
                    "rows {rows}, heads {heads}, head_dim {head_dim}: rotation needs \
                     at least one row and head and an even head_dim of at least 2"
                ),
            });
        }
        if !base.is_finite() || base <= 1.0 {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: "k5 rotate".to_string(),
                detail: format!("rope base {base} is not finite and greater than 1"),
            });
        }
        let width = heads * head_dim;
        let total_pairs = (rows * width / 2) as u32;
        let total_wg = u64::from(total_pairs).div_ceil(u64::from(WORKGROUP));
        let grid = crate::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::grid_dims(total_wg);
        let params: [u32; 6] = [
            width as u32,
            head_dim as u32,
            total_pairs,
            start_position as u32,
            base.to_bits(),
            grid.0,
        ];
        let param_bytes: Vec<u8> = params.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect();
        let params_buf = ctx.uniform_buffer("k5 rotate params", &param_bytes);
        let bind_group = ctx.device.create_bind_group(&wgpu::BindGroupDescriptor {
            label: Some("k5 rotate bind group"),
            layout: &self.rotate.get_bind_group_layout(0),
            entries: &[
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 0,
                    resource: buffer.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 1,
                    resource: params_buf.as_entire_binding(),
                },
            ],
        });
        Ok(K5RotateCall {
            pipeline: self.rotate.clone(),
            bind_group,
            params: params_buf,
            grid,
            diag: ctx.diag_stamp(crate::timestamps::DispatchMeta {
                kernel: "k5_rope_rotate",
                rows: rows as u64,
                cols: width as u64,
                quant: "",
                weight_bytes: 0,
                shape: format!("heads={heads} head_dim={head_dim} start={start_position}"),
            }),
        })
    }

    /// Rotate every row of `buffer` in place: `rows` rows of
    /// `heads * head_dim` channels, row `r` at absolute position
    /// `start_position + r`, interleaved pairing, the given base.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::InvalidTensor`] when the geometry is unusable
    /// (odd or zero head dim, zero rows).
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn rotate(
        &self,
        ctx: &GpuContext,
        buffer: &wgpu::Buffer,
        rows: usize,
        heads: usize,
        head_dim: usize,
        start_position: usize,
        base: f32,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let call = self.prepare_rotate(ctx, buffer, rows, heads, head_dim, start_position, base)?;
        let mut encoder = ctx
            .device
            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                label: Some("k5 rotate run"),
            });
        call.encode(&mut encoder);
        ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
        dbg_log!(
            "k5 rotate: rows={rows} heads={heads} head_dim={head_dim} start={start_position} base={base}"
        );
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Prepare an append dispatch: `rows` rows of K and V from
    /// the staging buffers into the layer's resident KV buffers,
    /// starting at absolute position `start_position`
    /// (rewritable through the returned call). `window` is the
    /// layer's ring size, or `None` for a global layer
    /// (slot = position).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::InvalidTensor`] when `rows` or `kv_width` is
    /// zero.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn prepare_append(
        &self,
        ctx: &GpuContext,
        k_src: &wgpu::Buffer,
        v_src: &wgpu::Buffer,
        k_dst: &wgpu::Buffer,
        v_dst: &wgpu::Buffer,
        rows: usize,
        kv_width: usize,
        start_position: usize,
        window: Option<usize>,
    ) -> Result<K5AppendCall> {
        if rows == 0 || kv_width == 0 {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: "k5 append".to_string(),
                detail: format!("rows {rows}, kv_width {kv_width}: nothing to append"),
            });
        }
        let total = (rows * kv_width) as u32;
        let total_wg = u64::from(total).div_ceil(u64::from(WORKGROUP));
        let grid = crate::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::grid_dims(total_wg);
        let params: [u32; 5] = [
            kv_width as u32,
            total,
            start_position as u32,
            window.map_or(0, |w| w as u32),
            grid.0,
        ];
        let param_bytes: Vec<u8> = params.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect();
        let params_buf = ctx.uniform_buffer("k5 append params", &param_bytes);
        let bind_group = ctx.device.create_bind_group(&wgpu::BindGroupDescriptor {
            label: Some("k5 append bind group"),
            layout: &self.append.get_bind_group_layout(0),
            entries: &[
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 0,
                    resource: k_src.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 1,
                    resource: v_src.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 2,
                    resource: k_dst.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 3,
                    resource: v_dst.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 4,
                    resource: params_buf.as_entire_binding(),
                },
            ],
        });
        Ok(K5AppendCall {
            pipeline: self.append.clone(),
            bind_group,
            params: params_buf,
            grid,
            diag: ctx.diag_stamp(crate::timestamps::DispatchMeta {
                kernel: "k5_kv_append",
                rows: rows as u64,
                cols: kv_width as u64,
                quant: "",
                weight_bytes: 0,
                shape: format!("rows={rows} kv_width={kv_width}"),
            }),
        })
    }

    /// Append `rows` rows of K and V from the staging buffers
    /// into the layer's resident KV buffers, starting at absolute
    /// position `start_position`. `window` is the layer's ring
    /// size, or `None` for a global layer (slot = position).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::InvalidTensor`] when `rows` or `kv_width` is
    /// zero.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn append(
        &self,
        ctx: &GpuContext,
        k_src: &wgpu::Buffer,
        v_src: &wgpu::Buffer,
        k_dst: &wgpu::Buffer,
        v_dst: &wgpu::Buffer,
        rows: usize,
        kv_width: usize,
        start_position: usize,
        window: Option<usize>,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let call = self.prepare_append(
            ctx,
            k_src,
            v_src,
            k_dst,
            v_dst,
            rows,
            kv_width,
            start_position,
            window,
        )?;
        let mut encoder = ctx
            .device
            .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
                label: Some("k5 append run"),
            });
        call.encode(&mut encoder);
        ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
        dbg_log!(
            "k5 append: rows={rows} kv_width={kv_width} start={start_position} window={window:?}"
        );
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// The ring slot of an absolute position, restating the
/// `attention` crate's `slot_of` for the host side of this
/// module's tests and callers: the position itself for global
/// layers, `position % window` for windowed ones.
#[must_use]
pub fn slot_of(position: usize, window: Option<usize>) -> usize {
    match window {
        None => position,
        Some(w) => position % w,
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn slot_of_matches_the_cache_law() {
        assert_eq!(slot_of(7, None), 7);
        assert_eq!(slot_of(7, Some(2048)), 7);
        assert_eq!(slot_of(2049, Some(2048)), 1);
        assert_eq!(slot_of(4096, Some(2048)), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn shaders_carry_their_entry_points() {
        assert!(ROTATE_SHADER.contains("fn rotate_main"));
        assert!(APPEND_SHADER.contains("fn append_main"));
        // The NORM pairing is adjacent channels, channels 2i and
        // 2i+1 of one head: the shader must index exactly that.
        assert!(ROTATE_SHADER.contains("2u * pair"));
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/k6_attention.rs =====
//! K6: grouped-query attention over resident GPU KV buffers
//! (BACKEND.md Section 3), plus the KV state the attention step
//! owns.
//!
//! The semantics are the `attention` crate's, restated for the
//! GPU and pinned by the crate's cross-backend tests: the score
//! scale is `1 / sqrt(head_dim)` (the crate's `AttentionParams`
//! default, which `cpu-compute` uses); a key at absolute position
//! `kp` is visible to a query at `p` when `kp <= p` (causal) and,
//! on windowed layers, when `kp` lies in `(p - window, p]`; query
//! heads group contiguously over KV heads (`kv_head = q_head /
//! (q_heads / kv_heads)`); softmax is max-subtracted.
//!
//! Three kernels, two forms of the same math:
//!
//! - **Scores**: one thread per (query row, Q head, stored key):
//!   the full dot product over the head dim, masked to negative
//!   infinity where the mask hides the key, written to a scratch
//!   buffer.
//! - **Reduce**: one workgroup per (query row, Q head), one lane
//!   per head-dim channel, running an online (streaming) softmax
//!   over the stored keys in oldest-first order while
//!   accumulating the value mix per channel. Online softmax is
//!   mathematically the reference's two-pass max-subtracted form;
//!   the float summation order differs, which is reassociation
//!   noise, disclosed here the same way K4 and K5 disclose
//!   theirs. Decode leanness: a single query row launches
//!   `q_heads` workgroups and reads each value row exactly once.
//!   Scores + reduce are the two-pass form; the trait path
//!   (`compute.rs`, one row per step) runs them.
//! - **Flash**: the fused form (see the flash shader below):
//!   scores, online softmax, and the value-weighted reduce in
//!   one dispatch, with no scores buffer at all. The resident
//!   session runs it at every shape, decode rows and prefill
//!   chunks alike (the chunk-plan switch is recorded in
//!   bench/flash-chunk-2026-11-04.md).
//! - **Flash, staged**: the same fused math with its memory
//!   traffic reorganized into llama.cpp's blocked form (see
//!   [`FLASH_STAGED_SHADER`]): K and V walked in blocks of
//!   32 keys staged in workgroup memory, 8 query rows per
//!   workgroup. Env-gated at the backend
//!   (`WGPU_COMPUTE_FLASH_STAGED` in `crate::compute`) and
//!   routed only for multi-row calls; it is the backend
//!   default for those calls (the variable's explicit
//!   `0` restores the shipped flash), and the shipped
//!   flash remains the single-row form in every switch
//!   position.
//! - **Flash over f16 KV**: both flash forms have an f16
//!   twin ([`FLASH_F16_SHADER`], [`FLASH_STAGED_F16_SHADER`])
//!   serving layers whose KV is stored as packed f16
//!   ([`KvStorage::F16`], selected per state at
//!   construction from `WGPU_COMPUTE_KV_F16` in
//!   `crate::compute`; default off). The twins bind the
//!   K/V buffers as `array<u32>` (two f16 values per word)
//!   and convert on read: the staged twin unpacks each
//!   staged element once into the same f32 workgroup tile
//!   the f32 form uses, so its workgroup-memory set is
//!   byte-identical; the shipped twin unpacks per load in
//!   its dot and reduce loops. Everything downstream of
//!   the unpack is the f32 form's operation sequence. The
//!   two-pass form has no f16 twin: it serves the trait
//!   path, whose state is f32 by construction, and its
//!   prepares refuse an f16 layer by name. The write-side
//!   conversion lives in K9's f16 preparation form (see
//!   `crate::kernels::k9_attn_prep`). Design, precision
//!   analysis, and the card gate that can move the
//!   default: bench/f16-kv-2026-11-07.md.
//!
//! KV state: like `cpu-compute`, this backend owns its KV
//! storage, because the `Cache` trait the forward hands over is
//! a position contract only. [`GpuKvState`] holds the
//! `attention` crate's `KvCache` as the host mirror (positions,
//! cross-checks, and the exact rows the GPU rotated, read back
//! once per call) plus one device buffer pair per layer. Global
//! layers address slots by absolute position and grow
//! geometrically; windowed layers are a fixed ring of `window`
//! slots, slot = `position % window`, exactly the host cache's
//! law. The device buffers are the ones K5's append writes and
//! this module's scores kernel reads.
//!
//! Head-dim bound: the reduce workgroup is 128 lanes, one per
//! channel, so `head_dim` above 128 refuses by name. Glimmer's
//! head dim is exactly 128; a future wider head needs a strided
//! reduce, which is a named extension, not a silent truncation.

use attention::{KvCache, LayerKind as AttnLayerKind};
use muse_glimmer::{GlimmerConfig, GlimmerError, LayerKind, Result as GlimmerResult};

use crate::device::GpuContext;
use crate::error::{Result, WgpuError};

use crate::diag::dbg_log;

/// Build a [`GlimmerError::StepFailed`] for `step` with `detail`
/// (the state half of this module speaks the trait's error, like
/// `cpu-compute` does).
fn step_failed(step: &'static str, detail: impl Into<String>) -> GlimmerError {
    GlimmerError::StepFailed {
        step,
        detail: detail.into(),
    }
}

/// Workgroup width of the reduce kernel: one lane per head-dim
/// channel, so also the largest head dim it serves.
const REDUCE_LANES: u32 = 128;

/// Threads per workgroup of the scores kernel.
const SCORES_WORKGROUP: u32 = 256;

/// The scores shader: one thread per (row, Q head, stored key).
const SCORES_SHADER: &str = r#"
struct ScoresParams {
    rows: u32,
    q_heads: u32,
    kv_heads: u32,
    head_dim: u32,
    stored: u32,
    first_pos: u32,
    start_pos: u32,
    window: u32,
    scale: f32,
    total: u32,
    grid_x: u32,
    ring: u32,
}

@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> q: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read> keys: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read_write> scores: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(3) var<uniform> params: ScoresParams;

@compute @workgroup_size(256)
fn scores_main(@builtin(workgroup_id) wid: vec3<u32>,
               @builtin(local_invocation_id) lid: vec3<u32>) {
    let flat = (wid.y * params.grid_x + wid.x) * 256u + lid.x;
    if (flat >= params.total) {
        return;
    }
    let idx = flat % params.stored;
    let head = (flat / params.stored) % params.q_heads;
    let row = flat / (params.stored * params.q_heads);
    let kp = params.first_pos + idx;
    let p = params.start_pos + row;

    // The mask, the attention crate's `attends` restated: causal
    // everywhere, plus the window on windowed layers (written as
    // kp + window > p so no subtraction can underflow).
    var visible = kp <= p;
    if (params.window != 0u && kp + params.window <= p) {
        visible = false;
    }
    if (!visible) {
        scores[flat] = -1.0e30;
        return;
    }
    // The slot modulus is the ring capacity, NOT the mask
    // window: the two are the same for a decode-step ring, but
    // a chunked prefill ring is larger than the window (it must
    // hold every position any query in the chunk can see), and
    // slotting by the window there would alias positions a
    // chunk apart onto one slot.
    var slot = kp;
    if (params.ring != 0u) {
        slot = kp % params.ring;
    }
    let kv_head = head / (params.q_heads / params.kv_heads);
    let q_base = (row * params.q_heads + head) * params.head_dim;
    let k_base = (slot * params.kv_heads + kv_head) * params.head_dim;
    var s = 0.0;
    for (var d = 0u; d < params.head_dim; d++) {
        s += q[q_base + d] * keys[k_base + d];
    }
    scores[flat] = s * params.scale;
}
"#;

/// The reduce shader: one workgroup per (row, Q head), one lane
/// per channel, online softmax over the stored keys.
const REDUCE_SHADER: &str = r#"
struct ReduceParams {
    q_heads: u32,
    kv_heads: u32,
    head_dim: u32,
    stored: u32,
    first_pos: u32,
    window: u32,
    grid_x: u32,
    ring: u32,
}

@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> scores: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read> values: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read_write> out: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(3) var<uniform> params: ReduceParams;

@compute @workgroup_size(128)
fn reduce_main(@builtin(workgroup_id) wid: vec3<u32>,
               @builtin(local_invocation_id) lid: vec3<u32>) {
    let flat_wg = wid.y * params.grid_x + wid.x;
    let head = flat_wg % params.q_heads;
    let row = flat_wg / params.q_heads;
    let d = lid.x;
    if (d >= params.head_dim) {
        return;
    }
    let kv_head = head / (params.q_heads / params.kv_heads);
    let scores_base = (row * params.q_heads + head) * params.stored;

    var m = -1.0e30;
    var sum = 0.0;
    var acc = 0.0;
    for (var idx = 0u; idx < params.stored; idx++) {
        let sc = scores[scores_base + idx];
        if (sc <= -1.0e29) {
            continue;
        }
        if (sc > m) {
            let corr = exp(m - sc);
            acc *= corr;
            sum *= corr;
            m = sc;
        }
        let w = exp(sc - m);
        let kp = params.first_pos + idx;
        // Slot modulus is the ring capacity, as in the scores
        // kernel (see its note): never the mask window.
        var slot = kp;
        if (params.ring != 0u) {
            slot = kp % params.ring;
        }
        let v = values[(slot * params.kv_heads + kv_head) * params.head_dim + d];
        acc += w * v;
        sum += w;
    }
    out[(row * params.q_heads + head) * params.head_dim + d] = acc / sum;
}
"#;

/// The flash shader: scores, online softmax, and the
/// value-weighted reduce fused into one kernel, one workgroup
/// of 256 lanes per (query row, Q head), for the session
/// calls where the two-pass form's scores buffer and second
/// dispatch are pure overhead. The math is the two-pass math,
/// operation for operation: the score phase computes each
/// tile's 256 scores with the scores kernel's thread-to-key
/// mapping and dot order (masked keys get its -1e30 sentinel),
/// stages them in workgroup memory, and the lanes under the
/// head dim then run the reduce kernel's online-softmax loop
/// over the tile in the same ascending order, carrying their
/// (max, sum, accumulator) state across tiles in registers.
/// The sequence of float operations per output element is the
/// two-pass sequence, so the outputs agree with it to the bit
/// in exact arithmetic and to reassociation noise in floats
/// (the scores are computed identically; only their storage
/// differs). The kernel is shape-generic: one workgroup per
/// (query row, Q head) at any row count, the causal position
/// taken per row (`start_pos + row`), keys slotted modulo the
/// ring exactly as in the scores kernel, so the sliding mask
/// and the chunked ring carry over unchanged. The resident
/// session runs this form for decode rows and prefill chunks
/// alike; the two-pass form remains for the trait path.
const FLASH_SHADER: &str = r#"
struct FlashParams {
    rows: u32,
    q_heads: u32,
    kv_heads: u32,
    head_dim: u32,
    stored: u32,
    first_pos: u32,
    start_pos: u32,
    window: u32,
    ring: u32,
    scale: f32,
    grid_x: u32,
}

@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> q: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read> keys: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read> values: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(3) var<storage, read_write> out: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(4) var<uniform> params: FlashParams;

var<workgroup> tile: array<f32, 256>;

@compute @workgroup_size(256)
fn flash_main(@builtin(workgroup_id) wid: vec3<u32>,
              @builtin(local_invocation_id) lid: vec3<u32>) {
    let flat_wg = wid.y * params.grid_x + wid.x;
    let head = flat_wg % params.q_heads;
    let row = flat_wg / params.q_heads;
    let lane = lid.x;
    let kv_head = head / (params.q_heads / params.kv_heads);
    let q_base = (row * params.q_heads + head) * params.head_dim;
    let p = params.start_pos + row;

    var m = -1.0e30;
    var sum = 0.0;
    var acc = 0.0;
    for (var t0 = 0u; t0 < params.stored; t0 += 256u) {
        // Score phase: lane l takes stored key t0 + l.
        let idx = t0 + lane;
        var sc = -1.0e30;
        if (idx < params.stored) {
            let kp = params.first_pos + idx;
            var visible = kp <= p;
            if (params.window != 0u && kp + params.window <= p) {
                visible = false;
            }
            if (visible) {
                var slot = kp;
                if (params.ring != 0u) {
                    slot = kp % params.ring;
                }
                let k_base = (slot * params.kv_heads + kv_head) * params.head_dim;
                var s = 0.0;
                for (var dd = 0u; dd < params.head_dim; dd++) {
                    s += q[q_base + dd] * keys[k_base + dd];
                }
                sc = s * params.scale;
            }
        }
        tile[lane] = sc;
        workgroupBarrier();
        // Reduce phase: the reduce kernel's loop over the
        // tile, ascending, state carried across tiles.
        if (lane < params.head_dim) {
            let tile_len = min(256u, params.stored - t0);
            for (var j = 0u; j < tile_len; j++) {
                let s2 = tile[j];
                if (s2 <= -1.0e29) {
                    continue;
                }
                if (s2 > m) {
                    let corr = exp(m - s2);
                    acc *= corr;
                    sum *= corr;
                    m = s2;
                }
                let w = exp(s2 - m);
                let kp = params.first_pos + t0 + j;
                var slot = kp;
                if (params.ring != 0u) {
                    slot = kp % params.ring;
                }
                let v = values[(slot * params.kv_heads + kv_head) * params.head_dim + lane];
                acc += w * v;
                sum += w;
            }
        }
        workgroupBarrier();
    }
    if (lane < params.head_dim) {
        out[q_base + lane] = acc / sum;
    }
}
"#;

/// Workgroup-memory bytes the staged flash form below
/// declares, pinned against its shader text by a unit test:
/// the K/V block tile (32 keys at a padded 129-float stride,
/// 4,128 f32), the query block tile (8 rows at the 128-float
/// head-dim bound, 1,024 f32), and the score tile (8 rows x
/// 32 keys, 256 f32): (4,128 + 1,024 + 256) * 4 = 21,632
/// bytes. A device granting less than this does not build
/// the staged pipeline at all (see
/// [`K6Pipeline::flash_staged_available`]); the backend
/// requests the adapter's own limits, and the server card
/// grants 64 KiB, so the staged set fits there with room.
pub const FLASH_STAGED_LDS_BYTES: u32 = 21_632;

/// The staged flash shader: the shipped flash math with the
/// memory traffic reorganized into llama.cpp's blocked form
/// (parity spec Family 5, bench/llama-parity-specs-2026-11-06.md
/// gap 5). One workgroup of 256 threads serves a block of
/// Br = 8 query rows for one Q head and walks the stored
/// keys in blocks of Bc = 32 (flash_attn_base.glsl:4-21's
/// Bc; the AMD scalar tuning at head dim 128 and row_split 1
/// picks block_rows 8 and block_cols 32, ggml-vulkan.cpp:
/// 1200-1245). Per KV block the workgroup stages the block's
/// K rows into workgroup memory with coalesced loads, scores
/// all 8 rows against the staged block, stages the block's
/// V rows into the same tile, and runs the online-softmax
/// accumulation reading V from workgroup memory. The query
/// block is staged once up front. The shipped form, by
/// contrast, stages only a 256-wide score tile: its score
/// phase reads every key row from global memory once per
/// query row and its reduce re-reads every value row from
/// global memory, which is the traffic that makes its cost
/// grow quadratically across a prompt (1,013.1 ms at 1,022
/// tokens, bench/prefill-profile-2026-11-05.md).
///
/// Thread map: `tid / 32` is the query row inside the block
/// and `tid % 32` is the lane. In the score phase lane `j`
/// owns key `j` of the block and computes the full dot over
/// the head dim from the two staged tiles. In the reduce
/// phase lane `l` owns channels `l`, `l + 32`, `l + 64`,
/// `l + 96` (those under the head dim) of its row and loops
/// the block's keys in ascending order. The K/V tile's row
/// stride is padded by one float (head_dim + 1) so the
/// score phase's simultaneous reads across keys and the
/// reduce phase's reads across channels both land on
/// distinct workgroup-memory banks at the head dims this
/// engine serves (128 and 64, both 0 mod 32).
///
/// Correctness contract: the per-element float operation
/// sequence is the shipped flash kernel's, exactly. Scores
/// are the same ascending-channel dot products of the same
/// values, multiplied by the same scale; masked keys take
/// the same -1.0e30 sentinel; the reduce carries (max, sum,
/// accumulator) across blocks in ascending key order with
/// the same per-key rescale and the same skip test. Only
/// the storage the operands pass through differs (workgroup
/// tiles instead of global buffers), so the outputs agree
/// with the shipped form to the bit in exact arithmetic and
/// to driver float-contraction noise in practice; the
/// device tests pin them against both the shipped flash and
/// the two-pass form. Staging reads the same KV slots the
/// shipped form reads: every key in the stored range is
/// visible to at least the block row at its own position,
/// so no slot outside the state's capacity is touched.
///
/// Bounds, stated: the head dim is capped at 128 by the
/// same `check_geom` the shipped form runs (the query tile
/// is sized at that bound), and the block walk is uniform
/// across the workgroup (every thread reaches every
/// barrier; rows past the call's row count stage as zeros,
/// compute, and are never written out).
const FLASH_STAGED_SHADER: &str = r#"
struct FlashParams {
    rows: u32,
    q_heads: u32,
    kv_heads: u32,
    head_dim: u32,
    stored: u32,
    first_pos: u32,
    start_pos: u32,
    window: u32,
    ring: u32,
    scale: f32,
    grid_x: u32,
}

@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> q: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read> keys: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read> values: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(3) var<storage, read_write> out: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(4) var<uniform> params: FlashParams;

// The K/V block tile: 32 keys at a padded (head_dim + 1)
// stride, sized at the head-dim bound of 128.
var<workgroup> kv_tile: array<f32, 4128>;
// The query block tile: 8 rows at the head-dim bound.
var<workgroup> q_tile: array<f32, 1024>;
// The score tile: 8 rows x 32 keys.
var<workgroup> s_tile: array<f32, 256>;

@compute @workgroup_size(256)
fn flash_staged_main(@builtin(workgroup_id) wid: vec3<u32>,
                     @builtin(local_invocation_id) lid: vec3<u32>) {
    let flat_wg = wid.y * params.grid_x + wid.x;
    let head = flat_wg % params.q_heads;
    let row_block = flat_wg / params.q_heads;
    let kv_head = head / (params.q_heads / params.kv_heads);
    let tid = lid.x;
    let row_in_block = tid / 32u;
    let lane = tid % 32u;
    let row = row_block * 8u + row_in_block;
    let p = params.start_pos + row;
    let hd = params.head_dim;
    let stride = hd + 1u;

    // Stage the query block once: rows past the call's row
    // count stage as zeros (they compute and never write
    // out, keeping every barrier uniform).
    for (var e = tid; e < 8u * hd; e += 256u) {
        let r = e / hd;
        let d = e % hd;
        let grow = row_block * 8u + r;
        var v = 0.0;
        if (grow < params.rows) {
            v = q[(grow * params.q_heads + head) * hd + d];
        }
        q_tile[r * hd + d] = v;
    }
    workgroupBarrier();

    var m = -1.0e30;
    var sum = 0.0;
    var acc0 = 0.0;
    var acc1 = 0.0;
    var acc2 = 0.0;
    var acc3 = 0.0;
    for (var t0 = 0u; t0 < params.stored; t0 += 32u) {
        let block_len = min(32u, params.stored - t0);
        // Stage this block's K rows, slot-mapped exactly as
        // the shipped kernels slot them (the ring modulus is
        // the ring capacity, never the mask window).
        for (var e = tid; e < block_len * hd; e += 256u) {
            let j = e / hd;
            let d = e % hd;
            let kp = params.first_pos + t0 + j;
            var slot = kp;
            if (params.ring != 0u) {
                slot = kp % params.ring;
            }
            kv_tile[j * stride + d] =
                keys[(slot * params.kv_heads + kv_head) * hd + d];
        }
        workgroupBarrier();
        // Score phase: lane j scores key t0 + j for this
        // thread's row, the shipped mask and dot order.
        var sc = -1.0e30;
        if (lane < block_len) {
            let kp = params.first_pos + t0 + lane;
            var visible = kp <= p;
            if (params.window != 0u && kp + params.window <= p) {
                visible = false;
            }
            if (visible) {
                var s = 0.0;
                for (var d = 0u; d < hd; d++) {
                    s += q_tile[row_in_block * hd + d] * kv_tile[lane * stride + d];
                }
                sc = s * params.scale;
            }
        }
        s_tile[row_in_block * 32u + lane] = sc;
        workgroupBarrier();
        // Stage this block's V rows into the same tile (the
        // score phase's reads of the K staging are done).
        for (var e = tid; e < block_len * hd; e += 256u) {
            let j = e / hd;
            let d = e % hd;
            let kp = params.first_pos + t0 + j;
