===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/k9_attn_prep.rs =====
//! K9: the fused attention preparation (a fusion product, not
//! a BACKEND.md numbered kernel): the Q and K per-head RMSNorms
//! (K4), the RoPE rotations (K5, sliding layers only), and the
//! KV append (K5) as ONE dispatch per layer.
//!
//! The unfused chain spends five dispatches here per sliding
//! layer (two norms, two rotates, one append) and three per
//! global layer, each over a few hundred to a few thousand
//! elements: at decode sizes these kernels are launch and
//! barrier cost, not math (bench/gpu-resident-2026-10-30.md
//! prices the resident chain's in-pass dispatch overhead at
//! roughly 12 microseconds a dispatch). The three steps also
//! chain with nothing between them but each other's outputs,
//! so they fuse without touching the step order or the math:
//!
//! - The norms are K4's weighted form at the file eps, with
//!   K4's exact per-lane distribution for a row of `head_dim`
//!   (at most 128 here, the K6 bound the session enforces):
//!   lane `d` holds channel `d`, lanes past the width
//!   contribute zero, and the sum of squares reduces through
//!   the same 256-lane partials tree K4 uses, so each norm's
//!   result is the value K4's own dispatch produces.
//! - The rotation is K5's interleaved (adjacent-pair, ggml
//!   NORM) form with K5's angle law, `position *
//!   base^(-2i / head_dim)` computed in f32, applied to the
//!   normed rows before they are written out. The normed row
//!   passes through workgroup memory so each adjacent pair is
//!   rotated by one lane; the pair values are the norm's own
//!   outputs, unrounded by any round trip.
//! - The append is K5's slot law: the position itself for
//!   global layers, `position % ring` for windowed ones (the
//!   ring capacity, not the mask window; see
//!   [`crate::kernels::k6_attention`]'s notes on the split).
//!   V rows are copied untouched, as the append always did.
//!
//! One workgroup of 256 lanes serves one head row. The grid
//! covers, in order, every Q head row, every K head row, and
//! every V head row of the chunk; the segment a workgroup
//! belongs to selects its source, its norm weight, and its
//! destination. Segment sources are addressed by a per-buffer
//! row stride plus a segment offset, so the same kernel reads
//! either three separate projection buffers (stride = the
//! buffer's own width, offset 0) or one concatenated QKV
//! buffer (stride = the concatenated width, offsets at the
//! segment starts); the session picks per layer.
//!
//! The trait path does not use this kernel: it composes the
//! K4 and K5 steps through the `Compute` trait's own seams,
//! and stays the executable reference this fusion is proven
//! against (the resident-session cross-path test and the
//! crate's fused-kernel test both compare the two).
//!
//! An f16 form of the same preparation ([`PREP_F16_SHADER`])
//! serves layers whose KV storage is packed f16
//! ([`crate::kernels::k6_attention::KvStorage::F16`], selected at the backend from
//! `WGPU_COMPUTE_KV_F16`, default off): identical norms,
//! rotation, and slot law, with the KV writes converting
//! on write through `pack2x16float`. K5's append has no
//! f16 form: it writes the trait path's KV, which is f32
//! by construction.

use crate::device::GpuContext;
use crate::error::{Result, WgpuError};

use crate::diag::dbg_log;

/// Largest head dim this kernel serves: the workgroup-memory
/// rotation staging is one f32 per channel, sized for the K6
/// reduce bound the session already enforces.
const MAX_HEAD_DIM: u32 = 128;

/// The fused preparation shader. See the module docs for the
/// segment layout and the numerics contract.
const PREP_SHADER: &str = r#"
struct PrepParams {
    rows: u32,
    q_heads: u32,
    kv_heads: u32,
    head_dim: u32,
    start_pos: u32,
    ring: u32,
    rotate: u32,
    base: f32,
    eps: f32,
    grid_x: u32,
    q_stride: u32,
    q_off: u32,
    kv_stride: u32,
    k_off: u32,
    v_off: u32,
    v_stride: u32,
}

@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> q_in: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read> k_in: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read> v_in: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(3) var<storage, read> q_w: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(4) var<storage, read> k_w: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(5) var<storage, read_write> q_out: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(6) var<storage, read_write> kv_k: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(7) var<storage, read_write> kv_v: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(8) var<uniform> params: PrepParams;

var<workgroup> partials: array<f32, 256>;
var<workgroup> inv_shared: f32;
var<workgroup> vals: array<f32, 128>;

@compute @workgroup_size(256)
fn prep_main(@builtin(workgroup_id) wid: vec3<u32>,
             @builtin(local_invocation_id) lid: vec3<u32>) {
    let seg = wid.y * params.grid_x + wid.x;
    let lane = lid.x;
    let total_q = params.rows * params.q_heads;
    let total_kv = params.rows * params.kv_heads;
    // Whole-workgroup early out: every lane shares `seg`, so
    // the exit is uniform and the barriers below stay legal.
    if (seg >= total_q + 2u * total_kv) {
        return;
    }
    let d = lane;
    let kv_width = params.kv_heads * params.head_dim;

    if (seg >= total_q + total_kv) {
        // V segment: the append's plain copy, no norm, no
        // rotation.
        let s2 = seg - total_q - total_kv;
        let row = s2 / params.kv_heads;
        let head = s2 % params.kv_heads;
        if (d < params.head_dim) {
            let position = params.start_pos + row;
            var slot = position;
            if (params.ring != 0u) {
                slot = position % params.ring;
            }
            kv_v[slot * kv_width + head * params.head_dim + d] =
                v_in[row * params.v_stride + params.v_off + head * params.head_dim + d];
        }
        return;
    }

    let is_q = seg < total_q;
    var row = 0u;
    var head = 0u;
    var src_base = 0u;
    if (is_q) {
        row = seg / params.q_heads;
        head = seg % params.q_heads;
        src_base = row * params.q_stride + params.q_off + head * params.head_dim;
    } else {
        let s2 = seg - total_q;
        row = s2 / params.kv_heads;
        head = s2 % params.kv_heads;
        src_base = row * params.kv_stride + params.k_off + head * params.head_dim;
    }

    // The norm, K4's distribution and tree for a row of
    // head_dim: lane d holds channel d (lanes past the width
    // hold zero), partials reduce 128, 64, ..., 1.
    var x = 0.0;
    if (d < params.head_dim) {
        x = q_in[src_base + d];
        if (!is_q) {
            x = k_in[src_base + d];
        }
    }
    partials[lane] = x * x;
    workgroupBarrier();
    var stride = 128u;
    while (stride > 0u) {
        if (lane < stride) {
            partials[lane] += partials[lane + stride];
        }
        workgroupBarrier();
        stride >>= 1u;
    }
    if (lane == 0u) {
        inv_shared = inverseSqrt(partials[0] / f32(params.head_dim) + params.eps);
    }
    workgroupBarrier();
    let inv = inv_shared;
    var y = 0.0;
    if (d < params.head_dim) {
        var w = q_w[d];
        if (!is_q) {
            w = k_w[d];
        }
        y = x * inv * w;
    }

    let position = params.start_pos + row;
    var slot = position;
    if (params.ring != 0u) {
        slot = position % params.ring;
    }
    let q_base = (row * params.q_heads + head) * params.head_dim;
    let k_base = slot * kv_width + head * params.head_dim;

    if (params.rotate == 1u) {
        if (d < params.head_dim) {
            vals[d] = y;
        }
        workgroupBarrier();
        // One lane per adjacent pair: K5's rotation, its angle
        // law and pairing, over the norm's own outputs.
        let pair = lane;
        if (pair < params.head_dim / 2u) {
            let angle = f32(position)
                * pow(params.base, -2.0 * f32(pair) / f32(params.head_dim));
            let c = cos(angle);
            let s = sin(angle);
            let a = vals[2u * pair];
            let b = vals[2u * pair + 1u];
            let r0 = a * c - b * s;
            let r1 = a * s + b * c;
            if (is_q) {
                q_out[q_base + 2u * pair] = r0;
                q_out[q_base + 2u * pair + 1u] = r1;
            } else {
                kv_k[k_base + 2u * pair] = r0;
                kv_k[k_base + 2u * pair + 1u] = r1;
            }
        }
        return;
    }
    if (d < params.head_dim) {
        if (is_q) {
            q_out[q_base + d] = y;
        } else {
            kv_k[k_base + d] = y;
        }
    }
}
"#;

/// The f16 preparation shader: [`PREP_SHADER`] with the
/// two KV bindings packed f16 (`array<u32>`, two values
/// per word) and the three KV write sites converting on
/// write through WGSL's `pack2x16float`. Everything else
/// (the norms, the rotation, the slot law, the params) is
/// the f32 form's, operation for operation; the Q output
/// stays f32 in both forms. The write sites, per segment:
///
/// - The rotation path already computes each adjacent
///   pair in one lane, so that lane packs its pair
///   directly: `pack2x16float(vec2(r0, r1))` at word
///   `(k_base + 2 * pair) / 2`.
/// - The non-rotated K path and the V path produce one
///   element per lane, so the head row is staged through
///   the workgroup `vals` array (the same array the
///   rotation path stages through) and the even lanes
///   pack the pairs. Head dim is even and at most 128
///   (this kernel's bound), so a pair never straddles a
///   head row or a workgroup.
///
/// Word indices divide the element index by two, which
/// is exact because every base is even: `kv_width` is
/// even (refused by name at KV allocation, see
/// [`crate::kernels::k6_attention::DeviceKv`]) and
/// `head_dim` is even (this kernel's own prepare bound).
/// Routed per layer from [`PrepArgs::kv_f16`]; an f32
/// layer never binds it. Design and precision analysis:
/// bench/f16-kv-2026-11-07.md.
const PREP_F16_SHADER: &str = r#"
struct PrepParams {
    rows: u32,
    q_heads: u32,
    kv_heads: u32,
    head_dim: u32,
    start_pos: u32,
    ring: u32,
    rotate: u32,
    base: f32,
    eps: f32,
    grid_x: u32,
    q_stride: u32,
    q_off: u32,
    kv_stride: u32,
    k_off: u32,
    v_off: u32,
    v_stride: u32,
}

@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> q_in: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read> k_in: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read> v_in: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(3) var<storage, read> q_w: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(4) var<storage, read> k_w: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(5) var<storage, read_write> q_out: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(6) var<storage, read_write> kv_k: array<u32>;
@group(0) @binding(7) var<storage, read_write> kv_v: array<u32>;
@group(0) @binding(8) var<uniform> params: PrepParams;

var<workgroup> partials: array<f32, 256>;
var<workgroup> inv_shared: f32;
var<workgroup> vals: array<f32, 128>;

@compute @workgroup_size(256)
fn prep_f16_main(@builtin(workgroup_id) wid: vec3<u32>,
                 @builtin(local_invocation_id) lid: vec3<u32>) {
    let seg = wid.y * params.grid_x + wid.x;
    let lane = lid.x;
    let total_q = params.rows * params.q_heads;
    let total_kv = params.rows * params.kv_heads;
    // Whole-workgroup early out: every lane shares `seg`, so
    // the exit is uniform and the barriers below stay legal.
    if (seg >= total_q + 2u * total_kv) {
        return;
    }
    let d = lane;
    let kv_width = params.kv_heads * params.head_dim;

    if (seg >= total_q + total_kv) {
        // V segment: stage the head row through workgroup
        // memory, then the even lanes pack each pair (the
        // f32 form copies element-wise; the packed form
        // cannot, since a word carries two elements).
        let s2 = seg - total_q - total_kv;
        let row = s2 / params.kv_heads;
        let head = s2 % params.kv_heads;
        if (d < params.head_dim) {
            vals[d] = v_in[row * params.v_stride + params.v_off
                + head * params.head_dim + d];
        }
        workgroupBarrier();
        if (d < params.head_dim && d % 2u == 0u) {
            let position = params.start_pos + row;
            var slot = position;
            if (params.ring != 0u) {
                slot = position % params.ring;
            }
            let word = (slot * kv_width + head * params.head_dim + d) / 2u;
            kv_v[word] = pack2x16float(vec2<f32>(vals[d], vals[d + 1u]));
        }
        return;
    }

    let is_q = seg < total_q;
    var row = 0u;
    var head = 0u;
    var src_base = 0u;
    if (is_q) {
        row = seg / params.q_heads;
        head = seg % params.q_heads;
        src_base = row * params.q_stride + params.q_off + head * params.head_dim;
    } else {
        let s2 = seg - total_q;
        row = s2 / params.kv_heads;
        head = s2 % params.kv_heads;
        src_base = row * params.kv_stride + params.k_off + head * params.head_dim;
    }

    // The norm, K4's distribution and tree for a row of
    // head_dim: lane d holds channel d (lanes past the width
    // hold zero), partials reduce 128, 64, ..., 1.
    var x = 0.0;
    if (d < params.head_dim) {
        x = q_in[src_base + d];
        if (!is_q) {
            x = k_in[src_base + d];
        }
    }
    partials[lane] = x * x;
    workgroupBarrier();
    var stride = 128u;
    while (stride > 0u) {
        if (lane < stride) {
            partials[lane] += partials[lane + stride];
        }
        workgroupBarrier();
        stride >>= 1u;
    }
    if (lane == 0u) {
        inv_shared = inverseSqrt(partials[0] / f32(params.head_dim) + params.eps);
    }
    workgroupBarrier();
    let inv = inv_shared;
    var y = 0.0;
    if (d < params.head_dim) {
        var w = q_w[d];
        if (!is_q) {
            w = k_w[d];
        }
        y = x * inv * w;
    }

    let position = params.start_pos + row;
    var slot = position;
    if (params.ring != 0u) {
        slot = position % params.ring;
    }
    let q_base = (row * params.q_heads + head) * params.head_dim;
    let k_base = slot * kv_width + head * params.head_dim;

    if (params.rotate == 1u) {
        if (d < params.head_dim) {
            vals[d] = y;
        }
        workgroupBarrier();
        // One lane per adjacent pair: K5's rotation, its angle
        // law and pairing, over the norm's own outputs. The
        // pair lane packs both rotated elements into one
        // word: the packed form of the f32 form's two
        // element writes at the same addresses.
        let pair = lane;
        if (pair < params.head_dim / 2u) {
            let angle = f32(position)
                * pow(params.base, -2.0 * f32(pair) / f32(params.head_dim));
            let c = cos(angle);
            let s = sin(angle);
            let a = vals[2u * pair];
            let b = vals[2u * pair + 1u];
            let r0 = a * c - b * s;
            let r1 = a * s + b * c;
            if (is_q) {
                q_out[q_base + 2u * pair] = r0;
                q_out[q_base + 2u * pair + 1u] = r1;
            } else {
                kv_k[(k_base + 2u * pair) / 2u] =
                    pack2x16float(vec2<f32>(r0, r1));
            }
        }
        return;
    }
    if (is_q) {
        if (d < params.head_dim) {
            q_out[q_base + d] = y;
        }
    } else {
        // Non-rotated K: stage the normed row and pack
        // pairs from the even lanes, like the V segment.
        if (d < params.head_dim) {
            vals[d] = y;
        }
        workgroupBarrier();
        if (d < params.head_dim && d % 2u == 0u) {
            kv_k[(k_base + d) / 2u] =
                pack2x16float(vec2<f32>(vals[d], vals[d + 1u]));
        }
    }
}
"#;

/// The buffers and geometry one fused preparation dispatch
/// binds. Sources carry a row stride and a segment offset so
/// one kernel serves separate projection buffers and a
/// concatenated QKV buffer alike (see the module docs).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct PrepArgs<'a> {
    /// Query rows as projected (read).
    pub q_in: &'a wgpu::Buffer,
    /// Row stride of `q_in`, in elements.
    pub q_stride: usize,
    /// Element offset of the Q segment within each `q_in` row.
    pub q_off: usize,
    /// Key rows as projected (read).
    pub k_in: &'a wgpu::Buffer,
    /// Row stride of the K source, in elements.
    pub kv_stride: usize,
    /// Element offset of the K segment within each source row.
    pub k_off: usize,
    /// Value rows as projected (read).
    pub v_in: &'a wgpu::Buffer,
    /// Row stride of the V source, in elements (separate from
    /// the K stride: a partial batch can carry K in the
    /// concatenated rows while V keeps its own buffer).
    pub v_stride: usize,
    /// Element offset of the V segment within each source row.
    pub v_off: usize,
    /// Query norm weight, `[head_dim]`.
    pub q_w: &'a wgpu::Buffer,
    /// Key norm weight, `[head_dim]`.
    pub k_w: &'a wgpu::Buffer,
    /// Normed (and, on sliding layers, rotated) query rows
    /// (written), `[rows][q_heads * head_dim]`.
    pub q_out: &'a wgpu::Buffer,
    /// The layer's resident KV key buffer (written at slots).
    pub kv_k: &'a wgpu::Buffer,
    /// The layer's resident KV value buffer (written at slots).
    pub kv_v: &'a wgpu::Buffer,
    /// Whether the KV buffers are packed f16
    /// ([`crate::kernels::k6_attention::KvStorage::F16`]): selects the f16 preparation
    /// form ([`PREP_F16_SHADER`], diag stamp
    /// `k9_attn_prep_f16`), whose KV writes convert on
    /// write. `false` runs the shipped form exactly; the
    /// two forms share params, grid, and every non-KV
    /// write. The caller takes this from the layer's own
    /// storage (`LayerKv::storage`), so a buffer can
    /// never be written through the wrong form.
    pub kv_f16: bool,
    /// Chunk rows.
    pub rows: usize,
    /// Query head count.
    pub q_heads: usize,
    /// KV head count.
    pub kv_heads: usize,
    /// Per-head dimension (even, at most [`MAX_HEAD_DIM`]).
    pub head_dim: usize,
    /// Absolute position of the chunk's first row (rewritable
    /// through the returned call).
    pub start_pos: usize,
    /// The windowed ring capacity, or `None` for a global
    /// layer (slot = position).
    pub ring: Option<usize>,
    /// Rotate Q and K after their norms (sliding layers);
    /// global layers pass `false` (NoPE).
    pub rotate: bool,
    /// The RoPE base (the config's resolved SWA base).
    pub base: f32,
    /// The norm epsilon (the file's rms eps).
    pub eps: f32,
}

/// One prepared fused-preparation dispatch, encodable any
/// number of times into any command encoder. The start
/// position is the one parameter a sequence changes per
/// forward, so the call keeps its uniform buffer and rewrites
/// that one word through
/// [`K9PrepCall::set_start_position`]; everything else is
/// fixed at prepare time. This is the device-resident
/// forward's unit of composition (see [`crate::session`]);
/// the trait path never prepares one.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct K9PrepCall {
    pipeline: wgpu::ComputePipeline,
    bind_group: wgpu::BindGroup,
    params: wgpu::Buffer,
    grid: (u32, u32),
    /// Diag timestamp stamp (see `crate::timestamps`); `None`
    /// unless the context carries a recorder.
    diag: Option<crate::timestamps::DiagStamp>,
}

impl K9PrepCall {
    /// Record this call's dispatch into `encoder`.
    pub fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut wgpu::CommandEncoder) {
        let mut pass = encoder.begin_compute_pass(&wgpu::ComputePassDescriptor {
            label: Some("k9 attention prep"),
            timestamp_writes: None,
        });
        self.encode_into(&mut pass);
    }

    /// Record this dispatch into an already-open compute
    /// `pass`: the composition form the device-resident
    /// session uses to chain a whole forward into one pass
    /// (wgpu inserts the hazard barriers between dispatches
    /// inside the pass).
    pub fn encode_into(&self, pass: &mut wgpu::ComputePass<'_>) {
        let slot = self.diag.as_ref().and_then(|d| d.begin(pass));
        pass.set_pipeline(&self.pipeline);
        pass.set_bind_group(0, &self.bind_group, &[]);
        pass.dispatch_workgroups(self.grid.0, self.grid.1, 1);
        if let (Some(d), Some(s)) = (&self.diag, slot) {
            d.end(pass, s);
        }
    }

    /// Point the preparation at a new absolute start position
    /// (the prepared rows sit at `start_position + row` for
    /// rotation angles and append slots). Same queue-ordering
    /// contract as
    /// [`crate::kernels::k5_rope_kv::K5RotateCall::set_start_position`]:
    /// call it while no submission using this call is in
    /// flight.
    pub fn set_start_position(&self, ctx: &GpuContext, start_position: usize) {
        // PrepParams word 4, after rows, q_heads, kv_heads,
        // head_dim.
        ctx.queue
            .write_buffer(&self.params, 16, &(start_position as u32).to_le_bytes());
    }
}

/// The compiled K9 pipelines (the shipped preparation
/// and its f16 KV form; one shader and entry point each).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct K9Pipeline {
    prep: wgpu::ComputePipeline,
    /// The f16 preparation form (see [`PREP_F16_SHADER`]),
    /// built unconditionally like its sibling so a shader
    /// defect fails at construction, not on first f16
    /// use; it serves only calls whose [`PrepArgs::kv_f16`]
    /// is set.
    prep_f16: wgpu::ComputePipeline,
}

impl K9Pipeline {
    /// Compile the K9 pipelines on `device`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::Pipeline`] when wgpu rejects a shader.
    pub fn new(device: &wgpu::Device) -> Result<Self> {
        let build = |source: &str, entry: &'static str, label: &'static str| {
            let module = device.create_shader_module(wgpu::ShaderModuleDescriptor {
                label: Some(label),
                source: wgpu::ShaderSource::Wgsl(source.into()),
            });
            device.create_compute_pipeline(&wgpu::ComputePipelineDescriptor {
                label: Some(label),
                layout: None,
                module: &module,
                entry_point: Some(entry),
                compilation_options: wgpu::PipelineCompilationOptions::default(),
                cache: None,
            })
        };
        let prep = build(PREP_SHADER, "prep_main", "k9 attention prep");
        let prep_f16 = build(PREP_F16_SHADER, "prep_f16_main", "k9 attention prep f16");
        dbg_log!("k9 pipelines built");
        Ok(K9Pipeline { prep, prep_f16 })
    }

    /// Prepare a fused preparation dispatch over device
    /// buffers (see [`PrepArgs`]).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::InvalidTensor`] when the geometry is
    /// unusable (zero rows or heads, an odd or oversized head
    /// dim, or a rotation base that is not finite and greater
    /// than 1 while rotating).
    pub fn prepare(&self, ctx: &GpuContext, args: &PrepArgs<'_>) -> Result<K9PrepCall> {
        if args.rows == 0 || args.q_heads == 0 || args.kv_heads == 0 {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: "k9 prep".to_string(),
                detail: format!(
                    "rows {}, q_heads {}, kv_heads {}: nothing to prepare",
                    args.rows, args.q_heads, args.kv_heads
                ),
            });
        }
        if args.head_dim < 2 || args.head_dim % 2 != 0 || args.head_dim > MAX_HEAD_DIM as usize {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: "k9 prep".to_string(),
                detail: format!(
                    "head_dim {} is outside the even range 2..={MAX_HEAD_DIM} this \
                     kernel's workgroup staging serves",
                    args.head_dim
                ),
            });
        }
        if args.rotate && (!args.base.is_finite() || args.base <= 1.0) {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: "k9 prep".to_string(),
                detail: format!("rope base {} is not finite and greater than 1", args.base),
            });
        }
        // One workgroup per segment (not per 256 elements):
        // the grid covers segments, each exactly one workgroup.
        let total = (args.rows * (args.q_heads + 2 * args.kv_heads)) as u64;
        let grid = crate::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::grid_dims(total.max(1));
        let params: [u32; 16] = [
            args.rows as u32,
            args.q_heads as u32,
            args.kv_heads as u32,
            args.head_dim as u32,
            args.start_pos as u32,
            args.ring.map_or(0, |r| r as u32),
            u32::from(args.rotate),
            args.base.to_bits(),
            args.eps.to_bits(),
            grid.0,
            args.q_stride as u32,
            args.q_off as u32,
            args.kv_stride as u32,
            args.k_off as u32,
            args.v_off as u32,
            args.v_stride as u32,
        ];
        let param_bytes: Vec<u8> = params.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect();
        let params_buf = ctx.uniform_buffer("k9 prep params", &param_bytes);
        // The args' storage flag picks the form: the two
        // pipelines' bind group layouts differ only in
        // the KV bindings' element type, and each layout
        // is taken from its own pipeline, so a packed
        // buffer can only ever bind to the packed shader.
        let (pipeline, kernel) = if args.kv_f16 {
            (&self.prep_f16, "k9_attn_prep_f16")
        } else {
            (&self.prep, "k9_attn_prep")
        };
        let bind_group = ctx.device.create_bind_group(&wgpu::BindGroupDescriptor {
            label: Some("k9 prep bind group"),
            layout: &pipeline.get_bind_group_layout(0),
            entries: &[
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 0,
                    resource: args.q_in.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 1,
                    resource: args.k_in.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 2,
                    resource: args.v_in.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 3,
                    resource: args.q_w.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 4,
                    resource: args.k_w.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 5,
                    resource: args.q_out.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 6,
                    resource: args.kv_k.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 7,
                    resource: args.kv_v.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 8,
                    resource: params_buf.as_entire_binding(),
                },
            ],
        });
        Ok(K9PrepCall {
            pipeline: pipeline.clone(),
            bind_group,
            params: params_buf,
            grid,
            diag: ctx.diag_stamp(crate::timestamps::DispatchMeta {
                kernel,
                rows: args.rows as u64,
                cols: (args.q_heads * args.head_dim) as u64,
                quant: "",
                weight_bytes: args.q_w.size() + args.k_w.size(),
                shape: format!(
                    "rows={} q_heads={} kv_heads={} head_dim={} rotate={} start={}",
                    args.rows,
                    args.q_heads,
                    args.kv_heads,
                    args.head_dim,
                    args.rotate,
                    args.start_pos
                ),
            }),
        })
    }
}

/// The ring slot of an absolute position under this kernel's
/// law, restating the shader's for host-side callers and
/// tests: the position itself for global layers, `position %
/// ring` for windowed ones. (Same law as
/// [`crate::kernels::k5_rope_kv::slot_of`]; this kernel's
/// `ring` parameter is the capacity, never the mask window.)
#[must_use]
pub fn slot_of(position: usize, ring: Option<usize>) -> usize {
    match ring {
        None => position,
        Some(r) => position % r,
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn shader_carries_its_entry_point_and_laws() {
        assert!(PREP_SHADER.contains("fn prep_main"));
        // The NORM pairing is adjacent channels, as in K5.
        assert!(PREP_SHADER.contains("2u * pair"));
        // The slot law splits ring (storage) from window
        // (mask): the shader takes the ring only.
        assert!(PREP_SHADER.contains("slot = position % params.ring"));
        // The norm's inverse-RMS form is K4's.
        assert!(PREP_SHADER.contains("inverseSqrt(partials[0] / f32(params.head_dim)"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn f16_shader_carries_the_same_laws_with_packed_writes() {
        assert!(PREP_F16_SHADER.contains("fn prep_f16_main"));
        // The shared laws, verbatim: the NORM pairing,
        // the slot law, the norm's inverse-RMS form.
        assert!(PREP_F16_SHADER.contains("2u * pair"));
        assert!(PREP_F16_SHADER.contains("slot = position % params.ring"));
        assert!(PREP_F16_SHADER.contains("inverseSqrt(partials[0] / f32(params.head_dim)"));
        // The packed bindings and all three converting
        // write sites: the rotation pair pack, the
        // staged non-rotated K pack, and the staged V
        // pack. The Q output stays an f32 element write
        // in both forms.
        assert!(PREP_F16_SHADER.contains("var<storage, read_write> kv_k: array<u32>;"));
        assert!(PREP_F16_SHADER.contains("var<storage, read_write> kv_v: array<u32>;"));
        assert!(PREP_F16_SHADER.contains("pack2x16float(vec2<f32>(r0, r1))"));
        assert_eq!(
            PREP_F16_SHADER
                .matches("pack2x16float(vec2<f32>(vals[d], vals[d + 1u]))")
                .count(),
            2
        );
        assert!(PREP_F16_SHADER.contains("q_out[q_base + 2u * pair] = r0;"));
        // The f32 form must never carry the packed
        // bindings (a swapped constant would compile
        // and silently corrupt the cache).
        assert!(!PREP_SHADER.contains("pack2x16float"));
        assert!(PREP_SHADER.contains("var<storage, read_write> kv_k: array<f32>;"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn f16_shader_validates_under_naga() {
        // The adapterless-machine shader gate (see the
        // staged-flash test in k6_attention for what
        // this does and does not prove).
        let module = naga::front::wgsl::parse_str(PREP_F16_SHADER).unwrap_or_else(|e| {
            panic!(
                "prep f16 WGSL parse failed: {}",
                e.emit_to_string(PREP_F16_SHADER)
            )
        });
        naga::valid::Validator::new(
            naga::valid::ValidationFlags::all(),
            naga::valid::Capabilities::all(),
        )
        .validate(&module)
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("prep f16 Naga validation failed: {e:?}"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn slot_of_matches_the_append_law() {
        assert_eq!(slot_of(7, None), 7);
        assert_eq!(slot_of(7, Some(2048)), 7);
        assert_eq!(slot_of(2049, Some(2048)), 1);
        assert_eq!(slot_of(4096, Some(2111)), 4096 % 2111);
    }
}

//! The kernel set, one module per kernel, in BACKEND.md
//! Section 3's priority order (bytes streamed per token on
//! Glimmer, then position on the critical path).
//!
//! The full set is implemented: K1, K2, and K3 (the three GEMV
//! kernels cover Glimmer's whole weight stream: Q4_K, Q6_K,
//! Q5_K), K4 (norms and the residual add), K5 (RoPE plus KV
//! append), K6 (grouped-query attention over the resident KV
//! buffers K5 fills), K7 (the elementwise activations), and K8
//! (the embedding gather and the head finishing math). Every
//! `Compute` step runs on the device; nothing in this crate
//! silently substitutes another path for a kernel (BACKEND.md
//! Section 6's ladder puts per-op CPU fallback at load time, as
//! a disclosed composition decision by the caller, not as a
//! quiet detour inside a step).
//!
//! Past the numbered set, the K9 module is a fusion product
//! for the device-resident forward: the attention preparation
//! (the Q/K norms, the sliding layers' rotations, and the KV
//! append) as one dispatch, proven against the K4/K5
//! composition it replaces in that path only. K10 and K11 are
//! the prefill GEMMs (Q4_K and Q6_K): tiled matrix-matrix
//! forms of K1 and K2 that stage dequantized weight tiles in
//! workgroup memory so a chunk's weights stream once instead
//! of once per row, proven against the GEMV composition they
//! replace in the resident session's chunk plans only. K12,
//! K13, and K14 are the prefill MMQ set: K12 quantizes the
//! chunk's activations to Q8_1 on the device (carrying the
//! activation transforms the GEMM pair fuses into its
//! product), and K13 (Q4_K) / K14 (Q6_K) run the product as
//! DP4A integer dots against the weights' packed payloads,
//! the design llama.cpp's MMQ reaches its prefill rates
//! with. The session prefers the MMQ form over the GEMM form
//! per projection when the device built it; the GEMM stays
//! as the named fallback for devices and shapes the MMQ
//! refuses. K15 (Q4_K) and K16 (Q6_K) are the wide-tile
//! double-buffered MMQ forms: a 128-class output tile, a
//! 4x8 per-thread sub-tile, and half-super-block staging
//! steps pipelined through two workgroup buffer sets, so
//! staging and compute overlap instead of alternating
//! across two barriers per super-block. The session tries
//! the wide form first at chunk row counts past its
//! threshold, then the standard MMQ, then the GEMM: one
//! ladder, every refusal named.
//!
//! K17 is the DFlash draft set: the NEOX (half-split)
//! rotate and the draft's non-causal, two-source
//! (committed plus block) sliding-window attention, the
//! two primitives the draft forward needs that the
//! Glimmer kernels do not provide; the rest of the draft
//! forward composes K1/K2/K3/K4/K7/K8 unchanged.
//!
//! K18 is the small-batch product set: K13/K14's MMQ
//! math at a 16-row batch cap, one weight stream per
//! dispatch for the 2..=16 row band the speculative
//! loop runs at, in all three quant families (Q4_K,
//! Q5_K, Q6_K). The session routes to it only under
//! its env-set threshold, which defaults off; see the
//! module's own docs for the reasoning.
//!
//! K19 is the counter-proposal to K18 in the same
//! band: the Q4_K small-batch product in llama.cpp's
//! mul_mat_vec register-streaming shape, batch
//! specialized into the shader as literals, weights
//! dequantized in registers with no weight staging in
//! workgroup memory at all (the streaming-rate
//! research's structural verdict on both staged
//! attempts). The session routes to it only under its
//! own env-set threshold, which also defaults off.
//!
//! K21 is the Q5_K arm of the register-streaming
//! small-batch family (K19 carries Q4_K): the same
//! 2..=16 band as K18, but llama.cpp mul_mat_vec's
//! shape instead of the MMQ's: weights dequantize in
//! registers and are never staged in workgroup
//! memory, the batch lives inside the workgroup as
//! generation-specialized register accumulators, and
//! the only workgroup array is the reduction
//! partials. The session routes to it only under the
//! shared MMV env threshold, which ships open at the
//! full band (16) since the 2026-11-06 baseline
//! verdict and is narrowed per shape by the band
//! routing table; see the module's own docs for the
//! reasoning.
//!
//! K21F is K21's finish-carrying form: the same
//! register-streaming Q5_K product with the head's
//! fused finishing map (logit scale, tanh softcap,
//! K3's modes and expressions) applied at the
//! reduction's final store, built because the
//! 2026-11-06 verdict showed plain K21 never fires
//! in the real forward: on the current model file
//! the Q5_K tensors are the head, and the head sites
//! prepare a finish this variant now carries. It is
//! registered at backend construction and routed at
//! the resident block head only under two gates: its
//! own switch (`WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD`, default on
//! since the wave18 retest met the reopen criterion
//! the guard wrote after the 2026-11-07
//! defaults-confirmation identity failure; `0`
//! closes it) and the shared MMV band; see
//! bench/k21-finish-2026-11-06.md,
//! bench/k21f-default-guard-2026-11-07.md, and
//! bench/k21f-default-flip-2026-11-07.md.
//!
//! K20 is the Q6_K register-streaming small-batch
//! product: K18's Q6_K band (2..=16 rows, one weight
//! stream per dispatch) in llama.cpp `mul_mat_vec`'s
//! shape instead of the MMQ shape, dequantizing in
//! registers and staging nothing but reduction
//! partials, as the counter-proposal to K18's and the
//! wide MMQ's workgroup-memory staging (the streaming
//! measurements behind it are in the module's own
//! docs). It shares its routing threshold with the
//! Q4_K register-streaming product (env
//! `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS`, shipped default 16,
//! the full band; set it to 1 to close the gate).
//!
//! K22 is the Q4_K MMQ product reorganized for
//! occupancy: the prefill profile measured K13 at
//! VGPR 256 (the architectural cap) streaming at under
//! 5% of the card's ceiling, so K22 runs the same MMQ
//! math in llama.cpp mul_mmq's register organization
//! (a per-thread register cache consumed column by
//! column, scalar integer dots, immediate folds) at the
//! same tile coverage. The session routes to it only
//! under its own env switch, which defaults off; see
//! the module's own docs for the reasoning.
//!
//! K23 is the same Q4_K MMQ product with the one
//! structural piece K22 left behind: llama.cpp's staging
//! repack. The staging rounds shrink to llama's 128-element
//! quantum, the staged qs arrays take llama's QPITCH skew,
//! and the scale pairs split into their own arrays, all
//! transcribed from mul_mmq_cm1; K13's thread organization
//! and math are unchanged, so a compiled or measured
//! difference is attributable to the staging alone. The
//! session routes to it only under its own env switch,
//! which defaults off; see the module's own docs and
//! `bench/k23-mmq-repack-2026-11-06.md`.

pub mod k10_q4k_gemm;
pub mod k11_q6k_gemm;
pub mod k12_q8_quant;
pub mod k13_q4k_mmq;
pub mod k14_q6k_mmq;
pub mod k15_q4k_mmq_wide;
pub mod k16_q6k_mmq_wide;
pub mod k17_dflash;
pub mod k18_small_batch;
pub mod k19_q4k_mmv;
pub mod k1_q4k_gemv;
pub mod k20_q6k_mmv;
pub mod k21_q5k_mmv;
pub mod k21_q5k_mmv_finish;
pub mod k22_q4k_mmq;
pub mod k23_q4k_coopmat;
pub mod k23_q4k_mmq;
pub mod k24_q4k_coopmat;
pub mod k2_q6k_gemv;
pub mod k3_q5k_gemv;
pub mod k4_rmsnorm;
pub mod k5_rope_kv;

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/src/kernels/splitk_reduce.rs =====
//! Split-K reduction: the second half of the MMQ split-K
//! products (the split forms of K13 and K14; see
//! `bench/splitk-mmq-2026-11-07.md` for the design record).
//!
//! A split product partitions the reduction (K) dimension
//! across `S` workgroups per output tile: slice `s` walks a
//! contiguous range of super-block columns and writes its
//! f32 partial sums to slice `s` of a scratch buffer laid
//! out `[splits][batch][out_rows]`. This kernel folds the
//! slices back into the output, one thread per output
//! element, summing in ascending slice order:
//! `out[i] = p[0][i] + p[1][i] + ... + p[S-1][i]`, each add
//! an ordinary f32 add in that fixed order.
//!
//! Drift contract, stated plainly: the integer dots inside
//! each slice are exact and each slice folds its
//! per-sub-block scale terms in the same order the unsplit
//! kernel folds them, but the unsplit kernel accumulates
//! one chain over the whole K range while the split form
//! accumulates one chain per slice and then adds the slice
//! sums. f32 addition is not associative, so the split
//! result is NOT bit-identical to the unsplit product in
//! general; it differs by float reassociation noise, the
//! same class the MMQ correctness gates already bound
//! against the host reference running the same quantized
//! math. The reduction order here is fixed by construction
//! (ascending slices, one thread per element, no atomics),
//! so a split run is deterministic run to run.
//!
//! The kernel is family-agnostic (it folds f32 partials);
//! the caller passes its quantization family name purely so
//! the diag stamp attributes the dispatch.

use crate::device::GpuContext;
use crate::error::{Result, WgpuError};

use crate::diag::dbg_log;

/// The largest split factor a split product accepts: the
/// resolver's ceiling (`WGPU_COMPUTE_MMQ_SPLITK` admits
/// 1..=8) and the prepare-time refusal bound share it, so
/// the two can never disagree.
pub const SPLITK_MAX: u32 = 8;

/// Threads per reduce workgroup.
const REDUCE_WORKGROUP: u32 = 256;

/// The reduction shader. One thread per output element;
/// the slice loop is a runtime loop over at most
/// [`SPLITK_MAX`] terms, deliberately not unrolled: the
/// kernel is pure bandwidth over `splits * total` f32
/// reads and the loop bound is uniform across the grid.
const REDUCE_WGSL: &str = r#"struct Params {
    total: u32,
    splits: u32,
}

@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> partials: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read_write> output: array<f32>;
@group(0) @binding(2) var<uniform> params: Params;

@compute @workgroup_size(256)
fn main(@builtin(global_invocation_id) gid: vec3<u32>) {
    let idx = gid.x;
    if (idx >= params.total) {
        return;
    }
    var acc = partials[idx];
    for (var s = 1u; s < params.splits; s++) {
        acc += partials[s * params.total + idx];
    }
    output[idx] = acc;
}
"#;

/// One prepared reduction dispatch: folds `splits` partial
/// slices of `total` f32 each into the output.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct SplitkReduceCall {
    pipeline: wgpu::ComputePipeline,
    bind_group: wgpu::BindGroup,
    grid: u32,
    /// Diag timestamp stamp (see `crate::timestamps`); `None`
    /// unless the context carries a recorder.
    diag: Option<crate::timestamps::DiagStamp>,
}

impl SplitkReduceCall {
    /// Record this dispatch into an already-open compute
    /// `pass`, after the split product that wrote the
    /// partials (the composition form the split calls use).
    pub fn encode_into(&self, pass: &mut wgpu::ComputePass<'_>) {
        let slot = self.diag.as_ref().and_then(|d| d.begin(pass));
        pass.set_pipeline(&self.pipeline);
        pass.set_bind_group(0, &self.bind_group, &[]);
        pass.dispatch_workgroups(self.grid, 1, 1);
        if let (Some(d), Some(s)) = (&self.diag, slot) {
            d.end(pass, s);
        }
    }
}

/// The compiled split-K reducer. One instance serves every
/// split product on the device; each split pipeline owns
/// one (compilation is one small shader, and ownership
/// keeps the split call types self-contained).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct SplitkReducer {
    pipeline: wgpu::ComputePipeline,
}

impl SplitkReducer {
    /// Compile the reducer on `device`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::Pipeline`] when the device rejects the
    /// shader.
    pub fn new(device: &wgpu::Device) -> Result<Self> {
        let module = device.create_shader_module(wgpu::ShaderModuleDescriptor {
            label: Some("splitk reduce shader"),
            source: wgpu::ShaderSource::Wgsl(REDUCE_WGSL.into()),
        });
        let pipeline = device.create_compute_pipeline(&wgpu::ComputePipelineDescriptor {
            label: Some("splitk reduce pipeline"),
            layout: None,
            module: &module,
            entry_point: Some("main"),
            compilation_options: wgpu::PipelineCompilationOptions::default(),
            cache: None,
        });
        dbg_log!("splitk reducer built (workgroup {REDUCE_WORKGROUP})");
        Ok(SplitkReducer { pipeline })
    }

    /// Prepare a reduction of `partials` (laid out
    /// `[splits][total]`) into `output` (`total` f32).
    /// `quant` names the caller's quantization family for
    /// the diag stamp only.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`WgpuError::InvalidTensor`] when `splits` is
    /// outside 2..=[`SPLITK_MAX`], `total` is zero, or a
    /// buffer is smaller than the geometry addresses.
    pub fn prepare(
        &self,
        ctx: &GpuContext,
        partials: &wgpu::Buffer,
        output: &wgpu::Buffer,
        total: u64,
        splits: u32,
        quant: &'static str,
    ) -> Result<SplitkReduceCall> {
        if !(2..=SPLITK_MAX).contains(&splits) {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: "splitk reduce call".to_string(),
                detail: format!(
                    "splits {splits} is outside 2..={SPLITK_MAX} (a split of 1 is the unsplit product)"
                ),
            });
        }
        if total == 0 {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: "splitk reduce call".to_string(),
                detail: "total is zero: nothing to reduce".to_string(),
            });
        }
        let need_partials = u64::from(splits) * total * 4;
        let need_out = total * 4;
        if partials.size() < need_partials || output.size() < need_out {
            return Err(WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
                name: "splitk reduce call".to_string(),
                detail: format!(
                    "buffer sizes (partials {}, out {}) are below the geometry's needs \
                     ({need_partials}, {need_out})",
                    partials.size(),
                    output.size()
                ),
            });
        }
        let total32 = u32::try_from(total).map_err(|_| WgpuError::InvalidTensor {
            name: "splitk reduce call".to_string(),
            detail: format!("total {total} exceeds one dispatch's index range"),
        })?;
        let grid = total32.div_ceil(REDUCE_WORKGROUP);
        let params: [u32; 2] = [total32, splits];
        let param_bytes: Vec<u8> = params.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect();
        let params_buffer = ctx.device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
            label: Some("splitk reduce params"),
            size: param_bytes.len() as u64,
            usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::UNIFORM | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
            mapped_at_creation: false,
        });
        ctx.queue.write_buffer(&params_buffer, 0, &param_bytes);
        let entries = vec![
            wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                binding: 0,
                resource: partials.as_entire_binding(),
            },
            wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                binding: 1,
                resource: output.as_entire_binding(),
            },
            wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                binding: 2,
                resource: params_buffer.as_entire_binding(),
            },
        ];
        let bind_group = ctx.device.create_bind_group(&wgpu::BindGroupDescriptor {
            label: Some("splitk reduce bind group"),
            layout: &self.pipeline.get_bind_group_layout(0),
            entries: &entries,
        });
        Ok(SplitkReduceCall {
            pipeline: self.pipeline.clone(),
            bind_group,
            grid,
            diag: ctx.diag_stamp(crate::timestamps::DispatchMeta {
                kernel: "splitk_reduce",
                rows: total,
                cols: u64::from(splits),
                quant,
                weight_bytes: 0,
                shape: format!("splits={splits} total={total}"),
            }),
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn reduce_shader_sums_slices_in_ascending_order() {
        // The fixed reduction order is the determinism
        // contract: slice 0 seeds the accumulator and the
        // loop walks the remaining slices ascending.
        assert!(REDUCE_WGSL.contains("var acc = partials[idx];"));
        assert!(REDUCE_WGSL.contains("for (var s = 1u; s < params.splits; s++)"));
        assert!(REDUCE_WGSL.contains("acc += partials[s * params.total + idx];"));
        assert!(REDUCE_WGSL.contains("@workgroup_size(256)"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn reduce_shader_validates_under_naga() {
        let module = naga::front::wgsl::parse_str(REDUCE_WGSL)
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("reduce shader must parse: {e}"));
        naga::valid::Validator::new(
            naga::valid::ValidationFlags::all(),
            naga::valid::Capabilities::all(),
        )
        .validate(&module)
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("reduce shader must validate: {e:?}"));
    }
}

//! `wgpu-compute`: the wgpu (Vulkan) implementation of
//! [`muse_glimmer::Compute`], sibling to `cpu-compute`.
//!
//! Naming: PLAN.md and BACKEND.md call the backend family
//! `itak-backend` (the backend trait, `detect()`, and its
//! implementations under one module contract). The implementations
//! land as their own crates beside each other, the way
//! `cpu-compute` landed for the CPU SIMD slot without taking the
//! family name; this crate is the family's wgpu member, and its
//! [`detect`] is the family's hardware detection: adapter facts,
//! a written selection policy, granted-limits verification, and
//! the chosen adapter recorded for the health surface.
//!
//! What is real in this landing (TODO T-4.2, first tiers):
//!
//! - **Device selection** ([`detect`]): Vulkan discrete GPU or a
//!   named refusal listing every adapter seen. llvmpipe counts as
//!   no adapter, per BACKEND.md Section 6. The device opens with
//!   the adapter's own limits and the granted limits are verified
//!   against the kernels' floor before anything runs.
//! - **K1, the Q4_K dequant GEMV** ([`kernels::k1_q4k_gemv`]):
//!   77.3 percent of Glimmer's streamed bytes, reading the ggml
//!   block layout directly in WGSL, checked against the `gguf`
//!   crate's CPU dequantizer plus `torch-math` on synthetic rows
//!   here and on the real file's tensors through the `k1_check`
//!   example, and benched against llama.cpp's measured 708 GB/s
//!   through the `k1_bench` example (results in BACKEND.md).
//! - **K2, the Q6_K dequant GEMV** ([`kernels::k2_q6k_gemv`]):
//!   17.1 percent of the stream (FFN down, attention V), same
//!   tuned parallel shape as K1, with a host-side repack into a
//!   word-aligned device layout (the 210-byte block is not a
//!   whole number of words; the module docs own the reasoning).
//!   Checked and benched through the `k2_check` and `k2_bench`
//!   examples.
//! - **K3, the Q5_K dequant GEMV** ([`kernels::k3_q5k_gemv`]):
//!   the 202,048-row output head, two-dimensional dispatch over
//!   the 65,535-workgroup cap. Checked and benched through the
//!   `k3_check` and `k3_bench` examples.
//!
//! Also wired: K4 (RMSNorm, plain and weighted, plus the
//! residual add) and K7 (SwiGLU and the attention gate), so the
//! FFN runs end to end; K5 (RoPE plus KV append) and K6
//! (grouped-query attention over device-resident KV buffers,
//! with the `attention` crate's cache mirrored on the host for
//! positions and cross-checks), so attention runs end to end;
//! and K8 (the embedding gather in every dtype `cpu-compute`
//! accepts, plus the scale-then-softcap head finishing kernel,
//! proven against `muse_glimmer::softcap_scale`; the trait
//! path's model applies the finishing itself, the resident
//! path runs this kernel). A forward over this backend
//! therefore runs every step on the GPU. Nothing falls back
//! silently; per-op CPU composition is the caller's load-time
//! decision (BACKEND.md Section 6, level L2).
//!
//! The device-resident forward ([`session`]) composes the same
//! kernels without the trait's host round trips: weights
//! upload once, activations and KV stay on the device, and
//! each forward chunk is one command-buffer chain with only
//! the finished logits read back. The trait path remains the
//! executable reference; the resident path is pinned to it by
//! the cross-path session test.

// The coopmat device bridge (coopmat_bridge) is this

#![deny(unsafe_code)]
