#[test]
fn k18_deep_width_and_tile_edge_geometry() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    // Width 768 = three super-blocks per row and 230
    // output rows (tile edges at every candidate), at
    // the band's working depths: the staging loops and
    // the column loop run off their round numbers.
    let (inn, out_rows) = (768usize, 230usize);
    let bytes4 = synthetic_q4k(inn, out_rows);
    let k1 = K1Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k1 pipeline");
    let w4 = k1
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q4k.small.deep", &bytes4, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k1 upload");
    let bytes5 = synthetic_q5k(inn, out_rows);
    let k3 = K3Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k3 pipeline");
    let w5 = k3
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q5k.small.deep", &bytes5, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k3 upload");
    let bytes6 = synthetic_q6k(inn, out_rows);
    let k2 = K2Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k2 pipeline");
    let w6 = k2
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q6k.small.deep", &bytes6, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k2 upload");
    for shape in tile_candidates() {
        for batch in [7usize, 16] {
            let x = lcg_input(900 + batch as u64, batch * inn);
            let (qs, ds) = host_quantize(&x, inn);
            if let Ok(small) = K18Q4KPipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape) {
                let got = small
                    .run(ctx, &w4, &qs, &ds, batch as u32)
                    .expect("k18 q4k deep run");
                let want = reference_mmq_q4k(&bytes4, inn, out_rows, &qs, &ds, batch);
                check_close(
                    &format!("k18 q4k {} deep batch {batch}", shape.name()),
                    &got,
                    &want,
                );
            }
            if let Ok(small) = K18Q5KPipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape) {
                let got = small
                    .run(ctx, &w5, &qs, &ds, batch as u32)
                    .expect("k18 q5k deep run");
                let want = reference_mmq_q5k(&bytes5, inn, out_rows, &qs, &ds, batch);
                check_close(
                    &format!("k18 q5k {} deep batch {batch}", shape.name()),
                    &got,
                    &want,
                );
            }
            if let Ok(small) = K18Q6KPipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape) {
                let got = small
                    .run(ctx, &w6, &qs, &ds, batch as u32)
                    .expect("k18 q6k deep run");
                let want = reference_mmq_q6k(&bytes6, inn, out_rows, &qs, &ds, batch);
                check_close(
                    &format!("k18 q6k {} deep batch {batch}", shape.name()),
                    &got,
                    &want,
                );
            }
        }
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/tests/k19_mmv.rs =====
//! K19 (the Q4_K register-streaming small-batch
//! product) against the CPU f32 reference and against
//! K1's GEMV on the same inputs, at the row band the
//! kernel exists for: 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 16.
//!
//! K19 computes the GEMV's own math (f32 activations,
//! weights dequantized in registers, f32 dots), so the
//! gates are tighter than K18's: the reference is the
//! crate's standard one (`gguf` dequantize plus
//! `torch-math` matvec per batch row), and the bound is
//! the sibling files' reassociation bound. The K1
//! cross-check runs the same inputs through the proven
//! GEMV: the two must agree inside the same bound,
//! which is the parity claim the routing relies on
//! (a plan can swap the forms without moving a byte or
//! changing the math).
//!
//! Every reduction shape the device can build is
//! gated (the workgroup-tree form always, the subgroup
//! form where the device grants SUBGROUP): the two
//! reductions sum the same partials in different
//! orders, and a slice-indexing defect in either is
//! exactly what this file exists to catch.
//!
//! These tests need a discrete Vulkan GPU under the
//! default selection policy. On a machine without one
//! they print the refusal and pass; shader validity on
//! any adapter is gated separately in
//! `shader_compile.rs`, and the real-file proof runs on
//! the server through the spec verdict runs
//! (bench/mmv-prototype-2026-11-05.md).

use gguf::GgmlType;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k19_q4k_mmv::{K19Pipeline, MmvShape};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::{K1Pipeline, K1Weights};
use wgpu_compute::{GpuContext, WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

/// A backend, or `None` after printing why this machine
/// cannot provide one.
fn backend_or_skip() -> Option<WgpuCompute> {
    match WgpuCompute::new() {
        Ok(b) => Some(b),
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            eprintln!(
                "skipping GPU test: no suitable adapter (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            None
        }
        Err(e) => panic!("backend construction failed unexpectedly: {e}"),
    }
}

/// Deterministic pseudo-random f32s in [-0.5, 0.5) via
/// a 64-bit LCG, matching the other kernel tests.
fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            ((state >> 40) as u32) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Deterministic pseudo-random bytes via a small LCG.
fn lcg_bytes(seed: u8, count: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut state = seed;
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state.wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(17);
            state
        })
        .collect()
}

/// A synthetic Q4_K tensor's raw bytes (the sibling
/// files' fixture: rotating (d, dmin) headers over LCG
/// payloads).
fn synthetic_q4k(in_elems: usize, out_rows: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let blocks_per_row = in_elems / 256;
    let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(out_rows * blocks_per_row * 144);
    let headers: [(u16, u16); 4] = [
        (0x3c00, 0x3400),
        (0x3800, 0x0000),
        (0x4000, 0x2e66),
        (0x3e00, 0x3800),
    ];
    for row in 0..out_rows {
        for blk in 0..blocks_per_row {
            let (d, dmin) = headers[(row + blk) % headers.len()];
            let mut block = [0u8; 144];
            block[0..2].copy_from_slice(&d.to_le_bytes());
            block[2..4].copy_from_slice(&dmin.to_le_bytes());
            block[4..144].copy_from_slice(&lcg_bytes((row * 7 + blk * 13 + 5) as u8, 140)[..]);
            data.extend_from_slice(&block);
        }
    }
    data
}

/// Assert two f32 sets agree within the sibling files'
/// reassociation bound, reporting the worst element.
fn check_close(label: &str, got: &[f32], want: &[f32]) {
    assert_eq!(got.len(), want.len(), "{label}: length mismatch");
    let scale = want.iter().fold(0.0f32, |a, w| a.max(w.abs()));
    let tol = 2e-3 + 5e-5 * scale;
    let mut max_diff = 0.0f32;
    for (i, (g, w)) in got.iter().zip(want.iter()).enumerate() {
        let diff = (g - w).abs();
        max_diff = max_diff.max(diff);
        assert!(
            diff <= tol,
            "{label}: element {i}: got {g}, want {w} (diff {diff}, tol {tol} at set scale {scale})"
        );
    }
    eprintln!(
        "{label}: max abs diff {max_diff:.3e} (set scale {scale:.3e}, rel {:.3e})",
        max_diff / scale.max(1.0)
    );
}

/// The CPU f32 reference: dequantize the tensor once,
/// then matvec per batch row.
fn reference_f32(bytes: &[u8], inn: usize, out_rows: usize, x: &[f32], batch: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let weights = gguf::dequant::dequantize(GgmlType::Q4K, bytes, inn * out_rows);
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(batch * out_rows);
    for b in 0..batch {
        out.extend_from_slice(
            &torch_math::matvec(&weights, out_rows, inn, &x[b * inn..(b + 1) * inn])
                .expect("cpu reference"),
        );
    }
    out
}

/// K1's GEMV over the same f32 rows.
fn run_gemv_q4k(
    ctx: &GpuContext,
    k1: &K1Pipeline,
    weights: &K1Weights,
    x: &[f32],
    batch: usize,
    out_rows: usize,
) -> Vec<f32> {
    let in_buf = ctx.upload_f32("k19 test gemv input", x);
    let out_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("k19 test gemv out", (batch * out_rows * 4) as u64);
    let call = k1
        .prepare(ctx, weights, &in_buf, &out_buf, batch as u32)
        .expect("k1 prepare");
    let mut encoder = ctx
        .device
        .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
            label: Some("k19 test gemv run"),
        });
    call.encode(&mut encoder);
    ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
    ctx.read_f32(&out_buf, batch * out_rows)
        .expect("gemv readback")
}

/// The reduction shapes to gate: the tree form always,
/// the subgroup form when the device grants it (the
/// shipped shape is whichever the device takes; both
/// are exercised so the shipped choice is never the
/// only proven one).
fn shape_candidates(features: wgpu::Features) -> Vec<MmvShape> {
    let mut shapes = vec![MmvShape::new(2, 128)];
    if features.contains(wgpu::Features::SUBGROUP) {
        shapes.push(MmvShape::new(2, 128).with_subgroup());
    }
    shapes
}

/// The batch counts the gates sweep: the task's named
/// rows across the band, including both cliff points
/// of llama.cpp's dose-response (9, where the stock
/// cap breaks, and 16, the cap this kernel ships).
const BAND: [usize; 6] = [2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 16];

#[test]
fn k19_matches_cpu_reference_and_gemv_at_small_batches() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    // Width 512 = two super-blocks per row; 100 output
    // rows = 50 two-row workgroups exactly.
    let (inn, out_rows) = (512usize, 100usize);
    let bytes = synthetic_q4k(inn, out_rows);
    let k1 = K1Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k1 pipeline");
    let weights = k1
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q4k.mmv", &bytes, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k1 upload");
    for shape in shape_candidates(ctx.device.features()) {
        let mmv = K19Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape).expect("k19 pipeline");
        for batch in BAND {
            let x = lcg_input(700 + batch as u64, batch * inn);
            let got = mmv.run(ctx, &weights, &x).expect("k19 run");
            let want = reference_f32(&bytes, inn, out_rows, &x, batch);
            check_close(
                &format!("k19 {} batch {batch} vs cpu", shape.name()),
                &got,
                &want,
            );
            let gemv = run_gemv_q4k(ctx, &k1, &weights, &x, batch, out_rows);
            check_close(
                &format!("k19 {} batch {batch} vs gemv", shape.name()),
                &got,
                &gemv,
            );
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn k19_deep_geometry_and_odd_row_count() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    // Width 768 = three super-blocks per row; 101
    // output rows: the last workgroup covers one row
    // of its two-row tile, exercising the row guard and
    // the guarded finish store.
    let (inn, out_rows) = (768usize, 101usize);
    let bytes = synthetic_q4k(inn, out_rows);
    let k1 = K1Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k1 pipeline");
    let weights = k1
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q4k.mmv.deep", &bytes, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k1 upload");
    let mmv = K19Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k19 pipeline");
    for batch in [3usize, 16] {
        let x = lcg_input(900 + batch as u64, batch * inn);
        let got = mmv.run(ctx, &weights, &x).expect("k19 run");
        let want = reference_f32(&bytes, inn, out_rows, &x, batch);
        check_close(&format!("k19 deep batch {batch} vs cpu"), &got, &want);
    }
}

#[test]
fn k19_band_edges_refuse_by_name() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let (inn, out_rows) = (512usize, 100usize);
    let bytes = synthetic_q4k(inn, out_rows);
    let k1 = K1Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k1 pipeline");
    let weights = k1
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q4k.mmv.edges", &bytes, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k1 upload");
    let mmv = K19Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k19 pipeline");
    let in_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("k19 test in", 4096);
    let out_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("k19 test out", 4096);
    // Below the floor: batch 1 is decode, the GEMV's
    // job; batch 0 is nothing at all.
    for batch in [0u32, 1] {
        let err = mmv
            .prepare(ctx, &weights, &in_buf, &out_buf, batch)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            err.to_string().contains("outside 2..=16"),
            "batch {batch} refusal names the band: {err}"
        );
    }
    // Past the cap: the GEMM ladder's territory.
    let err = mmv
        .prepare(ctx, &weights, &in_buf, &out_buf, 17)
        .unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        err.to_string().contains("outside 2..=16"),
        "batch 17 refusal names the band: {err}"
    );
    // The one-shot path derives the batch from the
    // input, so a single row refuses the same way.
    let x = lcg_input(42, inn);
    let err = mmv.run(ctx, &weights, &x).unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        err.to_string().contains("outside 2..=16"),
        "one-row run refusal names the band: {err}"
    );
}

===== END FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/tests/k19_mmv.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/tests/k1_synthetic.rs =====
//! K1 against a synthetic Q4_K tensor with known contents: the
//! GPU result must match the CPU reference (the `gguf` crate's
//! dequantizer plus `torch-math`'s matvec) within float
//! reassociation noise, and the `Compute::proj` weight cache
//! must refuse a tensor that arrives under a cached name with a
//! different dtype. (Q6_K and Q5_K end-to-end proofs live in
//! `k2_k3_synthetic.rs`; K2 and K3 landed after this file.)
//!
//! These tests need a discrete Vulkan GPU under the default
//! selection policy. On a machine without one (a CI box, this
//! workstation) they print the refusal and pass: the policy's
//! whole point is that llvmpipe does not count, and the real-file
//! proof runs on the server through the `k1_check` example. A
//! skip here is a reported event, never a silent one.

use std::sync::Arc;

use gguf::GgmlType;
use muse_glimmer::{Compute, Dtype, TensorView};
use wgpu_compute::{WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

/// A backend, or `None` after printing why this machine cannot
/// provide one.
fn backend_or_skip() -> Option<WgpuCompute> {
    match WgpuCompute::new() {
        Ok(b) => Some(b),
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            eprintln!(
                "skipping GPU test: no suitable adapter (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            None
        }
        Err(e) => panic!("backend construction failed unexpectedly: {e}"),
    }
}

/// One Q4_K super-block with chosen header values and
/// deterministic pseudo-random payload bytes.
fn synthetic_block(d: u16, dmin: u16, seed: u8) -> [u8; 144] {
    let mut block = [0u8; 144];
    block[0..2].copy_from_slice(&d.to_le_bytes());
    block[2..4].copy_from_slice(&dmin.to_le_bytes());
    let mut state = seed;
    for byte in &mut block[4..144] {
        state = state.wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(17);
        *byte = state;
    }
    block
}

/// A [256, 3] Q4_K tensor: one block per row, three different
/// (d, dmin) headers so the rows exercise different scales.
fn synthetic_tensor() -> TensorView {
    let mut data = Vec::new();
    data.extend_from_slice(&synthetic_block(0x3c00, 0x3400, 11)); // d 1.0, dmin 0.25
    data.extend_from_slice(&synthetic_block(0x3800, 0x0000, 47)); // d 0.5, dmin 0
    data.extend_from_slice(&synthetic_block(0x4000, 0x2e66, 91)); // d 2.0, dmin ~0.1
    TensorView {
        name: "synthetic.q4k".to_string(),
        dtype: Dtype::Q4K,
        shape: vec![256, 3],
        data: Arc::from(data.into_boxed_slice()),
    }
}

fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            ((state >> 40) as u32) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

#[test]
fn k1_proj_matches_cpu_reference_on_synthetic_rows() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let view = synthetic_tensor();
    let input = lcg_input(3, 256);
    let weights = gguf::dequant::dequantize(GgmlType::Q4K, &view.data, 256 * 3);
    let expected = torch_math::matvec(&weights, 3, 256, &input).expect("cpu reference");

    // One row (decode shape) and two rows (batch through one
    // dispatch) must both match.
    let one = backend.proj(&input, &view, 1).expect("gpu proj, one row");
    let mut two_input = input.clone();
    two_input.extend_from_slice(&input);
    let two = backend
        .proj(&two_input, &view, 2)
        .expect("gpu proj, two rows");
    let cases: [(&str, &[f32]); 3] = [
        ("one row", &one),
        ("batched row 0", &two[0..3]),
        ("batched row 1", &two[3..6]),
    ];
    for (label, got) in cases {
        let mut max_abs = 0.0f32;
        let mut scale = 0.0f32;
        for (g, e) in got.iter().zip(expected.iter()) {
            max_abs = max_abs.max((g - e).abs());
            scale = scale.max(e.abs());
        }
        let rel = max_abs / scale.max(1.0);
        assert!(
            rel < 1e-4,
            "{label}: max_abs_err {max_abs} at scale {scale} (rel {rel}) exceeds reassociation noise; got {got:?}, expected {expected:?}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn proj_refuses_a_dtype_change_under_a_cached_name() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let view = synthetic_tensor();
    let input = lcg_input(7, 256);
    backend.proj(&input, &view, 1).expect("first upload");
    // The same name now carrying a Q6_K tensor: Q6_K has a
    // kernel (K2), but not under this name. The cache identity
    // check refuses before any dtype routing happens.
    let impostor = TensorView {
        name: "synthetic.q4k".to_string(),
        dtype: Dtype::Q6K,
        shape: vec![256, 3],
        data: Arc::from(vec![0u8; 210 * 3].into_boxed_slice()),
    };
    let err = backend
        .proj(&input, &impostor, 1)
        .expect_err("a dtype change under a cached name must refuse");
    match err {
        muse_glimmer::GlimmerError::StepFailed { step, detail } => {
            assert_eq!(step, "proj");
            assert!(
                detail.contains("identity"),
                "refusal must name the identity rule: {detail}"
            );
        }
        other => panic!("expected StepFailed, got {other:?}"),
    }
}

#[test]
fn k1_reupload_under_a_cached_name_with_new_geometry_refuses() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let view = synthetic_tensor();
    let input = lcg_input(5, 256);
    backend.proj(&input, &view, 1).expect("first upload");
    // Same name, different shape and byte count: the name is an
    // identity, so this refuses rather than replacing the buffer.
    let impostor = TensorView {
        name: "synthetic.q4k".to_string(),
        dtype: Dtype::Q4K,
        shape: vec![256, 1],
        data: Arc::from(
            synthetic_block(0x3c00, 0x3400, 3)
                .to_vec()
                .into_boxed_slice(),
        ),
    };
    let err = backend
        .proj(&input, &impostor, 1)
        .expect_err("geometry change under a cached name must refuse");
    assert!(
        matches!(
            err,
            muse_glimmer::GlimmerError::StepFailed { step: "proj", .. }
        ),
        "got {err:?}"
    );
}

===== END FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/tests/k1_synthetic.rs =====

/// A synthetic Q6_K tensor's raw bytes (the sibling
/// files' fixture: 210-byte blocks of LCG payload with

/// The CPU f32 reference: dequantize the tensor once,
/// then matvec per batch row.
fn reference_f32(bytes: &[u8], inn: usize, out_rows: usize, x: &[f32], batch: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let weights = gguf::dequant::dequantize(GgmlType::Q6K, bytes, inn * out_rows);
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(batch * out_rows);
    for b in 0..batch {
        out.extend_from_slice(
            &torch_math::matvec(&weights, out_rows, inn, &x[b * inn..(b + 1) * inn])
                .expect("cpu reference"),
        );
    }
    out
}

/// K2's GEMV over the same f32 rows.
fn run_gemv_q6k(
    ctx: &GpuContext,
    k2: &K2Pipeline,
    weights: &K2Weights,
    x: &[f32],
    batch: usize,
    out_rows: usize,
) -> Vec<f32> {
    let in_buf = ctx.upload_f32("k20 test gemv input", x);
    let out_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("k20 test gemv out", (batch * out_rows * 4) as u64);
    let call = k2
        .prepare(ctx, weights, &in_buf, &out_buf, batch as u32)
        .expect("k2 prepare");
    let mut encoder = ctx
        .device
        .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
            label: Some("k20 test gemv run"),
        });
    call.encode(&mut encoder);
    ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
    ctx.read_f32(&out_buf, batch * out_rows)
        .expect("gemv readback")
}

/// The reduction shapes to gate: the tree form always,
/// the subgroup form when the device grants it (the
/// shipped shape is whichever the device takes; both
/// are exercised so the shipped choice is never the
/// only proven one).
fn shape_candidates(features: wgpu::Features) -> Vec<MmvShape> {
    let mut shapes = vec![MmvShape::new(2, 128)];
    if features.contains(wgpu::Features::SUBGROUP) {
        shapes.push(MmvShape::new(2, 128).with_subgroup());
    }
    shapes
}

/// The batch counts the gates sweep: the task's named
/// rows across the band, including both cliff points
/// of llama.cpp's dose-response (9, where the stock
/// cap breaks, and 16, the cap this kernel ships).
const BAND: [usize; 6] = [2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 16];

#[test]

    // rows = 50 two-row workgroups exactly.

                &format!("k20 {} batch {batch} vs gemv", shape.name()),

            );
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn k20_band_edges_refuse_by_name() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let (inn, out_rows) = (512usize, 100usize);
    let bytes = synthetic_q6k(inn, out_rows);
    let k2 = K2Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k2 pipeline");
    let weights = k2
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q6k.mmv.edges", &bytes, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k2 upload");
    let mmv = K20Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k20 pipeline");
    let in_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("k20 test in", 4096);
    let out_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("k20 test out", 4096);
    // Below the floor: batch 1 is decode, the GEMV's
    // job; batch 0 is nothing at all.
    for batch in [0u32, 1] {
        let err = mmv
            .prepare(ctx, &weights, &in_buf, &out_buf, batch)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            err.to_string().contains("outside 2..=16"),
            "batch {batch} refusal names the band: {err}"
        );
    }
    // Past the cap: the GEMM ladder's territory.
    let err = mmv
        .prepare(ctx, &weights, &in_buf, &out_buf, 17)
        .unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        err.to_string().contains("outside 2..=16"),
        "batch 17 refusal names the band: {err}"
    );
    // The one-shot path derives the batch from the
    // input, so a single row refuses the same way.
    let x = lcg_input(42, inn);
    let err = mmv.run(ctx, &weights, &x).unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        err.to_string().contains("outside 2..=16"),
        "one-row run refusal names the band: {err}"
    );
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/tests/k21_finish.rs =====
//! K21F (the finish-carrying Q5_K register-streaming
//! small-batch product) against two references on the
//! same inputs: the CPU f32 reference composed with
//! the head finishing map on the host, and K3's GEMV
//! with its fused finish (the shipped head's exact
//! composition). The band is K21's: 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 16.
//!
//! The claim these gates exist to prove: swapping
//! the block head's product engine from K3 to K21F
//! changes no output beyond the family's
//! reassociation bound, shrunk by the finish. The
//! raw products agree inside the sibling files'
//! bound (`2e-3 + 5e-5 * set scale`); the finishing
//! map is Lipschitz with constant `scale` in both
//! modes (the scale mode exactly, the softcap
//! because `cap * tanh(scale * v / cap)` has
//! derivative `scale * sech^2(..) <= scale`), so the
//! finished bound is `scale` times the raw bound,
//! plus a small absolute slack for the one
//! evaluation that is not shared arithmetic, the
//! driver's `tanh` against the host's. Against K3's
//! fused finish even that slack is principled
//! headroom only: both kernels evaluate the same
//! WGSL `tanh` text on the same driver.
//!
//! The finish values are Glimmer's real ones (the
//! file's logit scale 0.19611613 and softcap 20.0):
//! the gates run the head's actual map, not a
//! convenient one. Both finish modes are gated, and
//! every reduction shape the device can build (the
//! workgroup-tree form always, the subgroup form
//! where the device grants SUBGROUP), because the
//! finish sits in the reduction's store in each.
//!
//! These tests need a discrete Vulkan GPU under the
//! default selection policy. On a machine without
//! one they print the refusal and pass; shader
//! validity on any adapter is gated separately in
//! `shader_compile.rs`, and the real-file proof runs
//! on the server through the verdict protocol in
//! bench/k21-finish-2026-11-06.md.

use gguf::GgmlType;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k21_q5k_mmv::K21Shape;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k21_q5k_mmv_finish::K21FinishPipeline;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k3_q5k_gemv::{
    K3Pipeline, K3Weights, FINISH_NONE, FINISH_SCALE, FINISH_SOFTCAP,
};
use wgpu_compute::{GpuContext, WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

/// Glimmer's logit scale, the file value
/// (0.1961161345243454 in f64; the head consumes the
/// f32 rounding of it).
const GLIMMER_LOGIT_SCALE: f32 = 0.19611613;
/// Glimmer's logit softcap, the file value.
const GLIMMER_LOGIT_SOFTCAP: f32 = 20.0;

/// A backend, or `None` after printing why this
/// machine cannot provide one.
fn backend_or_skip() -> Option<WgpuCompute> {
    match WgpuCompute::new() {
        Ok(b) => Some(b),
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            eprintln!(
                "skipping GPU test: no suitable adapter (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            None
        }
        Err(e) => panic!("backend construction failed unexpectedly: {e}"),
    }
}

/// Deterministic pseudo-random f32s in [-0.5, 0.5)
/// via a 64-bit LCG, matching the other kernel
/// tests.
fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            ((state >> 40) as u32) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Deterministic pseudo-random bytes via a small
/// LCG.
fn lcg_bytes(seed: u8, count: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut state = seed;
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state.wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(17);
            state
        })
        .collect()
}

/// A synthetic Q5_K tensor's raw bytes (the sibling
/// files' fixture: 176-byte blocks, rotating (d,
/// dmin) headers over LCG payloads; the scales, qh,
/// and ql planes are payload).
fn synthetic_q5k(in_elems: usize, out_rows: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let blocks_per_row = in_elems / 256;
    let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(out_rows * blocks_per_row * 176);
    let headers: [(u16, u16); 4] = [
        (0x3c00, 0x3400),
        (0x3800, 0x0000),
        (0x4000, 0x2e66),
        (0x3e00, 0x3800),
    ];
    for row in 0..out_rows {
        for blk in 0..blocks_per_row {
            let (d, dmin) = headers[(row + blk) % headers.len()];
            let mut block = [0u8; 176];
            block[0..2].copy_from_slice(&d.to_le_bytes());
            block[2..4].copy_from_slice(&dmin.to_le_bytes());
            block[4..176].copy_from_slice(&lcg_bytes((row * 7 + blk * 13 + 5) as u8, 172)[..]);
            data.extend_from_slice(&block);
        }
    }
    data
}

/// The CPU f32 reference: dequantize the tensor
/// once, then matvec per batch row (the plain
/// product, no finish).
fn reference_f32(bytes: &[u8], inn: usize, out_rows: usize, x: &[f32], batch: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let weights = gguf::dequant::dequantize(GgmlType::Q5K, bytes, inn * out_rows);
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(batch * out_rows);
    for b in 0..batch {
        out.extend_from_slice(
            &torch_math::matvec(&weights, out_rows, inn, &x[b * inn..(b + 1) * inn])
                .expect("cpu reference"),
        );
    }
    out
}

/// The head finishing map on the host, in K8's
/// expression order: the CPU composition the fused
/// kernels must match.
fn finish_host(v: f32, mode: u32, scale: f32, cap: f32) -> f32 {
    match mode {
        FINISH_SCALE => v * scale,
        FINISH_SOFTCAP => {
            let x = v * scale;
            cap * (x / cap).tanh()
        }
        _ => unreachable!("tests only ask for finishing modes"),
    }
}

/// Assert two finished f32 sets agree within the
/// Lipschitz-shrunk bound: `scale` times the
/// family's raw reassociation bound at the raw
/// set's scale, plus the tanh slack. Reports the
/// worst element.
fn check_close_finished(label: &str, got: &[f32], want: &[f32], raw_scale: f32, scale: f32) {
    assert_eq!(got.len(), want.len(), "{label}: length mismatch");
    let tol = scale * (2e-3 + 5e-5 * raw_scale) + 2e-5;
    let mut max_diff = 0.0f32;
    for (i, (g, w)) in got.iter().zip(want.iter()).enumerate() {
        let diff = (g - w).abs();
        max_diff = max_diff.max(diff);
        assert!(
            diff <= tol,
            "{label}: element {i}: got {g}, want {w} (diff {diff}, tol {tol} at raw set scale {raw_scale})"
        );
    }
    eprintln!("{label}: max abs diff {max_diff:.3e} (tol {tol:.3e})");
}

/// K3's GEMV with its fused finish over the same f32
/// rows: the shipped head composition.
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
fn run_gemv_q5k_finish(
    ctx: &GpuContext,
    k3: &K3Pipeline,
    weights: &K3Weights,
    x: &[f32],
    batch: usize,
    out_rows: usize,
    mode: u32,
    scale: f32,
    cap: f32,
) -> Vec<f32> {
    let in_buf = ctx.upload_f32("k21 finish test gemv input", x);
    let out_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("k21 finish test gemv out", (batch * out_rows * 4) as u64);
    let call = k3
        .prepare_with_finish(
            ctx,
            weights,
            &in_buf,
            &out_buf,
            batch as u32,
            mode,
            scale,
            cap,
        )
        .expect("k3 finish prepare");
    let mut encoder = ctx
        .device
        .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
            label: Some("k21 finish test gemv run"),
        });
    call.encode(&mut encoder);
    ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
    ctx.read_f32(&out_buf, batch * out_rows)
        .expect("gemv finish readback")
}

/// The reduction shapes to gate: the tree form
/// always, the subgroup form when the device grants
/// it.
fn shape_candidates(features: wgpu::Features) -> Vec<K21Shape> {
    let mut shapes = vec![K21Shape::new(2, 128)];
    if features.contains(wgpu::Features::SUBGROUP) {
        shapes.push(K21Shape::new(2, 128).with_subgroup());
    }
    shapes
}

/// The batch counts the gates sweep (K21's band
/// points, including both of llama.cpp's
/// dose-response cliffs).
const BAND: [usize; 6] = [2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 16];

/// The finishes the gates run: Glimmer's scale-only
/// position and its shipped scale-plus-softcap
/// position.
const FINISHES: [(u32, f32, f32); 2] = [
    (FINISH_SCALE, GLIMMER_LOGIT_SCALE, 0.0),
    (FINISH_SOFTCAP, GLIMMER_LOGIT_SCALE, GLIMMER_LOGIT_SOFTCAP),
];

#[test]
fn k21_finish_matches_cpu_composition_and_k3_finish() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    // Width 512 = two super-blocks per row; 100
    // output rows = 50 two-row workgroups exactly.
    let (inn, out_rows) = (512usize, 100usize);
    let bytes = synthetic_q5k(inn, out_rows);
    let k3 = K3Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k3 pipeline");
    let weights = k3
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q5k.mmv.finish", &bytes, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k3 upload");
    for shape in shape_candidates(ctx.device.features()) {
        let mmv = K21FinishPipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape).expect("k21 finish pipeline");
        for batch in BAND {
            let x = lcg_input(700 + batch as u64, batch * inn);
            let raw = reference_f32(&bytes, inn, out_rows, &x, batch);
            let raw_scale = raw.iter().fold(0.0f32, |a, w| a.max(w.abs()));
            for (mode, scale, cap) in FINISHES {
                let got = mmv
                    .run_with_finish(ctx, &weights, &x, mode, scale, cap)
                    .expect("k21 finish run");
                let want: Vec<f32> = raw
                    .iter()
                    .map(|&v| finish_host(v, mode, scale, cap))
                    .collect();
                check_close_finished(
                    &format!(
                        "k21 finish {} batch {batch} mode {mode} vs cpu composition",
                        shape.name()
                    ),
                    &got,
                    &want,
                    raw_scale,
                    scale,
                );
                let gemv =
                    run_gemv_q5k_finish(ctx, &k3, &weights, &x, batch, out_rows, mode, scale, cap);
                check_close_finished(
                    &format!(
                        "k21 finish {} batch {batch} mode {mode} vs k3 finish",
                        shape.name()
                    ),
                    &got,
                    &gemv,
                    raw_scale,
                    scale,
                );
            }
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn k21_finish_refusals_are_named() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let (inn, out_rows) = (512usize, 100usize);
    let bytes = synthetic_q5k(inn, out_rows);
    let k3 = K3Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k3 pipeline");
    let weights = k3
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q5k.mmv.finish.edges", &bytes, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k3 upload");
    let mmv = K21FinishPipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k21 finish pipeline");
    let in_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("k21 finish test in", 4096);
    let out_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("k21 finish test out", 4096);
    // The plain product's mode is not a finishing
    // mode here, and neither is an unknown one: both
    // refuse with K3's words, at a batch inside the
    // band, so the finish check is the one that
    // fires.
    for mode in [FINISH_NONE, 7] {
        let err = mmv
            .prepare_with_finish(
                ctx,
                &weights,
                &in_buf,
                &out_buf,
                2,
                mode,
                GLIMMER_LOGIT_SCALE,
                GLIMMER_LOGIT_SOFTCAP,
            )
            .unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            err.to_string().contains("is not a finishing mode"),
            "mode {mode} refusal names the rule: {err}"
        );
    }
    // A softcap with no positive cap refuses; the
    // scale mode never reads the cap and prepares
    // fine with a zero one (K3's contract, kept).
    for cap in [0.0, -1.0] {
        let err = mmv
            .prepare_with_finish(
                ctx,
                &weights,
                &in_buf,
                &out_buf,
                2,
                FINISH_SOFTCAP,
                GLIMMER_LOGIT_SCALE,
                cap,
            )
            .unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            err.to_string().contains("is not positive"),
            "cap {cap} refusal names the rule: {err}"
        );
    }
    assert!(mmv
        .prepare_with_finish(
            ctx,
            &weights,
            &in_buf,
            &out_buf,
            2,
            FINISH_SCALE,
            GLIMMER_LOGIT_SCALE,
            0.0,
        )
        .is_ok());
    // The band still bounds the finish form: batch 1
    // (the standard head's size) and batch 17 refuse
    // by name, with a valid finish requested, so the
    // band check is the one that fires.
    for batch in [1u32, 17] {
        let err = mmv
            .prepare_with_finish(
                ctx,
                &weights,
                &in_buf,
                &out_buf,
                batch,
                FINISH_SOFTCAP,
                GLIMMER_LOGIT_SCALE,
                GLIMMER_LOGIT_SOFTCAP,
            )
            .unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            err.to_string().contains("outside 2..=16"),
            "batch {batch} refusal names the band: {err}"
        );
    }
    // The one-shot path derives the batch from the
    // input, so a single row refuses the same way.
    let x = lcg_input(42, inn);
    let err = mmv
        .run_with_finish(
            ctx,
            &weights,
            &x,
            FINISH_SOFTCAP,
            GLIMMER_LOGIT_SCALE,
            GLIMMER_LOGIT_SOFTCAP,
        )
        .unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        err.to_string().contains("outside 2..=16"),
        "one-row run refusal names the band: {err}"
    );
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/tests/k21_mmv.rs =====
//! K21 (the Q5_K register-streaming small-batch
//! product) against the CPU f32 reference and against
//! K3's GEMV on the same inputs, at the row band the
//! kernel exists for: 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 16.
//!
//! K21 computes the GEMV's own math (f32 activations,
//! weights dequantized in registers, f32 dots), so the
//! gates are tighter than K18's: the reference is the
//! crate's standard one (`gguf` dequantize plus
//! `torch-math` matvec per batch row), and the bound is
//! the sibling files' reassociation bound. The K3
//! cross-check runs the same inputs through the proven
//! GEMV: the two must agree inside the same bound,
//! which is the parity claim the routing relies on
//! (a plan can swap the forms without moving a byte or
//! changing the math).
//!
//! Every reduction shape the device can build is
//! gated (the workgroup-tree form always, the subgroup
//! form where the device grants SUBGROUP): the two
//! reductions sum the same partials in different
//! orders, and a slice-indexing defect in either is
//! exactly what this file exists to catch.
//!
//! These tests need a discrete Vulkan GPU under the
//! default selection policy. On a machine without one
//! they print the refusal and pass; shader validity on
//! any adapter is gated separately in
//! `shader_compile.rs`, and the real-file proof runs on
//! the server through the spec verdict runs
//! (bench/mmv-q5k-2026-11-05.md).

use gguf::GgmlType;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k21_q5k_mmv::{K21Pipeline, K21Shape};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k3_q5k_gemv::{K3Pipeline, K3Weights};
use wgpu_compute::{GpuContext, WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

/// A backend, or `None` after printing why this machine
/// cannot provide one.
fn backend_or_skip() -> Option<WgpuCompute> {
    match WgpuCompute::new() {
        Ok(b) => Some(b),
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            eprintln!(
                "skipping GPU test: no suitable adapter (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            None
        }
        Err(e) => panic!("backend construction failed unexpectedly: {e}"),
    }
}

/// Deterministic pseudo-random f32s in [-0.5, 0.5) via
/// a 64-bit LCG, matching the other kernel tests.
fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            ((state >> 40) as u32) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Deterministic pseudo-random bytes via a small LCG.
fn lcg_bytes(seed: u8, count: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut state = seed;
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state.wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(17);
            state
        })
        .collect()
}

/// A synthetic Q5_K tensor's raw bytes (the sibling
/// files' fixture: 176-byte blocks, rotating (d, dmin)
/// headers over LCG payloads; the scales, qh, and ql
/// planes are payload).
fn synthetic_q5k(in_elems: usize, out_rows: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let blocks_per_row = in_elems / 256;
    let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(out_rows * blocks_per_row * 176);
    let headers: [(u16, u16); 4] = [
        (0x3c00, 0x3400),
        (0x3800, 0x0000),
        (0x4000, 0x2e66),
        (0x3e00, 0x3800),
    ];
    for row in 0..out_rows {
        for blk in 0..blocks_per_row {
            let (d, dmin) = headers[(row + blk) % headers.len()];
            let mut block = [0u8; 176];
            block[0..2].copy_from_slice(&d.to_le_bytes());
            block[2..4].copy_from_slice(&dmin.to_le_bytes());
            block[4..176].copy_from_slice(&lcg_bytes((row * 7 + blk * 13 + 5) as u8, 172)[..]);
            data.extend_from_slice(&block);
        }
    }
    data
}

/// Assert two f32 sets agree within the sibling files'
/// reassociation bound, reporting the worst element.
fn check_close(label: &str, got: &[f32], want: &[f32]) {
    assert_eq!(got.len(), want.len(), "{label}: length mismatch");
    let scale = want.iter().fold(0.0f32, |a, w| a.max(w.abs()));
    let tol = 2e-3 + 5e-5 * scale;
    let mut max_diff = 0.0f32;
    for (i, (g, w)) in got.iter().zip(want.iter()).enumerate() {
        let diff = (g - w).abs();
        max_diff = max_diff.max(diff);
        assert!(
            diff <= tol,
            "{label}: element {i}: got {g}, want {w} (diff {diff}, tol {tol} at set scale {scale})"
        );
    }
    eprintln!(
        "{label}: max abs diff {max_diff:.3e} (set scale {scale:.3e}, rel {:.3e})",
        max_diff / scale.max(1.0)
    );
}

/// The CPU f32 reference: dequantize the tensor once,
/// then matvec per batch row.
fn reference_f32(bytes: &[u8], inn: usize, out_rows: usize, x: &[f32], batch: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let weights = gguf::dequant::dequantize(GgmlType::Q5K, bytes, inn * out_rows);
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(batch * out_rows);
    for b in 0..batch {
        out.extend_from_slice(
            &torch_math::matvec(&weights, out_rows, inn, &x[b * inn..(b + 1) * inn])
                .expect("cpu reference"),
        );
    }
    out
}

/// K3's GEMV over the same f32 rows.
fn run_gemv_q5k(
    ctx: &GpuContext,
    k3: &K3Pipeline,
    weights: &K3Weights,
    x: &[f32],
    batch: usize,
    out_rows: usize,
) -> Vec<f32> {
    let in_buf = ctx.upload_f32("k21 test gemv input", x);
    let out_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("k21 test gemv out", (batch * out_rows * 4) as u64);
    let call = k3
        .prepare(ctx, weights, &in_buf, &out_buf, batch as u32)
        .expect("k3 prepare");
    let mut encoder = ctx
        .device
        .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor {
            label: Some("k21 test gemv run"),
        });
    call.encode(&mut encoder);
    ctx.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
    ctx.read_f32(&out_buf, batch * out_rows)
        .expect("gemv readback")
}

/// The reduction shapes to gate: the tree form always,
/// the subgroup form when the device grants it (the
/// shipped shape is whichever the device takes; both
/// are exercised so the shipped choice is never the
/// only proven one).
fn shape_candidates(features: wgpu::Features) -> Vec<K21Shape> {
    let mut shapes = vec![K21Shape::new(2, 128)];
    if features.contains(wgpu::Features::SUBGROUP) {
        shapes.push(K21Shape::new(2, 128).with_subgroup());
    }
    shapes
}

/// The batch counts the gates sweep: the task's named
/// rows across the band, including both cliff points
/// of llama.cpp's dose-response (9, where the stock
/// cap breaks, and 16, the cap this kernel ships).
const BAND: [usize; 6] = [2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 16];

#[test]
fn k21_matches_cpu_reference_and_gemv_at_small_batches() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    // Width 512 = two super-blocks per row; 100 output
    // rows = 50 two-row workgroups exactly.
    let (inn, out_rows) = (512usize, 100usize);
    let bytes = synthetic_q5k(inn, out_rows);
    let k3 = K3Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k3 pipeline");
    let weights = k3
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q5k.mmv", &bytes, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k3 upload");
    for shape in shape_candidates(ctx.device.features()) {
        let mmv = K21Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape).expect("k21 pipeline");
        for batch in BAND {
            let x = lcg_input(700 + batch as u64, batch * inn);
            let got = mmv.run(ctx, &weights, &x).expect("k21 run");
            let want = reference_f32(&bytes, inn, out_rows, &x, batch);
            check_close(
                &format!("k21 {} batch {batch} vs cpu", shape.name()),
                &got,
                &want,
            );
            let gemv = run_gemv_q5k(ctx, &k3, &weights, &x, batch, out_rows);
            check_close(
                &format!("k21 {} batch {batch} vs gemv", shape.name()),
                &got,
                &gemv,
            );
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn k21_deep_geometry_and_odd_row_count() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    // Width 768 = three super-blocks per row; 101
    // output rows: the last workgroup covers one row
    // of its two-row tile, exercising the row guard and
    // the guarded finish store.
    let (inn, out_rows) = (768usize, 101usize);
    let bytes = synthetic_q5k(inn, out_rows);
    let k3 = K3Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k3 pipeline");
    let weights = k3
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q5k.mmv.deep", &bytes, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k3 upload");
    let mmv = K21Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k21 pipeline");
    for batch in [3usize, 16] {
        let x = lcg_input(900 + batch as u64, batch * inn);
        let got = mmv.run(ctx, &weights, &x).expect("k21 run");
        let want = reference_f32(&bytes, inn, out_rows, &x, batch);
        check_close(&format!("k21 deep batch {batch} vs cpu"), &got, &want);
    }
}

#[test]
fn k21_band_edges_refuse_by_name() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let (inn, out_rows) = (512usize, 100usize);
    let bytes = synthetic_q5k(inn, out_rows);
    let k3 = K3Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k3 pipeline");
    let weights = k3
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q5k.mmv.edges", &bytes, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k3 upload");
    let mmv = K21Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k21 pipeline");
    let in_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("k21 test in", 4096);
    let out_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("k21 test out", 4096);
    // Below the floor: batch 1 is decode, the GEMV's
    // job; batch 0 is nothing at all.
    for batch in [0u32, 1] {
        let err = mmv
            .prepare(ctx, &weights, &in_buf, &out_buf, batch)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            err.to_string().contains("outside 2..=16"),
            "batch {batch} refusal names the band: {err}"
        );
    }
    // Past the cap: the GEMM ladder's territory.
    let err = mmv
        .prepare(ctx, &weights, &in_buf, &out_buf, 17)
        .unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        err.to_string().contains("outside 2..=16"),
        "batch 17 refusal names the band: {err}"
    );
    // The one-shot path derives the batch from the
    // input, so a single row refuses the same way.
    let x = lcg_input(42, inn);
    let err = mmv.run(ctx, &weights, &x).unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        err.to_string().contains("outside 2..=16"),
        "one-row run refusal names the band: {err}"
    );
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/tests/k21f_head_routing.rs =====
//! The K21F head-routing pins (bench/k21-finish-2026-11-06.md,
//! guard in bench/k21f-default-guard-2026-11-07.md, default
//! flip in bench/k21f-default-flip-2026-11-07.md): the
//! resident block head's Q5_K product routes to the
//! finish-carrying MMV form (`k21_q5k_mmv_finish`) only
//! when BOTH gates admit: the route's own switch
//! (`WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD`: on when unset or `1`, off
//! when `0`, fail-closed off on any other value) and
//! the shared `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS` band at the
//! block batch. Otherwise the head stays on the K3 fused
//! call, with the finish (the fixture config's logit
//! scale and tanh softcap, Glimmer's own values) applied
//! identically on both paths.
//!
//! Arms, selected by the environment the test binary is
//! launched with (the diag smoke / capture-pin discipline:
//! each test self-skips with a printed reason when its
//! arm's conditions are not met):
//!
//! - Head switch off (explicit): launch with
//!   `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing`,
//!   `WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD=0`, and
//!   `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS` unset (the backend's
//!   shipped ceiling, 16, admits the block batch) or
//!   explicitly 16. The block head must stamp
//!   `k3_q5k_gemv` and never `k21_q5k_mmv_finish`: the
//!   open shared ceiling alone must not open the head
//!   route. An unrecognized switch value (anything but
//!   `1` or `0`, e.g. `true`) also lands in this arm by
//!   construction, which is the fail-closed pin. An
//!   unset switch does NOT land here: unset resolves
//!   on since the default flip, and the next arm pins
//!   that position.
//! - Default construction: launch with
//!   `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing` and both
//!   `WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD` and
//!   `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS` unset. The block head
//!   must stamp `k21_q5k_mmv_finish` at the block
//!   batch: the shipped defaults route the head, which
//!   is the flip's central pin.
//! - Band closed: launch with
//!   `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=1` (either switch
//!   position). The block head must stamp `k3_q5k_gemv`
//!   and never `k21_q5k_mmv_finish`.
//! - Both gates open (explicit): launch with
//!   `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG=timing`,
//!   `WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS=16`, and
//!   `WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD=1`. The block head must
//!   stamp `k21_q5k_mmv_finish` at the block batch,
//!   while a batch-1 forward's head still stamps
//!   `k3_q5k_gemv` (the standard head stays K3 by
//!   construction).
//!
//! All arms hold the block logits to the CPU model's
//! block forward at the cross-backend bar (per-row argmax
//! agreement, max-abs under 0.5): the CPU head applies the
//! true finish, so a finish the routing dropped, swapped,
//! or re-ordered on its way into the K21F call cannot pass
//! the open arms. All arms need a discrete Vulkan GPU and
//! skip where none qualifies.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::Arc;

use cpu_compute::CpuCompute;
use muse_glimmer::{
    expected_tensor_names, Dtype, GlimmerConfig, GlimmerError, GlimmerModel, LayerKind,
    PatternSource, PositionCache, Result, TensorSource, TensorView, Weights,
};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::f32_to_f16_bits;
use wgpu_compute::timestamps::DiagMode;
use wgpu_compute::{ResidentSession, WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

/// The shared MMV gate's env name (see
/// `wgpu_compute::compute::MMV_MAX_ROWS_ENV`; not
/// re-exported at the crate root).
const MMV_MAX_ROWS_ENV: &str = "WGPU_COMPUTE_MMV_MAX_ROWS";

/// The K21F head switch's env name (see
/// `wgpu_compute::compute::K21F_HEAD_ENV`; not
/// re-exported at the crate root).
const K21F_HEAD_ENV: &str = "WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD";

/// A tiny deterministic byte/float source (the cross-backend
/// fixture's generator, same seed discipline).
struct Rng(u64);

impl Rng {
    fn next_u8(&mut self) -> u8 {
        self.0 = self
            .0
            .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
            .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
        (self.0 >> 56) as u8
    }

    /// A value in [-0.5, 0.5).
    fn next_f32(&mut self) -> f32 {
        self.next_u8() as f32 / 256.0 - 0.5
    }
}

/// A Q4_K tensor of shape [inn, out] from by-construction
/// blocks, exactly the cross-backend fixture's construction.
fn q4k_tensor(rng: &mut Rng, name: &str, inn: usize, out: usize) -> TensorView {
    let blocks = inn * out / 256;
    let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(blocks * 144);
    for _ in 0..blocks {
        data.extend_from_slice(&f32_to_f16_bits(0.005).to_le_bytes());
        data.extend_from_slice(&f32_to_f16_bits(0.002).to_le_bytes());
        for _ in 0..12 {
            data.push(rng.next_u8() & 0x07);
        }
        for _ in 0..128 {
            data.push(rng.next_u8());
        }
    }
    TensorView {
        name: name.to_string(),
        dtype: Dtype::Q4K,
        shape: vec![inn as u64, out as u64],
        data: Arc::from(data.into_boxed_slice()),
    }
}

/// A Q5_K tensor of shape [inn, out], same construction,
/// with one deliberate divergence from the cross-backend
/// fixture: the twelve scale bytes are full-range, not
/// masked to `& 0x07`. This tensor is the head, the one
/// tensor the K21F route dequantizes; the masked fixture
/// shrank a dropped-nibble dequant error (the qc mask
/// bug, bench/k21f-mask-fix-2026-11-07.md) far under this
/// file's 0.5 bar by keeping every 6-bit scale field
/// tiny. Full-range scales (the k21_finish fixture's
/// discipline) make a wrong-nibble error land at full
/// size. The finish still bounds the comparison's
/// exposure: the logit scale (0.196) and the tanh
/// softcap compress the logits the bar reads, so the
/// wider weights do not widen honest reassociation
/// drift toward the bar.
fn q5k_tensor(rng: &mut Rng, name: &str, inn: usize, out: usize) -> TensorView {
    let blocks = inn * out / 256;
    let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(blocks * 176);
    for _ in 0..blocks {
        data.extend_from_slice(&f32_to_f16_bits(0.005).to_le_bytes());
        data.extend_from_slice(&f32_to_f16_bits(0.002).to_le_bytes());
        for _ in 0..12 {
            data.push(rng.next_u8());
        }
        for _ in 0..32 {
            data.push(rng.next_u8());
        }
        for _ in 0..128 {
            data.push(rng.next_u8());
        }
    }
    TensorView {
        name: name.to_string(),
        dtype: Dtype::Q5K,
        shape: vec![inn as u64, out as u64],
        data: Arc::from(data.into_boxed_slice()),
    }
}

/// An F32 tensor whose values cluster around `center`.
fn f32_tensor(rng: &mut Rng, name: &str, shape: &[u64], center: f32) -> TensorView {
    let count: u64 = shape.iter().product();
    let data: Vec<u8> = (0..count)
        .flat_map(|_| (center + rng.next_f32()).to_le_bytes())
        .collect();
    TensorView {
        name: name.to_string(),
        dtype: Dtype::F32,
        shape: shape.to_vec(),
        data: Arc::from(data.into_boxed_slice()),
    }
}

/// The synthetic config: the resident fixture's (hidden
/// 512, FFN 1024, vocab 1024, six layers in a sliding/
/// global mix, window 4), with Glimmer's real finish
/// values (logit scale, softcap 20.0) so the head finish
/// the routing forwards is the production finish shape.
fn cross_cfg() -> GlimmerConfig {
    GlimmerConfig {
        name: None,
        block_count: 6,
        context_length: 256,
        hidden: 512,
        ffn_hidden: 1024,
        q_heads: 32,
        kv_heads: 2,
        key_length: 128,
        value_length: 128,
        rope_freq_base: 500_000.0,
        rope_freq_base_swa: 500_000.0,
        rms_eps: 1e-5,
        sliding_window: 4,
        logit_softcap: 20.0,
        logit_scale: 0.196_116_13,
        vocab_size: 1024,
        layers: vec![
            LayerKind::SlidingWindow,
            LayerKind::SlidingWindow,
            LayerKind::SlidingWindow,
            LayerKind::Global,
            LayerKind::SlidingWindow,
            LayerKind::Global,
        ],
        pattern_source: PatternSource::MeasuredFallback,
    }
}

/// Build the full weight set for `cfg`, keyed by the exact
/// names `Weights::load` will ask for (the cross-backend
/// fixture's rules, tensor for tensor; the head,
/// `output.weight`, is Q5_K).
fn cross_weights(cfg: &GlimmerConfig) -> Weights {
    struct MapSource {
        tensors: HashMap<String, TensorView>,
    }
    impl TensorSource for MapSource {
        fn tensor(&self, name: &str) -> Result<TensorView> {
            self.tensors
                .get(name)
                .cloned()
                .ok_or_else(|| GlimmerError::MissingTensor {
                    name: name.to_string(),
                })
        }
    }

    let hidden = cfg.hidden as usize;
    let ffn = cfg.ffn_hidden as usize;
    let q_width = cfg.q_width() as usize;
    let kv_width = cfg.k_width() as usize;
    let vocab = cfg.vocab_size as usize;
    let head_dim = cfg.key_length as usize;

    let mut rng = Rng(0x5eed_c0de);
    let mut tensors: HashMap<String, TensorView> = HashMap::new();
    for name in expected_tensor_names(cfg) {
        let view = if name == "token_embd.weight" {
            q4k_tensor(&mut rng, &name, hidden, vocab)
        } else if name == "output.weight" {
            q5k_tensor(&mut rng, &name, hidden, vocab)
        } else if name == "output_norm.weight" {
            f32_tensor(&mut rng, &name, &[hidden as u64], 0.0)
        } else if name.ends_with("attn_q_norm.weight") || name.ends_with("attn_k_norm.weight") {
            f32_tensor(&mut rng, &name, &[head_dim as u64], 1.0)
        } else if name.ends_with("attn_norm.weight")
            || name.ends_with("post_attention_norm.weight")
            || name.ends_with("ffn_norm.weight")
            || name.ends_with("post_ffw_norm.weight")
        {
            f32_tensor(&mut rng, &name, &[hidden as u64], 1.0)
        } else if name.ends_with("attn_q.weight") || name.ends_with("attn_gate.weight") {
            q4k_tensor(&mut rng, &name, hidden, q_width)
        } else if name.ends_with("attn_k.weight") || name.ends_with("attn_v.weight") {
            q4k_tensor(&mut rng, &name, hidden, kv_width)
        } else if name.ends_with("attn_output.weight") {
            q4k_tensor(&mut rng, &name, q_width, hidden)
        } else if name.ends_with("ffn_gate.weight") || name.ends_with("ffn_up.weight") {
            q4k_tensor(&mut rng, &name, hidden, ffn)
        } else if name.ends_with("ffn_down.weight") {
            q4k_tensor(&mut rng, &name, ffn, hidden)
        } else {
            panic!("no fixture rule for tensor {name}");
        };
        tensors.insert(name, view);
    }
    Weights::load(&MapSource { tensors }, cfg).expect("fixture weights load")
}

fn argmax(logits: &[f32]) -> usize {
    logits
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .max_by(|a, b| a.1.partial_cmp(b.1).expect("logits are finite"))
        .map(|(i, _)| i)
        .expect("logits are non-empty")
}

fn max_abs(a: &[f32], b: &[f32]) -> f32 {
    assert_eq!(a.len(), b.len());
    a.iter()
        .zip(b.iter())
        .map(|(x, y)| (x - y).abs())
        .fold(0.0f32, f32::max)
}

/// Build a backend or skip the test: the resident tests'
/// discipline (a missing adapter is an environment fact,
/// not a failure).
fn backend_or_skip(test: &str) -> Option<WgpuCompute> {
    match WgpuCompute::new() {
        Ok(b) => Some(b),
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            eprintln!(
                "skipping {test}: no suitable adapter (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            None
        }
        Err(e) => panic!("backend construction failed unexpectedly: {e}"),
    }
}

/// The resolved MMV gate this process was launched with:
/// the block batch (16) is admitted exactly when the
/// parsed threshold reaches it. Unset and unparsable
/// values read as not-admitting here; the arms that
/// need those positions select on the raw env state
/// instead (see `mmv_ceiling_unset`,
/// `gate_explicitly_closed`).
fn gate_admits_block_batch() -> bool {
    std::env::var(MMV_MAX_ROWS_ENV)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|v| v.trim().parse::<u32>().ok())
        .is_some_and(|max_rows| max_rows >= 16)
}

/// Whether the shared ceiling env is set to a position
/// that closes the band at the block batch: set, and
/// either unparsable (the backend resolves those to
/// its fail-closed fallback, 1) or parsed below 16.
/// Unset is NOT closed: the shipped default is 16,
/// which admits the block batch. The closed-gate arm
/// selects on this so it can never proceed at the
/// shipped defaults and mistake the default-open
/// ceiling for a closed one.
fn gate_explicitly_closed() -> bool {
    match std::env::var(MMV_MAX_ROWS_ENV) {
        Err(_) => false,
        Ok(v) => v
            .trim()
            .parse::<u32>()
            .map_or(true, |max_rows| max_rows < 16),
    }
}

/// The resolved head switch this process was launched
/// with, mirroring the backend's resolver exactly:
/// unset and the exact value `1` (after trimming) are
/// on; the exact value `0` and every unrecognized
/// value read as off (the explicit off and the
/// fail-closed position, which is what places them in
/// the switch-off arm).
fn head_switch_on() -> bool {
    match std::env::var(K21F_HEAD_ENV) {
        Err(_) => true,
        Ok(v) => v.trim() == "1",
    }
}

/// Whether the head switch env is entirely unset: the
/// default-construction arm's selection condition.
fn head_switch_unset() -> bool {
    std::env::var_os(K21F_HEAD_ENV).is_none()
}

/// Whether the head switch was set to the exact `1`
/// explicitly: the both-gates-open arm's selection
/// condition (unset resolves on too since the default
/// flip, but that position belongs to the
/// default-construction arm).
fn head_switch_explicitly_on() -> bool {
    std::env::var(K21F_HEAD_ENV).is_ok_and(|v| v.trim() == "1")
}

/// Whether the shared ceiling env is entirely unset:
/// at the shipped default (16) the backend admits the
/// block batch, which is half of the default-
/// construction arm's selection condition.
fn mmv_ceiling_unset() -> bool {
    std::env::var_os(MMV_MAX_ROWS_ENV).is_none()
}

/// The diag conditions both arms read their exposure from:
/// timing mode on, and a recorder on the device (a device
/// that grants no timestamp features records nothing, and
/// the kernel-name assertions would read an empty table).
fn diag_ready(test: &str, backend: &WgpuCompute) -> bool {
    if DiagMode::from_env() != DiagMode::Timing {
        eprintln!("skipping {test}: WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG is not `timing`");
        return false;
    }
    if backend.context().diag_recorder().is_none() {
        eprintln!(
            "skipping {test}: timing requested but the device granted \
             no timestamp features, so no recorder exists"
        );
        return false;
    }
    true
}

const PROMPT: &[u32] = &[3, 100, 57, 900, 12, 640];
/// The spec block case: a verify block at the DFlash
/// block width, the batch the routing exists for.
const BLOCK: &[u32] = &[
    11, 222, 5, 999, 3, 77, 640, 12, 900, 57, 100, 3, 42, 8, 731, 256,
];

/// Run the fixture prompt and block on a fresh resident
/// session and the CPU model in lockstep, returning the
/// session (for its diag table) and both block logit sets.
fn run_block(backend: &WgpuCompute) -> (ResidentSession<'_>, Vec<f32>, Vec<f32>) {
    let cfg = cross_cfg();
    let weights = cross_weights(&cfg);
    let cpu_model = GlimmerModel::new(cfg.clone(), weights.clone(), Box::new(CpuCompute::new()));
    let mut session =
        ResidentSession::new(backend, &cfg, &weights).expect("resident session builds");
    let mut cpu_cache = PositionCache::new();
    cpu_model
        .forward_capturing(PROMPT, &mut cpu_cache, &[])
        .expect("cpu prompt forward");
    session.forward(PROMPT).expect("resident prompt forward");
    let (cpu_block, _) = cpu_model
        .forward_block_capturing(BLOCK, &mut cpu_cache, &[])
        .expect("cpu block forward");
    let (res_block, _) = session
        .forward_block_capturing(BLOCK, &[])
        .expect("resident block forward");
    session.finish_diag_report();
    (session, res_block, cpu_block)
}

/// The finish-agreement half of both arms: the resident
/// block logits against the CPU model's, per row, at the
/// cross-backend bar. The CPU head applies the fixture's
/// finish (scale, softcap) itself, so this is the pin
/// that the routed path's finish is that finish.
fn assert_block_matches_cpu(res_block: &[f32], cpu_block: &[f32], vocab: usize) {
    assert_eq!(res_block.len(), BLOCK.len() * vocab);
    assert_eq!(cpu_block.len(), BLOCK.len() * vocab);
    for row in 0..BLOCK.len() {
        let res_row = &res_block[row * vocab..(row + 1) * vocab];
        let cpu_row = &cpu_block[row * vocab..(row + 1) * vocab];
        assert_eq!(
            argmax(cpu_row),
            argmax(res_row),
            "block row {row} top-1 disagreement"
        );
        let d = max_abs(cpu_row, res_row);
        assert!(d < 0.5, "block row {row} logit drift beyond the bar: {d}");
        assert!(
            res_row.iter().all(|v| v.is_finite()),
            "block row {row} produced non-finite logits"
        );
    }
}

/// Head switch off, exercised explicitly
/// (`WGPU_COMPUTE_K21F_HEAD=0`, the one-variable
/// rollback; every unrecognized switch value lands
/// here too, fail-closed): even with the shared
/// ceiling at its shipped open position, the block head
/// is the K3 fused call and no `k21_q5k_mmv_finish`
/// stamp appears anywhere. The off position must be
/// reachable and exact at every point after the
/// default flip.
#[test]
fn block_head_stays_k3_when_the_head_switch_is_off() {
    let test = "k21f switch-off routing pin";
    if head_switch_on() {
        if head_switch_unset() {
            eprintln!(
                "skipping {test}: {K21F_HEAD_ENV} is unset, which resolves \
                 the head switch ON at the shipped default; this arm needs \
                 {K21F_HEAD_ENV}=0 (or an unrecognized value)"
            );
        } else {
            eprintln!(
                "skipping {test}: {K21F_HEAD_ENV}=1 resolves the head switch \
                 on; this arm needs {K21F_HEAD_ENV}=0 (or an unrecognized value)"
            );
        }
        return;
    }
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip(test) else {
        return;
    };
    if !diag_ready(test, &backend) {
        return;
    }
    let (session, res_block, cpu_block) = run_block(&backend);
    assert_block_matches_cpu(&res_block, &cpu_block, 1024);
    let names = session.diag_kernel_names();
    assert!(
        names.contains(&"k3_q5k_gemv"),
        "the switch-off block head must stamp the K3 GEMV, saw {names:?}"
    );
    assert!(
        !names.contains(&"k21_q5k_mmv_finish"),
        "the switch-off position must never stamp the finish form, saw {names:?}"
    );
}

/// Default construction (both envs unset: the head
/// switch at its shipped default ON, the shared
/// ceiling at its shipped default 16): the block head
/// routes to the finish form. This is the default
/// flip's central pin (bench/k21f-default-flip-2026-11-07.md):
/// it proves the position a run lands in when nobody
/// sets anything, the position the wave18 retest
/// proved on the real file
/// (bench/k21f-retest-2026-11-07.md).
#[test]
fn block_head_routes_to_k21f_at_default_construction() {
    let test = "k21f default-construction routing pin";
    if !head_switch_unset() {
        eprintln!(
            "skipping {test}: {K21F_HEAD_ENV} is set; this arm needs it \
             unset (the shipped default position)"
        );
        return;
    }
    if !mmv_ceiling_unset() {
        eprintln!(
            "skipping {test}: {MMV_MAX_ROWS_ENV} is set; this arm needs it \
             unset (the shipped ceiling, 16)"
        );
        return;
    }
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip(test) else {
        return;
    };
    if !diag_ready(test, &backend) {
        return;
    }
    let (session, res_block, cpu_block) = run_block(&backend);
    assert_block_matches_cpu(&res_block, &cpu_block, 1024);
    let names = session.diag_kernel_names();
    assert!(
        names.contains(&"k21_q5k_mmv_finish"),
        "default construction must stamp the finish form at the block \
         batch, saw {names:?}"
    );
}

/// Band closed: whatever the head switch says, a shared
/// ceiling that does not admit the block batch keeps the
/// block head on the K3 fused call, and no
/// `k21_q5k_mmv_finish` stamp appears anywhere.
#[test]
fn block_head_stays_k3_fused_with_the_gate_closed() {
    let test = "k21f closed-gate routing pin";
    if !gate_explicitly_closed() {
        eprintln!(
            "skipping {test}: {MMV_MAX_ROWS_ENV} is not set to a closing \
             value (unset resolves to the shipped ceiling 16, which admits \
             the block batch); this arm needs {MMV_MAX_ROWS_ENV}=1"
        );
        return;
    }
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip(test) else {
        return;
    };
    if !diag_ready(test, &backend) {
        return;
    }
    let (session, res_block, cpu_block) = run_block(&backend);
    assert_block_matches_cpu(&res_block, &cpu_block, 1024);
    let names = session.diag_kernel_names();
    assert!(
        names.contains(&"k3_q5k_gemv"),
        "the closed gate's block head must stamp the K3 GEMV, saw {names:?}"
    );
    assert!(
        !names.contains(&"k21_q5k_mmv_finish"),
        "the closed gate must never stamp the finish form, saw {names:?}"
    );
}

/// Both gates open at the block batch (head switch on,
/// shared band admitting): the block head routes to the
/// finish form, the batch-1 head stays K3, and the
/// routed block still carries the fixture's finish
/// (agreement with the CPU model at the bar).
#[test]
fn block_head_routes_to_k21f_with_the_gate_open() {
    let test = "k21f open-gate routing pin";
    if !gate_admits_block_batch() {
        eprintln!(
            "skipping {test}: {MMV_MAX_ROWS_ENV} does not admit the block \
             batch (unset, unparsable, or below 16); this is the open arm"
        );
        return;
    }
    if !head_switch_explicitly_on() {
        eprintln!(
            "skipping {test}: {K21F_HEAD_ENV} is not the exact \"1\"; this \
             arm needs the switch set explicitly (unset resolves on too, \
             but that position is the default-construction arm's)"
        );
        return;
    }
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip(test) else {
        return;
    };
    if !diag_ready(test, &backend) {
        return;
    }
    // The batch-1 head first, on its own session: even
    // with the gate open, a single-row forward's head is
    // the K3 fused call (the band floor refuses batch 1),
    // and no finish stamp appears.
    let cfg = cross_cfg();
    let weights = cross_weights(&cfg);
    let mut decode = ResidentSession::new(&backend, &cfg, &weights).expect("session builds");
    decode.forward(&[7]).expect("decode forward");
    decode.finish_diag_report();
    let names = decode.diag_kernel_names();
    assert!(
        names.contains(&"k3_q5k_gemv"),
        "the batch-1 head must stamp the K3 GEMV, saw {names:?}"
    );
    assert!(
        !names.contains(&"k21_q5k_mmv_finish"),
        "batch 1 must never route to the finish form, saw {names:?}"
    );
    drop(decode);

    let (session, res_block, cpu_block) = run_block(&backend);
    assert_block_matches_cpu(&res_block, &cpu_block, 1024);
    let names = session.diag_kernel_names();
    assert!(
        names.contains(&"k21_q5k_mmv_finish"),
        "the open gate's block head must stamp the finish form, saw {names:?}"
    );
}
