===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/tests/k22_mmq.rs =====
//! K22 (the Q4_K MMQ product in the register
//! organization) against the host reference running the
//! same quantized math, and against K13 (the shipped Q4_K
//! MMQ) on the same inputs, at the prefill band the kernel
//! exists for: batches 16, 32, 64, plus a 62-row chunk
//! tail (the 1,022-token prefill's last chunk shape).
//!
//! K22 runs K13's exact math (the same integer dots and
//! per-sub-block scale fold, in the same order), so both
//! gates use the crate's MMQ reassociation bound
//! (`check_close`, the GEMM gates' bound): the reference
//! gate is the correctness claim, and the K13 gate is the
//! parity claim the routing relies on (a plan can swap
//! the forms without moving a byte or changing the math
//! beyond float reassociation).
//!
//! These tests need a discrete Vulkan GPU under the
//! default selection policy. On a machine without one
//! they print the refusal and pass; shader validity on
//! any adapter is gated separately in
//! `shader_compile.rs`, and the real-file proof runs on
//! the server through the prefill A/B
//! (bench/k22-mmq-2026-11-05.md).

use wgpu_compute::kernels::k12_q8_quant::quantize_row_q8_1;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k13_q4k_mmq::{K13Pipeline, MmqShape};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::K1Pipeline;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k22_q4k_mmq::K22Pipeline;
use wgpu_compute::{WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

/// A backend, or `None` after printing why this machine
/// cannot provide one.
fn backend_or_skip() -> Option<WgpuCompute> {
    match WgpuCompute::new() {
        Ok(b) => Some(b),
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            eprintln!(
                "skipping GPU test: no suitable adapter (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            None
        }
        Err(e) => panic!("backend construction failed unexpectedly: {e}"),
    }
}

/// Deterministic pseudo-random f32s in [-0.5, 0.5) via a
/// 64-bit LCG, matching the other kernel tests.
fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            ((state >> 40) as u32) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Deterministic pseudo-random bytes via a small LCG.
fn lcg_bytes(seed: u8, count: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut state = seed;
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state.wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(17);
            state
        })
        .collect()
}

/// A synthetic Q4_K tensor's raw bytes (the MMQ test's
/// fixture: rotating (d, dmin) headers over LCG payloads).
fn synthetic_q4k(in_elems: usize, out_rows: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let blocks_per_row = in_elems / 256;
    let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(out_rows * blocks_per_row * 144);
    let headers: [(u16, u16); 4] = [
        (0x3c00, 0x3400),
        (0x3800, 0x0000),
        (0x4000, 0x2e66),
        (0x3e00, 0x3800),
    ];
    for row in 0..out_rows {
        for blk in 0..blocks_per_row {
            let (d, dmin) = headers[(row + blk) % headers.len()];
            let mut block = [0u8; 144];
            block[0..2].copy_from_slice(&d.to_le_bytes());
            block[2..4].copy_from_slice(&dmin.to_le_bytes());
            block[4..144].copy_from_slice(&lcg_bytes((row * 7 + blk * 13 + 5) as u8, 140)[..]);
            data.extend_from_slice(&block);
        }
    }
    data
}

/// Unpack a quantized row's words into per-element quants.
fn unpack_qs(words: &[u32]) -> Vec<i32> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(words.len() * 4);
    for w in words {
        for byte in w.to_le_bytes() {
            out.push(i32::from(byte as i8));
        }
    }
    out
}

/// ggml's `get_scale_min_k4`, mirrored from the gguf crate.
fn scale_min_k4(j: usize, scales: &[u8]) -> (u8, u8) {
    if j < 4 {
        (scales[j] & 63, scales[j + 4] & 63)
    } else {
        (
            (scales[j + 4] & 0xF) | ((scales[j - 4] >> 6) << 4),
            (scales[j + 4] >> 4) | ((scales[j] >> 6) << 4),
        )
    }
}

/// The host MMQ reference for Q4_K: exact integer dots of
/// the weight nibbles against the host-quantized
/// activations, folded per sub-block in super-block order
/// with the same f32 expression the kernels use
/// (`vec_dot_q4_K_q8_1`'s shape). Copied from the K13
/// test's reference: K22's gate is against the same math.
fn reference_mmq_q4k(
    raw: &[u8],
    in_elems: usize,
    out_rows: usize,
    qs: &[u32],
    ds: &[f32],
    batch: usize,
) -> Vec<f32> {
    let blocks_per_row = in_elems / 256;
    let blocks32 = in_elems / 32;
    let mut out = vec![0.0f32; batch * out_rows];
    for m in 0..batch {
        let qx = unpack_qs(&qs[m * blocks32 * 8..(m + 1) * blocks32 * 8]);
        let row_ds = &ds[m * blocks32 * 4..(m + 1) * blocks32 * 4];
        for n in 0..out_rows {
            let mut acc = 0.0f32;
            for b in 0..blocks_per_row {
                let block = &raw[(n * blocks_per_row + b) * 144..][..144];
                let d = gguf::dequant::f16_to_f32(u16::from_le_bytes([block[0], block[1]]));
                let dmin = gguf::dequant::f16_to_f32(u16::from_le_bytes([block[2], block[3]]));
                let scales = &block[4..16];
                let payload = &block[16..144];
                for j in 0..8usize {
                    let (sc, mn) = scale_min_k4(j, scales);
                    let g = j / 2;
                    let hi = j % 2 == 1;
                    let mut sumi: i64 = 0;
                    for l in 0..32 {
                        let byte = payload[g * 32 + l];
                        let nib = if hi { byte >> 4 } else { byte & 0xF };
                        sumi += i64::from(nib) * i64::from(qx[b * 256 + j * 32 + l]);
                    }
                    let blk32 = b * 8 + j;
                    let (dx, s) = (row_ds[blk32 * 4], row_ds[blk32 * 4 + 1]);
                    acc += (d * f32::from(sc)) * (dx * sumi as f32) - (dmin * f32::from(mn)) * s;
                }
            }
            out[m * out_rows + n] = acc;
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Assert two result sets agree within reassociation
/// noise (the GEMM test's bound: relative to the result
/// set's own magnitude scale, plus a small floor).
fn check_close(label: &str, got: &[f32], want: &[f32]) {
    assert_eq!(got.len(), want.len(), "{label}: length mismatch");
    let scale = want.iter().fold(0.0f32, |a, w| a.max(w.abs()));
    let tol = 2e-3 + 5e-5 * scale;
    let mut max_diff = 0.0f32;
    for (i, (g, w)) in got.iter().zip(want.iter()).enumerate() {
        let diff = (g - w).abs();
        max_diff = max_diff.max(diff);
        assert!(
            diff <= tol,
            "{label}: element {i}: got {g}, want {w} (diff {diff}, tol {tol} at set scale {scale})"
        );
    }
    eprintln!(
        "{label}: max abs diff {max_diff:.3e} (set scale {scale:.3e}, rel {:.3e})",
        max_diff / scale.max(1.0)
    );
}

/// Quantize every row of `x` on the host: the reference
/// the GPU pipeline runs are checked against.
fn host_quantize(x: &[f32], width: usize) -> (Vec<u32>, Vec<f32>) {
    let mut qs = Vec::new();
    let mut ds = Vec::new();
    for row in x.chunks_exact(width) {
        let (q, d) = quantize_row_q8_1(row);
        qs.extend_from_slice(&q);
        ds.extend_from_slice(&d);
    }
    (qs, ds)
}

/// The K13 pipeline this device can build for the parity
/// leg: the shipped shape, or the m64 tile directly when
/// the grant covers it (same math either way; the tile
/// only changes which workgroup computes a row).
fn k13_or_skip(backend: &WgpuCompute) -> Option<K13Pipeline> {
    let ctx = backend.context();
    if let Some(shape) = wgpu_compute::kernels::k13_q4k_mmq::shipped_shape(&ctx.device.limits()) {
        return K13Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape).ok();
    }
    K13Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, MmqShape::new(64)).ok()
}

#[test]
fn k22_mmq_matches_reference_and_k13_at_prefill_batches() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let k22 = K22Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k22 pipeline builds");
    let k13 = k13_or_skip(&backend);
    let (inn, out_rows) = (512usize, 100usize);
    let bytes = synthetic_q4k(inn, out_rows);
    let k1 = K1Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k1 pipeline");
    let weights = k1
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q4k.k22", &bytes, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k1 upload");
    for batch in [16usize, 32, 64] {
        let x = lcg_input(400 + batch as u64, batch * inn);
        let (qs, ds) = host_quantize(&x, inn);
        let got = k22
            .run(ctx, &weights, &qs, &ds, batch as u32)
            .expect("k22 run");
        let want = reference_mmq_q4k(&bytes, inn, out_rows, &qs, &ds, batch);
        check_close(&format!("k22 vs reference batch {batch}"), &got, &want);
        if let Some(k13) = &k13 {
            let shipped = k13
                .run(ctx, &weights, &qs, &ds, batch as u32)
                .expect("k13 run");
            check_close(&format!("k22 vs k13 batch {batch}"), &got, &shipped);
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn k22_mmq_matches_reference_and_k13_on_a_chunk_tail() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let k22 = K22Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k22 pipeline builds");
    let k13 = k13_or_skip(&backend);
    // The 1,022-token prefill runs fifteen 64-row chunks
    // and one 62-row tail; the tail's partial batch tile
    // (and an out_rows that is not a tile multiple) is
    // the shape the guards exist for.
    let (inn, out_rows, batch) = (512usize, 100usize, 62usize);
    let bytes = synthetic_q4k(inn, out_rows);
    let k1 = K1Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k1 pipeline");
    let weights = k1
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q4k.k22tail", &bytes, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k1 upload");
    let x = lcg_input(462, batch * inn);
    let (qs, ds) = host_quantize(&x, inn);
    let got = k22
        .run(ctx, &weights, &qs, &ds, batch as u32)
        .expect("k22 run");
    let want = reference_mmq_q4k(&bytes, inn, out_rows, &qs, &ds, batch);
    check_close("k22 vs reference batch 62", &got, &want);
    if let Some(k13) = &k13 {
        let shipped = k13
            .run(ctx, &weights, &qs, &ds, batch as u32)
            .expect("k13 run");
        check_close("k22 vs k13 batch 62", &got, &shipped);
    }
}

#[test]
fn k22_mmq_refuses_out_of_band_batches_by_name() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let k22 = K22Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k22 pipeline builds");
    let (inn, out_rows) = (512usize, 64usize);
    let bytes = synthetic_q4k(inn, out_rows);
    let k1 = K1Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k1 pipeline");
    let weights = k1
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q4k.k22band", &bytes, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k1 upload");
    let qs_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("k22 band qs", 4096);
    let ds_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("k22 band ds", 4096);
    let out_buf = ctx.scratch_buffer("k22 band out", 4096);

        let err = k22
            .prepare(ctx, &weights, &qs_buf, &ds_buf, &out_buf, batch)
            .expect_err("out-of-band batch must refuse");
        assert!(
            err.to_string().contains("outside 1..=64"),
            "batch {batch}: refusal names the band: {err}"
        );
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/tests/k23_coopmat.rs =====
//! K23 (the Q4_K coopmat MMQ product) against the host
//! reference running the same quantized math, and
//! against K13 (the shipped Q4_K MMQ) on the same
//! inputs, at the shape the lane protocol pins: batch
//! 64 at the model's hidden width 6656, plus a 62-row
//! chunk tail (the 1,022-token prefill's last chunk
//! shape).
//!
//! K23 runs K13's exact math (the same integer dots and
//! per-sub-block scale fold; the products issue to the
//! cooperative matrix units instead of scalar DP4A), so
//! both gates use the crate's MMQ reassociation bound
//! (`check_close`): the reference gate is the
//! correctness claim, and the K13 gate is the parity
//! claim the routing relies on.
//!
//! These tests need a discrete Vulkan GPU whose device
//! was opened through the coopmat bridge: run them with
//! WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT_BRIDGE=1. On a machine without
//! a suitable adapter, or with a stock device (no
//! bridge), they print the reason and pass: the kernel
//! cannot exist there by design, and the bridge smoke
//! plus the prefill A/B run on the server through the
//! resident suite and the profile tool
//! (bench/coopmat-build-2026-11-06.md). Naga cannot
//! validate the passthrough module, so this file's
//! on-card numeric gates are the shader's correctness
//! evidence, as the feasibility note disclosed.

use wgpu_compute::kernels::k12_q8_quant::quantize_row_q8_1;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k13_q4k_mmq::{K13Pipeline, MmqShape};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::K1Pipeline;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k23_q4k_coopmat::K23Pipeline;
use wgpu_compute::{WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

/// A backend, or `None` after printing why this machine
/// cannot provide one.
fn backend_or_skip() -> Option<WgpuCompute> {
    match WgpuCompute::new() {
        Ok(b) => Some(b),
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            eprintln!(
                "skipping GPU test: no suitable adapter (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            None
        }
        Err(e) => panic!("backend construction failed unexpectedly: {e}"),
    }
}

/// The K23 pipeline on this backend's device, or `None`
/// (with the reason printed) when the device is a stock
/// device or fails the kernel's gates: the pipeline
/// exists only behind the coopmat bridge.
fn k23_or_skip(backend: &WgpuCompute) -> Option<K23Pipeline> {
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let Some(info) = ctx.coopmat else {
        eprintln!(
            "skipping k23 test: stock device (no coopmat bridge); \
             run with WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT_BRIDGE=1 on a coopmat device"
        );
        return None;
    };
    match K23Pipeline::for_device(&ctx.device, &info) {
        Ok(Some(p)) => Some(p),
        Ok(None) => {
            eprintln!("skipping k23 test: device fails the kernel's gates (see diag log)");
            None
        }
        Err(e) => panic!("k23 pipeline construction failed unexpectedly: {e}"),
    }
}

/// Deterministic pseudo-random f32s in [-0.5, 0.5) via a
/// 64-bit LCG, matching the other kernel tests.
fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            ((state >> 40) as u32) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Deterministic pseudo-random bytes via a small LCG.
fn lcg_bytes(seed: u8, count: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut state = seed;
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state.wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(17);
            state
        })
        .collect()
}

/// A synthetic Q4_K tensor's raw bytes (the MMQ test's
/// fixture: rotating (d, dmin) headers over LCG payloads).
fn synthetic_q4k(in_elems: usize, out_rows: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let blocks_per_row = in_elems / 256;
    let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(out_rows * blocks_per_row * 144);
    let headers: [(u16, u16); 4] = [
        (0x3c00, 0x3400),
        (0x3800, 0x0000),
        (0x4000, 0x2e66),
        (0x3e00, 0x3800),
    ];
    for row in 0..out_rows {
        for blk in 0..blocks_per_row {
            let (d, dmin) = headers[(row + blk) % headers.len()];
            let mut block = [0u8; 144];
            block[0..2].copy_from_slice(&d.to_le_bytes());
            block[2..4].copy_from_slice(&dmin.to_le_bytes());
            block[4..144].copy_from_slice(&lcg_bytes((row * 7 + blk * 13 + 5) as u8, 140)[..]);
            data.extend_from_slice(&block);
        }
    }
    data
}

/// Unpack a quantized row's words into per-element quants.
fn unpack_qs(words: &[u32]) -> Vec<i32> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(words.len() * 4);
    for w in words {
        for byte in w.to_le_bytes() {
            out.push(i32::from(byte as i8));
        }
    }
    out
}

/// ggml's `get_scale_min_k4`, mirrored from the gguf crate.
fn scale_min_k4(j: usize, scales: &[u8]) -> (u8, u8) {
    if j < 4 {
        (scales[j] & 63, scales[j + 4] & 63)
    } else {
        (
            (scales[j + 4] & 0xF) | ((scales[j - 4] >> 6) << 4),
            (scales[j + 4] >> 4) | ((scales[j] >> 6) << 4),
        )
    }
}

/// The host MMQ reference for Q4_K: exact integer dots of
/// the weight nibbles against the host-quantized
/// activations, folded per sub-block in super-block order
/// with the same f32 expression the kernels use
/// (`vec_dot_q4_K_q8_1`'s shape). Copied from the K13
/// test's reference: K23's gate is against the same math.
fn reference_mmq_q4k(
    raw: &[u8],
    in_elems: usize,
    out_rows: usize,
    qs: &[u32],
    ds: &[f32],
    batch: usize,
) -> Vec<f32> {
    let blocks_per_row = in_elems / 256;
    let blocks32 = in_elems / 32;
    let mut out = vec![0.0f32; batch * out_rows];
    for m in 0..batch {
        let qx = unpack_qs(&qs[m * blocks32 * 8..(m + 1) * blocks32 * 8]);
        let row_ds = &ds[m * blocks32 * 4..(m + 1) * blocks32 * 4];
        for n in 0..out_rows {
            let mut acc = 0.0f32;
            for b in 0..blocks_per_row {
                let block = &raw[(n * blocks_per_row + b) * 144..][..144];
                let d = gguf::dequant::f16_to_f32(u16::from_le_bytes([block[0], block[1]]));
                let dmin = gguf::dequant::f16_to_f32(u16::from_le_bytes([block[2], block[3]]));
                let scales = &block[4..16];
                let payload = &block[16..144];
                for j in 0..8usize {
                    let (sc, mn) = scale_min_k4(j, scales);
                    let g = j / 2;
                    let hi = j % 2 == 1;
                    let mut sumi: i64 = 0;
                    for l in 0..32 {
                        let byte = payload[g * 32 + l];
                        let nib = if hi { byte >> 4 } else { byte & 0xF };
                        sumi += i64::from(nib) * i64::from(qx[b * 256 + j * 32 + l]);
                    }
                    let blk32 = b * 8 + j;
                    let (dx, s) = (row_ds[blk32 * 4], row_ds[blk32 * 4 + 1]);
                    acc += (d * f32::from(sc)) * (dx * sumi as f32) - (dmin * f32::from(mn)) * s;
                }
            }
            out[m * out_rows + n] = acc;
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Assert two result sets agree within reassociation
/// noise (the GEMM test's bound: relative to the result
/// set's own magnitude scale, plus a small floor).
fn check_close(label: &str, got: &[f32], want: &[f32]) {
    assert_eq!(got.len(), want.len(), "{label}: length mismatch");
    let scale = want.iter().fold(0.0f32, |a, w| a.max(w.abs()));
    let tol = 2e-3 + 5e-5 * scale;
    let mut max_diff = 0.0f32;
    for (i, (g, w)) in got.iter().zip(want.iter()).enumerate() {
        let diff = (g - w).abs();
        max_diff = max_diff.max(diff);
        assert!(
            diff <= tol,
            "{label}: element {i}: got {g}, want {w} (diff {diff}, tol {tol} at set scale {scale})"
        );
    }
    eprintln!(
        "{label}: max abs diff {max_diff:.3e} (set scale {scale:.3e}, rel {:.3e})",
        max_diff / scale.max(1.0)
    );
}

/// Quantize every row of `x` on the host: the reference
/// the GPU pipeline runs are checked against.
fn host_quantize(x: &[f32], width: usize) -> (Vec<u32>, Vec<f32>) {
    let mut qs = Vec::new();
    let mut ds = Vec::new();
    for row in x.chunks_exact(width) {
        let (q, d) = quantize_row_q8_1(row);
        qs.extend_from_slice(&q);
        ds.extend_from_slice(&d);
    }
    (qs, ds)
}

/// The K13 pipeline this device can build for the parity
/// leg: the shipped shape, or the m64 tile directly when
/// the grant covers it (same math either way; the tile
/// only changes which workgroup computes a row).
fn k13_or_skip(backend: &WgpuCompute) -> Option<K13Pipeline> {
    let ctx = backend.context();
    if let Some(shape) = wgpu_compute::kernels::k13_q4k_mmq::shipped_shape(&ctx.device.limits()) {
        return K13Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape).ok();
    }
    K13Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, MmqShape::new(64)).ok()
}

#[test]
fn k23_coopmat_matches_reference_and_k13_at_hidden_width() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let Some(k23) = k23_or_skip(&backend) else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let k13 = k13_or_skip(&backend);
    // The protocol's pinned shape: the model's hidden
    // width, a full 64-row prefill chunk. The output
    // width is cut to 512 rows so the host reference
    // stays tractable; the width that stresses the
    // kernel's chunk loop is the input width, kept whole.
    let (inn, out_rows) = (6656usize, 512usize);
    let bytes = synthetic_q4k(inn, out_rows);
    let k1 = K1Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k1 pipeline");
    let weights = k1
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q4k.k23", &bytes, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k1 upload");
    for batch in [64usize, 62] {
        let x = lcg_input(400 + batch as u64, batch * inn);
        let (qs, ds) = host_quantize(&x, inn);
        let got = k23
            .run(ctx, &weights, &qs, &ds, batch as u32)
            .expect("k23 run");
        let want = reference_mmq_q4k(&bytes, inn, out_rows, &qs, &ds, batch);
        check_close(&format!("k23 vs reference batch {batch}"), &got, &want);
        if let Some(k13) = &k13 {
            let shipped = k13
                .run(ctx, &weights, &qs, &ds, batch as u32)
                .expect("k13 run");
            check_close(&format!("k23 vs k13 batch {batch}"), &got, &shipped);
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn k23_coopmat_matches_k13_on_the_full_square() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let Some(k23) = k23_or_skip(&backend) else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let Some(k13) = k13_or_skip(&backend) else {
        eprintln!("skipping k23 full-square parity: no k13 pipeline on this device");
        return;
    };
    // The full attention-projection shape: 6656 out x
    // 6656 in at batch 64, K13 parity only (the host
    // reference at this size belongs to the test above).
    let (inn, out_rows, batch) = (6656usize, 6656usize, 64usize);
    let bytes = synthetic_q4k(inn, out_rows);
    let k1 = K1Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k1 pipeline");
    let weights = k1
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q4k.k23full", &bytes, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k1 upload");
    let x = lcg_input(723, batch * inn);
    let (qs, ds) = host_quantize(&x, inn);
    let got = k23
        .run(ctx, &weights, &qs, &ds, batch as u32)
        .expect("k23 run");
    let shipped = k13
        .run(ctx, &weights, &qs, &ds, batch as u32)
        .expect("k13 run");
    check_close("k23 vs k13 batch 64 full square", &got, &shipped);
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/tests/k23_mmq.rs =====
//! K23 (the Q4_K MMQ product with llama's staging
//! repack) against the host reference running the
//! same quantized math, and against K13 (the shipped Q4_K
//! MMQ) on the same inputs, at the prefill band the kernel
//! exists for: batches 16, 32, 64, plus a 62-row chunk
//! tail (the 1,022-token prefill's last chunk shape).
//!
//! K23 runs K13's exact math (the same integer dots and
//! per-sub-block scale fold, in the same order), so both
//! gates use the crate's MMQ reassociation bound
//! (`check_close`, the GEMM gates' bound): the reference
//! gate is the correctness claim, and the K13 gate is the
//! parity claim the routing relies on (a plan can swap
//! the forms without moving a byte or changing the math
//! beyond float reassociation).
//!
//! These tests need a discrete Vulkan GPU under the
//! default selection policy. On a machine without one
//! they print the refusal and pass; shader validity on
//! any adapter is gated separately in
//! `shader_compile.rs`, and the real-file proof runs on
//! the server through the prefill A/B
//! (bench/k23-mmq-repack-2026-11-06.md).

use wgpu_compute::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::K1Pipeline;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k23_q4k_mmq::K23Pipeline;
use wgpu_compute::{WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

}

/// The K13 pipeline this device can build for the parity
/// leg: the shipped shape, or the m64 tile directly when
/// the grant covers it (same math either way; the tile
/// only changes which workgroup computes a row).
fn k13_or_skip(backend: &WgpuCompute) -> Option<K13Pipeline> {
    let ctx = backend.context();

        return K13Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape).ok();
    }
    K13Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, MmqShape::new(64)).ok()
}

#[test]
fn k23_mmq_matches_reference_and_k13_at_prefill_batches() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let k23 = K23Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k23 pipeline builds");
    let k13 = k13_or_skip(&backend);
    let (inn, out_rows) = (512usize, 100usize);

    let weights = k1
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q4k.k23", &bytes, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k1 upload");

        let x = lcg_input(400 + batch as u64, batch * inn);
        let (qs, ds) = host_quantize(&x, inn);

            .run(ctx, &weights, &qs, &ds, batch as u32)
            .expect("k23 run");

            let shipped = k13
                .run(ctx, &weights, &qs, &ds, batch as u32)
                .expect("k13 run");
            check_close(&format!("k23 vs k13 batch {batch}"), &got, &shipped);
        }
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/tests/k24_coopmat.rs =====
//! K24 (the Q4_K coopmat MMQ v2, register-resident)
//! against the host reference running the same
//! quantized math, against K13 (the shipped Q4_K MMQ),
//! and against K23 (the v1 coopmat kernel) on the same
//! inputs, at the shape the lane protocol pins: batch
//! 64 at the model's hidden width 6656, plus a 62-row
//! chunk tail (the 1,022-token prefill's last chunk
//! shape).
//!
//! K24 runs K13's and K23's exact math (the same
//! integer dots and per-sub-block scale fold; the
//! products issue to the cooperative matrix units and
//! the fold reads the accumulator's elements directly
//! instead of round-tripping through a shared tile),
//! so all gates use the crate's MMQ reassociation bound
//! (`check_close`): the reference gate is the
//! correctness claim, the K13 gate is the parity claim
//! the routing relies on, and the K23 gate is the A/B
//! claim against the v1 kernel it succeeds. The
//! reference gate is also the proof of the wave64
//! accumulator element mapping the register fold
//! stands on (Mesa's GFX11 lowering: element e at row
//! (inv / 16) + 4e, column inv % 16; see the kernel
//! module's docs): a wrong mapping scrambles the
//! output rows and columns and fails this gate by a
//! wide margin, not by reassociation noise.
//!
//! These tests need a discrete Vulkan GPU whose device
//! was opened through the coopmat bridge: run them with
//! WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT_BRIDGE=1. On a machine without
//! a suitable adapter, or with a stock device (no
//! bridge), they print the reason and pass: the kernel
//! cannot exist there by design, and the bridge smoke
//! plus the prefill A/B run on the server through the
//! resident suite and the profile tool
//! (bench/coopmat-v2-2026-11-07.md). Naga cannot
//! validate the passthrough module, so this file's
//! on-card numeric gates are the shader's correctness
//! evidence, as the feasibility note disclosed.

use wgpu_compute::kernels::k12_q8_quant::quantize_row_q8_1;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k13_q4k_mmq::{K13Pipeline, MmqShape};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::K1Pipeline;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k23_q4k_coopmat::K23Pipeline;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k24_q4k_coopmat::K24Pipeline;
use wgpu_compute::{WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

/// A backend, or `None` after printing why this machine
/// cannot provide one.
fn backend_or_skip() -> Option<WgpuCompute> {
    match WgpuCompute::new() {
        Ok(b) => Some(b),
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            eprintln!(
                "skipping GPU test: no suitable adapter (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            None
        }
        Err(e) => panic!("backend construction failed unexpectedly: {e}"),
    }
}

/// The K24 pipeline on this backend's device, or `None`
/// (with the reason printed) when the device is a stock
/// device or fails the kernel's gates: the pipeline
/// exists only behind the coopmat bridge.
fn k24_or_skip(backend: &WgpuCompute) -> Option<K24Pipeline> {
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let Some(info) = ctx.coopmat else {
        eprintln!(
            "skipping k24 test: stock device (no coopmat bridge); \
             run with WGPU_COMPUTE_COOPMAT_BRIDGE=1 on a coopmat device"
        );
        return None;
    };
    match K24Pipeline::for_device(&ctx.device, &info) {
        Ok(Some(p)) => Some(p),
        Ok(None) => {
            eprintln!("skipping k24 test: device fails the kernel's gates (see diag log)");
            None
        }
        Err(e) => panic!("k24 pipeline construction failed unexpectedly: {e}"),
    }
}

/// The K23 (v1) pipeline on this backend's device, for
/// the A/B parity leg, or `None` (with the reason
/// printed) on the same terms as [`k24_or_skip`].
fn k23_or_skip(backend: &WgpuCompute) -> Option<K23Pipeline> {
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let Some(info) = ctx.coopmat else {
        eprintln!("skipping k24 v1-parity leg: stock device (no coopmat bridge)");
        return None;
    };
    match K23Pipeline::for_device(&ctx.device, &info) {
        Ok(Some(p)) => Some(p),
        Ok(None) => {
            eprintln!("skipping k24 v1-parity leg: device fails the v1 kernel's gates");
            None
        }
        Err(e) => panic!("k23 pipeline construction failed unexpectedly: {e}"),
    }
}

/// Deterministic pseudo-random f32s in [-0.5, 0.5) via a
/// 64-bit LCG, matching the other kernel tests.
fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            ((state >> 40) as u32) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Deterministic pseudo-random bytes via a small LCG.
fn lcg_bytes(seed: u8, count: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut state = seed;
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state.wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(17);
            state
        })
        .collect()
}

/// A synthetic Q4_K tensor's raw bytes (the MMQ test's
/// fixture: rotating (d, dmin) headers over LCG payloads).
fn synthetic_q4k(in_elems: usize, out_rows: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let blocks_per_row = in_elems / 256;
    let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(out_rows * blocks_per_row * 144);
    let headers: [(u16, u16); 4] = [
        (0x3c00, 0x3400),
        (0x3800, 0x0000),
        (0x4000, 0x2e66),
        (0x3e00, 0x3800),
    ];
    for row in 0..out_rows {
        for blk in 0..blocks_per_row {
            let (d, dmin) = headers[(row + blk) % headers.len()];
            let mut block = [0u8; 144];
            block[0..2].copy_from_slice(&d.to_le_bytes());
            block[2..4].copy_from_slice(&dmin.to_le_bytes());
            block[4..144].copy_from_slice(&lcg_bytes((row * 7 + blk * 13 + 5) as u8, 140)[..]);
            data.extend_from_slice(&block);
        }
    }
    data
}

/// Unpack a quantized row's words into per-element quants.
fn unpack_qs(words: &[u32]) -> Vec<i32> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(words.len() * 4);
    for w in words {
        for byte in w.to_le_bytes() {
            out.push(i32::from(byte as i8));
        }
    }
    out
}

/// ggml's `get_scale_min_k4`, mirrored from the gguf crate.
fn scale_min_k4(j: usize, scales: &[u8]) -> (u8, u8) {
    if j < 4 {
        (scales[j] & 63, scales[j + 4] & 63)
    } else {
        (
            (scales[j + 4] & 0xF) | ((scales[j - 4] >> 6) << 4),
            (scales[j + 4] >> 4) | ((scales[j] >> 6) << 4),
        )
    }
}

/// The host MMQ reference for Q4_K: exact integer dots of
/// the weight nibbles against the host-quantized
/// activations, folded per sub-block in super-block order
/// with the same f32 expression the kernels use
/// (`vec_dot_q4_K_q8_1`'s shape). Copied from the K13
/// test's reference: K24's gate is against the same math.
fn reference_mmq_q4k(
    raw: &[u8],
    in_elems: usize,
    out_rows: usize,
    qs: &[u32],
    ds: &[f32],
    batch: usize,
) -> Vec<f32> {
    let blocks_per_row = in_elems / 256;
    let blocks32 = in_elems / 32;
    let mut out = vec![0.0f32; batch * out_rows];
    for m in 0..batch {
        let qx = unpack_qs(&qs[m * blocks32 * 8..(m + 1) * blocks32 * 8]);
        let row_ds = &ds[m * blocks32 * 4..(m + 1) * blocks32 * 4];
        for n in 0..out_rows {
            let mut acc = 0.0f32;
            for b in 0..blocks_per_row {
                let block = &raw[(n * blocks_per_row + b) * 144..][..144];
                let d = gguf::dequant::f16_to_f32(u16::from_le_bytes([block[0], block[1]]));
                let dmin = gguf::dequant::f16_to_f32(u16::from_le_bytes([block[2], block[3]]));
                let scales = &block[4..16];
                let payload = &block[16..144];
                for j in 0..8usize {
                    let (sc, mn) = scale_min_k4(j, scales);
                    let g = j / 2;
                    let hi = j % 2 == 1;
                    let mut sumi: i64 = 0;
                    for l in 0..32 {
                        let byte = payload[g * 32 + l];
                        let nib = if hi { byte >> 4 } else { byte & 0xF };
                        sumi += i64::from(nib) * i64::from(qx[b * 256 + j * 32 + l]);
                    }
                    let blk32 = b * 8 + j;
                    let (dx, s) = (row_ds[blk32 * 4], row_ds[blk32 * 4 + 1]);
                    acc += (d * f32::from(sc)) * (dx * sumi as f32) - (dmin * f32::from(mn)) * s;
                }
            }
            out[m * out_rows + n] = acc;
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Assert two result sets agree within reassociation
/// noise (the GEMM test's bound: relative to the result
/// set's own magnitude scale, plus a small floor).
fn check_close(label: &str, got: &[f32], want: &[f32]) {
    assert_eq!(got.len(), want.len(), "{label}: length mismatch");
    let scale = want.iter().fold(0.0f32, |a, w| a.max(w.abs()));
    let tol = 2e-3 + 5e-5 * scale;
    let mut max_diff = 0.0f32;
    for (i, (g, w)) in got.iter().zip(want.iter()).enumerate() {
        let diff = (g - w).abs();
        max_diff = max_diff.max(diff);
        assert!(
            diff <= tol,
            "{label}: element {i}: got {g}, want {w} (diff {diff}, tol {tol} at set scale {scale})"
        );
    }
    eprintln!(
        "{label}: max abs diff {max_diff:.3e} (set scale {scale:.3e}, rel {:.3e})",
        max_diff / scale.max(1.0)
    );
}

/// Quantize every row of `x` on the host: the reference
/// the GPU pipeline runs are checked against.
fn host_quantize(x: &[f32], width: usize) -> (Vec<u32>, Vec<f32>) {
    let mut qs = Vec::new();
    let mut ds = Vec::new();
    for row in x.chunks_exact(width) {
        let (q, d) = quantize_row_q8_1(row);
        qs.extend_from_slice(&q);
        ds.extend_from_slice(&d);
    }
    (qs, ds)
}

/// The K13 pipeline this device can build for the parity
/// leg: the shipped shape, or the m64 tile directly when
/// the grant covers it (same math either way; the tile
/// only changes which workgroup computes a row).
fn k13_or_skip(backend: &WgpuCompute) -> Option<K13Pipeline> {
    let ctx = backend.context();
    if let Some(shape) = wgpu_compute::kernels::k13_q4k_mmq::shipped_shape(&ctx.device.limits()) {
        return K13Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape).ok();
    }
    K13Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, MmqShape::new(64)).ok()
}

#[test]
fn k24_coopmat_matches_reference_k13_and_k23_at_hidden_width() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let Some(k24) = k24_or_skip(&backend) else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let k13 = k13_or_skip(&backend);
    let k23 = k23_or_skip(&backend);
    // The protocol's pinned shape: the model's hidden
    // width, a full 64-row prefill chunk. The output
    // width is cut to 512 rows so the host reference
    // stays tractable; the width that stresses the
    // kernel's chunk loop is the input width, kept whole.
    let (inn, out_rows) = (6656usize, 512usize);
    let bytes = synthetic_q4k(inn, out_rows);
    let k1 = K1Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k1 pipeline");
    let weights = k1
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q4k.k24", &bytes, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k1 upload");
    for batch in [64usize, 62] {
        let x = lcg_input(400 + batch as u64, batch * inn);
        let (qs, ds) = host_quantize(&x, inn);
        let got = k24
            .run(ctx, &weights, &qs, &ds, batch as u32)
            .expect("k24 run");
        let want = reference_mmq_q4k(&bytes, inn, out_rows, &qs, &ds, batch);
        check_close(&format!("k24 vs reference batch {batch}"), &got, &want);
        if let Some(k13) = &k13 {
            let shipped = k13
                .run(ctx, &weights, &qs, &ds, batch as u32)
                .expect("k13 run");
            check_close(&format!("k24 vs k13 batch {batch}"), &got, &shipped);
        }
        if let Some(k23) = &k23 {
            let v1 = k23
                .run(ctx, &weights, &qs, &ds, batch as u32)
                .expect("k23 run");
            check_close(&format!("k24 vs k23 batch {batch}"), &got, &v1);
        }
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/tests/k2_k3_synthetic.rs =====
//! K2 and K3 against synthetic Q6_K and Q5_K tensors with known
//! contents: the GPU results must match the CPU reference (the
//! `gguf` crate's dequantizer plus `torch-math`'s matvec) within
//! float reassociation noise, end to end through
//! `Compute::proj`. K3 additionally proves the two-dimensional
//! dispatch on a row count whose workgroup total crosses the
//! 65,535 per-dimension cap, the head geometry in miniature.
//!
//! These tests need a discrete Vulkan GPU under the default
//! selection policy. On a machine without one (a CI box, this
//! workstation) they print the refusal and pass: the policy's
//! whole point is that llvmpipe does not count, and the real-file
//! proofs run on the server through the `k2_check` and
//! `k3_check` examples. A skip here is a reported event, never a
//! silent one.

use std::sync::Arc;

use gguf::GgmlType;
use muse_glimmer::{Compute, Dtype, TensorView};
use wgpu_compute::{WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

/// A backend, or `None` after printing why this machine cannot
/// provide one.
fn backend_or_skip() -> Option<WgpuCompute> {
    match WgpuCompute::new() {
        Ok(b) => Some(b),
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            eprintln!(
                "skipping GPU test: no suitable adapter (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            None
        }
        Err(e) => panic!("backend construction failed unexpectedly: {e}"),
    }
}

fn fill_payload(bytes: &mut [u8], seed: u8) {
    let mut state = seed;
    for byte in bytes.iter_mut() {
        state = state.wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(17);
        *byte = state;
    }
}

/// One Q6_K super-block (210 bytes): payload in the ql and qh
/// planes, a spread of signed scales (including negatives, which
/// exercise the sign extension), and the chosen f16 `d`.
fn synthetic_q6k_block(d_bits: u16, seed: u8) -> [u8; 210] {
    let mut block = [0u8; 210];
    fill_payload(&mut block[0..192], seed);
    for (i, sc) in block[192..208].iter_mut().enumerate() {
        *sc = (i as i8).wrapping_mul(3).wrapping_sub(20) as u8;
    }
    block[208..210].copy_from_slice(&d_bits.to_le_bytes());
    block
}

/// A [256, 3] Q6_K tensor: one block per row, three different
/// `d` headers.
fn synthetic_q6k_tensor() -> TensorView {
    let mut data = Vec::new();
    data.extend_from_slice(&synthetic_q6k_block(0x3c00, 13)); // d 1.0
    data.extend_from_slice(&synthetic_q6k_block(0x3800, 59)); // d 0.5
    data.extend_from_slice(&synthetic_q6k_block(0x4000, 97)); // d 2.0
    TensorView {
        name: "synthetic.q6k".to_string(),
        dtype: Dtype::Q6K,
        shape: vec![256, 3],
        data: Arc::from(data.into_boxed_slice()),
    }
}

/// One Q5_K super-block (176 bytes): d and dmin headers, the
/// packed scale/min bytes, the qh bit plane, and the ql nibbles.
fn synthetic_q5k_block(d_bits: u16, dmin_bits: u16, seed: u8) -> [u8; 176] {
    let mut block = [0u8; 176];
    block[0..2].copy_from_slice(&d_bits.to_le_bytes());
    block[2..4].copy_from_slice(&dmin_bits.to_le_bytes());
    fill_payload(&mut block[4..176], seed);
    block
}

/// A [256, 3] Q5_K tensor: one block per row, three different
/// (d, dmin) headers.
fn synthetic_q5k_tensor() -> TensorView {
    let mut data = Vec::new();
    data.extend_from_slice(&synthetic_q5k_block(0x3c00, 0x3400, 21)); // d 1.0, dmin 0.25
    data.extend_from_slice(&synthetic_q5k_block(0x3800, 0x0000, 67)); // d 0.5, dmin 0
    data.extend_from_slice(&synthetic_q5k_block(0x4000, 0x2e66, 111)); // d 2.0, dmin ~0.1
    TensorView {
        name: "synthetic.q5k".to_string(),
        dtype: Dtype::Q5K,
        shape: vec![256, 3],
        data: Arc::from(data.into_boxed_slice()),
    }
}

fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            ((state >> 40) as u32) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Compare a GPU result against the CPU reference at the
/// projection tolerance (1e-4 relative to the largest expected
/// magnitude, the reassociation noise band).
fn assert_matches(label: &str, got: &[f32], expected: &[f32]) {
    assert_eq!(got.len(), expected.len(), "{label}: length mismatch");
    let mut max_abs = 0.0f32;
    let mut scale = 0.0f32;
    for (g, e) in got.iter().zip(expected.iter()) {
        max_abs = max_abs.max((g - e).abs());
        scale = scale.max(e.abs());
    }
    let rel = max_abs / scale.max(1.0);
    assert!(
        rel < 1e-4,
        "{label}: max_abs_err {max_abs} at scale {scale} (rel {rel}) exceeds reassociation noise"
    );
}

#[test]
fn k2_proj_matches_cpu_reference_on_synthetic_rows() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let view = synthetic_q6k_tensor();
    let input = lcg_input(3, 256);
    let weights = gguf::dequant::dequantize(GgmlType::Q6K, &view.data, 256 * 3);
    let expected = torch_math::matvec(&weights, 3, 256, &input).expect("cpu reference");

    let one = backend.proj(&input, &view, 1).expect("gpu proj, one row");
    let mut two_input = input.clone();
    two_input.extend_from_slice(&input);
    let two = backend
        .proj(&two_input, &view, 2)
        .expect("gpu proj, two rows");
    assert_matches("k2 one row", &one, &expected);
    assert_matches("k2 batched row 0", &two[0..3], &expected);
    assert_matches("k2 batched row 1", &two[3..6], &expected);
}

#[test]
fn k3_proj_matches_cpu_reference_across_the_2d_grid() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    // 140,000 output rows at two rows per workgroup is 70,000
    // workgroups: past the 65,535 per-dimension cap, so the
    // dispatch wraps into the second grid dimension, the head
    // geometry in miniature (the real head is 202,048 rows).
    // Seven distinct blocks cycle through the rows; the cycle
    // length does not divide the grid span, so a row-indexing
    // error across the wrap lands on the wrong block and shows.
    const ROWS: usize = 140_000;
    let blocks: Vec<[u8; 176]> = (0..7u8)
        .map(|i| synthetic_q5k_block(0x3c00, 0x3400, 21 + i * 13))
        .collect();
    let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(ROWS * 176);
    for r in 0..ROWS {
        data.extend_from_slice(&blocks[r % blocks.len()]);
    }
    let view = TensorView {
        name: "synthetic.q5k.grid".to_string(),
        dtype: Dtype::Q5K,
        shape: vec![256, ROWS as u64],
        data: Arc::from(data.into_boxed_slice()),
    };
    let input = lcg_input(9, 256);
    let weights = gguf::dequant::dequantize(GgmlType::Q5K, &view.data, 256 * ROWS);
    let expected = torch_math::matvec(&weights, ROWS, 256, &input).expect("cpu reference");
    let got = backend.proj(&input, &view, 1).expect("gpu proj, 2d grid");
    assert_matches("k3 2d grid", &got, &expected);
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/tests/k4_k8_kernels.rs =====
//! K4 through K8 against the CPU references, kernel by kernel:
//! K4's norms and add against `cpu-compute` (and the fused
//! norm+residual form against the trait composition), K5's
//! rotate against `torch-math`'s `rope_interleaved` and its
//! append against the cache slot law, K6's attention against
//! `cpu-compute`'s whole attention step over a mixed
//! sliding/global pattern with ring eviction, K7's activations
//! against `torch-math` and `cpu-compute`, K8's gather against
//! `cpu-compute`'s embed for every dtype both backends accept,
//! and K8's finishing kernel against
//! `muse_glimmer::softcap_scale` at the real 202,048 vocab
//! width.
//!
//! These tests need a GPU. The pipeline-compile test takes any
//! adapter wgpu enumerates (shader validity is not a selection
//! policy question); the numeric tests take the backend's
//! default policy, a discrete Vulkan GPU, and skip with a
//! printed reason where none qualifies (this workstation, CI
//! boxes), exactly like the K1 tests. On David's server the
//! 7900 XTX answers and every test runs for real.

use std::sync::Arc;

use cpu_compute::CpuCompute;
use muse_glimmer::{
    AttentionRequest, Cache, Compute, Dtype, GlimmerConfig, GlimmerError, LayerKind, PatternSource,
    PositionCache, TensorView,
};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::f32_to_f16_bits;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k4_rmsnorm::K4Pipeline;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k5_rope_kv::K5Pipeline;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k8_head::K8Pipeline;
use wgpu_compute::{WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

/// A backend, or `None` after printing why this machine cannot
/// provide one (the K1 tests' pattern).
fn backend_or_skip() -> Option<WgpuCompute> {
    match WgpuCompute::new() {
        Ok(b) => Some(b),
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            eprintln!(
                "skipping GPU test: no suitable adapter (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            None
        }
        Err(e) => panic!("backend construction failed unexpectedly: {e}"),
    }
}

/// Deterministic pseudo-random values in [-0.5, 0.5).
fn lcg(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            ((state >> 40) as u32) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

/// The largest absolute difference between two equal-length
/// vectors (panics on a length mismatch: a shape bug must not
/// hide inside a tolerance).
fn max_abs(a: &[f32], b: &[f32]) -> f32 {
    assert_eq!(a.len(), b.len(), "length mismatch in comparison");
    a.iter()
        .zip(b.iter())
        .map(|(x, y)| (x - y).abs())
        .fold(0.0f32, f32::max)
}

/// A config literal with the fields a given test needs set;
/// everything else holds the tiny values the CPU backend's own
/// tests use.
fn test_cfg() -> GlimmerConfig {
    GlimmerConfig {
        name: None,
        block_count: 3,
        context_length: 256,
        hidden: 256,
        ffn_hidden: 512,
        q_heads: 32,
        kv_heads: 2,
        key_length: 128,
        value_length: 128,
        rope_freq_base: 500_000.0,
        rope_freq_base_swa: 500_000.0,
        rms_eps: 1e-5,
        sliding_window: 4,
        logit_softcap: 20.0,
        logit_scale: 0.196_116_13,
        vocab_size: 8,
        layers: vec![
            LayerKind::SlidingWindow,
            LayerKind::Global,
            LayerKind::SlidingWindow,
        ],
        pattern_source: PatternSource::MeasuredFallback,
    }
}

fn f32_view(name: &str, shape: &[u64], values: &[f32]) -> TensorView {
    let data: Vec<u8> = values.iter().flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes()).collect();
    TensorView {
        name: name.to_string(),
        dtype: Dtype::F32,
        shape: shape.to_vec(),
        data: Arc::from(data.into_boxed_slice()),
    }
}

#[test]
fn k4_to_k8_shaders_compile_on_any_available_adapter() {
    let instance = wgpu::Instance::new(&wgpu::InstanceDescriptor {
        backends: wgpu::Backends::all(),
        ..Default::default()
    });
    let adapters = instance.enumerate_adapters(wgpu::Backends::all());
    let Some(adapter) = adapters.into_iter().next() else {
        eprintln!("skipping K4-K8 shader compile test: wgpu enumerates no adapters here");
        return;
    };
    let info = adapter.get_info();
    let (device, _queue) = pollster::block_on(adapter.request_device(&wgpu::DeviceDescriptor {
        label: Some("wgpu-compute K4-K8 shader compile test"),
        required_features: wgpu::Features::empty(),
        required_limits: wgpu::Limits::default(),
        ..Default::default()
    }))
    .expect("device for shader compile test");
    K4Pipeline::new(&device).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("K4 must build on {}: {e}", info.name));
    K5Pipeline::new(&device).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("K5 must build on {}: {e}", info.name));
    wgpu_compute::K6Pipeline::new(&device)
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("K6 must build on {}: {e}", info.name));
    wgpu_compute::K7Pipeline::new(&device)
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("K7 must build on {}: {e}", info.name));
    K8Pipeline::new(&device).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("K8 must build on {}: {e}", info.name));
    eprintln!(
        "K4-K8 shipped shaders compiled on {} ({:?})",
        info.name, info.backend
    );
}

#[test]
fn k4_norms_and_add_match_cpu() {
    let Some(gpu) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let cpu = CpuCompute::new();
    let rows = 3;
    let width = 512;
    let x = lcg(41, rows * width);
    let w_values = lcg(42, width);
    let w = f32_view("norm.weight", &[width as u64], &w_values);

    for eps in [1e-5f32, 1e-8] {
        let want = cpu.rms_norm(&x, &w, rows, eps).expect("cpu norm");
        let got = gpu.rms_norm(&x, &w, rows, eps).expect("gpu norm");
        let d = max_abs(&got, &want);
        eprintln!("k4 rms_norm eps={eps}: max abs diff {d:.3e}");
        assert!(d < 1e-4, "rms_norm drifted: {d}");
    }
    let want = cpu.rms_norm_plain(&x, rows, 1e-5).expect("cpu plain");
    let got = gpu.rms_norm_plain(&x, rows, 1e-5).expect("gpu plain");
    let d = max_abs(&got, &want);
    eprintln!("k4 rms_norm_plain: max abs diff {d:.3e}");
    assert!(d < 1e-4, "rms_norm_plain drifted: {d}");

    let b = lcg(43, rows * width);
    let want = cpu.add(&x, &b).expect("cpu add");
    let got = gpu.add(&x, &b).expect("gpu add");
    assert_eq!(got, want, "the residual add is exact");

    // The fused norm+residual form against the trait composition
    // (norm the branch, then add): this is the settled post-norm
    // order, so the fused kernel must equal it.
    let ctx = gpu.context();
    let k4 = K4Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k4 pipeline");
    let branch = lcg(44, rows * width);
    let composed = {
        let normed = gpu
            .rms_norm(&branch, &w, rows, 1e-8)
            .expect("gpu branch norm");
        gpu.add(&x, &normed).expect("gpu add")
    };
    let fused = k4
        .norm_residual(ctx, &x, &branch, &w_values, rows, 1e-8)
        .expect("fused norm+residual");
    let d = max_abs(&fused, &composed);
    eprintln!("k4 norm_residual fused vs composed: max abs diff {d:.3e}");
    assert!(d < 1e-5, "fused norm+residual drifted: {d}");
}

fn k7_activations_match_references() {
    let Some(gpu) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let cpu = CpuCompute::new();
    let gate = lcg(51, 4096);
    let up = lcg(52, 4096);

    // swiglu_ffn wraps it in projections the sibling tests cover).

}

#[test]
fn k5_rotate_matches_torch_math_and_append_hits_cache_slots() {
    let Some(gpu) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = gpu.context();
    let k5 = K5Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k5 pipeline");
    let heads = 32usize;
    let head_dim = 128usize;
    let width = heads * head_dim;
    let rows = 3usize;
    let start = 5usize;
    let x = lcg(61, rows * width);

    let buf = ctx.upload_f32("k5 test q", &x);
    k5.rotate(ctx, &buf, rows, heads, head_dim, start, 500_000.0)
        .expect("rotate");
    let got = ctx.read_f32(&buf, x.len()).expect("readback");
    let mut want = Vec::with_capacity(x.len());
    for r in 0..rows {
        for h in 0..heads {
            let rotated = torch_math::rope_interleaved(
                &x[r * width + h * head_dim..r * width + (h + 1) * head_dim],
                start + r,
                500_000.0,
                head_dim,
            )
            .expect("torch-math rope");
            want.extend_from_slice(&rotated);
        }
    }
    let d = max_abs(&got, &want);
    eprintln!("k5 rotate (start {start}, base 500000): max abs diff {d:.3e}");
    assert!(d < 1e-3, "rotate drifted: {d}");

    // Append: windowed layer, window 4, positions 6 and 7 land in
    // ring slots 2 and 3; a global layer's positions 6 and 7 land
    // in slots 6 and 7.
    let kv_width = 256usize;
    let k_rows = lcg(62, 2 * kv_width);
    let v_rows = lcg(63, 2 * kv_width);
    let k_src = ctx.upload_f32("k5 test k", &k_rows);
    let v_src = ctx.upload_f32("k5 test v", &v_rows);
    for (window, slots) in [(Some(4usize), [2usize, 3]), (None, [6usize, 7])] {
        let capacity = window.unwrap_or(8);
        let k_dst = ctx.scratch_buffer("k5 test k dst", (capacity * kv_width * 4) as u64);
        let v_dst = ctx.scratch_buffer("k5 test v dst", (capacity * kv_width * 4) as u64);
        k5.append(ctx, &k_src, &v_src, &k_dst, &v_dst, 2, kv_width, 6, window)
            .expect("append");
        let got_k = ctx
            .read_f32(&k_dst, capacity * kv_width)
            .expect("k readback");
        let got_v = ctx
            .read_f32(&v_dst, capacity * kv_width)
            .expect("v readback");
        for (i, slot) in slots.iter().enumerate() {
            assert_eq!(
                &got_k[slot * kv_width..(slot + 1) * kv_width],
                &k_rows[i * kv_width..(i + 1) * kv_width],
                "window {window:?}: K row {i} must sit in slot {slot}"
            );
            assert_eq!(
                &got_v[slot * kv_width..(slot + 1) * kv_width],
                &v_rows[i * kv_width..(i + 1) * kv_width],
                "window {window:?}: V row {i} must sit in slot {slot}"
            );
        }
        eprintln!("k5 append window {window:?}: rows landed in slots {slots:?}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn k6_attention_matches_cpu_step_for_step() {
    let Some(gpu) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let cpu = CpuCompute::new();
    let cfg = test_cfg();
    let q_width = cfg.q_width() as usize;
    let k_width = cfg.k_width() as usize;
    let v_width = cfg.v_width() as usize;

    let mut cpu_cache = PositionCache::new();
    let mut gpu_cache = PositionCache::new();
    // A 3-token prefill, then decode steps out to position 6:
    // the sliding window is 4, so the ring evicts and the window
    // mask's edge is exercised on the sliding layers.
    let chunks = [3usize, 1, 1, 1, 1];
    let mut step = 0usize;
    for (chunk_idx, &rows) in chunks.iter().enumerate() {
        let q = lcg(100 + chunk_idx as u64, rows * q_width);
        let k = lcg(200 + chunk_idx as u64, rows * k_width);
        let v = lcg(300 + chunk_idx as u64, rows * v_width);
        for layer in 0..cfg.layers.len() {
            let req_cpu = AttentionRequest {
                q: &q,
                k: &k,
                v: &v,
                layer,
                kind: cfg.layers[layer],
                cfg: &cfg,
            };
            let want = cpu
                .attention(&req_cpu, &mut cpu_cache)
                .expect("cpu attention");
            let req_gpu = AttentionRequest {
                q: &q,
                k: &k,
                v: &v,
                layer,
                kind: cfg.layers[layer],
                cfg: &cfg,
            };
            let got = gpu
                .attention(&req_gpu, &mut gpu_cache)
                .expect("gpu attention");
            let d = max_abs(&got, &want);
            eprintln!(
                "k6 attention chunk {chunk_idx} layer {layer} ({:?}): max abs diff {d:.3e}",
                cfg.layers[layer]
            );
            assert!(
                d < 2e-3,
                "attention drifted at chunk {chunk_idx} layer {layer}: {d}"
            );
            step += 1;
        }
        cpu_cache.advance(rows);
        gpu_cache.advance(rows);
    }
    assert_eq!(step, 15);
    eprintln!("k6 attention: prefill + 4 decode steps x 3 layers all matched");
}

/// One quantized embedding table of `vocab` rows x `hidden`
/// channels for `dtype`, built from deterministic payload bytes
/// with small scale headers, plus the config that describes it.
fn embed_table(dtype: Dtype, hidden: usize, vocab: usize) -> (TensorView, GlimmerConfig) {
    let mut cfg = test_cfg();
    cfg.hidden = hidden as u32;
    cfg.vocab_size = vocab as u32;
    let bytes: Vec<u8> = match dtype {
        Dtype::F32 => lcg(71, vocab * hidden)
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|v| v.to_le_bytes())
            .collect(),
        Dtype::F16 => lcg(72, vocab * hidden)
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|v| f32_to_f16_bits(*v).to_le_bytes())
            .collect(),
        Dtype::Bf16 => lcg(73, vocab * hidden)
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|v| ((v.to_bits() >> 16) as u16).to_le_bytes())
            .collect(),
        Dtype::Q8_0 => {
            // 34-byte blocks of 32: f16 scale 0.05, signed bytes.
            let mut out = Vec::new();
            let mut payload = lcg(74, vocab * hidden).into_iter();
            for _ in 0..(vocab * hidden / 32) {
                out.extend_from_slice(&f32_to_f16_bits(0.05).to_le_bytes());
                for _ in 0..32 {
                    let val = payload.next().expect("payload");
                    out.push((val * 100.0) as i8 as u8);
                }
            }
            out
        }
        Dtype::Q4K | Dtype::Q5K | Dtype::Q6K => {
            let block_bytes = match dtype {
                Dtype::Q4K => 144,
                Dtype::Q5K => 176,
                _ => 210,
            };
            let blocks = vocab * hidden / 256;
            let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(blocks * block_bytes);
            let mut state = 88_172_645_463_325_252_u64;
            let mut next = move || {
                state = state
                    .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                    .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
                (state >> 56) as u8
            };
            for _ in 0..blocks {
                // Header: d and dmin as small f16s at the offsets
                // each format reads them from. Q6_K carries only
                // d, at the block's end; the K formats lead with
                // the pair.
                let mut block = vec![0u8; block_bytes];
                if dtype == Dtype::Q6K {
                    for b in block.iter_mut() {
                        *b = next() & 0x3f;
                    }
                    block[208..210].copy_from_slice(&f32_to_f16_bits(0.02).to_le_bytes());
                } else {
                    block[0..2].copy_from_slice(&f32_to_f16_bits(0.02).to_le_bytes());
                    block[2..4].copy_from_slice(&f32_to_f16_bits(0.005).to_le_bytes());
                    for b in block.iter_mut().skip(4) {
                        *b = next();
                    }
                    // Keep the packed 6-bit scales small.
                    for b in block.iter_mut().take(16).skip(4) {
                        *b &= 0x07;
                    }
                }
                out.extend_from_slice(&block);
            }
            out
        }
        other => panic!("embed_table does not build {other:?}"),
    };
    let view = TensorView {
        name: "token_embd.weight".to_string(),
        dtype,
        shape: vec![hidden as u64, vocab as u64],
        data: Arc::from(bytes.into_boxed_slice()),
    };
    (view, cfg)
}

#[test]
fn k8_embed_matches_cpu_for_every_shared_dtype() {
    let Some(gpu) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let cpu = CpuCompute::new();
    let tokens = [0u32, 3, 7, 5];
    for dtype in [
        Dtype::F32,
        Dtype::F16,
        Dtype::Bf16,
        Dtype::Q8_0,
        Dtype::Q4K,
        Dtype::Q5K,
        Dtype::Q6K,
    ] {
        let (table, cfg) = embed_table(dtype, 256, 8);
        let want = cpu.embed(&table, &tokens, &cfg).expect("cpu embed");
        let got = gpu.embed(&table, &tokens, &cfg).expect("gpu embed");
        let d = max_abs(&got, &want);
        eprintln!("k8 embed {dtype:?}: max abs diff {d:.3e}");
        assert!(d < 1e-4, "embed drifted for {dtype:?}: {d}");
    }

    // Refusals keep cpu-compute's boundary: a dtype outside the
    // shared set refuses by name.
    let (mut table, cfg) = embed_table(Dtype::F32, 256, 8);
    table.dtype = Dtype::Q4_0;
    let err = gpu
        .embed(&table, &[0], &cfg)
        .expect_err("Q4_0 embedding must refuse");
    assert!(
        matches!(err, GlimmerError::StepFailed { step: "embed", .. }),
        "unexpected refusal: {err:?}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn k8_finish_matches_softcap_scale_at_real_vocab_width() {
    let Some(gpu) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = gpu.context();
    let k8 = K8Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k8 pipeline");
    let logits = lcg(81, 202_048)
        .iter()
        .map(|v| v * 80.0)
        .collect::<Vec<f32>>();
    let mut want = logits.clone();
    muse_glimmer::softcap_scale(&mut want, 20.0, 0.196_116_13);
    let got = k8
        .finish(ctx, &logits, 0.196_116_13, 20.0)
        .expect("gpu finish");
    let d = max_abs(&got, &want);
    eprintln!("k8 finish over 202048 logits: max abs diff {d:.3e}");
    assert!(d < 1e-3, "finish drifted: {d}");
}

===== END FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/tests/k4_k8_kernels.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/tests/k8_argmax.rs =====
//! Gate: K8's on-device argmax against the host greedy pick
//! (maximum value, lowest index on an exact tie, the
//! `itak-engine` sampler's convention), over vectors sized
//! and shaped like the real head's output, including an
//! engineered exact tie and a maximum in the last reduction
//! group's tail.
//!
//! The one-shot [`K8Pipeline::argmax`] uploads host logits
//! and reads back the eight result bytes. Devices without a
//! suitable adapter skip, per the crate's test convention.

use wgpu_compute::{K8Pipeline, WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

fn backend_or_skip(test: &str) -> Option<WgpuCompute> {
    match WgpuCompute::new() {
        Ok(b) => Some(b),
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            eprintln!(
                "skipping {test}: no suitable adapter (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            None
        }
        Err(e) => panic!("backend construction failed unexpectedly: {e}"),
    }
}

/// The host greedy pick: a strictly-greater scan, so the
/// lowest index wins an exact tie.
fn host_greedy(logits: &[f32]) -> (u32, f32) {
    let mut best = 0usize;
    let mut best_val = f32::NEG_INFINITY;
    for (i, &v) in logits.iter().enumerate() {
        if v > best_val {
            best_val = v;
            best = i;
        }
    }
    (best as u32, best_val)
}

/// Deterministic pseudo-random logits in a bounded band.
fn lcg_logits(n: usize, seed: u32) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed;
    (0..n)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state.wrapping_mul(1_664_525).wrapping_add(1_013_904_223);
            ((state >> 8) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5) * 40.0
        })
        .collect()
}

#[test]
fn k8_argmax_matches_host_greedy() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip("k8 argmax") else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let k8 = K8Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k8 pipelines build");

    // The real vocabulary width, plus small widths around the
    // reduction's edges (one element, one workgroup, exactly
    // the stage stride, one past it).
    for n in [1usize, 255, 256, 257, 32_768, 32_769, 202_048] {
        let logits = lcg_logits(n, 0xA66E_0001 + n as u32);
        let (id, value) = k8.argmax(ctx, &logits).expect("device argmax");
        let (want_id, want_value) = host_greedy(&logits);
        assert_eq!(id, want_id, "winner disagrees at n={n}");
        assert_eq!(
            value, want_value,
            "winning logit must be bit-exact at n={n} (the reduction moves values, \
             never recomputes them)"
        );
    }

    // An exact tie between distant indices: the lowest wins.
    let mut logits = lcg_logits(202_048, 7);
    logits[123] = 99.5;
    logits[150_000] = 99.5;
    logits[150_001] = 99.5;
    let (id, value) = k8.argmax(ctx, &logits).expect("device argmax (tie)");
    assert_eq!(
        (id, value),
        (123, 99.5),
        "the lowest index wins an exact tie"
    );

    // The maximum in the final element, and an all-negative
    // vector (the winner below zero).
    let mut logits = lcg_logits(202_048, 99);
    let last = logits.len() - 1;
    logits[last] = 88.25;
    let (id, _) = k8.argmax(ctx, &logits).expect("device argmax (tail)");
    assert_eq!(id as usize, last);
    let logits: Vec<f32> = (0..4096).map(|i| -1.0 - (i % 97) as f32 * 0.01).collect();
    let (id, value) = k8.argmax(ctx, &logits).expect("device argmax (negative)");
    assert_eq!((id, value), host_greedy(&logits));

    // Empty input refuses by name rather than reducing nothing.
    let err = k8.argmax(ctx, &[]).expect_err("empty argmax refuses");
    assert!(err.to_string().contains("zero"), "unexpected error: {err}");
}

===== END FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/tests/k8_argmax.rs =====

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/tests/kv_f16.rs =====
//! The f16 KV storage pins (bench/f16-kv-2026-11-07.md):
//! the resident session can store its per-layer K and V
//! buffers as packed f16 instead of f32, behind
//! `WGPU_COMPUTE_KV_F16` (exact "1" only, default off).
//!
//! Three legs:
//!
//! - **Round-trip bounds (host, runs everywhere).** The
//!   conversion the shaders perform (`pack2x16float` on
//!   write, `unpack2x16float` on read) is mirrored on
//!   the host by the crate's own `f32_to_f16_bits` and
//!   gguf's `f16_to_f32`, and the per-element error is
//!   measured over a deterministic sweep: every
//!   representable f16 value round-trips exactly, and
//!   arbitrary f32 inputs stay inside the half-ulp bound
//!   (relative error at most 2^-11 for normals, absolute
//!   error at most 2^-25 for subnormal results). The
//!   packed word layout (even element in the low half)
//!   is pinned the same way.
//! - **Memory math (host, runs everywhere).** The
//!   full-context KV bytes are computed FROM the real
//!   Glimmer config shape by
//!   `full_context_kv_bytes`, never hardcoded in the
//!   formula: 3,653,238,784 bytes in f32 (K and V, 13
//!   global layers at 131,072 rows plus 39 windowed at
//!   2,048, 2 KV heads at head dim 128 per side), and
//!   exactly half, 1,826,619,392, in f16.
//! - **Session fixture (device; skips where no adapter
//!   qualifies).** The resident-session cross fixture
//!   (hidden 512, six layers in a sliding/global mix,
//!   window 4, both weight mixes) runs twice on the
//!   same weights: once on a backend built with the
//!   switch unset (f32 KV) and once on a backend built
//!   with the switch at "1" (f16 KV). Greedy feeding is
//!   shared (the f32 session's argmax feeds both, so
//!   the sequences cannot diverge), top-1 must agree at
//!   every step, and the measured max logit delta is
//!   printed. The assertion ceiling is the crate's
//!   cross-backend bar of 0.5, used here as a breakage
//!   tripwire and disclosed as such: the delta the card
//!   run prints replaces it (see the bench note). A
//!   second f32 session must reproduce the first
//!   session's logits bit for bit, proving the harness
//!   itself is deterministic before any cross-format
//!   delta is believed. The same test also pins the
//!   two-pass form's named refusal of an f16 layer.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::Arc;

use muse_glimmer::{
    expected_tensor_names, Dtype, GlimmerConfig, GlimmerError, LayerKind, PatternSource, Result,
    TensorSource, TensorView, Weights,
};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::f32_to_f16_bits;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k6_attention::{
    full_context_kv_bytes, AttendGeom, DeviceKv, K6Pipeline, KvStorage,
};
use wgpu_compute::{ResidentSession, WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

// ----------------------------------------------------------------
// Host conversion mirror
// ----------------------------------------------------------------

/// One packed word the way WGSL's `pack2x16float`
/// builds it: the even element (the vec's x) in the low
/// half, the odd element (y) in the high half.
fn pack_pair(lo: f32, hi: f32) -> u32 {
    u32::from(f32_to_f16_bits(lo)) | (u32::from(f32_to_f16_bits(hi)) << 16)
}

/// The two elements of a packed word, the way WGSL's
/// `unpack2x16float` reads them back.
fn unpack_pair(word: u32) -> (f32, f32) {
    (
        gguf::dequant::f16_to_f32(word as u16),
        gguf::dequant::f16_to_f32((word >> 16) as u16),
    )
}

#[test]
fn f16_round_trip_stays_inside_the_half_ulp_bound() {
    // Every representable finite f16 value decodes to an
    // exact f32 and re-encodes to the identical bits:
    // the stored cache holds exactly the representable
    // values, so this half of the round trip is lossless
    // by construction, and any encoder drift fails here.
    let mut exact = 0u32;
    for bits in (0x0000u32..=0x7bff).chain(0x8000..=0xfbff) {
        let value = gguf::dequant::f16_to_f32(bits as u16);
        assert!(value.is_finite(), "bits {bits:#06x} should be finite");
        assert_eq!(
            f32_to_f16_bits(value),
            bits as u16,
            "representable value at bits {bits:#06x} must round-trip exactly"
        );
        exact += 1;
    }

    // Arbitrary f32 inputs round to the nearest f16:
    // the error is at most half an f16 ulp, which is a
    // relative 2^-11 for normal results and an absolute
    // 2^-25 once the result is subnormal (or zero). The
    // sweep is a deterministic LCG stream across
    // magnitudes, plus the exact binade edges.
    let mut rng = Rng(0x0f16_0bad);
    let mut max_rel = 0.0f32;
    let mut max_abs_sub = 0.0f32;
    let mut checked = 0u32;
    let check = |x: f32, max_rel: &mut f32, max_abs_sub: &mut f32, checked: &mut u32| {
        if !x.is_finite() || x.abs() >= 65_504.0 {
            return;
        }
        let rt = gguf::dequant::f16_to_f32(f32_to_f16_bits(x));
        let err = (rt - x).abs();
        if x.abs() >= f32::from_bits(0x3880_0000) {
            // |x| >= 2^-14: the result is a normal f16
            // (or rounds up to one), so the bound is
            // relative.
            let rel = err / x.abs();
            assert!(
                rel <= 0.000_488_281_25,
                "round-trip relative error {rel:e} past 2^-11 at x={x:e}"
            );
            *max_rel = (*max_rel).max(rel);
        } else {
            assert!(
                err <= 0.000_000_029_802_322,
                "round-trip absolute error {err:e} past 2^-25 at x={x:e}"
            );
            *max_abs_sub = (*max_abs_sub).max(err);
        }
        *checked += 1;
    };
    for e in -20..=15i32 {
        for m in [1.0f32, 1.000_976_6, 1.5, 1.999_023_4, 0.5, 0.75] {
            let x = m * 2.0f32.powi(e);
            check(x, &mut max_rel, &mut max_abs_sub, &mut checked);
            check(-x, &mut max_rel, &mut max_abs_sub, &mut checked);
        }
    }
    for _ in 0..200_000 {
        // Random bit patterns biased to the K/V
        // magnitude range: exponents from 2^-20 to 2^15.
        let sign = if rng.next_u8() & 1 == 0 { 1.0 } else { -1.0 };
        let e = (rng.next_u8() % 36) as i32 - 20;
        let mant = 1.0 + (f32::from(rng.next_u8()) / 256.0 + f32::from(rng.next_u8()) / 65_536.0);
        check(
            sign * mant * 2.0f32.powi(e),
            &mut max_rel,
            &mut max_abs_sub,
            &mut checked,
        );
    }
    eprintln!(
        "f16 round trip: {exact} representable values exact; {checked} arbitrary inputs, \
         max relative error {max_rel:e} (bound 2^-11 = 4.8828125e-4), max subnormal \
         absolute error {max_abs_sub:e} (bound 2^-25 = 2.9802322e-8)"
    );
    assert!(checked > 200_000);
    assert!(max_rel > 0.0, "the sweep must actually measure error");
}

#[test]
fn packed_word_layout_is_even_low_odd_high() {
    // The layout both shader sides assume: element 2i in
    // the low half of word i, element 2i+1 in the high
    // half (WGSL pack2x16float's x/y order).
    let (lo, hi) = unpack_pair(pack_pair(1.5, -0.25));
    assert_eq!((lo, hi), (1.5, -0.25));
    let (lo, hi) = unpack_pair(pack_pair(0.0, 65_504.0));
    assert_eq!((lo, hi), (0.0, 65_504.0));
}

/// The real Glimmer config shape (the values the KV
/// byte math reads: layer pattern, context, window,
/// head counts and lengths; the rest rides along so
/// the literal is a complete config).
fn glimmer_cfg() -> GlimmerConfig {
    GlimmerConfig {
        name: None,
        block_count: 52,
        context_length: 131_072,
        hidden: 6656,
        ffn_hidden: 19_968,
        q_heads: 32,
        kv_heads: 2,
        key_length: 128,
        value_length: 128,
        rope_freq_base: 500_000.0,
        rope_freq_base_swa: 500_000.0,
        rms_eps: 1e-5,
        sliding_window: 2048,
        logit_softcap: 20.0,
        logit_scale: 0.196_116_13,
