#[test]
fn k15_k16_mmq_wide_shaders_compile_on_any_available_adapter() {
    use wgpu_compute::kernels::k15_q4k_mmq_wide::{
        q4k_wide_staging_bytes, shipped_wide_shape as shipped_q4k, K15Pipeline, WideMmqShape,
        WIDE_TILE_CANDIDATES,
    };
    use wgpu_compute::kernels::k16_q6k_mmq_wide::{
        q6k_wide_staging_bytes, shipped_wide_shape as shipped_q6k, K16Pipeline,
    };
    let instance = wgpu::Instance::new(&wgpu::InstanceDescriptor {
        backends: wgpu::Backends::all(),
        ..Default::default()
    });
    let adapters = instance.enumerate_adapters(wgpu::Backends::all());
    let Some(adapter) = adapters.into_iter().next() else {
        eprintln!("skipping k15-k16 compile test: wgpu enumerates no adapters here");
        return;
    };
    let info = adapter.get_info();
    let wanted = adapter.features() & (wgpu::Features::SUBGROUP | wgpu::Features::SHADER_F16);
    // First device: wgpu's default limits (16 KiB of
    // workgroup storage). No wide candidate's
    // double-buffered staging set fits there, so both
    // constructors must report absence (for_device) or
    // refuse by name (with_shape), never panic or degrade.
    let (capped, _q1) = pollster::block_on(adapter.request_device(&wgpu::DeviceDescriptor {
        label: Some("wgpu-compute k15-k16 capped test"),
        required_features: wanted,
        required_limits: wgpu::Limits::default(),
        ..Default::default()
    }))
    .expect("capped device for k15-k16 test");
    match K15Pipeline::for_device(&capped) {
        Ok(None) => {}
        Ok(Some(_)) => panic!("k15 under default limits must be Ok(None), got a pipeline"),
        Err(e) => panic!("k15 under default limits must be Ok(None), got error: {e}"),
    }
    match K16Pipeline::for_device(&capped) {
        Ok(None) => {}
        Ok(Some(_)) => panic!("k16 under default limits must be Ok(None), got a pipeline"),
        Err(e) => panic!("k16 under default limits must be Ok(None), got error: {e}"),
    }
    let err = match K15Pipeline::with_shape(&capped, WideMmqShape::new(64)) {
        Ok(_) => panic!("k15 w64 must refuse a 16 KiB storage grant by name"),
        Err(e) => e,
    };
    assert!(
        err.to_string().contains("workgroup memory"),
        "refusal names the binding limit: {err}"
    );
    // A tile width outside the candidate set refuses by
    // name on any device.
    let err = match K15Pipeline::with_shape(&capped, WideMmqShape::new(100)) {
        Ok(_) => panic!("k15 must refuse a non-candidate tile width by name"),
        Err(e) => e,
    };
    assert!(
        err.to_string().contains("is not one of"),
        "refusal names the candidate set: {err}"
    );
    // Second device: the adapter's own limits. Every
    // candidate whose staging the grant covers must
    // compile: this is the leg that validates the wide
    // shaders (the parity-unrolled pipeline, the parity
    // buffer sets) on whatever stack runs the test,
    // including this repo's build VM.
    let (full, _q2) = pollster::block_on(adapter.request_device(&wgpu::DeviceDescriptor {
        label: Some("wgpu-compute k15-k16 full test"),
        required_features: wanted,
        required_limits: adapter.limits(),
        ..Default::default()
    }))
    .expect("full-limits device for k15-k16 test");
    let granted = full.limits().max_compute_workgroup_storage_size;
    for cand in WIDE_TILE_CANDIDATES {
        let shape = WideMmqShape::new(cand);
        if granted >= q4k_wide_staging_bytes(&shape) {
            K15Pipeline::with_shape(&full, shape).unwrap_or_else(|e| {
                panic!(
                    "k15 {} must build on {} (grant {granted}): {e}",
                    shape.name(),
                    info.name
                )
            });
            eprintln!("k15 {} compiled on {}", shape.name(), info.name);
        }
        if granted >= q6k_wide_staging_bytes(&shape) {
            K16Pipeline::with_shape(&full, shape).unwrap_or_else(|e| {
                panic!(
                    "k16 {} must build on {} (grant {granted}): {e}",
                    shape.name(),
                    info.name
                )
            });
            eprintln!("k16 {} compiled on {}", shape.name(), info.name);
        }
    }
    // for_device picks exactly the shipped shape the
    // limits arithmetic names, on both families.
    match (shipped_q4k(&full.limits()), K15Pipeline::for_device(&full)) {
        (Some(want), Ok(Some(p))) => assert_eq!(p.shape(), want),
        (None, Ok(None)) => {}
        (want, got) => panic!(
            "k15 for_device disagrees with the shipped shape: want {want:?}, got {:?}",
            got.map(|o| o.map(|p| p.shape()))
        ),
    }
    match (shipped_q6k(&full.limits()), K16Pipeline::for_device(&full)) {
        (Some(want), Ok(Some(p))) => assert_eq!(p.shape(), want),
        (None, Ok(None)) => {}
        (want, got) => panic!(
            "k16 for_device disagrees with the shipped shape: want {want:?}, got {:?}",
            got.map(|o| o.map(|p| p.shape()))
        ),
    }
}

#[test]
fn k18_small_batch_shaders_compile_on_any_available_adapter() {
    use wgpu_compute::kernels::k18_small_batch::{
        q4k_small_staging_bytes, q5k_small_staging_bytes, q6k_small_staging_bytes,
        shipped_shape_q4k, shipped_shape_q5k, shipped_shape_q6k, K18Q4KPipeline, K18Q5KPipeline,
        K18Q6KPipeline, SmallShape,
    };
    let instance = wgpu::Instance::new(&wgpu::InstanceDescriptor {
        backends: wgpu::Backends::all(),
        ..Default::default()
    });
    let adapters = instance.enumerate_adapters(wgpu::Backends::all());
    let Some(adapter) = adapters.into_iter().next() else {
        eprintln!("skipping k18 compile test: wgpu enumerates no adapters here");
        return;
    };
    let info = adapter.get_info();
    let wanted = adapter.features() & (wgpu::Features::SUBGROUP | wgpu::Features::SHADER_F16);
    // First device: wgpu's default limits (16 KiB of
    // workgroup storage). The Q4_K and Q5_K tile-32
    // staging sets fit that grant (15,424 bytes), so
    // their constructors must produce the s32 pipeline;
    // the Q6_K set is 64 bytes over it, so its
    // constructor must report absence. The wide tile
    // refuses by name on all three, and a tile width
    // outside the candidate set refuses by name on any
    // device.
    let (capped, _q1) = pollster::block_on(adapter.request_device(&wgpu::DeviceDescriptor {
        label: Some("wgpu-compute k18 capped test"),
        required_features: wanted,
        required_limits: wgpu::Limits::default(),
        ..Default::default()
    }))
    .expect("capped device for k18 test");
    match K18Q4KPipeline::for_device(&capped) {
        Ok(Some(p)) => assert_eq!(p.shape(), SmallShape::new(32)),
        other => panic!("k18 q4k under default limits must be Ok(Some(s32)), got {other:?}"),
    }
    match K18Q5KPipeline::for_device(&capped) {
        Ok(Some(p)) => assert_eq!(p.shape(), SmallShape::new(32)),
        other => panic!("k18 q5k under default limits must be Ok(Some(s32)), got {other:?}"),
    }
    match K18Q6KPipeline::for_device(&capped) {
        Ok(None) => {}
        Ok(Some(p)) => panic!(
            "k18 q6k under default limits must be Ok(None), got a pipeline at {:?}",
            p.shape()
        ),
        Err(e) => panic!("k18 q6k under default limits must be Ok(None), got error: {e}"),
    }
    let err = match K18Q4KPipeline::with_shape(&capped, SmallShape::new(64)) {
        Ok(_) => panic!("k18 q4k s64 must refuse a 16 KiB storage grant by name"),
        Err(e) => e,
    };
    assert!(
        err.to_string().contains("workgroup memory"),
        "refusal names the binding limit: {err}"
    );
    let err = match K18Q4KPipeline::with_shape(&capped, SmallShape::new(100)) {
        Ok(_) => panic!("k18 must refuse a non-candidate tile width by name"),
        Err(e) => e,
    };
    assert!(
        err.to_string().contains("not 32 or 64"),
        "refusal names the candidate set: {err}"
    );
    // Second device: the adapter's own limits. Every
    // candidate whose staging the grant covers must
    // compile, on all three families: this is the leg
    // that validates the small-batch shaders (the
    // four-batch-lane setup, the Q5_K assembly stage)
    // on whatever stack runs the test.
    let (full, _q2) = pollster::block_on(adapter.request_device(&wgpu::DeviceDescriptor {
        label: Some("wgpu-compute k18 full test"),
        required_features: wanted,
        required_limits: adapter.limits(),
        ..Default::default()
    }))
    .expect("full-limits device for k18 test");
    let granted = full.limits().max_compute_workgroup_storage_size;
    for cand in [64, 32] {
        let shape = SmallShape::new(cand);
        if granted >= q4k_small_staging_bytes(&shape) {
            K18Q4KPipeline::with_shape(&full, shape).unwrap_or_else(|e| {
                panic!(
                    "k18 q4k {} must build on {} (grant {granted}): {e}",
                    shape.name(),
                    info.name
                )
            });
            eprintln!("k18 q4k {} compiled on {}", shape.name(), info.name);
        }
        if granted >= q5k_small_staging_bytes(&shape) {
            K18Q5KPipeline::with_shape(&full, shape).unwrap_or_else(|e| {
                panic!(
                    "k18 q5k {} must build on {} (grant {granted}): {e}",
                    shape.name(),
                    info.name
                )
            });
            eprintln!("k18 q5k {} compiled on {}", shape.name(), info.name);
        }
        if granted >= q6k_small_staging_bytes(&shape) {
            K18Q6KPipeline::with_shape(&full, shape).unwrap_or_else(|e| {
                panic!(
                    "k18 q6k {} must build on {} (grant {granted}): {e}",
                    shape.name(),
                    info.name
                )
            });
            eprintln!("k18 q6k {} compiled on {}", shape.name(), info.name);
        }
    }
    // for_device picks exactly the shipped shape the
    // limits arithmetic names, on all three families.
    match (
        shipped_shape_q4k(&full.limits()),
        K18Q4KPipeline::for_device(&full),
    ) {
        (Some(want), Ok(Some(p))) => assert_eq!(p.shape(), want),
        (None, Ok(None)) => {}
        (want, got) => panic!(
            "k18 q4k for_device disagrees with the shipped shape: want {want:?}, got {:?}",
            got.map(|o| o.map(|p| p.shape()))
        ),
    }
    match (
        shipped_shape_q5k(&full.limits()),
        K18Q5KPipeline::for_device(&full),
    ) {
        (Some(want), Ok(Some(p))) => assert_eq!(p.shape(), want),
        (None, Ok(None)) => {}
        (want, got) => panic!(
            "k18 q5k for_device disagrees with the shipped shape: want {want:?}, got {:?}",
            got.map(|o| o.map(|p| p.shape()))
        ),
    }
    match (
        shipped_shape_q6k(&full.limits()),
        K18Q6KPipeline::for_device(&full),
    ) {
        (Some(want), Ok(Some(p))) => assert_eq!(p.shape(), want),
        (None, Ok(None)) => {}
        (want, got) => panic!(
            "k18 q6k for_device disagrees with the shipped shape: want {want:?}, got {:?}",
            got.map(|o| o.map(|p| p.shape()))
        ),
    }
}

#[test]
fn k19_mmv_shaders_compile_on_any_available_adapter() {
    use wgpu_compute::kernels::k19_q4k_mmv::{MmvShape, MMV_MAX_BATCH, MMV_MIN_BATCH};
    use wgpu_compute::K19Pipeline;
    let instance = wgpu::Instance::new(&wgpu::InstanceDescriptor {
        backends: wgpu::Backends::all(),
        ..Default::default()
    });
    let adapters = instance.enumerate_adapters(wgpu::Backends::all());
    let Some(adapter) = adapters.into_iter().next() else {
        eprintln!("skipping k19 compile test: wgpu enumerates no adapters here");
        return;
    };
    let info = adapter.get_info();
    let wanted = adapter.features() & (wgpu::Features::SUBGROUP | wgpu::Features::SHADER_F16);
    let (device, _queue) = pollster::block_on(adapter.request_device(&wgpu::DeviceDescriptor {
        label: Some("wgpu-compute k19 compile test"),
        required_features: wanted,
        required_limits: wgpu::Limits::default(),
        ..Default::default()
    }))
    .expect("device for k19 compile test");
    let features = device.features();
    // The shipped pipeline builds on any adapter: its
    // only workgroup memory is the reduction partials,
    // far under the default grant.
    let _pipeline = K19Pipeline::new(&device)
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("K19 pipeline must build on {}: {e}", info.name));
    eprintln!(
        "K19 shipped shader compiled on {} ({:?})",
        info.name, info.backend
    );
    // Every batch variant in the band compiles, for
    // every shape the device can run: the batch is a
    // generation literal, so each count is its own
    // module and each one is gated here, not just the
    // band floor the constructor compiles.
    for shape in [MmvShape::new(2, 128), MmvShape::new(2, 128).with_subgroup()] {
        let pipe = match K19Pipeline::with_shape(&device, shape) {
            Ok(p) => p,
            Err(e) => {
                // A refusal is only acceptable when it
                // names the feature this device was not
                // granted.
                assert!(
                    shape.subgroup && !features.contains(wgpu::Features::SUBGROUP),
                    "shape {} must build on {} with features {features:?}: {e}",
                    shape.name(),
                    info.name
                );
                eprintln!("shape {} refused as expected: {e}", shape.name());
                continue;
            }
        };
        for batch in MMV_MIN_BATCH..=MMV_MAX_BATCH {
            pipe.precompile(&device, batch).unwrap_or_else(|e| {
                panic!(
                    "k19 shape {} batch {batch} must compile on {}: {e}",
                    shape.name(),
                    info.name
                )
            });
        }
        eprintln!(
            "k19 shape {} compiled all batches {MMV_MIN_BATCH}..={MMV_MAX_BATCH} on {}",
            shape.name(),
            info.name
        );
        // Past the cap the variant request refuses by
        // name.
        let err = pipe
            .precompile(&device, MMV_MAX_BATCH + 1)
            .expect_err("batch past the cap must refuse");
        assert!(
            err.to_string().contains("outside 2..=16"),
            "refusal names the band: {err}"
        );
    }
}

/// The K21F (finish-carrying Q5_K register-streaming)
/// shaders on any adapter wgpu enumerates here: the
/// shipped pipeline builds, and every generated batch
/// variant in the band compiles for every reduction
/// shape the device can run. The finish is uniform
/// state, not a generation literal, so the variant
/// count is K21's (one per batch); what this gate adds
/// over K21's is that the finish-carrying text (the
/// params tail, the `finish_apply` prelude, the
/// wrapped stores) compiles everywhere K21's does.
#[test]
fn k21_finish_shaders_compile_on_any_available_adapter() {
    use wgpu_compute::kernels::k21_q5k_mmv::{K21Shape, MMV_MAX_BATCH, MMV_MIN_BATCH};

        backends: wgpu::Backends::all(),
        ..Default::default()
    });
    let adapters = instance.enumerate_adapters(wgpu::Backends::all());
    let Some(adapter) = adapters.into_iter().next() else {
        eprintln!("skipping k21 finish compile test: wgpu enumerates no adapters here");
        return;
    };
    let info = adapter.get_info();
    let wanted = adapter.features() & (wgpu::Features::SUBGROUP | wgpu::Features::SHADER_F16);
    let (device, _queue) = pollster::block_on(adapter.request_device(&wgpu::DeviceDescriptor {
        label: Some("wgpu-compute k21 finish compile test"),
        required_features: wanted,
        required_limits: wgpu::Limits::default(),
        ..Default::default()
    }))
    .expect("device for k21 finish compile test");
    let features = device.features();
    // The shipped pipeline builds on any adapter: its
    // only workgroup memory is the reduction partials,
    // far under the default grant.
    let _pipeline = K21FinishPipeline::new(&device)
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("K21 finish pipeline must build on {}: {e}", info.name));
    eprintln!(
        "K21 finish shipped shader compiled on {} ({:?})",
        info.name, info.backend
    );
    // Every batch variant in the band compiles, for
    // every shape the device can run.
    for shape in [K21Shape::new(2, 128), K21Shape::new(2, 128).with_subgroup()] {
        let pipe = match K21FinishPipeline::with_shape(&device, shape) {
            Ok(p) => p,

                // names the feature this device was not

        );

        // name.

            .expect_err("batch past the cap must refuse");
        assert!(
            err.to_string().contains("outside 2..=16"),
            "refusal names the band: {err}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn k22_mmq_shader_compiles_on_any_available_adapter() {
    use wgpu_compute::kernels::k22_q4k_mmq::k22_staging_bytes;
    use wgpu_compute::K22Pipeline;
    let instance = wgpu::Instance::new(&wgpu::InstanceDescriptor {
        backends: wgpu::Backends::all(),
        ..Default::default()
    });
    let adapters = instance.enumerate_adapters(wgpu::Backends::all());
    let Some(adapter) = adapters.into_iter().next() else {
        eprintln!("skipping k22 compile test: wgpu enumerates no adapters here");
        return;
    };
    let info = adapter.get_info();
    let wanted = adapter.features() & (wgpu::Features::SUBGROUP | wgpu::Features::SHADER_F16);
    // First device: the default limits, whose workgroup
    // storage grant (16 KiB) is below K22's staging set.
    // for_device must answer Ok(None) (the composition
    // fallback), and the direct constructor must refuse
    // by name: the two halves of the K13 contract.
    let (capped, _q1) = pollster::block_on(adapter.request_device(&wgpu::DeviceDescriptor {
        label: Some("wgpu-compute k22 capped test"),
        required_features: wanted,
        required_limits: wgpu::Limits::default(),
        ..Default::default()
    }))
    .expect("capped device for k22 test");
    match K22Pipeline::for_device(&capped) {
        Ok(None) => {}
        Ok(Some(_)) => panic!("k22 under default limits must be Ok(None), got a pipeline"),
        Err(e) => panic!("k22 under default limits must be Ok(None), got error: {e}"),
    }
    let err = match K22Pipeline::new(&capped) {
        Ok(_) => panic!("k22 must refuse a 16 KiB storage grant by name"),
        Err(e) => e,
    };
    assert!(
        err.to_string().contains("workgroup memory"),
        "refusal names the binding limit: {err}"
    );
    // Second device: the adapter's own limits. When the
    // grant covers the staging set the one generated
    // shader (the geometry is fixed, so there is exactly
    // one variant) must compile; for_device must agree.
    let (full, _q2) = pollster::block_on(adapter.request_device(&wgpu::DeviceDescriptor {
        label: Some("wgpu-compute k22 full test"),
        required_features: wanted,
        required_limits: adapter.limits(),
        ..Default::default()
    }))
    .expect("full-limits device for k22 test");
    let granted = full.limits().max_compute_workgroup_storage_size;
    if granted >= k22_staging_bytes() {
        let _pipeline = K22Pipeline::new(&full)
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("k22 must build on {} (grant {granted}): {e}", info.name));
        eprintln!("k22 shader compiled on {} ({:?})", info.name, info.backend);
        assert!(
            matches!(K22Pipeline::for_device(&full), Ok(Some(_))),
            "for_device must agree with the grant on {}",
            info.name
        );
    } else {
        assert!(
            matches!(K22Pipeline::for_device(&full), Ok(None)),
            "for_device must refuse cleanly under the grant on {}",
            info.name
        );
        eprintln!(
            "k22 skipped on {}: grant {granted} below its staging set",
            info.name
        );
    }
}

===== FILE: crates/wgpu-compute/tests/splitk_mmq.rs =====
//! Split-K forms of the K13/K14 MMQ products against
//! synthetic tensors with known contents
//! (bench/splitk-mmq-2026-11-07.md is the design record).
//!
//! The gate is the plain MMQ gate, unchanged: the split
//! product must match a host reference running the SAME
//! quantized math (exact integer dots plus the
//! per-sub-block scale fold) within float reassociation
//! noise, the bound `k12_k14_mmq`'s `check_close` uses.
//! The split form is not bit-identical to the unsplit
//! product by construction (the f32 accumulation is
//! regrouped: one chain per slice, then the slice sums
//! added in ascending slice order), so split-vs-unsplit
//! is gated at the same reassociation bound and the
//! measured drift is printed, not hidden.
//!
//! Shapes covered: the 256-wide KV projection shape
//! (6656 in, 256 out) that motivates the split, widths
//! whose super-block count the factor does not divide
//! (5 blocks at factor 4: ranges 2/2/1/empty), and a
//! factor past the block count (8 over 3 blocks: the
//! trailing slices are empty and must contribute exact
//! zeros). These tests need a discrete Vulkan GPU under
//! the default selection policy; on a machine without
//! one they print the refusal and pass (the VM-side
//! gates are the shader text pins and the Naga
//! validation in the kernel modules).

use wgpu_compute::kernels::k12_q8_quant::quantize_row_q8_1;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k13_q4k_mmq::{K13Pipeline, MmqShape};
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k14_q6k_mmq::K14Pipeline;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k1_q4k_gemv::K1Pipeline;
use wgpu_compute::kernels::k2_q6k_gemv::K2Pipeline;
use wgpu_compute::{WgpuCompute, WgpuError};

/// A backend, or `None` after printing why this machine cannot
/// provide one.
fn backend_or_skip() -> Option<WgpuCompute> {
    match WgpuCompute::new() {
        Ok(b) => Some(b),
        Err(WgpuError::NoSuitableAdapter { seen, .. }) => {
            eprintln!(
                "skipping GPU test: no suitable adapter (enumerated: [{}])",
                seen.join("; ")
            );
            None
        }
        Err(e) => panic!("backend construction failed unexpectedly: {e}"),
    }
}

/// Deterministic pseudo-random f32s in [-0.5, 0.5) via a 64-bit
/// LCG, matching the other kernel tests.
fn lcg_input(seed: u64, count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut state = seed.max(1);
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            ((state >> 40) as u32) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32 - 0.5
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Deterministic pseudo-random bytes via a small LCG.
fn lcg_bytes(seed: u8, count: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut state = seed;
    (0..count)
        .map(|_| {
            state = state.wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(17);
            state
        })
        .collect()
}

/// A synthetic Q4_K tensor's raw bytes (the MMQ test's
/// fixture: rotating (d, dmin) headers over LCG payloads).
fn synthetic_q4k(in_elems: usize, out_rows: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let blocks_per_row = in_elems / 256;
    let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(out_rows * blocks_per_row * 144);
    let headers: [(u16, u16); 4] = [
        (0x3c00, 0x3400),
        (0x3800, 0x0000),
        (0x4000, 0x2e66),
        (0x3e00, 0x3800),
    ];
    for row in 0..out_rows {
        for blk in 0..blocks_per_row {
            let (d, dmin) = headers[(row + blk) % headers.len()];
            let mut block = [0u8; 144];
            block[0..2].copy_from_slice(&d.to_le_bytes());
            block[2..4].copy_from_slice(&dmin.to_le_bytes());
            block[4..144].copy_from_slice(&lcg_bytes((row * 7 + blk * 13 + 5) as u8, 140)[..]);
            data.extend_from_slice(&block);
        }
    }
    data
}

/// A synthetic Q6_K tensor's raw bytes (210-byte blocks, the
/// f16 super-scale at offset 208).
fn synthetic_q6k(in_elems: usize, out_rows: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let blocks_per_row = in_elems / 256;
    let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(out_rows * blocks_per_row * 210);
    let ds: [u16; 3] = [0x3c00, 0x3800, 0x4000];
    for row in 0..out_rows {
        for blk in 0..blocks_per_row {
            let mut block = lcg_bytes((row * 11 + blk * 7 + 3) as u8, 210);
            block[208..210].copy_from_slice(&ds[(row + blk) % ds.len()].to_le_bytes());
            data.extend_from_slice(&block);
        }
    }
    data
}

/// Unpack a quantized row's words into per-element quants.
fn unpack_qs(words: &[u32]) -> Vec<i32> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(words.len() * 4);
    for w in words {
        for byte in w.to_le_bytes() {
            out.push(i32::from(byte as i8));
        }
    }
    out
}

/// ggml's `get_scale_min_k4`, mirrored from the gguf crate.
fn scale_min_k4(j: usize, scales: &[u8]) -> (u8, u8) {
    if j < 4 {
        (scales[j] & 63, scales[j + 4] & 63)
    } else {
        (
            (scales[j + 4] & 0xF) | ((scales[j - 4] >> 6) << 4),
            (scales[j + 4] >> 4) | ((scales[j] >> 6) << 4),
        )
    }
}

/// The host MMQ reference for Q4_K (the k12_k14_mmq
/// reference, mirrored): exact integer dots folded per
/// sub-block in super-block order.
fn reference_mmq_q4k(
    raw: &[u8],
    in_elems: usize,
    out_rows: usize,
    qs: &[u32],
    ds: &[f32],
    batch: usize,
) -> Vec<f32> {
    let blocks_per_row = in_elems / 256;
    let blocks32 = in_elems / 32;
    let mut out = vec![0.0f32; batch * out_rows];
    for m in 0..batch {
        let qx = unpack_qs(&qs[m * blocks32 * 8..(m + 1) * blocks32 * 8]);
        let row_ds = &ds[m * blocks32 * 4..(m + 1) * blocks32 * 4];
        for n in 0..out_rows {
            let mut acc = 0.0f32;
            for b in 0..blocks_per_row {
                let block = &raw[(n * blocks_per_row + b) * 144..][..144];
                let d = gguf::dequant::f16_to_f32(u16::from_le_bytes([block[0], block[1]]));
                let dmin = gguf::dequant::f16_to_f32(u16::from_le_bytes([block[2], block[3]]));
                let scales = &block[4..16];
                let payload = &block[16..144];
                for j in 0..8usize {
                    let (sc, mn) = scale_min_k4(j, scales);
                    let g = j / 2;
                    let hi = j % 2 == 1;
                    let mut sumi: i64 = 0;
                    for l in 0..32 {
                        let byte = payload[g * 32 + l];
                        let nib = if hi { byte >> 4 } else { byte & 0xF };
                        sumi += i64::from(nib) * i64::from(qx[b * 256 + j * 32 + l]);
                    }
                    let blk32 = b * 8 + j;
                    let (dx, s) = (row_ds[blk32 * 4], row_ds[blk32 * 4 + 1]);
                    acc += (d * f32::from(sc)) * (dx * sumi as f32) - (dmin * f32::from(mn)) * s;
                }
            }
            out[m * out_rows + n] = acc;
        }
    }
    out
}

/// The host MMQ reference for Q6_K (the k12_k14_mmq
/// reference, mirrored): exact integer dots folded per
/// 16-element half.
fn reference_mmq_q6k(
    raw: &[u8],
    in_elems: usize,
    out_rows: usize,
    qs: &[u32],
    ds: &[f32],
    batch: usize,
) -> Vec<f32> {
    let blocks_per_row = in_elems / 256;
    let blocks32 = in_elems / 32;
    let mut out = vec![0.0f32; batch * out_rows];
    for m in 0..batch {
        let qx = unpack_qs(&qs[m * blocks32 * 8..(m + 1) * blocks32 * 8]);
        let row_ds = &ds[m * blocks32 * 4..(m + 1) * blocks32 * 4];
        for n in 0..out_rows {
            let mut acc = 0.0f32;
            for b in 0..blocks_per_row {
                let block = &raw[(n * blocks_per_row + b) * 210..][..210];
                let ql = &block[0..128];
                let qh = &block[128..192];
                let sc = &block[192..208];
                let d = gguf::dequant::f16_to_f32(u16::from_le_bytes([block[208], block[209]]));
                for j in 0..8usize {
                    let h = j / 4;
                    let s = j % 4;
                    let ql_h = &ql[h * 64..h * 64 + 64];
                    let qh_h = &qh[h * 32..h * 32 + 32];
                    let mut qw = [0i64; 32];
                    for l in 0..32 {
                        qw[l] = match s {
                            0 => i64::from((ql_h[l] & 0xF) | ((qh_h[l] & 3) << 4)),
                            1 => i64::from((ql_h[l + 32] & 0xF) | (((qh_h[l] >> 2) & 3) << 4)),
                            2 => i64::from((ql_h[l] >> 4) | (((qh_h[l] >> 4) & 3) << 4)),
                            _ => i64::from((ql_h[l + 32] >> 4) | (((qh_h[l] >> 6) & 3) << 4)),
                        };
                    }
                    let blk32 = b * 8 + j;
                    let dx = row_ds[blk32 * 4];
                    for half in 0..2usize {
                        let sci = sc[h * 8 + half + 2 * s] as i8;
                        let mut sumi: i64 = 0;
                        for l in 0..16 {
                            sumi +=
                                qw[half * 16 + l] * i64::from(qx[b * 256 + j * 32 + half * 16 + l]);
                        }
                        let sh = row_ds[blk32 * 4 + 2 + half];
                        acc += (d * f32::from(sci)) * (dx * sumi as f32 - 32.0 * sh);
                    }
                }
            }
            out[m * out_rows + n] = acc;
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Assert two result sets agree within reassociation noise
/// (the MMQ gate's bound: relative to the result set's own
/// magnitude scale, plus a small floor).
fn check_close(label: &str, got: &[f32], want: &[f32]) {
    assert_eq!(got.len(), want.len(), "{label}: length mismatch");
    let scale = want.iter().fold(0.0f32, |a, w| a.max(w.abs()));
    let tol = 2e-3 + 5e-5 * scale;
    let mut max_diff = 0.0f32;
    for (i, (g, w)) in got.iter().zip(want.iter()).enumerate() {
        let diff = (g - w).abs();
        max_diff = max_diff.max(diff);
        assert!(
            diff <= tol,
            "{label}: element {i}: got {g}, want {w} (diff {diff}, tol {tol} at set scale {scale})"
        );
    }
    eprintln!(
        "{label}: max abs diff {max_diff:.3e} (set scale {scale:.3e}, rel {:.3e})",
        max_diff / scale.max(1.0)
    );
}

/// Quantize every row of `x` on the host: the reference the
/// GPU pipeline runs are checked against.
fn host_quantize(x: &[f32], width: usize) -> (Vec<u32>, Vec<f32>) {
    let mut qs = Vec::new();
    let mut ds = Vec::new();
    for row in x.chunks_exact(width) {
        let (q, d) = quantize_row_q8_1(row);
        qs.extend_from_slice(&q);
        ds.extend_from_slice(&d);
    }
    (qs, ds)
}

/// The MMQ shapes this device can build (the shipped one
/// plus the wide tile when its storage grants it).
fn shapes(backend: &WgpuCompute) -> Vec<MmqShape> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    if let Some(s) =
        wgpu_compute::kernels::k13_q4k_mmq::shipped_shape(&backend.context().device.limits())
    {
        out.push(s);
    }
    let wide = MmqShape::new(64);
    if !out.contains(&wide) && K13Pipeline::with_shape(&backend.context().device, wide).is_ok() {
        out.push(wide);
    }
    out
}

#[test]
fn k13_split_matches_quantized_reference() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    // (in, out, batch, splits): the KV projection width at
    // the model's real K length; a ragged block count the
    // factor does not divide; a factor past the block
    // count, where trailing slices are empty.
    let cases: [(usize, usize, usize, u32); 5] = [
        (6656, 256, 4, 2),
        (6656, 256, 4, 8),
        (1280, 100, 3, 4),
        (768, 96, 5, 2),
        (768, 96, 5, 8),
    ];
    for shape in shapes(&backend) {
        let mmq = K13Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape).expect("k13 pipeline builds");
        for (inn, out_rows, batch, splits) in cases {
            let bytes = synthetic_q4k(inn, out_rows);
            let k1 = K1Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k1 pipeline");
            let weights = k1
                .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q4k.split", &bytes, inn, out_rows)
                .expect("k1 upload");
            let x = lcg_input(700 + batch as u64 + splits as u64, batch * inn);
            let (qs, ds) = host_quantize(&x, inn);
            let want = reference_mmq_q4k(&bytes, inn, out_rows, &qs, &ds, batch);
            let got = mmq
                .run_split(ctx, &weights, &qs, &ds, batch as u32, splits)
                .expect("k13 split run");
            check_close(
                &format!(
                    "k13 split {} in {inn} out {out_rows} batch {batch} splits {splits}",
                    shape.name()
                ),
                &got,
                &want,
            );
            if (inn, out_rows) == (6656, 256) {
                // The drift against the unsplit product
                // itself: reassociation class, printed.
                let plain = mmq
                    .run(ctx, &weights, &qs, &ds, batch as u32)
                    .expect("k13 run");
                check_close(
                    &format!("k13 split-vs-unsplit {} splits {splits}", shape.name()),
                    &got,
                    &plain,
                );
            }
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn k14_split_matches_quantized_reference() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    // The 256-wide KV projection shape first: it is the
    // shape the split exists for (6656 in, 256 out).
    let cases: [(usize, usize, usize, u32); 5] = [
        (6656, 256, 4, 2),
        (6656, 256, 4, 4),
        (6656, 256, 4, 8),
        (768, 96, 5, 2),
        (768, 96, 5, 8),
    ];
    for shape in shapes(&backend) {
        let mmq = K14Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, shape).expect("k14 pipeline builds");
        for (inn, out_rows, batch, splits) in cases {
            let bytes = synthetic_q6k(inn, out_rows);
            let k2 = K2Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k2 pipeline");
            let weights = k2
                .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q6k.split", &bytes, inn, out_rows)
                .expect("k2 upload");
            let x = lcg_input(900 + batch as u64 + splits as u64, batch * inn);
            let (qs, ds) = host_quantize(&x, inn);
            let want = reference_mmq_q6k(&bytes, inn, out_rows, &qs, &ds, batch);
            let got = mmq
                .run_split(ctx, &weights, &qs, &ds, batch as u32, splits)
                .expect("k14 split run");
            check_close(

                    "k14 split {} in {inn} out {out_rows} batch {batch} splits {splits}",

                &want,
            );

            }
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn split_factor_refusals_are_named() {
    let Some(backend) = backend_or_skip() else {
        return;
    };
    let ctx = backend.context();
    let (inn, out_rows, batch) = (512usize, 64usize, 2usize);
    let x = lcg_input(11, batch * inn);
    let (qs, ds) = host_quantize(&x, inn);
    let bytes4 = synthetic_q4k(inn, out_rows);
    let k1 = K1Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k1 pipeline");
    let w4 = k1
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q4k.refuse", &bytes4, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k1 upload");
    let mmq13 = K13Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, MmqShape::new(64)).expect("k13 builds");
    // A split of 1 is the unsplit product, 0 is nonsense,
    // and 9 is past the shared ceiling: all refuse.
    for splits in [0u32, 1, 9] {
        assert!(
            mmq13
                .run_split(ctx, &w4, &qs, &ds, batch as u32, splits)
                .is_err(),
            "k13 splits {splits} must refuse"
        );
    }
    let bytes6 = synthetic_q6k(inn, out_rows);
    let k2 = K2Pipeline::new(&ctx.device).expect("k2 pipeline");
    let w6 = k2
        .upload(ctx, "synthetic.q6k.refuse", &bytes6, inn, out_rows)
        .expect("k2 upload");
    let mmq14 = K14Pipeline::with_shape(&ctx.device, MmqShape::new(64)).expect("k14 builds");
    for splits in [0u32, 1, 9] {
        assert!(
            mmq14
                .run_split(ctx, &w6, &qs, &ds, batch as u32, splits)
                .is_err(),
            "k14 splits {splits} must refuse"
        );
    }
}

# cargo-deny policy for the iTaK Torch rebuild workspace.
# Written for the Wave 2 record lane (panel finding: cargo deny advisories
# and licenses FAIL with no deny.toml in the tree). Run with: cargo deny check

[advisories]
# paste 1.0.15 carries RUSTSEC-2024-0436 (unmaintained, not a soundness or
# vulnerability advisory). It is a proc-macro crate pulled in only by the
# metal crate on wgpu-hal's Apple target path (cargo tree --target all -i
# paste). It is never compiled for the Linux targets this project builds
# and ships. Removing it would require forking wgpu-hal's dependency set,
# so the advisory is ignored here with this justification instead.
ignore = [
    { id = "RUSTSEC-2024-0436", reason = "paste is an Apple-target-only proc-macro via wgpu-hal/metal; never compiled on Linux; unmaintained class only" },
]

[licenses]
# Exactly the license families the crates in this tree declare, read from
# cargo metadata: MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, CC0-1.0, ISC,
# Unicode-3.0, Unlicense, Zlib. All permissive; nothing copyleft.
allow = [
    "MIT",
    "Apache-2.0",
    "BSD-2-Clause",
    "CC0-1.0",
    "ISC",
    "Unicode-3.0",
    "Unlicense",
    "Zlib",
]

[bans]
multiple-versions = "warn"
# "warn", not "deny": every wildcard-class entry in this tree is a
# workspace-internal path dependency (this repo's own crates, which carry
# no version field by design). cargo-deny only exempts path dependencies
# for crates marked publish = false (allow-wildcard-paths), and these
# crates are not so marked. All registry dependencies carry explicit
# version requirements; if a true registry wildcard ever appears it will
# surface here as a warning to be fixed.
wildcards = "warn"

[sources]
unknown-registry = "deny"
unknown-git = "deny"
allow-registry = ["https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"]

# MAP: iTaK Torch Rebuild

The full relational diagram for this repo lives in
docs/relational-map/: INVENTORY.md (every node, its state, what it
owns, its source file), NODES.md and WIRES.md (the node and wire
tables), and DIAGRAM.md (the Mermaid diagrams). This page is the
short summary and the pointer. The detail lives there, not here.

State key: LIVE means code exists and does the job. LIVE, paused
means the line is paused by David's 2026-11-07 order and kept as
the parity scorekeeper. (planned) means a doc names it and no code
exists yet. The full map counts 72 nodes and 100 wires at the
2026-11-18 build (branch head b5522f2).

## The grid (summary by area)

| Area | Kind | Owns |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Mojo engine (LIVE) | engine | The current engine, in mojo-engine/: GGUF loader, tokenizer, KV cache, attention, ops, GPU kernels, GPU runtime, the Glimmer forward (CPU and GPU), the generation loop with the greedy sampler, and the runner entry points. Version 1.07. |
| Mojo serve and test bench (LIVE) | service, page | The Mojo only in-process HTTP API (mojo-engine/src/serve/): chat completions, model fact sheets, run history with hash chained records, the leaderboard, the debug log feed, the MCP style bridge, the OpenAPI contract, and the dashboard page that builds itself from those feeds. |
| Rust workspace (LIVE, paused) | engine | The 13 crates in crates/: itak-engine (the serving binary), the seam protocol, gguf, tokenizer, torch-math, attention, muse-glimmer, arch-llama, itak-loader, cpu-compute, wgpu-compute, dflash, itak-kv, itak-spec. |
| Go platform (LIVE, paused) | service | The front door, in platform/: cmd/torchd plus internal packages auth, cache, chattemplate, diag, engine (socket client), scheduler, server (HTTP routes and SSE), supervisor (engine lifecycle). |
| Support records (LIVE) | records | bench/ (101 dated notes; every speed claim ties to one), golden/ (the golden token records both lines are checked against), and the planning docs (PLAN.md, TODO.md, mojo-engine/DESIGN.md). |
| Planned work (planned) | modules | Wave F1-B striping and fusions, Wave F2 WMMA prefill, the full sampler family, the Qwen3.5 port, the vision generation path, streaming chat, the Mojo speculative wave, itak-core, itak-types, itak-ssm, itak-moe, itak-train, itak-dissect, advanced KV tiers, more backends, and the Go platform Phase 6 expansion. Each one is a named node in docs/relational-map/. |
| External | external | The client, the RX 7900 XTX server, the model files, the model registries, llama.cpp (the reference both engines are benchmarked against), the original Torch repos, and the GOAgent repo. |

Two absences the full map names plainly: there is no CI in this
tree yet, and the Go platform has no database (all of its state is
in memory).

## Links (summary)

The full wire table (100 wires, each with its backlink) is
docs/relational-map/WIRES.md. The load bearing wires:

- Client calls both front doors: the Go platform (paused line) and
  the Mojo serve API (live line).
- Go platform reaches the Rust engine only through the seam: NDJSON
  over a unix socket, with the supervisor owning the engine process.
- The Rust engine binary runs on cpu-compute only. wgpu-compute,
  itak-spec, and itak-kv hang off the bench and session paths, not
  the serving binary. The Cargo manifests say so.
- The Mojo runner drives the model through the ForwardModel trait;
  the serve loop and the CLI runner share the same generation loop,
  tokenizer, and loader.
- Both engine lines read the same model files and are verified
  against the same golden records, and both are benchmarked against
  llama.cpp on the same card.

## Diagram

The per-area diagrams are in docs/relational-map/DIAGRAM.md. This
overview matches them.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  C[Client] --> P[Go platform - paused]
  C --> S[Mojo serve API - LIVE]
  P --> SEAM[The seam]
  SEAM --> ENG[itak-engine - paused]
  ENG --> CPU[cpu-compute]
  S --> RUN[Mojo runner]
  RUN --> MODEL[Mojo model forward]
  MODEL --> GPU[Mojo gpu runtime]
  GPU --> CARD[RX 7900 XTX server]
  ENG -. bench path .-> WGPU[wgpu-compute]
  WGPU --> CARD
  GOLD[golden records] -. verifies .-> ENG
  GOLD -. verifies .-> MODEL
```

## Flows

1. **A chat request on the live (Mojo) line.** The client calls the
   serve API inside the Mojo engine process. The request is checked
   against the serve limits in config (greedy only today; anything
   else is refused by name), the prompt is tokenized with the
   model's own tokenizer, and the generation loop runs the Glimmer
   forward on the GPU runtime. The reply carries the run's speed
   and token counts, and the run is written to the hash chained
   history that the dashboard and leaderboard read.
2. **A chat request on the paused (Rust and Go) line.** The client
   calls the Go platform. The platform authenticates, checks the
   response cache, renders the chat template from the model's own
   GGUF template, and schedules the request. The request crosses
   the seam as a generate op; the Rust engine tokenizes, loads
   weights through itak-loader behind the coverage gate, and runs
   the muse-glimmer forward on cpu-compute. Token frames stream
   back over the socket and out to the client as SSE.
3. **A model arrives.** At engine start, each line's loader parses
   the GGUF file and refuses the model by name if any expected
   tensor is missing, so a model that does not load completely
   never serves. The Mojo fact sheets describe a file (family,
   layer split, vision proof) even for a family whose generation
   has not landed yet; the Qwen3.5 vision file is the standing
   example, and its images are refused by name until the vision
   path is built.

# RULES: how this project gets built

The build law for this repo, in one page. These rules come from David
Patton and apply to every module, every language, every time.

## Modularity: the grid and the tiles
- The main program or page is a GRID. Every section is a MODULE plugged
  into a grid slot: header, footer, each content block, each tile.
  Modular to the full max, never partial.
- Every feature is its own isolated module with a defined interface.
  One feature, one module, one commit, one push.
- Modules are independently replaceable and updatable on the fly. A
  broken module gets fixed or swapped alone; the system never rebuilds
  around it.

## Build 20 years ahead
- Design for the bottleneck that is COMING, not just today's.
- Interface seams at every change-prone boundary: model providers,
  executors, verifiers, storage, transports.
- Operational limits (timeouts, caps, retry counts, quotas) are config
  with sane defaults, never constants compiled into logic.
- Data formats carry version fields so future versions read today's data.

## Debugging and linting, in every module, from birth
- They are not the same thing. Linting reads the code for mistakes
  without running it. Debugging is finding out why the program
  misbehaved when it ran, backed by diagnostics built into the module.
- Every module ships with BOTH: structured diagnostics, a way to pull
  the bug information out, and lint gates that run clean. A module that
  cannot say what it did and why it refused is not done.

## Check the shelf before building
- Before building anything, check the take-shelf
  (~/workspace/google-org-harvest/USE-IT.md) and the wider harvest: if
  Google or another trusted source already built it under a usable
  license, take it or retrofit it. Rebuilding what exists is waste.
- For any new market or feature area, research the top 10 competitors
  (the customer's list and the platform's list) before designing.

## Security
- No secrets in the repo, ever: keys, tokens, and passwords live in
  secure storage only. Secret scanning (gitleaks or betterleaks) in
  the commit gates is the target state, not yet landed: the gate
  script is TODO T-1.5, still open, and no gate script or CI exists
  in the tree today. Until it lands, the rule is the first sentence,
  enforced by review.
- Every refusal, overage, and verdict emits through the project's
  diagnostic channel. Nothing fails silently.
- Untrusted input gets a bounded parser, not trust; the bounded
  parsers exist and are tested. A fuzz target for each one is the
  target state, not yet landed: no fuzz target exists in the tree
  today, and the gate work that would run them is TODO T-1.7,
  still open.

## Verification
- Done means proven: a test with asserted values, a log line, a bench
  note, or a live check. "It compiles" is not proof.
- Never blindly trust delegated work; re-run the gates before merging.
- Emulation-proven is not bench-proven; label which one a claim is.

## Writing
- Plain, direct, technical. No em dashes in prose, docs, or code.
- Brand casing is exact: AlphaVision, AlphaFlux, iTaK, Mimir,
  Patriot Pest Control (full name wherever there are words).
- Project docs: TODO.md tracks the work, PLAN.md holds the plan,
  IDEA.md holds David's ideas in his words.

## Project specifics

- **No garbage-collected language inside the token loop.** The engine
  crates allocate once and pool. A change that allocates per token is a
  design defect, not a style issue, and the allocation counter test in
  TODO T-2.4 is its gate.
- **Contracts are published and versioned.** Shared types live in
  itak-core (Go) and itak-types (Rust), both versioned artifacts with
  version fields in the data. Relative-path module references are
  forbidden; that is the failure that killed the original engine.
- **Benchmarks are claimed only from real hardware.** Emulation, other
  people's cards, and vendor numbers are labelled as such wherever they
  appear. This project's numbers come from the RX 7900 XTX record in
  docs/research/ or they do not appear.
- **Experiments behind flags, off by default.** Mamba-3 mode,
  cache-aware MoE routing, and linear-attention swaps enter as config
  flags and earn defaults only with proof filed in this repo
  (DECISIONS.md records the promotion).
- **Weights never on the root disk.** Model files live on the large
  array on the home server; see DECISIONS.md 2026-10-27.
- **The server never reboots for this project.** Any step that appears
  to need one stops and is reported instead (see docs/RUNBOOK.md).

### Relational diagram

- This project always has a relational diagram: the whole system as
  nodes and wires, every module and how it connects, each node
  marked LIVE, PLANNED, or ABSENT with its source file, built from
  the code. It lives in this repo under docs/relational-map/, and
  docs/MAP.md points at it.
- The diagram is updated after every build unit and after any
  change to any part of the project, in the same push cycle as the
  change itself. A unit is not fully landed until the diagram
  matches it.

# RUNBOOK: iTaK Torch Rebuild

## Build

Toolchains are pinned: `rust-toolchain.toml` at the repo root (rust 1.99.1) and the platform's `go.mod` toolchain line (go1.26.10). Build both halves from the repo root:

```bash
# Rust workspace: the engine binary plus the twelve library crates
cargo build --release -p itak-engine

# Go platform: the torchd daemon
(cd platform && go build -o torchd ./cmd/torchd)
```

## Run locally

The pair serves as two processes meeting on a Unix socket. Either start the engine by hand and point the platform at its socket, or let torchd supervise the engine. The full operator walkthrough is in SERVING.md; the short form:

```bash
# Engine by hand (loads the model; ready when the log says "serving on ...")
./target/release/itak-engine \
  --model /path/to/model.gguf \
  --socket /tmp/itak-engine.sock

# Platform against the socket (binds 127.0.0.1:8091)
TORCH_API_KEY=<your-key> ./platform/torchd \
  -engine-socket /tmp/itak-engine.sock -models glimmer
```

Engine flags, each with an `ITAK_ENGINE_*` environment twin; nothing is compiled in:

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `--model` | (required) | GGUF file to load |
| `--socket` | `/tmp/itak-engine.sock` | Unix socket to bind; created owner-only (0600) |
| `--model-name` | file metadata name, else file stem | Name requests must address |
| `--default-max-tokens` | 128 | Generation cap when a request omits `max_tokens` |
| `--slots` | 1 | Concurrent generations, each with its own compute and KV state |
| `--max-queued` | 8 | Jobs that may wait for a slot; past capacity refuses as `engine_busy` |
| `--max-frame-bytes` | 4194304 | Largest single NDJSON frame the engine accepts |
| `--max-embed-inputs` | 256 | Largest embed batch in one request |
| `--max-embed-tokens` | 8192 | Largest token count in one embed input |
| `--log-content` | off | Also log prompt ids and generated text; counts and timings only by default |

The socket refuses what it should: a first frame that is not a hello, a peer running under a different uid, an oversized or unterminated frame, and JSON nested past the parser's depth cap all get named refusals, and the engine never deletes a non-socket file found at the socket path.

torchd flags (the serving-relevant set; `torchd -h` prints them all): `-addr` (127.0.0.1:8091), `-engine-socket`, `-engine-bin` with `-engine-model` and `-engine-name` for supervised mode, `-engine-slots`, `-engine-max-queued`, `-engine-max-restarts` (5) and `-engine-restart-window` (5m) for the restart budget, `-models`, `-max-concurrent` (4), `-max-tokens` (8192 platform cap), `-generation-timeout` (1h), `-max-body-bytes` (1 MiB), `-read-header-timeout` (10s), `-idle-timeout` (90s), `-max-waiters-per-lane` (128), `-cache-ttl` (5m), `-cache-max-entries` (1024), `-cache-purge-interval` (1m). The daemon refuses to start without `TORCH_API_KEY` (minimum 16 characters) unless `TORCH_ALLOW_NO_AUTH=1` is set deliberately.

Expected: an authenticated chat completion streams or returns from the engine; without the key, 401; with no engine configured, engine routes answer 503 `engine_unavailable`. The recorded smoke transcript is bench/serving-smoke-2026-10-30.md.

Diagnostics switches. Every crate ships a diagnostic seam (the build law: debugging in every module from birth). The `*_DEBUG` switches share one shape, the gguf shape: the variable enables the seam when present with any value other than `0` or empty, checked on every call, so any binary linking the crate (the engine included) can be switched on with no rebuild and no code change. All default to off, and the off path is unchanged behavior. Refusals in gguf emit whether or not its switch is on.

| Variable | Owner module | Default | Effect |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `GGUF_DEBUG` | gguf | off | `[gguf][debug]` parse and load lines (errors emit unconditionally) |
| `ITAK_LOADER_DEBUG` | itak-loader | off | `[itak-loader][debug]` loader bridge lines: config loads, coverage verdicts, coercion refusals |
| `ATTENTION_DEBUG` | attention | off | `[attention::diag]` KV cache and attention lines |
| `CPU_COMPUTE_DEBUG` | cpu-compute | off | `[cpu-compute]` backend lines: KV construction, attention positions, resets |
| `WGPU_COMPUTE_DEBUG` | wgpu-compute | off | `[wgpu-compute]` backend lines: adapter selection, uploads, dispatches |
| `TORCH_MATH_DEBUG` | torch-math | off | `[torch-math]` reference-math operation and shape lines |
| `ITAK_KV_DEBUG` | itak-kv | off | `[itak-kv::diag]` prefix-KV store lines |
| `TOKENIZER_DEBUG` | tokenizer | off | `[tokenizer]` load, fallback, and refusal lines |
| `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG` | wgpu-compute | `off` | Per-dispatch kernel timing (`timing`) or timing plus run capture (`capture`); a separate system from `WGPU_COMPUTE_DEBUG`. `WGPU_COMPUTE_DIAG_OUT` names the capture output file |
| `ITAK_KV_PREFIX_STORE` | itak-kv | off | Master switch for the prefix-KV store; `ITAK_KV_PREFIX_DIR` sets its root, `ITAK_KV_PREFIX_MAX_BYTES` its byte cap |
| `TORCH_LOG_LEVEL` | platform (torchd) | `info` | Platform log verbosity: `debug`, `info`, `warn`, or `error` |

One reach limit, stated plainly: a torchd-supervised engine child receives an allowlisted environment (PATH plus `ITAK_ENGINE_*` only, supervisor's `childEnv`), so the switches above reach a hand-run engine today but not a supervised one. Extending that allowlist is tracked follow-up work, not a silent gap.
## Deploy

There is no automated deploy for this stack, and production Glimmer serving is down on the owner's explicit order until the engine work is finished; it stays down. Nothing in this repo restarts it. When serving is approved, a deploy is: build both binaries on the target host, start the engine (by hand or supervised by torchd), and run the Verify section against it. Rollback is the previous release binaries, or `git revert` and a rebuild; the pair holds no state that a rollback can strand (the response cache is in-memory, engine state is per-process).

## Verify

The gates, as plain commands (do not invent gate scripts; the one exception is `bench/gate.sh`, below):

```bash
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo deny check
(cd platform && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... && govulncheck ./...)
```

The Rust test suite has one scripted wrapper: `bench/gate.sh` runs `cargo test --workspace` (the first command above) with per-test output captured, and prints a summary line counting passed, failed, and ignored tests plus both skip counts: adapter skips (tests that passed vacuously because no qualifying GPU adapter is present) and other skips (named exceptions, counted but never gated). It fails the gate when any test fails, and on a machine with a qualifying adapter it also fails when any adapter skip occurs; on an adapterless machine the adapter skips are expected and reported beside the pass count, with a printed note when their number drifts from the enumerated expectation in the script's header. The remaining gates stay plain commands, run beside the wrapper, not through it.

Under the pinned go1.26.10 toolchain, govulncheck reports no vulnerabilities in the platform (this closes the panel's GO-2026-6809 finding, which was a standard library advisory against the older toolchain). After a serving change, repeat the smoke from SERVING.md and compare against bench/serving-smoke-2026-10-30.md. Benchmarks: compare new runs against docs/research/2026-10-26-glimmer-7900xtx-benchmarks.md and the bench/ notes for the same harness shape; anchors are harness-relative (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30), so a result more than a few percent off the recorded numbers for the same harness is a finding, not a rounding error. Accuracy: bench/accuracy-prompts.md at temp 0; empty content means the reasoning default trap is back.

## Where things live

- Home server: reached over Tailscale by its SSH config alias (ts-server). It runs Dokploy and live business sites; treat it as production at all times. The server is never rebooted on an agent's call.
- Model weights: on the server at /mnt/models/ (the 2TB Kioxia NVMe). The Glimmer file set lives in /mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/ (the Q4_K_M target, its mmproj, and the DFlash draft). The weights were never deleted. Never put model-sized files on the root disk.
- Reference stack on the server: llama.cpp trees build-vulkan (the reference serving path) and build-rocm. The server runs the Ubuntu native ROCm 7.1 stack; llama.cpp works on both Vulkan and HIP there, and Vulkan is the serving pick on the RX 7900 XTX (HIP wins prompt processing, Vulkan wins decode).
- The original engine: GitHub repos David2024patton/iTaKTorchQ4 (public) and itak-torch (private twin), plus the GOAgent repo, which still hosts the pkg/debug and pkg/eventbus ancestors Phase 1 ports from.
- Credentials: GitHub access goes through the stored custom.github connector credential. No credential value appears in this repo, ever.

## Gotchas

- **ROCm was broken, and is fixed; do not re-litigate it.** The 2026-10-26 symptom set (HIP loads, then spins at 0% GPU busy) traced to a mixed-version ROCm userland. The fix landed 2026-10-28: a single Ubuntu native ROCm 7.1 stack, proven from hello-world to a full 30B bench (STATUS.md; TODO T-P.2). Vulkan remains the serving pick on this card on decode speed, not because HIP is broken.
- **Total context is split across slots in the reference stack.** llama-server with -c 131072 and -np 4 gives each slot 32768 tokens. A poisoned oversized request can leave its slot failing with context-size errors until eviction; do not read that as a model fault.
- **Reasoning models eat the budget by default.** At default reasoning strength, Glimmer spent the entire 512-token cap thinking and returned empty content on code and logic prompts. Inject reasoning_strength low (chat template kwargs) at the proxy by default.
- **Never strip special tokens.** The model's channel protocol rides on its special tokens; a proxy that strips them collapses reasoning, tool calls, and replies into one mangled stream. Always run llama-server with --jinja, and the rebuild's own template renderer keeps them by construction.
- **Root disk discipline.** Model-sized files on the root NVMe filled the disk on 2026-10-27 and took Dokploy down. Weights go on the models drive, full stop.
- **A dead engine under supervision stays down when the budget is spent.** torchd restarts a crashed engine within its restart budget (default 5 restarts per 5 minutes). A model that can no longer load exhausts the budget and stays down, visibly, in /debug under engine_debug.supervisor; that is the designed behavior, not a hang.
- **The supervisor's child gets an allowlisted environment.** torchd passes the engine only PATH and ITAK_ENGINE_* variables. If a supervised engine seems to miss a setting, check the name is an ITAK_ENGINE_* twin before suspecting the flag wiring.

# Relational map: inventory

This is the full inventory for the relational diagram of this repo.
Built from the code at branch head b5522f2 (mojo-max-engine) on
2026-11-18. Code beats paper: every LIVE node below was read in the
tree at that head, and every PLANNED or ABSENT node names the doc or
comment that promises it.

Companion files in this folder:

- NODES.md: the compact node table (id, name, kind, state).
- WIRES.md: the connection table (from, to, kind, backlink).
- DIAGRAM.md: Mermaid diagrams of the same nodes and wires (one
  overview plus one diagram per area).

## State legend

- LIVE: code exists in the tree and does the job named.
- LIVE, paused: code exists and works, but the line is paused by
  David's 2026-11-07 order. The Rust workspace and the Go platform
  are the parity scorekeeper now, not the product line. They are
  kept, not deleted.
- PLANNED: a doc in this repo names it and no code exists yet.
- ABSENT: something in the repo speaks of it as if it were there
  (a target state, a comment, a rule), and it is not in the tree.

## External nodes

| ID | Node | Kind | State | Owns | Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| EXT-CLIENT | Client | external | LIVE | Sends requests to whichever front door is up; owns nothing here. | n/a |
| EXT-SERVER | RX 7900 XTX server | external | LIVE | The home server and its 24 GB card; all performance claims are measured here. | docs/research/, bench/ |
| EXT-MODELS | Model files | external | LIVE | The GGUF model files on the server array (Glimmer Q4_K_M, its DFlash draft, the staged Qwen3.5 vision file, others). | /mnt/models on the server (not in repo) |
| EXT-REG | Model registries | external | LIVE | HuggingFace and OCI: where model pulls would come from. | PLAN.md S9 |
| EXT-LLAMA | llama.cpp | external | LIVE | The reference implementation both engines are benchmarked against. Never the product. | bench/ |
| EXT-ORIG | Original Torch repos | external | LIVE | iTaKTorchQ4 and itak-torch on GitHub: reference implementation and feature specification for the rebuild. | README.md, SALVAGE.md |
| EXT-GOAGENT | GOAgent repo | external | LIVE | Hosts the surviving pkg/debug and pkg/event ancestors that itak-core ports from. | PLAN.md S4 |

## Rust workspace (paused line)

| ID | Node | Kind | State | Owns | Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| RS-ROOT | Cargo workspace root | workspace | LIVE, paused | The 13 crate members, shared package settings, workspace lint gates (warnings and clippy denied). | Cargo.toml |
| RS-ENGINE | itak-engine | binary crate | LIVE, paused | The Rust engine binary: one loaded model on worker threads, generation slots, a bounded queue, and the socket server. Submodules: engine (load and workers), protocol, json, sampler, streamer, diag. | crates/itak-engine/src/ |
| RS-SEAM | The seam | module | LIVE, paused | The NDJSON over unix socket protocol, defined once: six ops (hello, ping, debug, generate, embed, chat_template), streamed token frames, named errors. Socket is owner only (0600) with a peer uid check. | crates/itak-engine/src/protocol.rs, platform/internal/engine/ |
| RS-GGUF | gguf | library crate | LIVE, paused | Strict GGUF v3 loader: header, metadata, tensor directory, mmap file image, f32 dequantization, fail loud named errors. | crates/gguf/src/ |
| RS-TOK | tokenizer | library crate | LIVE, paused | Byte level BPE and SentencePiece BPE over the model's own GGUF vocabulary, merges, and scores: encode, decode, round trip. | crates/tokenizer/src/ |
| RS-MATH | torch-math | library crate | LIVE, paused | Reference f32 math: RMSNorm, RoPE, gated FFN activations, logit softcap and scale, matmul and matvec. Every constant is a parameter. Dependency free by design. | crates/torch-math/src/ |
| RS-ATTN | attention | library crate | LIVE, paused | The KvCache (global layers plus sliding window ring layers, checkpoint and restore) and grouped query attention reference math. | crates/attention/src/ |
| RS-GLIMMER | muse-glimmer | library crate | LIVE, paused | The Muse Glimmer architecture: config from GGUF metadata, the measured weight layout (14 tensors per layer), the structured forward for the 52 layer hybrid (39 sliding window plus 13 global). Compute and KV storage sit behind traits it owns. | crates/muse-glimmer/src/ |
| RS-ARCH | arch-llama | library crate | LIVE, paused | Generic dense architecture for the llama and qwen2 families: pre-norm, RoPE, GQA with KV cache, SwiGLU; config and weights from GGUF metadata. | crates/arch-llama/src/ |
| RS-LOADER | itak-loader | library crate | LIVE, paused | The loader bridge: implements the muse-glimmer and dflash Metadata and TensorSource traits over the gguf crate, and verifies a file's tensor inventory against expected names (the coverage gate). | crates/itak-loader/src/ |
| RS-CPU | cpu-compute | library crate | LIVE, paused | The CPU reference Compute backend: real f32 arithmetic via torch-math, dequantization via gguf, KV storage via attention. This is the backend the Rust serving engine runs. | crates/cpu-compute/src/ |
| RS-WGPU | wgpu-compute | library crate | LIVE, paused | The wgpu (Vulkan) Compute backend: kernels K1 through K24 plus the split-K reducer and cooperative matrix variants, the device resident forward session, and the DFlash session. Proven against the golden as a bench; not wired into the itak-engine binary. | crates/wgpu-compute/src/ |
| RS-DFLASH | dflash | library crate | LIVE, paused | The DFlash draft architecture: config from the draft file's own metadata, conditioning fused from named target layer inputs, non-causal block forward producing per position draft logits. | crates/dflash/src/ |
| RS-KV | itak-kv | library crate | LIVE, paused | The persistent tiered prefix KV store: versioned KV snapshots keyed by token prefix, verified token for token on load, written atomically, LRU bounded by bytes. | crates/itak-kv/src/ |
| RS-SPEC | itak-spec | library crate | LIVE, paused | The speculative decoding loop: DFlash block drafting against the target, exact output verification, KV checkpoint and rewind, rejection sampling, plus an n-gram proposer. Proven token identical on CPU; not in the serving path. | crates/itak-spec/src/ |

## Mojo engine (the live line)

Engine version 1.07 (mojo-engine/src/config.mojo). One Mojo source,
compiled per target chip. Toolchain pinned: Mojo 1.2.0, MAX 26.7
(mojo-engine/pixi.toml).

| ID | Node | Kind | State | Owns | Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| MJ-MAIN | main.mojo entry | module | LIVE | The bare entry point: prints the engine name and version, loads config, reports loader state, refuses cleanly by name on error. Generation and serving live in the runner. | mojo-engine/src/main.mojo |
| MJ-CONFIG | config | module | LIVE | EngineConfig: every limit in one place as env overridable defaults (model path, context length 131072, GPU budget, attention tile and split sizes, prefill thresholds, serve host and port 127.0.0.1:18767, attachment caps). Bad values refused by name. | mojo-engine/src/config.mojo |
| MJ-DIAG | diag seam | module | LIVE | The debug seam: MOJO_ENGINE_DEBUG consulted per call, named phase lines out. Imported by nearly every module in the engine. | mojo-engine/src/diag.mojo |
| MJ-GGUF | gguf loader (Mojo) | module | LIVE | GGUF loader: header, metadata, tensor directory, staged tensor reads. | mojo-engine/src/gguf/loader.mojo |
| MJ-TOK | tokenizer (Mojo) | module | LIVE | Byte level BPE and SentencePiece BPE selected by GGUF metadata: byte map, pre-tokenizer, SPM encoder, encode and decode. | mojo-engine/src/tokenizer/ |
| MJ-KV | kv cache (Mojo) | module | LIVE | CPU KV cache: per layer flat f32 K and V stores, the Glimmer layer pattern (sliding ring versus global), append and visible range reads. | mojo-engine/src/kv/cache.mojo |
| MJ-ATTN | attention (Mojo) | module | LIVE | Grouped query attention: single position CPU twin and GPU kernel, prefill loop, tiled and split-KV GPU path with exact merge. | mojo-engine/src/attention/attention.mojo |
| MJ-OPS | ops | module | LIVE | Row and elementwise ops, CPU and GPU: embedding gather, RMSNorm, RoPE, softmax, SwiGLU, residual add, final logit transform, device embedding. | mojo-engine/src/ops/ |
| MJ-KERNELS | kernels | module | LIVE | GPU kernels, one module per kernel: shared dequant, F32 and F16 GEMV, batched prefill GEMM, K1 Q4_K GEMV, Q5_K GEMV, Q6_K GEMV, each with a CPU twin. | mojo-engine/src/kernels/ |
| MJ-GPU | gpu runtime | module | LIVE | MAX device plumbing: GpuRuntime and the memory budget ledger, device resident weights (one buffer per tensor slot), device KV cache, and the Wave F scratch pool that recycles step buffers. | mojo-engine/src/gpu/ |
| MJ-MODEL | model forward | module | LIVE | The Glimmer transformer forward: CPU forward with ModelConfig from GGUF, and the GPU twin (GpuGlimmerModel, single position layer assembly, batched prefill layer assembly, step level activation residency from Wave F1-A). | mojo-engine/src/model/ |
| MJ-GEN | generate and sampler | module | LIVE | The generation loop behind the ForwardModel trait (prefill, step, logits), the resident device loop from Wave F1-A, and the greedy sampler. Greedy only today; see PL-SAMPLER. | mojo-engine/src/generate/ |
| MJ-RUNNER | runner entry points | module | LIVE | The two end to end entry points: the CLI generation runner over a real model file, and the serve accept loop (dispatch, generation wiring, MCP bridge dispatch, run ingest). | mojo-engine/src/runner/ |
| MJ-SERVE | serve API | module | LIVE | The Mojo only in-process HTTP API: POSIX socket transport through libc, HTTP parse and route, a minimal JSON dialect, pure dispatch, and the static OpenAPI contract at /openapi.json. Routes include /health, /v1/models, /v1/chat/completions, /stats, /debug/log, /history, /leaderboard, and the /mcp bridge. Non-streaming in v1. | mojo-engine/src/serve/ (http, server, socket, json, openapi) |
| MJ-DASH | dashboard page | page | LIVE | The test bench dashboard: one inline HTML and JS page built inside dashboard.mojo (no static files exist), served at GET /. Chat, debug log, model fact sheets, leaderboard, run history, and stats as tiles. It builds itself from the JSON feeds. | mojo-engine/src/serve/dashboard.mojo |
| MJ-FACT | fact sheets | module | LIVE | Per model GGUF fact sheets: family, layer split (sliding versus global, from metadata and tensor signatures), vision proof three ways, served at /v1/models and /v1/models/{id}. | mojo-engine/src/serve/factsheet.mojo |
| MJ-HIST | history and stats | module | LIVE | Run records (hash chained, record_sha256 per record), run history on disk, the leaderboard view, export and ingest of run bundles, and the in-memory stats plus debug ring behind /stats and /debug/log. | mojo-engine/src/serve/history.mojo, mojo-engine/src/serve/stats.mojo |
| MJ-TESTS | Mojo tests and proofs | tests | LIVE | The test bench gate: unit suites under tests/test_*.mojo run by tests/run_tests.sh (200 tests passing at this head), GPU proofs, and server card proof programs. Poison (negative control) gates live here too. | mojo-engine/tests/ |

## Drift found while building this map (old MAP.md against the code)

1. The old docs/MAP.md had no node for the Mojo engine at all. Its
   only Mojo entry was an external "Mojo lab" node that prototypes
   supposedly graduate from. The Mojo work is in this repo, in
   mojo-engine/, and it is the live line. Fixed by this map and by
   the MAP.md rewrite in the same landing.
2. mojo-engine/README.md carries a "Deliberately not built yet" list
   (GGUF loader, kernels past K1, attention, generation loop,
   sampler, serving front end). Every item on that list is built and
   in the tree. The README is stale; the code and DESIGN.md agree
   with each other, not with the README. Not fixed here (docs-only
   map landing); named so the next README pass can close it.
3. The old MAP.md grid said the Go platform pulls models from the
   registries. The Go tree has no outbound HTTP and no pull code;
   model operations are Phase 6 plan items. This map marks that
   wire PLANNED (see WIRES.md).
4. docs/RULES.md speaks of itak-types (Rust) as the contracts home
   in the present tense. No such crate exists; TODO T-1.4 still
   lists it. This map marks it PLANNED.
5. The old MAP.md said itak-kv is consumed by the wgpu resident
   session, which is right, but the engine binary itself has no
   itak-kv, itak-spec, wgpu-compute, or arch-llama dependency at
   all: the Rust serving path is CPU only. The wires in WIRES.md
   follow the Cargo manifests, not the old prose.

# Relational map: nodes

Compact node table for the relational diagram. The full inventory
(what each node owns, and its source file) is INVENTORY.md in this
folder. The connections are WIRES.md. The pictures are DIAGRAM.md.

Built from the code at branch head b5522f2 (mojo-max-engine),
2026-11-18.

State key: LIVE means code exists and does the job. LIVE, paused
means code exists on a line paused by David's 2026-11-07 order
(the Rust and Go trees are the parity scorekeeper). PLANNED means
a doc names it and no code exists. ABSENT means the repo speaks
of it as if present and it is not in the tree.

===== FILE: docs/relational-map/WIRES.md =====
# Relational map: wires

Every connection between the nodes in NODES.md, traced both ways:
the wire itself, and the backlink (the reverse relationship, named,
or "none"). Built from the code at branch head b5522f2
(mojo-max-engine), 2026-11-18: Cargo manifests for the Rust wires,
imports for the Go and Mojo wires.

Wires to or from PLANNED and ABSENT nodes are marked in the Kind
column. They describe the shape the plan promises, not code that
runs today.

## Rust workspace wires

| ID | From | To | Kind | Backlink |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| W01 | RS-ENGINE | RS-SEAM | hosts (serves the protocol on the socket) | RS-SEAM is served by RS-ENGINE |
| W02 | RS-ENGINE | RS-GGUF | calls (parse and dequantize) | RS-GGUF hands parsed files to RS-ENGINE |
| W03 | RS-ENGINE | RS-TOK | calls (encode and decode) | RS-TOK tokenizes for RS-ENGINE |
| W04 | RS-ENGINE | RS-LOADER | calls (load model behind the coverage gate) | RS-LOADER loads models for RS-ENGINE |
| W05 | RS-ENGINE | RS-GLIMMER | calls (architecture forward) | RS-GLIMMER returns logits to RS-ENGINE |
| W06 | RS-ENGINE | RS-CPU | calls (Compute backend; the only backend the binary depends on) | RS-CPU executes the forward for RS-ENGINE |
| W07 | RS-LOADER | RS-GGUF | reads (implements traits over the parsed file) | RS-GGUF is the file layer RS-LOADER bridges from |
| W08 | RS-LOADER | RS-GLIMMER | writes (implements its Metadata and TensorSource traits) | RS-GLIMMER receives metadata and tensors through RS-LOADER |
| W09 | RS-LOADER | RS-DFLASH | reads (draft file census and conditioning inputs) | RS-DFLASH files are inventoried through RS-LOADER |
| W10 | RS-CPU | RS-GLIMMER | reads (implements its Compute trait) | RS-GLIMMER runs on RS-CPU |
| W11 | RS-CPU | RS-MATH | calls (reference f32 arithmetic) | RS-MATH returns activations to RS-CPU |
| W12 | RS-CPU | RS-GGUF | calls (dequantization) | RS-GGUF dequantizes for RS-CPU |
| W13 | RS-CPU | RS-ATTN | reads and writes (KV storage) | RS-ATTN holds cache state for RS-CPU |
| W14 | RS-WGPU | RS-GLIMMER | reads (implements its Compute trait) | RS-GLIMMER can run on RS-WGPU (bench path) |
| W15 | RS-WGPU | RS-GGUF | calls (dequantization and upload) | RS-GGUF supplies weights to RS-WGPU |
| W16 | RS-WGPU | RS-ATTN | reads (KV shapes and masks) | RS-ATTN defines the cache layout RS-WGPU mirrors on device |
| W17 | RS-WGPU | RS-KV | reads and writes (prefix snapshots through the store seam) | RS-KV serves snapshot capture and restore to the RS-WGPU resident session |
| W18 | RS-WGPU | RS-DFLASH | calls (device DFlash session) | RS-DFLASH drafts on device for RS-WGPU |
| W19 | RS-KV | RS-ATTN | reads and writes (snapshots captured from and restored into KvCache) | RS-ATTN holds the cache state RS-KV persists |
| W20 | RS-ARCH | RS-GGUF | reads (metadata and tensors) | RS-GGUF supplies RS-ARCH |
