# SPEC: itak-spec, speculative decoding

Status: design, written 2026-10-29. Module slot: ARCHITECTURE.md
Section 3.1 (`itak-spec`: speculative execution; `draft(session) ->
candidates`, `verify(...)`; every mode config-gated, every gate with a
behavior test; depends on itak-forward and itak-arch). Plan authority:
PLAN.md S6 (the module in full) and S13 (the Glimmer fast path). This
spec covers the DFlash block loop in full, the shared verify and rollback
core every mode uses, the T-P.1 acceptance and depth sweep protocol, and
the Medusa salvage verdict. N-gram lookup is specified to the depth its
TODO item (T-3.1) needs, because it shares the verify and rollback core.
MTP, the EKF speculative update, early-exit drafting, and PowerInfer-style
activation prediction are named in PLAN S6 and are out of scope here;
they get their own specs when their phases open.

## 1. Measured ground and assumed ground

Measured, from this repo's own record:

| Fact | Value | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Glimmer plain decode, llama.cpp Vulkan, 7900 XTX | 44.31 tok/s | GLIMMER-DISSECTION.md; bench record 2026-10-28 |
| Glimmer with DFlash, llama.cpp, same card | 88.6 tok/s (2.00x) | bench/model-suite-2026-10-28.md |
| Conditions of the 88.6 | Solo profile: `-md <dflash gguf> --spec-type draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 4`, `-np 1` | docs/RUNBOOK.md serving profile; DECISIONS.md serving decision |
| DFlash draft file | Own arch string `dflash`, 5 layers, 1.51 GiB, 8 KV heads, `block_size` 16 | GLIMMER-DISSECTION.md (GGUF census 2026-10-29) |
| Target KV shape | 52 layers: 39 windowed rings of exactly 2048 slots, 13 global; 2 KV heads, head dim 128 | crates/attention/src/cache.rs `glimmer_layer_pattern()`; GLIMMER-DISSECTION.md |
| The pasted article's DFlash claim | Depth 16, 75 to 110+ tok/s | REFERENCES.md: graded unverified; its depth conflicts with our measured profile at depth 4. Settling it is T-P.1 |

Assumed, flagged wherever used below:

- llama.cpp's internal DFlash wiring (how the draft is conditioned, how
  it verifies) is llama.cpp's business. This spec designs our loop from
  the speculative sampling literature's standard form and from the
  interfaces in our own crates. Nothing in the design depends on
  llama.cpp internals; the 88.6 is a performance anchor, not a design
  input.
- Whether the `dflash` arch consumes target hidden states as a
  conditioning input was settled 2026-10-30: it consumes target
  layer-input hidden states at the layers its own metadata names,
  plus a token noise block (Section 10, Q1, with source citations).
  The trait design in Section 6 already carries the conditioning
  handle, so the answer did not change the trait.

## 2. The interfaces this design is built against (code that exists)

Read from the tree on 2026-10-29:

- `GlimmerModel::forward(&self, tokens: &[u32], cache: &mut dyn Cache)
  -> Result<Vec<f32>>` (crates/muse-glimmer/src/model.rs). Contract that
  matters: input is validated before any compute; on success the cache
  advances by `tokens.len()`; on any refusal the cache is untouched;
  the return is the FINAL position's logits only, already finished with
  the file's softcap and scale (`softcap_scale`, applied in the model,
  not the kernel). Two consequences drive this whole spec:
  1. Verify needs per-position distributions, so verify cannot use
     `forward` as it stands. Section 3 names the extension.
  2. The distribution the correction math runs on is the finished
     distribution (post softcap, post scale), bit-for-bit the same
     distribution the plain path samples from. Speculation that
     corrected against pre-softcap logits would not be the same model.
- `Cache` trait (crates/muse-glimmer/src/cache.rs): `position()` and
  `advance(n)` only. It is the position contract; real KV storage sits
  behind `Compute::attention` today and behind itak-kv when T-2.4 lands.
  The spec therefore places checkpoint and rewind on the KV store
  itself (the attention crate's `KvCache`), not on this trait.
- `KvCache` (crates/attention/src/cache.rs): one `LayerCache` per layer.
  Windowed layers are rings: slot is `position % window`,
  `slot_position[slot]` records which absolute position a slot holds,
  `appended` counts total appends and is the next expected position.
  `append` refuses out-of-order positions (`AttentionError::
  OutOfOrderPosition`). Global layers append rows at the tail of flat
  `Vec<f32>` key and value stores. `CacheView` reads visible positions
  oldest first, masks are defined over absolute positions, and
  `KvCache::stats()` exposes a per-layer snapshot for diagnostics. The
  rollback design in Section 5 is written against exactly these fields.
- `Compute::attention` applies RoPE to Q and K at the cache's current
  position (crates/muse-glimmer/src/compute.rs). Consequence: rows in
  the KV store are post-RoPE at absolute positions. A restored row is
  already correct for its position and must never be re-appended under
  a different one; the append order check enforces this.
- Error style (crates/muse-glimmer/src/error.rs, crates/attention/
  src/error.rs): hand-written enums, every variant named, `Display`
  states what failed and with what values, no fallback values anywhere.
  `SpecError` in Section 6 follows the same shape.
- Diag style (crates/muse-glimmer/src/diag.rs, model.rs): a `Diag`
  trait, `event(name, detail)` with dotted names (`forward.begin`,
  `forward.end`) and `key=value` detail strings. Section 6.4 fixes the
  itak-spec event catalogue in the same style. When itak-diag lands,
  these names become its stable codes unchanged.
- Salvage verdicts (SALVAGE.md, itak-spec table): the old FFI
  `spec_decode.go` is DROP (wired only into the retired FFI engine and
  never actually run in the serve loop; its lessons live in the bench
  record). The old native v1 `speculative_decoder.go` is RUST, the
  starting point for the verify design (it is a working draft and
  verify design, exercised only by its own test). The old Medusa
  `speculative_v2.go` is DROP as code; Section 8 is the concept verdict.

## 3. Required extensions (dependencies this spec names)

itak-spec cannot be built against the tree exactly as it stands. Three
extensions are required; each is proposed as a TODO item in Section 9.

E1. **Block forward with per-position logits.** A forward variant that
takes a block of tokens against a cache and returns the finished logits
for EVERY position in the block (row-major `[block][vocab]`, the same
softcap and scale finishing as `GlimmerModel::forward`). Teacher
forcing a block of length L yields L distributions; the round consumes
L of them (Section 4). Owned by the forward layer (itak-forward and the
arch forward), not by itak-spec: speculation is a caller of the forward,
never a special case inside it (ARCHITECTURE.md Section 3.1 gives
itak-spec `itak-forward` as a dependency, not the reverse).
LANDED 2026-10-30 (TODO T-2.10): `GlimmerModel::forward_block` in
crates/muse-glimmer/src/model.rs, sharing `forward`'s layer loop
(`forward_rows`), so the single-token path is the block-of-one case.
Per-position logits are proven against sequential single-token
forwards on a synthetic config, across a sliding-window boundary,
and at the convention tests' intermediate scale
(crates/cpu-compute/tests/forward_tests.rs, `block_and_spec`).

E2. **KvCache checkpoint and rewind.** A transactional API on the
attention crate's `KvCache`: `checkpoint()`, `rewind_to(checkpoint,
position)`, `release(checkpoint)`. Semantics in Section 5. Owned by the
attention crate (later itak-kv), used by itak-spec and by n-gram
rollback (T-3.1 names rollback in its proof for the same reason).
LANDED 2026-10-30 (TODO T-2.10): `KvCache::checkpoint(max_round_tokens)`,
`rewind_to`, and `release` in crates/attention/src/cache.rs, with the
Section 5 semantics as written (windowed layers save the round's
touched ring slots, global layers truncate, one live checkpoint,
appends past the saved range refused by name, a round bound past the
smallest window refused as `CheckpointTooDeep`). The position half is
`Cache::rewind_to` in crates/muse-glimmer/src/cache.rs, and the
backend surface is `CpuCompute::cache_checkpoint` / `cache_rewind` /
`cache_release`. Measured bound at Glimmer geometry (52 layers,
2 KV heads, head dim 128, window 2048, round bound 17): 1,357,824
bytes of saved rows, proven by
`checkpoint_memory_bound_at_glimmer_geometry` in
crates/attention/tests/checkpoint_tests.rs; the model-level round
trip is proven by `speculative_round_trip_rewind_restores_exact_continuation`.

E3. **A dflash arch module.** The draft is a model: it loads through the
same loader and arch seam as the target (ARCHITECTURE.md Section 6),
with its config read from its own file's metadata under the same
no-silent-default rule as `GlimmerConfig`. itak-spec defines the
contract it needs from that module (Section 6.2, the `Speculator`
implementation for DFlash); the module itself is a Phase 9 item.
LANDED 2026-10-30: the `dflash` crate (crates/dflash) with
`DflashConfig` from the file's `dflash.*` metadata, the 58-tensor
inventory loaded through `itak-loader` (`load_dflash_config`,
`coverage_dflash`, `load_dflash_weights`) behind the full coverage
gate, `DflashModel::inject` (conditioning fusion into the draft's
own KV cache) and `DflashModel::forward_block` (per-position draft
logits for a noise block, target embedding and head borrowed). Q1
and Q2 are settled in Section 10 from the file census and the
llama.cpp source. The target side exposes the conditioning rows
through the additive `GlimmerModel::forward_capturing` /
`forward_block_capturing` variants (crates/muse-glimmer), proven
not to change the verified forward's steps or logits. Arithmetic
proofs: closed-form and naive-reference tests in the dflash crate,
chunked/overwrite injection consistency, and a real-file run on
the server (coverage 58/58, one block forward, finite logits,
recorded in bench/dflash-e3-2026-10-30.md).

E4. **The loop itself (this spec's subject).**
LANDED 2026-10-30 (TODO T-3.6 and T-3.7): the `itak-spec` crate
(crates/itak-spec) with `SpecSession` implementing the Section 4 round
structure over E1/E2/E3, the Section 6.2 `Speculator` trait with the
DFlash implementation, the Section 6.1 error table, the Section 6.3
config block, the Section 6.4 diag catalogue and cumulative
`SpecStats`, and the correction walk as pure functions in the crate's
sampler module. Draft sync follows Q1/Q2 as settled: captures are
staged by absolute position at the verify forward, and commit injects
exactly the newly committed positions' concatenated layer-input rows;
the draft cache is never checkpointed by the target machinery. The
session owns the seeded RNG (a xorshift64*, the engine sampler's
generator), settling Q6 in the home Section 6.3 proposed. Proof:
temperature-0 token identity against plain greedy generation on
synthetic configs at depths 1, 2, 4, and 6; the verify-refusal refuse
and latch paths proven with a sabotage compute that fails one
attention call; creation refusals and the draft commit contract
covered by named tests; and a real-file identity run on the server
(16 tokens, depth 6, Stage 1 prompt) recorded in
bench/spec-loop-2026-10-30.md. Still open against this spec: T-9.6's
serving half (the loop proves the mechanism on CPU; the tok/s clause
belongs to the GPU path), T-9.7's depth sweep on this stack, T-3.1
(n-gram), T-3.3 (Medusa), T-3.2 (its proof names the original FFI
path's test cases, not in hand; the walk here is proven against
hand-computed distributions from Section 4), and the grammar-aware
walk (Q4).

## 4. The DFlash verify round

One round of speculative decode, for one sequence. Definitions:

- `base`: the target cache position at round start. The cache holds K/V
  for exactly the committed sequence prefix, positions `0..base`.
- `pending`: the most recently emitted token, sampled in an earlier
  round (or by prefill for the first round), not yet forwarded. The
  loop invariant of the whole design: the emitted sequence is the
  committed prefix plus `pending`; the target cache lags the emitted
  sequence by exactly the pending token.
- `n`: the verify depth for this round, `min(config.n_max, draft block
  size, remaining token budget)`. The draft file's block size is 16;
  `n_max` is config (Section 6.3), so `n <= 16` for Glimmer's draft.
- Speculation applies to decode only. Prefill is a plain forward over
  the prompt; its final logits sample the first `pending`.

The round, step by step:

1. **Checkpoint.** `cp = kv.checkpoint()` before anything speculative
   touches the cache. Draft state is not checkpointed (step 7).
2. **Propose.** The DFlash speculator drafts `t[1..=n]` as continuations
   after `pending`, returning the tokens and the draft's per-position
   distributions `q[i]` (the draft's finished distribution for the
   token following position `i-1`, in the notation of step 4). The
   draft may return fewer than `n` (its own EOS or its block
   boundary); the round proceeds with what it returned.
3. **Verify forward.** One block forward (E1) over
   `[pending, t[1], ..., t[n]]`, `n+1` tokens, appending their K/V.
   It returns finished logits for all `n+1` positions. Read them as
   distributions `p[0..=n]`, where `p[i]` is the target distribution
   for the token that follows the prefix extended by
   `[pending, t[1..=i]]`. Note `p[0]` judges `t[1]`, and `p[n]` is the
   distribution a fully accepted block draws its bonus token from.
   Because attention is causal, each position's K/V and distribution
   are exact: nothing later in the block influences them. This is what
   makes step 5's keep-the-prefix rule exact rather than approximate.
4. **Correct.** Walk `i = 1..=n`, drawing `r` uniform in `[0, 1)` from
   the session RNG (Section 6.3):
   - Accept `t[i]` if `r < min(1, p[i-1](t[i]) / q[i](t[i]))`.
   - On the first rejection at position `j`: sample the replacement
     token from the residual distribution
     `norm(max(0, p[j-1] - q[j]))` (elementwise, clipped at zero,
     renormalized over the full vocabulary). The walk stops.
   - If all `n` accept: sample the bonus token from `p[n]`.
   Greedy decoding is the special case where both distributions are
   point masses: accept exactly when the draft token equals the
   target's argmax, residual is the target argmax. At temperature 0
   the emitted sequence must be identical to non-speculative
   generation; that identity is the standing proof obligation
   (T-3.1, T-9.6) and a behavior test, not a hope.
   The sampler parameters of the session (temperature, top-p, top-k,
   penalties, per T-2.5) are applied to the target logits BEFORE the
   correction walk, so `p` is the distribution the plain path would
   sample from. The draft distributions `q` are taken under the
   draft's configured sampler (default: same temperature as the
   target; config, Section 6.3).
5. **Commit or rewind the target cache.** Let `a` be the number of
   accepted draft tokens (`a = j-1` on a rejection at `j`, `a = n` on
   full acceptance). The verify forward appended K/V for `pending`
   plus all `n` drafts; the committed prefix grows by `pending` plus
   the `a` accepted drafts, so `kv.rewind_to(cp, base + 1 + a)`
   (Section 5), then `kv.release(cp)`. The replacement or bonus token
   becomes the new `pending`: emitted, not yet forwarded, exactly the
   loop invariant. Emitted this round: `a + 1` tokens (accepted drafts
   plus the replacement or bonus). `pending` itself was emitted in an
   earlier round and is not re-emitted.
6. **Stop conditions inside a round.** If any emitted token (an
   accepted draft, the replacement, or the bonus) is EOS or matches a
   stop rule, the emitted stream truncates at that token and the
   session ends. Cache state after a terminal round is irrelevant
   (the session is torn down), but the round's diag events still fire
   (Section 6.4) so the acceptance record is complete.
7. **Draft state sync.** After the round, the speculator is told
   exactly the newly committed tokens, `[pending_old, t[1..=a]]`, via
   `commit()` (Section 6.2), and nothing else. The contract: after any
   sequence of `propose` and `commit` calls, the draft's internal
   state equals the state of having processed exactly the committed
   sequence, no more. How the draft holds that state (its own KV over
   the committed prefix, recomputed windows, hidden-state carry) is
   the draft module's business; speculative state the draft built
   while proposing is discarded by the draft itself and never leaks
   into the target cache. If a draft cannot honor this contract, it
   does not ship as a speculator.

Failure inside a round: if the verify forward refuses (any
`GlimmerError` or `AttentionError`), the spec layer rewinds to `base`
(discarding the pending token's rows too; `pending` stays pending),
releases the checkpoint, and returns the refusal wrapped in
`SpecError::VerifyRefused`. No partial commit exists. What happens
next is policy, fixed in Section 6.3: the default is that the request
fails with the named error. A latched fallback exists as config and is
never silent.

## 5. Cache rollback against windowed rings (the hard part, specified exactly)

### 5.1 Why naive append-and-truncate corrupts a ring

A windowed layer's ring holds the most recent `window` (2048)
positions, slot `position % window`. Appending position `p` overwrites
the slot that held position `p - window`. That evicted position is
still visible to the committed prefix: a query at the last committed
position `base - 1` attends over `[base - window, base - 1]`, and
`p - window >= base - window` for every speculative `p >= base`. So
the moment a speculative append lands in a ring, it destroys K/V that
committed tokens still attend to. Truncating `appended` afterward does
not bring the evicted rows back. Any rollback design that appends
first and restores only counters is corrupt by construction; this is
the trap the old tree's never-wired sliding window code never had to
face, and the reason T-3.1 names rollback in its proof.

Global layers have no such problem: rows append at the tail and a
rewind is a truncation. The design below treats the two kinds
accordingly.

### 5.2 Checkpoint contents

`KvCache::checkpoint()` captures, before the round's first speculative
append:

- For every layer: the `appended` count at checkpoint time (one
  number; all layers share the round's `base` in this design, but the
  checkpoint records it per layer because the cache API is per layer
  and the restore must not assume).
- For every WINDOWED layer: for each slot the round may touch, the
  slot's current key row, value row, and `slot_position` entry. The
  round forwards at most `max_round_tokens` positions (pending plus
  `n_max` drafts; a config bound, Section 6.3), so the touched slots
  are the `max_round_tokens` consecutive slots starting at
  `base % window`, wrapping. With Glimmer's numbers (17 tokens worst
  case, 39 windowed layers, rows of 2 heads x 128 dims x 4 bytes =
  1 KiB per K or V row) a checkpoint is at most about 1.4 MB,
  allocated once per session and reused every round (RULES.md: no
  per-token allocation; a per-round reused buffer is the same
  discipline).
- Global layers need no row copies: their restore is truncation.

One checkpoint may be outstanding per cache at a time. A second
`checkpoint()` while one is live is refused with
`SpecError`-adjacent cache error `CheckpointBusy` (in the attention
crate's error set since E2 landed, exactly as named here). Stack
discipline matches the caller: rounds
are sequential per sequence, and batching (Section 10, Q5) does not
nest checkpoints inside one sequence's cache.

### 5.3 Rewind semantics

`rewind_to(cp, target)` where `base <= target <= base + n + 1`:

- Every layer: `appended` becomes `target`.
- Global layers: key and value stores truncate to `target` rows. Rows
  for positions `base..target` (the kept speculative rows) stay; they
  are exact by the causality argument in Section 4 step 3.
- Windowed layers: slots holding kept positions (`base..target`) keep
  the speculative rows. For every other touched slot, restore the
  checkpoint's saved key row, value row, and `slot_position`. Slots
  the round never touched are untouched throughout.
- Postcondition, checkable and checked in tests: for every layer,
  `view()` after rewind returns exactly the rows that a cache fed only
  the committed prefix would hold, and the `slot_position` bookkeeping
  agrees with every visible row (the invariant `LayerCache::key`
  already debug-asserts). `stats()` after rewind shows
  `appended == target` on all layers.

Full-round abort is `rewind_to(cp, base)`: every touched windowed slot
restored, global stores truncated to `base`, draft told nothing.

### 5.4 What rollback never does

- It never re-appends a restored row under a new position (RoPE is
  baked in at append; Section 2). Restored rows return to their slots
  with their original absolute positions, and `slot_position` says so.
- It never runs on the muse-glimmer `Cache` position trait. Position
  and storage move together or the design has two truths; the position
  the arch forward sees is derived from the KV store's `appended` when
  itak-kv lands, and until then the engine session owns both and the
  round updates them in the same step.
- It is not a snapshot or persistence format. Checkpoints are
  in-memory, per-session, and die with the round. Versioned KV save
  and load is itak-kv's separate contract (ARCHITECTURE.md Section
  5.3: state save and load either round-trip verified or the verb
  does not exist).

## 6. Interfaces

### 6.1 Errors: named refusals only

`SpecError`, hand-written in the house style of `GlimmerError` and
`AttentionError`. Every variant names the thing that failed; there is
no variant for "fell back", because fallback is a state (Section 6.3),
not an error, and it is never entered silently.

| Variant | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ModeUnavailable { mode }` | Config names a speculation mode with no implementation loaded in this build |
| `DraftNotLoaded` | Mode requires a draft and none is attached to the session |
| `DraftArchMismatch { found, expected }` | The draft file's arch string is not the one the speculator serves (mirrors `GlimmerError::WrongArchitecture`) |
| `DraftLoadFailed { detail }` | The loader's coverage report for the draft named a gap; carries the report's wording |
| `EnvelopeMismatch { field, expected, actual }` | A versioned artifact (Medusa heads, Section 8) disagrees with the runtime context envelope on `field` |
| `ArtifactVersionUnsupported { found, supported }` | Artifact format version outside the supported set |
| `ZeroInitializedHeads { artifact }` | Medusa artifact loaded but its heads are zero-initialized; a reported load state, never served as if trained |
| `DepthOutOfRange { n_max, block_size }` | Configured `n_max` outside `1..=block_size` |
| `CheckpointBusy` | A cache checkpoint is already outstanding (raised by E2, surfaced unchanged) |
| `CacheOutOfSync { expected, actual }` | Post-round cache position is not the committed length; the round's bookkeeping and the cache disagree, which is a defect, reported as one |
| `GrammarConflict` | Speculation requested for a session with an active grammar, JSON mode, or schema constraint (v1 refusal; Q4) |
| `VerifyRefused { source }` | The verify forward refused; wraps the `GlimmerError` or `AttentionError` that caused it |

Session creation with speculation enabled validates everything
validatable up front (mode available, draft attached and loaded,
`n_max` in range, no grammar conflict) and refuses by name at creation.
A session that starts speculative never discovers a load-time problem
mid-stream.

### 6.2 The Speculator trait and the round driver

```rust
/// What a proposer believes about one position: the draft's finished
/// distribution, borrowed for the round. Row-major over the vocab.
pub struct DraftDist<'a> {
    /// Probabilities after the draft's own finishing and sampler,
    /// length = target vocab.
    pub probs: &'a [f32],
}

/// One round of drafting: tokens plus the distribution each was
/// drawn from, position-aligned.
pub struct BlockProposal<'a> {
    /// Drafted tokens, continuations after the pending token.
    pub tokens: &'a [u32],
    /// `dists[i]` is the distribution `tokens[i]` was drawn from.
    pub dists: &'a [DraftDist<'a>],
}

/// Everything a proposer may condition on. The hidden-state handle is
/// optional because the DFlash conditioning question is open (Q1);
/// a proposer that requires it and finds `None` refuses with
/// `SpecError::ModeUnavailable` naming the missing input rather than
/// drafting unconditioned garbage.
pub struct ProposeContext<'a> {
    /// The committed sequence prefix (at minimum its tail; the exact
    /// window a proposer may see is its own documented contract).
    pub committed: &'a [u32],
    /// The pending token the proposal continues from.
    pub pending: u32,
    /// Target final hidden states for the committed prefix, when the
    /// deployment provides them.
    pub target_hidden: Option<&'a [f32]>,
    /// Maximum tokens to propose this round (the round's `n`).
    pub max_tokens: usize,
}

/// A drafting mode. Implementations: DFlash (Section 4), n-gram
/// lookup (Section 7), Medusa (Section 8, later).
pub trait Speculator {
    /// Which mode this is (config and diagnostics name modes by this).
    fn mode(&self) -> SpecMode;
    /// The largest block this proposer can emit (16 for the shipped
    /// DFlash file; the n-gram proposer's configured match cap).
    fn max_depth(&self) -> usize;
    /// Draft the next block. Builds only proposer-internal state;
    /// touches neither the target cache nor the emitted sequence.
    fn propose(&mut self, ctx: &ProposeContext<'_>) -> Result<BlockProposal<'_>, SpecError>;
    /// Advance the proposer's state by exactly these committed
    /// tokens, in order. After any propose/commit sequence the
    /// proposer's state equals having processed exactly the committed
    /// sequence (Section 4 step 7).
    fn commit(&mut self, tokens: &[u32]) -> Result<(), SpecError>;
}
```

The round driver (owned by itak-spec, called by the engine's
generation loop; the loop calling it is the wiring ARCHITECTURE.md
Section 5.4 requires, so a configured-but-uncalled decoder is
impossible by construction):

```rust
/// The outcome of one round, also the source of the round's diag
/// events and the session's cumulative spec stats.
pub struct RoundOutcome {
    /// Tokens emitted this round (accepted drafts plus the
    /// replacement or bonus), in order. Length is `accepted + 1`
    /// unless a stop condition truncated it.
    pub emitted: Vec<u32>,
    /// Draft tokens proposed this round.
    pub proposed: usize,
    /// Draft tokens accepted this round.
    pub accepted: usize,
    /// Index of the first rejected draft token, if any.
    pub first_rejection: Option<usize>,
    /// Target cache position after the round's commit or rewind.
    pub cache_position: usize,
    /// True when a stop condition ended the session inside this round.
    pub stopped: bool,
}

/// Run one speculative round (Section 4). `forward_block` is E1,
/// `kv` is the session's target cache, `sampler` applies the
/// session's sampling parameters to raw finished logits.
pub fn run_round(
    spec: &mut dyn Speculator,
    session: &mut SpecSessionState,
    // ... forward_block, kv, sampler, rng, diag handles
) -> Result<RoundOutcome, SpecError>;
```

(Signature shown at design level: exact handle types land with the
crate, and the shape, not the spelling, is what this spec fixes.)

The correction walk itself (Section 4 step 4) is a pure function over
`(target_probs, proposal) -> (accepted, replacement_or_bonus)`, so
T-3.2's distribution tests exercise it without a model.

### 6.3 Config: every limit a knob, every knob behavior-tested

All under a `spec` config block; defaults in parentheses. Every entry
has a behavior test proving the knob changes behavior (ARCHITECTURE.md
Section 5.1: a flag read only by a log line is a build failure).

| Knob | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spec.mode` | `off` | `off`, `dflash`, `ngram`; `medusa` becomes valid when Section 8's path lands |
| `spec.dflash.n_max` | 6 | Verify depth for DFlash. 6 is the operating point the llama.cpp sweep measured on 2026-10-30 (bench/gpu-proof-2026-10-30.md: depth 6 at 107.39 tok/s against 41.64 plain, depths 8 and up harmful); the sweep on this stack (Section 9, TODO T-9.7) may re-default it with its table filed |
| `spec.dflash.draft_path` | none | The draft GGUF; required when mode is `dflash` |
| `spec.dflash.draft_temperature` | follow target | Draft sampler temperature |
| `spec.ngram.max_depth` | 8 | Longest n-gram proposal |
| `spec.ngram.min_match` | 2 | Shortest history match that may propose |
| `spec.max_round_tokens` | 17 | Bound on positions one round may append (pending + max depth); sizes the checkpoint (Section 5.2) |
| `spec.on_verify_error` | `refuse` | `refuse`: a verify refusal fails the request by name. `latch_off`: the first verify refusal latches speculation off for the session, emits `spec.fallback.latched`, and the session continues non-speculatively in that explicit, queryable state |

RNG: the correction walk draws from a per-session seeded RNG injected
into the driver, never a global. Temperature 0 needs no draws (the
greedy special case), and seeded draws make the sampled arm of the
sweep reproducible. Which crate owns the RNG implementation was Q6;
settled 2026-10-30 (itak-spec's session owns it).

### 6.4 Diagnostic events, per verify round

Through the module's diag channel, house style (`Diag::event`, dotted
names, `key=value` detail). A session's cumulative counters
(`spec_stats()`: rounds, proposed, accepted, rejections, rollbacks,
fallback state) are pullable the way `KvCache::stats()` is, because a
number only in a log stream is a number nobody can gate on.

| Event | When | Detail fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spec.session.begin` | Session created with speculation on | `mode`, `draft` (file + arch), `n_max`, `target` arch |
| `spec.session.end` | Session teardown | `rounds`, `proposed`, `accepted`, `accept_rate` |
| `spec.disabled` | Session created with mode `off` | `reason=config` (emitted once, so "off" is a queryable state, not an absence) |
| `spec.round.begin` | Round start | `round`, `base`, `pending` |
| `spec.propose.end` | Proposal returned | `proposed`, `draft_ms` |
| `spec.verify.end` | Verify forward returned | `verify_ms` |
| `spec.round.accept` | Correction walk done | `proposed`, `accepted`, `first_rejection` (or `none`), `emitted` |
| `spec.cache.rewind` | Any rewind, including commit-path | `from`, `to`, per-kind layer counts |
| `spec.cache.commit` | Round committed | `position` after commit |
| `spec.fallback.latched` | `on_verify_error=latch_off` fires | `reason` (the refusal's wording), `round` |
| `spec.refused` | Session creation refusal | the `SpecError` variant and its fields |
| `spec.heads.loaded` | Medusa artifact accepted (Section 8) | `artifact`, `version`, envelope fingerprint |
| `spec.sweep.row` | Bench mode only, one per grid cell | the full sweep row of Section 9, so bench tables are built from diag output, not scraped prose |

## 7. N-gram prompt lookup (T-3.1), to the depth it shares this core

The n-gram proposer needs no weights: it searches the committed
sequence (prompt plus generated so far) for the longest recent suffix
match and proposes the tokens that followed the earlier occurrence
(the algorithm is working today in the Mojo engine; PLAN S6 says port
the algorithm, and Mojo lab informs itak-spec per docs/MAP.md). It
implements the same `Speculator` trait: `propose` reads
`ProposeContext.committed`, `commit` is bookkeeping only, and verify,
correction, checkpoint, and rewind are literally the same code path as
DFlash. That sharing is why T-3.1's proof names KV state rollback:
SSM state in the hybrid families rolls back through the same
checkpoint discipline, with the SSM state block copied into the
checkpoint beside the ring rows (state size is a config-visible
quantity of the arch module, and a checkpoint that omits it is the
same corruption as Section 5.1 in a different store).

## 8. Medusa verdict: what salvaging the self-drafting heads requires, and why it sequences after DFlash

Verdict: the concept is sound and stays in the plan (PLAN S6, TODO
T-3.3, ENDGOAL.md names it a finished-system property). The old code is
not salvage: SALVAGE.md drops `speculative_v2.go` (zero references, no
test, and no train, load, or serialize path exists for its heads, so
they could never hold trained weights), and the 2026-10-26 research
note records the heads as random-init with acceptance near zero
expected until trained. Salvaging the IDEA requires building four
things that do not exist today, in this order:

1. **A training path (TODO T-7.3, Phase 7).** A job type of its own in
   the training stack: harvest final hidden states from the frozen
   target over a real corpus, train the K heads (the v2 design: K MLPs
   on the final hidden state predicting offsets +1..+K) against the
   target's own next-token labels. This needs a hidden-state export
   from the forward, which does not exist yet; Section 9 proposes it
   as its own item so it is scheduled rather than discovered.
2. **A versioned artifact format.** Heads ship as files with a version
   field (project law: data formats carry version fields), loaded
   through the same loader discipline as models: coverage checked,
   shapes checked, gaps named. Zero-initialized heads are a load state
   the engine reports (`SpecError::ZeroInitializedHeads`), never a
   silent default (ARCHITECTURE.md Section 5.4).
3. **The runtime-context envelope.** The artifact carries the envelope
   it was trained under, and the loader verifies it field by field
   before the heads may propose: target architecture string, hidden
   size, vocabulary size, layer count, the target file's identity
   (content fingerprint as registered by model operations), the
   tokenizer identity, and the artifact format version. Heads read
   the target's final hidden states, so any change to the backbone
   (a requant, a different checkpoint, a tokenizer swap) shifts the
   distribution the heads were trained on; an envelope mismatch is
   `SpecError::EnvelopeMismatch` naming the field, at load time,
   never a degraded acceptance rate discovered in production.
4. **Tree verify.** Medusa proposes a TREE (per-head top-k candidates
   branched), not a block. Verifying it needs E1 extended with tree
   attention masks (candidates attend only to their ancestors), which
   is a forward extension beyond per-position logits, plus the same
   correction math generalized per path. Rollback is unchanged:
   checkpoint and rewind do not care what shape was verified.

Why after DFlash, stated once and plainly:

- DFlash's weights exist. They were trained against this exact
  backbone by the model's authors, the file is on the server and
  byte-verified, and the pair is measured at 2.00x on David's card
  today. Medusa's weights exist nowhere; every gram of Medusa value
  waits on item 1.
- Medusa's critical path runs through the whole training stack
  (Phase 7) plus a forward export hook. DFlash's path needs only the
  loader, E1, and E2. Sequencing DFlash first puts working 2x
  speculation in the engine a full phase earlier.
- DFlash exercises the entire shared core (verify, correction,
  checkpoint, rewind, diag, config gates) with a single-path proposal,
  the simplest shape that can prove it. Medusa then adds exactly two
  new things (artifacts with envelopes, tree verify) on proven
  machinery, instead of debugging all of it at once.
- The plan already encodes this order (Phase 9 fast path carries
  DFlash, T-9.6 and T-9.7; T-3.3 consumes Phase 7 output, T-7.3).
  This spec ratifies it with reasons rather than re-deciding it.

## 9. The acceptance and depth sweep protocol (parked T-P.1; executed as T-9.7)

T-P.1 as parked asks a narrow question: draft depth 4 (our measured
profile) versus 16 (the article's claim). This protocol answers that
question and, in the same runs, produces the operating point the new
stack ships as config. It runs twice by design: first against
llama.cpp (that is T-P.1 itself, unblocking nothing but settling the
claim on the reference stack), then against itak-engine once T-9.6
lands (that run is T-9.7, and its output is the config default).

### 9.1 Grid

- Depth (`n_max`): 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16. Depth 1 is the control
  (speculation machinery on, one token verified per round). The plain
  non-speculative run is recorded alongside as the 44.31-class anchor.
  Depths above the draft's block size (16) do not exist for this file.
- Sampler arms: (a) temperature 0; (b) the deployment's recorded
  default sampler settings. Acceptance is sampler-dependent and the
  two arms are reported separately, never averaged together. Whether
  the proxy-layer reasoning_strength injection belongs in the bench
  prompts is frozen in the bench note before the run (Q7).
- Shape: solo, one slot (the conditions of the 88.6 measurement).
  Multi-slot speculation is Q5 and is not swept here.

### 9.2 Prompts and run discipline

- Prompts: the bench prompt set (bench/accuracy-prompts.md) plus a
  fixed long-form generation prompt and a code-shaped prompt, named
  in the bench note; every cell runs the identical set.
- Fixed generation length per prompt (256 tokens or the prompt set's
  own stop, whichever first), warm-up round discarded, at least 3
  repetitions per cell, median reported. Same binary, same commit,
  same model files for the whole grid; the commit hash is recorded in
  the bench note (the T-9.4 discipline).
- Harness anchor first: before any grid cell counts, the harness must
  reproduce the recorded profile on the reference stack (44.31 plain,
  88.6 at depth 4, each within a few percent; docs/RUNBOOK.md: a
  result more than a few percent off the recorded numbers is a
  finding, not a rounding error). An unanchored sweep is not run.

### 9.3 Measurements per cell

- Wall tok/s (end to end, the number that decides).
- Tokens accepted per verify round (mean), and overall acceptance
  rate (accepted / proposed).
- Per-position acceptance: for each draft position `i`, the fraction
  of rounds that reached position `i` and accepted it. This decay
  curve is the real output of the sweep: it shows where the draft
  stops paying, and it is what makes the operating point a reading
  rather than a guess.
- Draft ms and verify ms per round (from the diag events of
  Section 6.4 on our stack; from llama-server's own counters on the
  reference stack), so a depth that wins on acceptance but loses on
  draft cost is visible as such.

### 9.4 Picking the operating point

- The winner is the SMALLEST depth whose median wall tok/s is within
  2 percent of the grid's best median in the temperature 0 arm and not
  worse in the sampled arm. Ties and near-ties resolve shallower on
  purpose: shallower depth wastes less verify compute per rejection,
  rewinds less cache per round, and has better tail latency, and the
  sweep exists to find where depth stops paying, not to maximize
  depth.
- If per-position acceptance past some position `k` is under 5
  percent in both arms, depths above `k` are recorded as dead weight
  in the bench note regardless of the wall-clock outcome.
- Output: the sweep table filed in bench/ (per T-9.7's proof), the
  chosen depth written as the `spec.dflash.n_max` default, and, if
  the reference-stack run moves the recorded 88.6 anchor materially,
  a DECISIONS.md note in the same pass. The result is config, never
  code (ARCHITECTURE.md Section 6).

## 10. Open questions (explicit, with owners of the answer)

- Q1. DFlash conditioning. SETTLED 2026-10-30 (E3 research pass: the
  draft file's full census read with this repo's `gguf` crate, plus
  llama.cpp source on the server: `src/models/dflash.cpp`,
  `common/speculative.cpp` `common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash`,
  `src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp`, `src/llama-model.cpp`). The draft
  consumes BOTH, through two distinct inputs:
  - Conditioning features are TARGET LAYER-INPUT hidden states. The
    draft file's `dflash.target_layers` metadata names the target
    layers `[2, 14, 26, 38, 50]`; for every committed target
    position, the target graph exposes the residual stream ENTERING
    each named layer (`res->t_layer_inp[il] = inpL` in
    muse-glimmer.cpp: the pre-attention-norm residual; layer 0's is
    the embedding output after its weightless RMSNorm). The driver
    concatenates the named layers' rows per position, in
    `target_layers` order (width `5 * 6656 = 33280`, matching
    `fc.weight`'s stored input width), and submits them to the draft
    as an embedding batch at the target positions. The draft fuses
    them (`fc` projection, then RMSNorm with
    `enc.output_norm.weight`) and, per draft layer, projects the
    fused rows to K and V (per-head K RMSNorm, RoPE on K) and writes
    them into the DRAFT'S OWN KV cache at those positions. Q is not
    computed and the FFN does not run in this injection pass.
  - Drafting consumes token ids: one noise block per round whose
    position 0 is the anchor (the last committed token,
    `id_last`), positions 1.. are the file's
    `tokenizer.ggml.mask_token_id` (201818), at consecutive
    positions starting at the committed length. Token embeddings
    and the output head are the TARGET model's `token_embd.weight`
    and `output.weight`, borrowed because this draft file carries
    neither. Draft-layer attention over the block is NON-CAUSAL
    (the file carries no `dflash.attention.causal` key, so the
    llama.cpp default applies); committed history is visible
    through the injected KV. The block forward returns per-position
    logits for the whole block; position 0 is the anchor and is not
    itself a draft, so ordinary DFlash yields at most
    `block_size - 1 = 15` drafts per block. DFlash applies no logit
    scale or softcap of its own in this path. RoPE pairing is NEOX
    (half-split) for this file: `llama_model_rope_type` maps
    `LLM_ARCH_DFLASH` to NEOX unless rope sections (M-RoPE) or
    DeepSeek-V4 metadata are present, and this file has neither.
    This file is plain DFlash: no DFlash2 selector tensors or
    metadata, no DSpark Markov/conv tensors, no `d2t` tensor.
  Consequences for the trait: `ProposeContext.target_hidden` is not
  optional for this proposer; it carries the captured layer-input
  rows for the layers the DRAFT file names (read from the draft's
  own metadata, never hardcoded in the spec layer), and the target
  side exposes them through the captured-states forward variant
  landed with E3 (additive; the verified forward is unchanged).
- Q2. DFlash cache geometry. SETTLED 2026-10-30 with Q1, from the
  draft file's own metadata: 5 layers, all sliding-window
  (`dflash.attention.sliding_window_pattern` = [true x 5]) with the
  shared window 2048 (`dflash.attention.sliding_window`); 8 KV
  heads, key and value length 128 each; one shared RoPE base
  500000 for the whole draft (llama.cpp: "DFlash has a single rope,
  so the SWA rope == main rope"). The draft KV is the draft
  context's own cache, filled by the injection pass at target
  positions and read by the drafting pass; it is not the target's
  cache and is not checkpointed by the target-side E2 machinery.
- Q3. Where E1 lives in the phase order. T-2.4 scopes the forward as
  incremental single-token steps; per-position block logits were an
  addition nobody's TODO item owned. Settled: adopted as T-2.10 in
  Section 11 and landed 2026-10-30 (Section 3), so T-3.x and T-9.6
  are unblocked on this dependency.
- Q4. Grammar and speculation. v1 refuses the combination
  (`GrammarConflict`). The alternative, applying the grammar mask to
  both distributions before the correction walk, is mathematically
  available but unproven against T-3.5's conformance suite. Decided
  when T-3.5 integrates, not here.
- Q5. Batched rounds. This spec is one sequence per session (the solo
  profile every baseline was measured under). Continuous batching
  with ragged per-slot acceptance is undesigned; the scheduler phase
  (T-6.2) owns the question, and nothing here pretends otherwise.
- Q6. RNG ownership. The correction walk needs a per-session seeded
  RNG; no crate in the current tree owns one. Landing spot (sampler
  code beside T-2.5 is the natural home) is proposed, not settled.
  Settled 2026-10-30 by the itak-spec landing: the session owns a
  seeded xorshift64* (the same generator the engine sampler uses),
  injected through the spec config's seed and consumed only by
  temperature sampling; it lives in itak-spec's rng module beside the
  walk in its sampler module.
- Q7. Sweep prompt freeze. Whether the proxy layer's default
  reasoning_strength injection applies to the sweep's prompt set must
  be frozen in the bench note before T-P.1 runs, so the anchor and
  the grid are measured under one stated configuration.

===== FILE: golden/README.md =====
# Golden-output harness (TODO T-2.9)

The rebuild's engines do not get to grade their own homework. This
directory holds reference generations produced by llama.cpp (the
trusted path) on a fixed prompt set at temperature 0, stored as test
data. "Verified text" (T-9.4 and friends) means: an engine's output
on these prompts is diffed against these fixtures by `compare.py`,
mechanically, not eyeballed.

Nothing here diffs against the original Go native engine. llama.cpp
is the reference.

## Layout

- `prompts.jsonl` — the prompt set, version 1.0: 15 short raw
  completion prompts (factual, arithmetic, code, list continuation,
  accented French/German/Spanish text). Raw completions, not chat
  turns: the engine forward pass is what is being verified, so no
  chat template is applied anywhere in this harness. (The long-form
  Glimmer accuracy prompts live separately in
  `bench/accuracy-prompts.md` and are a different check.)
- `gen_golden.py` — the generator. Runs llama.cpp on the host that
  has the binaries and the model, writes one fixture per model.
- `fixtures/*.golden.jsonl` — the golden records.
- `compare.py` — the differ. Any engine that can emit the record
  shape below can be checked against a fixture.

## Fixture format

First line is metadata: model file name, SHA-256 and size, the exact
llama.cpp version, the binaries and flags used, and the prompt set's
SHA-256 (so a fixture can never silently drift from its prompts).
Then one record per prompt:

```json
{"id": "factual_capital", "category": "factual",
 "prompt": "The capital of France is",
 "prompt_token_ids": [1, 450, 7483, 310, 3444, 338],
 "completion_token_ids": [3681, 29889, "..."],
 "completion_text": " Paris.\n\n2. B.C. ...",
 "ended_with_eos": false}
```

`completion_token_ids` are the ids llama.cpp actually sampled,
including the terminal EOS id when generation stops on EOS (its text
piece is empty; see the Qwen2.5 `arithmetic_add` record, 30 tokens,
last id 151643). `ended_with_eos` records that stop.

## Why generation runs through llama-server

The sampled token ids are the point of the fixture, and
`llama-completion` / `llama-cli` cannot report them: no flag exists,
and `--verbose` dumps graph internals instead (verified against
llama.cpp build a7af149). Retokenizing the completion text cannot
recover them either, because tokenization is context-dependent:
`llama-tokenize` on a completion text standalone splits its first
token three ways (`[259, 2177, 275]`) where the in-context
tokenization of the same text has a single token (`[3681]`).

So `gen_golden.py` starts a throwaway `llama-server` on CPU
(`-ngl 0`, localhost, port 18923 by default) and calls `/completion`
with `n_probs=1`, which returns per step the sampled token's id, text
piece and raw bytes. Two assertions guard every record: the server's
evaluated prompt-token count must equal the `llama-tokenize --ids`
count, and the kept steps' bytes must concatenate to the response
text exactly. Ids and text in a fixture therefore provably come from
one and the same generation. The production Glimmer server is never
touched: different port, CPU only, small teardown models.

Decoding parameters, also recorded in each fixture's metadata:
temperature 0, seed 42 (recorded for completeness; the greedy sampler
does not use it), 64 predicted tokens, context 512, 8 threads, no
chat template. Fixtures contain no timestamps; regenerating with the
same llama.cpp build reproduces a fixture byte for byte (verified
for TinyLlama).

## Tooling choice

Both scripts are python3, standard library only. The generator's job
is HTTP plus JSON plus byte-exact consistency checks; bash would need
jq gymnastics for the UTF-8 byte validation, and a compiled tool
would drag in a JSON stack to produce test data. The scripts run
unchanged on the VM and on the server.

## Regenerating

On the server (or any host with the llama.cpp build and the models):

```sh
python3 gen_golden.py --model /mnt/models/teardown/tinyllama-1.1b-chat-v1.0.Q4_K_M.gguf
python3 gen_golden.py --model /path/to/qwen2.5-1.5b-q4km.gguf
```

`--bin-dir` defaults to `/home/server/llama.cpp/build-vulkan2/bin`;
`--out` defaults to `fixtures/<model-file-stem>.golden.jsonl`;
`--port` picks the throwaway server's port.

## Comparing an engine against a fixture

The engine (or an adapter around it) writes a JSONL file with the
same record fields; the metadata line is optional in candidates.

```sh
python3 compare.py fixtures/tinyllama-1.1b-chat-v1.0.Q4_K_M.golden.jsonl candidate.jsonl
```

Per prompt the verdict is `token-identical`, `text-identical` (ids
differ, text matches; the first token divergence is reported), or
`divergent` (first divergence reported in token space and in text
space), plus `missing` for prompts the candidate did not answer.
Exit code 0 means no divergence and nothing missing. `--strict`
additionally fails `text-identical`: verified text at temperature 0
means token-identical.

Self-test results against the TinyLlama fixture (all as expected):
identity run 15/15 token-identical, exit 0; a candidate whose
`factual_capital` ids were replaced by the standalone retokenization
of the same text (66 ids vs 64) reports text-identical with first
divergence at index 0, exit 0, and exit 1 under `--strict`; a
candidate with one flipped token id (index 5) and one flipped text
character reports divergent at exactly those positions, exit 1; a
candidate missing a record reports it missing, exit 1.

===== END FILE: golden/README.md =====

===== FILE: golden/RESULTS-integration-a.md =====
# Integration Run A: arch-llama vs llama.cpp golden fixtures

Date: 2026-10-29. Engine: crates/arch-llama (Rust CPU reference forward)
with crates/tokenizer fed from each model's own GGUF metadata.
Runner: crates/arch-llama/examples/golden_run.rs. Fixtures: golden/
harness, 15 prompts per model, greedy (temperature 0, seed 42 in the
reference), 64 completion tokens max, EOS ends generation.

Run conditions: David's ubuntu-server, release build,
RUSTFLAGS target-cpu=x86-64-v3, CPU only. The production Glimmer
llama-server on the GPU was not touched (verified still running as
its original pid after both runs). Wall times: TinyLlama 754 s,
Qwen2.5-1.5B 1006 s for the full 15 prompts each. No prompt set was
shrunk; both runs are complete.

## Headlines

| Model | Token-identical | Text-identical | Divergent | Missing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B Q4_K_M | 0 / 15 | 0 / 15 | 15 | 0 |
| TinyLlama-1.1B Q4_K_M | 0 / 15 | 0 / 15 | 15 | 0 |

Both --strict runs give the same verdicts. The two zeros have
completely different causes, detailed below. In short: for Qwen the
tokenizer is proven exact and the divergence is a forward math
discrepancy; for TinyLlama the divergence is a tokenizer family gap
that makes the run uninformative about the forward.

## Qwen2.5-1.5B: tokenization exact, forward diverges

Prompt tokenization matches the fixture on all 15 prompts (compare.py
reports no prompt-id notes, and candidate prompt lengths equal the
fixture's per prompt: 5, 6, 9, 7, 8, 17, 17, 10, 12, 8, 17, 14, 15,
13, 7). The tokenizer crate with the qwen2 pre-tokenizer pattern
reproduces llama.cpp's reference tokenization of this vocab exactly,
including single-digit tokens, accented text, and code.

Completions are coherent, on-topic continuations throughout, and
several track the golden trajectory for many steps before forking
(code_python 11 tokens, list_counting 15, factual_capital 5). Every
prompt eventually forks. First divergent completion token per prompt
(pieces from the model's vocab):

| Prompt | Index | Golden id (piece) | Candidate id (piece) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| factual_capital | 5 | 15344 (" Italy") | 279 (" the") |
| factual_science | 3 | 11 (",") | 13 (".") |
| factual_history | 0 | 33121 (" Neil") | 32671 (" ______") |
| arithmetic_add | 0 | 220 (" ") | 488 (" +") |
| arithmetic_divide | 2 | 17 ("2") | 16 ("1") |
| arithmetic_word | 0 | 510 (":\n") | 220 (" ") |
| code_python | 11 | 77 ("n") | 750 ("def") |
| code_go | 2 | 11009 ("\tfmt") | 92 ("}") |

| list_counting | 15 | 16 ("1") | 11 (",") |
| accented_french | 0 | 7906 (" au") | 7814 (" bon") |
| accented_german | 0 | 1863 (" Z") | 98886 (" Wien") |
| accented_spanish | 0 | 668 (" ab") | 24249 (" casa") |
| continuation_classic | 2 | 624 (".\n") | 13 (".") |

### Logit-level diagnosis (probe evidence)

A throwaway probe (not committed) fed fixture token ids directly to
both engines, so the tokenizer cannot be the cause of what follows.

Prefix sweep on the arithmetic_add prompt "17 + 25 =" (ids
16 22 488 220 17 20 284), top-1 prediction per prefix length:

| Prefix | llama.cpp top-1 | arch-llama top-1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "1" | 24 | 24 (agree) |
| "17" | 13 | 13 (agree) |
| "17 +" | 220 (" ") | 488 (" +", the last prompt token) |
| "17 + " | 16 ("1") | 488 (" +") |
| "17 + 2" | 15 | 15 (agree) |
| "17 + 25" | 284 (" =") | 488 (" +") |
| "17 + 25 =" | 220 (" ") | 488 (" +") |

The same pathology reproduces with "17 -" (ids 16 22 481): llama.cpp
predicts " " (220) first and does not rank 481 in its top 5;
arch-llama's top prediction is 481 itself, the operator just seen.

Measured gaps at three contexts:

- factual_history, prompt only: llama.cpp ranks " Neil" first with
  " ______" 0.207 logprob behind. arch-llama ranks " ______" first
  with " Neil" 0.095 behind. Same top-2 pair, order flipped: a
  near-tie flip, swing about 0.3 logits.
- factual_capital after the 5 shared tokens "...Paris. The capital
  of": llama.cpp ranks " Italy" first, " the" 0.90 behind.
  arch-llama ranks " the" first, " Italy" 2.02 behind. Same
  candidate set near the top; swing 1 to 3 logits.
- arithmetic_add, full prompt: llama.cpp ranks " " first by 2.43
  logprob, with " +" outside its top 10 (more than 5.5 behind).
  arch-llama ranks " +" first, with " " outside its top 10 (more
  than 3.8 behind). Not explainable by accumulation noise.

Diagnosis: cause class is a forward math discrepancy in the
attention/residual pathway. The visible signature is that the engine
over-boosts a salient in-context token (the operator 488 " +" or
481 " -") and predicts its repetition where the reference predicts
a continuation, from the third context token onward, with logit
swings between roughly 0.3 and over 5 depending on context. Ruled
out by the evidence: tokenization (prompt ids identical; the probe
bypasses the tokenizer), EOS handling (both engines' stop behavior
verified separately; the Qwen file declares EOS 151645 while golden
records stop on 151643, and the runner's stop set covers both),
bias handling (Qwen2 biases are exercised in the agreeing contexts
too), and any gross RoPE or config error (short factual contexts
land within 0.3 logits of the reference with the same top
candidates). Not fixed in this run: the black-box evidence does not
isolate the discrepancy to one unambiguous line, and guessing at
attention internals would violate the no-silent-fix rule. Follow-up:
layer-by-layer activation diffing against llama.cpp on the
arithmetic_add prefix (first departing layer localizes the step).

## TinyLlama-1.1B: tokenizer family gap, forward untested

Every prompt diverges at prompt-token index 1 (index 0, the BOS,
matches). The file's vocab is SentencePiece-style BPE: word pieces
carry the "▁" marker (450 "▁The", 29871 "▁") and its 61,249 merges
operate over those pieces. The tokenizer crate implements GPT-2
style byte-level BPE only, so its symbols never match this vocab's
merges and encoding falls back to near-byte pieces: for example
golden 450 ("▁The") vs candidate 1576 ("The") on the factual
prompts, golden 29871 ("▁") vs candidate 29896 ("1") on the
arithmetic prompts. Candidate prompt lengths balloon accordingly
(11 to 41 ids vs the fixture's 6 to 18).

Generation therefore ran on a byte-piece context the model was not
trained on; completions diverge from token 0 on 13 of 15 prompts
and the run says nothing about the arch-llama llama forward, for or
against. Diagnosis: tokenization, family not implemented. The fix
is a second tokenizer family (SentencePiece BPE over the file's own
pieces and merges) in the tokenizer crate, after which this fixture
becomes a real forward test. Not attempted here: a new tokenizer
family is a feature, not an unambiguous small fix.

## Runner fidelity notes

The runner mirrors two llama.cpp behaviors that the fixtures
proved: when tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token is absent from the file
(the TinyLlama case), BOS follows the family default (llama adds
BOS, gpt2 does not); and the stop set is the declared EOS plus the
<|endoftext|> token when present in the vocab, because the Qwen
fixtures stop on 151643 although the file declares 151645.
Candidate records carry the fixture fields (prompt_token_ids,
completion_token_ids, completion_text) and are written
incrementally, one flushed line per finished prompt.

## Files

- Runner: crates/arch-llama/examples/golden_run.rs
- Candidates: golden/candidates/qwen2.5-1.5b-q4km.candidate.jsonl,
  golden/candidates/tinyllama-1.1b-chat-v1.0.Q4_K_M.candidate.jsonl
- Diffs: python3 golden/compare.py <fixture> <candidate> (and
  --strict); both models exit 1 with the summaries above.

# Layer diff: Muse-Glimmer-30B forward vs llama.cpp, stage by stage

Date: 2026-11-05. Executes FORWARD-DIFF-PLAN.md
(`crates/itak-loader/FORWARD-DIFF-PLAN.md`), the localization plan
written after Integration Run B: our side of the diff (the
muse-glimmer trace tooling) was built on lane-01-forward-diff but
never merged, and the reference side (a llama.cpp per-layer
activation dump for Glimmer) never existed. Both sides now exist
and have been run against each other. This file is the Glimmer
sibling of `RESULTS-layer-diff-qwen.md` and is filed beside it for
that reason.

## Provenance

- Model: `/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf`
  (the production Q4_K_M file), on ubuntu-server.
- Prompt: the golden `factual_capital` prompt, "The capital of
  France is", tokenized as Run B tokenized it (BOS per the file's
  metadata): ids [200000, 954, 7963, 323, 11698, 373]. Both sides
  consumed exactly these ids; our side prints the match, the
  reference side took them as a literal argument.
- Our side: `crates/itak-loader/examples/glimmer_layer_trace.rs`
  over `GlimmerModel::forward_traced` (muse-glimmer `trace`
  module, ported from lane-01 onto current main in this branch;
  stage semantics follow current main's forward: `embed` is the
  residual after the weightless embedding norm, `layer.<i>.mid`
  is the residual after the attention half with the post-attention
  norm applied to the branch output before the residual add,
  `layer.<i>.out` the same for the FFN half). CPU compute backend,
  one prefill, 107 trace lines.
- Reference side: `golden/tools/cb_dump_glimmer.cpp`, a sibling of
  the proven `cb_dump.cpp`, built against the server's llama.cpp
  tree (`/home/server/llama.cpp`, build-vulkan2 libraries), CPU
  only (n_gpu_layers = 0), one prefill via `llama_decode` with the
  `cb_eval` callback copying the named graph tensors to .bin
  files. The production Glimmer server stayed down and untouched;
  nothing bound port 8080; the Qwen3-Embedding tenants were not
  touched.
- Diff: `golden/tools/compare_traces.py` reduces the reference
  bins to the trace's statistics (mean, population variance, max
  abs, first values; whole tensor and last row, computed in f64)
  and applies the plan's reading rules: a stage matches when mean
  and variance agree to roughly 1e-2 relative (means judged in
  units of the stream's own standard deviation, variances
  relatively), last row first, whole tensor second. The first
  stage whose input stage matched but which does not itself match
  is the defect's home.

## Tensor name mapping (read from the graph source)

Read from `/home/server/llama.cpp/src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp`
(201 lines) on 2026-11-05:

- `inp_embd` (build_inp_embd output) dumped as `embd_raw`, info
  only.
- Line 69-70: `inpL = build_norm(inpL, nullptr, nullptr,
  LLM_NORM_RMS, -1)` (weightless) then `cb(inpL, "embd_norm", -1)`:
  the post-embedding-norm residual, dumped as our `embed` stage.
- Line 150-151: `ffn_inp = ggml_add(cur, inpSA)` then
  `cb(ffn_inp, "ffn_inp", il)`: the residual after the attention
  half, our `layer.<i>.mid`. Lines 141-142 show the post-attention
  norm is `ggml_rms_norm` (eps hardcoded 1e-8, line 66) followed
  by `ggml_mul` with the post-norm weight, applied to the branch
  BEFORE the add: the same placement current main implements.
- Line 170-172: after the FFN post norm (lines 166-167, same
  shape), `cur = ggml_add(cur, ffn_inp)`, `cb(cur, "l_out", il)`:
  our `layer.<i>.out`.
- Line 180-181: final `build_norm` with `output_norm`,
  `cb(cur, "result_norm", -1)`: our `final_norm` (last position
  reduced).
- Line 185-195: `build_lora_mm(model.output)`, `ggml_scale` by
  the logit scale, then the softcap (scale by 1/cap, tanh, scale
  by cap), `cb(cur, "result_output", -1)`: our `logits` (last
  position reduced). Scale-then-softcap, the same order current
  main's `softcap_scale` implements.

Two plan hypotheses are settled by this source read alone, before
any numbers: hypothesis 1 (norm convention): line 90's comment
states the pre-attention norm's "(weight+1) folded at conversion
time", so the reference applies plain `x * w` RMSNorm to the
stored weights, as ours does. Hypothesis 4 (RoPE geometry): line
86-87, RoPE runs on the SWA layers only (`use_rope =
hparams.is_swa(il)`), matching our sliding/global split.

## Results

Self-checks first, per the plan: our side printed
`prompt_ids=[200000, 954, 7963, 323, 11698, 373]` with
`run_b_ids_match=true`, coverage 731/731 tensors, and exactly 107
trace lines. The reference side took the same ids as a literal
argument and its own sanity line (top-1 from the public logits
API) agrees with its dump: id 13796 at 17.3194. Run times: our
traced prefill 1,464 s on the CPU backend (24m38s wall for the
whole example); the reference dump 12 s. The server session ran
under the overnight phase lock, queued behind the other lanes.

Every one of the 106 stages from `embed` through `final_norm`
matches under the plan's reading rules. The worst last-row
variance disagreement anywhere in the stack is 9.6e-3 relative
(layer.39.mid), under the 1e-2 bar; mean shifts never exceed
5.8e-4 of a standard deviation. `embed` is essentially exact
(variance relative diff 3.2e-8), which kills hypothesis 0
(embedding handling) outright. Summary rows (last-row statistics;
mean shift in units of the stream's standard deviation):

| stage | mean shift (std) | var rel diff | whole-tensor var rel |
|---|---|---|---|
| embed | 3.8e-10 | 3.2e-08 | 1.7e-08 |
| layer.0.mid | 1.0e-04 | 6.0e-04 | 1.6e-03 |
| layer.0.out | 2.0e-04 | 3.6e-03 | 2.0e-03 |
| layer.26.out | 2.4e-04 | 3.7e-04 | 1.7e-03 |
| layer.51.out | 3.9e-04 | 6.8e-03 | 2.0e-03 |
| final_norm | 2.7e-04 | 7.5e-03 | 7.5e-03 |
| logits | 1.7e-02 | 3.0e-03 | 3.0e-03 |

The full 107-row table is `compare.txt` in the server staging
(`~/overnight-forward-diff/`); the comparison script prints it on
any rerun from the two dumps.

At `logits` the strict judge flags one metric over the bar (mean
shift 1.7e-2 of a standard deviation; the variance agrees to
3.0e-3). The substance underneath the flag: both sides put token
13796 (" Paris") on top, and the same five tokens hold the top
five slots (the 5th slot differs by 0.014 of a logit, a tie for
practical purposes). Per-token logit differences are small and
signed both ways (13796: +0.0245; 262: -0.0088; 290: -0.0404;
1085: +0.0133), so this is neither a uniform shift nor a scale
error. Top-1 probability: ours 0.403462, reference 0.396118.

One observation from our run's diagnostic stream, recorded for
completeness: the loader logged two metadata events
(`muse-glimmer.attention.sliding_window_pattern` type mismatch,
`muse-glimmer.rope.freq_base_swa` missing) and proceeded on its
fallbacks. The stage statistics above prove the values those
fallbacks produced agree with the reference graph at every layer,
so they are not implicated in anything this diff measured.

## Verdict

**No layer diverges. The forward's layer math is llama.cpp's.**
All 106 pre-logits stages match within the plan's tolerance, so
none of the plan's layer-level hypotheses (0 embedding handling,
1 norm convention, 2 post-norm and gate placement, 3 QK-norm,
4 RoPE geometry) is live: each is decided "same as the
reference" by the stage that was assigned to decide it, and
hypotheses 1 and 4 were additionally settled by the graph source
read above before any numbers ran.

The only remaining difference is at the `logits` stage itself,
and it is exactly the known first-token residue, now measured
end to end: same argmax, same top-5 set, top-1 probability
0.403462 (ours) against 0.396118 (llama.cpp), produced by small
token-dependent logit differences of a few hundredths. With
`final_norm` (the lm_head's input) matching, that residue lives
in the finishing path: the lm_head's accumulation over the
6656-wide dot product (summation order and intermediate
precision differ between the two engines) and its interaction
with the scale-and-softcap finish. It is a finishing-math
question, not a layer question, and this diff closes the layer
question for good. Localizing inside the head (for example,
comparing the pre-softcap logits or accumulating the head in
f64) is a separate, smaller follow-up; per this task's scope no
forward code was changed.

===== FILE: golden/RESULTS-layer-diff-qwen.md =====
# Layer diff: Qwen2.5-1.5B forward divergence localized and fixed

Date: 2026-10-29. Follow-up to integration run A
(`RESULTS-integration-a.md`), which proved Qwen2.5-1.5B tokenization
exact (15/15 prompt ids) but found the arch-llama forward diverging
from llama.cpp: a salient in-context token (the operator 488 " +")
was over-boosted and predicted as its own continuation, with logit
swings of 0.3 to over 5 from the third context token onward.

## Method

Both engines dumped per-layer activations for one prefill of the
arithmetic_add prefix ids [16, 22, 488, 220] ("17 + "), the shortest
context where run A's probe showed disagreement.

- llama.cpp side: `golden/tools/cb_dump.cpp`, a raw llama.h harness
  whose `cb_eval` callback copies the named graph tensors
  (`attn_norm`, `Qcur`, `Kcur`, `Vcur`, `ffn_inp`, `ffn_norm`,
  `ffn_out`, `l_out`, `result_norm`, `result_output`) to .bin files.
  CPU only (n_gpu_layers = 0); the production Glimmer server was
  not touched. Logits were enabled on all four positions so the
  last layer's intermediates stay unsliced.
- arch-llama side: `LlamaModel::forward_traced` (same code path as
  `forward`, sub-step buffers cloned out as they pass) plus the
  `crates/arch-llama/examples/layer_dump.rs` runner.
- Diff: `golden/tools/compare_layers.py` (max-abs and cosine per
  checkpoint, per-position breakdown for `l_out`, and a RoPE
  pairing experiment described below).

One harness trap worth recording: in this llama.cpp version Qcur's
ggml dims are [head_dim, rows, heads] (the rope node views Q
token-major), so its flat dump is [heads][rows][head_dim], while
Kcur is a flat [k_width, rows]. Reading Qcur as [rows][heads][dim]
scrambles it and mimics a broken Q projection (cosine 0.19);
read correctly, the projection is exact. `compare_layers.py`
encodes the correct reading.

## Localization

With the prefix above, before the fix:

| Checkpoint | max_abs | cosine |
| --- | --- | --- |
| embd | 0.000000 | 1.000000 |
| L00_attn_norm | 0.000001 | 1.000000 |
| L00_q | 106.48 | 0.1887 |
| L00_k | 9.90 | 0.9999 |
| L00_v | 0.027 | 0.9999 |
| L00_ffn_inp | 0.351 | 0.9826 |
| L00_l_out | 1.417 | 0.9433 |

The first divergent checkpoint is layer 0's Q, and the split
between Q/K on one side and V on the other is the fingerprint:
embedding, RMSNorm, all three projections, and biases are proven
by `attn_norm` (1e-6) and `v` (the un-rotated projection, at the
quant-kernel noise floor). Only the rotated tensors diverge, so
the defect sits in the rotation step, before attention mixes
anything. Downstream, L01_ffn_out already shows max_abs 2865: the
error amplifies through the stack exactly as run A's logit swings
said it should.

## Root cause

**RoPE pairing.** `torch_math::rope` paired adjacent channels
(2i, 2i+1) (ggml's NORM pairing) while its own doc comment claimed
it was applying the GPT-NeoX pairing. llama.cpp rotates qwen2 (and
llama) with ggml's NEOX pairing: pair i joins channels i and
i + head_dim/2, at the same frequency schedule base^(-2i/head_dim).

Proof, from the layer-0 dumps alone (identical input, proven
above): re-rotating this crate's pre-RoPE Q and K dumps offline
under each pairing and comparing against llama.cpp's Qcur/Kcur:

| Tensor | NEOX (half-split) | interleaved (as built) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L00 Q | max_abs 0.090, cos 0.999996 | max_abs 82.2, cos 0.948 |
| L00 K | max_abs 0.078, cos 1.000000 | max_abs 9.90, cos 0.9999 |

NEOX lands exactly on the quant noise floor set by V (0.027) and
by position 0, where rotation is the identity in any convention
(0.090). Interleaved is two to three orders of magnitude off.
Ruled out on the way: the fused-vs-split QKV question (this file
carries no `attn_qkv.weight`; both engines read the split tensors),
attention scale (1/sqrt(head_dim) on both sides), QK norms (qwen2
has none), per-layer config (eps 1e-6 and RoPE base 1e6 are read
from the file and reproduce in the meta dump), and the
decode-versus-prefill cache path (run A reproduced the divergence
in pure prefill probes).

Why the symptom looked like "attention over-boosts the last
token": with channels paired wrongly, each pair rotates at the
wrong frequency, so the relative-position structure of Q.K is
scrambled; the surviving signal is dominated by position-local
similarity, and the model repeats the salient operator. Position 0
is unaffected (identity rotation) and short contexts stay near the
reference, which is why run A saw agreement at prefix lengths 1, 2
and 5 but divergence at 3 and 4.

## The fix

`crates/torch-math/src/rope.rs`: `rope` / `rope_partial` now pair
(i, i + rotary_dim/2). The adjacent pairing survives as the
separately named `rope_interleaved`, because it is not wrong in
itself: llama.cpp selects NORM pairing for muse-glimmer (the Run B
follow-up settled that from `src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp`, and
cpu-compute's Glimmer path calls `rope_interleaved` for exactly
that reason). Pairing is a per-architecture convention, and the
two functions now carry the two names instead of one function
carrying the wrong one silently. The rope unit tests were updated
to values that distinguish the pairings (they previously encoded
the same wrong assumption as the code). torch-math: 42 passed.
arch-llama: 23 passed.

Note for the Glimmer line: this fix changes nothing on the
cpu-compute path (it never called `rope`), so run B's divergence
has a different cause; but any future arch module that reaches for
`torch_math::rope` now gets the llama/qwen2 convention by default,
which is the one the name was always supposed to mean.

## Verification after the fix

Same prefix, same harness, arch-llama rebuilt with the fix:

- Layer 0 is at the noise floor at every checkpoint (max_abs
  0.027 to 0.090, cosine >= 0.9993). Logits for the last position:
  top-5 identical in set, order, and value within 0.08
  (llama 21.404 / ours 21.324 for the winner); whole-vocab max_abs
  0.47, cosine 0.9989. The residual is accumulated Q4_K
  dequant-vs-ggml-kernel noise: its worst single element sits on a
  known outlier channel (L01_ffn_out: -2916.20 vs -2903.41, 0.44%
  relative), and it grows smoothly with depth instead of stepping
  at any layer or sub-step.
- Run A's probe cases, re-run as prefills (top-1):
  - "17 +" [16, 22, 488]: ours 220 (" "), llama.cpp 220. Was 488.
  - "17 -" [16, 22, 481]: ours 220 (" "), llama.cpp 220. Was 481.
  - factual_capital fork context (prompt + the 5 shared completion
    tokens): ours 15344 (" Italy"), golden 15344. Was 279 (" the").
- Full golden re-run (15 prompts, 64 tokens, greedy;
  `golden/candidates/qwen2.5-1.5b-q4km.fixed.candidate.jsonl`):
  **9/15 token-identical**, up from 0/15 in run A. The six
  remaining forks are late (first divergence at completion index
  2, 4, 8, 12, 20) or at a measured near-tie: for accented_spanish
  (fork at index 0) llama.cpp's own margin between its winner
  (668, logit 15.289) and our pick (10919, 15.094 in llama.cpp's
  logits) is 0.195 logits, while the cross-engine logit noise on
  that prompt measures up to 0.78 max (the top cluster sits within
  0.23 on both sides). A 0.195 margin inside a ~0.5 noise band is
  a coin flip, not a systematic error; the layer diff above shows
  no second math divergence for it to come from. Full 15/15 over
  64 greedy steps would require reproducing ggml's quantized
  kernels bit-for-bit, which an f32-dequantize reference does not
  do and run A's fixture comparison was never going to show once
  the real bug was gone.

## Files

- Harness: `golden/tools/cb_dump.cpp`,
  `golden/tools/compare_layers.py`,
  `crates/arch-llama/examples/layer_dump.rs` (runner),
  `crates/gguf/examples/qkv_probe.rs` (the fused-vs-split probe
  that cleared the tensor-source question),
  `LlamaModel::forward_traced` in `crates/arch-llama/src/model.rs`.
- Fix: `crates/torch-math/src/rope.rs`.

## Follow-up: pairing is per-architecture (the llama half of the claim above was wrong)

The root-cause section above says llama.cpp rotates "qwen2 (and
llama)" with NEOX. The qwen2 half is proven by the layer diff;
the llama half was asserted, not measured, and it is wrong.
llama.cpp's own table (`llama_model_rope_type` in
src/llama-model.cpp) maps `LLM_ARCH_LLAMA` to
`LLAMA_ROPE_TYPE_NORM` (adjacent), `LLM_ARCH_QWEN2` to
`LLAMA_ROPE_TYPE_NEOX` (half-split), `LLM_ARCH_MUSE_GLIMMER` to
NORM. Because 13643e0 flipped the one shared function
arch-llama calls for both architectures, it fixed qwen2 and
regressed TinyLlama from 6/15 to 0/15 token-identical in the
same edit; the TinyLlama re-run note
(`RESULTS-tinyllama-spm.md`, regression follow-up) caught it.

The structural fix has now landed: `LlamaConfig::rope_pairing`
(`crates/arch-llama/src/config.rs`) is the one place the mapping
lives, selecting `RopePairing::Interleaved` for llama and
`RopePairing::HalfSplit` for qwen2 from the file's own
architecture string, and refusing an unmapped architecture with
the named error `LlamaError::RopePairingUnknown`. `rope_rows`
dispatches on it; the interleaved partial-rotary form it needs
is `torch_math::rope_interleaved_partial`. The doc comment in
`crates/torch-math/src/rope.rs` that carried the wrong "llama
and qwen2" claim has been corrected to match.

### Re-run (this file's model)

Same conditions as the verification above: David's
ubuntu-server, release build, RUSTFLAGS target-cpu=x86-64-v3,
CPU only, runner `crates/arch-llama/examples/golden_run.rs`,
greedy, 64 tokens max. Production Glimmer llama-server
untouched (health check after both re-runs: `{"status":"ok"}`,
still on its original pid). Wall time 971.7 s.

| Model | Token-identical | Text-identical | Divergent | Missing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B Q4_K_M | 9 / 15 | 0 / 15 | 6 | 0 |

**9/15 holds exactly.** Stronger: the per-arch candidate is
token-for-token identical to this note's `.fixed` candidate on
all 15 prompts: same nine token-identical prompts, same six
fork points (factual_history 4, code_python 2, list_colors 8,
accented_french 12, accented_german 20, accented_spanish 0).
The dispatch is a pure no-op on the qwen2 path, as designed: it
routes to the same `rope_partial` with the same arguments, and
the paired TinyLlama re-run proves the other branch restores
that model's pre-regression trajectories exactly. Neither
model is below its best-known state, so the fix ships with
both fixtures guarding their own direction again.

### Files (per-arch fix)

- Candidate: `golden/candidates/qwen2.5-1.5b-q4km.perarch.candidate.jsonl`
- Fix: `crates/arch-llama/src/config.rs`, `crates/arch-llama/src/model.rs`,

# TinyLlama re-run with the SentencePiece tokenizer family

Follow-up to `RESULTS-integration-a.md`, whose TinyLlama half was
blocked on a tokenizer family gap: the file's vocabulary is
SentencePiece BPE and the tokenizer crate implemented only GPT-2
byte-level BPE, so every prompt diverged at prompt-token index 1
and the run said nothing about the forward.

The SentencePiece family is now implemented in the tokenizer crate
(`crates/tokenizer/src/spm.rs`, a port of llama.cpp's SPM path with
rules cited to `llama-vocab.cpp`; family selected from the file's
own `tokenizer.ggml.model`, scores plumbed from
`tokenizer.ggml.scores` through the gguf crate and the `.tokdata`
format v2). Tokenizer-level proof is
`crates/tokenizer/tests/spm_golden.rs`: all 15 golden prompt id
sequences reproduced exactly, all 15 fixture completion texts
reproduced by decode. See `crates/tokenizer/CONFORMANCE.md`.

## Generation re-run

Same conditions as Run A: David's ubuntu-server, release build,
RUSTFLAGS target-cpu=x86-64-v3, CPU only, runner
`crates/arch-llama/examples/golden_run.rs`, greedy, 64 tokens max.
Production Glimmer llama-server untouched (verified still on its
original pid 683675 after the run). Wall time 787.8 s for the full
15 prompts. The runner log confirms the family was selected from
the file: `tokenizer: model=llama pre=<absent> vocab=32000`.

Prompt tokenization now matches the fixture on all 15 prompts
(candidate prompt lengths 6, 7, 10, 9, 10, 19, 24, 16, 18, 15, 19,
16, 15, 17, 10; the Run A candidate had ballooned to 11..41 ids).
