### Fork table with llama.cpp's own margins

Margins were measured by feeding each fork's golden prefix
(prompt ids + golden completion ids before the fork) to a
throwaway CPU llama-server (same binary and flags as
`gen_golden.py`) with `n_probs=5` and reading the winner's
logprob gap over the best other token at that position
(`golden/tools/fork_margins.py`). The band column compares
against the cross-engine noise band the Qwen note measured
(up to ~0.78 logits); that band was measured on Qwen2.5-1.5B,
not on this model, so it is a reference scale, not a
TinyLlama-measured bound.

| Prompt | Fork index | Golden id | Candidate id | llama.cpp winner margin (logits) | vs 0.78 band | Candidate in llama.cpp top-5 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| factual_capital | 0 | 3681 | 278 | 0.519 | within | no |
| factual_science | 1 | 29889 | 29906 | 0.586 | within | yes (gap 1.493) |
| factual_history | 0 | 29334 | 263 | 2.041 | exceeds | no |
| arithmetic_add | 1 | 29946 | 29896 | 0.925 | exceeds | no |
| arithmetic_divide | 2 | 29946 | 29900 | 0.453 | within | no |
| arithmetic_word | 1 | 29953 | 29896 | 0.416 | within | no |
| code_python | 0 | 18755 | 302 | 3.137 | exceeds | yes (gap 3.137) |
| code_go | 7 | 13 | 28956 | 5.190 | exceeds | no |
| list_colors | 0 | 301 | 322 | 1.212 | exceeds | no |
| list_days | 1 | 24211 | 278 | 0.466 | within | yes (gap 4.223) |
| list_counting | 4 | 29947 | 29896 | 7.403 | exceeds | yes (gap 7.403) |

| accented_spanish | 0 | 1208 | 274 | 0.602 | within | no |
| continuation_classic | 0 | 17366 | 18786 | 4.177 | exceeds | no |

Eight forks exceed the band outright. At the seven within-band
forks the candidate token still sits outside llama.cpp's top-5
in six cases, and 1.49 to 4.22 logits behind the winner in the
rest: the engine did not pick a near-tie runner-up, it picked
tokens llama.cpp ranks far down. The forks are a systematic
error, not cross-engine noise, which the root cause below
confirms directly.

### Root cause: RoPE pairing is per-architecture; 13643e0 generalized qwen2's

llama.cpp's own source settles the pairing per architecture
(`llama_model_rope_type` in `src/llama-model.cpp`, the build
that generated the fixtures): `LLM_ARCH_LLAMA` returns
`LLAMA_ROPE_TYPE_NORM` (adjacent pairs), `LLM_ARCH_QWEN2`
returns `LLAMA_ROPE_TYPE_NEOX` (half-split), and
`LLM_ARCH_MUSE_GLIMMER` returns NORM. The 13643e0 commit
message asserts NEOX for "qwen2/llama"; the llama half of that
claim is wrong. The commit changed the one shared pairing
function arch-llama calls for both architectures, so it fixed
qwen2 and broke llama in the same edit.

Two cross-checks isolate the cause to the pairing, not to this
re-run's build or staging:

- The layer-diff agent's own post-fix `golden_run` binary,
  run on TinyLlama for the single prompt factual_capital,
  produces the identical wrong trajectory head
  ([278, 4272, 310, 3681, ...], " the city of Paris...") as
  this re-run's candidate.
- A discriminator experiment in the server staging copy only
  (never committed): the arch-llama call site in `rope_rows`
  was temporarily switched to `torch_math::rope_interleaved`
  for the full-rotary case (this file's rope_dim equals its
  head_dim), and factual_capital returned to fully
  token-identical over all 64 tokens, exactly as in the SPM
  run above.

The fix this names, not landed here: arch-llama must select
the pairing from the file's architecture at the call site,
the same structural rule the Glimmer backend already follows
(`rope_interleaved`'s module docs): `llama` takes the
interleaved pairing (a partial-rotary variant is needed for
llama-arch files whose rope_dim is below the head dim),
`qwen2` keeps the NEOX `rope_partial` from 13643e0. Until the
pairing is per-architecture, the two golden fixtures guard
opposite directions and either arch can regress silently
behind the other's fix.

### Files (this follow-up)

- Candidate: `golden/candidates/tinyllama-1.1b-chat-v1.0.Q4_K_M.fixed.candidate.jsonl`
- Margin probe: `golden/tools/fork_margins.py` (one-off
  analysis; margins above are its output, reproducible from
  the fixture and candidate)

## Per-architecture pairing fix: regression closed

The fix the section above named has landed. Pairing is now
selected in exactly one place from the file's own architecture
string: `LlamaConfig::rope_pairing` in
`crates/arch-llama/src/config.rs`, which maps `llama` to
`RopePairing::Interleaved` and `qwen2` to `RopePairing::HalfSplit`
(citing `llama_model_rope_type` in llama.cpp's
src/llama-model.cpp) and refuses any other architecture with the
named error `LlamaError::RopePairingUnknown` instead of guessing.
`rope_rows` in `crates/arch-llama/src/model.rs` dispatches on it;
the interleaved side needed a partial-rotary form, added as
`torch_math::rope_interleaved_partial` (adjacent pairs over the
first `rope_dim` channels, tail passed through, frequency
denominator `rotary_dim`, the same partial convention as
`rope_partial`). The muse-glimmer path is untouched: it already
called `rope_interleaved` by name. Selection is pinned by tests:
config-level (llama parses to Interleaved, qwen2 to HalfSplit, an
unmapped architecture is refused by name), call-site level
(`rope_rows` output equals the named torch-math function per
architecture, including a partial-rotary llama config), and a
full-forward KV proof over the partial interleaved path.
torch-math 44 passed, arch-llama 29 passed, clippy clean.

### Re-run

Same conditions as before: David's ubuntu-server, release build,
RUSTFLAGS target-cpu=x86-64-v3, CPU only, runner
`crates/arch-llama/examples/golden_run.rs`, greedy, 64 tokens max.
Production Glimmer llama-server untouched (health check after
the runs: ok; see the Qwen follow-up in
`RESULTS-layer-diff-qwen.md` for the paired re-run). Wall time
705.3 s for the full 15 prompts. Prompt tokenization exact on
all 15, as in the SPM run.

| Model | Token-identical | Text-identical | Divergent | Missing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TinyLlama-1.1B Q4_K_M | 6 / 15 | 0 / 15 | 9 | 0 |

Back to the pre-regression headline, and stronger than the
headline: the candidate is token-for-token identical to the SPM
run's candidate on all 15 prompts, fork for fork (factual_science
29, factual_history 31, arithmetic_add 4, arithmetic_divide 39,
arithmetic_word 23, code_go 0, accented_french 34,
accented_spanish 17, continuation_classic 23), with the same six
prompts fully token-identical (factual_capital, code_python,
list_colors, list_days, list_counting, accented_german). The
pre-regression trajectories are reproduced exactly, this time by
explicit per-architecture selection rather than by the shared
function happening to hold llama's pairing. The nine remaining
forks are the forward's known state after the SPM run (coherent,
late forks; the Qwen half of the same story is in
`RESULTS-layer-diff-qwen.md`), not pairing damage: the regressed
run's fork-at-0/1 pattern is gone entirely.

===== FILE: golden/compare.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Diff an engine's generation output against llama.cpp golden fixtures.

Usage:
    compare.py GOLDEN.jsonl CANDIDATE.jsonl [--strict]

Both files are JSONL in the golden fixture shape written by gen_golden.sh:
an optional first line {"meta": {...}} followed by one record per prompt:

    {"id": ..., "prompt": ...,
     "prompt_token_ids": [...],
     "completion_token_ids": [...],
     "completion_text": "..."}

Per prompt the verdict is one of:

    token-identical   completion token ids match the golden ids exactly
    text-identical    ids differ but the completion text matches exactly
    divergent         neither matches; the first divergence is reported
                      in token space (index, golden id vs candidate id)
                      and in text space (character offset)
    missing           the candidate has no record for this prompt

Exit code is 0 when every prompt is token-identical or text-identical,
1 otherwise. With --strict, text-identical also fails: verified text
(TODO T-9.4) means token-identical at temperature 0.

Standard library only, so this runs anywhere python3 does.
"""

import json
import sys


def load_records(path):
    meta = None
    records = {}
    order = []
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            obj = json.loads(line)
            if "meta" in obj and "id" not in obj:
                meta = obj["meta"]
                continue
            records[obj["id"]] = obj
            order.append(obj["id"])
    return meta, records, order


def first_token_divergence(golden_ids, cand_ids):
    """Return (index, golden_id_or_None, cand_id_or_None) of first mismatch."""
    n = min(len(golden_ids), len(cand_ids))
    for i in range(n):
        if golden_ids[i] != cand_ids[i]:
            return i, golden_ids[i], cand_ids[i]
    if len(golden_ids) != len(cand_ids):
        g = golden_ids[n] if n < len(golden_ids) else None
        c = cand_ids[n] if n < len(cand_ids) else None
        return n, g, c
    return None


def first_text_divergence(golden_text, cand_text):
    n = min(len(golden_text), len(cand_text))
    for i in range(n):
        if golden_text[i] != cand_text[i]:
            return i
    if len(golden_text) != len(cand_text):
        return n
    return None


def fmt_tok(t):
    return "EOS/end" if t is None else str(t)


def main(argv):
    args = [a for a in argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
    strict = "--strict" in argv
    if len(args) != 2:
        print(__doc__)
        return 2
    golden_path, cand_path = args
    _, golden, order = load_records(golden_path)
    _, cand, _ = load_records(cand_path)

    counts = {"token-identical": 0, "text-identical": 0, "divergent": 0, "missing": 0}
    for pid in order:
        g = golden[pid]
        c = cand.get(pid)
        if c is None:
            counts["missing"] += 1
            print(f"{pid}: missing (no candidate record)")
            continue

        notes = []
        if c.get("prompt_token_ids") != g["prompt_token_ids"]:
            div = first_token_divergence(g["prompt_token_ids"], c.get("prompt_token_ids", []))
            notes.append(
                f"prompt tokenization differs at index {div[0]} "
                f"(golden {fmt_tok(div[1])} vs candidate {fmt_tok(div[2])})"
            )

        g_ids, c_ids = g["completion_token_ids"], c["completion_token_ids"]
        if g_ids == c_ids:
            verdict = "token-identical"
        elif g["completion_text"] == c["completion_text"]:
            verdict = "text-identical"
            div = first_token_divergence(g_ids, c_ids)
            notes.append(
                f"first token divergence at index {div[0]} "
                f"(golden {fmt_tok(div[1])} vs candidate {fmt_tok(div[2])}), text still identical"
            )
        else:
            verdict = "divergent"
            div = first_token_divergence(g_ids, c_ids)
            if div is not None:
                notes.append(
                    f"first token divergence at index {div[0]} "
                    f"(golden {fmt_tok(div[1])} vs candidate {fmt_tok(div[2])})"
                )
            tdiv = first_text_divergence(g["completion_text"], c["completion_text"])
            if tdiv is not None:
                g_ctx = g["completion_text"][max(0, tdiv - 20):tdiv + 20]
                c_ctx = c["completion_text"][max(0, tdiv - 20):tdiv + 20]
                notes.append(f"first text divergence at char {tdiv}: golden ...{g_ctx!r} vs candidate ...{c_ctx!r}")

        counts[verdict] += 1
        suffix = "; ".join(notes)
        print(f"{pid}: {verdict}" + (f" ({suffix})" if suffix else ""))

    extra = [pid for pid in cand if pid not in golden]
    if extra:
        print(f"warning: candidate has {len(extra)} record(s) not in golden: {', '.join(extra)}")

    total = len(order)
    print(
        f"summary: {counts['token-identical']}/{total} token-identical, "
        f"{counts['text-identical']} text-identical, "
        f"{counts['divergent']} divergent, {counts['missing']} missing"
    )
    ok = counts["divergent"] == 0 and counts["missing"] == 0
    if strict:
        ok = ok and counts["text-identical"] == 0
    return 0 if ok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

===== END FILE: golden/compare.py =====

===== FILE: golden/gen_first_token_probs.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""First-token top-5 probability golden (TODO T-9.3 reference).

For each prompt in the golden prompt set this records the top 5
candidate first tokens with their probabilities, as reported by a
throwaway CPU llama-server (/completion, n_predict=1, n_probs=5,
temperature 0). The probabilities are PRE-sampling (logit)
probabilities: the request sets post_sampling_probs=false, because
post-sampling probabilities at temperature 0 collapse to a one-hot
(the sampled token reports prob 1.0 and the alternatives vanish),
which is useless as a reference. With post_sampling_probs=false
this llama.cpp build answers with "top_logprobs" (log-probabilities
from the raw logit distribution, server-task.cpp
completion_token_output::to_json); the generator converts them back
with exp() so the fixture carries plain probabilities. The
probability-level reference complements the token-level fixtures:
an engine's logit path (final norm, softcap, logit scale) can be
checked against these numbers within tolerance even where its
greedy trajectory would match anyway.

A hard validation guard runs before anything is written: every
record must hold exactly N_PROBS top entries and the top-1
probabilities must not be degenerate (all exactly 1.0). A run that
fails the guard raises and writes no fixture, so a bad probability
run can never file silently.

Same discipline as gen_golden.py: CPU only (-ngl 0), localhost,
port 18923 by default, the server is terminated in a finally block,
and the production Glimmer server is never touched. The prompt ids
come from llama-tokenize --ids and the server's evaluated prompt
count is asserted against them, exactly as in gen_golden.py.

Output: one metadata line, then one record per prompt:
{"id": ..., "prompt": ..., "prompt_token_ids": [...],
 "top5": [{"id": int, "text": str, "prob": float}, ...]}

Usage:
    gen_first_token_probs.py --model /path/to/model.gguf \
        [--bin-dir /home/server/llama.cpp/build-vulkan2/bin] \
        [--prompts prompts.jsonl] [--out fixtures/<model>.top5.jsonl] \
        [--port 18923]

Standard library only.
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import math
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

TEMPERATURE = 0
SEED = 42
CTX = 512
THREADS = 8
N_PROBS = 5
PROMPT_SET_VERSION = "1.0"


def sha256_of(path):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def load_prompts(path):
    prompts = []
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if line:
                prompts.append(json.loads(line))
    return prompts


def tokenize(bin_dir, model, prompt):
    out = subprocess.run(
        [str(bin_dir / "llama-tokenize"), "-m", str(model), "-p", prompt,
         "--ids", "--no-escape"],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
    )
    return json.loads(out.stdout.strip())


def llama_version(bin_dir):
    out = subprocess.run(
        [str(bin_dir / "llama-server"), "--version"],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
    )
    first = (out.stdout or out.stderr).splitlines()[0]
    return first.removeprefix("version: ").strip()


def wait_health(port, proc, log_path):
    url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/health"
    for _ in range(240):
        if proc.poll() is not None:
            tail = Path(log_path).read_text(errors="replace")[-2000:]
            raise RuntimeError(f"llama-server exited early; log tail:\n{tail}")
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=2) as r:
                if r.status == 200:
                    return
        except Exception:
            pass
        time.sleep(0.5)
    raise RuntimeError("llama-server did not become healthy in 120 s")


def complete_first(port, prompt):
    body = json.dumps({
        "prompt": prompt,
        "n_predict": 1,
        "temperature": TEMPERATURE,
        "seed": SEED,
        "n_probs": N_PROBS,
        "post_sampling_probs": False,
        "cache_prompt": False,
    }).encode("utf-8")
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/completion",
        data=body, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=900) as r:
        return json.loads(r.read().decode("utf-8"))


def validate_records(records):
    """Hard guard: refuse to file a degenerate probability fixture.

    Every record must carry exactly N_PROBS top entries, and the
    top-1 probabilities must not all be exactly 1.0 (the signature
    of post-sampling probabilities at temperature 0, which collapse
    to a one-hot). Raises RuntimeError, so the run exits nonzero
    and no fixture is written.
    """
    for r in records:
        if len(r["top5"]) != N_PROBS:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"validation failed: {r['id']} has {len(r['top5'])} top "
                f"entries, expected exactly {N_PROBS}; refusing to "
                f"write a degenerate fixture"
            )
    if records and all(r["top5"][0]["prob"] == 1.0 for r in records):
        raise RuntimeError(
            "validation failed: every top-1 probability is exactly "
            "1.0 (degenerate one-hot, the post-sampling-at-temperature-0 "
            "signature); refusing to write a degenerate fixture"
        )


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True, type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--bin-dir", type=Path,
                    default=Path("/home/server/llama.cpp/build-vulkan2/bin"))
    ap.add_argument("--prompts", type=Path, default=here / "prompts.jsonl")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=18923)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    model = args.model
    out = args.out or here / "fixtures" / (model.stem + ".top5.jsonl")
    prompts = load_prompts(args.prompts)

    meta = {
        "kind": "llama.cpp-first-token-top5",
        "version": 1,
        "model_file": model.name,
        "model_sha256": sha256_of(model),
        "model_bytes": model.stat().st_size,
        "llama_cpp_version": llama_version(args.bin_dir),
        "generation_binary": "llama-server (/completion, n_predict=1, n_probs=5)",
        "tokenize_binary": "llama-tokenize (--ids --no-escape)",
        "flags": {
            "n_gpu_layers": 0, "ctx_size": CTX, "threads": THREADS,
            "n_predict": 1, "n_probs": N_PROBS, "temperature": TEMPERATURE,
            "seed": SEED, "post_sampling_probs": False,
            "chat_template": "none (raw completion)",
        },
        "prompts_file": args.prompts.name,
        "prompt_set_version": PROMPT_SET_VERSION,
        "prompts_sha256": sha256_of(args.prompts),
    }

    records = []
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".log", delete=False) as log:
        log_path = log.name
    proc = subprocess.Popen(
        [str(args.bin_dir / "llama-server"), "-m", str(model),
         "-ngl", "0", "-c", str(CTX), "-t", str(THREADS),
         "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", str(args.port)],
        stdout=open(log_path, "ab"), stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
    )
    try:
        wait_health(args.port, proc, log_path)
        for p in prompts:
            prompt_ids = tokenize(args.bin_dir, model, p["prompt"])
            resp = complete_first(args.port, p["prompt"])
            if resp["tokens_evaluated"] != len(prompt_ids):
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"prompt token count mismatch for {p['id']}: server "
                    f"evaluated {resp['tokens_evaluated']}, llama-tokenize "
                    f"produced {len(prompt_ids)}"
                )
            steps = resp["completion_probabilities"]
            if len(steps) != 1:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"{p['id']}: expected exactly 1 probability step, "
                    f"got {len(steps)}"
                )
            # Pre-sampling (post_sampling_probs=false): this llama.cpp
            # build reports the per-step alternatives under
            # "top_logprobs", each {"id", "token", "bytes", "logprob"}
            # holding the log-probability from the raw logit
            # distribution (server-task.cpp,
            # completion_token_output::to_json). Convert back to plain
            # probabilities with exp() for the fixture.
            if "top_logprobs" not in steps[0]:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"{p['id']}: step has no top_logprobs; keys are "
                    f"{sorted(steps[0].keys())}"
                )
            top5 = [{"id": pr["id"], "text": pr["token"],
                     "prob": math.exp(pr["logprob"])}
                    for pr in steps[0]["top_logprobs"][:N_PROBS]]
            records.append({
                "id": p["id"],
                "category": p["category"],
                "prompt": p["prompt"],
                "prompt_token_ids": prompt_ids,
                "sampled_token_id": steps[0]["id"],
                "top5": top5,
            })
            best = top5[0]
            print(f"  {p['id']}: top1 id={best['id']} "
                  f"prob={best['prob']:.6f} text={best['text']!r}")
    finally:
        proc.terminate()
        try:
            proc.wait(timeout=10)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            proc.kill()

    validate_records(records)

    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps({"meta": meta}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        for r in records:
            f.write(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    print(f"wrote {out} ({len(records)} records)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

===== END FILE: golden/gen_first_token_probs.py =====

===== FILE: golden/gen_golden.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate llama.cpp golden-output fixtures for the Torch rebuild.

For each prompt in prompts.jsonl this records:
  - prompt_token_ids      from llama-tokenize --ids (the canonical
                          tokenization, BOS included, exactly what a
                          llama.cpp generation run evaluates)
  - completion_token_ids  the token ids llama.cpp actually sampled
  - completion_text       the text of that same generation

Why llama-server and not llama-completion for the generation step:
llama-completion/llama-cli cannot report the sampled token ids (no
flag exists; --verbose dumps graph internals, checked against build
a7af149). The ids are the whole point of the fixture, and they cannot
be recovered by retokenizing the completion text either: tokenization
is context-dependent (llama-tokenize on a completion text standalone
split its first token three ways where the in-context tokenization
of the same text has a single token), so text alone does not pin
down the trajectory an engine must reproduce.
llama-server's /completion with n_probs=1 returns, per step, the
sampled token's id, text piece and raw bytes; the bytes of the kept
steps must concatenate to the response content exactly, and this
script asserts that, so ids and text in a fixture provably come from
one and the same generation.

Decoding is greedy: temperature 0, seed 42 (recorded; unused by the
greedy sampler), 64 predicted tokens, raw completion (no chat
template), CPU only (-ngl 0) so the production GPU server is never
touched. Fixtures carry no timestamps: regenerating with the same
llama.cpp build and flags reproduces the file byte for byte.

Usage:
    gen_golden.py --model /path/to/model.gguf \
                  [--bin-dir /home/server/llama.cpp/build-vulkan2/bin] \
                  [--prompts prompts.jsonl] [--out fixtures/<model>.golden.jsonl] \
                  [--port 18923]

Standard library only.
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

N_PREDICT = 64
TEMPERATURE = 0
SEED = 42
CTX = 512
THREADS = 8
PROMPT_SET_VERSION = "1.0"


def sha256_of(path):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def load_prompts(path):
    prompts = []
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if line:
                prompts.append(json.loads(line))
    return prompts


def tokenize(bin_dir, model, prompt):
    out = subprocess.run(
        [str(bin_dir / "llama-tokenize"), "-m", str(model), "-p", prompt,
         "--ids", "--no-escape"],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
    )
    return json.loads(out.stdout.strip())


def llama_version(bin_dir):
    out = subprocess.run(
        [str(bin_dir / "llama-server"), "--version"],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
    )
    first = (out.stdout or out.stderr).splitlines()[0]
    return first.removeprefix("version: ").strip()


def wait_health(port, proc, log_path):
    url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/health"
    for _ in range(120):
        if proc.poll() is not None:
            tail = Path(log_path).read_text(errors="replace")[-2000:]
            raise RuntimeError(f"llama-server exited early; log tail:\n{tail}")
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=2) as r:
                if r.status == 200:
                    return
        except Exception:
            pass
        time.sleep(0.5)
    raise RuntimeError("llama-server did not become healthy in 60 s")


def complete(port, prompt):
    body = json.dumps({
        "prompt": prompt,
        "n_predict": N_PREDICT,
        "temperature": TEMPERATURE,
        "seed": SEED,
        "n_probs": 1,
        "cache_prompt": False,
    }).encode("utf-8")
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/completion",
        data=body, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=600) as r:
        return json.loads(r.read().decode("utf-8"))


def extract_record(resp, prompt_ids):
    """Pull (completion_ids, completion_text, ended_with_eos) out of a
    /completion response, asserting the ids and the text are consistent."""
    if resp["tokens_evaluated"] != len(prompt_ids):
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"prompt token count mismatch: server evaluated "
            f"{resp['tokens_evaluated']}, llama-tokenize produced {len(prompt_ids)}"
        )
    steps = resp["completion_probabilities"]
    if len(steps) != resp["tokens_predicted"]:
        raise RuntimeError("probability steps do not match tokens_predicted")
    content = resp["content"]
    # This build reports the stop reason in stop_type ("eos" / "limit");
    # stopped_eos is null. When generation stops on EOS, the EOS token
    # is part of the sampled trajectory and stays in the record (its
    # text piece is empty, so the byte check below still holds).
    ended_with_eos = resp.get("stop_type") == "eos" or bool(resp.get("stopped_eos"))

    joined = b"".join(bytes(s["bytes"]) for s in steps)
    if joined != content.encode("utf-8"):
        # A sampled EOS is reported as a step but contributes no text.
        if ended_with_eos and steps and \
                b"".join(bytes(s["bytes"]) for s in steps[:-1]) == content.encode("utf-8"):
            steps = steps[:-1]
        else:
            raise RuntimeError("step bytes do not concatenate to the completion text")
    return [s["id"] for s in steps], content, ended_with_eos


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True, type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--bin-dir", type=Path,
                    default=Path("/home/server/llama.cpp/build-vulkan2/bin"))
    ap.add_argument("--prompts", type=Path, default=here / "prompts.jsonl")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=18923)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    model = args.model
    out = args.out or here / "fixtures" / (model.stem + ".golden.jsonl")
    prompts = load_prompts(args.prompts)

    meta = {
        "kind": "llama.cpp-golden-fixture",
        "version": 1,
        "model_file": model.name,
        "model_sha256": sha256_of(model),
        "model_bytes": model.stat().st_size,
        "llama_cpp_version": llama_version(args.bin_dir),
        "generation_binary": "llama-server (/completion, n_probs=1)",
        "tokenize_binary": "llama-tokenize (--ids --no-escape)",
        "flags": {
            "n_gpu_layers": 0, "ctx_size": CTX, "threads": THREADS,
            "n_predict": N_PREDICT, "temperature": TEMPERATURE, "seed": SEED,
            "chat_template": "none (raw completion)",
        },
        "prompts_file": args.prompts.name,
        "prompt_set_version": PROMPT_SET_VERSION,
        "prompts_sha256": sha256_of(args.prompts),
    }

    records = []
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".log", delete=False) as log:
        log_path = log.name
    proc = subprocess.Popen(
        [str(args.bin_dir / "llama-server"), "-m", str(model),
         "-ngl", "0", "-c", str(CTX), "-t", str(THREADS),
         "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", str(args.port)],
        stdout=open(log_path, "ab"), stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
    )
    try:
        wait_health(args.port, proc, log_path)
        for p in prompts:
            prompt_ids = tokenize(args.bin_dir, model, p["prompt"])
            resp = complete(args.port, p["prompt"])
            comp_ids, comp_text, eos = extract_record(resp, prompt_ids)
            records.append({
                "id": p["id"],
                "category": p["category"],
                "prompt": p["prompt"],
                "prompt_token_ids": prompt_ids,
                "completion_token_ids": comp_ids,
                "completion_text": comp_text,
                "ended_with_eos": eos,
            })
            print(f"  {p['id']}: prompt {len(prompt_ids)} tokens, "
                  f"completion {len(comp_ids)} tokens, eos={eos}")
    finally:
        proc.terminate()
        try:
            proc.wait(timeout=10)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            proc.kill()

    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps({"meta": meta}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        for r in records:
            f.write(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    print(f"wrote {out} ({len(records)} records)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

===== FILE: golden/tools/cb_dump.cpp =====
// cb_dump: per-layer activation dump from llama.cpp (layer-diff
// harness, follow-up to integration run A).
//
// Loads a GGUF model on the CPU backend only, runs ONE prefill of
// fixed token ids through llama_decode with an eval callback
// (llama_context_params.cb_eval) attached, and writes every named
// graph intermediate the arch-llama side can also produce
// (crates/arch-llama/examples/layer_dump.rs) as raw little-endian
// f32 .bin files plus a manifest.json of shapes. Names are mapped
// to the shared scheme:
//
//   inp_embd        -> embd            attn_norm-<il> -> L<il>_attn_norm
//   Qcur-<il>       -> L<il>_q         Kcur-<il>      -> L<il>_k
//   Vcur-<il>       -> L<il>_v         ffn_inp-<il>   -> L<il>_ffn_inp
//   ffn_norm-<il>   -> L<il>_ffn_norm  ffn_out-<il>   -> L<il>_ffn_out
//   l_out-<il>      -> L<il>_l_out     result_norm--1 -> result_norm
//   result_output--1 -> logits
//
// ggml tensors are [ne0 = width, ne1 = rows]; rows are copied out
// honoring nb[1], so the files are flat [rows][width] f32, the same
// layout the Rust dumper writes.
//
// Usage: cb_dump <model.gguf> <out_dir> <id,id,...>
// Build (on the server, against its llama.cpp tree):
//   g++ -O2 -std=c++17 -I~/llama.cpp/include -I~/llama.cpp/ggml/include \
//       cb_dump.cpp -o cb_dump -L~/llama.cpp/build-vulkan2/bin \
//       -lllama -lggml -lggml-base -lggml-cpu \
//       -Wl,-rpath,/home/server/llama.cpp/build-vulkan2/bin

#include "llama.h"
#include "ggml.h"
#include "ggml-backend.h"

#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include <sys/stat.h>

static std::string g_outdir;
static bool g_armed = false;
static FILE * g_manifest = nullptr;
static bool g_first_entry = true;

// Map a graph tensor name to the shared file stem, or "" to skip.
static std::string map_name(const char * name) {
    const std::string n(name);
    if (n == "inp_embd" || n == "embd") return "embd";
    if (n.rfind("result_norm", 0) == 0) return "result_norm";
    if (n.rfind("result_output", 0) == 0) return "logits";
    static const struct { const char * base; const char * stem; } kLayers[] = {
        { "attn_norm-", "_attn_norm" },
        { "Qcur-",      "_q" },
        { "Kcur-",      "_k" },
        { "Vcur-",      "_v" },
        { "ffn_inp-",   "_ffn_inp" },
        { "ffn_norm-",  "_ffn_norm" },
        { "ffn_out-",   "_ffn_out" },
        { "l_out-",     "_l_out" },
    };
    for (const auto & e : kLayers) {
        const size_t blen = strlen(e.base);
        if (n.rfind(e.base, 0) == 0) {
            const int il = atoi(n.c_str() + blen);
            char buf[64];
            snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "L%02d%s", il, e.stem);
            return buf;
        }
    }
    return "";
}

static bool cb_eval(ggml_tensor * t, bool ask, void * user_data) {
    (void) user_data;
    if (!g_armed || t == nullptr || t->name[0] == '\0') {
        return false;
    }
    const std::string stem = map_name(t->name);
    if (stem.empty()) {
        return false;
    }
    if (ask) {
        return true; // ask the scheduler to hand us the computed data
    }
    if (t->type != GGML_TYPE_F32) {
        fprintf(stderr, "cb_dump: skip %s (type %s, not F32)\n", t->name, ggml_type_name(t->type));
        return true;
    }
    // Flatten in ggml element order (ne[0] fastest): for a
    // [width, rows] tensor that is exactly [rows][width] row-major,
    // and for [head_dim, heads, rows] (Qcur/Kcur/Vcur) it is
    // [rows][heads][head_dim], which is the Rust layout too.
    const int64_t ne0 = t->ne[0];
    std::vector<float> buf((size_t) ggml_nelements(t));
    size_t dst = 0;
    for (int64_t i3 = 0; i3 < t->ne[3]; ++i3) {
        for (int64_t i2 = 0; i2 < t->ne[2]; ++i2) {
            for (int64_t i1 = 0; i1 < t->ne[1]; ++i1) {
                const size_t off = (size_t) i1 * t->nb[1] + (size_t) i2 * t->nb[2]
                                 + (size_t) i3 * t->nb[3];
                ggml_backend_tensor_get(t, buf.data() + dst, off, (size_t) (ne0 * 4));
                dst += (size_t) ne0;
            }
        }
    }
    const std::string path = g_outdir + "/" + stem + ".bin";
    FILE * f = fopen(path.c_str(), "wb");
    if (f == nullptr) {
        fprintf(stderr, "cb_dump: cannot write %s\n", path.c_str());
        return true;
    }
    fwrite(buf.data(), 4, buf.size(), f);
    fclose(f);
    if (g_manifest != nullptr) {
        fprintf(g_manifest, "%s  \"%s\": [%lld", g_first_entry ? "" : "", stem.c_str(),
                (long long) t->ne[0]);
        for (int d = 1; d < ggml_n_dims(t); ++d) {
            fprintf(g_manifest, ", %lld", (long long) t->ne[d]);
        }
        fprintf(g_manifest, "],\n");
        g_first_entry = false;
        fflush(g_manifest);
    }
    return true;
}

int main(int argc, char ** argv) {
    if (argc != 4) {
        fprintf(stderr, "usage: cb_dump <model.gguf> <out_dir> <id,id,...>\n");
        return 1;
    }
    const char * model_path = argv[1];
    g_outdir = argv[2];
    std::vector<llama_token> ids;
    {
        std::string s(argv[3]);
        size_t at = 0;
        while (at < s.size()) {
            const size_t comma = s.find(',', at);
            ids.push_back((llama_token) atoi(s.substr(at, comma - at).c_str()));
            if (comma == std::string::npos) break;
            at = comma + 1;
        }
    }
    if (ids.empty()) {
        fprintf(stderr, "cb_dump: no ids\n");
        return 1;
    }
    mkdir(g_outdir.c_str(), 0755);

    llama_backend_init();
    llama_model_params mparams = llama_model_default_params();
    mparams.n_gpu_layers = 0; // CPU only: the production GPU server is not ours to touch
    llama_model * model = llama_model_load_from_file(model_path, mparams);
    if (model == nullptr) {
        fprintf(stderr, "cb_dump: model load failed\n");
        return 1;
    }
    llama_context_params cparams = llama_context_default_params();
    cparams.n_ctx = 128;
    cparams.n_batch = 128;
    cparams.no_perf = true;
    cparams.cb_eval = cb_eval;
    cparams.cb_eval_user_data = nullptr;
    llama_context * ctx = llama_init_from_model(model, cparams);
    if (ctx == nullptr) {
        fprintf(stderr, "cb_dump: context init failed\n");
        return 1;
    }

    const std::string mpath = g_outdir + "/manifest.json";
    g_manifest = fopen(mpath.c_str(), "w");
    fprintf(g_manifest, "{\n");

    llama_batch batch = llama_batch_init((int32_t) ids.size(), 0, 1);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < ids.size(); ++i) {
        batch.token[i] = ids[i];
        batch.pos[i] = (llama_pos) i;
        batch.n_seq_id[i] = 1;
        batch.seq_id[i][0] = 0;
        batch.logits[i] = 1; // logits on every position: keeps the last layer unsliced
    }
    batch.n_tokens = (int32_t) ids.size();

    g_armed = true;
    const int rc = llama_decode(ctx, batch);
    g_armed = false;
    if (rc != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "cb_dump: llama_decode failed (%d)\n", rc);
        return 1;
    }

    // Sanity: the last position's top-1 from the public logits API.
    const float * logits = llama_get_logits_ith(ctx, -1);
    const int n_vocab = llama_vocab_n_tokens(llama_model_get_vocab(model));
    int top = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i < n_vocab; ++i) {
        if (logits[i] > logits[top]) top = i;
    }
    fprintf(stderr, "cb_dump: %zu tokens, top-1 logit id %d (%.4f)\n", ids.size(), top, logits[top]);

    if (g_manifest != nullptr) {
        // Trim the trailing comma of the last entry: rewrite the tail.
        fclose(g_manifest);
        g_manifest = nullptr;
        std::string text;
        FILE * f = fopen(mpath.c_str(), "rb");
        char chunk[4096];
        size_t n;
        while ((n = fread(chunk, 1, sizeof(chunk), f)) > 0) text.append(chunk, n);
        fclose(f);
        const size_t comma = text.rfind(",\n");
        if (comma != std::string::npos) text.replace(comma, 2, "\n");
        text += "}\n";
        f = fopen(mpath.c_str(), "w");
        fwrite(text.data(), 1, text.size(), f);
        fclose(f);
    }

    FILE * meta = fopen((g_outdir + "/meta.txt").c_str(), "w");
    fprintf(meta, "engine=llama.cpp-cb_eval n_vocab=%d ids=", n_vocab);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < ids.size(); ++i) fprintf(meta, "%s%d", i ? "," : "", ids[i]);
    fprintf(meta, "\n");
    fclose(meta);

    llama_batch_free(batch);
    llama_free(ctx);
    llama_model_free(model);
    llama_backend_free();
    return 0;
}

===== END FILE: golden/tools/cb_dump.cpp =====

===== FILE: golden/tools/cb_dump_glimmer.cpp =====
// cb_dump_glimmer: per-layer activation dump from llama.cpp for
// the muse-glimmer architecture (layer-diff harness, Glimmer side
// of FORWARD-DIFF-PLAN.md in crates/itak-loader).
//
// Sibling of cb_dump.cpp (which serves the arch-llama graphs). The
// muse-glimmer graph names its own intermediates through cb() in
// src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp of the llama.cpp tree; the mapping
// below was read off that source (line numbers from the server's
// tree, 2026-11-05):
//
//   inp_embd            -> embd_raw     (build_inp_embd output)
//   embd_norm (cb, -1)  -> embed        (line 69-70: weightless
//                                        build_norm over the
//                                        embedding, then cb)
//   ffn_inp-<il>        -> L<il>_mid    (line 150-151: residual
//                                        after the attention half)
//   l_out-<il>          -> L<il>_out    (line 170-172: residual
//                                        after the full layer)
//   result_norm (-1)    -> result_norm  (line 180-181: final norm,
//                                        all positions)
//   result_output (-1)  -> logits       (line 185-195: lm_head,
//                                        logit scale, softcap)
//
// Extra per-layer tensors are dumped as insurance for a deeper
// split if a stage diverges (attn_norm, attn_post_norm, ffn_norm,
// ffn_out, ffn_post_norm): the post norms are separate graph nodes
// in this architecture (rms_norm then mul by the post-norm weight,
// lines 141-142 and 166-167, eps hardcoded 1e-8).
//
// Loads the GGUF on the CPU backend only, runs ONE prefill of
// fixed token ids through llama_decode with the eval callback
// attached, and writes raw little-endian f32 .bin files plus a
// manifest.json of ggml shapes ([ne0 = width, ne1 = rows, ...];
// files are flattened in ggml element order, ne0 fastest, which
// for a [width, rows] tensor is [rows][width] row-major).
// reduce with golden/tools/compare_traces.py against a
// glimmer_layer_trace dump.
//
// Usage: cb_dump_glimmer <model.gguf> <out_dir> <id,id,...>
// Build (on the server, against its llama.cpp tree):
//   g++ -O2 -std=c++17 -I/home/server/llama.cpp/include \
//       -I/home/server/llama.cpp/ggml/include \
//       cb_dump_glimmer.cpp -o cb_dump_glimmer \
//       -L/home/server/llama.cpp/build-vulkan2/bin \
//       -lllama -lggml -lggml-base -lggml-cpu \
//       -Wl,-rpath,/home/server/llama.cpp/build-vulkan2/bin

#include "llama.h"
#include "ggml.h"
#include "ggml-backend.h"

#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include <sys/stat.h>

static std::string g_outdir;
static bool g_armed = false;
static FILE * g_manifest = nullptr;
static bool g_first_entry = true;

// Map a graph tensor name to the shared file stem, or "" to skip.
static std::string map_name(const char * name) {
    const std::string n(name);
    if (n == "inp_embd") return "embd_raw";
    if (n.rfind("embd_norm", 0) == 0) return "embed";
    if (n.rfind("result_norm", 0) == 0) return "result_norm";
    if (n.rfind("result_output", 0) == 0) return "logits";
    static const struct { const char * base; const char * stem; } kLayers[] = {
        { "attn_norm-",      "_attn_norm" },
        { "attn_post_norm-", "_attn_post_norm" },
        { "ffn_inp-",        "_mid" },
        { "ffn_norm-",       "_ffn_norm" },
        { "ffn_out-",        "_ffn_out" },
        { "ffn_post_norm-",  "_ffn_post_norm" },
        { "l_out-",          "_out" },
    };
    for (const auto & e : kLayers) {
        const size_t blen = strlen(e.base);
        if (n.rfind(e.base, 0) == 0) {
            const int il = atoi(n.c_str() + blen);
            char buf[64];
            snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "L%02d%s", il, e.stem);
            return buf;
        }
    }
    return "";
}

static bool cb_eval(ggml_tensor * t, bool ask, void * user_data) {
    (void) user_data;
    if (!g_armed || t == nullptr || t->name[0] == '\0') {
        return false;
    }
    const std::string stem = map_name(t->name);
    if (stem.empty()) {
        return false;
    }
    if (ask) {
        return true; // ask the scheduler to hand us the computed data
    }
    if (t->type != GGML_TYPE_F32) {
        fprintf(stderr, "cb_dump_glimmer: skip %s (type %s, not F32)\n",
                t->name, ggml_type_name(t->type));
        return true;
    }
    // Flatten in ggml element order (ne[0] fastest).
    const int64_t ne0 = t->ne[0];
    std::vector<float> buf((size_t) ggml_nelements(t));
    size_t dst = 0;
    for (int64_t i3 = 0; i3 < t->ne[3]; ++i3) {
        for (int64_t i2 = 0; i2 < t->ne[2]; ++i2) {
            for (int64_t i1 = 0; i1 < t->ne[1]; ++i1) {
                const size_t off = (size_t) i1 * t->nb[1] + (size_t) i2 * t->nb[2]
                                 + (size_t) i3 * t->nb[3];
                ggml_backend_tensor_get(t, buf.data() + dst, off, (size_t) (ne0 * 4));
                dst += (size_t) ne0;
            }
        }
    }
    const std::string path = g_outdir + "/" + stem + ".bin";
    FILE * f = fopen(path.c_str(), "wb");
    if (f == nullptr) {
        fprintf(stderr, "cb_dump_glimmer: cannot write %s\n", path.c_str());
        return true;
    }
    fwrite(buf.data(), 4, buf.size(), f);
    fclose(f);
    if (g_manifest != nullptr) {
        fprintf(g_manifest, "%s  \"%s\": [%lld", g_first_entry ? "" : "", stem.c_str(),
                (long long) t->ne[0]);
        for (int d = 1; d < ggml_n_dims(t); ++d) {
            fprintf(g_manifest, ", %lld", (long long) t->ne[d]);
        }
        fprintf(g_manifest, "],\n");
        g_first_entry = false;
        fflush(g_manifest);
    }
    return true;
}

int main(int argc, char ** argv) {
    if (argc != 4) {
        fprintf(stderr, "usage: cb_dump_glimmer <model.gguf> <out_dir> <id,id,...>\n");
        return 1;
    }
    const char * model_path = argv[1];
    g_outdir = argv[2];
    std::vector<llama_token> ids;
    {
        std::string s(argv[3]);
        size_t at = 0;
        while (at < s.size()) {
            const size_t comma = s.find(',', at);
            ids.push_back((llama_token) atoi(s.substr(at, comma - at).c_str()));
            if (comma == std::string::npos) break;
            at = comma + 1;
        }
    }
    if (ids.empty()) {
        fprintf(stderr, "cb_dump_glimmer: no ids\n");
        return 1;
    }
    mkdir(g_outdir.c_str(), 0755);

    llama_backend_init();
    llama_model_params mparams = llama_model_default_params();
    mparams.n_gpu_layers = 0; // CPU only by contract: reference work never touches the GPU
    llama_model * model = llama_model_load_from_file(model_path, mparams);
    if (model == nullptr) {
        fprintf(stderr, "cb_dump_glimmer: model load failed\n");
        return 1;
    }
    llama_context_params cparams = llama_context_default_params();
    cparams.n_ctx = 128;
    cparams.n_batch = 128;
    cparams.no_perf = true;
    cparams.cb_eval = cb_eval;
    cparams.cb_eval_user_data = nullptr;
    llama_context * ctx = llama_init_from_model(model, cparams);
    if (ctx == nullptr) {
        fprintf(stderr, "cb_dump_glimmer: context init failed\n");
        return 1;
    }

    const std::string mpath = g_outdir + "/manifest.json";
    g_manifest = fopen(mpath.c_str(), "w");
    fprintf(g_manifest, "{\n");

    llama_batch batch = llama_batch_init((int32_t) ids.size(), 0, 1);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < ids.size(); ++i) {
        batch.token[i] = ids[i];
        batch.pos[i] = (llama_pos) i;
        batch.n_seq_id[i] = 1;
        batch.seq_id[i][0] = 0;
        batch.logits[i] = 1; // logits on every position: keeps the last layer unsliced
    }
    batch.n_tokens = (int32_t) ids.size();

    g_armed = true;
    const int rc = llama_decode(ctx, batch);
    g_armed = false;
    if (rc != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "cb_dump_glimmer: llama_decode failed (%d)\n", rc);
        return 1;
    }

    // Sanity: the last position's top-1 from the public logits API.
    const float * logits = llama_get_logits_ith(ctx, -1);
    const int n_vocab = llama_vocab_n_tokens(llama_model_get_vocab(model));
    int top = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i < n_vocab; ++i) {
        if (logits[i] > logits[top]) top = i;
    }
    fprintf(stderr, "cb_dump_glimmer: %zu tokens, top-1 logit id %d (%.4f)\n",
            ids.size(), top, logits[top]);

    if (g_manifest != nullptr) {
        fclose(g_manifest);
        g_manifest = nullptr;
        std::string text;
        FILE * f = fopen(mpath.c_str(), "rb");
        char chunk[4096];
        size_t n;
        while ((n = fread(chunk, 1, sizeof(chunk), f)) > 0) text.append(chunk, n);
        fclose(f);
        const size_t comma = text.rfind(",\n");
        if (comma != std::string::npos) text.replace(comma, 2, "\n");
        text += "}\n";
        f = fopen(mpath.c_str(), "w");
        fwrite(text.data(), 1, text.size(), f);
        fclose(f);
    }

    FILE * meta = fopen((g_outdir + "/meta.txt").c_str(), "w");
    fprintf(meta, "engine=llama.cpp-cb_eval arch=muse-glimmer n_vocab=%d ids=", n_vocab);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < ids.size(); ++i) fprintf(meta, "%s%d", i ? "," : "", ids[i]);
    fprintf(meta, "\n");
    fclose(meta);

    llama_batch_free(batch);
    llama_free(ctx);
    llama_model_free(model);
    llama_backend_free();
    return 0;
}

===== END FILE: golden/tools/cb_dump_glimmer.cpp =====

===== FILE: golden/tools/compare_layers.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Layer-by-layer activation diff: llama.cpp cb_eval dump vs
arch-llama forward_traced dump (follow-up to integration run A).

Usage: compare_layers.py <llama_dir> <rust_dir>

Both directories hold <stem>.bin raw little-endian f32 files in
[rows][width] layout plus manifest.json mapping stem -> [width,
rows]. Reports, for every checkpoint in execution order, the
max-abs difference and cosine similarity, a per-position breakdown
for l_out, and a RoPE pairing experiment: it re-rotates the Rust
pre-RoPE Q/K dumps under both pairing conventions (interleaved
adjacent pairs, ggml NORMAL; half-split pairs, ggml NEOX) and
reports which one reproduces llama.cpp's Qcur/Kcur.
"""

import json
import math
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np


def load(d, stem, manifest, shape=None):
    """Load a Rust dump tensor: manifest is [width, rows] and the
    file is [rows][width] row-major."""
    dims = manifest[stem]
    a = np.fromfile(Path(d) / f"{stem}.bin", dtype="<f4")
    total = 1
    for v in dims:
        total *= v
    assert a.size == total, f"{stem}: {a.size} != prod({dims})"
    if shape is not None:
        assert int(np.prod(shape)) == a.size, f"{stem}: cannot view as {shape}"
        return a.reshape(shape)
    if len(dims) == 2:
        return a.reshape(dims[1], dims[0])
    return a


def load_llama(d, stem, manifest):
    """Load a llama.cpp dump tensor, returned as [rows][width].

    Most graph tensors are ggml [width, rows]. Qcur is the
    exception in this llama.cpp version: its ggml dims are
    [head_dim, rows, heads] (the rope node views Q token-major),
    so the flat dump is [heads][rows][head_dim] and is transposed
    back here. Verified empirically: only under this reading does
    Qcur at position 0 (where RoPE is the identity) reproduce the
    split attn_q projection of the proven attn_norm input.
    """
    dims = manifest[stem]
    a = np.fromfile(Path(d) / f"{stem}.bin", dtype="<f4")
    total = 1
    for v in dims:
        total *= v
    assert a.size == total, f"{stem}: {a.size} != prod({dims})"
    if stem.endswith("_q") and len(dims) == 3:
        dim, rows, heads = dims
        return a.reshape(heads, rows, dim).transpose(1, 0, 2).reshape(rows, heads * dim)
    if len(dims) == 2:
        return a.reshape(dims[1], dims[0])
    raise ValueError(f"{stem}: unexpected llama dims {dims}")


def stats(a, b):
    d = np.abs(a - b)
    na = np.linalg.norm(a)
    nb = np.linalg.norm(b)
    if na == 0.0 or nb == 0.0:
        # Cosine against a zero tensor is undefined; report 1.0 only
        # when both sides are all zeros (identical dead tensors),
        # 0.0 when exactly one side is dead, so a dead-vs-live
        # checkpoint can never print a perfect cosine.
        cos = 1.0 if na == nb else 0.0
    else:
        cos = float(np.dot(a.ravel(), b.ravel()) / (na * nb))
    return float(d.max()), float(d.mean()), cos


def rope(x, positions, base, mode):
    """x: [rows][heads][dim]. Rotate per head vector at its position.
    mode 'neox': pair (i, i + dim/2); mode 'interleaved': pair (2i, 2i+1).
    Frequency for pair i in both: base^(-2i/dim)."""
    rows, heads, dim = x.shape
    out = x.copy()
    half = dim // 2
    freqs = base ** (-2.0 * np.arange(half) / dim)
    for r, p in enumerate(positions):
        ang = p * freqs
        cos = np.cos(ang)[None, :, None]  # [1][half][1]
        sin = np.sin(ang)[None, :, None]
        if mode == "neox":
            x1 = x[r, :, :half]
            x2 = x[r, :, half:]
            out[r, :, :half] = x1 * cos[:, :, 0] - x2 * sin[:, :, 0]
            out[r, :, half:] = x2 * cos[:, :, 0] + x1 * sin[:, :, 0]
        else:
            pairs = x[r].reshape(heads, half, 2)
            x1 = pairs[:, :, 0]
            x2 = pairs[:, :, 1]
            rot = np.empty_like(pairs)
            rot[:, :, 0] = x1 * cos[:, :, 0] - x2 * sin[:, :, 0]
            rot[:, :, 1] = x2 * cos[:, :, 0] + x1 * sin[:, :, 0]
            out[r] = rot.reshape(heads, dim)
    return out


def main():
    llama_dir, rust_dir = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    lm = json.loads((Path(llama_dir) / "manifest.json").read_text())
    rm = json.loads((Path(rust_dir) / "manifest.json").read_text())
    n_layers = 28
    positions = [0, 1, 2, 3]

    order = ["embd"]
    for il in range(n_layers):
        for s in ("attn_norm", "q", "k", "v", "ffn_inp", "ffn_norm", "ffn_out", "l_out"):
            order.append(f"L{il:02d}_{s}")
    order += ["result_norm", "logits"]

    print(f"{'checkpoint':22s} {'max_abs':>12s} {'mean_abs':>12s} {'cosine':>10s}")
    first_div = None
    for stem in order:
        b = load(rust_dir, stem, rm)
        a = load_llama(llama_dir, stem, lm)
        if stem in ("result_norm", "logits"):
            a = a[-1:]  # llama dump carries all positions; rust only the last
        assert a.shape == b.shape, f"{stem}: llama {a.shape} vs rust {b.shape}"
        mx, mean, cos = stats(a, b)
        flag = ""
        if cos < 0.999 or mx > 0.1:
            flag = "  <-- DIVERGENT"
            if first_div is None:
                first_div = stem
        if not a.any() and not b.any():
            # stats() reports cosine 1.0 for two all-zero tensors;
            # say so on the line so the 1.0 is not read as agreement
            # between live activations.
            flag += "  (both sides all zeros)"
        print(f"{stem:22s} {mx:12.6f} {mean:12.6f} {cos:10.6f}{flag}")
    print(f"\nfirst divergent checkpoint: {first_div}")

    print("\nl_out per-position max_abs:")
    print(f"{'layer':>5s} " + " ".join(f"{'pos'+str(p):>12s}" for p in positions))
    for il in range(n_layers):
        stem = f"L{il:02d}_l_out"
        b = load(rust_dir, stem, rm)
        a = load_llama(llama_dir, stem, lm)
        per = [float(np.abs(a[p] - b[p]).max()) for p in positions]
        print(f"{il:5d} " + " ".join(f"{v:12.6f}" for v in per))

    print("\nRoPE pairing experiment (base 1e6, head_dim 128):")
    for il in (0, 1, 13, 27):
        for kind, heads in (("q", 12), ("k", 2)):
            pre = load(rust_dir, f"L{il:02d}_{kind}_pre_rope", rm).reshape(4, heads, 128)
            ref = load_llama(llama_dir, f"L{il:02d}_{kind}", lm).reshape(4, heads, 128)
            ours = load(rust_dir, f"L{il:02d}_{kind}", rm).reshape(4, heads, 128)
            for mode in ("neox", "interleaved"):
                rot = rope(pre.astype(np.float64), positions, 1e6, mode)
                mx, _, cos = stats(ref, rot.astype(np.float32))
                print(f"  L{il:02d} {kind}: rust-pre + {mode:12s} vs llama {kind}cur: "
                      f"max_abs={mx:.6f} cos={cos:.6f}")
            mx, _, cos = stats(ref, ours)
            print(f"  L{il:02d} {kind}: rust {kind} (as built)   vs llama {kind}cur: "
                  f"max_abs={mx:.6f} cos={cos:.6f}")
            # position 0 only: rotation is identity there in any convention
            mx0, _, _ = stats(ref[0], ours[0])
            print(f"        position 0 alone: max_abs={mx0:.6f}")

    # The verdict is also the exit status: 1 when any checkpoint
    # diverged, 0 only on a full match. (The per-position and RoPE
    # sections above are diagnostics and do not gate.)
    return 1 if first_div is not None else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

===== END FILE: golden/tools/compare_layers.py =====

===== FILE: golden/tools/compare_traces.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stage-by-stage trace diff for muse-glimmer (FORWARD-DIFF-PLAN).

Usage: compare_traces.py <our_trace.txt> <llama_dump_dir>

Our side is a glimmer_layer_trace dump: trace v=1 lines carrying
whole-tensor and last-row statistics (mean, population variance,
max abs, first values) per stage (embed, layer.<i>.mid,
layer.<i>.out, final_norm, logits). The reference side is a
cb_dump_glimmer output directory (raw f32 .bin + manifest.json);
this script reduces its tensors to the identical statistics and
compares stage by stage in capture order.

Reading rules (from the plan): a stage matches when mean and
variance agree to roughly 1e-2 relative, last row first, whole
tensor second, with the first values tracking. The mean is judged
in units of the stream's own standard deviation (residual means
sit near zero, so a plain relative error is meaningless there);
variance is judged relatively. The first stage whose input stage
matched but which does not itself match is the defect's home.

The reference final_norm and logits tensors carry every position;
only the last position is reduced, matching our single-row
captures. The reference logits also yield the top-1 id and its
softmax probability, for the first-token residue comparison.
"""

import json
import math
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

FIRST_N = 8
LINE_RE = re.compile(
    r"stage=(?P<stage>\S+) rows=(?P<rows>\d+) cols=(?P<cols>\d+) n=(?P<n>\d+) "
    r"mean=(?P<mean>\S+) var=(?P<var>\S+) max_abs=(?P<max_abs>\S+) "
    r"last_mean=(?P<last_mean>\S+) last_var=(?P<last_var>\S+) "
    r"last_max_abs=(?P<last_max_abs>\S+) "
    r"first=\[(?P<first>[^\]]*)\] last_first=\[(?P<last_first>[^\]]*)\]"
)


def parse_first(s):
    return [float(v) for v in s.split(",") if v != ""]


def parse_ours(path):
    stages = {}
    order = []
    for line in Path(path).read_text().splitlines():
        m = LINE_RE.search(line)
        if not m:
            continue
        d = m.groupdict()
        rec = {
            "rows": int(d["rows"]),
            "cols": int(d["cols"]),
            "mean": float(d["mean"]),
            "var": float(d["var"]),
            "max_abs": float(d["max_abs"]),
            "last_mean": float(d["last_mean"]),
            "last_var": float(d["last_var"]),
            "last_max_abs": float(d["last_max_abs"]),
            "first": parse_first(d["first"]),
            "last_first": parse_first(d["last_first"]),
        }
        stages[d["stage"]] = rec
        order.append(d["stage"])
    return stages, order


def stats_of(a, first_n=FIRST_N):
    """Same reduction as muse_glimmer::trace::stats_of (f64)."""
    a64 = a.astype(np.float64)
    mean = float(a64.mean())
    var = float(a64.var())  # population variance
    return {
        "mean": mean,
        "var": var,
        "max_abs": float(np.abs(a64).max()),
        "first": [float(v) for v in a[:first_n]],
    }


def load_ref(d, stem, manifest):
    dims = manifest[stem]
    a = np.fromfile(Path(d) / f"{stem}.bin", dtype="<f4")
    total = 1
    for v in dims:
        total *= v
    assert a.size == total, f"{stem}: {a.size} != prod({dims})"
    return a, dims


def reduce_ref(d, manifest, n_layers):
    """Reduce the cb_dump_glimmer tensors to per-stage records in
    the same shape as the parsed trace lines."""
    out = {}

    def stream_record(stem):
        a, dims = load_ref(d, stem, manifest)
        width = dims[0]
        rows = a.size // width
        full = stats_of(a)
        last = stats_of(a[-width:])
        return {
            "rows": rows,
            "cols": width,
            "mean": full["mean"],
            "var": full["var"],
            "max_abs": full["max_abs"],
            "first": full["first"],
            "last_mean": last["mean"],
            "last_var": last["var"],
            "last_max_abs": last["max_abs"],
            "last_first": last["first"],
        }

    def last_row_record(stem):
        a, dims = load_ref(d, stem, manifest)
        width = dims[0]
        last = stats_of(a[-width:])
        return {
            "rows": 1,
            "cols": width,
            "mean": last["mean"],
            "var": last["var"],
            "max_abs": last["max_abs"],
            "first": last["first"],
            "last_mean": last["mean"],
            "last_var": last["var"],
            "last_max_abs": last["max_abs"],
            "last_first": last["first"],
        }

    if "embed" in manifest:
        out["embed"] = stream_record("embed")
    for il in range(n_layers):
        mid, outp = f"L{il:02d}_mid", f"L{il:02d}_out"
        if mid in manifest:
            out[f"layer.{il}.mid"] = stream_record(mid)
        if outp in manifest:
            out[f"layer.{il}.out"] = stream_record(outp)
    if "result_norm" in manifest:
        out["final_norm"] = last_row_record("result_norm")
    logits_info = None
    if "logits" in manifest:
        out["logits"] = last_row_record("logits")
        a, dims = load_ref(d, "logits", manifest)
        width = dims[0]
        last = a[-width:].astype(np.float64)
        top = int(np.argmax(last))
        p = float(np.exp(last - last.max())[top] / np.exp(last - last.max()).sum())
        logits_info = (top, float(last[top]), p)
    extra = {}
    if "embd_raw" in manifest:
        extra["embd_raw"] = stream_record("embd_raw")
    return out, extra, logits_info


def rel(a, b):
    return abs(a - b) / max(abs(a), abs(b), 1e-12)


def judge(our, ref):
    """Plan reading rule. Returns (ok, metrics dict)."""
    std = math.sqrt(max(our["last_var"], ref["last_var"]))
    mean_shift = abs(our["last_mean"] - ref["last_mean"]) / max(std, 1e-12)
    var_rel = rel(our["last_var"], ref["last_var"])
    wstd = math.sqrt(max(our["var"], ref["var"]))
    w_mean_shift = abs(our["mean"] - ref["mean"]) / max(wstd, 1e-12)
    w_var_rel = rel(our["var"], ref["var"])
    first_d = max(
        (abs(x - y) for x, y in zip(our["last_first"], ref["last_first"])),
        default=0.0,
    )
    first_rel = first_d / max(std, 1e-12)
    ok = (
        mean_shift <= 1e-2
        and var_rel <= 1e-2
        and w_mean_shift <= 1e-2
        and w_var_rel <= 1e-2
        # The reading rule's "first values tracking": the first
        # values gate at the same band as the other criteria. This
        # is the only per-element check the comparator has; without
        # it a permutation passes as a match.
        and first_rel <= 1e-2
    )
    return ok, {
        "mean_shift_std": mean_shift,
        "var_rel": var_rel,
        "w_mean_shift_std": w_mean_shift,
        "w_var_rel": w_var_rel,
        "first_max_diff": first_d,
        "first_rel_std": first_rel,
    }


def main():
    our_path, ref_dir = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    manifest = json.loads((Path(ref_dir) / "manifest.json").read_text())
    ours, order = parse_ours(our_path)
    n_layers = sum(1 for s in ours if s.endswith(".out"))
    ref, extra, logits_info = reduce_ref(ref_dir, manifest, n_layers)

    print(f"{'stage':16s} {'verdict':9s} {'last mean shift (std)':>22s} "
          f"{'last var rel':>13s} {'whole var rel':>14s} {'first diff':>11s}")
    first_div = None
    no_ref = False
    prev_ok = True
    for stage in order:
        if stage not in ref:
            print(f"{stage:16s} {'NO REF':9s}")
            no_ref = True
            continue
        ok, mt = judge(ours[stage], ref[stage])
        verdict = "match" if ok else "DIVERGENT"
        mark = ""
        if not ok and first_div is None:
            first_div = stage
            mark = "  <-- FIRST DIVERGENT (input stage matched: %s)" % prev_ok
        print(f"{stage:16s} {verdict:9s} {mt['mean_shift_std']:22.3e} "
              f"{mt['var_rel']:13.3e} {mt['w_var_rel']:14.3e} "
              f"{mt['first_max_diff']:11.3e}{mark}")
        prev_ok = ok

    print(f"\nfirst divergent stage: {first_div}")
    if "embd_raw" in extra:
        e = extra["embd_raw"]
        print(f"reference embd_raw (pre-norm, info only): mean={e['mean']:.6e} "
              f"var={e['var']:.6e} max_abs={e['max_abs']:.6e}")
    if logits_info is not None:
        top, val, p = logits_info
        print(f"reference logits: top-1 id={top} logit={val:.4f} prob={p:.4f}")
    # The verdict is also the exit status: 1 on any divergence or on
    # a stage with no reference, 0 only on a full match.
    return 1 if (first_div is not None or no_ref) else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

===== END FILE: golden/tools/compare_traces.py =====

===== FILE: golden/tools/fork_margins.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fork-margin probe for a golden candidate (one-off analysis tool).

For every prompt where the candidate's completion diverges from the
golden fixture, find the first divergent index k, then ask llama.cpp
itself (throwaway CPU llama-server, same flags as gen_golden.py) for
the top-5 probabilities at that exact position, feeding the golden
prefix (prompt ids + golden completion ids before k) as token ids.

The reported margin is llama.cpp's own logit gap at the fork:
ln(p_winner) - ln(p_best_other). Greedy forks on margins smaller
than the cross-engine logit noise band are coin flips, not math
errors. The band referenced is the one RESULTS-layer-diff-qwen.md
measured on Qwen2.5-1.5B (up to ~0.78 logits); it was NOT measured
on the model probed here, and this script says so in its output.

Usage:
    fork_margins.py --golden <fixture.jsonl> --candidate <cand.jsonl>
                    --model <file.gguf>
                    [--bin-dir /home/server/llama.cpp/build-vulkan2/bin]
                    [--port 18931]

Standard library only.
"""

import argparse
import json
import math
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

QWEN_BAND = 0.78  # logits, cross-engine noise max measured on Qwen2.5


def load_records(path):
    records, order = {}, []
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            obj = json.loads(line)
            if "meta" in obj and "id" not in obj:
                continue
            records[obj["id"]] = obj
            order.append(obj["id"])
    return records, order


def first_divergence(g_ids, c_ids):
    n = min(len(g_ids), len(c_ids))
    for i in range(n):
        if g_ids[i] != c_ids[i]:
            return i
    if len(g_ids) != len(c_ids):
        return n
    return None


def wait_health(port, proc, log_path):
    url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/health"
    for _ in range(120):
        if proc.poll() is not None:
            tail = Path(log_path).read_text(errors="replace")[-2000:]
            raise RuntimeError(f"llama-server exited early; log tail:\n{tail}")
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=2) as r:
                if r.status == 200:
                    return
        except Exception:
            pass
        time.sleep(0.5)
    raise RuntimeError("llama-server did not become healthy in 60 s")


def top_probs(port, prefix_ids, n_probs=5):
    body = json.dumps({
        "prompt": prefix_ids,
        "n_predict": 1,
        "temperature": 0,
        "seed": 42,
        "n_probs": n_probs,
        "cache_prompt": False,
    }).encode("utf-8")
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/completion",
        data=body, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=600) as r:
        resp = json.loads(r.read().decode("utf-8"))
    if resp["tokens_evaluated"] != len(prefix_ids):
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"prefix length mismatch: server evaluated "
            f"{resp['tokens_evaluated']}, probe fed {len(prefix_ids)}")
    steps = resp["completion_probabilities"]
    if len(steps) != 1:
        raise RuntimeError(f"expected exactly 1 step, got {len(steps)}")
    return steps[0]


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--golden", required=True, type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--candidate", required=True, type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True, type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--bin-dir", type=Path,
                    default=Path("/home/server/llama.cpp/build-vulkan2/bin"))
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=18931)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    golden, order = load_records(args.golden)
    cand, _ = load_records(args.candidate)

    forks = []
    for pid in order:
        g, c = golden[pid], cand.get(pid)
        if c is None:
            print(f"{pid}: MISSING in candidate, skipped")
            continue
        if g["prompt_token_ids"] != c.get("prompt_token_ids"):
            print(f"{pid}: prompt ids differ, fork probe not meaningful, skipped")
            continue
        k = first_divergence(g["completion_token_ids"],
                             c["completion_token_ids"])
        if k is None:
            continue
        g_id = g["completion_token_ids"][k] if k < len(g["completion_token_ids"]) else None
        c_id = c["completion_token_ids"][k] if k < len(c["completion_token_ids"]) else None
        prefix = g["prompt_token_ids"] + g["completion_token_ids"][:k]
        forks.append((pid, k, g_id, c_id, prefix))

    if not forks:
        print("no divergent prompts to probe")
        return 0

    import tempfile
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".log", delete=False) as log:
        log_path = log.name
    proc = subprocess.Popen(
        [str(args.bin_dir / "llama-server"), "-m", str(args.model),
         "-ngl", "0", "-c", "512", "-t", "8",
         "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", str(args.port)],
        stdout=open(log_path, "ab"), stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
    )
    try:
        wait_health(args.port, proc, log_path)
        print(f"probing {len(forks)} fork(s); band reference: {QWEN_BAND} "
              f"logits (measured on Qwen2.5-1.5B, not this model)")
        for pid, k, g_id, c_id, prefix in forks:
            step = top_probs(args.port, prefix)
            # This llama.cpp build returns per-step "top_logprobs":
            # [{id, token, bytes, logprob}], already in logit units.
            tops = step.get("top_logprobs") or []
            by_id = {p["id"]: p["logprob"] for p in tops}
            win = tops[0] if tops else None
            others = [p for p in tops if p["id"] != g_id]
            lp_win = by_id.get(g_id)
            lp_other = others[0]["logprob"] if others else None
            line = f"{pid}: fork at {k}, golden {g_id} vs candidate {c_id}"
            if win is not None and win["id"] != g_id:
                line += (f"; NOTE llama.cpp top-1 here is {win['id']} "
                         f"(logprob={win['logprob']:.3f}), "
                         f"not the fixture winner")
            if lp_win is not None and lp_other is not None:
                margin = lp_win - lp_other
                verdict = ("within" if margin < QWEN_BAND else "EXCEEDS")
                line += (f"; llama.cpp winner margin = {margin:.3f} logits "
                         f"-> {verdict} the {QWEN_BAND} band")
            else:
                line += "; winner not in returned top-5, margin not measurable"
            if c_id in by_id and lp_win is not None:
                gap = lp_win - by_id[c_id]
                line += f"; winner-vs-candidate gap = {gap:.3f} logits"
            elif c_id is not None:
                line += "; candidate token outside llama.cpp top-5"
            print(line)
    finally:
        proc.terminate()
        try:
            proc.wait(timeout=10)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            proc.kill()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

===== END FILE: golden/tools/fork_margins.py =====

===== FILE: golden/tools/test_verdict_tools.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Regression tests for the golden verdict tools' verdict plumbing.

Pins the critic-panel Category F fixes (2026-11-07):

- compare_traces: the first values gate the match (a permuted tensor
  with identical mean/variance must print DIVERGENT), and the process
  exits 1 on a divergence or a stage with no reference, 0 only on a
  full match.
- compare_layers stats(): cosine is 0.0 when exactly one side is all
  zeros, 1.0 only when both are (or when the tensors truly agree).

Fixtures are generated in a temp dir; nothing is read from the tree
beyond the tools themselves. Usage: test_verdict_tools.py; exits 0
when every case passes.
"""

import importlib.util
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
FAILURES = []


def check(name, cond, detail=""):
    print(f"{'PASS' if cond else 'FAIL'}  {name}" + (f"  ({detail})" if detail else ""))
    if not cond:
        FAILURES.append(name)


def run_traces(trace_path, ref_dir):
    return subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, str(HERE / "compare_traces.py"), str(trace_path), str(ref_dir)],
        capture_output=True, text=True)


def trace_line(stage, first):
    f = ",".join(repr(float(v)) for v in first)
    return (f"stage={stage} rows=1 cols=4 n=4 mean=2.5 var=1.25 max_abs=4.0 "
            f"last_mean=2.5 last_var=1.25 last_max_abs=4.0 "
            f"first=[{f}] last_first=[{f}]")


def main():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
        td = Path(td)
        ref = td / "ref"
        ref.mkdir()
        # Reference embed tensor [1,2,3,4].
        np.array([1, 2, 3, 4], dtype="<f4").tofile(ref / "embed.bin")
        (ref / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps({"embed": [4, 1]}))

        # A permutation has identical mean, population variance and
        # max_abs; only the first values differ. It must NOT match.
        perm = td / "permuted.txt"
        perm.write_text(trace_line("embed", [4, 3, 2, 1]) + "\n")
        r = run_traces(perm, ref)
        check("compare_traces: permuted tensor is DIVERGENT",
              "DIVERGENT" in r.stdout and "first divergent stage: embed" in r.stdout,
              f"rc={r.returncode}")
        check("compare_traces: permuted tensor exits 1", r.returncode == 1)

        # The faithful trace matches and exits 0.
        clean = td / "clean.txt"
        clean.write_text(trace_line("embed", [1, 2, 3, 4]) + "\n")
        r = run_traces(clean, ref)
        check("compare_traces: faithful trace matches and exits 0",
              "match" in r.stdout and "first divergent stage: None" in r.stdout
              and r.returncode == 0, f"rc={r.returncode}")

        # A stage with no reference tensor fails the run.
        noref = td / "noref.txt"
        noref.write_text(trace_line("embed", [1, 2, 3, 4]) + "\n"
                         + trace_line("layer.0.out", [1, 2, 3, 4]) + "\n")
        r = run_traces(noref, ref)
        check("compare_traces: NO REF stage exits 1",
              "NO REF" in r.stdout and r.returncode == 1, f"rc={r.returncode}")

    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("compare_layers", HERE / "compare_layers.py")
    cl = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(cl)
    zeros = np.zeros((2, 4))
    live = np.full((2, 4), 0.05)
    check("compare_layers stats: dead vs live cosine is 0.0",
          cl.stats(zeros, live)[2] == 0.0, f"cos={cl.stats(zeros, live)[2]}")
    check("compare_layers stats: live vs dead cosine is 0.0",
          cl.stats(live, zeros)[2] == 0.0)
    check("compare_layers stats: both dead cosine is 1.0",
          cl.stats(zeros, zeros)[2] == 1.0)
    check("compare_layers stats: identical live cosine is 1.0",
          abs(cl.stats(live, live)[2] - 1.0) < 1e-12,
          f"cos={cl.stats(live, live)[2]}")

    print(f"\n{len(FAILURES)} failure(s)" if FAILURES else "\nall cases passed")
    return 1 if FAILURES else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

===== END FILE: golden/tools/test_verdict_tools.py =====
