# Mojo/MAX engine: design

Status: Waves A, B, C, D, and E landed, 2026-11-07/08, branch
`mojo-max-engine`, engine version 1.6. Wave E is CLOSED:
the batch (GEMM) prefill step now runs the resident chain
and the tiled split-KV attention (E1: 1,022-token batch arm
34,852 ms against the per-row arm's 45,042 ms on the final
tree, inversion removed; routing rule per-row below 16
tokens, batch at/above, as a config knob), decode launch
overhead cut (E2: zero-fill launches removed, splits==1
direct-output attention; step+logits wall 35,230 -> 32,491
us steady state), and the Wave A/C hygiene debts paid (E3:
budget-ledger unreserve, harness verdict-line extraction,
GLIMMER_* defaults folded into EngineConfig); golden PASS
on the final tree, record in
`bench/mojo-engine-wave-e-2026-11-08.md`. Wave D (the speed
wave) is CLOSED: all four lanes integrated (D1 GEMM prefill,
D2 attention occupancy, D3 GEMV tuning beyond K1, D4
activation residency + device KV wrap), record in
`bench/mojo-engine-wave-d-2026-11-08.md`. Wave B is CLOSED: the
end-to-end golden passed on the real Glimmer file (first 8
generated tokens exactly [13796, 26, 1573, 373, 290, 2167,
26899, 1212]), rung 3 (teacher-forced) passed 8/8, and rung 2
was counted by an independent Python Float64 spot check.
Wave C is CLOSED: the same generation now runs on the GPU
(device-resident weights and KV, per-position step semantics
unchanged) and the end-to-end golden passed on device -
GOLDEN_FIRST8_MATCH 1 in two consecutive runs, all 16 tokens
identical to the CPU run, teacher-forced 8/8 on device with
winning logits matching the CPU rung-3 record to about
1e-3. First GPU numbers (no verdict beyond the arithmetic):
prefill 684 ms for the 6-token prompt (CPU: 1,411,755 ms),
decode 0.1511 s/step, about 6.62 tok/s (CPU: about 253.6
s/step). The full records are
`bench/mojo-engine-wave-a-2026-11-07.md`,
`bench/mojo-engine-wave-b-2026-11-07.md`, and
`bench/mojo-engine-wave-c-2026-11-07.md`.
This branch starts the engine over on Mojo and MAX, on David's
order ("pause rust and golang.. create a new branch and let's
start over with Max and Mojo"). The Rust and Go trees are paused,
not deleted: they stay on `main` as the proven reference this
engine must match, piece by piece, under the parity law below.

## The stack, top to bottom

1. **Front end:** the engine's own Mojo API endpoint and
   testing dashboard (step 7, decided Mojo-only by David on
   2026-11-08). The Go platform and MAX Serve were both
   considered and rejected on that ruling.
2. **Host engine: Mojo.** Model loading, KV cache management,
   scheduling, sampling, the generation loop. One language for
   host and kernels is the point of the restart.
3. **Kernels: Mojo.** MAX's own kernel library where it fits
   (its tuned matmul, attention, and MoE kernels are Apache 2.0);
   hand-written, hand-TUNED custom kernels where it does not
   (our quantized formats, Q4_K first). Custom does not mean
   naive: see the speed law.
4. **Plumbing: MAX.** The MAX runtime compiles Mojo to the
   target chip and feeds it work. No wgpu, no Vulkan layer, no
   ash in this stack.
5. **Vendor drivers.** AMD's HIP stack on the RX 7900 XTX
   (gfx1100, a listed MAX target, proven in-house 2026-11-07),
   NVIDIA's driver on NVIDIA cards. Every stack ends here; this
   layer is never ours to write.

## Build order, piece by piece

Each step lands as its own lane on this branch, proves parity
(step's law below), and only then counts.

1. **GGUF loader. DONE (Wave A, Lane A1).** Parses the real
   Glimmer file: header, metadata, tensor directory, staged
   load (Mojo 1.2's stdlib has no mmap binding; staged reads
   serve the same bytes). Proven: 731 tensors, metadata spot
   values exact, fixture tensor bytes hash-matched.
2. **Dequant + GEMV kernels, TUNED from the start. DONE
   (Wave A, Lanes A2/A3).** K1 tuned to the r2sg shape:
   624.1 GB/s median, 74.4% of the recorded wgpu median, under
   the within-10% line; the correctness gate (rel 1.267e-07)
   is the binding constraint, gap analysis in the wave note.
   Q6_K, Q5_K, F32/F16 kernels built and GPU-proven at the
   recorded bars (straight ports; tuning them is later work).
   The elementwise ops (norms, RoPE, SwiGLU, residual, softmax,
   final-logit transform, embedding gather) also landed
   (Lane A4), and the tokenizer (Lane A5, 16/16 prompt parity).
3. **Attention. DONE (Wave B, Lane B2), GPU-proven.** Scores,
   masking, the sliding-window and global layer split, a
   flash-style decoding kernel (online softmax, no
   materialized score row). **OCCUPANCY DONE (Wave D, Lane
   D2):** shared-memory K/V tile staging (tile 32) and
   split-KV parallelism (exact logsumexp merge, splits by
   stored count, span 512, cap 8) are the production GPU
   path; at stored 4,096 the tiled split launch measured
   486.9 us against the Wave B kernel's 3,138.4 us
   interleaved (6.45x), correctness inside the Wave B bars
   on every fixture including 4,096-position RoPE and
   NoPE; record in bench/mojo-engine-wave-d-d2-2026-11-07.md.
4. **One full layer, then all layers. DONE (Wave B, Lane
   B3).** The full 52-layer forward runs per position on the
   CPU path; rung 1 (synthetic, both layer kinds, Float64
   reference) passes, rung 2 (real layers 0 and 3) is counted
   by the independent Float64 spot check, and rung 3
   (teacher-forced golden) passed 8/8 on the real file.
5. **Generation loop. DONE (Wave B, Lanes B1 + B4); GOLDEN
   VERDICT PASS.** Prefill and decode over the KV cache; the
   end-to-end run on the real file (runner at 4dc4921)
   produced 16 tokens whose first 8 are exactly the recorded
   golden [13796, 26, 1573, 373, 290, 2167, 26899, 1212],
   decoded text " Paris. It is the most populous city in
   France and the most populous". First-light CPU numbers
   (no verdict): prefill 1,411,755 ms for the 6-token prompt,
   decode about 253.6 s per step (about 0.0039 tok/s);
   speed is a later wave's work.
   **GPU PORT DONE (Wave C, Lanes C1-C4); GOLDEN VERDICT
   PASS ON DEVICE.** The forward now also runs as a
   device-resident GPU model (src/gpu/ plumbing, GPU layer
   assembly, GpuGlimmerModel behind the same ForwardModel
   trait, runner selects it with MOJO_ENGINE_GPU): weights
   and KV resident on the card (20,933,677,056 B reserved of
   the 24,696,061,952 B budget cap at full context), the
   end-to-end golden passed on device twice, and the
   teacher-forced walk passed 8/8 on device. GPU numbers:
   prefill 684 ms, decode 0.1511 s/step (about 6.62 tok/s),
   model open about 31.8 s (CPU model read plus device
   upload). Still owed, recorded in the wave note: a
   device-side visible-order KV gather, attention
   shared-memory tiling / split-KV occupancy work,
   activation residency, and GEMV tuning beyond K1.
   **ALL FOUR LANDED IN WAVE D** (Lanes D4, D2, D4, and D3
   respectively): windowed layers now run past the 2,048
   wrap on device, layer activations stay resident across
   the layer's ops (1.91x/1.60x warm medians on the C2
   harness shapes), and Q6_K/Q5_K/F16 GEMVs are tuned
   (410.9 / 361.9 / 717.9 GB/s). Wave D also added the
   batched GEMM prefill path (Lane D1): one GEMM launch per
   projection for the whole prompt batch, GEMM outputs
   bit-identical to the GEMV kernels per row, 1,022-token
   prefill 1.83x on its lane tree (74,636 ms vs 136,467 ms)
   and 402 ms for the 6-token golden prompt against Wave
   C's 684 ms. Still owed after Wave D: activation
   residency INSIDE prefill (KV appends and causal
   attention still run per position there) - LANDED IN
   WAVE E (Lane E1: the batch step is resident and runs
   the batched tiled split-KV attention; prefill routes
   per-row below 16 tokens and batched at/above, by the
   MOJO_ENGINE_PREFILL_BATCH_MIN_TOKENS knob). The
   temperature/top-k/top-p sampler family remains owed;
   the serving seam (step 7) is decided and built.
6. **Sampler. GREEDY LANDED (Wave B, Lane B4).** First-max
   tie-break, EOS excluded per engine.rs. The
   temperature/top-k/top-p family is still to come.
7. **Serving seam. DECIDED (David, 2026-11-08): Mojo-only.**
   The endpoint lives inside the engine process, written in
   Mojo (`src/serve/` + `src/runner/serve_main.mojo`): an
   OpenAI-shaped POST /v1/chat/completions over the generation
   loop (greedy only in v1, locked by name), /health,
   /v1/models with per-file fact sheets read from each GGUF's
   own metadata and tensor signatures, /stats, /debug/log,
   /openapi.json, a JSON-fed testing dashboard at /, on-disk
   run history at /history with export/import bundles, a
   measured-only /leaderboard (llama.cpp and the paused Rust
   engine appear as marked reference rows), and an MCP-style
   bridge (/mcp/tools, /mcp/call, JSON-RPC subset at /mcp).
   Transport is pure Mojo over POSIX sockets via libc FFI.
   MAX Serve is rejected (Python-based, not Mojo) and socket
   parity with the paused Go platform is rejected (Go) on the
   same Mojo-only ruling. Proof record:
   bench/mojo-engine-api-endpoint-2026-11-08.md.

## The parity law

Every piece proves its answers against the Rust engine's
recorded references before it counts: same fixture, same bars
(cosine and max relative error as recorded per kernel; identity
and golden token checks at the loop level). A piece that cannot
show its numbers is not done, however clean it compiles. The
kernel test set the pattern: the straight Mojo K1 port recorded
cosine 1.000000000, rel 8.941e-08 against the CPU reference on
the real fixture tensor, tighter than the shipped wgpu kernel's
own 1.267e-07.

## The speed law

A straight port is a correctness proof, not a speed result. The
kernel test measured it: in one interleaved cleared-card window,
the tuned wgpu K1 ran a median 838.4 GB/s; the straight Mojo
port of the same math ran 39.8 GB/s, 21x slower, because it
recomputes dequant per element, loads a byte at a time, and has
no subgroup reduction. Tuning is therefore budgeted work in
every kernel lane's plan, never an afterthought and never a
surprise. No kernel is called fast on a port's numbers.

Measured state after Wave D (2026-11-08): K1 624.1 GB/s
(74.4% of the wgpu median; its correctness gate is the
binding constraint and the bar question stays David's open
call), Q6_K 410.9 GB/s, Q5_K 361.9 GB/s, F16 717.9 GB/s
(D3); decode on the D3 lane tree 9.09 tok/s against Wave
C's 6.62; prefill 402 ms for the 6-token prompt and
74,636 ms at 1,022 tokens on the D1 lane tree (1.83x over
the Wave C path interleaved); attention at stored 4,096
runs 6.45x the Wave B kernel (D2). Reference points on the
same card: the paused Rust engine's plain decode about
34.5 tok/s, llama.cpp Vulkan decode 44.59 tok/s - the
remaining decode gap is the next speed target, and its
named lever is prefill/decode activation residency plus
further kernel tuning, in that order of evidence.

Measured state after Wave E (2026-11-08): prefill
residency landed in the batch step; on the final tree
the 1,022-token arms read batch 34,852 ms (29.3 tok/s)
against per-row 45,042 ms (22.7 tok/s) interleaved, and
the 6-token prefill 217 ms (per-row route). Decode:
E2's profile showed the step is launch-bound (about
3,900 enqueues/step; isolated ops sum well above the
whole-layer wall); zero-fill launch removal and the
splits==1 direct-output attention cut the steady-state
step+logits wall from 35,230 to 32,491 us (28.38 ->
30.78 tok/s by that measure); the runner's approximate
decode read 20.35 tok/s on the final tree. The next
named decode lever is step-level activation residency:
the hidden row still crosses host<->device between all
52 layers, and the KV append's mid-layer synchronize
caps host lookahead.

## Licensing constraints (facts, as of MAX 26.7)

- Mojo the language: Apache 2.0 with LLVM Exceptions.
- MAX: the MAX License. Free and royalty-free, including
  commercial use, on any hardware. Conditions that bind a
  public engine: MAX ships inside a product in object code
  form with the MAX License included; modified MAX source may
  not be published except by forking to contribute back to
  Modular's project; MAX may not be used as AI input to
  reimplement MAX; selling MAX as a hosted inference service
  carries the Modular Accelerated branding condition and
  written approval through Modular's brand portal.
- Each MAX release keeps the license terms it shipped with;
  later term changes do not reach back into 26.7.
- Our own code stays ours, under our own terms.

## Modularity

Grid-and-tiles, as everywhere in David's projects: one module
per job under `src/` (config, diag, gguf/, kernels/, and the
modules the build order adds), each independently testable,
each with the diag seam wired and named refusals for bad
inputs from birth. Operational limits are config with defaults
(`src/config.mojo`), never compiled-in constants.

===== FILE: mojo-engine/README.md =====
# mojo-engine

The from-scratch Mojo/MAX inference engine, started 2026-11-07
on the `mojo-max-engine` branch. It pauses the Rust engine and
the Go platform (both stay on `main`, proven, as the reference
this engine must match) and rebuilds the engine piece by piece
in Mojo, on the MAX runtime. Design, build order, and the
parity and speed laws: [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md).

## Setup

The toolchain is pinned by `pixi.toml` (Mojo 1.2.0, MAX 26.7,
the exact versions proved on the RX 7900 XTX by
`bench/mojo-kernel-test-2026-11-07.md`):

```sh
cd mojo-engine
pixi install
```

## Run

```sh
pixi run engine        # hello + config load (foundation scope)
```

Configuration is env over defaults in `src/config.mojo`:
`MOJO_ENGINE_MODEL_PATH`, `MOJO_ENGINE_CONTEXT_LEN`, and the
debug seam `MOJO_ENGINE_DEBUG` (any value but "" / "0" enables;
see `src/diag.mojo`).

## Test

```sh
pixi run test          # tests/run_tests.sh: mojo test, both seam modes
```

The suite covers config (defaults, env override, named
refusals), the diag seam (on fires, off silent, "0" does not
enable), and a CPU fixture test of the K1 kernel module on
synthetic Q4_K data with its own in-test reference. The real
Glimmer fixture runs on the server through the GPU path; see
`bench/mojo-engine-foundation-2026-11-07.md` for the foundation
proof and which fixture each half used.

## Layout

- `src/main.mojo` - entry point (hello, config, clean refusals)
- `src/config.mojo` - config: env over defaults, named refusals
- `src/diag.mojo` - the debug seam (MOJO_ENGINE_DEBUG)
- `src/gguf/loader.mojo` - loader interface; named
  not-implemented refusal until the loader lane lands
- `src/kernels/k1_gemv.mojo` - K1 Q4_K GEMV (GPU kernel + CPU
  twin), carried over from the kernel test, untuned by design
- `tests/` - the test suite and its runner

## Deliberately not built yet

The GGUF loader (next lane), every kernel past K1, attention,
the generation loop, the sampler, and any serving front end.
K1 is present as a correctness citizen, not a speed result:
its straight-port numbers and the tuning debt are recorded in
DESIGN.md under the speed law.

===== END FILE: mojo-engine/README.md =====

===== FILE: mojo-engine/WAVE_B_INTERFACES.md =====
# Wave B shared interfaces (coordinator contract, 2026-11-07)

Every Wave B lane builds against THIS page plus the Rust twins
named in its brief. Where a lane finds this contract wrong, it
stops and reports; it does not silently change the contract.
The coordinator reconciles at integration.

## Ground truth (Glimmer, from the Rust census, verified)

- 52 layers. Global attention at indices 3, 7, 11, ..., 51
  (index % 4 == 3; 13 layers). All other 39 layers are sliding
  window 2048 (`crates/attention/src/cache.rs`
  `glimmer_layer_pattern`, `crates/muse-glimmer/src/config.rs`).
- hidden 6656, FFN 19968, 32 Q heads, 2 KV heads, head dim 128.
  Q width 4096, KV width 256 per token per layer.
- RoPE base 500,000, interleaved (adjacent) pairing, sliding
  layers ONLY; globals are NoPE. In the Rust CPU path RoPE is
  applied to Q and K rows inside the attention step
  (`crates/cpu-compute/src/cpu.rs` rope_row + attention fn;
  `crates/attention/src/attention.rs` holds the math core).
- Score scale 1/sqrt(128) (`AttentionParams` default).
- RMS eps 1e-5 for the named norms; POST_NORM_EPS 1e-8 for the
  two post norms (`crates/muse-glimmer/src/model.rs`).
- Final logits: multiply by logit scale 0.1961161345243454
  FIRST, then softcap 20.0 * tanh(z/20) (Wave A final_logit op).
- Golden: prompt "The capital of France is" tokenizes (with
  BOS) to [200000, 954, 7963, 323, 11698, 373]; greedy
  generation must produce first 8 ids [13796, 26, 1573, 373,
  290, 2167, 26899, 1212] (" Paris. It is the most populous").
  First-token top-1 probability recorded ~0.4035 on the Rust
  CPU stack (llama.cpp 0.3962); a probability sanity band, not
  a gate. EOS from model metadata: tokenizer.ggml.eos_token_id
  = 200001 for this file; the golden run does not hit EOS in
  the first 8.

## Layer forward order (crates/muse-glimmer/src/model.rs
## forward_rows; the ONLY correct order)

embed(tokens) -> rms_norm_plain (weightless, eps 1e-5); then per
layer: residual = x; h = rms_norm(residual, attn_norm);
q = proj(h, attn_q); k = proj(h, attn_k); v = proj(h, attn_v);
q = rms_norm per-head (attn_q_norm, rows*32); k = rms_norm
per-head (attn_k_norm, rows*2); attn = attention(q, k, v, layer
kind, cache) [RoPE inside for sliding]; gate = proj(h,
attn_gate); attn = attn * sigmoid(gate); out = proj(attn,
attn_output); out = rms_norm(out, post_attention_norm, eps
1e-8); x = residual + out; residual = x; h = rms_norm(residual,
ffn_norm); ffn = swiglu_ffn(h) (gate/up projs, SwiGLU, down
proj); ffn = rms_norm(ffn, post_ffw_norm, eps 1e-8);
x = residual + ffn. Finish: final norm (output_norm weight,
eps 1e-5; confirm exact finish in model.rs finish_last) ->
lm_head (output.weight, Q5_K) -> final_logit transform.

Tensor names follow the GGUF file (blk.{i}.attn_norm.weight,
attn_q, attn_k, attn_v, attn_q_norm, attn_k_norm, attn_gate,
attn_output, post_attention_norm, ffn_norm, ffn_gate, ffn_up,
ffn_down, post_ffw_norm; token_embd.weight; output_norm.weight;
output.weight). Verify each against the loader census in code,
never from memory.

## B1 KV cache contract (src/kv/)

Mirror `crates/attention/src/cache.rs` semantics:
- LayerKind: Global | Windowed(window). Pattern fn for Glimmer.
- One layer store: flat f32 keys and values, one row per
  position (global) or ring slot (windowed), row =
  [num_kv_heads][head_dim] = 256 floats. Windowed slot =
  position % window; slot_position tracked; appended count is
  the next expected position.
- append(layer, k_row, v_row, position): refuses by name when
  position != appended for that layer (the Rust contract),
  when layer id is out of range, and on shape mismatch.
- Reads: key(layer, position, kv_head) / value(...) slices for
  positions still visible; visible range = [appended -
  stored, appended); a read of an evicted or future position
  refuses by name. stored_len(layer), next_position(layer).
- NO checkpoint/rewind in Wave B (spec decoding is a later
  wave); say so in the module header.
- Sizes from parameters (layer count, kinds, kv heads, head
  dim, context/window), never literals; the Glimmer defaults
  come from config at the call site.
- CPU-true storage (List[Float32]) with the layout above; the
  device seam is the row access functions. B2 reads through
  this contract only.

## B2 attention contract (src/attention/)

- CPU reference fn: attention_cpu(q for ONE position
  [32][128], cache view for the layer, position, kind) ->
  [32][128] output, computing: for each Q head h, kv_head =
  h // 16; scores over visible positions, scale 1/sqrt(128),
  causal by construction (only appended positions visible),
  window by the cache's visible range; softmax (Wave A
  softmax_cpu); weighted sum of values.
- RoPE: the CPU attention path applies rope to the Q row and
  to K rows exactly as the Rust CPU compute does (read
  cpu.rs: which K rows get rotated, at which positions, and
  whether rotated K is what the cache stores or rotation
  happens at read time; MIRROR IT, do not invent).
- GPU path: a kernel computing the same for one position
  against a device-resident copy of the layer's K/V rows;
  proven against the CPU twin on the card.
- Prefill (multi-position) attention may be built as the loop
  of the single-position fn over positions with the cache
  appended incrementally (llama-style causal), stated plainly
  if so; a batched prefill kernel is NOT required in Wave B.

## B3 model contract (src/model/)

- ModelWeights: built from the Wave A loader; per-layer tensor
  byte ranges + dtypes kept as loader views, dequant/GEMV via
  the Wave A kernels family CPU twins for the CPU path
  (k1_gemv_cpu for Q4_K, q6k_gemv_cpu, q5k_gemv_cpu,
  f32_gemv_cpu) so the whole forward runs on CPU for parity
  rungs; GPU residency is NOT required in Wave B (first light
  is a correctness wave; say so in the note).
- forward(tokens, cache) -> final hidden rows; logits_last(
  hidden_row) -> 202048 logits after final_logit transform.
- Per-layer capture hooks mirroring the Rust forward_capturing
  idea (layer input clone at named layers) for divergence
  isolation, behind the diag seam.

## B4 generation contract (src/generate/)

- generate(config, model, cache, prompt_ids, max_tokens) ->
  List[Int] generated ids: prefill = forward over prompt ids
  (positions 0..n-1 appended to cache layer by layer inside
  forward), then decode loop: argmax of logits_last -> next
  id; stop when id == eos (from metadata via the caller) or
  max_tokens reached; the sampled token is fed back as a
  one-token forward at the next position.
- Greedy argmax with first-max tie-break (lowest index), the
  Rust sampler's greedy rule; confirm in
  crates/itak-engine/src/sampler.rs.
- Diag per token through the seam: token id + position.
- The loop depends on B3's forward/logits signatures and B1's
  cache type; until integration it builds against a mock
  forward with the same shapes (the brief's VM proof).

## Suite wiring

New TestSuite files are added to tests/run_tests.sh's list by
the COORDINATOR at integration, not by lanes (one editor of
that file). Lanes ship their test files and state their
expected tallies. Every module: diag wired, named refusals,
`mojo format` clean, no compiler warnings introduced.

===== END FILE: mojo-engine/WAVE_B_INTERFACES.md =====

===== FILE: mojo-engine/WAVE_C_INTERFACES.md =====
# Wave C interfaces contract: the device seam

Status: coordinator contract, written before Lane C1/C2/C3
code, 2026-11-07 (the wave closes 2026-11-08 by the clock if
it runs long; the bench note carries the real date). Branch
`mojo-max-engine`, base ae0a053 (engine 1.3, Wave B golden
PASS on the CPU path). This file is the agreement the lanes
code against; the coordinator reconciles deviations at
integration and updates this file to match what shipped.

## The port shape (decided, not negotiable per lane)

The CPU twins stay as the parity reference and the fallback.
The GPU path is a device-resident forward with the CPU
model's EXACT per-position step semantics (Wave B shape:
step(token, position) through embedding, 52 layers, head;
prefill is the step loop, there is no batched prefill):

- Weights are uploaded ONCE at load and stay resident.
- The KV cache is resident on device with B1's exact layout
  and semantics (see DeviceKv below); its CPU semantics do
  not change.
- Activations are host `List[Float32]` rows at the layer
  boundary: each op uploads its input row(s), launches its
  device kernel against resident weights/KV, and downloads
  its output row. Activation traffic per step is tens of KB;
  weight and KV traffic is zero after load. A fully
  device-resident activation chain is a later wave's
  optimization, not this wave's correctness risk.
- Argmax parity is the hard gate at the model level; float32
  accumulation reordering on device is expected and reported
  inside the established tolerance class (cosine / max rel
  vs the CPU twin, bars as in Waves A and B).

## Memory budget (planned in numbers before the first run)

Card: RX 7900 XTX, 24 GiB = 25,769,803,776 B total.

- Weights resident: the sum of the file's tensor data bytes,
  computed exactly from the loader at upload time and printed
  by the C1 proof. Planning upper bound: the whole file,
  16,756,683,904 B.
- Device KV (f32, window-capped at the configured context
  length, B1 accounting): 3,653,238,784 B at context 131,072
  (13 global layers x 131,072 positions + 39 windowed layers
  x 2,048 positions, 2,048 B per position per layer for K+V).
- Scratch and activations envelope: 536,870,912 B (512 MiB).
  The largest single activation is the logits row,
  202,048 x 4 B = 808,192 B; everything else is hidden/FFN
  rows and one-row staging buffers.
- Planning total: 20,946,793,600 B, about 19.5 GiB, under
  the cap below by about 3.75 GB.

Budget cap: card total minus a 1 GiB reserve =
24,696,061,952 B by default, overridable through config
(`MOJO_ENGINE_GPU_BUDGET_BYTES`, parsed and refused by name
in config.mojo like the other values; Lane C1 owns that
config addition). If the computed resident total exceeds
the cap, construction refuses by name:
`gpu_budget_exceeded`. The observed resident figure (sysfs
VRAM used delta in the server window) is recorded in the
bench note next to this plan.

## Lane C1: src/gpu/ (device plumbing) - owns this package

New package `src/gpu/` with `__init__.mojo`, containing:

- `context.mojo`: `GpuRuntime` - owns the MAX
  `DeviceContext`, the budget accounting (weights bytes +
  KV bytes + scratch envelope vs cap, refusal above), and
  the copy helpers every other lane uses:
  `upload_u8(rt, List[UInt8]) -> DeviceBuffer[DType.uint8]`,
  `upload_f32(rt, List[Float32]) -> DeviceBuffer[DType.float32]`,
  `download_f32(rt, DeviceBuffer[DType.float32], n) -> List[Float32]`,
  plus zero-filled device buffer constructors by dtype and
  element count. Named refusals: `gpu_no_device` (context
  creation finds no device), `gpu_budget_exceeded`,
  `gpu_copy_shape` (length mismatches). Diag lines through
  the existing seam (`gpu` phase).
- `weights.mojo`: `DeviceWeights` - built from a
  `GlimmerModel`'s slots (the CPU model stays the loader of
  record; its cached bytes are the upload source). One
  device buffer per tensor slot: quantized and F16 slots as
  uint8 byte buffers over the slot's raw bytes, F32 slots as
  float32 buffers over the slot's values. The embedding
  slot, the output (head) slot, and the final-norm values
  get named accessors; per-layer slots are reached by
  (layer, suffix_index) exactly as `GlimmerModel.slot`.
  Accessors return the buffer AND the slot's type_id, rows,
  cols so launchers never guess. The exact resident byte
  total is accumulated during construction and checked
  against the budget before the last buffer is created
  (refuse first, allocate second, where the sizes are known
  up front - they are).
- `device_kv.mojo`: `DeviceKvCache` - per layer, two float32
  device buffers (K and V), each
  `capacity_positions x kv_heads x head_dim`, where
  capacity_positions is the layer's window (2,048) for
  windowed layers and the configured context length for
  global layers: B1's layout, byte for byte (row = one
  position's [kv_heads][head_dim], slot = position % window
  for windowed layers, slot = position for global layers).
  Semantics mirror `KvCache` exactly: appends in order only,
  reads by absolute position, the same refusal names as B1
  for out-of-order append / evicted or unwritten read / bad
  shape (prefix `gpu_kv_` where a name would collide).
  Append path: the caller passes the position's K and V rows
  as host lists (already rotated for sliding layers - the
  rotation is the model layer's job, exactly as in the CPU
  step); the implementation stages the row and scatters it
  into the slot (a small copy kernel in this file is the
  expected shape; whole-buffer copies are forbidden - they
  would move gigabytes per token).
  Read path for attention: `key_buffer(layer)` /
  `value_buffer(layer)` expose the raw device buffers, plus
  `stored_len(layer)` and `first_visible_position(layer)`
  with B1's meanings. WAVE C LIMIT, stated plainly: the
  attention kernel consumes visible rows in position order
  from offset 0, which equals slot order only before a
  windowed layer wraps. The GPU layer therefore refuses by
  name (`gpu_kv_window_wrapped`) when a windowed layer's
  append would wrap past its window; the CPU path remains
  the fallback for contexts beyond 2,048 positions and a
  device-side visible-order gather is owed work, recorded
  in the bench note. The golden run (22 positions) never
  approaches the wrap.
  Proof obligations (Lane C1): VM unit tests for the pure
  parts (budget arithmetic, slot/layout arithmetic, refusal
  names) wired by the coordinator into run_tests.sh; a
  server proof main (`tests/server_proof_gpu_plumbing.mojo`)
  that uploads the real model and hashes
  blk.0.ffn_gate.weight back from the device byte-exact
  against the loader's bytes (the Wave A FNV-1a64 /
  sha256 fixture check is the pattern), then runs a KV
  write/read sequence on device (including positions
  2047/2048/2049 on a small synthetic window config and a
  global sibling) compared element-exact against B1's CPU
  cache fed the same rows.

## Lane C2: GPU layer assembly - owns these files

- `src/model/gpu_layer.mojo`: host-side launch wrappers and
  the layer step. Public surface the other lanes code
  against:
  - `gpu_logits(rt, weights, hidden) -> List[Float32]`:
    final rms_norm (rms_norm_kernel, grid = 1 row) + the
    head GEMV dispatched by the output slot's dtype (Q5_K
    on Glimmer: q5k_gemv_kernel over 202,048 rows) +
    final_logit_kernel (scale-then-softcap). Same math as
    `GlimmerModel.logits`, device kernels.
  - `gpu_layer_step(rt, weights, kv, cpu_model, x, layer,
    position) -> List[Float32]`: statement-for-statement the
    CPU `layer_step`, with every projection and op launched
    on device: rms_norm_kernel for the norms (per-head Q/K
    norms launch rms_norm_kernel with grid = head count,
    width = head_dim, exactly as gpu_proof_ops proved the
    launcher); GEMV launches dispatched by slot dtype
    (k1 grid rows//ROWS_PER_WG block THREADS from
    k1_gemv.mojo; q6k/q5k/f32/f16 grid rows block 256);
    RoPE via rope_kernel (positions buffer filled with the
    step's absolute position; sliding layers rotate the K
    row BEFORE the DeviceKv append - write-time rotation,
    cache holds rotated K, the Wave B law - and rotate the
    Q row before the attention launch, because
    attention_kernel's contract is PRE-ROTATED Q and K);
    attention via attention_kernel launched directly on the
    DeviceKv buffers (grid = q_heads, block = ATTN_THREADS,
    stored = kv.stored_len, group = q_heads // kv_heads,
    scale = 1/sqrt(head_dim)); the sigmoid gate assembly
    (attn * sigmoid(gate)) and SwiGLU (swiglu_kernel exists;
    the gate assembly needs one small new elementwise kernel
    - put it in this file); residual adds via
    residual_add_kernel or host adds (say which, and why;
    host adds on downloaded rows are acceptable in this
    wave's shape).
    `cpu_model` is borrowed for config and the F32 norm
    weight values until DeviceWeights grows f32 accessors
    for every norm - prefer DeviceWeights accessors; if a
    norm weight must be uploaded per call, say so in the
    bench note (they are 26 KB; correctness first).
  - Captures: the same capture hooks as the CPU step
    (embed, named-layer in/out) or an explicit statement
    that the CPU model's captures are the isolation tool
    (they are; C3's divergence work uses CPU captures plus
    C2's per-layer server proof).
- `src/ops/gpu_embedding.mojo`: the device embedding row:
  a kernel that dequantizes one row of the embedding table
  on device for the table's actual dtype (Q4_K on Glimmer;
  Q6_K/Q5_K/F16/F32 handled or refused by name), proven
  against `GlimmerModel.embed_token` (the CPU twin) on the
  VM-independent server proof and in C2's layer proof by
  construction. Public surface:
  `gpu_embed_token(rt, weights, token) -> List[Float32]`.
- Proof obligations (Lane C2): a server proof main
  (`tests/server_proof_gpu_layer.mojo`) running layer 0
  (sliding) and layer 3 (global) at position 0 on the real
  weights with the rung-2 input construction (the model's
  own embedding + plain norm for token 13796, position 0),
  compared against the COUNTED rung-2 outputs (layer 0 sum
  65.22733633872122, first8 [0.08513339, 0.026624471,
  -0.42816293, 3.276528, -1.1669861, 2.0494282, -0.08531731,
  0.34014347]; layer 3 sum 157.77914571017027, first8
  [1.254974, -0.3695352, -0.49299628, 1.3146128, -0.27929068,
  1.1605207, 0.099737644, 0.68446195]). Bar: cosine >=
  0.999999 and max rel <= 1e-4 against those rows (the
  rung-1 bar class; the spot check counted the CPU rows at
  ~1e-6 against Float64, so this bar has two orders of
  headroom for device accumulation reordering), sums
  reported alongside. A fresh position-0 step on a FRESH
  DeviceKv per layer proof (each proof layer runs as the
  model's layer index so its kind and weights are real;
  state exactly how the proof drives a single layer).

## Lane C3: GPU generation - owns these files

- `src/model/gpu_model.mojo`: `GpuGlimmerModel` implementing
  the SAME `ForwardModel` trait (step/logits) over
  GpuRuntime + DeviceWeights + DeviceKvCache + C2's
  gpu_layer_step / gpu_logits / gpu_embed_token, with the
  CPU GlimmerModel held for config, captures, and fallback.
  step() mirrors the CPU step statement for statement
  (embedding via gpu_embed_token, plain rms_norm via
  rms_norm_kernel, layers via gpu_layer_step).
- `src/runner/generate_main.mojo` (edit, minimal): select
  the GPU model when the environment variable
  `MOJO_ENGINE_GPU` is set to a value other than "" and
  "0" (the diag seam's convention), default CPU exactly as
  Wave B shipped, so the Wave B proof still reproduces.
  The runner's printed lines (PROMPT_IDS, TOKENS,
  GOLDEN_FIRST8_MATCH, TEXT_STRICT_OK, timings) stay
  byte-compatible; add one line naming the path taken
  (MODEL_PATH_KIND gpu|cpu).
- `tests/server_proof_gpu_generate.mojo`: proof order per
  the wave brief: (1) teacher-forced check on device,
  positions 0..7 against the golden walk (prompt
  [200000, 954, 7963, 323, 11698, 373] teacher-forced must
  predict [13796, 26, 1573, 373, 290, 2167, 26899, 1212],
  8 of 8, printed per position); (2) the end-to-end runner
  run itself is the coordinator's integration window, not
  this file's job - this file prints its own verdict lines
  and exits nonzero on any mismatch.

## Lane C4: measurement - owns the bench note and timing

- `mojo-engine/tests/wave_c_timing.sh`: the timing harness
  for the final window: staged from the exact commit,
  runs the runner on the GPU path (and the C3 teacher-forced
  proof), captures prefill ms (the runner's own printed
  prefill measurement construction, same as Wave B's: a
  fresh model stepping the prompt ids) and decode s/step
  and tok/s from the generate run, each number read back
  from the actual log file in the foreground (the evidence
  law: backgrounded exec-completion output is not evidence).
- The bench note itself is written by the coordinator from
  the lane reports plus C4's timing output; C4's lane
  report supplies the protocol and any control runs it
  executed.

## Shared rules (all lanes)

- File ownership above is exclusive. `tests/run_tests.sh`
  is coordinator-only; lanes add test files and name them
  in their reports for wiring. `src/config.mojo` is C1-only
  this wave. Existing kernel/op modules are read-only for
  all lanes (their kernels are launched, never edited); a
  defect found in one is reported to the coordinator, not
  fixed inside a lane.
- Every module keeps the house law: diag seam wired, named
  refusals, limits from config with defaults.
- Server windows: phase lock
  `flock -w 14400 /tmp/itak-phase.lock`, one heavy job at a
  time, fresh staging (git archive of the exact commit,
  STAGED_COMMIT stamp, staged file hash), tenants per the
  CURRENT host state (see the wave brief: only
  cortex-embed.service holds the card; the two retired
  containers do not exist), VRAM measured via sysfs at both
  ends of every window, restore exactly what was stopped.
- GPU tests skip cleanly on the VM (no device) and RUN on
  the card; every tally in every report says which.
