# attention package: grouped-query attention for the Mojo/MAX
# engine (single-position CPU twin + GPU kernel, prefill loop).
# Lane B2, 2026-11-07. See attention.mojo for the seam contract
# (flat visible-order K/V stores, never a cache object) and the
# RoPE read-time/write-time note.

===== END FILE: mojo-engine/src/attention/__init__.mojo =====

===== FILE: mojo-engine/src/attention/attention.mojo =====
# attention.mojo - single-position grouped-query attention,
# Lane B2 (Wave B). CPU twin + GPU kernel.
#
# Semantic references (Rust, branch main):
#   crates/attention/src/attention.rs::gqa_attention
#     The math core: GQA head sharing (kv_head = q_head //
#     (num_q_heads / num_kv_heads); Glimmer 32 Q / 2 KV, so
#     kv_head = q_head // 16), score scale 1/sqrt(head_dim),
#     causal + window masking over absolute positions, softmax
#     (max-subtracted), weighted sum of values. That core takes
#     PRE-ROTATED queries and keys: "RoPE is the caller's job."
#   crates/cpu-compute/src/cpu.rs::Compute::attention +
#     rope_row (the caller, and the RoPE finding this lane
#     mirrors exactly):
#     - The loop is one position at a time: rotate, append,
#       attend. Prefill and decode share this path; decode is
#       the rows == 1 case.
#     - RoPE runs on SLIDING-window layers only, at the SWA
#       base (500,000 for Glimmer). Global layers are NoPE:
#       Q and K pass through unrotated.
#     - rope_row rotates EVERY head of the position's Q row
#       (all 32 Q heads) and EVERY head of the position's K
#       row (both KV heads), each head at the SAME absolute
#       position (the position being appended), interleaved
#       pairing via torch-math rope_interleaved (Wave A
#       ops/rope.rope_cpu).
#     - The ROTATED K row is what gets appended: the Rust
#       cache holds rotated K (and raw V). Rotation happens
#       at WRITE time, once, when the position is appended;
#       keys already in the cache are never re-rotated.
#
# THE SEAM (stated plainly, per the Wave B brief): this module
# never takes a cache object. Per layer, the caller passes
# plain flat stores in VISIBLE ORDER plus range parameters:
#   keys   flat [stored][num_kv_heads][head_dim]
#   values flat [stored][num_kv_heads][head_dim]
#   first_visible: the absolute position of row 0
#   stored: the number of visible rows
# Visible order is exactly the Rust CacheView's presentation:
# row i is view index i, its absolute position is
# first_visible + i (CacheView::position_at), and the head
# slice is view.key(i, kv_head) / view.value(i, kv_head). The
# coordinator wires B1's accessors to this layout at
# integration; for a windowed (ring) layer that means rows
# gathered in position order starting at slot
# first_visible % window, NOT the raw ring buffer when it has
# wrapped.
#
# RoPE AT READ TIME (the one deliberate storage difference):
# attention_cpu takes RAW (unrotated) Q and K and applies the
# rotation at read time: Q at `position`, every visible K row
# at its own absolute position first_visible + i, both via
# Wave A's rope_cpu, both only when rope_base != ROPE_NONE.
# The outputs are the Rust path's outputs: rotation is a
# fixed per-position transform, so applying it to a K row at
# read time yields the same rotated row the Rust path stored
# at write time (rope_cpu is deterministic on the same raw
# values). The storage consequence for integration: a caller
# using attention_cpu must pass RAW keys, so B3 must append
# raw K to the B1 cache on this seam. If the coordinator
# instead keeps the Rust storage exactly (B1 holds ROTATED
# K), call attention_cpu_rotated_cache below, which rotates
# only Q and never touches the keys. The two functions share
# one implementation; the flag is explicit, never guessed.
#
# Sliding vs global differs ONLY through (a) the visible
# range the caller passes (the window is the cache's job,
# B1) and (b) the rope parameter: a base for sliding layers,
# ROPE_NONE for globals (NoPE). There is no layer-kind
# argument and no window arithmetic in the single-position
# function, exactly as the contract states.
#
# GPU kernel: attention_kernel mirrors the Rust math core
# (attention.rs): it consumes PRE-ROTATED Q/K device buffers
# (rotation is the separate Wave A rope op / rope_cpu step,
# as in Rust where gqa_attention takes pre-rotated inputs).
# It is a flash-style DECODING kernel: one block per Q head,
# a single streaming pass over positions, online softmax
# (running max, running sum, per-channel accumulators
# rescaled per position), the score row is never
# materialized, and each position's dot is a shared-memory
# tree reduction. That kernel is RETAINED unchanged as the
# Wave B reference shape (the A/B baseline in the proofs).
#
# WAVE D (Lane D2, occupancy): attention_tiled_kernel +
# attention_merge_kernel below are the production GPU path.
# The tiled kernel stages K/V tiles of TILE positions in
# shared memory (one tile buffer, reused for K then V), one
# block per (Q head, split): the KV sequence is SPLIT across
# blocks (split-KV), each block runs the same online-softmax
# over its range tile by tile and writes an UNNORMALIZED
# partial (acc, max, sum); the merge kernel combines the
# partials in split order with exact logsumexp rescaling
# (each partial rescaled by exp(its max - the combined max),
# no approximation). Scores are computed per tile from the
# staged K (one thread per position, sequential over the
# head dim in shared memory), so the per-position shared-
# memory tree reduction of the Wave B kernel (a barrier
# chain per position) is gone: barriers happen per tile.
# WAVE E (Lane E2): attention_tiled_direct_kernel is the
# splits == 1 form of the tiled kernel with the merge folded
# into the same launch (direct normalized write, no partial
# buffers, no merge launch); its CPU twin is
# attention_direct_cpu. The resident chain launches it
# exactly when its split chooser returns 1 (the short
# regime, stored <= one split span); splits >= 2 keep the
# tiled + merge pair unchanged.
#
# Prefill note: this engine has no batched prefill kernel -
# per the Wave C contract, prefill IS the step loop, so
# prefill positions run through this same kernel at growing
# stored counts; the split chooser keeps splits at 1 until
# the stored count passes one split span, so short prefill
# steps pay no merge cost beyond the trivial 1-split pass.
# The CPU twins of the split path (attention_split_partials_
# cpu / attention_merge_partials_cpu / attention_split_cpu)
# mirror the kernels' Float32 arithmetic tile by tile and
# are the VM-side proof surface. Trial record (tile sizes,
# split factors, kept structure): bench/mojo-engine-wave-d-
# 2026-11-07.md.
#
# Named refusals: attention_cpu_bad_shape,
# attention_cpu_nondivisible_heads,
# attention_cpu_no_visible_keys, attention_cpu_bad_position,
# attention_cpu_bad_rope_base, attention_tiled_bad_tile,
# attention_split_bad_shape, attention_split_bad_splits,
# attention_split_bad_config, attention_split_bad_range,
# attention_split_empty_partials.

from std.math import sqrt, exp, isnan, isinf
from max.gpu import thread_idx, block_idx, block_dim, barrier
from max.gpu.memory import AddressSpace
from std.memory import stack_allocation

from diag import log_debug
from ops.rope import rope_cpu
from ops.softmax import softmax_cpu

comptime ROPE_NONE = Float32(0.0)
comptime ATTN_THREADS = 128


def _validate(
    q_len: Int,
    keys_len: Int,
    values_len: Int,
    first_visible: Int,
    stored: Int,
    num_q_heads: Int,
    num_kv_heads: Int,
    head_dim: Int,
    position: Int,
    rope_base: Float32,
) raises -> Int:
    """Shared shape/range checks; returns the causal row count."""
    if head_dim < 2 or head_dim % 2 != 0:
        raise Error(
            "attention_cpu_bad_shape: head_dim must be even and >= 2, got "
            + String(head_dim)
        )
    if num_q_heads <= 0 or num_kv_heads <= 0:
        raise Error(
            "attention_cpu_bad_shape: head counts must be > 0, got "
            + String(num_q_heads)
            + " q heads, "
            + String(num_kv_heads)
            + " kv heads"
        )
    if num_q_heads % num_kv_heads != 0:
        raise Error(
            "attention_cpu_nondivisible_heads: "
            + String(num_q_heads)
            + " q heads do not divide into "
            + String(num_kv_heads)
            + " kv heads"
        )
    if q_len != num_q_heads * head_dim:
        raise Error(
            "attention_cpu_bad_shape: q has "
            + String(q_len)
            + " elements, expected "
            + String(num_q_heads * head_dim)
            + " ([num_q_heads][head_dim])"
        )
    if stored <= 0:
        raise Error(
            "attention_cpu_no_visible_keys: stored visible range is empty"
            " (stored "
            + String(stored)
            + ") for query position "
            + String(position)
        )
    var row = num_kv_heads * head_dim
    if keys_len != stored * row or values_len != stored * row:
        raise Error(
            "attention_cpu_bad_shape: keys/values have "
            + String(keys_len)
            + "/"
            + String(values_len)
            + " elements, expected "
            + String(stored * row)
            + " each ([stored][num_kv_heads][head_dim])"
        )
    if first_visible < 0 or position < 0:
        raise Error(
            "attention_cpu_bad_position: first_visible and position must"
            " be >= 0, got "
            + String(first_visible)
            + " and "
            + String(position)
        )
    if position < first_visible:
        raise Error(
            "attention_cpu_no_visible_keys: query position "
            + String(position)
            + " precedes the visible range starting at "
            + String(first_visible)
        )
    if (
        isnan(rope_base)
        or isinf(rope_base)
        or rope_base < Float32(0.0)
        or (rope_base != ROPE_NONE and rope_base <= Float32(1.0))
    ):
        raise Error(
            "attention_cpu_bad_rope_base: rope_base must be 0 (NoPE) or"
            " finite and > 1, got "
            + String(rope_base)
        )
    # Causal by construction: rows past the query position are
    # never scored, even if a caller hands them over.
    var effective = stored
    if position - first_visible + 1 < effective:
        effective = position - first_visible + 1
    return effective


def _attention_impl(
    q: List[Float32],
    keys: List[Float32],
    values: List[Float32],
    first_visible: Int,
    stored: Int,
    num_q_heads: Int,
    num_kv_heads: Int,
    head_dim: Int,
    position: Int,
    rope_base: Float32,
    rotate_keys: Bool,
) raises -> List[Float32]:
    var effective = _validate(
        len(q),
        len(keys),
        len(values),
        first_visible,
        stored,
        num_q_heads,
        num_kv_heads,
        head_dim,
        position,
        rope_base,
    )
    var group = num_q_heads // num_kv_heads
    var row = num_kv_heads * head_dim

    # RoPE (sliding layers only; ROPE_NONE leaves both raw).
    # Q: every Q head at the query position. K: every KV head
    # of every visible row at that row's absolute position.
    var q_rot: List[Float32]
    var k_rot: List[Float32]
    if rope_base != ROPE_NONE:
        var q_pos = List[Int](capacity=num_q_heads)
        q_pos.resize(num_q_heads, position)
        q_rot = rope_cpu(q, q_pos, head_dim, rope_base)
        if rotate_keys:
            var k_pos = List[Int](capacity=stored * num_kv_heads)
            k_pos.resize(stored * num_kv_heads, 0)
            for i in range(stored):
                for kv in range(num_kv_heads):
                    k_pos[i * num_kv_heads + kv] = first_visible + i
            k_rot = rope_cpu(keys, k_pos, head_dim, rope_base)
        else:
            k_rot = keys.copy()
    else:
        q_rot = q.copy()
        k_rot = keys.copy()

    var scale = Float64(1.0) / sqrt(Float64(head_dim))
    var out = List[Float32](capacity=num_q_heads * head_dim)
    out.resize(num_q_heads * head_dim, Float32(0.0))
    for h in range(num_q_heads):
        var kv_head = h // group
        var q_off = h * head_dim
        var scores = List[Float32](capacity=effective)
        scores.resize(effective, Float32(0.0))
        for i in range(effective):
            var k_off = i * row + kv_head * head_dim
            var dot = Float64(0.0)
            for d in range(head_dim):
                dot += Float64(q_rot[q_off + d]) * Float64(k_rot[k_off + d])
            scores[i] = Float32(dot * scale)
        var probs = softmax_cpu(scores, effective)
        var o_off = h * head_dim
        for d in range(head_dim):
            var acc = Float64(0.0)
            for i in range(effective):
                var v_off = i * row + kv_head * head_dim
                acc += Float64(probs[i]) * Float64(values[v_off + d])
            out[o_off + d] = Float32(acc)
    _ = log_debug(
        "attention.cpu",
        "q_heads "
        + String(num_q_heads)
        + " kv_heads "
        + String(num_kv_heads)
        + " head_dim "
        + String(head_dim)
        + " visible "
        + String(effective)
        + " position "
        + String(position)
        + " rope "
        + String(rope_base),
    )
    return out^


def attention_cpu(
    q: List[Float32],
    keys: List[Float32],
    values: List[Float32],
    first_visible: Int,
    stored: Int,
    num_q_heads: Int,
    num_kv_heads: Int,
    head_dim: Int,
    position: Int,
    rope_base: Float32,
) raises -> List[Float32]:
    """Single-position GQA attention over RAW flat K/V stores.

    q is one position's raw query row [num_q_heads][head_dim];
    keys/values are the layer's visible rows in visible order
    (see the module header for the seam and the RoPE-at-read-
    time note). rope_base is the interleaved RoPE base for
    sliding layers, or ROPE_NONE (0.0) for global/NoPE layers.
    Returns [num_q_heads][head_dim].
    """
    return _attention_impl(
        q,
        keys,
        values,
        first_visible,
        stored,
        num_q_heads,
        num_kv_heads,
        head_dim,
        position,
        rope_base,
        True,
    )


def attention_cpu_rotated_cache(
    q: List[Float32],
    keys: List[Float32],
    values: List[Float32],
    first_visible: Int,
    stored: Int,
    num_q_heads: Int,
    num_kv_heads: Int,
    head_dim: Int,
    position: Int,
    rope_base: Float32,
) raises -> List[Float32]:
    """Same as attention_cpu, for Rust-exact storage: keys are
    ALREADY rotated (the cache holds rotated K, as in the Rust
    CPU path), so only the raw Q row is rotated here. Never
    pass raw keys to this variant: K would stay unrotated."""
    return _attention_impl(
        q,
        keys,
        values,
        first_visible,
        stored,
        num_q_heads,
        num_kv_heads,
        head_dim,
        position,
        rope_base,
        False,
    )


def attention_prefill_cpu(
    q_rows: List[Float32],
    k_rows: List[Float32],
    v_rows: List[Float32],
    num_positions: Int,
    num_q_heads: Int,
    num_kv_heads: Int,
    head_dim: Int,
    first_position: Int,
    window: Int,
    rope_base: Float32,
) raises -> List[Float32]:
    """Multi-position prefill: the Rust session's semantics.

    The Rust CPU path is append-then-attend per position
    (rotate, append, attend), so position p sees exactly the
    rows appended up to and including itself, window-truncated
    on windowed layers (a key at kp is visible to p when
    kp <= p and kp > p - window, crates/attention attends()).
    This helper mirrors that loop over raw per-position rows:
    q_rows/k_rows/v_rows are [num_positions][width] with the
    per-position layouts of attention_cpu; window is 0 for
    global layers (no truncation) or the sliding window size.
    Later rows are never passed to an earlier position's call,
    so causality holds by construction, not by masking.
    Returns [num_positions][num_q_heads][head_dim].
    """
    if num_positions <= 0:
        raise Error(
            "attention_cpu_bad_shape: num_positions must be > 0, got "
            + String(num_positions)
        )
    if window < 0:
        raise Error(
            "attention_cpu_bad_shape: window must be >= 0 (0 = global), got "
            + String(window)
        )
    if first_position < 0:
        raise Error(
            "attention_cpu_bad_position: first_position must be >= 0, got "
            + String(first_position)
        )
    var q_width = num_q_heads * head_dim
    var kv_width = num_kv_heads * head_dim
    if (
        len(q_rows) != num_positions * q_width
        or len(k_rows) != num_positions * kv_width
        or len(v_rows) != num_positions * kv_width
    ):
        raise Error(
            "attention_cpu_bad_shape: prefill rows have "
            + String(len(q_rows))
            + "/"
            + String(len(k_rows))
            + "/"
            + String(len(v_rows))
            + " elements for "
            + String(num_positions)
            + " positions"
        )
    var out = List[Float32](capacity=num_positions * q_width)
    out.resize(num_positions * q_width, Float32(0.0))
    for idx in range(num_positions):
        var start_idx = 0
        if window > 0 and idx - window + 1 > 0:
            start_idx = idx - window + 1
        var count = idx - start_idx + 1
        var q_row = List[Float32](capacity=q_width)
        q_row.resize(q_width, Float32(0.0))
        for i in range(q_width):
            q_row[i] = q_rows[idx * q_width + i]
        var k_sub = List[Float32](capacity=count * kv_width)
        k_sub.resize(count * kv_width, Float32(0.0))
        var v_sub = List[Float32](capacity=count * kv_width)
        v_sub.resize(count * kv_width, Float32(0.0))
        for r in range(count):
            for i in range(kv_width):
                k_sub[r * kv_width + i] = k_rows[(start_idx + r) * kv_width + i]
                v_sub[r * kv_width + i] = v_rows[(start_idx + r) * kv_width + i]
        var row_out = attention_cpu(
            q_row,
            k_sub,
            v_sub,
            first_position + start_idx,
            count,
            num_q_heads,
            num_kv_heads,
            head_dim,
            first_position + idx,
            rope_base,
        )
        for i in range(q_width):
            out[idx * q_width + i] = row_out[i]
    _ = log_debug(
        "attention.prefill",
        "positions "
        + String(num_positions)
        + " first_position "
        + String(first_position)
        + " window "
        + String(window),
    )
    return out^


def attention_kernel(
    q: Pointer[Float32, MutAnyOrigin],
    keys: Pointer[Float32, MutAnyOrigin],
    values: Pointer[Float32, MutAnyOrigin],
    y: Pointer[Float32, MutAnyOrigin],
    stored: Int32,
    num_kv_heads: Int32,
    head_dim: Int32,
    group: Int32,
    scale: Float32,
):
    """GPU single-position attention: one block per Q head.

    Buffers are PRE-ROTATED Q/K (the Rust gqa_attention core's
    contract; rotation is the caller's separate rope step) in
    the same visible-order flat layout as the CPU seam. Flash-
    style online softmax: a single streaming pass over the
    visible positions with a running max/sum and per-channel
    accumulators; the score row is never materialized. Host
    validates shapes before launch: block_dim must equal
    ATTN_THREADS and head_dim must be <= ATTN_THREADS (each
    thread owns one channel).
    """
    var head = Int(block_idx.x)
    var tid = Int(thread_idx.x)
    var hd = Int(head_dim)
    var kv_head = head // Int(group)
    var row = Int(num_kv_heads) * hd
    var shared = stack_allocation[
        ATTN_THREADS, Float32, address_space=AddressSpace.SHARED
    ]()
    var d = tid
    var q_d = q[unsafe_offset=head * hd + d] if d < hd else Float32(0.0)
    var acc = Float32(0.0)
    var run_max = Float32(-3.4028235e38)
    var run_sum = Float32(0.0)
    for vi in range(Int(stored)):
        var k_off = vi * row + kv_head * hd
        var prod = q_d * keys[unsafe_offset=k_off + d] if d < hd else Float32(
            0.0
        )
        shared[unsafe_offset=tid] = prod
        barrier()
        var stride = ATTN_THREADS // 2
        while stride > 0:
            if tid < stride:
                shared[unsafe_offset=tid] = (
                    shared[unsafe_offset=tid]
                    + shared[unsafe_offset=tid + stride]
                )
            barrier()
            stride //= 2
        var score = shared[unsafe_offset=0] * scale
        var new_max = run_max if run_max > score else score
        var alpha = exp(run_max - new_max)
        var w = exp(score - new_max)
        var v_d = values[unsafe_offset=k_off + d] if d < hd else Float32(0.0)
        acc = acc * alpha + w * v_d
        run_sum = run_sum * alpha + w
        run_max = new_max
        barrier()
    if d < hd:
        y[unsafe_offset=head * hd + d] = acc / run_sum


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Wave D (Lane D2): shared-memory K/V tiling + split-KV.
#
# Constants: the tiled kernel is compiled for tile sizes
# 8/16/32/64 positions (attn_validate_tile is the host-side
# gate) and head_dim up to ATTN_MAX_HEAD_DIM (= ATTN_THREADS,
# one thread per channel, the Wave B kernel's same limit).
# ATTN_NEG_INF is the online-softmax sentinel: the largest
# finite Float32 magnitude, negated, so sentinel arithmetic
# (exp of a huge negative difference) underflows to 0
# instead of producing NaN; the merge additionally guards
# empty partials (sum == 0) explicitly.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

comptime ATTN_MAX_HEAD_DIM = 128
comptime ATTN_NEG_INF = Float32(-3.4028235e38)


def attn_validate_tile(tile: Int) raises:
    """Refuse by name a tile size with no compiled kernel
    instantiation (8/16/32/64 positions)."""
    if tile != 8 and tile != 16 and tile != 32 and tile != 64:
        raise Error(
            "attention_tiled_bad_tile: tile positions must be one of"
            " 8/16/32/64 (the compiled instantiations), got "
            + String(tile)
        )


def attn_split_count(stored: Int, span: Int, max_splits: Int) raises -> Int:
    """How many split-KV partials a stored count earns: 1
    while stored fits one span, else ceil(stored / span)
    capped at max_splits. Pure; the chooser gpu_layer uses."""
    if stored <= 0 or span <= 0 or max_splits <= 0:
        raise Error(
            "attention_split_bad_config: stored, span and max_splits"
            " must be positive, got stored "
            + String(stored)
            + " span "
            + String(span)
            + " max_splits "
            + String(max_splits)
        )
    if stored <= span:
        return 1
    var n = (stored + span - 1) // span
    if n > max_splits:
        n = max_splits
    return n


def attn_split_range(
    stored: Int, splits: Int, split: Int
) raises -> Tuple[Int, Int]:
    """(start, length) of one split's position range: ranges
    partition [0, stored) in order, lengths differ by at most
    one, earlier splits take the remainder. splits > stored
    is legal: trailing splits are empty (length 0) and their
    partials merge as no-ops. Pure; shared by the CPU twin,
    the host launcher, and the tests (the kernel recomputes
    the same arithmetic inline)."""
    if stored < 0 or splits <= 0 or split < 0 or split >= splits:
        raise Error(
            "attention_split_bad_range: stored "
            + String(stored)
            + " splits "
            + String(splits)
            + " split "
            + String(split)
            + " is not a valid split range request"
        )
    var base = stored // splits
    var rem = stored % splits
    if split < rem:
        return (split * (base + 1), base + 1)
    return (rem * (base + 1) + (split - rem) * base, base)


def _validate_split(
    q_len: Int,
    keys_len: Int,
    values_len: Int,
    stored: Int,
    num_q_heads: Int,
    num_kv_heads: Int,
    head_dim: Int,
    splits: Int,
) raises:
    """Shape gate for the split path over PRE-ROTATED stores;
    refusal names are the attention_split_ family."""
    if head_dim < 2 or head_dim % 2 != 0 or head_dim > ATTN_MAX_HEAD_DIM:
        raise Error(
            "attention_split_bad_shape: head_dim must be even, >= 2 and <= "
            + String(ATTN_MAX_HEAD_DIM)
            + ", got "
            + String(head_dim)
        )
    if num_q_heads <= 0 or num_kv_heads <= 0:
        raise Error(
            "attention_split_bad_shape: head counts must be > 0, got "
            + String(num_q_heads)
            + " q heads, "
            + String(num_kv_heads)
            + " kv heads"
        )
    if num_q_heads % num_kv_heads != 0:
        raise Error(
            "attention_split_bad_shape: "
            + String(num_q_heads)
            + " q heads do not divide into "
            + String(num_kv_heads)
            + " kv heads"
        )
    if splits <= 0:
        raise Error(
            "attention_split_bad_splits: splits must be > 0, got "
            + String(splits)
        )
    if stored <= 0:
        raise Error(
            "attention_split_bad_shape: stored must be > 0, got "
            + String(stored)
        )
    if q_len != num_q_heads * head_dim:
        raise Error(
            "attention_split_bad_shape: q has "
            + String(q_len)
            + " elements, expected "
            + String(num_q_heads * head_dim)
        )
    var row = num_kv_heads * head_dim
    if keys_len != stored * row or values_len != stored * row:
        raise Error(
            "attention_split_bad_shape: keys/values have "
            + String(keys_len)
            + "/"
            + String(values_len)
            + " elements, expected "
            + String(stored * row)
            + " each ([stored][num_kv_heads][head_dim])"
        )


def attention_split_partials_cpu(
    q: List[Float32],
    keys: List[Float32],
    values: List[Float32],
    stored: Int,
    num_q_heads: Int,
    num_kv_heads: Int,
    head_dim: Int,
    splits: Int,
    tile: Int,
) raises -> Tuple[List[Float32], List[Float32], List[Float32]]:
    """CPU twin of attention_tiled_kernel: the partials.

    q/keys are PRE-ROTATED (the GPU kernels' contract);
    values raw, all in the flat visible-order layout. Returns
    (partial_out, partial_max, partial_sum) with layouts
    [splits][num_q_heads][head_dim] and [splits][num_q_heads]:
    partial_out is the UNNORMALIZED online-softmax
    accumulator (divide by partial_sum after merging - never
    before). The Float32 arithmetic mirrors the kernel tile
    by tile: per tile, scores from ascending-dim dots, the
    tile max folded into the running max, one rescale by
    exp(old max - new max) (0 on the first tile), probs
    exp(score - new max), accumulate, sum. Mirroring the tile
    structure matters: the rescale points are part of the
    float path, so a different tile gives a different (still
    in-bar) rounding, exactly as on device.
    """
    _validate_split(
        len(q),
        len(keys),
        len(values),
        stored,
        num_q_heads,
        num_kv_heads,
        head_dim,
        splits,
    )
    attn_validate_tile(tile)
    var group = num_q_heads // num_kv_heads
    var row = num_kv_heads * head_dim
    var scale = Float32(1.0) / sqrt(Float32(head_dim))
    var p_out = List[Float32](capacity=splits * num_q_heads * head_dim)
    p_out.resize(splits * num_q_heads * head_dim, Float32(0.0))
    var p_max = List[Float32](capacity=splits * num_q_heads)
    p_max.resize(splits * num_q_heads, ATTN_NEG_INF)
    var p_sum = List[Float32](capacity=splits * num_q_heads)
    p_sum.resize(splits * num_q_heads, Float32(0.0))
    for h in range(num_q_heads):
        var kv_head = h // group
        for s in range(splits):
            var rng = attn_split_range(stored, splits, s)
            var start = rng[0]
            var end = start + rng[1]
            var acc = List[Float32](capacity=head_dim)
            acc.resize(head_dim, Float32(0.0))
            var run_max = ATTN_NEG_INF
            var run_sum = Float32(0.0)
            var ts = start
            while ts < end:
                var tcount = tile
                if end - ts < tcount:
                    tcount = end - ts
                var scores = List[Float32](capacity=tcount)
                scores.resize(tcount, Float32(0.0))
                for t in range(tcount):
                    var k_off = (ts + t) * row + kv_head * head_dim
                    var dot = Float32(0.0)
                    for d in range(head_dim):
                        dot += q[h * head_dim + d] * keys[k_off + d]
                    scores[t] = dot * scale
                var new_max = run_max
                for t in range(tcount):
                    if scores[t] > new_max:
                        new_max = scores[t]
                var alpha = Float32(0.0)
                if run_sum != Float32(0.0):
                    alpha = exp(run_max - new_max)
                var probs = List[Float32](capacity=tcount)
                probs.resize(tcount, Float32(0.0))
                var psum = Float32(0.0)
                for t in range(tcount):
                    probs[t] = exp(scores[t] - new_max)
                    psum += probs[t]
                for d in range(head_dim):
                    var a = acc[d] * alpha
                    for t in range(tcount):
                        var v_off = (ts + t) * row + kv_head * head_dim
                        a += probs[t] * values[v_off + d]
                    acc[d] = a
                run_sum = run_sum * alpha + psum
                run_max = new_max
                ts += tile
            var base = (s * num_q_heads + h) * head_dim
            for d in range(head_dim):
                p_out[base + d] = acc[d]
            p_max[s * num_q_heads + h] = run_max
            p_sum[s * num_q_heads + h] = run_sum
    _ = log_debug(
        "attention.split",
        "partials q_heads "
        + String(num_q_heads)
        + " stored "
        + String(stored)
        + " splits "
        + String(splits)
        + " tile "
        + String(tile),
    )
    return (p_out^, p_max^, p_sum^)


def attention_merge_partials_cpu(
    p_out: List[Float32],
    p_max: List[Float32],
    p_sum: List[Float32],
    splits: Int,
    num_q_heads: Int,
    head_dim: Int,
) raises -> List[Float32]:
    """CPU twin of attention_merge_kernel: combine partials
    in split order by exact logsumexp rescaling.

    For each head: walk the splits; a split with sum 0 is
    empty and skipped; the first non-empty split is adopted
    whole; every later split rescales BOTH accumulators by
    exp(max - combined max) before adding, so the merged
    (acc, sum) is the single-pass online-softmax state for
    the union of the ranges, and the output is acc / sum.
    No approximation: the rescale factors are the exact
    exponentials of the max differences.
    """
    if splits <= 0:
        raise Error(
            "attention_split_bad_splits: splits must be > 0, got "
            + String(splits)
        )
    if num_q_heads <= 0 or head_dim <= 0:
        raise Error(
            "attention_split_bad_shape: head counts must be > 0, got "
            + String(num_q_heads)
            + " q heads, head_dim "
            + String(head_dim)
        )
    if (
        len(p_out) != splits * num_q_heads * head_dim
        or len(p_max) != splits * num_q_heads
        or len(p_sum) != splits * num_q_heads
    ):
        raise Error(
            "attention_split_bad_shape: partial buffers have "
            + String(len(p_out))
            + "/"
            + String(len(p_max))
            + "/"
            + String(len(p_sum))
            + " elements for splits "
            + String(splits)
            + " q_heads "
            + String(num_q_heads)
            + " head_dim "
            + String(head_dim)
        )
    var out = List[Float32](capacity=num_q_heads * head_dim)
    out.resize(num_q_heads * head_dim, Float32(0.0))
    for h in range(num_q_heads):
        var acc = List[Float32](capacity=head_dim)
        acc.resize(head_dim, Float32(0.0))
        var run_max = ATTN_NEG_INF
        var run_sum = Float32(0.0)
        for s in range(splits):
            var ps = p_sum[s * num_q_heads + h]
            if ps == Float32(0.0):
                continue
            var pm = p_max[s * num_q_heads + h]
            var base = (s * num_q_heads + h) * head_dim
            if run_sum == Float32(0.0):
                run_max = pm
                run_sum = ps
                for d in range(head_dim):
                    acc[d] = p_out[base + d]
            else:
                var new_max = run_max if run_max > pm else pm
                var a1 = exp(run_max - new_max)
                var a2 = exp(pm - new_max)
                for d in range(head_dim):
                    acc[d] = acc[d] * a1 + p_out[base + d] * a2
                run_sum = run_sum * a1 + ps * a2
                run_max = new_max
        if run_sum == Float32(0.0):
            raise Error(
                "attention_split_empty_partials: every split partial for head "
                + String(h)
                + " is empty (all sums zero)"
            )
        for d in range(head_dim):
            out[h * head_dim + d] = acc[d] / run_sum
    return out^


def attention_split_cpu(
    q: List[Float32],
    keys: List[Float32],
    values: List[Float32],
    stored: Int,
    num_q_heads: Int,
    num_kv_heads: Int,
    head_dim: Int,
    splits: Int,
    tile: Int,
) raises -> List[Float32]:
    """Single-position GQA attention over PRE-ROTATED flat
    stores, computed as tiled partials + exact merge: the
    full CPU twin of the GPU tiled + merge launch pair."""
    var parts = attention_split_partials_cpu(
        q,
        keys,
        values,
        stored,
        num_q_heads,
        num_kv_heads,
        head_dim,
        splits,
        tile,
    )
    return attention_merge_partials_cpu(
        parts[0], parts[1], parts[2], splits, num_q_heads, head_dim
    )


def attention_direct_cpu(
    q: List[Float32],
    keys: List[Float32],
    values: List[Float32],
    stored: Int,
    num_q_heads: Int,
    num_kv_heads: Int,
    head_dim: Int,
    tile: Int,
) raises -> List[Float32]:
    """Single-position GQA attention over PRE-ROTATED flat
    stores, computed as ONE tiled pass with a direct
    normalized write: the CPU twin of
    attention_tiled_direct_kernel (Wave E, Lane E2).

    The splits==1 shape of the split path with the merge
    step folded in: the single partial's accumulator is
    divided by its own sum per head, which is exactly what
    attention_merge_partials_cpu does when it adopts the
    one non-empty partial whole - so this twin's float path
    is the partials path tile by tile plus that final
    divide, and its outputs match attention_split_cpu at
    splits == 1 to the last bit on the same fixtures (the
    VM suite asserts exactly that)."""
    var parts = attention_split_partials_cpu(
        q, keys, values, stored, num_q_heads, num_kv_heads, head_dim, 1, tile
    )
    var out = List[Float32](capacity=num_q_heads * head_dim)
    out.resize(num_q_heads * head_dim, Float32(0.0))
    for h in range(num_q_heads):
        var run_sum = parts[2][h]
        if run_sum == Float32(0.0):
            raise Error(
                "attention_split_empty_partials: the single direct"
                " partial for head "
                + String(h)
                + " is empty (sum zero)"
            )
        for d in range(head_dim):
            out[h * head_dim + d] = parts[0][h * head_dim + d] / run_sum
    return out^


def attention_tiled_kernel[
    TILE: Int
](
    q: Pointer[Float32, MutAnyOrigin],
    keys: Pointer[Float32, MutAnyOrigin],
    values: Pointer[Float32, MutAnyOrigin],
    p_out: Pointer[Float32, MutAnyOrigin],
    p_max: Pointer[Float32, MutAnyOrigin],
    p_sum: Pointer[Float32, MutAnyOrigin],
    stored: Int32,
    num_kv_heads: Int32,
    num_q_heads: Int32,
    head_dim: Int32,
    group: Int32,
    scale: Float32,
    splits: Int32,
):
    """GPU tiled split-KV attention: partials, one block per
    (Q head, split).

    Buffers are PRE-ROTATED Q/K in the visible-order flat
    layout (the Wave B kernel's contract). Block index x is
    head * splits + split; the block owns attn_split_range's
    range for its split and writes its unnormalized partial
    (acc, max, sum) for attention_merge_kernel to combine.
    Online softmax stays (no materialized score row; scores
    live in a TILE-sized shared array). Per tile: K is staged
    into the shared tile buffer cooperatively, scores are
    computed from shared (one thread per position, ascending
    dim), the tile max folds into the running max with one
    rescale, then V replaces K in the same buffer and the
    per-channel accumulators update from shared. Host
    validates before launch: block_dim == ATTN_THREADS,
    head_dim <= ATTN_MAX_HEAD_DIM, TILE a compiled size.
    """
    var n_splits = Int(splits)
    var head = Int(block_idx.x) // n_splits
    var split = Int(block_idx.x) % n_splits
    var tid = Int(thread_idx.x)
    var hd = Int(head_dim)
    var kv_head = head // Int(group)
    var row = Int(num_kv_heads) * hd
    var nstored = Int(stored)
    var base_chunk = nstored // n_splits
    var rem = nstored % n_splits
    var start: Int
    var length: Int
    if split < rem:
        start = split * (base_chunk + 1)
        length = base_chunk + 1
    else:
        start = rem * (base_chunk + 1) + (split - rem) * base_chunk
        length = base_chunk
    var end = start + length
    var tile_buf = stack_allocation[
        TILE * ATTN_MAX_HEAD_DIM, Float32, address_space=AddressSpace.SHARED
    ]()
    var scores = stack_allocation[
        TILE, Float32, address_space=AddressSpace.SHARED
    ]()
    var q_sh = stack_allocation[
        ATTN_MAX_HEAD_DIM, Float32, address_space=AddressSpace.SHARED
    ]()
    var red = stack_allocation[
        ATTN_THREADS, Float32, address_space=AddressSpace.SHARED
    ]()
    if tid < hd:
        q_sh[unsafe_offset=tid] = q[unsafe_offset=head * hd + tid]
    barrier()
    var d = tid
    var acc = Float32(0.0)
    var run_max = ATTN_NEG_INF
    var run_sum = Float32(0.0)
    var tile_start = start
    while tile_start < end:
        var tcount = TILE
        if end - tile_start < tcount:
            tcount = end - tile_start
        # Stage the K tile: element e is (t, dd) row-major.
        var e = tid
        while e < tcount * hd:
            var t = e // hd
            var dd = e % hd
            tile_buf[unsafe_offset=e] = keys[
                unsafe_offset=(tile_start + t) * row + kv_head * hd + dd
            ]
            e += ATTN_THREADS
        barrier()
        # Scores from shared: one thread per tile position.
        if tid < tcount:
            var s = Float32(0.0)
            for dd2 in range(hd):
                s += (
                    q_sh[unsafe_offset=dd2]
                    * tile_buf[unsafe_offset=tid * hd + dd2]
                )
            scores[unsafe_offset=tid] = s * scale
        barrier()
        if tid == 0:
            var m = run_max
            for t2 in range(tcount):
                if scores[unsafe_offset=t2] > m:
                    m = scores[unsafe_offset=t2]
            red[unsafe_offset=0] = m
        barrier()
        var new_max = red[unsafe_offset=0]
        var alpha = Float32(0.0)
        if run_sum != Float32(0.0):
            alpha = exp(run_max - new_max)
        if tid < tcount:
            scores[unsafe_offset=tid] = exp(scores[unsafe_offset=tid] - new_max)
        barrier()
        # Stage the V tile into the same shared buffer (the K
        # tile is dead once every score thread has read it,
        # which the barrier above guarantees).
        e = tid
        while e < tcount * hd:
            var t3 = e // hd
            var dd3 = e % hd
            tile_buf[unsafe_offset=e] = values[
                unsafe_offset=(tile_start + t3) * row + kv_head * hd + dd3
            ]
            e += ATTN_THREADS
        barrier()
        if tid == 0:
            var psum = Float32(0.0)
            for t4 in range(tcount):
                psum += scores[unsafe_offset=t4]
            red[unsafe_offset=1] = psum
        if d < hd:
            var a = acc * alpha
            for t5 in range(tcount):
                a += (
                    scores[unsafe_offset=t5]
                    * tile_buf[unsafe_offset=t5 * hd + d]
                )
            acc = a
        barrier()
        run_sum = run_sum * alpha + red[unsafe_offset=1]
        run_max = new_max
        tile_start += TILE
    var p_base = (split * Int(num_q_heads) + head) * hd
    if d < hd:
        p_out[unsafe_offset=p_base + d] = acc
    if tid == 0:
        p_max[unsafe_offset=split * Int(num_q_heads) + head] = run_max
        p_sum[unsafe_offset=split * Int(num_q_heads) + head] = run_sum


def attention_tiled_direct_kernel[
    TILE: Int
](
    q: Pointer[Float32, MutAnyOrigin],
    keys: Pointer[Float32, MutAnyOrigin],
    values: Pointer[Float32, MutAnyOrigin],
    y: Pointer[Float32, MutAnyOrigin],
    stored: Int32,
    num_kv_heads: Int32,
    num_q_heads: Int32,
    head_dim: Int32,
    group: Int32,
    scale: Float32,
):
    """GPU tiled attention, DIRECT-OUTPUT form (Wave E,
    Lane E2): the splits == 1 case of attention_tiled_kernel
    with the merge folded into the same launch.

    One block per Q head over the whole visible range; the
    tile loop, shared-memory staging, and online-softmax
    rescale points are the tiled kernel's, statement for
    statement, so the float path is the splits==1 partials
    path plus the merge's final divide by the head's own
    sum - no approximation, and no partial buffers or
    second (merge) launch. Buffers are PRE-ROTATED Q/K in
    the visible-order flat layout, as everywhere in this
    module. Host validates before launch: block_dim ==
    ATTN_THREADS, head_dim <= ATTN_MAX_HEAD_DIM, TILE a
    compiled size, and the caller launches this form only
    when its split chooser returned 1."""
    var head = Int(block_idx.x)
    var tid = Int(thread_idx.x)
    var hd = Int(head_dim)
    var kv_head = head // Int(group)
    var row = Int(num_kv_heads) * hd
    var nstored = Int(stored)
    var tile_buf = stack_allocation[
        TILE * ATTN_MAX_HEAD_DIM, Float32, address_space=AddressSpace.SHARED
    ]()
    var scores = stack_allocation[
        TILE, Float32, address_space=AddressSpace.SHARED
    ]()
    var q_sh = stack_allocation[
        ATTN_MAX_HEAD_DIM, Float32, address_space=AddressSpace.SHARED
    ]()
    var red = stack_allocation[
        ATTN_THREADS, Float32, address_space=AddressSpace.SHARED
    ]()
    if tid < hd:
        q_sh[unsafe_offset=tid] = q[unsafe_offset=head * hd + tid]
    barrier()
    var d = tid
    var acc = Float32(0.0)
    var run_max = ATTN_NEG_INF
    var run_sum = Float32(0.0)
    var tile_start = 0
    while tile_start < nstored:
        var tcount = TILE
        if nstored - tile_start < tcount:
            tcount = nstored - tile_start
        var e = tid
        while e < tcount * hd:
            var t = e // hd
            var dd = e % hd
            tile_buf[unsafe_offset=e] = keys[
                unsafe_offset=(tile_start + t) * row + kv_head * hd + dd
            ]
            e += ATTN_THREADS
        barrier()
        if tid < tcount:
            var sc = Float32(0.0)
            for dd2 in range(hd):
                sc += (
                    q_sh[unsafe_offset=dd2]
                    * tile_buf[unsafe_offset=tid * hd + dd2]
                )
            scores[unsafe_offset=tid] = sc * scale
        barrier()
        if tid == 0:
            var m = run_max
            for t2 in range(tcount):
                if scores[unsafe_offset=t2] > m:
                    m = scores[unsafe_offset=t2]
            red[unsafe_offset=0] = m
        barrier()
        var new_max = red[unsafe_offset=0]
        var alpha = Float32(0.0)
        if run_sum != Float32(0.0):
            alpha = exp(run_max - new_max)
        if tid < tcount:
            scores[unsafe_offset=tid] = exp(scores[unsafe_offset=tid] - new_max)
        barrier()
        e = tid
        while e < tcount * hd:
            var t3 = e // hd
            var dd3 = e % hd
            tile_buf[unsafe_offset=e] = values[
                unsafe_offset=(tile_start + t3) * row + kv_head * hd + dd3
            ]
            e += ATTN_THREADS
        barrier()
        if tid == 0:
            var psum = Float32(0.0)
            for t4 in range(tcount):
                psum += scores[unsafe_offset=t4]
            red[unsafe_offset=1] = psum
        if d < hd:
            var a = acc * alpha
            for t5 in range(tcount):
                a += (
                    scores[unsafe_offset=t5]
                    * tile_buf[unsafe_offset=t5 * hd + d]
                )
            acc = a
        barrier()
        run_sum = run_sum * alpha + red[unsafe_offset=1]
        run_max = new_max
        tile_start += TILE
    if d < hd:
        y[unsafe_offset=head * hd + d] = acc / run_sum


def attention_merge_kernel(
    p_out: Pointer[Float32, MutAnyOrigin],
    p_max: Pointer[Float32, MutAnyOrigin],
    p_sum: Pointer[Float32, MutAnyOrigin],
    y: Pointer[Float32, MutAnyOrigin],
    num_q_heads: Int32,
    head_dim: Int32,
    splits: Int32,
):
    """GPU split-KV merge: one block per Q head, one thread
    per channel, splits combined in order with exact
    logsumexp rescaling (exp of max differences), mirroring
    attention_merge_partials_cpu statement for statement,
    including the empty-partial (sum == 0) skip and the
    first-non-empty adoption. Output y[head][d] = acc / sum.
    Host guarantees at least one non-empty partial per head
    (stored >= 1 upstream)."""
    var head = Int(block_idx.x)
    var tid = Int(thread_idx.x)
    var hd = Int(head_dim)
    var qh = Int(num_q_heads)
    var d = tid
    var acc = Float32(0.0)
    var run_max = ATTN_NEG_INF
    var run_sum = Float32(0.0)
    for s in range(Int(splits)):
        var ps = p_sum[unsafe_offset=s * qh + head]
        if ps != Float32(0.0):
            var pm = p_max[unsafe_offset=s * qh + head]
            var base = (s * qh + head) * hd
            if run_sum == Float32(0.0):
                run_max = pm
                run_sum = ps
                if d < hd:
                    acc = p_out[unsafe_offset=base + d]
            else:
                var new_max = run_max if run_max > pm else pm
                var a1 = exp(run_max - new_max)
                var a2 = exp(pm - new_max)
                if d < hd:
                    acc = acc * a1 + p_out[unsafe_offset=base + d] * a2
                run_sum = run_sum * a1 + ps * a2
                run_max = new_max
    if d < hd:
        y[unsafe_offset=head * hd + d] = acc / run_sum

===== END FILE: mojo-engine/src/attention/attention.mojo =====

# config.mojo - engine configuration.
#
# David's law: operational limits are config with defaults, never
# compiled-in constants scattered through the code. Every setting
# below lives in exactly one place (the DEFAULT_* block), each one
# overridable by an env var at launch, and a bad value is refused
# BY NAME at load time instead of being silently clamped or
# ignored. Nothing else in the engine reads env vars directly.

from std.math import isnan, isinf
from std.os import getenv

# The new engine line starts at 1.1 under the repo's versioning
# scheme (1.<release number>, counting up, never resets).
# 1.2: Wave A landed (GGUF loader, tuned K1, the GEMV shape
# family, the elementwise ops, the tokenizer).
comptime ENGINE_NAME = "mojo-engine"
comptime ENGINE_VERSION = "1.07"

# Defaults. These are configuration defaults, stated once here;
# env vars of the same name override them per launch.
comptime DEFAULT_MODEL_PATH = (
    "/mnt/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf"
)
comptime DEFAULT_CONTEXT_LEN = 131072

# GPU memory budget (Wave C): the RX 7900 XTX carries
# 25,769,803,776 B total; the engine keeps a 1 GiB reserve for
# the rest of the system, so the default budget cap is the
# card total minus the reserve = 24,696,061,952 B. Device
# construction refuses by name (gpu_budget_exceeded, in
# src/gpu/context.mojo) when the computed resident total
# (weights + KV + scratch envelope) exceeds this cap.
comptime GPU_CARD_TOTAL_BYTES = 25769803776
comptime GPU_RESERVE_BYTES = 1073741824
comptime DEFAULT_GPU_BUDGET_BYTES = GPU_CARD_TOTAL_BYTES - GPU_RESERVE_BYTES

# Attention occupancy knobs (Wave D, Lane D2): the GPU
# attention path stages K/V in shared-memory tiles of
# DEFAULT_ATTN_TILE_POSITIONS positions and, once the stored
# sequence grows past one split span, splits the KV sequence
# across workgroups (split-KV) up to DEFAULT_ATTN_MAX_SPLITS
# partials merged by exact logsumexp rescaling. These are the
# operator-tunable defaults; the attention module validates
# the tile against its compiled instantiations by name
# (attention_tiled_bad_tile) and the split chooser's inputs
# by name (attention_split_bad_config). Trial record:
# bench/mojo-engine-wave-d-2026-11-07.md.
comptime DEFAULT_ATTN_TILE_POSITIONS = 32
comptime DEFAULT_ATTN_MAX_SPLITS = 8
# Span 512 (not the 1024 first cut): the recorded card
# trials (bench/mojo-engine-wave-d-2026-11-07.md) show the
# split path still gaining at 8 splits on the 4,096-position
# fixture (tile 32: 512 us at 8 splits vs 896 us at 4), so
# the chooser reaches 8 splits at 4,096 stored; at or below
# 512 stored the launch stays single-split.
comptime DEFAULT_ATTN_SPLIT_SPAN_POSITIONS = 512

# Prefill GEMM knobs (Wave D, Lane D1): a prompt batch at or
# above PREFILL_GEMM_MIN_BATCH rows takes the batched GEMM
# projection path on device (below it the per-row GEMV path is
# kept - at one or two rows the GEMV launches are already the
# cheap shape, and decode always uses GEMV); at or above
# GEMM_TILED_MIN_BATCH rows the register-tiled GEMM structure
# is used instead of the straightforward batched one. Setting
# PREFILL_GEMM_MIN_BATCH above any real prompt length disables
# the GEMM path entirely (the A/B control the Wave D timing
# harness uses). Both are positive whole numbers, refused by
# name like every other value here.
comptime DEFAULT_PREFILL_GEMM_MIN_BATCH = 2
comptime DEFAULT_GEMM_TILED_MIN_BATCH = 8

# =====================================================================
# BEGIN Wave E Lane E3 block: Glimmer op defaults, folded in
# from src/ops/ (Wave A open item). Keep this block together:
# lane E1 also edits this file and the merge is meant to stay
# mechanical.
#
# Before this fold, the ops modules each carried their own

comptime DEFAULT_VOCAB = 202048

# Prefill routing knob (Wave E, Lane E1): a prompt at or
# above PREFILL_BATCH_MIN_TOKENS tokens takes the batched
# prefill route (GEMM projections + resident batch layer
# step + batched tiled attention); below it, prefill runs
# the per-row resident step loop. The route is taken only
# when BOTH this knob and PREFILL_GEMM_MIN_BATCH admit the
# prompt, so the Wave D A/B control (raising the GEMM
# minimum above any prompt length) still forces the
# per-row arm on its own. The default is the measured
# batch-vs-per-row crossover on the real model
# (2026-11-08, RX 7900 XTX, interleaved fresh-model
# arms): at 6 tokens the batch arm loses (286 ms vs the
# per-row arm's 218 ms); at 16 tokens it wins (364 ms vs
# 557 ms) and it stays ahead at every larger measured
# length (32/64/128/256/512/1022). So prompts below 16
# tokens prefill per-row and prompts at or above 16 take
# the batch route. The trial record is
# bench/mojo-engine-wave-e1-batch-2026-11-08.md.
comptime DEFAULT_PREFILL_BATCH_MIN_TOKENS = 16

# Serving seam knobs (DESIGN.md step 7, decided 2026-11-08:
# the endpoint is Mojo-only, an HTTP server inside the engine
# process; see src/serve/). The default port is deliberately
# NOT 8080: production Glimmer stays down and port 8080 stays
# clear. The host default is loopback only; serving beyond the
# host is an operator's explicit env choice. Body and token
# limits are config for the same reason every other limit is:
# a request past them refuses BY NAME (serve_body_too_large /
# serve_max_tokens_exceeded), never silently truncates.
comptime DEFAULT_SERVE_HOST = "127.0.0.1"
comptime DEFAULT_SERVE_PORT = 18767
comptime DEFAULT_SERVE_MAX_BODY_BYTES = 65536
comptime DEFAULT_SERVE_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 64
comptime DEFAULT_SERVE_MAX_TOKENS = 512
comptime DEFAULT_SERVE_DEBUG_RING_LINES = 200
comptime DEFAULT_SERVE_MAX_CONTEXT_BYTES = 32768
# History / fact-sheet / fingerprint knobs (amendments,
# David 2026-11-08): history persists as JSON lines under
# serve_history_dir (relative paths are under the process
# working directory, which is mojo-engine/ in the bench
# harness); the fact sheet registry dir is scanned for
# *.gguf files whose fact sheets /models serves (the served
# model is always listed first, read from its own file).

comptime DEFAULT_SERVE_HISTORY_DIR = "serve_history"
comptime DEFAULT_SERVE_MODELS_DIR = "/mnt/models"
comptime DEFAULT_SERVE_BACKEND_TARGET = "gfx1100 / MAX 26.7"
comptime DEFAULT_SERVE_ATTACH_WARN_TOKENS = 4096
# Card peak memory bandwidth (GB/s) for the run record's
# bandwidth_pct_of_peak. An operator fact about the card
# (RX 7900 XTX: 960 GB/s), from config, never hardcoded in

comptime DEFAULT_GPU_PEAK_BANDWIDTH_GBPS = 960.0


def parse_context_len(raw: String) raises -> Int:
    """Parse and validate a context length value.

    Split out of load() so the refusal names are directly
    testable. Raises mojo_engine_config on anything that is not
    a positive whole number.
    """
    var parsed: Int
    try:
        parsed = Int(raw)
    except:
        raise Error(
            "mojo_engine_config: MOJO_ENGINE_CONTEXT_LEN is not a"
            " whole number: '"
            + raw
            + "'"
        )
    if parsed <= 0:
        raise Error(
            "mojo_engine_config: MOJO_ENGINE_CONTEXT_LEN must be positive, got "
            + String(parsed)
        )
    return parsed

def prefill_uses_batch(
    prompt_len: Int, gemm_min_batch: Int, batch_min_tokens: Int
) -> Bool:
    """The prefill routing rule (pure, VM-testable): the
    batched route serves a prompt only when its length
    reaches BOTH the GEMM minimum batch (the Wave D A/B
    control) and the batch-route minimum token count (the
    Wave E crossover knob)."""
    return prompt_len >= gemm_min_batch and prompt_len >= batch_min_tokens

def parse_ipv4(host: String) raises -> List[Int]:
    """Parse a dotted-quad IPv4 host into its 4 octets.

    The serve socket binds an IPv4 address; hostnames are
    refused BY NAME as mojo_engine_config instead of being
    resolved by a hidden DNS call. Pure and testable: digits
    accumulate numerically, so no substring surgery is needed.
    """
    var bytes = host.as_bytes()
    var parts = List[Int]()
    var value = 0
    var digits = 0
    for i in range(len(bytes) + 1):
        if i == len(bytes) or bytes[i] == 46:  # '.'
            if digits == 0 or digits > 3 or value > 255:
                raise Error(
                    "mojo_engine_config: MOJO_ENGINE_SERVE_HOST is not"
                    " a dotted-quad IPv4 address: '"
                    + host
                    + "'"
                )
            parts.append(value)
            value = 0
            digits = 0
        else:
            var b = Int(bytes[i])
            if b < 48 or b > 57:
                raise Error(
                    "mojo_engine_config: MOJO_ENGINE_SERVE_HOST is not"
                    " a dotted-quad IPv4 address: '"
                    + host
                    + "'"
                )
            value = value * 10 + (b - 48)
            digits += 1
    if len(parts) != 4:
        raise Error(
            "mojo_engine_config: MOJO_ENGINE_SERVE_HOST is not"
            " a dotted-quad IPv4 address: '"
            + host
            + "'"
        )
    return parts^

def parse_gpu_peak_bandwidth_gbps(raw: String) raises -> Float64:
    """MOJO_ENGINE_GPU_PEAK_BANDWIDTH_GBPS: the card's peak
    memory bandwidth in GB/s, the denominator of the run
    record's bandwidth_pct_of_peak (deep-telemetry addendum).
    Digits with at most one dot, strictly positive; anything
    else refuses as mojo_engine_config."""
    var digits = 0
    var dots = 0
    for b in raw.as_bytes():
        if b >= 48 and b <= 57:
            digits += 1
        elif b == 46:
            dots += 1
        else:
            raise Error(
                "mojo_engine_config: MOJO_ENGINE_GPU_PEAK_BANDWIDTH_GBPS"
                " '"
                + raw
                + "' is not a plain positive number"
            )
    if digits == 0 or dots > 1:
        raise Error(
            "mojo_engine_config: MOJO_ENGINE_GPU_PEAK_BANDWIDTH_GBPS"
            " '"
            + raw
            + "' is not a plain positive number"
        )
    var value = Float64(raw)
    if value <= 0.0:
        raise Error(
            "mojo_engine_config: MOJO_ENGINE_GPU_PEAK_BANDWIDTH_GBPS"
            " must be positive"
        )
    return value

    return raw

# naming its env var.

def _parse_float(raw: String, env_name: String) raises -> Float32:
    """Shared finite-float parse for the op-default knobs.

    Float64(raw) refuses non-numeric text itself; NaN and the
    infinities PARSE in Mojo, so they are refused here by
    name, matching the ops' own bad-value rules (their CPU
    twins refuse non-finite eps/base/scale/cap by name too).
    """
    var parsed: Float64
    try:
        parsed = Float64(raw)
    except:
        raise Error(
            "mojo_engine_config: "
            + env_name
            + " is not a number: '"
            + raw
            + "'"
        )
    if isnan(parsed) or isinf(parsed):
        raise Error(
            "mojo_engine_config: "
            + env_name
            + " must be finite, got '"
            + raw
            + "'"
        )
    return Float32(parsed)


def parse_rms_eps(raw: String) raises -> Float32:
    """MOJO_ENGINE_RMS_EPS: RMSNorm epsilon; the op refuses
    eps <= 0 by name, so config does too."""
    var v = _parse_float(raw, "MOJO_ENGINE_RMS_EPS")
    if v <= Float32(0.0):
        raise Error(
            "mojo_engine_config: MOJO_ENGINE_RMS_EPS must be positive, got "
            + String(v)
        )
    return v


def parse_rope_base(raw: String) raises -> Float32:
    """MOJO_ENGINE_ROPE_BASE: RoPE frequency base; the op
    refuses base <= 1 by name, so config does too."""
    var v = _parse_float(raw, "MOJO_ENGINE_ROPE_BASE")
    if v <= Float32(1.0):
        raise Error(
            "mojo_engine_config: MOJO_ENGINE_ROPE_BASE must be > 1, got "
            + String(v)
        )
    return v


def parse_logit_scale(raw: String) raises -> Float32:
    """MOJO_ENGINE_LOGIT_SCALE: final-logit scale; any finite
    value is legal (the op refuses only non-finite)."""
    return _parse_float(raw, "MOJO_ENGINE_LOGIT_SCALE")


def parse_logit_softcap(raw: String) raises -> Float32:
    """MOJO_ENGINE_LOGIT_SOFTCAP: final-logit softcap; the op
    refuses cap < 0 by name (0 = no cap), so config does too.
    """
    var v = _parse_float(raw, "MOJO_ENGINE_LOGIT_SOFTCAP")
    if v < Float32(0.0):
        raise Error(
            "mojo_engine_config: MOJO_ENGINE_LOGIT_SOFTCAP must be"
            " >= 0 (0 = no cap), got "
            + String(v)
        )
    return v


def parse_head_dim(raw: String) raises -> Int:
    """MOJO_ENGINE_HEAD_DIM: attention head dimension."""
    return _parse_positive(raw, "MOJO_ENGINE_HEAD_DIM")


def parse_hidden(raw: String) raises -> Int:
    """MOJO_ENGINE_HIDDEN: model hidden width."""
    return _parse_positive(raw, "MOJO_ENGINE_HIDDEN")


def parse_vocab(raw: String) raises -> Int:
    """MOJO_ENGINE_VOCAB: tokenizer vocabulary size."""
    return _parse_positive(raw, "MOJO_ENGINE_VOCAB")


# ===== END Wave E Lane E3 block (parsers) =====


struct EngineConfig(Copyable, Movable):
    """One loaded configuration; build via EngineConfig.load()."""

    var model_path: String
    var context_len: Int
    var gpu_budget_bytes: Int
    var attn_tile_positions: Int
    var attn_max_splits: Int
    var attn_split_span_positions: Int
    var prefill_gemm_min_batch: Int
    var gemm_tiled_min_batch: Int
    # -- BEGIN Wave E Lane E3 fields: Glimmer op defaults --
    var rms_eps: Float32
    var rope_base: Float32
    var logit_scale: Float32
    var logit_softcap: Float32
    var head_dim: Int
    var hidden: Int
    var vocab: Int
    # -- END Wave E Lane E3 fields --
    var prefill_batch_min_tokens: Int
    # -- Serving seam fields (step 7) --
    var serve_host: String
    var serve_port: Int
    var serve_max_body_bytes: Int
    var serve_default_max_tokens: Int
    var serve_max_tokens: Int

    var serve_max_context_bytes: Int

    var serve_models_dir: String
    var serve_backend_target: String
    var serve_attach_warn_tokens: Int
    # -- Deep-telemetry addendum field (2026-11-08) --
    var gpu_peak_bandwidth_gbps: Float64
    # -- Hash-chain field (zero-trust gate 3, 2026-11-08):
    # the git head sha of the tree this binary was built
    # from, supplied through config at launch
    # (MOJO_ENGINE_BUILD_SHA) and stamped into every run

    def __init__(
        out self,

        prefill_gemm_min_batch: Int = DEFAULT_PREFILL_GEMM_MIN_BATCH,
        gemm_tiled_min_batch: Int = DEFAULT_GEMM_TILED_MIN_BATCH,
        # -- BEGIN Wave E Lane E3 init params --
        rms_eps: Float32 = DEFAULT_RMS_EPS,
        rope_base: Float32 = DEFAULT_ROPE_BASE,
        logit_scale: Float32 = DEFAULT_LOGIT_SCALE,
        logit_softcap: Float32 = DEFAULT_LOGIT_SOFTCAP,
        head_dim: Int = DEFAULT_HEAD_DIM,
        hidden: Int = DEFAULT_HIDDEN,
        vocab: Int = DEFAULT_VOCAB,
        # -- END Wave E Lane E3 init params --
        prefill_batch_min_tokens: Int = DEFAULT_PREFILL_BATCH_MIN_TOKENS,
        serve_host: String = DEFAULT_SERVE_HOST,
        serve_port: Int = DEFAULT_SERVE_PORT,
        serve_max_body_bytes: Int = DEFAULT_SERVE_MAX_BODY_BYTES,
        serve_default_max_tokens: Int = DEFAULT_SERVE_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS,
        serve_max_tokens: Int = DEFAULT_SERVE_MAX_TOKENS,

        serve_max_context_bytes: Int = DEFAULT_SERVE_MAX_CONTEXT_BYTES,

        self.gpu_budget_bytes = gpu_budget_bytes

    @staticmethod
    def load() raises -> EngineConfig:
        """Load from the environment over the defaults.

        Raises a named error (mojo_engine_config: ...) on any bad
        value; the caller decides how to present the refusal.
        """
        var model_path = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_MODEL_PATH")
        if model_path == "":
            model_path = DEFAULT_MODEL_PATH

        var context_len = DEFAULT_CONTEXT_LEN
        var raw_ctx = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_CONTEXT_LEN")
        if raw_ctx != "":
            context_len = parse_context_len(raw_ctx)

        var gpu_budget_bytes = DEFAULT_GPU_BUDGET_BYTES
        var raw_budget = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_GPU_BUDGET_BYTES")
        if raw_budget != "":
            gpu_budget_bytes = parse_gpu_budget_bytes(raw_budget)

        var attn_tile = DEFAULT_ATTN_TILE_POSITIONS
        var raw_tile = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_ATTN_TILE_POSITIONS")
        if raw_tile != "":
            attn_tile = parse_attn_tile_positions(raw_tile)

        var attn_splits = DEFAULT_ATTN_MAX_SPLITS
        var raw_splits = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_ATTN_MAX_SPLITS")
        if raw_splits != "":
            attn_splits = parse_attn_max_splits(raw_splits)

        var attn_span = DEFAULT_ATTN_SPLIT_SPAN_POSITIONS
        var raw_span = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_ATTN_SPLIT_SPAN_POSITIONS")
        if raw_span != "":
            attn_span = parse_attn_split_span(raw_span)

        var prefill_gemm_min_batch = DEFAULT_PREFILL_GEMM_MIN_BATCH
        var raw_min = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_PREFILL_GEMM_MIN_BATCH")
        if raw_min != "":
            prefill_gemm_min_batch = parse_prefill_gemm_min_batch(raw_min)

        var gemm_tiled_min_batch = DEFAULT_GEMM_TILED_MIN_BATCH
        var raw_tiled = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_GEMM_TILED_MIN_BATCH")
        if raw_tiled != "":
            gemm_tiled_min_batch = parse_gemm_tiled_min_batch(raw_tiled)

        # -- BEGIN Wave E Lane E3 load: Glimmer op defaults --
        var rms_eps = DEFAULT_RMS_EPS
        var raw_eps = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_RMS_EPS")
        if raw_eps != "":
            rms_eps = parse_rms_eps(raw_eps)

        var rope_base = DEFAULT_ROPE_BASE
        var raw_base = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_ROPE_BASE")
        if raw_base != "":
            rope_base = parse_rope_base(raw_base)

        var logit_scale = DEFAULT_LOGIT_SCALE
        var raw_scale = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_LOGIT_SCALE")
        if raw_scale != "":
            logit_scale = parse_logit_scale(raw_scale)

        var logit_softcap = DEFAULT_LOGIT_SOFTCAP
        var raw_cap = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_LOGIT_SOFTCAP")
        if raw_cap != "":
            logit_softcap = parse_logit_softcap(raw_cap)

        var head_dim = DEFAULT_HEAD_DIM
        var raw_hd = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_HEAD_DIM")
        if raw_hd != "":
            head_dim = parse_head_dim(raw_hd)

        var hidden = DEFAULT_HIDDEN
        var raw_hidden = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_HIDDEN")
        if raw_hidden != "":
            hidden = parse_hidden(raw_hidden)

        var vocab = DEFAULT_VOCAB
        var raw_vocab = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_VOCAB")
        if raw_vocab != "":
            vocab = parse_vocab(raw_vocab)
        # -- END Wave E Lane E3 load --

        var prefill_batch_min_tokens = DEFAULT_PREFILL_BATCH_MIN_TOKENS
        var raw_route = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_PREFILL_BATCH_MIN_TOKENS")
        if raw_route != "":
            prefill_batch_min_tokens = parse_prefill_batch_min_tokens(raw_route)

        var serve_host = DEFAULT_SERVE_HOST
        var raw_host = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_SERVE_HOST")
        if raw_host != "":
            serve_host = parse_serve_host(raw_host)

        var serve_port = DEFAULT_SERVE_PORT
        var raw_port = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_SERVE_PORT")
        if raw_port != "":
            serve_port = parse_serve_port(raw_port)

        var serve_max_body = DEFAULT_SERVE_MAX_BODY_BYTES
        var raw_body = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_SERVE_MAX_BODY_BYTES")
        if raw_body != "":
            serve_max_body = parse_serve_max_body_bytes(raw_body)

        var serve_default_max_tokens = DEFAULT_SERVE_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS
        var raw_dmt = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_SERVE_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS")
        if raw_dmt != "":
            serve_default_max_tokens = parse_serve_default_max_tokens(raw_dmt)

        var serve_max_tokens = DEFAULT_SERVE_MAX_TOKENS
        var raw_mt = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_SERVE_MAX_TOKENS")
        if raw_mt != "":
            serve_max_tokens = parse_serve_max_tokens(raw_mt)
        var serve_debug_ring_lines = DEFAULT_SERVE_DEBUG_RING_LINES
        var raw_ring = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_SERVE_DEBUG_RING_LINES")
        if raw_ring != "":
            serve_debug_ring_lines = parse_serve_debug_ring_lines(raw_ring)

        var serve_max_context_bytes = DEFAULT_SERVE_MAX_CONTEXT_BYTES
        var raw_ctx_bytes = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_SERVE_MAX_CONTEXT_BYTES")
        if raw_ctx_bytes != "":
            serve_max_context_bytes = parse_serve_max_context_bytes(
                raw_ctx_bytes
            )

        var serve_history_dir = DEFAULT_SERVE_HISTORY_DIR
        var raw_hist = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_SERVE_HISTORY_DIR")
        if raw_hist != "":
            serve_history_dir = parse_serve_dir(
                raw_hist, "MOJO_ENGINE_SERVE_HISTORY_DIR"
            )

        var serve_models_dir = DEFAULT_SERVE_MODELS_DIR
        var raw_models = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_SERVE_MODELS_DIR")
        if raw_models != "":
            serve_models_dir = parse_serve_dir(
                raw_models, "MOJO_ENGINE_SERVE_MODELS_DIR"
            )

        var serve_backend_target = DEFAULT_SERVE_BACKEND_TARGET
        var raw_backend = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_SERVE_BACKEND_TARGET")
        if raw_backend != "":
            serve_backend_target = parse_serve_backend_target(raw_backend)

        var serve_attach_warn_tokens = DEFAULT_SERVE_ATTACH_WARN_TOKENS
        var raw_warn = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_SERVE_ATTACH_WARN_TOKENS")
        if raw_warn != "":
            serve_attach_warn_tokens = parse_serve_attach_warn_tokens(raw_warn)

        var gpu_peak_bandwidth_gbps = DEFAULT_GPU_PEAK_BANDWIDTH_GBPS
        var raw_peak = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_GPU_PEAK_BANDWIDTH_GBPS")
        if raw_peak != "":
            gpu_peak_bandwidth_gbps = parse_gpu_peak_bandwidth_gbps(raw_peak)

        # Build provenance for the run-record hash chain: a
        # plain stamp, taken as given ("" when unset).
        var build_sha = getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_BUILD_SHA")

        if serve_default_max_tokens > serve_max_tokens:
            raise Error(
                "mojo_engine_config: MOJO_ENGINE_SERVE_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS"
                " exceeds MOJO_ENGINE_SERVE_MAX_TOKENS"
            )

        return EngineConfig(
            model_path,
            context_len,
            gpu_budget_bytes,
            attn_tile,
            attn_splits,
            attn_span,
            prefill_gemm_min_batch,
            gemm_tiled_min_batch,
            # -- BEGIN Wave E Lane E3 load return values --
            rms_eps,
            rope_base,
            logit_scale,
            logit_softcap,
            head_dim,
            hidden,
            vocab,
            # -- END Wave E Lane E3 load return values --
            prefill_batch_min_tokens,
            serve_host,
            serve_port,
            serve_max_body,
            serve_default_max_tokens,
            serve_max_tokens,
            serve_debug_ring_lines,
            serve_max_context_bytes,
            serve_history_dir,
            serve_models_dir,
            serve_backend_target,
            serve_attach_warn_tokens,
            gpu_peak_bandwidth_gbps,
            build_sha,
        )

===== FILE: mojo-engine/src/diag.mojo =====
# diag.mojo - the Mojo engine's debug seam.
#
# Same shape as the Rust tree's diag seam: one env var,
# MOJO_ENGINE_DEBUG, enables the channel. The var is consulted on
# EVERY call (never cached at startup), so any binary or test that
# links this module can be switched at launch with no wiring and
# no rebuild. A present value enables, except "" and "0", which
# do not. While off, log lines are never printed and their message
# arguments are the caller's business alone, mirroring the Rust
# seam's no-format-while-off contract as closely as Mojo allows.
#
# Every emitted line is named: [mojo_engine][<phase>] <message>.

from std.os import getenv


def debug_value_enabled(value: String) -> Bool:
    """Pure predicate over a raw env value; the seam's whole rule.

    Split out from debug_enabled() so the rule itself is testable
    without mutating the process environment.
    """
    return value != "" and value != "0"


def debug_enabled() -> Bool:
    """True when MOJO_ENGINE_DEBUG currently enables the seam."""
    return debug_value_enabled(getenv("MOJO_ENGINE_DEBUG"))


def format_line(phase: String, msg: String) -> String:
    """The named line the seam emits for (phase, msg)."""
    return "[mojo_engine][" + phase + "] " + msg


def log_debug(phase: String, msg: String) -> String:
    """Emit one named debug line when the seam is on.

    Returns the emitted line, or "" when the seam is off (nothing
    printed). The return value is what the self-test asserts on:
    on fires (line returned and printed), off is silent.
    """
    if not debug_enabled():
        return ""
    var line = format_line(phase, msg)
    print(line)
    return line

===== END FILE: mojo-engine/src/diag.mojo =====
