===== FILE: mojo-engine/src/tokenizer/byte_level.mojo =====
# byte_level.mojo - the GPT-2 byte-to-unicode map at the heart of
# byte-level BPE, plus the UTF-8 codec helpers the package shares.
#
# Mirror of crates/tokenizer/src/byte_level.rs. Every byte
# 0..=255 is assigned a printable Unicode codepoint so BPE
# operates on text with no invisible control characters. Bytes in
# the ranges !..=~, ¡..=¬, ®..=ÿ map to the codepoint with the
# same value; the remaining 68 bytes map to U+0100 and upward in
# byte order. The space byte 0x20 maps to Ġ (U+0120), which is
# why raw GGUF token strings show Ġ where a space belongs: decode
# must run this map in reverse.
#
# The UTF-8 helpers work on codepoint lists (List[Int], one entry
# per Unicode scalar) because the rest of the package scans text
# by codepoint, exactly as the Rust side scans by char. Strict
# decoding validates like Rust's String::from_utf8: overlong
# forms, surrogates, and values above U+10FFFF are refused, and
# the refusal names the byte offset of the valid prefix
# (Utf8Error::valid_up_to on the Rust side).


def is_direct_byte(b: Int) -> Bool:
    """True when byte `b` maps to the codepoint with its value."""
    return (
        (0x21 <= b and b <= 0x7E)
        or (0xA1 <= b and b <= 0xAC)
        or (0xAE <= b and b <= 0xFF)
    )


def byte_to_codepoint(b: Int) -> Int:
    """The printable codepoint assigned to byte `b` (0..=255)."""
    if is_direct_byte(b):
        return b
    var next_cp = 256
    for cand in range(256):
        if not is_direct_byte(cand):
            if cand == b:
                return next_cp
            next_cp += 1
    return b  # unreachable for 0..=255


def codepoint_to_byte(cp: Int) -> Int:
    """The byte assigned to `cp`, or -1 when `cp` is not part of
    the byte-level alphabet (for example a literal character from
    a control token's text). Mirrors char_to_byte's None."""
    if cp >= 0 and cp <= 0xFF and is_direct_byte(cp):
        return cp
    if cp >= 256 and cp < 256 + 68:
        var idx = cp - 256
        var seen = 0
        for cand in range(256):
            if not is_direct_byte(cand):
                if seen == idx:
                    return cand
                seen += 1
    return -1


def byte_token_name(b: Int) -> String:
    """The GGUF byte-token name for a byte: `<0x0A>` and friends
    (uppercase hex, as the Rust side formats it)."""
    var hi = (b >> 4) & 0xF
    var lo = b & 0xF
    return "<0x" + _hex_char(hi) + _hex_char(lo) + ">"


def _hex_char(v: Int) -> String:
    var cp = (0x30 + v) if v < 10 else (0x41 + v - 10)
    return String(Codepoint.from_u32(UInt32(cp)).value())


def _hex_value(b: Int) -> Int:
    if 0x30 <= b and b <= 0x39:  # '0'..='9'
        return b - 0x30
    if 0x61 <= b and b <= 0x66:  # 'a'..='f'
        return b - 0x61 + 10
    if 0x41 <= b and b <= 0x46:  # 'A'..='F'
        return b - 0x41 + 10
    return -1


def parse_byte_token(text: String) -> Int:
    """Parse a `<0xXX>` byte-token name back to its byte,
    accepting upper or lower case hex. Returns -1 for any other
    shape (the Rust side's None)."""
    var bytes = List[UInt8]()
    for b in text.as_bytes():
        bytes.append(b)
    if len(bytes) != 6:
        return -1
    if (
        Int(bytes[0]) != 0x3C  # '<'
        or Int(bytes[1]) != 0x30  # '0'
        or Int(bytes[2]) != 0x78  # 'x'
        or Int(bytes[5]) != 0x3E  # '>'
    ):
        return -1
    var hi = _hex_value(Int(bytes[3]))
    var lo = _hex_value(Int(bytes[4]))
    if hi < 0 or lo < 0:
        return -1
    return (hi << 4) | lo


# --- UTF-8 codec over codepoint lists ---


def codepoints_of(text: String) -> List[Int]:
    """The codepoints of `text`, in order."""
    var out = List[Int]()
    for cp in text.codepoints():
        out.append(Int(cp.to_u32()))
    return out^


def string_from_codepoints(cps: List[Int], start: Int, end: Int) -> String:
    """Build the String for cps[start:end]. Callers pass valid
    scalar values from real text or the byte alphabet."""
    var out = String()
    for i in range(start, end):
        var opt = Codepoint.from_u32(UInt32(cps[i]))
        if Bool(opt):
            out += String(opt.value())
    return out^


def append_utf8(cp: Int, mut out: List[UInt8]):
    """Append the UTF-8 encoding of codepoint `cp` to `out`."""
    if cp < 0x80:
        out.append(UInt8(cp))
    elif cp < 0x800:
        out.append(UInt8(0xC0 | (cp >> 6)))
        out.append(UInt8(0x80 | (cp & 0x3F)))
    elif cp < 0x10000:
        out.append(UInt8(0xE0 | (cp >> 12)))
        out.append(UInt8(0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F)))
        out.append(UInt8(0x80 | (cp & 0x3F)))
    else:
        out.append(UInt8(0xF0 | (cp >> 18)))
        out.append(UInt8(0x80 | ((cp >> 12) & 0x3F)))
        out.append(UInt8(0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F)))
        out.append(UInt8(0x80 | (cp & 0x3F)))


def utf8_len_of_codepoint(cp: Int) -> Int:
    if cp < 0x80:
        return 1
    if cp < 0x800:
        return 2
    if cp < 0x10000:
        return 3
    return 4


def bytes_of_codepoints(cps: List[Int]) -> List[UInt8]:
    var out = List[UInt8]()
    for cp in cps:
        append_utf8(cp, out)
    return out^


def bytes_of_string(text: String) -> List[UInt8]:
    var out = List[UInt8]()
    for b in text.as_bytes():
        out.append(b)
    return out^


def decode_utf8_strict(bytes: List[UInt8]) raises -> List[Int]:
    """Decode UTF-8 bytes to codepoints, strictly.

    Raises tokenizer_invalid_utf8 naming the valid prefix length
    on the first invalid or truncated sequence, mirroring
    String::from_utf8 + Error::InvalidUtf8 on the Rust side.
    """
    var out = List[Int]()
    var n = len(bytes)
    var i = 0
    while i < n:
        var b0 = Int(bytes[i])
        if b0 < 0x80:
            out.append(b0)
            i += 1
            continue
        var need: Int
        var cp: Int
        var lo2 = 0x80
        var hi2 = 0xBF
        if 0xC2 <= b0 and b0 <= 0xDF:
            need = 2
            cp = b0 & 0x1F
        elif b0 == 0xE0:
            need = 3
            cp = b0 & 0x0F
            lo2 = 0xA0
        elif 0xE1 <= b0 and b0 <= 0xEC:
            need = 3
            cp = b0 & 0x0F
        elif b0 == 0xED:
            need = 3
            cp = b0 & 0x0F
            hi2 = 0x9F
        elif 0xEE <= b0 and b0 <= 0xEF:
            need = 3
            cp = b0 & 0x0F
        elif b0 == 0xF0:
            need = 4
            cp = b0 & 0x07
            lo2 = 0x90
        elif 0xF1 <= b0 and b0 <= 0xF3:
            need = 4
            cp = b0 & 0x07
        elif b0 == 0xF4:
            need = 4
            cp = b0 & 0x07
            hi2 = 0x8F
        else:
            raise Error(
                "tokenizer_invalid_utf8: decoded bytes are not valid"
                " UTF-8 (valid up to byte "
                + String(i)
                + ")"
            )
        if i + need > n:
            raise Error(
                "tokenizer_invalid_utf8: decoded bytes are not valid"
                " UTF-8 (valid up to byte "
                + String(i)
                + ")"
            )
        var b1 = Int(bytes[i + 1])
        if b1 < lo2 or b1 > hi2:
            raise Error(
                "tokenizer_invalid_utf8: decoded bytes are not valid"
                " UTF-8 (valid up to byte "
                + String(i)
                + ")"
            )
        cp = (cp << 6) | (b1 & 0x3F)
        var ok = True
        for k in range(2, need):
            var bk = Int(bytes[i + k])
            if bk < 0x80 or bk > 0xBF:
                ok = False
                break
            cp = (cp << 6) | (bk & 0x3F)
        if not ok:
            raise Error(
                "tokenizer_invalid_utf8: decoded bytes are not valid"
                " UTF-8 (valid up to byte "
                + String(i)
                + ")"
            )
        out.append(cp)
        i += need
    return out^


def string_from_bytes_strict(bytes: List[UInt8]) raises -> String:
    """The String for a byte stream that must be valid UTF-8
    (decode's contract); see decode_utf8_strict."""
    var cps = decode_utf8_strict(bytes)
    return string_from_codepoints(cps, 0, len(cps))


def string_from_bytes_lossy(bytes: List[UInt8]) -> String:
    """The String for a byte stream with invalid sequences
    replaced by U+FFFD, mirroring String::from_utf8_lossy.

    Simplification, stated plainly: an invalid sequence is
    replaced per byte here, where Rust replaces the maximal
    invalid subpart, so a truncated multi-byte sequence at the
    end of the stream can yield more replacement characters
    here than in Rust. decode_lossy is not on the conformance
    path; decode (strict) matches exactly.
    """
    var out = String()
    var n = len(bytes)
    var i = 0
    while i < n:
        var b0 = Int(bytes[i])
        if b0 < 0x80:
            out += String(Codepoint.from_u32(UInt32(b0)).value())
            i += 1
            continue
        var need = 0
        if 0xC2 <= b0 and b0 <= 0xDF:
            need = 2
        elif 0xE0 <= b0 and b0 <= 0xEF:
            need = 3
        elif 0xF0 <= b0 and b0 <= 0xF4:
            need = 4
        if need == 0 or i + need > n:
            out += String(Codepoint.from_u32(UInt32(0xFFFD)).value())
            i += 1
            continue
        var slice = List[UInt8]()
        for k in range(need):
            slice.append(bytes[i + k])
        try:
            var cps = decode_utf8_strict(slice)
            out += string_from_codepoints(cps, 0, len(cps))
            i += need
        except:
            out += String(Codepoint.from_u32(UInt32(0xFFFD)).value())
            i += 1
    return out^

===== END FILE: mojo-engine/src/tokenizer/byte_level.mojo =====

===== FILE: mojo-engine/src/tokenizer/gguf_vocab.mojo =====
# gguf_vocab.mojo - the tokenizer's vocabulary source: produce
# TokenizerData from a GGUF file through Lane A1's loader
# (src/gguf/loader.mojo).
#
# History: Lane A5 landed with a temporary self-contained GGUF
# metadata reader in this file so the tokenizer could be built
# in parallel with Lane A1. At Wave A integration the seam was
# swapped, as chartered: this module now parses the file with
# the engine's GGUF loader and maps its metadata getters onto
# TokenizerData (the Rust shape: crates/gguf TokenizerInfo ->
# TokenizerData, as in crates/tokenizer/examples/
# conformance.rs's data_from_info). Nothing outside this file
# knows GGUF exists: tokenizer.mojo consumes TokenizerData
# only. The interface preserved is load_tokenizer_data(path)
# -> TokenizerData.
#
# Keys read: tokenizer.ggml.model, .pre, .tokens, .token_type,
# .merges, .scores, .bos_token_id, .eos_token_id,
# .unknown_token_id, .padding_token_id (the crates/gguf
# TokenizerInfo set plus pre). Malformed files refuse inside
# the loader with its gguf_* names; a file whose tokenizer
# metadata has the wrong shape refuses here with
# tokenizer_gguf_type_mismatch, and a file with no
# tokenizer.ggml.tokens refuses with
# tokenizer_missing_vocab_metadata.

from diag import log_debug
from gguf.loader import (
    META_ARRAY,
    META_F32,
    META_F64,
    META_STRING,
    GgufFile,
    parse_gguf,
)
from tokenizer.tokenizer import TokenizerData


def _string_array(
    file: GgufFile, key: String, required: Bool
) raises -> List[String]:
    var out = List[String]()
    if not file.has_metadata(key):
        if required:
            raise Error(
                "tokenizer_missing_vocab_metadata: GGUF file carries no " + key
            )
        return out^
    var idx = file.require_metadata(key)
    var value = file.metadata[idx].value.copy()
    if value.type_id != META_ARRAY or value.array_elem_type != META_STRING:
        raise Error(
            "tokenizer_gguf_type_mismatch: "
            + key
            + " must be an array of strings"
        )
    for s in value.array_strings:
        out.append(s)
    return out^


def _int_array(file: GgufFile, key: String) raises -> List[Int]:
    var out = List[Int]()
    if not file.has_metadata(key):
        return out^
    var n = file.metadata_array_len(key)
    for i in range(n):
        out.append(Int(file.metadata_array_i64(key, i)))
    return out^


def _float_array(file: GgufFile, key: String) raises -> List[Float64]:
    var out = List[Float64]()
    if not file.has_metadata(key):
        return out^
    var idx = file.require_metadata(key)
    var value = file.metadata[idx].value.copy()
    if value.type_id != META_ARRAY or (
        value.array_elem_type != META_F32 and value.array_elem_type != META_F64
    ):
        raise Error(
            "tokenizer_gguf_type_mismatch: "
            + key
            + " must be an array of floats"
        )
    for v in value.array_floats:
        out.append(v)
    return out^


def _int_value(file: GgufFile, key: String) raises -> Int:
    if not file.has_metadata(key):
        return -1
    return Int(file.get_i64(key))


def load_tokenizer_data(path: String) raises -> TokenizerData:
    """Read the tokenizer metadata from the GGUF file at `path`
    into TokenizerData, through the engine's GGUF loader.
    Refuses by name on anything malformed (the loader's gguf_*
    refusals, or this module's tokenizer_* ones)."""
    var file = parse_gguf(path)
    var data = TokenizerData()
    if file.has_metadata("tokenizer.ggml.model"):
        data.model = file.get_string("tokenizer.ggml.model")
        data.has_model = True
    if file.has_metadata("tokenizer.ggml.pre"):
        data.pre = file.get_string("tokenizer.ggml.pre")
        data.has_pre = True
    data.tokens = _string_array(file, "tokenizer.ggml.tokens", True)
    if len(data.tokens) == 0:
        _ = log_debug(
            "tokenizer",
            "refusing: no tokenizer.ggml.tokens in " + path,
        )
        raise Error(
            "tokenizer_missing_vocab_metadata: GGUF file "
            + path
            + " carries no tokenizer.ggml.tokens metadata"
        )
    data.token_types = _int_array(file, "tokenizer.ggml.token_type")
    data.merges = _string_array(file, "tokenizer.ggml.merges", False)
    if file.has_metadata("tokenizer.ggml.scores"):
        data.scores = _float_array(file, "tokenizer.ggml.scores")
        data.has_scores = True
    data.bos_token_id = _int_value(file, "tokenizer.ggml.bos_token_id")
    data.eos_token_id = _int_value(file, "tokenizer.ggml.eos_token_id")
    data.unknown_token_id = _int_value(file, "tokenizer.ggml.unknown_token_id")
    data.padding_token_id = _int_value(file, "tokenizer.ggml.padding_token_id")
    _ = log_debug(
        "tokenizer",
        "gguf vocab loaded tokens="
        + String(len(data.tokens))
        + " merges="
        + String(len(data.merges))
        + " from "
        + path,
    )
    return data^

===== FILE: mojo-engine/src/tokenizer/pretokenize.mojo =====
# pretokenize.mojo - the pre-tokenizer: a hand-written scanner
# implementing the llama4 / GPT-4o split pattern, a direct port
# of crates/tokenizer/src/pretokenize.rs (see that file and
# crates/tokenizer/src/lib.rs for the pattern text). BPE runs per
# piece, never across piece boundaries. The split is lossless:
# concatenating the pieces reproduces the input exactly.
#
# The pattern, as the Rust crate documents it:
#
#   [^\\r\\n\\p{L}\\p{N}]?[\\p{Lu}\\p{Lt}\\p{Lm}\\p{Lo}\\p{M}]*[\\p{Ll}\\p{Lm}\\p{Lo}\\p{M}]+(?:'s|'t|'re|'ve|'m|'ll|'d)?
#   | [^\\r\\n\\p{L}\\p{N}]?[\\p{Lu}\\p{Lt}\\p{Lm}\\p{Lo}\\p{M}]+[\\p{Ll}\\p{Lm}\\p{Lo}\\p{M}]*(?:'s|'t|'re|'ve|'m|'ll|'d)?
#   | \\p{N}{1,3}
#   |  ?[^\\s\\p{L}\\p{N}]+[\\r\\n/]*
#   | \\s*[\\r\\n]+
#   | \\s+(?!\S)
#   | \\s+
#
# The two word alternatives span the same maximal letter run, so
# the scanner implements them as one letter run plus the optional
# contraction suffix. There is no standalone contraction
# alternative: a contraction that does not follow a word (the 've
# in you'd've, the 's in 90's) is picked up by the prefix-char
# word branch instead.
#
# Deviations, mirroring the Rust crate's stated ones and adding
# this port's own:
# - Rust approximates \\p{L} by char::is_alphabetic and \\p{N} by
#   char::is_numeric, and \\s by char::is_whitespace (the exact
#   Unicode White_Space property, reproduced exactly below).
# - Mojo has no Unicode property tables, so is_alphabetic /
#   is_numeric below are curated codepoint range tables covering
#   the major scripts (Latin incl. extensions, Greek, Cyrillic,
#   Armenian, Hebrew, Arabic, Indic, Thai, CJK, kana, Hangul,
#   Ethiopic, Georgian, and the other blocks listed in the
#   ranges). Combining marks U+0300..=U+036F count as letters,
#   matching the pattern's \\p{M} inside word runs. Digits are
#   classified before letters, so a digit block inside a broad
#   script range still classifies as a number. Rare scripts and
#   newer Unicode additions can classify as symbols where Rust
#   says letter (or the reverse at block edges); splitting is
#   always lossless either way. The 16-prompt Glimmer parity set
#   (Latin, accented Latin, CJK, kana, digits, emoji, symbols)
#   sits entirely inside the covered ranges.

from tokenizer.byte_level import codepoints_of


def is_whitespace_cp(cp: Int) -> Bool:
    """The Unicode White_Space property, exactly (Rust's
    char::is_whitespace set)."""
    if 0x09 <= cp and cp <= 0x0D:
        return True
    if cp == 0x20 or cp == 0x85 or cp == 0xA0 or cp == 0x1680:
        return True
    if 0x2000 <= cp and cp <= 0x200A:
        return True
    if cp == 0x2028 or cp == 0x2029 or cp == 0x202F or cp == 0x205F:
        return True
    return cp == 0x3000

def is_letter(cps: List[Int], idx: Int) -> Bool:
    return is_letter_cp(cps[idx])


def is_number(cps: List[Int], idx: Int) -> Bool:
    return is_numeric_cp(cps[idx])


def is_symbol_cp(cp: Int) -> Bool:
    """A character the symbol branch consumes: not whitespace,
    not a letter, not a number (Rust's is_symbol)."""
    return (
        not is_whitespace_cp(cp)
        and not is_letter_cp(cp)
        and not is_numeric_cp(cp)
    )


def _ascii_lower(cp: Int) -> Int:
    if 0x41 <= cp and cp <= 0x5A:
        return cp + 32
    return cp


def contraction_len(cps: List[Int], i: Int) -> Int:
    """If a contraction starts at `i` (cps[i] is `'`), returns
    its length in codepoints including the apostrophe, else 0.
    Suffixes, longest first: re, ve, ll, then s, t, m, d; ASCII
    case-insensitive (port of the Rust helper)."""
    var c1 = -1
    var c2 = -1
    if i + 1 < len(cps):
        c1 = _ascii_lower(cps[i + 1])
    if i + 2 < len(cps):
        c2 = _ascii_lower(cps[i + 2])
    # 'r' 'e' / 'v' 'e' / 'l' 'l'
    if (
        (c1 == 0x72 and c2 == 0x65)
        or (c1 == 0x76 and c2 == 0x65)
        or (c1 == 0x6C and c2 == 0x6C)
    ):
        return 3
    if c1 == 0x73 or c1 == 0x74 or c1 == 0x6D or c1 == 0x64:  # s t m d
        return 2
    return 0


def letter_run(cps: List[Int], start: Int) -> Int:
    """Consumes a run of letters starting at `start`; returns
    the end index."""
    var i = start
    while i < len(cps) and is_letter_cp(cps[i]):
        i += 1
    return i


def word_end(cps: List[Int], end: Int) -> Int:
    """The end of a word piece whose letters end at `end`:
    absorbs one trailing contraction when one starts there."""
    if end < len(cps) and cps[end] == 0x27:  # '\''
        var clen = contraction_len(cps, end)
        if clen > 0:
            return end + clen
    return end


def symbol_run(cps: List[Int], start: Int) -> Int:
    """Consumes a symbol run starting at `start`, plus any
    \\r/\\n run that immediately follows it (the pattern's
    [\\r\\n]* tail); returns the end index."""
    var i = start
    while i < len(cps) and is_symbol_cp(cps[i]):
        i += 1
    while i < len(cps) and (cps[i] == 0x0D or cps[i] == 0x0A):
        i += 1
    return i


def scan_whitespace(cps: List[Int], i: Int) -> Int:
    """The whitespace branches: \\s*[\\r\\n]+, then \\s+(?!\\S),
    then \\s+. Port of the Rust helper."""
    var n = len(cps)
    var run_end = i
    while run_end < n and is_whitespace_cp(cps[run_end]):
        run_end += 1
    # Run contains a newline: take the run up to the end of its
    # last newline; spaces after that newline are rescanned.
    var last_newline = -1
    for k in range(i, run_end):
        if cps[k] == 0x0D or cps[k] == 0x0A:
            last_newline = k
    if last_newline >= 0:
        return last_newline + 1
    # Run reaches the end of the text: \\s+(?!\S) matches all.
    if run_end == n:
        return run_end
    # Run of 2+ before non-whitespace: \\s+(?!\S) backtracks by
    # one, leaving the final space to prefix the next piece.
    if run_end - i >= 2:
        return run_end - 1
    # A single whitespace char before non-whitespace prefixes a
    # letter or symbol piece; before a digit it stands alone.
    var next_cp = cps[run_end]
    if is_letter_cp(next_cp):
        return word_end(cps, letter_run(cps, run_end))
    if is_symbol_cp(next_cp):
        return symbol_run(cps, run_end)
    return run_end


def scan_piece(cps: List[Int], i: Int) -> Int:
    """Scans one piece starting at codepoint index `i` and
    returns the index just past its end. Mirrors the alternation
    order of the pattern. There is deliberately no standalone
    contraction branch: see word_end."""
    var n = len(cps)
    var c = cps[i]
    # 1. Letter branch, bare.
    if is_letter_cp(c):
        return word_end(cps, letter_run(cps, i))
    # 2. Letter branch with one prefix char. Covers " word",
    #    "-word", and a contraction left over after a word piece.
    if (
        not is_numeric_cp(c)
        and c != 0x0D
        and c != 0x0A
        and i + 1 < n
        and is_letter_cp(cps[i + 1])
    ):
        return word_end(cps, letter_run(cps, i + 1))
    # 3. Number branch: \\p{N}{1,3}.
    if is_numeric_cp(c):
        var j = i
        while j < n and j - i < 3 and is_numeric_cp(cps[j]):
            j += 1
        return j
    # 4. Whitespace branches.
    if is_whitespace_cp(c):
        return scan_whitespace(cps, i)
    # 5. Symbol branch.
    return symbol_run(cps, i)


def pretokenize(cps: List[Int]) -> List[List[Int]]:
    """Splits codepoints into the pieces BPE will encode
    independently. Lossless: the pieces concatenate to the
    input."""
    var pieces = List[List[Int]]()
    var i = 0
    while i < len(cps):
        var end = scan_piece(cps, i)
        var piece = List[Int]()
        for k in range(i, end):
            piece.append(cps[k])
        pieces.append(piece^)
        i = end
    return pieces^


def pretokenize_text(text: String) -> List[String]:
    """String convenience wrapper over pretokenize, matching
    the Rust signature pretokenize(&str) -> Vec<&str> in
    content."""
    from tokenizer.byte_level import string_from_codepoints

    var cps = codepoints_of(text)
    var pieces = pretokenize(cps)
    var out = List[String]()
    for piece in pieces:
        out.append(string_from_codepoints(piece, 0, len(piece)))
    return out^

===== END FILE: mojo-engine/src/tokenizer/pretokenize.mojo =====

===== FILE: mojo-engine/src/tokenizer/spm.mojo =====
# spm.mojo - SentencePiece BPE: the "llama" tokenizer family.
#
# Direct port of crates/tokenizer/src/spm.rs, which is itself a
# direct port of llama.cpp's SPM path (rules cited there to
# src/llama-vocab.cpp in llama.cpp 0.7.0-dev, commit a7af149):
#
# 1. The escaped text prefixes one space when the caller says
#    the previous fragment was special (or this is the start),
#    then every space becomes ▁ (U+2581).
# 2. Symbols start as single codepoints, lengths from the
#    unicode_len_utf8 high-nibble table. Adjacent pairs merge
#    one at a time by the COMBINED token's score from
#    tokenizer.ggml.scores (highest first, ties to the leftmost
#    pair); no scores array means every score is 0.0.
# 3. Re-segmentation: a final symbol whose text is a token emits
#    it; one that is not is split back through the recorded
#    rev_merge pair, and a text with no recorded split is emitted
#    byte by byte via <0xXX> byte tokens.
#
# Port note: the Rust side drives merges from a binary heap of
# queued bigrams. This port rescans the live symbol chain each
# round and merges the single best adjacent pair (highest
# score, ties to the smallest left index), which selects the
# same merge at every step: the candidate set at any moment is
# exactly the adjacent live pairs whose concatenation is a
# vocabulary token, and a pair's score does not change. The
# rev_merge table here records pair TEXTS (not symbol indices)
# at scan time; that table is only consulted for final symbols
# whose text is not a token, which ordinary vocabularies never
# produce (merges only ever form vocabulary tokens), as the
# Rust side notes too.

from std.collections import Dict

from tokenizer.byte_level import (
    byte_token_name,
    bytes_of_codepoints,
    string_from_codepoints,
)

comptime SPM_SPACE = 0x2581  # ▁


def escape_whitespace_cps(cps: List[Int]) -> List[Int]:
    """llama_escape_whitespace on codepoints: space -> ▁."""
    var out = List[Int]()
    for cp in cps:
        out.append(SPM_SPACE if cp == 0x20 else cp)
    return out^


def unescape_whitespace(text: String) -> String:
    """llama_unescape_whitespace: every ▁ becomes a space."""
    from tokenizer.byte_level import codepoints_of

    var cps = codepoints_of(text)
    var out = List[Int]()
    for cp in cps:
        out.append(0x20 if cp == SPM_SPACE else cp)
    return string_from_codepoints(out, 0, len(out))


def utf8_len(lead: Int) -> Int:
    """unicode_len_utf8 from llama.cpp's src/unicode.cpp: a
    lookup on the lead byte's high nibble ([1]*12 + [2,2,3,4]).
    Continuation bytes (0x80..=0xBF) report 1."""
    var nibble = (lead >> 4) & 0xF
    if nibble < 12:
        return 1
    if nibble == 12 or nibble == 13:
        return 2
    if nibble == 14:
        return 3
    return 4


def _pair_text(
    text_bytes: List[UInt8],
    sym_start: List[Int],
    sym_n: List[Int],
    left: Int,
    right: Int,
) raises -> String:
    """The concatenated text of two chain-adjacent symbols,
    from their current byte ranges."""
    from tokenizer.byte_level import decode_utf8_strict

    var both = List[UInt8]()
    for k in range(sym_n[left]):
        both.append(text_bytes[sym_start[left] + k])
    for k in range(sym_n[right]):
        both.append(text_bytes[sym_start[right] + k])
    var cps = decode_utf8_strict(both)
    return string_from_codepoints(cps, 0, len(cps))


def _slice_string(bytes: List[UInt8], start: Int, length: Int) raises -> String:
    """The String for bytes[start:start+length], which is a
    symbol slice of valid escaped text (always valid UTF-8)."""
    from tokenizer.byte_level import decode_utf8_strict

    var slice = List[UInt8]()
    for k in range(length):
        slice.append(bytes[start + k])
    var cps = decode_utf8_strict(slice)
    return string_from_codepoints(cps, 0, len(cps))


def _byte_to_token(vocab: Dict[String, Int], byte: Int) raises -> Int:
    """llama_vocab::byte_to_token for the SPM type: the <0xXX>
    token, falling back to the byte as a one-character token
    (ASCII only). Named refusal when neither exists."""
    from diag import log_debug

    var name = byte_token_name(byte)
    if name in vocab:
        return vocab[name]
    if byte < 0x80:
        var single = string_from_codepoints(List[Int]([byte]), 0, 1)
        if single in vocab:
            return vocab[single]
    _ = log_debug("tokenizer", "refusing byte: no byte token in vocabulary")
    raise Error(
        "tokenizer_missing_byte_token: vocabulary has no byte token for byte "
        + String(byte)
    )


def encode_segment(
    vocab: Dict[String, Int],
    scores: List[Float64],
    segment: List[Int],
    prefix_space: Bool,
) raises -> List[Int]:
    """Tokenizes one raw-text segment (as codepoints) the
    SentencePiece way. `prefix_space` mirrors llama.cpp's
    add_space_prefix && is_prev_special: one space is prepended
    before escaping, so the segment's first word takes its
    ▁-initial form."""
    # Escaped codepoints, then their UTF-8 bytes (symbols index
    # into the byte string, as in llama.cpp).
    var escaped = List[Int]()
    if prefix_space:
        escaped.append(SPM_SPACE)
    var seg_escaped = escape_whitespace_cps(segment)
    for cp in seg_escaped:
        escaped.append(cp)
    var text_bytes = bytes_of_codepoints(escaped)

    # Split into one symbol per UTF-8 codepoint.
    var sym_start = List[Int]()
    var sym_n = List[Int]()
    var sym_prev = List[Int]()
    var sym_next = List[Int]()
    var offs = 0
    var index = 0
    while offs < len(text_bytes):
        var ln = utf8_len(Int(text_bytes[offs]))
        var remain = len(text_bytes) - offs
        if ln > remain:
            ln = remain
        sym_start.append(offs)
        sym_n.append(ln)
        sym_prev.append(index - 1)
        sym_next.append(-1 if offs + ln == len(text_bytes) else index + 1)
        offs += ln
        index += 1

    var rev_left = Dict[String, String]()
    var rev_right = Dict[String, String]()

    # Merge loop: rescan the chain, merge the best pair, repeat
    # (see the module header for the equivalence argument).
    while True:
        var best_found = False
        var best_left = -1
        var best_right = -1
        var best_score = Float64(0.0)
        var cur = 0 if len(sym_n) > 0 else -1
        while cur != -1:
            var nxt = sym_next[cur]
            if nxt != -1:
                var text = _pair_text(text_bytes, sym_start, sym_n, cur, nxt)
                if text in vocab:
                    var tok = vocab[text]
                    if tok >= 0 and tok < len(scores):
                        # Offer: record the split for this text,
                        # as try_add_bigram does.
                        var lt = _slice_string(
                            text_bytes, sym_start[cur], sym_n[cur]
                        )
                        var rt = _slice_string(
                            text_bytes, sym_start[nxt], sym_n[nxt]
                        )
                        rev_left[text] = lt
                        rev_right[text] = rt
                        var score = scores[tok]
                        if not best_found or score > best_score:
                            best_found = True
                            best_left = cur
                            best_right = nxt
                            best_score = score
            cur = nxt
        if not best_found:
            break
        # Merge the right symbol into the left one.
        var right_next = sym_next[best_right]
        sym_n[best_left] = sym_n[best_left] + sym_n[best_right]
        sym_n[best_right] = 0
        sym_next[best_left] = right_next
        if right_next >= 0:
            sym_prev[right_next] = best_left

    # Re-segment the final symbols.
    var output = List[Int]()
    var stack = List[String]()
    var i = 0 if len(sym_n) > 0 else -1
    # Walk the chain, pushing symbol texts in reverse so pops
    # come out in chain order through the shared stack below.
    var chain_texts = List[String]()
    while i != -1:
        chain_texts.append(_slice_string(text_bytes, sym_start[i], sym_n[i]))
        i = sym_next[i]
    for ci in range(len(chain_texts)):
        stack.append(chain_texts[len(chain_texts) - 1 - ci])
    while len(stack) > 0:
        var text = stack.pop()
        if text in vocab:
            output.append(vocab[text])
            continue
        if text in rev_left:
            # Push right first so left is processed first.
            stack.append(rev_right[text])
            stack.append(rev_left[text])
            continue
        var tb = List[UInt8]()
        for b in text.as_bytes():
            tb.append(b)
        for b in tb:
            output.append(_byte_to_token(vocab, Int(b)))
    return output^

===== END FILE: mojo-engine/src/tokenizer/spm.mojo =====

===== FILE: mojo-engine/src/tokenizer/tokenizer.mojo =====
# tokenizer.mojo - the tokenizer itself: construction from
# TokenizerData, byte-level BPE encoding, SentencePiece encoding,
# and byte-faithful decoding.
#
# Mirror of crates/tokenizer/src/tokenizer.rs + data.rs +
# error.rs. The semantics contract, from the Rust crate docs:
#
# - Input is already-parsed GGUF metadata as plain values
#   (TokenizerData): tokenizer.ggml.model, .tokens, .token_type,
#   .merges, .scores, and the bos/eos/unknown/padding ids. This
#   module does not parse GGUF itself; gguf_vocab.mojo is the
#   temporary seam that produces TokenizerData from a file.
# - Family selection by model string: absent or "gpt2" is
#   byte-level BPE; "llama" is SentencePiece BPE; anything else
#   is refused by name (tokenizer_unsupported_model).
# - Byte-level: text is split by pretokenize (the GPT-4o /
#   llama4 scanner), each piece byte-mapped and merged by rank
#   (lowest rank first, every occurrence of the best pair per
#   pass). Special (control / user-defined) tokens in the text
#   match literally, longest first, and emit as their own ids.
# - SentencePiece: see spm.mojo. The merges array does not drive
#   that family and is not even parsed for it.
# - Decode always runs the family's inverse map (Ġ becomes a
#   real space; ▁ becomes a space), <0xXX> byte tokens fold back
#   into the byte stream, and specials render literally, so a
#   multibyte character split across tokens reassembles.
# - Ids use Int with -1 for "absent" where Rust uses
#   Option<u32> (roles, token_id lookups). Every refusal is a
#   raised Error whose message starts with a tokenizer_* name,
#   mirroring the Rust Error variants one for one:
#   tokenizer_empty_vocab, tokenizer_duplicate_token,
#   tokenizer_token_type_length_mismatch, tokenizer_invalid_merge,
#   tokenizer_special_token_out_of_range,
#   tokenizer_unsupported_model, tokenizer_scores_length_mismatch,
#   tokenizer_unencodable_symbol, tokenizer_invalid_token_id,
#   tokenizer_malformed_byte_token, tokenizer_invalid_utf8,
#   tokenizer_missing_byte_token (the last three live in
#   byte_level.mojo / spm.mojo).

from std.collections import Dict

from diag import log_debug
from tokenizer.byte_level import (
    byte_to_codepoint,
    byte_token_name,
    bytes_of_codepoints,
    bytes_of_string,
    codepoint_to_byte,
    codepoints_of,
    decode_utf8_strict,
    parse_byte_token,
    string_from_bytes_lossy,
    string_from_bytes_strict,
    string_from_codepoints,
    append_utf8,
)
from tokenizer.pretokenize import pretokenize
from tokenizer.spm import encode_segment as spm_encode_segment
from tokenizer.spm import unescape_whitespace

# Token types, mirroring GGUF tokenizer.ggml.token_type
# (llama.cpp's llama_token_type) as mapped by the Rust
# TokenType::from_gguf.
comptime TT_UNDEFINED = 0
comptime TT_NORMAL = 1
comptime TT_UNKNOWN = 2
comptime TT_CONTROL = 3
comptime TT_USER_DEFINED = 4
comptime TT_UNUSED = 5
comptime TT_BYTE = 6

# Tokenizer families.
comptime FAMILY_BYTE_LEVEL = 0
comptime FAMILY_SENTENCEPIECE = 1


def token_type_from_gguf(value: Int) -> Int:
    """Raw GGUF token-type integer -> TT_* constant.
    Unrecognized values map to TT_UNDEFINED."""
    if 1 <= value and value <= 6:
        return value
    return TT_UNDEFINED


def token_type_is_special(tt: Int) -> Bool:
    """Whether this token is matched literally against the
    input text during encoding (control / user-defined)."""
    return tt == TT_CONTROL or tt == TT_USER_DEFINED


struct TokenizerData(Copyable, Movable):
    """Everything a tokenizer needs, already parsed: the
    GGUF tokenizer.ggml.* metadata as plain values, so this
    module stays decoupled from the GGUF parser (the Rust
    crate's TokenizerData, with Option fields as has_* flags /
    -1 sentinels, plus the file's pre-tokenizer name, which the
    Rust tokdata format carries beside the data)."""

    var model: String
    var has_model: Bool
    var pre: String
    var has_pre: Bool
    var tokens: List[String]
    var token_types: List[Int]
    var merges: List[String]
    var scores: List[Float64]
    var has_scores: Bool
    var bos_token_id: Int
    var eos_token_id: Int
    var unknown_token_id: Int
    var padding_token_id: Int

    def __init__(out self):
        self.model = String()
        self.has_model = False
        self.pre = String()
        self.has_pre = False
        self.tokens = List[String]()
        self.token_types = List[Int]()
        self.merges = List[String]()
        self.scores = List[Float64]()
        self.has_scores = False
        self.bos_token_id = -1
        self.eos_token_id = -1
        self.unknown_token_id = -1
        self.padding_token_id = -1


def _string_from_bytes(
    bytes: List[UInt8], start: Int, end: Int
) raises -> String:
    var slice = List[UInt8]()
    for i in range(start, end):
        slice.append(bytes[i])
    var cps = decode_utf8_strict(slice)
    return string_from_codepoints(cps, 0, len(cps))


def _check_role(role: String, id: Int, vocab_size: Int) raises:
    if id >= 0 and id >= vocab_size:
        raise Error(
            "tokenizer_special_token_out_of_range: "
            + role
            + " token id "
            + String(id)
            + " is outside the vocabulary of size "
            + String(vocab_size)
        )


struct Tokenizer(Movable):
    """A tokenizer over a fixed vocabulary, in one of the two
    families the file's tokenizer.ggml.model selects. Build via
    Tokenizer.build(); construction validates the data and
    refuses loudly on anything malformed."""

    var family: Int
    var tokens: List[String]
    var token_types: List[Int]
    var types_supplied: Bool
    var vocab: Dict[String, Int]
    var merge_ranks: Dict[String, Int]
    var merge_sep: String
    var scores: List[Float64]
    var specials_texts: List[String]
    var specials_ids: List[Int]
    var specials_cps: List[List[Int]]
    var bos: Int
    var eos: Int
    var unk: Int
    var pad: Int

    def __init__(
        out self,
        family: Int,
        var tokens: List[String],
        var token_types: List[Int],
        types_supplied: Bool,
        var vocab: Dict[String, Int],
        var merge_ranks: Dict[String, Int],
        var merge_sep: String,
        var scores: List[Float64],
        var specials_texts: List[String],
        var specials_ids: List[Int],
        var specials_cps: List[List[Int]],
        bos: Int,
        eos: Int,
        unk: Int,
        pad: Int,
    ):
        self.family = family
        self.tokens = tokens^
        self.token_types = token_types^
        self.types_supplied = types_supplied
        self.vocab = vocab^
        self.merge_ranks = merge_ranks^
        self.merge_sep = merge_sep^
        self.scores = scores^
        self.specials_texts = specials_texts^
        self.specials_ids = specials_ids^
        self.specials_cps = specials_cps^
        self.bos = bos
        self.eos = eos
        self.unk = unk
        self.pad = pad

    @staticmethod
    def build(var data: TokenizerData) raises -> Tokenizer:
        """Builds a tokenizer from parsed GGUF tokenizer
        metadata, mirroring Tokenizer::new on the Rust side,
        validation order included."""
        # Family selection.
        var family: Int
        if not data.has_model or data.model == "gpt2":
            family = FAMILY_BYTE_LEVEL
        elif data.model == "llama":
            family = FAMILY_SENTENCEPIECE
        else:
            _ = log_debug(
                "tokenizer",
                "refusing unsupported tokenizer model " + data.model,
            )
            raise Error(
                "tokenizer_unsupported_model: unsupported"
                " tokenizer.ggml.model family: "
                + data.model
            )
        if len(data.tokens) == 0:
            _ = log_debug("tokenizer", "refusing empty vocabulary")
            raise Error("tokenizer_empty_vocab: tokenizer vocabulary is empty")
        # Scores.
        var scores = List[Float64]()
        if data.has_scores:
            if len(data.scores) != len(data.tokens):
                raise Error(
                    "tokenizer_scores_length_mismatch: scores length "
                    + String(len(data.scores))
                    + " does not match tokens length "
                    + String(len(data.tokens))
                )
            for s in data.scores:
                scores.append(s)
        else:
            # llama.cpp's vocab load: no scores array means
            # every token scores 0.0.
            for _ in range(len(data.tokens)):
                scores.append(Float64(0.0))
        # Token types.
        if len(data.token_types) != 0 and len(data.token_types) != len(
            data.tokens
        ):
            raise Error(
                "tokenizer_token_type_length_mismatch: token_types length "
                + String(len(data.token_types))
                + " does not match tokens length "
                + String(len(data.tokens))
            )
        var types_supplied = len(data.token_types) != 0
        var token_types = List[Int]()
        if types_supplied:
            for raw in data.token_types:
                token_types.append(token_type_from_gguf(raw))
        else:
            for _ in range(len(data.tokens)):
                token_types.append(TT_UNDEFINED)
        # Vocabulary map, refusing duplicates.
        var vocab = Dict[String, Int]()
        for idx in range(len(data.tokens)):
            var token = data.tokens[idx]
            if token in vocab:
                raise Error(
                    "tokenizer_duplicate_token: duplicate token in vocabulary: "
                    + token
                )
            vocab[token] = idx
        # Merge ranks drive only the byte-level family; the
        # SentencePiece family does not parse the array at all.
        var sep = string_from_codepoints(List[Int]([1]), 0, 1)
        var merge_ranks = Dict[String, Int]()
        if family == FAMILY_BYTE_LEVEL:
            for index in range(len(data.merges)):
                var merge = data.merges[index]
                var mb = bytes_of_string(merge)
                var split = -1
                for bi in range(len(mb)):
                    if Int(mb[bi]) == 0x20:
                        split = bi
                        break
                var valid = split > 0 and split < len(mb) - 1
                var right_has_space = False
                if valid:
                    for bi in range(split + 1, len(mb)):
                        if Int(mb[bi]) == 0x20:
                            right_has_space = True
                            break
                    valid = not right_has_space
                if not valid:
                    raise Error(
                        "tokenizer_invalid_merge: merge entry "
                        + String(index)
                        + " is not two token strings separated by one space: "
                        + merge
                    )
                var left = _string_from_bytes(mb, 0, split)
                var right = _string_from_bytes(mb, split + 1, len(mb))
                merge_ranks[left + sep + right] = index
        # Special token roles.
        _check_role("bos", data.bos_token_id, len(data.tokens))
        _check_role("eos", data.eos_token_id, len(data.tokens))
        _check_role("unk", data.unknown_token_id, len(data.tokens))
        _check_role("padding", data.padding_token_id, len(data.tokens))
        # Specials, longest text first (stable, as Rust's
        # sort_by_key over byte length).
        var specials_texts = List[String]()
        var specials_ids = List[Int]()
        var specials_cps = List[List[Int]]()
        for idx in range(len(data.tokens)):
            var text = data.tokens[idx]
            if (
                token_type_is_special(token_types[idx])
                and text.byte_length() > 0
            ):
                var pos = len(specials_texts)
                for si in range(len(specials_texts)):
                    if specials_texts[si].byte_length() < text.byte_length():
                        pos = si
                        break
                specials_texts.insert(pos, text)
                specials_ids.insert(pos, idx)
                specials_cps.insert(pos, codepoints_of(text))
        _ = log_debug(
            "tokenizer",
            "loaded family="
            + (
                String("llama") if family
                == FAMILY_SENTENCEPIECE else String("gpt2")
            )
            + " vocab="
            + String(len(data.tokens))
            + " merges="
            + String(len(data.merges))
            + " specials="
            + String(len(specials_texts)),
        )
        var bos_id = data.bos_token_id
        var eos_id = data.eos_token_id
        var unk_id = data.unknown_token_id
        var pad_id = data.padding_token_id
        return Tokenizer(
            family,
            data.tokens.copy(),
            token_types^,
            types_supplied,
            vocab^,
            merge_ranks^,
            sep^,
            scores^,
            specials_texts^,
            specials_ids^,
            specials_cps^,
            bos_id,
            eos_id,
            unk_id,
            pad_id,
        )

    def family_kind(self) -> Int:
        """FAMILY_BYTE_LEVEL or FAMILY_SENTENCEPIECE."""
        return self.family

    def family_name(self) -> String:
        """The GGUF model string for this family."""
        return "llama" if self.family == FAMILY_SENTENCEPIECE else "gpt2"

    def vocab_size(self) -> Int:
        return len(self.tokens)

    def has_token(self, id: Int) -> Bool:
        return 0 <= id and id < len(self.tokens)

    def token_text(self, id: Int) -> String:
        """The text of a token, verbatim as stored
        (byte-mapped). Empty string for an out-of-range id;
        check has_token() when that distinction matters."""
        if not self.has_token(id):
            return String()
        return self.tokens[id]

    def token_id(self, text: String) -> Int:
        """The id of a token by its stored text, or -1."""
        return self.vocab.get(text, -1)

    def bos_id(self) -> Int:
        return self.bos

    def eos_id(self) -> Int:
        return self.eos

    def unk_id(self) -> Int:
        return self.unk

    def pad_id(self) -> Int:
        return self.pad

    # --- encode ---

    def encode(self, text: String) raises -> List[Int]:
        """Encodes text to token ids. Special tokens present in
        the text are matched literally, longest first; the text
        between them goes through pre-tokenization and BPE (or
        the SentencePiece path). No BOS/EOS is added: that is
        the caller's job, as on the Rust side."""
        var cps = codepoints_of(text)
        var out = List[Int]()
        if len(self.specials_texts) == 0:
            self._encode_plain(cps, 0, len(cps), out)
            return out^
        var seg_start = 0
        while seg_start < len(cps):
            var hit_pos = -1
            var hit_id = -1
            var hit_len = 0
            var p = seg_start
            while p < len(cps) and hit_pos < 0:
                for si in range(len(self.specials_cps)):
                    var sc_len = len(self.specials_cps[si])
                    if p + sc_len <= len(cps):
                        var matches = True
                        for k in range(sc_len):
                            if cps[p + k] != self.specials_cps[si][k]:
                                matches = False
                                break
                        if matches:
                            hit_pos = p
                            hit_id = self.specials_ids[si]
                            hit_len = sc_len
                            break
                if hit_pos < 0:
                    p += 1
            if hit_pos < 0:
                self._encode_plain(cps, seg_start, len(cps), out)
                seg_start = len(cps)
            else:
                if hit_pos > seg_start:
                    self._encode_plain(cps, seg_start, hit_pos, out)
                out.append(hit_id)
                seg_start = hit_pos + hit_len
        return out^

    def _encode_plain(
        self, cps: List[Int], start: Int, end: Int, mut out: List[Int]
    ) raises:
        """Encodes a segment known to contain no special
        tokens, by family."""
        if end <= start:
            return
        var segment = List[Int]()
        for i in range(start, end):
            segment.append(cps[i])
        if self.family == FAMILY_SENTENCEPIECE:
            # The space prefix is unconditional here, as on the
            # Rust side: a plain segment only ever occurs at the
            # start or right after a special token, and llama.cpp
            # prefixes in both cases.
            var ids = spm_encode_segment(self.vocab, self.scores, segment, True)
            for id in ids:
                out.append(id)
            return
        var pieces = pretokenize(segment)
        for piece in pieces:
            self._encode_piece(piece, out)

    def _encode_piece(self, piece: List[Int], mut out: List[Int]) raises:
        """Byte-maps one pre-tokenizer piece and runs BPE over
        it (lowest merge rank first; every occurrence of the
        best pair merges in each pass)."""
        var piece_bytes = bytes_of_codepoints(piece)
        var symbols = List[String]()
        for b in piece_bytes:
            var mapped = List[Int]([byte_to_codepoint(Int(b))])
            symbols.append(string_from_codepoints(mapped, 0, 1))
        while len(symbols) > 1:
            var best_rank = -1
            var best_at = -1
            for i in range(len(symbols) - 1):
                var key = symbols[i] + self.merge_sep + symbols[i + 1]
                if key in self.merge_ranks:
                    var rank = self.merge_ranks[key]
                    if best_rank < 0 or rank < best_rank:
                        best_rank = rank
                        best_at = i
            if best_at < 0:
                break
            var left = symbols[best_at]
            var right = symbols[best_at + 1]
            var merged = List[String]()
            var i = 0
            while i < len(symbols):
                if (
                    i + 1 < len(symbols)
                    and symbols[i] == left
                    and symbols[i + 1] == right
                ):
                    merged.append(left + right)
                    i += 2
                else:
                    merged.append(symbols[i])
                    i += 1
            symbols = merged^
        for symbol in symbols:
            out.append(self._symbol_id(symbol))

    def _symbol_id(self, symbol: String) raises -> Int:
        """Resolves one BPE symbol to a token id: vocabulary
        first, then the <0xXX> byte-token fallback for single
        characters, then the unknown token, then a named
        refusal."""
        if symbol in self.vocab:
            return self.vocab[symbol]
        var cps = codepoints_of(symbol)
        if len(cps) == 1:
            var byte = codepoint_to_byte(cps[0])
            if byte >= 0:
                var name = byte_token_name(byte)
                if name in self.vocab:
                    _ = log_debug(
                        "tokenizer", "byte fallback for symbol " + symbol
                    )
                    return self.vocab[name]
        if self.unk >= 0:
            _ = log_debug("tokenizer", "unk fallback for symbol " + symbol)
            return self.unk
        _ = log_debug("tokenizer", "refusing unencodable symbol " + symbol)
        raise Error(
            "tokenizer_unencodable_symbol: symbol has no token,"
            " byte fallback, or unk: "
            + symbol
        )

    # --- decode ---

    def decode_bytes(self, ids: List[Int]) raises -> List[UInt8]:
        """Decodes token ids into the raw byte stream they
        represent. A multibyte UTF-8 character split across
        several tokens reassembles in this stream."""
        var out = List[UInt8]()
        for id in ids:
            self._append_token_bytes(id, out)
        return out^

    def _append_token_bytes(self, id: Int, mut out: List[UInt8]) raises:
        if not self.has_token(id):
            raise Error(
                "tokenizer_invalid_token_id: token id "
                + String(id)
                + " is outside the vocabulary"
            )
        var text = self.tokens[id]
        var ty = self.token_types[id]
        if self.family == FAMILY_SENTENCEPIECE:
            self._append_token_bytes_spm(text, ty, out)
            return
        if ty == TT_BYTE:
            var byte = parse_byte_token(text)
            if byte < 0:
                raise Error(
                    "tokenizer_malformed_byte_token: byte token is"
                    " not in <0xXX> form: "
                    + text
                )
            out.append(UInt8(byte))
            return
        if ty == TT_CONTROL or ty == TT_USER_DEFINED:
            for b in text.as_bytes():
                out.append(b)
            return
        # With no type array, a <0xXX>-shaped token can only be
        # a byte token.
        if not self.types_supplied:
            var byte = parse_byte_token(text)
            if byte >= 0:
                out.append(UInt8(byte))
                return
        for cp in codepoints_of(text):
            var byte = codepoint_to_byte(cp)
            if byte >= 0:
                out.append(UInt8(byte))
            else:
                append_utf8(cp, out)

    def _append_token_bytes_spm(
        self, text: String, ty: Int, mut out: List[UInt8]
    ) raises:
        """SentencePiece decode, the LLAMA_VOCAB_TYPE_SPM case
        of llama.cpp's token_to_piece (see the Rust side)."""
        if ty == TT_BYTE:
            var byte = parse_byte_token(text)
            if byte < 0:
                raise Error(
                    "tokenizer_malformed_byte_token: byte token is"
                    " not in <0xXX> form: "
                    + text
                )
            out.append(UInt8(byte))
            return
        if ty == TT_CONTROL or ty == TT_USER_DEFINED or ty == TT_UNKNOWN:
            for b in text.as_bytes():
                out.append(b)
            return
        if ty == TT_NORMAL:
            var un = unescape_whitespace(text)
            for b in un.as_bytes():
                out.append(b)
            return
        if ty == TT_UNUSED:
            return
        # TT_UNDEFINED.
        if not self.types_supplied:
            var byte = parse_byte_token(text)
            if byte >= 0:
                out.append(UInt8(byte))
                return
            var un = unescape_whitespace(text)
            for b in un.as_bytes():
                out.append(b)

    def decode(self, ids: List[Int]) raises -> String:
        """Decodes token ids to a string, requiring the full
        byte stream to be valid UTF-8."""
        var bytes = self.decode_bytes(ids)
        return string_from_bytes_strict(bytes)

    def decode_lossy(self, ids: List[Int]) raises -> String:
        """Decodes token ids to a string, replacing invalid
        UTF-8 sequences with the replacement character."""
        var bytes = self.decode_bytes(ids)
        return string_from_bytes_lossy(bytes)

===== END FILE: mojo-engine/src/tokenizer/tokenizer.mojo =====

# config_probe.mojo - process-level config check for the runner.
