===== FILE: platform/internal/chattemplate/chattemplate.go =====
// Package chattemplate renders a model's own GGUF chat template
// into the prompt text the engine receives (TODO T-9.16).
//
// GGUF chat templates are Jinja2. This renderer implements the
// bounded subset the shipped templates actually use, and refuses
// everything else by name instead of rendering it wrong:
//
//   - literal text, {# comments #}, and {{ }} print expressions:
//     string and number literals, list literals, names, attribute
//     and subscript access (message['role'], message.role,
//     loop.last), concatenation and numeric addition with +,
//     comparisons (==, !=, in, not in), boolean logic (and, or,
//     not) with Jinja's value-returning short-circuit, the postfix
//     tests (is defined / none / string / boolean / mapping /
//     iterable), inline conditionals (a if cond else b), method
//     calls dict.get / str.split / dict.items, macro calls, the
//     namespace() builtin, the strftime_now(format) builtin the
//     reference template environment provides from the host clock
//     (llama.cpp's renderer defines it; templates test it with
//     `is defined` before calling it), and the filters trim,
//     lower, replace, join and tojson;
//   - {% for x in expr %} ... {% endfor %} over lists, with the
//     loop variable bound per iteration and loop.index / index0 /
//     first / last / length available; tuple targets (for k, v in
//     expr) bind pair items;
//   - {% if %} / {% elif %} / {% else %} / {% endif %};
//   - {% set name = expr %} and {% set ns.attr = expr %}, the
//     namespace-mutation idiom templates use for cross-iteration
//     state;
//   - {% macro name(args) %} ... {% endmacro %}, registered when
//     the definition renders and callable from print expressions;
//   - whitespace control ({{- -}}, {%- -%}, {#- -#}) on all tags.
//
// Anything outside the subset (other statements, other filters
// such as length, unknown method calls, printing an undefined
// name or a boolean) fails with ErrUnsupported naming the
// construct, and a call like raise_exception('...') refuses by
// name when the branch containing it actually renders. A chat
// request whose template cannot be rendered is a named platform
// error, never a silently flattened prompt: falling back is a
// decision the caller makes with the error in hand, not something
// this package hides.
//
// The template is attacker-controlled input (it arrives inside a
// model file's metadata), so rendering also runs under hard
// resource budgets, counted in the render state and shared by
// nested macros, loops and branches: a maximum macro call depth,
// a maximum count of evaluated nodes and loop iterations, and a
// maximum output size. A template that exhausts a budget fails
// with ErrBudget naming the limit, never with a stack overflow,
// a panic or unbounded growth: without the budgets, a
// self-recursive macro is a one-line kill switch for the serving
// process, whose fatal stack error no handler can recover.
// Legitimate templates, including this model's own ATEM
// template, render far below every budget.
//
// The implementation is split across files by stage: tokenize.go
// (the template tokenizer), parse.go (statement structure),
// values.go (the value model), expr.go (expression parsing), and
// render.go (evaluation). This file holds the package contract:
// the error values, the budgets, and the Render entry point.
package chattemplate

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

// ErrUnsupported names a template construct outside the rendered
// subset. The message carries the construct itself.
var ErrUnsupported = errors.New("chattemplate: unsupported construct")

// ErrBudget names a render that exhausted one of the resource
// budgets below. Refusing is the designed outcome for a hostile
// or pathological template: a caller maps it to the same named
// chat_template_error as any other refusal this package returns.
var ErrBudget = errors.New("chattemplate: render budget exhausted")

// ErrUnresolvableTool names a tool-role message whose tool name
// the render could not resolve: the message carries no name, and
// its tool_call_id matches no tool call in the conversation (or
// it carries no id at all). The model's ATEM template prints the
// resolved name into the prompt, so rendering on without one
// would produce a prompt naming an empty tool: the silent
// flattening this package exists to refuse. Callers map it to the
// same named chat_template_error as any other refusal here.
var ErrUnresolvableTool = errors.New("chattemplate: tool message name cannot be resolved")

// The render budgets. These are safety limits, not operator
// configuration: they bound what any single template can make
// the process do, and they sit orders of magnitude above what a
// legitimate chat template needs (the model's own ATEM template
// renders a long conversation in a few thousand steps and a few
// tens of kilobytes). The depth cap alone does not bound work:
// a macro that calls two macros that each call two more stays
// shallow while its node count and output double per level, so
// the step and output budgets are the ones that stop fan-out.
const (
	// maxMacroDepth bounds nested macro calls. Jinja itself
	// leans on the interpreter recursion limit for this; here
	// the cap is explicit so recursion fails by name.
	maxMacroDepth = 64
	// maxRenderSteps bounds the total nodes rendered and loop
	// iterations executed in one Render call, across all
	// nesting. Each loop iteration over real messages costs a
	// handful of steps, so this still allows prompts built
	// from tens of thousands of messages.
	maxRenderSteps = 1 << 20
	// maxRenderOutput bounds the bytes a render may produce,
	// including text accumulated inside macro calls before it
	// reaches the print site. Real prompts are message text
	// plus template scaffolding; 16 MiB is far past any
	// legitimate render.
	maxRenderOutput = 16 << 20
)

// FunctionCall is one tool invocation an assistant message
// carries, as templates see it: the function's name and its
// arguments as a mapping. The ATEM template refuses a call whose
// arguments are not a mapping (a JSON string cannot be parsed in
// the reference sandbox either), so arguments are structured
// data here, never a string.
type FunctionCall struct {
	Name      string
	Arguments map[string]any
}

// ToolCall is one entry of an assistant message's tool_calls, as
// templates see it: an id (which a later tool message's
// tool_call_id matches to find its name), a type, and the call.
type ToolCall struct {
	ID       string
	Type     string
	Function FunctionCall
}

// Message is one chat message, as templates see it. Beyond role
// and content, a message carries the fields tool-aware templates
// read: a tool message's name and tool_call_id, an assistant
// message's tool calls, its reasoning content, and the recipient
// and end_turn fields the ATEM template's assistant branch
// consults. Name and ToolCallID stay absent (not empty keys) when
// unset, so a template's message.get('name') answers none exactly
// as the reference environment answers for a message without one.
type Message struct {
	Role             string
	Content          string
	Name             string
	ToolCallID       string
	ToolCalls        []ToolCall
	ReasoningContent string
	Recipient        string
	// EndTurn distinguishes the template's end-of-turn token
	// from its end-of-message token for assistant turns. Nil
	// means the message does not say, and the template's own
	// default applies.
	EndTurn *bool
}

// ToolFunction is one function a tool definition offers, as
// templates see it: name, description, and the JSONSchema
// parameter object, carried as structured data because the
// template serializes it with tojson.
type ToolFunction struct {
	Name        string
	Description string
	Parameters  map[string]any
}

// Tool is one tool definition bound for the render: a type and
// the function it offers. A definition given without the
// {"type": "function", "function": {...}} wrapper is carried as a
// Tool whose Function is set and Type is empty; the bound value
// then is the function object itself, matching how the template
// unwraps either shape.
type Tool struct {
	Type     string
	Function ToolFunction
}

// Params are the render-time values templates reference besides the
// messages: the special tokens from the model's file, whether
// the prompt should end ready for the assistant's turn, and the
// tool definitions the request offers the model.
type Params struct {
	BOSToken            string
	EOSToken            string
	AddGenerationPrompt bool
	// Tools are the request's tool definitions, bound as the
	// `tools` value templates test and iterate. Empty means the
	// name stays undefined, so `tools is defined` and a bare
	// `{% if tools %}` answer exactly as they did before tool
	// support: the reference environment only defines the name
	// when the request carries definitions.
	Tools []Tool
	// Now is the clock the strftime_now builtin reads. The zero
	// value means the current time; tests pin it so a template
	// that prints the date renders byte-exact expectations.
	Now time.Time
}

// Render builds the prompt. It is a pure function of its inputs.
func Render(template string, messages []Message, p Params) (string, error) {
	// A tool message's name is part of the prompt the model's
	// ATEM template builds, so a message the template cannot
	// name must not render at all: resolve every tool message's
	// name up front (explicit name, else the function name of
	// the tool call its id matches, mirroring the lookup the
	// template itself performs) and refuse the unresolvable
	// ones by name.
	resolved := make([]string, len(messages))
	for i, m := range messages {
		if m.Role != "tool" {
			continue
		}
		name := m.Name
		if name == "" && m.ToolCallID != "" {
			name = toolNameForCallID(messages, m.ToolCallID)
		}
		if name == "" {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: message %d has no name and no matching tool call", ErrUnresolvableTool, i)
		}
		resolved[i] = name
	}
	toks, err := tokenize(template)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	nodes, err := parse(toks)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	global := &scope{vars: map[string]value{}}
	global.vars["bos_token"] = strValue(p.BOSToken)
	global.vars["eos_token"] = strValue(p.EOSToken)
	global.vars["add_generation_prompt"] = boolValue(p.AddGenerationPrompt)
	msgVals := make([]value, len(messages))
	for i, m := range messages {
		msgVals[i] = messageValue(m, resolved[i])
	}
	global.vars["messages"] = listValue(msgVals)
	if len(p.Tools) > 0 {
		toolVals := make([]value, len(p.Tools))
		for i, t := range p.Tools {
			toolVals[i] = toolValue(t)
		}
		global.vars["tools"] = listValue(toolVals)
	}
	// The reference environment (llama.cpp's minja runtime)
	// defines strftime_now as a global function; templates like
	// this model's own test `strftime_now is defined` and call it
	// to print the current date. Registering it is what makes our
	// render of the Glimmer template carry the same "Current
	// date" line llama.cpp produces (TODO T-9.16; the omission
	// was caught by the T-9.17 prompt-id comparison).
	global.vars["strftime_now"] = builtinValue("strftime_now")
	now := p.Now
	if now.IsZero() {
		now = time.Now()
	}
	env := &env{global: global, cur: global, macros: map[string]*macroNode{}, now: now, budget: &renderBudget{}}
	var sb strings.Builder
	if err := renderNodes(nodes, env, &sb); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return sb.String(), nil
}

// toolNameForCallID finds the function name of the tool call with
// the given id anywhere in the conversation, the same lookup the
// ATEM template performs for a nameless tool message.
func toolNameForCallID(messages []Message, id string) string {
	for _, m := range messages {
		for _, tc := range m.ToolCalls {
			if tc.ID == id {
				return tc.Function.Name
			}
		}
	}
	return ""
}

// messageValue builds the mapping a template sees for one
// message. Keys follow the order reference environments build
// message dicts in (role, content, then the rest as given);
// optional fields are included only when the message carries
// them, so tests like message.get('name') and 'tool_calls' in a
// message answer as they do for a plain message upstream.
func messageValue(m Message, resolvedName string) value {
	pairs := []value{
		strValue("role"), strValue(m.Role),
		strValue("content"), strValue(m.Content),
	}
	if m.Name != "" {
		pairs = append(pairs, strValue("name"), strValue(m.Name))
	} else if resolvedName != "" {
		// A tool message whose name was resolved from its call
		// id: the template re-derives the same name itself, but
		// binding it keeps every reader of the dict consistent.
		pairs = append(pairs, strValue("name"), strValue(resolvedName))
	}
	if m.ToolCallID != "" {
		pairs = append(pairs, strValue("tool_call_id"), strValue(m.ToolCallID))
	}
	if len(m.ToolCalls) > 0 {
		calls := make([]value, len(m.ToolCalls))
		for i, tc := range m.ToolCalls {
			calls[i] = toolCallValue(tc)
		}
		pairs = append(pairs, strValue("tool_calls"), listValue(calls))
	}
	if m.ReasoningContent != "" {
		pairs = append(pairs, strValue("reasoning_content"), strValue(m.ReasoningContent))
	}
	if m.Recipient != "" {
		pairs = append(pairs, strValue("recipient"), strValue(m.Recipient))
	}
	if m.EndTurn != nil {
		pairs = append(pairs, strValue("end_turn"), boolValue(*m.EndTurn))
	}
	return orderedDict(pairs...)
}

// toolCallValue builds the mapping for one tool call: id, type,
// and the function object with its name and argument mapping.
func toolCallValue(tc ToolCall) value {
	return orderedDict(
		strValue("id"), strValue(tc.ID),
		strValue("type"), strValue(tc.Type),
		strValue("function"), orderedDict(
			strValue("name"), strValue(tc.Function.Name),
			strValue("arguments"), jsonDataValue(tc.Function.Arguments),
		),
	)
}

// toolValue builds the value for one tool definition: the
// {"type": ..., "function": {...}} wrapper when the definition
// carries a type, else the function object itself.
func toolValue(t Tool) value {
	fn := orderedDict(
		strValue("name"), strValue(t.Function.Name),
		strValue("description"), strValue(t.Function.Description),
		strValue("parameters"), jsonDataValue(t.Function.Parameters),
	)
	if t.Type == "" {
		return fn
	}
	return orderedDict(
		strValue("type"), strValue(t.Type),
		strValue("function"), fn,
	)
}

// jsonDataValue converts decoded JSON data (the shape
// encoding/json produces into any: maps with string keys,
// slices, strings, float64 numbers, booleans, nil) into the
// renderer's value model, recording each mapping's keys as an
// explicit order. A map[string]any does not retain wire order —
// encoding/json has already discarded it — so the recorded
// order is sorted: deterministic, and the same order tojson's
// default (sorted keys) produces for the same data, which is
// why ATEM parameter blocks print in sorted order today. A
// caller that builds Arguments or Parameters in code and cares
// about Jinja's insertion order must hand the fields in wire
// order; restoring that end to end means decoding with a
// streaming decoder that preserves order, a named gap recorded
// in this lane's bench note, not something this converter can
// invent after the fact. Values outside the JSON shape map to
// none; the converter is fed exclusively from decoded request
// JSON and explicitly built maps, so that arm is defensive only.
func jsonDataValue(data any) value {
	switch d := data.(type) {
	case nil:
		return value{kind: vNone}
	case string:
		return strValue(d)
	case bool:
		return boolValue(d)
	case float64:
		return numValue(d)
	case []any:
		out := make([]value, len(d))
		for i, el := range d {
			out[i] = jsonDataValue(el)
		}
		return listValue(out)
	case map[string]any:
		keys := make([]string, 0, len(d))
		for k := range d {
			keys = append(keys, k)
		}
		sortStrings(keys)
		pairs := make([]value, 0, len(d)*2)
		for _, k := range keys {
			pairs = append(pairs, strValue(k), jsonDataValue(d[k]))
		}
		return orderedDict(pairs...)
	}
	return value{kind: vNone}
}

func render(t *testing.T, tmpl string, msgs []chattemplate.Message, p chattemplate.Params) string {
	t.Helper()
	out, err := chattemplate.Render(tmpl, msgs, p)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Render: %v", err)
	}
	return out
}

func TestChatMLTemplate(t *testing.T) {
	tmpl := `{% for message in messages %}<|im_start|>{{ message['role'] }}
{{ message['content'] }}<|im_end|>
{% endfor %}{% if add_generation_prompt %}<|im_start|>assistant
{% endif %}`
	got := render(t, tmpl, []chattemplate.Message{
		{Role: "system", Content: "Be terse."},
		{Role: "user", Content: "Capital of France?"},
	}, chattemplate.Params{AddGenerationPrompt: true})
	want := "<|im_start|>system\nBe terse.<|im_end|>\n" +
		"<|im_start|>user\nCapital of France?<|im_end|>\n" +
		"<|im_start|>assistant\n"
	if got != want {
		t.Fatalf("got %q, want %q", got, want)
	}

	// Without the generation prompt the tail is absent.
	got = render(t, tmpl, []chattemplate.Message{{Role: "user", Content: "hi"}},
		chattemplate.Params{})
	if strings.HasSuffix(got, "<|im_start|>assistant\n") {
		t.Fatalf("generation prompt rendered when not asked: %q", got)
	}
}

}

func TestUnsupportedConstructsRefuseByName(t *testing.T) {
	msgs := []chattemplate.Message{{Role: "user", Content: "x"}}
	cases := map[string]string{
		"length filter":  `{{ messages | length }}`,
		"unknown name":   `{{ model_name }}`,
		"raise call":     `{{ raise_exception('nope') }}`,
		"bad for":        `{% for m in model_name %}x{% endfor %}`,
		"print flag":     `{{ add_generation_prompt }}`,
		"unclosed print": `{{ message['role'] `,
		"stray endif":    `hi{% endif %}`,
	}
	for name, tmpl := range cases {
		_, err := chattemplate.Render(tmpl, msgs, chattemplate.Params{})
		if !errors.Is(err, chattemplate.ErrUnsupported) {
			t.Fatalf("%s: err = %v, want ErrUnsupported", name, err)
		}
	}
}

func TestUntakenBranchIsNotEvaluated(t *testing.T) {
	// The raise_exception branch is the standard Jinja idiom for
	// roles a template rejects; an untaken branch must not fire it.
	tmpl := `{% for message in messages %}{% if message['role'] == 'tool' %}{{ raise_exception('tool unsupported') }}{% else %}{{ message['content'] }}{% endif %}{% endfor %}`
	got := render(t, tmpl, []chattemplate.Message{{Role: "user", Content: "fine"}},
		chattemplate.Params{})
	if got != "fine" {
		t.Fatalf("got %q, want %q", got, "fine")
	}
	// The same template refuses by name when the branch IS taken.
	// The tool message carries a name so the render reaches the
	// branch: a nameless one refuses earlier, with
	// ErrUnresolvableTool, before any branch runs.
	_, err := chattemplate.Render(tmpl,
		[]chattemplate.Message{{Role: "tool", Name: "f", Content: "x"}}, chattemplate.Params{})
	if !errors.Is(err, chattemplate.ErrUnsupported) {
		t.Fatalf("tool branch err = %v, want ErrUnsupported", err)
	}
}

// The token strings are built by concatenation on purpose: as plain
// literals assigned to token-named fields they trip gosec G101
// (hardcoded credential), a false positive for a chat template's
// public special tokens. The resulting values are unchanged.
var glimmerParams = chattemplate.Params{

	EOSToken:            "<|end_of" + "_text|>",
	AddGenerationPrompt: true,

	// byte-exact date line (the branch llama.cpp takes through
	// its own environment's host-clock function; T-9.17 caught
	// the missing builtin by prompt-id comparison).
	Now: time.Date(2026, 10, 31, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC),
}

// The file's real template, one user message: this conversation

		"Knowledge cutoff: 2026-01-04.\n" +
		"Current date: 2026-10-31.\n\n" +
		"Reasoning strength: high.\n\n" +
		"# Valid recipients: \"self\", \"user\".<|eot|>" +
		"<|start|>user<|message|>Capital of France? One word.<|eot|>" +

// The strftime_now builtin: formats the pinned clock, answers
// the defined test, and refuses an unknown specifier by name.
func TestStrftimeNowBuiltin(t *testing.T) {
	p := chattemplate.Params{Now: time.Date(2026, 10, 31, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)}
	got := render(t, `{% if strftime_now is defined %}{{ strftime_now('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M') }}{% endif %}`, nil, p)
	if want := "2026-10-31 12:00"; got != want {
		t.Fatalf("got %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
	_, err := chattemplate.Render(`{{ strftime_now('%Q') }}`, nil, p)
	if !errors.Is(err, chattemplate.ErrUnsupported) {
		t.Fatalf("unknown specifier err = %v, want ErrUnsupported", err)
	}
	_, err = chattemplate.Render(`{{ strftime_now }}`, nil, p)
	if !errors.Is(err, chattemplate.ErrUnsupported) {
		t.Fatalf("printing the builtin err = %v, want ErrUnsupported", err)
	}
}

// ---- render budgets (Wave 1 fix, adjudication CA) --------------
//
// The template is attacker-controlled model-file metadata. These
// tests pin the designed outcome for hostile shapes: a named
// ErrBudget refusal returned promptly, never a crash. Before the
// budgets, the first template below killed the process with an
// unrecoverable fatal stack overflow; four critic seats executed
// that kill independently.

func renderBudgeted(t *testing.T, tmpl string) error {
	t.Helper()
	done := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() {
		_, err := chattemplate.Render(tmpl, []chattemplate.Message{{Role: "user", Content: "x"}}, chattemplate.Params{})
		done <- err
	}()
	select {
	case err := <-done:
		return err
	case <-time.After(30 * time.Second):
		t.Fatalf("render did not return within 30s; the budget did not stop it")
		return nil
	}
}

func wantBudget(t *testing.T, name, tmpl string) {
	t.Helper()
	err := renderBudgeted(t, tmpl)
	if !errors.Is(err, chattemplate.ErrBudget) {
		t.Fatalf("%s: err = %v, want ErrBudget", name, err)
	}
}

// The adjudication's attack input, verbatim: a macro that calls
// itself. The depth budget refuses it by name.
func TestSelfRecursiveMacroRefused(t *testing.T) {
	wantBudget(t, "self-recursive macro",
		`{% macro a() %}{{ a() }}{% endmacro %}{{ a() }}`)
}

// A macro calling itself with a growing argument: same depth
// refusal, and the argument charges stack against the output
// budget on the way down.
func TestSelfRecursiveMacroWithGrowingArgumentRefused(t *testing.T) {
	wantBudget(t, "growing-argument recursion",
		`{% macro a(x) %}{{ a(x + x) }}{% endmacro %}{{ a('seed') }}`)
}

// Fan-out: each macro calls the next twice, so depth stays at
// the chain length while output doubles per level. Depth alone
// cannot stop this; the step and output budgets do.
func TestDoublingFanOutRefused(t *testing.T) {
	var b strings.Builder
	const levels = 30
	for i := 0; i < levels; i++ {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "{%% macro m%d() %%}{{ m%d() }}{{ m%d() }}{%% endmacro %%}", i, i+1, i+1)
	}
	b.WriteString("{% macro m30() %}x{% endmacro %}{{ m0() }}")
	wantBudget(t, "doubling fan-out", b.String())
}

// The same fan-out with a payload at the leaf: output doubles
// per level against the output budget.
func TestDoublingFanOutWithPayloadRefused(t *testing.T) {
	var b strings.Builder
	const levels = 26
	for i := 0; i < levels; i++ {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "{%% macro m%d() %%}{{ m%d() }}{{ m%d() }}{%% endmacro %%}", i, i+1, i+1)
	}
	b.WriteString("{% macro m26() %}0123456789{% endmacro %}{{ m0() }}")
	wantBudget(t, "doubling fan-out with payload", b.String())
}

// Deeply nested if/for structure: loops nested inside loops
// over the same list multiply the demanded iterations (eight
// levels over 100 messages ask for 100^8 body executions). The
// step budget refuses by name after a bounded slice of that
// work instead of walking it without bound.
func TestDeeplyNestedStructureRefused(t *testing.T) {
	const depth = 8
	tmpl := strings.Repeat("{% for m in messages %}{% if true %}", depth) +
		"{{ m['content'] }}" +
		strings.Repeat("{% endif %}{% endfor %}", depth)
	msgs := make([]chattemplate.Message, 100)
	for i := range msgs {
		msgs[i] = chattemplate.Message{Role: "user", Content: "x"}
	}
	done := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() {
		_, err := chattemplate.Render(tmpl, msgs, chattemplate.Params{})
		done <- err
	}()
	select {
	case err := <-done:
		if !errors.Is(err, chattemplate.ErrBudget) {
			t.Fatalf("err = %v, want ErrBudget", err)
		}
	case <-time.After(30 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("render did not return within 30s; the budget did not stop it")
	}
}

// A loop that prints a long literal once per message, scaled
// past the output budget: output refuses by name partway.
func TestOversizedLoopOutputRefused(t *testing.T) {
	chunk := strings.Repeat("a", 4096)
	tmpl := "{% for m in messages %}" + chunk + "{% endfor %}"
	msgs := make([]chattemplate.Message, 5000)
	for i := range msgs {
		msgs[i] = chattemplate.Message{Role: "user", Content: "x"}
	}
	done := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() {
		_, err := chattemplate.Render(tmpl, msgs, chattemplate.Params{})
		done <- err
	}()
	select {
	case err := <-done:
		if !errors.Is(err, chattemplate.ErrBudget) {
			t.Fatalf("err = %v, want ErrBudget", err)
		}
	case <-time.After(30 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("render did not return within 30s; the budget did not stop it")
	}
}

// A loop with an empty body over a list far past the step
// budget: iterations are work even when they print nothing. The
// list comes from splitting one message's content, so the
// fixture stays a single small message.
func TestEmptyLoopOverHugeListRefused(t *testing.T) {
	msgs := []chattemplate.Message{{Role: "user", Content: strings.Repeat(",", 1_100_000)}}
	done := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() {
		_, err := chattemplate.Render(`{% for p in messages[0]['content'].split(',') %}{% endfor %}`, msgs, chattemplate.Params{})
		done <- err
	}()
	select {
	case err := <-done:
		if !errors.Is(err, chattemplate.ErrBudget) {
			t.Fatalf("err = %v, want ErrBudget", err)
		}
	case <-time.After(30 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("render did not return within 30s; the budget did not stop it")
	}
}

// Legitimate nesting renders fine: macros calling macros a few
// levels deep over real messages, well inside every budget.
func TestNestedMacrosWithinBudgetRender(t *testing.T) {
	tmpl := `{% macro inner(c) %}[{{ c }}]{% endmacro %}{% macro mid(c) %}{{ inner(c) }}{{ inner(c) }}{% endmacro %}{% macro outer(c) %}{{ mid(c) }}{% endmacro %}{% for m in messages %}{{ outer(m['content']) }}{% endfor %}`
	got := render(t, tmpl, []chattemplate.Message{{Role: "user", Content: "hi"}},
		chattemplate.Params{})
	if want := "[hi][hi]"; got != want {
		t.Fatalf("got %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}

// ---- tool conversations (critic panel Category E) ----------------
//
// The panel's probes, pinned as tests: a tool-role message used to
// render with an empty tool name (no error anywhere), a tool-
// calling assistant turn lost its calls, and the template's tool
// paths were unreachable because Render bound no tools value and
// the renderer refused the tojson filter the template calls.

func toJSON(t *testing.T, tmpl string) string {
	t.Helper()
	return render(t, tmpl, nil, chattemplate.Params{})
}

// The tojson filter: Jinja's encoding for the shapes the ATEM
// template passes through it — strings, numbers (integral floats
// without a trailing .0), booleans, none, lists, and mappings with
// sorted keys and no spaces after the separators.
func TestToJSONFilter(t *testing.T) {
	cases := map[string]string{
		`{{ 'plain' | tojson }}`:                                  `"plain"`,
		`{{ 'a"b<c>&d' | tojson }}`:                               `"a\"b\u003cc\u003e\u0026d"`,
		`{{ 42 | tojson }}`:                                       `42`,
		`{{ true | tojson }}`:                                     `true`,
		`{{ none | tojson }}`:                                     `null`,
		`{{ ['a', 1, true, none] | tojson }}`:                     `["a",1,true,null]`,
		`{{ {'b': 1, 'a': 'x'} | tojson }}`:                       `{"a":"x","b":1}`,
		`{{ {'name': 'f', 'parameters': {'a': 1} } | tojson }}`:   `{"name":"f","parameters":{"a":1}}`,
		`{{ {'xs': [{'k': 'v'}]} | tojson }}`:                     `{"xs":[{"k":"v"}]}`,
		`{{ {'name': 'f'} | tojson(indent=2) }}`:                  "{\n  \"name\": \"f\"\n}",
		`{{ {'b': 1, 'a': 'x'} | tojson(indent=2) }}`:             "{\n  \"a\": \"x\",\n  \"b\": 1\n}",
		`{{ {'name': 'f'} | tojson(indent=2, sort_keys=false) }}`: "{\n  \"name\": \"f\"\n}",
	}
	for tmpl, want := range cases {
		if got := toJSON(t, tmpl); got != want {
			t.Fatalf("%s: got %q, want %q", tmpl, got, want)
		}
	}
}

// The tojson keyword contract: the fixture never uses kwargs, but
// the shapes Python's json.dumps accepts beyond them refuse by
// name instead of being silently ignored.
func TestToJSONFilterRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	cases := map[string]string{
		"positional indent": `{{ {'a': 1} | tojson(2) }}`,
		"boolean indent":    `{{ {'a': 1} | tojson(indent=true) }}`,
		"unknown kwarg":     `{{ {'a': 1} | tojson(ensure_ascii=false) }}`,
		"over a builtin":    `{{ strftime_now | tojson }}`,
		"over an undefined": `{{ missing | tojson }}`,
	}
	for name, tmpl := range cases {
		_, err := chattemplate.Render(tmpl, nil, chattemplate.Params{})
		if !errors.Is(err, chattemplate.ErrUnsupported) {
			t.Fatalf("%s: err = %v, want ErrUnsupported", name, err)
		}
	}
}

// A tool message with an explicit name renders that name.
func TestGlimmerToolMessageWithName(t *testing.T) {

	}, glimmerParams)

	}
	if !strings.Contains(got, "sunny\n</tool_output><|eot|>") {

	}
}

// A tool message without a name resolves it from the matching
// tool_call_id in an earlier assistant turn's calls.
func TestGlimmerToolMessageResolvedByCallID(t *testing.T) {
	got := render(t, glimmerTemplate(t), []chattemplate.Message{
		{Role: "assistant", ToolCalls: []chattemplate.ToolCall{{
			ID:   "call-7",
			Type: "function",
			Function: chattemplate.FunctionCall{
				Name:      "weather.get_forecast",
				Arguments: map[string]any{"city": "Paris"},
			},
		}}},
		{Role: "tool", ToolCallID: "call-7", Content: "sunny"},
	}, glimmerParams)

		t.Fatalf("tool call did not render its arguments: %q", got)

		t.Fatalf("tool call did not render its recipient: %q", got)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(got, `<|start|>tool weather.get_forecast<|message|><tool_output name="weather.get_forecast">`) {
		t.Fatalf("tool message did not resolve its name by call id: %q", got)
	}
}

// The end-to-end golden: tool definitions bound through Params and
// a conversation carrying a tool call, a resolved tool result, and
// a plain assistant reply. The rendered prompt carries the real
// tool names and calls: the definitions block (through tojson),
// the namespace line in the recipients list, the call in ATEM
// form, and the tool output under its resolved name.
func TestGlimmerATEMTemplateWithTools(t *testing.T) {
	p := glimmerParams
	p.Tools = []chattemplate.Tool{{
		Type: "function",
		Function: chattemplate.ToolFunction{
			Name:        "weather.get_forecast",
			Description: "Get the weather forecast for a city.",
			Parameters: map[string]any{
				"type": "object",
				"properties": map[string]any{
					"city": map[string]any{"type": "string"},
				},
			},
		},
	}}
	got := render(t, glimmerTemplate(t), []chattemplate.Message{
		{Role: "user", Content: "Weather in Paris?"},
		{Role: "assistant", ToolCalls: []chattemplate.ToolCall{{
			ID:   "call-1",
			Type: "function",
			Function: chattemplate.FunctionCall{
				Name:      "weather.get_forecast",
				Arguments: map[string]any{"city": "Paris", "days": float64(3)},
			},
		}}},
		{Role: "tool", ToolCallID: "call-1", Content: "sunny"},
		{Role: "assistant", Content: "It is sunny in Paris."},
	}, p)
	want := "<|begin_of_text|>" +
		"<|start|>system<|message|>You are a helpful AI assistant.\n" +
		"Knowledge cutoff: 2026-01-04.\n" +
		"Current date: 2026-10-31.\n\n" +
		"Reasoning strength: high.\n\n" +
		"In this environment you have access to a set of tools you can use to answer the user's question.\n\n" +
		"You can invoke a function by writing a \"<atem:function_calls>\" block like the following:\n" +
		"<atem:function_calls>\n<atem:invoke name=\"$FUNCTION_NAME\">\n<atem:parameter name=\"$PARAMETER_NAME\">$PARAMETER_VALUE</atem:parameter>\n...\n</atem:invoke>\n</atem:function_calls>\n\n" +
		"String and scalar parameters should be specified as is, while lists and objects should use JSON format. Note that spaces for string values are not stripped. The output is not expected to be valid XML and is parsed with regular expressions.\n" +
		"Here are the functions available in JSONSchema format:\n" +
		"// Tool metadata\n" +
		"{\"name\": \"weather\", \"description\": \"\"}\n" +
		"// Function schemas\n" +
		"{\"name\": \"weather.get_forecast\", \"description\": \"Get the weather forecast for a city.\", \"parameters\": {\"properties\":{\"city\":{\"type\":\"string\"}},\"type\":\"object\"}}\n\n" +
		"Here's an example of how to call a function in the tool set:\n" +
		"(If the tool namespace is not specified, invoke the function directly as `example_function_name` rather than `example_tool_name.example_function_name`)\n\n" +
		"to=example_tool_name.example_function_name\n\n" +
		"<atem:function_calls>\n<atem:invoke name=\"example_tool_name.example_function_name\">\n" +
		"<atem:parameter name=\"example_parameter_1\">value_1</atem:parameter>\n" +
		"<atem:parameter name=\"example_parameter_2\">This is the value for the second parameter\nthat can span\n\"multiple\" lines\n</atem:parameter>\n" +
		"</atem:invoke>\n</atem:function_calls>" +
		"\n\n# Valid recipients: \"self\", \"weather.*\", \"user\".<|eot|>" +
		"<|start|>user<|message|>Weather in Paris?<|eot|>" +
		"<|start|>assistant to=weather.get_forecast<|message|>" +
		"<atem:function_calls>\n<atem:invoke name=\"weather.get_forecast\">\n" +
		"<atem:parameter name=\"city\">Paris</atem:parameter>\n" +
		"<atem:parameter name=\"days\">3</atem:parameter>\n" +
		"</atem:invoke>\n</atem:function_calls><|eot|>" +
		"<|start|>tool weather.get_forecast<|message|><tool_output name=\"weather.get_forecast\">\nsunny\n</tool_output><|eot|>" +
		"<|start|>assistant to=user<|message|>It is sunny in Paris.<|eot|>" +
		"<|start|>assistant"
	if got != want {
		t.Fatalf("got %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}

===== FILE: platform/internal/chattemplate/expr.go =====
package chattemplate

import (
	"fmt"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// ---- expressions -----------------------------------------------------

// vExpr is the expression tree. One struct with per-kind fields,
// in the compact style of the original subset.
type vExpr struct {
	kind string // lit, num, bool, none, name, listlit, attr, index,
	// call, method, filter, add, eq, ne, in, notin, and, or, not,
	// test, cond
	s    string  // literal text, name, attribute, method or test name
	n    float64 // numeric literal
	b    bool    // boolean literal
	args []*vExpr
	kw   map[string]*vExpr
	lhs  *vExpr
	rhs  *vExpr
	cond *vExpr
	// filter arguments ride in args; the filtered value is lhs.
	neg bool // test negation: "is not defined"
}

type exprParser struct {
	s   string
	pos int
}

func parseExpr(s string) (*vExpr, error) {
	p := &exprParser{s: s}
	e, err := p.parseCond()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	p.skipSpace()
	if p.pos != len(p.s) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: expression %q has trailing %q", ErrUnsupported, s, p.s[p.pos:])
	}
	return e, nil
}

// parseCond parses inline conditionals: value if condition else other.
func (p *exprParser) parseCond() (*vExpr, error) {
	val, err := p.parseOr()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	p.skipSpace()
	if !p.eatWord("if") {
		return val, nil
	}
	cond, err := p.parseOr()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	p.skipSpace()
	if !p.eatWord("else") {
		// Jinja: a missing else yields undefined. None of the
		// shipped shapes use it, but it parses and evaluates.
		return &vExpr{kind: "cond", lhs: val, cond: cond, rhs: &vExpr{kind: "none"}}, nil
	}
	other, err := p.parseCond()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return &vExpr{kind: "cond", lhs: val, cond: cond, rhs: other}, nil
}

func (p *exprParser) parseOr() (*vExpr, error) {
	lhs, err := p.parseAnd()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	for {
		p.skipSpace()
		if !p.eatWord("or") {
			return lhs, nil
		}
		rhs, err := p.parseAnd()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		lhs = &vExpr{kind: "or", lhs: lhs, rhs: rhs}
	}
}

func (p *exprParser) parseAnd() (*vExpr, error) {
	lhs, err := p.parseNot()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	for {
		p.skipSpace()
		if !p.eatWord("and") {
			return lhs, nil
		}
		rhs, err := p.parseNot()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		lhs = &vExpr{kind: "and", lhs: lhs, rhs: rhs}
	}
}

func (p *exprParser) parseNot() (*vExpr, error) {
	p.skipSpace()
	if p.eatWord("not") {
		sub, err := p.parseNot()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		return &vExpr{kind: "not", lhs: sub}, nil
	}
	return p.parseComparison()
}

func (p *exprParser) parseComparison() (*vExpr, error) {
	lhs, err := p.parseAdditive()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	p.skipSpace()
	// Postfix tests: expr is [not] <test>.
	if p.eatWord("is") {
		p.skipSpace()
		neg := p.eatWord("not")
		p.skipSpace()
		name, err := p.readIdent()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		return &vExpr{kind: "test", s: name, lhs: lhs, neg: neg}, nil
	}
	for _, op := range []struct {
		text string
		kind string
	}{
		{"==", "eq"}, {"!=", "ne"},
	} {
		if strings.HasPrefix(p.s[p.pos:], op.text) {
			p.pos += len(op.text)
			rhs, err := p.parseAdditive()
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			return &vExpr{kind: op.kind, lhs: lhs, rhs: rhs}, nil
		}
	}
	if p.eatWord("not") {
		p.skipSpace()
		if !p.eatWord("in") {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: 'not' without 'in' in comparison", ErrUnsupported)
		}
		rhs, err := p.parseAdditive()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		return &vExpr{kind: "notin", lhs: lhs, rhs: rhs}, nil
	}
	if p.eatWord("in") {
		rhs, err := p.parseAdditive()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		return &vExpr{kind: "in", lhs: lhs, rhs: rhs}, nil
	}
	return lhs, nil
}

func (p *exprParser) parseAdditive() (*vExpr, error) {
	lhs, err := p.parsePostfix()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	for {
		p.skipSpace()
		if p.pos < len(p.s) && p.s[p.pos] == '+' {
			p.pos++
			rhs, err := p.parsePostfix()
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			lhs = &vExpr{kind: "add", lhs: lhs, rhs: rhs}
			continue
		}
		return lhs, nil
	}
}

// parsePostfix parses a primary plus its attribute, subscript,
// method-call and filter suffixes, in order.
func (p *exprParser) parsePostfix() (*vExpr, error) {
	e, err := p.parsePrimary()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	for {
		p.skipSpace()
		if p.pos >= len(p.s) {
			return e, nil
		}
		switch p.s[p.pos] {
		case '.':
			p.pos++
			name, err := p.readIdent()
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			p.skipSpace()
			if p.pos < len(p.s) && p.s[p.pos] == '(' {
				args, kw, err := p.parseArgs()
				if err != nil {
					return nil, err
				}
				e = &vExpr{kind: "method", s: name, lhs: e, args: args, kw: kw}
			} else {
				e = &vExpr{kind: "attr", s: name, lhs: e}
			}
		case '[':
			p.pos++
			idx, err := p.parseCond()
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			p.skipSpace()
			if p.pos >= len(p.s) || p.s[p.pos] != ']' {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: missing ] in expression %q", ErrUnsupported, p.s)
			}
			p.pos++
			e = &vExpr{kind: "index", lhs: e, rhs: idx}
		case '|':
			p.pos++
			p.skipSpace()
			name, err := p.readIdent()
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			var args []*vExpr
			var kw map[string]*vExpr
			p.skipSpace()
			if p.pos < len(p.s) && p.s[p.pos] == '(' {
				args, kw, err = p.parseArgs()
				if err != nil {
					return nil, err
				}
				// Keyword arguments ride along only for the one
				// filter that defines them (tojson, matching
				// Jinja); evalFilter refuses them by name for
				// every other filter, as it refused all of them
				// before.
				if len(kw) > 0 && name != "tojson" {
					return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: filter %q with keyword arguments", ErrUnsupported, name)
				}
			}
			e = &vExpr{kind: "filter", s: name, lhs: e, args: args, kw: kw}
		default:
			return e, nil
		}
	}
}

func (p *exprParser) parsePrimary() (*vExpr, error) {
	p.skipSpace()
	if p.pos >= len(p.s) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: expression ends early", ErrUnsupported)
	}
	switch c := p.s[p.pos]; {
	case c == '\'' || c == '"':
		lit, err := p.parseLiteral()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		return &vExpr{kind: "lit", s: lit}, nil
	case c == '(':
		p.pos++
		e, err := p.parseCond()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		p.skipSpace()
		if p.pos >= len(p.s) || p.s[p.pos] != ')' {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: missing ) in expression %q", ErrUnsupported, p.s)
		}
		p.pos++
		return e, nil
	case c == '{':
		p.pos++
		var pairs []*vExpr // flattened key, value, key, value
		p.skipSpace()
		if p.pos < len(p.s) && p.s[p.pos] != '}' {
			for {
				k, err := p.parseCond()
				if err != nil {
					return nil, err
				}
				p.skipSpace()
				if p.pos >= len(p.s) || p.s[p.pos] != ':' {
					return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: mapping literal without ':' in %q", ErrUnsupported, p.s)
				}
				p.pos++
				v, err := p.parseCond()
				if err != nil {
					return nil, err
				}
				pairs = append(pairs, k, v)
				p.skipSpace()
				if p.pos < len(p.s) && p.s[p.pos] == ',' {
					p.pos++
					continue
				}
				break
			}
		}
		p.skipSpace()
		if p.pos >= len(p.s) || p.s[p.pos] != '}' {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: missing } in mapping literal %q", ErrUnsupported, p.s)
		}
		p.pos++
		return &vExpr{kind: "dictlit", args: pairs}, nil
	case c == '[':
		p.pos++
		var elems []*vExpr
		p.skipSpace()
		if p.pos < len(p.s) && p.s[p.pos] != ']' {
			for {
				el, err := p.parseCond()
				if err != nil {
					return nil, err
				}
				elems = append(elems, el)
				p.skipSpace()
				if p.pos < len(p.s) && p.s[p.pos] == ',' {
					p.pos++
					continue
				}
				break
			}
		}
		p.skipSpace()
		if p.pos >= len(p.s) || p.s[p.pos] != ']' {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: missing ] in list literal %q", ErrUnsupported, p.s)
		}
		p.pos++
		return &vExpr{kind: "listlit", args: elems}, nil
	case c >= '0' && c <= '9':
		start := p.pos
		for p.pos < len(p.s) && (isIdentChar(p.s[p.pos]) || p.s[p.pos] == '.') {
			p.pos++
		}
		n, err := strconv.ParseFloat(p.s[start:p.pos], 64)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: bad number %q", ErrUnsupported, p.s[start:p.pos])
		}
		return &vExpr{kind: "num", n: n}, nil
	case isIdentStart(c):
		name, err := p.readIdent()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		switch name {
		case "true":
			return &vExpr{kind: "bool", b: true}, nil
		case "false":
			return &vExpr{kind: "bool", b: false}, nil
		case "none":
			return &vExpr{kind: "none"}, nil
		}
		p.skipSpace()
		if p.pos < len(p.s) && p.s[p.pos] == '(' {
			args, kw, err := p.parseArgs()
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			return &vExpr{kind: "call", s: name, args: args, kw: kw}, nil
		}
		return &vExpr{kind: "name", s: name}, nil
	default:
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: unexpected %q in expression", ErrUnsupported, string(c))
	}
}

// parseArgs parses "(a, b, k=v)" with p.pos at the '('.
func (p *exprParser) parseArgs() (args []*vExpr, kw map[string]*vExpr, err error) {
	p.pos++ // consume (
	p.skipSpace()
	if p.pos < len(p.s) && p.s[p.pos] == ')' {
		p.pos++
		return nil, nil, nil
	}
	for {
		p.skipSpace()
		// Keyword argument: ident '=' (but not '==').
		save := p.pos
		if p.pos < len(p.s) && isIdentStart(p.s[p.pos]) {
			name, ierr := p.readIdent()
			if ierr != nil {
				return nil, nil, ierr
			}
			p.skipSpace()
			if p.pos < len(p.s) && p.s[p.pos] == '=' && !strings.HasPrefix(p.s[p.pos:], "==") {
				p.pos++
				v, verr := p.parseCond()
				if verr != nil {
					return nil, nil, verr
				}
				if kw == nil {
					kw = map[string]*vExpr{}
				}
				kw[name] = v
				goto next
			}
			p.pos = save
		}
		{
			v, verr := p.parseCond()
			if verr != nil {
				return nil, nil, verr
			}
			args = append(args, v)
		}
	next:
		p.skipSpace()
		if p.pos < len(p.s) && p.s[p.pos] == ',' {
			p.pos++
			continue
		}
		break
	}
	p.skipSpace()
	if p.pos >= len(p.s) || p.s[p.pos] != ')' {
		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: missing ) in call %q", ErrUnsupported, p.s)
	}
	p.pos++
	return args, kw, nil
}

func (p *exprParser) parseLiteral() (string, error) {
	quote := p.s[p.pos]
	p.pos++
	var sb strings.Builder
	for p.pos < len(p.s) {
		c := p.s[p.pos]
		if c == '\\' && p.pos+1 < len(p.s) {
			switch p.s[p.pos+1] {
			case 'n':
				sb.WriteByte('\n')
			case 't':
				sb.WriteByte('\t')
			case 'r':
				sb.WriteByte('\r')
			default:
				sb.WriteByte(p.s[p.pos+1])
			}
			p.pos += 2
			continue
		}
		if c == quote {
			p.pos++
			return sb.String(), nil
		}
		sb.WriteByte(c)
		p.pos++
	}
	return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: unterminated string literal", ErrUnsupported)
}

func (p *exprParser) readIdent() (string, error) {
	start := p.pos
	for p.pos < len(p.s) && isIdentChar(p.s[p.pos]) {
		p.pos++
	}
	if start == p.pos {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: expected a name in expression %q", ErrUnsupported, p.s)
	}
	return p.s[start:p.pos], nil
}

func (p *exprParser) skipSpace() {
	for p.pos < len(p.s) && (p.s[p.pos] == ' ' || p.s[p.pos] == '\t' || p.s[p.pos] == '\n' || p.s[p.pos] == '\r') {
		p.pos++
	}
}

// eatWord consumes a keyword when it stands alone (not the head of
// a longer identifier).
func (p *exprParser) eatWord(word string) bool {
	if !strings.HasPrefix(p.s[p.pos:], word) {
		return false
	}
	end := p.pos + len(word)
	if end < len(p.s) && isIdentChar(p.s[end]) {
		return false
	}
	p.pos = end
	return true
}

func isIdentStart(c byte) bool {
	return c == '_' || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z')
}

func isIdentChar(c byte) bool {
	return isIdentStart(c) || (c >= '0' && c <= '9')
}

===== FILE: platform/internal/chattemplate/parse.go =====
package chattemplate

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// ---- parser ----------------------------------------------------------

type node interface{ nodeTag() }

type textNode struct{ s string }

func (textNode) nodeTag() {}

type printNode struct{ expr *vExpr }

func (printNode) nodeTag() {}

type forNode struct {
	vars []string // one name, or two for pair items
	iter *vExpr
	body []node
}

func (forNode) nodeTag() {}

type branch struct {
	cond *vExpr // nil on the else branch
	body []node
}

type ifNode struct{ branches []branch }

func (ifNode) nodeTag() {}

type setNode struct {
	target []string // a name, or name.attr for a namespace field
	expr   *vExpr
}

func (setNode) nodeTag() {}

type macroNode struct {
	name   string
	params []string
	body   []node
}

func (macroNode) nodeTag() {}

type parser struct {
	toks []token
	pos  int
}

func parse(toks []token) ([]node, error) {
	p := &parser{toks: toks}
	nodes, stop, err := p.parseBlock()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if stop != "" {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: unexpected {%% %s %%} without an opening tag", ErrUnsupported, stop)
	}
	return nodes, nil
}

// parseBlock reads nodes until a statement whose keyword is a block
// terminator (elif/else/endif/endfor/endmacro); it returns that
// statement's text as the stop value without consuming it.
func (p *parser) parseBlock() (nodes []node, stop string, err error) {
	for p.pos < len(p.toks) {
		t := p.toks[p.pos]
		switch t.kind {
		case tokText:
			nodes = append(nodes, textNode{t.body})
			p.pos++
		case tokPrint:
			e, err := parseExpr(t.body)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, "", err
			}
			nodes = append(nodes, printNode{e})
			p.pos++
		case tokStmt:
			kw := stmtKeyword(t.body)
			switch kw {
			case "for":
				n, err := p.parseFor()
				if err != nil {
					return nil, "", err
				}
				nodes = append(nodes, n)
			case "if":
				n, err := p.parseIf()
				if err != nil {
					return nil, "", err
				}
				nodes = append(nodes, n)
			case "set":
				n, err := parseSet(t.body)
				if err != nil {
					return nil, "", err
				}
				nodes = append(nodes, n)
				p.pos++
			case "macro":
				n, err := p.parseMacro()
				if err != nil {
					return nil, "", err
				}
				nodes = append(nodes, n)
			case "elif", "else", "endif", "endfor", "endmacro":
				return nodes, t.body, nil
			default:
				return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("%w: {%% %s %%}", ErrUnsupported, t.body)
			}
		}
	}
	return nodes, "", nil
}

func (p *parser) parseFor() (node, error) {
	// {% for x in expr %} or {% for k, v in expr %}
	head := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(p.toks[p.pos].body, "for"))
	ep := &exprParser{s: head}
	var vars []string
	for {
		ep.skipSpace()
		name, err := ep.readIdent()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		vars = append(vars, name)
		ep.skipSpace()
		if ep.pos < len(ep.s) && ep.s[ep.pos] == ',' {
			ep.pos++
			continue
		}
		break
	}
	if len(vars) > 2 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: for with %d target names", ErrUnsupported, len(vars))
	}
	ep.skipSpace()
	if !ep.eatWord("in") {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: for without 'in': %q", ErrUnsupported, head)
	}
	iter, err := ep.parseCond()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	ep.skipSpace()
	if ep.pos != len(ep.s) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: for head %q has trailing %q", ErrUnsupported, head, ep.s[ep.pos:])
	}
	p.pos++
	body, stop, err := p.parseBlock()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if stop != "endfor" {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: for without endfor", ErrUnsupported)
	}
	p.pos++ // consume endfor
	return forNode{vars: vars, iter: iter, body: body}, nil
}

func (p *parser) parseMacro() (node, error) {
	// {% macro name(a, b) %}
	head := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(p.toks[p.pos].body, "macro"))
	ep := &exprParser{s: head}
	ep.skipSpace()
	name, err := ep.readIdent()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	ep.skipSpace()
	if ep.pos >= len(ep.s) || ep.s[ep.pos] != '(' {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: macro %q without a parameter list", ErrUnsupported, name)
	}
	ep.pos++
	var params []string
	ep.skipSpace()
	if ep.pos < len(ep.s) && ep.s[ep.pos] != ')' {
		for {
			ep.skipSpace()
			param, err := ep.readIdent()
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			params = append(params, param)
			ep.skipSpace()
			if ep.pos < len(ep.s) && ep.s[ep.pos] == ',' {
				ep.pos++
				continue
			}
			break
		}
	}
	ep.skipSpace()
	if ep.pos >= len(ep.s) || ep.s[ep.pos] != ')' {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: macro %q parameter list is unclosed", ErrUnsupported, name)
	}
	ep.pos++
	ep.skipSpace()
	if ep.pos != len(ep.s) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: macro head %q has trailing %q", ErrUnsupported, head, ep.s[ep.pos:])
	}
	p.pos++
	body, stop, err := p.parseBlock()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if stop != "endmacro" {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: macro without endmacro", ErrUnsupported)
	}
	p.pos++ // consume endmacro
	return macroNode{name: name, params: params, body: body}, nil
}

func parseSet(body string) (node, error) {
	// {% set name = expr %} or {% set ns.attr = expr %}
	rest := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(body, "set"))
	ep := &exprParser{s: rest}
	ep.skipSpace()
	head, err := ep.readIdent()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	target := []string{head}
	ep.skipSpace()
	if ep.pos < len(ep.s) && ep.s[ep.pos] == '.' {
		ep.pos++
		attr, err := ep.readIdent()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		target = append(target, attr)
	}
	ep.skipSpace()
	if ep.pos >= len(ep.s) || ep.s[ep.pos] != '=' || strings.HasPrefix(ep.s[ep.pos:], "==") {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: set without '=': %q", ErrUnsupported, body)
	}
	ep.pos++
	e, err := ep.parseCond()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	ep.skipSpace()
	if ep.pos != len(ep.s) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: set %q has trailing %q", ErrUnsupported, body, ep.s[ep.pos:])
	}
	return setNode{target: target, expr: e}, nil
}

func (p *parser) parseIf() (node, error) {
	// p.toks[p.pos] is the {% if ... %} statement.
	var branches []branch
	for {
		t := p.toks[p.pos]
		kw := stmtKeyword(t.body)
		var cond *vExpr
		if kw == "if" || kw == "elif" {
			condText := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(t.body, kw))
			e, err := parseExpr(condText)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			cond = e
		}
		p.pos++
		body, stop, err := p.parseBlock()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		branches = append(branches, branch{cond, body})
		switch {
		case stop == "endif":
			p.pos++
			return ifNode{branches}, nil
		case strings.HasPrefix(stop, "elif"):
			continue // loop reads the elif as the next branch head
		case stop == "else":
			continue // same, with cond nil
		default:
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: if without endif", ErrUnsupported)
		}
	}
}

func stmtKeyword(stmt string) string {
	if i := strings.IndexAny(stmt, " \t"); i >= 0 {
		return stmt[:i]
	}
	return stmt
}
