===== FILE: platform/internal/chattemplate/render.go =====
package chattemplate

import (
	"fmt"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

// ---- evaluation --------------------------------------------------------

type scope struct {
	vars   map[string]value
	parent *scope
}

func (s *scope) lookup(name string) (value, bool) {
	for cur := s; cur != nil; cur = cur.parent {
		if v, ok := cur.vars[name]; ok {
			return v, true
		}
	}
	return value{}, false
}

type env struct {
	global *scope
	cur    *scope
	macros map[string]*macroNode
	now    time.Time
	budget *renderBudget
}

func (e *env) child(vars map[string]value) *env {
	return &env{global: e.global, cur: &scope{vars: vars, parent: e.cur}, macros: e.macros, now: e.now, budget: e.budget}
}

// renderBudget is the shared accounting every render in one
// Render call draws from: child scopes and macro invocations all
// carry the same pointer, so nesting cannot reset a budget.
type renderBudget struct {
	steps   int // nodes rendered plus loop iterations executed
	depth   int // macro calls currently open
	written int // bytes produced, output and intermediate alike
}

// step charges one unit of work against the step budget.
func (b *renderBudget) step() error {
	b.steps++
	if b.steps > maxRenderSteps {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: more than %d evaluated nodes and loop iterations", ErrBudget, maxRenderSteps)
	}
	return nil
}

// write charges produced text against the output budget. Every
// sink counts, including a macro's private buffer, so text must
// fit the budget at production time, not at the print site.
func (b *renderBudget) write(n int) error {
	b.written += n
	if b.written > maxRenderOutput {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: more than %d bytes of output", ErrBudget, maxRenderOutput)
	}
	return nil
}

// enterMacro opens a macro call against the depth budget.
func (b *renderBudget) enterMacro(name string) error {
	b.depth++
	if b.depth > maxMacroDepth {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: macro call depth over %d at %q", ErrBudget, maxMacroDepth, name)
	}
	return nil
}

func renderNodes(nodes []node, e *env, sb *strings.Builder) error {
	for _, n := range nodes {
		if err := e.budget.step(); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		switch n := n.(type) {
		case textNode:
			if err := e.budget.write(len(n.s)); err != nil {
				return err
			}
			sb.WriteString(n.s)
		case printNode:
			v, err := eval(n.expr, e)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			s, err := v.stringify()
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			if err := e.budget.write(len(s)); err != nil {
				return err
			}
			sb.WriteString(s)
		case setNode:
			v, err := eval(n.expr, e)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			if err := assign(e, n.target, v); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		case macroNode:
			e.macros[n.name] = &n
		case forNode:
			iter, err := eval(n.iter, e)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			if iter.kind != vList {
				return fmt.Errorf("%w: for over a non-list value", ErrUnsupported)
			}
			for i, item := range iter.list {
				// An empty loop body spends no node steps, so
				// iterations charge the step budget directly:
				// a loop over an attacker-sized list is work
				// even when it prints nothing.
				if err := e.budget.step(); err != nil {
					return err
				}
				vars := map[string]value{
					"loop": dictValue(map[string]value{
						"index":  numValue(float64(i + 1)),
						"index0": numValue(float64(i)),
						"first":  boolValue(i == 0),
						"last":   boolValue(i == len(iter.list)-1),
						"length": numValue(float64(len(iter.list))),
					}),
				}
				if len(n.vars) == 2 {
					if item.kind != vList || len(item.list) != 2 {
						return fmt.Errorf("%w: for pair target over a non-pair item", ErrUnsupported)
					}
					vars[n.vars[0]] = item.list[0]
					vars[n.vars[1]] = item.list[1]
				} else {
					vars[n.vars[0]] = item
				}
				if err := renderNodes(n.body, e.child(vars), sb); err != nil {
					return err
				}
			}
		case ifNode:
			for _, br := range n.branches {
				if br.cond == nil {
					if err := renderNodes(br.body, e, sb); err != nil {
						return err
					}
					break
				}
				cond, err := eval(br.cond, e)
				if err != nil {
					return err
				}
				if cond.truthy() {
					if err := renderNodes(br.body, e, sb); err != nil {
						return err
					}
					break
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// assign implements {% set %}: a plain name binds in the current
// scope; name.attr mutates the named mapping in place, which is
// how namespace() state survives loop iterations.
func assign(e *env, target []string, v value) error {
	if len(target) == 1 {
		e.cur.vars[target[0]] = v
		return nil
	}
	base, ok := e.cur.lookup(target[0])
	if !ok || base.kind != vDict {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: set %s.%s on a non-mapping", ErrUnsupported, target[0], target[1])
	}
	// A key the mapping does not carry yet joins its iteration
	// order at the end, as Python dict assignment does; the
	// scope's stored copy of the mapping header has to see the
	// new order slice, so write it back.
	if _, seen := base.dict[target[1]]; !seen && base.keys != nil {
		base.keys = append(base.keys, target[1])
		if scopeVars, found := findScopeVars(e.cur, target[0]); found {
			scopeVars[target[0]] = base
		}
	}
	base.dict[target[1]] = v
	return nil
}

// findScopeVars returns the vars map that binds name, walking the
// scope chain the way lookup does.
func findScopeVars(s *scope, name string) (map[string]value, bool) {
	for cur := s; cur != nil; cur = cur.parent {
		if _, ok := cur.vars[name]; ok {
			return cur.vars, true
		}
	}
	return nil, false
}

func eval(x *vExpr, e *env) (value, error) {
	switch x.kind {
	case "lit":
		return strValue(x.s), nil
	case "num":
		return numValue(x.n), nil
	case "bool":
		return boolValue(x.b), nil
	case "none":
		return value{kind: vNone}, nil
	case "name":
		if v, ok := e.cur.lookup(x.s); ok {
			return v, nil
		}
		return undefValue(x.s), nil
	case "listlit":
		elems := make([]value, 0, len(x.args))
		for _, a := range x.args {
			v, err := eval(a, e)
			if err != nil {
				return value{}, err
			}
			elems = append(elems, v)
		}
		return listValue(elems), nil
	case "dictlit":
		d := make(map[string]value, len(x.args)/2)
		for i := 0; i+1 < len(x.args); i += 2 {
			k, err := eval(x.args[i], e)
			if err != nil {
				return value{}, err
			}
			if k.kind != vStr {
				return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: mapping literal key is not a string", ErrUnsupported)
			}
			v, err := eval(x.args[i+1], e)
			if err != nil {
				return value{}, err
			}
			d[k.s] = v
		}
		return dictValue(d), nil
	case "attr":
		base, err := eval(x.lhs, e)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		return getAttr(base, x.s), nil
	case "index":
		base, err := eval(x.lhs, e)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		idx, err := eval(x.rhs, e)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		return getIndex(base, idx)
	case "add":
		l, err := eval(x.lhs, e)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		r, err := eval(x.rhs, e)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		// The ATEM template concatenates a string with a filtered
		// value ('...' + rns.recipients | join(', ')): Jinja binds
		// the filter tighter than +, so the right operand parses
		// as one filtered primary. This parser reads a whole
		// conditional expression there instead, leaving the
		// filter node as the top of its tree; evaluate that node
		// here, which composes because filters are pure. The
		// parse-level binding stays the subtree case this
		// codebase has always had: a filter whose base is itself
		// the concatenation is outside it and refuses by name.
		if r.kind == vUndef {
			if fr, ok := trailingFilter(x.rhs); ok {
				r, err = evalFilter(fr, e)
				if err != nil {
					return value{}, err
				}
			}
		}
		out, err := addValues(l, r)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		// Concatenation materializes a new string or list, so
		// it charges the output budget: a doubling chain of
		// '+' over a value produces bytes long before any
		// print site sees them.
		if err := e.budget.write(valueBytes(out)); err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		return out, nil
	case "eq", "ne":
		l, err := eval(x.lhs, e)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		r, err := eval(x.rhs, e)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		eq := valuesEqual(l, r)
		if x.kind == "ne" {
			eq = !eq
		}
		return boolValue(eq), nil
	case "in", "notin":
		l, err := eval(x.lhs, e)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		r, err := eval(x.rhs, e)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		in, err := valueIn(l, r)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		if x.kind == "notin" {
			in = !in
		}
		return boolValue(in), nil
	case "and":
		l, err := eval(x.lhs, e)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		if !l.truthy() {
			return l, nil
		}
		return eval(x.rhs, e)
	case "or":
		l, err := eval(x.lhs, e)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		if l.truthy() {
			return l, nil
		}
		return eval(x.rhs, e)
	case "not":
		l, err := eval(x.lhs, e)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		return boolValue(!l.truthy()), nil
	case "test":
		return evalTest(x, e)
	case "cond":
		c, err := eval(x.cond, e)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		if c.truthy() {
			return eval(x.lhs, e)
		}
		return eval(x.rhs, e)
	case "filter":
		return evalFilter(x, e)
	case "method":
		return evalMethod(x, e)
	case "call":
		return evalCall(x, e)
	}
	return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: expression kind %q", ErrUnsupported, x.kind)
}

// trailingFilter reports whether an expression tree's root is a
// bare filter application over a name or attribute chain — the
// shape the add case completes. Grouped operands (parentheses in
// Jinja) parse as the same root shape here, which is harmless:
// those are exactly the operands Jinja binds the filter to.
func trailingFilter(x *vExpr) (*vExpr, bool) {
	if x == nil || x.kind != "filter" {
		return nil, false
	}
	switch x.lhs.kind {
	case "name", "attr", "index":
		return x, true
	}
	return nil, false
}

func getAttr(base value, name string) value {
	if base.kind == vDict {
		if v, ok := base.dict[name]; ok {
			return v
		}
	}
	if base.kind == vUndef {
		return base
	}
	return undefValue(name)
}

func getIndex(base, idx value) (value, error) {
	switch base.kind {
	case vDict:
		if idx.kind != vStr {
			return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: mapping index is not a string", ErrUnsupported)
		}
		if v, ok := base.dict[idx.s]; ok {
			return v, nil
		}
		return undefValue(idx.s), nil
	case vList:
		if idx.kind != vNum {
			return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: list index is not a number", ErrUnsupported)
		}
		i := int(idx.n)
		if i < 0 || i >= len(base.list) {
			return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: list index %d out of range", ErrUnsupported, i)
		}
		return base.list[i], nil
	case vUndef:
		return base, nil
	}
	return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: indexing a non-container", ErrUnsupported)
}

func addValues(l, r value) (value, error) {
	switch {
	case l.kind == vStr && r.kind == vStr:
		return strValue(l.s + r.s), nil
	case l.kind == vNum && r.kind == vNum:
		return numValue(l.n + r.n), nil
	case l.kind == vList && r.kind == vList:
		out := make([]value, 0, len(l.list)+len(r.list))
		out = append(out, l.list...)
		out = append(out, r.list...)
		return listValue(out), nil
	}
	return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: '+' over values that do not add", ErrUnsupported)
}

// valueBytes measures the bytes a value stands for, for the
// output budget: the string itself, or the element total of a
// container. Scalars carry no production cost worth charging.
func valueBytes(v value) int {
	switch v.kind {
	case vStr:
		return len(v.s)
	case vList:
		n := 0
		for _, el := range v.list {
			n += valueBytes(el)
		}
		return n
	case vDict:
		n := 0
		for _, el := range v.dict {
			n += valueBytes(el)
		}
		return n
	}
	return 0
}

func evalTest(x *vExpr, e *env) (value, error) {
	v, err := eval(x.lhs, e)
	if err != nil {
		return value{}, err
	}
	var out bool
	switch x.s {
	case "defined":
		out = v.kind != vUndef
	case "undefined":
		out = v.kind == vUndef
	case "none":
		out = v.kind == vNone
	case "string":
		out = v.kind == vStr
	case "boolean":
		out = v.kind == vBool
	case "number":
		out = v.kind == vNum
	case "mapping":
		out = v.kind == vDict
	case "iterable":
		out = v.kind == vList || v.kind == vDict || v.kind == vStr
	default:
		return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: test %q", ErrUnsupported, x.s)
	}
	if x.neg {
		out = !out
	}
	return boolValue(out), nil
}

func evalFilter(x *vExpr, e *env) (value, error) {
	base, err := eval(x.lhs, e)
	if err != nil {
		return value{}, err
	}
	argStr := func(i int) (string, error) {
		if len(x.args) <= i {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: filter %q needs %d arguments", ErrUnsupported, x.s, i+1)
		}
		v, err := eval(x.args[i], e)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		if v.kind != vStr {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: filter %q argument is not a string", ErrUnsupported, x.s)
		}
		return v.s, nil
	}
	switch x.s {
	case "trim":
		if base.kind != vStr {
			return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: filter trim over a non-string", ErrUnsupported)
		}
		return strValue(strings.TrimSpace(base.s)), nil
	case "lower":
		if base.kind != vStr {
			return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: filter lower over a non-string", ErrUnsupported)
		}
		return strValue(strings.ToLower(base.s)), nil
	case "replace":
		if base.kind != vStr {
			return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: filter replace over a non-string", ErrUnsupported)
		}
		from, err := argStr(0)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		to, err := argStr(1)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		out := strings.ReplaceAll(base.s, from, to)
		// A replace can multiply its input (every byte becomes
		// a longer string), so the result charges the output
		// budget like any other produced text.
		if err := e.budget.write(len(out)); err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		return strValue(out), nil
	case "join":
		if base.kind != vList {
			return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: filter join over a non-list", ErrUnsupported)
		}
		sep, err := argStr(0)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		parts := make([]string, 0, len(base.list))
		for _, el := range base.list {
			s, err := el.stringify()
			if err != nil {
				return value{}, err
			}
			parts = append(parts, s)
		}
		out := strings.Join(parts, sep)
		if err := e.budget.write(len(out)); err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		return strValue(out), nil
	case "tojson":
		return evalToJSON(x, e, base)
	}
	return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: filter %q", ErrUnsupported, x.s)
}

// evalToJSON implements the tojson filter with Jinja's semantics:
// the value is serialized as Python's json.dumps serializes it,
// then marked safe, which in this print-only renderer means the
// JSON text passes through unchanged (without the HTML entity
// escaping Jinja applies on top, which belongs to autoescaping
// web contexts, not prompt building). The default dump uses the
// compact separators and sorts mapping keys — the ATEM template
// relies on exactly this when it serializes tool schemas, whose
// key order in the prompt is therefore sorted, as under Jinja.
// The indent keyword (a non-negative integer) switches to the
// pretty form with ", " after colons and one entry per line, and
// sort_keys (default true) may be set false to keep recorded
// insertion order. The encoded text charges the output budget
// like any other produced text: a filter can be applied to a
// whole tool schema at every message.
func evalToJSON(x *vExpr, e *env, base value) (value, error) {
	if len(x.args) > 0 {
		return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: filter \"tojson\" takes keyword arguments only", ErrUnsupported)
	}
	indent := -1
	sortKeys := true
	for name, argExpr := range x.kw {
		v, err := eval(argExpr, e)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		switch name {
		case "indent":
			if v.kind != vNum || v.n < 0 || v.n != float64(int(v.n)) {
				return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: filter \"tojson\" indent is not a non-negative integer", ErrUnsupported)
			}
			indent = int(v.n)
		case "sort_keys":
			if v.kind != vBool {
				return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: filter \"tojson\" sort_keys is not a boolean", ErrUnsupported)
			}
			sortKeys = v.b
		default:
			return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: filter \"tojson\" argument %q", ErrUnsupported, name)
		}
	}
	var sb strings.Builder
	if err := writeJSONValue(&sb, base, indent, sortKeys, 0); err != nil {
		return value{}, err
	}
	out := sb.String()
	if err := e.budget.write(len(out)); err != nil {
		return value{}, err
	}
	return strValue(out), nil
}

// writeJSONValue serializes a value the way Python's json.dumps
// does, which is what Jinja's tojson wraps: strings escape the
// backslash and control characters as \u00XX (with the short
// escapes for newline, tab, and carriage return), the quote
// itself as \" (or \u0022 in Jinja's HTML-safe pass, which also
// escapes <, >, & and ' the same unicode way; the fixture's
// schema dumps come through llama.cpp's minja runtime, whose
// tojson is a plain nlohmann::json dump, and this encoder
// follows that plain form for the quote — tool schemas pinned
// against the reference environment are byte-compared in the
// golden tests), plus <, >, and & as \u003c, \u003e, \u0026
// (shared by the HTML-safe form), and non-ASCII characters as
// \uXXXX because ensure_ascii defaults to true. Numbers print
// as Python prints them: integral floats without a fraction,
// other floats in the shortest round-trip decimal; NaN and the
// infinities print as Python's bare NaN/Infinity/-Infinity
// tokens, as json.dumps emits them by default. Mappings print
// their keys sorted unless sortKeys is false and the mapping
// carries an insertion order. Container nesting is bounded
// explicitly (Python bounds it with its recursion limit): a
// pathological value refuses by name instead of overflowing the
// stack.
func writeJSONValue(sb *strings.Builder, v value, indent int, sortKeys bool, depth int) error {
	const maxJSONDepth = 512
	if depth > maxJSONDepth {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: filter \"tojson\" over a value nested deeper than %d", ErrUnsupported, maxJSONDepth)
	}
	switch v.kind {
	case vStr:
		writeJSONString(sb, v.s)
	case vNum:
		sb.WriteString(jsonNumber(v.n))
	case vBool:
		if v.b {
			sb.WriteString("true")
		} else {
			sb.WriteString("false")
		}
	case vNone:
		sb.WriteString("null")
	case vList:
		if len(v.list) == 0 {
			sb.WriteString("[]")
			return nil
		}
		sb.WriteByte('[')
		for i, el := range v.list {
			if i > 0 {
				sb.WriteByte(',')
			}
			writeJSONIndent(sb, indent, depth+1, i > 0)
			if err := writeJSONValue(sb, el, indent, sortKeys, depth+1); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
		writeJSONIndent(sb, indent, depth, len(v.list) > 0)
		sb.WriteByte(']')
	case vDict:
		if len(v.dict) == 0 {
			sb.WriteString("{}")
			return nil
		}
		keys := v.orderedKeys()
		if !sortKeys {
			// Insertion order already; nothing to arrange.
		} else {
			sorted := make([]string, len(keys))
			copy(sorted, keys)
			sortStrings(sorted)
			keys = sorted
		}
		sb.WriteByte('{')
		for i, k := range keys {
			if i > 0 {
				sb.WriteByte(',')
			}
			writeJSONIndent(sb, indent, depth+1, i > 0)
			writeJSONString(sb, k)
			sb.WriteByte(':')
			if indent >= 0 {
				sb.WriteByte(' ')
			}
			if err := writeJSONValue(sb, v.dict[k], indent, sortKeys, depth+1); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
		writeJSONIndent(sb, indent, depth, len(v.dict) > 0)
		sb.WriteByte('}')
	default:
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: filter \"tojson\" over a value with no JSON form", ErrUnsupported)
	}
	return nil
}

// writeJSONIndent emits the pretty-print line break and padding
// for one entry when indent is on, and nothing in compact form.
// The first entry of a container opens on the container's own
// line; every entry, first included, ends up indented by its
// level once the comma or opening bracket before it is written.
func writeJSONIndent(sb *strings.Builder, indent, level int, afterComma bool) {
	if indent < 0 {
		return
	}
	_ = afterComma
	sb.WriteByte('\n')
	for i := 0; i < indent*level; i++ {
		sb.WriteByte(' ')
	}
}

// writeJSONString writes one string with Python json escaping.
func writeJSONString(sb *strings.Builder, s string) {
	sb.WriteByte('"')
	for _, r := range s {
		switch {
		case r == '"':
			sb.WriteString(`\"`)
		case r == '\\':
			sb.WriteString(`\\`)
		case r == '\n':
			sb.WriteString(`\n`)
		case r == '\r':
			sb.WriteString(`\r`)
		case r == '\t':
			sb.WriteString(`\t`)
		case r == '\b':
			sb.WriteString(`\b`)
		case r == '\f':
			sb.WriteString(`\f`)
		case r == '<':
			sb.WriteString(`\u003c`)
		case r == '>':
			sb.WriteString(`\u003e`)
		case r == '&':
			sb.WriteString(`\u0026`)
		case r < 0x20:
			fmt.Fprintf(sb, `\u%04x`, r)
		case r < 0x80:
			sb.WriteRune(r)
		case r <= 0xFFFF:
			fmt.Fprintf(sb, `\u%04x`, r)
		default:
			// Above the basic multilingual plane, Python emits
			// a UTF-16 surrogate pair.
			r -= 0x10000
			fmt.Fprintf(sb, `\u%04x\u%04x`, 0xD800+(r>>10), 0xDC00+(r&0x3FF))
		}
	}
	sb.WriteByte('"')
}

// jsonNumber formats a float the way Python's repr does for the
// magnitudes chat data carries: integral values print without a
// fraction, others in the shortest decimal that round-trips.
// strconv's shortest form differs from repr only in exponent
// formatting (Go writes 1e+21 where Python writes 1e+21 as well
// for floats this size; both agree on the plain range), which is
// acceptable here: the values tojson serializes from templates
// are tool schemas, names, and arguments, not float extremes.
func jsonNumber(n float64) string {
	if n != n {
		return "NaN"
	}
	if n > 1.7976931348623157e308 {
		return "Infinity"
	}
	if n < -1.7976931348623157e308 {
		return "-Infinity"
	}
	if n == float64(int64(n)) && n < 9.0e15 && n > -9.0e15 {
		return strconv.FormatInt(int64(n), 10)
	}
	return strconv.FormatFloat(n, 'g', -1, 64)
}

func evalMethod(x *vExpr, e *env) (value, error) {
	base, err := eval(x.lhs, e)
	if err != nil {
		return value{}, err
	}
	switch x.s {
	case "get":
		if base.kind != vDict {
			return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: method get on a non-mapping", ErrUnsupported)
		}
		if len(x.args) < 1 || len(x.args) > 2 {
			return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: method get with %d arguments", ErrUnsupported, len(x.args))
		}
		key, err := eval(x.args[0], e)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		if key.kind != vStr {
			return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: method get with a non-string key", ErrUnsupported)
		}
		if v, ok := base.dict[key.s]; ok {
			return v, nil
		}
		if len(x.args) == 2 {
			return eval(x.args[1], e)
		}
		return value{kind: vNone}, nil
	case "split":
		if base.kind != vStr {
			return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: method split on a non-string", ErrUnsupported)
		}
		if len(x.args) != 1 {
			return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: method split with %d arguments", ErrUnsupported, len(x.args))
		}
		sep, err := eval(x.args[0], e)
		if err != nil {
			return value{}, err
		}
		if sep.kind != vStr || sep.s == "" {
			return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: method split with a bad separator", ErrUnsupported)
		}
		parts := strings.Split(base.s, sep.s)
		out := make([]value, len(parts))
		for i, part := range parts {
			out[i] = strValue(part)
		}
		return listValue(out), nil
	case "items":
		if base.kind != vDict {
			return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: method items on a non-mapping", ErrUnsupported)
		}
		// Pair items in the mapping's iteration order: the
		// insertion order caller data arrived in, or sorted
		// order for mappings without one (see values.go). The
		// ATEM template prints one parameter block per pair,
		// so this order is prompt text, not an internal detail.
		keys := base.orderedKeys()
		out := make([]value, 0, len(keys))
		for _, k := range keys {
			out = append(out, listValue([]value{strValue(k), base.dict[k]}))
		}
		return listValue(out), nil
	}
	return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: method call %s(...)", ErrUnsupported, x.s)
}

func sortStrings(s []string) {
	for i := 1; i < len(s); i++ {
		for j := i; j > 0 && s[j] < s[j-1]; j-- {
			s[j], s[j-1] = s[j-1], s[j]
		}
	}
}

func evalCall(x *vExpr, e *env) (value, error) {
	if x.s == "namespace" {
		d := map[string]value{}
		for name, argExpr := range x.kw {
			v, err := eval(argExpr, e)
			if err != nil {
				return value{}, err
			}
			d[name] = v
		}
		if len(x.args) > 0 {
			return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: namespace() with positional arguments", ErrUnsupported)
		}
		return dictValue(d), nil
	}
	if _, isMacro := e.macros[x.s]; !isMacro {
		if v, ok := e.cur.lookup(x.s); ok && v.kind == vBuiltin {
			return evalBuiltin(v.s, x, e)
		}
	}
	m, ok := e.macros[x.s]
	if !ok {
		// raise_exception and every other unknown call refuse by
		// name when actually evaluated; untaken branches never
		// reach here.
		return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: function call %s(...)", ErrUnsupported, x.s)
	}
	vars := map[string]value{}
	for i, param := range m.params {
		if i < len(x.args) {
			v, err := eval(x.args[i], e)
			if err != nil {
				return value{}, err
			}
			if err := e.budget.write(valueBytes(v)); err != nil {
				return value{}, err
			}
			vars[param] = v
		} else if kwExpr, ok := x.kw[param]; ok {
			v, err := eval(kwExpr, e)
			if err != nil {
				return value{}, err
			}
			if err := e.budget.write(valueBytes(v)); err != nil {
				return value{}, err
			}
			vars[param] = v
		} else {
			vars[param] = undefValue(param)
		}
	}
	// A macro call charges a step of its own, on top of the
	// nodes its body renders, so the total call count in one
	// render is bounded directly and not only through bodies.
	if err := e.budget.step(); err != nil {
		return value{}, err
	}
	if err := e.budget.enterMacro(x.s); err != nil {
		return value{}, err
	}
	defer func() { e.budget.depth-- }()
	// Macros see the global scope plus their parameters, as in
	// Jinja; the caller's locals do not leak in.
	macroEnv := &env{global: e.global, cur: &scope{vars: vars, parent: e.global}, macros: e.macros, now: e.now, budget: e.budget}
	var sb strings.Builder
	if err := renderNodes(m.body, macroEnv, &sb); err != nil {
		return value{}, err
	}
	// The returned text is materialized here and will be
	// charged again wherever it is consumed (printed or passed
	// on as an argument); charging it at production too keeps
	// a macro that duplicates its argument a constant number
	// of times per call from growing memory a level at a time
	// while the charges land only at the final print.
	if err := e.budget.write(sb.Len()); err != nil {
		return value{}, err
	}
	return strValue(sb.String()), nil
}

// evalBuiltin runs a call to a builtin function value. The only
// builtin is strftime_now(format), the host-clock function the
// reference template environment defines; it exists so templates
// that print the current date (guarded by `is defined`, as the
// Glimmer ATEM template does) render the same text llama.cpp
// renders. The format language is the strftime subset chat
// templates use; an unknown specifier refuses by name.
func evalBuiltin(name string, x *vExpr, e *env) (value, error) {
	if name != "strftime_now" {
		return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: function call %s(...)", ErrUnsupported, name)
	}
	if len(x.args) != 1 || len(x.kw) > 0 {
		return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: strftime_now takes one format argument", ErrUnsupported)
	}
	fv, err := eval(x.args[0], e)
	if err != nil {
		return value{}, err
	}
	if fv.kind != vStr {
		return value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: strftime_now format is not a string", ErrUnsupported)
	}
	out, err := formatStrftime(e.now, fv.s)
	if err != nil {
		return value{}, err
	}
	return strValue(out), nil
}

func formatStrftime(t time.Time, format string) (string, error) {
	var sb strings.Builder
	for i := 0; i < len(format); i++ {
		if format[i] != '%' {
			sb.WriteByte(format[i])
			continue
		}
		i++
		if i >= len(format) {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: strftime format ends with a lone %%", ErrUnsupported)
		}
		switch format[i] {
		case '%':
			sb.WriteByte('%')
		case 'Y':
			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "%04d", t.Year())
		case 'y':
			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "%02d", t.Year()%100)
		case 'm':
			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "%02d", int(t.Month()))
		case 'd':
			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "%02d", t.Day())
		case 'H':
			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "%02d", t.Hour())
		case 'M':
			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "%02d", t.Minute())
		case 'S':
			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "%02d", t.Second())
		case 'j':
			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "%03d", t.YearDay())
		default:
			return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: strftime specifier %%%c", ErrUnsupported, format[i])
		}
	}
	return sb.String(), nil
}

{#
  Template: Muse Glimmer ATEM Chat Template
  Renders the ATEM tool-calling protocol: reasoning channel (to=self), tool
  channels (to=<tool>), and the user channel, plus tool definitions and the
  valid-recipient list in the system block.

  Whitespace note: every tag uses the {%- -%} / {{- -}} stripping markers, so
  the indentation below is purely for readability and contributes nothing to
  the rendered output.
#}
{%- macro render_content(content) -%}
    {%- if content is string -%}
        {{- content -}}
    {%- elif content is not none -%}
        {%- for part in content -%}
            {%- if part['type'] == 'image' -%}
                {{- '<|patch|>' -}}
            {%- elif part['type'] == 'video' -%}
                {{- '<|video|>' -}}
            {%- elif part['type'] == 'text' -%}
                {{- part['text'] -}}
            {%- endif -%}
        {%- endfor -%}
    {%- endif -%}
{%- endmacro -%}
{%- macro render_atem(tc) -%}
    {%- set args = tc.function.arguments -%}
    {%- if args is not mapping -%}
        {{- raise_exception('Muse Glimmer ATEM chat template requires tool_call.function.arguments to be a dict (mapping); a JSON string cannot be parsed in the HF jinja sandbox.') -}}
    {%- endif -%}
    {{- '<atem:function_calls>\n<atem:invoke name="' + tc.function.name + '">\n' -}}
    {%- for k, v in args.items() -%}
        {{- '<atem:parameter name="' + k + '">' -}}
        {%- if v is boolean -%}
            {%- if v -%}
                true
            {%- else -%}
                false
            {%- endif -%}
        {%- elif v is none -%}
            null
        {%- elif v is mapping or (v is iterable and v is not string) -%}
            {{- v | tojson -}}
        {%- else -%}
            {{- v -}}
        {%- endif -%}
        {{- '</atem:parameter>\n' -}}
    {%- endfor -%}
    {{- '</atem:invoke>\n</atem:function_calls>' -}}
{%- endmacro -%}
{%- macro render_tool_defs(tools) -%}
    {{- 'In this environment you have access to a set of tools you can use to answer the user\'s question.\n\n' -}}
    {{- 'You can invoke a function by writing a "<atem:function_calls>" block like the following:\n' -}}
    {{- '<atem:function_calls>\n<atem:invoke name="$FUNCTION_NAME">\n<atem:parameter name="$PARAMETER_NAME">$PARAMETER_VALUE</atem:parameter>\n...\n</atem:invoke>\n</atem:function_calls>\n\n' -}}
    {{- 'String and scalar parameters should be specified as is, while lists and objects should use JSON format. Note that spaces for string values are not stripped. The output is not expected to be valid XML and is parsed with regular expressions.\n' -}}
    {{- 'Here are the functions available in JSONSchema format:\n' -}}
    {{- '// Tool metadata\n' -}}
    {%- set nsns = namespace(seen=[]) -%}
    {%- for tool in tools -%}
        {%- set fn = tool.function if tool.function is defined else tool -%}
        {%- set tns = fn.name.split('.')[0] -%}
        {%- if tns not in nsns.seen -%}
            {%- set nsns.seen = nsns.seen + [tns] -%}
        {%- endif -%}
    {%- endfor -%}
    {%- set nd = tool_namespace_descriptions if tool_namespace_descriptions is defined else {} -%}
    {%- for tns in nsns.seen -%}
        {{- '{"name": ' + (tns | tojson) + ', "description": ' + ((nd[tns] if tns in nd else '') | tojson) + '}\n' -}}
    {%- endfor -%}
    {{- '// Function schemas' -}}
    {%- for tool in tools -%}
        {%- set fn = tool.function if tool.function is defined else tool -%}
        {{- '\n{"name": ' + (fn.name | tojson) + ', "description": ' + (fn.description | tojson) + ', "parameters": ' + (fn.parameters | tojson) + '}' -}}
    {%- endfor -%}
    {{- '\n\nHere\'s an example of how to call a function in the tool set:\n' -}}
    {{- '(If the tool namespace is not specified, invoke the function directly as `example_function_name` rather than `example_tool_name.example_function_name`)\n\n' -}}
    {{- 'to=example_tool_name.example_function_name\n\n' -}}
    {{- '<atem:function_calls>\n<atem:invoke name="example_tool_name.example_function_name">\n' -}}
    {{- '<atem:parameter name="example_parameter_1">value_1</atem:parameter>\n' -}}
    {{- '<atem:parameter name="example_parameter_2">This is the value for the second parameter\nthat can span\n"multiple" lines\n</atem:parameter>\n' -}}
    {{- '</atem:invoke>\n</atem:function_calls>' -}}
{%- endmacro -%}
{%- macro render_reasoning() -%}
    {%- set rs = reasoning_strength if reasoning_strength is defined and reasoning_strength else 'high' -%}
    {{- 'Reasoning strength: ' + rs + '.' -}}
{%- endmacro -%}
{%- macro render_system_meta(tools) -%}
    {%- set rns = namespace(recipients=['"self"'], nslist=[]) -%}
    {%- if tools -%}
        {%- for tool in tools -%}
            {%- set fn = tool.function if tool.function is defined else tool -%}
            {%- set tns = fn.name.split('.')[0] -%}
            {%- if tns not in rns.nslist -%}
                {%- set rns.nslist = rns.nslist + [tns] -%}
            {%- endif -%}
        {%- endfor -%}

            {%- set rns.recipients = rns.recipients + ['"' + tns + '.*"'] -%}
        {%- endfor -%}
    {%- endif -%}
    {%- set rns.recipients = rns.recipients + ['"user"'] -%}
    {{- '# Valid recipients: ' + rns.recipients | join(', ') + '.' -}}
{%- endmacro -%}
{{- bos_token -}}
{%- set ns = namespace(has_system=false) -%}
{%- for m in messages -%}
    {%- if m['role'] == 'system' -%}
        {%- set ns.has_system = true -%}
    {%- endif -%}
{%- endfor -%}
{%- if not ns.has_system -%}
    {{- '<|start|>system<|message|>You are a helpful AI assistant.' -}}
    {%- set kc = knowledge_cutoff if knowledge_cutoff is defined and knowledge_cutoff else '2026-01-04' -%}
    {{- '\nKnowledge cutoff: ' + kc + '.' -}}
    {%- if current_date is defined and current_date -%}
        {{- '\nCurrent date: ' + current_date + '.' -}}
    {%- elif strftime_now is defined -%}
        {{- '\nCurrent date: ' + strftime_now('%Y-%m-%d') + '.' -}}
    {%- endif -%}
    {{- '\n\n' -}}
    {{- render_reasoning() -}}
    {%- if tools -%}
        {{- '\n\n' -}}
        {{- render_tool_defs(tools) -}}
    {%- endif -%}
    {{- '\n\n' -}}
    {{- render_system_meta(tools) -}}
    {{- '<|eot|>' -}}
{%- endif -%}
{%- for message in messages -%}
    {%- set role = message['role'] -%}
    {%- set end_token = '<|eom|>' if (not loop.last and messages[loop.index0 + 1]['role'] == role) else '<|eot|>' -%}
    {%- if role == 'system' -%}
        {#- Callers sometimes write the directive into the system prompt themselves.
            Normalise "Reasoning effort" to "Reasoning strength" (jinja has no

        {%- set sys_text = render_content(message['content'])

    {%- elif role == 'user' -%}
        {{- '<|start|>user<|message|>' -}}

    {{- '<|start|>assistant' -}}
{%- endif -%}

===== FILE: platform/internal/chattemplate/tokenize.go =====
package chattemplate

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// ---- tokenizer -------------------------------------------------------

type tokKind int

const (
	tokText tokKind = iota
	tokPrint
	tokStmt
)

type token struct {
	kind tokKind
	body string // text content, or the tag's inner text (trimmed)
}

func tokenize(tmpl string) ([]token, error) {
	var toks []token
	rest := tmpl
	trimNextLeft := false
	for len(rest) > 0 {
		// The earliest of {{, {% and {# opens the next tag; a
		// comment's body is never lexed, so tag lookalikes inside
		// {# ... #} (the Glimmer template's header comment names
		// the {%- -%} markers) stay inert.
		i, kind := -1, tokText
		for _, cand := range []struct {
			mark string
			kind tokKind
		}{{"{{", tokPrint}, {"{%", tokStmt}, {"{#", tokText}} {
			if j := strings.Index(rest, cand.mark); j >= 0 && (i < 0 || j < i) {
				i, kind = j, cand.kind
			}
		}
		isComment := i >= 0 && strings.HasPrefix(rest[i:], "{#")
		if i < 0 {
			text := rest
			if trimNextLeft {
				text = strings.TrimLeft(text, " \t\r\n")
			}
			if text != "" {
				toks = append(toks, token{tokText, text})
			}
			break
		}
		text := rest[:i]
		if trimNextLeft {
			text = strings.TrimLeft(text, " \t\r\n")
			trimNextLeft = false
		}
		j := i + 2
		trimPrev := false
		if j < len(rest) && rest[j] == '-' {
			trimPrev = true
			j++
		}
		if trimPrev {
			text = strings.TrimRight(text, " \t\r\n")
		}
		if text != "" {
			toks = append(toks, token{tokText, text})
		}
		if isComment {
			end := strings.Index(rest[j:], "#}")
			if end < 0 {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: unclosed comment", ErrUnsupported)
			}
			inner := rest[j : j+end]
			if strings.HasSuffix(inner, "-") {
				trimNextLeft = true
			}
			rest = rest[j+end+2:]
			continue
		}
		close := "}}"
		if kind == tokStmt {
			close = "%}"
		}
		end := strings.Index(rest[j:], close)
		if end < 0 {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: unclosed tag at %q", ErrUnsupported, rest[i:min(len(rest), i+16)])
		}
		inner := rest[j : j+end]
		if strings.HasSuffix(inner, "-") {
			trimNextLeft = true
			inner = inner[:len(inner)-1]
		}
		toks = append(toks, token{kind, strings.TrimSpace(inner)})
		rest = rest[j+end+2:]
	}
	return toks, nil
}

===== FILE: platform/internal/chattemplate/values.go =====
package chattemplate

import (
	"fmt"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// ---- values ----------------------------------------------------------

type vKind int

const (
	vUndef vKind = iota
	vNone
	vBool
	vNum
	vStr
	vList
	vDict
	vBuiltin
)

// value is a Jinja value at render time. An undefined name resolves
// to vUndef carrying the name: it is falsy and answers the defined
// test, but printing one refuses by name instead of rendering
// empty text the caller never asked for.
//
// A dict value also carries its keys' insertion order in keys:
// mappings built from caller data (tool definitions, tool-call
// arguments, content parts) keep the order that data arrived in,
// the order Jinja's environment iterates. The dict literal and
// the namespace() builtin have no caller order worth preserving —
// a literal's keys are authored in the template, not the data —
// so they leave keys nil and iterate in sorted-key order, the
// deterministic order they have always used.
type value struct {
	kind vKind
	name string // vUndef: the unresolved name
	b    bool
	n    float64
	s    string
	list []value
	dict map[string]value
	keys []string // vDict: insertion order of dict's keys, nil = sorted
}

func strValue(s string) value            { return value{kind: vStr, s: s} }
func boolValue(b bool) value             { return value{kind: vBool, b: b} }
func numValue(n float64) value           { return value{kind: vNum, n: n} }
func listValue(l []value) value          { return value{kind: vList, list: l} }
func dictValue(d map[string]value) value { return value{kind: vDict, dict: d} }
func undefValue(name string) value       { return value{kind: vUndef, name: name} }
func builtinValue(name string) value     { return value{kind: vBuiltin, s: name} }

// orderedDict builds a mapping from key/value pairs in the given
// order, recording that order for iteration and tojson. A later
// pair with an already-seen key replaces the value and keeps the
// key's first position, as Python dict assignment does.
func orderedDict(pairs ...value) value {
	d := make(map[string]value, len(pairs)/2)
	keys := make([]string, 0, len(pairs)/2)
	for i := 0; i+1 < len(pairs); i += 2 {
		k := pairs[i].s
		if _, seen := d[k]; !seen {
			keys = append(keys, k)
		}
		d[k] = pairs[i+1]
	}
	return value{kind: vDict, dict: d, keys: keys}
}

// orderedKeys returns the keys a mapping iterates in: the recorded
// insertion order when the mapping carries one, else sorted order.
func (v value) orderedKeys() []string {
	if v.keys != nil {
		return v.keys
	}
	keys := make([]string, 0, len(v.dict))
	for k := range v.dict {
		keys = append(keys, k)
	}
	sortStrings(keys)
	return keys
}

func (v value) truthy() bool {
	switch v.kind {
	case vUndef, vNone:
		return false
	case vBool:
		return v.b
	case vNum:
		return v.n != 0
	case vStr:
		return v.s != ""
	case vList:
		return len(v.list) > 0
	case vDict:
		return len(v.dict) > 0
	case vBuiltin:
		return true
	}
	return false
}

// stringify renders a value into print output. Booleans and
// undefined or none values refuse by name: a template printing one
// is asking for text the subset does not define.
func (v value) stringify() (string, error) {
	switch v.kind {
	case vStr:
		return v.s, nil
	case vNum:
		return strconv.FormatFloat(v.n, 'f', -1, 64), nil
	case vUndef:
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: name %q is not defined", ErrUnsupported, v.name)
	case vNone:
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: cannot print none", ErrUnsupported)
	case vBool:
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: cannot print a boolean", ErrUnsupported)
	case vBuiltin:
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: cannot print the builtin function %q", ErrUnsupported, v.s)
	default:
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: cannot print a list or mapping", ErrUnsupported)
	}
}

func valuesEqual(a, b value) bool {
	if a.kind == vNone || b.kind == vNone {
		return a.kind == b.kind
	}
	if a.kind == vUndef || b.kind == vUndef {
		return a.kind == b.kind
	}
	if a.kind != b.kind {
		return false
	}
	switch a.kind {
	case vBool:
		return a.b == b.b
	case vNum:
		return a.n == b.n
	case vStr:
		return a.s == b.s
	}
	return false
}

func valueIn(item, container value) (bool, error) {
	switch container.kind {
	case vList:
		for _, el := range container.list {
			if valuesEqual(item, el) {
				return true, nil
			}
		}
		return false, nil
	case vDict:
		if item.kind != vStr {
			return false, fmt.Errorf("%w: 'in' over a mapping needs a string key", ErrUnsupported)
		}
		_, ok := container.dict[item.s]
		return ok, nil
	case vStr:
		if item.kind != vStr {
			return false, fmt.Errorf("%w: 'in' over a string needs a string", ErrUnsupported)
		}
		return strings.Contains(container.s, item.s), nil
	}
	return false, fmt.Errorf("%w: 'in' over a non-container", ErrUnsupported)
}

===== END FILE: platform/internal/chattemplate/values.go =====

===== FILE: platform/internal/diag/diag.go =====
// Package diag is the platform's built-in diagnostics registry.
//
// Every module reports into a Registry: request counts per route, error
// counts, engine call outcomes. The /debug endpoint serves a Snapshot of
// the registry, so a running torchd can always answer "what have you done
// and what went wrong" without log archaeology. Counters are atomic and
// the registry is safe for concurrent use.
package diag

import (
	"sort"
	"sync"
	"sync/atomic"
	"time"
)

// Registry collects platform diagnostics from birth: it is constructed
// with the process and never nil in a wired server.
type Registry struct {
	startedAt time.Time

	requests  atomic.Int64
	errors    atomic.Int64
	authFails atomic.Int64

	engineCalls  atomic.Int64
	engineErrors atomic.Int64

	mu     sync.Mutex
	routes map[string]*atomic.Int64
}

// New returns an empty registry stamped with the current time.
func New() *Registry {
	return &Registry{
		startedAt: time.Now(),
		routes:    make(map[string]*atomic.Int64),
	}
}

// RecordRequest counts one served request for a route pattern.
func (r *Registry) RecordRequest(route string) {
	r.requests.Add(1)
	r.mu.Lock()
	c, ok := r.routes[route]
	if !ok {
		c = &atomic.Int64{}
		r.routes[route] = c
	}
	r.mu.Unlock()
	c.Add(1)
}

// RecordError counts one error response.
func (r *Registry) RecordError() { r.errors.Add(1) }

// RecordAuthFailure counts one rejected API key check.
func (r *Registry) RecordAuthFailure() { r.authFails.Add(1) }

// RecordEngineCall counts one call into the engine client.
func (r *Registry) RecordEngineCall() { r.engineCalls.Add(1) }

// RecordEngineError counts one failed engine call.
func (r *Registry) RecordEngineError() { r.engineErrors.Add(1) }

// Snapshot is a point-in-time copy of the registry for /debug.
type Snapshot struct {
	UptimeSeconds int64            `json:"uptime_seconds"`
	Requests      int64            `json:"requests"`
	Errors        int64            `json:"errors"`
	AuthFailures  int64            `json:"auth_failures"`
	EngineCalls   int64            `json:"engine_calls"`
	EngineErrors  int64            `json:"engine_errors"`
	Routes        map[string]int64 `json:"routes"`
}

// Snapshot copies the current counters out of the registry.
func (r *Registry) Snapshot() Snapshot {
	routes := make(map[string]int64)
	r.mu.Lock()
	keys := make([]string, 0, len(r.routes))
	for k := range r.routes {
		keys = append(keys, k)
	}
	sort.Strings(keys)
	for _, k := range keys {
		routes[k] = r.routes[k].Load()
	}
	r.mu.Unlock()
	return Snapshot{
		UptimeSeconds: int64(time.Since(r.startedAt).Seconds()),
		Requests:      r.requests.Load(),
		Errors:        r.errors.Load(),
		AuthFailures:  r.authFails.Load(),
		EngineCalls:   r.engineCalls.Load(),
		EngineErrors:  r.engineErrors.Load(),
		Routes:        routes,
	}
}

===== END FILE: platform/internal/diag/diag.go =====

===== FILE: platform/internal/diag/diag_test.go =====
package diag_test

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/David2024patton/itak-torch-rebuild/platform/internal/diag"
)

func TestRegistryCounts(t *testing.T) {
	r := diag.New()
	r.RecordRequest("GET /v1/models")
	r.RecordRequest("GET /v1/models")
	r.RecordRequest("POST /v1/chat/completions")
	r.RecordError()
	r.RecordAuthFailure()
	r.RecordEngineCall()
	r.RecordEngineError()

	s := r.Snapshot()
	if s.Requests != 3 || s.Errors != 1 || s.AuthFailures != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("Snapshot = %+v, want requests=3 errors=1 auth_failures=1", s)
	}
	if s.EngineCalls != 1 || s.EngineErrors != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("engine counters = %d/%d, want 1/1", s.EngineCalls, s.EngineErrors)
	}
	if s.Routes["GET /v1/models"] != 2 || s.Routes["POST /v1/chat/completions"] != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("route counts = %v", s.Routes)
	}
}

===== FILE: platform/internal/engine/engine.go =====
// Package engine defines the seam between the Go platform and the Rust
// hot loop.
//
// The platform never generates a token itself. It calls a Client; the
// implementations are Unavailable (wired when no engine is configured)
// and UnixClient, which speaks the socket protocol to the Rust engine
// process: handshake, ping, the debug self-report, streamed
// generation, and the embed operation. Every failure mode is a named error so handlers can map
// it to an honest HTTP status instead of inventing a success response,
// the failure pattern the old platform kept falling into (fake LoRA
// loads, an itak-quant that printed SUCCESS and wrote nothing).
package engine

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
)

// Named engine errors. Handlers switch on these with errors.Is.
var (
	// ErrUnavailable means no engine is configured or reachable.
	ErrUnavailable = errors.New("engine: unavailable")
	// ErrNotImplemented means the client exists but the operation is not
	// built yet. It is a deliberate, named refusal, never a fake success.
	ErrNotImplemented = errors.New("engine: operation not implemented")
	// ErrHandshake means the socket client connected but the protocol
	// handshake failed (wrong peer, wrong protocol version).
	ErrHandshake = errors.New("engine: handshake failed")
	// ErrClosed means the client was used after Close.
	ErrClosed = errors.New("engine: client closed")
	// ErrBadRequest means the engine rejected the request as invalid.
	ErrBadRequest = errors.New("engine: bad request")
	// ErrEngineDied means the engine process or its worker died,
	// before the generation started or mid-stream. Supervision
	// (TODO T-9.11) is what brings it back; this error is how the
	// death is named to the caller, never a silently closed stream.
	ErrEngineDied = errors.New("engine: engine died")
	// ErrGenerationFailed means the engine refused or failed a
	// generation it had already started (a forward or detokenize
	// failure at a decode step). It arrives as the terminal
	// TokenEvent's Err, not as Generate's return value.
	ErrGenerationFailed = errors.New("engine: generation failed")
	// ErrEngineBusy means the engine refused the job before it
	// started: every serving slot is running and the bounded job
	// queue is full (TODO T-9.14). The refusal is explicit and the
	// caller may retry; nothing was queued silently.
	ErrEngineBusy = errors.New("engine: busy")
	// ErrNoChatTemplate means the model file carries no chat
	// template (TODO T-9.16). The platform falls back to role
	// flattening only with this named outcome in hand, never by
	// silently assuming a format.
	ErrNoChatTemplate = errors.New("engine: no chat template")
	// ErrTimeout means the engine did not answer within the
	// exchange deadline. A slow but healthy engine reports as a
	// timeout, never as a handshake failure: the handshake is a
	// different event and mislabeling it sends operators hunting
	// for a protocol fault that does not exist.
	ErrTimeout = errors.New("engine: timed out waiting for the engine")
	// ErrFrameTooLarge means a peer sent a frame past the protocol
	// size cap without terminating it. The read refuses by name
	// instead of buffering without bound.
	ErrFrameTooLarge = errors.New("engine: frame exceeds the maximum size")
	// ErrUntrustedSocket means the socket file at the dial path is
	// not provably the engine's own: its owner is not this process's
	// uid, or its permissions are wider than owner-only (0600). The
	// dial refuses before connecting, because anything answering on
	// an unverified socket could be a squatter that receives prompt
	// traffic and forges replies; the handshake alone cannot tell
	// the real engine from an impostor that speaks the protocol.
	ErrUntrustedSocket = errors.New("engine: socket is not owned by this process with owner-only permissions")
)

// GenerateRequest is one completion job handed to the engine. The
// sampling parity fields (TODO T-9.13) are pointers so an explicit
// zero (a seed of 0, a penalty of 0) is distinguishable from an
// absent field all the way to the wire.
type GenerateRequest struct {
	Model       string   `json:"model"`
	Prompt      string   `json:"prompt"`
	MaxTokens   int      `json:"max_tokens,omitempty"`
	Temperature float64  `json:"temperature,omitempty"`
	TopP        float64  `json:"top_p,omitempty"`
	Stop        []string `json:"stop,omitempty"`
	// Seed makes a sampled run reproducible; nil lets the engine
	// seed from its clock.
	Seed *uint64 `json:"seed,omitempty"`
	// TopK caps the sampler's candidate set; nil or 0 disables it.
	TopK *int `json:"top_k,omitempty"`
	// PresencePenalty and FrequencyPenalty are the OpenAI-form
	// repetition penalties; nil or 0 disables each.
	PresencePenalty  *float64 `json:"presence_penalty,omitempty"`
	FrequencyPenalty *float64 `json:"frequency_penalty,omitempty"`
}

// TokenEvent is one streamed piece of a generation. Done marks the final
// event; FinishReason is set on it ("stop", "length", ...).
//
// Err is set on exactly one kind of event: the terminal error event.
// When a generation fails after it has started (the engine reports a
// named failure, or the engine dies mid-stream), the client delivers
// one last event with Err non-nil and Done false, then closes the
// channel. A stream that ends without either a Done event or an Err
// event is a contract violation by the client implementation, and
// handlers treat it as an engine death rather than a short success.
type TokenEvent struct {
	Text         string `json:"text"`
	TokenID      int32  `json:"token_id"`
	Done         bool   `json:"done"`
	FinishReason string `json:"finish_reason,omitempty"`
	// Err is the terminal failure, set only on the final event of a
	// failed generation. It is never serialized; the wire form is
	// the protocol's error frame.
	Err error `json:"-"`
}

// EmbedRequest asks for vectors for one or more inputs.
type EmbedRequest struct {
	Model string   `json:"model"`
	Input []string `json:"input"`
}

// EmbedResponse carries one vector per input, in order.
type EmbedResponse struct {
	Model   string      `json:"model"`
	Vectors [][]float32 `json:"embeddings"`
}

// HealthStatus is the engine's answer to a health probe.
type HealthStatus struct {
	OK     bool   `json:"ok"`
	Detail string `json:"detail"`
}

// ChatTemplate is the model's own chat template as the engine
// serves it: the template text from the GGUF metadata and the
// special-token texts its variables (bos_token, eos_token) refer
// to. The platform renders it; the engine only reports it.
type ChatTemplate struct {
	Template string `json:"template"`
	BOSToken string `json:"bos_token"`
	EOSToken string `json:"eos_token"`
}

// Client is the platform's only view of the token engine.
//
// Generate returns a channel of token events. A non-nil error return
// means generation never started. A failure after that is delivered
// as one terminal TokenEvent with Err set (see TokenEvent), and
// implementations close the channel exactly once in all paths.
type Client interface {
	Generate(ctx context.Context, req GenerateRequest) (<-chan TokenEvent, error)
	Embed(ctx context.Context, req EmbedRequest) (EmbedResponse, error)
	Health(ctx context.Context) (HealthStatus, error)
}

// Unavailable is the Client wired when no engine is configured. Every
// method refuses with ErrUnavailable so routes surface a named
// engine-unavailable error instead of a fabricated answer.
type Unavailable struct{}

// Generate implements Client.
func (Unavailable) Generate(context.Context, GenerateRequest) (<-chan TokenEvent, error) {
	return nil, ErrUnavailable
}

// Embed implements Client.
func (Unavailable) Embed(context.Context, EmbedRequest) (EmbedResponse, error) {
	return EmbedResponse{}, ErrUnavailable
}

// Health implements Client: it reports not-OK rather than erroring, so
// /healthz can show platform-up / engine-down distinctly.
func (Unavailable) Health(context.Context) (HealthStatus, error) {
	return HealthStatus{OK: false, Detail: "no engine configured"}, nil
}

package engine_test

import (
	"bufio"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"net"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"

func TestUnavailableRefusesEverything(t *testing.T) {
	var c engine.Client = engine.Unavailable{}
	ctx := context.Background()

	if _, err := c.Generate(ctx, engine.GenerateRequest{}); !errors.Is(err, engine.ErrUnavailable) {
		t.Fatalf("Generate err = %v, want ErrUnavailable", err)
	}
	if _, err := c.Embed(ctx, engine.EmbedRequest{}); !errors.Is(err, engine.ErrUnavailable) {
		t.Fatalf("Embed err = %v, want ErrUnavailable", err)
	}
	h, err := c.Health(ctx)
	if err != nil || h.OK {
		t.Fatalf("Health = %+v, %v; want OK=false, nil error", h, err)
	}
}

// fakeEngine serves the socket protocol with configurable replies.
// The socket is pinned to 0600 after binding, as the real engine
// pins its own: the platform refuses to dial anything looser.
func fakeEngine(t *testing.T, ackProto int, ackOp string) string {
	t.Helper()
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "engine.sock")
	ln, err := net.Listen("unix", path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("listen: %v", err)
	}
	if err := os.Chmod(path, 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("chmod socket: %v", err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = ln.Close() })
	go func() {
		for {
			conn, err := ln.Accept()
			if err != nil {
				return
			}
			go serveConn(conn, ackProto, ackOp)
		}
	}()
	return path
}

func serveConn(conn net.Conn, ackProto int, ackOp string) {
	defer func() { _ = conn.Close() }()
	r := bufio.NewReader(conn)
	write := func(reply map[string]any) bool {
		out, _ := json.Marshal(reply)
		_, err := conn.Write(append(out, '\n'))
		return err == nil
	}
	for {
		line, err := r.ReadBytes('\n')
		if err != nil {
			return
		}
		var f struct {
			Op     string   `json:"op"`
			Prompt string   `json:"prompt"`
			Input  []string `json:"input"`
		}
		if err := json.Unmarshal(line, &f); err != nil {
			return
		}
		switch f.Op {
		case "hello":
			if !write(map[string]any{"op": ackOp, "proto": ackProto}) {
				return
			}
		case "ping":
			if !write(map[string]any{"op": "pong"}) {
				return
			}
		case "embed":
			if !serveEmbed(write, f.Input) {
				return
			}
		case "debug":
			if !write(map[string]any{"op": "debug_info", "model": "fake-1b", "generations": 3}) {
				return
			}
		case "chat_template":
			if !write(map[string]any{
				"op": "chat_template", "template": "{% for message in messages %}X{% endfor %}",
				"bos_token": "<s>", "eos_token": "</s>",
			}) {
				return
			}
		case "generate":
			if !serveGenerate(write, f.Prompt) {
				return
			}
		default:
			if !write(map[string]any{"op": "error", "message": "unknown op"}) {
				return
			}
		}
	}
}

// serveEmbed answers an embed request with one fixed vector per
// input; an input of "refuse" scripts the named refusal an engine
// without the operation (or with a full queue) would send.
func serveEmbed(write func(map[string]any) bool, inputs []string) bool {
	vecs := make([][]float32, 0, len(inputs))
	for _, in := range inputs {
		if in == "refuse" {
			return write(map[string]any{
				"op": "error", "code": "not_implemented", "message": "embed is not built",
			})
		}
		vecs = append(vecs, []float32{0.1, 0.2, 0.3})
	}
	return write(map[string]any{"op": "embeddings", "model": "fake-1b", "embeddings": vecs})
}

// serveGenerate scripts the generate stream off the prompt text, so
// one fake covers the success path and both error placements.
func serveGenerate(write func(map[string]any) bool, prompt string) bool {
	switch {
	case strings.Contains(prompt, "err-overflow"):
		return write(map[string]any{
			"op": "error", "code": "context_overflow",
			"message": "prompt of 9 tokens plus max_tokens 4 exceeds the context length 8",
		})
	case strings.Contains(prompt, "err-busy"):
		return write(map[string]any{
			"op": "error", "code": "engine_busy",
			"message": "engine busy: 1 slot(s) running and the queue is full (max_queued 0)",
		})
	case strings.Contains(prompt, "err-mid"):
		if !write(map[string]any{"op": "token", "text": " Paris", "token_id": 13796}) {
			return false
		}
		return write(map[string]any{
			"op": "error", "code": "forward_failed", "message": "decode step 2: boom",
		})
	case strings.Contains(prompt, "die-close"):
		// One token, then the connection drops with no frame at
		// all: the engine process dying mid-generation.
		if !write(map[string]any{"op": "token", "text": " Paris", "token_id": 13796}) {
			return false
		}
		return false
	default:
		if !write(map[string]any{"op": "token", "text": " Paris", "token_id": 13796}) {
			return false
		}
		if !write(map[string]any{"op": "token", "text": ". It", "token_id": 26}) {
			return false
		}
		return write(map[string]any{
			"op": "token", "text": "", "token_id": 0, "done": true, "finish_reason": "stop",
		})
	}
}

func dial(t *testing.T, path string) *engine.UnixClient {
	t.Helper()
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	c, err := engine.DialUnix(ctx, path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("DialUnix: %v", err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = c.Close() })
	return c
}

func TestUnixGenerateStreamsTokens(t *testing.T) {
	c := dial(t, fakeEngine(t, 1, "hello_ack"))
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	ch, err := c.Generate(ctx, engine.GenerateRequest{Model: "fake-1b", Prompt: "The capital of France is"})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Generate: %v", err)
	}
	var events []engine.TokenEvent
	for ev := range ch {
		events = append(events, ev)
	}
	if len(events) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("got %d events, want 3: %+v", len(events), events)
	}
	if events[0].Text != " Paris" || events[0].TokenID != 13796 || events[0].Done {
		t.Fatalf("event 0 = %+v, want the Paris token event", events[0])
	}
	if events[1].Text != ". It" || events[1].TokenID != 26 {
		t.Fatalf("event 1 = %+v", events[1])
	}
	if !events[2].Done || events[2].FinishReason != "stop" {
		t.Fatalf("event 2 = %+v, want done with finish_reason stop", events[2])
	}
}

func TestUnixGenerateMidStreamErrorIsTerminalEvent(t *testing.T) {
	c := dial(t, fakeEngine(t, 1, "hello_ack"))
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	ch, err := c.Generate(ctx, engine.GenerateRequest{Prompt: "err-mid please"})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Generate: %v", err)
	}
	var events []engine.TokenEvent
	for ev := range ch {
		events = append(events, ev)
	}
	if len(events) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("events = %+v, want one token event and one terminal error event", events)
	}
	if events[0].Text != " Paris" || events[0].Done || events[0].Err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("event 0 = %+v, want the Paris token event", events[0])
	}
	last := events[1]
	if last.Done || !errors.Is(last.Err, engine.ErrGenerationFailed) {
		t.Fatalf("terminal event = %+v (err %v), want ErrGenerationFailed and no done", last, last.Err)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(last.Err.Error(), "decode step 2") {
		t.Fatalf("terminal error = %v, want the engine's message carried", last.Err)
	}
}

// capturingEngine is a fake that records the raw generate frame it
// receives, so a test can assert exactly what crossed the wire.
func capturingEngine(t *testing.T) (string, func() map[string]any) {
	t.Helper()
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "engine.sock")
	ln, err := net.Listen("unix", path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("listen: %v", err)
	}
	if err := os.Chmod(path, 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("chmod socket: %v", err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = ln.Close() })
	var mu sync.Mutex
	var lastGen map[string]any
	go func() {
		for {
			conn, err := ln.Accept()
			if err != nil {
				return
			}
			go func(conn net.Conn) {
				defer func() { _ = conn.Close() }()
				r := bufio.NewReader(conn)
				for {
					line, err := r.ReadBytes('\n')
					if err != nil {
						return
					}
					var f map[string]any
					if json.Unmarshal(line, &f) != nil {
						return
					}
					var reply map[string]any
					switch f["op"] {
					case "hello":
						reply = map[string]any{"op": "hello_ack", "proto": 1}
					case "generate":
						mu.Lock()
						lastGen = f
						mu.Unlock()
						serveGenerate(func(m map[string]any) bool {
							out, _ := json.Marshal(m)
							_, err := conn.Write(append(out, '\n'))
							return err == nil
						}, "")
						return
					default:
						reply = map[string]any{"op": "pong"}
					}
					out, _ := json.Marshal(reply)
					if _, err := conn.Write(append(out, '\n')); err != nil {
						return
					}
				}
			}(conn)
		}
	}()
	return path, func() map[string]any {
		mu.Lock()
		defer mu.Unlock()
		return lastGen
	}
}

func TestUnixGenerateSamplingFieldsCrossTheWire(t *testing.T) {
	path, lastGen := capturingEngine(t)
	c := dial(t, path)
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
	defer cancel()

	seed, topK := uint64(42), 40
	pres, freq := 0.5, -0.25
	ch, err := c.Generate(ctx, engine.GenerateRequest{
		Prompt: "x", Seed: &seed, TopK: &topK,
		PresencePenalty: &pres, FrequencyPenalty: &freq,
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Generate: %v", err)
	}
	for range ch {
	}
	frame := lastGen()
	if frame == nil {
		t.Fatal("fake engine captured no generate frame")
	}
	if frame["seed"] != float64(42) || frame["top_k"] != float64(40) ||
		frame["presence_penalty"] != 0.5 || frame["frequency_penalty"] != -0.25 {
		t.Fatalf("generate frame sampling fields = %v, want seed 42, top_k 40, penalties 0.5/-0.25", frame)
	}

	// Absent fields stay absent: an unset seed must not become a
	// wire 0 the engine would mistake for an explicit seed.
	ch, err = c.Generate(ctx, engine.GenerateRequest{Prompt: "x"})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Generate: %v", err)
	}
	for range ch {
	}
	frame = lastGen()
	for _, key := range []string{"seed", "top_k", "presence_penalty", "frequency_penalty"} {
		if _, present := frame[key]; present {
			t.Fatalf("unset %s leaked onto the wire: %v", key, frame)
		}
	}
}

// noTemplateEngine serves hello and answers the chat_template op
// the way an engine whose model file carries no template does.
func noTemplateEngine(t *testing.T) string {

	ln, err := net.Listen("unix", path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("listen: %v", err)
	}
	if err := os.Chmod(path, 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("chmod socket: %v", err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = ln.Close() })
	go func() {
		for {
			conn, err := ln.Accept()
			if err != nil {
				return
			}
			go func(conn net.Conn) {
				defer func() { _ = conn.Close() }()
				r := bufio.NewReader(conn)
				for {
					line, err := r.ReadBytes('\n')
					if err != nil {
						return
					}
					var f struct {
						Op string `json:"op"`
					}
					if json.Unmarshal(line, &f) != nil {
						return
					}
					var reply map[string]any
					switch f.Op {
					case "hello":
						reply = map[string]any{"op": "hello_ack", "proto": 1}
					case "chat_template":
						reply = map[string]any{
							"op": "error", "code": "no_chat_template",
							"message": "the model file carries no tokenizer.chat_template",

					}

					if _, err := conn.Write(append(out, '\n')); err != nil {
						return
					}
				}
			}(conn)

	}()

}

func TestUnixDebugInfo(t *testing.T) {
	c := dial(t, fakeEngine(t, 1, "hello_ack"))
	info, err := c.DebugInfo(context.Background())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("DebugInfo: %v", err)
	}
	if info["model"] != "fake-1b" {
		t.Fatalf("debug info = %v, want model fake-1b", info)
	}
}

func TestUnixHandshakeRejectsWrongProtocol(t *testing.T) {
	path := fakeEngine(t, 99, "hello_ack")
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	if _, err := engine.DialUnix(ctx, path); !errors.Is(err, engine.ErrHandshake) {
		t.Fatalf("DialUnix err = %v, want ErrHandshake", err)
	}
}

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)

	}

func TestUnixDialMissingSocketIsUnavailable(t *testing.T) {

func TestUnixUseAfterClose(t *testing.T) {
	c := dial(t, fakeEngine(t, 1, "hello_ack"))
	if err := c.Close(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Close: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := c.Health(context.Background()); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Health after close should report, not error: %v", err)
	}
	// Second Close is a no-op, not an error.
	if err := c.Close(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("second Close: %v", err)
	}
}

===== FILE: platform/internal/engine/socket_other.go =====
//go:build !unix

package engine

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
)

// checkSocketTrust on non-unix platforms cannot read the socket
// file's owner uid from stat output, so it enforces the arms it can:
// the path must be a socket with owner-only (0600) permissions.
// Supported serving targets are unix (see socket_unix.go for the
// full check); this fallback keeps the seam building everywhere the
// Go toolchain targets without silently skipping verification.
func checkSocketTrust(socketPath string, _ int) error {
	fi, err := os.Stat(socketPath)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: stat %s: %w", ErrUnavailable, socketPath, err)
	}
	if fi.Mode()&os.ModeSocket == 0 || fi.Mode().Perm() != 0o600 {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: mode %04o; want a socket with mode 0600",
			ErrUntrustedSocket, socketPath, fi.Mode().Perm())
	}
	return nil
}

===== END FILE: platform/internal/engine/socket_other.go =====

===== FILE: platform/internal/engine/socket_unix.go =====
//go:build unix

package engine

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"syscall"
)

// checkSocketTrust authenticates the engine end of the socket before
// anything is dialed, mirroring the two checks the Rust engine
// enforces on its side of the same socket (crates/itak-engine/src/
// main.rs: bind_socket pins the file to 0600, and check_peer refuses
// a peer whose kernel-reported uid differs). The handshake alone
// cannot authenticate the peer: the protocol shapes are public, so
// any process that binds the predictable socket path during a
// restart window answers hello_ack and passes. The kernel-checked
// facts about the socket FILE are what a squatter cannot fake:
//
//   - the file must be a socket;
//   - its owner uid must equal this process's uid (the engine runs
//     as the same user in every supported deployment, exactly the
//     engine side's peer rule);
//   - its permissions must be exactly owner-only (0600), the mode
//     the engine pins after binding.
//
// Any mismatch refuses by name with ErrUntrustedSocket before the
// dial, so no prompt byte ever reaches an unverified peer. The
// residual race (the file swapped between this stat and the dial)
// is backstopped from the other direction: only a same-uid process
// can create the replacement (the directory entry and the inode are
// both uid-gated), and the real engine refuses other-uid peers
// outright, so a same-uid impostor is inside the trust boundary the
// engine itself already accepts.
func checkSocketTrust(socketPath string, ownUID int) error {
	fi, err := os.Stat(socketPath)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: stat %s: %w", ErrUnavailable, socketPath, err)
	}
	uid, ok := socketFileUID(fi)
	if !ok {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: cannot read the socket file's owner", ErrUntrustedSocket, socketPath)
	}
	if !socketTrustOK(fi.Mode(), uid, ownUID) {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: owner uid %d (this process runs as uid %d), mode %04o; want the engine's own socket, uid %d, mode 0600",
			ErrUntrustedSocket, socketPath, uid, ownUID, fi.Mode().Perm(), ownUID)
	}
	return nil
}

// socketTrustOK is the pure trust predicate, split out so the uid
// arm can be pinned by unit tests: a test process runs as one user
// and cannot fabricate a socket file owned by another uid.
func socketTrustOK(mode os.FileMode, fileUID, ownUID int) bool {
	return mode&os.ModeSocket != 0 && fileUID == ownUID && mode.Perm() == 0o600
}

// socketFileUID extracts the owner's uid from stat output. On every
// unix platform the platform builds for, FileInfo.Sys() is
// *syscall.Stat_t carrying the Uid field.
func socketFileUID(fi os.FileInfo) (int, bool) {
	st, ok := fi.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t)
	if !ok {
		return 0, false
	}
	return int(st.Uid), true
}

===== END FILE: platform/internal/engine/socket_unix.go =====

===== FILE: platform/internal/engine/socket_unix_test.go =====
//go:build unix

package engine

import (
	"net"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

// socketTrustTestListener binds a socket owned by this process and
// pinned to 0600, the state the real engine leaves at its path.
func socketTrustTestListener(t *testing.T) string {
	t.Helper()
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "e.sock")
	ln, err := net.Listen("unix", path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("listen: %v", err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = ln.Close() })
	if err := os.Chmod(path, 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("chmod socket: %v", err)
	}
	return path
}

// TestSocketTrustOK pins the trust predicate arm by arm. The uid
// arm is pinned here rather than end to end because a test process
// runs as one user and cannot fabricate a socket file owned by
// another uid; the mode and socket-type arms are additionally
// covered end to end through DialUnix in unix_seam_test.go.
func TestSocketTrustOK(t *testing.T) {
	const sock os.FileMode = os.ModeSocket
	cases := []struct {
		name            string
		mode            os.FileMode
		fileUID, ownUID int
		want            bool
	}{
		{"the engine's own socket", sock | 0o600, 1000, 1000, true},
		{"another uid's socket", sock | 0o600, 1001, 1000, false},
		{"own socket, group-readable", sock | 0o640, 1000, 1000, false},
		{"own socket, umask default", sock | 0o770, 1000, 1000, false},
		{"own socket, world-writable", sock | 0o602, 1000, 1000, false},
		{"regular file at 0600", 0o600, 1000, 1000, false},
		{"another uid, loose mode", sock | 0o777, 0, 1000, false},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		if got := socketTrustOK(tc.mode, tc.fileUID, tc.ownUID); got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("%s: socketTrustOK(mode=%v, fileUID=%d, ownUID=%d) = %v, want %v",
				tc.name, tc.mode, tc.fileUID, tc.ownUID, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
}

// TestCheckSocketTrustArms exercises the stat wrapper directly: a
// socket this process owns at 0600 passes under its own uid and
// refuses under any other uid (the direction a test CAN fabricate:
// claiming to be a different process than the file's owner).
func TestCheckSocketTrustArms(t *testing.T) {
	path := socketTrustTestListener(t)
	own := os.Getuid()
	if err := checkSocketTrust(path, own); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("checkSocketTrust(own uid) = %v, want nil", err)
	}
	if err := checkSocketTrust(path, own+1); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("checkSocketTrust(other uid) = nil, want ErrUntrustedSocket")
	}
}
