===== FILE: platform/internal/server/server.go =====
// Package server is the platform's HTTP face.
//
// The shape is the correction to the old platform's serving layer:
//
//   - Binds where main tells it (127.0.0.1 by default there); this
//     package never widens the bind on its own.
//   - Every route except /healthz sits behind the auth middleware.
//   - Handlers validate requests fully before touching the engine, and
//     engine failures map to named, honest HTTP errors. No handler
//     fabricates a success: unconfigured engine = 503 engine_unavailable,
//     unimplemented engine op = 501 not_implemented.
//   - Requests flow through the scheduler's priority lanes and
//     non-streaming completions through the exact-match response
//     cache — except unseeded sampled requests (temperature > 0
//     with no seed): those bypass the cache on both sides, because
//     replaying the first caller's sample would freeze the
//     variation the caller asked the temperature for. Seeded and
//     temperature-0 requests are deterministic and do cache.
//   - Every operational limit (generation cap and deadline, body
//     size, header and idle timeouts, lane queue caps, cache size)
//     is operator config with a default, threaded from torchd's
//     flags; nothing is a compiled-in literal.
//   - /debug (behind auth) serves the diag registry plus scheduler and
//     cache stats, so the running system can explain itself.
package server

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/rand"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"log/slog"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/David2024patton/itak-torch-rebuild/platform/internal/auth"
	"github.com/David2024patton/itak-torch-rebuild/platform/internal/cache"
	"github.com/David2024patton/itak-torch-rebuild/platform/internal/chattemplate"
	"github.com/David2024patton/itak-torch-rebuild/platform/internal/diag"
	"github.com/David2024patton/itak-torch-rebuild/platform/internal/engine"
	"github.com/David2024patton/itak-torch-rebuild/platform/internal/scheduler"
)

// Defaults for the operational limits Config leaves unset. They are
// the values torchd's flags default to as well; the flags are how an
// operator changes them, never a rebuild.
const (
	defaultMaxTokensCap       = 8192
	defaultGenerationTimeout  = time.Hour
	defaultMaxBodyBytes       = 1 << 20 // 1 MiB
	defaultReadHeaderTimeout  = 10 * time.Second
	defaultIdleTimeout        = 90 * time.Second
	defaultMaxWaitersPerLane  = 128
	defaultCacheMaxEntries    = 1024
	defaultCachePurgeInterval = time.Minute
)

// Config wires the server. Zero values get safe defaults in New.
type Config struct {
	// Engine is the token engine client. Nil means none configured:
	// routes then refuse with engine_unavailable.
	Engine engine.Client
	// APIKey is required on every route except /healthz. Empty fails
	// closed (the middleware rejects everything).
	APIKey string
	// Models is the advertised model list for /v1/models.
	Models []string
	// CacheTTL is the response-cache retention; <= 0 disables caching.
	CacheTTL time.Duration
	// MaxConcurrent bounds simultaneous engine jobs; < 1 becomes 4.
	MaxConcurrent int
	// MaxTokensCap bounds one request's max_tokens; a request past
	// the cap is refused by name before the engine is touched.
	// < 1 becomes 8192.
	MaxTokensCap int
	// GenerationTimeout is the per-generation wall-clock deadline:
	// one generation may hold its engine slot at most this long.
	// <= 0 becomes 1 hour.
	GenerationTimeout time.Duration
	// MaxBodyBytes caps one request body. < 1 becomes 1 MiB.
	MaxBodyBytes int64
	// ReadHeaderTimeout bounds how long a client may take to send
	// request headers. <= 0 becomes 10 seconds.
	ReadHeaderTimeout time.Duration
	// IdleTimeout bounds how long an idle keep-alive connection is
	// held open. <= 0 becomes 90 seconds.
	IdleTimeout time.Duration
	// MaxWaitersPerLane caps each scheduler lane's wait queue; a
	// request past the cap is refused as engine_busy. < 1 becomes 128.
	MaxWaitersPerLane int
	// CacheMaxEntries caps the response cache's size. < 1 becomes 1024.
	CacheMaxEntries int
	// CachePurgeInterval is how often the cache janitor runs
	// PurgeExpired. <= 0 becomes 1 minute.
	CachePurgeInterval time.Duration
	// ChatTemplate, when set, is the chat template every chat
	// request is rendered with (TODO T-9.16), overriding the
	// engine-reported one. ChatBOSToken and ChatEOSToken supply its
	// special-token variables. When unset, the template comes from
	// the engine (the model's own GGUF template); a model with no
	// template falls back to role flattening, visibly, in /debug.
	ChatTemplate string
	// ChatBOSToken is the bos_token value for a configured template.
	ChatBOSToken string
	// ChatEOSToken is the eos_token value for a configured template.
	ChatEOSToken string
	// Logger receives handler diagnostics; nil uses slog.Default().
	Logger *slog.Logger
}

// Server is the wired HTTP handler plus its modules.
type Server struct {
	cfg   Config
	log   *slog.Logger
	eng   engine.Client
	diag  *diag.Registry
	cache *cache.Cache[[]byte]
	sched *scheduler.Scheduler
	mux   http.Handler

	// Cache janitor lifecycle: the goroutine runs while the server
	// does, and Close stops it before closing the scheduler.
	cacheStop chan struct{}
	cacheDone chan struct{}
	closeOnce sync.Once

	// Chat template resolution (TODO T-9.16): resolved lazily and
	// cached once the outcome is definitive (a template, or the
	// engine's named no-template answer). Transient fetch errors
	// surface to the request that hit them and are retried on the
	// next request rather than cached. tplMu guards the cached
	// outcome only; it is never held across the fetch.
	tplMu     sync.Mutex
	tpl       *engine.ChatTemplate
	tplSource string // "", "config", "engine", "none"
	tplDone   bool
}

// New builds the route table and modules.
func New(cfg Config) *Server {
	if cfg.Logger == nil {
		cfg.Logger = slog.Default()
	}
	if cfg.MaxConcurrent < 1 {
		cfg.MaxConcurrent = 4
	}
	if cfg.MaxTokensCap < 1 {
		cfg.MaxTokensCap = defaultMaxTokensCap
	}
	if cfg.GenerationTimeout <= 0 {
		cfg.GenerationTimeout = defaultGenerationTimeout
	}
	if cfg.MaxBodyBytes < 1 {
		cfg.MaxBodyBytes = defaultMaxBodyBytes
	}
	if cfg.ReadHeaderTimeout <= 0 {
		cfg.ReadHeaderTimeout = defaultReadHeaderTimeout
	}
	if cfg.IdleTimeout <= 0 {
		cfg.IdleTimeout = defaultIdleTimeout
	}
	if cfg.MaxWaitersPerLane < 1 {
		cfg.MaxWaitersPerLane = defaultMaxWaitersPerLane
	}
	if cfg.CacheMaxEntries < 1 {
		cfg.CacheMaxEntries = defaultCacheMaxEntries
	}
	if cfg.CachePurgeInterval <= 0 {
		cfg.CachePurgeInterval = defaultCachePurgeInterval
	}
	eng := cfg.Engine
	if eng == nil {
		eng = engine.Unavailable{}
	}
	s := &Server{
		cfg:   cfg,
		log:   cfg.Logger,
		eng:   eng,
		diag:  diag.New(),
		cache: cache.NewWithLimit[[]byte](cfg.CacheTTL, cfg.CacheMaxEntries),
		sched: scheduler.New(cfg.MaxConcurrent, cfg.MaxWaitersPerLane),
	}
	if cfg.CacheTTL > 0 {
		s.cacheStop = make(chan struct{})
		s.cacheDone = make(chan struct{})
		go s.cacheJanitor()
	}

	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /healthz", s.handleHealthz)
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/models", s.handleModels)
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /v1/chat/completions", s.handleChatCompletions)
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /v1/embeddings", s.handleEmbeddings)
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /debug", s.handleDebug)

	mw := auth.New(cfg.APIKey, s.diag, "/healthz")
	s.mux = mw.Wrap(mux)
	return s
}

// Handler returns the fully wrapped route table.
func (s *Server) Handler() http.Handler { return s.mux }

// Close stops the cache janitor, then the scheduler, failing any
// queued requests. It is safe to call more than once.
func (s *Server) Close() {
	s.closeOnce.Do(func() {
		if s.cacheStop != nil {
			close(s.cacheStop)
			<-s.cacheDone
		}
		s.sched.Close()
	})
}

// cacheJanitor is the production caller of the cache's PurgeExpired:
// expired entries leave on the configured interval instead of only
// when their key happens to be read again.
func (s *Server) cacheJanitor() {
	defer close(s.cacheDone)
	t := time.NewTicker(s.cfg.CachePurgeInterval)
	defer t.Stop()
	for {
		select {
		case <-s.cacheStop:
			return
		case <-t.C:
			if n := s.cache.PurgeExpired(); n > 0 {
				s.log.Debug("response cache janitor purged expired entries", "count", n)
			}
		}
	}
}

// HTTPServer builds the http.Server with production timeouts. There is
// deliberately no WriteTimeout or ReadTimeout: generations stream for
// minutes (bounded by the per-generation deadline instead). Header
// reads and idle conns are bounded by the configured values.
func (s *Server) HTTPServer(addr string) *http.Server {
	return &http.Server{
		Addr:              addr,
		Handler:           s.mux,
		ReadHeaderTimeout: s.cfg.ReadHeaderTimeout,
		IdleTimeout:       s.cfg.IdleTimeout,
	}
}

// --- shared helpers ----------------------------------------------------

type errorBody struct {
	Error apiError `json:"error"`
}

type apiError struct {
	Code    string `json:"code"`
	Message string `json:"message"`
	Param   string `json:"param,omitempty"`
}

func writeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, v any) {
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	w.WriteHeader(status)
	_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)
}

func (s *Server) writeError(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, code, message, param string) {
	s.diag.RecordError()
	writeJSON(w, status, errorBody{Error: apiError{Code: code, Message: message, Param: param}})
}

func (s *Server) invalidRequest(w http.ResponseWriter, message, param string) {
	s.writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid_request", message, param)
}

// engineErrorStatus maps a named engine error to its honest HTTP
// status and wire code. It is the single mapping both the plain
// error path and the streaming terminal-error frame use, so a
// failure carries the same name however it surfaces.
func engineErrorStatus(err error) (status int, code string) {
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, engine.ErrUnavailable):
		return http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "engine_unavailable"
	case errors.Is(err, engine.ErrNotImplemented):
		return http.StatusNotImplemented, "not_implemented"
	case errors.Is(err, engine.ErrBadRequest):
		return http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid_request"
	case errors.Is(err, engine.ErrEngineDied):
		return http.StatusBadGateway, "engine_died"
	case errors.Is(err, engine.ErrEngineBusy):
		return http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "engine_busy"
	case errors.Is(err, engine.ErrGenerationFailed):
		return http.StatusBadGateway, "generation_failed"
	case errors.Is(err, engine.ErrTimeout):
		return http.StatusGatewayTimeout, "engine_timeout"
	case errors.Is(err, engine.ErrFrameTooLarge):
		return http.StatusBadGateway, "engine_frame_too_large"
	default:
		return http.StatusBadGateway, "engine_error"
	}
}

// engineError maps a named engine error to its honest HTTP form.
func (s *Server) engineError(w http.ResponseWriter, err error) {
	s.diag.RecordEngineError()
	status, code := engineErrorStatus(err)
	if status == http.StatusBadGateway && code == "engine_error" {
		s.log.Error("engine call failed", "err", err)
	}
	s.writeError(w, status, code, err.Error(), "")
}

func (s *Server) decodeBody(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, v any) error {
	r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, s.cfg.MaxBodyBytes)
	dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
	if err := dec.Decode(v); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("body is not valid JSON: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}

func newID(prefix string) string {
	var b [8]byte
	if _, err := rand.Read(b[:]); err != nil {
		return prefix + "static"
	}
	return prefix + hex.EncodeToString(b[:])
}

// acquire takes a scheduler slot for an engine call, writing the error
// response itself when the slot cannot be had. ok=false means the
// handler must return immediately.
//
// Priority is assigned here, server-side, and every HTTP request takes
// the normal lane: the high lane is reserved for in-process operator
// work, and a client header must never be able to claim it (the old
// X-Torch-Priority header is ignored).
func (s *Server) acquire(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (release func(), ok bool) {
	release, err := s.sched.Acquire(r.Context(), scheduler.PriorityNormal)
	if err != nil {
		if errors.Is(err, scheduler.ErrClosed) {
			s.writeError(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "scheduler_closed", "server is shutting down", "")
		}
		if errors.Is(err, scheduler.ErrQueueFull) {
			// The same refusal the engine gives when its own
			// bounded queue fills: engine_busy, by name.
			s.writeError(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "engine_busy", "all engine slots are busy and the wait queue is full", "")
		}
		// Otherwise the client went away mid-wait; nothing to write to.
		return nil, false
	}
	return release, true
}

// --- handlers ----------------------------------------------------------

func (s *Server) handleHealthz(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	s.diag.RecordRequest("GET /healthz")
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), 2*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	h, _ := s.eng.Health(ctx)
	// This route is unauthenticated, so its detail is static: a
	// coarse state class only. The engine's own error strings
	// (socket paths, supervisor state) stay behind auth on /debug.
	detail := "down"
	if h.OK {
		detail = "ok"
	} else if _, unavail := s.eng.(engine.Unavailable); unavail {
		detail = "unavailable"
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
		"status": "ok",
		"engine": map[string]any{"ok": h.OK, "detail": detail},
	})
}

func (s *Server) handleModels(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
	s.diag.RecordRequest("GET /v1/models")
	data := make([]map[string]any, 0, len(s.cfg.Models))
	for _, m := range s.cfg.Models {
		data = append(data, map[string]any{"id": m, "object": "model", "owned_by": "itak-torch"})
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"object": "list", "data": data})
}

// toolFunction is the wire shape of one function inside a tool
// definition or a tool call. Parameters and Arguments are
// decoded JSON objects, kept as maps: templates serialize them
// with tojson, whose sorted-key default makes the rendered form
// independent of map order.
type toolFunction struct {
	Name        string         `json:"name"`
	Description string         `json:"description"`
	Parameters  map[string]any `json:"parameters"`
	Arguments   map[string]any `json:"arguments"`
}

// chatTool is the wire shape of one entry of a request's tools
// array: {"type": "function", "function": {...}}.
type chatTool struct {
	Type     string       `json:"type"`
	Function toolFunction `json:"function"`
}

// chatToolCall is the wire shape of one entry of an assistant
// message's tool_calls array.
type chatToolCall struct {
	ID       string       `json:"id"`
	Type     string       `json:"type"`
	Function toolFunction `json:"function"`
}

type chatMessage struct {
	Role    string `json:"role"`
	Content string `json:"content"`
	// Tool fields (OpenAI-shaped): a tool message's name and
	// tool_call_id, and an assistant message's tool calls,
	// reasoning content, recipient, and end-of-turn flag. They
	// ride to the chat template, whose tool branches read them;
	// before they existed here, a tool message rendered with an
	// empty name and a tool call rendered as plain text.
	Name             string         `json:"name"`
	ToolCallID       string         `json:"tool_call_id"`
	ToolCalls        []chatToolCall `json:"tool_calls"`
	ReasoningContent string         `json:"reasoning_content"`
	Recipient        string         `json:"recipient"`
	EndTurn          *bool          `json:"end_turn"`
}

type chatRequest struct {
	Model       string        `json:"model"`
	Messages    []chatMessage `json:"messages"`
	Tools       []chatTool    `json:"tools"`
	Stream      bool          `json:"stream"`
	MaxTokens   int           `json:"max_tokens"`
	Temperature *float64      `json:"temperature"`
	TopP        *float64      `json:"top_p"`
	Stop        []string      `json:"stop"`
	// Sampling parity fields (TODO T-9.13), OpenAI-shaped.
	Seed             *uint64  `json:"seed"`
	TopK             *int     `json:"top_k"`
	PresencePenalty  *float64 `json:"presence_penalty"`
	FrequencyPenalty *float64 `json:"frequency_penalty"`
}

func (s *Server) handleChatCompletions(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	s.diag.RecordRequest("POST /v1/chat/completions")
	var req chatRequest
	if err := s.decodeBody(w, r, &req); err != nil {
		s.invalidRequest(w, err.Error(), "")
		return
	}
	if msg := validateChat(&req); msg != nil {
		s.invalidRequest(w, msg.text, msg.param)
		return
	}
	if req.MaxTokens > s.cfg.MaxTokensCap {
		s.invalidRequest(w, fmt.Sprintf("max_tokens exceeds the server cap of %d", s.cfg.MaxTokensCap), "max_tokens")
		return
	}
	// One generation gets one bounded context. The per-generation
	// deadline is what keeps a single context-sized request from
	// holding its engine slot on any operational horizon: when it
	// fires, the generation ends and is named, below and in the
	// streaming path.
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), s.cfg.GenerationTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	r = r.WithContext(ctx)
	prompt, err := s.buildPrompt(r.Context(), &req)
	if err != nil {
		// The model's own template could not be rendered. That is
		// a named platform failure, never a silent fallback to
		// flattening: the caller learns the prompt would be wrong.
		s.log.Error("chat template render failed", "err", err)
		s.writeError(w, http.StatusBadGateway, "chat_template_error", err.Error(), "")
		return
	}
	greq := engine.GenerateRequest{
		Model:            req.Model,
		Prompt:           prompt,
		MaxTokens:        req.MaxTokens,
		Stop:             req.Stop,
		Seed:             req.Seed,
		TopK:             req.TopK,
		PresencePenalty:  req.PresencePenalty,
		FrequencyPenalty: req.FrequencyPenalty,
	}
	if req.Temperature != nil {
		greq.Temperature = *req.Temperature
	}
	if req.TopP != nil {
		greq.TopP = *req.TopP
	}

	if req.Stream {
		s.streamChat(w, r, greq)
		return
	}

	cacheable := chatCacheable(&req)
	var cacheKey string
	if cacheable {
		cacheKey = chatCacheKey(&req)
		if body, hit := s.cache.Get(cacheKey); hit {
			w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
			w.Header().Set("X-Torch-Cache", "hit")
			w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
			_, _ = w.Write(body)
			return
		}
	}

	release, ok := s.acquire(w, r)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	defer release()

	s.diag.RecordEngineCall()
	ch, err := s.eng.Generate(r.Context(), greq)
	if err != nil {
		s.engineError(w, err)
		return
	}
	var sb strings.Builder
	finish := "stop"
	sawDone := false
	for ev := range ch {
		if ev.Err != nil {
			// Terminal error event (TODO T-9.12): the generation
			// failed after it started. Nothing has been written
			// yet on this path, so the failure answers with its
			// honest HTTP status instead of a truncated 200.
			s.engineError(w, ev.Err)
			return
		}
		sb.WriteString(ev.Text)
		if ev.Done {
			sawDone = true
			if ev.FinishReason != "" {
				finish = ev.FinishReason
			}
		}
	}
	if !sawDone {
		switch {
		case errors.Is(r.Context().Err(), context.DeadlineExceeded):
			// The per-generation deadline fired and ended the
			// stream: a named failure, never a short success.
			s.engineError(w, fmt.Errorf("%w: generation exceeded the configured deadline of %s",
				engine.ErrGenerationFailed, s.cfg.GenerationTimeout))
		case r.Context().Err() != nil:
			// The stream died with the client; no honest response exists.
			s.diag.RecordEngineError()
		default:
			// The client closed the channel with neither a done nor an
			// error event: a contract violation, reported as an engine
			// death rather than served as a short completion.
			s.engineError(w, fmt.Errorf("%w: generation stream ended without a terminal event", engine.ErrEngineDied))
		}
		return
	}

	resp := map[string]any{
		"id":      newID("chatcmpl-"),
		"object":  "chat.completion",
		"created": time.Now().Unix(),
		"model":   req.Model,
		"choices": []map[string]any{{
			"index":         0,
			"message":       map[string]any{"role": "assistant", "content": sb.String()},
			"finish_reason": finish,
		}},
	}
	body, err := json.Marshal(resp)
	if err != nil {
		s.engineError(w, fmt.Errorf("marshal completion: %w", err))
		return
	}
	if cacheable {
		s.cache.Set(cacheKey, body)
		w.Header().Set("X-Torch-Cache", "miss")
	} else {
		w.Header().Set("X-Torch-Cache", "skip")
	}
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
	_, _ = w.Write(body)
}

func (s *Server) streamChat(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, greq engine.GenerateRequest) {
	release, ok := s.acquire(w, r)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	defer release()

	s.diag.RecordEngineCall()
	ch, err := s.eng.Generate(r.Context(), greq)
	if err != nil {
		s.engineError(w, err)
		return
	}
	flusher, ok := w.(http.Flusher)
	if !ok {
		s.writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "streaming_unsupported", "response writer cannot stream", "")
		return
	}
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
	w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)

	id := newID("chatcmpl-")
	created := time.Now().Unix()
	writeChunk := func(content string, finish *string) {
		chunk := map[string]any{
			"id":      id,
			"object":  "chat.completion.chunk",
			"created": created,
			"model":   greq.Model,
			"choices": []map[string]any{{
				"index":         0,
				"delta":         map[string]any{"content": content},
				"finish_reason": finish,
			}},
		}
		b, _ := json.Marshal(chunk)
		_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(w, "data: %s\n\n", b)
		flusher.Flush()
	}
	sawDone := false
	for ev := range ch {
		if ev.Err != nil {
			// Terminal error event (TODO T-9.12): the 200 and any
			// chunks are already gone, so the named failure rides
			// the stream itself as an error frame and the stream
			// ends without [DONE]. A client reading only tokens
			// sees the failure by name, not a truncated answer.
			_, code := engineErrorStatus(ev.Err)
			s.diag.RecordEngineError()
			b, _ := json.Marshal(errorBody{Error: apiError{Code: code, Message: ev.Err.Error()}})
			_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(w, "data: %s\n\n", b)
			flusher.Flush()
			return
		}
		if ev.Done {
			sawDone = true
			fr := ev.FinishReason
			if fr == "" {
				fr = "stop"
			}
			writeChunk(ev.Text, &fr)
		} else {
			writeChunk(ev.Text, nil)
		}
	}
	// The channel closed. [DONE] is written only when the engine
	// actually finished: a channel that closes with neither a done
	// nor an error event is the client contract violation the
	// non-streaming path names as an engine death, and it is named
	// here too, never dressed as a clean end.
	switch {
	case sawDone:
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, "data: [DONE]\n\n")
		flusher.Flush()
	case errors.Is(r.Context().Err(), context.DeadlineExceeded):
		s.writeStreamError(w, flusher, engine.ErrGenerationFailed,
			fmt.Sprintf("generation exceeded the configured deadline of %s", s.cfg.GenerationTimeout))
	case r.Context().Err() != nil:
		// The client went away mid-stream; nothing honest to send.
		s.diag.RecordEngineError()
	default:
		s.writeStreamError(w, flusher, engine.ErrEngineDied,
			"generation stream ended without a terminal event")
	}
}

// writeStreamError sends one named terminal error frame on an open
// event stream and flushes it.
func (s *Server) writeStreamError(w http.ResponseWriter, flusher http.Flusher, err error, message string) {
	_, code := engineErrorStatus(err)
	s.diag.RecordEngineError()
	b, _ := json.Marshal(errorBody{Error: apiError{Code: code, Message: message}})
	_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(w, "data: %s\n\n", b)
	flusher.Flush()
}

type fieldError struct{ text, param string }

func validateChat(req *chatRequest) *fieldError {
	if req.Model == "" {
		return &fieldError{"model is required", "model"}
	}
	if len(req.Messages) == 0 {
		return &fieldError{"messages must not be empty", "messages"}
	}
	for i, m := range req.Messages {
		if m.Role == "" {
			return &fieldError{fmt.Sprintf("messages[%d].role is required", i), "messages"}
		}
		// An assistant turn that only calls tools carries no
		// content text; every other message must carry some.
		if m.Content == "" && len(m.ToolCalls) == 0 {
			return &fieldError{fmt.Sprintf("messages[%d].content is required", i), "messages"}
		}
	}
	if req.MaxTokens < 0 {
		return &fieldError{"max_tokens must be >= 0", "max_tokens"}
	}
	if req.Temperature != nil && (*req.Temperature < 0 || *req.Temperature > 2) {
		return &fieldError{"temperature must be between 0 and 2", "temperature"}
	}
	if req.TopP != nil && (*req.TopP < 0 || *req.TopP > 1) {
		return &fieldError{"top_p must be between 0 and 1", "top_p"}
	}
	if req.TopK != nil && *req.TopK < 0 {
		return &fieldError{"top_k must be >= 0", "top_k"}
	}
	if req.PresencePenalty != nil && (*req.PresencePenalty < -2 || *req.PresencePenalty > 2) {
		return &fieldError{"presence_penalty must be between -2 and 2", "presence_penalty"}
	}
	if req.FrequencyPenalty != nil && (*req.FrequencyPenalty < -2 || *req.FrequencyPenalty > 2) {
		return &fieldError{"frequency_penalty must be between -2 and 2", "frequency_penalty"}
	}
	return nil
}

// chatTemplater is the optional engine-client capability the
// template resolution probes for (the socket client and the
// supervisor both offer it).
type chatTemplater interface {
	ChatTemplate(context.Context) (engine.ChatTemplate, error)
}

// resolveTemplate returns the chat template to render with, or
// (nil, nil) when the model definitively has none (the flattening
// fallback). A transient fetch failure is neither: it returns an
// error, because flattening on a hiccup would silently build the
// wrong prompt — the two nil outcomes used to be indistinguishable
// and a fetch error took the flattening path with no signal.
//
// The outcome is cached once definitive: a configured template
// wins outright; the engine's own template is fetched once; the
// engine's named ErrNoChatTemplate settles it as none. Fetch
// errors are logged and NOT cached, so a later request retries.
// tplMu guards the cached outcome only and is never held across
// the fetch: one slow fetch must not serialize every chat request
// behind it. Concurrent requests may fetch twice; both cache the
// same outcome (first writer wins in cacheTemplateOutcome).
func (s *Server) resolveTemplate(ctx context.Context) (*engine.ChatTemplate, error) {
	s.tplMu.Lock()
	done, tpl := s.tplDone, s.tpl
	s.tplMu.Unlock()
	if done {
		return tpl, nil
	}
	if s.cfg.ChatTemplate != "" {
		return s.cacheTemplateOutcome(&engine.ChatTemplate{
			Template: s.cfg.ChatTemplate,
			BOSToken: s.cfg.ChatBOSToken,
			EOSToken: s.cfg.ChatEOSToken,
		}, "config"), nil
	}
	ct, ok := s.eng.(chatTemplater)
	if !ok {
		return s.cacheTemplateOutcome(nil, "none"), nil
	}
	fetchCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	fetched, err := ct.ChatTemplate(fetchCtx)
	switch {
	case err == nil:
		return s.cacheTemplateOutcome(&fetched, "engine"), nil
	case errors.Is(err, engine.ErrNoChatTemplate):
		return s.cacheTemplateOutcome(nil, "none"), nil
	default:
		s.log.Warn("chat template fetch failed; will retry on the next request", "err", err)
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("chat template fetch failed: %w", err)
	}
}

// cacheTemplateOutcome records a definitive template outcome
// (first writer wins, so concurrent fetches agree) and returns
// the recorded template.
func (s *Server) cacheTemplateOutcome(tpl *engine.ChatTemplate, source string) *engine.ChatTemplate {
	s.tplMu.Lock()
	defer s.tplMu.Unlock()
	if !s.tplDone {
		s.tpl, s.tplSource, s.tplDone = tpl, source, true
	}
	return s.tpl
}

// templateSource reports how the prompt is being built, for /debug:
// "config", "engine", "none (role flattening)", or "unresolved".
func (s *Server) templateSource() string {
	s.tplMu.Lock()
	defer s.tplMu.Unlock()
	if s.tplSource == "none" {
		return "none (role flattening)"
	}
	if s.tplSource == "" {
		return "unresolved"
	}
	return s.tplSource
}

// buildPrompt produces the engine prompt for one chat request: the
// model's own chat template rendered over the messages when the
// model carries one (TODO T-9.16), role flattening when it carries
// none. A render failure — and a template fetch failure — is an
// error, not a fallback.
func (s *Server) buildPrompt(ctx context.Context, req *chatRequest) (string, error) {
	tpl, err := s.resolveTemplate(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if tpl == nil {
		return flattenMessages(req.Messages), nil
	}
	converted := make([]chattemplate.Message, len(req.Messages))
	for i, m := range req.Messages {
		converted[i] = convertMessage(m)
	}
	tools := make([]chattemplate.Tool, len(req.Tools))
	for i, t := range req.Tools {
		tools[i] = chattemplate.Tool{
			Type: t.Type,
			Function: chattemplate.ToolFunction{
				Name:        t.Function.Name,
				Description: t.Function.Description,
				Parameters:  t.Function.Parameters,
			},
		}
	}
	return chattemplate.Render(tpl.Template, converted, chattemplate.Params{
		BOSToken:            tpl.BOSToken,
		EOSToken:            tpl.EOSToken,
		AddGenerationPrompt: true,
		Tools:               tools,
	})
}

// convertMessage maps one wire message to the template's message
// shape, carrying the tool fields the template reads.
func convertMessage(m chatMessage) chattemplate.Message {
	out := chattemplate.Message{
		Role:             m.Role,
		Content:          m.Content,
		Name:             m.Name,
		ToolCallID:       m.ToolCallID,
		ReasoningContent: m.ReasoningContent,
		Recipient:        m.Recipient,
		EndTurn:          m.EndTurn,
	}
	for _, tc := range m.ToolCalls {
		out.ToolCalls = append(out.ToolCalls, chattemplate.ToolCall{
			ID:   tc.ID,
			Type: tc.Type,
			Function: chattemplate.FunctionCall{
				Name:      tc.Function.Name,
				Arguments: tc.Function.Arguments,
			},
		})
	}
	return out
}

func flattenMessages(msgs []chatMessage) string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	for _, m := range msgs {
		sb.WriteString(m.Role)
		sb.WriteString(": ")
		sb.WriteString(m.Content)
		sb.WriteString("\n")
	}
	sb.WriteString("assistant:")
	return sb.String()
}

// chatCacheable reports whether a chat request may use the
// response cache at all. An unseeded temperature > 0 request asks
// the sampler for variation; caching it would replay the first
// caller's sample byte-identical to every later identical caller
// for the TTL, freezing the variation the temperature was set to
// obtain. Seeded requests are deterministic (same seed, same
// sample) and temperature 0 is greedy, so both keep the cache.
// Uncacheable requests skip the read AND the write and answer
// X-Torch-Cache: skip.
func chatCacheable(req *chatRequest) bool {
	return req.Seed != nil || req.Temperature == nil || *req.Temperature <= 0
}

func chatCacheKey(req *chatRequest) string {
	// Pointer fields marshal distinctly from absent ones, so temperature
	// 0 and no temperature do not collide. Every field of the request
	// is in the hash; that distinctness is pinned field by field in
	// cachekey_internal_test.go and over HTTP in server_cache_test.go,
	// because a key that silently stops covering a field serves one
	// caller's completion to every other caller of the model.
	b, _ := json.Marshal(req)
	sum := sha256.Sum256(b)
	return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
}

type embedRequestBody struct {
	Model string          `json:"model"`
	Input json.RawMessage `json:"input"`
}

func (s *Server) handleEmbeddings(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	s.diag.RecordRequest("POST /v1/embeddings")
	var body embedRequestBody
	if err := s.decodeBody(w, r, &body); err != nil {
		s.invalidRequest(w, err.Error(), "")
		return
	}
	if body.Model == "" {
		s.invalidRequest(w, "model is required", "model")
		return
	}
	inputs, err := parseEmbedInput(body.Input)
	if err != nil {
		s.invalidRequest(w, err.Error(), "input")
		return
	}

	release, ok := s.acquire(w, r)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	defer release()

	s.diag.RecordEngineCall()
	resp, err := s.eng.Embed(r.Context(), engine.EmbedRequest{Model: body.Model, Input: inputs})
	if err != nil {
		s.engineError(w, err)
		return
	}
	if len(resp.Vectors) != len(inputs) {
		s.engineError(w, fmt.Errorf("%w: engine returned %d vectors for %d inputs",
			engine.ErrBadRequest, len(resp.Vectors), len(inputs)))
		return
	}
	data := make([]map[string]any, 0, len(resp.Vectors))
	for i, v := range resp.Vectors {
		data = append(data, map[string]any{"object": "embedding", "index": i, "embedding": v})
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"object": "list", "model": body.Model, "data": data})
}

func parseEmbedInput(raw json.RawMessage) ([]string, error) {
	if len(raw) == 0 {
		return nil, errors.New("input is required")
	}
	var single string
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &single); err == nil {
		if single == "" {
			return nil, errors.New("input must not be empty")
		}
		return []string{single}, nil
	}
	var many []string
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &many); err != nil {
		return nil, errors.New("input must be a string or an array of strings")
	}
	if len(many) == 0 {
		return nil, errors.New("input must not be empty")
	}
	for _, s := range many {
		if s == "" {
			return nil, errors.New("input entries must not be empty")
		}
	}
	return many, nil
}

func (s *Server) handleDebug(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	s.diag.RecordRequest("GET /debug")
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), 2*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	h, herr := s.eng.Health(ctx)
	if herr != nil {
		h = engine.HealthStatus{OK: false, Detail: herr.Error()}
	}
	out := map[string]any{
		"diag":          s.diag.Snapshot(),
		"scheduler":     s.sched.Stats(),
		"cache":         s.cache.Stats(),
		"engine":        map[string]any{"ok": h.OK, "detail": h.Detail},
		"models":        s.cfg.Models,
		"chat_template": s.templateSource(),
	}
	// When the wired engine client can report on itself (the socket
	// client can), its self-report rides along: loaded model,
	// coverage result, serving counters.
	if d, ok := s.eng.(interface {
		DebugInfo(context.Context) (map[string]any, error)
	}); ok {
		if info, err := d.DebugInfo(ctx); err == nil {
			out["engine_debug"] = info
		} else {
			out["engine_debug"] = map[string]any{"error": err.Error()}
		}
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, out)
}

package server_test

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"

// --- cache key distinctness (critic panel Category E, HIGH) -----------

func cacheEntryCount(t *testing.T, ts *httptest.Server) int {
	t.Helper()
	_, _, body := do(t, ts, http.MethodGet, "/debug", "", testKey)
	var v struct {
		Cache struct {
			Entries int `json:"entries"`
		} `json:"cache"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &v); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("debug body is not JSON: %v (%s)", err, body)
	}
	return v.Cache.Entries
}

// TestChatCacheDistinctRequestsGetDistinctEntries posts requests
// that differ from a base request in exactly one field each and
// requires a cache miss, one more engine call, and one more cache
// entry for every one of them. The panel's mutation — a cache key
// hashing only the model name — turns the first same-model variant
// into a hit and fails this test; before it existed, that mutation
// survived the full suite. Every variant here stays cacheable
// (temperature absent, zero, or seeded), so a miss can only mean
// the key told the requests apart.
func TestChatCacheDistinctRequestsGetDistinctEntries(t *testing.T) {
	fake := &fakeEngine{}
	ts := newServer(t, fake)

	base := `{"model":"glimmer","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello"}]}`
	variants := map[string]string{ //nolint:gosec // request bodies, not credentials: gosec G101 pattern-matches the "max_tokens" field name inside them
		"message content":    `{"model":"glimmer","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say goodbye"}]}`,
		"message role":       `{"model":"glimmer","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"Say hello"}]}`,
		"message appended":   `{"model":"glimmer","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello"},{"role":"user","content":"again"}]}`,
		"max_tokens":         `{"model":"glimmer","max_tokens":8,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello"}]}`,
		"temperature zero":   `{"model":"glimmer","temperature":0,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello"}]}`,
		"seed":               `{"model":"glimmer","seed":7,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello"}]}`,
		"seeded temperature": `{"model":"glimmer","temperature":0.7,"seed":7,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello"}]}`,
		"top_p":              `{"model":"glimmer","top_p":0.5,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello"}]}`,
		"top_k":              `{"model":"glimmer","top_k":40,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello"}]}`,
		"stop":               `{"model":"glimmer","stop":["END"],"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello"}]}`,
		"model":              `{"model":"other-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello"}]}`,
	}

	post := func(body string) http.Header {
		t.Helper()
		code, hdr, respBody := do(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/v1/chat/completions", body, testKey)
		if code != http.StatusOK {
			t.Fatalf("chat status = %d (%s)", code, respBody)
		}
		return hdr
	}

	if hdr := post(base); hdr.Get("X-Torch-Cache") != "miss" {
		t.Fatalf("base request X-Torch-Cache = %q, want miss", hdr.Get("X-Torch-Cache"))
	}
	wantCalls, wantEntries := int64(1), 1
	for name, body := range variants {
		if hdr := post(body); hdr.Get("X-Torch-Cache") != "miss" {
			t.Fatalf("%s: X-Torch-Cache = %q, want miss (a hit means its key collides with an earlier request)", name, hdr.Get("X-Torch-Cache"))
		}
		wantCalls++
		wantEntries++
		if n := fake.generateCalls.Load(); n != wantCalls {
			t.Fatalf("%s: engine Generate called %d times, want %d (a repeat means a shared cache entry)", name, n, wantCalls)
		}
		if n := cacheEntryCount(t, ts); n != wantEntries {
			t.Fatalf("%s: cache holds %d entries, want %d distinct entries", name, n, wantEntries)
		}
	}

	// And the base request still hits its own entry afterwards.
	if hdr := post(base); hdr.Get("X-Torch-Cache") != "hit" {
		t.Fatalf("base request repeated: X-Torch-Cache = %q, want hit", hdr.Get("X-Torch-Cache"))
	}
	if n := fake.generateCalls.Load(); n != wantCalls {
		t.Fatalf("engine Generate called %d times after the base repeat, want %d", n, wantCalls)
	}
}

// --- sampled generations bypass the cache (Category E, MEDIUM) --------

// sampledEngine returns a different completion on every call, the
// way a sampling engine does, so a replayed answer is visible in
// the response body itself, not just in call counts.
type sampledEngine struct {
	calls atomic.Int64
}

func (e *sampledEngine) Generate(_ context.Context, _ engine.GenerateRequest) (<-chan engine.TokenEvent, error) {
	n := e.calls.Add(1)
	ch := make(chan engine.TokenEvent, 2)
	ch <- engine.TokenEvent{Text: fmt.Sprintf("take %d", n), TokenID: 1}
	ch <- engine.TokenEvent{Done: true, FinishReason: "stop"}
	close(ch)
	return ch, nil
}

func (e *sampledEngine) Embed(_ context.Context, req engine.EmbedRequest) (engine.EmbedResponse, error) {
	vecs := make([][]float32, len(req.Input))
	for i := range vecs {
		vecs[i] = []float32{0.1, 0.2, 0.3}
	}
	return engine.EmbedResponse{Model: req.Model, Vectors: vecs}, nil
}

func (e *sampledEngine) Health(context.Context) (engine.HealthStatus, error) {
	return engine.HealthStatus{OK: true, Detail: "sampled engine"}, nil
}

func completionContent(t *testing.T, body []byte) string {
	t.Helper()
	var v struct {
		Choices []struct {
			Message struct {
				Content string `json:"content"`
			} `json:"message"`
		} `json:"choices"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &v); err != nil || len(v.Choices) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("chat body = %s, err = %v", body, err)
	}
	return v.Choices[0].Message.Content
}

// TestChatUnseededSampledRequestsBypassCache: an unseeded
// temperature > 0 request asks for variation. Serving the second
// identical caller the first caller's sample byte-identical (the
// old behavior) freezes exactly what the temperature was set to
// vary, so these requests must skip the cache on both sides: no
// read, no write, the engine called every time.
func TestChatUnseededSampledRequestsBypassCache(t *testing.T) {
	eng := &sampledEngine{}
	ts := newServer(t, eng)
	body := `{"model":"glimmer","temperature":0.7,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"roll the dice"}]}`

	contents := map[string]bool{}
	for i := 1; i <= 2; i++ {
		code, hdr, respBody := do(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/v1/chat/completions", body, testKey)
		if code != http.StatusOK {
			t.Fatalf("request %d status = %d (%s)", i, code, respBody)
		}
		if got := hdr.Get("X-Torch-Cache"); got != "skip" {
			t.Fatalf("request %d X-Torch-Cache = %q, want skip (unseeded sampled requests never touch the cache)", i, got)
		}
		contents[completionContent(t, respBody)] = true
	}
	if len(contents) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("two unseeded sampled requests produced %d distinct completions, want 2 (the second was a replay): %v", len(contents), contents)
	}
	if n := eng.calls.Load(); n != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("engine Generate called %d times, want 2", n)
	}
	if n := cacheEntryCount(t, ts); n != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("cache holds %d entries after unseeded sampled requests, want 0 (nothing was written)", n)
	}
}

// TestChatSeededSampledRequestsStillCache: a seed pins the sample,
// so a seeded temperature > 0 request is deterministic and keeps
// the cache — the bypass above must not widen to it.
func TestChatSeededSampledRequestsStillCache(t *testing.T) {
	eng := &sampledEngine{}
	ts := newServer(t, eng)
	body := `{"model":"glimmer","temperature":0.7,"seed":42,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"roll the dice"}]}`

	_, hdr, first := do(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/v1/chat/completions", body, testKey)
	if got := hdr.Get("X-Torch-Cache"); got != "miss" {
		t.Fatalf("first request X-Torch-Cache = %q, want miss", got)
	}
	_, hdr, second := do(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/v1/chat/completions", body, testKey)
	if got := hdr.Get("X-Torch-Cache"); got != "hit" {
		t.Fatalf("second request X-Torch-Cache = %q, want hit (a seeded request is deterministic)", got)
	}
	if c1, c2 := completionContent(t, first), completionContent(t, second); c1 != c2 {
		t.Fatalf("seeded repeat returned %q after %q; a cache hit must replay the stored body", c2, c1)
	}
	if n := eng.calls.Load(); n != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("engine Generate called %d times, want 1", n)
	}
}

// TestChatZeroTemperatureRequestsStillCache: temperature 0 is
// greedy decoding, deterministic with or without a seed, so it
// keeps the cache as well.
func TestChatZeroTemperatureRequestsStillCache(t *testing.T) {
	eng := &sampledEngine{}
	ts := newServer(t, eng)
	body := `{"model":"glimmer","temperature":0,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"be exact"}]}`

	_, hdr, _ := do(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/v1/chat/completions", body, testKey)
	if got := hdr.Get("X-Torch-Cache"); got != "miss" {
		t.Fatalf("first request X-Torch-Cache = %q, want miss", got)
	}
	_, hdr, _ = do(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/v1/chat/completions", body, testKey)
	if got := hdr.Get("X-Torch-Cache"); got != "hit" {
		t.Fatalf("second request X-Torch-Cache = %q, want hit", got)
	}
	if n := eng.calls.Load(); n != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("engine Generate called %d times, want 1", n)
	}
}

// --- template fetch failures (Category E, MEDIUM) ---------------------

// flakyTemplateEngine fails the template fetch with a transient
// error (not the named no-template outcome) until told to stop,
// then serves the ChatML template.
type flakyTemplateEngine struct {
	*fakeEngine
	fail atomic.Bool
}

func (e *flakyTemplateEngine) ChatTemplate(context.Context) (engine.ChatTemplate, error) {
	if e.fail.Load() {
		return engine.ChatTemplate{}, errors.New("template store unreachable")
	}
	return engine.ChatTemplate{Template: chatMLTemplate}, nil
}

// TestChatTemplateFetchFailureIsNamedNotFlattened: a transient
// template-fetch error used to return the role-flattened prompt
// with a nil error, and the flattened generation was then cached
// as if correct. It must instead take the handler's named 502
// path, generate nothing, cache nothing — and the next request
// must retry the fetch and succeed.
func TestChatTemplateFetchFailureIsNamedNotFlattened(t *testing.T) {
	fake := &fakeEngine{}
	eng := &flakyTemplateEngine{fakeEngine: fake}
	eng.fail.Store(true)
	ts := newServerWithConfig(t, eng, nil)

	code, _, body := do(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/v1/chat/completions", chatBody, testKey)
	if code != http.StatusBadGateway || errorCode(t, body) != "chat_template_error" {
		t.Fatalf("status = %d, body = %s; want 502 chat_template_error, never a flattened 200", code, body)
	}
	if n := fake.generateCalls.Load(); n != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("engine Generate called %d times on a failed template fetch, want 0", n)
	}
	if n := cacheEntryCount(t, ts); n != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("cache holds %d entries after a failed template fetch, want 0", n)
	}

	eng.fail.Store(false)
	code, _, body = do(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/v1/chat/completions", chatBody, testKey)
	if code != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("retry status = %d (%s), want 200 once the fetch recovers", code, body)
	}
	want := "<|im_start|>user\nSay hello<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n"
	if got := lastPrompt(t, fake); got != want {
		t.Fatalf("engine prompt after recovery = %q, want the templated %q", got, want)
	}
	// The recovered generation is the one that gets cached.
	_, hdr, _ := do(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/v1/chat/completions", chatBody, testKey)
	if got := hdr.Get("X-Torch-Cache"); got != "hit" {
		t.Fatalf("repeat after recovery X-Torch-Cache = %q, want hit", got)
	}
	if n := fake.generateCalls.Load(); n != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("engine Generate called %d times, want 1", n)
	}
}

// blockingTemplateEngine parks inside the template fetch until
// released, so a test can hold one fetch open and watch what a
// concurrent request does.
type blockingTemplateEngine struct {
	*fakeEngine
	entered chan struct{}
	release chan struct{}
}

func (e *blockingTemplateEngine) ChatTemplate(ctx context.Context) (engine.ChatTemplate, error) {
	e.entered <- struct{}{}
	select {
	case <-e.release:
		return engine.ChatTemplate{Template: chatMLTemplate}, nil
	case <-ctx.Done():
		return engine.ChatTemplate{}, ctx.Err()
	}
}

// TestChatTemplateFetchDoesNotSerializeRequests: the template
// mutex used to be held across the network fetch, so one slow
// fetch serialized every concurrent chat request behind it. With
// the first fetch parked, a second request must still reach its
// own fetch.
func TestChatTemplateFetchDoesNotSerializeRequests(t *testing.T) {
	fake := &fakeEngine{}
	eng := &blockingTemplateEngine{
		fakeEngine: fake,
		entered:    make(chan struct{}, 2),
		release:    make(chan struct{}),
	}
	ts := newServerWithConfig(t, eng, nil)
	var releaseOnce sync.Once
	release := func() { releaseOnce.Do(func() { close(eng.release) }) }
	defer release()

	type result struct {
		code int
		err  error
	}
	results := make(chan result, 2)
	post := func() {
		req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, ts.URL+"/v1/chat/completions", strings.NewReader(chatBody))
		if err != nil {
			results <- result{0, err}
			return
		}
		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+testKey)
		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		resp, err := ts.Client().Do(req)
		if err != nil {
			results <- result{0, err}
			return
		}
		_, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, resp.Body)
		_ = resp.Body.Close()
		results <- result{resp.StatusCode, nil}
	}

	go post()
	<-eng.entered // the first request's fetch is in flight and parked
	go post()
	select {
	case <-eng.entered:
		// The second request reached its own fetch while the
		// first was still parked: the mutex is not held across it.
	case <-time.After(3 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("second chat request never reached the template fetch while the first was parked: the template mutex is held across the network fetch")
	}
	release()
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		res := <-results
		if res.err != nil || res.code != http.StatusOK {
			t.Fatalf("concurrent request = %d, err = %v; want 200", res.code, res.err)
		}
	}
}

package server_test

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"sync/atomic"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/David2024patton/itak-torch-rebuild/platform/internal/engine"
	"github.com/David2024patton/itak-torch-rebuild/platform/internal/server"
)

const testKey = "test-key"

// fakeEngine is a deterministic stand-in at the platform's engine seam.
type fakeEngine struct {
	generateCalls atomic.Int64
	lastRequest   atomic.Value // engine.GenerateRequest
}

func (f *fakeEngine) Generate(_ context.Context, req engine.GenerateRequest) (<-chan engine.TokenEvent, error) {
	f.generateCalls.Add(1)
	f.lastRequest.Store(req)
	ch := make(chan engine.TokenEvent, 3)
	ch <- engine.TokenEvent{Text: "Hello", TokenID: 1}
	ch <- engine.TokenEvent{Text: " world", TokenID: 2}
	ch <- engine.TokenEvent{Text: "", Done: true, FinishReason: "stop"}
	close(ch)
	return ch, nil
}

func (f *fakeEngine) Embed(_ context.Context, req engine.EmbedRequest) (engine.EmbedResponse, error) {
	vecs := make([][]float32, len(req.Input))
	for i := range vecs {
		vecs[i] = []float32{0.1, 0.2, 0.3}
	}
	return engine.EmbedResponse{Model: req.Model, Vectors: vecs}, nil
}

func (f *fakeEngine) Health(context.Context) (engine.HealthStatus, error) {
	return engine.HealthStatus{OK: true, Detail: "fake engine"}, nil
}

// notImplEngine refuses Generate the way the socket skeleton does.
type notImplEngine struct{ *fakeEngine }

func (notImplEngine) Generate(context.Context, engine.GenerateRequest) (<-chan engine.TokenEvent, error) {
	return nil, engine.ErrNotImplemented
}

// midFailEngine streams one token, then fails the generation the way
// the socket client now reports a mid-stream engine failure: a
// terminal event carrying the named error (TODO T-9.12).
type midFailEngine struct{ *fakeEngine }

func (midFailEngine) Generate(context.Context, engine.GenerateRequest) (<-chan engine.TokenEvent, error) {
	ch := make(chan engine.TokenEvent, 2)
	ch <- engine.TokenEvent{Text: "Hello", TokenID: 1}
	ch <- engine.TokenEvent{Err: engine.ErrGenerationFailed}
	close(ch)
	return ch, nil
}

func newServer(t *testing.T, eng engine.Client) *httptest.Server {
	t.Helper()
	srv := server.New(server.Config{
		Engine:   eng,
		APIKey:   testKey,
		Models:   []string{"glimmer"},
		CacheTTL: time.Minute,
	})
	ts := httptest.NewServer(srv.Handler())
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		ts.Close()
		srv.Close()
	})
	return ts
}

func do(t *testing.T, ts *httptest.Server, method, path, body, key string) (int, http.Header, []byte) {
	t.Helper()
	var rdr io.Reader
	if body != "" {
		rdr = strings.NewReader(body)
	}
	req, err := http.NewRequest(method, ts.URL+path, rdr)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("NewRequest: %v", err)
	}
	if body != "" {
		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	}
	if key != "" {
		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+key)
	}
	resp, err := ts.Client().Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Do: %v", err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = resp.Body.Close() }()
	b, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ReadAll: %v", err)
	}
	return resp.StatusCode, resp.Header, b
}

func errorCode(t *testing.T, body []byte) string {
	t.Helper()
	var v struct {
		Error struct {
			Code string `json:"code"`
		} `json:"error"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &v); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("error body is not JSON: %v (%s)", err, body)
	}
	return v.Error.Code
}

const chatBody = `{"model":"glimmer","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello"}]}`

func TestChatCompletionAndCache(t *testing.T) {
	fake := &fakeEngine{}
	ts := newServer(t, fake)

	code, hdr, body := do(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/v1/chat/completions", chatBody, testKey)
	if code != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("chat status = %d (%s)", code, body)
	}
	if hdr.Get("X-Torch-Cache") != "miss" {
		t.Fatalf("first request X-Torch-Cache = %q, want miss", hdr.Get("X-Torch-Cache"))
	}
	var v struct {
		Choices []struct {
			Message struct {
				Content string `json:"content"`
			} `json:"message"`
		} `json:"choices"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &v); err != nil || len(v.Choices) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("chat body = %s, err = %v", body, err)
	}
	if got := v.Choices[0].Message.Content; got != "Hello world" {
		t.Fatalf("content = %q, want %q", got, "Hello world")
	}

	code, hdr, _ = do(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/v1/chat/completions", chatBody, testKey)
	if code != http.StatusOK || hdr.Get("X-Torch-Cache") != "hit" {
		t.Fatalf("second request = %d, X-Torch-Cache = %q; want 200/hit", code, hdr.Get("X-Torch-Cache"))
	}
	if n := fake.generateCalls.Load(); n != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("engine Generate called %d times, want 1 (second served from cache)", n)
	}
}

func TestChatSamplingFieldsReachTheEngine(t *testing.T) {
	fake := &fakeEngine{}
	ts := newServer(t, fake)
	body := `{"model":"glimmer","seed":42,"top_k":40,"presence_penalty":0.5,"frequency_penalty":-0.25,` +
		`"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}`
	code, _, respBody := do(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/v1/chat/completions", body, testKey)
	if code != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("status = %d (%s)", code, respBody)
	}
	got, ok := fake.lastRequest.Load().(engine.GenerateRequest)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("engine saw no generate request")
	}
	if got.Seed == nil || *got.Seed != 42 || got.TopK == nil || *got.TopK != 40 ||
		got.PresencePenalty == nil || *got.PresencePenalty != 0.5 ||
		got.FrequencyPenalty == nil || *got.FrequencyPenalty != -0.25 {
		t.Fatalf("engine request = %+v, want seed 42, top_k 40, penalties 0.5/-0.25", got)
	}
}

const chatMLTemplate = `{% for message in messages %}<|im_start|>{{ message['role'] }}
{{ message['content'] }}<|im_end|>
{% endfor %}{% if add_generation_prompt %}<|im_start|>assistant
{% endif %}`

func newServerWithConfig(t *testing.T, eng engine.Client, mutate func(*server.Config)) *httptest.Server {
	t.Helper()
	cfg := server.Config{
		Engine:   eng,
		APIKey:   testKey,
		Models:   []string{"glimmer"},
		CacheTTL: time.Minute,
	}
	if mutate != nil {
		mutate(&cfg)
	}
	srv := server.New(cfg)
	ts := httptest.NewServer(srv.Handler())
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		ts.Close()
		srv.Close()
	})
	return ts
}

func lastPrompt(t *testing.T, fake *fakeEngine) string {
	t.Helper()
	got, ok := fake.lastRequest.Load().(engine.GenerateRequest)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("engine saw no generate request")
	}
	return got.Prompt
}

func TestChatUsesConfiguredTemplate(t *testing.T) {
	fake := &fakeEngine{}
	ts := newServerWithConfig(t, fake, func(c *server.Config) {
		c.ChatTemplate = chatMLTemplate
	})
	code, _, body := do(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/v1/chat/completions", chatBody, testKey)
	if code != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("chat status = %d (%s)", code, body)
	}
	want := "<|im_start|>user\nSay hello<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n"
	if got := lastPrompt(t, fake); got != want {
		t.Fatalf("engine prompt = %q, want the templated %q", got, want)
	}
}

// The tool wire flow, end to end over HTTP: a request carrying
// tool definitions and a tool-calling conversation renders through
// the model's template shape with the real tool names — the tool
// definitions block (through the tojson filter), the assistant
// call in ATEM form, and the tool result under the name resolved
// from its tool_call_id.
func TestChatWithToolsRendersToolNames(t *testing.T) {
	fake := &fakeEngine{}
	ts := newServerWithConfig(t, fake, func(c *server.Config) {
		c.ChatTemplate = `{% if tools %}DEFS[{% for tool in tools %}{{ tool.function.name }}:{{ tool.function.parameters | tojson }};{% endfor %}]{% endif %}{% for message in messages %}{% if message['role'] == 'assistant' and message.get('tool_calls') %}{% for tc in message['tool_calls'] %}CALL[{{ tc.function.name }}|{{ tc.function.arguments | tojson }}]{% endfor %}{% elif message['role'] == 'tool' %}OUT[{{ message.get('name') }}:{{ message['content'] }}]{% else %}{{ message['role'] }}:{{ message['content'] }};{% endif %}{% endfor %}`
	})
	body := `{"model":"glimmer","tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_weather","description":"d","parameters":{"type":"object"}}}],"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"},{"role":"assistant","content":"","tool_calls":[{"id":"c1","type":"function","function":{"name":"get_weather","arguments":{"city":"Paris"}}}]},{"role":"tool","tool_call_id":"c1","content":"sunny"}]}`
	code, _, respBody := do(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/v1/chat/completions", body, testKey)
	if code != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("chat status = %d (%s)", code, respBody)
	}
	want := `DEFS[get_weather:{"type":"object"};]user:hi;CALL[get_weather|{"city":"Paris"}]OUT[get_weather:sunny]`
	if got := lastPrompt(t, fake); got != want {
		t.Fatalf("engine prompt = %q, want the tool-carrying %q", got, want)
	}
}

}

func TestChatTemplateRenderFailureIsNamed(t *testing.T) {

	}
}

func TestChatValidation(t *testing.T) {
	ts := newServer(t, &fakeEngine{})
	cases := map[string]string{
		"no model":      `{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"x"}]}`,
		"no messages":   `{"model":"glimmer"}`,
		"empty role":    `{"model":"glimmer","messages":[{"role":"","content":"x"}]}`,
		"bad temp":      `{"model":"glimmer","temperature":9,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"x"}]}`,
		"bad top_k":     `{"model":"glimmer","top_k":-1,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"x"}]}`,
		"bad presence":  `{"model":"glimmer","presence_penalty":3,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"x"}]}`,
		"bad frequency": `{"model":"glimmer","frequency_penalty":-3,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"x"}]}`,
		"not json":      `{oops`,
	}
	for name, body := range cases {
		code, _, respBody := do(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/v1/chat/completions", body, testKey)
		if code != http.StatusBadRequest || errorCode(t, respBody) != "invalid_request" {
			t.Fatalf("%s: status = %d, body = %s; want 400 invalid_request", name, code, respBody)
		}
	}
}

// --- Wave 1 bounds -----------------------------------------------------

// silentCloseEngine streams one token, then closes the channel with
// neither a done nor an error event: the client contract violation.
type silentCloseEngine struct{ *fakeEngine }

func (silentCloseEngine) Generate(context.Context, engine.GenerateRequest) (<-chan engine.TokenEvent, error) {
	ch := make(chan engine.TokenEvent, 1)
	ch <- engine.TokenEvent{Text: "Hello", TokenID: 1}
	close(ch)
	return ch, nil
}

// blockingEngine never emits; its channel closes when the request
// context ends, which is how a real client's stream ends when the
// per-generation deadline fires.
type blockingEngine struct{ *fakeEngine }

func (blockingEngine) Generate(ctx context.Context, _ engine.GenerateRequest) (<-chan engine.TokenEvent, error) {
	ch := make(chan engine.TokenEvent)
	go func() {
		<-ctx.Done()
		close(ch)
	}()
	return ch, nil
}

// gateEngine blocks inside Generate until released, so a test can
// hold the only scheduler slot and watch the queue behind it.
type gateEngine struct {
	*fakeEngine
	started chan struct{}
	release chan struct{}
	once    sync.Once
}

func newGateEngine() *gateEngine {
	return &gateEngine{
		fakeEngine: &fakeEngine{},
		started:    make(chan struct{}),
		release:    make(chan struct{}),
	}
}

func (g *gateEngine) Generate(ctx context.Context, _ engine.GenerateRequest) (<-chan engine.TokenEvent, error) {
	g.once.Do(func() { close(g.started) })
	ch := make(chan engine.TokenEvent, 1)
	go func() {
		defer close(ch)
		select {
		case <-g.release:
			ch <- engine.TokenEvent{Text: "", Done: true, FinishReason: "stop"}
		case <-ctx.Done():
		}
	}()
	return ch, nil
}

func waitForBody(t *testing.T, ts *httptest.Server, what, want string) {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second)
	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
		_, _, body := do(t, ts, http.MethodGet, "/debug", "", testKey)
		if strings.Contains(string(body), want) {
			return
		}
		time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
	}
	t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for %s (%q in /debug)", what, want)
}

func TestHealthzDetailIsStatic(t *testing.T) {
	ts := newServer(t, &fakeEngine{})
	_, _, body := do(t, ts, http.MethodGet, "/healthz", "", "")
	if !strings.Contains(string(body), `"detail":"ok"`) {
		t.Fatalf("healthz detail = %s, want the static ok class", body)
	}
	if strings.Contains(string(body), "fake engine") {
		t.Fatalf("healthz leaked the engine's own detail string: %s", body)
	}

	tsDown := newServer(t, nil) // no engine configured
	_, _, body = do(t, tsDown, http.MethodGet, "/healthz", "", "")
	if !strings.Contains(string(body), `"detail":"unavailable"`) {
		t.Fatalf("healthz with no engine = %s, want the static unavailable class", body)
	}
	if strings.Contains(string(body), "no engine configured") {
		t.Fatalf("healthz leaked the engine's own detail string: %s", body)
	}
}

func TestPriorityHeaderDoesNotClaimHighLane(t *testing.T) {
	gate := newGateEngine()
	ts := newServerWithConfig(t, gate, func(c *server.Config) {
		c.MaxConcurrent = 1
	})
	done := make(chan int, 2)
	post := func(priority string) {
		req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, ts.URL+"/v1/chat/completions", strings.NewReader(chatBody))
		if err != nil {
			done <- -1
			return
		}
		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+testKey)
		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		if priority != "" {
			req.Header.Set("X-Torch-Priority", priority)
		}
		resp, err := ts.Client().Do(req)
		if err != nil {
			done <- -1
			return
		}
		_ = resp.Body.Close()
		done <- resp.StatusCode
	}
	go post("")
	<-gate.started // the only slot is held
	go post("high")
	// The header-carrying request must queue in the NORMAL lane.
	waitForBody(t, ts, "second request queued in the normal lane", `"normal_queued":1`)
	_, _, dbg := do(t, ts, http.MethodGet, "/debug", "", testKey)
	if !strings.Contains(string(dbg), `"high_queued":0`) {
		t.Fatalf("client header claimed the high lane: %s", dbg)
	}
	close(gate.release)
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		if code := <-done; code != http.StatusOK {
			t.Fatalf("queued request status = %d, want 200", code)
		}
	}
}

func TestSchedulerQueueFullMapsToEngineBusy(t *testing.T) {
	gate := newGateEngine()
	ts := newServerWithConfig(t, gate, func(c *server.Config) {
		c.MaxConcurrent = 1
		c.MaxWaitersPerLane = 1
	})
	done := make(chan int, 2)
	post := func() {
		code, _, _ := do(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/v1/chat/completions", chatBody, testKey)
		done <- code
	}
	go post()
	<-gate.started
	go post()
	waitForBody(t, ts, "one waiter queued", `"normal_queued":1`)

	// Slot held, lane full: the third request is refused at once
	// with the engine's own busy name.
	code, _, body := do(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/v1/chat/completions", chatBody, testKey)
	if code != http.StatusServiceUnavailable || errorCode(t, body) != "engine_busy" {
		t.Fatalf("status = %d, body = %s; want 503 engine_busy", code, body)
	}
	close(gate.release)
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		if c := <-done; c != http.StatusOK {
			t.Fatalf("queued request status = %d, want 200", c)
		}
	}
}

===== FILE: platform/internal/supervisor/supervisor.go =====
// Package supervisor keeps the Rust engine process alive.
//
// The engine is a separate process by design (the Go/Rust seam in
// ARCHITECTURE.md), which makes its death a platform problem: before
// this package existed, a dead engine meant in-flight generations
// ended as silently closed streams and every later request failed
// its dial until an operator restarted the process by hand (the
// 2026-10-30 serving smoke recorded exactly that death). The
// supervisor owns the lifecycle instead:
//
//   - It starts the engine binary with the operator's arguments and
//     dials the socket once the engine has loaded its model and is
//     serving (a 30B load takes seconds; the dial polls).
//   - A monitor watches the process. An unexpected exit closes the
//     stale client, is counted against a configured restart budget
//     (a maximum number of restarts inside a window, so a model
//     that can no longer load fails visibly instead of crash
//     looping forever), and is restarted after a bounded backoff.
//   - In-flight generations are not rescued, they are named: the
//     engine client's terminal error event reports ErrEngineDied
//     (TODO T-9.12), and the NEXT request is served by the
//     restarted engine. That pair is the T-9.11 proof shape.
//   - State() exposes the lifecycle (pid, restarts, budget,
//     exhaustion, last exit) for the platform's /debug view, so the
//     running system can explain its engine's health.
//
// The supervisor itself implements engine.Client by delegating to
// the current socket client, so the server neither knows nor cares
// that the process underneath it was replaced.
package supervisor

import (
	"bufio"
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/David2024patton/itak-torch-rebuild/platform/internal/engine"
)

// Config configures one supervised engine process. Command and
// SocketPath are required; the rest take the defaults New applies.
type Config struct {
	// Command is the engine binary path (itak-engine).
	Command string
	// Args are the engine's arguments. They must point the engine
	// at SocketPath (--socket), or the dial will never succeed.
	Args []string
	// SocketPath is the engine's Unix socket.
	SocketPath string
	// MaxRestarts bounds restarts inside Window. 0 means no
	// restarts: the first death is final (and reported exhausted).
	MaxRestarts int
	// Window is the restart-budget window. Default 5 minutes.
	Window time.Duration
	// MinBackoff is the first restart delay; it doubles per
	// consecutive restart up to MaxBackoff. Defaults 250ms / 5s.
	MinBackoff time.Duration
	// MaxBackoff caps the restart delay. Default 5 seconds.
	MaxBackoff time.Duration
	// DialTimeout bounds how long one start waits for the engine
	// to load and serve before the start counts as failed.
	// Default 120 seconds (a 30B model load is slow).
	DialTimeout time.Duration
	// Logger receives lifecycle diagnostics; nil uses slog.Default().
	Logger *slog.Logger
}

// State is the supervisor's self-report for /debug.
type State struct {
	Running   bool   `json:"running"`
	PID       int    `json:"pid,omitempty"`
	Restarts  int    `json:"restarts"`
	Exhausted bool   `json:"exhausted"`
	LastExit  string `json:"last_exit,omitempty"`
	// StartedAt is the current incarnation's start time, RFC 3339.
	StartedAt string `json:"started_at,omitempty"`
}

// incarnation is one run of the engine process.
type incarnation struct {
	cmd  *exec.Cmd
	done chan struct{} // closed when the process has been waited on
	err  error         // the Wait result, valid after done closes
}

// Supervisor is a restart-budgeted owner of one engine process. It
// implements engine.Client by delegating to the live socket client.
type Supervisor struct {
	cfg Config
	log *slog.Logger

	mu         sync.RWMutex
	client     *engine.UnixClient
	inc        *incarnation
	restarts   []time.Time // restart instants inside the budget window
	exhausted  bool
	lastExit   string
	startedAt  time.Time
	stopping   bool
	stopOnce   sync.Once
	stopCh     chan struct{} // closed by Stop
	monitorDon chan struct{}
}

// New applies config defaults. It does not start the process; call
// Start.
func New(cfg Config) *Supervisor {
	if cfg.Logger == nil {
		cfg.Logger = slog.Default()
	}
	if cfg.Window <= 0 {
		cfg.Window = 5 * time.Minute
	}
	if cfg.MinBackoff <= 0 {
		cfg.MinBackoff = 250 * time.Millisecond
	}
	if cfg.MaxBackoff < cfg.MinBackoff {
		cfg.MaxBackoff = 5 * time.Second
	}
	if cfg.DialTimeout <= 0 {
		cfg.DialTimeout = 120 * time.Second
	}
	if cfg.MaxRestarts < 0 {
		cfg.MaxRestarts = 0
	}
	return &Supervisor{
		cfg:        cfg,
		log:        cfg.Logger,
		stopCh:     make(chan struct{}),
		monitorDon: make(chan struct{}),
	}
}

// Start launches the engine and waits for it to serve. An initial
// start failure is returned (the caller decides whether to run
// without an engine); restarts after a successful start are the
// monitor's job and are reported through State and the log, not
// returned.
func (s *Supervisor) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
	if s.cfg.Command == "" || s.cfg.SocketPath == "" {
		return errors.New("supervisor: Command and SocketPath are required")
	}
	if err := s.launch(ctx); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	// The monitor deliberately outlives the Start call's context:
	// its lifetime is the supervisor's, ended by Stop (stopCh).
	go s.monitor() //nolint:gosec // lifecycle bound by Stop, not the start ctx
	return nil
}

// stderrLineCap is the stderr pump's per-line buffer. The engine
// logs whole prompt summaries on single lines; the bufio default
// of 64 KiB ended the pump on the first long line and wedged the
// engine on a full pipe (merged adjudication H-2), so the cap is
// set explicitly, at 1 MiB.
const stderrLineCap = 1 << 20

// childEnv builds the engine child's environment from an allowlist:
// PATH plus the engine's own ITAK_ENGINE_* variables. The child
// never inherits the platform's wider environment, in particular
// TORCH_API_KEY: the engine has no use for the platform credential,
// and leaving it in the child's environment exposes it to any
// same-uid reader of /proc for the child's whole life.
func childEnv() []string {
	env := make([]string, 0, 8)
	for _, kv := range os.Environ() {
		key, _, _ := strings.Cut(kv, "=")
		if key == "PATH" || strings.HasPrefix(key, "ITAK_ENGINE_") {
			env = append(env, kv)
		}
	}
	return env
}

// launch starts one incarnation and dials it. On any failure the
// half-started process is killed and waited on before returning.
func (s *Supervisor) launch(ctx context.Context) error {
	cmd := exec.Command(s.cfg.Command, s.cfg.Args...) //nolint:gosec // operator-configured engine binary and args, by design
	cmd.Env = childEnv()
	stderr, err := cmd.StderrPipe()
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("supervisor: engine stderr pipe: %w", err)
	}
	if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("supervisor: start engine %q: %w", s.cfg.Command, err)
	}
	inc := &incarnation{cmd: cmd, done: make(chan struct{})}
	go s.pumpStderr(stderr)
	go func() {
		inc.err = cmd.Wait()
		close(inc.done)
	}()
	s.mu.Lock()
	s.inc = inc
	s.startedAt = time.Now()
	s.mu.Unlock()
	s.log.Info("engine started", "pid", cmd.Process.Pid, "socket", s.cfg.SocketPath)

	client, err := s.dialUntil(ctx, inc)
	if err != nil {
		s.kill(inc)
		return err
	}
	s.mu.Lock()
	if s.client != nil {
		_ = s.client.Close()
	}
	s.client = client
	s.mu.Unlock()
	s.log.Info("engine serving", "pid", cmd.Process.Pid, "socket", s.cfg.SocketPath)
	return nil
}

// pumpStderr forwards the engine's stderr, its diagnostic channel,
// into the platform log until the process ends. The scanner buffer
// is sized explicitly (stderrLineCap): with the bufio default, one
// long engine line ends the scan, the pipe stops draining, and the
// engine blocks mid-job on a full pipe while the supervisor reports
// it running. An abnormal pump end is reported through the log; a
// clean EOF at process exit is silent.
func (s *Supervisor) pumpStderr(stderr io.Reader) {
	sc := bufio.NewScanner(stderr)
	sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 64<<10), stderrLineCap)
	for sc.Scan() {
		s.log.Info("engine output", "line", sc.Text())
	}
	if err := sc.Err(); err != nil {
		s.log.Error("engine stderr forwarding ended abnormally; later engine output is lost",
			"err", err)
	}
}

// dialUntil polls the socket until the engine serves or the
// incarnation dies or the dial budget runs out. Loading a model
// takes seconds, so a refused dial is retried, not fatal.
func (s *Supervisor) dialUntil(ctx context.Context, inc *incarnation) (*engine.UnixClient, error) {
	deadline := time.Now().Add(s.cfg.DialTimeout)
	for {
		select {
		case <-inc.done:
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("supervisor: engine exited during startup: %w", waitErr(inc))
		case <-ctx.Done():
			return nil, ctx.Err()
		default:
		}
		dialCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 2*time.Second)
		client, err := engine.DialUnix(dialCtx, s.cfg.SocketPath)
		cancel()
		if err == nil {
			return client, nil
		}
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("supervisor: engine not serving within %s: %w", s.cfg.DialTimeout, err)
		}
		select {
		case <-inc.done:
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("supervisor: engine exited during startup: %w", waitErr(inc))
		case <-ctx.Done():
			return nil, ctx.Err()
		case <-time.After(150 * time.Millisecond):
		}
	}
}

func waitErr(inc *incarnation) error {
	if inc.err != nil {
		return inc.err
	}
	return errors.New("exit status 0")
}

// kill terminates an incarnation and waits for it to be reaped. A
// synthesized incarnation (the failed-launch record) has no process;
// its done channel is already closed.
func (s *Supervisor) kill(inc *incarnation) {
	if inc.cmd != nil && inc.cmd.Process != nil {
		_ = inc.cmd.Process.Kill()
	}
	<-inc.done
}

// monitor is the restart loop: one iteration per incarnation death.
func (s *Supervisor) monitor() {
	defer close(s.monitorDon)
	for {
		s.mu.RLock()
		inc := s.inc
		s.mu.RUnlock()
		if inc == nil {
			return
		}
		<-inc.done

		s.mu.Lock()
		if s.stopping {
			s.mu.Unlock()
			return
		}
		// The client of a dead process is stale the moment the
		// process exits; drop it before anything new is dialed.
		if s.client != nil {
			_ = s.client.Close()
			s.client = nil
		}
		s.lastExit = waitErr(inc).Error()
		now := time.Now()
		cutoff := now.Add(-s.cfg.Window)
		kept := s.restarts[:0]
		for _, t := range s.restarts {
			if t.After(cutoff) {
				kept = append(kept, t)
			}
		}
		s.restarts = kept
		if len(s.restarts) >= s.cfg.MaxRestarts {
			s.exhausted = true
			s.mu.Unlock()
			s.log.Error("engine died and the restart budget is exhausted; engine stays down",
				"last_exit", s.lastExit, "restarts", len(s.restarts), "window", s.cfg.Window)
			return
		}
		backoff := s.cfg.MinBackoff << len(s.restarts)
		if backoff > s.cfg.MaxBackoff || backoff <= 0 {
			backoff = s.cfg.MaxBackoff
		}
		s.restarts = append(s.restarts, now)
		restartNo := len(s.restarts)
		s.mu.Unlock()

		s.log.Warn("engine died; restarting within budget",
			"last_exit", s.lastExit, "restart", restartNo, "budget", s.cfg.MaxRestarts, "backoff", backoff)
		select {
		case <-time.After(backoff):
		case <-s.stopCh:
			return
		}
		if err := s.launch(context.Background()); err != nil {
			s.log.Error("engine restart failed to launch", "err", err)
			// A failed launch is another death for budget
			// purposes: synthesize an incarnation record so the
			// loop counts it instead of spinning.
			s.mu.Lock()
			s.lastExit = err.Error()
			s.inc = &incarnation{done: closedChan(), err: err}
			s.mu.Unlock()
		}
	}
}

var (
	closedOnce sync.Once
	closedCh   = make(chan struct{})
)

func closedChan() chan struct{} {
	closedOnce.Do(func() { close(closedCh) })
	return closedCh
}

// Stop shuts the supervisor down deliberately: no restart follows,
// the live client closes, and the engine process is killed. It is
// safe to call more than once.
func (s *Supervisor) Stop() {
	s.stopOnce.Do(func() {
		s.mu.Lock()
		s.stopping = true
		close(s.stopCh)
		client := s.client
		s.client = nil
		inc := s.inc
		s.mu.Unlock()
		if client != nil {
			_ = client.Close()
		}
		if inc != nil {
			s.kill(inc)
		}
	})
}

// Close is Stop under the name io.Closer users expect.
func (s *Supervisor) Close() error {
	s.Stop()
	return nil
}

// State snapshots the lifecycle for /debug.
func (s *Supervisor) State() State {
	s.mu.RLock()
	defer s.mu.RUnlock()
	st := State{
		Restarts:  len(s.restarts),
		Exhausted: s.exhausted,
		LastExit:  s.lastExit,
	}
	if s.client != nil && s.inc != nil && s.inc.cmd != nil && s.inc.cmd.Process != nil {
		st.Running = true
		st.PID = s.inc.cmd.Process.Pid
		st.StartedAt = s.startedAt.Format(time.RFC3339)
	}
	return st
}

func (s *Supervisor) current() *engine.UnixClient {
	s.mu.RLock()
	defer s.mu.RUnlock()
	return s.client
}

// Generate delegates to the live engine client. While the engine is
// down (restarting or budget-exhausted) it refuses with
// engine.ErrUnavailable; a generation the death catches mid-stream
// ends with the client's ErrEngineDied terminal event.
func (s *Supervisor) Generate(ctx context.Context, req engine.GenerateRequest) (<-chan engine.TokenEvent, error) {
	c := s.current()
	if c == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: engine down (supervisor state: %+v)", engine.ErrUnavailable, s.State())
	}
	return c.Generate(ctx, req)
}

// Embed delegates to the live engine client.
func (s *Supervisor) Embed(ctx context.Context, req engine.EmbedRequest) (engine.EmbedResponse, error) {
	c := s.current()
	if c == nil {
		return engine.EmbedResponse{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: engine down (supervisor state: %+v)", engine.ErrUnavailable, s.State())
	}
	return c.Embed(ctx, req)
}

// ChatTemplate delegates to the live engine client, so the
// platform's template probe works the same supervised or not.
func (s *Supervisor) ChatTemplate(ctx context.Context) (engine.ChatTemplate, error) {
	c := s.current()
	if c == nil {
		return engine.ChatTemplate{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: engine down (supervisor state: %+v)", engine.ErrUnavailable, s.State())
	}
	return c.ChatTemplate(ctx)
}

// Health reports the engine's health through the supervisor's own
// state when no client is live, so /healthz can say why it is down.
func (s *Supervisor) Health(ctx context.Context) (engine.HealthStatus, error) {
	c := s.current()
	if c == nil {
		st := s.State()
		detail := "engine down"
		if st.Exhausted {
			detail = fmt.Sprintf("engine down: restart budget exhausted, last exit: %s", st.LastExit)
		} else if st.LastExit != "" {
			detail = fmt.Sprintf("engine down: restarting after exit: %s", st.LastExit)
		}
		return engine.HealthStatus{OK: false, Detail: detail}, nil
	}
	return c.Health(ctx)
}

// DebugInfo merges the engine's self-report with the supervisor's
// lifecycle state, under the "supervisor" key.
func (s *Supervisor) DebugInfo(ctx context.Context) (map[string]any, error) {
	out := map[string]any{"supervisor": s.State()}
	c := s.current()
	if c == nil {
		return out, nil
	}
	info, err := c.DebugInfo(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		out["engine_debug_error"] = err.Error()
		return out, nil
	}
	for k, v := range info {
		out[k] = v
	}
	return out, nil
}

// Compile-time proof the supervisor is an engine.Client.
var _ engine.Client = (*Supervisor)(nil)
